Dwarf remains are a quest item used only in Dwarf Cannon. The remains are those of Gilob, and are given to Captain Lawgof after recovering them during the quest. It is found on the 1st floor of the watchtower south of the Coal Trucks.

Duplicates cannot be obtained, as it does not respawn after the player has picked it up for the first time.
1:
The toolkit is a quest item used only in Dwarf Cannon . It is obtained from Captain Lawgof after rescuing Lollk in the Goblin Cave .

It is used to fix the broken multicannon he has set up nearby in the dwarven outpost, south of the Coal Trucks near Baxtorian Falls .

Duplicates can be banked by talking to Captain Lawgof to obtain another. After speaking to Captain Lawgof after fixing the multicannon, all copies of the toolkit in the inventory are deleted.
2:
Steel cannonballs are ammunition used for a dwarf multicannon , as well as for a boat cannon during boat combat . They can be fired from steel cannons or stronger.

Four can be made from a single steel bar with level 35 Smithing , granting 25.6 experience per bar. Smithing cannonballs require the use of an ammo mould , which requires partial completion of Dwarf Cannon to obtain. Alternatively, a double ammo mould (requiring Foundry Reputation to purchase via the Giants' Foundry minigame) allows players to process two bars into eight cannonballs at the same speed as a regular ammo mould processes one bar into four.

Players with level 87 Sailing can further speed up smithing cannonballs by using the ancient furnace in the Grimstone Dungeon , which halves the time it takes to create cannonballs from 8 ticks to 4 ticks. Combining this with a double ammo mould, players can smith cannonballs at four times the normal speed.

Lastly, players with level 50 Smithing can use granite dust on steel cannonballs to create granite cannonballs , which gives superior stats on boat cannons, and increases the max hit of dwarf multicannons by 5. This yields no experience.
3:
Nulodion's notes are a quest item used only in Dwarf Cannon . It is obtained from Nulodion after speaking to Captain Lawgof after repairing his broken dwarf multicannon .

It is given to Captain Lawgof alongside Ammo mould to complete the quest.

Duplicates can be banked by talking to Nulodion to obtain another.
4:
An ammo mould is a quest item used in Dwarf Cannon . It is obtained from Nulodion after speaking to Captain Lawgof after repairing his broken dwarf multicannon . Additional moulds can be purchased from Nulodion's Multicannon parts for sale store for 5 coins .

It is given to Captain Lawgof alongside Nulodion's notes to complete the quest. It is also used to smith cannonballs with metal bars at a furnace to make 4 cannonballs per bar.

The double ammo mould is the upgraded version of this mould obtainable from Giants' Foundry , capable of producing up to 8 cannonballs at once, using two bars at once.

With 87 Sailing , the Ancient Furnace can be accessed within the Grimstone Dungeon and used to smelt cannonballs at double speed.
5:
The Instruction manual , or Dwarf Multicannon Manual , is a book that details how to set up and fire the dwarf multicannon , how to create cannonballs , and includes warranty information for the dwarf multicannon.

After completion Dwarf Cannon , it is found on a bookshelf in a player-owned house or is purchasable from Multicannon parts for sale for 10 coins or Rasolo the Wandering Merchant for 20 coins.
6:
The cannon base is the first part of the dwarf multicannon to be set up, followed by the stand. The Dwarf Cannon quest must be completed to use it. It is purchased from Multicannon parts for sale for 200,625 coins.

The cannon base by itself can decay without having the full cannon set up. When lost, a new cannon base can be obtained from Nulodion , free of charge.
8: The cannon stand is the second part of the dwarf multicannon set up on the ground after the cannon base and before cannon barrels . It is purchased from Multicannon parts for sale for 200,625 coins.
10: Cannon barrels are the third part of the dwarf multicannon set up on top of the cannon base after placing the cannon stand and before the cannon furnace . They shoot the enemy with a barrage of steel cannonballs or granite cannonballs . It is purchased from Multicannon parts for sale for 200,625 coins.
12: The cannon furnace powers the dwarf multicannon . It is the last part to be setup after the cannon barrels . Once setup, 30 steel cannonballs or granite cannonballs can be loaded for the dwarf multicannon to fire. It is purchased from Multicannon parts for sale for 200,625 coins.
14:
A railing is a quest item used only in Dwarf Cannon. In the quest, six railings are obtained from Captain Lawgof and used to replace six bent railings in the fence surrounding the Coal Trucks. A hammer is also needed to repair the fence.

There is a chance to fail when repairing sections of the fence, and the player may receive small amounts of damage which will deal 1-2 Hitpoints. The player will also receive a message saying either You cut your hand on the rusty old railing., You strain your back trying to handle the railings., or You accidentally crush your hand in the railing.
15:
The holy table napkin is a quest item obtained from Galahad in the Holy Grail quest. It is used to see the magic whistle spawn in Draynor Manor's top floor.

If the player wants to return to the Fisher Realm, it can be safely dropped if the player has access to fairy rings or keeps the magic whistle from the quest.
16:
The magic whistle is a quest item in the Holy Grail quest which is originally obtained in the southern room on the top floor of Draynor Manor . This spawn can only be seen and picked up while the player has a holy table napkin in their inventory. In this spawn location, there are two whistles, one for the player and one which must be given to Sir Percival .

Blowing the magic whistle while standing in the location where all of the mysterious statues point, under the tower north-west of Brimhaven , allows players to access the Fisher Realm . Blowing the magic whistle in the Fisher Realm returns the player to Karamja. Attempting to blow the whistle anywhere else will display the following message: The whistle makes no noise. It will not work in this location.

If lost after the quest, another may be obtained in the same manner as during the quest, or if the player has access to the fairy rings , there are several spawns in the Fisher Realm: one on a table inside the house in the north-west, one just outside that house, and one on a table just inside the castle.
17:
The grail bell is a quest item in the Holy Grail quest . It spawns just outside of castle in the Fisher Realm . When the bell is rung near the castle, a message will appear in the chatbox saying "Somehow you are now inside the castle." and the player will enter the castle.

Only one can be owned at a time; players cannot obtain another bell after completing the quest.
18:
The magic gold feather is a quest item used in the Holy Grail quest given to the player by King Arthur to help find Sir Percival .

Blowing on the feather will cause the feather to point either north, east, south, or west until the player reaches Goblin Village . Once the quest is completed, the feather has no use and can be safely dropped.
19:
The holy grail is a quest item in both the Holy Grail and King's Ransom quests .

During the Holy Grail quest, the main objective is to retrieve it from a table on the 2 nd floor [ UK ] 3 rd floor [ US ] of the east side of the Fisher King's castle in the Fisher Realm . During the quest, King Arthur informs you that it has just passed between dimensions into Gielinor . Should you choose to accept the quest and retrieve the Holy grail, you must travel to the Fisher Realm. If you attempt to take it before it's time, you will receive a message saying that you're not worthy of it. It is used to finish the quest by speaking to King Arthur while in your possession.

It is not possible to have more than one grail at a time. Attempting to take another yields the message: " You feel that taking more than one Holy Grail might be greedy... " Likewise, Telekinetic Grab cannot be cast on the grail. However, it is possible to obtain another grail after giving one to King Arthur during King's Ransom.

During the King's Ransom quest, the player must free King Arthur, his knights, and Merlin . The holy grail is found after answering a riddle, selecting the correct container, then using the animate rock scroll on King Arthur with it and granite in the inventory. This frees King Arthur and speaking to him in Camelot ends the quest.
20:
The white cog is a quest item used only in Clock Tower . It is found behind a gate that can be opened by adding rat poison to the food trough in the Clock Tower 's basement.

It is used to repair the western white clock spindle on the 2 nd floor [ UK ] 3 rd floor [ US ] .

Duplicates can be acquired by picking up another one after putting the first cog on the clock spindle and before completing the quest. Once the quest is completed, the cog can not be picked up from the spawn or if the duplicate is dropped.
21:
The black cog is a quest item used only in Clock Tower . It is found in a burning room in the Clock Tower 's basement, requiring a bucket of water in the inventory, or ice gloves or smiths gloves (i) equipped to pick up.

It is used to repair the eastern black clock spindle in the basement.

Duplicates can be acquired by picking up another one after putting the first cog on the clock spindle and before completing the quest. Once the quest is completed, the cog can not be picked up from the spawn or if the duplicate is dropped.
22:
The blue cog is a quest item used only in Clock Tower . It is found in a rat cage at the end of the path behind a push-able wall, which is accessed through a ladder north-east of the Clock Tower and south of the camel habitat of the Ardougne Zoo .

It is used to repair the southern blue clock spindle on the 1 st floor [ UK ] 2 nd floor [ US ] .

Duplicates can be acquired by picking up another one after putting the first cog on the clock spindle and before completing the quest. Once the quest is completed, the cog can not be picked up from the spawn or if the duplicate is dropped.
23:
The red cog is a quest item used only in Clock Tower . It is found in a room with three ogres in the Clock Tower 's basement.

It is used to repair the northern red clock spindle on the ground floor [ UK ] 1 st floor [ US ] .

Duplicates can be acquired by picking up another one after putting the first cog on the clock spindle and before completing the quest. Once the quest is completed, the cog can not be picked up from the spawn or if the duplicate is dropped.
24:
Rat poison is a quest item used in Clock Tower and Ratcatchers.

In the Clock Tower quest, players can pick up the rat poison spawn in the basement of the Clock Tower before retrieving the white cog. It is used on the rats' feeding trough to poison them, killing them, thus opening the western door to pick up the white cog.

In the Ratcatchers quest, if the player has a vial, kwuarm, and red spiders' eggs, after talking about the rat infestation, Hooknosed Jack will make rat poison to use on four pieces of cheese to make poisoned cheese. He will not make rat poison for the player after this quest.
25:
The red vine worm is used in the Fishing Contest quest to catch the giant carp that wins the contest. They also may be needed to make a pair of magic secateurs in the quest A Fairy Tale I - Growing Pains , and can be possible a clue for finding Solus Dellagar in the quest Wanted! .

They are obtained by digging with spade near the red vines that can be found in McGrubor's Wood . The fairy ring code A L S can be used to quickly reach the vines.
26:
The fishing trophy is a quest item used only in Fishing Contest . It is obtained from Bonzo after catching a raw giant carp .

It is given to either Austri or Vestri to complete the quest.

Multiple fishing trophies can be obtained by using the drop trick ; drop the original trophy given by Bonzo , ask for another, then pick up the other trophy from the floor. Using additional trophies on either Austri or Vestri after the quest will cause them to be taken off you.
27:
The fishing pass is a quest item used only in Fishing Contest . It is obtained from Austri or Vestri upon starting the quest.

It is shown to Morris to enter the competition area each time.

If lost, the dwarves can replace it with another. More fishing passes cannot be acquired after completing the quest. It is not needed to enter the competition area after talking to Aggie about white dyes during the Land of the Goblins quest.
28:
Insect repellent is a container of bug spray that can be used on beehives , large mosquitoes , and mosquito swarms .

Using insect repellent on beehives, located in the apiary west of Catherby and in southern Seers' Village , causes the bees to leave. Using a bucket on the beehive then gives a bucket of wax , which is used in Merlin's Crystal and Troll Romance . Insect repellent must be used on the beehive every time, otherwise the bees will have returned and no wax will be collected.

It is also used on large mosquitoes and mosquito swarms encountered in the Tai Bwo Wannai Cleanup minigame to halve their combat stats and prevent them from attacking for six seconds. This can be done multiple times until their stats are reduced to 1. Giant mosquitoes found on Mos Le'Harmless are unaffected.
30:
A bucket of wax is obtained by interacting with a beehive in the apiary south of Seers' Village , west of Catherby . The player must have an empty bucket in their inventory, and either wear full beekeeper's outfit or use insect repellent on the beehive first. This process must be repeated per bucket of wax. It is used in the Merlin's Crystal and Troll Romance quests .

There is a bucket spawn right beside the gate of the apiary.

In the Merlin's Crystal quest, Morgan Le Faye tells the player how to release Merlin in exchange for sparing Sir Mordred 's life, requiring a black candle among other things. The Candle maker in Catherby offers to make one for the player if they bring him a bucket of wax.

In the Troll Romance quest, swamp tar is used on a bucket of wax with a cake tin in the inventory to make wax . The wax is then used on the sled , so that players can slide down Trollweiss Mountain to get to the trollweiss they need to pick.
32:
A black candle is a light source used in the Merlin's Crystal quest.

During Merlin's Crystal, in exchange for sparing Sir Mordred's life, Morgan Le Faye details how to free Merlin, requiring a black candle among other things. The Candle maker in Catherby offers to make one if the player brings him a bucket of wax. Once all the other items are obtained, it is lit with a tinderbox when inside the magical symbol, inside the fence on the north-east side of Camelot Castle. After the remaining items are used, and with the correct incantation, Thrantax the Mighty is summoned for the player to command to free Merlin.

Black candles can not be purchased from the Candle maker after Merlin's Crystal, but multiple can be obtained during the quest. Although they aren't tradeable, they can be put in empty candle lanterns to make candle lanterns, which are tradeable.
33:
A candle is the lowest tier of Firemaking light sources. It can be lit with a tinderbox. Lit candles can be extinguished by clicking extinguish on them or falling into swamp water in the Lumbridge Caves. Candles may be acquired through various means such as finding them within certain houses, purchasing them from a candle seller or candle maker, or by trading with other players.

A candle is a required item for Enlightened Journey and Enakhra's Lament.
34:
A lit candle is an unobtainable version of the Lit candle. Candles were previously tradeable and could be turned into banknotes. However, they were made untradeable due to an unfixable bug where trading a lit candle in a dark area would not update the lighting for either player. Any player who had a noted Lit candle was given this now discontinued item. Originally, the item was identical to the real lit candle, except being stackable.

As this change occurred prior to August 2007, the item has never been obtainable in Old School RuneScape.
35:
Excalibur is a one-handed sword and a quest item obtained from the Merlin's Crystal quest and used in the Holy Grail quest. It requires 20 Attack to wield and has similar stats to the adamant longsword , except for 6 less strength bonus and 1 more magic defence.

In the Merlin's Crystal quest, the player must use Excalibur on the crystal to smash and free Merlin . It is obtained from Lady of the Lake after she tests the purity of the player's spirit when giving a beggar bread at Grum's Gold Exchange in Port Sarim .

In the Holy Grail quest, Excalibur must be equipped as the Black Knight Titan dies in order to enter the Fisher Realm and be able to continue the quest. If another weapon is equipped when he dies, the fight will restart.

Low level players may find Excalibur useful for combat because of its stats, low requirements to obtain and wield, and is free the first time.

If lost, it can be retrieved from the Lady of the Lake in Taverley for 500 coins.

Bronze arrowtips are made with a bronze bar requiring 5 Smithing, yielding 12.5 Smithing experience and 15 bronze arrowtips. They are made into bronze arrows when used with headless arrows, requiring 1 Fletching, yielding 19.5 Fletching experience per 15 arrows.

They are purchased for 1 coin at the ranging shops: Hickton's Archery Emporium in Catherby, Armoury in the Combat Training Camp, Dargaud's Bow and Arrows in the Ranging Guild, Gulluck and Sons on the 2nd floor of the Grand Tree, and Void Knight Archery Store at the Void Knights' Outpost.
40:
Iron arrowtips are made with an iron bar requiring 20 Smithing , yielding Smithing 25 experience and 15 iron arrowtips. They are made into iron arrows when used with headless arrows , requiring 15 Fletching , yielding 37.5 experience per 15 arrows.

They are purchased for 2 coins at the ranging shops: Hickton's Archery Emporium in Catherby , Dargaud's Bow and Arrows in the Ranging Guild , Gulluck and Sons on the 2 nd floor [ UK ] 3 rd floor [ US ] of the Grand Tree , Void Knight Archery Store at the Void Knights' Outpost , and Ava's Odds and Ends in Draynor Manor . They are purchased for 3 coins at the Armoury in the Combat Training Camp .
41:
Steel arrowtips are made with a steel bar requiring 35 Smithing, yielding 37.5 Smithing experience and 15 steel arrowtips. They are made into steel arrows when used with headless arrows, requiring 30 Fletching, yielding 75 experience per 15 arrows.

At 47 Thieving, they can be stolen from chests in Hemenster, Rellekka, and West Ardougne.

There is an item spawn in the northern section of the Edgeville Dungeon at level 10 Wilderness by the earth warriors.

They are purchased for 6 coins at the ranging shops: Hickton's Archery Emporium in Catherby, Dargaud's Bow and Arrows in the Ranging Guild, Gulluck and Sons on the 2nd floor of the Grand Tree, and Void Knight Archery Store at the Void Knights' Outpost. They are purchased for 7 coins at Ava's Odds and Ends in Draynor Manor, and they are also purchased for 9 coins at the Armoury in the Combat Training Camp.
42:
Mithril arrowtips are made with a mithril bar requiring 55 Smithing , yielding 50 Smithing experience and 15 mithril arrowtips. They are made into mithril arrows when used with headless arrows , requiring 45 Fletching , yielding 112.5 experience per 15 arrows.

They are purchased for 16 coins at the ranging shops: Hickton's Archery Emporium in Catherby , Dargaud's Bow and Arrows in the Ranging Guild , Gulluck and Sons on the 2 nd floor [ UK ] 3 rd floor [ US ] of the Grand Tree , and Void Knight Archery Store at the Void Knights' Outpost . They are purchased for 24 coins at the Armoury in the Combat Training Camp .
43:
Adamant arrowtips are made with an adamant bar requiring 75 Smithing , yielding 62.5 Smithing experience and 15 adamant arrowtips. They are made into adamant arrows when used with headless arrows , requiring 60 Fletching , yielding 150 experience per 15 arrows.

They are purchased for 40 coins at the ranging shops: Hickton's Archery Emporium in Catherby , Dargaud's Bow and Arrows in the Ranging Guild , and Void Knight Archery Store at the Void Knights' Outpost .
44:
Rune arrowtips are made with a runite bar requiring 90 Smithing, yielding 75 Smithing experience and 15 rune arrowtips. They are made into rune arrows when used with headless arrows, requiring 75 Fletching, yielding 187.5 experience per 15 arrows.

They are purchased for 200 coins at the ranging shops: Hickton's Archery Emporium in Catherby, Dargaud's Bow and Arrows in the Ranging Guild, and Void Knight Archery Store at the Void Knights' Outpost.
45:
Opal bolt tips are created by using a chisel on a cut opal with 11 Fletching, yielding 1.5 Fletching experience and 12 opal bolt tips.

They are made into opal bolts when used with bronze bolts, requiring 11 Fletching, yielding 16 Fletching experience per 10 bolts. They can also be made into opal dragon bolts, requiring 84 Fletching, yielding 16 Fletching experience per 10 bolts. Both of these can then be enchanted into opal bolts (e) and opal dragon bolts (e) respectively.
46:
Pearl bolt tips are created by using a chisel on an oyster pearl or oyster pearls with 41 Fletching , yielding 3.2 Fletching experience both, but 6 and 24 pearl bolt tips respectively.

They are made into pearl bolts when used with iron bolts , requiring 41 Fletching, yielding 32 Fletching experience per 10 bolts . They can also be made into pearl dragon bolts , requiring 84 Fletching, yielding 32 Fletching experience per 10 bolts. Both of these can then be enchanted into pearl bolts (e) and pearl dragon bolts (e) respectively.
47: Barb bolttips are bolt tips that are made into barbed bolts when used with bronze bolts , requiring 51 Fletching , yielding 95 Fletching experience per 10 bolts . 30 barb bolttips can be purchased for 140 archery tickets from the Ranging Guild Ticket Exchange in the Ranging Guild .
48: A longbow (u) is made using a knife with logs , requiring 10 Fletching and yielding 10 Fletching experience . Stringing a longbow (u) with a bowstring makes a longbow , also requiring 10 Fletching and yielding an additional 10 Fletching experience.
50: A shortbow (u) is made using a knife with logs , requiring 5 Fletching and yielding 5 Fletching experience . Stringing a shortbow (u) with a bowstring makes a shortbow , also requiring 5 Fletching and yielding an additional 5 Fletching experience.
52:
An arrow shaft is used in Fletching to make arrows. Arrow shafts can be cut from different types of logs by using a knife on them, each tier yielding 5 additional Fletching experience per set of 15 arrow shafts. 15 Feathers can be attached to 15 arrow shafts at 1 Fletching, yielding 15 experience and 15 headless arrows. Arrowtips are then attached to headless arrows to create arrows. Spider on shaft can be made by using an arrow shaft on a spider carcass with 16 Cooking.

Arrow shafts are purchased for 1 coin at Dargaud's Bow and Arrows in the Ranging Guild.
53:
A headless arrow is used in Fletching to make arrows. Attaching 15 feathers to 15 arrow shafts, requiring 1 Fletching, yields 15 Fletching experience and 15 headless arrows. 15 arrowtips can be attached to headless arrows to make arrows.

There are several item spawns of headless arrows in the Scorpion Pit, deep in the Wilderness.
54: An oak shortbow (u) is made using a knife with oak logs , requiring 20 Fletching and yielding 16.5 Fletching experience . Stringing an oak shortbow (u) with a bowstring makes an oak shortbow , also requiring 20 Fletching and yielding an additional 16.5 Fletching experience.
56: An Oak longbow (u) is made using a knife with oak logs, requiring level 25 Fletching and yielding 25 Fletching experience. Stringing an oak longbow (u) with a bowstring makes an oak longbow, also requiring 25 Fletching and yielding an additional 25 experience.
58: A willow longbow (u) is made using a knife with willow logs , requiring 40 Fletching and yielding 41.5 Fletching experience . Stringing a willow longbow (u) with a bowstring makes a willow longbow , also requiring 40 Fletching and yielding an additional 41.5 experience.
60: A willow shortbow (u) is made using a knife with willow logs , requiring 35 Fletching and yielding 33.3 Fletching experience . Stringing a willow shortbow (u) with a bowstring makes a willow shortbow , also requiring 35 Fletching and yielding an additional 33.3 Fletching experience.
62: A maple longbow (u) is made using a knife with maple logs, requiring 55 Fletching and yielding 58.3 Fletching experience. Stringing a maple longbow (u) with a bowstring makes a maple longbow, also requiring 55 Fletching and yielding an additional 58.2 Fletching experience.
64: A maple shortbow (u) is made using a knife with maple logs , requiring 50 Fletching and yielding 50 Fletching experience . Stringing a maple shortbow (u) with a bowstring makes a maple shortbow , also requiring 50 Fletching and yielding an additional 50 Fletching experience.
66: A yew longbow (u) is made using a knife with yew logs , requiring 70 Fletching and yielding 75 Fletching experience . Stringing a yew longbow (u) with a bowstring makes a yew longbow , also requiring 70 Fletching and yielding an additional 75 Fletching experience.
68: A yew shortbow (u) is made using a knife with yew logs , requiring 65 Fletching and yielding 67.5 Fletching experience . Stringing a yew shortbow (u) with a bowstring makes a yew shortbow , also requiring 65 Fletching and yielding an additional 67.5 Fletching experience.
70: A magic longbow (u) is made using a knife with magic logs , requiring 85 Fletching and yielding 91.5 Fletching experience . Stringing a magic longbow (u) with a bowstring makes a magic longbow , also requiring 85 Fletching and yielding an additional 91.5 Fletching experience.
72: A magic shortbow (u) is made using a knife with magic logs, requiring level 80 Fletching and yielding 83.3 Fletching experience. Stringing a magic shortbow (u) with a bowstring makes a magic shortbow, also requiring 80 Fletching and yielding an additional 83.3 Fletching experience.
74:
A Khazard helmet is a quest item in the Fight Arena quest . It is a dark coloured medium helmet that is part of the Khazard armour set . It has stats similar to an iron med helm , except unlike most medium helmets , it does not have a penalty to Magic , making it a viable choice for mages and rangers.

In the Fight Arena quest, a Khazard helmet and Khazard armour can only be found by searching the chest in a building north of the Fight Arena . They both must be worn to enter the Khazard prisons. Unequipping either the helmet or armour inside the jail causes the guards to kick the player out.

If lost, it can be reobtained in the same chest. Multiple armour pieces can be obtained through the drop trick .
75:
A Khazard armour is a quest item in the Fight Arena quest . It is a dark coloured platebody that is part of the Khazard armour set . It has stats worse than a bronze platebody , but unlike most melee armours, it does not have a penalty to Magic or Ranged accuracy, nor does it interfere with Ava's devices , making it a viable choice for mages and rangers. It also weighs far less than a typical platebody . Another nearby quest item, Carnillean armour , has over double the stab defence and +3 slash defence bonuses, at the cost of -2 crush defence and nearly 20x the weight .

In the Fight Arena quest, a Khazard helmet and Khazard armour can only be found by searching the chest in a building north of the Fight Arena . They both must be worn to enter the Khazard prisons. Unequipping either the helmet or armour inside the jail causes the guards to kick the player out.

If lost, it can be reobtained in the same chest. Multiple armour pieces can be obtained through the drop trick .
76: Khazard cell keys are a quest item in the Fight Arena quest . They are obtained by giving a Khali brew to the Head Guard in the south-eastern room of the jail at the Fight Arena , north of Yanille . The keys are used to unlock the door to the cell that holds Sammy Servil prisoner.
77: Khali brew is a quest item in the Fight Arena quest . Once the player has spoken to the Head Guard in the south-eastern room of the jail, it is possible to buy the beer for 5 coins from the Khazard barman in the bar in the south-west corner of the Fight Arena . The Khazard barman suggests lying down before drinking it so there is less distance to collapse ; however, there is no option for the player to drink it. Giving it to the Head Guard will get him drunk and allow you to steal the Khazard cell keys .
78:
Ice arrows are a quest item in the Temple of Ikov quest . They have the same Ranged Strength as steel arrows , but must be fired from a yew bow or better.

In the Temple of Ikov quest, they are collected randomly when searching chests in the eastern Temple of Ikov dungeon and required to defeat the Fire Warrior of Lesarkus . While not required, ice arrows can also be used to defeat Fareed from the Desert Treasure I quest, as all other ammunition will drop to the floor as ashes , bypassing the ammo-saving effect of Ava's devices .

Upon completion of the quest, players can still go back and obtain more should they desire it.
83:
The lever is a quest item in the Temple of Ikov quest . It is found in the eastern room in the Temple of Ikov after crossing the bridge which requires the player's weight to be below 0 kg (using boots of lightness or other weight-reducing clothing ) to successfully cross. It is used to operate a broken lever which opens a door leading further into the temple.

After the quest, the item is still obtainable, but has no further use beyond the quest.
84:
The Staff of Armadyl is a quest item in the Temple of Ikov quest. If allied with Lucien, the staff of Armadyl is stolen from a table within the Temple of Ikov dungeon after killing a Guardian of Armadyl and brought to Lucien to complete the quest. If allied with the guardians, the player will receive an Armadyl pendant to equip and prove they are no longer allies of Lucien, then go and kill him.

Multiple copies of the staff cannot be obtained. The staff also cannot be telekinetically grabbed. If the staff is dropped and then the quest is completed, attempting to pick up the staff will yield the message: "You have completed the quest of the Temple of Ikov."

However, by dying while carrying the staff, it can be sent to Death’s Domain. This allows the player to take another staff, and any extra staves stored there will remain when the quest is completed.

A replica of the staff is on display at the Varrock Museum after explaining what it looks like to the museum curator on the 1st floor with the quest complete.
85: The shiny key is obtainable after partial completion of the Temple of Ikov quest , found at the end of the Temple of Ikov dungeon . It is used to take the shortcut from the house in McGrubor's Wood to the lesser demon area of the Temple of Ikov dungeon. It can be placed on the steel key ring .
86:

If lost it can be reobtained by:

After completion of Temple of Ikov it is no longer necessary to open the northern dungeon door in the Temple of Ikov dungeon, and after completion of While Guthix Sleeps it can no longer be reobtained by any means.
87:
The Armadyl pendant is a quest item in the Temple of Ikov quest . A Guardian of Armadyl in the Temple of Ikov dungeon gives the player the pendant if the player sides with them. Equipping it allows players to attack Lucien , once he is defeated, the quest is complete.

This pendant is the easiest obtainable protection against Armadyl and followers of Armadyl in the God Wars Dungeon .

If lost, it can be reobtained by:

A shiny key is needed for the fastest method. Down the ladder of the house in McGrubor's Wood , fairy ring ALS, walk west until there is a wall with the "Push" option. Depending on alignment, kill or talk to a Guardian for a replacement pendant.

Multiple Armadyl pendants can be obtained through the drop trick .

113:
A Strength potion is a potion that can be made by free-to-play players in addition to members. Both non-members and members can make a strength potion (4) by providing the Apothecary in Varrock with 5 coins, a limpwurt root , and red spiders' eggs . Members who have attained at least level 12 Herblore additionally have the ability to use a limpwurt root on a tarromin potion (unf) , yielding a Strength potion(3) and 50 Herblore experience . A dose of Strength potion provides a temporary skill boost to Strength equal to 3 + 10% of the player's current Strength level, rounded down. This is less than the super Strength 's and super combat potion 's boost of 5 + 15% of the player's current Strength level, rounded down.

After Barbarian Herblore Training , roe or caviar can be added to a Strength potion(2), requiring 14 Herblore, yielding a Strength mix and 17 Herblore experience. A Strength mix has 2 doses, boosts Strength equal to 3 + 10% of the player's current Strength level, rounded down, and heals 3 Hitpoints .

A Strength potion(2) can occasionally be obtained from a chest inside the maze random event .

A Strength potion(3) can be purchased from the Warriors' Guild potion shop for 15 coins.

A Strength potion(4) is a reward from Jekyll and Hyde random events if a guam leaf is given to Dr Jekyll. If the player talks to Dr Jekyll and does not give a herb, then Dr Jekyll gives a Strength potion(2).

A restore potion is a potion made by using red spiders' eggs on a harralander potion (unf) , requiring 22 Herblore , yielding a restore potion(3) and 62.5 Herblore experience . A dose of restore potion restores levels of temporarily reduced stats in Attack , Strength , Defence , Ranged , and Magic equal to 10 + 30% of the related maximum level, rounded down, for each skill. It does not restore Prayer points or any other skill that is not listed like a super restore . Restore potions will not boost any skill above its base level, even if the listed restore is greater than the current reduction.

After Barbarian Herblore Training , roe or caviar can be added to a restore potion(2), requiring 24 Herblore, yielding a Restore mix and 21 Herblore experience. A restore mix has 2 doses, restores the listed stats equal to 10 + 30% of the related current level, rounded down, for each skill, and heals 3 Hitpoints .

A restore potion(4) is a reward from Jekyll and Hyde random events if a harralander is given to Dr Jekyll.

187:
Weapon poison is a potion made by using dragon scale dust on a kwuarm potion (unf), requiring 60 Herblore, yielding a weapon poison and 137.5 Herblore experience. It can be applied to all metal arrows (including amethyst), normal metal bolts, javelins, darts, and throwing knives, most daggers, spears and hastae as well. Weapon poison can be removed from a weapon with a cleaning cloth.

A single vial of weapon poison can poison only 5 arrows, bolts, darts, or throwing knives. This makes poisoning a substantial amount of ammo quite costly.

Melee attacks apply poison at 25% chance, where Ranged attacks apply poison at 12.5% chance. This chance only applies if the hit was successful (non-zero). Weapon poison initially deals 4 damage when applied using melee attacks, or 2 damage with Ranged attacks. The poison hits every 18 seconds, and if not reapplied to the target, the poison damage will deal 1 less damage every 5 hits until the target is no longer poisoned. Ranged weapons with Weapon poison applied, however, will only hit 2 once before starting to hit 1s. For melee weapons this means a total of 50 damage will be dealt from the poison, whilst for ranged weapons this will only be 7.

It is a possible reward from the Observatory Quest if the player identifies the Scorpio constellation.
189:
A Zamorak brew is a potion made by using jangerberries on a torstol potion (unf), requiring 78 Herblore, yielding a Zamorak brew(3) and 175 Herblore experience. A dose of Zamorak brew provides a temporary skill boost to Attack equal to 2 + 20% of the player's base Attack level, rounded down, and Strength equal to 2 + 12% of the player's base Strength level, rounded down. It temporarily lowers Defence equal to 2 + 10% of the player's current Defence level, rounded down, and current Hitpoints by 12%, rounded down, though it will not lower a player's Hitpoints below the minimum of 1. Additionally, 10% of the player's current Prayer level is restored as Prayer points. When used in conjunction with a Saradomin brew, Attack and Defence will be boosted, Prayer and Health will be restored (possibly boosted by the brew), Ranged and Magic will be lowered.

Restore potions are frequently used with Zamorak brews to raise lowered Defence. A super strength potion will always boost Strength level higher than a Zamorak brew; however, the Zamorak brew's Attack boost is slightly better than a super attack potion. At levels 85, 86, 90-93, and 95-99, the Zamorak brew will give a boost of 2 levels more than a Super attack potion. You can also use a super strength potion or a dragon battleaxe special attack before you sip a dose to increase your Strength level to the max.

After Barbarian Herblore Training is completed, caviar can be added to a Zamorak brew(2) to produce a Zamorak mix. This requires 85 Herblore and provides 58 Herblore experience. A Zamorak mix has 2 doses, each of which heals 6 Hitpoints in addition to the usual Zamorak brew behaviour.

At level 99 Prayer, Zamorak brews cost 15.98 per Prayer point restored.

195:
A potion is given to a player by asking the Apothecary in Varrock for a free sample. The Apothecary will give it roughly half the time, otherwise refusing to do so. Multiple potions can be obtained using the drop trick . It can also be obtained as a rare drop from killing Imps , or failing The Gauntlet .

The Apothecary indicates that the potion is a spot cream. If used on various citizens in Sophanem before completing Beneath Cursed Sands , it is revealed that the potion is used to relieve itching.
197: A poison chalice is a cocktail obtained for free from Stankers, a dwarven miner near the Coal Trucks west of Seers' Village. Drinking a poison chalice applies a random effect, and leaves behind an empty cocktail glass. Drinking the poison chalice cannot lower your Hitpoints past 4.
199:
A grimy guam leaf is a herb that can be cleaned, requiring 3 Herblore , and yielding a guam leaf and 2.5 Herblore experience .

Grimy guam leaves can be harvested from herb patches after planting a guam seed , requiring 9 Farming .

Guam leaves are used to make Attack potions , Guthix rests , and guam tar .

A grimy guam leaf spawns in the Deep Wilderness Dungeon .

When cleaned, the message You clean the Grimy guam leaf. is displayed.
201:
A grimy marrentill is a herb that has not yet been cleaned to make a marrentill . Grimy marrentills may be grown from a Marrentill seed with a Farming level of 14. It is also dropped by certain monsters . Cleaning a Grimy marrentill requires a Herblore level of 5 and gives 3.8 Herblore experience. Clean marrentills are used in the making of antipoisons at level 5 Herblore , Guthix rests at level 18 Herblore, and marrentill tar at level 31. Marrentill can also be used to light incense burners in player-owned houses .

When cleaned, the message You clean the Grimy marrentill. is displayed.
203:
A grimy tarromin is a herb that has not yet been cleaned to make a tarromin. Grimy tarromins may be grown from a tarromin seed with a Farming level of 19. It is dropped by certain NPCs. Cleaning a grimy tarromin requires a Herblore level of 11 and gives 5 Herblore experience. Clean tarromins are used to make Strength potions and Serum 207s with a Herblore level of 12 and a Herblore level of 15 respectively. Clean tarromins can also be used with swamp tar to create tarromin tar at level 39 Herblore.

When cleaned, the message You clean the Grimy tarromin. is displayed.
205:
A grimy harralander is a herb that has not yet been cleaned to make a harralander . Grimy harralanders may be grown from a harralander seed with a Farming level of 26. It is dropped by certain NPCs . Cleaning a grimy harralander requires a Herblore level of 20 and gives 6.3 Herblore experience. Clean harralanders are used to make Guthix rests , compost potions , restore potions , Guthix balance potions , Blamish oil (for the Heroes' Quest ) and Energy potions with Herblore levels of 18, 21, 22, 22, and 26 respectively. Using harralander to make harralander tar is a popular and very fast method for training Herblore, without having to do many steps.

When cleaned, the message You clean the Grimy harralander. is displayed.
207:
A grimy ranarr weed is a herb that can be cleaned to make a ranarr weed . Grimy ranarr weeds may be grown from a ranarr seed with a Farming level of 32 and gives 30.5 Farming experience. Cleaning a grimy ranarr requires a Herblore level of 25 and gives 7.5 Herblore experience. Clean ranarr weeds are used to make defence potions and prayer potions with a Herblore level of 30 and 38, respectively.

Grimy herbs, including ranarr, are commonly found by killing chaos druids and elder chaos druids , although they reside in the Wilderness . Killing flesh crawlers and chaos druids are also a relatively good strategy to collect grimy ranarrs.
209:
A grimy irit leaf is a herb that has not yet been cleaned to make an irit leaf . Grimy irit leaves may be grown from an irit seed with a Farming level of 44. It is dropped by certain NPCs . Cleaning a grimy irit requires a Herblore level of 40 and gives 8.8 Herblore experience. Clean irits are used to make super attack , super anti-poison potions , irit tar , and antidote++ with Herblore levels of 45, 48, 55, and 79 respectively. They are dropped inside the Edgeville Dungeon and Taverley Dungeon by the Chaos druids .

When cleaned, the message You clean the Grimy irit leaf. is displayed.
211:

Cleaning a grimy avantoe requires a Herblore level of 48 and gives 10 Herblore experience. Clean avantoes are used to make fishing potions , super energy potions and hunter potions , requiring levels 50, 52, and 53 Herblore respectively.

When cleaned, the message You clean the Grimy avantoe. is displayed.
213:
A grimy kwuarm is a kwuarm that has not been cleaned yet, requiring a Herblore level of 54. Cleaning a grimy kwuarm yields 11.3 experience. Grimy kwuarms may be grown from a kwuarm seed with a Farming level of 56 or dropped by certain NPCs . Clean kwuarms are used to make super strength potion and weapon poisons with a Herblore level of 55 and a Herblore level of 60 respectively.

When cleaned, the message You clean the Grimy kwuarm. is displayed.
215:

Cleaning a grimy cadantine requires a Herblore level of 65 and gives 12.5 Herblore experience. Cadantines are used to make super defence potions with a Herblore level of 66.

When cleaned, the message You clean the Grimy cadantine. is displayed.
217:
A grimy dwarf weed is the second-highest level herb . A player with 70 Herblore may clean it and produce a dwarf weed for 13.8 Herblore experience . Dwarf weed is mainly used to create ranging potions .

It may be grown from a dwarf weed seed at 79 Farming , granting 192 experience per herb during harvest.
219:
A grimy torstol is a herb that has not yet been cleaned to make a torstol. Grimy torstols may be grown from a torstol seed with a Farming level of 85, granting 224.5 experience per herb during harvest. Cleaning a grimy torstol requires a Herblore level of 75 and gives 15 Herblore experience. Clean torstols are used to make Super combat potions with a Herblore level of 90 or Zamorak brews with a Herblore level of 78. Grimy torstol is one of the five herbs that cannot be obtained from the Sorceress's Garden.

One grimy torstol plus 8 other grimy herbs can be obtained from the Sinister chest in the Yanille Agility dungeon when unlocked with a Sinister key.
221:
An eye of newt is used in Herblore to make attack potions and super attack potions. They can obtained in bulk by purchasing eye of newt packs from various herblore shops.

One eye of newt is needed for the Witch's Potion and Recipe for Disaster quests. After completing Tower of Life, they can be used in the Creature Creation activity together with a feather to create a newtroost.
223:
Red spiders' eggs are a Herblore ingredient that members can use to make one of three different potions. Those with level 22 Herblore can combine them with a harralander potion (unf) (made by adding harralander to a vial of water) to make a restore potion and gain 62.5 experience points. Those with level 63 Herblore can combine the eggs with a snapdragon potion (unf) (made by adding snapdragon to a vial of water) to make a super restore potion and gain 142.5 experience. Those with level 73 herblore can combine the eggs with coconut milk and a cactus spine to make weapon poison(+) and gain 190 experience.

All players can give red spiders' eggs along with a limpwurt root and 5 coins to the apothecary in Varrock, and he will give them a 4-dose strength potion in return.
225:
Limpwurt roots are a Herblore secondary ingredient that can be grown through the Farming skill at level 26 with limpwurt seeds . 15 limpwurt roots are used to protect growing teak trees .

They are useful in free-to-play to make strength potions (or super strength for members ). The Apothecary in Varrock will exchange them for four-dose antipoison , energy potions , and strength potions. Adding them to a compost bin makes regular compost .

Limpwurt roots can easily be obtained from hill giants and hobgoblins ; ogresses also commonly drop them.
227:
A vial of water is an item made by using a vial on a water source other than a well. It is mainly used for training Herblore .

Vials of water can be purchased from the general store in Ardougne , Shilo Village , Rellekka , Jiminua's Jungle Store , and from Jossik in the Lighthouse . It can also be purchased from the Nightmare Zone using 145 reward points . You may buy them in packs of 100, called a water-filled vial pack , which starts at 201 coins .
229: Vials are typically filled up with water and are most commonly used in the Herblore skill to make potions or mixes. Upon finishing a potion, the empty vial is left in the player's inventory; however with completion of Alfred Grimhand's Barcrawl , players may speak to the barbarian guard outside of the Barbarian Outpost to learn how to automatically smash vials upon finishing a potion. This feature also works in free-to-play. The player may also toggle this feature from the settings menu.
231:
Snape grass is a Herblore secondary ingredient that can be grown through the Farming skill at level 61 with snape grass seeds . 8 snape grass are needed to protect growing potato cactus .

It is used to make prayer potions and fishing potions . It is also used when making the hangover cure quest item. When placed in a compost bin , snape grass will create supercompost .

Farming snape grass gives a decent amount of experience and thus is a great way for players (especially ironmen ) to train the skill.
233:
The pestle and mortar is a tool used to crush items for use in Herblore and many quests, as well as the Sorceress's Garden minigame.

It can be bought from Herbalists and certain general stores. If used to auto-crush items, it will do so every three game ticks.
235:
Unicorn horn dust is a Herblore ingredient obtained by using a unicorn horn with a pestle and mortar or as a drop from cave bugs and cave crawlers. It can be used with a marrentill potion (unf) to make antipoison or with an irit potion (unf) to make superantipoison. It is also one of the ingredients required to turn super restores into Sanfew serums. One unicorn horn dust is used on the quest Ratcatchers.

Wesley in Nardah can crush unnoted or noted herblore secondary items for 50 coins per item.
237: A unicorn horn is used to make a herblore ingredient that can be obtained as a drop from unicorns and black unicorns. It can be ground down to unicorn horn dust using a pestle and mortar. The dust can then be used as an ingredient in antipoison, super antipoison, and sanfew serum potions. It is also used alongside a cowhide to summon a Unicow in Creature Creation.
239:
White berries can be harvested from a bush patch after planting whiteberry seeds. They are used in Herblore to make defence potions and super defences.

Adding them to a compost bin makes supercompost, though this is not recommended as watermelons or pineapples are far cheaper and have the same effect.

Farmers can be paid 10 white berries to protect a camphor tree.
241:
Dragon scale dust is the result of using a pestle and mortar on a blue dragon scale. It is used in Herblore for mixing weapon poisons and antifire potions.

Wesley (in Nardah) will crush unnoted or noted herblore secondary items for 50 coins per item.
243: Blue dragon scales are an indirect secondary ingredient in Herblore that is ground with a pestle and mortar to create dragon scale dust, which can then be used to make antifire potions and weapon poison. Scales can be found on the ground by the blue dragons in Taverley Dungeon, Corsair Cove Dungeon, part of the Myths' Guild, in the Isle of Souls Dungeon, and in the Ruins of Tapoyauik. They can also be obtained as an uncommon drop from brutal blue dragons located within the Catacombs of Kourend. All variants of blue dragons also have a chance to drop scaly blue dragonhide, which can be cut with a knife to get 50 blue dragon scales.
245:
Wine of Zamorak is a secondary ingredient used in Herblore. It can be found on both floors of Asgarnia's Chaos Temple and the Chaos Temple south-west of the Chaos Fanatic in level 38 Wilderness, in which both locations have their wine respawn by default every 30 seconds. It can also be found at the end of the Deep Wilderness Dungeon, where it respawns every 6.6 seconds and is obtained in noted form if players have completed the hard Wilderness Diary. Respawn rates for wines are affected by the amount of players on a world, reducing the time to spawn with more players on a world; Asgarnia's Chaos Temple on high population worlds has an approximate respawn rate of 16 seconds, and Deep Wilderness Dungeon has an approximate respawn rate of every 4.2 seconds.

The wine can also be made by using Zamorak's grapes with a jug of water, requiring Level 65 Cooking and granting 200 Cooking experience.

Wines of Zamorak cannot be consumed, but are used as a secondary ingredient in creating ranging and bastion potions. The bloody grimoire states that the wine is incredibly unholy but has a sweet taste that makes it easily addictive. Additionally, using Telekinetic Grab on the wine in Asgarnia's Chaos Temple is a medium task in the Falador Diary.
247:
Jangerberries can be harvested from a bush patch after planting jangerberry seeds . They are used in Herblore to make Zamorak brews or as protection payment for snape grass (x5).

Jangerberries restore 2 hitpoints , 1 prayer point , temporarily boosts Attack by 2 and Strength by 1, and reduces Defence by 1. Adding them to a compost bin makes supercompost , though this is not recommended as watermelons or pineapples are far cheaper and have the same effect.
249:
Guam leaves are the first herbs that a player can clean, with a Herblore level of 3, giving 2.5 Herblore experience. They are used to make attack potions , for fuelling swamp lizards in the form of guam tar , and for making Guthix rest potions, after completing the related segment of the One Small Favour quest. Guam leaves can be grown in a herb patch with a Farming level of 9. To create a potion, you need to add the cleaned herb to a vial of water to create a guam potion (unf) , and then add the secondary ingredient.

Guam leaves, along with Marrentills , are used in the Lunar Diplomacy quest to make Guam-marr vial . The vial can then be destroyed and received again from Baba Yaga .
251:
Marrentill is the second lowest level herb. It can be cleaned at level 5 Herblore, giving 3.8 experience. It is used for making antipoison, marrentill tar and Guthix rest potions. Marrentill is also used to light incense burners, in player-owned houses, to boost Prayer experience when sacrificing bones (usually dragon bones).

Marrentill is rarely used for Herblore purposes. Guthix rests and marrentill tar have limited uses and demand among players, and antipoison requires unicorn horn dust as a secondary ingredient, which is costly, due to its use in superantipoison potions. As well as this, antipoison potions can be easily obtained from Jiminua's Jungle Store, further decreasing the demand. If you want to create a potion, you need to add the cleaned herb to a vial of water to create a marrentill potion (unf), and then add the secondary ingredient.

Despite its lack of popularity in Herblore training, marrentills nonetheless are frequently acquired by players who wish train Prayer at their Gilded Altar, as the incense burners which provide the additional experience boost for the altar can only be lit with marrentil herbs.

Marrentill, along with Guam leaves, is used in the Lunar Diplomacy quest to make a Guam-marr vial. The vial can then be destroyed and received again from Baba Yaga.

According to the book Gielinor's flora - herbs, marrentill is often associated with purity and is believed to be a mistranslation of the word miryam, which is an ancient menaphite word meaning "sea of bitterness", referencing its extreme bitter taste.
253:
Tarromin is the third lowest level herb. It can be cleaned at level 11 Herblore , and it is used for making strength potions , serum 207 , shrink-me-quick and tarromin tar . It can be grown with the Farming skill with a level of 19, by planting a tarromin seed in a herb patch . To create a potion, you need to add the cleaned herb to a vial of water to create a tarromin potion (unf) , and then add the secondary ingredient.

According to the book Gielinor's flora - herbs , tarromin are native to tropical regions and it is believed to be one of the earliest cultivated plants of Gielinor.
255:
Harralander is a herb that can be cleaned at level 20 Herblore. It can be obtained as a monster drop or through the Farming skill, with a level of 26, by planting a harralander seed in a herb patch. It is used to make Guthix rest potions, compost potions, restore potions, blamish oil, energy potions, Greenman's ale, combat potions, harralander tar and goading potions. To create a potion, you need to add the cleaned herb to a vial of water to create a harralander potion (unf), and then add the secondary ingredient.

According to the book Gielinor's flora - herbs, harralander naturally grows on rocky crevices, and upon reaching maturity, its root system often causes large cracks to form in the rock.
257:
Ranarr weed , commonly referred to simply as ranarr , is a herb that can be cleaned at level 25 Herblore . The herb can be grown by players with level 32 in Farming by planting ranarr seeds in herb patches . It's also an uncommon drop from various monsters. Despite being one of the lowest-level herbs available, ranarr is one of the most valuable herbs in the game, due to its role in making prayer potions .

Ranarr is one of three herbs with "weed" in its title, alongside snake weed and dwarf weed . According to Gielinor's Flora , the plant's name comes from the word "rana," meaning "eye-catching" in an ancient Kharidian language, and is considered a weed due to how fast it grows.
259:
Irit leaf ( Jagex : / ɪ . ˈ r ɪ t / ih- RIT ) is a mid level herb that can be cleaned at level 40 Herblore . Each cleaned irit leaf yields 8.8 Herblore experience. It is commonly dropped while fighting chaos druids , but can be dropped by almost every monster capable of dropping herbs.

To create a potion, you need to add the cleaned herb to a vial of water to create an irit potion (unf) , and then add the secondary ingredient. You can create super attack potions by adding an eye of newt . Creating super attack potions is considered one of the easiest methods to train Herblore, especially for ironmen , as eyes of newt are very easy to obtain, and the finished product is very useful for combat purposes. Eye of newt packs can be bought for 300 gp at various shops , and contain 100 eyes of newt. You can also create superantipoison potions by adding unicorn horn dust . In order to create an antidote++ however, you need to add the irit leaf to a vial of coconut milk , creating antidote++ (unf) , and add magic roots as secondary ingredients.

According to the book Gielinor's flora - herbs , irit has always had cultural significance due to its connection with the dead and is often synonymous with Icthlarin , the Menaphite god of death, and is often found growing in or near graveyards.
261:
Avantoe is a mid-level herb, requiring a Herblore level of 48 to clean from the grimy version. It can be obtained as a monster drop or through the Farming skill, with a level of 50, by planting an avantoe seed in a herb patch. It is used to make fishing potions, super energy potions, and hunter potions. To create a potion, you need to add the cleaned herb to a vial of water to create an avantoe potion (unf), and then add the secondary ingredient.

According to the book Gielinor's flora - herbs, the name means "moment", likely due to its unusual lifecycle caused by the harsh climate of the Kharidian Desert. Avantoe sprouts only after rain and then dies shortly in a matter of days.
263:
Kwuarm is a medium level herb requiring 54 Herblore to clean. It can be grown from kwuarm seeds at a herb patch at level 56 Farming and is used in the making of weapon poison and the super strength potion. To create a potion, you need to add the cleaned herb to a vial of water to create a kwuarm potion (unf), and then add the secondary ingredient.

According to the book Gielinor's flora - herbs, the herb was originally native to Kourend, with the name being given to it by dwarves, meaning warm death. The name is due to the plant's poisonous sap which is said to cause a burning fever when ingested. Since its discovery, it has often been used as a main ingredient in poison for various pests.

Kwuarm can be used in the Ratcatchers quest to create Rat poison.

Zahur is able to clean grimy herbs for players for a fee of 200 coins each, regardless of the player's Herblore level.
265:
Clean cadantine is a high level herb. It is used to make super defence potions at level 66 Herblore. Players can obtain it by cleaning a Grimy cadantine at level 65 Herblore, which gives 12.5 Herblore experience for cleaning.

One way to obtain cadantine herbs is through farming Cadantine seeds which requires 67 Farming.

When used in conjunction with White berries it makes a super defence potion which gives 150 Herblore experience. Chaos druids are mainly killed to get cadantine drops. Aberrant spectres also drop cadantine herbs often. To create a potion, you need to add the cleaned herb to a vial of water to create a cadantine potion (unf), and then add the secondary ingredient.

According to the book Gielinor's flora - herbs, its name comes from the word Cadan, meaning "spirit of war" in a lost mage tongue.
267:
Dwarf weed is the second highest level herb. Cleaning dwarf weed requires level 70 herblore and yields 13.8 Herblore experience. It is used with wine of Zamorak to create ranging potions. To create a potion, you need to add the cleaned herb to a vial of water to create a dwarf weed potion (unf), and then add the secondary ingredient.

One way to obtain dwarf weed is by planting dwarf weed seed in a herb patch at level 79 Farming. This gives you grimy dwarf weed which you can clean to obtain clean dwarf weed.

According to the book Gielinor's flora - herbs, it is found naturally in entrances to dwarven tunnels, and is not known why it thrived in such a specific environment.
269:
Torstol is the highest level herb, which requires level 75 Herblore to clean and yields 15 experience . Torstol can be grown in herb patches at level 85 Farming with a torstol seed .

Obtaining torstol herbs may be difficult as they are only rarely dropped by monsters. They can be obtained by Farming , looting nature implings , or rarely as drops from Zulrah and the Kalphite Queen . They can also be obtained in their grimy form from the Sinister chest , Skotizo , Cerberus , and the Chambers of Xeric . To create a Zamorak brew , you need to add the cleaned herb to a vial of water to create a torstol potion (unf) , and then add jangerberries .

According to the book Gielinor's flora - herbs , the name comes from torst , an old Fremennik word meaning "thirsty". This refers to the plant's need for a lot of water, and as such is often found growing near rivers and ponds.

A torstol may also be given to the Dr Jekyll random event in exchange for a Stamina potion(4) .
271:
The pressure gauge is a quest item used only in Ernest the Chicken . It is found submerged in the waters of the piranha-infested fountain in the south-western area of Draynor Manor . To get this item, the player must kill the piranhas using poisoned fish food . If the player does not use poisoned fish food, the piranhas will deal 1 hitpoint of damage.

It is one of three items needed to repair Professor Oddenstein 's machine along with an oil can and a rubber tube , so he can turn Ernest back into a human. Duplicates can be obtained with the drop trick and searching the fountain again. Upon completion of the quest duplicates are destroyed and it can no longer be obtained.
272:
Fish food is used in the Ernest the Chicken quest, used to feed fish that members can obtain as pets, and used in a step as part of Crack the Clue III. The poison found in the kitchen of Draynor Manor can be combined with the fish food to create poisoned fish food, which is used to kill the piranhas in the fountain south-west of Draynor Manor, allowing the player to retrieve a pressure gauge needed for the quest.

It can be found on the second level of Draynor Manor in the room with the ghost, south of the stairs.

Using the fish food on mayor of Catherby will consume the fish food along with a message saying "The mayor accepts your generous donation to his campaign".
273:
Poison is an item used during the Ernest the Chicken and Hazeel Cult quests. It can be found as a spawn inside Draynor Manor, or purchased from Rasolo near the Baxtorian Falls or Jossik in the Lighthouse.

It is used to poison the fish food and the piranhas found in the fountain on the grounds of Draynor Manor during the Ernest the Chicken quest. Finally, it is used to poison the Carnillean household's food in Hazeel Cult. You can try to use the poison obtained from the Hazeel Cult to poison the sheep in Sheep Herder, but a message will appear saying: "The sheep isn't going to drink the poison from the bottle. Perhaps you should try feeding it something else more appropriate."

Attempting to use poison on the Carnillean household stove before picking a side or siding with the Carnilleans will yield the message, "Random murder isn't good".
274:
Poisoned fish food is a quest item used in Ernest the Chicken, and in Crack the Clue III. It is made by using poison with fish food (both found in Draynor Manor).

Poisoned fish food is used to kill the piranhas in the fountain in order to retrieve the pressure gauge.
275:
The Key is a quest item used only in Ernest the Chicken. It is found by using a spade on the compost heap inside Draynor Manor's west wall during the quest.

It is used to open the door to the room containing a skeleton and the rubber tube. It can only be obtained during the quest and is kept upon completion.
276:
The rubber tube is a quest item used only in Ernest the Chicken. It is found in the main floor of Draynor Manor inside a locked room, which is guarded inside by a level 22 skeleton. The locked room can be opened using a key, which is dug out using a spade on the compost heap.

It is one of three items needed to repair Professor Oddenstein's machine along with an oil can and a pressure gauge, so he can turn Ernest back into a human. Duplicates can be obtained after the quest if the key is kept, but it serves no further use.
277:
The oil can is a quest item used only in Ernest the Chicken. It is found in the basement of Draynor Manor at the end of a maze puzzle.

It is one of three items needed to repair Professor Oddenstein's machine along with a pressure gauge and a rubber tube, so he can turn Ernest back into a human. Duplicates can be obtained after the quest, but it serves no further use.
278:
The cattleprod is a quest item used in Sheep Herder. It can be found next to the incinerator in the fenced off pen north of East Ardougne or taken from the cattle prod supply next to the Wyrmscraig Goat hunting area on Wyrmscraig.

It is used to prod sick-looking sheep in order to move them from their habitats into the pen to be incinerated and to prod Wyrmscraig Goats when goat hunting.

It has the same combat stats as a bronze dagger.
279:
Sheep feed is a quest item used only in Sheep Herder . It is obtained from Councillor Halgrive at the start of the quest.

It is used on sick-looking sheep that the player has herded into the slaughterhouse set up by Farmer Brumty .
280:
Sheep bones (1) is a quest item used only in Sheep Herder. It is dropped by a Red Sheep that is in the pen and after feeding it sheep feed.

The bones cannot be buried but are instead incinerated.

Incinerating the bones will remove any duplicates the player may have in their bank.
281:
Sheep bones (2) is a quest item used only in Sheep Herder. It is dropped by a Green Sheep that is in the pen and after feeding it sheep feed.

The bones cannot be buried but are instead incinerated.

Incinerating the bones will remove any duplicates the player may have in their bank.
282:
Sheep bones (3) is a quest item used only in Sheep Herder. It is dropped by a Blue Sheep that is in the pen and after feeding it sheep feed.

The bones cannot be buried but are instead incinerated.

Incinerating the bones will remove any duplicates the player may have in their bank.
283:
Sheep bones (4) is a quest item used only in Sheep Herder . It is dropped by a Yellow Sheep that is in the pen and after feeding it sheep feed .

The bones cannot be buried but are instead incinerated .

Incinerating the bones will remove any duplicates the player may have in their bank.
284:
The plague jacket is a quest item used only in Sheep Herder . It and the plague trousers are obtained from Doctor Orbon by purchasing it from him for 100 coins. It cannot be obtained again after completing the quest.

It must be worn when prodding the sick-looking sheep into the pen. It forms half of the plague suit set, the other half being the plague trousers.

It is identical to a Mourner top , except that it has built-in gloves. Wearing the plague jacket will automatically unequip gloves. Attempting to equip the jacket while wearing gloves with a full inventory will fail, instead giving the message "You should empty your hands first." Attempting to equip gloves while the plague jacket is on will provide the message "You can't wear those on top of this protective jacket." Despite this, wearing the plague jacket does not provide protection when picking nettles .
285:
The plague trousers is a quest item used only in Sheep Herder . It and the plague jacket are obtained from Doctor Orbon by purchasing it from him for 100 coins. It cannot be obtained again after completing the quest.

It must be worn when prodding the sick-looking sheep into the pen. It forms half of the plague suit set, the other half being the plague jacket. It appears visually identical to the Mourner trousers .
286:
Orange goblin mail is made by using orange dye on a goblin mail . Like all goblins mail, it is too small for players to normally wear as armour.

It is used during the Goblin Diplomacy quest, along with a blue and un-dyed goblin mail with Generals Bentnoze and Wartface fighting over what colour they prefer.

During the Land of the Goblins quest, the player can turn into a goblin using a transmogrification potion and wear the orange goblin mail in order to access the Narogoshuun tribal room of the Goblin Temple .
287:
Blue goblin mail is made by using blue dye on a goblin mail. Like all goblins mail, it is too small for players to normally wear as armour.

It is used during the Goblin Diplomacy quest, along with an orange and un-dyed goblin mail with Generals Bentnoze and Wartface fighting over what colour they prefer.

During the Land of the Goblins quest, the player can turn into a goblin using a transmogrification potion and wear the blue goblin mail in order to access the Ekeleshuun tribal room of the Goblin Temple.
288:
Goblin mail is armour for goblins. Although this item has the "Wear" option, this item cannot be equipped by players as it is too small to fit humans. However, during the Land of the Goblins quest, the player can turn into a goblin using a transmogrification potion and wear the goblin mail.

It can be dyed into various colours, in which certain colours are used for the Land of the Goblins quest.

Goblin mail is obtained as an uncommon drop from goblins. In addition, three goblin mails can be found in Goblin Village, north of Falador. One can be found in a crate in a building west of General Bentnoze and General Wartface, another in a crate on the balcony up the ladder near the entrance, and a third one in a crate just north of the building of Bentnoze and Wartface. Three are used in the Goblin Diplomacy quest. During the Land of the Goblins quest, there are crates which contain infinite goblin mail in the Goblin Temple.
290:
A Research package is an item that players must deliver to Aubury in the quest Rune Mysteries . It is obtained from Archmage Sedridor . If a player dies while having the research package in their inventory, Sedridor will give the player a replacement.

If the player leaves the item in their bank and asks Sedridor for another, he will provide one and the copy in the bank will be removed.

According to the Wise Old Man when asking you to check your bank for you, Sedridor's research into the mysteries of the runes is very interesting, but you don't need it.
291: Research notes are obtained in Rune Mysteries from Aubury after players give them the research package . They must then be given to Archmage Sedridor to complete the quest. There is no other use for this item.
292:
The Book on Baxtorian can be found by searching a bookcase in the Tourist Information Centre just south of the Baxtorian Falls . In it is a brief history on Baxtorian , his treasure, and the reason he hid himself away beneath the waterfall, as well as a lot of useful hints and information concerning how a player might get in to retrieve the treasure.

The book is used in the Waterfall Quest and after finding the book it can be found on the shelves in a player-owned house . It can also be found in the Grand Library in Prifddinas , which requires completion of Song of the Elves to access.
293:
The key is an item found in the Tree Gnome Village Dungeon. Prior to starting the Roving Elves quest, it can be found in a crate in the north-east storeroom, among the south-east group of crates. It opens the door to the jail, found north-west of the dungeon entrance. Upon finding it, the player will receive the message "You found a large key". The crate can be searched for another key if the player loses it. It cannot be stored on a Steel key ring.

Note that if a player has a low combat level, they will likely receive damage from the surrounding monsters whilst searching the crates for the key.

The key is first used during the Waterfall Quest. The key is needed to unlock the door to the jail where the gnome named Golrie is hiding from hobgoblins that have invaded the dungeon. Once the door is unlocked, Golrie will give the player Glarial's pebble, which is required to enter Glarial's Tomb near Baxtorian Falls.

The key may also be needed during The Path of Glouphrie quest, as the player may need to access the jail again to speak to Golrie to acquire information about a device. The key is not needed if the player has started Roving Elves, as Golrie has traded places with the hobgoblins and is no longer located behind the locked door.

After the player has started Roving Elves, the key is no longer obtainable via searching the crate and can be re-obtained by speaking to Golrie.
294:
Glarial's pebble is an item used in the Waterfall Quest and Roving Elves. It is given to the player by Golrie as a reward for freeing him from the dungeon under the Tree Gnome Village. If you lose this pebble all you have to do is go back to Golrie to obtain another.

The pebble is used to gain access to the Glarial's Tomb dungeon near the Baxtorian Falls. Note that in order to enter the dungeon, the player may not be carrying weapons, armour, runes, or various other items. See the Glarial's Tomb page for a more comprehensive list of disallowed items.

The tombstone is covered in elven script. Some of the writing is in common tongue. It reads: "Here lies Glarial, wife of Baxtorian, true friend of nature in life and death. May she now rest knowing only visitors with peaceful intent can enter."
295:
Glarial's amulet is used during the Waterfall Quest to grant access to the Waterfall Dungeon. Attempting to enter the dungeon during the quest without the amulet results in the player taking damage, being swept away to downstream from the door. After the quest, the amulet is not needed to enter the dungeon.

The amulet can be recovered in the western chest inside Glarial's Tomb if lost. Players may enter the tomb by having Glarial's pebble and having no armour, weapons, or runes equipped or in their inventory. Beware of the moss guardians in the tomb. Players may obtain more than one amulet through the drop trick.

Glarial's amulet is identical in appearance to the gnome amulet.
296: Glarial's urn is an item used in the Waterfall Quest and has no known use after the quest. The urn can be obtained by searching the tomb in the Glarial's tomb. After the completion of the Waterfall Quest, the urn becomes empty.
297: Glarial's urn is an item used in the Waterfall Quest and has no known use after the quest. The urn can be obtained by searching the tomb in the Glarial's tomb. After the completion of the Waterfall Quest, the urn becomes empty.
298:
Key is an item found in the Waterfall Dungeon by searching a crate in the eastern chamber of the dungeon. It is used to open the two doors in western part of the dungeon, towards the Chalice of Eternity. It also spawns in the chamber between these two doors, allowing the player to pass back through the door if they were to drop it.

The key is used in several quests. It cannot be stored on a steel key ring.
299:
Mithril seeds are a magical type of seed that can be planted almost anywhere to grow some flowers in the ground, and are purchasable from the Legends Guild Shop of Useful Items.

Upon planting the seeds, the player will move one adjacent square west if possible; if there's an obstacle preventing movement to the west, the flowers will attempt to move the player to the east first, then south, then north. Once the flower is grown, players are then given the option to pick them, producing one of nine different colours of flowers.

Mithril seeds are primarily used in PvP activities in the Wilderness, or in minigames such as Last Man Standing, as it forces the user to move one tile even if the player is frozen. Adamant seeds, a variant of the item, will move the opposite direction from mithril seeds.

Seeds are sometimes used to grief players training Hunter and Firemaking as well, as traps and fires cannot be placed on the same tile as a planted flower.

40 seeds are awarded upon completion of the Waterfall Quest. Players can buy them at the Legends' Guild.
300:
A Rat's tail is a quest item used in the Witch's Potion quest. It can be obtained by killing any standard rat after the player has begun Witch's Potion. The item has a 100% chance to drop once you begin the quest.

Brian's Archery Supplies, a store that sells Ranged supplies, has a couple of rats which are very convenient for the player, since the store is located near Hetty the Witch's house.

After completion of the quest, the tail is unobtainable unless the player uses the drop trick to obtain multiple tails during the quest. If the player shows a Rat's Tail to the Wise Old Man after completing the quest, he will tell the player to get rid of it. (Before completing he says "You have brought me a tail of a rat!" and "Yes, I think you should keep it for now.")
301:
Lobster pots are items that can be bought from major fishing shops for 20 coins each and are used to fish lobsters from cage/harpoon fishing spots with 40 Fishing, which are a common healing food that restores 12 Hitpoints. A lobster pot spawn is found within the Fishing Guild.

They are also used in dark crab fishing. Dark crab fishing spots are only in the Wilderness and require level 85 fishing,
303:
A small fishing net is used to catch fish such as shrimps, anchovies, karambwanji, minnows, and monkfish. Nets can be purchased from various fishing shops for 5 coins. It can also be obtained for free from either the Fishing tutor south of Lumbridge near the coast east of the swamp, or from the Spirit Angler at the Ruins of Unkah.

The small fishing net, used along with a rope, can also be used in the Hunter skill to capture swamp lizards and salamanders.
305:
A big fishing net can be purchased from various fishing shops . They can be used at three types of big fishing net spots. The big net, harpoon can be used to catch bass from 46 Fishing and a rare chance at the Big bass . The Camdozaal fishing spot can be used for passive prayer training and a rare chance for a barronite handle . Finally, the Fortis fishing spot can be used to passively earn house keys or moon key loop halves .

Because of the large variety of practically worthless fish and other objects that will quickly fill the player's inventory while fishing in this way, it is rarely used other than for the bass it produces, which may be used with a Ring of Charos(a) to re-enchant lyres , a rare chance at the big bass, or caskets which may rarely contain half keys or higher-level talismans.

If a player is lucky, the net may catch multiple (2-9) fish and/or items at once. Each fish/item has one roll, except for raw mackerel which has two. [ 1 ] Wearing a skills necklace with at least one charge while big net fishing will slightly increase the chance of finding a casket . [ 2 ]

If multiple types of fish are gained in the same catch, the player will receive a roll to obtain the heron pet for each type of fish that is caught. [ 3 ]
307:
The fishing rod is an item used to catch fish through the Fishing skill . It can be bought from various fishing shops . To use a fishing rod, one will need fishing bait (except sandworms for anglerfish ) to catch fish. It can be bought from fishing stores for 5 coins . There is also a fishing rod spawn in a house on south-eastern side of Entrana.

The equipable version of the fishing rod, the pearl fishing rod , can be bought with molch pearls from Alry the Angler .

The following fish are caught with a fishing rod:
309:
