A fly fishing rod can be used to fish trout , salmon (both with feathers ), and rainbow fish (with stripy feathers ). They can be bought from various fishing shops . Fly fishing rods are used at fishing spots with the lure option. Popular fishing spots include the Barbarian Village , the Grand Tree , and Shilo Village . Fly fishing rods use feathers as bait. Feathers are dropped frequently from chickens or purchased from fishing shops.

The equipable version of the fly fishing rod, the pearl fly fishing rod , can be bought with molch pearls from Alry the Angler .

A fly fishing rod also spawns on the Isle of Souls in the south-east region.

The following fish are caught with a fly fishing rod:
311:
A harpoon is an item used to catch certain types of fish, as part of the Fishing skill. It can be used to catch tuna at level 35, swordfish at level 50, and sharks at level 76. Swordfish and tuna can be caught at cage/harpoon fishing spots, while sharks can be caught at big net/harpoon spots. Harpoons are also used when fighting Tempoross, to catch harpoonfish and fish from the spirit pools that weaken the boss.

Harpoons can be purchased from most fishing shops and can be stored in a tackle box.

For pay-to-play players, several other types of harpoons exist. The barb-tail harpoon is wieldable, allowing saving one inventory space over an ordinary harpoon. The dragon harpoon is also wieldable, has a 20% increased catch rate compared to other harpoons, and has a special attack that boosts Fishing level by 3, but requires 61 Fishing to use and 60 Attack to wield. The crystal harpoon is an improved version of the dragon harpoon, with a 35% increased catch rate and increased requirements to use.

Alternately, pay-to-play players who learn barbarian fishing can forego a harpoon entirely by learning how to barehand fish.
313:
Fishing bait is an item used with the fishing rod . It is used to fish in any fishing spot as long as the spot has the Bait Fishing Spot option. Each successful catch uses up one piece of bait, so bring an appropriate amount in your inventory if you wish to catch a lot of fish.

Fishing bait can also be used for barbarian fishing , replacing feathers as bait.

Most shops that sell fishing bait also sell bait packs , which contain 100 bait per pack.

Using fishing bait with a fishing rod, you can catch the following types of fish:
314:
Feathers are used in the Fishing and Fletching skills . In Fishing, feathers are used as lures for fly fishing . Feathers may also be used as bait for barbarian heavy-rod fishing , as a cheaper alternative to fishing bait. In Fletching, feathers are used to make arrows , darts , and bolts . Feathers cannot be noted , as they are stackable.

These are the only feathers that can be used to summon a newtroost during the Creature Creation activity in the Tower of Life , as coloured feathers are not accepted by the altar.

Most shops that sell feathers also sell feather packs which contain 100 feathers per pack.

In fletching recipes, blue , orange , red , yellow , stripy , gryphon , and stymphike feathers can all be used in place of regular feathers.
315:
Shrimp is a type of fish that restores 3 Hitpoints when eaten. It can be obtained by cooking raw shrimp on a fire or cooking range, granting 30 experience when successful. When cooking there is a chance to fail, resulting in burnt shrimp. The burn rate decreases as the player's Cooking level increases. Shrimp is one of a number of foods with a reduced burn rate while using the Lumbridge Castle range with Cook's Assistant completed. It will stop burning entirely at Cooking level 34, or 31 when using the Lumbridge range.

Shrimp are one of the fish required by Caleb in the quest Family Crest.

Rick can make shrimps for the player in a player-owned house.
317: Raw shrimps can be caught at 1 Fishing with a small fishing net at a net fishing spot, granting 10 experience per catch. They can be cooked into shrimps at level 1 Cooking, granting 30 Cooking experience when successful. Raw shrimps can be used as a source of food for a growing kitten.
319:
Anchovies are a type of fish that restores 1 Hitpoint when eaten. It can be obtained by cooking raw anchovies on a fire or cooking range, granting 30 experience when successful. When cooking there is a chance to fail, resulting in burnt anchovies. The burn rate decreases as the player's Cooking level increases. Anchovies are one of a number of foods with a reduced burn rate while using the Lumbridge Castle range with Cook's Assistant completed. It will stop burning entirely at Cooking level 34, or 31 when using the Lumbridge range.

Anchovies are an ingredient in anchovy pizzas, and are also used in the creation of impling jars.
321: Raw anchovies are a fish that require a Fishing level of at least 15 to be caught. Doing so requires a small fishing net , and grants 40 Fishing experience. This makes anchovies a useful source of Fishing experience for players looking to train Fishing from level 15 to 20. Raw anchovies can be bought from Charley in Mos Le'Harmless for 16 coins .
323:
Burnt fish is the result of accidentally burning raw anchovies while attempting to make anchovies . The burn rate while cooking these will decrease as players reach higher Cooking levels, stopping entirely at level 34.

The burnt fish has no use whatsoever. Like most other burnt food, it is tradeable to other players but not on the Grand Exchange .
325: Sardine is a type of fish that restores 4 Hitpoints when eaten. It can be obtained by cooking raw sardine on a fire or cooking range, granting 40 experience when successful. When cooking there is a chance to fail, resulting in a burnt sardine. The burn rate decreases as the player's Cooking level increases. Sardine is one of a number of foods with a reduced burn rate while using the Lumbridge Castle range with Cook's Assistant completed. It will stop burning entirely at Cooking level 38, or 34 when using the Lumbridge range.
327:
Raw sardines are fish that require a Fishing level of 5 to catch by using a normal fishing rod on a bait fishing spot, by the sea. Fishing bait is required in the inventory, one being used for each catch, which yields 20 Fishing experience. Raw sardines may be cooked at level 1 Cooking to produce cooked sardines.

In the quest Gertrude's Cat, players have to rub a sardine with doogle leaves to feed Gertrude's lost cat. This creates a seasoned sardine.

Sardines may be bought from Gerrant's Fishy Business as well as Lovecraft's Tackle for 10 coins each. They are also available at Warrens Fish Monger in the The Warrens for 13 coins each, with a quickly replenishing stock of 200; this can be a convenient source for early cooking levels, as there are fires and a cooking range within 12 and 17 tiles (respectively). They are also available from the Fish monger in Rellekka, which is a good option if you are needing to bank them for activities such as the Tower of Life's Spidine, as you can deposit items directly to your bank by using Peer the Seer (With Fremennik Easy Diary), who is located close by to the south-west. In addition, using a fish barrel can speed up acquiring them.
329:
Salmon is a type of fish that restores 9 Hitpoints when eaten. It can be obtained by cooking raw salmon on a fire or cooking range , requiring level 25 Cooking and granting 90 experience when successful. When cooking there is a chance to fail, resulting in a burnt fish . The burn rate decreases as the player's Cooking level increases. Salmon is one of a number of foods with a reduced burn rate while using the Lumbridge Castle range with Cook's Assistant completed. It will stop burning entirely at Cooking level 58, or 55 when using the Lumbridge range.

Salmon is one of the fish required by Caleb during the quest Family Crest .

Salmon is used as an ingredient for admiral pie which requires Cooking level 70 to make.

When eaten, the message You eat the salmon. is displayed.
331: Raw salmon are fish that can be caught with a Fishing level of 30, granting 70 Fishing experience per catch. It can be cooked into salmon with a Cooking level of 25. Players will stop burning salmon unaided at a Cooking level of 58 or 55 when using the Lumbridge Castle range. Successfully cooking a salmon yields 90 Cooking experience. Raw salmon are caught through fly fishing, which requires a Fishing level of 30, a fly fishing rod, and feathers. The fish are caught with the lure option at Lure/Bait fishing spots found in rivers. Fly fishing trout and salmon is a very common way for players to train Fishing quickly.
333:
Trout is a type of fish that restores 7 Hitpoints when eaten. It can be obtained by cooking raw trout on a fire or cooking range, requiring level 15 Cooking and granting 70 experience when successful. When cooking there is a chance to fail, resulting in a burnt trout. The burn rate decreases as the player's Cooking level increases. Trout is one of a number of foods with a reduced burn rate while using the Lumbridge Castle range with Cook's Assistant completed. It will stop burning entirely at Cooking level 49, or 45 when using the Lumbridge range.

Trout is used as an ingredient in fish pie which requires Cooking level 47 to make. 10 Trout are required during the Death Plateau quest.

When eaten, the message You eat the trout. is displayed.
335:
Raw trout are fish that can caught through fly fishing, which requires a fly fishing rod and feathers.

This method can also net salmon at the appropriate Fishing level. The fish are caught with the lure option at Lure/Bait fishing spots found in rivers, granting 50 Fishing experience per catch. It can be cooked into trout with a Cooking level of 15. Players will stop burning trout at level 49 if using a range, or 50 if using a fire. Successfully cooking a raw trout gives 70 Cooking experience.
337:
Giant carp are a type of fish that restores 6 Hitpoints when eaten. They can be obtained by cooking a raw giant carp on a fire or cooking range , giving no Cooking experience. When cooking there is a chance to fail, resulting in a burnt fish . The burn rate decreases as the player's Cooking level increases. Giant carp is one of a number of foods with a reduced burn rate while using the Lumbridge Castle range with Cook's Assistant completed. It will stop burning entirely at Cooking level 45, or 41 when using the Lumbridge range.

Raw giant carp can only be caught as part of the Fishing Contest quest before receiving the fishing trophy during the quest. Level 10 Fishing is required, along with a fishing rod and red vine worms for bait — the latter can be dug up in McGrubor's Wood with a spade .
338:
A raw giant carp is a quest item used only in Fishing Contest. It requires Level 10 Fishing and is caught with a fishing rod and red vine worms after stuffing the pipe with a garlic. Catching one gives no Fishing experience. It can be cooked into a giant carp, but this gives no Cooking experience.

It is given to Bonzo in order to win the Fishing trophy. After receiving the fishing trophy, more fish can no longer be caught.

Bonzo will take all copies of raw giant carp in the player's inventory. That said, if you catch two you can put one on the ground, give the "winning fish" to Bonzo, and then pick up the other raw giant carp after you get the trophy.
339:
Cod is a type of fish that restores 7 Hitpoints when eaten. It can be obtained by cooking raw cod on a fire or cooking range, requiring level 18 Cooking and granting 75 experience when successful. When cooking there is a chance to fail, resulting in a burnt fish. The burn rate decreases as the player's Cooking level increases. Cod is one of a number of foods with a reduced burn rate while using the Lumbridge Castle range with Cook's Assistant completed. It will stop burning entirely at Cooking level 51 on a fire, 49 on a range, or 46 when using the Lumbridge range.

Cod is used as an ingredient in fish pie which requires Cooking level 47 to make.
341:
Raw cod is a fish that can be caught with a big fishing net at any fishing spot . It requires a Fishing level of 23 to catch and grants 45 fishing experience per catch. It can be cooked into cod with level 18 Cooking . The most common spot to fish cod is Catherby .

Raw cod is used for the Freeing Pirate Pete section of the Recipe for Disaster quest. It is also used for the Cold War quest, but it can be substituted with the use of the Ring of Charos(a) .
343:
Burnt fish is the result of accidentally burning either raw giant carp, raw trout, raw cod, raw pike, or raw salmon. The burn rate while cooking these will decrease as players reach higher Cooking levels.

Giant carp stops being burnt at level 45.

Trout stops being burnt at level 49.

Cod stops being burnt at level 51.

Pike stops being burnt at level 54.

Salmon stops being burnt at level 58.

The burnt fish has no use whatsoever. Like most other burnt food, it is tradeable to other players but not on the Grand Exchange.
345:
Raw herring is an item that is obtained through the Fishing skill by using a fishing rod with fishing bait on a net/bait fishing spot using the bait option. Herrings can only be caught in fishing spots by the sea. Catching a raw herring grants 30 Fishing experience. It can be cooked into herring with a Cooking level of 5, granting 50 Cooking experience.

This fish can be caught at level 10 Fishing and cooked at level 5 Cooking.

River fishing spots do not provide raw herring.
347: Herring is a type of fish that restores 5 Hitpoints when eaten. It can be obtained by cooking raw herring on a fire or cooking range, requiring level 5 Cooking and granting 50 experience when successful. When cooking there is a chance to fail, resulting in a burnt herring. The burn rate decreases as the player's Cooking level increases. Herring is one of a number of foods with a reduced burn rate while using the Lumbridge Castle range with Cook's Assistant completed. It will stop burning entirely at Cooking level 41, or 38 when using the Lumbridge range.
349:
Raw pike are fish that can be caught with a Fishing level of 25, granting 60 fishing experience per catch. They can be cooked into pike with a Cooking level of 20. Successfully cooking a raw pike gives 80 Cooking experience. Raw pike are caught through bait fishing, which requires a fishing rod and bait .

The fish are caught with the bait option at lure/bait fishing spots found in rivers. While fishing there, a roll is made every 5 ticks (3 seconds) to catch a pike, although there is a 1/5 chance the interval is increased by 1 tick to 6 ticks (3.6 seconds) instead with the casting animation happening twice, one tick apart. [ 1 ]
351: Pike is a type of fish that restores 8 Hitpoints when eaten. It can be obtained by cooking raw pike on a fire or cooking range, requiring level 20 Cooking and granting 80 experience when successful. When cooking there is a chance to fail, resulting in a burnt pike. The burn rate decreases as the player's Cooking level increases. Pike is one of a number of foods with a reduced burn rate while using the Lumbridge Castle range with Cook's Assistant completed. It will stop burning entirely at Cooking level 54, or 49 when using the Lumbridge range.
353: Raw mackerel is a fish that can be caught with a big fishing net at any big net fishing spot . It requires a Fishing level of 16 to catch and can be cooked into mackerel with level 10 Cooking . The most common spot to fish mackerel is Catherby . There's a possibility that 10 raw mackerel will be required for a part in the quest In Aid of the Myreque .
355: Mackerel is a type of fish that restores 6 Hitpoints when eaten. It can be obtained by cooking raw mackerel on a fire or cooking range, requiring level 10 Cooking and granting 60 experience when successful. When cooking there is a chance to fail, resulting in a burnt fish. The burn rate decreases as the player's Cooking level increases. Mackerel is one of a number of foods with a reduced burn rate while using the Lumbridge Castle range with Cook's Assistant completed. It will stop burning entirely at Cooking level 45, or 41 when using the Lumbridge range.
357:
Burnt fish is the result of accidentally burning either raw herring or raw mackerel . Cooking herring requires 5 Cooking and stops being burnt at level 41, and mackerel requires 10 Cooking and stops being burnt at level 45.

The burnt fish has no use whatsoever. Like most other burnt food, it is tradeable to other players but not on the Grand Exchange .

This item also spawns on a table inside of a Catherby range.
359:
Raw tuna is a type of fish, obtained by harpoon fishing at a cage/harpoon fishing spot. Raw tuna require 35 Fishing to catch and award the player 80 experience when caught. They can be sold, or cooked with a Cooking level of 30 to produce tuna, granting 100 experience in Cooking and will no longer be burned after level 63. The cooked version is often used by mid-levelled players when training combat.

Raw tuna can also be bought from Flosi Dalksson in Jatizso or thieved from the Fish stalls in The Warrens, Rellekka, Miscellania, and Etceteria, requiring a Thieving level of 42.
361:
Tuna is a type of fish that restores 10 Hitpoints when eaten. It can be obtained by cooking raw tuna on a fire or cooking range , requiring level 30 Cooking and granting 100 experience when successful. When cooking there is a chance to fail, resulting in a burnt tuna . The burn rate decreases as the player's Cooking level increases, and it will stop burning entirely at Cooking level 63 on both ranges and fires.

Tuna is one of the fish required by Caleb in the quest Family Crest .

Tuna is used with sweetcorn to make tuna and corn which requires Cooking level 67 to make and restores 13 hitpoints when eaten. Potato with butter can also be added to tuna and corn to create a tuna potato which requires Cooking level 68 to make, restoring 22 Hitpoints when eaten.

When eaten, the message You eat the tuna. is displayed.
363:
A raw bass can be caught by players with a Fishing level of 46 or higher using a big fishing net at a fishing spot , this cannot be boosted. Doing so yields 100 Fishing experience per bass caught. They can be cooked into bass with a Cooking level of 43.

It is also possible for players to catch a big bass which can be stuffed by the taxidermist in Canifis and subsequently displayed in the Skill Hall of one's player-owned house .

Players wearing a Ring of Charos(a) can trade a raw bass to the Fossegrimen located at her sacrifice altar south of Rellekka as a replacement for a raw shark to enchant their lyre .

Bass are not frequently fished, as it is a bit unpredictable as to how many the player will get in one hour, and are frequently caught with other fish like raw cod and raw mackerel or items like caskets and seaweed .
365:
Bass is a type of fish that restores 13 Hitpoints when eaten. It can be obtained by cooking raw bass on a fire or cooking range , requiring level 43 Cooking and granting 130 experience when successful. When cooking there is a chance to fail, resulting in a burnt fish . The burn rate decreases as the player's Cooking level increases, and it will stop burning entirely at Cooking level 80 on both ranges and fires.

Bass are one of the fish required by Caleb in the quest Family Crest .

When eaten, the message You eat the bass. is displayed.
367:
Burnt fish is the result of accidentally burning raw tuna or raw bass. The burn rate while cooking these will decrease as players reach higher Cooking levels. Tuna requires 30 Cooking to attempt to cook and stops being burnt at level 63, while bass requires 43 Cooking and stops being burnt at level 80.

The burnt fish has no use whatsoever. Like most other burnt food, it is tradeable to other players but not on the Grand Exchange.
369:
A burnt fish is the result of burning a raw sardine while attempting to cook a sardine . The burn rate while cooking these will decrease as players reach higher Cooking levels, stopping entirely at level 38.

The burnt fish has no use whatsoever. Like most other burnt foods, it is tradeable to other players but not on the Grand Exchange .
371:
A raw swordfish is a type of fish that players can catch at level 50 Fishing with a harpoon at cage and harpoon fishing spots, and can be cooked at level 45 Cooking. It also can be obtained at level 60 fishing while drift net fishing which cannot be boosted.

Catching a swordfish grants 100 Fishing experience. Fishing for swordfish takes longer than lobsters because Tuna is caught along with it. Free-to-play fishing on Karamja generally drop their tuna (often cooking it first for the experience), but the members-only fishing spots in Catherby, Port Piscarilius, Jatizso, and the Fishing Guild are close enough to banks that it is actually faster for players to bank the raw tuna than to drop it, additionally, the Fishing Guild gives an invisible +7 fishing boost. Cooking Swordfish will grant 140 experience.

Barbarian fishing is another possible option when fishing for swordfish. Hand fishing gives an extra 10 Strength experience for each swordfish, and requires level 70 Fishing and level 50 Strength.

Players may also rarely receive a big swordfish while fishing. These are hung up in a skill hall in player-owned houses for those with level 56 Construction or above.

Five raw swordfish can be obtained when opening the crystal chest.

Raw swordfish is used in Creature Creation together with a raw chicken to make a swordchick.
373:
Swordfish is a type of fish that restores 14 Hitpoints when eaten. It can be obtained by cooking raw swordfish on a fire or cooking range , requiring level 45 Cooking and granting 140 experience when successful. When cooking there is a chance to fail, resulting in a burnt swordfish . The burn rate decreases as the player's Cooking level increases, and it will stop burning entirely at Cooking level 80 on ranges and level 86 on fires.

Swordfish are one of the fish required by Caleb during the quest Family Crest .

When eaten, the message You eat the swordfish. is displayed.

Swordfish are the best single-serving food in free-to-play worlds with 2 more hitpoints than lobsters . It is the fastest way to gain health in free-to-play worlds if eaten with an anchovy pizza in one tick .
375:
Burnt swordfish is the result of accidentally burning a raw swordfish while attempting to make a swordfish . The burn rate while cooking these will decrease as players reach higher Cooking levels, stopping entirely at level 86; wearing cooking gauntlets will stop them from burning at level 81 instead.

The burnt swordfish has no use whatsoever. Like most other burnt food, it is tradeable to other players but not on the Grand Exchange .
377:
A raw lobster is a type of crustacean which can be caught at level 40 Fishing with a lobster pot , resulting in 90 Fishing experience . It can be cooked into lobster at level 40 Cooking , yielding 120 Cooking experience. Starting at level 74 Cooking, raw lobsters will no longer burn ; wearing cooking gauntlets reduces this threshold to 64 Cooking instead.

Raw lobster is also used in Creature Creation together with a raw jubbly to make a jubster .
379:
Lobster is a type of fish that restores 12 Hitpoints when eaten. It can be obtained by cooking raw lobster on a fire or cooking range, requiring level 40 Cooking and granting 120 experience when successful. When cooking there is a chance to fail, resulting in a burnt lobster. The burn rate decreases as the player's Cooking level increases, and it will stop burning entirely at Cooking level 74.

When eaten, the message You eat the lobster. is displayed.
381:
Burnt lobster is the result of accidentally burning a raw lobster while attempting to make a lobster. The burn rate while cooking these will decrease as players reach higher Cooking levels, stopping entirely at level 74; wearing cooking gauntlets will stop them from burning at level 64 instead.

The burnt lobster has no use whatsoever. Like most other burnt food, it is tradeable to other players but not on the Grand Exchange.
383:
Raw sharks can be fished with a harpoon with level 76 Fishing. They require level 80 Cooking to cook into sharks and heal 20 Hitpoints each. Raw sharks can be caught at many net/harpoon fishing spots with locations including the Fishing Guild, Catherby, Burgh de Rott, Rellekka, Iorwerth Camp, East of Hosidius, Jatizso, Isle of Souls, Gwenith, and Salvager Overlook. They can be caught by sailing a raft at sea north-west of Musa Point. Raw sharks can also be caught without using a harpoon at level 96 Fishing and 76 Strength by starting the second part of barbarian fishing with Otto Godblessed. The rate at which they are caught can be increased with the use of shark lure, but doing so will reduce the experience gained.

A single raw shark can also be bought at Rufus' Meat Emporium in Canifis for 221 coins. 25 raw sharks can be bought at Frankie's Fishing Emporium starting at 170 coins.

Sharks give 110 Fishing experience per catch and 210 Cooking experience when cooked. Although they yield decent experience per catch, fishing sharks is extremely slow and therefore not recommended for players seeking fast experience. There is a very rare chance that a big shark is obtained when fishing.

However, fishing minnows in the Fishing Guild gives a decent amount of fishing experience per hour, and 40 can be exchanged for a raw shark. Sharks can be obtained from minnow fishing at a much faster rate, but also requires more attention compared to fishing sharks directly.

Lyres can be imbued by giving Fossegrimen 200-1000 raw sharks in addition to an equal amount of raw bass, raw sea turtles, and raw manta rays with the quantity depending on the tier of Fremennik Diary completed.

Fishing and cooking 5 sharks with the cooking gauntlets in Catherby is a requirement for the Kandarin elite diary. Catching a shark barehanded in Burgh de Rott is a requirement for the Morytania elite diary.

Raw sharks can also be cut into fine fish offcuts.
385:
Shark is a type of fish that restores 20 Hitpoints when eaten. It can be obtained by cooking raw shark on a fire or cooking range, requiring level 80 Cooking and granting 210 experience when successful. When cooking there is a chance to fail, resulting in a burnt shark. The burn rate decreases as the player's Cooking level increases. It will only stop burning entirely if the player is wearing a Cooking cape, or using Cooking gauntlets at level 94 (84 if elite Kourend & Kebos Diary is completed while cooking at the Hosidius kitchen).

When eaten, the message You eat the shark. is displayed.

In addition to being cooked or purchased from other players, sharks can be obtained from Bardur in the Waterbirth Island Dungeon, who will exchange one shark for a Fremennik blade, Fremennik helm, or Fremennik shield.

Fishing and cooking 5 sharks with the cooking gauntlets in Catherby is a requirement for the Kandarin elite diary.
387:
Burnt shark is the result of accidentally burning a raw shark while attempting to cook it. The burn rate while cooking these will decrease as players reach higher Cooking levels, stopping entirely at level 94 when wearing cooking gauntlets .

The burnt shark has no use whatsoever. Like most other burnt food, it is tradeable to other players but not on the Grand Exchange . Because of that, some players collect them or resell them to other burnt food collectors.
389:
Raw manta ray are fish that can be obtained with level 81 Fishing . They can be caught while playing the Fishing Trawler , from the Tempoross Reward pool , or while drift net fishing at Fossil Island with 90 Fishing , which cannot be boosted. They are also a possible reward from a bowl of fish bought from Mairin's Market . They can be cooked into manta rays with 91 Cooking , giving 216.3 experience.

Wearing the Cooking cape while cooking manta rays will prevent players from burning them.

A raw manta ray can be used as an offering to Fossegrimen in Rellekka to enchant a lyre to create an enchanted lyre .

Catching a manta ray at Fishing Trawler and cooking it in Port Khazard is a requirement for the Elite Ardougne Diary .
391:
The manta ray is a type of food that restores 22 Hitpoints when eaten. It can be obtained by cooking raw manta ray on a fire or cooking range , requiring level 91 Cooking and granting 216.3 experience when successful. When cooking there is a chance to fail, resulting in a burnt manta ray . The burn rate decreases as the player's Cooking level increases. It will only stop burning entirely when the Cooking cape is worn.

The manta ray is the second highest instant-health single consumption food, behind the marlin , alongside the dark crab , bluefin , anglerfish , and tuna potato . It is recommended to check the prices before using manta rays as a primary source of healing, as they are often more expensive than the other fish that heal the same amount.

Cooked moonlight antelope and cooked dashing kebbit heals 26 and 23 health respectively, but part of the healing is delayed, making them not always practical in the same situations.

Catching and cooking a manta ray is a requirement for the elite Ardougne Diary .
393:
Burnt manta ray is the result of accidentally burning a raw manta ray while attempting to make a manta ray. The burn rate while cooking these will decrease as players reach higher Cooking levels. There is no level where manta rays stop being burned, although wearing a Cooking cape will prevent players from burning any food.

The burnt manta ray has no use whatsoever, although you can unsuccessfully attempt to eat it. Like most other burnt food, it is tradeable to other players but not on the Grand Exchange.
395:
Raw sea turtle are fish that can be obtained with level 79 Fishing. They can be caught while playing the Fishing Trawler minigame, from the Tempoross Reward pool, or while drift net fishing at Fossil Island with 80 Fishing, which cannot be boosted. They are also a possible reward from a bowl of fish bought from Mairin's Market. They can be cooked into sea turtles with 82 Cooking, giving 211.3 experience.

With level 99 Cooking, about 23% of sea turtles will be burnt. Wearing the Cooking cape while cooking sea turtles will prevent players from burning them.

A raw sea turtle can be used as an offering to Fossegrimen in Rellekka to enchant a lyre to create an enchanted lyre.
397:
Sea turtles are a type of food that restores 21 Hitpoints when eaten. It can be obtained by cooking raw sea turtle on a fire or cooking range , requiring level 82 Cooking and granting 211.3 experience when successful. When cooking there is a chance to fail, resulting in a burnt sea turtle . The burn rate decreases as the player's Cooking level increases. Sea turtles never stop burning altogether even at level 99, unless the player is wearing a Cooking cape .

Players without the cooking cape are encouraged to cook sea turtles on the clay oven within the Hosidius Kitchen , as this provides the player the best chances to successfully cook them.
399:
Burnt sea turtle is the result of accidentally burning a raw sea turtle while attempting to make a sea turtle . The burn rate while cooking these will decrease as players reach higher Cooking levels. There is no level where sea turtles stop being burned, although wearing a Cooking cape will prevent players from burning any food.

The burnt sea turtle has no use whatsoever. Like most other burnt food, it is tradeable to other players but not on the Grand Exchange .
401: Seaweed is an item dropped by creatures near water, like rock crabs. It can also be obtained from Fishy salvage. It can be used with a filled fishbowl to catch a fish in the Catherby aquarium, or be cooked on a range or fire to create soda ash. Seaweed may also be used in place of soda ash in the superglass make Lunar spell, skipping the need to convert it to soda ash. Seaweed can be used for normal compost.
403:
Edible seaweed is an edible version of seaweed that restore 4 Hitpoints. Edible seaweed can be cooked on a range or fire to create soda ash (an ingredient in molten glass), granting no experience.

The item is one of the possible random items required during the quest Fairytale I - Growing Pains.
405:
A casket is an item occasionally dropped by monsters that are near oceans or bodies of water. It can also be obtained via big net fishing , at a rate of about 1/128 at lower levels and 1/85.3 at higher levels. The fishing spot in Civitas illa Fortis has around a 1 in 5 chance of rewarding a casket, making this one of the most reliable places to obtain them. It can be opened to receive a small amount of treasure. Wearing a skills necklace with at least one charge while big net fishing will slightly increase the chance of finding a casket. [ 1 ]

For ironmen, these can be a good early source of a Cosmic talisman .
407: An oyster has a chance to contain an oyster pearl or be an empty oyster. They can sometimes be obtained by fishing with a big fishing net (requires 16 Fishing), by drift net fishing, or through panning at the Digsite. They can also be obtained as a drop from various monsters. The pearls found from an oyster can be made into pearl bolt tips at level 41 Fletching by using a chisel on them.
409: An empty oyster is an oyster which has been opened and does not contain a pearl. It has no known use, but is collected by some players who like accumulating large amounts of difficult to obtain items such as burnt food and crushed gems. These items are not traded on the Grand Exchange, and are often discarded by players because they serve no real purpose.
411:
An oyster pearl is a small, round, milky-coloured semi-precious gem obtained by opening oysters. They can also be collected by fishing with a big fishing net, participating in the Fishing Trawler minigame, panning in the river at the Digsite, sorting large salvage, or by killing various monsters.

Players with 41 Fletching can use a chisel on this item to gain 6 pearl bolt tips, which can be attached to iron bolts or dragon bolts to make pearl bolts or pearl dragon bolts.
413: Oyster pearls are a reward from the Sea Slug quest. They can also be dropped by some monsters or obtained through shipwreck salvaging. Players with 41 Fletching can use a chisel on this item to gain 24 pearl bolt tips, which can be attached to iron bolts or dragon bolts to make pearl bolts or pearl dragon bolts.
415:
Ethenea is a quest item used only in Biohazard. It is obtained from Elena after returning her distillator to her.

It is first given to Da Vinci, who will smuggle it into the Dancing Donkey Inn, past the Guard conducting body searches. After retrieving it from Da Vinci, it is given to Guidor in south-east Varrock, alongside plague sample, liquid honey, sulphuric broline, and touch paper.

Duplicates can be drop tricked by talking to Elena to obtain another. Copies in the bank will be deleted after giving it to Da Vinci in Rimmington. After talking to Guidor about the results of the test, all copies of the ethenea in the inventory are deleted. Unlike the sulphuric broline and liquid honey, the ethenea is colourless, meaning Da Vinci will not try to paint with it.
416:
Liquid honey is a quest item used only in Biohazard . It is obtained from Elena after returning her distillator to her.

It is first given to Chancy , who will smuggle it into the Dancing Donkey Inn , past the Guard conducting body searches. After retrieving it from Chancy, it is given to Guidor in south-east Varrock , alongside plague sample , sulphuric broline , ethenea , and touch paper .

Duplicates can be drop tricked by talking to Elena to obtain another. Copies in the bank will be deleted after giving it to Chancy in Rimmington. After talking to Guidor about the results of the test, all copies of the liquid honey in the inventory are deleted. As stated in the examine text, liquid honey has little value, meaning Chancy will not attempt to gamble with it.
417:
Sulphuric broline is a quest item used only in Biohazard . It is obtained from Elena after returning her distillator to her.

It is first given to Hops , who will smuggle it into the Dancing Donkey Inn , past the Guard conducting body searches. After retrieving it from Hops, it is given to Guidor in south-east Varrock , alongside plague sample , liquid honey , ethenea , and touch paper .

Duplicates can be drop tricked by talking to Elena to obtain another. Copies in the bank will be deleted after giving it to Hops in Rimmington. After talking to Guidor about the results of the test, all copies of the sulphuric broline in the inventory are deleted. If this item is given to either Da Vinci or Chancy , they will fail to bring it to the Dancing Donkey Inn as requested. Da Vinci will use it in a work of art, and Chancy will gamble it away. Hops will not drink it because it is poisonous, so he cannot drink it. Even though it is said to be poisonous, it is not edible so players cannot inflict self-injury by drinking it.
418:
The plague sample is a quest item used only in Biohazard . It is obtained from Elena after returning her distillator to her.

It is given to Guidor in south-east Varrock , alongside liquid honey , sulphuric broline , ethenea , and touch paper .

Duplicates can be drop tricked by talking to Elena to obtain another. After talking to Guidor about the results of the test, all copies of the plague sample in the player's bank and inventory are deleted.
419:
Touch paper is a quest item used only in Biohazard. It is obtained from the Chemist in Rimmington after Elena has given the player the testing materials.

It is given to Guidor in south-east Varrock, alongside plague sample, liquid honey, sulphuric broline, and ethenea.

Duplicates can be drop tricked by talking to the Chemist to obtain another. After talking to Guidor about the results of the test, all copies of touch paper in the player's bank and inventory are deleted.
420:
The distillator is a quest item used only in Biohazard. It is found in a crate within the storeroom on the 1st floor of the Mourner Headquarters. Players are able to access the storeroom after killing the level 13 Mourner to obtain a key used to unlock the gate.

It is returned to Elena in order to run some tests.

Duplicates can be drop tricked by searching the crate to obtain another. After returning them to Elena, she will take all copies from the player's bank and inventory.
421:
Lathas' amulet is a discontinued quest item from the Elf quest series. It was given out as part of the reward for the Biohazard quest in RuneScape Classic. Players were given the amulet by King Lathas so that he could inform them upon the discovery of a way into the forests of Isafdar; similar to how Lathas' Messenger appears for Regicide. The amulet's gem was green until the release of Underground Pass, when it changed red. To begin the quest, players needed to visit King Lathas.

The amulet was also originally required in RuneScape Classic to gain access to the Combat Training Camp. Players had to show the amulet to the Guard outside to gain permanent access. At some point however, this requirement was removed.

The amulet could still be obtained as a reward from Biohazard during the early stages of RuneScape 2 but was discontinued at some point before July 2004. As a result, it has never been obtainable in Old School RuneScape.
422:
Bird feed is a quest item used only in Biohazard . It is found by searching the cupboard in Jerico 's house, immediately south of the northern bank in East Ardougne .

It is thrown onto the watchtower fence to cause a distraction by releasing the pigeons from the pigeon cage , in order for the player to climb the rope ladder near Omart to access West Ardougne .

Duplicates can be drop tricked by searching the cupboard to acquire another. However, throwing one bird feed at the watchtower will delete additional copies, and the player will no longer be able to acquire any more bird feed.
423:
The Key is a quest item used only in Biohazard. It is automatically placed into the player's inventory after killing the level-13 Mourner on the 1st floor of the Mourner Headquarters in West Ardougne.

It is used to open a gate to access a stockroom full of crates, one of which holds a distillator.

Duplicates can be drop tricked by killing the mourner to obtain another. After talking to King Lathas about the plague hoax, all copies of the key in the player's bank and inventory are deleted. This key cannot be added to the steel key ring.
424:
A pigeon cage is a quest item used in Biohazard and One Small Favour. It can be found in the garden behind Jerico's house, immediately south of the northern bank in East Ardougne.

In Biohazard, it is used to distract the mourner guards on the watchtower with bird seed. In One Small Favour, five of them are turned into chicken cages by using a steel bar.

The answer to the medium clue scroll step asking how many are behind Jerico's house is 3.
425:
A pigeon cage is a quest item used in Biohazard and One Small Favour. It can be found in the garden behind Jerico's house, immediately south of the northern bank in East Ardougne.

In Biohazard, it is used to distract the mourner guards on the watchtower with bird seed. In One Small Favour, five of them are turned into chicken cages by using a steel bar.

The answer to the medium clue scroll step asking how many are behind Jerico's house is 3.
426:
Priest gown (top) is top half of the Priest gown set. A priest gown set is used in the Biohazard quest .

It can be bought from Thessalia's Fine Clothes in Varrock .
428:
Priest gown (bottom) is the bottom half of the Priest gown set. A priest gown set is used in the Biohazard quest .

It can be bought from Thessalia's Fine Clothes in Varrock .
430:
The medical gown is a quest item used in Biohazard and A Tail of Two Cats. It is found in the cupboard of Nurse Sarah's house, south-west of the west Ardougne church.

While it is equipped, the player is allowed to enter the Mourners' Headquarters in the north-east corner of West Ardougne after poisoning the stew in the back yard with a rotten apple. This item may also be used as part of a medical disguise in A Tail of Two Cats.

Duplicates can be drop tricked by searching the cupboard to obtain another. Duplicates can be obtained after completing the quests, but it serves only as a cosmetic item.
431:
Karamjan rum is the local drink of Karamja. It can be bought from Karamja Wines, Spirits, and Beers shop on Karamja and the Dead Man's Chest in Brimhaven. Members can use the rum on a piece of silk to create a cleaning cloth, which is used to remove poison from weapons.

Drinking the rum heals 5 Hitpoints and also boosts Strength equal to 1 + 5% of the player's base Strength level, rounded down. Drinking it also temporarily lowers the drinker's Attack equal to 3 + 2% of the player's current Attack level, rounded down. Upon drinking the rum, the chatbox displays the message You drink the rum. You feel slightly reinvigorated... ...and slightly dizzy too..

Smuggling Karamjan rum off Karamja and giving it to Redbeard Frank is the primary focus of the Pirate's Treasure quest. It also plays a smaller role in the Tai Bwo Wannai Trio quest, where it needs to be combined with sliced banana to create a special banana rum requested by Tinsay. Note that if a player does not slice the banana before placing it in the bottle, they will in fact place the entire banana in it and receive the amusing line, "You stuff the banana in the neck of the bottle. You begin to wonder why." This makes the rum into a useless item, as the banana cannot be removed.
432:
The Chest key is a quest item used only in Pirate's Treasure . It is given to the player by Redbeard Frank after giving him some Karamjan rum .

It is used to open the chest in one of the guest rooms upstairs in the Blue Moon Inn in Varrock to retrieve a pirate message . The key can only be obtained during the quest and is kept upon completion.

Opening the chest will give the player the following messages in their chatbox:

If the player uses the drop trick to obtain multiple keys, selecting 'Open' on the chest for a second time will tell the player that the chest is locked, even though they have a key in their inventory. However, if the player manually uses the key on the chest, it will open, allowing the player to obtain multiple pirate messages.

However, this can no longer be done after the pirate message is read and the quest stage is advanced. Instead, the player will receive the following messages in their chatbox:
433:
The Pirate message is a quest item used only in Pirate's Treasure. It is found in a locked chest, that is unlocked with a key, on the 1st floor of the Blue Moon Inn.

The message informs the player of the buried treasure's location somewhere in Falador Park. It is kept upon quest completion, but has no use.

If the player uses the drop trick to obtain multiple chest keys, selecting "open" on the chest for a second time will tell the player that the chest is locked, even though they have a key in their inventory. However, if the player manually uses the key on the chest, it will open, allowing the player to obtain multiple pirate messages. After reading the pirate message it will be no longer possible to obtain duplicates; the key will snap and be destroyed.
434:
Clay (sometimes called hard clay to distinguish it from soft clay ) is mined from clay rocks , requiring 1 Mining , and yielding 5 Mining experience . When mined it respawns in one game tick . Using a water container, such as a bucket of water , on it makes soft clay . Alternatively the Lunar spell humidify can do the same.

Soft clay is used to make pottery in Crafting , furniture in Construction , and Magic tablets . Mining a clay rock while wearing a bracelet of clay yields soft clay , similar to how it can also be mined directly from soft clay rocks in Trahaearn mine in Prifddinas .

Clue geodes are still obtainable when using a bracelet of clay.
436: Copper ore can be mined at level 1 Mining providing 17.5 Mining experience. After mining copper rocks , it will take 2.4 seconds until it reappears. Copper ore is used with tin ore to smelt bronze bars , or used with nickel ore to smelt Cupronickel bars . Smelting a bronze bar gives 6.2 Smithing experience.
438: Tin ore can be mined at level 1 Mining providing 17.5 Mining experience. After mining tin rocks, it will take 2.4 seconds until it reappears. Tin ore is used with copper ore to smelt bronze bars. Smelting a bronze bar gives 6.2 Smithing experience.
440: Iron ore can be mined from iron rocks at level 15 Mining , providing 35 Mining experience . It can be smelted at a furnace into an iron bar at level 15 Smithing , or along with two coal into a steel bar at level 30 Smithing. Smelting iron bars has a 50% success rate, unless the player is wearing a ring of forging , using the Superheat Item spell, or using the Blast Furnace . Smelting iron ore into a bar gives 12.5 Smithing experience, and smelting a steel bar gives 17.5 Smithing experience.
442:
Silver ore can be mined at level 20 Mining , providing 40 Mining experience. After silver rocks are mined, it takes 60 seconds for them to respawn. Smelting silver ore will turn it into a silver bar , requiring 20 Smithing and giving 13.7 Smithing experience. The bar can then be crafted into various types of jewellery through the Crafting skill at a furnace, rather than at an anvil like other metallic bars. Doing so requires the usage of a mould , depending on the type of jewellery desired.

Wearing mining gloves , superior mining gloves , or expert mining gloves allows 1, 2, or 3 additional ores (respectively) to be mined before depletion.
444:
Gold ore can be mined from gold rocks at level 40 Mining , providing 65 Mining experience. After it is mined, it takes 60 seconds to regenerate. Gold ore is used to smelt gold bars at a furnace . Smelting a gold bar requires level 40 Smithing and gives 22.5 Smithing experience, or 56.2 with goldsmith gauntlets equipped. The bar can then be used again on a furnace to craft various types of jewellery , with sufficient Crafting skill, and an appropriate mould . An anvil is only used to make a gold helmet , and golden bowl for the quests Between a Rock... and Legends' Quest respectively.

A frequently occurring item, gold ore can be acquired through various means, beyond mining. It can be bought from shops, obtained from monster drops and pick-pocketing, as a reward from a variety of chests and reward crates, through the Gnome Restaurant and Volcanic Mine minigames, and can also be obtained by handing in nuggets to Terry Balando at the Digsite .

The chance to successfully mine gold ore scales linearly with the player's mining level. Were it possible to mine gold ore at level 1, players would have a 3% chance per mining cycle to successfully mine the ore. At level 99, players have a 29% chance to successfully mine the ore per mining cycle. [ 1 ]

Wearing either mining gloves , superior mining gloves , or expert mining gloves while mining a gold rock generates additional mineable gold. This allows you to mine the same rock once, twice, or thrice more, respectively, before depletion.

Smelting gold ore currently gives some of the fastest Smithing experience available in the game whilst wearing goldsmith gauntlets (or a Smithing cape / Max cape ) and smelting at the Blast Furnace . This method tends to average 250,000-350,000 experience per hour, but at maximum efficiency players can reach upwards of 420,000 experience per hour. For non-Ironmen, this method currently has a profit/XP of −1.17 , along with additional costs of 72,000 /hour to use the Blast Furnace, and 34,884 /hour, assuming an average of 36 doses of Stamina potion used per hour. See Blast Furnace/Strategies .
446:
'Perfect' gold ore is ore mined in the Witchaven Dungeon, found south-east of Ardougne. It requires 40 Mining to mine and can be smelted into a 'perfect' gold bar.

'Perfect' gold ore is the same as regular gold ore. The differences are only seen by Avan from Family Crest quest. He will say that he'll give you his piece of the crest if you make him a necklace and ring made from a 'perfect gold bar' with rubies in them.

Smelting 'perfect' gold ore while wearing the Goldsmith gauntlets received after the quest will result in the standard double experience (56.2 exp with the gauntlets, rather than 22.5 from smelting it normally).

'Perfect' gold bars can be used as a substitute for regular gold bars when making other jewellery, but it will function as if regular gold was used, and it will not receive the prefix 'perfect'.

If the player is wearing Varrock armour 1 or higher while mining 'perfect' gold ore, and the additional ore mining perk activates, the player will receive one gold ore and one 'perfect' gold ore rather than two 'perfect' gold ore. The chance to smith two at once at the Edgeville furnace also applies. The various tiers of Mining gloves will provide their ore saving effect when mining the 'perfect' gold ore.
447:
Mithril ore can be mined at level 55 Mining providing 80 Mining experience. After mithril rocks are mined, it will take two minutes until it reappears. Mithril ore is used with four coal to smelt mithril bars . Smelting a mithril bar gives 30 Smithing experience.

Wearing either superior mining gloves or expert mining gloves while mining a mithril rock makes the rock not deplete upon mining mithril, allowing you to mine one or two additional ore, respectively, before depleting.
449:
Adamantite ore can be mined at level 70 Mining providing 95 Mining experience. After adamantite rocks are mined, it will take four minutes until it reappears. Adamantite ore is used with six coal to smelt adamantite bars . Smelting an adamantite bar gives 37.5 Smithing experience.

Wearing either superior mining gloves or expert mining gloves while mining an adamantite rock makes the rock not deplete upon mining adamantite, allowing you to mine one or two additional ore, respectively, before depleting.
451:
Runite ore can be mined at level 85 Mining providing 125 Mining experience. After runite rocks are mined, it will take twelve minutes until it reappears. Runite ore is used with eight coal to smelt runite bars. Smelting a runite bar gives 50 Smithing experience.

Wearing expert mining gloves while mining a runite rock grants a guaranteed extra gather before depleting.
453:
Coal can be mined at level 30 Mining providing 50 Mining experience. After coal rocks are mined, it will take 30 seconds until it reappears. Coal is required to smelt all ores above iron (other than gold , silver , lead , and nickel ), in increasing amounts.

Members can store 27 pieces of coal in one inventory space by using a coal bag , obtained from Prospector Percy's Nugget Shop for 100 golden nuggets at Motherlode Mine .

Wearing mining gloves , superior mining gloves , or expert mining gloves while mining coal rocks makes the rock not deplete upon mining coal, allowing you to mine one, two, or three additional coal, respectively, before depleting.
455:
The barcrawl card records player's progress in the Alfred Grimhand's Barcrawl miniquest . It is given to player by the Barbarian guard when they first try to enter the Barbarian Outpost north of Baxtorian Falls . If players try to read the card after finishing the crawl they will be told: "You are too drunk to be able to read the barcrawl card."

Passing the Barcrawl test gives the player access to the outpost, although in order to access the agility course within they still require 35 agility.

Completing Alfred Grimhand's Barcrawl is a requirement for the Horror from the Deep quest during which players must talk to Gunnjorn inside of the agility course to obtain a spare key to the Lighthouse . It is also a requirement for the Scorpion Catcher quest, as one of the scorpions is inside the outpost (however the agility level is not required since the scorpion is located at the entrance section).

See Alfred Grimhand's Barcrawl for more info.
456:
The scorpion cage is an item obtained from Thormac at the beginning of Scorpion Catcher. This item is used in the quest to capture the scorpions which are obtainable from: Taverley Dungeon, Barbarian Outpost and Edgeville Monastery. According to Thormac, these scorpions are rare. If you lose the cage, you can get another by talking to Thormac again. After losing the cage, you will need to recapture any previously caught scorpions.

It's possible to get this item from Thormac without starting Scorpion Catcher. It's also possible to obtain duplicates by having a full backpack when Thormac attempts to give the player a cage. However, the cage serves no purpose outside the quest.

464:
The strange fruit is an item that can be picked from the strange plant random event , obtained from the Flowering Tree Forestry event, or stolen from fruit stalls .

It can be eaten to cure poison, venom, and restore 30% run energy, making it a potential substitute for energy potions and antipoisons / anti-venoms in situations where they are both needed. Upon being consumed, it prevents further re-application of poison or venom for approximately 18 seconds (note that this is not traditional immunity, therefore cannot be used to mitigate special attacks from a Dreadborn Araxyte ). [ 1 ] No Hitpoints are restored upon eating the fruit.

When eaten, the message You eat the fruit. It tastes great, some of your energy is restored! is displayed.

Strange fruits cannot be noted by Tool Leprechauns .
466:
A pickaxe handle was the handle of a pickaxe . When players were mining , a random event may have caused the pickaxe head to fly off. Players had to pick it up and attach it back onto the handle. A similar thing used to happen to players while woodcutting , only with an axe head and axe handle .

After random events were voted to be reworked in late 2014 , they were subsequently removed from the game with the next update.
468:
A broken bronze pickaxe was a bronze pickaxe that had been broken by an exploding rock . It could be fixed at Nurmof 's Pickaxe Shop in the Dwarven Mine .

If the broken pickaxe was equipped before being broken, it would remain in the weapon slot. Once unequipped, it could not be equipped again.

After an update on 11 September 2014 making random events optional, all existing broken pickaxes were automatically repaired.
470:
A broken iron pickaxe was an iron pickaxe that had been broken by an exploding rock . It could be fixed at Nurmof 's Pickaxe Shop in the Dwarven Mine for 50 coins .

After an update on 11 September 2014 making random events optional, all existing broken pickaxes were automatically repaired.

480:
A bronze pick head was obtained as part of a discontinued random event, in which the bronze pickaxe head flew off the handle while the player was mining. To fix it, the player had to collect it off the ground and reattach it to the handle.

If players were not paying attention when this occurred, the head would disappear from the ground or be picked up by another player, requiring them to purchase another.

The pick heads were all repaired in an update on 11 September 2014, and the event was discontinued.
482:
An iron pick head was obtained as part of a discontinued random event , in which the iron pickaxe head flew off the handle while the player was mining. To fix it, the player had to collect it off the ground and reattach it to the handle.

If players were not paying attention when this occurred, the head would disappear from the ground or be picked up by another player, requiring them to purchase another.

The pick heads were all repaired in an update on 11 September 2014 , and the event was discontinued.

492:
Axe handles were items created through a random event that caused axe heads to fly off whilst Woodcutting . Heads and handles were either re-attached or deleted to prevent them from becoming discontinued items.

Dragon axes were included in this event. As they were worth over 2 million at the time, players who were not paying constant attention risked substantial losses. Curiously, although a special version of the Dragon axe handle was added in 2006, it was still possible to combine a Dragon axe head and a regular Axe handle.

Axe handles were removed in an update on 17 July 2007 , prior to the release of Old School RuneScape , so they have never been obtainable.
494:
A broken bronze axe was a bronze axe that has been broken by an ent from a random event. It can be fixed at Bob's axe shop in Lumbridge.

If the broken axe was equipped before being broken, it will remain in the weapon slot. Once unequipped, it cannot be equipped again.

After an update on 11 September 2014 making random events optional, all existing broken axes were automatically repaired.

522:
Enchanted beef is a quest item used only in Druidic Ritual . It is made by dipping raw beef into the Cauldron of Thunder .

It is given to Sanfew to create a potion.

Multiple enchanted beef can be made during the quest. After the quest, it cannot be made again.
523:

It is given to Sanfew to create a potion.
