526:
Bones are the remains of most creatures with an animalistic or humanoid appearance.

Bones give 4.5 Prayer experience when buried. This can be increased by offering the bones in different ways:

Players may also use the Bones to Bananas or Bones to Peaches spells to turn normal bones to edible bananas or peaches .

25 regular bones are used in the Demon Slayer quest .
528:
Burnt bones are one of the few bones that free players can bury to train Prayer , with the others being normal bones , big bones , and monkey bones . They can be found in the Kebos Battlefront , the Lizardman Canyon , the Dragon Nest , and various locations in the Wilderness .

Burnt bones give 4.5 Prayer experience when buried. This can be increased by offering the bones in different ways:

It is not recommended to train Prayer with burnt bones, as they are no different from regular bones , which are much easier to obtain. Additionally, unlike regular bones, they cannot be blessed on the exposed altar .
530:
Bat bones are a type of bone which are dropped by bats and giant bats . Players will need bat bones for some quests , including Merlin's Crystal , Forgettable Tale... , and Watchtower .

Bat bones give 5.3 Prayer experience when buried. This can be increased by offering the bones in different ways:
532:
Big bones are a bigger variant of bones. They are always dropped by certain large monsters including giants, ogres, trolls, cyclopes, and the lizards in the Kharidian Desert just north of Nardah. A few spawns of big bones can also be found in the Bone Yard in the Wilderness, and in the area around the Colossal Wyrm Remains located in Varlamore's Avium Savannah.

Big bones are also used to charge teleports on the giantsoul amulet, with each set of big bones and a law rune providing one teleport charge. Players can exchange excess amulets for 30 bones by speaking to the Odd Old Man with the amulets in their inventory.

Big bones give 15 Prayer experience when buried. As a member, this can be increased by offering the bones in different ways:

45 XP when casting Sinister Offering.

45 XP when offered at the sacred bone burner after the appropriate faith level has been achieved.

52.5 XP when offered at a gilded altar with two burners lit.

60 XP when offered at the Ectofuntus in the form of big bonemeal.

60 XP when blessed and broken down into blessed bone shards and offered at the libation bowl, or 72 XP when offered with a jug of blessed sunfire wine. Virilis outside the altar will exchange noted bones for 10 coins each.

105 XP on average when offered at the Chaos Temple in the Wilderness. Each offering gives 52.5 XP, which is the same as the gilded altars with two burners lit, but with an additional 50% chance to not consume the bones.
534:
Babydragon bones are dropped by baby green , blue , red and black dragons . They can also be obtained as a common loot from dragon impling jars and crystal impling jars .

Babydragon bones give 30 Prayer experience when buried. This can be increased by offering the bones in different ways:

Using babydragon bones instead of dragon bones is a slower but cheaper method to gain Prayer experience.

A babydragon bone is on the item list that Thorgel gives you. Giving him all of the items on the list rewards the player with a Death talisman .
536:
Dragon bones are bones dropped by most adult dragons, which give 72 Prayer experience when buried. This can be increased by offering the bones in different ways:

216 XP when casting Sinister Offering.

216 XP when offered at the sacred bone burner after the appropriate faith level has been achieved.

252 XP when offered at a gilded altar with two burners lit.

288 XP when offered at the Ectofuntus in the form of dragon bonemeal.

290 XP when blessed and broken down into blessed bone shards and offered at the libation bowl, or 348 XP when offered with a jug of blessed sunfire wine. Virilis outside the altar will exchange noted bones for 10 coins each.

504 XP on average when offered at the Chaos Temple in the Wilderness. Each offering gives 252 XP, which is the same as the gilded altars with two burners lit, but providing a 50% chance to not consume the bones.

The relative ease of collecting dragon bones, combined with the amount of experience earned from them, makes them widely viewed as a fast, cost-effective way to train Prayer.

A set of dragon bones is required for the Watchtower quest.
538: The druid's robe (bottom) is part of the druid's robes set. Pieces of the druid robes can be obtained by killing druids in Taverley .
540: The druid's robe top is part of the druid's robes set. Pieces of the druid robes can be obtained by killing druids in Taverley .
542: Monk's robe is a part of Monk's robes and is found lying on the table upstairs in the Edgeville Monastery, which requires a Prayer level of at least 31 to enter. The monk's robe bottom provides a +5 Prayer bonus while having no requirements to wear.
544: Monk's robe top is a part of Monk's robes and can be found lying on the table upstairs in the Edgeville Monastery, which requires a Prayer level of 31 to enter. The monk's robe top is useful in that it provides a +6 Prayer bonus while having no requirements to wear.
546:
Shade robe top is a part of Shade robes and is dropped by shades . It provides 2 higher Prayer bonus than a priest gown , but 1 less than a monk's robe top .

This item can be stored in the fancy dress box of a costume room , as part of the Shade Robes set. Ultimate Ironmen will be unable to retrieve individual pieces until the full set is stored.
548:
Shade robe is a part of Shade robes and is dropped by shades . It provides +1 higher Prayer bonus than a priest gown , but 1 less than a monk's robe .

This item can be stored in the fancy dress box of a costume room , as part of the Shade Robes set. Ultimate Ironmen will be unable to retrieve individual pieces until the full set is stored.
550:
A Newcomer map is a map sold at many general stores for one coin. It is also sold by Rasolo and Trader crewmembers for 2 coins.

The map helps new players of the game find their way around Gielinor . The map does not give clear directions, but shows a general view of eastern Asgarnia and western Misthalin , being the main Free-to-play area of the game. The map will also display the rough location of the player with a blinking grey cross on the map. This item is not particularly useful anymore due to the world map interface (added in 2017) serving a similar purpose. The cross is rather offset; standing next to the Al Kharid gate shows the cross north of Al Kharid .
552:
A ghostspeak amulet is an item worn in the neck slot that enables the wearer to talk to ghosts. Partial completion of The Restless Ghost is required to obtain the item, as it is given to players by Father Urhney in order to speak to the ghost haunting the Lumbridge graveyard during the quest. Normally players can only get one ghostspeak amulet as Father Urhney will not give an amulet to players who have one in their possession, although the drop trick can be used to obtain more.

An enchanted ghostspeak amulet is given to players by the old crone in order to control Necrovarus during the Ghosts Ahoy quest.

Players who have completed the Morytania Medium Diary may use Morytania legs in place of a ghostspeak amulet anywhere it is required, except during the miniquest The General's Shadow as the ghostly robes must be worn, and the miniquest Curse of the Empty Lord as armour is not allowed on Entrana.

Players who have lost their amulet may obtain another one from Father Urhney.
553:
The ghost's skull is a quest item used only in The Restless Ghost . It is found in the Wizards' Tower basement by searching the altar.

After searching the altar a skeleton will appear. Killing it is optional, and the player may run if desired. Putting the skull back into the restless ghost 's coffin will complete the quest.
554: Fire runes are one of the four elemental runes . They are used to cast fire-based combat spells in the standard spellbook , as well as casting many spells from other spellbooks . Some notable use cases for fire runes include casting alchemy spells to convert items into coins , charging a trident of the seas or trident of the swamp , and resurrecting high level thralls . Several items throughout the game, such as the staff of fire , provide infinite fire runes while equipped. Fire runes or packs can be bought from Magic shops , such as Aubury's Rune Shop in Varrock . Non- ironman players can also purchase them from the Nightmare Zone using 25 reward points.
555:
Water runes are one of the four elemental runes . They are used to cast water-based combat spells in the standard spellbook , as well as many spells found in other spellbooks . The Confuse , Weaken , and Curse spells, often regarded as an inexpensive source of Magic experience , require water runes in conjunction with body and earth runes to cast. Some items, such as a staff of water , provide infinite water runes while equipped.

Water runes or packs can be bought from Magic shops , such as Aubury's Rune Shop in Varrock . Non- ironman players can also purchase them from the Nightmare Zone using 25 reward points.
556:
Air runes are one of the four elemental runes. They are used in every combat spell and most teleportation spells in the standard spellbook, as well as in many spells from other spellbooks. Because they are used very often, players are recommended to purchase an item that can provide infinite air runes while equipped, such as a staff of air.

A common way for beginning players to obtain air runes is to talk to the magic tutor in Lumbridge. She will give you 30 air and mind runes if you don't have any in your inventory or bank. Air runes or packs can be bought from Magic shops, such as Aubury's Rune Shop in Varrock. Non-ironman players can also purchase them from the Nightmare Zone using 25 reward points.
557: Earth runes are one of the four elemental runes . They are used to cast earth-based combat spells in the standard spellbook , as well as many spells found in other spellbooks ; Earth runes are used especially often for spells in the Lunar spellbook . The Confuse , Weaken , and Curse spells, often regarded as an inexpensive source of Magic experience , require earth runes in conjunction with body and water runes to cast. Some items, such as a staff of earth , provide infinite earth runes while equipped.
558:
The mind rune is used for the strike spells including Wind Strike, Water Strike, Earth Strike, and Fire Strike, as well as the Magic Dart spell.

Mind runes are craftable at level 2 Runecraft. Crafting mind runes provides 5.5 Runecraft experience per rune or pure essence used. Using mind cores in place of essences will yield an increased amount of mind runes. Members can also use Warped extracts to increase the quantity of crafted mind runes by 250 per pure essence, requiring partial completion of Desert Treasure II - The Fallen Empire and access to the Scar essence mine.

The Mind Altar is located north of Falador, in between Goblin Village and Ice Mountain, very near to the Wilderness. The Arceuus spellbook teleport to the Mind Altar can be used in conjunction with rings of dueling and essence pouches to achieve approximately 30k experience to upwards of 43k experience per hour at level 99 when crafting mind runes.

If you have no mind runes in your bank or inventory, and you have not dropped any right under you, you can obtain 30 new ones from the magic tutor in Lumbridge along with 30 air runes. Mind runes can be purchased from a myriad of shops, such as Betty in Port Sarim, the Void Knight Magic Store on Pest Control Island, or from Aubury just south of Varrock east bank in Aubury's Rune Shop.

There is a Falador Diary task in the hard section to craft 140 Mind runes at the same time. This requires level 56 Runecraft.
559:
Body runes are low level runes used for confuse , weaken , curse and Monster Inspect spells in the standard spellbook , as well as Dream and Stat Spy in the Lunar spellbook . They are also used for the reanimation spells Basic Reanimation and Adept Reanimation in the Arceuus spellbook .

Body runes can be created using Runecraft skill at level 20 at the Body Altar south of Edgeville Monastery , providing 7.5 Runecraft experience per essence. They are the highest level rune Free to Play players can craft.

2 body runes can be consistently found outside of the eastern wall of the Grand Exchange in Varrock, respawning approximately every 20 seconds. 15 body runes can be found among lesser demons at the Lava Maze deep within the Wilderness .
560:
Death runes are one of the runes used to cast spells in the Magic skill. They are required to cast medium-level missile spells, like Wind Blast, Water Blast, Earth Blast, and Fire Blast. Members with 65 Runecraft and who have completed Mourning's End Part II can craft death runes at the Death Altar by using pure essence on it, with each essence yielding one death rune. Each death rune yields 10 Runecraft experience. Players with 99 Runecraft will always craft two death runes per essence. Crafting death runes from essence is a requirement for the Hard Ardougne Diary.

Death runes can be bought from most Magic shops. Several monsters, such as ankou, nechryael, and dark beasts, commonly drop death runes. They can also be found in the Barrows Chest with at least 631 rewards potential.

Players can exchange any cat that is not a kitten with the civilians in West Ardougne for 100 death runes, or 200 if they have completed the easy Ardougne diary.

Barbarian Assault uses a unique variant of death runes that are untradeable and have an alchemy value of 0 to prevent potential exploits. Nightmare Zone also uses a variant, also being untradeable and having an alchemy value of 0, in addition to being unusable for non-combat spells.
561:
Nature runes are runes used for transmutation spells such as Low and High Alchemy and Superheat Item . They are also used for the spells Bind , Snare , and Entangle , and several spells on the Lunar and Arceuus spellbooks . They can be purchased from many magic shops .

Nature runes can be crafted from pure essence by members with level 44 Runecraft at the Nature Altar , granting 9 experience per pure essence used. Players with 91 Runecraft will always craft two nature runes per essence.

Nature runes are one of the most traded non-elemental runes, because many players need the runes to train their Magic using profitable spells such as High Level Alchemy and Plank Make .

Nature runes can be used to charge Bryophyta's staff , allowing the player to save some runes and use spells that require nature runes without using an inventory space.
562:
Chaos runes are used for low level missile spells, such as wind bolt, water bolt, earth bolt and fire bolt. They are also used to charge the bone staff, warped sceptre, trident of the seas, trident of the swamp, the Eye of Ayak, and Tumeken's shadow.

They spawn in the Wilderness near some moss giants, in the north-west corner of the Dark Warriors' Fortress, and can also be bought from the Varrock and Port Sarim magic shops.

Members can make them with the Runecraft skill at level 35 at the Chaos Altar, by having pure essence in the inventory and a chaos tiara equipped or a chaos talisman in the inventory, granting 8.5 experience per rune crafted. At level 74 Runecraft and above, two chaos runes are made per essence at the Chaos Altar.

Barbarian Assault uses a unique variant of chaos runes that are untradeable and have an alchemy value of 0 to prevent potential exploits. Nightmare Zone also uses a variant, also being untradeable and having an alchemy value of 0, in addition to being unusable for non-combat spells.
563: The law rune is a rune used in all teleportation and telekinesis spells , as well as in many of the supportive and utility spells on the Lunar Spellbook . For non-members , the main source of law runes is from monster drops, as most monsters that drop runes may occasionally drop law runes. For members , they may be purchased in the Mage Arena Rune Shop or in the Wizards' Guild , requiring 66 Magic and completion of The Hand in the Sand . They can also be purchased from Ali Morrisane after partial completion of the Rogue Trader miniquest (after completing The Feud quest ), from the magic store on Ape Atoll after obtaining the greegree as part of the Monkey Madness I quest, or from the magic store in Prifddinas after completing Song of the Elves . Guardians of the Rift offers an efficient and affordable way of acquiring law runes.
564:
The cosmic rune is a rune used primarily in enchanting spells . Enchanting spells enchant jewellery , such as rings and amulets , into something that has an effect when worn or operated. For example, when the player casts Lvl-4 Enchant on a diamond ring , the ring will become a ring of life . Cosmic runes are also used for the Lunar spells Astral Contact , Cure Me , Cure Group , and Spellbook Swap and for the resurrection spells in the Arceuus spellbook .

They can be crafted at the Cosmic Altar in Zanaris through the Runecraft skill at level 27 for 8 experience per pure essence after the Lost City quest . They can also be purchased at Lundail's Arena-side Rune Shop in the Mage Arena in the Wilderness , Amlodd's Magical Supplies in Prifddinas after completing Song of the Elves , or from Ali Morrisane after completing The Feud and the Rogue Trader miniquest. At level 59 Runecraft, the amount crafted doubles to two cosmic runes per pure essence. Twisted extracts can also be used to increase the quantity of crafted cosmic runes by 60 per pure essence, requiring partial completion of Desert Treasure II and access to the Scar essence mine .

There is a cosmic rune spawn in the north-western part of Wilderness, on the icy area just south of the members ' gate. A total of three cosmic runes spawn here with a respawn time of 1 minute and 53 seconds. This is a dangerous area due to player killers and aggressive ice warriors and ice giants .
565: Blood runes are one of the runes used to cast spells in the Magic skill. They are used in some of the highest level spells, the lowest of which is Ruby Crossbow Bolt Enchant , and the highest is Heal Group . Blood runes are also used in charging the scythe of Vitur , Sanguinesti staff , ring of shadows , and soul bearer .
566: Soul runes are one of the runes used to cast spells in the Magic skill. It is used for the strongest curse spells , the teleport-other spells , Enchant Crossbow Bolt (Dragonstone) , Blood Barrage , the shadow spells , and most Reanimation spells. Soul runes are also used in charging Tumeken's shadow , the soul bearer , and Kharedst's memoirs , as well as creating Elidinis' ward (f) .
567: An unpowered orb is an item used to make air orbs , water orbs , earth orbs , or fire orbs using the Magic skill.
569:
A fire orb is a glass orb that has been charged at the Obelisk of Fire by using the Charge Fire Orb spell, requiring 63 Magic , on the obelisk. The spell requires an unpowered orb , 30 fire runes , and 3 cosmic runes , yielding 73 Magic experience . The Fire Obelisk is located at the end of Taverley Dungeon , west of the black dragons .

A fire orb can be used on a battlestaff , requiring 62 Crafting , yielding a fire battlestaff and 125 Crafting experience.

They are also obtainable by pickpocketing gnomes , heroes , and elves or from killing Cerberus , killerwatts , lava dragons , tormented demons or level 61 zombies in Tarn's Lair .
571:
A water orb is a glass orb that has been charged at the Obelisk of Water by using the Charge Water Orb spell, requiring 56 Magic , on the obelisk. The spell requires an unpowered orb , 30 water runes , and 3 cosmic runes , yielding 66 Magic experience .

The Water Obelisk is located on the island across from the shore of Catherby , getting there by climbing a ladder at the end of Taverley Dungeon by the black dragons . Accessing this section of the dungeon requires the dusty key or 70 agility.

A water orb can be used on a battlestaff , requiring 54 Crafting , yielding a water battlestaff and 100 Crafting experience.
573:
An air orb is a glass orb that has been charged at the Obelisk of Air by using the Charge Air Orb spell, requiring 66 Magic, on the obelisk. The spell requires an unpowered orb, 30 air runes, and 3 cosmic runes, yielding 76 Magic experience. The Air Obelisk is located in level 7 Wilderness, north of Edgeville. To get there, climb the ladder north of the black demons in Edgeville Dungeon.

An air orb can be used on a battlestaff, requiring 66 Crafting, yielding an air battlestaff and 137.5 Crafting experience. Charging air orbs is also a hard Wilderness Diary task.
575:
An earth orb is a glass orb that has been charged at the Obelisk of Earth by using the Charge Earth Orb spell, requiring 60 Magic , on the obelisk. The spell requires an unpowered orb , 30 earth runes , and 3 cosmic runes , yielding 70 Magic experience . The Earth Obelisk is located in the Edgeville Dungeon , south of the black demons beyond the poison spiders and Chronozon .

An earth orb can be used on a battlestaff , requiring 58 Crafting , yielding an earth battlestaff and 112.5 Crafting experience.
577:
A blue wizard robe is the most basic piece of chest armour for low level Magic users. It can be turned into a black robe by using black dye on it; similarly, it can be created by using blue dye on a black robe.

The blue robe is often worn with the blue wizard hat and blue skirt for aesthetics.

One of only three free-to-play bodies with a magic attack bonus, the Blue wizard robe, Black robe, and their ornamental variants get +1 Magic attack and -3 Prayer bonus compared to the Zamorak monk top.
579: A blue wizard hat is low-level armour that provides a small Magic attack and Defence bonus. This hat can also be dyed into a black wizard hat by using black dye.
581:
A Black robe is one of the basic pieces of chest armour for low level Magic users. Black robes are often dropped by the dark wizards in the stone circle south of Varrock. It has identical stats to the blue wizard robe, as well as its trimmed and gold-trimmed versions. It can be created by using black dye on a blue wizard robe; similarly, it can also be turned into a blue wizard robe by using blue dye on it.

The black robe is often worn with the black wizard hat and black skirt for aesthetics. The hat has a slightly darker tone than the robes, instead more closely matching the priest gown. This is not the case with the robe's trimmed versions.

One of only three free-to-play bodies with a magic attack bonus, the Black robe, Blue wizard robe, and their ornamental variants get +1 Magic attack and -3 Prayer bonus compared to the Zamorak monk top.
583:
A bailing bucket is used in the Fishing Trawler minigame. Its sole purpose is to bail water out of the trawler. It is recommended for all players to have this item before going on a fishing trawler trip, as there is always a need to bail at least once.

Players can obtain bailing buckets from either the Khazard General Store (conveniently close to the Fishing Trawler) and Rasolo west of the Fishing Guild. However, the latter store is not recommended due to the location and stock. If players don't have a bailing bucket when starting a Fishing Trawler run, the crates on the deck of the Trawler can be searched for one. Bailing buckets can be traded with other players but not through the Grand Exchange.

Its default click option is to bail-with, followed by empty. The bucket can be emptied outside of the minigame, but when bail-with is used outside of the minigame, the player gets the message "You don't really need to bail yet."

It cannot be used in place of a regular bucket, and likewise a regular bucket cannot be used in place of a bailing bucket. Casting the Lunar spell Humidify will not fill the bucket.
585:

587:
The Orb of Protection is a quest item that the player must recover during the Tree Gnome Village. At the start of the quest the orb has been stolen by Khazard troops and this one is currently being held in the Khazard stronghold north-east of the Tree Gnome Village.

To recover this orb the player must break a hole in the stronghold's defences using a nearby ballista, climb in and either kill the Khazard commander or loot the chest upstairs.
588:
The Orbs of Protection are a quest item that players must recover during the Tree Gnome Village quest. They are stolen by a Khazard warlord during the quest and the player must find and defeat him in order to reclaim the orbs.

Once the orbs have been recovered the player must return them to King Bolren in the centre of the Tree Gnome Village maze.

Players cannot use the drop trick to keep a second one; if attempted, the chatbox will state "You already have the orbs", and it will be deleted. Using Telekinetic Grab does not work either. Attempting to pick up any additional orbs after the quest, will delete the item and the chatbox will state "King Bolren doesn't need anymore orbs from you".
589:
The gnome amulet is awarded to players by King Bolren after completion of the Tree Gnome Village quest. Should the player happen to lose the amulet, another can be obtained for free from King Bolren . It is made from the same material as the orbs of protection that are retrieved during the quest.

It functions as a melee-only amulet of defence , having +13 in all melee defences but no magic and ranged defence. For melee-only situations, this amulet is recommended over the amulet of defence .
590:
The tinderbox is used primarily for lighting fires by clicking 'use' on the tinderbox, then clicking a log. A tinderbox can be bought in most general stores. It is also used to light and relight candles and lanterns, so any player venturing into a dark area such as the Lumbridge Caves should bring one in case their light source goes out.

When used on logs that the player has the Firemaking level to light, the messages You attempt to light the logs. and The fire catches and the logs begin to burn. are displayed. If the player does not have the Firemaking level, a variation of the message will display You need a Firemaking level of X to burn X logs.

If the player is standing on a tile where they are unable to light logs, the message You can't light a fire here. is displayed instead.

The tinderbox is also used regularly in many quests.
592:
Ashes are a common item that are produced when a fire burns out. Ashes are used as a Herblore secondary, and are needed in a number of quests. They are commonly discarded, and can often be found where players are lighting fires for Firemaking training. If a player acquires multiple of Old man's message and starts a new task at the Wise Old Man , the duplicates will explode into ashes when attempting to read them.

Ashes can be crushed into ground ashes using a pestle and mortar .
594:
An unlit torch may be used with a tinderbox or used on a fire or range to get a lit torch. It is useful for dark tunnels and smoking Hunter traps once lit. 39 Hunter is required to smoke traps. Smoking traps increases the chance of catching a creature by 2% (additive).

Unlit torches are dropped by many cave dwelling creatures including the level 49 and level 76-78 Catablepons, and Cave slimes. They can also sometimes be found inside barrels in the Shaman Caves.

When lit, a torch can be used as a light source in dark dungeons and in some quests such as Shilo Village. Multiple torches (up to 3) can be used at the same time for brighter lighting (this also works with candles).

This can be a dangerous source of light in some places such as the Lumbridge Swamp Caves due to the fact that its open flame can ignite the "swamp gases" within the caves. If the player does not leave the swamp gas area immediately, or does not extinguish the flame, then the swamp gas may explode, damaging the player and putting out all light sources in the player's inventory.

Lit torches are also used in the Construction skill, as a lighting option in Dungeons, Oubliettes, and Treasure Rooms in a player-owned house.
595:
A Torch is an unobtainable version of the Lit torch . Torches were previously tradeable and could be turned into banknotes. However, they were made untradeable due to an unfixable bug where trading a lit torch in a dark area would not update the lighting for either player. [ 1 ] Any player who had a noted lit torch was given this now discontinued item. Originally, the item was identical to the real lit torch, except being stackable.

As this change occurred prior to August 2007, the item has never been obtainable in Old School RuneScape.

598:
Bronze fire arrows are bronze arrows wrapped in an oily cloth , which are then lit by using them on a tinderbox . They, along with any other fire arrow , are primarily used to pierce the guide rope in the Underground Pass to lower the bridge so that a player may walk across.

They have the same ranged strength as regular bronze arrows .
599:
"Pretty girl" was the name originally given to an unobtainable item that exists in the game cache. It was created to replace the noted form of Grip's keyring . Since items could not be fully removed once created, it was added in a hidden update in 2005 to fill this slot. The actual item was just a copy of a pink skirt.

If players attempted to view the pretty girl in game by using cheating software, they would be given a Hex edit detected instead.

In RuneScape 2 , the item later became viewable via Quick Chat, causing much confusion. It was deleted from the game cache in 2017, being replaced by Buchu seeds .
600:
The Astronomy book , or The Tale of Scorpius , is obtained during the Observatory Quest . It has a brief history of Scorpius and how he introduced astronomy to Gielinor .

After finding the book, a copy can also be found in the shelves in your house .
601:
The goblin kitchen key is a quest item in the Observatory Quest. It found in a chest in the Observatory Dungeon and is used to open the Kitchen gate in the same dungeon. The chest in which the key is found is different for every player, but remains the same once found. Attempting to obtain another from the chest while one is in the inventory yields the message: Another one will be of little use. However, it is possible to obtain duplicates if it is banked. It can be reobtained after the quest.

It cannot be added to the key ring.
602:
The lens mould is a quest item in the Observatory Quest . It is obtained by searching a stove in a locked kitchen in the Observatory Dungeon . The kitchen is accessed by killing the goblin guard nearby and then using the goblin kitchen key on the gate.

The mould must be given to the Observatory professor along with a piece of molten glass to make a new observatory lens for the telescope. He will be unable to make the lens and will return the mould and glass so the player can make it.

It should be noted that only one mould can be obtained at a time and only during the quest. It can also be kept after the quest if the player banks it before giving the observatory lens to the professor. Additionally, if the mould was kept after the quest, players can make multiple observatory lens, but it would serve no purpose.
603: The observatory lens is a quest item made and used during the Observatory Quest. During the quest, a lens mould and a piece of molten glass must be given to the professor in the Observatory. The professor will then attempt to craft the lens but be unable to do so. He will then return the mould and glass to the player and request it be crafted. Once made, the lens should be given to the professor so that the telescope can be repaired.
604:
The bone shard is a quest item that is given to the player by the spirit of Zadimus during the Shilo Village quest. When the player buries the corpse of Zadimus next to the tribal totem in Tai Bwo Wannai , Zadimus's spirit appears and thanks the player. The bone shard then emerges from the soil.

If the shard is dropped, it will crumble to dust, and players will have to retrieve Zadimus' corpse from the temple (rumoured to be Ah Za Rhoon ) and bury it again.

The shard is used later in the quest, when the player must fashion it into a Bone key using a chisel in order to enter Rashiliyia's Tomb .
605:
The bone key is used in the Shilo Village quest to open and enter Rashiliyia's Tomb . It can be made by using a chisel on a bone shard . Besides this function, it has no further use besides selling it to Yanni Salika for 100 coins.

The bone key can be added to the steel key ring to save bank space. Attempting to drop it will result in the chatbox stating This looks quite valuable. As you go to throw the item away Zadimus' words come to you again. 'I am the key, but only kin may approach her'.

If lost, it can be obtained again by speaking to Yanni Salika for 100 coins.
606:
The stone-plaque is a quest item that is obtained during the Shilo Village quest by using a chisel, a spade, or a pickaxe on a strange looking stone in Ah Za Rhoon.

The tablet is close to the ruined table by the hand-like water. The plaque should be given to Trufitus in Tai Bwo Wannai village along with a tattered scroll (pink), crumpled scroll (green), and the Zadimus corpse in order to progress through the quest. Trufitus translates it as a message left by Rashiliyia dooming Zadimus to eternal suffering.

Attempting to read it results in a message stating "The markings are very intricate. It's a very strange language. The meaning of it evades you though. Perhaps Trufitus can decipher the markings?"

Players can sell the plaque for 100 gold to Yanni Salika after the quest.

When you try to drop the item, you will receive a confirmation message, then when you drop it you will receive a text stating, "You drop the plaque and it bounces in a stream never to be seen again".
607:
The tattered scroll is a quest item that is obtained during the Shilo Village quest by searching a pile of loose rocks in the temple of Ah Za Rhoon . The scroll must be read before the player can enter the Tomb of Bervirius . It can also be used on Trufitus in Tai Bwo Wannai village for helpful dialogue. It is not used after the quest and can be sold to Yanni Salika in Shilo Village for 100 coins. If dropped it will "Slip down a narrow crevice never to be seen again".

The scroll details the death and resurrection of Bervirius .
608:
The crumpled scroll is a quest item that is obtained during the Shilo Village quest by searching some sacks in the temple of Ah Za Rhoon. The scroll must be read during the quest before the player can combine the bone beads with bronze wire to create the Beads of the Dead. It can also be used on Trufitus in Tai Bwo Wannai village for helpful dialogue.

Players can sell the scroll for 100 coins to Yanni Salika after the quest. If you drop the scroll, it will be destroyed, as it will "be blown away by the wind".
609: The rashiliyia corpse is a quest item used in the Shilo Village quest. It is obtained near the end of the quest by defeating the three forms of Nazastarool in the tomb of Rashiliyia. The corpse must then be placed upon the dolmen within the Tomb of Bervirius, located underneath Cairn Isle, to complete the quest.
610:
The Zadimus corpse is a quest item that is obtained during the Shilo Village quest by searching an ancient gallows in the temple of Ah Za Rhoon. The corpse must be given to Trufitus in Tai Bwo Wannai village. Afterward, it must be buried next to the Tribal Statue in the middle of Tai Bwo Wannai. The Spirit of Zadimus then appears and gives the player the key to Rashiliyia's tomb.

Though it cannot be dropped, the Zadimus corpse can be lost upon death or alchemised using Magic (albeit for 0 coins). Simply search the gallows again to reclaim it.

Note that burying the corpse does not give any prayer experience.
611:
The locating crystal is a quest item that is obtained during the Shilo Village quest by searching the dolmen in the Tomb of Bervirius. It is used to locate the tomb of Rashiliyia. In order for it to function the player is required to have at least 10 prayer points. After the quest is finished, it no longer functions but can be sold to Yanni Salika in Shilo Village for 500 coins.

If the player tries to drop the crystal, it will break and may damage the player for 1-10 Hitpoints. In case a player has less than 15 points of health however, dropping a locating crystal will inflict an amount of damage equal to half their Hitpoints instead. No damage is inflicted if the crystal is dragged to the incinerator in their bank.
612: The locating crystal is an unobtainable item that appears during the Shilo Village quest. When the player obtains the Locating crystal, they can use it to locate the tomb of Rashiliyia. A different coloured version of the crystal will appear in the chatbox, depending on how close the player is to the tomb. The actual recoloured crystals, however, cannot be obtained by the player.
613: The locating crystal is an unobtainable item that appears during the Shilo Village quest. When the player obtains the Locating crystal, they can use it to locate the tomb of Rashiliyia. A different coloured version of the crystal will appear in the chatbox, depending on how close the player is to the tomb. The actual recoloured crystals, however, cannot be obtained by the player.

616:
The Beads of the Dead are used during the Shilo Village quest to enter safely into Rashiliyia's Tomb . It is made by using bone beads on bronze wire . If lost, you can obtain another necklace from Yanni Salika in Shilo Village for 1,200 coins . He will also buy the necklace for 1,000 coins.

The beads must be worn when entering Rashiliyia's Tomb in order for the player to be adequately protected from her magical powers.
617:
Coins are found in Rashiliyia's Tomb , entered during the Shilo Village quest. Attempting to pick up the coins will cause four undead ones to spawn, accompanied by the following message:

The coins will not disappear from the floor, but they cannot be picked up. However, casting Telekinetic Grab on the item will allow the player to obtain it.
618: Bone beads are a quest item that are obtained during the Shilo Village quest by using a chisel on the sword pommel found in the tomb of Beverius. When combined with bronze wire they form a Beads of the Dead necklace that can be used to protect the player in Rashiliyia's Tomb. There are only three beads in the inventory icon, yet there are five on the necklace.
619:
A paramaya ticket is a ticket that allows a player to spend the night in the dormitory of the Paramaya Inn . It looks identical to an Archery ticket . Gaining access to the dormitory is a purely aesthetic feature which has no function, as players cannot actually sleep in the beds there.

One ticket may be purchased from Kaleb Paramaya for 35 coins or a pack of five can be bought for 175 coins. This item was made untradeable in an update on 22 January 2007 because of its use in scams. [ Explain ]

Paramaya tickets can sometimes be found inside barrels in the Shaman Caves .

It was mainly used in RuneScape Classic . Players had to sleep in a bed to reduce their fatigue so they could train their stats. Those without a sleeping bag would have to buy a Paramaya Ticket to use the bed in Shilo Village.
620:
A Paramaya ticket is an unobtainable version of the Paramaya ticket . Tickets could previously be traded and turned into bank notes; however, they were made untradeable in 2007 due to frequent use in scams. Any player who had a noted Paramaya ticket was given this now discontinued item. It is identical to the real ticket, except it is stackable.

As this change occurred prior to August 2007, the item has never been obtainable in Old School RuneScape .
621:
Ship tickets are tickets for the Lady of the Waves . It can be exchanged to Captain Shanks for a boat ride to Port Khazard or Port Sarim .

They can be purchased in Shilo Village from Seravel above the fishing shop north of the entrance. They can also be purchased from Captain Shanks who sells it for a varying price (usually between 26-45 coins).

Ship tickets can sometimes be found inside barrels in the Shaman Caves , visited during Legends' Quest .
623: The sword pommel is an item that is obtained during the Shilo Village quest by searching the dolmen in the Tomb of Bervirius . The pommel must be given to Trufitus in Tai Bwo Wannai village. The player must then use a chisel on the pommel to turn it into bone beads which, when combined with bronze wire , form a Beads of the Dead necklace. If lost, the pommel can be regained by returning to the tomb and searching the dolmen again.
624:
The bervirius notes is a quest item that is obtained during the Shilo Village quest by searching the dolmen in Tomb of Bervirius. The notes must be given to Trufitus in Tai Bwo Wannai Village.

When clicked, it will give you an option to read a Tattered Yellow papyrus, a Crusty Orange papyrus, or a Decayed White papyrus.

After the quest, the notes can be sold to Yanni Salika for 100 coins.

If dropped, flavour text reads, As you drop the delicate scrolls onto the floor, they disintegrate immediately.
625: A wampum belt is a quest item used in the Shilo Village quest. It is given to the player at the start of the quest by Mosol Rei outside the east entrance to Shilo Village. The player gives the belt to Trufitus in Tai Bwo Wannai village in order to find out more about the curse placed on Shilo Village.
626: Pink boots can be purchased at the Tree Gnome Stronghold from Rometti at his store, Fine Fashions , located north-east on the 1 st floor [ UK ] 2 nd floor [ US ] of the Grand Tree . Their stats are identical to Leather boots .
628: Green boots can be purchased at the Tree Gnome Stronghold from Rometti at his store, Fine Fashions , located north-east on the 1 st floor [ UK ] 2 nd floor [ US ] of the Grand Tree .

652: Cream robe bottoms can be purchased at the Tree Gnome Stronghold from Rometti at his store, Fine Fashions . You can find Rometti on the 1 st floor [ UK ] 2 nd floor [ US ] of the Grand Tree , in the north-eastern area.
654: Turquoise robe bottoms can be purchased at the Tree Gnome Stronghold from Rometti at his store, Fine Fashions . You can find Rometti on the 1 st floor [ UK ] 2 nd floor [ US ] of the Grand Tree , in the north-eastern area.
656: A pink hat is a piece of headwear that can be purchased at the Tree Gnome Stronghold from Rometti at his store Fine Fashions , located to the north-east on the 1 st floor [ UK ] 2 nd floor [ US ] of the Grand Tree . The hats are a slight upgrade from wizard hats , offering one more Magic attack and defence.
658:
A green hat can be purchased at the Tree Gnome Stronghold from Rometti at his store, Fine Fashions, located north-east on the 1st floor of the Grand Tree. These hats are a slight upgrade from Wizard hats, as Gnome hats have 1 more Magic attack and defence.

The hat may be required to complete an emote clue during a Treasure Trail.
660: A blue hat can be purchased at the Tree Gnome Stronghold from Rometti at his store, Fine Fashions , located north-east on the 1 st floor [ UK ] 2 nd floor [ US ] of the Grand Tree . These hats are a slight upgrade from Wizard hats , as Gnome hats have 1 more Magic attack and defence.
662:
A cream hat can be purchased at the Tree Gnome Stronghold from Rometti at his store, Fine Fashions , located north-east on the 1 st floor [ UK ] 2 nd floor [ US ] of the Grand Tree . These hats are a slight upgrade from Wizard hats , as Gnome hats have 1 more Magic attack and defence.

This item can be obtained when the player is chasing Solus during the Wanted! quest.
664: A turquoise hat can be purchased at the Tree Gnome Stronghold from Rometti at his store, Fine Fashions , located north-east on the 1 st floor [ UK ] 2 nd floor [ US ] of the Grand Tree . These hats are a slight upgrade from Wizard hats , as Gnome hats have 1 more Magic attack and defence.
666:
The portrait is a quest item used only in The Knight's Sword. It is found in a cupboard on the 2nd floor of the White Knights' Castle in Falador after talking to the Squire.

It is given to Thurgo so he can study the sword design.

Duplicates can be drop tricked to obtain another. After talking to Thurgo about the picture, all copies of the portrait in the inventory are deleted.
667:
The blurite sword is a longsword quest item used only in The Knight's Sword . It requires 1 Attack to wield, and is obtained by giving a blurite ore and two iron bars to Thurgo after showing him a portrait of the sword.

The blurite sword has the same attack and defence bonuses as a steel longsword with the strength bonus of an iron longsword . It is slightly worse than Silverlight . Because of this and the fact that there is no Attack level needed to wield it, the blurite sword is sought by some lower level players at the start of the game.

Duplicates of the sword can be obtained by bringing Thurgo an extra blurite ore and two iron bars. During the quest, any swords must be drop tricked to obtain duplicates, but this is not necessary after quest completion.
668:
Blurite ore is a quest item used in The Knight's Sword . It can be mined at level 10 Mining , and grants 17.5 Mining experience when mined. After being mined, a blurite ore rock takes approximately 25 seconds to respawn.

Rocks containing blurite are found only in the mine in the Asgarnian Ice Dungeon , located south of Port Sarim on the tip of the Asgarnian Peninsula and north of Mudskipper Point ( Fairy ring A I Q ). The Ice Caves are guarded by Ice warriors and Ice giants , both of which can hit up to 7. Although blurite ore is mineable by non-members, only members can smith it. Thus, it is worthless to non-members except for doing The Knight's Sword.

At level 13 Smithing , members can smelt blurite ore into a blurite bar for smithing into blurite bolts or blurite crossbow limbs (for the easy Falador diary task) for use in a blurite crossbow .
669:
A specimen jar is an item that is obtainable during The Dig Site quest, used to dig in the level 3 digs. Specimen jars can be obtained by searching sacks in the Digsite, or by searching the cupboard on the south wall in the west room in the Exam Centre.

In addition to being used for level 3 digs, specimen jars can be used to dig in specimen trays for charcoal and other loot.

If a player does not have a specimen jar in their inventory upon searching the specimen tray, they will be stopped by a nearby digsite workman.
670:
Specimen brush is an item used in the Digsite. It is needed in The Dig Site quest and to dig in level 3 sites. It can be obtained by pickpocketing a Digsite workman. You can also take it from the tool rack in the Varrock Museum. It cannot be withdrawn as a bank note.

It is also given to the player during the quest Another Slice of H.A.M.
671:
Rock samples were items originally obtained during The Dig Site . Players were required to find three rock samples and give them to the Students , who in return would provide the correct answers to the Digsite exam.

In August 2006, the quest was reworked. The three rock samples were replaced by the Animal skull , Special cup , and Teddy , which are all obtained in the same way and serve the same purpose.
672:
Rock samples were items originally obtained during The Dig Site . Players were required to find three rock samples and give them to the Students , who in return would provide the correct answers to the Digsite exam.

In August 2006, the quest was reworked. The three rock samples were replaced by the Animal skull , Special cup , and Teddy , which are all obtained in the same way and serve the same purpose.
673:
Rock samples were items originally obtained during The Dig Site . Players were required to find three rock samples and give them to the Students , who in return would provide the correct answers to the Digsite exam.

In August 2006, the quest was reworked. The three rock samples were replaced by the Animal skull , Special cup , and Teddy , which are all obtained in the same way and serve the same purpose.
674:
A cracked sample is found whilst digging in training digs or searching the chests in the Exam Centre south of the Digsite . After the certification exam has been completed, it can be smashed with a rock pick causing it to disintegrate, displaying the messages You smash the rocks with the pick. and They disintegrated. .

When shown to Terry Balando , he says "What a shame it's cracked; this looks like it would have been a good sample."
675: A rock pick is needed to dig for items in the Level 2 Digs in the Digsite and to clean finds at the Varrock Museum . They can be found at the Exam Centre in a cupboard on the northern wall of the same room with Terry Balando or on the tool rack on the southern wall of the roped-off archaeology area in the museum. The rock pick cannot be equipped nor can it be used as a pickaxe for Mining .
676:
The trowel is an item used in the Digsite to dig level 1 and 3 sites. One is also needed in The Dig Site quest to find the Ancient talisman, as well as Another Slice of H.A.M. to dig up ancient goblin artefacts. They can be obtained after clearing the first exam of the quest. Players can get another from examiners if they lose theirs. After the quest, players can also use a trowel to clean Uncleaned finds in the Varrock Museum activity.

Digging grants 6 Mining experience at level 1 sites and 8 Mining experience at level 3 sites. Items you can obtain digging with a trowel are as follows:

Ancient talisman (in Level 3 dig site during The Dig Site)

677:
The panning tray is a quest item used during The Dig Site quest to retrieve a special cup . One spawns in the tent near the south-eastern shore of the Digsite east of Varrock.

To use it, the panning guide must be bribed with a cup of tea or nettle tea . This can be done before the quest is started.

In addition to the special cup found during the quest, other items can be found, such as an opal (one of which is needed in the quest), gold nuggets (three of which can be exchanged for a piece of gold ore ), an oyster , an uncut opal , an uncut jade , coins , or just plain mud, which yields no items. Panning provides 2 Fishing experience and 2 Mining experience.
678:
The panning tray is an unobtainable item that is used during The Dig Site . In the quest, the player is required to use the panning tray to retrieve a special cup . There is a chance of finding gold nuggets when searching the panning tray, causing this item to appear in the chatbox. The actual panning tray full of gold cannot be obtained by the player however.

In RuneScape Classic , the item could be obtained after searching the muddy panning tray. It is unknown what happened to these items on the transition to RuneScape 2 .
679:
The panning tray is a quest item used during The Dig Site quest to retrieve a special cup . One spawns in the tent near the south-eastern shore of the Digsite east of Varrock.

To use it, the panning guide must be bribed with a cup of tea or nettle tea . This can be done before the quest is started.

In addition to the special cup found during the quest, other items can be found, such as an opal (one of which is needed in the quest), gold nuggets (three of which can be exchanged for a piece of gold ore ), an oyster , an uncut opal , an uncut jade , coins , or just plain mud, which yields no items. Panning provides 2 Fishing experience and 2 Mining experience.
680: Nuggets are pieces of gold found at the Digsite when panning with a panning tray . Players can trade three of them to Terry Balando at the Exam Centre for one gold ore .
681:
Ancient talisman is a quest item. It is obtained and used in The Dig Site quest. Once you have passed all exams, go to dig in level 3 site (requires trowel and specimen brush ) and you will eventually find the ancient talisman. Bring it to archaeological expert Terry Balando to learn that it is actually a talisman of Zaros . The archaeology expert is impressed and will give you an invitation letter to enter winches.

Additionally, duplicates can only be obtained during this part of the quest. In order to obtain a duplicate it must be done via the drop-trick while excavating the level 3 dig site. The duplicates are not removed from one's inventory upon completing the quest's section.

The talisman's inscription reads: " Zaros will return and wreak his vengeance upon Zamorak the pretender. "

After the quest, the talisman is on display at the Varrock Museum .
682: The unstamped letter is received from an Examiner by talking to her and choosing "Can I take an exam?" This item starts The Dig Site quest . It needs to be stamped by the Curator of the Varrock Museum , in order to continue on with the quest. If you lose this item, you can get another by talking to an Examiner in the Exam Centre .
683: The sealed letter is a quest item used in The Dig Site. It is obtained by taking the unstamped letter to the Curator in Varrock's museum. He will then add his seal to the letter and the player can then return to the digsite exam centre to continue the quest. If you happen to lose your sealed letter, you can acquire a replacement for free from the Curator.
684: A belt buckle can be found while using a trowel on the soil in the level 3 dig site in the north-eastern Digsite , along with a specimen brush and a specimen jar in the inventory. When shown to Terry Balando , he says "This is a belt buckle. Not so unusual - I should imagine it came from a guard." The belt buckle has no other uses.
685: An old boot is an untradeable, useless item. It cannot be worn, nor can it be used with another old boot or any other item.
686:
A rusty sword is a broken sword that can be repaired by bringing it to Tindel Marchant in Port Khazard and paying 100 coins or repaired on a whetstone or on an armour stand in a Player-owned house workshop. All three options have a chance to break the sword, however the chance of it breaking on the whetstone or armour stand decreases with Smithing level. Successfully repairing a rusty sword yields 25 Smithing experience.

The easiest way for low-level players to obtain a rusty sword is by pickpocketing H.A.M. Members (requires 15 Thieving, reached by picking the H.A.M. Hideout trapdoor), killing H.A.M. Guards (levels 12, 18, 22, reached by the same method), or by playing Fishing Trawler (Requires 15 Fishing). Alternatively, it can be obtained from monster drops or at the Digsite after partial completion of The Dig Site quest.
687:
A broken arrow can be found in certain item spawn points, such as in the Ranging Guild and playing the Fishing Trawler minigame. An Ava's accumulator can also randomly attract one to the player's inventory. If it is caught during Fishing Trawler, then the player will receive 5 Fishing experience. Searching certain boxes on the table during the King's Ransom quest provides unlimited broken arrows.

Broken arrows, along with broken staves and broken armour can be repaired at a repair bench in a player-owned house. Successfully repairing a broken arrow gives 8 Fletching experience and creates up to a mithril arrow. Failing to repair the broken arrow destroys it.

When shown to Terry Balando, he says "No doubt this arrow was shot by a strong warrior – it's split in half! It is not a valuable object though."
688:
Buttons are dropped by H.A.M. Guards, thieved from H.A.M. Members in the H.A.M. Hideout behind the Lumbridge General Store, earned from the Fishing Trawler minigame, dug up at the Digsite, or obtained from Ogre Coffins.

Polishing them into polished buttons requires 3 Crafting, yielding 5 Crafting experience and the message You rub the buttons on your clothes and they become more shiny.. Polished buttons are used in the Animal Magnetism quest. Without the required Crafting level the message says You rub the buttons on your clothes but they aren't improved by the process..
689:
A broken staff is an item that can be repaired into different kinds of staves at a repair bench, whetstone, or armour stand in the workshop of a player-owned house. Repairing one gives 14.5 Crafting experience.

Broken staves can be dug up at the Digsite or fished up on the Fishing Trawler.

When shown to Terry Balando, he says, "Look at this... Interesting... This appears to belong to a cleric of some kind; certainly not a follower of Saradomin, however. I wonder if there was another civilization here before the Saradominists?"
690:
Broken glass is an item that could originally be obtained when searching soil in the Digsite . Although it was obtainable in RuneScape Classic and early RuneScape 2 , at some point the soil was changed to give the standard broken glass found at the Fishing Platform . It is unknown exactly when this occurred, but it was possibly with the rework of The Dig Site on 22 August 2006.

It may also have been obtainable by searching various chests or sacks, which would provide various pieces of junk. This feature was removed in an update on 27 September 2006.
691:
The level 1 certificate is a quest item used during The Dig Site . Players may obtain one after completing the first archaeology exam. The certificate allows players to dig at level 1 sites in the Digsite .

Players may bring the certificate to the Varrock Museum curator, who will take it for safekeeping. This is not required to claim the reward from giving in the Level 3 certificate . You will not get the certificate back.

There is no method to recover the item should it be lost. Players should be careful if they wish to keep the certificate as a souvenir.
692:
The level 2 certificate is a quest item used during The Dig Site . Players may obtain one after completing the second archaeology exam. The certificate allows players to dig at level 2 sites in the Digsite .

Players may bring the certificate to the Varrock Museum curator, who will take it for safekeeping. This is not required to claim the reward from giving in the Level 3 certificate . You will not get the certificate back.

There is no method to recover the item should it be lost. Players should be careful if they wish to keep the certificate as a souvenir.
693:
The level 3 certificate is a quest item used during The Dig Site . Players may obtain one after completing the third archaeology exam. The certificate allows players to dig at level 3 sites in the Digsite .

Players may bring the certificate to the Varrock Museum curator to get a Fruit blast or a Chocolate cake . The item will be consumed once given to the museum's curator. You will lose the reward if you exit the dialogue after he has taken your certificate, but before you have chosen the reward.

There is no method to recover the item should it be lost. Players should be careful if they wish to claim the post-quest rewards or keep the certificate as a souvenir.

In Leagues , the item can be infinitely reclaimed from the examiners in the Exam Centre .
694: Ceramic remains can be found at the Digsite . When shown to Terry Balando , he says "Yes, many parts are discovered. The inhabitants of these parts were great potters." The item has no other uses.
695:
An old tooth can be found while digging at the digsite using a trowel , obtained from the Varrock Museum or an Examiner , on the digging area west of the animal skull or panning in the panning area with a panning tray .

When shown to Terry Balando , he says "Oh, an old tooth. It looks like it has come from a mighty being. Pity there are no tooth fairies around here!" The old tooth has no other uses.
696:
The invitation letter is a quest item used in The Dig Site to gain access to the winches. It is obtained from Terry Balando after the player has brought him the Ancient talisman . Giving it to any digsite workman grants them access to the dig shafts.

It is possible to obtain multiple letters by using the drop trick . Should the player use another letter on a workman, they will ask "What an earth are you giving me another scroll for?"
697:
Damaged armour is an item that can be found by digging at the digsite , from the Fishing Trawler minigame, or from pick-pocketing certain monsters (including H.A.M. members). It is also found in ogre coffins (see ogre coffin key ), can be telegrabbed inside the Ranging Guild 's archery competition spot, and is found in the Uzer Mastaba by searching the first skeleton directly east of the stairs. Players may use the drop trick as a free and quick way to obtain lots of the damaged armour item from this skeleton.

Players may also find damaged armours scattered throughout the world in the form of scenery. However, these may not be picked up.

Members can repair it at an armour stand (55 Construction required to build, but players could use others') in the workshop of a player-owned house . It will then become a platebody armour made from a random metal up to mithril , although there is a significant chance of breaking it beyond repair. The most common armour produced this way is an iron platebody , though bronze , steel , black , and mithril are also possible. Successfully repairing a damaged armour gives 25 Smithing experience.
698:
Broken armour can only be found by digging in the Digsite. It can be repaired at an armour stand (55 Construction required to build, but players could use others') in the workshop of a player-owned house. It will give 25 Smithing experience and become a platelegs or plateskirt of random metal, from bronze to mithril. However, there is a chance of breaking it beyond repair, destroying the item.

When shown to Terry Balando at the Exam Centre in Misthalin, he says "It looks like the wearer of this fought a mighty battle."
699:
The stone tablet is a quest item. It is used in The Dig Site quest to find that the digsite was a temple dedicated to Zaros . Giving it to Terry Balando finishes the quest. It is found from a cave that can only be entered with a chemical compound .

If the player tries to give another tablet after the quest, Terry will say: "I don't need another tablet! One is enough, thank you."
700:
Ammonium nitrate is a quest item. It is used in The Dig Site quest along with nitroglycerin , ground charcoal , and arcenia root to make a chemical compound .

It is obtained by using the chest key to open the chest near the panning point, and is brought to Terry Balando , who identifies it as ammonium nitrate. Before he identifies it, it is known as chemical powder.
701:
Ammonium nitrate is a quest item. It is used in The Dig Site quest along with nitroglycerin , ground charcoal , and arcenia root to make a chemical compound .

It is obtained by using the chest key to open the chest near the panning point, and is brought to Terry Balando , who identifies it as ammonium nitrate. Before he identifies it, it is known as chemical powder.
702:
Nitroglycerin is a vial of chemicals used in The Dig Site quest which, when combined with ammonium nitrate, ground charcoal and an arcenia root, create a chemical compound. Unidentified liquid may be obtained by using an empty vial on the barrel with a skull & crossbones symbol, to the west of the tent south of the Digsite, before being brought to Terry Balando for identification. After Terry has identified the liquid, all vials in your inventory will be converted to Nitroglycerin. If the barrel has not previously been opened, a trowel may be used on it in order to do so.

When dropped, a vial of unidentified liquid does 25 damage to the player and causes them to say Ow! The liquid exploded!. This damage is increased to 35 if dropping a vial of nitroglycerin and the message is changed to Ow! the nitroglycerin exploded! However, neither can kill the player in the event that the player's Hitpoints are already 25 or below (35 or below for nitroglycerin). They may be alchemised or destroyed using the incinerator to safely dispose of them.

704: Ground charcoal is an item used during The Dig Site. It is obtained by grounding normal charcoal with a pestle and mortar. It is used in The Dig Site quest where it is necessary to make Chemical compound (along with nitroglycerin, ammonium nitrate and arcenia root) to blow up bricks blocking the path below the digsite. It can also be used in Recipe for Disaster/Freeing the Goblin generals when Mudknuckles asks for charcoal.
705:
Mixed chemicals are used in the The Dig Site to create the chemical compound . It is made by combining nitroglycerin with ammonium nitrate , granting 2 Herblore experience. The chemicals can then be combined with ground charcoal , granting 2.5 Herblore experience, to make step 2 of the compound. Finally, it can be combined with an arcenia root to make the chemical compound , granting 3 Herblore experience.

Due to the nitroglycerin, dropping the mixed chemicals will cause an explosion that destroy the item and deals a significant amount of damage to the player. The chemicals deal 45 damage after step 1, or 55 damage after the addition of ground charcoal in step 2, but the damage is not lethal.
706:
Mixed chemicals are used in the The Dig Site to create the chemical compound . It is made by combining nitroglycerin with ammonium nitrate , granting 2 Herblore experience. The chemicals can then be combined with ground charcoal , granting 2.5 Herblore experience, to make step 2 of the compound. Finally, it can be combined with an arcenia root to make the chemical compound , granting 3 Herblore experience.

Due to the nitroglycerin, dropping the mixed chemicals will cause an explosion that destroy the item and deals a significant amount of damage to the player. The chemicals deal 45 damage after step 1, or 55 damage after the addition of ground charcoal in step 2, but the damage is not lethal.
707:
Chemical compound is a quest item used in The Dig Site quest to blow up bricks blocking the path below the digsite . It can be lit using a tinderbox . Creating the compound requires 10 Herblore and gives 7.5 Herblore experience .

Warning: Dropping the vial will deal 65 damage to the player, but this will never kill the player, at most reducing them to a single hitpoint. If the chemical compound is dropped while the player only has a single hitpoint, they will say Ow! That really hurt! but take no damage.
708: Arcenia root is a quest item used in the quest The Dig Site to make Chemical compound along with nitroglycerin, ammonium nitrate and ground charcoal to blow up bricks blocking the path below digsite. It is obtained from tunnels where players can only enter with the invitation letter. Entering the tunnels requires 10 Agility.
709:
The chest key is a members -only quest item. This version of chest key is used in The Dig Site quest. It is obtained from Doug Deeping and opens a chest near the panning area on the River Salve , where players find ammonium nitrate .

If players wish to use the ammonium nitrate to create chemical compounds to damage themselves, they should do the drop trick to obtain multiple copies. Banking the keys does not allow you to get another, it must be dropped.
710:
A vase can be found while digging in the Digsite at a level 1 dig or searching skeletons in the Uzer Mastaba . It has no use.

Although this item can be found at the Digsite, Terry Balando doesn't have any dialogue when showing it to him.
711:
The Book on chemicals , or Volatile chemicals - Experimental Test Notes , is part of The Dig Site quest. It has some information on how to make a Chemical compound that can be used to destroy some blocks.

After the quest it can be found on the shelves in your house .
712:
The cup of tea is a discontinued item that previously could be found at the Tea stall in Varrock. In RuneScape Classic this item was known as display tea , and could be obtained by casting telekinetic grab. As the item was frequently used in scams, it was made untradeable with the release of RuneScape 2 and renamed, whereas the stall was changed to display a regular cup of tea . However, it still can be distinguished from the normal tea by its unique examine information.

As the cup of tea was discontinued before 2007, it has never been obtainable in Old School RuneScape .
713:
"Enjifern" was the name originally given to an unobtainable item that exists in the game cache. It was created to replace the noted form of the display tea, which was made untradeable. Since items could not be fully removed once created, Enjifern was added in a hidden update in 2005 to fill this slot. The actual item is just a copy of a pink skirt.

If players attempted to view Enjifern in game by using cheating software, they would be given a hex edit detected instead.

In RuneScape 2, the item later became viewable via Quick Chat, causing much confusion. It has since been renamed to clue scroll.
714:
Radimus notes is a quest item given to the player by Radimus Erkle during the Legends' Quest and is needed to enter the Kharazi Jungle . The notes consist of an incomplete map of the Kharazi Jungle, which Radimus wants to have fully charted. The player must take the notes to the western, central and eastern parts of the jungle, and use the notes at each location with 3 papyrus and a piece of charcoal in their inventory.

Once the map is completed, the player should give the notes to a Jungle Forester in exchange for a bullroarer . The Jungle Forester will copy them and return them so you can turn them in to Radimus at the end of the quest.

If you lose the notes at any time during the quest, you can talk to Radimus Erkle and pay 30 coins to get them back, though any previous progress is lost.

It is also used in the Freeing Sir Amik Varze section of Recipe for Disaster only if the player has not yet completed Legends' Quest .
715:

716:
The bullroarer is a quest item used during and after the Legends' Quest. During the quest, it is obtained by giving a complete map of Kharazi Jungle to a forester just outside the Kharazi Jungle. The bullroarer is used to summon a local tribesman named Gujuo from the dense jungle at various points during the quest for advice on how to proceed at each point. When used, players swing it around their heads, making a whirring sound.

Sometimes, swinging it near an oomlie bird or a tormented warrior makes them angry for disturbing the jungle's peace, whereupon they attack the player. Also, swinging it not far enough into the jungle makes nothing happen, with a message in the chat box saying, You feel a bit silly at first, but soon it makes an interesting sound. If used in an area other than the Kharazi Jungle, nothing will happen.

If lost, the bullroarer can be bought from any of the foresters at the price of a cooked oomlie wrap (by using the cooked oomlie wrap on the foresters). The drop trick works on the foresters during the quest to get multiple bullroarers by using Radimus notes on one.

Once the Legends' Quest is complete, players should keep it for the master clue step which requires swinging the bullroarer. They may also keep it to summon Gujuo to turn gold bowls into blessed gold bowls, used to make holy water to fight demons.
717: The scrawled note is an item obtained while searching the crate in the Shaman Caves during Legends' Quest. It cannot be reobtained after completing the quest.
718: A scribbled note is an item obtained while searching the table in the Shaman Caves during Legends' Quest . It cannot be reobtained after completing the quest.
719: The scrumpled note is an item obtained while searching the bed in the Shaman Caves during Legends' Quest . It cannot be reobtained after completing the quest.
720:
The sketch is a quest item obtained from Gujuo during the Legends' Quest . Gujuo gives the sketch to the player after speaking with his tribe's shaman, Ungadulu , who is currently trapped in a magical flame pit inside a cave in the jungle.

The sketch is a rough drawing of a gold bowl that the player must make in order to quench the flames that are holding Ungadulu prisoner.

During the quest, the player must have the sketch on them when making a gold bowl, but this is no longer required after completion of the quest.
721:
The gold bowl is a quest item used during the Legends' Quest . According to Gujuo , the required vessel for holy water is a bowl "made from the metal of the sun", referring to gold. The bowl is made by using two gold bars on an anvil while holding the sketch given to the player by Gujuo; after completion of the quest, it is possible to make the bowl without the sketch, though there remains a chance of failing. This gives 30 Smithing experience per bowl. The bowl must then be blessed with Gujuo's help to turn it into a blessed gold bowl . The blessed version is the only vessel capable of holding water with holy properties; trying to fill a normal gold bowl with the pure spring's water will yield a message along the lines of having mere normal water. A successful fill will result in a message saying that "the water seems to bubble and sparkle as if alive."

There is a chance that the player will fail in making the gold bowl, causing one or two gold bars to be destroyed without a resultant bowl. When successfully made, 30 Smithing experience is gained and a message of the achievement appears in the chat box.

Multiple gold bowls may be made during and after the quest to efficiently produce large amounts of Holy water . They will have to be blessed individually by Gujuo, however.
722:
The blessed gold bowl is a quest item made during or after the Legends' Quest . It is described by Gujuo as a bowl made of the metal of the sun.

The player must make the gold bowl by using two gold bars and a hammer at an anvil while holding the sketch given to the player by Gujuo to make a gold bowl . The bowl can then be taken back to Gujuo to be blessed (must have 42 prayer points, however they will not be consumed), to make it ready for it to hold the holy water needed to free Ungadulu . It is possible to fail when blessing the bowl causing the player to lose 5 prayer points in the process. If the blessed bowl is filled with the sacred pure water of the Kharazi water pool, it becomes a golden bowl containing sacred pure water that can be used with an enchanted vial to make a vial of holy water : one bowl can fill up to 10 vials. After making one successful golden bowl, the player can smith a gold bowl at any anvil, without need of the sketch, for 30 Smithing experience (though there remains a chance of failure); the bowl can then be taken to Gujuo to have it blessed.

Note: Filling an unblessed gold bowl from the Kharazi water pool will also create a golden bowl, but the examine information will reveal that the water is pure but no longer sacred. Filling a gold bowl or a blessed bowl with plain water from some other water source results in only plain water.
723:
The golden bowl is a quest item used during the Legends' Quest. It is made by first smithing a gold bowl from 2 gold bars, granting 30 Smithing exp, and then giving it to Gujuo in the Kharazi Jungle to bless it, making it into a blessed gold bowl. The player must then head to the pond in the middle of the jungle, cut a hollow reed by using a machete on the tall reeds next to the pond, and use the reed on the pond to turn the bowl into a golden bowl containing sacred pure water.

Note: Filling an unblessed gold bowl from the Kharazi water pool will also create a golden bowl, but the examine information will reveal that the water is pure but no longer sacred. Filling a gold bowl or a blessed gold bowl with plain water from some other water source will likewise cause it to be renamed a golden bowl, but the examine information will reveal that the water is only plain water.

Moving inside or outside of the Kharazi Jungle through the dense vegetation causes the water inside the bowl to evaporate. However, the player can use a Teleportation method to retain the filled bowl even outside the jungle. If you drop the bowl, the water will evaporate as well.

The bowl is required to fill holy water vials.
