894:
The Horse shoe was an unobtainable item present in the RuneScape 2 beta files. It was used in the original design for Death Plateau . Presumably, it would have been made by the Burthorpe smith and used to ascend the plateau.

The item could never be obtained by players, and was removed before the end of the beta. In the final version of Death Plateau released in August, it was replaced by Spiked boots .
942:
Bronze fire arrows are bronze arrows wrapped in an oily cloth , which are then lit by using them on a tinderbox . They, along with any other fire arrow , are primarily used to pierce the guide rope in the Underground Pass to lower the bridge so that a player may walk across.

They have the same ranged strength as regular bronze arrows .
943: A Worm is an unobtainable item seen when conversing with a Gnome child . When talking to a gnome child, they have a chance of offering you a snack, which displays a picture of this item in the chatbox. Although the "Worm" item is shown, King worms are obtained instead.
945: The throwing rope is an animation item used in the Underground Pass . It is temporarily wielded by the player during the animation when tying a rope to the rope swing . Aside from this, the item cannot be obtained.
946:
A knife is a multi-functional tool used for a large variety of tasks, primarily used for fletching logs in the Fletching skill and cutting food in the Cooking skill. It sees secondary usage in the Crafting skill. Additionally, it can be used to cut through webs and setup Hunter traps.

They are sold in many general stores, at Trader Stan's Trading Post on Karamja, or the Ardougne Spice Stall. A knife can also be found by searching a sack between two webs in front of the lever to the Mage Arena bank, if the player does not have a knife in their inventory.
948:
Bear fur is an item obtained by killing a bear . It can be sold to Baraek for 12 coins, or 20 with the Ring of Charos(a) . Bears are located in, among other places, north-east of East Ardougne , the Wilderness , near Goblin Village , in Isafdar , east of Varrock and north of Falador . Bear fur can also be purchased from the fur merchant in the marketplace in East Ardougne.

Although the examine text says, " This would make warm clothing, " currently no clothing can actually be made by players from the fur. Wooden cats , used in the The Great Brain Robbery quest, can be made with bear fur.

One piece of bear fur is needed during the quest Mourning's End Part I and the quest Getting Ahead .
950:
Silk can be bought from various silk traders around Gielinor.

Silk can be stolen from silk stalls with a Thieving level of 20, yielding 24 experience. The Silk merchant who runs the silk stall in Ardougne will buy silk from the player for as much as 60 coins through his dialogue, if the player first offers to sell them for 120 coins each.
952:
A spade is a multi-functional tool used for a variety of activities. One of its major uses is in the Farming skill, though it also comes in handy for many quests and Treasure Trails . A spade is also needed to enter the Barrows crypts and the Mole Hole .

Spades are sold in farming shops and many general stores , and an infinite supply can be added to the player-owned house by making a tool store 2 . They can also be obtained from a rogue kit , or taken from scenery objects found in various places. Finally, players can ask Konoo at the saltpetre mine in Hosidius for a spare spade.
954:
Rope is an item used for many things, such as quests and the creation of certain items. It can be obtained by purchasing at a shop, trading with Ned in exchange for 4 balls of wool, or by a player spinning yak hair on a spinning wheel.

The best store to buy rope, without requirements, is at Ned's shop in Draynor Village. However, you can get a full inventory of rope for free from the Tempoross minigame in the ropes container. A convenient place to get rope is in the Ardougne general store (helpful for those doing the Waterfall Quest and Plague City) where there is a stock of 20, but Martin Thwait's Lost and Found at Rogues' Den is a far better option since it stocks 50 and is next to a bank (although it requires 50 Thieving and 50 Agility to access his shop). Khazard General Store is also within close proximity of a bank.
956:
A flyer is a virtually useless item that, when examined , advertises Bob's Brilliant Axes . It is one of the possible required items that must be traded for a Kelda seed in the Forgettable Tale... quest . Additionally, it is one of the items that can be requested by Gunslik or the rowdy dwarf when doing Keldagrim tasks .

It can be dropped by barbarians and imps or obtained as a reward from a mystery box from the Quiz Master random event . Talking to men or women has a 1/128 chance of being offered a flyer. [ 1 ]
958:
Grey wolf fur is an item dropped by werewolves. Grey wolf fur can also be bought, or stolen from the East Ardougne fur trader, the Port Roberts fur stall and the Rellekka fur trader (after The Fremennik Trials quest).

Grey wolf fur can also be obtained from salvaging at merchant shipwrecks and sorting the Opulent salvage recovered. Level 87 sailing is required.

Baraek the fur trader will buy grey wolf furs for 120 coins, or 150 coins with the Ring of Charos(a). He will not buy any noted fur.
960: A plank is a common Construction item and is used in several quests . Made from normal logs , it is the lowest-level type of plank . Each plank used while training Construction yields 29 experience . They are also used to repair fishing cranes , which yields Crafting and Construction experience equal to 4 times the player's current level.
962:
Christmas crackers are a tradeable holiday item that can be obtained by completing one of the Christmas holiday events that occur once per year. They can be used on another player to provide party hats and rewards to both participants.

Ironmen cannot use party crackers on other players, so they have no use for crackers other than to sacrifice them to Death's coffer. Group ironmen however can open crackers with members of their group.
964:
A Skull is an item that can be found in various places, and is used as a material for Construction in player-owned houses. The player can use them to make a skeleton throne (level 88), skull torches (level 94), and hanging skeletons (level 94).

Skulls are involved in Mourning's End Part II, where Thorgel's item list includes a skull.
965:
A skull is an unobtainable version of the Skull. The skull could previously be traded and turned into bank notes; however, it was made untradeable in 2007. Any player who had a noted Skull was given this now discontinued item. It is identical to the real skull, except it is stackable.

As this change occurred prior to August 2007, the item has never been obtainable in Old School RuneScape.
966:
A tile is a formerly useless item that can be found in certain places in the Wilderness. Some tiles spawn in the Graveyard of Shadows and the western ruins.

Prior to the release of the Construction skill in 2006, many players speculated that tiles would be used in player-owned houses; however, they were never given a purpose when the skill was released. The tile remained a useless item until the robe bottom of ruin was discovered during the Crack the Clue III event, as a tile is required to obtain this reward.

This item cannot be traded on the Grand Exchange.
968:
Rocks are items created when a chisel is used on a piece of limestone in an attempt to craft a limestone brick unsuccessfully. 12 Crafting is required to do so, but there is a chance to fail. Failing to craft a limestone brick yields 1.5 experience. Players stop failing at level 40 Crafting.

Rocks can also sometimes be found inside barrels in the Shaman Caves.

This rock is obtained during In Aid of the Myreque, where the player must shift a great number of rubble from the basement of a building in Burgh de Rott during the quest, in order to prepare the area for use as the Myreque's new base of operations.
970:
Papyrus is an item used in building various furniture in a player-owned house . Additionally, after completing Enlightened Journey , using a ball of wool and unlit candle on a papyrus results in an origami balloon .

Papyrus is notably required for the following quests:
972:
Used papyrus is an unobtainable item that was released during the RuneScape 2 beta. It is a version of papyrus that has been used to write something using charcoal . Presumably, it was intended to be used during Shilo Village , which had been slightly reworked during the transition to RuneScape 2. However, for unknown reasons the used papyrus was never added to the game.

If the player loses the Bervirius notes at any point during the quest, they must recreate them using both Papyrus and Charcoal. It is possible therefore that the used papyrus would have either been a product of this action, or merely appear as a chatbox message similar to the Locating crystal .

Regardless, used papyrus has never been available in Old School RuneScape . However, it remains in the game files.
973: Charcoal is used as a writing and sketching tool in quests. It is often used with papyrus.
975:
The machete is an item used in the Woodcutting skill. It can be obtained from the mainland Karamja general store and Shilo Village general store or by trading with another player. It can also be found by looking in Radimus Erkle's cupboard in the Legends' Guild; however, after the quest is complete you may no longer search the cupboard for a machete and are given the message "You don't think Radimus Erkle would be very pleased if he caught you rifling through his possessions".

The machete can be used as a weapon but is primarily used to cut Jungle during the Tai Bwo Wannai Cleanup minigame. It has no requirements to wield though cutting Light, Medium, and Dense jungle requires 10, 20, and 35 Woodcutting to harvest respectively. A machete is also required to gain access to Kharazi Jungle if the player doesn't have access to the level 79 agility shortcut to the south-east of Shilo Village.

You can also obtain opal, jade, and red topaz machetes, which have a progressively higher speed at chopping down the jungles. To obtain these machetes, you can buy them from Gabooty in Tai Bwo Wannai, or speak to Safta Doc and make an exchange with him. Alternatively you can buy them from players or on the Grand Exchange.
977: The cooking pot is an interface item visible in the Cooking skill guide summary and it previously appeared in the Cooking level-up interface. However, the leveling up interface was updated on 26 June 2007 with an image of a different pot, before the release of Old School RuneScape. As a result, it served no purpose and could not be seen or obtained by players during normal gameplay until the skill guide summaries update in 26 March 2025 .
979:
The Highwayman mask is an unobtainable item that was added to the RuneScape 2 beta. It has an identical name and appearance to the Highwayman mask obtainable from Treasure Trails .

Its purpose is unknown, though it may have been accidentally added to the game early when the Highwayman mask's model was added to the level up screen for Thieving .
981:
The disk of returning is an item purchased from Diango's Toy Store for 21,000 coins. Players can activate the disk, which requires them to be inside the Dwarven Mine ; when activated, the player is teleported into the Blackhole , where Thordur resides. To leave, simply activate the disk again. This will cause players to reappear in the Dwarven Mine, next to Boot and the sign in the north-western corner of the mine. This means it could conceivably be used to quickly travel from the south-eastern part of the mine to the north-western part. This can be useful for Free-to-play Ultimate Ironmen to train their Smithing with Superheat Item in the mines, by accessing the anvils next to the respawn location after leaving the black hole, or for players running from Falador to the Ruins of Camdozaal .

The 'blackout' option on the disk may also be used in the easternmost part of the White Knights' Castle Crypt , although the 'activate' option does not work. This may be used to quickly reach certain clue step locations by teleporting to Falador, entering the crypt, and then entering and leaving the blackhole.

If not inside the Dwarven Mines, activating the disk of returning simply returns the message You can only enter Thordur's Blackholes from the Dwarven Mines, beneath Falador.

Attempting to drop it while inside the blackhole will result in a confirmation message asking, "Really drop your Disk of Returning?" Choosing "Yes, something cool might happen" will give the message "That was disappointing" . Occasionally, though, the chatbox message will state "Something cool happens" as the player performs the dance and clap emotes . This interaction is a reference to a scam that frequently occurred in RuneScape Classic , where visitors of the blackhole were told "something interesting would happen" if they dropped their disk of returning, resulting in a significant number of unoffending players getting stuck inside.

Note: You can still get out of both holes after dropping the disk of returning, either by talking to Thordur and asking how to get out, or by exiting through the light in the blacker blackhole. Any items dropped on the ground in either hole will be deleted upon leaving.
983:
The brass key is a key which allows the player to enter the locked shed found west of the Cooking Guild . The shed provides an alternate entrance to the Edgeville Dungeon , entering north of the Hill Giant room.

To get the key, you must enter the Edgeville Dungeon through the entrance south of the Edgeville bank and make your way through the dungeon. Just north of the hill giant room, there is a small circular room with the key on the ground. It re-spawns every minute.

This key is tradeable and can also be placed on the steel key ring .
985:
The tooth half of key is an item dropped by any monster that has access to the gem drop table or the rare drop table . It is also a reward from various random events , the gnome restaurant , from Managing Miscellania , caskets , looting magpie implings , and unlocking the crystal chest in Taverley . It can also be found in the Barrows chest as a separate item if the player has 100% [ 1 ] rewards potential.

The tooth half of a key is used with a loop half of key to make a crystal key , which is used to unlock the crystal chest , which contains a dragonstone and an assortment of other items.
987:
The loop half of key is an item dropped by any monster that has access to the gem drop table or the rare drop table . It is also a reward from various random events , the gnome restaurant , from Managing Miscellania , caskets , looting magpie implings , and unlocking the crystal chest in Taverley . It can also be found in the Barrows chest as a separate item if the player has 100% [ 1 ] rewards potential.

The loop half of a key is used with a tooth half of key to make a crystal key , which is used to unlock the crystal chest , which contains a dragonstone and an assortment of other items.
989:
The crystal key is created by combining a tooth half of key with a loop half of key , displaying the message, " You join the two halves of the key together. " Key halves can be obtained as rewards from Barrows , the Gnome Restaurant minigame , Managing Miscellania , Treasure Trails , looting magpie implings , random events , the rare drop table , etc.

It is used to open the crystal chest located inside a house in Taverley . The chest always contains an uncut dragonstone in addition to a variety of other items. Some items of note are 3 runite bars , rune platelegs / plateskirt (depending on the player's gender), or another half of the crystal key. After the key is used, it disappears and the player must use another one if they want to open the chest again.

The crystal key may not be placed on the steel key ring , as it is non-reusable.

The crystal key can be upgraded to an enhanced crystal key at a singing bowl in Prifddinas , for the cost of 10 crystal shards .

One is required for a medium Falador Diary task of opening a Crystal chest.
991:
The muddy key is a key that can be used to open the muddy chest in the centre of the Lava Maze in the Wilderness . You will need a knife or sword to access it. It can be obtained as a drop from chaos dwarves (in both the Wilderness and Taverley Dungeon ), and the crazy archaeologist .

Using a muddy key to open the muddy chest is a medium Wilderness Diary task.
993:
The sinister key is used to open the sinister chest in the Yanille Agility dungeon. The sinister chest contains nine noted grimy herbs: 2 harralanders, 3 ranarr weeds, 1 irit leaf, 1 avantoe, 1 kwuarm, and 1 torstol. The sinister key is dropped by Salarin the twisted and the Chaos Fanatic, and can also be looted from a Magpie impling.

The value of the sinister key is linked to the value of the herbs contained in the sinister chest. Buying a key, opening the chest, and selling the grimy herbs from it currently produces a profit of 4,538.

A lockpick is required if you're entering the dungeon via the house in Yanille.
995:
Coins (also referred to as gold pieces, gp, gold, or simply money) are the most common form of currency in Gielinor. They are used among players and non-player characters alike to exchange for items and services.

Players often refer to one thousand (1,000) coins as 1k and one million (1,000,000) coins as 1m or 1mil. Both can be applied to larger numbers, for example, 10m refers to ten million coins (10,000,000). 1b or 1bil refers to one billion coins (1,000,000,000).

Alchemy spells, which create coins, cannot be cast on coins. If a player attempts it, a message will inform the player that Coins are already made of gold. Curiously, other items made of gold, such as gold ore and gold bars, can be turned into coins with Alchemy spells.

Wearing a ring of wealth will automatically pick up coins dropped by NPCs upon killing them as long as the player has inventory space available.
1005: A white apron is a piece of clothing that gives no stat bonuses and is largely worn for fashion. It is used in the Pirate's Treasure and Mourning's End Part II quest. A white apron respawns in Gerrant's Fishy Business every 10 ticks, and another spawns in Wydin's Food Store in Port Sarim, though players must be wearing a white apron to grab the one in Wydin's Grocery.
1007: A red cape can be made by using red dye on another coloured cape , or purchased from Thessalia's Fine Clothes in Varrock or Barkers' Haberdashery in Canifis .
1009:
A brass necklace is a cosmetic piece of jewellery . It provides no stat bonuses and does not have any uses.

The necklace cannot be made using the Crafting skill; it can only be obtained as a drop from goblins and cave goblins , or as an item spawn in Edgeville Dungeon near the hobgoblins and in the Varrock west bank basement (requires the Telekinetic Grab spell or completion of Crack the Clue III to obtain).
1011:
A blue skirt is clothing that provides no bonuses. It can be purchased at Thessalia's Fine Clothes in Varrock for 2 coins.

Although the skirt aesthetically matches the Blue wizard hat and Blue wizard robe, the blue skirt offers no bonuses. Zamorak monk bottoms, however, are the only leg slot item with offensive magic bonuses in free-to-play.
1013:
A pink skirt is one of several skirts available to free players. It is used in the quest Prince Ali Rescue as part of the disguise Prince Ali wears in order to impersonate Lady Keli and escape from prison. The rowdy dwarf may ask for this item in the quest Forgettable Tale... in return for a Kelda seed .

It can be stored in the STASH unit outside the southern entrance to the Grand Exchange together with a pink robe top and a body tiara .

It cannot be created by using pink dye on a blue or black skirt .
1015:
Black skirts are one of several skirts available. They are sold by various clothes shops , including Thessalia 's shop, Thessalia's Fine Clothes , located in Varrock . They can also be dropped by Forgotten Souls .

Black robe skirts are often worn with black robe tops, in the same way blue skirts are worn with wizard tops . However, they provide no bonuses.
1017:
A black wizard hat is an item of clothing that can be worn in the head slot. It has the same bonuses as the blue wizard hat . It can be purchased from Betty's Magic Emporium in Port Sarim , and can be found as a drop from the dark wizards south of Varrock .

It can be created by using black dye on a blue wizard hat ; similarly, blue dye can be used on it to create a blue wizard hat.
1019: A black cape is a low-level cape that is commonly obtained by killing a highwayman. It can also be made by using black dye on any coloured cape, and can be purchased from Barkers' Haberdashery in Canifis and Shayzien Styles in Shayzien.
1021:
A Blue cape can be made by using blue dye on another coloured cape and can be purchased from Barkers' Haberdashery in Canifis , Valaine's Shop of Champions in the Champions' Guild , or Shayzien Styles in Shayzien .

A blue cape may also be among the items you can obtain from chasing Solus Dellagar during the Wanted! quest , the player calls this cape the "Cape of Champions" during the quest because it is sold in the Champions' Guild .
1023: A yellow cape can be made by using yellow dye on another coloured cape and can be purchased from Barkers' Haberdashery in Canifis, Fancy Clothes Store in the Varrock, or Shayzien Styles in Shayzien.
1025:
A right eye patch is an item commonly worn by pirates, and can be obtained as a drop from them. An eye patch can be bought from the Fancy Dress Shop or Trader Stan's Trading Post. When equipped, the eye patch takes place in the head slot, which means players may not wear a helmet or any other headgear at the same time.

Players who have completed Cabin Fever can pay Patchy 500 coins to sew together an eye patch and pirate bandana to create a bandana eyepatch. Players can also bring Patchy an eye patch and pirate's hat, to create a hat eyepatch, or a big pirate hat and eye patch to create a pirate hat & patch. It is also possible to ask Patchy to combine this item with a left eye patch to create a double eye patch. A book o' Piracy is not required.

It is one of the possible items that the rowdy dwarf may ask players to bring him during the Forgettable Tale of a Drunken Dwarf quest. It is also a possible request from Gunslik or the rowdy dwarf when doing Keldagrim tasks.

This item can be stored in the mahogany treasure chest of a costume room under master tier.
1027: A green cape can be made by using green dye on another coloured cape and can be purchased from Barkers' Haberdashery in Canifis .
1029: A purple cape is made by using purple dye on another coloured cape.
1031: An orange cape is made by using orange dye on another coloured cape .
1033:
The Zamorak monk bottom is part of the Zamorak monk robes set. They are bright red, and like the related Zamorak monk top they are dropped by disciples of Iban and monks of Zamorak .

Zamorak monk robes are commonly used by mages in the Wilderness due to providing decent Prayer and Magic bonuses and being easy to replace if lost. They can also be used to telegrab Wine of Zamorak at the Chaos Temple (Asgarnia) without being attacked.

The Zamorak monk bottom counts as a Zamorak item in the God Wars Dungeon .

The Zamorak monk bottom is notable for being the only free-to-play leg slot item with a Magic attack bonus.
1035:
The Zamorak monk top is part of the Zamorak monk robes set. They are bright red, and like the related Zamorak monk bottom they are dropped by disciples of Iban , necromancers and monks of Zamorak .

Zamorak monk robes are commonly used by mages in the Wilderness due to providing decent Prayer and Magic bonuses and being easy to replace if lost. They can also be used to telegrab Wine of Zamorak at the Chaos Temple (Asgarnia) without being attacked.

One of only three free-to-play bodies with a magic attack bonus, the Zamorak monk top has 1 less Magic attack and 3 more Prayer bonus when compared to the Black robe , Blue wizard robe , and their ornamental variants .

The Zamorak monk top counts as a Zamorak item in the God Wars Dungeon .
1037:
Bunny ears are an untradeable cosmetic holiday item worn on the head. A pair of bunny ears can be obtained by completing one of the Easter holiday events that occur once per year. This also rewards the player with all other holiday items associated with Easter.

Previously, they were obtainable during the 2013 Rare Drops event (from 14 July to 21 July) as part of a rare item drop.

If destroyed, a replacement can be obtained from Diango in Draynor Village or from the toy box of a costume room. Thessalia in Varrock will also return this item to the player if destroyed.
1038:
Red partyhats are tradeable cosmetic items obtained by completing one of the Christmas holiday events that occur once per year.

Previously, they were obtainable during the 2013 Rare Drops event (from 4 July to 14 July ) as part of a rare item drop .
1040:
Yellow partyhats are tradeable cosmetic items obtained by completing one of the Christmas holiday events that occur once per year.

Previously, they were obtainable during the 2013 Rare Drops event (from 4 July to 14 July ) as part of a rare item drop .
1042:
Blue partyhats are tradeable cosmetic items obtained by completing one of the Christmas holiday events that occur once per year.

It can be sewn with sagacious spectacles to make Partyhat & specs by talking to Patchy , along with 500 coins . Doing so requires the completion of Cabin Fever and a book o' Piracy .

Previously, they were obtainable during the 2013 Rare Drops event (from 4 July to 14 July ) as part of a rare item drop .
1044:
Green partyhats are tradeable cosmetic items obtained by completing one of the Christmas holiday events that occur once per year.

Previously, they were obtainable during the 2013 Rare Drops event (from 4 July to 14 July ) as part of a rare item drop .
1046:
Purple partyhats are tradeable cosmetic items obtained by completing one of the Christmas holiday events that occur once per year.

Previously, they were obtainable during the 2013 Rare Drops event (from 4 July to 14 July ) as part of a rare item drop .
1048:
White partyhats are tradeable cosmetic items obtained by completing one of the Christmas holiday events that occur once per year.

Previously, they were obtainable during the 2013 Rare Drops event (from 4 July to 14 July ) as part of a rare item drop .
1050: Santa hats are tradeable cosmetic items obtained by completing one of the Christmas holiday events that occur once per year.
1052:
The cape of legends is a cape that can be bought for 675 coins from Siegfried Erkle at the Legends Guild Shop of Useful Items on the western portion of the 2 nd floor [ UK ] 3 rd floor [ US ] of the Legends' Guild . They can also purchase it from Perdu for 1,900 coins should they lose it after purchasing it at least once. Like the obsidian cape , it has balanced defence bonuses, but has 2 less in each stat while also being much cheaper.

As the Guild's interior can only be accessed upon completion of the Legends' Quest , this cape can only be owned by those that have completed said quest and became a member of the Guild. There are various NPCs who appear to be wearing the cape or some variation thereof. (See Trivia )

The cape may be mounted in the Quest Hall of a player-owned house in the Guild trophy space. This requires 3 teak planks and grants 300 Construction experience. This has little purpose other than showing guests that the host has completed the Legends' Quest.

This item can be stored in the cape rack of a costume room .
1053:
The Green halloween mask is a tradeable cosmetic item. Green halloween masks can be obtained by completing one of the Halloween holiday events that occur once per year. This also rewards the player with all other holiday items associated with Halloween.

After player decided polls, it was decided that all tradeable rares will be distributed during their corresponding holiday events thus making them seasonal rares and not completely rare, this to prevent them from being worth hundreds of millions of coins again, like in RuneScape 3.

Previously, they were obtainable during the 2013 Rare Drops event (from 17 June to 24 June) as part of a rare item drop.
1055:
The Blue halloween mask is a tradeable cosmetic item. Blue halloween masks can be obtained by completing one of the Halloween holiday events that occur once per year. This also rewards the player with all other holiday items associated with Halloween.

After player decided polls, it was decided that all tradeable rares will be distributed during their corresponding holiday events thus making them seasonal rares and not completely rare, to prevent them from being worth hundreds of millions of coins again, like in RuneScape 3 .

Previously, they were obtainable during the 2013 Rare Drops event (from 17 June to 24 June ) as part of a rare item drop .
1057:
The Red halloween mask is a tradeable cosmetic item. Red halloween masks can be obtained by completing one of the Halloween holiday events that occur once per year. This also rewards the player with all other holiday items associated with Halloween.

After the playerbase was polled, it was decided that all tradeable rares will be distributed during their corresponding holiday events thus making them seasonal rares and not completely rare, this to prevent them from being worth hundreds of millions of coins again, like in RuneScape 3 .

Previously, they were obtainable during the 2013 Rare Drops event (from 17 June to 24 June ) as part of a rare item drop .
1059: Leather gloves are basic gloves worn in the hands slot, offering slight defensive bonuses. Making them requires 1 Crafting, 1 leather, 1 thread, and a needle, yielding 13.8 Crafting experience.
1061: Leather boots is a part of leather armour worn on the foot slot that offer slight bonuses to defence. They can also be found while big net fishing .
1063:
Leather vambraces are leather armour worn on the hands. With no requirements to equip, they are most commonly used by low-level rangers, and often mages (as there is no magic penalty). Overall they are generally a superior alternative to leather gloves with a notable exception of the crush defence, and could be considered the best "gloves" for free-to-play users who lack 40 Ranged to equip green dragonhide vambraces, as well as the best-in-slot mage gloves due to their lack of negative penalties.

Kebbit claws can be used on these vambraces to make spiky vambraces, requiring a Crafting level of 32.
1065:
Green d'hide vambraces is a piece of armour worn by rangers in the hand slot . They require level 40 Ranged to be worn.

This item is a considerable choice for rangers in free-to-play servers, as well as for melee combat because they have higher total defence bonuses than either leather gloves or leather vambraces while having no negative melee attack bonuses. However, they should not be used for magic combat due to the substantial negative magic attack bonus. They offer the highest ranged accuracy bonus among free-to-play hand slot items, although their defensive bonuses are surpassed by the gilded d'hide vambraces . Notable for no Defence requirement, these vambraces are commonly used by the free-to-play combat pures .

The aforementioned negative magic bonus has the effect of making this item popular for splashing in free-to-play servers since it is one of the only ways, along with Gilded d'hide vambraces , to reach the required -64 Magic attack bonus without using the cursed goblin staff .
1067:
Iron platelegs are melee leg armour made of iron. There is no Defence requirement to wear them, as is the same with bronze armour. As such, it is recommended to skip bronze tier items and start out with iron tier items. They have the same defensive stats as an iron plateskirt but weigh more.

They can be made at level 31 Smithing with 3 iron bars, granting 75 experience.
1069:
Steel platelegs are the third weakest platelegs in the game. They have the same bonuses and penalties as a steel plateskirt but weigh more. A player with 46 Smithing can make them by using three steel bars on an anvil while carrying a hammer, granting 112.5 Smithing experience. They can also be bought from Louie's Armoured Legs Bazaar. They require 5 Defence to wear.

As they spawn in the Wilderness at the Ruins north of the Graveyard of Shadows, they are one of the most easily accessible and most popular money making methods for new Ironman accounts when being sold to Louie's Armoured Legs Bazaar starting at 650 each at base stock of 2, reducing by 10 per extra set.

Their respawn rate in the Wilderness is between 10 and 20 minutes, depending on the number of players in a world.

This item can be stored in the armour case of a costume room, as part of the Ardougne knight armour set. Ultimate Ironmen will be unable to retrieve individual pieces until the full set is stored.
1071: Mithril platelegs are the third best free-to-play platelegs. They require level 20 Defence to equip. A player with 66 Smithing can make it by using three mithril bars on an anvil while carrying a hammer, granting 150 Smithing experience. Mithril platelegs offer similar stats to a mithril plateskirt but weigh more.
1073:
Adamant platelegs are platelegs made of Adamant and, as such, require a Defence level of 30 to wear. These platelegs have the same stats as the Adamant plateskirt, but are 1kg heavier.

Adamant platelegs can be smithed using 3 adamant bars at level 86 Smithing, granting 187.5 experience.
1075:
Bronze platelegs are leg armour made of bronze , requiring level 1 Defence to wear (as is the same with other bronze and iron items ). They share the same defensive stats as a bronze plateskirt but weigh more. They can be made at level 16 Smithing by using a hammer and 3 bronze bars at an anvil.

These can be bought from Louie's Armoured Legs Bazaar in Al Kharid .
1077:
Black platelegs have the same bonuses as the black plateskirt but weigh more. They require level 10 Defence to wear. They can be bought from Louie's Armoured Legs Bazaar in Al Kharid or Valaine's Shop of Champions in the Champions' Guild. Like all other black armour, it cannot be made with the Smithing skill.

Black platelegs are used in King's Ransom and Heroes' Quest if you're part of the Black Arm Gang.

Black platelegs (t) and (g) can both be obtained as a reward from easy Treasure Trails. They provide no extra bonuses than regular black platelegs other than being aesthetically improved.
1079:
Rune platelegs are platelegs made of runite. They require level 40 Defence to wear. Rune platelegs are identical in function to the rune plateskirt, but is 1kg heavier. Players may receive these from the crystal chest if they are a body type A character.

They can be created with the Smithing skill by using 3 runite bars and a hammer on an anvil; this requires level 99 Smithing and yields 225 Smithing experience.

Along with the rune plateskirt and two-handed sword, this is the best bar-per-alch item in the game. If smithing for money, rune platelegs, plateskirt and two-handed sword will give the best value for each bar.

They can also be put into the nest found on top of the Aldarin windmill in Varlamore in order to get a runite bar.
1081:
The iron plateskirt is a plateskirt made from iron. It has the same stats as iron platelegs but weighs less.

They can be made at level 31 Smithing with 3 iron bars, granting 75 experience.
1083: The Steel plateskirt is a plateskirt made from steel, requiring level 5 Defence to wear. It can be made at level 46 Smithing by using 3 Steel bars on an anvil with a hammer in the inventory. It has identical stats to the steel platelegs, with the notable exception that it weighs less.
1085: Mithril plateskirts give the fifth best stat bonuses of all plateskirts. This piece of armour can be made with Level 66 Smithing by using 3 mithril bars on an anvil, therefore granting the player with 150 smithing experience. At least 20 Defence is required to wear it. Mithril plateskirts have similar stats to mithril platelegs but weigh less.
1087: A bronze plateskirt is the weakest plateskirt in Old School RuneScape . It has identical stat bonuses to the bronze platelegs but weighs less. A player with 16 Smithing can make it by using three bronze bars on an anvil while carrying a hammer , granting 37.5 smithing experience . They can be bought from Ranael's Super Skirt Store in Al Kharid .
1089:
The black plateskirt has the same stats as black platelegs but weighs less. The black plateskirt requires 10 Defence to wear. One can be bought from Ranael's Super Skirt Store in Al Kharid.

As with all black and white equipment, the black plateskirt cannot be made from raw materials using the Smithing skill.
1091:
The Adamant plateskirt is a plateskirt made out of adamant . At least 30 Defence is required to wear it. The plateskirt has the same stats as the Adamant platelegs , but are 1kg lighter.

They can be made at level 86 Smithing using 3 adamantite bars , which grants 187.5 experience.
1093:
The rune plateskirt is a plateskirt made out of runite. It requires level 40 Defence to wear. The rune plateskirt is identical in function to rune platelegs, but is 1 kg lighter.

It can be created with the Smithing skill by using 3 runite bars and a hammer on an anvil; this requires level 99 Smithing and yields 225 Smithing experience.

Characters may receive these from the crystal chest.

Along with the rune 2h sword and platelegs, this is the best bar-per-alch item in the game. If smithing for money, rune 2h sword, platelegs, and plateskirt will give the best value for each bar.
1095: Leather chaps is a part of leather armour that is worn in the legs slot , most commonly by low-level rangers . Low-levelled player mages also often wear these chaps, since they give a slight defence bonuses without a magic attack penalty.
1097: Studded chaps are part of studded leather armour set and they require 20 Ranged to equip.
1099: Green d'hide chaps , short for green dragonhide chaps, is a type of legwear designed for rangers . They are part of the green dragonhide armour set, and can be worn at level 40 Ranged . They offer the best ranged accuracy bonus out of all free-to-play leg armours, although their defensive bonuses are surpassed by the gilded d'hide chaps . Notable for no Defence requirement, this piece of armour is commonly used by the free-to-play combat pures .
1101:
The iron chainbody is the second weakest chainbody, and can be worn by a player with 1 Defence. A player with 26 Smithing can make the chainbody by using three iron bars on an anvil while carrying a hammer, granting 75 Smithing experience.

An iron chainbody is required for the Black Knights' Fortress, King's Ransom, and While Guthix Sleeps quests.
1103: The bronze chainbody is a chainbody that can be made at an anvil with 3 bronze bars and a hammer with a Smithing level of 11, granting 37.5 Smithing experience. Since it requires a Defence level of 1 to wear, it can be worn by any player. It is one of the weakest armour chest pieces in the game and is seldom worn. The bronze chainbody can be obtained through a spawn located in the Dwarven Mine.
1105:
The Steel chainbody is the third weakest chainbody, and it can be worn by a player with level 5 Defence .

A player with level 41 Smithing can forge the steel chainbody by using three steel bars on an anvil with a hammer in their inventory, granting 112.5 Smithing experience . It can also be bought from Wayne's Chains in Falador , or Horvik's Armour Shop in Varrock .
1107:
The black chainbody is stronger than the steel chainbody , and can be worn by players with 10 Defence . Players can purchase this item at the Keldagrim and Falador Chainmail shops . This item cannot be made using the Smithing skill, and has the same bonuses as a white chainbody , except it lacks a prayer bonus .

Sold at Wayne's Chains shop in southern Falador for 1,440 coins, and at Saro 's armour shop in Keldagrim for 1,872 coins.

As with all black and white equipment , the black chainbody cannot be made from raw materials using the Smithing skill.
1109:
The Mithril chainbody is a chainbody made out of mithril. As with all mithril armour, it requires 20 Defence to wear.

Like all chainbodies, it provides better Crush defence than a platebody made of the same material, at the cost of lower Stab and Slash defence.

The Mithril chainbody can be made with level 61 Smithing using 3 mithril bars, and grants 150 Smithing experience.
1111: Adamant chainbody is piece of armour made from adamantite . A player can create an adamant chainbody by using an adamantite bar on an anvil while a hammer and 3 adamantite bars are in the player's inventory. A Smithing level of 81 is required to make an adamant chainbody and doing so will grant the player 187.5 Smithing experience. Level 30 Defence is required to wear an adamant chainbody. It can also be bought from Wayne's Chains in south Falador . One adamant chainbody is required for Song of the Elves .
1113:
A rune chainbody is a chainbody made of runite. To wear this chainbody, a player needs at least level 40 Defence. This piece of body armour is less resistant than the rune platebody in all stats except crush and magic and wearing it does not require completion of Dragon Slayer I. For this reason it is commonly worn by players who have not finished said quest or who are fighting against monsters that use crush attacks. It is also useful for rangers since it has higher defence bonuses than the green d'hide body and it does not penalise ranged attack.

A player with 96 Smithing can make the chainbody by using three runite bars on an anvil, granting 225 Smithing experience. It can also be bought at Scavvo's Rune Store in the Champions' Guild, or for members, at Seddu's Adventurer's Store in Nardah.
1115:
The iron platebody is an armour used in melee with stat bonuses between bronze and steel. It has no Defence requirement to equip, which makes it the best platebody for players just starting out. It also provides greater protection than an iron chainbody. Like all platebodies, however, it gives a crippling negative bonus to the user's Ranged and Magic stats.

If playing as an Ironman, an ironman platebody with equivalent stats can be acquired by talking to the Ironman tutor in Lumbridge.

Players with level 33 Smithing can make one by using 5 iron bars on an anvil while carrying a hammer, granting 125 experience. Alternatively, they can be bought from Horvik's Smithy or Zenesha's Plate Mail Body Shop.
1117:
The bronze platebody is an armour used in melee and the weakest of all platebodies. It has no Defence requirement to equip and provides greater protection than a bronze chainbody. Like all platebodies, however, it gives a crippling negative bonus to the user's Ranged and Magic stats.

Players with level 18 Smithing can make one by using 5 bronze bars on an anvil while carrying a hammer, granting 62.5 experience. Alternatively, they can be bought from Horvik's Smithy or Zenesha's Plate Mail Body Shop.
1119:
The steel platebody is an armour used in melee with stat bonuses between iron and mithril (not including the black and white platebodies). It requires 5 Defence to equip and provides greater protection than a steel chainbody. Like all platebodies, however, it gives a crippling negative bonus to the user's Ranged and Magic stats.

Players with level 48 Smithing can make one by using 5 steel bars on an anvil while carrying a hammer, granting 187.5 experience. Alternatively, they can be bought from Horvik's Smithy, Zenesha's Plate Mail Body Shop, or in Varlamore.
1121:
The mithril platebody is an armour used in melee with stat bonuses between steel and adamant (not including the black and white platebodies). It requires 20 Defence to equip and provides greater protection than a mithril chainbody . Like all platebodies , however, it gives a crippling negative bonus to the user's Ranged and Magic stats.

Players with level 68 Smithing can make one by using 5 mithril bars on an anvil while carrying a hammer , granting 250 Smithing experience . Alternatively, they can be bought from a handful of armour shops.

Smithing a mithril platebody is a requirement for the Ardougne and Desert Achievement Diaries .
1123:
The adamant platebody is an armour used in melee with stat bonuses between mithril and rune. It requires 30 Defence to equip and provides greater protection than an adamant chainbody. Like all platebodies, however, it gives a crippling negative bonus to the user's Ranged and Magic stats.

Players with level 88 Smithing can make one by using 5 adamantite bars on an anvil while carrying a hammer, granting 312.5 experience.

Smithing an adamant platebody is a requirement for the elite Lumbridge & Draynor Diary.
1125:
The black platebody is an armour used in melee with the same stat bonuses as a white platebody , excluding the Prayer bonus. It requires 10 Defence to equip and provides greater protection than a black chainbody . Like all platebodies , however, it gives a crippling negative bonus to the user's Ranged and Magic stats.

It cannot be made using the Smithing skill , though it's easily obtainable as it can be bought from Horvik , Zenesha or another player.

A black platebody is used in King's Ransom and Heroes' Quest if the player joins the Black Arm Gang .
1127:
The rune platebody is an armour used in melee and the strongest of all free-to-play platebodies . It requires 40 Defence and completion of the quest Dragon Slayer I to equip. It also provides greater protection than a rune chainbody , with the exception of a slightly lower crush defence. Like all platebodies, however, it gives a crippling negative bonus to the user's Ranged and Magic stats.

Players with level 99 Smithing can make one by using 5 runite bars on an anvil while carrying a hammer , granting 375 experience .
1129: Leather body is a part of leather armour and is the weakest ranged torso in the game. It requires 1 Ranged to equip. By using steel studs on a leather body, members can turn them into a studded body at level 41 Crafting .
1131: The hardleather body is low-level ranged armour . It may be equipped in the torso slot by players with 1 Ranged and 10 Defence . It provides better protection from melee , Magic , and Ranged attacks than the leather body and grants a modest boost to one's Ranged accuracy.
1133: A studded body is a part of studded leather armour set and it requires 20 Ranged and Defence to equip.
1135:
The green d'hide body is a part of the green dragonhide armour set. In order to wear the body, a player must first have completed the Dragon Slayer I quest and have level 40 Ranged and Defence . It offers the best ranged accuracy bonus among all free-to-play body armours, although its defensive bonuses are surpassed by the gilded d'hide body .

Although players must complete Dragon Slayer I in order to wear a green d'hide body, completion of this quest is not required to equip blue , red , and black d'hide bodies.
1137: The iron med helm is the second weakest medium helmet. A player with 18 Smithing can make the helmet by using one iron bar on an anvil while carrying a hammer , granting 25 Smithing experience .
1139:
The bronze med helm is the weakest medium helmet. It can be equipped to give a player small Defence bonuses in combat. Players can make a bronze med helm with a Smithing level of 3 by using one bronze bar on an anvil with a hammer in their inventory, giving the player 12.5 Smithing experience. Players can purchase this medium helmet from Peksa's Helmet Shop in the Barbarian Village or in the Warrior Guild Armoury from Anton.

A bronze med helm is required for the Black Knights' Fortress, King's Ransom, and While Guthix Sleeps quests. A bronze med helm spawn exists in the south-eastern corner of Draynor Manor. Falador and Edgeville town guards wear these helms as part of their uniform; as well the Black Knights' Fortress' guards.
1141: A steel med helm is the third-weakest medium helmet. A player with 33 Smithing can make this helmet by using one steel bar on an anvil while carrying a hammer, granting 37.5 Smithing experience. It requires 5 Defence to equip.
1143: The mithril med helm is a medium helmet made of mithril . This helm requires 20 Defence to wear. It provides more protection than its bronze , iron and steel counterparts. It can be made at level 53 Smithing using a mithril bar .
1145:
The adamant med helm is a medium helmet made of adamantite. This helm requires 30 Defence to wear. It provides more protection than its mithril counterpart. It can be made at level 73 Smithing using an adamantite bar, granting 62.5 experience.

Though the helmet provides a smaller Defence bonus than that of an adamant full helm, it has a lower penalty to Magic and Ranged attack. This means it is potentially more useful than the full helm to players who are training the Magic skill.
1147: The rune med helm is a medium helmet made out of rune, requiring a Defence level of 40 to wear. A Smithing level of 88 is required to smith one from a runite bar , granting 75 experience . It can also be obtained as a drop from a variety of monsters.
1149:
The dragon med helm is a piece of armour which requires 60 Defence to equip. It was the first piece of dragon armour to be released.

Zulrah , revenants , Sarachnis and some dragons can drop the dragon med helm. Any monster that has access to the standard rare drop table can also drop the dragon med helm. It can also be found in the Barrows chest as a separate item with 1012 rewards potential and all brothers killed. [ 1 ]

Offering slightly more defensive power than the helm of Neitiznot , many players favour other helmets that provide offensive bonuses, or penalise magic attack bonus less. The dragon med helm is often considered less prestigious than other helmets due to its lack of any quest requirements.

As with most Dragon equipment , players cannot make this item using the Smithing skill .
1151: A black med helm is the sixth-strongest med helm . It requires a Defence level of 10 to wear, and can be purchased from Seddu's Adventurers' Store in Nardah for 576 coins. It can be received as an uncommon drop from dark warriors , and a common drop from mutated bloodvelds . It can also be obtained through shade burning , and is quite commonly found at the Digsite .
1153:
The Iron full helm is a full helm made of iron. It is the second weakest full helmet available. While it grants greater defensive stats than its medium helmet counterpart, it has worse magic and ranged attack stats. There are no Defence requirements for wearing this helmet.

Players with level 22 Smithing can create an iron full helm by using two iron bars on an anvil while having a hammer in their inventory. Doing so will grant the player 50 Smithing experience.
1155:
The bronze full helmet is the weakest full helmet in Old School RuneScape . The bronze full helmet grants greater defensive bonuses than its medium helmet counterpart , though at a cost of offensive bonuses for Ranged and Magic . There are no Defence requirements for wearing this helmet.

To create a bronze full helmet the player needs at least 7 Smithing, a hammer and 2 bronze bars . To make a helmet use one of the bars on an anvil with the hammer in the inventory. This grants 25 Smithing experience.
1157:
The steel full helm is the third weakest full helm . The steel full helm grants greater defensive bonuses than its medium helmet counterpart, though at a cost of offensive bonuses for Ranged and Magic . Wearing this helmet requires at least 5 Defence .

To create a steel full helmet you need at least 37 Smithing , a hammer , and two steel bars . Then use one of the bars on an anvil with the hammer in your inventory. This will grant 75 Smithing experience.

Members with 16+ Construction can use a steel full helmet on a pluming stand to make a steel heraldic helm , a steel full helm designed in the colours of the player's family crest. Family crests are obtained from Sir Renitee in Falador Castle .
1159: The mithril full helm is the fourth best full helmet. It requires 20 Defence to equip. It offers better defensive stats than its med helm counterpart, at the cost of having lower magic and ranged attack, and greater weight. One can be made by a player with level 57 Smithing at any anvil with a hammer and 2 mithril bars.
1161: An adamant full helm is a full helmet made out of adamant . It can be worn with at least level 30 in Defence and can be smithed with at least level 77 Smithing using 2 adamantite bars (this grants 125 Smithing experience ). These helms are stronger than mithril full helms but weaker than rune full helms .
1163: The rune full helm is the best full helmet available to free-to-play players (excluding Rune god armour full helmets, which provide an additional +1 Prayer bonus). Equipping this helmet requires 40 Defence . It can be made at 92 Smithing with two runite bars , granting 150 Smithing experience .
1165:
The black full helm is a full helmet that requires 10 Defence to equip. As with all black armour, it cannot be made using the Smithing skill. It can be bought at Valaine's Shop of Champions in the Champions' Guild for 1,372 coins. It can also be obtained as a Treasure Trails reward.

A black full helm is used in King's Ransom and, if you're part of the Black Arm Gang, Heroes' Quest.
1167: Leather cowls are leather armour worn on the head, most commonly by low-levelled rangers.
1169:
A coif is an improved cowl that requires 20 Ranged to equip. Coifs are the best ranged headgear available for free to play. It can be made by members at level 38 Crafting with one leather (soft), a needle, and thread.

Making a coif in the Lumbridge cow field is a requirement for the medium Lumbridge & Draynor Diary.
1171:
A wooden shield is the weakest shield available, but one of a small group with no penalties to any form of combat. It is round in shape, and while all warriors should quickly progress to something better (such as an iron kiteshield , which can also be equipped at 1 Defence), it is better than nothing for magic users, since it has no penalties. It can be purchased from Cassie's Shield Shop in Falador , found north of the Varrock city wall as a respawn, and one is given free on Tutorial Island .

Its combat stats are equal to the training shield but worse than the anti-dragon shield . The training shield also weighs approximately twice as much.

There is a gold-trimmed version available as an easy clue scroll reward.
1173: The Bronze sq shield is the lowest level defence square shield in Old School RuneScape . It can be equipped to give a player better defence bonuses in combat. Its recommended use is in melee combat . Players can make a bronze square shield with 2 bronze bars at level 8 Smithing , granting 25 Smithing experience . It can also be bought from Cassie's Shield Shop in Falador .
1175: An Iron square shield is the second weakest square shield. A player with 23 Smithing can make the shield by using two iron bars on an anvil while carrying a hammer, granting 50 experience. This shield can also be bought at Cassie's Shield Shop in northern Falador.
1177: A steel sq shield is the third weakest square shield . It requires 5 Defence to equip. A player with 38 Smithing can make the shield by using two steel bars on an anvil while carrying a hammer , granting 75 experience .
1179: The black square shield (abbreviated in-game as black sq shield) is a square shield made of black metal requiring 10 Defence to equip. Its defensive bonuses are slightly better than those of a steel kiteshield , but slightly inferior to those of a black kiteshield . Like all other black armour , it cannot be made with the Smithing skill .
1181:
A mithril square shield is the fourth strongest square shield. Players with level 58 Smithing can make the shield by using two mithril bars on an anvil while carrying a hammer, granting 100 Smithing experience.

This shield can be bought from Raum Urda-Stein on Jatizso. This shield provides less defence than the mithril kiteshield, but is much lighter. As with all pieces of mithril armour, it requires 20 Defence to wield.
1183: Adamant square shields are the third-strongest square shields , requiring 30 Defence to wield. A player with level 78 Smithing can make the shield by using two adamant bars on an anvil while carrying a hammer , granting 125 Smithing experience .
1185:
The rune square shield is the second strongest square shield in Old School RuneScape , requiring a Defence level of 40 to wield. It is obtainable via the rare drop table . A player with level 93 Smithing can make the shield by using two rune bars on an anvil while carrying a hammer , granting 150 experience . Rune square shields can also be obtained from Magpie impling jars as well as a common drop from a Greater Nechryael .

Any monster that has access to the rare drop table can also drop the rune square shield.
1187:
The dragon sq shield is the strongest square shield in Old School RuneScape . It requires 60 Defence to wield, along with completion of Legends' Quest . The dragon square shield is created by combining the shield left half , a mega-rare drop from the rare drop table , and the shield right half , which must be purchased for 750,000 coins from Siegfried Erkle in the Legends' Guild or Erdan in the Myths' Guild . The two shield halves are combined at any anvil with a hammer in the inventory to produce the dragon square shield, a process that requires level 60 Smithing and grants 75 experience .

Smithing this shield in West Ardougne is a task required in the hard set of the Ardougne Diary .

A dragon sq shield can be combined with a dragon sq shield ornament kit to make a gold-trimmed dragon sq shield (g) . This cosmetic enhancement won't change the stats in any way.

After the completion of Dragon Slayer II , and with level 75 Smithing, the shield may be combined with a dragon metal shard and a dragon metal slice to create a dragon kiteshield .

The dragon sq shield can easily be confused with the anti-dragon shield , which protects against dragonfire . The dragon sq shield does not protect against dragonfire.
1189: The Bronze kiteshield is the weakest smithable kiteshield, requiring 1 Defence to wield. A player with 12 Smithing can make the shield by using 3 bronze bars on an anvil while carrying a hammer, granting 37.5 Smithing experience. It can also be bought from Cassie's Shield Shop in Falador.
1191:
The Iron kiteshield is the second-weakest smithable kiteshield , requiring 1 Defence to wield. A player with 27 Smithing can make the shield by using three iron bars on an anvil while carrying a hammer , granting 75 Smithing experience . It cannot be bought from Cassie's Shield Shop for ironmen , as there is no stock available.

The iron kiteshield yields the highest melee defence bonuses for any shield slot item at 1 Defence .
1193: The steel kiteshield is the fourth-best smithable kiteshield , requiring 5 Defence to wield. A player with 42 Smithing can make the shield by using three steel bars on an anvil while carrying a hammer , granting 112.5 Smithing experience .
1195:
The black kiteshield is a Black Knight kiteshield that requires 10 Defence to wield. The black kiteshield has the same defensive bonuses as a white kiteshield , but without the +1 prayer bonus.

The black kiteshield can be found in trimmed and heraldic forms from Treasure Trails .

As with all black items , it can not be made with the Smithing skill.
1197: The mithril kiteshield is the third best smithable kiteshield , requiring 20 Defence to wield. A player with 62 Smithing can make the shield by using three mithril bars on an anvil while carrying a hammer , granting 150 Smithing experience .
1199: The Adamant kiteshield is the second-best smithable kiteshield , requiring 30 Defence to wield. A player with 82 Smithing can make the shield by using three adamantite bars on an anvil while carrying a hammer , granting 187.5 Smithing experience .
1201:
The Rune kiteshield is the second best smithable kiteshield , surpassed only by the Dragon kiteshield . The rune kiteshield requires 40 Defence to wield. A player with 97 Smithing can make the shield by using three runite bars and a hammer on an anvil , granting 225 Smithing experience .

The rune kiteshield is often used as a tank shield by low-risk and void rangers; despite the negative ranged attack bonus, it is much cheaper, and provides a substantial melee defence bonus, which the Odium ward lacks.

Players with at least level 43 Crafting are also able to paint the rune kiteshield at a player-owned house to create an untradeable heraldic shield , provided that they have visited Sir Renitee to obtain a crest in advance. A painted rune kiteshield will provide protection in the God Wars Dungeon . It will also turn bandits hostile, if painted in the colours of Saradomin or Zamorak .

Any monster that has access to the rare drop table can also drop the rune kiteshield.
1203:
The iron dagger is a dagger stronger than the bronze dagger. Players can make an iron dagger with the Smithing skill at level 15 using 1 iron bar, giving the player 25 Smithing experience. Members can poison this weapon, giving them an advantage in combat. Players can purchase this dagger from the Varrock Swordshop. There are also several spawn points throughout the map. As with most daggers, it can be poisoned.

Players with at least level 32 Thieving can get an iron dagger (p) by pickpocketing Rogues. Rogues are located south-west of the deep Wilderness Mage Arena.

It is superior in accuracy to the bronze sword, but inferior in strength. As it is a common and inexpensive item, an iron dagger is more likely to be obtained by new players than other iron weaponry. It is often used by low level ironman accounts to kill higher-leveled enemies with poison.
1205: The bronze dagger is the most basic dagger in Old School RuneScape , and can be made at an anvil using the Smithing skill. This requires one bronze bar and a hammer , and yields 12.5 Smithing experience . There are no level requirements to create or wield a bronze dagger; like many melee weapons, it can be poisoned .
1207:
The steel dagger is the third-weakest dagger , requiring level 5 Attack to wield. They can be bought from shops and obtained drops from monsters, and can also be smithed from a steel bar at level 30 Smithing . As with most daggers, steel daggers can be poisoned .

Players must bring Veliaf a steel dagger during In Search of the Myreque .
1209: The mithril dagger is a dagger made out of mithril. Mithril daggers can be smithed from a single mithril bar at level 50 Smithing. Each mithril dagger created grants 50 experience. Mithril daggers are the fifth strongest daggers, the next strongest being the adamant dagger. Like all mithril weapons, mithril daggers require 20 Attack to wield. As with most daggers, this weapon can be poisoned. Players can purchase this dagger from the Varrock Swordshop.
1211: The adamant dagger is a dagger made of adamantite . It can be created by using one Adamant bar and a hammer on an anvil at level 70 Smithing , granting 62.5 Smithing experience . As with most daggers , it can be poisoned .
1213: The rune dagger is a dagger made from rune . Rune daggers can be made from a single rune bar at level 85 Smithing . Each rune dagger created grants 75 experience. Rune daggers are the third-strongest daggers, behind the dragon dagger and the abyssal dagger . Like most rune weapons they require 40 Attack to wield. As with most daggers, this weapon can be poisoned .
1215:
The dragon dagger is the second-strongest dagger available in Old School RuneScape , behind the abyssal dagger . It can be wielded by players with at least 60 Attack after completion of the Lost City quest. As with most daggers, it can be poisoned .

If casting either of the alchemy spells on a dragon dagger, use a cleaning cloth on poisoned versions to make more profit, as the value of the unpoisoned dagger is higher than any of the poisoned versions: 18,000 coins compared to 14,400 coins .

As with most dragon equipment , the dragon dagger cannot be made from raw materials using the Smithing skill.
1217:
The black dagger is a dagger slightly more accurate than the steel dagger . Like most daggers it can be poisoned , giving an advantage in combat . Like all black weapons , wielding it requires an Attack level of 10.

As with all black and white equipment , the black dagger cannot be made from raw materials using the Smithing skill.
1219:
The iron dagger is a dagger stronger than the bronze dagger. Players can make an iron dagger with the Smithing skill at level 15 using 1 iron bar, giving the player 25 Smithing experience. As with most daggers, this weapon can be poisoned .
