1233:
The black dagger is a dagger slightly more accurate than the steel dagger . Like most daggers it can be poisoned , giving an advantage in combat . Like all black weapons , wielding it requires an Attack level of 10.

As with all black and white equipment , the black dagger cannot be made from raw materials using the Smithing skill.
1235:
The Poisoned dagger is an unobtainable item that was added during the RuneScape 2 beta. It uses the default untextured model for poisoned daggers. Its purpose is unknown; however, it may have been created in order to test poisoned daggers in RuneScape 2, or as part of an interface. Its stats are identical to the black dagger.

With the release of Weapon poison(+) and Weapon poison(++), extra strong and super strong poison variants of the dagger were added too.

The item briefly appeared in the search interface of the trading post. Aside from this, it has never been obtainable in Old School RuneScape.
1237:
The bronze spear is a two-handed melee weapon made from bronze and is the weakest spear in Old School RuneScape . Spears are members -only weapons. Bronze spears can also be used to create a scarecrow .

Bronze spears can be easily obtained from low-level monsters such as goblins . There is a bronze spear spawn in the Haunted Mine on the second level near other assorted bronze equipment. A (kp) version can be bought from Tamayu after finishing the Tai Bwo Wannai Trio quest. Using the Smithing skill, players can create bronze spears. However, players must have begun Barbarian Smithing training to be able to smith these spears. It can also be found by digging at Level 3 digging spots at the Digsite , with a specimen brush , specimen jar and trowel in the inventory, or bought from the Fortis Blacksmith .

Like most spears, the bronze spear can be poisoned .
1239: The iron spear is a members-only two-handed melee weapon. An iron spear can be obtained by buying one from the Fortis Blacksmith, buying one from another player, or receiving it as a monster drop. The only way it can be created using the Smithing skill is through Barbarian Training after completing Tai Bwo Wannai Trio. It can be poisoned.
1241: The steel spear is a two-handed melee weapon that requires 5 Attack to wield. It can be bought from the Mount Karuulm Weapon Shop or Fortis Blacksmith , or obtained as a drop from monsters. Players who have started learning Barbarian Smithing and have level 35 Smithing may produce a spear at a Barbarian anvil from one steel bar and one willow log , receiving 75 Smithing experience . Smithing spears at the Barbarian anvil requires completion of Tai Bwo Wannai Trio . Like most spears , it can be poisoned .
1243: The mithril spear is a two-handed melee weapon made from mithril requiring 20 Attack to wield. Mithril spears are a members-only weapon. It can be bought from the Mount Karuulm Weapon Shop or Fortis Blacksmith, or obtained as a drop from monsters. Using the Smithing skill, players can create mithril spears on one of the barbarian anvils in either Otto's Grotto or Barbarian Village. However, players must have begun Barbarian Smithing training to be able to smith these spears. Like most spears, the mithril spear can be poisoned.
1245: The adamant spear is a two-handed members '-only melee weapon requiring 30 Attack to wield. It can be bought from the Mount Karuulm Weapon Shop or Fortis Blacksmith , or obtained as a drop from monsters. Using the Smithing skill, players can create adamant spears with level 75 Smithing This requires 1 adamantite bar and 1 yew log . However, players must have begun Barbarian Smithing training to be able to smith these spears. Like most spears, the adamant spear can be poisoned . Smithing an adamant spear at the anvil at Otto's Grotto is a requirement for the Kandarin Hard Diary .
1247:
The rune spear is a two-handed melee weapon requiring 40 Attack to wield. Unlike most other rune equipment , rune spears are members -only. Rune spears can be created at a barbarian anvil with 90 Smithing , requiring one runite bar and one magic log , as well as partial completion of the Barbarian Training miniquest . Like most spears, the rune spear can be poisoned .

A rune spear is also a requirement for a hard clue scroll . Ironmen can acquire it by completing Tai Bwo Wannai Trio for a rune spear (kp) then using a cleaning cloth on it, or by buying it from Mount Karuulm Weapon Shop .

This item is a rare drop from the rare drop table . Wearing a ring of wealth will increase the chances of receiving one from the rare drop table.
1249:
The dragon spear is a two-handed melee weapon that requires level 60 Attack to wield. It does not require the completion of a quest to equip. Like most spears, it can be poisoned.

The spear is a rare drop from both the rare and gem drop tables. On the gem drop table, the spear will only drop if the Legends' Quest has been completed, otherwise a talisman will be dropped in its place. However, the rare drop table does not require the quest's completion in order to be able to receive it as a drop. Wearing a ring of wealth will increase the chances of receiving one from both tables.

Goraks fought in the Gorak Plane while wearing a ring of wealth are more likely to drop the dragon spear than any other monster, with a drop rate of 1 in 325. Brutal black dragons are also frequent droppers of dragon spears, dropping it directly with a drop rate of 1 in 512 (while also having access to the rare drop table so they drop it slightly more common than this overall).

The spear is primarily used for player killing scenarios; outside of this, it is sought after by ironmen, as two elite clue steps require it.

As with most dragon equipment, the dragon spear cannot be made from raw materials using the Smithing skill.
1251:
The bronze spear is a two-handed melee weapon made from bronze and is the weakest spear in Old School RuneScape . Spears are members -only weapons. Bronze spears can also be used to create a scarecrow .

Bronze spears can be easily obtained from low-level monsters such as goblins . There is a bronze spear spawn in the Haunted Mine on the second level near other assorted bronze equipment. A (kp) version can be bought from Tamayu after finishing the Tai Bwo Wannai Trio quest. Using the Smithing skill, players can create bronze spears. However, players must have begun Barbarian Smithing training to be able to smith these spears. It can also be found by digging at Level 3 digging spots at the Digsite , with a specimen brush , specimen jar and trowel in the inventory, or bought from the Fortis Blacksmith .

Like most spears, the bronze spear can be poisoned .
1253: The iron spear is a members-only two-handed melee weapon. An iron spear can be obtained by buying one from the Fortis Blacksmith, buying one from another player, or receiving it as a monster drop. The only way it can be created using the Smithing skill is through Barbarian Training after completing Tai Bwo Wannai Trio. It can be poisoned.
1255: The steel spear is a two-handed melee weapon that requires 5 Attack to wield. It can be bought from the Mount Karuulm Weapon Shop or Fortis Blacksmith , or obtained as a drop from monsters. Players who have started learning Barbarian Smithing and have level 35 Smithing may produce a spear at a Barbarian anvil from one steel bar and one willow log , receiving 75 Smithing experience . Smithing spears at the Barbarian anvil requires completion of Tai Bwo Wannai Trio . Like most spears , it can be poisoned .
1257: The mithril spear is a two-handed melee weapon made from mithril requiring 20 Attack to wield. Mithril spears are a members-only weapon. It can be bought from the Mount Karuulm Weapon Shop or Fortis Blacksmith, or obtained as a drop from monsters. Using the Smithing skill, players can create mithril spears on one of the barbarian anvils in either Otto's Grotto or Barbarian Village. However, players must have begun Barbarian Smithing training to be able to smith these spears. Like most spears, the mithril spear can be poisoned.
1259: The adamant spear is a two-handed members '-only melee weapon requiring 30 Attack to wield. It can be bought from the Mount Karuulm Weapon Shop or Fortis Blacksmith , or obtained as a drop from monsters. Using the Smithing skill, players can create adamant spears with level 75 Smithing This requires 1 adamantite bar and 1 yew log . However, players must have begun Barbarian Smithing training to be able to smith these spears. Like most spears, the adamant spear can be poisoned . Smithing an adamant spear at the anvil at Otto's Grotto is a requirement for the Kandarin Hard Diary .
1261:
The rune spear is a two-handed melee weapon requiring 40 Attack to wield. Unlike most other rune equipment , rune spears are members -only. Rune spears can be created at a barbarian anvil with 90 Smithing , requiring one runite bar and one magic log , as well as partial completion of the Barbarian Training miniquest . Like most spears, the rune spear can be poisoned .

A rune spear is also a requirement for a hard clue scroll . Ironmen can acquire it by completing Tai Bwo Wannai Trio for a rune spear (kp) then using a cleaning cloth on it, or by buying it from Mount Karuulm Weapon Shop .

This item is a rare drop from the rare drop table . Wearing a ring of wealth will increase the chances of receiving one from the rare drop table.
1263:
The dragon spear is a two-handed melee weapon that requires level 60 Attack to wield. It does not require the completion of a quest to equip. Like most spears, it can be poisoned.

The spear is a rare drop from both the rare and gem drop tables. On the gem drop table, the spear will only drop if the Legends' Quest has been completed, otherwise a talisman will be dropped in its place. However, the rare drop table does not require the quest's completion in order to be able to receive it as a drop. Wearing a ring of wealth will increase the chances of receiving one from both tables.

Goraks fought in the Gorak Plane while wearing a ring of wealth are more likely to drop the dragon spear than any other monster, with a drop rate of 1 in 325. Brutal black dragons are also frequent droppers of dragon spears, dropping it directly with a drop rate of 1 in 512 (while also having access to the rare drop table so they drop it slightly more common than this overall).

The spear is primarily used for player killing scenarios; outside of this, it is sought after by ironmen, as two elite clue steps require it.

As with most dragon equipment, the dragon spear cannot be made from raw materials using the Smithing skill.
1265:
A bronze pickaxe is a pickaxe made of bronze. It is given to players during the Mining part of Tutorial Island and is part of the starting gear given to the player when leaving Tutorial Island. It mines on an 8-tick cycle, making it the slowest pickaxe.

Bronze pickaxes spawn in several locations in Misthalin and Asgarnia, and they can also be bought from various shops. It can also be obtained for free from Monlum, the mining tutor, in the East Lumbridge Swamp mine. A bronze pickaxe is also given to the player by Doric when starting Doric's Quest.
1267:
The iron pickaxe is a pickaxe that mines on a 7- tick cycle, 1-tick faster than the bronze pickaxe . It can be used in combat or to mine rocks.

As with all pickaxes, players cannot smith an iron pickaxe.
1269:
The steel pickaxe is a pickaxe that mines on a 6-tick cycle, 1-tick faster than the iron pickaxe. It can be used in combat or in mining to mine rocks. The steel pickaxe requires 6 Mining to use, and 5 Attack to equip. Players lacking 5 Attack can still use it for mining.

Like all pickaxes, a steel pickaxe cannot be made with the Smithing skill.
1271:
The adamant pickaxe is a pickaxe that is stronger than the mithril pickaxe, but weaker than the rune pickaxe. It requires an Attack level of 30 to wield, and a Mining level of 31 to mine with.

The adamant pickaxe mines on a 4-tick cycle, unlike other pickaxes. This allows it to be used for tick manipulation in various places, such as mining shooting stars.
1273:
The mithril pickaxe is a pickaxe that is weaker than the adamant pickaxe . It requires an Attack level of 20 to wield, and a Mining level of 21 to mine with. It mines on a 5-tick cycle, 1-tick faster than the steel pickaxe and the same speed as the black pickaxe .

It is also one of the lightest pickaxes in the game (although heavier than the black pickaxe), making it ideal for activities such as training Runecraft via the Abyss.
1275: The rune pickaxe is the third best pickaxe , after the crystal pickaxe and the dragon pickaxe variants. It mines on a 3- tick cycle and is the best pickaxe in free-to-play . The rune pickaxe requires 41 Mining to use, and 40 Attack to equip. Players lacking 40 Attack can still use it for mining. Like all pickaxes, it cannot be smithed, so it must be obtained from other players or from a shop, as a monster drop, or as a reward from the quest Between a Rock... .
1277:
The bronze sword is a low-level weapon made of bronze . It can be purchased from the Varrock Swordshop , or made at level 4 Smithing using 1 bronze bar , granting 12.5 experience.

A bronze sword is given to the player by Vannaka on Tutorial Island .
1279: The iron sword is a low-level weapon made of iron , stronger than the bronze sword . It can be purchased from Varrock Swordshop or made at level 19 Smithing with 1 iron bar , granting 25 experience.
1281:
The steel sword is a low-level weapon made of steel , stronger than the iron sword . It can be purchased from the Varrock Swordshop , or made at level 34 Smithing using 1 steel bar , granting 37.5 experience. It requires 5 Attack to wield.

Two swords are needed for the In Search of the Myreque quest, along with some other steel equipment.
1283:
The black sword is a low-mid level weapon made of black , which is stronger than steel . It requires level 10 Attack to wield.

As with all black equipment, it offers the same bonuses as white equipment , minus the prayer bonus . Similarly, it cannot be smithed using the Smithing skill.

It can be obtained from various monsters including cyclops , abyssal demons , and black demons , or bought from the Varrock Swordshop .
1285:
The Mithril sword is a sword stronger than the black sword. It requires 20 Attack to wield.

Players can make this sword at level 54 Smithing by using one mithril bar and a hammer on an anvil, granting 50 experience. It can also be purchased from the Varrock Swordshop.
1287:
The adamant sword is the second-strongest sword available to free players , after the rune sword . As with most adamant weapons , level 30 Attack is required to wield it.

Adamant swords can be created at level 74 Smithing . One adamant bar is required to make the sword, and 62.5 Smithing experience is rewarded per sword created.
1289:
A rune sword is a medium-level sword made out of rune . Like all rune weapons , it requires 40 Attack to wield.

A rune sword can be created at level 89 Smithing using 1 rune bar , giving the player 75 Smithing experience .

Rune swords are ideal for non-member Ironmen as the only way to obtain a rune scimitar in a free-to-play world is to create it from scratch, requiring 90 Smithing (89 with a Dwarven stout ), whereas a rune sword can be purchased from Scavvo's Rune Store in the Champions' Guild for a price of 20,800 after obtaining 32 quest points .
1291: The bronze longsword is a longsword made of bronze. It is the weakest longsword available, and any player can wield it. It requires 2 bronze bars and level 6 Smithing to make, granting 25 experience. The bronze longsword is available for purchase at Varrock Swordshop in Varrock. It is rarely used due to the existence of the iron longsword, which is stronger and has the same requirements. It can be found as a drop from various monsters.
1293: The iron longsword is a longsword stronger than the bronze longsword , but weaker than the steel longsword . Like all other iron weapons , it can be wielded at level 1 Attack . It can be created at level 21 Smithing using two iron bars , granting 50 experience. This longsword can be purchased at Varrock Swordshop .
1295: The steel longsword is a longsword that is stronger than the iron longsword, but weaker than the black longsword. Like all other steel weapons, it requires 5 Attack to wield. Players can make a steel longsword with a Smithing level of 36 using two steel bars and a hammer on an anvil, granting 75 experience.
1297:
The black longsword is a longsword stronger than the steel longsword , but weaker than the mithril longsword . Like all other black weapons , it requires 10 Attack to wield, and cannot be made using the Smithing skill. Players can purchase this longsword from the Varrock Swordshop in Varrock .

The black longsword and the steel longsword have the same strength bonus. Black longswords have the same bonuses as a white longsword , other than the +1 prayer bonus the latter offers.

As with all black and white equipment , the black longsword cannot be made from raw materials using the Smithing skill.
1299: The mithril longsword is a longsword that is stronger than the black longsword / White longsword , but weaker than the adamant longsword . Like all other mithril weapons , it requires an Attack level of 20 to wield. Players can make a mithril longsword with a Smithing level of 56 using two mithril bars , granting 100 experience. Players can purchase this longsword from the Varrock Swordshop .
1301: The adamant longsword is a longsword that is stronger than the Mithril longsword, but weaker than the Rune longsword. Like all other adamant weapons, it requires 30 Attack to wield. Players can make an adamant longsword with 76 Smithing using 2 adamantite bars, granting 125 experience. It can be bought from the Varrock Swordshop for 3,200 coins.
1303: The rune longsword is a longsword requiring 40 Attack to wield. It can be made using 2 runite bars at level 91 Smithing . It is the strongest longsword in free-to-play , surpassing the adamant longsword . Even though it has better melee strength and attack, it underperforms compared to the Rune scimitar due to its attack speed being 25% slower (5 ticks compared to 4). Its higher attack bonus may outperform rune scimitar and rune sword against higher defence monsters.
1305:
The dragon longsword is the third-strongest longsword available in Old School RuneScape , and can only be wielded by players who have at least 60 Attack and have completed the Lost City quest.

As with all dragon weapons , players cannot make this item using the Smithing skill. However, it can be purchased in the Zanaris marketplace from Jukat for 100,000 coins (requires a Diamond for entry). The weapon can also be received as a reward from elite Treasure Trails .

It is a preferred weapon for players buying their first dragon weapon as it has a low cost but can still inflict significant damage. For a long time, prior to the 2005 introduction of the abyssal whip and dragon scimitar , this was the weapon of choice for both player killing and training.

It can be upgraded to the Dragon longsword (bh) with a Dragon longsword imbue scroll , which has a +4 increased stab and +6 slash attack bonus, and a +25% accuracy bonus to the special attack. In addition, the special attack consumes only 15% special attack energy rather than 25%, and is one tick faster (2.4 seconds instead of 3.0 seconds). The upgraded version can only be used for PKing in the Bounty Hunter minigame.
1307:
The bronze 2h sword is the weakest two-handed sword in Old School RuneScape. Like all bronze weaponry, it can be wielded at level 1 Attack.

It can be created at level 14 Smithing by using 3 bronze bars on an anvil with a hammer in the inventory, granting 37.5 Smithing experience.
1309:
The iron 2h sword is a two-handed sword that is stronger than the bronze 2h sword . As with other iron weaponry , it can be wielded at level 1 Attack .

Players can make an iron 2h sword with the Smithing skill at level 29 using 3 iron bars , giving the player 75 Smithing experience .
1311:
The steel 2h sword is a two-handed sword that requires 5 Attack to wield.

Players may smith one at level 44 Smithing with 3 Steel bars for 112.5 experience. Steel 2h swords can also be acquired from several monsters and one of the few two-handed sword shops, like Gaius' Two Handed Shop in Taverley.
1313:
The black 2h sword is a two-handed sword stronger than the steel 2h sword, requiring level 10 Attack to wield. Players can purchase this two-handed sword from Gaius' Two Handed Shop in Taverley. It can also be a reward from the Observatory Quest, from the Shades of Mort'ton minigame, completing a Treasure Trail or as a drop from various monsters.

As with all black and white equipment, the black 2h sword cannot be made from raw materials using the Smithing skill.
1315:
The mithril 2h sword is a two-handed sword made of mithril. As with all mithril weaponry , it requires 20 Attack to wield.

At level 64 Smithing , players can make one from three mithril bars , granting 150 Smithing experience . Players can also purchase one from a few shops, including Gaius' Two Handed Shop in Taverley and Gulluck and Sons in the Grand Tree .

Mithril 2h sword is also used to create the bowsword during the Devious Minds quest.
1317:
The adamant 2h sword is a two-handed sword that requires 30 Attack to wield. As with other two-handed weapons , a shield may not be equipped while wielding one.

Players may smith one at level 84 Smithing with 3 adamantite bars for 187.5 Smithing experience .

Its strength bonus is identical to that of a rune scimitar .
1319:
The rune 2h sword is a two-handed sword that is made of rune . It is stronger than the Adamant 2h sword , while being weaker than the Dragon 2h sword . It can be made using the Smithing skill at level 99 using 3 runite bars and a hammer on an anvil granting 225 Smithing experience . It requires 40 Attack to wield.

The rune 2h sword is often used on free-to-play worlds in player-killing to finish players off because it has the highest strength bonus, equal to the hill giant club , and the highest slash bonuses of all free-to-play equipment.

The rune 2h sword can also be dropped by any monster that has access to the rare drop table .
1321:
The bronze scimitar is a scimitar made of bronze . The weakest scimitar in the game, it requires level 1 Attack to wield. Players can make a bronze scimitar with level 5 Smithing using 2 bronze bars , granting 25 Smithing experience . Players can purchase this scimitar from Zeke's Superior Scimitars in Al Kharid .

One can be found for free on the top floor of a house in Rimmington .

There is also a bronze scimitar spawn in Corsair Cove , in the hut with Arsen the Thief and Cabin Boy Colin .
1323: The iron scimitar is a melee weapon that can be used in combat. It is stronger than the bronze scimitar. Players can make an iron scimitar with 20 Smithing using 2 iron bars, giving 50 experience.
1325:
The steel scimitar is a scimitar made by using 2 steel bars on an anvil , as long as you have a hammer and at least level 35 Smithing , granting 75 experience. Players can purchase this scimitar from Zeke's Superior Scimitars in Al Kharid .

Players require 5 Attack to wield steel weapons .
1327:
The black scimitar is a scimitar with a slightly higher attack bonus than the steel scimitar. It requires level 10 Attack to wield.

A black scimitar can be found in King Lathas' castle in East Ardougne. The respawn rate of a black scimitar here is about 12 minutes and 30 seconds. It requires level 61 Thieving to access. It can also be bought from Briget's Weapons.

As with all black and white equipment, the black scimitar cannot be made from raw materials using the Smithing skill.
1329: The Mithril scimitar is a scimitar stronger than the black scimitar. Like all mithril weapons, it requires 20 Attack to wield. It can only be used in combat. Players can make a mithril scimitar with the Smithing skill at level 55 using 2 mithril bars, giving 100 experience.
1331:
The adamant scimitar is the fourth strongest scimitar in the game, behind rune , gilded and dragon . Like most adamant weapons , it requires 30 Attack to wield.

Players can make it with 75 Smithing using two adamantite bars , earning 125 experience . The scimitar can also be obtained from killing monsters , and is a reward from the quest The Feud .

Smithing an adamant scimitar in the Resource Area is a task for the Wilderness Hard Diary .
1333:
The rune scimitar is a scimitar requiring level 40 Attack to wield. It can be created with 2 runite bars at level 90 Smithing , or dropped by various monsters such as Zamorak warriors or Fire giants .

It is the second strongest scimitar available behind the Dragon scimitar , and the strongest scimitar in free-to-play . Furthermore, it is considered the strongest melee weapon in most situations in free-to-play due to its unmatched attack and strength bonuses for its attack speed.

Ironmen may prefer to create a barronite mace or purchase a rune sword from the Champions' Guild (requiring 32 Quest points ). Members -only alternatives to the rune scimitar include the rapier (after Cabin Fever ), brine sabre , and ancient staff (after Desert Treasure I ).

Players can attach a Guthix , Saradomin or Zamorak ornament kit , obtained from beginner Treasure Trails , to create a Guthix , Saradomin and Zamorak rune scimitar , respectively. This only alters its appearance, and gives no stat enhancements, though the Saradomin and Zamorak variants will provide protection from the respective factions in the God Wars Dungeon . It can be dismantled at any time, returning the scimitar and ornament kit.
1335:
The iron warhammer is a warhammer stronger than the bronze warhammer . It can be wielded at level 1 Strength . Players can make an iron warhammer with the Smithing skill at level 24 using 3 iron bars , giving 75 Smithing experience .

One spawns in the ruined castle near the bandits just south-west of the Hosidius Mess .

The iron warhammer can be used as a substitute for a regular hammer when banging the big door at the entrance of Bandos' Stronghold in the God Wars Dungeon .
1337:
A bronze warhammer is a warhammer made with 3 bronze bars , requiring 9 Smithing , yielding 37.5 Smithing experience .

It can be purchased from Skulgrimen's Battle Gear and Vigr's Warhammers for 61 coins.

One can substitute a regular hammer when banging the big door at the entrance of Bandos' Stronghold in the God Wars Dungeon .
1339:
The steel warhammer is a warhammer stronger than the iron warhammer . Unlike other steel weapons , it requires 5 Strength to wield. Players can make a steel warhammer with the Smithing skill at level 39 using three steel bars , giving 112.5 Smithing experience .

A steel warhammer is one of the weapons requested during the In Search of the Myreque quest .

The steel warhammer can be used as a substitute for a regular hammer when banging the big door at the entrance of Bandos' Stronghold in the God Wars Dungeon .
1341:
The black warhammer is a warhammer stronger than the steel warhammer . Members can purchase it from Vigr's Warhammers in Keldagrim and Skulgrimen's Battle Gear in Rellekka . The black warhammer requires 10 Strength to wield.

The black warhammer can be used as a substitute for a regular hammer when banging the big door at the entrance of Bandos' Stronghold in the God Wars Dungeon .

As with all black and white equipment , the black warhammer cannot be made from raw materials using the Smithing skill.
1343:
The mithril warhammer is a warhammer stronger than the black warhammer , being made out of mithril. It may be used as an effective way of killing monsters weak to crush , such as earth warriors . Unlike other mithril weapons , it requires level 20 in Strength to wield.

Players can make a mithril warhammer with the Smithing skill at level 59 using 3 mithril bars , giving the player 150 Smithing experience . Members can purchase this warhammer from Skulgrimen's Battle Gear in Rellekka , and Vigr's Warhammers in Keldagrim .

The mithril warhammer can be used as a substitute for a regular hammer when banging the big door at the entrance of Bandos' Stronghold in the God Wars Dungeon .
1345:
The adamant warhammer is a warhammer stronger than the mithril warhammer . Unlike other adamant weapons , it requires 30 Strength to wield. They are the fourth-strongest warhammers for all players. Players can make them using the Smithing skill at level 79 using 3 adamantite bars , giving the player 187.5 Smithing experience .

The adamant warhammer can be used as a substitute for a regular hammer when banging the big door at the entrance of Bandos' Stronghold in the God Wars Dungeon .

An adamant warhammer is required for a medium clue emote step.
1347:
The rune warhammer is the second strongest type of warhammer in the game, better than the adamant warhammer but weaker than the dragon warhammer . Players can make a rune warhammer with the Smithing skill at level 94 using 3 runite bars , giving 225 Smithing experience .

Unlike other rune weapons , it requires 40 Strength to wield and has no Attack requirement, making it popular as a knockout weapon for free-to-play strength pures .

The rune warhammer can be used as a substitute for a regular hammer when banging the big door at the entrance of Bandos' Stronghold in the God Wars Dungeon .
1349:
The iron axe is the second weakest axe in Old School RuneScape , being slightly better than the bronze axe . It can be used in combat or in Woodcutting to cut trees . An iron axe has the same level requirements as a bronze axe, making it the better choice for new players.

The success rate for chopping a log is approximately 150% that of the Bronze axe .

Players can make an iron axe with the Smithing skill at level 16 using one iron bar , giving the player 25 Smithing experience . Players can purchase this axe from Bob's Brilliant Axes in Lumbridge and Aemad's Adventuring Supplies. in Ardougne .
1351:
The bronze axe is the weakest axe in Old School RuneScape. It can be wielded for combat, or used to cut trees in Woodcutting. It requires an Attack level of 1 to be equipped, and a Woodcutting level of 1 to be used.

Players can make a bronze axe with the Smithing skill at level 1 using one bronze bar, giving the player 12.5 Smithing experience. Players can take one for free from logs found at various locations, such as at the chicken farm by the Lumbridge cow field, or Fred the Farmer's house. One can also be obtained by talking to the Woodsman tutor.

Various activities require the use of an any axe, such as chopping Kraken tentacles on the Fishing Trawler, defeating the growthlings during the Bryophyta boss fight, or cutting bruma roots to fight Wintertodt. A bronze axe is available to the player from the nearby environment in these activities: on the Fishing Trawler from a crate marked axes, at Bryophyta from a pile of logs, and at Wintertodt from a crate.
1353:
The steel axe is slightly stronger than the iron axe. It can be used in combat or in Woodcutting to cut trees. It requires an Attack level of 5 to be equipped, and a Woodcutting level of 6 to be used.

The success rate for chopping a log is approximately 200% that of the bronze axe, or 33% better than an iron axe.

Players can make a steel axe with the Smithing skill at level 31 using one steel bar, giving the player 37.5 Smithing experience.
1355:
A mithril axe is an axe stronger than the black axe , and weaker than the adamant axe . Like all mithril weapons, it requires level 20 Attack to wield. It can be used in combat or in Woodcutting to cut trees . To cut a tree with this axe, a player must have 21 Woodcutting.

The success rate for chopping a log is approximately 250% that of the Bronze axe , or 11% better than a Black axe .

A player with 51 Smithing can make it using 1 mithril bar on an anvil while carrying a hammer , granting 50 Smithing experience .

A mithril axe is required in the Animal Magnetism quest, in which it is combined with a holy symbol and becomes a blessed axe .

The axe can be bought from Perry's Chop-chop Shop or Lunami's Axe Shop for 1,664 or 520 coins , respectively.
1357:
An adamant axe is a one-handed axe requiring 30 Attack to wield and 31 Woodcutting to use to cut trees . Making one requires 1 adamant bar and 71 Smithing , yielding 62.5 Smithing experience . As with all axes, it can be used to cut trees even when in the player's inventory.

The success rate for getting a set of logs is approximately 300% that of a bronze axe and 20% better than a mithril axe .
1359:
The rune axe is in the third-best tier of Woodcutting axes available to members and is the best tier axe available to free-to-play players. It is outclassed by the crystal axe, infernal axe, 3rd Age axe, and dragon axe, and is equivalent to the gilded axe (which is also available in free-to-play). Level 41 Woodcutting is required to use this axe.

Like any Woodcutting axe, its primary use is as a tool to cut trees in order to obtain logs and gain experience in the Woodcutting skill. As with all axes, it does not need to be wielded to cut down trees, but will work from the inventory. The success rate for receiving a set of logs when chopping a tree with a rune axe is approximately 350% that of a bronze axe, or 17% better than an adamant axe. It can also be used as a weapon for melee combat; the player must have an Attack level of 40 to wield this axe.

Players can make a rune axe with the Smithing skill at level 86 using one runite bar, granting 75 Smithing experience. It can be purchased from Perry's Chop-chop Shop for 40,960.
1361:
A black axe is an item mostly used in the Woodcutting skill. Using this axe requires level 11 Woodcutting. Level 10 Attack is required to equip it. As with all axes, carrying it in your inventory along with the necessary Woodcutting level will work.

The success rate for chopping a log is approximately 225% that of the bronze axe, or 12.5% better than a steel axe.

As with all black equipment and white equipment, the black axe cannot be made from raw materials using the Smithing skill.
1363:
The iron battleaxe is the second-weakest battleaxe in Old School RuneScape, being more powerful than the bronze battleaxe. Like all iron weapons, it can be wielded at level 1 Attack.

Players can make an iron battleaxe with level 25 Smithing using three iron bars, giving 75 experience. It is a slashing weapon, which makes it good for monsters with a slash weakness. Players can purchase this battleaxe from Brian's Battleaxe Bazaar in Port Sarim and Bob's Brilliant Axes shop in Lumbridge.
1365: The steel battleaxe is a battleaxe stronger than the iron battleaxe . The steel battleaxe requires 5 Attack to wield. Players can make a steel battleaxe with the Smithing skill at level 40 using 3 steel bars , giving the player 112.5 experience . Players can purchase this battleaxe from Brian's Battleaxe Bazaar in Port Sarim or Bob's Brilliant Axes in Lumbridge .
1367:
The black battleaxe is a battleaxe stronger than the steel battleaxe, but weaker than the Mithril battleaxe. It requires 10 Attack to wield. Players can purchase this battleaxe from Brian's Battleaxe Bazaar in Port Sarim. It can also be received as a drop from a Dark beast, and as a reward from a beginner clue scroll or easy clue scroll.

As with all black and white equipment, the black battleaxe cannot be made from raw materials using the Smithing skill.
1369:
A mithril battleaxe is a battleaxe made from 3 mithril bars, requiring 60 Smithing, yielding 150 Smithing experience. 20 Attack is required to wield it. It is stronger than the black battleaxe, but weaker than the adamant battleaxe.

Players can purchase it from Brian's Battleaxe Bazaar in Port Sarim, Bob's Brilliant Axes in Lumbridge, or Gulluck and Sons in the Tree Gnome Stronghold.
1371:
The adamant battleaxe is a battleaxe that is stronger than a mithril battleaxe , but weaker than a rune battleaxe . Like most adamant weapons , 30 Attack is required in order to wield it.

Players are able to obtain adamant battleaxes via trading with players, monster drops, or purchasing it at Brian's Battleaxe Bazaar (located in Port Sarim ). It may also be a reward from a clue scroll . At level 80 Smithing , players can use 3 adamant bars to smith an adamant battleaxe, granting 187.5 experience.
1373:
The rune battleaxe is the fourth strongest battleaxe, with zombie axe being the strongest, followed by the leaf-bladed battleaxe and the dragon battleaxe. Like most rune weapons, it requires 40 Attack to wield.

Players may make a rune battleaxe with 95 Smithing by using 3 rune bars at an anvil with a hammer, giving the player 225 Smithing experience.

Any monster that has access to the rare drop table can also drop the rune battleaxe.
1375: The bronze battleaxe is a battleaxe made of bronze. The weakest battleaxe in the game, it requires 1 Attack to wield. Players can make a bronze battleaxe with the Smithing skill at level 10 using 3 bronze bars, giving 37.5 experience. It is a slashing weapon, which makes it good for monsters with a slash weakness. Players can purchase this battleaxe from Brian's Battleaxe Bazaar in Port Sarim.
1377:
The dragon battleaxe is a one-handed axe requiring 60 Attack and the completion of Heroes' Quest to wield. Though not commonly used as a primary weapon, it has a useful strength-boosting special attack that can be activated before switching to a more powerful weapon to attack with.

As with most dragon equipment , the dragon battleaxe cannot be made from raw materials using the Smithing skill.
1379:
A staff is a cheap magic weapon which provides modest magical bonuses and the autocast option when equipped. Due to not possessing any elemental features and offering poor combat stats, it is only useful as a very cheap option for autocasting.

The staff can most easily be purchased from Zaff's staff shop in Varrock. It can also be bought on the Grand Exchange, obtained through other players or dropped by various enemies.

Although it is obtainable for a lower price than other staffs, investing into an elemental staff will save a lot more over time in rune costs.
1381:
A staff of air is the basic air elemental staff. It provides unlimited amounts of air runes as well as the autocast option when equipped. All elemental staves offer the same Magic bonuses and only differ by the type of rune they supply and their Melee stats.

The staff can be purchased from various shops across Gielinor, including Zaff's Superior Staffs! in Varrock. It can also be bought on the Grand Exchange, obtained through other players, dropped by various enemies, or obtained as a reward from beginner and easy clue caskets.

Players with access to a crystal ball within a player-owned house may change the element of this staff.
1383:
A staff of water is the basic water elemental staff . It provides unlimited amounts of water runes as well as the autocast option when equipped. All elemental staves offer the same Magic bonuses and only differ by the type of rune they supply and their Melee stats.

The staff can be purchased from various shops across Gielinor , including Zaff's Superior Staffs! in Varrock . It can also be bought on the Grand Exchange , obtained through other players, dropped by various enemies, or obtained as a reward from an easy tier clue scrolls .

Players with access to a crystal ball within a player-owned house may change the element of this staff.
1385:
A staff of earth is the basic earth elemental staff . It provides unlimited amounts of earth runes as well as the autocast option when equipped. All elemental staves offer the same Magic bonuses and only differ by the type of rune they supply and their Melee stats.

The staff can be purchased from various shops across Gielinor , including Zaff's Superior Staffs! in Varrock . It can also be bought on the Grand Exchange , obtained through other players, dropped by various enemies, or found as a continually spawning item in the lava maze .

Players with access to a crystal ball within a player-owned house may change the element of this staff.
1387:
A staff of fire is the basic fire elemental staff . It provides unlimited amounts of fire runes as well as the autocast option when equipped. All elemental staves offer the same Magic bonuses and only differ by the type of rune they supply and their Melee stats.

The staff can be purchased from various shops across Gielinor , including Zaff's Superior Staffs! in Varrock . It can also be bought on the Grand Exchange , obtained through other players, or dropped by various enemies.

Players with access to a crystal ball within a player-owned house may change the element of this staff.

When equipped, players are granted the fiery attribute and will therefore receive additional damage in PvP from the special effects of Pearl bolts (e) and Pearl dragon bolts (e) .
1389:
A magic staff is a magic weapon providing standard magical bonuses and the autocast option when equipped. It is an improvement over the basic staff, with over double the magical bonuses and higher melee bonuses. Due to not possessing any elemental features, it is a very unpopular weapon of choice.

The staff can most easily be purchased from Zaff's Superior Staffs! in Varrock, dropped by various enemies, or obtained as a reward from the Shades of Mort'ton minigame.

Despite being obtainable for a lower price than other staffs, an initial investment on an elemental staff would result in saving a lot more in rune costs.
1391:
A battlestaff is a members-only magic weapon which provides standard magical bonuses, heightened melee bonuses, and the autocast option when equipped. It requires 30 Attack and 30 Magic to wield. Due to not having any elemental features, this staff has limited long-term use. Its advantage over basic tier elemental staves and other lesser staves are its melee and magic bonuses.

The staff can be purchased from Zaff's Superior Staffs! in Varrock after the completion of the quest What Lies Below , and he'll stock 15 to 120 extra staves daily for players who have fully completed task tiers of the Varrock Diary (they can be obtained by interacting with the barrel in the north-west corner of the shop). The magic store owner in the Wizards' Guild and Baba Yaga on the Lunar Isle also stock them. It can also be bought on the Grand Exchange , obtained through other players, dropped by various enemies, or fletched from Celastrus bark with level 40 Fletching .

Battlestaves can be used to make elemental battlestaves . By using the appropriate ( air , water , earth , fire ) charge orb spell on an Obelisk with an unpowered orb in their inventory , a player can make an elemental orb, which can then be used on a battlestaff to make the corresponding elemental battlestaff. Elemental battlestaves can be upgraded to mystic staves by giving 40,000 to Thormac after the completion of the quest Scorpion Catcher . After completion of the Hard Kandarin Diary and Elite Kandarin Diary , Thormac will only require 30,000 and 20,000 respectively.
1393:
The fire battlestaff is an elemental staff requiring 30 Attack and 30 Magic to wield. In addition to increased Melee and Magic Attack bonuses, the staff provides unlimited amounts of fire runes as well as the autocast option when equipped.

This staff can be created at level 62 Crafting by combining a fire orb and battlestaff . It can also be upgraded to a mystic fire staff by paying Thormac 40,000 coins to upgrade it (less with the completion of certain Kandarin Diaries ). The mystic fire staff is an even stronger alternative, providing better melee and magic stat bonuses.

When equipped, players are granted the fiery attribute and will therefore receive additional damage in PvP from the special effects of Pearl bolts (e) and Pearl dragon bolts (e) .
1395:
The water battlestaff is an elemental staff requiring 30 Attack and 30 Magic to wield. In addition to increased Melee and Magic Attack bonuses, the staff provides unlimited amounts of water runes as well as the autocast option when equipped.

This staff can be created at level 54 Crafting by combining a water orb and battlestaff . It can also be upgraded to a mystic water staff by paying Thormac 40,000 coins to upgrade it (less with the completion of certain Kandarin Diaries ). The mystic water staff is an even stronger alternative, providing better melee and magic stat bonuses.
1397:
The air battlestaff is an elemental staff requiring 30 Attack and 30 Magic to wield. In addition to increased Melee and Magic Attack bonuses, the staff provides unlimited amounts of air runes as well as the autocast option when equipped.

This staff can be created at level 66 Crafting by combining an air orb and battlestaff . It can also be upgraded to a mystic air staff by paying Thormac 40,000 coins to upgrade it (less with the completion of certain Kandarin Diaries ). The mystic air staff is an even stronger alternative, providing better melee and magic stat bonuses.
1399:
The earth battlestaff is an elemental staff requiring 30 Attack and 30 Magic to wield. In addition to increased Melee and Magic Attack bonuses, the staff provides unlimited amounts of earth runes as well as the autocast option when equipped.

This staff can be created at level 58 Crafting by combining an earth orb and battlestaff . It can also be upgraded to a mystic earth staff by paying Thormac 40,000 coins to upgrade it (less with the completion of certain Kandarin Diaries ). The mystic earth staff is an even stronger alternative, providing better melee and magic stat bonuses.
1401:
The mystic fire staff is an elemental staff requiring 40 Attack and 40 Magic to wield. In addition to increased Melee and Magic Attack bonuses, the staff provides unlimited amounts of fire runes as well as the autocast option when equipped.

This staff can be created after the completion of the quest Scorpion Catcher by taking a fire battlestaff and 40,000 to Thormac . After completion of the Hard Kandarin Diary and Elite Kandarin Diary , Thormac will only require 30,000 or 20,000 respectively.

When equipped, players are granted the fiery attribute and will therefore receive additional damage in PvP from the special effects of Pearl bolts (e) and Pearl dragon bolts (e) .
1403:
The mystic water staff is an elemental staff requiring 40 Attack and 40 Magic to wield. In addition to increased Melee and Magic Attack bonuses, the staff provides unlimited amounts of water runes as well as the autocast option when equipped.

This staff can be created after the completion of the quest Scorpion Catcher by taking a water battlestaff and 40,000 to Thormac . After completion of the Hard Kandarin Diary and Elite Kandarin Diary , Thormac will only require 30,000 or 20,000 respectively.
1405:
The mystic air staff is an elemental staff requiring 40 Attack and 40 Magic to wield. In addition to increased Melee and Magic Attack bonuses, the staff provides unlimited amounts of air runes as well as the autocast option when equipped.

This staff can be created after the completion of the quest Scorpion Catcher by taking an air battlestaff and 40,000 to Thormac . After completion of the Hard Kandarin Diary and Elite Kandarin Diary , Thormac will only require 30,000 or 20,000 respectively.
1407:
The mystic earth staff is an elemental staff requiring 40 Attack and 40 Magic to wield. In addition to increased Melee and Magic Attack bonuses, the staff provides unlimited amounts of earth runes as well as the autocast option when equipped.

This staff can be created after the completion of the quest Scorpion Catcher by taking an earth battlestaff and 40,000 to Thormac . After completion of the Hard Kandarin Diary and Elite Kandarin Diary , Thormac will only require 30,000 or 20,000 respectively.
1409:
Iban's staff is a staff used to cast Iban Blast . It is obtained by defeating the evil mage Iban at the end of the Underground Pass quest . Iban's staff requires 50 Magic and 50 Attack to wield. Casting Iban Blast on a monster consumes one charge from the staff and casting it on another player consumes two charges. Casting other spells , like Fire Blast , does not consume any charges. The maximum hit with Iban Blast is 25.

If Iban's staff is lost, Koftik will give a broken staff to the player. It must then be brought to the Dark Mage with 200,000 coins to repair it. If Iban's staff is not protected on death (including PvP ), it will be sent to a gravestone .

The Dark Mage in West Ardougne will upgrade an Iban's staff to an Iban's staff (u) for 200,000 coins , which increases the charges it holds to 2,500 instead of 120 and fully charges the staff. A broken Iban's staff can also be repaired and upgraded at the same time for 400,000 coins .

As a melee weapon, the Iban staff is equivalent to a mystic staff .

Upgrading Iban's staff or wielding an Iban's staff (u) is a medium Ardougne Diary task.
1410:
Iban's staff is a staff used to cast Iban Blast . It is obtained by defeating the evil mage Iban at the end of the Underground Pass quest . Iban's staff requires 50 Magic and 50 Attack to wield. Casting Iban Blast on a monster consumes one charge from the staff and casting it on another player consumes two charges. Casting other spells , like Fire Blast , does not consume any charges. The maximum hit with Iban Blast is 25.

If Iban's staff is lost, Koftik will give a broken staff to the player. It must then be brought to the Dark Mage with 200,000 coins to repair it. If Iban's staff is not protected on death (including PvP ), it will be sent to a gravestone .

The Dark Mage in West Ardougne will upgrade an Iban's staff to an Iban's staff (u) for 200,000 coins , which increases the charges it holds to 2,500 instead of 120 and fully charges the staff. A broken Iban's staff can also be repaired and upgraded at the same time for 400,000 coins .

As a melee weapon, the Iban staff is equivalent to a mystic staff .

Upgrading Iban's staff or wielding an Iban's staff (u) is a medium Ardougne Diary task.
1411:
The Farmer's fork is an unobtainable item added to the game with the release of RuneScape 2. Although it is classified internally as a weapon, it lacks a wield option and does not have any equip animations defined.

It is very similar, but not identical, to the forks that are wielded by farmers.
1413:
The halberd is an unobtainable item released alongside RuneScape 2 . Although it is classified internally as a weapon, it lacks a wield option and does not have any equip animations defined.

Its release predates the release of obtainable halberds by several months. Presumably it was created in order to test the implementation of the new halberd weapons in RuneScape 2 while Regicide was developed.
1415:
The warhammer is an unobtainable item released alongside RuneScape 2. Although it is classified internally as a weapon, it lacks a wield option and does not have any equip animations defined.

It was presumably a leftover from development, created in order to test the implementation of the new warhammers in RuneScape 2.
1417:
The javelin is an unobtainable item release alongside RuneScape 2 . Although it is classified internally as a weapon, it lacks a wield option and does not have any equip animations defined.

It was presumably a leftover from development, created to test the implementation of the new javelin weapons in RuneScape 2 .
1419:
The scythe is an untradeable event reward . It can be obtained by completing one of the Halloween holiday events that occur once per year.

The scythe is not particularly powerful, as it is intended to be a decorative weapon . It has very low bonuses and a slow attack speed. Notably, it has several unique attack animations.

Previously, they were obtainable during the 2013 Rare Drops event (from 3 June to 10 June ) as part of a rare item drop .

If destroyed, a replacement can be obtained from Diango in Draynor Village or from the toy box of a costume room . Thessalia in Varrock will also return this item to the player if destroyed.
1420:
The Iron mace is a mace made of iron . It is the second weakest mace available in the game. It requires level 1 Attack to wield, and can be created by using an iron bar on an anvil (as long as the player has level 17 Smithing ). It can be bought at Flynn's Mace Market in Falador .

It can be found in the Edgeville jail and in a house to the east of the Ardougne market .
1422: The Bronze mace is a mace made of bronze. It is the weakest mace in the game, and can be equipped at level 1 Attack. A bronze mace can be created at level 2 Smithing using 1 bronze bar. This item spawns in Sorceress' house in southern Al Kharid, and can be bought at Flynn's Mace Market in Falador.
1424: The steel mace is a mace stronger than the iron mace, requiring 5 Attack to wield. Players can make it with the Smithing skill at level 32 using one steel bar, giving 37.5 Smithing experience.
1426:
A black mace is a melee weapon stronger than the steel mace , requiring 10 Attack to wield. It is only obtainable in free-to-play by killing dark warriors , from beginner clue scrolls or from Camdozaal Vault lockboxes . Members can also loot it from bronze chests in the Shade Catacombs in the Shades of Mort'ton minigame or from level 106 Cyclops in the Warriors' Guild basement.

As with most maces , it has a Prayer bonus and like all black equipment it cannot be made from raw materials with Smithing .
1428:
The mithril mace is a mace made of mithril. Like all mithril weapons , it requires 20 Attack to wield, and is exclusively used in melee combat.

Players can make a mithril mace with the Smithing skill at level 52 by using a mithril bar on an anvil with a hammer in their inventory, giving the player 50 Smithing experience.

It can be bought from Flynn's Mace Market in Falador .
1430: An adamant mace is a mace that requires level 30 Attack to wield. Players can make an adamant mace with the Smithing skill at level 72 using 1 Adamant bar, giving 62.5 Smithing experience. Players can purchase this mace from Flynn's Mace Market in Falador or the weapons shop in the Warriors' Guild, and is also dropped by Twisted Banshees.
1432:
A rune mace is a mace made of runite . It requires 40 Attack . It can be made at level 87 Smithing using one Rune bar .

It is currently the sixth-strongest mace in the game, surpassed by the Void knight mace , Barronite mace , Dragon mace , Tzhaar-ket-em , and the Inquisitor's mace . It is the second strongest free-to-play mace, behind the Barronite mace which has a higher crush and strength bonus, but a lower prayer bonus.

The rune mace can be purchased from Scavvo's Rune Store in the Champions' Guild for a price of 14,400 coins after obtaining 32 quest points . It can also be purchased from Spike's Spikes in Outer Fortis for 18,720 coins , only requiring access to Varlamore .

The rune mace can be combined with Scurrius' spine on an anvil using a hammer to create the bone mace , requiring 35 Smithing . Alternatively, Historian Aldo can do so for a fee of 50,000 coins .
1434:
The dragon mace is a one-handed spiked weapon and the strongest of the standard maces . It can only be wielded by players who have an Attack level of at least 60 and who have completed the Heroes' Quest .

The mace can be purchased for 50,000 coins at the Happy Heroes' H'emporium in the Heroes' Guild , or from other players.

It can also be obtained as a reward from elite clues and master clues .

It can be upgraded to the Dragon mace (bh) with a Dragon mace imbue scroll , which has a +4 increased stab and crush attack bonus. In addition, the special attack consumes only 15% special attack energy rather than 25%, and rolls against 60% of the target's crush defence rather than 100%. The upgraded version can only be used for PKing in the Bounty Hunter minigame .

As with most dragon equipment , the dragon mace cannot be made from raw materials using the Smithing skill.
1436:
Rune essence is a raw material used in the Runecraft skill that can be crafted into low-level runes , namely air , mind , water , earth , fire , and body runes . Unlike runes, rune essence does not stack. Players need pure essence to craft any other type of rune, which can only be mined in members worlds.

There are a few ways of obtaining rune essence, other than by trading with other players.

Free players may mine rune essence in the rune essence mine , unlocked after completing the Rune Mysteries quest. To reach these mines, players need to be teleported by one of several NPCs . In members worlds, players will also mine Rune essence until reaching level 30 Mining when they will automatically mine pure essence . Mining from one of the rocks that have an unlimited supply of essence gives 5 Mining experience per essence. A pickaxe is needed, just like any other mining activity.
1438:
The air talisman is a talisman that allows players to enter the Air Altar. At the altar, the player can use the Runecraft skill to turn rune essence or pure essence into air runes.

Also at the Air Altar, an air talisman can be combined with a silver tiara to make an air tiara for 25 Runecraft experience by using the tiara on the altar while having an air talisman in the inventory. This consumes the talisman, but the air tiara can be used the same as an air talisman and can be worn, opening an inventory slot to carry another essence.

Air talismans can be used to create combination runes. The talisman is consumed when used as the "secondary" talisman to make these runes.

Air talismans can be obtained as a reward from the Rune Mysteries quest, or as drops from various monsters.
1440: An earth talisman is a type of talisman that lets the player access the Earth Altar. Use the talisman on the altar to get inside to create earth runes. You can also access the Earth Altar by using an earth tiara, which can be equipped to save inventory space and is made using the earth talisman. When you make an earth tiara, you are granted 32.5 Runecraft experience. If you are a member, it can be used to runecraft dust runes at the Air Altar, mud runes at the Water Altar, or lava rune at the Fire Altar. The earth talisman is consumed in the process.
1442:
The fire talisman is a talisman used in the Runecraft skill to enter the Fire Altar north of Al Kharid . It can also be combined with a tiara to create a fire tiara , which grants you 35 Runecraft experience.

It is dropped by a variety of monsters , including skeletons , fire wizards (1/20), dark wizards , creatures in the Abyss and lava dragons . The drop rate is noted to be slightly higher from dark wizards than regular wizards but more commonly by fire wizards and creatures in the Abyss.
1444: A water talisman is a type of talisman that lets the player use the Water Altar . Use the talisman on the altar to get inside allowing one to create water runes at the altar. It is also used to make a water tiara if you have a tiara and a water talisman and use them on the altar, granting 30 Runecraft experience. If you are a member, it can be used to runecraft mist runes at the Air Altar , steam runes at the Fire Altar , or mud runes at the Earth Altar . The water talisman is consumed in the process.
1446:
A body talisman is a talisman used in the Runecraft skill. It allows players to enter the Body Altar and create body runes from rune, pure, or daeyalt essence.

At the Body Altar, a body talisman can be combined with a tiara to make a body tiara for 37.5 Runecraft experience by using the tiara on the altar. This makes the talisman disappear, but the body tiara also grants access to the Body Altar when worn.

Making body tiaras is one of the fastest runecraft training methods for free to play, making these talismans desired by these players. Because of this, body talismans are relatively expensive on the Grand Exchange.
1448:
The mind talisman is a talisman used to access the Mind Altar located between Ice Mountain and Goblin Village. It can be combined with a tiara to make a mind tiara for 27.5 Runecraft experience at the Mind Altar by using the tiara on the altar. This makes the talisman disappear, but the tiara can be used in just the same way and can be worn.

One is required to create a mind tiara for the Easy Falador Diary.
1450:
The blood talisman is a talisman that allows players to enter the Blood Altar where blood runes are crafted. The Blood Altar is located in the Meiyerditch Laboratories, which is discovered during Sins of the Father. Making blood runes requires level 77 Runecraft. The talisman is not required to access Kourend's Blood Altar, as it is not the true Blood Altar.

Blood talismans can be obtained from the Temple Supplies shop at the Guardians of the Rift minigame, granted the player has completed Sins of the Father. It can be combined with a tiara to make a blood tiara for 52.5 Runecraft experience at the Blood Altar, by using the tiara on the altar. This makes the talisman disappear, but the blood tiara can be used in just the same way and can be worn on the head, saving an inventory space when crafting blood runes. The Catalytic talisman and tiara can be used as a cheaper alternative access to the Blood Altar.

Though it has a locate option, using it will give the message,The talisman doesn't seem to work. Maybe the ruins are deep underground. This message will persist even if the player is in the Meiyerditch Laboratories.
1452:
The chaos talisman is a talisman that allows players to enter the Chaos Altar in the Wilderness just north-west of Edgeville. It can be combined with a tiara to make a chaos tiara for 42.5 Runecraft experience. This will make the talisman disappear, but the tiara will allow one-click entry to the Chaos Altar when worn. Both the tiara and the talisman allow players to craft chaos runes.

The chaos talisman is also a part of the rare drop table, therefore any monster with access to the rare drop table has a chance of either dropping this talisman or a nature talisman (with a couple of exceptions being able to drop both, such as fire giants and abyssal demons). Mid-level ironmen might find it easiest to get this by fighting Abyssal Leeches in the Abyssal Area using the Fairy Ring circles.
1454:
A cosmic talisman is a talisman needed to enter the Cosmic Altar in the southern part of Zanaris. It can be combined with a tiara to make a cosmic tiara for 40 Runecraft experience at the Cosmic Altar by using the tiara on the altar. This makes the talisman disappear, but the tiara can be used in just the same way and can be worn. Both the tiara and the talisman allow players to craft cosmic runes at level 27 Runecraft.

To enter the altar the player needs to have completed the Lost City quest or Enter the Abyss if using the Abyss.

Cosmic talismans can be obtained from several sources, including:

Certain monsters, especially abyssal monsters and those found in the Waterbirth Island Dungeon

Certain random events such as Rick Turpentine, certers, Mysterious Old Man, and Pillory Guard

Caskets obtained from big fishing nets, large salvage, plundered salvage, or killing Rock Crabs, Sand Crabs, and Ammonite Crabs.
1456:
The death talisman is a talisman that allows players to enter the Death Altar where death runes are crafted . The Death Altar is located in the Temple of Light , which is discovered during Mourning's End Part II . Making death runes requires level 65 Runecraft .

Death talismans can be obtained by killing dark beasts with level 90 Slayer . They can also be obtained during and after Mourning's End Part II by giving the dwarf Thorgel , located at the entrance to the Death Altar, all 50 items on his item list . Thorgel will give one death talisman for every item list completed. Upon completion of Mourning's End Part II, Death talismans can be obtained from the Temple Supplies shop at the Guardians of the Rift minigame, or as a reward from the Rewards Guardian .

The talisman can be combined with a tiara to make a death tiara for 50 Runecraft experience at the Death Altar, by using the tiara on the altar. This makes the talisman disappear, but the death tiara can be used in just the same way and can be worn on the head, saving an inventory space when crafting death runes.
1458:
The law talisman is a talisman used to access the Law Altar located on Entrana for the purpose of runecraft . It can also be combined with a silver tiara by using the tiara on the Law Altar with the talisman in your inventory, resulting in a law tiara . Once inside the altar a player can make law runes . This requires 54 Runecraft.

The law talisman is a reward for completing the Troll Stronghold quest, and can be acquired again from Dunstan in Burthorpe for 1000 coins each if lost or if you want to have spare talismans. Dunstan will not sell you another law talisman if there are already five in your inventory or bank.

Law talismans can also be purchased as rewards from Guardians of the Rift , and can be purchased regardless of how many you already own.
1459:
Auto-weed is an interface item seen in-game via the shop interface when browsing Farmer Gricoller's Rewards.

Before it is unlocked, the first version auto-weed is displayed in the interface until it is purchased for 50 Tithe points. After it is unlocked, the interface item is displayed as auto-weed (activated) when active and auto-weed (deactivated) when inactive, and can be freely toggled through the shop interface using the "Buy-1" Button.
1460:
The soul talisman was an unobtainable item that would allow players to enter the Soul Altar . As the Soul Altar did not exist at the time of its release, it was not made available.

With the release of the Soul Altar in Arceuus on 7 January 2016 (which does not require a soul talisman) it was removed from the game, but was re-added - though remaining unobtainable - with the release of Yama on 14 May 2025 .
1462:
The nature talisman is a talisman used to gain access to the Nature Altar, located north of Shilo Village on the island of Karamja, where players can craft nature runes. The talisman can also be combined with a tiara at the Nature Altar by having both the nature talisman and tiara in your inventory, and using the tiara on the altar. This action grants the player 45 Runecraft experience; some players choose to do this in order to save an extra inventory space and make quicker trips when crafting nature runes, as the Nature Altar may be accessed simply by left-clicking on it while the player is wearing the nature tiara.

A good way to obtain the talisman is to kill abyssal leeches in the abyss after completing the Enter the Abyss miniquest. Keep in mind that the abyss is very dangerous and you may find yourself quickly overwhelmed without proper armour and food. Always bring a teleport in case you need a quick escape. The nature talisman is also a part of the rare drop table, therefore any monster with access to the rare drop table has a chance of either dropping this talisman or a chaos talisman (with a couple of exceptions being able to drop both, such as fire giants and abyssal demons).

A nature talisman is a possible requirement for obtaining the magic secateurs in Fairytale I - Growing Pains.
1464:
An archery ticket is the reward given for using the target range at the Ranging Guild . The quantity received varies from 0-100 tickets per 10 shots at the cost of 200 coins. They can be exchanged with the Ticket Merchant within the guild for prizes, most notably rune arrows and green d'hide bodies.

The archery ticket is one of the items that may be asked for during Mourning's End Part II .
1465:
Weapon poison is an unobtainable item that was intended to be released with the Ranging Guild , but for unknown reasons was cut before launch. Most likely, it would have been sold by the weapon poison salesman , who was also not released. Since weapon poison was relatively difficult to obtain at the time, it is possible the developers feared making it available in a store would cause the item to become too common.

It is referred to in the game files as display_weapon_poison . This suggests that, similar to the tea seller , the weapon poison salesman would have owned a stall, and yelled at any player who attempted to take the display poison.

The item has never been available in Old School RuneScape , but remains in the game files.
1466:
A Sea slug is an item that players can pick up using the Telekinetic Grab spell on a sea slug that Kent knocks off the player during the Sea Slug quest .

Without Telekinetic Grab, it will merely damage the player for 3 hitpoints , causing them to exclaim "Ouch!" If dropped, players can only pick it up again using another Telekinetic Grab spell.

Attempting to cast alchemy spells on a sea slug will fail with the message Ugly parasites have feelings too!

Sea slugs are one of a handful of lethal self-damaging items; most self-damaging items cannot kill the player.

However, if the sea slug is left on the floor when an instance closes (e.g: death in most private instances, server update, etc.), the sea slug will be permanently deleted.
1467: Damp sticks are used with broken glass to make dry sticks in the Sea Slug Quest . The dry sticks can then be used to light a torch . They can be found on the Fishing Platform .
1468: Dry sticks are the result of using broken glass on damp sticks . They are used in the Sea Slug quest to light a torch on the Fishing Platform . They can be kept after the quest, and with 30 Firemaking can be used at any time to light a torch by selecting the "rub-together" option. Unlike a tinderbox , clicking to use the sticks on an unlit torch has no effect.
1469:
Broken glass is an item which is the result of some glass being broken. Its main use is during the Sea Slug quest , where the player must use the glass on the damp sticks to get dry sticks , which have a "Rub-together" option to light a torch needed to continue with the quest.

It also is also involved in the Forgettable Tale... quest, in which the rowdy dwarf requests a random item in exchange for his Kelda seed , with broken glass being a possible item he requests.

Both Gunslik and the rowdy dwarf can also request broken glass when doing Keldagrim tasks .
1470:
The red bead is a bead used in Imp Catcher quest. It is a drop from Imps and is returned to Wizard Mizgog in the Wizards' Tower along with Black bead , White bead and Yellow bead to finish the quest.

The bead can also be used to bait traps when hunting imps .
1472:
The Yellow bead is a bead used in the Imp Catcher quest. It is returned to Wizard Mizgog in the Wizards' Tower along with a black bead, a white bead and a red bead to finish the quest. It can be obtained by killing imps.

The bead can also be used to bait traps when hunting imps.
1474:
The Black bead is a bead used in Imp Catcher quest. It is a drop from Imps and is returned to Wizard Mizgog in the Wizards' Tower along with White bead, Red bead and Yellow bead to finish the quest.

The bead can also be used to bait traps when hunting imps.
1476:
The white bead is a bead used in the Imp Catcher quest. It is a drop from imps and must be returned to Wizard Mizgog in the Wizards' Tower along with a black bead, red bead, and yellow bead to finish the quest.

Beads are used as optional bait in the box catching of imps.
1478:
An amulet of accuracy is a reward from the Imp Catcher quest. To complete Imp Catcher, Wizard Mizgog trades an amulet of accuracy for a set of black, red, white, and yellow beads. After the quest it is possible to give him one of each bead again for another amulet.

The amulet is easily obtainable for new players because the quest has no requirements apart from killing imps; however, it is only recommended if the player is an Ironman lacking Magic levels to enchant better amulets. Amulet of power is already a straight upgrade across all stats.
1480:
Rocks are received when killing earth elementals, mining rocks in the Feldip Hills, smashing boulders in the Shaman Caves, or picked up from the ground after failing some of the first traps in the Underground Pass and dropping into a pit. The tool leprechaun by the Troll Stronghold herb patch also sells them.

Rocks are mainly used in the quest Recipe for Disaster when freeing Skrach Uglogwee, where they are used for jubbly hunting. It can be also used to turn an ore-attuned rock golem pet back into its original state.
1481:
An orb of light, also known as a Sphere of Light, is a magical orb used in Underground Pass quest. The player destroys four of these orbs in the furnace found in the dungeon in order to progress into the next part (note: one cannot destroy the orbs in another furnace outside the underground pass). Destroying an orb yields the message, You feel a cold shudder run down your spine as the light of the orb fades.

According to the old journal, they were placed in the Underground Pass by the warrior, Randas, in a failed attempt to ward off the darkness prior to the player's involvement.

Orbs of light cannot be banked, and duplicates cannot be held or picked up after that version is destroyed (spawn version or player-dropped version). The item spawn cannot be seen by Telekinetic Grab, however, a player-dropped variant can, but the spell cannot be used on it.
1482:
An orb of light, also known as a Sphere of Light, is a magical orb used in Underground Pass quest. The player destroys four of these orbs in the furnace found in the dungeon in order to progress into the next part (note: one cannot destroy the orbs in another furnace outside the underground pass). Destroying an orb yields the message, You feel a cold shudder run down your spine as the light of the orb fades.
