1714: Unstrung symbols can be made at 16 Crafting with a silver bar and a holy mould at a furnace , granting 50 crafting experience . It can be used with a ball of wool to create an unblessed symbol . This can then be taken to Brother Jered who will bless it at level 31 Prayer (including F2P), or it can be blessed at level 50 Prayer using a completed Holy book .
1716:
Unblessed symbols are made by using a ball of wool with an unstrung symbol, granting the player 4 Crafting experience.

Players with a Prayer level of 31 or higher can have their unblessed symbols blessed by Brother Jered in the Edgeville Monastery, turning them into holy symbols.

A player with a Prayer level of 50 or higher can bless a symbol themselves by using a completed Holy book or book of balance at the expense of 2 Prayer points with the holy book and 7 Prayer points with the book of balance.
1718:
A holy symbol is an amulet in the shape of a symbol of Saradomin. Holy symbols are made by having an unblessed symbol blessed by Brother Jered in the Edgeville Monastery, or by blessing it via using a holy book or book of Balance on an unblessed symbol at 50 Prayer, requiring a few prayer points. As Brother Jered is located on the upper floor of the monastery, blessing the symbol effectively requires a minimum of level 31 Prayer due to the entry requirement.

It has the third highest prayer bonus for an amulet in game (after god stoles and the dragonbone necklace). It is cheap, easy to obtain, and is commonly used in conjunction with Proselyte armour and other high prayer granting armour when using protect prayers as a form of defence while training.

Wearing a holy symbol while being attacked by a Feral Vampyre occasionally reduces their Attack, Strength, Defence, and Magic by 25%.

Wearing a holy symbol allows players to use a prayer book to cure poison.

A holy symbol will count as a Saradominist item within the God Wars Dungeon.

A holy symbol is required for the quests Animal Magnetism and The Great Brain Robbery.
1720: Unstrung emblems can be used with a ball of wool to create an unpowered symbol . The Spirit of Scorpius in the Grave of Scorpius will bless an unpowered symbol, resulting in an unholy symbol , for players who have completed the Observatory Quest . Players with an Unholy book or a Book of Balance and a Prayer level of at least 50 can bless their own unpowered symbols to create unholy symbols at a cost of 4 Prayer points each.
1722:
An unpowered symbol is a symbol of Zamorak made by stringing an unstrung emblem with a ball of wool , requring 1 Crafting , yielding 4 Crafting experience .

It is made into an unholy symbol by using a completed Unholy book or Book of Balance , requiring 50 Prayer, or talking to the Spirit of Scorpius after completion of the Observatory Quest which also requires claiming an unholy mould from him. He will not give the player an unholy mould if there is one already in their inventory.
1724:
An unholy symbol is a silver symbol blessed to imbue it with the unholy power of Zamorak . Players can make unholy symbols by using the Crafting skill, with a Crafting level of 17. First, a player must use a silver bar with a furnace while they have an unholy mould in their inventory and must have one free inventory space. This will give the player an unstrung emblem and they will receive 50 Crafting experience . Next, the player must string the symbol with a ball of wool , giving the player 4 Crafting experience and making the item into an unpowered symbol .

Finally, the symbol must be blessed either by the Spirit of Scorpius at the Grave of Scorpius , north of the Observatory , or by using an unholy book or Book of Balance with it. To bless the symbol using one of the books, a player must have a Prayer level of 50 or higher, and blessing the symbol makes the player expend ( 1 10 * C u r r e n t P r a y e r P o i n t s ) + 2 amount of Prayer points. Once blessed, the unpowered symbol becomes an unholy symbol and gains stat bonuses.

This item can be obtained when the player is chasing Solus during the Wanted! quest.
1725:
The amulet of strength is an enchanted ruby amulet . Players frequently use it to increase their max hit . At level 50 Crafting , players can craft a ruby amulet. With at least 49 Magic , Lvl-3 Enchant can be cast on a ruby amulet to create an amulet of strength.

A trimmed version of the amulet of strength is available from medium clue scrolls .
1727:
An amulet of magic is an amulet that gives a Magic attack bonus when worn. It is created by casting Lvl-1 Enchant on a sapphire amulet . It is one of the cheapest and most common amulets in the game because of the low Crafting level to craft it, how common sapphires are, and the low Magic level to enchant the amulet.

A normal amulet of magic, as well as its trimmed variant are both possible reward for the completion of easy Treasure Trails .
1729:
The amulet of defence is created when an emerald amulet has been enchanted using the Lvl-2 Enchant spell. It is not widely used, as it only gives defence bonuses. However, it can prove useful in situations where more damage is going to be taken than dealt, such as skilling in the Wilderness or activities like Pyramid Plunder. For this purpose, for Members, the Gnome amulet can be a better option as it has nearly twice the melee defensive bonuses (but no ranged or magic defensive bonuses).

Amulets of defence can be sold to Davon's Amulet Store in Brimhaven, starting at 1,147 coins each if none are in stock. The amulet of defence (t), a cosmetic variant, can be obtained as a rare reward from beginner clue scrolls.
1731:
An amulet of power offers a good balance of attack and defence bonuses for all classes of combat . It is created by casting Lvl-4 Enchant on a diamond amulet , and has no requirements to be worn.

This item is a less expensive option for players who do not wish to buy an amulet of glory . It lacks the glory's teleportation capabilities and has weaker attack and Prayer bonuses , but has the same strength bonus as well as higher defence bonuses .

This amulet is currently the best overall amulet for F2P players, although the amulet of strength is better in some cases, such as fighting low defence targets with melee.

A helpful way for P2P Ironmen to obtain one is by looting the H.A.M. Store rooms for a diamond amulet, and then enchanting it with 57 Magic . Shipwreck Salvaging at Mercenary shipwrecks (73 Sailing ) also commonly provides them.
1733:
A needle is an item used along with thread to create armour out of leather and dragon leather through the Crafting skill. It can be bought in crafting stores, such as Dommik's Crafting Store in Al Kharid. They can also be bought from Moon Clan Fine Clothes on Lunar Isle, the Canifis General Store and Fancy Clothes Store in Varrock (Members). After completion of Death on the Isle, a Costume needle can be used for crafting without needing thread.

Needles can also be found from digging in the Digsite. They can also be found with a 10% probability by searching haystacks or hay bales - this is a reference to the idiom "finding a needle in a haystack", meaning something that is almost impossible to find because it is hidden among so many other things. When your character finds one this way, they will remark on how rare an occurrence it is.

Needles are stackable items, presumably because they are small, although normal usage does not require them to be.

During the Witch's House quest, a needle can be found by searching the crates in the basement.
1734:
Thread is used along with a needle to make armour out of leather , dragon leather and cured yak-hide . Each thread spool has 5 uses before it is consumed. A "use" means an action performed, not number of leathers used (e.g. making vambraces, which use 1 hide each, consumes thread at the same rate as making chaps, which use 2 hides each).

After completion of Death on the Isle , a Costume needle can be used for crafting without needing thread.
1735:
Shears can be bought in almost any general store for 1 gp. They are required to shear wool from sheep, and are needed for the Sheep Shearer quest if you choose to gather the wool yourself. They are also needed for the quest A Tail of Two Cats.

They can be picked up off of the table in Fred the Farmer's house for the quest Sheep Shearer. It can also be found in Hosidius, in the building just north of the estate agent.
1737:
Wool is gathered from sheep and alpacas using shears . It can be spun at a spinning wheel to be made into a ball of wool for 2.5 Crafting experience. Wool cannot be obtained from rams or the fake sheep . In free-to-play , the best method of collecting wool is by shearing sheep north of Lumbridge , then going to Lumbridge Castle to bank on the 2 nd floor [ UK ] 3 rd floor [ US ] .

Alternatively, members can shear sheep behind Watson's house , spin it inside his house, and then bank it at the Hosidius Kitchen for a similar distance.

One piece of wool is required in the quest Sleeping Giants to repair the polishing wheel.
1739:
Cowhides are dropped by cows or undead cows when they are killed. If it is brought to a tanner, it can be turned into soft leather for 1 coin or hard leather for 3 coins. Tanners can be found in Al Kharid, the Ranging Guild, Forthos Dungeon, Canifis, Auburnvale, Neitiznot, Kebos Lowlands, and the Crafting Guild. Soft and hard leathers can then be crafted into various pieces of equipment through the Crafting skill.

It is also used alongside a unicorn horn to generate a unicow in the Tower of Life.

Good places to gather cowhides are the pastures in Lumbridge, north of Ardougne market, and south of Falador, though the Falador pastures are closer to a bank.

If a player has completed the Hard tier of the Falador Diary or is level 99 in Crafting, then they can access the bank chest in the Crafting Guild, which is quite close to a field of cows. Note that access to the guild requires a brown apron, golden apron, or a Crafting cape.

Another option is to teleport to the Lumbridge cow field with the Cowbell amulet, then teleport to a bank (such as with a Ring of dueling to Castle Wars) to bank the cowhides.
1741:
Leather , or soft leather , is obtained from tanning a cowhide . Leather can be used with a needle and thread to be crafted into leather gloves , leather boots , leather cowl , leather vambraces , leather body , a coif or leather chaps , granting Crafting experience. On every fifth piece of leather used, one thread will be consumed, effectively necessitating a 1/5 ratio of thread needed per leather when creating armour.

A single piece of leather can be found on top of a table in the Shayzien Encampment . You must use telekinetic grab to pick it up.

A crate in the Elemental Workshop can be searched for a piece of leather once during Elemental Workshop I .

One piece of leather is required for the quests Mourning's End Part I , Cold War , and Elemental Workshop I .
1743:
Hard leather is made by taking cowhides to a tanner . The lunar spell Tan Leather can also be used at level 78 Magic , and tans up to 5 cowhides at once into hard leather.

Combined with thread and a needle , it can be used to make hardleather bodies at level 28 Crafting , granting 35 crafting experience. With a hammer and 15 bronze nails , members can attach two hard leathers onto an oak shield to create a hard leather shield . Doing so requires level 41 Crafting and grants 70 experience.

Hard leather can also be obtained as rare loot from baby implings .

One piece of hard leather is required for Animal Magnetism .
1745: Green dragon leather is used in the Crafting skill to make green dragonhide armour . It can be created by giving a green dragonhide to a tanner . Tanners can be found in Al Kharid , the Ranging Guild , Forthos Dungeon , Kebos Lowlands , Auburnvale , Canifis , and the Crafting Guild . Alternatively, green dragon leather can be made using the Tan Leather spell . Crafting any piece of green dragonhide armour will grant the player 62 experience per hide.
1747: Black dragonhide (also called Black d'hide by tanners ) is a 100% drop from black dragons , brutal black dragons , lava dragons , and the King Black Dragon . The hide can be tanned to become black dragon leather by paying a tanner or by using the Tan Leather lunar spell. A tanner will charge 20 coins for each hide, or 45 in Canifis. Tanners can be found in Al Kharid , the Ranging Guild , Canifis , the Crafting Guild , Auburnvale , and Forthos Dungeon .
1749:
Red dragonhide (also called Red d'hide by tanners) is a 100% drop from red dragons when they die. The hide can be tanned to become red dragon leather by paying a tanner or by using the Tan Leather lunar spell. A tanner will charge 20 coins for each hide, or 45 in Canifis. Tanners can be found in Al Kharid, the Ranging Guild, Canifis, Forthos Dungeon, and the Crafting Guild.

Players can then make red dragonhide armour from red dragon leather via the Crafting skill if they have a high enough level.
1751:
Blue dragonhide (also known as blue d'hide) is a 100% drop item from blue dragons when killed. Players can take hides to a tanner to make blue dragon leather for a fee of 20 coins at a tanner (45 coins from Sbott in Canifis) or by using the Tan Leather lunar spell. Tanners can be found in Al Kharid, the Ranging Guild, Forthos Dungeon, Canifis, the Kebos Lowlands, Auburnvale and the Crafting Guild.

Members can craft pieces of blue dragonhide armour from blue dragon leather with level 66 Crafting.
1753:
Green dragonhide is a 100% drop from green dragons . It can be tanned to make green dragon leather , which in turn is used to make green dragonhide armour , by paying a tanner or by using the Tan Leather Lunar spell . A tanner will charge 20 coins for each hide, or 45 in Canifis . Tanners can be found in Al Kharid , the Ranging Guild , Forthos Dungeon , Canifis , and the Crafting Guild .

The 100% drop rate makes green dragon hunting a popular money making method for many players.
1755:
A chisel is a tool used in the Crafting skill to cut and shape hard non-metals, mainly gems and limestone. Chisels are also used in Fletching to cut gems into bolt tips. Chisels can be purchased for 1 coin at all general stores, except for those in Dorgesh-Kaan and Ardougne. There is a free-to-play chisel spawn in the Crafting Guild.

At level 15 Construction, members can make a tool store 1 for the workshop room of their house, which will provide an unlimited supply of chisels.
1757:
Brown aprons are used to enter the Crafting Guild . They can be purchased from several clothing stores, such as Thessalia's Fine Clothes store in the centre of Varrock, for 2 coins.

A brown apron can be obtained from the Tool store 3 built in the Workshop of a player-owned house . Members can also claim them from Malignius Mortifer after the Swan Song quest.
1759:
A ball of wool is used in the Crafting skill . It is made by using a spinning wheel .

Players looking to obtain large numbers of balls of wool often use Neitiznot supplies. in Neitiznot as it has the largest stock of any store with a bank in the same building. After Monkey Madness II , Hamab's Crafting Emporium on Ape Atoll is also located close to a bank.
1761:
Soft clay is used to create items in the Crafting and Construction skills and to make magic tablets. It can be created by using a container of water such as a vial of water, jug of water, or bucket of water on clay, by using the Humidify spell, or by mining clay rocks whilst wearing a bracelet of clay. It is used on a potter's wheel to craft various Crafting items.

The only place to mine soft clay directly is in the Trahaearn mine, where soft clay rocks can be found. In addition, wearing a bracelet of clay in this mine can yield 2 soft clays per action, whereas mining clay rocks elsewhere yields only a single soft clay per action.

In addition to mining soft clay in Prifddinas, soft clay packs can be bought from Prospector Percy's Nugget Shop in Motherlode Mine for 10 golden nuggets each, Dusuri's Star Shop at the Mining Guild entrance in Falador for 150 stardust each, and Belona's Mining Guild Mineral Exchange for 10 unidentified minerals each. Each soft clay pack contains 100 Soft Clay.
1763:
Red dye is a dye created by taking 3 redberries to Aggie in Draynor Village along with 5 coins or Ali the dyer in Pollnivneach along with 25 coins. It can also be bought in Lletya from Oronwen for 6 coins. It can also be found in the Sisterhood Sanctuary in Slepe, as well as in the farmhouse featured in Getting Ahead, south of the Farming Guild, located in the shelves next to the stairs in the house.

Red dye can be combined with yellow dye to make orange dye, or with blue dye to make purple dye. It can be used to dye normal capes red. Red dye is used in Enlightened Journey, Getting Ahead, Song of the Elves, and Goblin Diplomacy if making orange dye. It is also a possible required item for Ghosts Ahoy because the colour needed is random.
1765: Yellow dye is a dye that can be created by taking 2 onions and 5 coins to Aggie in Draynor Village, or 2 onions and 25 coins if taken to Ali the dyer in Pollnivneach. It can also be bought in Lletya from Oronwen for 6 coins. It can also be found in the farmhouse featured in Getting Ahead, south of the Farming Guild, located in the shelves next to the stairs in the house. Yellow dye can be combined with red dye to create orange dye, and with blue dye to create green dye. It can be used to dye normal capes yellow.
1767:
Blue dye can be obtained from Aggie in Draynor Village in exchange for 2 woad leaves and 5 coins, or from Ali the dyer in Pollnivneach in exchange for 2 woad leaves and 25 coins. It can also be purchased from Oronwen in Lletya, Guinevere in Prifddinas, or Xochitl in Tal Teklan.

Blue dye is mainly used in the Goblin Diplomacy, Land of the Goblins, Ghosts Ahoy and Mourning's End Part I quests. Blue dye can be used with a black cape (or any other colour) to create a blue cape. It can also be used to turn a black robe into a blue robe.
1769:
Orange dye is a dye made by combining red dye and yellow dye . Its main use is in the quest Goblin Diplomacy , when the player must use the dye on goblin mail . This item can also be bought from the Lletya Seamstress for 6 coins. In order to access the shop, one must have at least started the Mourning's End Part I quest.

Players can also obtain red and yellow dye from Aggie in Draynor Village provided she is given the ingredients needed and 5 coins per bottle of dye. Players can then combine the red and yellow dye to make orange dye.
1771: Green dye is a dye made by combining blue dye and yellow dye, which can both be made from Aggie, the dye maker in Draynor. It can also be purchased from Oronwen in Lletya. Members can also use it to make a green balloon after the Enlightened Journey quest by using the dye on an origami balloon. When used with a cape, the cape becomes a green cape and gives 2.5 crafting experience.
1773:
Purple dye is a dye made by combining blue dye and red dye, both of which may be made by Aggie in Draynor Village. It is used for colouring capes, granting 2.5 Crafting experience in the process, and for dying orange slices during Recipe for Disaster.

It respawns to the north of the Clock Tower, near the spirit tree, south of East Ardougne, as well as on a table on the top floor of the church in Hosidius. It can also be bought at Lletya Seamstress in Lletya. Players must have at least started the Mourning's End Part I quest to access this shop.
1775:
Molten glass is used in the Crafting and Construction skills, as well as some quests, to form glass items. It is created through the Crafting skill by using a bucket of sand and soda ash on a furnace, granting 20 Crafting experience. This only requires level 1 Crafting. Alternatively, players can use the Lunar spell Superglass Make, which combines all buckets of sand and all seaweed or soda ash in the player's inventory into molten glass, granting 10 Crafting experience per pair of items.

Molten glass is used in some quests such as Observatory Quest, Horror from the Deep, Wanted!, Desert Treasure I, Another Slice of H.A.M. and The Fremennik Exiles. Although molten glass cannot be bought in any shop, buckets of sand and soda ash are available from the charter ship shops. This is especially useful for ironmen, who could buy both items and then smelt them in a furnace. For larger amounts, giant seaweed and sandstone are efficient sources of the materials required; as a result, making and blowing glass is a common method of training Crafting.
1777:
A bow string is used in the Fletching skill to create bows . It is created by using flax on a spinning wheel , or by casting the Spin Flax spell.

Using a spinning wheel, it takes 50.2 seconds to spin a full inventory of 28 flax , requiring 10 Crafting and granting a total of 420 experience .

The Medium Kandarin Diary allows players to spin flax 33% faster at the spinning wheel in Seers' Village . A full inventory of 28 flax takes 33.6 seconds after completion of the diary, not including banking time.
1779:
Flax is a resource that can be picked from plants in various locations around Gielinor. Multiple can be collected from the same plant. Flax can also be harvested from a hops patch after planting flax seeds with 18 Farming.

It is used to make bow strings at a spinning wheel, requiring 10 Crafting, yielding 15 Crafting experience. Flax can also be spun via the Spin Flax Lunar spell. It is also used to spin linen yarn or as payment to protect hemp plants (x6). Linen yarn can be used to build a linen trawling net or woven into bolts of linen, which can be used to upgrade masts and sails on a player's boat.

Completing the Kandarin Diary allows players to exchange noted flax with the flax keeper once a day in exchange for bow strings. The easy diary unlocks 30 per day, medium 60 per day, hard 120 per day, and elite 250 per day.

Flax in the Tree Gnome Stronghold does not exist in Deadman Mode worlds.
1781:
Soda ash is made into Molten glass to make glass items in Crafting. Soda ash is made using seaweed, giant seaweed, swamp weed, or edible seaweed on a range, oven, or fire. Smelting it with a bucket of sand in a furnace or the Lunar spell Superglass Make produces molten glass.

It can be purchased from Trader Stan's Trading Post at charter ships for 5 coins; the closest one to a bank is in Port Khazard. Another option close to a bank is the Corsair Cove shop, which is about 10 tiles farther from a bank but may be more likely to have soda ash in stock.
1783: A bucket of sand can be obtained by using an empty bucket with a sand pit or sand pile . They may also be obtained from Drew by mining sandstone and depositing it in the grinder next to him. They are a key component in creating molten glass , which is often used in Crafting and Construction , either via a furnace along with soda ash or by casting Superglass Make along with soda ash, seaweed or giant seaweed .
1785: A glassblowing pipe is a tool used to make items from molten glass using the Crafting skill. It is required to make glass items. The item can be obtained from Fritz the Glassblower's house found in the south-western area of Entrana, taken from a tool store 3 in a player-owned house (required 35 Construction), from Grandpa Jack's house (from Fishing Contest quest), bought from the Piscatoris Fishing Colony after finishing Swan Song, or bought from charter ship locations (from the crew).
1787: An unfired pot is made by using soft clay on a potter's wheel , which requires level 1 Crafting and yields 6.3 Crafting experience. The unfired pot can be fired in a pottery oven to produce a pot , granting 6.3 Crafting experience upon success. Unlike shaping the clay, firing it has no Crafting level requirement. At lower levels, an unfired pot can crack in the oven, destroying the pot and granting no experience.
1789:
An unfired pie dish is made by using soft clay on a potter's wheel , which requires level 7 Crafting and yields 15 Crafting experience. The unfired pie dish can be fired in a pottery oven to produce a pie dish , granting 10 Crafting experience upon success. Unlike shaping the clay, firing it has no Crafting level requirement.

At lower levels, an unfired pie dish can crack in the oven, destroying the pie dish and granting no experience.
1791:
An unfired bowl is made by using soft clay on a potter's wheel which requires 8 Crafting and yields 18 Crafting experience. The unfired bowl can be fired in a pottery oven to produce a bowl , granting 15 Crafting experience upon success. Unlike shaping the clay, firing it has no Crafting level requirement. At lower levels, the bowl can crack in the oven, destroying the bowl and granting no experience.

For the quest Dragon Slayer I , an unfired bowl is required as one of four items in order to obtain Thalzar 's map piece from the Oracle on Ice Mountain .
1793:
Woad leaves can be harvested from a flower patch after planting woad seeds . They are used to make blue dye and, by extension, green and purple dye . Players must take two woad leaves and 5 coins to Aggie to make blue dye, which is enough to dye one item.

They can either be grown through Farming or bought from Wyson the gardener in Falador Park . Offering him 20 coins provides the best value since he actually gives two for being so generous. Adding them to a compost bin makes regular compost .
1794: Bronze wire can be created by players with level 4 in Smithing by using one bronze bar on an anvil with a hammer in your inventory. A total of 7 are used in quests , such as Creature of Fenkenstrain (3 required, unnoted), Recipe for Disaster/Freeing Pirate Pete (3 required) and Shilo Village (1 required).

It can be dusted with flour and used with flypaper to obtain Anna's print , which can be compared with the unknown print to see if Anna is the killer.

This item will disappear if a player has it in their bank or inventory upon finishing the quest. It is a unique cosmetic item, so if a player wishes to keep it, they must drop it before finishing the quest and pick it up again afterwards. It cannot be obtained again after the quest is finished.

1811: Flypaper can be taken from sacks in the gardening shed on the west end of Sinclair Mansion . It is used during the Murder Mystery quest to lift fingerprints from a number of silver items that belong to the people suspected of committing the murder of Lord Sinclair .
1812:
The pungent pot is a quest item found at the murder scene during the Murder Mystery quest. It is later used as evidence during the murder investigation.

Using the pot on a barrel of flour will result in a message stating You probably shouldn't use evidence from a crime scene to keep flour in...
1813:
The Criminal's dagger is a quest item that is found at the murder scene during the Murder Mystery quest . This dagger cannot be equipped and is used to help gather evidence against the culprit during the quest. In the quest, you must use a pot of flour on the dagger to dust it, then use flypaper on the dagger to get the unknown print . You must do the same with the items belonging to the suspects. Then compare them by using a suspect's fingerprints on the criminal's fingerprint to get the killer's print .

If you lose it, it will respawn in the same place as where you got it.

1815: The killer's print is an item used in Murder Mystery , found by using the criminal's dagger on a pot of flour and some flypaper . Players compare this item to the prints of the Sinclair family, and find out who the killer is.

1822:
The unknown print is a quest item used in the Murder Mystery quest. It is lifted off of the murder weapon by using a pot of flour and a sheet of flypaper and can then be compared with similar prints lifted off of the suspects possessions in order to identify the murderer.

After the murderer is identified, the unknown print becomes the killer's print.
1823:
A waterskin carries up to four servings of water, and provides protection against the desert heat effect in the Kharidian Desert. The amount of water will be noted by the waterskins name in parenthesis e.g. "Waterskin (4)" is a waterskin that is holding the maximum amount of water.

These can be bought from Shantay, in the Shantay Pass, south of Al Kharid. There are several ways to refill waterskins. In the table below, different methods of refilling are given, along with the amount of water doses are refilled by that method. Note that it is possible to decant water into other containers, for example using a vial of water on an empty bucket. Doing this before refilling the waterskin will quadruple the amount of water refilled in the skin.

After completing Beneath Cursed Sands, a charged circlet of water can be used as an alternative to carrying waterskins, though it must be equipped to take effect.

Desert shirts are suitable for desert environments, like the Kharidian Desert south of Shantay Pass . When worn, this clothing item delays the desert heat effect by 12 additional seconds. It has no other bonuses.

A full set of desert clothing is needed for the The Tourist Trap quest. They are given to a slave miner in exchange for a set of slave robes to allow the player access to a deeper area of the mining camp.

During the Shadow of the Storm quest, the desert shirt can be changed into a black desert shirt when it is dyed using black dye . Note that the black desert shirt will no longer offer protection from the desert heat.
