2132: Raw beef is an uncooked food . Raw beef is one of the requirements of the Druidic Ritual quest. Players require only level 1 Cooking to cook raw beef. It gives 30 Cooking experience when cooked. When cooked, the raw beef may become cooked meat or burnt meat . Players can buy it from Rufus' Meat Emporium in Canifis and from Wydin's Food Store in Port Sarim . Raw beef is always dropped from cows . Members can convert raw beef into sinew by using it on a range and choosing the "Make sinew" option.
2134:
Raw rat meat is usually obtained by killing a giant rat . It can be cooked on a range or on a fire. It requires level 1 Cooking to be turned into Cooked meat , granting 30 Cooking experience if successful. It is one of the four raw meats needed in the Druidic Ritual quest. It can be used as bait when trapping sabre-toothed kebbits . Raw rat meat can be bought from Rufus in Canifis . Unlike raw beef , raw boar meat , and raw bear meat , raw rat meat cannot be turned into sinew .

If looking for a giant rat to kill, level 3 giant rats are common in Lumbridge Swamp and always drop raw rat meat. The level 6 giant rat in Lumbridge Swamp, the giant rat near the mine south-east of Varrock and the giant rats in the Stronghold of Security rarely drop rat meat.

Raw rat meat is always dropped by brine rats , and brine rats sometimes drop 18 noted raw rat meat.

Raw rat meat spawns cannot be picked up by ironmen .
2136:
Raw bear meat can be obtained by killing any bear (except Callisto or Artio ), or by purchasing it from Rufus in Canifis . It is dipped in the Cauldron of Thunder during the Druidic Ritual quest . It can be cooked at level 1 Cooking , granting 30 Cooking experience if successful. After successfully cooking it, it will simply be cooked meat, burning it will result in burnt meat (burning can be achieved at any level by cooking it twice). The raw bear meat can also be made into sinew at level 1 Cooking by using it on a range.

Bears can be found throughout Gielinor , mainly in woodland areas such as near Castle Wars , south of Yanille and in a cage in Varrock castle . To get to this a player must go through the Varrock Sewers . A single black bear can be found south of the South-east Varrock mining site , along with two unicorns . Another good place to kill bears is north-east of Ardougne , near the Legends' Guild .

Raw bear meat is one of the ingredients in making a wild pie .
2138:
A Raw chicken is an uncooked food item dropped by chickens or roosters . They are also sold at Rufus' Meat Emporium in Canifis and Wydin's Food Store in Port Sarim .

There is also a crate in Wydin's shop in Port Sarim that provides unlimited raw chicken. A white apron is required to enter the room which contains the crate.

Raw chicken can be cooked into cooked chicken by using it on a fire , a range , or an ogre spit-roast . Doing so requires only level 1 Cooking for the fire and the range, and grants 30 experience points. The ogre spit-roast requires level 30 Cooking. At level 34 Cooking, raw chicken can no longer be accidentally burnt.

Raw chicken is used with together with a raw swordfish to make a swordchick in Creature Creation after completion of Tower of Life .
2140:
Cooked chicken is a type of food that restores 3 Hitpoints when eaten. It can be obtained by cooking raw chicken on a fire or cooking range , granting 30 experience when successful. When cooking there is a chance to fail, resulting in burnt chicken . The burn rate decreases as the player's Cooking level increases. Cooked chicken is one of a number of foods with a reduced burn rate while using the Lumbridge Castle range with Cook's Assistant completed. It will stop burning entirely at Cooking level 34, or 31 when using the Lumbridge range.

Cooked chicken does not require a cooking level to cook, and can be used as an ingredient to make a stew or curry . It is an easily obtainable early food source, as killing chickens at the Lumbridge East Farm is a common activity for a low level player.
2142:
Cooked meat is a type of food that restores 3 Hitpoints when eaten. It can be obtained by cooking various raw meats on a fire or cooking range, granting 30 experience when successful. When cooking there is a chance to fail, resulting in burnt meat. The burn rate decreases as the player's Cooking level increases. Cooked meat is one of a number of foods with a reduced burn rate while using the Lumbridge Castle range with Cook's Assistant completed. It will stop burning entirely at Cooking level 34, or 31 when using the Lumbridge range.

Cooked meat is used in the making of stews, pies, and steak sandwiches, or as a topping on pizzas.

Unlike most food, players can deliberately burn cooked meat by using it on a fire or cooking range. One burnt meat is required for Witch's Potion.
2144:
Burnt chicken is the result of accidentally burning a raw chicken while attempting to make cooked chicken . The burn rate while cooking these will decrease as players reach higher Cooking levels, stopping entirely at level 34. Players can also deliberately make burnt chicken by cooking a piece of cooked chicken, displaying the chatbox message, You deliberately burn the nicely cooked chicken.

Burnt chicken may be used for the Forgettable Tale... quest, in which it may be one of the random items requested by the rowdy dwarf before he will give the player his Kelda seed . It is also one of the items that Gunslik and the rowdy dwarf can request when doing Keldagrim tasks .

Like most other burnt food, it is tradeable to other players but not on the Grand Exchange .
2146:
Burnt meat is the result of accidentally burning various raw meat while attempting to make cooked meat. The burn rate while cooking these will decrease as players reach higher Cooking levels, stopping entirely at level 34. Players can also deliberately make burnt meat by cooking a piece of cooked meat, displaying the chatbox message "You deliberately burn the nicely cooked meat."

Burnt meat is used for the Witch's Potion quest. It is often dropped by Imps, and is also a reward from Burntmeat after Eadgar's Ruse and My Arm's Big Adventure.

Like most other burnt food, it is tradeable to other players but not on the Grand Exchange.
2148:
Raw lava eels require level 53 Fishing to catch, and a Cooking level of 53 to cook. Raw lava eels may be caught using an oily fishing rod and bait in the lava rivers found in Taverley Dungeon , the Wilderness Lava Maze , the Charred Dungeon (level 60 Sailing ), and the Wyrmscraig Cavern (after completion of Fallen From Grace ).

During the Heroes' Quest , guild-master Achietties will ask players to obtain a cooked lava eel to prove that they are worthy of membership to the Heroes' Guild . Players will then need to visit Gerrant in Port Sarim to learn how to make an oily fishing rod to catch them.

Catching a raw lava eel in the Lava Maze is a hard Wilderness Diary task.

Lava eels do not offer the player a chance to roll a pet drop while fishing. [ 1 ]
2149: Lava eel is a type of untradeable fish that restores 11 Hitpoints when eaten. During Heroes' Quest, guild master Achietties will ask players to obtain a cooked lava eel to prove that they are worthy of membership to the Heroes' Guild. It can be obtained by cooking raw lava eel on a fire or cooking range, requiring level 53 Cooking and granting 30 experience when successful. There is no chance of burning a lava eel.
2150:
A swamp toad is a small creature with removable legs. Doing so yields toad's legs in place of the swamp toad. Toad's legs heal for 3 Hitpoints, are used as the second ingredient for agility potions (toadflax potion unf), and the gnome cooking foods: Tangled toad's legs, toad batta, and toad crunchies.

Collecting a swamp toad at the Gnome Stronghold is a requirement for the easy Western Provinces Diary.

The text "You pull the legs off the toad. Poor toad. At least they'll grow back." appears in the chat box after pulling the legs off.

These swamp toads cannot be used to fill ogre bellows; only swamp toads found around Feldip Hills will fill them. Attempting to do so results in the chatbox message stating "The chompy bird doesn't like this species of toad."
2152:
Toad's legs are a food used in Cooking and Herblore. They are made by pulling the legs off of swamp toads found in the swamp of Tree Gnome Stronghold or lake south of Taverley, and from pickpocketing gnomes, requiring 75 Thieving. They heal for 3 Hitpoints. Adding them to a toadflax potion (unf) makes an Agility potion (3), requiring 34 Herblore, and yielding 80 Herblore experience. Toad's legs are main ingredients of the gnome cooking foods: Tangled toad's legs, toad batta and toad crunchies.

Toad's legs can be used as a fast food, a subtype of food that incurs non-standard attack or eating delays when consumed. Toad's legs may be consumed after other foods with almost no delay; this does not work if the toad's legs are eaten first, and does not work when eating two toad's legs in a row. This technique (commonly referred to as combo eating) can be further enhanced by drinking a dose of Saradomin brew after your alternative food item, and before your toad's legs (food>brew>toad's legs).
2154:
Equa toad's legs was previously obtained during Gnome cooking when making a Toad batta . It could be made by adding Equa leaves to Toad's legs . Gnome spice was then added to these in order to create Seasoned legs , an ingredient in the Toad batta.

As this process was unnecessarily intricate, it was altered with the Gnome Restaurant rework in 2006. Now, the toad's legs, equa leaves and gnome spice are all automatically added at once to create a Half made crunchy . If the player attempts to add equa leaves to toad's legs, nothing happens.

Because the item was removed before 2007, it has never been present in Old School RuneScape . However, it remains in the game files.

2160:

2162:
King worms are used in gnome cooking to make worm crunchies, worm holes, and worm battas. They can be eaten to heal 2 Hitpoints. When eaten, the message You eat the king worm. It's a bit chewy. is displayed. It is a possible item chosen randomly from a list in the Fairytale I - Growing Pains and Forgettable Tale... quests, to enchant the Secateurs, and trade for the Rowdy dwarf's kelda seed.

When talking to a gnome woman, they occasionally give king worms.

King worms are also used to feed the Cormorant while Aerial fishing on the island on Lake Molch.
2164:
A batta tin is used for making battas in the Gnome Restaurant minigame . It can be obtained in the Grand Tree by buying from the Gnome Restaurant food shop owned by Hudo , by searching the nearby cupboard to find one, or by looting it from the gnomes in the stronghold.

If one gianne dough is added into the tin a raw batta is created, and if this is cooked over the gnome cooker or any other range , half baked batta will be made. From here, any of the battas in the gnome cuisine can be made. Examples of battas include worm batta , toad batta , cheese and tomato batta , fruit batta , and vegetable batta .

Please see gnome cooking for more information on gnome cuisine.
2165: Crunchy trays are items used in gnome cooking. They can be obtained by buying them from the Grand Tree, the Grand Exchange or by trading with other players. The trays can be combined with gianne dough to make raw crunchies.
2166:
A gnomebowl mould is an item used in gnome cooking . It can be bought in the Grand Tree by talking to Hudo in the north-west corner on the 1 st floor [ UK ] 2 nd floor [ US ] , or it can be acquired for free by searching the tree gnome kitchen cabinet at the northernmost part of the Grand Tree for a "gnome bowl".

Adding gianne dough to the mould will create a raw gnomebowl , the basis for gnomebowl cooking .
2167:
Gianne's cook book is a cook book written by Aluft Gianne. It is full of Gnome recipes, and useful for the Gnome Restaurant minigame, or if players want to make gnome foods for themselves.

The cook book can be obtained from Aluft Gianne himself, Hudo the nearby grocer, or from the bookcase in a player-owned house. The book will not be available in your bookcase until completing the cooking tutorial with Aluft Gianne snr.. It mentions Pukkamay, a great Gnome cook.

Note that this book does not contain Gnome cocktail recipes, as these recipes are written in the The Blurberry Cocktail Guide.
2169:
Gnome Spice is an ingredient used to make spicy sauce and certain gnome foods . It can be bought from Grand Tree Groceries , run by Hudo in the Grand Tree . It will never run out while making Gnome foods.

To create spicy sauce , gnome spice is used with chopped garlic . This uses up the gnome spice.

When placing it into nest atop the Aldarin mill and then logging out of the game, it will transform into an iron pickaxe .
2171: Gianne dough is an ingredient in gnome cooking used to make gnomebowls, gnome crunchies, and gnome battas. It can be bought from Hudo in the Grand Tree. Gianne dough cannot be cooked by itself; instead, players must use the dough on a crunchy tray, batta tin, or gnomebowl mould and then precook it on a range. It was probably named after Aluft Gianne snr., the gnome cook. 100 Gianne dough is also given as a reward for completing the Gnome Restaurant training.
2173:
An odd gnomebowl was previously obtained during Gnome cooking . If a player added incorrect ingredients to a Half baked bowl , they would receive this item.

As the cooking process was unnecessarily intricate, it was altered with the Gnome Restaurant rework in 2006. Now, all ingredients are automatically added via the reworked interface, which eliminated the possibility of any mistakes by the player. As a result, the odd gnomebowl was discontinued.

Because the item was removed before 2007, it has never been present in Old School RuneScape . However, it remains in the game files.
2175:
Burnt gnomebowl is the result of accidentally burning a raw gnomebowl while attempting to make a half baked bowl. The burn rate while cooking these will decrease as players reach higher Cooking levels, stopping entirely at level 38.

The burnt gnomebowl has no use whatsoever, although it can be emptied to reclaim a gnomebowl mould. Like most other burnt food, it is tradeable to other players but not on the Grand Exchange.
2177: The half baked bowl is an item used in gnome cooking and is obtained by using gianne dough with a gnomebowl mould , then using the resulting raw gnomebowl on a range . The raw ingredients can be added by selecting prepare and choosing a gnomebowl type. This creates a half made bowl .
2178:
Raw gnomebowls are the base of gnomebowl cooking and are obtained by using gianne dough on a gnomebowl mould. They can be used on a range to make half baked bowls.

Unlike other items requiring a range, raw gnomebowls cannot be cooked using Mor Ul Rek sulphur vents.
2179:
An unfinished bowl was previously obtained during Gnome cooking when making a Chocolate bomb. It could be made by adding four Chocolate bars and some Equa leaves to a Half baked bowl, then baking it. The following items could then be added:

A pot of cream to make the second unfinished bowl

Another pot of cream to make the third unfinished bowl

Some chocolate dust to complete the chocolate bomb

If a mistake was made at any point, an Odd gnomebowl would be received instead.

As this process was unnecessarily intricate, it was altered with the Gnome Restaurant rework in 2006. Now, the initial ingredients are automatically added to create a Half made bowl, which can then be cooked to produce the new Unfinished bowl. The chocolate and cream garnishes are now added at once.

Because the item was removed before 2007, it has never been present in Old School RuneScape. However, it remains in the game files.

2185:
A chocolate bomb is a food that players consume in one bite, healing 15 hitpoints . Players may need to make one as part of Training part I for the Gnome Restaurant minigame. Premade chocolate bombs are sold by gnome waiters in the north-west corner of the 1 st floor [ UK ] 2 nd floor [ US ] of the Grand Tree for 160 coins , with 3 in stock.

Members can make a chocolate bomb via gnome cooking with 42 Cooking , yielding 190 experience . Like all gnome foods, they stop burning at Cooking level 38.

Making a chocolate bomb is a requirement for the Medium Western Provinces Diary .

This food is an order in the Gnome Restaurant minigame and may also be obtained by completing an order through a Gnome restaurant Reward token . Like all gnome cooking, premade versions cannot be used in the minigame.

Gianne dough , gnomebowl moulds , chocolate (decadently added), chocolate dust , pots of cream , and equa leaves can be bought from Hudo who is located in the north-west corner the 1 st floor [ UK ] 2 nd floor [ US ] of the Grand Tree.
2187:
A tangled toad's legs is a food that players consume in one bite, healing 15 hitpoints. Players may need to make one as part of Training part I for the Gnome Restaurant minigame. Premade tangled toad's legs are sold by gnome waiters in the north-west corner of the 1st floor of the Grand Tree for 160 coins, with 3 in stock.

Members can make a tangled toad's legs via gnome cooking with 40 Cooking, yielding 185 experience. Like all gnome foods, they stop burning at Cooking level 38.

This food is an order in the Gnome Restaurant minigame and may also be obtained by completing an order through a Gnome restaurant Reward token. Like all gnome cooking, premade versions cannot be used in the minigame.

Gianne dough, gnomebowl moulds, cheese, equa leaves, dwellberries, and gnome spice can be bought from Hudo who is located in the north-west corner the 1st floor of the Grand Tree. While toad's legs are not sold, swamp toads may be found in the swamp north-west of the Grand Tree, in the Tree Gnome Stronghold.

During the The Path of Glouphrie quest, Gianne jnr. asks the player to deliver a long-standing Aluft Aloft Gnome Food Delivery Service order of tangled toad's legs to the gnome Longramble. While this is not required to progress the quest, if the player completes the delivery, Longramble will give the player a mint cake as payment.
2189:
An unfinished bowl was previously obtained during Gnome cooking when making a Worm hole. It could be made by adding four King worms, two Onions, and some Gnome spice to a Half baked bowl, then baking it. Finally, Equa leaves were added to make a worm hole. If a mistake was made at any point, an Odd gnomebowl would be received instead.

As this process was unnecessarily intricate, it was altered with the Gnome Restaurant rework in 2006. Now, all ingredients are automatically added to create a Half made bowl, which can then be cooked to produce the new Unfinished bowl. Once again, equa leaves are used to convert this into a Worm hole.

Because the item was removed before 2007, it has never been present in Old School RuneScape. However, it remains in the game files.

2245:
An odd batta was previously obtained during Gnome cooking . If a player added incorrect ingredients to a Half baked batta , they would receive this item.

As the cooking process was unnecessarily intricate, it was altered with the Gnome Restaurant rework in 2006. Now, all ingredients are automatically added via the reworked interface, which eliminated the possibility of any mistakes by the player. As a result, the odd batta was discontinued.

Because the item was removed before 2007, it has never been present in Old School RuneScape . However, it remains in the game files.
2247:
Burnt batta is the result of accidentally burning a raw batta while attempting to make a half baked batta . The burn rate while cooking these will decrease as players reach higher Cooking levels, stopping entirely at level 38.

The burnt batta has no use whatsoever, although it can be emptied to reclaim a batta tin . Like most other burnt food, it is tradeable to other players but not on the Grand Exchange .
2249: A half baked batta is created by cooking a raw batta on a range . The raw ingredients can be added by selecting prepare and choosing a batta type. This creates a half made batta .
2250:

2283: A pizza base is an ingredient used to make pizza . It can be made by using either a bucket of water , bowl of water , or jug of water with a pot of flour . With a Cooking level of 35 it can be used with a tomato and cheese to make an uncooked pizza , which can then be cooked. Tomato must be added first, then cheese to make an uncooked pizza. Pizza bases can also be purchased from Tony's Pizza Bases in the Bandit Camp .
2285:
An Incomplete pizza is an item that players will usually make only intermittently whilst making a plain pizza. It is made by using a tomato with a pizza base.

As the examine text implies, players will usually use this with cheese to make an uncooked pizza, which they will then cook on a range to make a plain pizza. This requires level 35 Cooking, and is open to members and non-members.

Incomplete pizza cannot be made by adding cheese to a pizza base, as the tomato has to be put on first.
2287: Uncooked pizza requires 35 Cooking to make and is obtained by using a pizza base with tomato and cheese . It can be cooked on a range (but not a fire) into a plain pizza , which gives 143 Cooking experience. Some toppings can then be added, see the pizza page for more details. It is possible to fail the cooking, which will result in a burnt pizza .
2289:
Plain pizza is a type of pizza that restores 14 Hitpoints in total, 2 bites each healing for 7. It can be obtained by baking an uncooked pizza on a cooking range , requiring level 35 Cooking and granting 143 experience when successful. When cooking there is a chance to fail, resulting in burnt pizza . The burn rate decreases as the player's Cooking level increases, and it will stop burning entirely at Cooking level 68.

Toppings can be added to the plain pizza in order to create meat pizza ( meat or chicken ), anchovy pizza ( anchovies ), or pineapple pizza ( chunks or ring ).

2301:
Pineapple pizza is a type of pizza that restores 22 Hitpoints in total, 2 bites each healing for 11. It can be obtained by using pineapple chunks or pineapple rings on a cooked plain pizza, requiring 65 Cooking and granting 45 experience. It is recommended to cut the pineapple into rings, as this yields four rings for use on multiple pizzas, compared to the single chunk if dicing it. Pineapple pizza is one of the highest healing foods in the game and are also a type of fast food.

100 noted pineapple pizzas can be given to Yama to initiate a fight that is identical to the aether catalyst, oathplate shard, and diabolic worm acquisition contract fights, as a way to practice these fights in exchange for standard loot rolls.

A Cook in a player-owned house can make a pineapple pizza for the player.

The burnt pizza has no use whatsoever. Like most other burnt food, it is tradeable to other players but not on the Grand Exchange .
2307: Bread dough is made by mixing either a bucket of water , bowl of water , or jug of water with a pot of flour . It can be used on a range to make a loaf of bread at level 1 Cooking , granting 40 experience and healing 5 hitpoints when consumed. It is one of the most basic items used for the Cooking skill. Players will also get a pot of flour and a bucket of water to make bread dough on Tutorial Island , as a tutorial for cooking.
2309: Bread is a type of food that restores 5 Hitpoints when eaten. It can be obtained by baking bread dough on a cooking range , granting 40 experience when successful. When cooking there is a chance to fail, resulting in burnt bread . The burn rate decreases as the player's Cooking level increases. Bread is one of a number of foods with a reduced burn rate while using the Lumbridge Castle range with Cook's Assistant completed. It will stop burning entirely at Cooking level 38, or 34 when using the Lumbridge range. Bread may also be bought or stolen from the Ardougne Baker's Stall in the Ardougne marketplace.
2311:
Burnt bread is the result of accidentally burning bread dough while attempting to bake bread . The burn rate while cooking these will decrease as players reach higher Cooking levels, stopping entirely at level 38.

The burnt bread has no use whatsoever. Like most other burnt food, it is tradeable to other players but not on the Grand Exchange .
2313:
A pie dish is used in Cooking to bake pies. Players must add a pastry dough (a pot of flour and either a jug of water, a bucket of water, or a bowl of water combined) to the pie dish to form a pie shell. It then can be filled by the filling of choice. Afterwards, the pie can then be baked in an oven. Players can create this in a pottery oven.

Despite unfired pie dishes requiring 7 Crafting to make, turning an unfired pie dish into a pie dish has no Crafting requirement and can be done at level 1.
2315:
A pie shell is used to make various kinds of pie. It is made by using a pastry dough on a pie dish. Players can fill a pie shell with any of several fillings to make a raw pie which must be cooked on a range.

Possible fillings include: redberries for redberry pie, cooked meat or cooked chicken for meat pie, or cooking apple for an apple pie and many more. Members have access to a wider variety of fillings from mud pies to summer pies.
2317:
An uncooked apple pie is an uncooked food item made by using a cooking apple on a pie shell that has already had pastry dough added to it. Players need at least level 30 Cooking to make it. If successfully cooked, an apple pie provides 130 Cooking experience .

The uncooked pie can be cooked on a range (but not a fire ) to make an apple pie . However, there is a risk that the pie will burn and become a burnt pie . Like other pies, apple pies can also be cooked with the Lunar spell Bake Pie without the chance of burning.

A convenient place to make uncooked apple pies and cook them is the Cooks' Guild , which requires level 32 Cooking and a Chef's hat to enter. All of the ingredients needed to make apple pie are found around the guild, as it has 3 cooking apple spawns, a pie dish respawn, a jug respawn, a sink, a mill, wheat, and cooking ranges.
2319: An uncooked meat pie is made by adding cooked meat or cooked chicken to a pie shell . It can be cooked to make meat pie , or if unsuccessful, a Burnt pie .
2321: An Uncooked berry pie is made by adding Redberries to a Pie shell . Its cooked variant is a redberry pie .

It can be created by baking an uncooked apple pie on a cooking range , requiring level 30 Cooking and granting 130 experience when successful. When cooking there is a chance to fail, resulting in burnt pie . The burn rate decreases as the player's Cooking level increases, and it will stop burning entirely at Cooking level 63. Alternatively, casting the Bake Pie spell from the lunar spellbook will always create a pie without burning it.

Meat pie is a type of pie that restores 12 Hitpoints in total, 2 bites each healing for 6. A pie dish will remain after both bites are consumed.

It can be created by baking an uncooked meat pie on a cooking range , requiring level 20 Cooking and granting 110 experience when successful. When cooking there is a chance to fail, resulting in burnt pie . The burn rate decreases as the player's Cooking level increases. Meat pie is one of a number of foods with a reduced burn rate while using the Lumbridge Castle range with Cook's Assistant completed. It will stop burning entirely at Cooking level 54, or 49 when using the Lumbridge range. Alternatively, casting the Bake Pie spell from the lunar spellbook will always create a pie without burning it.

Meat pie is a possible task from Romily Weaklax in the Cooks' Guild . Three meat pies are given to the player when starting Nature Spirit .
2329:
Burnt pie is the result of accidentally burning any kind of pie . The burn rate while cooking pies will decrease as players reach higher Cooking levels.

The burnt pie has no use whatsoever, but it can be emptied to reclaim a pie dish . Like most other burnt food, it is tradeable to other players but not on the Grand Exchange .
2331:
Meat pie is a type of pie that restores 12 Hitpoints in total, 2 bites each healing for 6. A pie dish will remain after both bites are consumed.

It can be created by baking an uncooked meat pie on a cooking range , requiring level 20 Cooking and granting 110 experience when successful. When cooking there is a chance to fail, resulting in burnt pie . The burn rate decreases as the player's Cooking level increases. Meat pie is one of a number of foods with a reduced burn rate while using the Lumbridge Castle range with Cook's Assistant completed. It will stop burning entirely at Cooking level 54, or 49 when using the Lumbridge range. Alternatively, casting the Bake Pie spell from the lunar spellbook will always create a pie without burning it.

Meat pie is a possible task from Romily Weaklax in the Cooks' Guild . Three meat pies are given to the player when starting Nature Spirit .
2333:
Redberry pies are a type of pie that restores 10 Hitpoints in total, 2 bites each healing for 5. A pie dish will remain after both bites.

It can be created by baking an uncooked berry pie on a cooking range , requiring level 10 Cooking and granting 78 experience when successful. When cooking there is a chance to fail, resulting in burnt pie . The burn rate decreases as the player's Cooking level increases. Redberry pie is one of a number of foods with a reduced burn rate while using the Lumbridge Castle range with Cook's Assistant completed. It will stop burning entirely at Cooking level 45, or 42 when using the Lumbridge range. Alternatively, casting the Bake Pie spell from the lunar spellbook will always create a pie without burning it.

A redberry pie is required in the quests The Knight's Sword , The Giant Dwarf , and Prying Times and is a possible task from Romily Weaklax in the Cooks' Guild .
2335:
Apple pie is a type of pie that restores 14 Hitpoints in total, 2 bites each healing for 7. A pie dish will remain after both bites are consumed.

It can be created by baking an uncooked apple pie on a cooking range , requiring level 30 Cooking and granting 130 experience when successful. When cooking there is a chance to fail, resulting in burnt pie . The burn rate decreases as the player's Cooking level increases, and it will stop burning entirely at Cooking level 63. Alternatively, casting the Bake Pie spell from the lunar spellbook will always create a pie without burning it.

Apple pie is a possible task from Romily Weaklax in the Cooks' Guild . Three apple pies and three meat pies are given to the player when starting Nature Spirit .
2337:
Raw oomlie may be obtained by killing the oomlie birds found in the depths of the Kharazi Jungle , south of Shilo Village . To get into the Kharazi Jungle, the player must have started Legends' Quest . At 50 Cooking , it can be wrapped in a palm leaf to get a wrapped oomlie , which can then be cooked to get a cooked oomlie wrap .

Wrapping it in a palm leaf is required to cook it; the raw oomlie cannot be cooked on its own. Attempting to do so will always fail (even with a cooking cape ), resulting in a burnt oomlie , with the message You cook the Oomlie Meat on the fire... , and after the player burns it, "The meat is far too delicate to cook like this. Perhaps you should wrap it up to protect it from the heat."

Eating a cooked oomlie wrap is a hard task in the Karamja Diary .

Raw oomlie is sometimes given as a tip from the Gnome Restaurant minigame .
2339:
Palm leaves may be obtained by 'shaking' the leafy palm trees located around the small pool of water in the middle of the Kharazi Jungle or on Remote Island . This is a primary ingredient in the oomlie wrap made for the Karamja Hard Diary , as they protect the delicate meat of the oomlie bird from burning. This item is also used during Troubled Tortugans to craft makeshift bandages .

There is a hard Karamja Diary task to collect five palm leaves, though one can drop and pick up the same leaf multiple times to complete the task.
2340:
A Palm leaf is an unobtainable version of the Palm leaf . Palm leaves could previously be traded and turned into bank notes; however, they were made untradeable in 2007 due to frequent use in scams. Any player who had a noted palm leaf was given this now discontinued item. It is identical to the real leaf, except it is stackable.

As this change occurred prior to August 2007, the item has never been obtainable in Old School RuneScape .
2341:
Wrapped oomlies are uncooked food made from the raw oomlie and a palm leaf. If cooked, it creates a cooked oomlie wrap.

Wrapped oomlies can be cooked with a Cooking level of 50 or higher, granting 30 Cooking experience.

Cooking a raw oomlie on a fire will burn it. Attempting to do so gives the message "The meat is far too delicate to cook like this. Perhaps you should wrap something around it to protect it from the heat." To protect the raw oomlie, it must be wrapped with a palm leaf, which is obtained by shaking a leafy palm tree. There are three of these trees located near the water pool in the centre of the Kharazi Jungle. Once wrapped, oomlies will never burn except under controlled circumstances.
2343:
Cooked oomlie wrap is a food made from cooking a wrapped oomlie. It heals 14 Hitpoints when eaten, and gives the message "You eat the oomlie meat; it tastes very gamy."

Cooked oomlie wraps can be cooked with a Cooking level of 50 or higher, granting 30 Cooking experience.

Cooking a raw oomlie on a fire will always burn it. Attempting to do so gives the message "The meat is far too delicate to cook like this. Perhaps you should wrap something around it to protect it from the heat."

To protect the raw oomlie, it must be wrapped with a palm leaf, which is obtained by shaking a leafy palm tree. This creates a wrapped oomlie. There are three of these trees located near the water pool in the centre of the Kharazi Jungle. Additionally, eating an oomlie wrap is a hard task in the Karamja Diary.
2345: Burnt oomlie wrap is the result of burning a wrapped oomlie while attempting to make a cooked oomlie wrap . The burn rate while cooking these will decrease as players reach higher Cooking levels, stopping entirely at level 40 when cooking on a range and level 44 when cooking on a fire . [ 1 ]
2347:
A hammer is a tool used for smithing items on an Anvil , and it is vital to level the Smithing skill. Hammers can be bought from most general stores and will never break. Alternatively, players can obtain a hammer by talking to the Master smithing tutor at the West Varrock anvil. A hammer is also used in the Construction skill when making furniture, and it is required for some minigames. At 15 Construction, members can make a Tool store 1 for the workshop room of their house; this tool store provides an unlimited supply of hammers.

A hammer is required to access Bandos' stronghold in the God Wars Dungeon ; warhammers are an acceptable substitute.

The Imcando hammer can be used instead of a hammer when performing tasks like Construction or Smithing .
2349:
A bronze bar is a bar of refined bronze. It can be created through the Smithing skill at level 1 by using a copper ore and a tin ore on a furnace, granting 6.2 Smithing experience. A bronze bar can be smithed on an anvil through the Smithing skill to create bronze weapons and armour. A list of bronze items that can be smithed from bronze bars and the Smithing levels required can be found here. When smithed, each bar gives 12.5 experience, with a maximum of 62.5 experience given for the bronze platebody.

Members can purchase bronze bars from the Shantay Pass Shop in the Shantay Pass south of Al Kharid for 8 coins each, or from Jiminua's Jungle Store north of Tai Bwo Wannai village for 12 coins each.

4-6 bronze bars are required for quests. Observatory Quest requires 1, The Tourist Trap requires 1-3 (dependent on the luck), Prince Ali Rescue requires 1 and One Small Favour requires 1. Furthermore, Creature of Fenkenstrain and Recipe for Disaster/Freeing Pirate Pete require 3 bronze wires each, for a total of 10-12 bronze bars.
2351:
An iron bar is a bar of refined iron . It can be created through the Smithing skill at level 15 by using iron ore on a furnace , granting 12.5 Smithing experience . When smelting iron ore, there is a 50% chance that it will be too impure; it disappears, yielding no Smithing experience nor an iron bar. However, wearing a ring of forging , casting Superheat Item , or using the Blast Furnace would give a 100% success rate.

An iron bar can be smithed on an anvil through the Smithing skill to create iron weapons and armour . When smithed, each bar grants 25 experience, with a maximum of 125 being given for the iron platebody .
2353:
A Steel bar is an item used for creating steel weaponry and armour. It can be smelted using the Smithing skill at level 30 Smithing by using 1 iron ore and 2 coal on a furnace, providing 17.5 experience points. Steel bars can be used with an anvil to make steel armour and weaponry, granting 37.5 Smithing experience per bar, unless the bar is used with a furnace and cannonball mould to make steel cannonballs, granting 25.6 experience per bar instead, which is profitable experience popular among low and mid-level smiths. Steel bars are also used in the Mahogany Homes minigame.

Currently, smelting a steel bar yields a profit of 204. For players without a coal bag, the most bars one can smith at a time is 9, achieved with an inventory of 18 coal and 9 iron ore.

Steel bars can be received as monster drops from some creatures such as moss giants, fire giants and as a guaranteed drop of 5 from steel dragons.

While wearing the Varrock armour, players have a 10% chance of smelting 2 bars at once using the Edgeville furnace.
2355:
A silver bar is a bar of metal, refined through the Smithing skill by smelting a silver ore in a furnace, requiring 20 Smithing and granting 13.7 Smithing experience. It may also be bought (or stolen) from a silver merchant, such as the one in Ardougne market, or from other players.

The primary use of a silver bar is to create jewellery with the Crafting skill. To craft silver bars into jewellery players must use a silver bar on a furnace with a proper mould in their inventory. If players wish to craft jewellery with gems inset, the cut gems must be present in the player's inventory before crafting the jewellery. One silver bar is used during the Creature of Fenkenstrain quest, and another during Shadow of the Storm.

Unlike gold bars, which cannot be made into weapons, silver bars can be made into silver sickles. They can also be ground to silver dust in the Ectofuntus grinder for use as an ingredient in the guthix balance potion.

Currently, smelting a silver bar yields a profit of 41.

One effective method of gathering silver bars is exchanging reward tokens gained for completing Temple Trekking minigame. This method is commonly used by ironman players, as it can net upwards of 1000 silver bars per hour.
2357:
A gold bar is a bar of refined gold created through the Smithing skill at level 40 by using a gold ore with a furnace, or by casting Superheat Item on it. By default, this gives 22.5 Smithing experience per bar, but if the goldsmith gauntlets from the Family Crest quest are worn, the experience given is boosted to 56.2.

The primary use of gold bars is to create jewellery through the Crafting skill. To craft gold bars into jewellery, players must use a gold bar on a furnace with the proper mould in their inventory. If players wish to craft jewellery with gems inset, they must also have the respective cut gems.

Apart from jewellery, gold bars can be used to create gold helmets, used in the Between a Rock... quest, gold bowls which are used in the Legends' Quest, and the enchanted bar used in Monkey Madness I.

Through questing, a player can obtain one gold bar upon completion of the Goblin Diplomacy quest, two from the Waterfall Quest, and two from The Dig Site quest.

Using the Telekinetic Grab spell, one can obtain a gold bar and a gold ore from the basement of Varrock west bank or gold bars in the Corsair Cove Dungeon (south of the bank vault). The northernmost section of the cave at Corsair Cove (accessible after Dragon Slayer I) has an additional three gold bar spawns available without the need of Telekinetic Grab.
2359:
A Mithril bar is a bar of refined mithril ore . It can be created through the Smithing skill by using a mithril ore and 4 pieces of coal on a furnace , granting 30 experience . The Superheat Item spell can also be used to make mithril bars. Both ways of creating mithril bars require level 50 Smithing. It can also be created in the Blast Furnace , which can be considerably cheaper as it halves the amount of coal needed.

A mithril bar can be smithed on an anvil by using the Smithing skill to create mithril weapons and armour , granting 50 Smithing experience per bar used. A list of mithril items that can be smithed from mithril bars and the Smithing levels required can be found at Smithing tables.

Currently, smelting a mithril bar yields a profit of 242 in a standard furnace and 538 in the blast furnace.
2361: Adamantite bars can be smelted with 6 coal and 1 adamantite ore at level 70 Smithing . Smelting the bar grants 37.5 Smithing experience , and any item that is smithed from adamantite bars grants 62.5 Smithing experience per bar, yielding a net of 100 experience.
2363:
Runite bars are used in the Smithing skill to smith various runite weaponry and armour. At level 85 Smithing, players can smelt a runite bar by using runite ore and 8 pieces of coal with a furnace, granting 50 Smithing experience for smelting and 75 Smithing experience for smithing, yielding a net of 125 experience.

For free-to-play, apart from smelting, the chest in Bryophyta's lair is the only way of obtaining runite bars.

Three of them can be obtained occasionally when opening the crystal chest.

A runite bar is required for Song of the Elves; Ironmen may choose to offer the buyable rune platelegs to the nest on the top of the Aldarin windmill as an easy way of quickly obtaining one.
2365:
A 'perfect' gold bar is an untradeable gold bar smelted from 'perfect' gold ore. It is used in the Family Crest quest with a ruby and a necklace mould or ring mould to craft a 'perfect' necklace and 'perfect' ring respectively. It can be used as a normal gold bar when crafting any other item of jewellery, creating a normal piece of jewellery, which will not receive the prefix of 'perfect'.

Just like normal gold ore, two 'perfect' gold bars can be smelted at once at the Edgeville furnace if the appropriate tier of Varrock armour is worn.

It cannot be used to make a gold helmet or gold bowl.
2366:
The shield left half is an item that can be joined with the right half to create the dragon square shield with level 60 Smithing . Joining the right half with the left half nets 75 Smithing experience. The other half of the shield is sold by Siegfried Erkle in the Legends Guild Shop of Useful Items for 750,000 coins.

This item is a rare drop from the rare drop table . Wearing a ring of wealth will increase the chances of receiving one from the rare drop table. Goraks fought in the Gorak Plane are likely droppers of the shield left half, with a drop rate of 1/243.75 (with a ring of wealth equipped) if Fairytale II - Cure a Queen and Legends' Quest have been completed. [ 1 ] [ 2 ]

Skotizo is the monster most likely to drop the shield left half, with a drop rate of 1/100, and is the only monster to have it on its standard drop table.

The intricate pouch from Guardians of the Rift has a chance to contain the shield left half, as well as other dragon items.

Creating a dragon square shield from the two halves in West Ardougne is a hard task in the Ardougne Diary .
2368:
The shield right half is an item which can be bought in the Legends' Guild or the Myths' Guild for 750,000 coins . It can be combined with the shield left half (provided that you have 60 Smithing ) to form the dragon square shield . A hammer and anvil is needed to combine the shield.

Creating a Dragon square shield from the two halves in West Ardougne is a hard task in the Ardougne Diary .
2370: Steel studs can be smithed from a steel bar at an anvil with level 36 Smithing , granting 37.5 experience. They can then be used on leather bodies with level 41 Crafting or leather chaps with level 44 Crafting, to make studded bodies and studded chaps respectively.
2372:
An ogre relic is a quest item that appears in the Watchtower quest . During the quest, it is given as a gift to the ogre guards, who stand at the gates of Gu'Tanoth . In return, they grant the player permanent access to the city. It should also be noted from a lore point of view that upon gifting the relic to the guards, they recognise it as a statue of the ogre warrior, Dalgroth .

The player can make the ogre relic by giving the three individual pieces to the Watchtower Wizard and having him combine them, each of which is obtained by performing tasks for ogres who live in and around Gu'Tanoth . Attempting to use the pieces on each other in order to combine the pieces will only result with the game message, " The pieces look like they would fit together, but you can't work out how to do it. Maybe someone with more experience of ogres could help. "

Should the item be lost or destroyed before being given to the ogre guards near the gates of the ogre city, it can be reobtained by speaking to the Watchtower Wizard .
2373:
The relic part 1 is a quest item that appears in the Watchtower quest. When combined with Relic part 2 and Relic part 3 it forms an Ogre relic which can be used to access the ogre town of Gu'Tanoth.

To obtain Relic part 1 the player must retrieve a bar of gold that Toban stole from Og.
2374:
The relic part 2 is a quest item in the Watchtower quest. Combining it with the relic part 1 and relic part 3 makes the ogre relic required to access the ogre town of Gu'Tanoth.

To obtain it, the player must defeat Gorad and return his Ogre tooth to Grew.
2375: The relic part 3 is a quest item that appears in the Watchtower quest. When combined with Relic part 1 and Relic part 2 it forms an Ogre relic which can be used to access the ogre town of Gu'Tanoth. To obtain Relic part 3 the player must give the ogre Toban a dragon bone.
2376:
The skavid map is required to successfully navigate the Skavid caves around Gu'Tanoth. Without possession of this map, players entering into one of the Skavid caves will immediately exit the next cave entrance in a clockwise direction, the last one being next to Toban's island, before starting at the north-west cave again. Players do not need to read the map to enter the Skavid caves, only have it in their inventory.

During the Watchtower quest, you obtain the map by visiting the ogre city guards all the way at the end of the path leading into Gu'Tanoth. To obtain the map the first time, you will need a rock cake, a death rune and 20 coins to reach the city guard and buy the map. If you lose the map, you'll only need 20 coins to get back to the city guard to replace it.

After the quest, the map can be freely reobtained if lost by talking to one of the two city guards. The city guards are located next to the ogre named Keef, on top of the eastern hill next to the agility shortcut. You can access here by climbing the agility shortcut (71 Agility required), or by following the four bridges around to it, starting at the south-west of the city. Please note that if you're following the four bridges, you will once again have to pay 20 coins to cross the last bridge even with the quest finished. However, a rock cake and a death rune are no longer necessary.

A skavid map is required in order to pick cave nightshade from a skavid cave for a medium achievement in the Ardougne Diary. One can be found in the northernmost cave entrance, west of Yanille, and south of the lake with the island in it.
2377:
The ogre tooth is obtained from the corpse of Gorad when he is killed by the player during the Watchtower quest.

The player must then bring the tooth to Grew , as proof that his request for Gorad's death was fulfilled.
2378:
Toban's key is given by Og in the Watchtower quest to open the chest near Gorad. After opening the chest you will find Toban's gold and the key will be consumed.

If you should happen to destroy Toban's gold bar or lose it by any means, return to Og to be given another key and return to the chest to obtain another gold bar.
2379:
A rock cake is a strange ogre delicacy. It is a cake made of stone. Players cannot buy rock cakes from the ogres. Instead, they are stolen from the market stall in the ogre town of Gu'Tanoth . Stealing a rock cake requires a Thieving level of 15 and yields 6.5 Thieving experience.

Rock cakes cannot be gained until the relevant part of the Watchtower quest. A rock cake is required as a bribe in order to access the central parts of the Gu'Tanoth , which is necessary during the Watchtower quest. The player must give a rock cake to an ogre guard in order to be allowed to climb over a rampart that blocks the way to a rope bridge.

Rock cakes are inedible by a human . When "eaten", the player character will say, " Ow! I nearly broke a tooth! ". After this dialogue is dismissed, the player loses a fraction of their current HP, and the cake is destroyed. Using the "guzzle" option will deal twice as much damage as using the "eat" option.

Even though Ogre rock cakes can be obtained after the Watchtower quest, they aren't an optimal method of depleting one's own hitpoints; many have to be "eaten" in order to fall under 10% Hitpoints. The dwarven rock cake has similar effects when "eaten", although it won't be destroyed in the process and can be eaten again with no delay.
2380: Crystal is a quest item that appears in the Watchtower quest. As the quest opens, ogres have stolen the four crystals needed to power the watchtower and protect Yanille from invasion by the ogres. There are four crystals, each a different colour, and the player must retrieve them by performing various tasks around Gu'Tanoth .
2381: Crystal is a quest item that appears in the Watchtower quest. As the quest opens, ogres have stolen the four crystals needed to power the watchtower and protect Yanille from invasion by the ogres. There are four crystals, each a different colour, and the player must retrieve them by performing various tasks around Gu'Tanoth .
2382: Crystal is a quest item that appears in the Watchtower quest. As the quest opens, ogres have stolen the four crystals needed to power the watchtower and protect Yanille from invasion by the ogres. There are four crystals, each a different colour, and the player must retrieve them by performing various tasks around Gu'Tanoth .
2383: Crystal is a quest item that appears in the Watchtower quest. As the quest opens, ogres have stolen the four crystals needed to power the watchtower and protect Yanille from invasion by the ogres. There are four crystals, each a different colour, and the player must retrieve them by performing various tasks around Gu'Tanoth .
2384:
Fingernails is a quest item that appears in the Watchtower quest. During the quest, the player can find it by searching the bushes surrounding the Watchtower outside the north wall of Yanille .

The fingernails must be given to the wizard in the Watchtower in order for him to be able to identify who stole the power crystals that make the tower operate.

The fingernails are from a skavid , as they are also found in two of the Skavid caves. After the quest, the item can be reobtained, but it serves no purpose.
2385:
Old robe is a quest item that appears in the Watchtower quest and it can be found after the quest's completion. The player can find it by searching the bushes surrounding the Watchtower outside the north wall of Yanille .

This item serves no purpose and is most likely there as a red herring. It cannot be worn.
2386: Unusual armour is a quest item found during the Watchtower quest. Players can find it by searching the bushes surrounding the Watchtower outside the north wall of Yanille , even after the quest is complete. It serves no purpose during the quest and is merely a red herring. It cannot be worn.
2387:
The damaged dagger is a quest item that appears in the Watchtower quest and it can be found after the quest's completion. The player can find it by searching the bushes surrounding the Watchtower outside the north wall of Yanille . It serves no purpose during the quest and is there as a red herring.

While it cannot be used as a weapon, it can be used to slash webs.
2388: The tattered eye patch is a quest item that appears in the Watchtower quest and it can be found after the quest's completion. Players can find it by searching the bushes surrounding the Watchtower outside the north wall of Yanille . It serves no purpose during the quest, and it cannot be worn.
2389:
A Vial is made in the Watchtower Quest by adding jangerberries to a vial of water .

Adding a guam leaf will cause the potion to explode, dealing 5 damage to the player, destroying the items, and printing the message You mixed the ingredients incorrectly and the mixture exploded. . The jangerberries must be added to an unfinished guam potion to create a vial containing the berry and herb mixture .

The mixture can be created after completing the quest; however, it has no further use.
2390:
A Vial is made in the Watchtower quest by adding a jangerberries to an unfinished guam potion . After adding ground bat bones , it can be enchanted by the Watchtower Wizard to make a Magic ogre potion . Adding a guam to a vial of jangerberries instead will cause the potion to explode and deal 5 damage.

The mixture can be created after completing the quest; however, it has no further use.
2391: Ground bat bones is an item used in the Watchtower quest and in the Herblore skill. They are made by using a pestle and mortar on bat bones. Provided that the player has level 14 Herblore, when combined with a Guam potion (unf) it will explode (dealing 5 damage), and will leave the empty vial only. Should the player have their hitpoints less than 8, it will not kill them and will deal less than 5 damage. Additionally, when the item is combined with a vial of water, the water will evaporate followed by a dialogue box with the player saying, "Oh dear, the mixture has evaporated." This also leaves an empty vial. The item can be created before, during, and after the quest; however, it serves no purpose outside of the quest.
2393: Toban's gold is a bar of gold stolen from Og by his nemesis, Toban. The player must recover this item from Toban as part of the Watchtower quest. This is a unique gold bar, and Og will not accept a gold bar created by normal use of the Smithing skill.
2394:
The potion is a quest item that is created during the Watchtower quest. It is used to kill the ogre shaman that lives in the caves below Gu'Tanoth .

To make the potion the player must mix guam leaf , jangerberries , and ground bat bones into a vial of water . This specific order must be followed or the potion will explode, damaging the player. Then, it needs to be enchanted by the Watchtower Wizard , to turn it into a Magic ogre potion . This item will disappear when dropped. Before dropping the item, it will ask for confirmation, stating: "This item will likely break if you put it down here, and you will have to go looking for another."

The mixture can be created after completing the quest; however, it has no further use. Additionally, using the potion on the Watchtower Wizard will result in the wizard taking the item, stating that it is too dangerous and may cause an injury.

Mixing the ground bat bones into the vial (jangerberries and guam leaf) to create the potion prints the message You mix the ground bones into the liquid. , followed by You produce a strong potion. .
2395:
The magic ogre potion is a quest item in the Watchtower quest . It is used to kill ogre shamans in the Ogre Enclave below Gu'Tanoth .

It is made by adding to a vial of water a guam leaf , jangerberries , and ground bat bones , in that order, and then bringing the resulting potion to the Watchtower Wizard to enchant. Making the potion requires 14 Herblore . This item will disappear when dropped. Before dropping the item, it will ask for confirmation, stating: "This item will likely break if you put it down here, and you will have to go looking for another."

Using the potion to kill the ogre shamans during the quest requires 14 Magic . After using it to kill the last Ogre shaman it will become an empty vial . The magic ogre potion cannot be made after the quest, and if one is brought to the Watchtower Wizard, he will confiscate the potion, claiming it is too dangerous.
2396: Spell scroll is a scroll that you receive as a reward from the quest, Watchtower. When read, the player learns the Watchtower Teleport (requires level 58 Magic). If a player loses the scroll before use, they can speak to the Watchtower Wizard. The player may learn the spell even without the requirement of level 58 Magic to use it. The drop trick may be performed to obtain multiple scrolls, allowing the player to 'learn' this spell multiple times.
2397: The shaman robe is an item that can be found during or after the Watchtower Quest on the ground inside the Ogre Enclave. The robe cannot be worn. It only serves for the purpose of retrieving the cyan crystal if during the quest the player has lost it. The crystal can be found by searching the robe. After doing so, it has no other use and it can be safely dropped.
2398:
Cave nightshade , also known as cave belladonna , is used in Herblore to make weapon poison(++) or as an addition to dynamite for poison dynamite .

Players can eat nightshade, but this is not recommended in most situations. When eaten, the player will say, "Ahhhh! What have I done!" and take up to 15 damage (damage taken scales with the player's current Hitpoints ). Like most self-damaging items, it is impossible for the player to kill themselves with it. ( Note: It is possible for players to eat this without losing health; if the player were to accidentally eat the nightshade, they can teleport away to avoid losing any hitpoints, provided they don't click "Continue" on the dialogue text.)

Damage taken is given by the following formula:

D a m a g e ( H i t p o i n t s ) = { 15 , if H i t p o i n t s ≥ 20 ⌊ H i t p o i n t s 2 ⌋ if H i t p o i n t s < 20

There are two spawns in the Skavid caves by the ogre city Gu'Tanoth south of Yanille : the northern-most cave entrance, just south of the western entrance to Yanille, and the southern-most cave entrance within the city of Gu'Tanoth across a bridge. The skavid map (obtained during the Watchtower quest ) and a light source are needed to enter these caves. These spawns can be picked up without wearing gloves or gauntlets and respawn about every 54 seconds. Collecting a cave nightshade from one of these spawns is a task in the medium Ardougne Diary . The Reagent pouch does NOT hold Cave nightshade, saying "You can't possibly put that in there. It would spoil your pouch."
2399:
Silverlight key is one of the three keys needed to unlock Silverlight from its sealed casing during the Demon Slayer quest. At the start of the quest, this key is in the possession of a wizard named Traiborn , who is residing at the 1 st floor [ UK ] 2 nd floor [ US ] of the Wizards' Tower .

Traiborn will ask the player for 25 bones in order for him to summon his secret wardrobe (Examine reads, "A wardrobe brought forth by magic"), which contains this key. Once he summons his wardrobe, Traiborn will hand over this key to the player.

Should players lose it again, they must bring another 25 bones.
2400:
Silverlight key is one of the three keys needed to open the three locks of the sealed box which contains the sword Silverlight , a crucial item in the quest Demon Slayer . It is acquired from Captain Rovin after the player has started the quest and has asked Sir Prysin for the location of the keys. This key is the easiest of the three to acquire. Captain Rovin is on the topmost tower on the west side of the castle. Choose the correct phrases to say, then Captain Rovin will give the key. Select the option that says "Sir Prysin said you would give me the key" and then select the option that says "Then why did he give you the key?" After bringing up Sir Prysin's clumsiness he will hand it to you. It will take some arguing, though.

If destroyed, the player has to repeat the entire dialogue to obtain another one.
2401:
Silverlight key is one of the three keys needed to unlock Silverlight from its sealed casing during the Demon Slayer quest. During the start of the quest the player learns that Sir Prysin dropped his key down a drain. Using a bucket of water on the drain outside of the Varrock Palace kitchen will make the key fall down into Varrock Sewers .

This key unlike the other Silverlight keys is rusted, most likely due to it being stuck in the drain for a long time.

If destroyed, the player has to use another bucket of water on the drain to make a new key spawn in the sewers.
2402:
Silverlight is a magical sword used in Demon Slayer and Shadow of the Storm . It is a demonbane sword that is very effective against demonic creatures. As it is a silver weapon , it is also effective against most vampyres . It is obtained by bringing the three Silverlight keys to Sir Prysin during Demon Slayer.

In Demon Slayer, it is used to defeat Delrith . In Shadow of the Storm, it is dyed black using black dye , and later transforms into Darklight when it gets stained with the blood of Agrith-Naar .

It can be mounted on the wall in the quest hall of a player-owned house .
2403: The Hazeel scroll is a scroll containing the incantation used to free Hazeel in the evil side of the Hazeel Cult quest. The scroll is located up in a secret room on the 2nd floor of the Carnillean Mansion in a locked chest which can only be opened with a chest key. It is used by Alomone to reconstruct Hazeel's body.
2404: The Chest key is a key found during the Hazeel Cult quest . It is located in the basement of the Carnillean Mansion in Ardougne . It opens the chest in the secret room, which gives the player the scroll needed to revive Hazeel . This key is no longer needed after the quest and may be safely dropped.
2405: Carnillean armour is obtainable only during Ceril 's side of the Hazeel Cult quest by killing Alomone and looting the nearby chest. It is possible to get multiple armour pieces by looting the chest multiple times. Carnillean requires a Defence level of 1 to wear but has lower defensive bonuses than the iron platebody . Some mages or archers may wish to use Carnillean armour due to it not lowering magic or ranged attacks. This piece of armour will not interfere with Ava's devices .
2406:
Hazeel's mark is a quest item from the quest Hazeel Cult. The item is only obtained when you choose Hazeel's side. It does not give any stat bonuses and is not used in any other quests.

If lost, Hazeel's mark can be reclaimed from Clivet. Multiple marks can be obtain using the drop trick.
2407:
The ball is a quest item used only in Witch's House . It is found in the shed of Nora T. Hagg 's garden and can be picked up after killing the witch's experiment .

It is returned to the boy to complete the quest.

Duplicates cannot be obtained. If players try to use Telekinetic Grab on the ball, the message I can't reach that! will appear in the chatbox; therefore they must fight the experiment to retrieve it. Players may re-enter the shed to fight the experiment again, but they cannot take a duplicate ball. If they try to, they will receive the message: You already have the boys ball... [ sic ]

After completing the quest, the ball can still be seen in the shed once it has respawned, but cannot be retrieved. This is because Nora's garden becomes inaccessible after the quest; attempting to open the door to her house will result in the chatbox message: It would be rude to break into this house.

If the player somehow manages to have a second ball on the ground outside the witch's house and tries to pick it up after the quest, the game will give the message, " Another ball! The witch must have found another one. You decide to leave this one here. "
2408:
The witch's diary is a quest item used only in Witch's House . It is found on the desk on the ground floor [ UK ] 1 st floor [ US ] of Nora T. Hagg 's house.

It reveals information on some of the witch's experiments, giving the player clues on how to get into the back yard and what to expect during the fight.

Before starting Grim Tales , it only includes entries up to the 9th of Pentember, afterwards additional days are revealed upon progressing through Grim Tales .

Duplicates can be obtained during the quest, but it serves no further use. It can be found in the bookcases of the player's house .
2409:
The Door key is a quest item used in Witch's House , Grim Tales , and Mourning's End Part II . It is found by searching under a potted plant left of the front door of the witch's house in Taverley . Additionally, another key spawns on the 1 st floor [ UK ] 2 nd floor [ US ] of Nora T. Hagg 's house. In Grim Tales , a key may be obtained from Princess Miazrqa after Rupert has been freed.

In Witch's House and Grim Tales, it is used to open the front door of Nora T. Hagg's house. In Mourning's End Part II, it may be needed to obtain the death talisman .

Duplicates can be obtained during the quest. This key cannot be added to a key ring . If the message You didn't find anything interesting. appeared, then a player may need to start the quest first by talking to the Boy south of the house or the key may be in the player's inventory or bank.
2410:
The magnet is a quest item used only in Witch's House . It is found in a cupboard in the basement of the witch's house behind an electrified gate .

It is used on the back of a mouse to unlock the elaborate locking mechanism on the door into her garden.

Duplicates can be drop tricked by searching the cupboard to obtain another, but it serves no further use.
2411:
The key is a quest item used during the Witch's House quest to open the shed door and retrieve the ball. It is found by searching the fountain in Nora T. Hagg's garden.

Duplicates can be drop tricked by searching the fountain to obtain another. This key cannot be added to a steel key ring.
2412:
The Saradomin cape is a reward from Mage Arena I miniquest . To receive the cape, the player must defeat Kolodion in his four guises, then speak to him, step through the nearby sparkling pool, and finally pray at the Statue of Saradomin . Upon praying at the statue, the Saradomin cape will appear next to the player and can be picked up.

The Saradomin cape and the Saradomin staff are required to benefit from the Charge spell, which enables the player to hit up to 50% more damage with the Saradomin Strike spell.

Once lost, a player can get a new cape by once again praying at the statue of Saradomin. Kolodion does not have to be fought again. Alternatively, players can purchase one from Perdu for 23,000 coins (although this requires the player obtain the cape at least once from the Mage Arena).

The Saradomin cape can be imbued with the items dropped by Justiciar Zachariah , Porazdir , and Derwen , during the Mage Arena II miniquest to make an imbued Saradomin cape . Subsequent imbues will require only the Justiciar's hand .

The Saradomin cape can be combined with the max cape to change its appearance by turning it into the Saradomin max cape .
2413:

The Guthix cape can be imbued with the items dropped by Justiciar Zachariah , Porazdir , and Derwen , during the Mage Arena II miniquest to make an imbued Guthix cape . Subsequent imbues will require only the ent's roots .

The Guthix cape can be combined with the max cape to change its appearance by turning it into the Guthix max cape .
2414:

The Zamorak cape can be imbued with the items dropped by Justiciar Zachariah, Porazdir, and Derwen, during the Mage Arena II miniquest to make an imbued Zamorak cape. Subsequent imbues will require only the Demon's heart.

The Zamorak cape can be combined with the max cape to change its appearance by turning it into the Zamorak max cape.

This item can be stored in the cape rack of a costume room.
2415:
The Saradomin staff is a god staff that can only be obtained by finishing the Mage Arena minigame. Like the other God staves, this staff requires level 60 Magic to acquire and therefore wield. To get it, the player must defeat Kolodion the mage in all of his forms. Afterwards, they will have to pick a god to worship to receive a cape and the staff corresponding to that god. If the player has already chosen another god, the staff can be purchased from the Chamber Guardian for 80,000 coins.

The staff allows wielders to cast the Saradomin Strike spell, which must be cast 100 times inside the Mage Arena minigame to gain the ability to use it outside of the arena. The spell can deal a maximum of 20 damage. Saradomin Strike lowers the target's Prayer level by one point on each successful cast.
2416:
The Guthix staff is a god staff that can only be obtained by finishing Mage Arena I miniquest. Like the other God staves, this staff requires level 60 Magic to acquire and therefore wield. To get it, the player must defeat Kolodion the mage in all of his forms. Afterwards, they will have to pick a god to worship to receive a cape and the staff corresponding to that god. If the player has already chosen another god, the staff can be purchased from the Chamber Guardian for 80,000 coins.

The staff allows wielders to cast the Claws of Guthix spell, which must be cast 100 times inside the Mage Arena minigame to gain the ability to use it outside of the arena. The spell has a chance to lower the opponent's defence by 5% on a successful hit, which does not stack with subsequent hits and will not re-occur until the opponents defence has returned to their original level. The spell can also be temporarily powered up by casting the Charge spell first.
2417:
The Zamorak staff is a god staff aligned with Zamorak, obtainable after completing Mage Arena I miniquest by defeating Kolodion. Like the other God staves, this staff requires 60 Magic to acquire and wield.

After the miniquest, players pick a god to worship to receive a god cape and the god staff corresponding to that god. If a different god is chosen, the staff can be purchased from the chamber guardian for 80,000 coins. This staff and corresponding runes are required to cast Flames of Zamorak from the standard spellbook.
2418:
The bronze key is made by giving a key print and a bronze bar to Osman or by using the same items on any furnace, and it is collected from Leela during Prince Ali Rescue to open the cell door to Prince Ali.

Should players lose the key, they must pay 15 coins to reclaim it from Leela.
2419:
The wig is an item used in the Prince Ali Rescue quest. Ned creates it if three balls of wool are given to him. A yellow dye can be used on a grey wig to turn it blonde. The player may ask Ned to create as many as they want.

The wig is one of the necessary items to disguise Prince Ali as Lady Keli, as part of the rescue operation.

The wig is removed from the inventory after talking to Prince Ali.
2420:
"Brass monkey" was the name originally given to an unobtainable item that exists in the game cache. It was created to replace the noted form of the dyed wig from Prince Ali Rescue . Since items could not be fully removed once created, it was added in a hidden update in 2005 to fill this slot. The actual item was just a copy of a pink skirt.

If players attempted to view the brass monkey in game by using cheating software, they would be given a Hex edit detected instead.

In RuneScape 2 , the item later became viewable via Quick Chat, causing much confusion. It was deleted from the game cache in 2017, being replaced by Buchu seeds .
2421:
