The wig is one of the necessary items to disguise Prince Ali as Lady Keli, as part of the rescue operation.

The wig is removed from the inventory after talking to Prince Ali.
2422:
"Skull" was the name originally given to an unobtainable item that exists in the game cache. It was created to replace the noted form of the plain wig from Prince Ali Rescue. Since items could not be fully removed once created, it was added in a hidden update in 2005 to fill this slot. The actual item was just a copy of a pink skirt.

If players attempted to view the skull in game by using cheating software, they would be given a hex edit detected instead.

It was deleted from the game cache in 2005, being replaced by the unobtainable blue partyhat seen in the Draynor Bank Robbery.
2423:
A key print is a quest item in the Prince Ali Rescue quest . It is obtained by pressing Lady Keli 's cell key into soft clay . The key print is used to make a bronze key that unlocks the cell door.

If lost, you must speak to Lady Keli again with soft clay , pink skirt , paste , and a dyed yellow wig in your inventory to obtain a new key print.
2424:
Paste is a quest item used in Prince Ali Rescue to disguise Prince Ali so he can escape from Lady Keli's prison.

Aggie can make it from ashes, redberries, flour, and water for free.
2425: Vorkath's head is an unobtainable item released with Dragon Slayer II.
2426:
Burnt oomlie is the result of burning a raw oomlie . This requires 50 Cooking , but unless it is wrapped in a palm leaf first, it will always be burnt.

The burnt oomlie has no use whatsoever. Like most other burnt food, it is tradeable to other players but not on the Grand Exchange .
2428:
An attack potion is a potion made by using an eye of newt on a guam potion (unf) , requiring 3 Herblore , yielding an attack potion(3) and 25 Herblore experience . It is the first available potion to make with the Herblore skill. A dose of attack potion provides a temporary skill boost to Attack equal to 3 + 10% of the player's current Attack level, rounded down. This is less than the super attack 's boost of 5 + 15% of the player's current Attack level, rounded down.

After Barbarian Herblore Training , roe or caviar can be added to an attack potion(2), requiring 4 Herblore, yielding an attack mix and 8 Herblore experience. An attack mix has 2 doses, boosts Attack equal to 3 + 10% of the player's current Attack level, rounded down, and heals 3 Hitpoints per dose.
2430:
A restore potion is a potion made by using red spiders' eggs on a harralander potion (unf) , requiring 22 Herblore , yielding a restore potion(3) and 62.5 Herblore experience . A dose of restore potion restores levels of temporarily reduced stats in Attack , Strength , Defence , Ranged , and Magic equal to 10 + 30% of the related maximum level, rounded down, for each skill. It does not restore Prayer points or any other skill that is not listed like a super restore . Restore potions will not boost any skill above its base level, even if the listed restore is greater than the current reduction.

After partial completion of the In Aid of the Myreque quest , garlic can be added to a restore potion(3), requiring 22 Herblore, yielding a Guthix balance (unf) and 25 Herblore experience.

After Barbarian Herblore Training , roe or caviar can be added to a restore potion(2), requiring 24 Herblore, yielding a Restore mix and 21 Herblore experience. A restore mix has 2 doses, restores the listed stats equal to 10 + 30% of the related current level, rounded down, for each skill, and heals 3 Hitpoints .

A restore potion(4) is a reward from Jekyll and Hyde random events if a harralander is given to Dr Jekyll.
2432:
A Defence potion is a potion made by using white berries on a ranarr potion (unf) , requiring 30 Herblore , yielding a Defence potion(3) and 75 Herblore experience . A dose of Defence potion provides a temporary skill boost to Defence equal to 3 + 10% of the player's current Defence level, rounded down. This is less than the super Defence 's boost of 5 + 15% of the player's current Defence level, rounded down.

After Barbarian Herblore Training , caviar can be added to a Defence potion(2), requiring 33 Herblore, yielding a Defence mix and 25 Herblore experience. A Defence mix has 2 doses, boosts Defence equal to 3 + 10% of the player's current Defence level, rounded down, and heals 6 Hitpoints .

A Defence potion(3) can be purchased from the Warrior Guild Potion Shop for 144 coins.

A Defence potion(4) is a reward from Jekyll and Hyde random events if a toadflax is given to Dr Jekyll.

A Defence potion (3) or (4) is used in the A Kingdom Divided quest.
2434:
A Prayer potion is a potion made by using snape grass on a ranarr potion (unf), requiring 38 Herblore, yielding a Prayer potion(3) and 87.5 Herblore experience. A dose of Prayer potion restores Prayer points equal to 7 + 25% of the player's current Prayer level, rounded down. If a Prayer cape, Max cape or ring of the gods (i) is equipped or a Prayer cape, Max cape or holy wrench is in the player's inventory, the restore increases to 7 + 27% of the player's current Prayer level, rounded down. It provides less Prayer point restoration than a super restore potion by 1 point per dose.

Prayer potions are always in high demand due to use of Prayers during combat or skilling activities and a need to restore points without travelling to an altar.

After Barbarian Herblore Training, caviar can be added to a Prayer potion(2), requiring 42 Herblore, yielding a Prayer mix and 29 Herblore experience. A Prayer mix has 2 doses, restores Prayer by the same amounts, and heals 6 Hitpoints.
2436:
A super attack is a potion made by using an eye of newt on an irit potion (unf), requiring 45 Herblore, yielding a super attack(3) and 100 Herblore experience. A dose of super attack provides a temporary skill boost to Attack equal to 5 + 15% of the player's current Attack level, rounded down.

Super attacks along with super strengths are popular for player killing, bossing, Slayer, or melee training.

Crystal dust may be added to super attack, 1 dust per dose of potion, to make a divine super attack potion, requiring 70 Herblore.

A super attack(4), super defence(4), super strength(4), and a torstol can be combined to make a super combat potion, requiring 90 Herblore.

After Barbarian Herblore Training, caviar can be added to a super attack(2), requiring 47 Herblore, yielding a superattack mix and 33 Herblore experience. A superattack mix has 2 doses, boosts Attack equal to 5 + 15% of the player's current Attack level, rounded down, and heals 6 Hitpoints.

A super attack(4) is a reward from Jekyll and Hyde random events if an avantoe is given to Dr Jekyll.
2438:
A Fishing potion is a potion made by using snape grass on an avantoe potion (unf) , requiring 50 Herblore , yielding a Fishing potion(3) and 112.5 Herblore experience . A dose of Fishing potion provides a temporary skill boost to Fishing of +3. It can be stored in a tackle box .

After Barbarian Herblore Training , caviar can be added to a Fishing potion(2), requiring 53 Herblore, yielding a Fishing mix and 38 Herblore experience. A Fishing mix has 2 doses, boosts Fishing by 3, and heals 6 Hitpoints .
2440:
A super strength is a potion made by using a limpwurt root on a kwuarm potion (unf) , requiring 55 Herblore , yielding a super strength(3) and 125 Herblore experience . A dose of super strength provides a temporary skill boost to Strength equal to 5 + 15% of the player's current Strength level, rounded down.

Super strength along with super attacks are popular for player killing , bossing , Slayer , or melee training . The dragon battleaxe special may be preferable for melee training because it provides a similar boost while being much cheaper in the long run.

Crystal dust may be added to super strength, 1 dust per dose of potion, to make a divine super strength potion , requiring 70 Herblore.

A super strength(4), super attack(4) , super defence(4) , and a torstol can be combined to make a super combat potion , requiring 90 Herblore.

After Barbarian Herblore Training , caviar can be added to a super strength(2), requiring 59 Herblore, yielding a super str. mix and 42 Herblore experience. A super str. mix has 2 doses, boosts Strength equal to 5 + 15% of the player's current Strength level, rounded down, and heals 6 Hitpoints .
2442:
A super defence is a potion made by using white berries on a cadantine potion (unf), requiring 66 Herblore, yielding a super defence(3) and 150 Herblore experience. A dose of super defence provides a temporary skill boost to Defence equal to 5 + 15% of the player's current Defence level, rounded down.

Crystal dust may be added to super defence, 1 dust per dose of potion, to make a divine super defence potion, requiring 70 Herblore.

A super defence(4), super attack(4), super strength(4), and a torstol can be combined to make a super combat potion, requiring 90 Herblore.

After Barbarian Herblore Training, caviar can be added to a super defence(2), requiring 71 Herblore, yielding a super def. mix and 50 Herblore experience. A super def. mix has 2 doses, boosts Defence equal to 5 + 15% of the player's current Defence level, rounded down, and heals 6 Hitpoints.

A super defence(4) is a reward from Jekyll and Hyde random events if a lantadyme is given to Dr Jekyll.

Creating a super defence in the Fremennik Province is a requirement for completing the hard Fremennik Diary.
2444:
A ranging potion is a potion made by using a wine of Zamorak on a dwarf weed potion (unf) , requiring 72 Herblore , yielding a ranging potion(3) and 162.5 Herblore experience . A dose of ranging potion provides a temporary skill boost to Ranged equal to 4 + 10% of the player's current Ranged level, rounded down, and will wear off at a rate of 1 level every 60 seconds (90 with preserve).

Crystal dust may be added to ranging potion, 1 dust per dose of potion, to make a divine ranging potion , requiring 74 Herblore.

After Barbarian Herblore Training , caviar can be added to a ranging potion(2), requiring 80 Herblore, yielding a ranging mix and 54 Herblore experience. A ranging mix has 2 doses, boosts Ranged equal to 4 + 10% of the player's current Ranged level, rounded down, and heals 6 Hitpoints .
2446:
An antipoison is a potion made by using unicorn horn dust on a marrentill potion (unf) , requiring 5 Herblore , yielding an antipoison(3) and 37.5 Herblore experience . A dose of antipoison cures poison and provides immunity to poison for 90 seconds. Drinking two doses of antipoison will cure venom . The first dose will reduce the venom to poison and the second will remove the poison.

The next cheapest alternative, superantipoison , cures poison and provides immunity for 6 minutes.

After Barbarian Herblore Training , roe or caviar can be added to an antipoison(2), requiring 6 Herblore, yielding an antipoison mix and 12 Herblore experience. An antipoison mix has 2 doses, cures poison and provides immunity to poison for 90 seconds, and heals 3 Hitpoints .
2448:
A superantipoison is a potion made by using unicorn horn dust on an irit potion (unf) , requiring 48 Herblore , yielding a superantipoison(3) and 106.3 Herblore experience . A dose of superantipoison cures poison and provides poison immunity for 6 minutes. Drinking two doses of superantipoison will cure venom . The first dose will reduce the venom to poison and the second will remove the poison.

A superantipoison(1) can be found in the southern most collapsed building north-east of the Observatory , near the entrance to the Observatory Dungeon with a respawn time of 55 seconds.

Creating a superantipoison from scratch in the Seers' Village / Catherby area is a requirement for the medium Kandarin Diary .

After Barbarian Herblore Training is completed, caviar can be added to a superantipoison(2) to produce an anti-poison supermix . This requires 51 Herblore and provides 35 Herblore experience. An anti-poison supermix has 2 doses, each of which heals 6 Hitpoints in addition to the normal superantipoison immunity.
2450:
A Zamorak brew is a potion made by using jangerberries on a torstol potion (unf), requiring 78 Herblore, yielding a Zamorak brew(3) and 175 Herblore experience. A dose of Zamorak brew provides a temporary skill boost to Attack equal to 2 + 20% of the player's base Attack level, rounded down, and Strength equal to 2 + 12% of the player's base Strength level, rounded down. It temporarily lowers Defence equal to 2 + 10% of the player's current Defence level, rounded down, and current Hitpoints by 12%, rounded down, though it will not lower a player's Hitpoints below the minimum of 1. Additionally, 10% of the player's current Prayer level is restored as Prayer points. When used in conjunction with a Saradomin brew, Attack and Defence will be boosted, Prayer and Health will be restored (possibly boosted by the brew), Ranged and Magic will be lowered.

Restore potions are frequently used with Zamorak brews to raise lowered Defence. A super strength potion will always boost Strength level higher than a Zamorak brew; however, the Zamorak brew's Attack boost is slightly better than a super attack potion. At levels 85, 86, 90-93, and 95-99, the Zamorak brew will give a boost of 2 levels more than a Super attack potion. You can also use a super strength potion or a dragon battleaxe special attack before you sip a dose to increase your Strength level to the max.

After Barbarian Herblore Training is completed, caviar can be added to a Zamorak brew(2) to produce a Zamorak mix. This requires 85 Herblore and provides 58 Herblore experience. A Zamorak mix has 2 doses, each of which heals 6 Hitpoints in addition to the usual Zamorak brew behaviour.

At level 99 Prayer, Zamorak brews cost 15.98 per Prayer point restored.
2452:
An antifire potion provides slight immunity to a dragon's breath . When used in conjunction with an anti-dragon shield or dragonfire shield , a single dose will provide complete immunity against dragonfire for 6 minutes. It can be made by a player with 69 Herblore by mixing clean lantadyme and then dragon scale dust in a vial of water , which grants 157.5 Herblore experience. It may only be used after starting Dragon Slayer I . Additionally, it can be upgraded to either an extended or super antifire by adding lava scale shards with 84 Herblore or crushed superior dragon bones with 92 Herblore, respectively.

Players will get a warning in their chatbox when the potion is about to wear off after approximately 5 minutes, 45 seconds: " Your antifire potion is about to expire. " Then they will get another message when it has worn off, approximately 6 minutes in total: " Your antifire potion has expired. " This allows you to keep track of how long you have until you have to drink again.

Protect from Magic , in conjunction with an antifire or extended antifire, may be used in place of an anti-dragon shield or dragonfire shield to grant complete immunity to close-range dragonfire attacks, such as those from chromatic dragons . Using Protect from Magic does not provide any dragonfire protection from the long-range dragonfire attacks of metal dragons , such as mithril or rune dragons , and an anti-dragon shield or dragonfire shield must be used for complete immunity.

It can reduce the damage from Cerberus ' lava pool attack if combined with other sources of dragonfire resist. [ 1 ]

Warning : Players should remember that an antifire potion alone will not fully protect them from dragonfire (players will get a message in their text box stating that they have been horribly burnt by the fire). The potion's protection is so slight that, when used alone, even a single dragon can cause extensive damage to the player from its breath. Only when the potion is combined with the anti-dragon shield or dragonfire shield will players be completely immune to dragonfire.

Protect from Magic , in conjunction with an antifire or extended antifire, may be used in place of an anti-dragon shield or dragonfire shield to grant complete immunity to close-range dragonfire attacks, such as those from chromatic dragons . Using Protect from Magic does not provide any dragonfire protection from the long-range dragonfire attacks of metal dragons , such as mithril or rune dragons , and an anti-dragon shield or dragonfire shield must be used for complete immunity.

It can reduce the damage from Cerberus ' lava pool attack if combined with other sources of dragonfire resist. [ 1 ]

Warning : Players should remember that an antifire potion alone will not fully protect them from dragonfire (players will get a message in their text box stating that they have been horribly burnt by the fire). The potion's protection is so slight that, when used alone, even a single dragon can cause extensive damage to the player from its breath. Only when the potion is combined with the anti-dragon shield or dragonfire shield will players be completely immune to dragonfire.

Assorted flowers are a type of flower that can be harvested after planting mithril or adamant seeds .

When planting the seeds, players have an option to either pick the flowers (and obtaining a random coloured flower) or leave them planted on the ground. A player only has one chance to pick their flowers; if they refuse to do so, they will not get the option again unless they plant another seed. Flowers that are left on the ground will stay there temporarily for around 5 minutes.

Flowers can be wielded in the weapon slot , and are classified as a fun weapon in legacy duels within the Emir's Arena because it gives the wielding player negative bonuses.

"Firestarter" was the name originally given to an unobtainable item that exists in the game cache. It was created to replace the noted form of ground charcoal. Since items could not be fully removed once created, it was added in a hidden update in 2005 to fill this slot. The actual item was just a copy of a pink skirt.

If players attempted to view the firestarter in game by using cheating software, they would be given a hex edit detected instead.

In RuneScape 2, the item later became viewable via Quick Chat, causing much confusion. It was deleted from the game cache in 2017.
2481:
Lantadyme is a high level herb requiring a Herblore level of 67 to clean. It is obtained by cleaning grimy lantadyme which can be grown from a lantadyme seed with a Farming level of 73.

Lantadymes are used to make anti-fire potions (with ground blue dragon scales) and magic potions (with potato cactus). To create a potion, you need to add the cleaned herb to a vial of water to create a lantadyme potion (unf), and then add the secondary ingredient.
2483: A lantadyme potion (unf) is an unfinished potion made by using a lantadyme on a vial of water, requiring 69 Herblore. Using dragon scale dust on a lantadyme potion (unf) with 69 Herblore yields an antifire potion (3) and 157.5 Herblore experience. Using a potato cactus on a lantadyme potion (unf) with 76 herblore yields a magic potion (3) and 172.5 Herblore experience.
2485: A grimy lantadyme is a herb that has not yet been cleaned to make a lantadyme . Grimy lantadymes may be grown from a lantadyme seed with a Farming level of 73. It is also dropped by certain NPCs . Cleaning a grimy lantadyme requires a Herblore level of 67 and gives 13.1 Herblore experience. Clean lantadymes are used to make antifire potions and Magic potion with a Herblore level of 69 and 76 respectively. When planting and harvesting lantadymes you will receive 134 experience for planting, and 151.5 experience for harvesting.

Kebbit claws can be used on these vambraces to make blue spiky vambraces , requiring a Crafting level of 32.

A blue d'hide body is a piece of blue dragonhide armour worn in the body slot. It is crafted by using 3 blue dragon leather and a needle and thread with level 71 Crafting . To wear a blue d'hide body, a player must have a Ranged level of 50 and a Defence level of 40.

Although players must complete Dragon Slayer I in order to wear the green d'hide body , completion of this quest is not required to equip the blue, red , and black dragonhide bodies.
2501:
A red d'hide body is red dragonhide armour equipped in the body slot, requiring 60 Ranged and 40 Defence.

Although the Dragon Slayer I quest must be completed to equip the green d'hide body, it is not required to equip the blue d'hide body, red d'hide body, or black d'hide body.
2503:
Black d'hide body is a part of the black dragonhide armour set. It requires at least level 70 Ranged and 40 Defence to be worn.

It is the strongest standard dragonhide body and is among the most resilient armours against Magic damage. However, Blessed dragonhide armour provides higher defensive stats while maintaining the same offensive stats.

Due to its effectiveness relative to its low cost, it is a very commonly used piece of armour in the Wilderness , however not as ubiquitous as it used to be since the stats were reduced.

Although players must complete Dragon Slayer I in order to wear the green d'hide body , completion of this quest is not required to equip the blue , red , or black dragonhide bodies.
2505: Blue dragon leather is used in the Crafting skill to make blue dragonhide armour. Players can obtain it by taking a blue dragonhide (a drop from blue dragons) and 20 coins to a tanner, or 45 coins for the Canifis tanner. Tanners can be found in Al Kharid, the Crafting Guild, the Ranging Guild, Canifis, the Forthos Dungeon, and Auburnvale. Crafting any piece of blue dragonhide armour will grant the player 70 experience per hide.
2507: Red dragon leather is used in the Crafting skill to make red dragonhide armour. It can be created by giving a red dragonhide and 20 coins to a tanner. Tanners can be found in Al Kharid, the Ranging Guild, Canifis, Forthos Dungeon, Crafting Guild, Kebos Lowlands, and Auburnvale. The last two tanners require the completion of Getting Ahead and children of the Sun, respectively. Alternatively, red dragon leather can be made using the Tan Leather spell. Crafting any piece of red dragonhide armour will grant the player 78 experience per hide.
2509: Black dragon leather is used in the Crafting skill to make black d'hide armour . It can be created by giving a black dragonhide and 20 coins to a tanner (45 coins at Sbott in Canifis ). Tanners can be found in Al Kharid , the Ranging Guild , Forthos Dungeon , Canifis , Auburnvale , and the Crafting Guild . Alternatively, black dragon leather can be made using the Tan Leather spell . Crafting any piece of black dragonhide armour will grant the player 86 experience per hide.

A second variant of the logs can be obtained from the alternate Tutorial Island available to some players in 2020.

In April 2004, Tutorial Island was reworked; cooking raw shrimp there now provides the regular shrimps instead. The item and its banknote were deleted from the game, and replaced by the box of delights and waste disposal respectively.

Since items could not be fully removed once created, it was added in a hidden update in 2005 to fill this slot. The actual item was just a copy of a pink skirt.

If players attempted to view the waste disposal in game by using cheating software, they would be given a hex edit detected instead.

Later in 2006, four more waste disposals were added to replace the noted forms of the roll , square sandwich , triangle sandwich , and baguette .

A second variant of the raw shrimps could be obtained from the alternate Tutorial Island available to some players in 2020.

Lev the Master Chef gives the player the pot of flour and a bucket of water, and teaches them how to combine the two to make bread dough. Players must bake the bread in order to proceed with the tutorial.

The pot of flour was not available in the alternative Tutorial Island experienced by some players in 2020, as the Master Chef was replaced with the Master Navigator.

Rotten tomatoes are inedible items obtained by filling a compost bin entirely with tomatoes and letting them rot, or by purchasing them from one of the several Pelters' Veg Stalls found in various cities. They can be thrown at players stuck in a pillory or anywhere snowballs can be thrown. [ confirmation needed ]

Rotten tomatoes can only be created in compost bins containing tomatoes and no other compostable items. Adding other compostable items to a bin containing tomatoes provides an option to convert it to create regular compost instead.

The lamp is a reward obtained from several random events or by opening an Intricate Pouch that differs from those awarded by quests. Lamps always go to your gravestone on death unless protected.
2529:
A dead orb is an unobtainable item released alongside the Underground Pass quest. Previously, it was a fifth orb of light that could not be obtained, and it was silently renamed to "Dead orb" in an update on 15 June 2017.

During the Underground Pass quest, the player is required to collect four orbs of light. The first three spawn on the ground and can easily be picked up, however the fourth is in front of a swinging log that must be disarmed. The item that appeared on the ground was a fake orb that was actually an object, and was programmed to trigger the trap if players attempted to pick it up. To give the illusion of being real, an invisible Orb of light item was set to spawn on the same tile, so a red dot would appear on the minimap.

After disarming the trap, the real orb would be manually placed in the player's inventory, and both fake orbs (the object and the invisible item) would disappear. However, as a result of an oversight discovered in 2017, if the player disarmed the trap with a full inventory, the invisible orb item would not disappear and could be picked up. Since this made progressing in the quest impossible, the orb was renamed to "Dead orb" and no longer spawns ingame.

2550: A ring of recoil is created by using Lvl-1 Enchant on a sapphire ring . When worn, a small percentage of damage received is dealt to the attacker; it has limited uses before it shatters. They can be used to charge a ring of suffering for the same recoil effect.
2552:
The ring of dueling is a teleportation ring that may be made by casting Lvl-2 Enchant on an emerald ring, granting 37 Magic experience. A full ring of dueling will provide 8 teleports before it crumbles away into nothing.

When teleporting using the ring, the message You rub the ring... will be displayed, followed by a message with the number of charges remaining, ex. Your ring of dueling has four uses left. If using the last charge on the ring, the message Your ring of dueling crumbles to dust. will be displayed instead.

Due to the low cost of the ring, many players use it to bank quickly at the Castle Wars chest. Furthermore, the Ferox Enclave teleport allows a player to use the Pool of Refreshment whilst gaining full health, prayer and run energy, although the Ferox Enclave teleport places the player slightly farther away from a bank chest.

Each charge costs 116.13 coins if all 8 charges are used, 43.43 if using High Level Alchemy (as described below), or 79.86 if using Low Level Alchemy. Alternatively, Explorer's ring can be used 30 times per day for a cost of 59.86. This is viable if fewer than 210 charges are used on average each day, though it gives no Magic experience.

2568:
A ring of forging gives smelting iron ore a 100% success rate of creating an iron bar while it is worn. It can be made by casting Lvl-3 Enchant on a ruby ring , or by paying 250 coins with a ruby ring to Murky Matt in the south-east quadrant of the Grand Exchange .

A newly-enchanted ring has 140 charges. Each time the player smelts an iron ore while wearing the ring, one charge is consumed; after all charges are consumed, the ring crumbles to dust. If the player auto-smelts more iron ores than the number of remaining charges, the smelting will stop once the ring crumbles. The number of charges is specific to the player, not the ring, so swapping, dropping, or alching rings before 140 charges are used will not reset the number of smelts the player has left before a ring breaks. Players can right-click a ring of forging to either "check" how many charges remain in it or "break" it and reset the next one they use to its maximum charges.

When smelting multiples of an ore at the Edgeville furnace while wearing Varrock armour , there is a chance to smelt 2 bars at once. If this activates while smelting iron with a ring of forging, 2 charges from the ring will be used.
2570:
The ring of life is a diamond ring that has been enchanted with Lvl-4 Enchant . While worn, if the wearer is attacked and has 10% or less of their Hitpoints remaining, the ring automatically teleports the wearer to their respawn point . The ring crumbles to dust after one use. A Defence cape can be worn for the same effect, which does not destroy itself on activation. An Escape crystal can be configured to provide the same effect and more.

The ring does not guarantee total safety, as a player wearing one will still die if they are hit from above 10% of their maximum Hitpoints to zero (for example, being hit 15 while at 15 hitpoints), and it will not cure poison . Self-inflicted damage, such as guzzling a dwarven rock cake or using a locator orb , can also activate the effect. If it is worn along with a phoenix necklace , the necklace effect will trigger first. In PvP , the Tele Block spell will prevent a player's ring of life from activating.

It is one the few items whose teleports will work up to level 30 Wilderness, while most other means of teleportation will not work above level 20 Wilderness.

In Wintertodt , the ring will activate if warmth drops below 10%.

Upon the completion of medium Ardougne Diary , the teleport destination can be toggled to East Ardougne .
2572:
The ring of wealth is a dragonstone ring that has been enchanted by the Lvl-5 Enchant spell. Like other enchanted dragonstone jewellery , it can be charged to provide teleports. Unlike the other pieces, the ring can only be charged by the Fountain of Rune . Wearing this ring (whether charged or not) while killing monsters will automatically pick up coins , Tokkul , or numulites dropped by monsters. This effect can be toggled off in the right-click menu when held in the inventory. When worn it also removes the chance to receive a "nothing" drop when accessing the rare drop table and gem drop table . See below for more information about this feature.

The price difference between a fully charged ring and an uncharged ring is 2,651 coins , so each charge costs about 530 coins .

Players can imbue the ring using a ring of wealth scroll , which can be purchased from Justine's stuff for the Last Shopper Standing for 5 Last Man Standing points. Wearing an imbued ring in the Wilderness doubles the chance of obtaining a clue scroll from monsters and from skilling.

Like other dragonstone jewellery, it is one the few items whose teleports will work up to level 30 Wilderness, while most other means of teleportation will not work above level 20 Wilderness.
2574:
A sextant is an item used for solving coordinate clues whilst on a Treasure Trail . It does not need to be brought with the player if the exact coordinate is known beforehand.

A chart can be obtained by first talking to the Observatory professor (who may be at the Observatory or the nearby Observatory reception building to the north-east, depending upon whether the player has completed the Observatory Quest ), then, speaking to Murphy in Port Khazard , who will give you a sextant. Murphy is found on the dock near the trawler for the Fishing Trawler . Brother Kojo in the Clock Tower can then give the player a watch .

After first obtaining a sextant from Murphy, the player may thereafter make sextants with level 23 Crafting or higher. A sextant can be made by having one steel bar in the inventory and clicking on a crafting table 4 in the Workshop of a player's house . Making a sextant will give 15 Crafting experience .

Operating the sextant is a fairly simple task. The idea is to put the horizon and the sun in the middle of the screen.

First use the vertical 'arrow buttons' on the right to put the horizon in the centre of the viewer on the right hand side. Then use the horizontal arrow buttons to move the sun onto the horizon in the middle of the screen. Clicking 'get location' will give the coordinates of the player's position. This consists of two numbers; the first indicates how far the player is north or south of the Observatory , in degrees and minutes, and the second how far east or west. Note that one degree is 60 minutes, and each game square is approximately 1.875 minutes.
2575:
A watch is an item for solving coordinate clues whilst on Treasure Trails . A chart can be obtained by first talking to the Observatory professor (who may be at the Observatory or the nearby Observatory reception building to the north-west, depending upon whether the player has completed the Observatory Quest ). After talking to him, you have to receive the sextant from Murphy at Port Khazard in order for Brother Kojo to give you a watch at the Clock Tower .

Although not required for coordinate clues, a watch can be used with a sextant and a chart in the inventory to find the coordinates.

After first obtaining a watch from Brother Kojo, the player may thereafter make watches with level 28 Crafting or higher. A watch can be made by having one steel bar and one clockwork in the inventory and clicking on a crafting table 4 at the Workshop of a player's house . Making a watch will give 15 Crafting experience .
2576: A chart is used for coordinate clues for Treasure Trails . It is used along with a watch and sextant if one wishes to find a coordinate clue. A chart can be obtained from the Observatory professor at the Observatory . It is not necessary to have a sextant and a watch to obtain the chart. The drop trick can be used to obtain multiple charts if desired.
2577:
Ranger boots are a rare reward received from the completion of medium Treasure Trails . It is part of the ranger kit , and requires 40 Ranged to wear; it can also be stored in a treasure chest . Ranger boots are the third best Ranged footwear in terms of ranged attack bonus.

The drop rate of ranger boots is 1/1,133 per slot. [ 1 ] With each medium clue reward, a player will receive 3-5 slots of items; this makes the effective drop rate ~1/283.6 per casket. The ranger boots are the most valuable drop from medium clues.

With level 60 in Runecraft and Magic , ranger boots can be combined with a pegasian crystal to create a pair of pegasian boots , which has increased stats, and remains tradeable. The process cannot be reversed.

This item can be stored in the treasure chest of a costume room , provided that the interface of the corresponding clue tier is opened before attempting to store the item. Alternatively, the item can be used on the opened treasure chest to insert it without viewing the interface.

The highwayman mask is a black mask similar to the ones highwaymen wear. It can be obtained from Easy Treasure Trails . Some players argue that it is very different, but when shown on a player while in game, they look almost identical to the ones worn by the NPC highwaymen. 2714:
A casket could previously be received after completing any step of a Treasure Trail . These caskets did not always contain a reward, and sometimes only gave another clue scroll.

On 28 July 2016 Treasure Trails were updated. Caskets were replaced with new items called Reward caskets . They are only received once all steps have been completed, and are guaranteed to contain a reward.

Although caskets are no longer obtainable, they are still ingame for any player who had one before the update, making them a rare example of a discontinued item in Old School RuneScape .
2715:
The Casket is an unobtainable item added to the game with the release of Treasure Trails . Previously, every clue where the player was required to dig would give a casket . Due to an oversight when Treasure Trails were originally released, banknote versions were created of the caskets obtained from the three easy map clues at the Champions' Guild, Varrock Mine, and Falador.

The next update, these were converted into unique stackable copies of the Caskets. As this occurred before August 2007, they have never been obtainable in Old School RuneScape .

Although caskets are no longer obtainable, they are still ingame for any player who had one before the update, making them a rare example of a discontinued item in Old School RuneScape .

Puzzle boxes can be obtained by doing hard, elite, and master Treasure Trails . Before you are able to continue with your clue scroll, you will have to complete the puzzle.

A puzzle box is always scrambled 101 times before being handed to the player, by randomly sliding a piece into the empty position starting from the solved state. [ 1 ]

If you have a duplicate puzzle box, (obtained by a method such as the Drop trick ) in your inventory or bank after completing the clue, you cannot obtain another clue.

2832:
A key is an item needed to unlock a chest or drawer during a Treasure Trail.

There will be a clue telling you where to get it. The key is a drop only when carrying the clue scroll. It disappears when used to open the chest or drawer. Keys are non-tradeable objects, specific to the player who finds them. They are used on all levels of treasure trails.

It is possible to obtain more than one key using the drop trick. However, after taking a clue from the chest/drawer, the key won't open it again, and the player gets a message: "The chest (or drawer) is locked." Keys obtained this way from the same clue will still remain in the bank; however, keys obtained from different clues will not stack.

Challenge scrolls are riddles given to players by an NPC during a Treasure Trail. Challenge scrolls appear in medium, hard, and elite clue steps. Players must solve the challenge scroll in order to advance in their Treasure Trail. The challenge scroll is not a separate step in the Treasure Trail.

The questions for the challenge scrolls are always the same. Players do not have to read the challenge scroll in order to answer the question. Players only need to talk to the NPC again after receiving the scroll to answer the answer. There are no penalties for incorrect answers.

2859:
Wolf bones are an item obtained by killing a wolf or werewolf . Wolf bones have various uses, including in skills (such as Prayer , Fletching , Crafting ) and in some quests .

Wolf bones look very similar to regular bones , except wolf bones are slightly more greyish in colour.
2861:
Wolfbone arrowtips are used as to create the ogre arrows used in the Big Chompy Bird Hunting quest. Players must partially complete Big Chompy Bird Hunting in order to fletch the arrowtips. They require level 5 in Fletching to make. Using a chisel with wolf bones will result in 2-6 arrowheads and gives 2.5 Fletching and Crafting experience per arrowtip. The amount of arrowtips carved out of each wolf bone is random, and is not influenced by Fletching or Crafting level. [ 1 ]

Use these on some flighted ogre arrows to create completed ogre arrows.
2862:
Achey tree logs are logs that can be obtained at level 1 Woodcutting from Achey trees for 25 experience each. Players can burn these logs at level 1 Firemaking for 40 experience each.

These logs are needed for the Big Chompy Bird Hunting quest to make ogre arrows, as well as composite ogre bows for Zogre Flesh Eaters.

With a knife, they can be made into 2-6 ogre arrow shafts for 1.5 Fletching experience per shaft made. With a knife and wolf bones, players can make an unstrung comp bow.

After giving Uglug Nar a relicym's balm during Zogre Flesh Eaters, he will open his store which stocks 100 achey tree logs at a base price of 4 coins. Uglug's store is the quickest way to obtain achey tree logs.
2864: Ogre arrow shafts are components used in making ogre arrows and brutal arrows . They require level 5 Fletching and starting the quest Big Chompy Bird Hunting to make. They are made by cutting an Achey tree and using a knife on the Achey tree logs . The amount of shafts given is random; between two and six will be made. 1.6 Fletching experience is gained per shaft made. Adding 4 feathers to each shaft makes flighted ogre arrows .
2865:
Flighted ogre arrows are made by using a knife on achey logs to make ogre arrow shafts, and then using 4 feathers per arrow shaft made. Doing so requires level 5 Fletching, granting 0.9 Fletching experience per flighted arrow.

Adding wolfbone arrowtips makes ogre arrows, while adding nails with a hammer will make brutal arrows instead.
2866:
Ogre arrows are used for hunting large game birds such as Chompy birds and Jubbly birds . These arrows can only be fired from ogre bows or composite ogre bows . Ogre arrows are required in Big Chompy Bird Hunting and the Freeing Skrach Uglogwee sub-quest of Recipe for Disaster .

They can be created through the Fletching skill at level 5, by using wolfbone arrowtips on flighted ogre arrows . 6 arrows can be made at a time with 1.0 Fletching experience granted per arrow made.

The player can claim ogre arrows once daily for free from Rantz after completion of the Western Provinces diary . He will give players 25, 50, 100, or 150 free ogre arrows each day, depending on completion of the easy, medium, hard, and elite diaries, respectively.
2871:
Ogre bellows are obtained by "unlocking" the Locked Ogre chest (i.e. pushing a boulder off from on top of it) in the north-west part of the cave near Rantz (not on worldmap) in eastern Feldip Hills where the ogre Rantz and his son and daughter live, directly north from the quest start icon where Big Chompy Bird Hunting is started ( fairy ring code A K S is nearby). Multiple ogre bellows can be taken from Rantz's chest.

This item is also needed for obtaining various chompy bird hats , a section of the quest Recipe for Disaster , Mourning's End Part I , and the Western Provinces Diary .

The bellows are first filled with three loads of swamp gas from the swamp to the west. They are then used on the swamp toads found nearby to produce bloated toads . Only three toads may be carried at any one time in your inventory, though more than three may be laid on the ground. The now incapacitated bloated toad may be placed anywhere in the ogre area to attempt to attract a chompy bird . When filling the bellows, your character will attempt to fill all the bellows in your inventory automatically. Alternatively, the player can use the bellows on the swamp bubbles to fill them without delay.

Swamp toads that can be picked up cannot be used to fill ogre bellows. Attempting to do so results in the chatbox message stating " The chompy bird doesn't like this species of toad. "

When filling the bellows, your character will attempt to fill all the bellows in your inventory automatically. Alternatively, the player can use the bellows on the swamp bubbles to fill them without delay.

Swamp toads that can be picked up cannot be used to fill ogre bellows. Attempting to do so results in the chatbox message stating " The chompy bird doesn't like this species of toad. "
2875:
Bloated toads are used to catch chompy birds during and after the Big Chompy Bird Hunting quest . Their dyed variant, coloured toads , are used during Mourning's End Part I . Bloated toads can be obtained by using ogre bellows which have been filled with swamp gas on a swamp toad . Only three toads may be obtained at one time, and they cannot be banked .

Bloated toads may only be dropped in the ogre areas east and south of Gu'Tanoth . Once dropped, they have a chance of causing a chompy bird to land, lasting 1 minute before exploding and dealing 1-2 damage to all players within one tile (including diagonally). This damage cannot kill players.

Inflating a toad a second time by using filled ogre bellows on a bloated toad will lead to the toad floating away in a comical manner if the player is not in the possession of a ball of wool and a suitable rock ; if these materials are available, however, a balloon toad will be created instead.
2876:
A raw chompy is obtained by killing a chompy bird . It can be cooked on an iron spit or at the ogre spit-roast near Rantz's cave , to make cooked chompy . Failure to cook it properly will result in a ruined chompy . Raw chompy is one of the three main ingredients in a wild pie .

The ability to hunt chompies is unlocked during the Big Chompy Bird Hunting quest. They are also used in the quest Recipe for Disaster during the portion where Skrach Uglogwee needs to be freed.
2878:
Cooked chompy is an ogre delicacy obtained by skewering a raw chompy with an iron spit, then cooking the skewered chompy on a fire, requiring level 30 Cooking and granting 100 experience when successful. Players may burn the chompy while cooking one, resulting in a ruined chompy; the burn rate while cooking these will decrease as players reach higher Cooking levels. It will stop burning entirely at Cooking level 99.

Cooked chompy heals 10 Hitpoints. If hunting chompy birds, due to the meat's weight of 10 kg, it is recommended to do so south-west of Castle Wars. Big Chompy Bird Hunting is required to hunt them.
2880:
Ruined chompy is the result of accidentally burning a raw chompy while attempting to make a cooked chompy . The burn rate while cooking these will decrease as players reach higher Cooking levels, stopping entirely at level 99.

Cooking chompy on a fire alone is not possible - it needs to either be used on one of the ogre spits , or used with an iron spit and then cooked on a fire.

The ruined chompy has no use whatsoever. Like most other burnt food, it is tradeable to other players but not on the Grand Exchange .
2882: A seasoned chompy is used in the Big Chompy Bird Hunting quest. It is made by obtaining the seasonings specified by Rantz, Fycie and Bugs and then cooking a raw chompy on the ogre spit roast with the seasoning items in your inventory. It is given to Rantz to complete the quest.
2883:
The ogre bow is a weapon requiring 30 Ranged to wield. Along with the comp ogre bow , it is used to kill chompies . The bow cannot be fletched , and it can fire ogre arrows as well as brutal arrows up to mithril brutals .

The ogre bow is obtained from Rantz during the Big Chompy Bird Hunting quest. If the bow is lost, another can be purchased from him for an amount which changes each time, but is in the range of 500-550 coins . The bow is also required for Freeing Skrach Uglogwee in the Recipe for Disaster quest.

The bow has the same ranged attack bonus but a much slower attack speed than the comp version; additionally, the comp bow is tradeable. For this reason, the regular ogre bow is rarely used after the quest is complete.

The player can check the number of chompy birds they have killed by selecting the "Check kills" option on the bow. Kills are only tracked after completing Big Chompy Bird Hunting.
2884: Chompy bird obj is an interface item released alongside the Big Chompy Bird Hunting quest. It appears in the chatbox when checking the number of chompy birds killed on the Ogre bow. The actual item, however, cannot be obtained.
2885:
"Whoopsie" is the name given to several unobtainable items in the cache. Many items were changed to have their noted forms removed: since items could not be fully removed once created, Whoopsies were added in a hidden update to fill these slots. The actual item was just a copy of a pink skirt.

In RuneScape 2, the item later became viewable via Quick Chat, causing much confusion.

All of the Whoopsies were gradually removed from Old School RuneScape and replaced; however, one remains, which was originally the noted form of the "Chompy bird object" item that appears in the chatbox when checking the Chompy bird kill count.
2886:
The battered book , titled Book of the Elemental Shield , is a quest item used in Elemental Workshop I . It is found by searching the east bookcase in the building with a cooking range , south of the building with anvils in it in Seers' Village .

It is read to start the quest. When a knife or any slash weapon is used on it, the player will receive a battered key to get into the Workshop and the book will become a slashed book . The battered or slashed book also acts as a tool in the player's inventory to make elemental shields . After the Elemental Workshop II quest, mind shields can also be smithed.

The battered book (or the slashed book ) may be one of the items on the item list , given by Thorgel , that is needed to receive a death talisman during or after Mourning's End II ; however, it is not needed to finish the quest as long as you already have a death talisman or catalytic talisman .

Duplicates can be drop tricked by searching the bookcase to obtain another. If the player searches the bookcase after creating the slashed book , all copies in the player's inventory and bank are deleted. Duplicates cannot be obtained after creating the slashed book. It can also be found in the bookcase in your house after getting it from Seers' Village.
2887:
The battered key is a quest item used in Elemental Workshop I . It is made by using a knife on a battered book . Additionally, it can be found by searching the bookcase where the battered book was originally found, only after creating a slashed book for the first time.

It is used to open the Odd looking wall in the building with the anvils in Seers' Village in order to access the workshop .

Duplicates can be drop tricked by searching the bookcase to obtain another only after the player has created a slashed book. Duplicates can be obtained after completing the quest. This key can be added to a steel key ring .
2888:
A stone bowl [ sic ] is a quest item used only in Elemental Workshop I . It is found by searching the boxes north-east of the hatch in the Elemental Workshop .

It is used to make a stone bowl filled with lava from a lava trough . The full stone bowl is then used on the furnace to heat it up.

Duplicates can be drop tricked by searching the boxes to obtain another.
2889:
A stone bowl [ sic ] is a quest item used only in Elemental Workshop I . It is found by searching the boxes north-east of the hatch in the Elemental Workshop .

It is used to make a stone bowl filled with lava from a lava trough . The full stone bowl is then used on the furnace to heat it up.

Duplicates can be drop tricked by searching the boxes to obtain another.
2890:
The elemental shield may be made during and after the Elemental Workshop I quest in the Elemental Workshop dungeon.

To make the shield, players must have a Smithing level of 20, an elemental metal , a hammer , and either a battered book or slashed book in their inventory. Use the elemental metal on a workbench in the elemental workshop to make the shield. Smithing the shield grants the player 20 Smithing experience . To equip the shield, players must have completed the Elemental Workshop I quest.

An elemental shield can be used for partial protection against the breath of skeletal wyverns and wyverns . When worn, it reduces the maximum damage of wyvern icy breath attacks to 10.

Upon completion of Elemental Workshop II , players can equip the mind shield for an additional +3 magic defence over the elemental shield.
2892:
Elemental ore is an ore that may only be obtained by killing a level 35 earth elemental after trying to mine the elemental rock. This ore can only be obtained during and after the Elemental Workshop I quest, and turned into elemental metals. Elemental ore is only found in the Elemental Workshop dungeon beneath the Seers' Village, in the house with the anvil, next to the bank. Earth elementals are found in the western area on the first level of the workshop.

The second level is to make bars, and repairs are needed here too. One elemental ore and four coal may be smelted into a bar of elemental metal using the blast furnace in the southern area of the Elemental Workshop (level 20 Smithing is required). This bar is used to smith the elemental shield and helmet.

At level 30 Smithing, the elemental metal may be primed and turned into a primed elemental bar. This may be used to create the mind shield and mind helmet in the Elemental Workshop II quest.
2893:
Elemental metal is a metal bar that is used in the quests Elemental Workshop I and Elemental Workshop II. It is made by using one elemental ore and four coal on the furnace on the south side of the first floor of the Elemental Workshop. Each bar must be made individually.

The elemental metal can be used to make an elemental shield or an elemental helmet. During Elemental Workshop II, it is also used to make an elemental claw and is processed into a primed bar in the second level of the Elemental Workshop.
2894:

Unlike leather boots, these cannot be crafted. Because of their stats, they are mostly worn for cosmetic purposes.

2944:
The golden key is a quest item used only in Priest in Peril. It is dropped by the hooded level 30 Monk of Zamorak in the Paterdomus Temple.

It is used to open the first gate under Paterdomus after killing the Temple Guardian and then it is exchanged for the iron key by using it on the southern monument (the one referencing to "Saradomin being the key"). After unlocking the first gate for the first time, it is not required to be in the inventory to open the gate again.

Duplicates can be drop tricked by killing another monk to obtain another before unlocking Drezel's cell. Additionally, should the player lose the iron key they can get another by swapping (using) a golden key at the southern monument. The golden key also cannot be added to a steel key ring.
2945:
The iron key is a quest item used only in Priest in Peril . It is obtained by using a golden key on the southern Monument in the Paterdomus mausoleum .

It is used to unlock the cell Drezel is detained in. Once used, the key disappears.

Duplicates can be obtained by using another golden key on the monument even if there is already a golden key on it. This can only be done before using the blessed water on the coffin . The iron key also cannot be added to a steel key ring .
2946:
A golden tinderbox is a quest item used only in Priest in Peril . It is obtained by using a tinderbox on the south-east Monument in the Paterdomus mausoleum .

It serves no purpose in the quest, and has no uses outside the quest, as it cannot be used for lighting fires. However, players can cast Low or High Level Alchemy on it.

It cannot be obtained once Drezel has moved to the dungeon after the player has exhausted all dialogue with him after using the blessed water on the coffin.
2947:
A golden candle is a quest item used only in Priest in Peril. It is obtained by using a candle (extinguished) on the north-west Monument in the Paterdomus mausoleum.

It serves no purpose in the quest, and has no uses outside the quest, as it cannot be used as a light source in a dark area. However, players can cast Low Alchemy or High alchemy on it.

It cannot be obtained once Drezel has moved to the dungeon after the player has exhausted all dialogue with him after using the blessed water on the coffin.
2948:
A golden pot is a quest item used only in Priest in Peril. It is obtained by using a pot on the west Monument in the Paterdomus mausoleum.

It serves no purpose in the quest, and has no uses outside the quest, as it cannot be used for storing any materials. However, players can cast Low Alchemy or High alchemy on it.

It cannot be obtained once Drezel has moved to the dungeon after the player has exhausted all dialogue with him after using the blessed water on the coffin.
2949:
A golden hammer is a quest item used only in Priest in Peril. It is obtained by using a hammer on the north Monument in the Paterdomus mausoleum.

It serves no purpose in the quest, and has no uses outside the quest, as it cannot be used in Smithing, Construction, or for opening the Bandos door in the God Wars Dungeon. However, players can cast Low Alchemy or High alchemy on it.

It cannot be obtained once Drezel has moved to the dungeon after the player has exhausted all dialogue with him after using the blessed water on the coffin.
2950:
A Golden feather is a quest item used only in Priest in Peril. It is obtained by using a feather on the east Monument in the Paterdomus mausoleum.

It serves no purpose in the quest, and has no uses outside the quest, as it cannot be used in Fishing or Fletching. However, players can cast Low Alchemy or High alchemy on it.

It cannot be obtained once Drezel has moved to the dungeon after the player has exhausted all dialogue with him after using the blessed water on the coffin.
2951:
A golden needle is a quest item used only in Priest in Peril. It is obtained by using a needle on the south Monument in the Paterdomus mausoleum.

It serves no purpose in the quest, and has no uses outside the quest, as it cannot be used in Crafting. However, players can cast Low Alchemy or High Alchemy on it.

It cannot be obtained once Drezel has moved to the dungeon after the player has exhausted all dialogue with him after using the blessed water on the coffin.
2952:
Wolfbane is a dagger given as a quest item reward in Priest in Peril . It is obtained from Drezel after completion of the quest.

It is used to keep the citizens of Canifis from transforming into werewolves when the player attacks them. As a silver item, it can also be used against tier 1 Vampyres . It has the same bonuses as a mithril dagger except it also gives a prayer bonus . Wolfbane cannot be poisoned . It can be reclaimed by talking to Drezel in the dungeon below Paterdomus ; players are only allowed to own one at a time but more can be obtained with the drop trick .

Killing a citizen of Canifis using wolfbane is an Easy Morytania Diary task.
2953:
The murky water is a quest item used only in Priest in Peril . It can only be made during the quest by using a bucket on the well in the Paterdomus mausoleum to obtain water from the River Salve .

It is used to make blessed water by speaking to Drezel .

Duplicates can only be made during the quest. After talking to Drezel to bless it, all copies in the inventory are converted into blessed water . Duplicates cannot be obtained after completing the quest, as using a bucket on the well will only make a bucket of water .
2954:
Blessed water is a quest item used only in Priest in Peril. It is made by speaking to Drezel to bless the murky water.

It is poured onto the coffin enclosing the vampyre within to allow Drezel to escape from his prison without waking it.

Duplicates can be obtained by having multiple copies of murky water in the inventory. Duplicates cannot be obtained after completing the quest.
2955:
Moonlight mead is a type of ale that restores 4 Hitpoints. It can be obtained through brewing at level 44 Cooking, granting 380 experience. It is brewed using 2 buckets of water, 2 barley malt, 4 mushrooms, and a pot of ale yeast. The stronger, mature version of the ale is the moonlight mead(m).

It can be bought for 5 coins from Roavar in the Hair of the Dog tavern, located in Canifis.

Upon drinking, the chatbox will state "You drink the foul smelling brew. It tastes like something just died in your mouth."
2957:
The druid pouch is an item first obtained during the Nature Spirit quest. Its main use is to protect the player against the ghasts that haunt the Mort Myre Swamp .

If lost, an empty druid pouch can be reclaimed from the inside of the Nature Spirit's grotto - one respawns near the grotto pool.

Building the Fire of Dehumidification after completing Making Friends with My Arm is a strictly better, non-consumable alternative to druid pouches, though the fire does not have any effect within the Temple Trekking minigame.
2958:

2959:
Rotten food is food that has been attacked by ghasts in Mort Myre Swamp . It is inedible and almost useless, where the only use is to have it converted to stew by Abidor Crank encountered rarely during the Temple Trekking minigame.

Players can prevent ghasts rotting their food by:

Rotten food is obtained during the Zogre Flesh Eaters quest, when the player searches the backpack found deep within the Jiggig crypts.

It cannot be used to make Compost .
2961: A silver sickle can be made at 18 Crafting with a silver bar and a sickle mould at a furnace , granting 50 Crafting experience . It can be turned into a Silver sickle (b) during Nature Spirit quest , and can also be blessed after the quest by dipping it in the pool of water in the nature spirit's grotto . A blessed sickle can be used to cast Bloom ; when cast, this spell drains your prayer slightly, and if you are in the Mort Myre Swamp , it may grow fungi, saplings and golden pears on rotting logs, branches, and small bushes respectively, which can be used to fill a druid pouch .
2963:
The silver sickle (b) is a silver sickle that was blessed by dipping it in the grotto water after completion of Nature Spirit . It protects the player from the swamp's decaying effects when wielded or in the inventory. This item can be used during the quest In Aid of the Myreque . There is a possibility of this item being needed for Fairytale I - Growing Pains . The sickle can be obtained again after the quest by using a silver sickle on the altar of nature found in the Nature Grotto .

The sickle has a right-click "bloom" option which can be used next to rotten logs, branches, or bushes in Mort Myre swamp to obtain Mort myre fungi , stems , and pears . This costs 1-6 prayer points per cast, and cannot be used if the player has no prayer points remaining. These items can be used to fill the Druid pouch which allows the player to fight Ghasts . Bloom can also be cast on dead vines in the Ancient Guthixian Temple to grow them into flowering vines which can be picked to obtain a vine flower .

The blessed silver sickle can be turned into an emerald sickle (b) or ruby sickle (b) by using it with a cut emerald or ruby after completing A Taste of Hope .

It can also be used to harm Vampyres and Vampyre Juvinates , but is not recommended due to its weak stats.

The player can reclaim the sickle from a crate found within the old Myreque Hideout under Old Man Ral 's house after partial completion of A Taste of Hope .
2964: A washing bowl can be found on a bench in Filliman Tarlock 's Nature Grotto , south of the Mort Myre Swamp . Hidden underneath it is a mirror required for the Nature Spirit quest . The bowl respawns almost instantly and serves no purpose in the quest after revealing the mirror.
2966: A mirror is used in the Nature Spirit quest to prove to Filliman Tarlock that he is dead. It can be found under the washing bowl on a bench near the entrance to the Nature Grotto south of the Mort Myre Swamp . It is also obtainable after the quest, but it serves no purpose.
2967:
Filliman Tarlock's journal is one of a number of items that are simply called 'Journal' in the inventory. This particular journal is obtained by searching the tree in the middle of Filliman's grotto south of Mort Myre Swamp during the Nature Spirit quest. The player must read the journal to find vague instructions on how Filliman can transcend his current ghostly form to become a nature spirit.

The journal is not available from the tree after the quest. It is not found in the bookcase in a player-owned house.
2968:
The druidic spell is a spell scroll that can cast Bloom on rotten logs in Mort Myre Swamp to grow Mort myre fungi .

The spell is given to the player by Filliman Tarlock during the Nature Spirit quest and can be used only once, after which it turns into a used spell . The spell can only be used once the player has been blessed by Drezel during the quest. Attempting to use the spell before receiving Drezel's blessing will yield the message, " You need to be blessed before you can cast this spell. " However, after completing the quest, the player can cast Bloom using a Silver sickle(b) , or any of: Emerald sickle (b) , Enchanted emerald sickle (b) , Ruby sickle (b) , Enchanted ruby sickle (b) , Blisterwood sickle , Ivandis flail , or Blisterwood flail . For collectors, be cautious about dropping this item inside the grotto right before the quest's end. If left on the ground, it will disappear when the grotto shifts.
2969: A used spell is one of the results of using the druidic spell given to the player by Filliman Tarlock during the Nature Spirit quest. When the player uses the druidic spell to cast Bloom , it turns into a used spell. This item must later be used on the grey stone outside of the nature spirit's grotto to progress in the quest.
2970:
Mort myre fungi can be obtained in Mort Myre Swamp . It can be used to add 1 charge to a Druid pouch or to make super energy potions . They are also required to bait and catch wild broavs .

It is obtained by casting Bloom with a Druidic spell or blessed silver sickle (both obtained during the Nature Spirit quest ) near rotting logs . All variants and flail upgrades of the blessed silver sickle can also cast Bloom. Alternatively, they can be obtained as a drop from certain monsters or by chopping sulliuscep mushrooms .

Collecting Mort myre fungi to sell is an effective way of making money, as they are valued by players due to their use in the Herblore skill.

It is a possible item requirement in Fairytale I - Growing Pains .
2972:
Mort myre stems can be obtained by operating a silver sickle (b) near rotting branches on the ground in Mort Myre Swamp . Each stem can be used to add 2 charges to a druid pouch for use as protection from ghasts .

It is a possible item requirement in Fairytale I - Growing Pains .
2974:
A mort myre pear is obtained during or after the Nature Spirit quest . It appears when the Bloom spell is cast, using a silver sickle(b) near certain small bushes in the Mort Myre Swamp . Each pear can be used to add 3 charges to a druid pouch for use as protection from ghasts . However, they are not common, and it is generally easier to find Mort myre fungi or Mort myre stems .

It is a possible item requirement in Fairytale I - Growing Pains .
2976:
A sickle mould is a type of mould that can be used together with a silver bar to create a silver sickle. One can make a silver sickle at a Crafting level of 18.

The sickle mould can be purchased from the following shops:

Dommik's Crafting Store in Al Kharid

Jamila's Craft Stall in Sophanem

Rasolo the Wandering Merchant west of the Fishing Guild

Rommik's Crafty Supplies in Rimmington
2978:
The ogre bowman hat (in-game: Chompy bird hat ) is a members only decorative hat. To wear this hat, the player needs at least 5 Fletching and 30 Ranged . To obtain this hat the player must first kill at least 30 Chompy birds , then talk to Rantz . As this hat is purely for decoration, it gives the player no bonuses.

This item can be stored in the armour case of a costume room , as part of the Chompy bird hat set. Ultimate Ironmen will be unable to retrieve individual pieces until the full set is stored.

2996:
Agility arena tickets were earned from tagging ticket dispensers within the Brimhaven Agility Arena minigame. Each ticket was rewarded after tagging more than one dispenser in a row. Tickets could then be redeemed for Agility experience and rewards from the Brimhaven Agility Arena Ticket Exchange run by Pirate Jackie the Fruit .

Exchanging larger amounts of tickets for Agility experience offered experience bonuses, up to 33% more per ticket. Wearing Karamja Gloves 2 or higher from completing the medium Karamja Diary when exchanging tickets rewarded 10% more total experience. Completing the elite Karamja Diary rewarded a 10% chance of receiving double tickets when tagging a pillar. The experience rewards increased by 5 per ticket for each Agility level above 40.

The item was discontinued and a new version was introduced following the 9 May 2024 Project Rebalance update , which can only be redeemed for Agility experience at a flat rate, as well as introduced Brimhaven vouchers , which can be exchanged for items. The discontinued tickets, as well as the former shop, are still available in-game for players who have the discontinued tickets to redeem. Players can also exchange the discontinued tickets for Brimhaven vouchers by using the ticket on Pirate Jackie the Fruit.
2997:
The pirate's hook is a reward from the Brimhaven Agility Arena that occupies the glove slot. It can be purchased from Pirate Jackie the Fruit for 800 Brimhaven vouchers.

Without the completion of the elite Karamja diary, it takes a minimum of 800 minutes (or 13 hours 20 minutes) to earn enough tickets for this item, assuming no dispensers are missed. Players with the diary completed have a 10% chance to gain double tickets, which lowers the time to 728 minutes (12 hours 8 minutes).

Players who have completed Cabin Fever can pay Patchy 500 coins to combine the hook with a crab claw to make a crabclaw hook. The hook cannot be stored in the player-owned house.
2998:
Toadflax is a low level herb, requiring level 30 Herblore to clean. It can be acquired from Random events or grown with a Farming level of 38, by planting toadflax seeds in herb patches. It can also be acquired by trading in 3 vouchers from the Brimhaven Agility Arena or as a reward from Temple Trekking. It is used to make agility potions and most commonly, Saradomin brews. To create a potion, you need to add the cleaned herb to a vial of water to create a toadflax potion (unf), and then add the secondary ingredient.

Using Toadflax in the coconut milk based Antidote+ potion is often considered a waste, as Antidote++ is vastly preferred by PvM'ers, whereas the Antidote+ is not usually in demand. However, Antidote+ can be a viable and cheaper option in certain situations, such as fending off poison while training Ranged or Magic at the Skeletal Monkeys on Ape Atoll. Ironmen may also prefer to create Antidote+ until they reach a high enough level to create its more potent counterpart.

According to the book Gielinor's flora - herbs, the flowers of a toadflax plant are often believed to resemble a toad's mouth, which is likely where it got the name. In addition, it is often mistaken for snapdragon and is widespread in rural spots.
3000:
Snapdragon is a herb which can be cleaned at level 59 Herblore. It may be grown from a snapdragon seed with a Farming level of 62, granting 98.5 Farming experience for every snapdragon grown. Once planted, the herb takes 80 minutes to fully grow.

Snapdragons are used to make super restore potions and sanfew serums with a Herblore level of 63 and a Herblore level of 65 respectively. To create a potion, you need to add the cleaned herb to a vial of water to create a snapdragon potion (unf) , and then add the secondary ingredient.

According to the book Gielinor's flora - herbs , snapdragon is native to the rocky areas of Tirannwn , and is supposedly named due to its resemblance of the face of a dragon.
3002:
A toadflax potion (unf) is an unfinished potion made by using a toadflax on a vial of water, requiring 34 Herblore. Using toad's legs on a toadflax potion (unf) with 34 Herblore yields an agility potion (3) and 80 Herblore experience. Using a crushed nest on a toadflax potion (unf) with 81 Herblore yields a saradomin brew (3) and 180 Herblore experience.

One is used in the Land of the Goblins quest.
3004: A snapdragon potion (unf) is an unfinished potion made by using a snapdragon on a vial of water , requiring 63 Herblore . Using red spiders' eggs on a snapdragon potion (unf) with 63 Herblore yields a super restore(3) and 142.5 Herblore experience .
3006: A firework is an unobtainable potion released alongside snapdragon and the Brimhaven Agility Arena. It was presumably intended to be a cosmetic potion created from snapdragons, but was scrapped for unknown reasons.
3008:
An energy potion restores 15% of the player's run energy per dose. It can be made at level 26 Herblore by mixing a harralander in a vial of water and then adding chocolate dust, granting 67.5 Herblore experience.

After Barbarian Herblore Training, caviar can be added to a 2 dose energy potion, which requires 29 Herblore and yields a 2 dose energy mix and 14 Herblore experience. An energy mix heals 3 hitpoints in addition to restoring 15% run energy.

It can be purchased from Apothecary's Potions in Varrock for 1 chocolate dust and 2 limpwurt roots, obtained from Dr Jekyll in exchange for a ranarr weed, or obtained as a common drop from various early game monsters, such as goblins, dark wizards, NPCs with the standard "human" drop table such as men, and low level Slayer monsters.

3016:
A super energy is a potion made by mixing avantoe with mort myre fungi in a vial of water, giving 117.5 Herblore experience. It requires level 52 Herblore.

Super energy potions recover 20% of run energy per dose.

At 77 Herblore they can be used to make stamina potions using amylase crystals.

After Barbarian Herblore Training is completed, caviar can be added to a super energy(2) to produce a super energy mix. This requires 56 Herblore and provides 39 Herblore experience. A super energy mix has 2 doses, each of which heals 6 Hitpoints in addition to the normal super energy recovery.

Super energy potions can be a budget friendly option for players wishing to save costs on supplies. Super energy potions give the same 20% run energy restore as Stamina potions just without the 70% reduction in run energy depletion for 2 minutes. Stamina potions can run as much as 3x the cost of super energy potions so players may wish to use super energies when reduction in run energy depletion isn't needed, and only additional run energy is needed for their current task. Additionally, players can make unused Super energy potions into stamina potions as they progress their accounts as mentioned above.

3024:
A super restore is a potion that restores all player stats that have been lowered, including Prayer , but not Hitpoints . Players with level 63 Herblore can make a super restore potion by using a red spiders' eggs on a snapdragon potion (unf) , giving 142.5 experience . Super restores can further be made into Sanfew serums by adding (in order) unicorn horn dust , snake weed , and nail beast nails into a super restore potion.

The restore value obtained per dose is 8 + 25% of the player's base level (rounded down) in each of the affected skills . For example, a player with 84 Thieving and 63 Smithing would restore both 29 points of Thieving and 23 points of Smithing for each dose consumed. The maximum amount of points that can be restored with this potion is 32 at level 96. This means that a super restore potion will restore 1 more Prayer point per dose than a prayer potion .

If a Prayer cape or ring of the gods (i) is equipped, or a holy wrench is in the player's inventory, the prayer restore increases to 8 + 27% of the player's current Prayer level, rounded down. This does not affect the rate of restoration of stats other than Prayer.

Two 3-dose super restores can be obtained by starting the Zogre Flesh Eaters quest .

After Barbarian Herblore Training is completed, caviar can be added to a super restore(2) to produce a super restore mix . This requires 67 Herblore and provides 48 Herblore experience. A super restore mix has 2 doses, each of which heals 6 Hitpoints in addition to the super restore recovery.

3032:
Agility potions are made by mixing toadflax into a vial of water , creating a Toadflax potion (unf) , and then adding toad's legs . This requires level 34 Herblore , and grants 80 Herblore experience. Agility potions temporarily raise your Agility by 3.

A 4-dose agility potion is required for Tai Bwo Wannai Trio . Ironmen who want to complete the quest but do not have the Herblore requirement can have an irit leaf cleaned by Zahur in Nardah (for 200 coins), then wait for the Dr Jekyll random event, for which he will trade the irit leaf for a 4-dose agility potion. Alternatively, level 40, 63, 72, and 77 skeletons in Tarn's Lair as well as the level 77 skeletons nearby the entrance to the Ruins of Ullek can drop 2-dose agility potions, which can be decanted into a 4-dose potion.

It is also possible to obtain a 4-dose agility potion from the Possessed Priest at the end of Icthlarin's Little Helper . Due to the unique mechanics that determines what potion the priest drops, players looking to get an agility potion from the quest are advised to wear equipment with high magic defence in order to make getting the agility potion more likely.

After Barbarian Herblore Training is completed, caviar can be added to an Agility potion(2) to produce an Agility mix . This requires 37 Herblore and provides 27 Herblore experience. An Agility mix has 2 doses, each of which heals 6 Hitpoints in addition to the normal Agility potion boost.

Alternatively, level 40, 63, 72, and 77 skeletons in Tarn's Lair as well as the level 77 skeletons nearby the entrance to the Ruins of Ullek can drop 2-dose agility potions, which can be decanted into a 4-dose potion.

It is also possible to obtain a 4-dose agility potion from the Possessed Priest at the end of Icthlarin's Little Helper . Due to the unique mechanics that determines what potion the priest drops, players looking to get an agility potion from the quest are advised to wear equipment with high magic defence in order to make getting the agility potion more likely.

After Barbarian Herblore Training is completed, caviar can be added to an Agility potion(2) to produce an Agility mix . This requires 37 Herblore and provides 27 Herblore experience. An Agility mix has 2 doses, each of which heals 6 Hitpoints in addition to the normal Agility potion boost.

Using a magic potion temporarily raises the player's Magic level by 4.

A player with a boosted Magic level will not be able to equip armour/weapons with Magic requirements above their unboosted level, but will be able to cast spells with a higher requirement.

After Barbarian Herblore Training is completed, caviar can be added to a magic potion(2) to produce a magic mix. This requires 83 Herblore and provides 57 Herblore experience. A magic mix has 2 doses, each of which heals 6 Hitpoints in addition to the usual magic potion boost.
