3363:
A thin snail is a piece of raw meat dropped by snails in Mort Myre Swamp . It may be cooked on either a range or a fire , requiring level 12 Cooking . This yields 70 experience and thin snail meat , which heals 5 to 7 hitpoints in one bite.

When used on a pestle and mortar it can be used to create blamish snail slime provided you have a sample bottle in your inventory to collect it. The slime can be used to create blamish oil which is used for an oily fishing rod .

Cooking a thin snail on the Port Phasmatys range is an easy task for the Morytania Diary .
3365:
Lean snail is dropped by snails . They are made into lean snail meat with 17 Cooking yielding 80 Cooking experience . It heals 5-7 Hitpoints . These can be used for Temple Trekking .

When raw, lean snail looks like thin snail , but turns deep red when cooked.

In the activities Temple Trekking /Burgh de Rott Ramble, cooked lean snail can be given to the player's follower for the trek.

Grinding the lean snail produces blamish snail slime used in the blamish oil for Heroes' Quest . You are required to have a sample bottle in your inventory to collect it.
3367:
Fat snails are dropped by Bruise blamish snails and Blood blamish snails in Mort Myre Swamp. They are made into fat snail meat with 22 Cooking yielding 95 Cooking experience. It heals 7-9 Hitpoints. These can be used for Temple Trekking.

It may also be used in Fairytale I - Growing Pains as a quest item for magic secateurs.

It can be ground with a pestle and mortar to produce blamish snail slime used in the blamish oil for the Heroes' Quest. This requires you to have a sample bottle in your inventory to collect it.
3369:
Thin snail meat is a type of food that restores 5 to 7 Hitpoints when eaten. It can be obtained by cooking thin snails on a fire or cooking range , requiring level 12 Cooking and granting 70 experience when successful. When cooking there is a chance to fail, resulting in a burnt snail . Thin snail meat is one of a number of foods with a reduced burn rate while using the Lumbridge Castle range with Cook's Assistant completed. It will stop burning entirely at Cooking level 47, or 43 when using the Lumbridge range.

Cooking thin snail meat is a task in the easy Morytania Diary .
3371: Lean snail meat is a type of food that restores 5 to 8 Hitpoints when eaten. It can be obtained by cooking lean snails on a fire or cooking range , requiring level 17 Cooking and granting 80 experience when successful. When cooking there is a chance to fail, resulting in a burnt snail . The burn rate decreases as the player's Cooking level increases. Lean snail has an unusual burn rate, and has a reduced chance of burning on fires compared to ranges. However lean snail meat is one of a number of foods with a reduced burn rate while using the Lumbridge Castle range with Cook's Assistant completed, and will burn less than on a fire when using this range. It will stop burning entirely on fires at Cooking level 47 and on ranges at level 50, or 43 when using the Lumbridge range.
3373: Fat snail meat is a type of food that restores 7 to 9 Hitpoints when eaten. It can be obtained by cooking fat snail on a fire or cooking range, requiring level 22 Cooking and granting 95 experience when successful. When cooking there is a chance to fail, resulting in a burnt snail. The burn rate decreases as the player's Cooking level increases. Fat snail meat is one of a number of foods with a reduced burn rate while using the Lumbridge Castle range with Cook's Assistant completed. It will stop burning entirely at Cooking level 56 or 51 when using the Lumbridge range.
3375:
Burnt snail is the result of accidentally burning either a thin snail , lean snail , or fat snail The burn rate while cooking these will decrease as players reach higher Cooking levels.

The burnt snail has no use whatsoever. Like most other burnt food, it is tradeable to other players but not on the Grand Exchange .
3377:
A sample bottle can be purchased from Fidelio in the Canifis General Store or from Rasolo the Wandering Merchant. It is used to collect blamish snail slime.

The best way of obtaining a sample bottle is to go to Canifis and buy it for 10 coins from Fidelio. Although it resembles an empty vial, it cannot be used for any of a normal vial's storage functions.

A sample bottle is also obtained when using the strange potion on Sithik Ints' tea during the Zogre Flesh Eaters quest. Another sample bottle is obtained during Heroes' Quest in the process of creating Blamish oil.
3379:
Raw slimy eel is a fish that can be caught with a fishing rod and fishing bait. They require a Fishing level of 28 to catch, and grant 80 Fishing experience per catch when caught in the Lumbridge Swamp Caves, Dorgesh-Kaan South Dungeon, or the Ruins of Camdozaal. They grant 65 Fishing experience when caught in the Mort Myre Swamp. It can be cooked into cooked slimy eel with a Cooking level of 28.

Raw slimy eel is one of the required items in Land of the Goblins, where it is used as bait to catch a Hemenster whitefish. It is also a possible item needed to obtain the magic secateurs in Fairytale I - Growing Pains.
3381: Cooked slimy eel is a type of fish that restores 6 to 10 Hitpoints when eaten. It can be obtained by cooking raw slimy eels on a fire or cooking range , requiring level 28 Cooking and granting 95 experience when successful. When cooking there is a chance to fail, resulting in a burnt eel . The burn rate decreases as the player's Cooking level increases, and it will stop burning entirely at Cooking level 61.
3383: Burnt eel is the result of accidentally burning a slimy eel while attempting to make a cooked slimy eel . The burn rate while cooking these will decrease as players reach higher Cooking levels, stopping entirely at level 61.
3385:
A splitbark helm is a piece of splitbark armour worn in the headwear slot . Level 40 Magic and 40 Defence are required to wear it. A splitbark helm can be created by using a needle and thread on two pieces of fine cloth and two bark , requiring 61 Crafting. Alternatively, it can be made without the Crafting requirement by giving two bark , two fine cloth , and 6,000 coins to Wizard Jalarast at the Wizards' Tower . They can also be obtained by looting ninja implings found in Puro-Puro or around Gielinor .

The splitbark helm can be stored in the Magic wardrobe of the Costume Room in a player-owned house .
3387:
The splitbark body is a piece of splitbark armour worn in the body slot . 40 Magic and 40 Defence are required to wear it. A splitbark body can be created by using a needle and thread on four pieces of fine cloth and four bark , requiring 62 Crafting. Alternatively, it can be made without the Crafting requirement by giving four bark , four fine cloth , and 37,000 coins to Wizard Jalarast at the Wizards' Tower . An alternative to this is the Lunar torso which has slightly lower defence stats.

It can be stored in a magic wardrobe in a player-owned house.
3389:
Splitbark legs are a piece of splitbark armour worn in the legs slot . 40 Magic and 40 Defence are required to wear them. Splitbark legs can be created by using a needle and thread on three pieces of fine cloth and three bark , requiring 62 Crafting. Alternatively, they can be made without the Crafting requirement by giving three bark , three fine cloth , and 32,000 coins to Wizard Jalarast at the Wizards' Tower .

It can be stored in a magic wardrobe in a player-owned house.
3391:
Splitbark gauntlets are a piece of splitbark armour worn in the hands slot . 40 Magic and 40 Defence are required to wear them. Splitbark gauntlets can be created by using a needle and thread on a piece of fine cloth and bark , requiring 60 Crafting. Alternatively, they can be made without the Crafting requirement by giving a bark , a fine cloth , and 1,000 coins to Wizard Jalarast at the Wizards' Tower . They can also be obtained by looting magpie implings found in Puro-Puro or around Gielinor .

It can be stored in a magic wardrobe in a player-owned house.
3393:
Splitbark boots are a piece of splitbark armour worn in the feet slot . 40 Magic and 40 Defence are required to wear them. Splitbark boots can be created by using a needle and thread on a piece of fine cloth and bark , requiring 60 Crafting. Alternatively, they can be made without the Crafting requirement by giving a bark , a fine cloth , and 1,000 coins to Wizard Jalarast at the Wizards' Tower . They have similar bonuses as Iron boots , except for the better magic bonuses.

It can be stored in a magic wardrobe in a player-owned house.
3395:
The Diary of Herbi Flax , titled Diary in-game, is found on the shelves in a ruined house towards the south-west side of Mort'ton during the Shades of Mort'ton quest. It describes some experiments run by Herbi Flax as he was trying to find a cure for the strange malady affecting the people of Mort'ton and describes how to make Serum 207 and Serum 208 .

It can also be found in the bookcase in your house or on the same shelf of the same Mort'ton house during the Temple Trekking shades event.

If players take the Diary of Herbi Flax to the Apothecary in Varrock during or after the quest, they will get an extra 335 Herblore experience. This can only be done once.
3396:
Loar remains are an item found and used in the Shades of Mort'ton minigame. To obtain these remains, the player must kill loar shades, located around Mort'ton. To burn the loar remains, the player needs some pyre logs (see table for more info) and a tinderbox. First place the pyre logs on a funeral pyre, followed by the loar remains, then light the pyre. This will grant the player Firemaking and Prayer experience (see table).

Once burned, a bronze shade key or some coins will appear next to the pyre. The keys can be used either to enter the catacombs or to open the corresponding coloured doors to chests containing valuable items.

Coins and keys dropped by cremating these remains will not despawn for five minutes, and cannot be taken by other players during this time. When dropped by the player, they will despawn and become visible to others at the normal rate.
3398:
Phrin remains are an item found and used in the Shades of Mort'ton minigame . To obtain these remains, the player must kill phrin shades , located in the Shade Catacombs .

To burn the phrin remains, the player needs some pyre logs (see table for more info) and a tinderbox . First place the pyre logs on a funeral pyre , followed by the phrin remains, then light the pyre. This will grant the player Firemaking and Prayer experience (see table). Once burned, a bronze or steel shade key , or some coins , will appear next to the pyre. The keys can be used to either enter the catacombs or open the corresponding coloured doors to chests containing valuable items.

Coins and keys dropped by cremating these remains will not despawn for five minutes, and cannot be taken by other players during this time. When dropped by the player, they will despawn and become visible to others at the normal rate.
3400:
Riyl remains are an item found and used in the Shades of Mort'ton minigame . To obtain these remains, the player must kill riyl shades , located behind a solid steel door in the Shade Catacombs .

To burn the riyl remains, the player needs willow pyre logs or better and a tinderbox . First place the pyre logs on a funeral pyre , followed by the riyl remains, then light the pyre. This will grant the player Firemaking and Prayer experience (see table). Once burned, a steel or black shade key , or some coins , will appear next to the pyre. The keys can be used to either enter the catacombs or open the corresponding coloured doors to chests containing valuable items.

Coins and keys dropped by cremating these remains will not despawn for five minutes, and cannot be taken by other players during this time. When dropped by the player, they will despawn and become visible to others at the normal rate.
3402:
Asyn remains are an item found and used in the Shades of Mort'ton minigame . To obtain these remains, the player must kill asyn shades , located behind a solid black door in the Shade Catacombs . Shades encountered during Temple Trekking may also drop asyn remains.

To burn the asyn remains, the player needs yew pyre logs or better, level 65 Firemaking, and a tinderbox . First place the pyre logs on a funeral pyre , followed by the asyn remains, then light the pyre. This will grant the player Firemaking and Prayer experience (see table). Once burned, a black or silver shade key , or some coins , will appear next to the pyre. The keys can be used to either enter the catacombs or open the corresponding coloured doors to chests containing valuable items.

Coins and keys dropped by cremating these remains will not despawn for five minutes, and cannot be taken by other players during this time. When dropped by the player, they will despawn and become visible to others at the normal rate.
3404:
Fiyr remains are an item found and used in the Shades of Mort'ton minigame . To obtain these remains, the player must kill fiyr shades , located behind a solid silver door in the Shade Catacombs . Shades encountered during Temple Trekking may also drop fiyr remains.

To burn the fiyr remains, first place magic , ironwood , redwood or rosewood pyre logs on a funeral pyre , followed by the fiyr remains, then light the pyre with a tinderbox . This will grant the player Firemaking and Prayer experience (see table). Once burned, a silver or gold shade key , or some coins , will appear next to the pyre.

Gold keys give unrestricted access to all areas of the Shade Catacombs and can open gold rewards chests, while silver keys give access to all areas up to the fiyr area in the north-west corner of the catacombs and can open silver rewards chests.

Coins and keys dropped by cremating these remains will not despawn for five minutes, and cannot be taken by other players during this time. When dropped by the player, they will despawn and become visible to others at the normal rate.
3406: An unfinished potion is made by using ashes on a vial of water after reaching a certain point in Shades of Mort'ton . Using a tarromin on an unfinished potion yields Serum 207 and 50 Herblore experience.
3408:
Serum 207 is a potion that can be made after reading the diary of Herbi Flax during the Shades of Mort'ton quest, by adding ashes to a tarromin potion (unf), requiring level 15 Herblore and yielding 50 Herblore experience. It can be used to temporarily cure the otherwise incoherent, afflicted villagers of Mort'ton in exchange for a reward, as part of the Shades of Mort'ton minigame. It can also be used on the lit fire altar inside the Mort'ton temple, requiring 20% sanctity, to turn it into serum 208, which can be used to cure the afflicted in return for better rewards.

As the possible rewards for curing the afflicted include all the items required to make the potion, and the only other potions that can be made with tarromin are strength potions, which give the same experience but require limpwurt root to make, making serum 207 can be used as an inexpensive, albeit slow, method of training Herblore.

Unlike other potions, the process of creating serum 207 doesn't have make-x option; instead, the player will keep creating them automatically until they run out of supplies.

3416:
Serum 208 is a permanent cure for the afflicted villagers of Mort'ton. It is used during or after the Shades of Mort'ton quest to turn the afflicted back to normal. It can be created by using Serum 207 on the sacred flame at the rebuilt temple. Players must have at least 20% sanctity in order to convert Serum 207 into Serum 208, consuming 5% sanctity per dose. Therefore, it is recommended to convert Serum 207 with at least 2 doses to permanently cure the necessary NPCs (total of two) without wasting additional sanctity. Unlike Serum 207, it cannot be stored in Potion storage.

It is suggested it be used on Razmire Keelgan, so he will always be coherent for the player and open his general and builder's stores. When used on an afflicted villager, they will turn into Mort'ton locals and reward the player with items such as Olive oil, Tarromin, and Coins.

Limestone bricks can be crafted through the Crafting skill at level 12 by using a chisel with limestone , granting 6 Crafting experience . Note that you may inadvertently create a rock if you are too heavy-handed with the chisel.

Bricks can be purchased for 26 coins from the Stonemason in Keldagrim or Metla in the Stonecutter Outpost , or for 21 coins from Razmire at his builders store in Mort'ton . Rasolo , the wandering merchant south-east of Baxtorian Falls , also sells two for 40 coins.

Limestone bricks are used in the Construction skill, providing 20 Construction experience each. They are also used in rebuilding the Mort'ton temple during the Shades of Mort'ton quest and minigame , as well as to construct additional Quetzal Transport System landing zones, requiring 3 limestone bricks each. The Flamtaer bag , obtainable from chests within the Shade Catacombs is able to store up to 60 limestone bricks.

Olive oil is an item used in the Shades of Mort'ton minigame . It may be purchased from Razmire 's general store in Mort'ton for 28 coins or from Rasolo the wandering merchant for 40 coins. It is also sometimes received from giving Serum 207 or Serum 208 to the Afflicted found wandering in the town.

To create sacred oil , an item used in the preparation of pyre logs , players must first help to restore the Temple of Mort'ton that lies to the north-east of the town. Restoration also earns points. Once the temple is rebuilt, players may light the altar in the centre of the temple and use their olive oil on the fire. This converts the ordinary olive oil into sacred oil , consuming sanctity. Each 4 dose item, when sanctified, consumes 3.6% sanctity, but requires at least 10% to sanctify.

Sacred oil is a vial of blessed olive oil that is used to make pyre logs . It is obtained from the Shades of Mort'ton minigame , by using vials of olive oil on the fire altar , once the temple has been fully repaired and the altar lit. Converting olive oil to sacred oil costs sanctity points, which are gained by repairing the temple's walls or by killing the loar shades that attack the temple. Each dose of olive oil costs about 0.9% sanctity to convert; a 4-dose vial of olive oil will cost about 3.6% sanctity to convert into sacred oil. Additionally, players must have at least 10% sanctity in order to convert olive oil into sacred oil.

Sacred oil's sole use is to create pyre logs, which may be used to cremate the remains of various shades. Pyre logs are made by adding sacred oil to logs , which grants 5 Firemaking experience per dose of oil used on the log. Different logs require different amounts of sacred oil, with low-end logs requiring 2 doses, mid-tier logs requiring 3 doses, and high-end logs requiring 4 doses.

Note: Players who haven't completed the Shades of Mort'ton quest will not be able to use sacred oil to create pyre logs. Attempting to do so gives the message This sacred oil doesn't seem fresh. You should make your own.

Cremating shade remains in Mort'ton is necessary to obtain various keys that allow access to the Shade Catacombs and the reward chests within. In both cases, Firemaking and Prayer experience are gained in the process.

This item can be stored in the treasure chest of a costume room, provided that the interface of the corresponding clue tier is opened before attempting to store the item. Alternatively, the item can be used on the opened treasure chest to insert it without viewing the interface, as part of the black trimmed armour. Ultimate Ironmen will be unable to retrieve individual pieces until the full set is stored.

The Zamorak plateskirt is a decorated rune plateskirt affiliated with the god Zamorak. Sharing the same stats as the rune plateskirt (with the exception of a +1 prayer bonus and weighing 1kg more), the Zamorak plateskirt also looks visually similar. Its appearance differs in that the skirt features an ornamental red trim, manifesting as the symbol of Zamorak.

The plateskirt requires 40 Defence to wear and cannot be made using the Smithing skill. Players can obtain a Zamorak plateskirt as a reward for completing hard Treasure Trails.

Wearing any piece of this armour set will cause followers of Zamorak to become unaggressive to the player upon entering the God Wars Dungeon.

This item can be stored in the treasure chest of a costume room, provided that the interface of the corresponding clue tier is opened before attempting to store the item. Alternatively, the item can be used on the opened treasure chest to insert it without viewing the interface, as part of the Zamorak armour set. Ultimate Ironmen will be unable to retrieve individual pieces until the full set is stored.

A casket could previously be received after completing any step of a Treasure Trail . These caskets did not always contain a reward, and sometimes only gave another clue scroll.

On 28 July 2016 Treasure Trails were updated. Caskets were replaced with new items called Reward caskets . They are only received once all steps have been completed, and are guaranteed to contain a reward.

Although caskets are no longer obtainable, they are still ingame for any player who had one before the update, making them a rare example of a discontinued item in Old School RuneScape .

3565:
Puzzle boxes can be obtained by doing hard, elite, and master Treasure Trails . Before you are able to continue with your clue scroll, you will have to complete the puzzle.

A puzzle box is always scrambled 101 times before being handed to the player, by randomly sliding a piece into the empty position starting from the solved state. [ 1 ]

If you have a duplicate puzzle box, (obtained by a method such as the Drop trick ) in your inventory or bank after completing the clue, you cannot obtain another clue.

On 28 July 2016 Treasure Trails were updated. Caskets were replaced with new items called Reward caskets . They are only received once all steps have been completed, and are guaranteed to contain a reward.

Although caskets are no longer obtainable, they are still ingame for any player who had one before the update, making them a rare example of a discontinued item in Old School RuneScape .

A key is an item needed to unlock a chest or drawer during a Treasure Trail.

There will be a clue telling you where to get it. The key is a drop only when carrying the clue scroll. It disappears when used to open the chest or drawer. Keys are non-tradeable objects, specific to the player who finds them. They are used on all levels of treasure trails.

It is possible to obtain more than one key using the drop trick. However, after taking a clue from the chest/drawer, the key won't open it again, and the player gets a message: "The chest (or drawer) is locked." Keys obtained this way from the same clue will still remain in the bank; however, keys obtained from different clues will not stack.

"Viking toy ship" was the internal name used for an unobtainable item added on 26 October 2004. Aside from this, nothing is known about the item.

Presumably it would have served a similar purpose as the Toy ship obtained during The Fremennik Trials , although the toy ship is a separate item with the internal name "Viking pointless ship toy" instead. It is possible that the item was accidentally added to the live game a week early.

By 2 November 2004, the item had been deleted. It was later replaced by the Lifeboat .

The Flamtaer hammer is an item used during the Shades of Mort'ton minigame. It is a replacement for the regular hammer when building the temple, and is approximately 75% faster. It acts as an invisible +40 Crafting boost while rebuilding the temple in the Shades of Mort'ton minigame. The Flamtaer hammer can be bought from Razmire Keelgan at the Mort'ton general store or from Rasolo the Wandering Merchant near Baxtorian Falls.

It can also be obtained from the keys made from shade remains when looting various chests in the Shade Catacombs.

The Fremennik is an interface item that can be seen in the Thieving skill guide, representing Fremennik citizens.

Skill guides are in fact inventories containing a series of items. In order to represent NPCs or scenery in a skill guide, examinable items had to be created for each.

The actual item cannot be obtained by players.
3688: An unstrung lyre can be made by cutting a branch from the swaying tree east of Rellekka (requires an axe ) and then using a knife on it. The unstrung lyre can be strung using a ball of golden wool , which turns it into a normal lyre .
3689:
A lyre is crafted by a player during The Fremennik Trials quest. The lyre is needed in the quest to perform in the longhall to get Olaf the Bard's vote to become a Fremennik.

The lyre can then be enchanted by Fossegrimen to make an enchanted lyre and progress with the quest.
3690:
The enchanted lyre is acquired in The Fremennik Trials quest . It is used in the quest to perform in the longhall to get Olaf the Bard 's vote for the player to become a Fremennik . The lyre can be made by using an axe to cut a branch from the swaying tree east of Rellekka , and then using a knife on the branch to obtain an unstrung lyre , then attaching spun golden fleece . This part needs 25 Fletching . Alternatively, players may receive one as a drop from Lanzig , Borrokar , or Freidir in their huts in the south-eastern area of the village.

After the quest, the player can enchant their normal lyre into an enchanted lyre by charging it with Fossegrimen to be used as a teleport to Rellekka . When the hard Fremennik Diary is completed, the enchanted lyre can also teleport to Waterbirth Island , and gains the ability to teleport to Jatizso and Neitiznot after completion of the elite Fremennik Diary .

3692: A branch can be cut from the swaying tree east of Rellekka . The branch may be turned into an unstrung lyre by using a knife on it, and the lyre may be strung by using golden wool on the unstrung lyre. Golden wool may be spun from golden fleece , an item obtained from Lalli . Doing so requires level 40 Crafting . The branch may be cut before starting The Fremennik Trials .
3693:
Golden fleece is a quest item obtained during The Fremennik Trials quest. It is obtained from Lalli for making stew with a 'magical' pet rock. The fleece is spun into golden wool at a spinning wheel, which can then be used to string the unstrung lyre. Note that the spinning wheel in Rellekka cannot be used to spin the fleece, since the use of facilities in Rellekka requires completion of The Fremennik Trials. The closest available spinning wheel is therefore in Seers' Village.

If players have not yet finished the Bard's Trial portion of the quest, they can use the drop trick to obtain more than one golden fleece. However, after the entire quest is completed, Lalli will sell the fleece for 1000 coins each.
3694: Golden wool is a special ball of wool used to string an unstrung lyre during The Fremennik Trials quest , creating a normal lyre . The wool can be obtained by using some golden fleece on a spinning wheel (granting 2.5 crafting experience), the closest of which being in south-west Rellekka , in the same building as the anvil .
3695:
A pet rock can be obtained from Askeladden during and after The Fremennik Trials quest. After the quest multiple pet rocks can be obtained by talking to him again.

Rocks are a good choice for a pet, as they do not require food or exercise. [ 1 ] The pet rock is comfortably held in both hands, meaning it cannot be used as a weapon ; unarmed attacks are instead used while the pet rock is equipped. The pet rock does not confer any stat bonuses or penalties.

Pet rocks will happily live in the cat basket or menagerie of a player-owned house . When dropped inside a house, it will responsibly stay in its spot, patiently waiting for the player to come back. Picking your pet rock up while standing in your POH Menagerie is a task in the Medium Fremennik Diary . If a pet rock is dropped in the centre of a globe or boss lair display hotspot, the furniture can be built, but it will not be possible to retrieve the rock without destroying the furniture.

The pet rock is not lost on death, despite being a pet, and instead loyally waits at the player's gravestone.
3696:
The Hunters' talisman is a quest item used in The Fremennik Trials quest. It is given to the player by Sigli the Huntsman in order to track down an otherwise invisible spirit called the Draugen. The player must use the talisman to locate and then defeat the Draugen to earn Sigli's vote during the quest.

It's possible to obtain multiple talismans via the drop-trick. This can also be done after defeating Draugen. However, doing this will force you to hunt him down again.

3698: The exotic flower is a quest item used in the merchanting section of The Fremennik Trials quest. It is obtained by giving a Fremennik ballad to the sailor in the north-west corner of Rellekka . The flower can then be given to Sigmund the Merchant in order to complete his part of the quest.
3699:
The Fremennik ballad is a quest item used in The Fremennik Trials quest and is used as part of the favour used to obtain Sigmund the Merchant's vote.

It is obtained by giving a pair of sturdy boots to Olaf the Bard in Rellekka. The ballad can then be given to the sailor in the north-west corner of Rellekka in exchange for an exotic flower. If it is lost or dropped, another can be obtained from Olaf.
3700: Sturdy boots are a quest item used in The Fremennik Trials quest. They are obtained by giving a fiscal statement to Yrsa in Rellekka. The boots can then be given to Olaf the Bard who will then compose a Fremennik ballad, which you will then have to give to the sailor. He will then give you an exotic flower which when given to Sigmund the Merchant, will be exchanged for his vote.
3701: The tracking map is a quest item used in The Fremennik Trials quest. It is obtained by giving a custom bowstring to Sigli the Huntsman in Rellekka. The map can then be given to Brundt the Chieftain in exchange for a fiscal statement.
3702: The custom bow string is a quest item used in The Fremennik Trials quest. It is obtained by giving an Unusual fish to Skulgrimen in Rellekka . The bowstring can then be given to Sigli the Huntsman in exchange for a Tracking map .
3703: The unusual fish is a quest item used in Sigmund the Merchant section of the The Fremennik Trials quest. It is obtained by giving a sea fishing map to the fisherman in Rellekka . The fish can then be given to Skulgrimen in exchange for a custom bowstring .
3704: The sea fishing map is a quest item used in The Fremennik Trials quest . It is obtained by giving a weather forecast from Peer the Seer to Swensen in exchange for an unusual fish for Skulgrimen .
3705: The weather forecast is a quest item used in The Fremennik Trials quest . It is obtained by giving a warriors' contract to Peer the Seer in Rellekka . The forecast can then be given to Swensen in exchange for a sea fishing map . It is an absolute requirement for the completion of The Fremennik Trials quest.
3706: The champions token is a quest item in The Fremennik Trials quest. It is obtained by giving a legendary cocktail to Manni the Reveller in Rellekka. The token is given to Thorvald the Warrior in exchange for a warriors' contract, which is exchanged for a Weather forecast from Peer the Seer.
3707:
The legendary cocktail is a quest item used in The Fremennik Trials quest. It is obtained by giving a promissory note to Thora the Barkeep in Rellekka. The cocktail can then be given to Manni the Reveller in exchange for a champions token.

If one asks Manni what it tastes like after giving it to him, he'll say it was mostly like tomato juice.
3708:
The fiscal statement is a quest item used in The Fremennik Trials quest and is used as part of the favour used to obtain Sigmund the Merchant's vote.

It is obtained by giving a tracking map to Brundt the Chieftain in Rellekka. The statement can then be given to Yrsa in exchange for a pair of sturdy boots. The statement confirms that the sales tax that is enforced on the salespeople of Rellekka, including Yrsa, is taken out of effect.
3709:
The promissory note is a quest item used in The Fremennik Trials. It is obtained by giving 5,000 coins to Askeladden in Rellekka. The note can then be given to Thora the Barkeep in exchange for a legendary cocktail.

The promissory note is basically a contract to stop Askeladden from entering the bar because he is underage. However, as he is Fremennik, he will be able to enter the bar after completing his trials, as he will get a new Fremennik name.
3710: The warriors' contract is a quest item in The Fremennik Trials quest . Thorvald the Warrior will exchange it for a champions token . It is given to Peer the Seer for a weather forecast .
3711: A keg of beer is found in the Rellekka Longhall during The Fremennik Trials . Unlike the normal keg of beer , it does not have a drink option. The keg is used to challenge Manni the Reveller to a drinking contest, although with this keg, you will always lose. To get his vote in the quest, you need to switch out this keg with a low alcohol keg .
3712: A low alcohol keg is a quest item used in The Fremennik Trials quest. It can be bought from the poison salesman in Seers' Village bar for 250 coins and then swapped for a regular keg so the player can beat Manni the Reveller in a drinking contest. According to the salesman, it tastes like a beer, but without side effects.
3713:
A strange object is a quest item obtained from the council workman in the Fremennik Trials quest by giving him a beer. Upon use on a tinderbox (or vice versa), it will become a Lit strange object.

Due to its appearance and explosive properties, the strange object is presumed to be a cherry bomb. This item can take the users Hitpoints to 0, resulting in death, making it potentially useful for suiciding.

This object remains obtainable after the quest.
3714:
The lit strange object is an item obtained during the The Fremennik Trials quest by using a tinderbox on a strange object (or vice versa). In the quest, the lit strange object is placed in a pipe outside the Rellekka longhall to distract its occupants while you replace a keg of beer with non-alcoholic beer.

The lit strange object will explode if in the player's inventory within 70-100 seconds after igniting a strange object. This will deal 4% of the player's current Hitpoints in damage, rounded down, with a minimum of 2. This can kill the player. Any remaining lit strange objects in the inventory will revert to an unlit state after the explosion.
3718: The magnet is found during The Fremennik Trials as part of Peer the Seer 's puzzle. It is a useless item that distracts from the solution to the puzzle. Its examine text is a physics pun.
3719: Blue thread is a quest item found during The Fremennik Trials quest. It is found while searching Peer the Seer's house when trying to solve the challenge to get his vote. It serves no purpose during the quest.
3720: The small pick is a quest item found during The Fremennik Trials quest. It is found while searching Peer the Seer 's house while trying to solve his challenge to get his vote. The small pick is the real red herring as it serves no purpose during the quest. Players using the pick on the locked chest will get the message, You might be able to break the chest open using this pick... ... if you stood here tapping at it for twenty years or so. In addition, players who use the pick on the vase will get the message, This pick wouldn't be strong enough to break the vase open.
3721:
The toy ship is a quest item found during The Fremennik Trials quest. It is found while searching Peer the Seer's house while trying to solve his challenge to get his vote.

Although the player will also find a red herring while searching, the toy ship is the real red herring as it serves no purpose during the quest.
3722: The Full bucket is used in Peer the Seer 's trial for the quest The Fremennik Trials .
3723: A 4/5ths full bucket is used in Peer the Seer's trial for the quest The Fremennik Trials. This is used on the chest with the scale on top to receive a vase.
3724: A 3/5ths full bucket is used in Peer the Seer 's trial for the quest The Fremennik Trials . To get this, players must use an empty jug on the tap to get a full jug , then use the full jug on the empty bucket .
3725: A 2/5ths full bucket is used in Peer the Seer's trial for the quest The Fremennik Trials.

3728: The frozen bucket is a quest item found in The Fremennik Trials quest. It is made by using the full bucket on the frozen table. It has no use during the quest, but can be used on the range to create an empty bucket again.
3729: The full jug is a quest item found in The Fremennik Trials quest. It is made by using the empty jug on the tap. The full jug is used in conjunction with the empty bucket to create a 4/5ths full bucket , needed to progress in the quest.
3730: The 2/3rds full jug is a quest item found in The Fremennik Trials quest. This is obtained by using a full bucket on an empty jug, emptying the jug in the drain, then using the 2/5ths full bucket again onto the empty jug.
3731: The 1/3rds full jug is a quest item in The Fremennik Trials quest. It is made by using a full jug on an empty bucket, then filling up the jug again and pouring it into the bucket. Using it on a 3/5ths full bucket makes the 4/5ths full bucket needed to advance the quest.
3732: The empty jug is a quest item found in The Fremennik Trials quest. It can be found by searching a chest to the east in Peer the Seer's house during his challenge.
3733: The frozen jug is a quest item found in The Fremennik Trials quest. It is made by using the full jug on the frozen table. It has no use during the quest, but can be used on the range to create a jug again.
3734: The vase is a quest item used in The Fremennik Trials quest. It is found during Peer the Seer 's part of the quest while searching upstairs in his house. 3735: The vase of water is a quest item used in The Fremennik Trials quest. It is made by using the vase on the water tap in Peer the Seer 's trial. The vase lid can then be used on it, creating a sealed vase , which can be frozen and shattered, revealing the frozen key inside.
3736: The frozen vase is a quest item used in The Fremennik Trials quest . It is made by using the vase of water on the frozen table in Peer the Seer 's task, but it has no use. To proceed with the quest, the vase lid must be used on the vase of water, and then used on the frozen table.

3748:
Fremennik helms are a medium level helmet that requires 30 Defence and completion of The Fremennik Trials quest to wear. Fremennik helms are dropped by Fremennik guards and Dagannoth on Waterbirth Island , and they can also be obtained from Fremennik shipwrecks . It has the same combat stats as an adamant full helm , but is a bit lighter.

Bardur in Waterbirth Island dungeon will give a cooked shark in exchange for a Fremennik helm, Fremennik blade or Fremennik shield .
3749:
The archer helm can be purchased from the Skulgrimen's Battle Gear for 78,000 coins after completing The Fremennik Trials quest. Players must have a Defence level of at least 45 and have completed The Fremennik Trials quest in order to wear it. It is also a possible reward from the High Gamble in Barbarian Assault.

The archer helm is commonly worn by players in the Wilderness, as its low cost makes it easy to replace for both standard and ironman accounts if lost to a player killer.
3751:
The berserker helm is a mid-levelled melee-based helmet. Players must have level 45 Defence and also have completed the quest The Fremennik Trials in order to wear it. It can be purchased from Skulgrimen's Battle Gear shop in Rellekka for 78,000 coins. It's also a possible reward from Barbarian Assault High Gambles or a drop from a dagannoth.

This helmet is favoured among combat pures for being the second lowest level headgear to offer a Strength bonus, which offers the same strength bonus as a helm of Neitiznot and an obsidian helmet.

The berserker helm's defensive bonuses are roughly on par with the rune full helm. More specifically, the berserker helm is slightly better than the rune full helm in both stab and crush defence, but is slightly worse in slash defence.

Skulgrimen's Battle Gear will buy this helmet from a player for 42,000 coins, which is more than the High Level Alchemy price of 36,000 coins.
3753:
A warrior helm is a piece of armour that can be worn by players who have completed The Fremennik Trials quest and have a Defence level of 45. The helm can be bought at the Skulgrimen's Battle Gear shop in Rellekka for 78,000 coins . It's also a possible reward from Barbarian Assault High Gambles .

Due to its lack of a strength bonus, the warrior helm is far less popular than its counterpart, the berserker helm , despite having a small slash bonus (+5) and better defence against the slash attacks (+33 instead of +29). However, it is a good alternative to the fighter hat , assuming those who plan to use the warrior helm are using a slash weapon, especially considering that it provides slightly better resistance to all attacks.
3755: The farseer helm is a piece of Fremennik armour. To wear a farseer helm, players must have completed The Fremennik Trials quest and have a Defence level of at least 45. To obtain this helmet you can buy one from Skulgrimen in Rellekka for 78,000 coins, trade with another player or receive one as a drop from Dagannoth. It can also be obtained through gambling points in the Barbarian Assault minigame and as loot from sorting Fremennik salvage.
3757:
The Fremennik blade is a slash weapon equivalent to an adamant scimitar. This weapon is dropped by various Fremennik people in Rellekka, Fremennik warriors, and some monsters on Waterbirth Island. Completion of The Fremennik Trials and 30 Attack is required to equip it. The sword is not tradeable.

Bardur, in the Waterbirth Island Dungeon, will trade a cooked shark for any Fremennik blade, shield, or helm brought to him.

The player will be awarded a Fremennik blade if they successfully defeat Koschei the deathless' final form. However, they still need to complete the quest in order to wield it.
3758:
The Fremennik shield is a shield commonly worn by Fremennik warriors. To wield one, the player must have completed The Fremennik Trials quest. They can be obtained as a monster drop from Fremennik market guards , dagannoth (only in the Waterbirth Island Dungeon ) or Fremennik warriors . A Defence level of 30 is required to wield the shield.

The stats of the shield are identical to those of an adamant kiteshield except that the Fremennik shield is lighter.

Bardur , located in the Waterbirth Island dungeon, will trade you one shark for a Fremennik blade , a Fremennik shield or a Fremennik helm . However, it is usually more cost-effective to high-alch them, due to how out of the way Bardur is, and the value of sharks. This is still useful to players who are slaying dagannoth, as trading it for food can extend their trips.

Bardur will also sell players a shield for 150,000 during The Fremennik Exiles . He can also be charmed into giving the player one for free with the Ring of Charos(a) .

The Fremennik shield is a required item in The Fremennik Exiles quest.

3801:
A keg of beer is a large barrel of ale that restores 15 Hitpoints and temporarily boosts Strength by 10% +2, while draining Attack by 50% + 5 (see table below).

It can be bought in the Rellekka Longhall for 325 coins, provided that the player has completed The Fremennik Trials quest. It can also be bought from the merchant Rasolo for 500 coins, who is north of Ardougne near Baxtorian Falls . A special keg of beer can be found on the table in the longhall, which is swapped out with a low alcohol keg during The Fremennik Trials in order to win the drinking contest.

Upon drinking it, the chatbox states, "You chug the keg. You feel reinvigorated... ...but extremely drunk, too." while the player character raises the keg above their head and chugs the entire barrel . This also causes the perspective of the player's screen to swing back and forth for a minute, as if their character is drunk. This can be stopped by teleporting .

Kegs of beer can also be sold to Askeladden on Waterbirth Island . He will buy them for 500 before The Fremennik Trials and 700 after. He will not buy noted kegs of beer, however.
3803:
A beer tankard is a type of ale that restores 4 Hitpoints and temporarily boosts Strength by 4% + 2 while draining Attack by 10% +2.

Players can buy a tankard of beer from Thora the Barkeep in the Rellekka Longhall Bar . The spawn within the bar cannot be taken unless you have started The Fremennik Trials ; Manni the Reveller will tell you to get your hands off his beer . Unlike other ales, it cannot be brewed .

After drinking the beer, the message reads "You quaff the beer. You feel slightly reinvigorated... but very dizzy too".
3805:
A tankard is the Fremennik equivalent of a beer glass. Players are unable to make them. However, they may be picked up from the tankard respawn point in the Rellekka longhall.

Players can buy a beer tankard from Thora the Barkeep in the Rellekka longhall for 26 coins. Drinking the tankard of beer leaves an empty tankard and causes the usual beer effects to players. Just as with beer glasses, if a player uses a tankard on a barrel with a tap on it and the examine info says "It's got ale in it", they will get free beer.

The damaged book is a book held in the shield slot that can be obtained for 5,000 coins from Jossik after completing Horror from the Deep . The four Saradomin pages can be added to upgrade it to the holy book , which gives a defence bonus. Both the damaged and upgraded book count as a god item for Saradomin in the God Wars Dungeon .

After completing Horror from the Deep, you are rewarded with a damaged book of your choice: either Saradomin, Guthix, or Zamorak. You do not need to complete your current damaged book before obtaining a new one of a different type from Jossik. You can buy every damaged book in the same day. Dropping or destroying a damaged book and talking to Jossik results in him returning it to you.

You can check which pages are currently in your incomplete book with the "Check" option. Once you have filled the book, you cannot take the pages out.
3840:
The holy book is a book held in place of a shield , and is the god book aligned with Saradomin . God books are commonly used for their prayer bonus, something few shields offer. The Holy book is obtained from the Horror from the Deep quest. The book is received from the quest as just a cover, and requires 4 Saradomin pages obtained from Treasure Trails to be completed. The book will not give any bonuses (with the exception of the +5 prayer bonus) until it is completed. An incomplete holy book does count as a Saradomin item in the Hallowed Sepulchre . With 50 Prayer and a completed book, players can enchant unblessed symbols into holy symbols .

Equipping a holy book allows the player to preach and perform ceremonies, such as blessing, last rites, and wedding rites, by operating it (none of which have any effect on the game itself, and are simply recited lines of text), costing 25% of the player's special attack energy.

Lost holy books can be reclaimed by speaking to Jossik , complete with all pages that have been added, for no cost. Alternatively, for those who do not wish to travel to the Lighthouse , Perdu will return them to players for 12,000 coins .

Due to its lack of offensive bonuses and the defensive bonuses being relatively small compared to other offhands, Holy book is among the less popular godbooks, however it can still be useful for some dangerous activities where fighting back is not desired but the prayer bonus or easy reclaimability is advantageous, such as Pyramid Plunder or skilling in the Wilderness (e.g. hunting black chinchompas , mining runite ore , Runecrafting through the Abyss , running the Wilderness Agility Course ).

Filling the holy book currently costs 3,151 coins when buying each page individually or 13,985 coins when buying the item set .

It can be filled with the 4 pages obtained from Treasure Trails , granting attack bonuses and the ability to preach lines from the book. With 50 Prayer and a completed book, players can enchant unpowered symbols into unholy symbols .

The Zamorak unholy book provides the best all-around attack bonuses of the original three.

If the player is not planning to use more than one combat style at a time, they are advised to purchase the law or darkness books, as they both give better attack bonuses for ranged and magic respectively, and the law book is cheaper than the unholy book.

Equipping an unholy book allows the player to preach and perform ceremonies, such as blessing, last rites, and wedding rites, costing 25% of the player's special attack energy. None of these have any effect on the game itself, and are simply recited lines of text.

Lost unholy books can be reclaimed by speaking to Jossik , complete with all pages that have been added, for no cost. Alternatively, for those who do not wish to travel to the Lighthouse , Perdu will return them to players for 12,000 coins .
3843:
The damaged book is a book held in the shield slot that can be obtained for 5,000 coins from Jossik after completing Horror from the Deep . The four Guthix pages can be added to upgrade it to the book of balance , which gives a damage bonus.

After completing Horror from the Deep, you are rewarded with a damaged book of your choice: either Saradomin, Guthix, or Zamorak. You do not need to complete your current damaged book before obtaining a new one of a different type from Jossik. You can buy every damaged book in the same day. Dropping or destroying a damaged book and talking to Jossik results in him returning it to you.

You can check which pages are currently in your incomplete book with the "Check" option. Once you have filled the book, you cannot take the pages out.
3844:
The book of balance is a book held in place of a shield, and is the god book aligned with Guthix. It can be received as a reward from the Horror from the Deep quest. Books of balance must be made using all four torn Guthix pages which can be purchased from other players or obtained from Treasure Trails. It also allows players with a Prayer level of 50 or greater to bless holy symbols and unholy symbols, at the cost of 6 prayer points per blessing (compared to 4 points lost when using the other two main god book).

Equipping a book of balance allows the player to preach and perform ceremonies, such as blessing, last rites, and wedding rites, by operating it (none of which have any effect on the game itself, and are simply recited lines of text), costing 25% of the player's special attack energy.

Lost books of balance can be reclaimed by speaking to Jossik, complete with all pages that have been added, for no cost. Alternatively, for those who do not wish to travel to the lighthouse, Perdu will return them to players for 12,000 coins.

Filling the book of balance currently costs 4,044 coins coins when buying each page individually or 12,207 coins when buying the item set.
3845:
A journal is obtainable from the bookcase on the 1st floor of the Lighthouse. It contains an account of Jossik, his search for the fate of his uncle, and association with the local people. In a way, it also hints at what the player has to deal with to complete the quest.

After finishing the quest, the player can also find a copy of the book in the shelves in their house.
3846:
The Ancient Diary is found during the Horror from the Deep quest in the bookcase on the 1 st floor [ UK ] 2 nd floor [ US ] of the Lighthouse , belonging to Silas , the missing uncle of the most recent inhabitant of the lighthouse . Among its chaotic ramblings, it gives hints as to how to open the strange door down in the basement.

After reading the book, the diary can be found in the bookcases of a player-owned house .
3847:
The lighthouse manual is found in the bookcase on the 1 st floor [ UK ] 2 nd floor [ US ] of the Lighthouse , and is actually a manual about the care and upkeep of the lighthouse itself. It's used as a guide of sorts when attempting to repair the light.

After completing the quest, a copy of the book can also be found in a player's house .
3848:
The lighthouse key is an item used in Horror from the Deep . It is given to the player by Gunnjorn , who is inside the Barbarian Outpost agility arena, after starting the quest and is used to unlock the door to the lighthouse north of the Barbarian Outpost.

If you lose it, it can be re-obtained from Gunnjorn; however, you do not need to use the key to unlock the lighthouse after you have already unlocked the door once. This key cannot be attached onto the steel key ring .
3849:
The rusty casket is a quest item found by the player during the Horror from the Deep quest after killing the Dagannoth Mother. After completing the quest, players can take this to Jossik by going up the stairs of the lighthouse and he will tell them something is written on it.

Depending on which answer they give, he will give them a damaged prayer book in one of three colours, which correspond to the three major gods of Gielinor: Guthix, Saradomin, and Zamorak. You can buy the other books from him afterwards for 5000 coins each, including those for Armadyl, Bandos, and Zaros.

The pages for these books can be received from all levels of Treasure Trails, except for beginner clues.

Note: Dropping the casket and trying to pick it back up, the game will yield the message, It is too old and fragile to pick up. Speaking to Jossik will state that he found the dropped casket and prompt the player to select a prayer book. Additionally, Telekinetic Grab cannot be cast on the dropped casket and if it was ever banked, Jossik would ask the player to retrieve it before proceeding to the prayer book selection.
3853:
A games necklace is a sapphire necklace which has been enchanted using the Lvl-1 Enchant spell. It has 8 charges which can teleport the player to Burthorpe, Barbarian Outpost, Corporeal Beast, Tears of Guthix, and the Wintertodt Camp. After all 8 charges are used, the necklace will be destroyed.

When teleporting using the necklace, the message You rub the necklace... will be displayed, followed by a message with the number of charges remaining, ex. Your games necklace has three uses left. If using the last charge on the necklace, the message Your games necklace crumbles to dust. will be displayed instead.

When a games necklace has one charge remaining, it is recommended not to use the last charge, but instead to save it and cast High Level Alchemy on it, as the necklace's alchemy value is irrespective of its charge.

3893:
Stools are unobtainable items used while playing games in the Burthorpe Games Room , the Games Zone , or in pubs. The stools are technically wieldable items, used to display the sitting animation.

It has the appearance of a steel axe in the player's inventory, as only the equipped model is ever supposed to be seen ingame.
3894:
The awful anthem is a quest item used in the Throne of Miscellania quest. Players require a new anthem for Etceteria to replace the old one, which is the condition for the peace between Etceteria and Miscellania .

Players can obtain one from the want-to-be bard Prince Brand , the son of King Vargas . It is used to settle the war between Etceteria and Miscellania. The player must take the awful anthem to Advisor Ghrim who will then make a number of improvements to the song, turning it into a good anthem , which must be taken to Queen Sigrid . The revised version of the anthem has a lighter colouring.

Attempting to bank the awful anthem prints the message You have more urgent things to do with this anthem! . After the quest, players can no longer get the Awful anthem.
3895:
The good anthem is a quest item used in the Throne of Miscellania quest. To obtain it the player must take the awful anthem to Advisor Ghrim who will then make a number of improvements to the song, turning it into a good anthem.

Attempting to bank the good anthem prints the message You have more urgent things to do with this anthem! .

If lost, the player has to get another awful anthem from Prince Brand and give it to Advisor Ghrim.
3896: The treaty is an item a player receives when they present Queen Sigrid with the good anthem during the Throne of Miscellania quest. Players need to take it to King Vargas for his signature, where they will discover that he can't hold a normal pen due to his affliction. King Vargas will take the treaty from the player while they construct a Giant pen. Players cannot get it back after this point.
3897:
The giant nib is a quest item used in the Throne of Miscellania quest . Players must obtain it in order to construct a pen large enough for King Vargas to sign a peace treaty with Etceteria .

Derrik , the Miscellanian blacksmith, will be able to make a giant nib once provided with an iron bar . Players are then able to use the giant nib with any set of logs in order to make a giant pen .
3898: The giant pen is an item used during the Throne of Miscellania . King Vargas needs a pen to sign the peace treaty between his kingdom and Etceteria . To make it, the player must ask Derrik (near the anvil on northern Miscellania ) to make them a giant nib for their pen using an iron bar . Then the player can use any type of logs on the nib to finish it off. The pen can then be given to the king, who will sign the treaty.
3899:
Iron sickles can be purchased from Gardener Gunnhild on the island of Miscellania for 15 coins each. Players must have completed the Fremennik Trials quest to get to the island of Miscellania.

The item has no uses; if you ask Gunnhild what the iron sickle is used for, she says, "I can't think of anything just now. But you can buy one if you like, Your Highness!"

The iron sickle, along with the silver sickle, were historically used during the Throne of Miscellania quest to weed the herb garden. These interactions were removed with the release of Royal Trouble.
3901:
Ghrim's book, or Managing Thine Kingdom for Noobes, is a book that details the finer workings of running your own kingdom. It was written by Advisor Ghrim.

The book is given to you after completing the Throne of Miscellania quest, and after completing Royal Trouble, it upgrades to the 2nd Edition and talks about the resources of Etceteria will let you use. After completing the quest, you can also find the book on the shelves in your house, or in the bookcases in Queen Sigrid's throne room.
