4236:
The signed oak bow is obtained during the Ghosts Ahoy quest. It is identical to an oak longbow but has been signed by Robin in Port Phasmatys after the player beats him in several games of Rune-Draw. Ak-Haranu has the translation manual which the player requires, and requests the signed oak bow in exchange for it.

It is possible to obtain multiple signed oak bows through use of the drop trick, however, players are no longer able to request a signed oak bow from Robin after returning the bow to Ak-Haranu. Additionally, upon completing the quest, any duplicates will NOT be lost.

Unlike its regular counterpart, this item cannot be used to light a fire as part of the Barbarian firemaking training.
4237: Nettle-water is an item created in the process of making nettle tea . This item is made by adding nettles to a bowl of water . This requires a Cooking level of 20. Historically, this item gave 1 cooking exp per creation, however this is no longer the case. The player is healed 1 Hitpoint when drank. However, it is not advised to consume this item because it has potential to heal more when made into tea. Nettle-water can be cooked on a range or fire to produce nettle tea. This item is usually only used during the Ghosts Ahoy quest and the Skippy and the Mogres miniquest .
4238:
A puddle of slime is an unobtainable item released alongside Ghosts Ahoy and the Ectofuntus .

Presumably, the puddle of slime would have been a fake item that players could not pick up, similar to Flour . Players would have had to use a bucket on it in order to obtain a bucket of slime . Instead, buckets of slime are obtained directly from the pool of slime below the Ectofuntus instead.
4239:
Nettle tea is a hot drink that can be obtained by cooking nettle-water on a fire or cooking range , requiring level 20 Cooking and granting 52 experience when successful. Players may accidentally let the water boil over, returning an empty bowl; the rate of success while making these will increase as players reach higher Cooking levels. It will stop boiling over entirely at Cooking level 54 on both ranges and fires.

Drinking the tea heals 3 hitpoints . If you are not at full health, the tea will also refresh some run energy (5%), but if you are already at full hitpoints, run energy will not be restored. This item is used during the Ghosts Ahoy quest , as well as the miniquest Skippy and the Mogres . This item also can be used to bribe Panning guide to unlock panning instead of Cup of tea .

This particular kind of tea cannot be added to a tea flask .
4240:
Milky nettle tea is made by using a bucket of milk on nettle tea . It can be used on an empty cup to make a cup of milky tea .

Drinking the tea heals 3 hitpoints . If you are not at full health, the tea will also refresh some run energy (5%), but if you are already at full hitpoints, run energy will not be restored.

Milky nettle tea is given to the Old Crone during the Ghosts Ahoy quest to allow her to remember her time as an apprentice of Necrovarus .
4241:
Nettles are the key ingredient in nettle tea . They can be found in various locations throughout Runescape. Players must wear gloves in order to pick nettles ( Beekeeper's gloves will not work). If no gloves are worn, no nettles will be obtained and the player will be dealt up to 2 Hitpoints of damage. Although the resulting hitsplat is green, similar to poison, the player will not be poisoned.

Once picked, they may be used on a bowl of water to create nettle-water , which can then be cooked on a range or fire to create nettle tea .
4242:
A Cup of tea (nettle) is a drink that restores 3 Hitpoints and 5% run energy, provided you have missing hitpoints. It can be obtained by using nettle tea on an empty cup.

A bucket of milk may also be added to the tea to create Cup of tea (milky nettle) which has the same effects and is used during the Ghosts Ahoy quest.

This particular kind of tea cannot be added to a tea flask. Nettle tea can be used in place of a regular cup of tea for the Panning guide during The Dig Site quest.
4243:
A cup of milky tea is made by using milky nettle tea on an empty cup. It must be put into a porcelain cup in order to become a cup of tea that the Old Crone will take during the quest Ghosts Ahoy.

Drinking the tea heals 3 hitpoints. If you are not at full health, the tea will also refresh some run energy (5%), but if you are already at full hitpoints, run energy will not be restored.

This particular kind of tea cannot be added to a tea flask. Nettle tea can be used in place of a regular cup of tea for the Panning guide during The Dig Site quest.
4244: The porcelain cup is an item used during the Ghosts Ahoy quest when making a Cup of tea (Ghost Ahoy) for the Old Crone . In the quest, players use this item with nettle tea and then with a bucket of milk . The milky tea helps the Old Crone remember some aged memories for the player. They can be kept after the quest via use of the Drop trick , and they function identically to a normal teacup.
4245: A cup of tea is an item made during the Ghosts Ahoy quest. Players pour nettle tea into a porcelain cup given to them by the Old Crone. She refuses to drink the tea until the player adds milk. The player uses a bucket of milk on this item which only changes the colour of the liquid and the examine text. Once given to the Old Crone, she is able to recall some aged memories for the player.
4246: A cup of tea is an item made during the Ghosts Ahoy quest. Players pour nettle tea into a porcelain cup given to them by the Old Crone. She refuses to drink the tea until the player adds milk. The player uses a bucket of milk on this item which only changes the colour of the liquid and the examine text. Once given to the Old Crone, she is able to recall some aged memories for the player.
4247: The mystical robes are found during the Ghosts Ahoy quest . After showing Necrovarus the Petition form with 10 signatures, he burns it to ashes and then drops the key , which you use to enter the room upstairs. Once in the room, open and search the coffin to find the robes. Upon giving the Old Crone the robes, any duplicates will be removed from the inventory or bank; however, completing the quest does not eliminate any duplicates.
4248:
The Book of Haricanto is a book written by an ancient sorcerer from the Eastern Lands named Haricanto, and is found during the Ghosts Ahoy quest. It is one of three items that players must present to the Old Crone.

Players can find it on Dragontooth Island by starting one square west of the statue of Saradomin near the north-western peninsula and following the instructions on the treasure map. They must then dig with a spade to find the book.

In order to obtain the book whilst digging, the player must have the complete treasure map in their inventory.
4249: The translation manual is received from Ak-Haranu during the Ghosts Ahoy quest . He will give it to you in exchange for an oak longbow signed by Robin , who is staying in the nearby The Green Ghost . Once obtained, give it to the Old Crone to continue the quest.
4250:
A ghostspeak amulet is an item worn in the neck slot that enables the wearer to talk to ghosts. Partial completion of The Restless Ghost is required to obtain the item, as it is given to players by Father Urhney in order to speak to the ghost haunting the Lumbridge graveyard during the quest. Normally players can only get one ghostspeak amulet as Father Urhney will not give an amulet to players who have one in their possession, although the drop trick can be used to obtain more.

An enchanted ghostspeak amulet is given to players by the old crone in order to control Necrovarus during the Ghosts Ahoy quest.

Players who have completed the Morytania Medium Diary may use Morytania legs in place of a ghostspeak amulet anywhere it is required, except during the miniquest The General's Shadow as the ghostly robes must be worn, and the miniquest Curse of the Empty Lord as armour is not allowed on Entrana.

Players who have lost their amulet may obtain another one from Father Urhney.
4251:
The ectophial is a reward for completing the Ghosts Ahoy quest. Players can empty it, causing them to be teleported to the Ectofuntus outside Port Phasmatys. Once the player teleports, they will automatically refill it. The player cannot interrupt the refilling animation themselves, and is immune to damage for the duration; on PvP worlds, an attacker will still gain experience on a successful hit, but no damage will be dealt.

When used to teleport to the Ectofuntus, the messages You empty the ectoplasm onto the ground around your feet... and ...and the world changes around you. will be displayed. When refilling the ectophial, the message You refill the ectophial from the Ectofuntus. will be shown.

If the player loses the ectophial, they can get a replacement from Velorina in Port Phasmatys (must wear a ghostspeak amulet or Morytania legs 2 or better) or purchase it from Perdu for 4,600 coins. Claiming a replacement from Velorina will give the player a full ectophial. Claiming an ectophial from Velorina if the player already has one will give an empty one instead, which the player first has to fill at the Ectofuntus before they can use it.

It can be used to quickly escape from fights because it is easy to replace, costs nothing, and is a one click teleport from your inventory.

Like most teleport items, the ectophial does not work past level 20 Wilderness.

4272: The Bone key is an item dropped by Necrovarus when he is shown the completed petition form in the Ghosts Ahoy quest. Use the key to enter the room on the top floor of the Ectofuntus . After the quest, the key is useless. This key cannot be put on the Steel key ring acquired from completion of One Small Favour .
4273: The chest key is a quest item used during the Ghosts Ahoy quest . The player uses this key to obtain a map scrap from the chest by the old man during the quest. Once used, it disappears and cannot be reobtained after completion of the quest.
4274:
Map scrap refers to one of three quest items found during the Ghosts Ahoy quest. Each one is part of a Treasure map.

Players need to have all three scraps in their inventory, and then use one scrap on another to form the complete Treasure map.

One map part can be found in a chest on the lower level of the Ghost pirate ship wreckage opposite the farm between Frankenstrain's castle and the Ectofuntus and Port Phasmatys. When you open the chest a level 32 Giant lobster will attack you- kill it and search the chest again.

Next, climb up the ladder on the ship and cross the gang plank (to the north) jump from rock to rock in the following order: north, west, west, north, north, west. And open the chest on this last rock, then jump back the way you came to get back to the pirate ship.

Finally Search a chest on the 1st floor of the ghost pirate ship. To open the chest, you need a Chest key.

The key is given to you by the Old man, at the ghost pirate ship, in exchange for a Model ship.

Use it with the other two map pieces to make a Treasure map.

4277:
The treasure map is a quest item made during the Ghosts Ahoy quest by combining the three map scraps found during the quest.

Players can read the map to view Dragontooth Island, where a red cross shows the starting point on a north-western peninsula. The instructions read:

6 - South

8 - East

2 - North

4 - East

22 - South

To obtain this item, players must have a spade in their inventory. Start one square west of the statue near the landing point on the island, then follow the instructions on the map. The numbers show how many squares to move from the starting position, i.e. 6 squares south, then 8 east, and so on.

When at the final position, players should dig with a spade to find the book of Haricanto.

The map also has a right-click Follow option, which can be used to move several paces at once. The player must choose which direction to walk in (N, S, E, W), and then the number of paces (1, 2, 4, 10). The Follow option can only be used on Dragontooth Island.
4278: Ecto-tokens are a currency used in Port Phasmatys. In addition to being used to enter the town, they have several uses in and around the area, and can also be used to charge a bonecrusher. Players may obtain them by offering bonemeal to the Ectofuntus.
4283:
The petition form is given during the Ghosts Ahoy quest to collect signatures from ghost villagers in Port Phasmatys . It is used to protest Necrovarus and his control over Port Phasmatys . Multiple signatures from a single ghost is allowed.

If dropped, a message will appear in the chatbox stating " You drop the petition form; it blows away in the wind. ". Should you drop it, another form can be provided by Gravingas , the ghost activist; however, the player's signature count will reset to zero .

10 signatures are needed for it to be completed, but they can be obtained from 2 villagers over and over. For the villagers to provide signatures, you must be wearing a bedsheet dipped in ectoplasm .
4284:
The bedsheet is obtained from the innkeeper of Port Phasmatys during the Ghosts Ahoy quest to be given to Robin in a nearby room. It is worn in the head slot.

Although it is brown when received, it can be changed to a light green colour by covering it in ectoplasm, making it an ectoplasm-covered bedsheet. To do this, players must dip it into the pool of slime on the bottom floor of the cavern beneath the Ectofuntus or dip it into a bucket of slime collected from the pool. Although this is supposed to make players resemble a ghost, when talking to residents of the port, they will merely joke at them.

When worn, the bedsheet makes the player resemble a classic "bedsheet" ghost. The bedsheet is not wearable in any other place than Port Phasmatys; attempting to do so will result in receiving a message, stating: "I'll only wear the bedsheet inside Port Phasmatys."

It is impossible to charter a ship while players are carrying a bedsheet.

4286:
Buckets of slime are filled with a slimy green glowing liquid, gathered from the basement of the Ectofuntus near Port Phasmatys . Necrovarus uses this liquid to control the ghosts of Port Phasmatys, but he is thwarted by the player during Ghosts Ahoy . It apparently has hidden magical properties regarding ghosts and the undead, which is the reason Necrovarus can control the ghosts of Phasmatys and also why he, along with his disciples, are still able to interact with living beings, even after many years of death.

They are used along with bonemeal to worship the Ectofuntus for training Prayer . If bones are ground and used with ectoplasm to worship the Ectofuntus , four times the normal amount of experience for the bones is given; which makes it a useful item that greatly impacts and cheapens training Prayer. Equipping the full set of Zealot's robes will provide a 5% chance (1.25% per piece) to save both the bonemeal and bucket of slime while worshipping the Ectofuntus .
4287:
Raw beef is an item obtained by killing undead cows in Morytania . Raw beef can be cooked at level 1 Cooking by using it on a range or fire . When cooked, undead raw beef becomes cooked meat (undead) , granting 30 Cooking experience.

Undead cows can only be found west of Port Phasmatys on Alice 's farm, along with undead chickens .
4289: Raw chicken is an item obtained by killing undead chickens on Alice 's farm in Morytania . It can be cooked into a cooked chicken (undead) on any fire or stove just like a normal raw chicken , granting 30 Cooking experience . The cooked version of this item heals 1 hitpoint .
4291:
Cooked chicken is food made by cooking a raw chicken (undead) on a range or fire, requiring 1 Cooking and yielding 30 Cooking experience.

Despite cooked undead chicken's appearance, it is safe to eat and heals 1 Hitpoints.

When eaten, it will give the message: You eat the chicken. It tastes absolutely disgusting.

The Team-1 cape is a team cape that can be purchased for 50 coins from William. Another player with the same team cape equipped will show up on the minimap as a blue dot rather than white, and the left-click "Attack" option will be moved to a right-click, as if the other player is of higher level than the player. 4415: The blunt axe is a quest item used in the One Small Favour quest. It is obtained by talking to the Jungle Forester in the Kharazi Jungle , south-east of Shilo Village . The player is asked to take the axe to Captain Shanks to get it sharpened, although Captain Shanks will tell the player to take it to the axe shop in Port Sarim instead.
4416: Herbal tincture is a quest item used in the One Small Favour quest. It is obtained by talking to the Apothecary in Varrock. The player is asked to make an airtight pot to replace the one the Apothecary drops in return for the breathing salts that are needed along with the tincture. It must then be taken to Horvik to complete the next step in the quest.
4417:
Guthix rest is a type of tea with 1-4 doses where each dose will:

Heal 5 Hitpoints, which can also boost up to 5 above your HP level if you are at full health.

Restore 5% energy

Reduce venom to poison, or reduce poison damage by 1

Once Sanfew explains how players can make it during the One Small Favour quest, they unlock the ability to consume and make their own, requiring 18 Herblore.

Guthix rest is made by combining 2 guam leaves, a harralander, and a marrentill on a cup of hot water. Add one of the herbs to the cup while the rest of the herbs are in your inventory to automatically create a 3 dose Guthix Rest. The cup of hot water can be created by heating a cup of water on a range or fire. Alternatively, a bowl of water can be heated on a range or fire to create a bowl of hot water, which then may be poured into an empty cup, although this is far slower and more click-intensive.

If you do not have all of the herbs in your inventory when adding to the cup, the incomplete herb tea mix will be created. The remaining herbs can then be added in any order one at a time to this mix to create the 3 dose Guthix Rest. Adding incorrect herbs results in a warning that your tea will be ruined: if you choose to proceed it will produce a ruined herb tea.

Making it grants a total of 59 Herblore experience, with 14, 14.5, 15, 15.5 experience granted for the first, second, third, and fourth herbs, respectively.

Guthix rest can be decanted to create a 4 dose version. For example, when adding two Guthix Rest (3) together, the result will be a Guthix Rest (4) and Guthix Rest (2). Bob Barter at the Grand Exchange can perform this service for the player for free as well, with both noted and unnoted Guthix rests.

Guthix rest effectively functions as a potion, meaning players can use Guthix rests to heal during combat without delaying their attacks. Despite this, the amulet of chemistry has no effect when making the tea, nor will it consume any charges. Prescription goggles also do not have any effect when making the tea. Zahur can not make unfinished Guthix rests as she does with normal potions. The attack of a Ghast may also still turn it into rotten food (as is expected for any food item).

The remaining herbs can then be added in any order one at a time to this mix to create the 3 dose Guthix Rest. Adding incorrect herbs results in a warning that your tea will be ruined: if you choose to proceed it will produce a ruined herb tea.

Making it grants a total of 59 Herblore experience, with 14, 14.5, 15, 15.5 experience granted for the first, second, third, and fourth herbs, respectively.

Guthix rest can be decanted to create a 4 dose version. For example, when adding two Guthix Rest (3) together, the result will be a Guthix Rest (4) and Guthix Rest (2). Bob Barter at the Grand Exchange can perform this service for the player for free as well, with both noted and unnoted Guthix rests.

Guthix rest effectively functions as a potion, meaning players can use Guthix rests to heal during combat without delaying their attacks. Despite this, the amulet of chemistry has no effect when making the tea, nor will it consume any charges. Prescription goggles also do not have any effect when making the tea. Zahur can not make unfinished Guthix rests as she does with normal potions. The attack of a Ghast may also still turn it into rotten food (as is expected for any food item).

4425:
The stodgy mattress is a quest item used in the One Small Favour quest. It is obtained by talking to a man in Port Khazard, who asks the player to stuff the mattress with feathers in exchange for some iron oxide. The stodgy mattress must be taken to Rantz the Ogre in the Feldip Hills in order to obtain the feathers.

If players lose the mattress they must pay the Tindel Marchant 100 coins to reclaim it.
4426:
The comfy mattress is a quest item used in One Small Favour. It is made by taking the stodgy mattress from a man in Port Khazard and adding the feathers given by Rantz. The player should then return the mattress to the man in Port Khazard in exchange for some iron oxide. This must then be taken to Wizard Cromperty in Ardougne in order to proceed in the quest.

If players lose the mattress they will need to bring another Stodgy mattress and pay Rantz 200 coins.
4427: Iron oxide is a quest item used in the One Small Favour quest. It is obtained by talking to Tindel Marchant in Port Khazard . The player is asked to stuff the man's stodgy mattress in return for the iron oxide. The oxide must then be taken to Wizard Cromperty in Ardougne in order to complete the next step in the quest. If lost, Marchant will charge 200 coins for a new one.
4428:
The animate rock scroll is a quest item used in the One Small Favour and King's Ransom quests. It contains the incantation Um nahi listic durooo-rah!, for a spell that brings rocks to life, or re-animates beings who have been turned to rock or stone.

It is first obtained during One Small Favour by giving iron oxide to Wizard Cromperty in Ardougne. If lost, it can be obtained by speaking to Wizard Cromperty again when King's Ransom has been started, without having to give him anything. However, once the player has completed King's Ransom, the scroll becomes unobtainable (although it has no use at this point anyway). Warning: All duplicates disappear after finishing the King's Ransom quest.

The scroll is used on a girl named Petra who has been accidentally embedded into the rock face of a cave near the Fishing Guild. The player attempts to use it to free her, but misfires the spell, accidentally animating some nearby rocks and bringing Slagilith to life. The player must kill this creature before trying again and successfully releasing Petra. Trying to cast the spell with Slagilith alive results in the message, "You're a little too busy fighting to cast that right now." The player then returns to Phantuwti to progress to the next part of the quest.

Some players have the issue of being unable to use the scroll during One Small Favour, receiving the message, "You don't feel that you should cast this with enemies around". This issue can be resolved by killing the giant bats and goblins directly outside the room.

In King's Ransom, it is needed to free King Arthur from the statue underneath the Black Knights' Fortress.
4429:
Broken weathervane parts are a quest item used in One Small Favour. They are obtained by climbing onto the roof of Phantuwti Fanstuwi Farsight's house in Seers' Village and examining the weather vane there.

Each part must be repaired using a different metal bar - the ornament on top must be repaired with a bronze bar, the weathervane pillar needs an iron bar, and the directionals require a steel bar to repair.

Should the player lose the parts somehow, they must pay Phantuwti 1,000 coins to reclaim them. These replacement parts will not grant Smithing XP when repaired, unlike the initial pieces.

Once repaired, the parts can be returned to their position on top of the house in order to continue with the quest.
4430:
The directionals are a quest item used in the One Small Favour quest. They are obtained by climbing onto the roof of Phantuwti 's house in Seers' Village and removing the broken vane parts . The directionals must then be repaired using a steel bar at an anvil and returned to the top of the house along with the repaired weathervane pillar and ornament .

Once the three repaired vane parts have been returned to their position the player can speak to Phantewti in order to complete the next step in the quest.

4435:
The weather report is a quest item used in the One Small Favour quest . It is obtained by talking to Phantuwti , a Seer who lives in Seers' Village . Before he will give the player the weather report, the player must first rescue a missing person and repair the weather vane on the top of his house.

The player must then take the weather report to Arhein , who lives in Catherby, in order to proceed in the quest.
4436:
An airtight pot is a quest item used in One Small Favour and Swan Song. It is made by using a pot lid on an empty pot.

An airtight pot must be given to the Apothecary in Varrock during the events of One Small Favour. In Swan Song, an airtight pot is used to hold bone seeds to create an army of skeleton mages.
4438: An unfired pot lid is made by using soft clay on a potter's wheel after partial completion of One Small Favour , requiring level 25 Crafting and granting 20 Crafting experience. Once the unfired pot lid is created, it must be fired in a pottery oven , producing a pot lid and granting 20 Crafting experience upon success. Unlike shaping the clay, firing it has no Crafting level requirement. At lower levels, an unfired pot lid can crack in the oven, destroying the pot lid and granting no experience.
4440: Pot lids are items that when used on pots create an airtight pot, an item required for the One Small Favour and Swan Song quests. They can be created by using a piece of soft clay on a Potter's wheel and then firing the unfired pot lid in a Pottery oven.
4442:
Breathing salts are a quest item used in the One Small Favour quest. They are obtained by giving an airtight pot to the Apothecary in Varrock . The player must then take them to Horvik in order to complete the next step in the quest.

If players lose the breathing salts they will need to bring 200 coins and another airtight pot to the Apothecary.
4443:
The chicken cage is a quest item used in the One Small Favour quest. Seth Groats requires five chicken cages to hold the chickens in, and asks the player to give Horvik three steel bars that he owes to him. After giving Horvik five pigeon cages and the herbal tincture and breathing salts , he will create the chicken cages. The player must then take the cages to Seth Groats to complete the next step in the quest.

If the player loses a cage, it can be replaced by giving Horvik 100 coins and another pigeon cage.
4444:
The sharpened axe is a quest item used in the One Small Favour quest. It is obtained by giving the blunt axe to Brian in Port Sarim after helping his friend Aggie free her apprentice, Jimmy the Chisel. The player must take the sharpened axe back to the forester south-east of Shilo Village in order to proceed in the quest. Brian, unlike many other people in the quest whom you must do favours for, will be happy to supply you with another axe without charge should you lose the first one.

It cannot be used as a woodcutting axe to fell trees.
4445:
Red mahogany logs are used in the One Small Favour quest. They are obtained by giving a sharpened axe to the Jungle Forester near the Kharazi Jungle , south-east of Shilo Village . More logs can be obtained for 200 coins each.

The quest is completed after delivering the log to Yanni Salika in the antiques shop in the village. Warning: Yanni Salika will take all the Red mahogany logs in the player's inventory!
4446:
The steel key ring is a reward for completing One Small Favour . It stores certain re-usable keys to save bank space. Using a key on the key ring adds it on, and clicking the key ring opens an interface that shows which keys are on it where they can also be removed. Keys do not need to be removed to use them. The weapon store key and maze key can be used in free-to-play while they are on the steel key ring. When adding or removing a key from the key ring, a message will be displayed, ex. You add the shiny key to your key ring. and You remove the shiny key from your key ring.

When opening a door with its key stored on the key ring, the message You use your keyring to unlock the door. will be displayed.

This item is not lost on death; it is kept in your inventory with the keys intact. However, when lost, the keys stored on it are lost as well. A new key ring can be bought from Yanni Salika in Shilo Village for 500 coins and the keys must be collected again. This also requires having used the antique lamps from completing the One Small Favour quest , otherwise Yanni will not offer to sell the key ring.

The drop trick can be used to receive multiple key rings, however, it must be done before adding keys to the key ring. Doing so with any amount of keys on the key ring will lose all of the keys on the key ring. However, as long as there is at least one key ring in the bank, keys are not lost when losing a different key ring. The drop trick cannot be used until the antique lamps rewarded from completing One Small Favour have been used.

It can hold the following 13 keys [ 1 ] :
4447:
The antique lamp is an item obtained from Yanni Salika after completing the One Small Favour quest. Two are given to the player, and each lamp grants 10,000 experience in a skill of the player's choosing, given that the skill is over level 30. The lamp cannot be banked, but either of the two lamps can be reclaimed if dropped, even if the other of the two was used.

Even though the lamp can be dropped instead of being destroyed, and many can be dropped to the ground, extras cannot be obtained with the drop trick, as the player may only hold a maximum of two before using the first lamp, and then a maximum of one until using the second lamp, whereupon no further lamps can be picked back up.

Note: the One Small Favour quest will not really be considered completed, being shown in yellow in the quest log and stopping the player from being able to start King's Ransom and Swan Song, until both antique lamps are used. This happens even if the lamps are dropped in order to be retrieved later from Yanni Salika. Whether this is by design or is a bug is unclear.
4456:
A bowl of hot water can be created by using a normal bowl on a water source to turn it into a bowl of water and then heating this on a stove, a range, or a fire. When added to an empty cup, a cup of hot water is made.

A bowl of hot water is used to make Guthix rest and also used in the quest One Small Favour.
4458:
A cup of water is an item made by using an empty cup on a water source. Nettles cannot be added to this item — they must be instead added to a bowl of water , and add Nettle tea to an empty cup.

A cup of water cannot be used to counter the desert heat effect.
4460: A cup of hot water is created by using a bowl of hot water on an empty tea cup or by heating a cup of water on a range or fire. It is solely used to make a Guthix rest potion. It is not drinkable like tea is, and it can do nothing by itself.

4484: The safety guarantee is a quest item used in Mountain Daughter quest. It is given to the player by Brundt the Chieftain to guarantee Svidi safe passage into Rellekka . When you try to get two of these using the drop trick , a message appears, You don't need another one, really. but it can still be collected via Telekinetic grab .
4485:
The white pearl can be obtained by picking thorny bushes located on top of White Wolf Mountain , next to a gnome glider .

The white pearl can be eaten, healing 2 hitpoints , and when eaten, a message will say "You eat the White Pearl and spit out the seed when you're done. Mmm, tasty." The remnants of the fruit will become a white pearl seed. The White pearl seed is needed during the Mountain Daughter quest.

In order to pick the white pearl, the player must be equipped with any pair of the following gloves :

After the quest this may no longer be picked.

If you try to obtain two, a message says "No need, you already have one of these." If you try to obtain two, using the drop trick , a message will yield "One piece of the White Pearl fruit is enough for you." If you have a seed in your inventory, and you try to pick a fruit, a message reads "You're content with having the seed of the fruit." If you try to get two seeds you will get a message saying "One seed should be enough." However, if you drop the seed on the ground (having no fruit or seed in your inventory), you will be able to pick another fruit. You may also get extras with the use of the telekinetic grab spell.
4486:
The white pearl seed is obtained by eating a White pearl fruit. This seed must be given to Jokul during the Mountain Daughter quest.

This seed can not be planted in any farming patches.

If the player tries to obtain two seeds using the drop trick , a message will state "One seed should be enough." However, Telekinetic Grab can be used to bypass this. Another method for players who want more than one seed or fruit can pick a fruit and drop it, pick another fruit and eat it, then pick up the fruit that was dropped.

While no more white pearls can be obtained after the quest, if the player used the drop trick to obtain multiple, they can still be eaten after the quest to obtain the seeds.
4487:
The half a rock is a quest item used in the Mountain Daughter quest. The teardrop-shaped rock is obtained by using a pickaxe on the Ancient Rock in a tent in the Mountain Camp . The player must give the rock to Brundt the Chieftain in Rellekka to obtain a safety guarantee for Svidi .

Interestingly, when the player tries to obtain two pieces of the rock using the drop trick , they receive a message stating, "While two halves make one whole, it's better to just have half a rock." However, a player may obtain two pieces by using the drop trick and casting telekinetic grab on one of the halves. Using both halves together in the inventory will not create a whole rock.
4488:
Corpse of woman is an item that is briefly used during the quest, Mountain Daughter . It is actually the corpse of Hamal the Chieftain 's daughter, Asleif . It is found in the Kendal 's lair located near the Mountain Camp . During the quest the player must show the 14-year-old corpse to the Chieftain, to confirm Asleif's death. The player must then bury the skeleton at the small island in the lake.

The item has a bury option, but it may not be used until the player is on the small island. If you try to bury the corpse, a message will read, "You'd better bring this back to the chieftain instead."

If you try to get two of these, a message will yield, "This must be someone else's corpse, you already have Asleif's corpse."

Trying to bury the corpse after the quest is finished will delete the item and give a message, "You suddenly realize [ sic ] you don't even have the corpse."
4489:
Asleif's necklace is a quest item used in Mountain Daughter quest. It is given to the player by Ragnar toward the end of the quest to bury with Corpse of woman , which the player has to retrieve during the course of the quest.

If you try to obtain two necklaces using the drop trick , a message will yield "You only need one piece of jewelry." However, you can drop it and use the Telekinetic Grab spell.
4490:
Mud is a quest item used in the Mountain Daughter quest . It can be found in the south of the Mountain Camp , where the mudpool is. Players must "Dig-up" the mud from the mudpool. This can be done by hand, a spade is not necessary.

During Mountain Daughter, it is used to provide grip on a tree that the player is otherwise unable to climb, to the centre of the lake. This only needs to be done once, so this item becomes useless afterwards.
4492: The muddy rock is an item used in Mountain Daughter quest. It can be picked up off the ground near the mud pit and in the goat pens in the Mountain Camp . Five muddy rocks are used on the burial mound of the body of Asleif to complete the burial and the quest.
4494: A pole is a quest item used in Mountain Daughter . It can be found in the goat's pen in the Mountain Camp , east of Rellekka . It is used to catapult the player across the stones in the middle of the lake near the Mountain Camp; however, any staff will work for this as well. There is also a broken pole found on the south-western side of the lake which cannot be repaired and has no known use.
4495:
A Pole is an unobtainable version of the Pole . Poles were previously tradeable and could be turned into banknotes. However, they were made untradeable in 2007. Any player who had a noted pole was given this now discontinued item. Originally, the item was identical to the real pole, except being stackable.

As this change occurred prior to August 2007, the item has never been obtainable in Old School RuneScape.
4496: The broken pole is an item found near the lake during Mountain Daughter . It is the broken form of the pole used during the quest to jump across the stones in the middle of the lake. The broken pole is useless, only existing to hint that a pole or staff must be used to cross over the rocks to reach the lake's central island.
4498:
The Rope is an unused animation item presumably intended for use during Mountain Daughter, when using a rope to climb down the cliffside into the Mountain Camp. Although it has a model for use when equipped, it is not used in any animations.

Its inventory icon has the appearance of mud, as it was never meant to be seen outside of the animation.
4500:
The pole is an animation item used during Mountain Daughter . It is temporarily wielded by the player when using a pole to pole-vault over the rocks near the lake. Aside from this, it cannot be obtained.

Its inventory icon has the appearance of mud , as it was never meant to be seen outside of the animation.
4501:
The pole is an animation item used during Mountain Daughter . It is temporarily wielded by the player when using a pole to pole-vault over the rocks near the lake. Aside from this, it cannot be obtained.

Its inventory icon has the appearance of mud , as it was never meant to be seen outside of the animation.
4502:
A Bearhead is a piece of low level headgear that is obtained after killing The Kendal during the Mountain Daughter quest.

This piece of headgear has surprisingly high defensive bonuses given that it has no requirements to equip. It is popular amongst one-defence pures due to its defensive bonuses being comparable to a black full helm and among Abyss runecrafters due to its low weight. Its Magic defence is competitive with many other helmets with higher requirements.

If lost before completing Mountain Daughter, another can be obtained in the Kendal's Lair. If the quest is completed, it can also be reclaimed by speaking to Hamal the Chieftain. Players can also reclaim it from Perdu for 10,000 should they lose it.
4503:
The decorative sword (white) can be bought in the Castle Wars area south of the Observatory for 50 Castle wars tickets from Lanthus. The sword offers the same stats as a mithril longsword, and requires level 20 Attack to wield. Also, it has similar shape and colour palette to the blurite sword. However, the blurite sword is considerably weaker.

This item can be stored in the armour case of a costume room.
4504:
The White decorative body can be bought in the Castle Wars area south of the observatory for 80 Castle Wars tickets. They can only be bought from Lanthus . The white decorative body offers the same stats as a mithril platebody . It requires level 20 Defence to wear.

This item can be stored in the armour case of a costume room , as part of the Castle Wars armour (2) set. Ultimate Ironmen will be unable to retrieve individual pieces until the full set is stored.

The White decorative legs can be bought in the Castle Wars area south of the observatory for 60 Castle Wars tickets. They can only be bought from Lanthus . Oil lamps are a light source for use in dark places. Like all low-quality light sources, it is recommended that several lamps are used if this is the only option, and a tinderbox is available in case the lamp goes out.

Empty oil lamps can be made using the Crafting skill at level 12 by glassblowing molten glass, or bought from Dorgesh-Kaan or from other players. To light it, players require level 12 in Firemaking. Note that the oil lamp must be filled with lamp oil to be lit.

An oil lamp can be combined with an oil lantern frame (forged from iron) to make an oil lantern for 50 Crafting experience. Combining the lantern frame with the lamp does not require a furnace or anvil, but does require 26 Crafting.

As it is an open light source, it can set off gas explosions in certain parts of the Lumbridge Swamp Caves.

The empty candle lantern is an incomplete light source used in the Firemaking skill.

The empty candle lantern can be filled with a white candle or black candle to make a candle lantern . It can then be lit to use as a light source in dark areas. Lighting the candle lantern requires a tinderbox and level 4 Firemaking . No experience is received when lighting a candle lantern.

Candle lanterns are recommended for the Lumbridge Swamp Caves , as they have a lower chance of igniting the swamp gas, which will cause an explosion and damage the player. However, a better alternative is a bullseye lantern , and if that is not available then an oil lantern will suffice.

The empty candle lantern can be filled with a black candle to give a black candle lantern.

4542: Lantern lens are used with a bullseye lantern (unf) to make a bullseye lantern. A cut sapphire can then be used on the lantern to extract the lantern lens and produce a sapphire lantern at the same time.
4544:
Bullseye lantern (unf) are unfinished bullseye lanterns. To make the steel frame, a Smithing level of 49 and a steel bar are required. Glass lenses for the frames can be made with level 49 Crafting by blowing glass; however, a cut sapphire can be used in place of the lens. Lamp oil, obtained by distilling swamp tar at the Chemist's House in Rimmington or at Miltog's Lamps in Dorgesh-Kaan, is used to fuel bullseye lanterns. Bullseye lanterns can be lit using a tinderbox at level 49 Firemaking - doing so at the Chemist's House is a requirement for the Falador Medium Diary.

The frame combined with a sapphire lens makes a sapphire lantern, which is required in the Tears of Guthix and While Guthix Sleeps quests. In Lunar Diplomacy, an emerald lens is used with the frame to make an emerald lantern.
4546:
A bullseye lantern (empty) is a bullseye lantern (unf) which has been fitted with a lantern lens but is empty of fuel.

The lamp oil used for fuel is obtained by distilling swamp tar in the chemist's house in Rimmington or at the Miltog's Lamps in Dorgesh-Kaan.

When filled with fuel it becomes a bullseye lantern. Level 49 Firemaking is required to light it.

Bullseye lanterns can also be stolen from chests in Dorgesh-Kaan, which require either 52 or 78 Thieving (either one yields them very often). They can also be stolen from cave goblins or purchased from Miltog in the Dorgesh-Kaan marketplace. Some of these methods will still require the use of lamp oil to complete them.

Lantern lens, sapphires, and emerald lens can be swapped with each other when the lantern is finished and unlit. Inserting the lantern lens requires 49 Crafting (cannot be boosted), inserting the sapphire lens requires 20 Crafting, and the emerald lens has no requirements.
4548:
A bullseye lantern is a light source used to illuminate dark areas with the highest brightness value of three. Lighting it with a tinderbox requires 49 Firemaking. Creating one from scratch requires 49 Smithing to make the bullseye lantern (unf) and 49 Crafting to make the lantern lens. Adding a lens to the unfinished bullseye lantern makes a bullseye lantern (empty) which must be filled up with lamp oil by distilling swamp tar in a lamp oil still at the Chemist's house in Rimmington or at Miltog's Lamps in Dorgesh-Kaan.

Lantern lens, sapphires, and emerald lens can be swapped with each other when the lantern is finished and unlit. Inserting the lantern lens requires 49 Crafting (cannot be boosted), inserting the sapphire lens requires 20 Crafting, and the emerald lens has no requirements.

Bullseye lanterns do not ignite swamp gas in the Lumbridge Swamp Caves and they will not extinguish when falling into water except in the Abandoned Mine. In the Sophanem Dungeon, the Scarab mage has a rare attack that magically extinguishes light sources including bullseye lanterns. Activating the scarab trap in the Sophanem Dungeon and falling into the trap extinguishes all light sources as well.

4558:
Chocolate eggs were part of the 2005 Easter event. Players were given a basket of eggs by the Easter Bunny and could use it to give eggs to other players.

When the eggs were eaten, the player would perform the Rubber chicken's Chicken Dance emote, but not heal any hitpoints. When the event was removed on 4 April, all leftover eggs were replaced by Chocolate dust . However, since chocolate dust was a members only item at this time, free to play players received them as Members objects instead.

The eggs remained in the game cache until the 2005 Halloween event, when they were overwritten by sweets. As the 2005 Easter event was never brought back, these items have never been obtainable in Old School RuneScape .

The Easter basket was given out as a reward by the Easter Bunny during the 2014 Easter event. It can be operated when worn to perform an emote, flinging two easter eggs randomly in a 5x5 radius.

While worn, the player's walking and running animations will be replaced with a skipping animation.

If destroyed, a replacement can be obtained from Diango in Draynor Village or from the toy box of a costume room.
4566:
A Rubber chicken is a event reward that can be obtained by completing an Easter holiday event, which occurs once per year.

The Rubber chicken can be equipped and has the same attack styles as a warhammer. It gives very large attack penalties and is nearly useless as an actual weapon. As such it is allowed during fun weapon fights in legacy duels within the Emir's Arena. When wielded, players will see a "Whack" option on all other players. Picking that option will cause the player to hit the other player. The hit is just an animation and no damage is dealt, nor does it count as entering combat. If a player whacks a large number of other players, they may "fumble" the chicken, dropping it to the ground where it must be picked up again and re-equipped.

Players can right click the chicken, either in their Inventory or on the Worn Equipment screen, and select a dance option, making them do the chicken dance emote, which includes a short song which shares the same beat from a portion of Scape Santa. The dance and song could also be accessed by eating one of the event's Easter eggs, however once the event was concluded, this method no longer worked. Players who distract the eyes in the Abyss will sometimes perform the Chicken Dance emote, even if they do not have a Rubber chicken.

Previously, they were obtainable during the 2013 Rare Drops event (from 12 August to 19 August) as part of a rare item drop.

If destroyed, a replacement can be obtained from Diango in Draynor Village or from the toy box of a costume room.
4567:
The gold helmet is a helmet the player must smith during the Between a Rock... quest using 3 gold bars . It requires level 30 Defence to wear. Smithing the helmet requires 50 Smithing and gives 30 Smithing experience. More than one helmet can be made by using the drop trick and casting Telekinetic Grab on any helmets dropped on the ground. The helmet must be worn to use Dondakan 's cannon and to enter the massive Arzinian Mines , found in the mines south of Keldagrim .

During the quest, once in the mines, the helmet will begin to get heavy. Because of this, a player may only stay in the mines for eight minutes before the helmet becomes so heavy that they are magically forced out. After the quest, the helmet will not force players out, although it must still be worn to enter the mines. It is the heaviest piece of equipment in the game. Entering the mine after completing the quest unlocks the In Between song.

To leave the mines, a player must remove the helmet. When this is done, they will automatically be teleported outside. This costs the player one inventory space, so some players log out instead; if a player logs out in the mines, they will automatically be teleported outside while still wearing the helmet.

To make the helmet after the quest, have 3 gold bars and a hammer in your inventory and smith it on any anvil (option won't be available if you have one in your bank already).

Smithing a gold helmet in the Resource Area is a medium task in the Wilderness diary . Note: Pures do not need to complete the quest to complete this wilderness task.
4568:
The dwarven lore book is given to players only after they give Rolad all of its pages during the Between a Rock... quest . After the quest it is stored in the bookcase of a player-owned house . The book tells players about the history and legend of The Arzinian Being of Bordanzan . Inside the book are base schematics .

If dropped during the quest, it can be re-obtained from Rolad at the Ice Mountain entrance to the Dwarven Mine .
4569: Book page 1 is used in the Between a Rock... quest . It is found by killing scorpions in the Dwarven Mine . When combined with book page 2 and book page 3 , it creates pages , which the player must give to Rolad .
4570: Book page 2 is used in the Between a Rock... quest . It is found by searching mine carts in the Dwarven Mine . When combined with book page 1 and book page 3 , it creates pages , which the player must give to Rolad .
4571: Book page 3 is a quest item in the Between a Rock... quest , found by mining rocks in the Dwarven Mine . When combined with book page 1 and book page 2 , pages are created which must be given to Rolad .
4572: Pages are an unobtainable item released with Between a Rock... , depicting two of the three Book Pages that the player is required to collect for Rolad combined. However, it is only possible to combine the pages when all three have been obtained, so this version of the item is unobtainable.
4573: Pages are used in the Between a Rock... quest . They are formed when players have found all three missing pages. The three items will automatically combine once you have all three in your inventory. The pages talk about the impenetrable rock.
4574: Base schematics are used in Between a Rock... to line up the other three schematics. They are found when reading the dwarven lore book.
4575: The schematic is used in the Between a Rock... quest along with the other schematics to find out how to modify the cannon. It must be adjusted over the base schematics . It is given to the player by Dondakan the Dwarf .
4576: The schematics are used in Between a Rock... , along with the other schematics, to find out how to modify the cannon. It must be adjusted over the Base schematics . It is given to the player by the Dwarf Engineer .
4577: The schematics are used in Between a Rock... , along with the other schematics, to find out how to modify the cannon. It must be adjusted over the Base schematics . It is given to the player by Khorvak, a dwarven engineer .
4578: The schematic is used in Between a Rock... to find out how to modify the cannon. It is made by adjusting the three other schematics over the Base schematics .
4579:
The golden cannon ball is an item created and used for Dondakan's multicannon in the Between a Rock... quest . Players make it by using a gold bar on a furnace , with an ammo mould or double ammo mould in their inventory , granting 37.5 Smithing experience . This makes only one large cannon ball, instead of the four steel cannonballs that are usually made from a steel bar .

During the quest, the cannon ball is used to shoot at Dondakan's rock in an attempt to break it open, as every other material simply bashes against the rock to no effect.

Although the quest itself requires level 50 Smithing to complete, it is not required to create the cannon ball, instead being only required to create the gold helmet used later in the quest. After completing the quest, golden cannon balls can no longer be made.

As with all black and white equipment , the black spear cannot be made from raw materials using the Smithing skill.

Unlike most spears, there is no equivalent tier of hasta .

4585:
The dragon plateskirt is a rare piece of armour that requires a Defence level of 60 to be worn. It has the same stats as the dragon platelegs.

Dragon plateskirts can be combined with a dragon legs/skirt ornament kit to make a gold-trimmed dragon plateskirt (g). This cosmetic enhancement won't change the stats in any way.

As with most dragon armour, players cannot make this item using the Smithing skill.
4587:
The dragon scimitar is the strongest scimitar available in Old School RuneScape. It can only be wielded by players who have 60 Attack and have completed the Monkey Madness I quest.

It may be purchased from Daga on Ape Atoll for 100,000 coins. A monkeyspeak amulet does not need to be worn, as players can just right-click 'Trade' on Daga; however, you still must be in monkey form, unless you have completed Monkey Madness II after which the monkey form is no longer required. Players who have freed King Awowogei in Recipe for Disaster can easily reach Marim through the Ape Atoll Teleport spell (requires 64 Magic) to access Daga's shop on Ape Atoll quicker. The scimitar is also a rare drop from the Wilderness boss Scorpia or the Zombie Pirate's Locker.

As with most dragon equipment, the dragon scimitar cannot be made from raw materials using the Smithing skill.

One good alternative is the Arkan blade, which has very similar stats, the same 4-tick attack speed, and a great special attack, and is earned as a reward for completing The Final Dawn quest. This saves players the 100,000 coins used for purchasing the Dragon Scimitar.
4589: The keys open the front door to the home of Ali the Mayor in Pollnivneach . Members acquire them as part of The Feud quest . They enable players to burgle the house of Ali the Mayor, stealing the jewels to impress Ali the Operator . The house of Ali the Mayor can be entered after the quest without the keys.
4590: Jewels are used in The Feud quest in order to gain the trust of the Menaphite gang. Players must steal them from Ali the Mayor's house in Pollnivneach in order to convince Ali the Operator to let the player join the Menaphites gang. The jewels used to belong to the mayor's wife before they were stolen.
4591:
The Kharidian headpiece is used during The Feud quest to form a desert disguise , by combining it with a fake beard . It can be bought from Ali Morrisane in Al Kharid or the Pollnivneach general store .

Despite having no 'Wear' option, the headpiece would delay the onset of desert heat by 12 seconds if it could be equipped.
4593: A fake beard can be bought from Ali Morrisane in Al Kharid or the Pollnivneach general store . It mainly serves as a quest item .
4595: The karidian disguise is an unobtainable item that only appears when searching the Grand Exchange . It is presumably an item intended for use during The Feud quest , but was replaced by the desert disguise during development for unknown reasons.
4597:
The Note is an item that players find as part of The Feud whilst burgling the home of Ali the Mayor in Pollnivneach.

Along with the other note that players find, this gives the clue about the combination for the safe in the house. The combination is the first six Fibonacci numbers after zero.
4598:
The note is an item that players find whilst burgling the home of Ali the Mayor in Pollnivneach during The Feud. It includes the first part of the combination to the safe in the mayor's home.

The combination is the series of Fibonacci numbers starting after zero, though the note only lists the first five, and the player must deduce the last number required. A hint is provided in the other note found during the quest.
4599:
The oak blackjack is a melee weapon that has no level requirement to wield and is mainly used to knockout certain NPCs. An oak blackjack can be obtained from Ali the Operator during The Feud quest. When fighting with a blackjack, there is a slight chance to stun the opponent.

There are three NPCs that can be knocked out: Villagers, bandits and Menaphite Thugs, all located in Pollnivneach. While there is no level requirement to knock out a villager, the Bandits require level 45 Thieving (or 55 for scimitar wielding ones), and the Menaphite Thugs level 65 Thieving.
4600:
The willow blackjack is a melee weapon that has no level requirement to wield and is mainly used to knockout certain NPCs . A willow blackjack can be obtained by completing the blackjack section of the Rogue Trader miniquest or from Ali the Operator during The Feud quest. Alternatively, it can be bought from the Blackjack seller in Pollnivneach directly behind Ali the Kebab seller or as a reward for The Feud quest. When fighting with a blackjack, there is a slight chance to stun the opponent.

There are three NPCs that can be knocked out: Villagers , Bandits and Menaphite Thugs , all located in Pollnivneach. While there is no level requirement to knock out a villager, the Bandits require level 45 Thieving (or 55 for scimitar wielding ones), and the Menaphite Thugs level 65 Thieving .
4601:
Ugthanki dung is camel dung that can be collected in a bucket. It plays a small role in Forgettable Tale... , My Arm's Big Adventure , and The Feud quests. Additionally, Ugthanki dung is used to fully recharge the Camulet obtained in Enakhra's Lament , with one bucket providing 4 charges.

Ugthanki dung is traditionally obtained by using a bottle of red hot sauce on the animal trough in Pollnivneach where Ali the Camel Man has camels behind his tent (this method can be used during the The Feud quest and the Forgettable Tale... quest). A camel will eat from the trough and drop dung a moment later. Use a bucket on the dung to pick up the Ugthanki dung. Buckets are sold by the market seller north-east of the camels' pen and there is a spawn inside the building attached to the camel pen.

If you are halfway through My Arm's Big Adventure quest or have completed it, you can also obtain Ugthanki dung by talking to certain camels , such as Al the Camel , while having the Camulet equipped. Eventually, after talking for a while, Ugthanki dung will appear on the ground. Use a bucket on the dung to place the dung in your inventory. This method can't be used during The Feud. This method may take some time, so it is recommended to use the red hot sauce instead.

If a player tries to pick up dung directly from the floor without a bucket, or tries to pick up green dung, a message appears in the chatbox that says, You're kidding me! I'm not picking that up. , No way am I picking that up. , Yuck! Im not touching that. [ sic ] , I wouldn't pick that up for all the runes in Gielinor. or I would rather wrestle a black dragon bare-handed.

The total required dung for all quests is 5: 1 for Forgettable Tale... (has a chance to be required, not guaranteed), 3 for My Arm's Big Adventure, and 1 for The Feud.
4602:
Ugthanki dung is an unobtainable variant of the regular Ugthanki dung. Occasionally, Ali the Camel will produce a green dung after red hot sauce is poured into his trough. However, the player cannot use the spade to pick it up unlike the normal dung; attempting to do so results in the player stating "I wouldn't pick that up for all the runes in Gielinor!"

Interestingly, the item's internal name refers to it as a poisoned dung bucket, while the examine information suggests it would have been obtained by feeding the camel something other than red hot sauce.
4603: A receipt is a quest item obtained during The Feud . It is obtained by buying two camels to give to each of the two gangs, Menaphites and Bandits , in Pollnivneach . However, this fails, and both of them ask for 10 camels instead. Players must go through a certain conversation path in order to obtain receipts.
4604: Hag's poison is a quest item used in The Feud quest. It is made for the player by Ali the Hag after giving her a full snake basket and a bucket of Ugthanki dung . The poison must then be slipped into a beer on the table of the inn in Pollnivneach in order to kill a traitor.
4605:
A snake charm is an item that players use in the two quests, The Feud and Ratcatchers, and in the minigame Pyramid Plunder.

In The Feud, players use it to lure a snake into a basket used for a poison. During Ratcatchers, they use it to charm rats into the sea, in a homage to the Pied Piper.

In the Pyramid Plunder minigame, players have the option to use the charm to distract snakes while they loot the pots in each room. To do this, players must first search an urn for a snake. Once a snake appears, use the snake charm on the urn, and you will play a quick song to distract the snake, allowing you to loot the urn.

Players obtain this item by putting two coins into the snake charmer's pouch. They also get a snake basket. The charm and a basket are available behind the bar in Pollnivneach for three coins.

The basket will be used during The Feud, but the charm remains with the player. Players can reacquire them from Ali the Snake Charmer.

These items can also be obtained from Wingstone in the Gnome Restaurant minigame.

Note: If you already have a snake charm in your inventory or your bank (such as from a previous quest) when speaking to Ali, he will make note of this, and thus will not provide you with another one.

The snake charm is one of four items that allow you to compose your own music, the other items being the piano found in the manor during the Misthalin Mystery quest, the piano in the Witch's house, and the clan hall piano. By playing it, a menu opens up that allows you to pick how many holes you want to hold down for each note, allowing you to string brief tunes together.

After completion of Ratcatchers, if you attempt to play the tune that charmed the rats again, your character comments that they don't think they should do that here.
4606: A snake basket is used to store desert snakes which are lured by use of the snake charm during The Feud. When a snake is successfully charmed, the snake will go into the basket and become a full snake basket. Ali the Hag will then take the full snake basket and use it to make a poison intended for Traitorous Ali. If you have lost your basket, put one gold coin into Ali the snake charmer's money pot and select chat option "wow, a snake charmer! Can I have a go? Can I have a go? Please?". This is the only chat option to retrieve another basket.
4607: A snake basket full is obtained by using a snake charm along with a snake basket on a desert snake during The Feud. The player must take the resulting full snake basket to the hag in Pollnivneach so she can make a poison to kill Traitorous Ali.
4608:
A super kebab is a kebab that has had red hot sauce added to make it spicy. They are sold by Ali the Kebab seller for 5 coins . Much like the normal kebab , the super kebab has a 5/8 chance to restore Hitpoints by 3 + 7% of the player's Hitpoints level. [ 1 ] It also has a 1/32 chance of reducing any stats except Hitpoints .

To make a super kebab, the player must use red hot sauce (obtained from Ali the Kebab seller ) on either a normal kebab or ugthanki kebab . A strange-smelling ugthanki kebab will also work.
4610:
Red hot sauce can be obtained from the kebab shop in the town centre of Pollnivneach . It is used in The Feud and My Arm's Big Adventure quests to obtain Camel dung which is necessary to make the poison used to kill Traitorous Ali . It can also be used on an ordinary kebab to turn it into a super kebab , consuming the bottle.

Isma'il the Kebab seller will not give the player a second bottle of red hot sauce while the player has one in their inventory or in the bank, nor can the player pick up any they may have dropped once another has been received from Ali. However, one can obtain another via Telekinetic Grab . It should be noted, if the intention of obtaining this item is to be used to gather Camel dung, only one is necessary as the sauce can be re-used indefinitely.

If the player attempts to use the bottle on Drunken Ali 's drink on the table in the Pollnivneach bar, the character will say "You know what? This is childish. I'm not doing it."
4611:
The desert disguise is used in The Feud quest . It can be made by combining a fake beard and a Kharidian headpiece , both of which can be bought from Ali Morrisane 's stall just north of Al Kharid . Upon completing the quest, the disguise can still be created and the materials will still be obtainable.

Wearing the disguise will delay the onset of desert heat by 12 seconds.
4613:
The spinning plate is a toy bought from Diango in Draynor Village. It is a white plate with a red picture of a dragon on it. The player can click on the plate to have their character spin the plate on a stick. This has no in-game effect and is purely cosmetic.

The spinning plate is one of the items the rowdy dwarf can request from the player during Forgettable Tale of a Drunken Dwarf.
4614:
The Broken plate is an unobtainable item that appears in the game cache but cannot be obtained.

Spinning plates used to have a chance of being dropped when the player spun it, turning into a broken plate. The plate would break the majority of the time, and was impossible to repair. This feature was heavily criticised, as players had no option except to discard the now-useless item and buy a new plate. As a result, the plates were hotfixed on the same day to no longer break. Therefore, broken plates have never been obtainable in Old School RuneScape .

Despite not having an option to equip it, the broken plate has a model for use while equipped, which was used in the breaking animation.
4615:
The letter is a quest item in The Golem quest, obtained towards the beginning of the quest after the player has spoken to the Clay golem . It is found lying on the floor in the ruined city of Uzer , in one of the remains of the houses.

The letter details the next step of the quest; journeying to the Digsite near Varrock to find Varmen , and eventually to steal a statuette from Varrock Museum in order to help fix the golem and make it understand that Thammaron is dead, and its task is complete.

It can be reobtained after the quest, though it has no further use.
4616:
Varmen's notes is a book found while doing The Golem and offers insight into the Ruins of Uzer and the existence of the Clay golem. The book is also titled The Ruins of Uzer and was written by Varmen.

After doing the quest, the book can be found in the shelves in a player's house and in the bookshelves in the Digsite Exam Centre.
4617:
The display cabinet key is used during The Golem to open a cabinet in Varrock Museum where a statuette is kept. The key can be pickpocketed from the curator within the museum. Only one copy of the key can be obtained.

This key cannot be put on the Steel key ring acquired from completion of One Small Favour. Since it opens only the one cabinet, it becomes useless after the quest.
4618:
The statuette is a small stone figure required for The Golem quest. The key for its cabinet (30) is obtained by pickpocketing Curator Haig Halen in the Varrock Museum.

After the statuette is stolen, the display case reads: "Recently this display was stolen and its whereabouts are unknown." However, if the player loses the statuette during the quest, they can get another one by using the display cabinet key with the now empty display case.

Attempting to return this item to the display it came from yields "Nothing interesting happens.".
4619:
The strange implement is found in the basement of the temple ruins located in the ruins of Uzer . During The Golem quest , players use it to open the clay golem 's head to reprogram it with the golem program . It also is used in Shadow of the Storm to make the golem help in the ceremony to resummon the demon .

This key cannot be put on the steel key ring acquired from completion of One Small Favour .
4620:
The black mushroom is a quest item in The Golem , Shadow of the Storm and Land of the Goblins quests , found beneath the Ruins of Uzer and in the Goblin Cave by the entrance to the Goblin Temple .

When used with a pestle and mortar and a vial in the inventory, black dye is made, which is used to dye several items black.
4621:
Phoenix feathers can be grabbed from the desert phoenix north-east of the River Elid , by the clay mines. One feather at a time can be plucked from the bird's tail, but the player may fail, in which case the phoenix stuns the player and does a small amount of damage. Players do not kill the bird when plucking feathers. When a feather is successfully plucked, the player earns 26 Thieving experience points.

A phoenix feather is used in The Golem quest, where it is used on black dye to turn it into a phoenix quill pen .

Only one phoenix feather or phoenix quill pen can be owned at a time, however if neither are owned, it is possible to reobtain the phoenix feather even after quest completion.
4622:
Black dye is made by using a pestle and mortar on black mushrooms while having an empty vial in the inventory. It is used in The Golem quest to write a program containing new instructions for the Golem to run. It is also used in Land of the Goblins to dye goblin mail black.

Warning: Dyeing Silverlight black will consume all copies of the sword in your inventory, leaving you with only one dyed sword.

It functions as a black dye and can be used on several items:

Desert shirt, to create a black desert shirt.

Desert robe, to create a black desert robe.

Blue wizard hat, to create a black wizard hat.

Blue wizard robe, to create a black robe.

Any basic coloured cape, to create a black cape.

Any coloured goblin mail, to create a black goblin mail.

Orange slices, to create dyed orange, after partial completion of Freeing the Goblin generals.

Origami balloons.

Phoenix feather, to create a phoenix quill pen which does not consume the ink.

Black sails (10 are need per boat).
4623:
The phoenix quill pen is a quest item used in The Golem quest. It is created by using black dye on a phoenix feather . It can then be used to write a program that contains new instructions for the Golem, thus completing the quest.

If lost, even after quest completion, it can be remade by using black dye on a newly plucked phoenix feather.
4624:
The golem program is a quest item used in The Golem quest to reprogram the golem . It is made by using a phoenix quill pen on a sheet of papyrus .

The program is required to convince the golem that the demon Thammaron is dead.
4625:
Bandits are interface items that can be seen in the Thieving skill guide, representing Bandits.

Skill guides are in fact inventories containing a series of items. In order to represent NPCs or scenery in a skill guide, examinable items had to be created for each.

The actual items cannot be obtained by players.
4627:
Bandit's brew is a type of ale that restores 1 Hitpoint and temporarily boosts Thieving and Attack by 1, while draining Strength and Defence by ⌊Level×6100⌋+3 (see table below).

It can be purchased at The Big Heist Lodge in the Kharidian Desert Bandit Camp for 650 coins only after reaching the appropriate step of the quest Desert Treasure I. Unlike other ales, it cannot be made through brewing.

One bandit's brew is required for the quest Desert Treasure I.
4629:
Spells are a series of unobtainable items that exist in the game cache. Presumably, they are used in the Spellbook interface. While originally a Spell item existed for every magic spell, since 2014 this has not been necessary.

In an update in 2018 which reworked the Spellbook, the original scroll appearance of the items was removed.

4653:
Fire is an unobtainable item that was presumably intended for use during the Desert Treasure I quest. It would most likely have been found in the Smoke Dungeon , as part of a subquest for finding the Fire diamond, alongside the fire key. As the fire diamond was changed to the smoke diamond instead, the fire key was changed to the Warm key , and the Fire object was removed.

While on the ground it cannot be picked up. Instead, it has the option of "study", giving the message "A strangely bright burning flame..."
4654: The etchings are an item used in Desert Treasure I. The player receives them from Asgarnia Smith at the Bedabin Camp who wants the player to take them to Terry Balando, the archaeological expert located at the Digsite. After talking to him, he will give the player a translation in exchange for the etchings.
4655:
Translation (also called Four Diamonds translation and Translation Primer ) is part of the Desert Treasure I quest, given to you by Terry Balando at the Digsite after you give him etchings given to you by Asgarnia Smith . It gives some information of the diamonds you use to open the pyramid and their origin.

After doing the quest, you can also find the book on the shelves in your house .
4656:
The warm key is obtained from the burnt chest in the Smoke Dungeon. The player must light all four torches in the corners of dungeon and then search the chest in the centre of the dungeon to obtain the key before any of the torches go out. Ice gloves are not required to pick it up, however they are used to fight Fareed.

The key is used to permanently unlock the gate to enter the area to fight Fareed in the Desert Treasure I quest. It is consumed upon use and is not reobtainable after opening the gate, attempting to get another yields the message: "There is nothing inside the chest."

The key is only taken when used on the gate, so players may get the key and leave the dungeon to restock supplies without losing the key.

Duplicates can be obtained only via drop trick and searching the chest again. Banking them will not work. Duplicate keys will not be taken when unlocking the gate.

After the quest, Fareed's room can still be accessed.
4657:
The ring of visibility is a special ring that can be obtained from Rasolo the merchant, after the player retrieves his gilded cross for him during the quest Desert Treasure I . Wearing the ring lets the player see mysterious ghosts and other objects that are normally invisible. The ring of visibility cannot be made using the Crafting skill. It cannot be equipped in the Lassar Undercity .

If lost, the ring can be reclaimed by talking to Rasolo , who is located west of the Fishing Guild and south of the Baxtorian Falls . After completion of Desert Treasure II , the ring of shadows can be used as an upgrade to the ring of visibility.

If the player dies with the ring equipped or in their inventory, they will always lose it and it will be turned into 42 coins , even if they had fewer than 3 items (or four with Protect Item ). The two exceptions are if the player dies while fighting Damis during Desert Treasure I, in which case they will keep the ring like normal, or if the player dies in the Shadow Realm during Desert Treasure II, in which case it will be kept or appear in your gravestone loot.

It may be possible for the ring to not remain in the player's inventory upon death in the Shadow Dungeon . If this happens, the player can only retrieve their items from Death's Office as they will not be able to use the ghostly ladder without the ring. Ultimate Iron accounts always keep the ring upon death.
4658:
The Silver pot is a quest item used in the Desert Treasure I quest , obtained by giving Ruantun a silver bar .

It is filled with blood when talking to Malak where he will attack the player for 5 Hitpoints . The damage will decrease so that it does not kill the player and instead leave them with at minimum 1 Hitpoints. Spice and garlic can then be added. It can be blessed at any point (whether empty, with blood, etc.) by talking to the High Priest on Entrana . Once it has been blessed and all ingredients have been added, it can be used to summon Dessous .

Note: Dessous can be summoned with just the silver pot filled with blood, but as long as all the steps are not completed he cannot be killed.

After the player completes their task from Malak and collects the blood diamond , all variants of the pot will be taken. To avoid this, the copies must be dropped before talking to him. If the blood diamond is lost and needs to be reclaimed, the duplicated pots need to be dropped again to avoid confiscation.
4659:
The blessed pot is a quest item created by taking a silver pot made by Ruantun to be blessed by the High Priest on Entrana.

Talking to Malak will let him damage you for 5 hitpoints, filling the pot with blood. Spices and garlic must then be added (in either order) to complete it, after which it can be used to summon Dessous. If the player has 5 or less hitpoints, he will do damage that leaves at least 1 hitpoint. It should also be noted that even if the player has one hitpoint, he will instead hit a zero and the player will still obtain a pot with their blood.

After the player completes their task from Malak and collects the blood diamond, he will confiscate the pot (all variants) from the player's inventory or bank. Should the player wish to keep it or a copy, they should drop it before speaking to Malak. If the player loses the blood diamond and reclaims it from him, he will again confiscate any blessed pots the player may have in their possession.
4660:
The Silver pot is a quest item used in the Desert Treasure I quest , obtained by giving Ruantun a silver bar .

It is filled with blood when talking to Malak where he will attack the player for 5 Hitpoints . The damage will decrease so that it does not kill the player and instead leave them with at minimum 1 Hitpoints. Spice and garlic can then be added. It can be blessed at any point (whether empty, with blood, etc.) by talking to the High Priest on Entrana . Once it has been blessed and all ingredients have been added, it can be used to summon Dessous .

Note: Dessous can be summoned with just the silver pot filled with blood, but as long as all the steps are not completed he cannot be killed.

After the player completes their task from Malak and collects the blood diamond , all variants of the pot will be taken. To avoid this, the copies must be dropped before talking to him. If the blood diamond is lost and needs to be reclaimed, the duplicated pots need to be dropped again to avoid confiscation.
