4668: Garlic powder is created by using a pestle and mortar on garlic . It is used with a blessed pot to defeat Dessous during the Desert Treasure I quest . The item can be created at anytime, regardless the player having started or completed the quest.
4670:
The blood diamond is one of four Diamonds of Azzanadra obtained during the Desert Treasure I quest . It is obtained by defeating Dessous and then talking to Malak who will give the player the diamond.

It is recommended that players deposit this gem in the bank as soon as they obtain it, along with the other Diamonds of Azzanadra, as a level 95 stranger may appear and attack them if they are holding one of them. The more diamonds you have on you, the more likely the stranger will appear and attack you.

Should the player lose the diamond or want to collect another via drop trick , speaking to Malak will allow another one to be obtained. However, all variants of the silver or blessed pot will be taken from the player and the only way to avoid this is dropping them. To keep a copy of the diamond after the quest, drop a duplicate before putting the last Diamond of Azzanadra into the pyramid's final unpowered obelisk and it will be safely kept afterwards, even upon quest completion.
4671:
The ice diamond is one of the four Diamonds of Azzanadra which must be obtained during the Desert Treasure I quest . It is obtained from the troll child by defeating Kamil and then freeing his parents from ice.

It is recommended that players deposit this gem on the bank as soon as they obtain it, along with the other Diamonds of Azzanadra, as a level 95 stranger may appear and attack them if they are holding one of them. The more diamonds you have on you, the more likely the stranger will appear and attack you.

Should the player lose the diamond or want to collect another via the drop trick , speak to the troll child to obtain another. To keep a copy of the diamond after the quest, drop a duplicate before putting the last Diamond of Azzanadra into the pyramid's final unpowered obelisk and it will be safely kept afterwards, even upon quest completion.
4672:
The smoke diamond is one of the four Diamonds of Azzanadra which must be obtained during the Desert Treasure I quest . It is obtained by defeating Fareed in the smoke dungeon.

It is recommended that players deposit this gem in the bank as soon as they obtain it, along with the other Diamonds of Azzanadra, as a level 95 stranger may appear and attack them if they are holding one of them. The more diamonds you have on you, the more likely the stranger will appear and attack you.

Should the player lose the diamond or want to collect another via the drop trick , entering the gated area, where Fareed was fought, will spawn another. To keep a copy of the diamond after the quest, drop a duplicate before putting the last Diamond of Azzanadra into the pyramid's final unpowered obelisk and it will be safely kept afterwards, even upon quest completion.
4673:
The shadow diamond is one of the four Diamonds of Azzanadra which must be obtained during the Desert Treasure I quest . It is located in the Shadow Dungeon and is obtained by killing both of Damis ' forms.

It is recommended that players deposit this gem on the bank as soon as they obtain it, along with the other Diamonds of Azzanadra , as a level 95 stranger may appear and attack them if they are holding one of them. The more diamonds you have on you, the more likely the stranger will appear and attack you.

Should the player lose the diamond or want to collect another via the drop trick , crossing into the dungeon's multi-combat zone at the end of the corridor connecting to the open area where Damis was fought, will spawn another. To keep a copy of the diamond after the quest, drop a duplicate before putting the last Diamond of Azzanadra into the pyramid's final unpowered obelisk and it will be safely kept afterwards, even upon quest completion.
4674:
The gilded cross is found as part of the Desert Treasure I quest when looking for the Diamond of Shadow. It must be stolen from the Desert Bandit Camp where it is found in a secure chest, which requires players to lockpick it three times in a row successfully in order to be opened. Once obtained, it may be traded with Rasolo for the ring of visibility.

If a player loses the gilded cross before they give it to Rasolo, another can be obtained by searching the chest again. They do not need to unlock the chest again.
4675:
The ancient staff is a one-handed magical weapon that can be used to autocast spells from the Ancient spellbook and standard spellbook . It requires 50 Attack and 50 Magic to wield, along with completion of Desert Treasure I . The staff is decorated with the symbol of Zaros .

It is frequently used in high-level player-killing due to its high magical accuracy. It, along with its upgraded versions, are the only items that have negative Prayer bonus.

Similarly to bladed staves , this staff has an attack speed of 4, making it a suitable weapon for melee combat, displaying similar stats as those of the rune scimitar with slightly higher strength bonus and lower attack bonus. It is outclassed in melee combat by the granite hammer , which also requires 50 Attack to wield, with an additional requirement of 50 Strength .

The staff may be bought once from Eblis for 80,000 coins after completing Desert Treasure I. For this reason, Ironmen are not recommended to alch or drop it because it is used in a master clue step , and the only other way the staff can be acquired is either as a rare drop from several boss monsters or as a very rare drop from mummies in the Ancient Pyramid .
4677: The catspeak amulet is a special amulet that allows the wearer to speak with cats. It is received after the completion of Icthlarin's Little Helper, and is used in several subsequent quests. If players lose the amulet, the Sphinx will give them a replacement amulet, but only if they have a cat following them. During Dragon Slayer II, players gain the ability to speak to cats without needing the amulet.
4678:
The canopic jar is a quest item for Icthlarin's Little Helper that contains Klenter 's organs. The High Priest will get mad at the player for carrying it during parts of the quest. It is also part of a plan for Amascut . During the quest it may be temporarily stored in the bank and duplicates can be received, however using one canopic jar will remove any others from your bank.

After the quest, it cannot be stored in the bank , displaying the message, A magical force prevents you from banking this item! . When the player drops it, it says, The burial jar magically turns to dust as you drop it.

Even if a player manages to get rid of the jar during the quest, upon entering the pyramid, they'll get a message: You see a strange jar on the floor. It seems oddly familiar, as if you'd seen it before, so you decide to pick it up. During the second flashback, the player also has to pick up one of four canopic jars, depending on the one they had in real time.

4682:
The holy symbol is a quest item obtained from the Carpenter during the Icthlarin's Little Helper quest. The High Priest tells the player they need to obtain one from the carpenter for the ceremony in the burial pyramid to take place. The player needs to speak to the carpenter who needs some willow logs to carve it. After waiting for awhile, the carpenter puts the finishing touches to the symbol before handing it over. After the battle with the Possessed Priest at the end of the quest, the player comments that the symbol was useless as they had already started the ceremony without it. Although the High Priest refutes that the symbol is what finally put the former, deceased High Priest to rest and also helped greatly in defeating the Possessed priest and Amascut.

If a player loses the symbol, they may obtain another one by speaking to the carpenter again.

The item represents Icthlarin's god symbol, displayed to the left. The symbol is an ankh (☥), a symbol used by the Egyptians. The unholy symbol also used during the quest appears to be near identical, except it is inverted.

The symbol is immune to many forms of Magic, such as the Low Alchemy spells, with the message: "Some magical force blocks the alchemy spell."

While it is possible to obtain another holy symbol if the first is lost, it is not possible to simultaneously bear two Holy Symbols using the drop trick method, as "I don't really need any one of these." However, you can bypass this by simply using the Telekinetic Grab spell.
4683:
The Unholy symbol is a quest item obtained upon entering the burial pyramid during the Icthlarin's Little Helper quest. When the wanderer (Amascut) hypnotises the player, she hands over the symbol and says they will know what to do with it when the time comes. During one of the flashbacks, the player learns they placed this item in one of the sarcophagi so Amascut may enter the pyramid at ease. In the end of the quest, this led to her appearing during the ceremony, controlling a priest and attempting to kill/destroy all present at the ceremony. The adventurer defeats the priest and Amascut teleports away.

The symbol represents Amascut, displayed to the left. The symbol is an inverted ankh (☥), a symbol used by the Egyptians. The holy symbol also used during the quest appears to be near identical, except it is upside-down.

It is not possible to cast any kind of Alchemy spell upon the Unholy symbol, as "I can't do that, the mistress wouldn't permit it."
4684: Linen is an item available from Raetul in Sophanem . It currently has only one use in the game: it is one of the items needed in the quest Icthlarin's Little Helper . It can be traded.
4686:
The embalming manual, or The Little Book of Embalming, is a book written by Bod E. Wrapper which can be found during the Icthlarin's Little Helper quest. The manual is found in Sophanem on the 1st floor of the embalmer's house. After the quest, the manual can be found in the bookcase of a player-owned house whether or not it was obtained during the quest.

The book details how cadavers are handled in Sophanem, and contains hints as to where the player can find the items requested by the embalmer during the quest.
4687:
A bucket of sap is obtained by using a knife with some types of trees, while having an empty bucket in the player's inventory.

Contrary to popular belief that sap must be obtained from an evergreen tree , there are also many trees that give sap that are not described as 'Evergreen'. These are typically the slightly taller and pointier trees, and can be told apart by their examine text, which is "A commonly found tree.", instead of "One of the most common trees in Gielinor." Sap is used in two quests: Icthlarin's Little Helper and The Eyes of Glouphrie . In Icthlarin's Little Helper, the bucket of sap is given to the embalmer. In Eyes of Glouphrie, the bucket of sap is used with ground mud runes to create magic glue .

A fast way to get the sap is by using the nightmare zone minigame teleport, as there is a tree directly south of the teleport that will give sap. An alternative is by using the fairy ring A K Q to teleport to the Piscatoris hunter area where there are multiple evergreen trees immediately next to the fairy ring. A games necklace can also be used to teleport to the Burthorpe Games Room ; from there, the player can run south until they reach the entrance where a few evergreen trees are located on the east. Most of the trees around the Grand Exchange also give sap.
4689:
A pile of salt is an item that can be made by using a bucket of saltwater on the suntrap in Sophanem. It is created during the quest Icthlarin's Little Helper.

This item cannot be used in place of a bag of salt to kill rockslugs.
4691:
The Sphinx's token is a quest item obtained from the Sphinx in Sophanem during the Icthlarin's Little Helper quest.

Upon asking for help from the Sphinx, she will give you the token and direct you to talk to the High Priest. Initially when speaking to the priest, he wishes to not communicate with you. Although when the player presents the token, the priest surprisingly says that he will listen to the player, if they have somehow received the Sphinx's approval. He then takes the token and the player is free to talk to him at any time without approval.

If the player manages to lose the token, they can ask the Sphinx for another one as long as the player hasn't given one to the high priest.
4692:
The Gold leaf is an unobtainable item that appears in the game's code but does not spawn anywhere. Despite not having an option to equip it, the gold leaf has a model for use while equipped.

While the leaf was added alongside Icthlarin's Little Helper , it does not appear to have been intended for use during the quest. It may have been related to Raetul .
4693: A bucket of saltwater is used in Icthlarin's Little Helper . It is a bucket that has been filled with salty water from the lake just north of Sophanem . If used on the suntrap south of the food shop in Sophanem, it can be dried into a pile of salt .
4694:
Magic scrolls were six unobtainable items added to the game cache in 2005. They were created as placeholders for the six combination runes.

The examine information of the magic scrolls all suggested they could be exchanged for exceptional amounts of wealth. This was possibly designed to trick players at the time who used hex editing software to view unobtainable items.

On 13 June 2005, the six combination runes were released with the Runecraft update, and the magic scrolls were removed from the game.

4700:
A sapphire lantern is a bullseye lantern that has a sapphire in place of its more usual glass lens. Making the lantern from scratch requires level 49 Smithing (Frame) and 20 Crafting (Cut Sapphire).

Note: Lamp oil needs to be added before the lantern can be lit if crafted with a Bullseye lantern (empty). This can be accomplished by either bringing swamp tar to the chemist in Rimmington, or using swamp tar on the Lamp Still at Miltog's market stall within Dorgesh-Kaan while the lantern is still in your inventory.

To make the Sapphire Lantern, the player must use a cut sapphire on a normal or unlensed bullseye lantern. If the lantern used had a lens, the player will receive a lens in their inventory. After the player is finished using the sapphire lantern, they may use a bullseye lantern lens to convert it back into a normal bullseye lantern and retrieve the sapphire.

The lantern is a light source and is used for attracting light creatures in the Chasm of Tears. Players need to use these creatures to traverse the cavern in the Tears of Guthix and While Guthix Sleeps quests.

When extinguished, the message You extinguish the lantern. is displayed.

The lantern can be made at any time, independent of quests and activities. The lantern is kept in the inventory on death.

4703:
Magic stones are used in the quest Tears of Guthix to make the stone bowl, using a Chisel. It is mined from magical rocks near Juna within the Chasm of Tears.

You must have a sapphire lantern with you to access the stones. Use the sapphire lantern on a light creature and select to go "across the chasm" and you will see the magical rocks. Without starting the Tears of Guthix quest, one can still mine the stone, but upon completing the quest it becomes unobtainable (along with the ability to craft stone bowls). The stone can be kept after the quest by dropping one before completing the quest and picking it back up after completing the quest.
4704:
The stone bowl is used in the Tears of Guthix minigame to catch tears from the cave protected by Juna.

During the Tears of Guthix quest, to make the bowl, the player must use a pickaxe on the magical rocks in the Chasm of Tears to get a magic stone, and then use a chisel to craft it into a bowl. To get to the mine, you must use a sapphire lantern on one of the light creatures in the cave.

This bowl is given to Juna to complete the quest, and when a player wants to participate in the Tears of Guthix minigame, Juna will have the player wield the bowl.

This bowl should not be confused with the other stone bowl used during Elemental Workshop I, which cannot be used in this item's place.
4707:
The crumbling tome, or Legend of the Brothers, is found on a desk in a building just east of the entrance to the Barrows. It is also obtained from the Strange Old Man in the Barrows if the conversation begins as "what? I didn't ask for a book!"

It describes the story of the brave heroes that are buried there and what just happened to them to bring about the beginning of their end.

Players can also find it in the bookshelf in their player-owned houses, under the name Legend of the Brothers.
4708:
Ahrim's hood is magic armour worn in the headwear slot that is part of Ahrim the Blighted's set of barrows equipment . To wear Ahrim's hood, a player must have 70 Defence and 70 Magic .

Players may opt to use a farseer helm instead of Ahrim's hood, unless the set effect or damage bonus is desired. Compared to the farseer helm, Ahrim's hood has higher level requirements to wear but no quest requirements, and provides +1% Magic damage bonus. However, the hood provides an identical magic attack bonus and incurs repair costs.

Being part of Ahrim's barrows set, if Ahrim's hood is worn along with all of the other pieces of equipment in Ahrim's barrows set the player's successful magic attacks have a chance of temporarily lowering the opponent's Strength level. This is cumulative with other effects that lower strength, namely the spell Enfeeble .

Additionally, wearing Ahrim's set with an amulet of the damned will allow players to autocast Ancient Magicks , and also grant players a 25% chance of dealing a hit with 30% increased damage.
4710:
Ahrim's staff is a one-handed magic weapon that is part of Ahrim the Blighted's set . To wield Ahrim's staff, the player must have 70 Magic and 70 Attack . It increases Magic damage by 5%.

If Ahrim's staff is wielded along with all of the other pieces of equipment in Ahrim's barrows set, the player's successful magic attacks have a chance of temporarily lowering the opponent's Strength level. This is cumulative with other effects that lower strength, namely the spell Enfeeble .

It is able to autocast Standard combat spells as well as being one of the few weapons able to autocast Arceuus combat spells . Additionally, wearing Ahrim's set with an Amulet of the damned will allow players to autocast Ancient Magicks , and also grant players a 25% chance of dealing a hit with 30% increased damage.

4724:
Guthan's helm is melee armour worn in the headwear slot that is part of Guthan the Infested's set of barrows equipment . To wear Guthan's helm, a player must have 70 Defence .

If Guthan's helm is wielded together with all other pieces of Guthan's armour set, then successful melee attacks have a 25% chance of restoring health to the user equal to the damage dealt to the target. This set has the potential to be extremely useful in a variety of combat situations, due to its healing reducing the need to bring food . While the set has strong combat stats, its durability can be conserved through only equipping it when a player needs to heal, and carrying alternative non-degradable armour and weaponry.

4732:
Karil's coif is ranged armour worn in the headwear slot that is part of Karil the Tainted's set of barrows equipment . To wear Karil's coif, a player must have 70 Defence and 70 Ranged .

Being part of Karil's barrows set, if Karil's coif is worn along with the other three pieces of Karil's set, the player's attacks gains a special effect: on successful attacks with Karil's crossbow against another player, there is a 25% chance that it may temporarily lower that player's Agility level by 20%. Additionally, if an amulet of the damned is worn alongside the set, there is also a 25% chance for each attack to deal a second hit for half the damage of the first.
4734:
Karil's crossbow is a two-handed ranged weapon that is part of Karil the Tainted's set . It requires 70 Ranged to wield. It fires bolt racks , which break upon firing. When equipped with the other three pieces of Karil the Tainted 's set the wearer will receive the set effect, which has a chance to temporarily lower their target's Agility level. Additionally, if an amulet of the damned is worn alongside the set, there is also a 25% chance for each attack to deal a second hit for half the damage of the first.

Unlike standard crossbows, it is wielded in both hands. Furthermore, regular crossbows fire fewer, more powerful shots, meaning Karil's crossbow is actually similar in function to a shortbow ; this gives it a potentially higher damage per second, at the expense of the shield slot. The crossbow has an attack range of 8. Longrange increases attack range by 2.

This weapon is comparable to a magic shortbow and its imbued counterpart . While Karil's offers a longer range, a +15 or +9 greater ranged attack bonus respectively, and a passive chance to hit twice when using the full Karil set and amulet of the damned, the magic shortbow variants offer identical strength when using amethyst arrows , which are not guaranteed to be consumed with each shot. In addition, the magic shortbows do not degrade. Players on a budget or fighting monsters with low ranged defence may find the magic shortbow to be the preferable option.

4740:
Bolt racks are ammunition exclusively used by the Karil's crossbow. They are a reward from Barrows with at least 881 reward potential, purchased from Ak-Haranu's Exotic Shop on the Port Phasmatys docks, or purchased from the Last Man Standing shop.

Unlike other bolts, they always disappear after being fired and cannot be retrieved by Ava's devices.
4745:
Torag's helm is melee armour worn in the headwear slot that is part of Torag the Corrupted's set of Barrows equipment. To wear Torag's helmet, a player must have 70 Defence.

Being part of Torag's barrows set, if Torag's helmet is worn along with all of the other pieces of equipment in Torag's barrows set the player gains a set effect. Damaging melee attacks have a chance of lowering the victim's run energy by 20%.

Torag's helmet is not commonly used due to its lack of Strength or Prayer bonuses. Furthermore, the set effect is considered mediocre. As a result, it is inexpensive compared to the other barrows helmets. However, it is often used in PKing, especially by ranged tanks, as there are few other inexpensive helm options for rangers and the negative ranged attack bonus is small.

For more details on the mechanics and strategies for this equipment, see the set page.
4747:
Torag's hammers are a two-handed blunt weapon that is part of Torag the Corrupted's set of barrows equipment. To wield Torag's hammers, a player must have 70 Attack and Strength.

Being part of Torag's barrows set, if Torag's hammers are wielded along with all of the other pieces of equipment in Torag's barrows set the player gains a special effect: damaging melee attacks have a chance of lowering the victim's run energy by 20%.

Torag's hammers have lower popularity and value compared to other Barrows weapons, as the hammers have a lower strength bonus and Torag's special effect is not as useful in combat. However, they have a high crush bonus and can be one of the more likely out of the melee Barrows weapons to hit as most armours have less crush defensive bonus than slash.

Like the glacial temotli, sulphur blades, and Earthbound tecpatl, the hammers perform two independently rolled hits per attack. The maximum damage of each hit is determined by calculating the combined max hit as normal and dividing it by two. If the combined max hit is odd, one max hit is rounded up while the other is rounded down (e.g., 45 → 22 + 23). This unique effect is useful when fighting NPCs with negative flat armour, such as the Blue Moon, as the flat damage increase gets applied to each hitsplat separately.

4753:
Verac's helm is melee armour worn in the headwear slot that is part of Verac the Defiled's set of Barrows equipment. To wear Verac's helmet, a player must have 70 Defence.

Verac's helm has a lesser magic penalty compared to other helmets at +0 magic defence but slightly less ranged defence bonuses compared to Guthan's or Torag's helm, which are equal bonuses. This helmet is often used in 'tank' combat due to the high defensive bonuses as well as a prayer bonus. This helmet is commonly used during the TzHaar Fight Cave minigame because of its good melee and ranged defence and prayer bonus.

If Verac's helm is worn along with all of the other pieces of equipment in Verac's set, the player receives the Defiler set effect. With this set effect active, player attacks have a chance (averaging 1/4) of hitting through an opponent's defence and prayer entirely. This effect can be devastating towards tank opponents who rely on high defence. With this set effect, Verac's flail can be considered one of the best weapons for certain PvM situations.

4808:
The black prism can be obtained during Zogre Flesh Eaters quest. During the quest, it can be found in the coffin to the west of the skeleton on the floor. If you look-at it, there is a description which suggests that it was involved in the explosion that hit the area, and was blasted into the coffin. Zavistic Rarve identifies it as a tool of necromancy.

This artefact has been used to resurrect the dead ogres in Jiggig as Zogres and Skogres. Later in the quest, the player discovers that it was Sithik Ints who has used to do so out of his hatred toward ogres. After the quest, you can sell it to Zavistic Rarve for 2000 coins or Yanni Salika for 5000 coins.
4809:
The torn page is found on a broken lectern in Jiggig during the Zogre Flesh Eaters quest. If the player reads it, the player will discover that it was used to place a curse on the area, raising the dead "for all time"; the player will also find a guild emblem on it, a clue that it relates in some way to the Wizards' Guild in Yanille .

The page has been torn from the necromancy book , which can be confirmed by using it on that book. In combination with other evidence, it persuades Zavistic Rarve that Sithik Ints might have had something to do with the curse. He then assists the player to catch Sithik.

If the player drops the torn page after showing it to Zavistic Rarve, it cannot be re-obtained. However, the player will still be able to receive the strange potion if all of the other pieces of evidence are shown to him.
4810:
The ruined backpack is dropped by a zombie during the Zogre Flesh Eaters quest , in the caves of Jiggig . It contains items that players use to investigate Brentle Vahn 's death. These items are a dragon inn tankard , rotten food and a knife . The tankard is the only item in the backpack that is required for the quest.

The backpack automatically disappears after the player clicks to check what is inside it. If the player has multiple copies of the backpack, they will all be destroyed at the same time.
4811:
The dragon inn tankard is one of the items which players take out of the ruined backpack during the Zogre Flesh Eaters quest. It has the "look at" option. Doing so reveals that it has the dragon emblem and the words "Ye Olde Dragon Inn" on it, a clue to seek further evidence at the Dragon Inn.

Showing it to the bartender in Yanille prompts him to tell the player that it belonged to Brentle Vahn, a fighter with a reputation for selling his skills unwisely. The bartender then remarks that he's seen Brentle in the company of a shady wizard; since the player found the tankard among skeletal human remains, it becomes clear that Brentle met his end while on some errand for this wizard.

It is used again at a later stage of the same quest to persuade Zavistic Rarve that Brentle was the body in the Zogre cave. In combination with other evidence, this leads Zavistic to help the player catch the culprit.

This is the only item during Zogre Flesh Eaters which disappears from both the player's bank and inventory when the quest is finished, including all duplicates.
4812:
Zogre bones are bones obtained from killing zogres and skogres , which give 22.5 Prayer experience when buried. This can be increased by offering the bones in different ways:

If burying the zogre bones in Jiggig , there's a 1 in 3 [ confirmation needed ] chance and to spawn a skogre alongside the regular experience drop. The skogre will despawn after 5 minutes. A message in the chatbox appears "The creature rises from the grave... again!".
4814:
The Sithik portrait is an item used in the quest Zogre Flesh Eaters. During the quest, the player must create the Sithik portrait by using a piece of papyrus on Sithik Ints with a piece of charcoal in the inventory.

If successful, the player can then take the portrait to the Bartender at the Dragon Inn to have it signed, affirming that Sithik was present at that bar.

If the player fails to produce the portrait, they will be left with a bad Sithik portrait, which is useless, and the player must try again.

4816:
The signed portrait of Sithik Ints is an item used in Zogre Flesh Eaters. During the quest, the player must take a Sithik portrait to the Bartender to be signed, in order to charge Sithik Ints with leading Brentle Vahn to his death.

If players use the signed portrait on Sithik, Sithik will offer to bribe the player with 2 million gold, in order to buy the signed portrait. Whether the player accepts or rejects, Sithik will not buy the portrait, instead insisting that no one would believe the player anyway.

If players produce a bad Sithik portrait during their attempt, he will not sign it and the player will have to attempt to create the portrait again.
4817:
The book of portraiture is a quest item and has no use other than the one involved in Zogre Flesh Eaters quest, in which it provides a hint to the player. It is found, along with charcoal and a piece of papyrus, in the drawers in the room of Sithik Ints.

By following the book's directions with the piece of papyrus and charcoal (but not necessarily the book) in the player's inventory while in Sithik's room, the player produces a Sithik portrait.

The book cannot be placed in a player-owned house bookshelf.
4818:
The ogre artefact is a sacred item to the ogres of Gu'Tanoth , and is requested to be retrieved by Grish during the Zogre Flesh Eaters quest. It is dropped by a level 111 undead ourg named Slash Bash , who appears to be wearing the artefact as a helmet prior to being slain.

If lost during the quest, it can be found by searching the stand again. Slash Bash cannot be refought.
4819:
Bronze nails are nails made with a bronze bar on an anvil with a hammer in the player's inventory, requiring level 4 Smithing, yielding 15 bronze nails and granting 12.5 Smithing experience per bar. They can also be bought from a few shops, most notably the Sawmill, as well as the Shipyard, which can be teleported to for free by any Shipwright NPC found in major ports.

Bronze nails can be used to construct certain types of wooden furniture, however, they bend and break very easily. With 7 Fletching, they can be used on flighted ogre arrows to create bronze brutal arrows, granting 1.4 Fletching experience per arrow. With 41 Crafting, fifteen bronze nails can be used with an oak shield and two pieces of hard leather to craft a hard leather shield, granting 70 Crafting experience per shield. One bronze nail is required in The Fremennik Isles quest in order to make a Neitiznot shield.

Since nails cannot be bent while constructing STASH units, bronze nails are the most economical option for them.
4820:
Iron nails are nails made with an iron bar on an anvil with a hammer in the player's inventory , requiring level 19 Smithing , yielding 15 iron nails and granting 25 Smithing experience per bar. Additionally, players can obtain iron nails in sets of ten from the workbench north of the tanner in the Kebos Lowlands . They can also be bought from a few shops, most notably the Sawmill , as well as the Shipyard , which can be teleported to for free by any Shipwright found at major ports.

Iron nails can be used to construct certain types of wooden furniture . With 18 Fletching , they can be used on flighted ogre arrows to create iron brutal arrows, granting 2.6 Fletching experience per arrow. With 56 Crafting , fifteen iron nails can be used with a willow shield and two pieces of snakeskin to craft a snakeskin shield , granting 100 Crafting experience per shield.
4821:
Black nails are nails which, unlike other nails, cannot be made by players. Black nails can be obtained from thieving Ogre coffins or as a drop from zombies in Tarn's Lair . They may also be obtained while clearing rubble during the In Aid of the Myreque quest.

Black nails can be used to construct certain types of wooden furniture . With 38 Fletching , they can be used on flighted ogre arrows to create black brutal arrows, granting 6.5 Fletching experience per arrow.
4822:
Mithril nails are nails made with a mithril bar on an anvil with a hammer in the player's inventory , requiring 54 Smithing , yielding 15 mithril nails and granting 50 Smithing experience per bar.

Mithril nails can be used to construct certain types of wooden furniture . With 56 Construction , five mithril nails can be used along with two oak planks to repair broken bridges in the Hallowed Sepulchre , granting 300 Construction experience; without a hallowed hammer in the player's inventory, there is a chance of failing to repair the bridge and breaking nails in the process. With 49 Fletching , they can be used on flighted ogre arrows to create mithril brutal arrows, granting 7.5 Fletching experience per arrow. With 69 Crafting , fifteen mithril nails can be used with a yew shield and two pieces of blue dragon leather to craft a blue d'hide shield , granting 140 Crafting experience per shield.
4823:
Adamantite nails are nails made with an adamantite bar on an anvil with a hammer in the player's inventory , requiring 74 Smithing , yielding 15 adamantite nails and granting 62.5 Smithing experience per bar.

Adamantite nails can be used to construct certain types of wooden furniture . With 56 Construction , five adamantite nails can be used along with two teak planks to repair broken bridges in the Hallowed Sepulchre , granting 450 Construction experience; without a hallowed hammer in the player's inventory, there is a chance of failing to repair the bridge and breaking nails in the process. With 62 Fletching , they can be used on flighted ogre arrows to create adamant brutal arrows, granting 10.2 Fletching experience per arrow. With 76 Crafting , fifteen adamantite nails can be used with a magic shield and two pieces of red dragon leather to craft a red d'hide shield , granting 156 Crafting experience per shield.
4824:
Rune nails are the second strongest type of nail . They are made by using a runite bar on an anvil with a hammer in the player's inventory , requiring 89 Smithing , yielding 15 rune nails and granting 75 Smithing experience per bar.

Rune nails can be used to construct certain types of wooden furniture . They rarely break but are expensive relative to other types of nails. With 56 Construction , five rune nails can be used along with two mahogany planks to repair broken bridges in the Hallowed Sepulchre , granting 700 Construction experience; without a hallowed hammer in the player's inventory, there is a chance of failing to repair the bridge and breaking nails in the process. With 77 Fletching , they can be used on flighted ogre arrows to create rune brutal arrows, granting 12.5 Fletching experience per arrow. With 83 Crafting , fifteen rune nails can be used with a redwood shield and two pieces of black dragon leather to craft a black d'hide shield , granting 172 Crafting experience per shield.

Rune nails are required for use in Shipbuilding components at the Runite and Ironwood tier.

Three zombies found in Tarn's Lair , near the Odovacar banker, drop rune nails at a 1/25 rate.
4825: An unstrung comp bow is made by using a knife on Achey tree logs with wolf bones in the inventory. Stringing it with a Bow string creates a Comp ogre bow . Level 30 Fletching and partial completion of Zogre Flesh Eaters is required.
4827:
The comp ogre bow was released with the quest Zogre Flesh Eaters and is made by using a knife on an achey tree logs with wolf bones in a player's inventory to create an unstrung comp bow, which can then be strung with a bow string to create the finished bow. This requires 30 Fletching, and grants 45 experience. This is the only composite bow that can be made through the Fletching skill. It can fire any type of brutal arrow, as well as ogre arrows.

When compared to the normal ogre bow, the comp bow has the same attack bonus and a faster attack speed, but a shorter range. It requires 30 Ranged to wield.

In order to equip this bow, players must first speak with Grish after reaching a certain point in the Zogre Flesh Eaters (before the final battle).

Players can select the "Check kills" option on the ogre bow or comp ogre bow to check how many chompy birds they have killed in the Chompy bird hunting activity, to see if they qualify for a Chompy bird hat. After scratching 100,000 notches on a comp ogre bow, there will be no more space to continue tracking chompy kills.
4829:
The Book of 'H.A.M' is used during the Zogre Flesh Eaters quest. It is found in the wardrobe in Sithik Ints' room.

When used on Sithik Ints, he asks if the player has fought for their life against the odd monster or two. In response to the player accusing him of hating monsters and ogres in particular, he challenges the player to back it up with facts.

When used on Zavistic Rarve, it persuades him that Sithik Ints might have had motive to destroy Jiggig. In combination with other evidence, it leads Zavistic to help the player catch Sithik. This means that Sithik Ints is part of the Humans Against Monsters group. When used on Johanhus Ulsbrecht, he reveals that he was the one who wrote the book.
4830:
Fayrg bones are bones available from looting ogre coffins, which will often break lockpicks and decrease players' thieving abilities upon opening using thieving methods.

Fayrg bones give 84 Prayer experience when buried. This can be increased by offering the bones in different ways:

252 XP when casting Sinister Offering.

252 XP when offered at the sacred bone burner after the appropriate faith level has been achieved.

294 XP when offered at a gilded altar with two burners lit.

335 XP when blessed and broken down into blessed bone shards and offered at the libation bowl.

336 XP when offered at the Ectofuntus in the form of fayrg bonemeal.

402 XP when blessed and broken down into blessed bone shards and offered at the libation bowl with jug of blessed sunfire wine. Virilis outside the altar will exchange noted bones for 10 coins each.

588 XP on average when offered at the Chaos Temple in the Wilderness. Each offering gives 294 XP, which is the same as the gilded altars with two burners lit, but with an additional 50% chance to not consume the bones.

If burying the fayrg bones in Jiggig, there's a 1 in 3 chance to give no Prayer experience, and to instead spawn a skogre. The skogre will despawn after 5 minutes. A message in the chatbox appears "The creature rises from the grave... again!".
4832:
Raurg bones are bones available from looting ogre coffins , which will often break lockpicks and decrease players' thieving abilities upon opening using thieving methods.

Raurg bones give 96 Prayer experience when buried. This can be increased by offering the bones in different ways:

If burying the raurg bones in Jiggig , there's a 1 in 3 [ confirmation needed ] chance to give no Prayer experience, and to instead spawn a skogre . The skogre will despawn after 5 minutes. A message in the chatbox appears "The creature rises from the grave... again!".
4834:
Ourg bones are bones obtained by killing Slash Bash, the boss from Zogre Flesh Eaters, stealing them from ogre coffins via the Thieving skill, or using keys dropped by zogres and skogres on nearby chests. As Slash Bash cannot be respawned after he has been killed once, ourg bones cannot be farmed from the boss.

Ourg bones give 140 Prayer experience when buried. This can be increased by offering the bones in different ways:

420 XP when casting Sinister Offering.

420 XP when offered at the sacred bone burner after the appropriate faith level has been achieved.

490 XP when offered at a gilded altar with two lit burners.

560 XP when offered at the Ectofuntus in the form of ourg bonemeal.

560 XP when blessed and broken down into blessed bone shards and offered at the libation bowl.

672 XP when blessed and broken down into blessed bone shards and offered at the libation bowl with jug of blessed sunfire wine. Virilis outside the altar will exchange noted bones for 10 coins each.

980 XP on average when offered at the Chaos Temple in the Wilderness. Each offering gives 490 XP, which is the same as the gilded altars with two burners lit, but with an additional 50% chance to not consume the bones.

Due to only being able to obtain them once from Slash Bash, and ogre coffins being slow to loot, Ourg bones are relatively rare, and as a result are generally much pricier than bones that provide similar Prayer experience.

Ourg bones provide the second most Prayer experience of all bones in the game, surpassed only by superior dragon bones. Unlike superior dragon bones, they do not have a Prayer level requirement to offer them, and grant almost as much experience.
4836:
The strange potion is a quest item obtained during Zogre Flesh Eaters. After the player convinces Zavistic Rarve that Sithik Ints might be involved in the curse on Jiggig, Zavistic gives the player the strange potion with instructions to find some way to use the potion on Sithik and then question him.

The player must use the potion on the cup of tea in Sithik's room, then leave and return. The player will then find that Sithik has been transformed into an ogre. The potion can not be used on any other object or character.
4837:
The Necromancy book is used during the Zogre Flesh Eaters quest. It is found in the room of Sithik Ints, within the cupboard. Using the torn page on the book reveals that it comes from this book.

When used on Sithik, he initially claims to not be sure why it is in the room, then later claims it is for his research, isn't dangerous unless it falls into the wrong hands, and is pretty safe with him.

Using the book on Irwin Feaselbaum reveals that it was loaned to the Wizards' Guild by the Necromancer Tower. This is further supported when searching the bookcase in the Necromancer's Tower, discovering an empty spot and a note saying that a book was loaned to the Wizards' Guild.
4838:
The Cup of tea is an unobtainable item encountered during Zogre Flesh Eaters. It is found in the room of Sithik Ints in Yanille, but cannot be picked up.

During the quest, the strange potion should be used on the cup of tea to turn Sithik into an ogre, whereupon he reveals the secret to making Relicym's balm and brutal arrows.

When the "take" option is selected, Sithik Ints yells at the player, Hey! What do you think you're doing? Leave my tea alone!. When a telegrab is attempted, he will say Hey! What do you think you're doing? Don't go casting that kind of spell anywhere near my tea! Leave my tea alone you telegrabbing fiend!
4839:
The ogre gate key is obtained from Grish toward the end of the quest Zogre Flesh Eaters to gain entrance to the Ogre's ceremonial chamber in Jiggig .

If lost during the quest, the player can get another key from Grish. This key cannot be placed onto the steel key ring .
4840:
An unfinished rogue's purse potion is an unfinished potion made via the Herblore skill. Players make it by using a rogue's purse on a vial of water , earning no experience .

It is used to make the Relicym's balm at level 8 by adding a snake weed . This requires completion of Zogre Flesh Eaters .
4842:
Relicym's balm is a potion that can cure disease. To do so, multiple doses of relicym's balm must be drunk, with each dose weakening the strength of the disease. However, the potion does not offer any temporary immunity, unlike Sanfew serum.

The potion is made by mixing rogue's purse and snake weed in a vial of water, giving 40 Herblore experience. It requires level 8 Herblore and completion of the Zogre Flesh Eaters quest to the point where Sithik Ints tells the player how to cure the Zogre disease.

Players may purchase 3 dose potions from Uglug Nar for 200 coins once they've learned how to make the potion. To open Uglug Nar's store, simply give him a Relicym's balm potion of any dosage, for which he will pay 100 (1 dose), 300 (2 doses), 650 (3 doses) or 1000 (4 doses) gold. Note that Uglug will buy these potions from players for 120 gold as well if he has none in stock, but it must be a 3 dose potion for him to make an offer.

After Barbarian Herblore Training, roe or caviar can be added to a 2 dose relicym's balm, requiring 9 Herblore, yielding a Relicym's mix and 14 Herblore experience.

Relicym's balm is the preferred weapon to use against yellow broodoo victims during the Tai Bwo Wannai Cleanup minigame, as it can deal over 25 damage to them. Relicym's balm can also be used as a cheaper alternative to Sanfew serums to reduce the damage caused by parasites when fighting The Nightmare.

Six Relicym's balm are needed to construct an innoculation station on a ship, which provides immunity to fetid waters when sailing the seas.

Ogre coffin keys are items which open the locked coffins in the Jiggig cave, which first becomes available during the quest Zogre Flesh Eaters . The keys are dropped by zogres and skogres , who always drop one key upon death.

4856:
Ahrim's hood is magic armour worn in the headwear slot that is part of Ahrim the Blighted's set of barrows equipment . To wear Ahrim's hood, a player must have 70 Defence and 70 Magic .

Players may opt to use a farseer helm instead of Ahrim's hood, unless the set effect or damage bonus is desired. Compared to the farseer helm, Ahrim's hood has higher level requirements to wear but no quest requirements, and provides +1% Magic damage bonus. However, the hood provides an identical magic attack bonus and incurs repair costs.

Being part of Ahrim's barrows set, if Ahrim's hood is worn along with all of the other pieces of equipment in Ahrim's barrows set the player's successful magic attacks have a chance of temporarily lowering the opponent's Strength level. This is cumulative with other effects that lower strength, namely the spell Enfeeble .

Additionally, wearing Ahrim's set with an amulet of the damned will allow players to autocast Ancient Magicks , and also grant players a 25% chance of dealing a hit with 30% increased damage.

4934:
Karil's crossbow is a two-handed ranged weapon that is part of Karil the Tainted's set . It requires 70 Ranged to wield. It fires bolt racks , which break upon firing. When equipped with the other three pieces of Karil the Tainted 's set the wearer will receive the set effect, which has a chance to temporarily lower their target's Agility level. Additionally, if an amulet of the damned is worn alongside the set, there is also a 25% chance for each attack to deal a second hit for half the damage of the first.

Unlike standard crossbows, it is wielded in both hands. Furthermore, regular crossbows fire fewer, more powerful shots, meaning Karil's crossbow is actually similar in function to a shortbow ; this gives it a potentially higher damage per second, at the expense of the shield slot. The crossbow has an attack range of 8. Longrange increases attack range by 2.

This weapon is comparable to a magic shortbow and its imbued counterpart . While Karil's offers a longer range, a +15 or +9 greater ranged attack bonus respectively, and a passive chance to hit twice when using the full Karil set and amulet of the damned, the magic shortbow variants offer identical strength when using amethyst arrows , which are not guaranteed to be consumed with each shot. In addition, the magic shortbows do not degrade. Players on a budget or fighting monsters with low ranged defence may find the magic shortbow to be the preferable option.

4952:
Torag's helm is melee armour worn in the headwear slot that is part of Torag the Corrupted's set of Barrows equipment. To wear Torag's helmet, a player must have 70 Defence.

Being part of Torag's barrows set, if Torag's helmet is worn along with all of the other pieces of equipment in Torag's barrows set the player gains a set effect. Damaging melee attacks have a chance of lowering the victim's run energy by 20%.

Torag's helmet is not commonly used due to its lack of Strength or Prayer bonuses. Furthermore, the set effect is considered mediocre. As a result, it is inexpensive compared to the other barrows helmets. However, it is often used in PKing, especially by ranged tanks, as there are few other inexpensive helm options for rangers and the negative ranged attack bonus is small.

For more details on the mechanics and strategies for this equipment, see the set page.

4958:
Torag's hammers are a two-handed blunt weapon that is part of Torag the Corrupted's set of barrows equipment. To wield Torag's hammers, a player must have 70 Attack and Strength.

Being part of Torag's barrows set, if Torag's hammers are wielded along with all of the other pieces of equipment in Torag's barrows set the player gains a special effect: damaging melee attacks have a chance of lowering the victim's run energy by 20%.

Torag's hammers have lower popularity and value compared to other Barrows weapons, as the hammers have a lower strength bonus and Torag's special effect is not as useful in combat. However, they have a high crush bonus and can be one of the more likely out of the melee Barrows weapons to hit as most armours have less crush defensive bonus than slash.

Like the glacial temotli, sulphur blades, and Earthbound tecpatl, the hammers perform two independently rolled hits per attack. The maximum damage of each hit is determined by calculating the combined max hit as normal and dividing it by two. If the combined max hit is odd, one max hit is rounded up while the other is rounded down (e.g., 45 → 22 + 23). This unique effect is useful when fighting NPCs with negative flat armour, such as the Blue Moon, as the flat damage increase gets applied to each hitsplat separately.

Being part of Torag's barrows set, if Torag's platelegs is worn along with all of the other pieces of equipment in Torag's barrows set the player receives a special attack. Damaging melee attacks have a chance of lowering the target's run energy by 20%.

For more details on the mechanics and strategies for this equipment, see the set page.

4976:
Verac's helm is melee armour worn in the headwear slot that is part of Verac the Defiled's set of Barrows equipment. To wear Verac's helmet, a player must have 70 Defence.

Verac's helm has a lesser magic penalty compared to other helmets at +0 magic defence but slightly less ranged defence bonuses compared to Guthan's or Torag's helm, which are equal bonuses. This helmet is often used in 'tank' combat due to the high defensive bonuses as well as a prayer bonus. This helmet is commonly used during the TzHaar Fight Cave minigame because of its good melee and ranged defence and prayer bonus.

If Verac's helm is worn along with all of the other pieces of equipment in Verac's set, the player receives the Defiler set effect. With this set effect active, player attacks have a chance (averaging 1/4) of hitting through an opponent's defence and prayer entirely. This effect can be devastating towards tank opponents who rely on high defence. With this set effect, Verac's flail can be considered one of the best weapons for certain PvM situations.

Verac's brassard is melee armour worn in the body slot that is part of Verac's equipment. To wear Verac's brassard, a player must have 70 Defence.

Verac's brassard offers significantly less melee and ranged protection than Guthan, Torag and Dharok's platebodies (which all have equal stats), however it is better than the Rune platebody, with the exception of having -1 stab defence bonus. Because of this, Verac's brassard is rarely seen being used outside of the full set. However, Verac's brassard does not penalise ranged and magic attack bonuses nearly as much as regular melee armour.

If Verac's brassard is worn along with all of the other pieces of equipment in Verac's set, the player receives the Defiler set effect. With this set effect active, player attacks have a chance (averaging 1/4) of hitting through an opponent's defence and prayer entirely. This effect can be devastating towards tank opponents who rely on high defence.

For more details on the mechanics and strategies for this equipment, see the set page.

5000:
Spells are a series of unobtainable items that exist in the game cache. Presumably, they are used in the Spellbook interface. While originally a Spell item existed for every magic spell, since 2014 this has not been necessary.

In an update in 2018 which reworked the Spellbook, the original scroll appearance of the items was removed.
5001:
Raw cave eels are fish that require a Fishing level of 38 to be caught and grants 80 fishing experience per catch, as well as a Cooking level of 38 to be cooked; doing so turns it into a cave eel . They can be used with Giant frog legs on the life altar in Creature Creation to make a frogeel .

They can be caught with a Fishing rod and bait in the Lumbridge Swamp Caves , the Dorgesh-Kaan South Dungeon , and the Ruins of Camdozaal .

Cave eels or slimy eels are the primary ingredients in the popular Dorgeshuun dish eel sushi . The eel is presumably served raw and wrapped in swamp weed . However, the dish cannot be made by the player. It is also a possible item needed to obtain the magic secateurs in Fairytale I - Growing Pains .

It is recommended to bring extra fishing bait when catching these in case raw slimy eel is caught instead.
5002:
Burnt cave eel is the result of accidentally burning a raw cave eel while attempting to make a cave eel . The burn rate while cooking these will decrease as players reach higher Cooking levels, stopping entirely at level 74.

The burnt cave eel has no use whatsoever. Like most other burnt food, it is tradeable to other players but not on the Grand Exchange .
5003: Cave eel is a type of fish that restores 8 to 12 Hitpoints when eaten. It can be obtained by cooking raw cave eel on a fire or cooking range, requiring level 38 Cooking and granting 115 experience when successful. When cooking there is a chance to fail, resulting in a burnt cave eel. The burn rate decreases as the player's Cooking level increases, and it will stop burning entirely at Cooking level 74.
5004:
Frog spawn is a type of food that restores 3 to 6 Hitpoints when eaten. Frog spawn can be obtained by using a small fishing net in the Lumbridge Swamp Caves, Dorgesh-Kaan South Dungeon, and in the Ruins of Camdozaal, requiring level 33 Fishing and granting 75 experience. They can also be obtained by catching a gourmet impling or looting a gourmet impling jar.

On consumption the message You eat the frogspawn. Yuck. will appear.

Frog spawn may also be used to feed a player's pet cat.
5008:
The brooch is an item that is obtained during The Lost Tribe quest . Players can find it at the first fork of the Lumbridge Castle cellar caves, heading towards the Dorgeshuun Mines . This item does not have a respawn time - it immediately appears on the ground right after it is taken.

Players must bring the brooch to Duke Horacio . After looking through the Goblin symbol book , the player finds that the brooch belongs to the lost Dorgeshuun goblin tribe, as it bears the symbol of the tribe.

After the quest, the brooch can be given to Mistag in exchange for a mining helmet . The brooch is otherwise useless.
5009:
The Goblin symbol book, or A History of the Goblin Race, is a quest item in The Lost Tribe quest. The player shows Reldo a brooch, which prompts him to tell the player to search for the book on the northern bookcase on the west wall in the Varrock Palace Library. It details the names of twelve ancient goblin tribes and provides the translations of their names from the ancient goblin language, and has symbols in it that help the players following the carved symbols and navigate the maze of tunnels leading to the Dorgesh-Kaan mine.

After completing the quest, it is re-obtainable from the palace library or any bookcase in a player-owned house.
5010:
Key is an item used during The Lost Tribe. It is obtained by pickpocketing Sigmund. It can be used to open the chest in the room next to Duke Horacio's room, and disappears once the chest is unlocked. The chest is Sigmund's and contains H.A.M clothing, revealing that he is a Humans Against Monsters member. If you search the chest after receiving the clothing, you also get a 1-dose Antipoison.

Attempting to pickpocket Sigmund again after receiving the key gives the message You have already stolen Sigmund's key.
5011:
Silverware is an item that a player must find during The Lost Tribe quest . The silverware can be found in a crate inside the H.A.M. Dungeon , north-west of Lumbridge Castle .

The silverware was stolen by Sigmund , Duke Horacio 's trusted adviser, in order to start a war with the Dorgeshuun who live in tunnels under the castle.
5012:
The peace treaty is an item used as part of The Lost Tribe . Players obtain it from Duke Horacio .

Players cannot read the treaty themselves, and must simply deliver it to Mistag in the Dorgeshuun Mines .
5013:
A mining helmet is an item primarily dropped by Cave goblin miners. It is dropped unlit, but can be lit by players who have a Firemaking level of 65. It can also be obtained by showing the brooch to Mistag after completing The Lost Tribe quest, or purchased from Miltog's Lamps in the Dorgesh-Kaan market place. It has the same stats as an iron med helm.

This is one of six light sources that can be equipped; the others being the Kandarin headgear, the Firemaking cape, the max cape, the Abyssal Lantern, and the Bruma torch.

A lit mining helmet does not go out on its own, so you don't need a tinderbox when visiting a dark place if you have this helmet. You can extinguish it if you want it unlit. It can however, be 'Magically extinguished' when in combat with Scabarites.

Lighting this helmet in the Lumbridge Castle cellar is a hard requirement for the Lumbridge & Draynor Diary. One can be obtained by giving a brooch (found at the cellar side of the goblin maze) to Mistag.

You are able to boost in order to light the helmet. It does not need to be worn for its light source effect to function.

5016:
The bone spear can be purchased from Nardok in the Dorgesh-Kaan mine weapons shop . This weapon cannot be poisoned .

The bone spear has slightly lower attack bonuses than a steel spear aside from its strength bonus which is slightly higher. It also has a slower attack speed of six ticks , rather than the four-tick speed used by most spears.

Despite the stat bonuses, the bone spear is also the only one-handed spear , so it can be worn with a shield for higher defence bonuses, or a defender to advance the wearer's attack/defence bonuses.
5018: The bone club can be purchased from Nardok's Bone Weapons store, run by Nardok in the Dorgeshuun Mines after completing The Lost Tribe quest . It may also be obtained as a drop from either a cave goblin or cave goblin guard . Its power is between that of an iron warhammer and a steel warhammer .
5020: A minecart ticket is an item that allows players to ride the Mine carts to and from Keldagrim. The carts can travel to the Dwarven Mine (listed as Ice Mountain) and the tunnels under White Wolf Mountain, after the Fishing Contest quest is completed. It is also possible to use the carts for travel between the Grand Exchange and Keldagrim, although this service is free and doesn't require a ticket.

Despite being designed for dwarves , players are able to wear it.
5054:
The dwarf is an unobtainable item depicting a statue of King Alvis. It is only seen on the reward scroll of The Giant Dwarf quest, and cannot actually be obtained by players.

Prior to the removal of the trading post, players were able to search for this item.
5056:
The dwarven battleaxe is a quest item from The Giant Dwarf . It can be obtained by talking to Santiri , a dwarf who lives in Keldagrim near the bank . Initially in a poor state of repair, the player first must use three sapphires to repair the hilt, and then take it to Thurgo south of Port Sarim to have it sharpened.

Once fully repaired, the battleaxe can be delivered to Riki the sculptor's model as part of the attire required to complete the new Giant Dwarf statue.

The player may not equip the battleaxe despite a "wield" option. If they attempt to do so before repair, their character says "I should be very careful with this battleaxe, it's almost a museum piece! I don't want to damage it by wielding it." Once restored, they instead say "I went through all this trouble to restore this axe, I'm not going to ruin it now by wielding it and accidentally smashing it to pieces. I'd better take it to the sculptor."

5060: The Dwarven battleaxe is an animation item used during The Giant Dwarf . It is temporarily wielded by the player during the animation where they attach sapphires to the dwarven battleaxe . There are two different versions, depending upon whether the battleaxe has been sharpened by Thurgo first. Aside from this, it cannot be obtained.
5061: The Dwarven battleaxe is an animation item used during The Giant Dwarf . It is temporarily wielded by the player during the animation where they attach sapphires to the dwarven battleaxe . There are two different versions, depending upon whether the battleaxe has been sharpened by Thurgo first. Aside from this, it cannot be obtained.
5062:
The left boot is a quest item in the The Giant Dwarf quest. Players steal the boot from Dromund by taking it from the table near the door while Dromund isn't looking. The matching right boot is obtained by using Telekinetic Grab through the north window.

After obtaining both boots, they automatically turn into exquisite boots and can then be delivered to Riki the sculptor's model.

Attempting to equip the left boot yields the message: "What, wear just one boot? Besides, the boot is too precious for that."

Upon completing the quest's section (including after the quest), if the player attempts to grab the boot physically or by Telekinetic Grab, the game will yield the message, "You don't need this boot".
5063:
The right boot is a quest item used during the Giant Dwarf quest. A player can steal the boot from Dromund by walking next to his north-western window and Telegrabbing it when Dromund isn't looking. The matching Left boot can be obtained by taking it from the table near the door when Dromund isn't looking.

Once the player has received both boots, they automatically turn into Exquisite boots and can be delivered to Riki the sculptor's model.

Should the player attempt to equip just the right boot, a message appears saying "What, wear just one boot? Besides, the boot is too precious for that." Attempting to equip both provokes "I shouldn't wear these boots, I don't want anything to happen to them before I bring them to the sculptor."

Upon completing the quest's section (including after the quest), if the player attempts to grab the boot physically or by Telekinetic Grab, the game will yield the message, "You don't need this boot".
5064:
Exquisite boots are a quest item used during The Giant Dwarf quest. They must be stolen from Dromund , a Dwarf who lives on the west side of Keldagrim . The left boot can be stolen by taking it when Dromund isn't looking, and the right boot must be stolen by using Telekinetic Grab through the window of his house.

Once the player has obtained the boots they must be taken to Blasidar the Sculptor along with the repaired Dwarven battleaxe and the exquisite clothes so that he can dress his model for the new Giant Dwarf statue.
5065: The Book on costumes , or Scholars Guide to Dwarven Costumes , is a quest item found during The Giant Dwarf quest . It cannot be read. In order to get the book you have to talk to the librarian in Keldagrim during the quest and then search a nearby bookcase. The book is given to Vermundi to make the Exquisite clothes for Riki the sculptor's model .
5066: Meeting notes are the minutes of the meeting at the end of The Giant Dwarf quest. They can substitute for watching the full cutscene but you get them regardless. Should the notes be lost, they can be reclaimed from the director of the company the player chose during the quest. If the game is unable to determine which company the player joined, the player's chosen company in the meeting notes will be "the Black Bug"
5067:
The exquisite clothes are a quest item used during The Giant Dwarf quest. Vermundi will make them for 200 coins once the player helps her repair her steam-powered sewing machine with coal , logs , and a tinderbox .

Along with the repaired Dwarven battleaxe and the Exquisite boots , they serve as clothing for the model of the new Giant Dwarf statue.

Once the player has obtained the clothes, they can be delivered to Riki the sculptor's model .

If the player attempts to wear them, they receive the message: "These clothes are too small for me, I might ruin them if I put them on. I'd better take them to the sculptor instead."

If they are lost, they can be obtained from Vermundi for 200 coins.
5068:
The Master farmer is an interface item that can be seen in the Thieving skill guide, representing Master Farmers .

Skill guides are in fact inventories containing a series of items. In order to represent NPCs or scenery in a skill guide, examinable items had to be created for each.

The actual item cannot be obtained by players.
5070:
A bird nest with an egg can be found while woodcutting most types of trees and several other activities. Bird nests contain one of a red, blue, or green bird's egg , and also provide an empty nest . The chance of getting a bird nest from a tree is 1/256 each time you would normally get a log, regardless of the type of tree. If a nest appears while a player is cutting a tree, a chirping sound will usually be heard, and the player will get a message in the chat box stating, " A bird's nest falls out of the tree. " The nest is dropped on the ground and will despawn after 2 minutes if not picked up. Redwood trees do not drop egg nests, and instead only drop clue nests .

Birds' eggs can be offered to the shrine in the Woodcutting Guild to receive 100 Prayer experience and a seed nest , or instead, rarely, a piece of the evil chicken outfit .

When woodcutting , a roll is done to determine the type of nest the player will receive. The table contains 100 slots: 3/100 egg nest (one for each colour), 32/100 ring nest , 65/100 seed nest . When wearing a strung rabbit foot , five seed slots are removed, making the chances 3/95 for bird's egg, 32/95 for a ring, and 60/95 for seeds. [ 1 ] The twitcher's gloves has similar effects to the strung rabbit foot and can increase the chance of receiving a type of nest (clue, egg, or seed) by 20%. [ 2 ]

During bird house trapping , up to 10 nest rolls are performed with a chance of getting a bird nest. For successful rolls, the chance is 3/100 for an egg nest. Wearing a strung rabbit foot removes 5 empty nest slots, making the chance for an egg nest 3/95.

Egg nests are also rewarded from Managing Miscellania when subjects are tasked with collecting maple, teak or mahogany logs.

5073:
The discontinued bird nest with seeds is an old variant of the seed nest that was obtainable before the release of the Farming Guild . All nests previously obtained remained in banks and inventories, and all new nests obtained can now reward dragonfruit , celastrus , and redwood tree seeds . This change was made to prevent players from obtaining large quantities of the new seeds immediately upon release of the content.

This variant of bird nest can be seen in Cyrisus's bank during Dream Mentor , but it can't be removed from the bank interface.
5074:
A bird nest with a ring can be found while woodcutting most types of trees , as well as several other activities. Bird nests contain a random gold , sapphire , emerald , ruby , or diamond ring , and also provide an empty nest . The chance of getting a bird nest from a tree is 1/256 each time you would normally get a log, regardless of the type of tree. If a nest appears while a player is cutting a tree, a chirping sound will usually be heard, and the player will get a message in the chat box stating, " A bird's nest falls out of the tree. " The nest is dropped on the ground and will despawn after 2 minutes if not picked up. Redwood trees do not drop ring nests, and instead only drop clue nests .

When woodcutting , a roll is done to determine the type of nest the player will receive. The table contains 100 slots: 3/100 egg nest (one for each colour), 32/100 ring nest, 65/100 seed nest . When wearing a strung rabbit foot , five seed slots are removed, making the chances 3/95 for bird's egg, 32/95 for ring and 60/95 for seeds. [ 1 ]

During bird house trapping , up to 10 nest rolls are performed with a chance of getting a ring nest. For successful rolls, the chance is 32/100 for a ring nest. Wearing a strung rabbit foot removes 5 empty nest slots, making the chance for a ring nest 32/95.

Wyson will sometimes reward ring nests in exchange for mole skins and mole claws , which will be packed in a nest box if there isn't enough room in the inventory to hold all the nests.

Ring nests are also rewarded from Managing Miscellania when subjects are tasked with collecting maple, teak or mahogany logs.
5075:
An empty bird nest is the result of emptying a bird nest with seeds, rings, or eggs. Empty nests can be crushed with a pestle and mortar to get a crushed nest , which is used in Herblore to create Saradomin brews . Bird nests are only tradeable when empty or crushed. Wesley in Nardah will crush both noted and un-noted bird nests for a fee of 50 coins each.

Some activities can directly award empty nests. In bird house trapping , up to 10 nest rolls are performed with a chance of getting an empty nest. For successful rolls, the chance is 65/100 for an empty nest. Wearing a strung rabbit foot removes 5 empty nest slots, making the chance 60/95, and improving the chance of getting ring or egg nests instead.

Wyson occasionally rewards empty nests when trading in mole claws and mole skins . If the player's inventory is too full to hold the nests, he may instead reward a nest box containing empty nests.
5076:
A bird's egg can be obtained from egg bird nests which come from various sources, such as falling out of a tree while Woodcutting or as loot from Bird house trapping . They can come in three different colours: green, blue, and red which represent the colours of Guthix , Saradomin , and Zamorak , respectively.

These eggs can be offered to the shrine in the Woodcutting Guild to receive 100 Prayer experience and a bird nest with seeds or a piece of the evil chicken outfit as a reward. Each piece of the evil chicken outfit has a 1/1200 chance of being awarded, resulting in approximately a 1/300 chance of receiving any outfit piece. [ 1 ] Any outfit piece will replace a nest, so a full inventory will not compromise receiving the outfit piece.

Considering the value of the nest with seeds from the shrine, the value of all pieces of the evil chicken outfit, and the chance of obtaining one of these pieces, the average value of one egg is 7,352.00 .

The chances of getting a bird nest from a tree is 1/256 each time a player would normally get a log (except the blisterwood tree and redwood tree , which do not drop bird nests other than clue nests). When a player receives a nest, the chance of the nest containing a bird's egg is 3/100 (each colour egg being 1/100). When wearing a strung rabbit foot the chances are increased slightly to 3/95 [ 2 ] by decreasing the chance of getting seeds.
