5086:
The Smithing is an interface item that can be seen in the Smithing skill guide representing the Smithing .

The actual item cannot be obtained by players.
5091:
The Black chinchompa is an interface item that can be seen in the Hunter skill guide representing the Black chinchompa

The actual item cannot be obtained by players.
5096:
Marigold seeds can be planted in a flower patch at level 2 Farming to yield marigolds , which are used to make imp repellent or as payment to protect hammerstone hops (x1). When fully grown, it protects potato , onion , and tomato plants from disease .

A nearby gardener will not watch over growing marigolds . It is recommended to use compost when planting them.

These seeds can be stolen from master farmers and seed stalls . They are purchasable from the Draynor Seed Market or Amelia's Seed Shop in the Farming Guild .
5097:
Rosemary seeds can be planted in a flower patch at level 11 Farming to yield rosemary. When fully grown, it protects cabbages from disease.

A nearby gardener will not watch over a growing rosemary plant. It is recommended to use compost when planting them.

These seeds can be stolen from master farmers and seed stalls. They are purchasable from the Draynor Seed Market or Amelia's Seed Shop in the Farming Guild.
5098:
Nasturtium seeds can be planted in a flower patch at level 24 Farming to yield nasturtiums , which are used as payment to protect wildblood hops (x1). When fully grown, it protects watermelons from disease .

A nearby gardener will not watch over growing nasturtiums . It is recommended to use compost when planting them.

These seeds can be stolen from master farmers and seed stalls or obtained from seed packs .
5099:
Woad seeds can be planted in a flower patch at level 25 Farming to yield woad leaves , which are used to make blue dye and, by extension, green and purple dye .

A nearby gardener will not watch over a growing woad plant . It is recommended to use compost when planting them.

These seeds can be stolen from master farmers or obtained from seed packs .
5100:
Limpwurt seeds can be planted in a flower patch at level 26 Farming to yield limpwurt roots , which are used as a Herblore secondary ingredient and protection payment for teak trees (x15).

A nearby gardener will not watch over a growing limpwurt plant . It is recommended to use compost when planting them; however, this does not increase yield.

Limpwurt seeds are dropped by many monsters . They can also be stolen from master farmers , obtained from seed packs or as a reward from rummaging Vale offerings .
5101:
Redberry seeds can be planted in a bush patch at level 10 Farming to yield redberries , which are used in Cooking to make redberry pies or to create dyes .

A nearby gardener will watch over a growing redberry bush for 4 sacks of cabbages .

These seeds can be stolen from master farmers or obtained from seed packs .
5102:
Cadavaberry seeds can be planted in a bush patch at level 22 Farming to yield cadava berries , which are used as payment to protect cactus (x6).

A nearby gardener will watch over a growing cadavaberry bush for 3 baskets of tomatoes .

These seeds can be stolen from master farmers or obtained from seed packs .
5103:
Dwellberry seeds can be planted in a bush patch at level 36 Farming to yield dwellberries , which are used in quests and gnome cooking .

A nearby gardener will watch over a growing dwellberry bush for 3 baskets of strawberries .

These seeds can be stolen from master farmers or obtained from seed packs .
5104:
Jangerberry seeds can be planted in a bush patch at level 48 Farming to yield jangerberries , which are used in Herblore to make Zamorak brews or as protection payment for snape grass (x5).

A nearby gardener will watch over a growing jangerberry bush for 6 watermelons .

Jangerberry seeds are dropped by many monsters . They can also be stolen from master farmers or obtained from seed packs .
5105:
Whiteberry seeds can be planted in a bush patch at level 59 Farming to yield white berries, which are used in Herblore to make defence potions and super defences.

A nearby gardener will watch over a growing whiteberry bush for 8 bittercap mushrooms.

These seeds can be stolen from master farmers or obtained from seed packs.
5106:
Poison ivy seeds can be planted in a bush patch at level 70 Farming to yield poison ivy berries, which are used in Herblore to make weapon poison(++) or as protection payment for calquat trees (x8).

There is no need to pay a gardener to watch over a growing poison ivy bush because "it is pretty hardy stuff, and most animals will avoid eating it." For this reason, they will never become diseased, and there is no benefit to adding compost to the soil.

Poison ivy seeds are dropped by many monsters. They can also be stolen from master farmers or obtained from seed packs.

Harvesting poison ivy berries from the patch near the Ardougne Monastery is a task in the hard Ardougne Diary.
5166:
The Potato seed is an interface item that can be seen in the Farming skill guide representing the Potato seed

The actual item cannot be obtained by players.
5171:
The Seeds is an interface item that can be seen in the Thieving skill guide representing seed stalls .

The actual item cannot be obtained by players.
5280:
Cactus seeds can be planted in a cactus patch found in Al Kharid and the Farming Guild. They require level 55 Farming to plant and after 9 hours and 20 minutes of growth time will produce a cactus. Players can harvest cactus spines from the mature plant, which often fetch a high price due to their uses in Farming and Herblore.

Ayesha in Al Kharid or Alan in the Farming Guild will look after your growing cactus plant in exchange for 6 cadava berries.

Cactus seeds are dropped by aberrant spectres, dagannoth, ice giants, moss giants, ogres, cave horrors and other monsters. They can also be obtained by pickpocketing a Master Farmer.
5281:
Belladonna seeds can be planted in the belladonna patches in Draynor Manor and Auburnvale at level 63 Farming to yield nightshade , which is used in Herblore to make weapon poison(++) or as an addition to dynamite for poison dynamite .

There is no nearby gardener to watch over growing belladonna . It is recommended to use compost when planting them.

Belladonna seeds are dropped by many monsters . They can also be stolen from master farmers or obtained from seed packs .

Harvesting nightshade is a task in the hard Lumbridge and Draynor Diary .
5282:
Mushroom spores can be planted at the mushroom patch at level 53 Farming to yield six bittercap mushrooms . The only mushroom patch in game can be found west of Canifis ( Fairy ring C K S ). Successfully harvesting these mushrooms is a task in the hard tier of the Morytania diary .

This patch does not have a nearby gardener and therefore cannot be protected from disease. Having an attas plant growing in the anima patch makes it possible to harvest more than six mushrooms per spore.

Mushroom spores can be obtained by pickpocketing from Master Farmers (requiring level 38 Thieving ), from seed packs , or as a drop from various monsters.
5283:
An apple tree seed grows into an Apple tree which produces cooking apples . Players with a Farming level of 27 can grow Apple trees in a fruit tree patch . An Apple tree will take 16 hours to grow completely.

You can pay a farmer 9 raw sweetcorn (may be noted) to take care of it. They can also be found in bird nests.
5284:
Banana tree seeds may be grown into a banana tree which gives 6 bananas per harvest. They can be occasionally obtained from bird nests . Level 33 Farming is required to plant it; before planting into the fruit tree patch , the seed must first be planted into a plant pot and watered.

A nearby gardener will watch over your growing banana tree at the cost of 4 baskets of apples .

Banana tree seeds are not as popular as other tree seeds, due to the low value of their harvest, and the high cost of their gardener's payment.
5285:
Orange tree seeds may be grown into a orange tree which gives oranges. You must have level 39 Farming to plant it. To plant it, you will need to put it into a plant pot and water with a watering can to turn it into a orange sapling. Then you can put it into a fruit tree patch with a gardening trowel.

A nearby gardener will watch over your growing orange tree at the cost of 3 baskets of Strawberries.
5286:
Curry tree seeds may be grown into a curry tree which gives curry leaves . Curry tree seeds are obtained from bird nests or by trading. Players must have level 42 Farming to plant this seed. It takes 5 minutes for the potted curry tree seed to mature into a sapling and 960 minutes (16 hours) for the planted sapling to become a full curry tree.

A nearby gardener will watch over your growing curry tree at the cost of a payment of 5 baskets of bananas .
5287:
Pineapple seeds may be grown into a pineapple plant which gives pineapples . Level 51 Farming is required to plant it.

A nearby gardener will watch over your growing pineapple plant at the cost of 10 watermelons either noted or unnoted.

To plant it, you must use it with a plant pot filled with dirt while having a gardening trowel in your inventory , then water it with a watering can to get a pineapple seedling . Then wait for approximately 5 minutes for it to become a pineapple sapling . Transfer the sapling to the patch. It takes 960 minutes (roughly 16 hours) to finish growing. A standard 6 pineapples grow from the plant. You can visually see each of the 6 pineapples being taken from the stalk as it is harvested.

They can be obtained by looting Magpie implings or bird nests .
5288:
Papaya tree seeds may be grown into a papaya tree by planting the seed in a filled plant pot , watering it and then planting the sapling into a fruit tree patch . The tree will give 6 papayas at a full harvest, and the papayas will regrow over time. Players must have level 57 Farming to plant it.. The tree takes a minimum of 960 minutes (roughly 16 hours) to finish growing. Seeds may be obtained as drops from various monsters as well as from bird nests .

A nearby gardener will watch over your growing papaya tree at the cost of 10 pineapples , which can be in either item or noted form.
5289:
Palm tree seeds can be planted in a plant pot to make a palm seedling , which grows into a palm sapling ; the sapling can be planted in a fruit tree patch to be grown into a palm tree . Players require at least 68 Farming to plant it. Palm trees, when fully grown, bear coconuts .

A nearby gardener will watch over your growing palm tree at the cost of 15 papaya fruits .

Palm trees, like all fruit trees, ideally take six 160-minute farming cycles to fully grow, but certain factors can delay this. Palm trees are usually fully grown within 24 hours, however.

Palm tree seeds may be found rarely in a bird nest , which can be obtained randomly while Woodcutting , Bird house trapping or from Managing Miscellania . Another way to obtain palm tree seeds is via Barbarian Assault High Level Gambles.

The Ardougne Hard Diary , Western Provinces Hard Diary , and Karamja Elite diary each require checking the health of a successfully grown Palm Tree.
5290:
A calquat tree seed can be planted in a filled plant pot at level 72 Farming . After watering the calquat seedling it will grow into a calquat sapling , which may then be planted in the calquat patches in Tai Bwo Wannai , the Summer Shore in the Great Conch , and Kastori to grow into a calquat tree . When fully grown, calquat fruits may be harvested.

Once grown, players can harvest a maximum of 6 calquat fruits at a time. If the player does not dig up the tree, more fruits will grow eventually.

A fully grown calquat tree will give a total of 12,516.5 experience, with 129.5 experience for planting, 12,096 experience for checking and 291 experience for harvesting 6 fruit.

The nearby gardener, Imiago , Tziuhtla or Guppa , will watch over your growing calquat tree at the cost of a payment of 8 poison ivy berries . No quest is required to use the calquat patch or for paying the gardener, although Children of the Sun is needed to reach Kastori and Troubled Tortugans is needed to reach The Great Conch .

The seeds provide a very high amount of experience compared to their cost and growth time, however there are only three calquat patches in the game. A calquat farming patch can be cleared by using a spade on the barren tree.

5306:

5312:
Acorns are seeds used in the Farming skill and acquired from bird nests , mammoths , Brutus , and seed packs or by searching the Reward Cart after subduing the Wintertodt . It requires 15 Farming to grow an acorn into an oak tree.

Using it on a plant pot while a gardening trowel is in the inventory, and watering it with a watering can , does not grant any experience. After several minutes (in the bank or the player's inventory), it will then turn into an oak sapling . It can then be planted in a tree patch and left to grow. A farmer can be paid 1 basket of tomatoes to watch over it and ensure its survival.

An oak tree takes 200 minutes to grow (5 stages of 40 minutes each) and grants 481.3 experience when its health is checked. In order to plant a new one, the tree must be chopped and then dug up, rewarding the player with oak roots . The amount of roots given depends on the player's Farming level ( boosts can be used):

Acorns may be given to the giant squirrel or the squirrels on Fossil Island . It provides no benefit, but grants some special dialogue. If the skilling pet Tangleroot has had its appearance changed, one acorn may be used on it to revert it to its base form.
5313:
Willow seeds may be grown into a willow which gives willow logs . Planting one requires level 30 Farming . It costs 1 basket of apples to protect as payment to the farmer, and takes roughly 240 minutes (4 hours) to finish growing. Willow seeds can be obtained by searching a bird nest , looting nature implings or by doing Wintertodt .

If this tree becomes diseased, using secateurs or magic secateurs on it to prune the diseased leaves will bring it back to a healthy state and will yield leaves .

By using secateurs on a fully grown willow tree, the player can harvest willow branches . These branches start to grow only after the tree's health has been checked, at a rate of 1 every 5 minutes, up to a maximum of 6 grown at a time.

In order to plant a new one, the tree must be chopped and then dug up, rewarding the player with willow roots . The amount of roots given depends on the player's Farming level ( boosts can be used):
5314:
Maple seeds are the third highest level tree seeds. At level 45 Farming, maple seeds may be planted in plant pots with a gardening trowel to become Maple seedling and watered to become maple seedling (w) which grow into maple saplings while sitting in your inventory or bank.

After planting the sapling in a tree patch and waiting for it to fully grow (takes 5 hours and 20 minutes), the plant will grow into a maple tree, which can be cut to yield maple logs (and grant Woodcutting experience). Checking the health of the tree yields 3448 experience.

If this tree becomes diseased, using secateurs or magic secateurs on it to prune the diseased leaves will bring it back to a healthy state and will yield leaves.

When cut down, the tree will automatically regrow after a period of time. Alternatively, it can be dug up using a spade, yielding some maple roots in the process, or by paying the gardener a small fee of 200 coins.

The gardener will look after your maple tree in exchange for 1 basket of oranges.
5315:
Yew seeds are the second highest level tree seeds that can be grown in a standard tree patch, after magic seeds . Players must have level 60 Farming to plant it. Boosts are allowed. Boosts are not needed to prune the tree in case of disease.

A yew seed, when planted in a plant pot , allowed to sprout into a sapling and then planted in a tree patch , may grow into a yew tree . Planting the seed takes a maximum of 6.083 hours (365 minutes) to be fully grown. Checking the health gives 7150.9 experience. If this tree becomes diseased, using secateurs or magic secateurs on it to prune the diseased leaves will bring it back to a healthy state and will yield leaves .

They are obtained from a bird nest that has dropped from a tree, received from a bird house , by exchanging the drops from a Giant Mole under Falador Park , or as a drop from certain boss monsters. It is also possible to obtain this seed from a bird nest from the Managing Miscellania rewards at Miscellania (after Throne of Miscellania ) and Etceteria (after Royal Trouble ).

The farmer will tend a player's yew tree for 10 cactus spines (these can be noted). If the player wants to buy the spines from other players, they should be aware that the Grand Exchange price for 10 cactus spines is currently 16,530 , while a yew tree seed currently costs 20,156 . About 1/8 yew saplings will die. In a test of 257 yew trees with no farmer payments, only 36 have died. This gives a cost per surviving yew tree of 36,686 with protection and 23,439.33 without, with the latter method being about 1/8th slower.

A fully grown yew tree can be cut to yield yew logs and grant Woodcutting experience. After it is cut down, it will eventually regrow, or a spade may be used on the stump to produce yew roots and clear the patch for planting a new tree. The amount of roots given depends on the player's Farming level (boosts can be used):
5316:
Magic seeds are high-level tree seeds. At level 75 Farming, magic seeds may be planted in plant pots with a gardening trowel and watered to become magic saplings.

After about 8 hours it will be a fully grown magic tree, granting 13,913.8 Farming experience when inspected, and can then be cut to yield magic logs (and grant Woodcutting experience). After the tree has been cut down, it will regrow after 2 minutes. Using a spade on the cut tree roots before the tree has regrown yields magic roots and makes the tree patch available for planting a new tree. Alternatively, you can ask the nearby gardener to chop down the tree for 200 coins. This instantly removes the tree whether or not it has been cut down from the patch, making the patch available for a new seed to be planted, but no magic roots are obtained.

The farmer next to the patch will protect a growing magic tree if it becomes diseased, in exchange for 25 coconuts. If buying the magic sapling and coconuts on the Grand Exchange, it will cost around 108,818 per tree, assuming one pays a gardener. If this tree becomes diseased, using secateurs or magic secateurs on it to prune the diseased leaves will bring it back to a healthy state and will yield leaves.

In order to plant a new one, the tree must be chopped and then dug up, rewarding the player with magic roots. The amount of roots given depends on the player's Farming level (boosts can be used):

At level 75, a player obtains one magic root.

At level 83, a player obtains two magic roots.

At level 91, a player obtains three magic roots.

At level 99, a player obtains four magic roots.

Magic seeds may be found rarely in bird nests, which can be obtained randomly while Woodcutting or from Managing Miscellania, as well as doing bird house runs.

Paying Prissy Scilla to protect a magic tree is an elite task in the Western Provinces Diary. Obtaining at least 3 Magic roots at once when digging up your magic tree in Falador is an elite task in the Falador Diary.
5317:
A spirit seed is a rare seed that members can use to grow a spirit tree at level 83 Farming. Players can pay a gardener five monkey nuts, one monkey bar, and one ground tooth to watch over a growing spirit tree.

There are five patches players can grow, one each at Port Sarim, Etceteria, Brimhaven, Hosidius, and the Farming Guild (at level 85 Farming). Players can only have one planted at 83, two at 88, three at 93, and four at 96. Upon reaching 99 Farming, the restriction is removed, and players can plant unlimited spirit trees. Players are not limited to the number of spirit tree saplings they can own, only planted saplings based on the appropriate Farming level. A spirit tree can also be planted in a Player-owned house with level 75 Construction and does not count towards the player's tree limit. There are also eight other spirit trees which players can use, but already exist and do not need to be grown.

Spirit seeds are obtainable from bird nests. This means it is possible for players to indirectly buy them by purchasing mole skin/claws from other players on the Grand Exchange and trading them to Wyson until a spirit seed is found in a nest. They are also a potential reward for completing easy, medium, and hard farming contracts in the Farming Guild or defeating certain monsters.

Garden pies and spicy stews can be used to boost a player's Farming level, up to 3 levels and 5 levels respectively, allowing them to create spirit tree saplings or plant them. Boosting is required when creating the sapling and when planting the tree. It is also possible to use boosts to be able to plant more spirit trees than the player's normal Farming level allows. When boosting, note that planting the seed in the pot and planting the sapling both require 83 farming. They can both be done in one boost if timed correctly. Saplings grow on a global tick which occurs once every 5 minutes. First determine when this tick happens with a different seedling. Also, check with a different boost if the skill reduction tick isn't too close to the sapling tick. If the ticks don't overlap, you can easily grow the seedling and plant the sapling in one boost.

As there are limited spots the player can plant spirit trees, any excess spirit seeds the player has can be traded in at Guildmaster Jane for tier 5 Seed packs which are worth an average of 85,785.89. Tier 5 seed packs have an approximately 1/22 chance of containing another spirit seed which can itself be traded in for an additional pack, meaning the average value of a seed pack when trading in all spirit seeds obtained for additional packs converges to the slightly higher value of 89,870.93.
5318:
Potato seeds are the first seeds a player can plant with the Farming skill. 3 seeds are sown in an allotment patch to grow potato plants , which yield potatoes : a food item used in Cooking . They take 40 minutes to grow.

A nearby gardener will watch over growing potato plants for 2 buckets of compost . Fully grown marigolds or white lilies in a nearby flower patch will also protect the potatoes from disease .

Many medium and low-level monsters drop potato seeds, including guards , farmers , and hill giants . These seeds can be stolen from master farmers and seed stalls . They are purchasable from the Draynor Seed Market or Amelia's Seed Shop in the Farming Guild . There is a small chance to obtain a potato seed while picking potatoes from a field .

Potato seeds are a good choice for bird houses due to them being very cheap and easy to acquire.

1 sack of potatoes is needed to protect growing onions .
5319:
Onion seeds are the second seeds a player can plant with the Farming skill. 3 seeds are sown in an allotment patch to grow onion plants , which yield onions : a food item used in Cooking and to make yellow dye . They take 40 minutes to grow.

A nearby gardener will watch over growing onion plants for 1 sack of potatoes . Fully grown marigolds or white lilies in a nearby flower patch will also protect the onions from disease .

Many medium and low-level monsters drop onion seeds, including guards , farmers , and hill giants . These seeds can be stolen from master farmers and seed stalls . They are purchasable from the Draynor Seed Market or Amelia's Seed Shop in the Farming Guild . There is a small chance to obtain an onion seed while picking onions from a field .

Onion seeds are a good choice for bird houses due to them being very cheap and easy to acquire.

1 sack of onions is needed to protect growing cabbages and Asgarnian hops .
5320:
Sweetcorn seeds can be planted at level 20 Farming . 3 seeds are sown in an allotment patch to grow sweetcorn plants , which yield sweetcorn : an item used in Cooking . They take 1 hour to grow.

A nearby gardener will watch over growing sweetcorn plants for 10 jute fibres . Fully grown white lilies in a nearby flower patch will also protect the sweetcorn from disease . Alternatively, a scarecrow may be placed in a flower patch for the same effect.

Many medium and low-level monsters drop sweetcorn seeds, including guards , farmers , and hill giants . These seeds can be stolen from master farmers and seed stalls . There is a small chance to obtain a sweetcorn seed while picking sweetcorn from a field .

9 sweetcorn is needed to protect growing apple trees .
5321:
Watermelon seeds can be planted at level 47 Farming. 3 seeds are sown in an allotment patch to grow watermelons, which yield the watermelon food item used in Cooking to make summer pies. They take 1 hour and 20 minutes to grow.

A nearby gardener will watch over growing watermelons (excluding Harmony Island) for 10 curry leaves, either noted or unnoted. Fully grown nasturtiums or white lilies in a nearby flower patch will also protect the watermelons from disease.

These seeds can be stolen from master farmers and seed stalls. They may also be obtained from Temple Trekking, the Wintertodt reward cart, high-level gambling at the Barbarian Assault minigame, and Farming Guild seed packs.

Harvesting watermelons from the patch on Harmony Island is a task in the hard Morytania Diary. There is no gardener on the island to watch over the crops.
5322:
Tomato seeds can be planted at level 12 Farming. 3 seeds are sown in an allotment patch to grow tomato plants, which yield tomatoes: a food item used in Cooking. They take 40 minutes to grow.

A nearby gardener will watch over growing tomato plants for 2 sacks of cabbages. Fully grown marigolds or white lilies in a nearby flower patch will also protect the tomatoes from disease.

Many medium and low-level monsters drop tomato seeds, including guards, farmers, and hill giants. These seeds can be stolen from master farmers and seed stalls.

Baskets of tomatoes are needed to protect growing Yanillian hops (x1), cadavaberry bushes (x3), and oak trees (x1).
5323:
Strawberry seeds can be planted at level 31 Farming. 3 seeds are sown in an allotment patch to grow strawberry plants, which yield strawberries: a food item used in Cooking to make summer pies. They take 1 hour to grow.

A nearby gardener will watch over growing strawberry plants for 1 basket of apples. Fully grown white lilies in a nearby flower patch will also protect the strawberries from disease.

Many medium and low-level monsters drop strawberry seeds, including guards, farmers, and hill giants. These seeds can be stolen from master farmers and seed stalls.

Harvesting strawberries from the patch north of East Ardougne is a task in the medium Ardougne Diary.

Baskets of strawberries are needed to protect growing dwellberry bushes (x3) and orange trees (x3).
5324:
Cabbage seeds are the third seeds a player can plant with the Farming skill. 3 seeds are sown in an allotment patch to grow cabbages, which yield the cabbage food item used in Cooking. They take 40 minutes to grow.

A nearby gardener will watch over growing cabbages for 1 sack of onions. Fully grown rosemary or white lilies in a nearby flower patch will also protect the cabbages from disease.

Many medium and low-level monsters drop cabbage seeds, including guards, farmers, and hill giants. These seeds can be stolen from master farmers and seed stalls. They are purchasable from the Draynor Seed Market or Amelia's Seed Shop in the Farming Guild. There is a small chance to obtain a cabbage seed while picking cabbages from a field.

Sacks of cabbages are needed to protect growing tomatoes (x2), Krandorian hops (x3), and redberry bushes (x4).
5325:
A gardening trowel is used in the members only skill Farming . It is used both to fill a plant pot with earth from a weeded patch, and to plant a tree seed into that plant pot to begin the process of growing a tree.

These can be bought from Farming shops , or obtained by trading other players.

Players can withdraw unlimited amounts of gardening trowels from the tool store 5 .

The tool leprechaun can store 100 of these tools for you.
5327:
A spade handle was previously obtained as part of a random event . It formed part of a spade , along with the spade head . A spade would randomly break into these two parts.

The only use for this item was to combine it with the spade head (which was strewn randomly around the surrounding area) to form a whole spade again.

In 2014, the random event was discontinued and all spade handles were automatically repaired.
5328:
A spade head was previously obtained as part of a random event . Previously, a spade might randomly break into two items whilst using it (the other being a spade handle ).

Players kept the handle in their inventory , and would find the head strewn somewhere in the immediate vicinity. The only use for a spade head was to combine it with the spade handle to form a complete spade again.

In 2014, the random event was discontinued and all spade heads were automatically repaired.
5329:
Secateurs are used to prune diseased leaves from trees or bushes grown using the Farming skill. They can be bought at most farming shops, and can be acquired freely from a Tool Store 5. They can also be stored at the tool leprechauns.

Apart from being used to cure plants from disease, they can be used to obtain willow branches from farmed willow trees. Up to 6 willow branches can be cut at a time, after which the branches regrow one at a time at regular intervals of approximately 10 minutes.
5331:
Watering cans are used in the Farming skill to water allotment, flower, and hops patches, as well as to water seedlings to grow saplings. Watering reduces the risk of disease occurring at the end of that growth cycle by varying amounts. During the next growth cycle, the plant moves from being watered back to normal and returns to the standard rate of disease once more, unless it is watered again.

A watering can holds eight doses. It can be refilled at any water supply, by using a bucket of water, bowl of water, or jug of water on it, or by casting Humidify. Vials of water can be used to fill them indirectly, by first using it to fill one of the aforementioned containers. Gricoller's can, an untradeable reward from Tithe Farm, holds 1,000 charges.

Watering cans can be bought from farming shops, obtained as a drop from farmers, or withdrawn from a tool store 5.

Watering cans with water inside can be used to extinguish the flame walls in the Chambers of Xeric.

A watering can holds eight doses. It can be refilled at any water supply, by using a bucket of water, bowl of water, or jug of water on it, or by casting Humidify. Vials of water can be used to fill them indirectly, by first using it to fill one of the aforementioned containers. Gricoller's can, an untradeable reward from Tithe Farm, holds 1,000 charges.

Watering cans can be bought from farming shops, obtained as a drop from farmers, or withdrawn from a tool store 5.

Watering cans with water inside can be used to extinguish the flame walls in the Chambers of Xeric.

5341: Rakes are used in the Farming skill to remove weeds from farming patches . It can be bought from Farming shops . In addition, it can also be purchased from most of the gardeners who look after your farming patches. A tool leprechaun can store one for you.
5343:
A seed dibber is used to plant seeds in Farming patches . Up to 100 can be stored with tool leprechauns near Farming patches. They can be purchased from farming shops or any farmer that protects patches. An unlimited amount can be taken from a tool store 5 .

Completion of the Farming portion of the Barbarian Training miniquest allows players to plant seeds without requiring a seed dibber.

A seed dibber is required for the quests: Grim Tales , Forgettable Tale... , My Arm's Big Adventure , Garden of Tranquillity , A Tail of Two Cats , and While Guthix Sleeps .
5345: Gardening boots are boots that can be obtained as a unique and fairly rare drop from farmers. They are purely cosmetic and do not provide stat bonuses, nor do they provide any bonuses to the Farming skill.
5347:
A rake handle forms part of a rake , along with the rake head . A rake handle can potentially be obtained during My Arm's Big Adventure ; the player must then fix the rake and hand it back to My Arm .

There used to be a random event in which a rake would break into these two parts. The only use for this item is to combine it with the rake head (which will be strewn randomly around the surrounding area) to form a whole rake again.
5348:

There used to be a random event in which a rake would break into these two parts, with the head being thrown on the ground in close proximity to the player. The only use for this item is to combine it with the rake handle to form a whole rake again.
5350:
Plant pots are used in the Farming skill to turn tree seeds into seedlings.

With the appropriate Farming level and a gardening trowel in their inventory, a player can create a seedling by using a tree seed on a filled plant pot. After watering a seedling with a watering can, a few minutes later it will sprout into a sapling and be ready for planting in a tree patch.

An empty plant pot can be filled by using it on any farming patch while carrying a gardening trowel. The patch must be empty and weed-free for this to work.

Filled plant pots are also available from farming shops for the same price as empty plant pots.

Completion of the Farming portion of Barbarian Training allows players to automatically destroy empty plant pots when planting trees.
5352: An unfired plant pot is made by using soft clay on a potter's wheel , requiring 19 Crafting , and yielding 20 Crafting experience . Firing it in a pottery oven produces an empty plant pot , granting 17.5 Crafting experience upon success. Unlike shaping the clay, firing it has no Crafting level requirement. At lower levels, an unfired plant pot can crack in the oven, destroying the plant pot and granting no experience.
5354:
Filled plant pots are used in the Farming skill to turn tree seeds into seedlings.

With the appropriate Farming level and a gardening trowel in their inventory, a player can create a seedling by using a tree seed on a filled plant pot. After watering a seedling with a watering can or Humidify a few minutes later it will sprout into a sapling and be ready for planting in a tree patch.

A plant pot can be filled by using the empty pot on any farming patch, while carrying a gardening trowel. The patch must be empty and weed-free for this to work.

The filled plant pots are also available from farming shops for the same price as empty plant pots.
5356:
The Plant pot is an unobtainable item related to Farming . It features a much lighter colour soil than the regular Filled plant pot .

It is unknown what the item would have been used for, but in RuneScape it was briefly turned into a plant pot containing supercompost .

5370:
Oak saplings are saplings that can be used to grow oak trees at level 15 Farming.

They can be made by planting an acorn in a filled plant pot, with a gardening trowel in your inventory, and then watering the oak seedling with a watering can or by using Humidify. When watered, the seedling will sprout into a sapling in one crop cycle (0-5 minutes).

Planting the sapling in a tree patch, with a spade in your inventory, will give 14 Farming experience. It will grow into an oak tree after 200 minutes (3 hours and 20 minutes), which gives 467.5 Farming experience.

Players can ask the gardener to protect their tree from disease whilst it grows, which requires payment of a basket of five tomatoes. This payment can be noted.

Once the tree has fully grown, it can be cut down like a regular oak tree. The remaining stump can be dug up to gain oak roots.
5371:
Willow saplings are saplings that can be used to grow willow trees at level 30 Farming .

They can be made by planting a willow seed in a filled plant pot , with a gardening trowel in the player's inventory, and then watering the willow seedling with a watering can or by using Humidify . When watered, the seedling will sprout into a sapling in one crop cycle (0-5 minutes), resulting in a profit of 408 coins .

Planting the sapling in a tree patch , with a spade in your inventory, will give 25 Farming experience. It will grow into a willow tree after 240 minutes (4 hours), which gives 1,456.5 Farming experience .

Players can ask the gardener to protect their tree from disease whilst it grows, which requires payment of a basket of five apples . This payment can be noted.

Paying Prissy Scilla to protect a magic tree is an elite task in the Western Provinces Diary. Obtaining at least 3 magic roots at once when digging up your magic tree in Falador is an elite task in the Falador Diary.
5375:
Spirit saplings are saplings that can be used to grow spirit trees starting at level 83 Farming. They can be made by planting a spirit seed in a filled plant pot, with a gardening trowel in your inventory, and then watering the spirit seedling with a watering can or by using the Humidify spell. When watered, the seedling will sprout into a sapling in one crop cycle (0-5 minutes). Unlike other saplings, Tool leprechauns will not note spirit saplings.

Planting the sapling in a spirit tree patch requires a spade in your inventory. It takes 3840 minutes (2 days and 16 hours) for a sapling to grow into a spirit tree. Players can ask the nearby gardener to protect their tree from disease whilst it grows, which requires a payment of 5 monkey nuts, 1 monkey bar, and 1 ground tooth. This payment can be noted.

At level 83 Farming, players can only have one spirit tree planted at a time, not including the one in their player-owned house. They can have two at 88, three at 93, and four at 96. Upon reaching 99 Farming, the restriction is removed, and players can plant unlimited spirit trees. As there are limited spots the player can plant spirit trees, any excess spirit saplings may be traded in at Guildmaster Jane for seed packs (tier 5).

Spirit trees can be planted starting from as low as level 78 Farming by boosting with spicy stews. When boosting, note that planting the seed in the pot and planting the sapling in a patch both require 83 Farming, however both can be done in one boost if timed correctly. Saplings grow on every growth tick, which occurs once every 5 minutes, with some variance as to the exact timing for each player. First, determine when this tick happens for you with a different seedling. Then, check with another skill boost if the skill reduction tick isn't too close to the sapling tick. If the ticks don't overlap, you can easily grow the seedling and plant the sapling in one boost.

A fully grown spirit tree which has not had its health checked by the player cannot be teleported to from other spirit trees.
5376:
A basket can be used to carry up to five pieces of fruit. This can be created by using a loom .

Baskets can be filled with apples , bananas , oranges , strawberries , or tomatoes .
5378:
A basket of apples is obtained by adding 1 to 5 cooking apples into a basket . This is a convenient way to carry them and reduces used inventory space. Like all baskets, it has the same functions, such as "remove one" and "empty".

A basket of 5 apples is used in the Farming skill as payment to pay a farmer to protect strawberries in an allotment patch or willow trees in a tree patch, and four baskets are used as payment to grow Banana trees . Payments to farmers can be noted, but loose items cannot be used if baskets of items are requested. The baskets must be full.

Apples, individually, are called cooking apples in-game. Cooking apples can be purchased from the Culinaromancer's Chest after starting the quest Recipe for Disaster , picked from apple trees , found at the Cooks' Guild or thieved from Fruit Stalls in Kourend ; north of the Xeric's talisman teleport to Xeric's glade.

5388:
A basket of oranges is a basket containing 1 to 5 oranges. The best use for a full basket of oranges is to pay a farmer to watch over a Maple tree. Putting oranges in a basket will instantly place all oranges in your inventory, up to 5, into the basket, thus it is possible to have incomplete baskets if you had less than 5 oranges in your inventory at the time.

The number of oranges stored in the basket is displayed in the item's name, in parentheses: Oranges (5), for example.

Oranges may be collected through a player-grown Orange tree at level 39 Farming, and may be found in gnome shops or chartership shops.

An orange may be sliced into orange slices by using a knife on it.

Oddly, a basket of oranges weighs less than 5 oranges and a basket.

A basket of bananas is a basket containing 1 to 5 bananas . A basket of bananas can be obtained by either buying them from other players or filling a basket with 1-5 bananas. 5 full baskets of bananas are used as payment for a farmer to watch a curry tree .

Baskets of bananas are commonly used when hunting maniacal monkeys in Kruk's Dungeon .
5418:
Empty sacks are used to store potatoes, onions, and cabbages (10 per sack). Players can make a sack using a loom.

Apart from being used in Farming for carrying vegetables, 8 of them are used during Enlightened Journey to make sandbags. Sacks full of vegetables can also be used as payment for a farmer watching over a player's crops. Sacks may also be used to make scarecrows, by using a sack on a haystack to make a hay sack. The hay sack can then be used with a bronze spear and a watermelon to produce the scarecrow.

The Fill Sack option will instantly fill a sack with 10 vegetables. Vegetables chosen to go automatically into the sack are cabbages first, then onions, and lastly potatoes. Cabbages from Draynor Manor cannot be stored in a sack.
5420:
Potatoes is a sack containing between one and ten potatoes . Using the fill option will put up to ten potatoes in the sack and using a potato on it will only add that potato to the sack. Shift-clicking will remove as many potatoes from as the sack into the inventory as possible.

Sacks can be bought from many farming shops , such as Sarah's farming shop north of Port Sarim.

A full sack of potatoes is a requirement for Enlightened Journey and Mourning's End Part II if completing Thorgel 's Item list .

If onions or cabbage are also in the inventory, they will go into an empty sack before the potatoes. In this case it is recommended to 'use' the sack on a potato and then fill it.

A full sack of 10 potatoes can be used to protect a growing onion plant .

5440:
Onions is a sack that contains between one and ten onions . They are used namely in the Farming skill. If a player has an empty sack in their inventory and clicks on it while onions are also in the inventory up to ten onions will be placed in the sack. To remove onions from the sack requires right clicking the sack of onions and selecting the menu option that removes one onion at a time. Sacks can be bought from many farming stores , such as the one in the chicken farm north of Port Sarim . A maximum of ten onions can be put into a sack. Once ten onions are in the sack and a player tries to put more, it will be full. This works the same way with cabbages and potatoes , except for cabbages in Draynor Manor .

Note that cabbages will go into an empty sack before onions if a player has cabbages in their inventory. As such it is recommended to 'use' the sack on one onion at which point the player can click on the partially full sack of onions to continue filling it.

Onions are useful for Temple Trekking , as players must feed five NPCs with any piece of food to stop them from turning into ghasts in one of the events. One sack of onions can complete two events, and they are cheaper than cabbages and potatoes . Note that a Ghast can turn an entire sack of onions into a piece of rotten food .

5460:
Cabbages is a sack that contains between one and ten cabbages. If a player has an empty sack in their inventory and clicks on it while cabbages are also in the inventory up to ten cabbages will be placed in the sack. To remove cabbages from the sack requires right clicking the sack of cabbages and selecting the menu option that removes one cabbage at a time. Cabbages will need to be removed from the sack before they can be eaten.

Sacks can be bought from many farming shops, such as the one in the chicken farm north-east of Rimmington. A maximum of ten cabbages can be put into a sack. Once ten cabbages are in the sack and a player tries to put more, it will be full. This works the same way with onions and potatoes, but cabbages from Draynor Manor will not go into the sack.

Note that cabbages will go into an empty sack before onions or potatoes if a player has cabbages in their inventory. As such it is recommended to 'use' the sack on an onion or potato if the player wants a sack of either of those instead. After placing the selected vegetable in an empty sack the player can click on the partially full sack of vegetables to continue filling it.

The number of cabbages in the sack will be shown in brackets in the items name e.g. "cabbages (10)".

Two full sacks of cabbages can be paid to a farmer to tend a growing allotment of tomatoes and ensure that it successfully grows to maturity, three can be paid to a farmer to tend to Krandorian Hops, and four can be paid to tend to a redberry bush.

These sacks cannot be brought into the marketplace in Zanaris to bring more Cabbage into the area, due to the market's security rules.

Cabbages is a sack that contains between one and ten cabbages. If a player has an empty sack in their inventory and clicks on it while cabbages are also in the inventory up to ten cabbages will be placed in the sack. To remove cabbages from the sack requires right clicking the sack of cabbages and selecting the menu option that removes one cabbage at a time. Cabbages will need to be removed from the sack before they can be eaten.

Sacks can be bought from many farming shops, such as the one in the chicken farm north-east of Rimmington. A maximum of ten cabbages can be put into a sack. Once ten cabbages are in the sack and a player tries to put more, it will be full. This works the same way with onions and potatoes, but cabbages from Draynor Manor will not go into the sack.

Note that cabbages will go into an empty sack before onions or potatoes if a player has cabbages in their inventory. As such it is recommended to 'use' the sack on an onion or potato if the player wants a sack of either of those instead. After placing the selected vegetable in an empty sack the player can click on the partially full sack of vegetables to continue filling it.

The number of cabbages in the sack will be shown in brackets in the items name e.g. "cabbages (10)".

Two full sacks of cabbages can be paid to a farmer to tend a growing allotment of tomatoes and ensure that it successfully grows to maturity, three can be paid to a farmer to tend to Krandorian Hops, and four can be paid to tend to a redberry bush.

These sacks cannot be brought into the marketplace in Zanaris to bring more Cabbage into the area, due to the market's security rules.

5480:
An apple seedling is the result of planting an apple seed in a plant pot filled with soil.

To accomplish this, you need one apple seed , one gardening trowel , one filled plant pot and one watering can . To fill an empty plant pot with soil, take it, along with a rake and a gardening trowel in your inventory to any empty farming patch. Use the rake to weed the patch first, then use the plant pot on the patch. You then have a pot ready to plant your apple seed in.

Then use the apple seed on the plant pot and water using a watering can .

Once watered, the apple seedling becomes apple seedling (w) . It will take approximately 210 seconds, or 3 1/2 minutes to grow into an Apple sapling . You need level 27 farming to plant the seed in a fruit tree patch.
5481: A banana seedling is created by sowing a banana tree seed in a plant pot filled with soil with a gardening trowel . Once watered, it will grow into a banana sapling . A banana sapling requires level 33 Farming to plant in a fruit tree patch .
5482: Orange seedlings are the result of planting an orange tree seed in a plant pot with a gardening trowel . Once watered these seedlings will take approximately 5 minutes to grow into an orange sapling . You must have 39 Farming to plant the seed.
5483: A curry seedling is created by sowing a curry tree seed in a plant pot filled with soil with a gardening trowel . Once watered, it will grow into a curry sapling . A curry sapling requires level 42 Farming to plant in a fruit tree patch .
5484: Pineapple seedlings are the result of planting a pineapple seed in a plant pot filled with dirt with a gardening trowel . Once watered these seedlings will take approximately 5 minutes to grow into a Pineapple sapling . You must have 51 farming to plant the seedling into a Fruit tree patch .
5485: Papaya seedlings are created by planting a papaya tree seed in a plant pot with a gardening trowel . Once watered, these saplings will grow into an papaya sapling , which can then be planted in a fruit tree patch . You must have 57 farming to plant the seeds . Once the seedling is in the patch, you can pay the nearby farmer 10 pineapples to protect it. The farmer will accept noted pineapples.
5486: Palm seedlings are the result of planting a palm tree seed in a plant pot with a gardening trowel . Once watered, these seedlings will take approximately 5 minutes to grow into a Palm sapling . 68 Farming is needed to plant the seed. When it has grown, players may place it in a tree patch to grow a palm tree . Players can pay 15 papayas for the farmer to look after a palm tree.
5487: A calquat seedling is created by sowing a calquat tree seed in a plant pot filled with soil with a gardening trowel . Once watered, it will grow into a calquat sapling . A calquat sapling requires level 72 Farming to plant in a calquat tree patch .

5496:
Apple saplings are saplings that can be used to grow apple trees at level 27 Farming .

They can be made by planting an apple tree seed in a filled plant pot , with a gardening trowel in your inventory, and then watering the apple seedling with a watering can or by using Humidify . When watered, the seedling will sprout into a sapling in one crop cycle (0-5 minutes).

Planting the sapling in a fruit tree patch , with a spade in your inventory, will give 22 Farming experience. It will grow into an apple tree after 960 minutes (16 hours), which gives 1,199.5 Farming experience.

Players can ask the gardener to protect their tree from disease whilst it grows, which requires payment of 9 raw sweetcorn . This payment can be noted.

5504:
A strawberry is a food item that can be grown through the Farming skill at level 31 with strawberry seeds. They heal 1-6 hitpoints, calculated by 1 + 6% of maximum Hitpoints.

They are used in Cooking to make summer pie, which restores hitpoints, run energy, and temporarily boosts Agility level by 5.

Up to 5 strawberries may be put in a basket, which, when full, has the ability to hold 30 hitpoints of food, making it Fifth to purple sweets, Saradomin brews, Armadyl Brews, and the reward token (Gnome Restaurant) when it comes to the amount of hitpoints of food that can be held in one inventory slot. Baskets of strawberries are needed to protect growing dwellberry bushes (x3) and orange trees (x3). Adding strawberries to a compost bin makes regular compost.

Harvesting strawberries from the allotment patch north of East Ardougne is a task in the medium Ardougne Diary.
5506:
The Old man's message is an item as used in several tasks that members could do for the Wise Old Man of Draynor Village. A player must deliver the message to a variety of NPCs around Gielinor, including:

Abbot Langley in the Monastery

Father Aereck of Lumbridge Church

Father Lawrence in Varrock

The High Priest of Entrana

The Oracle on Ice Mountain

Reldo, librarian of Varrock

Thurgo, south of Port Sarim

Upon the delivery of the message, the player will be rewarded by the recipient of the message.

If a player keeps this item through use of banking or the drop trick and goes on another Wise Old Man's Task they will receive 0 damage upon reading the note and it will explode into ashes.
5507:
The strange book is a book found randomly on the bookshelves in the Wise Old Man 's house in Draynor Village , along with the book on chickens and the book of folklore . Players can return the book by using it on the Wise Old Man.

This book cannot be stored in a player-owned house bookcase . Trying to store the book on a bookshelf will result in the following message: "There doesn't seem to be room for that on the bookshelf."
5508:
The book of folklore, titled The Myth of the Elder-dragons, is a book found randomly on the bookshelves in the Wise Old Man's house in Draynor Village, along with the strange book and the book on chickens. Players can return the book by using it on the Wise Old Man.

This book cannot be stored in a player-owned house bookcase.
5509:
Small pouches are bags that can hold 3 rune , pure , daeyalt , or guardian essence for use in the Runecraft skill . This item may be initially obtained from the Mage of Zamorak , who provides one free small pouch upon completion of the Enter the Abyss miniquest . If lost, the Mage of Zamorak will not provide players with a replacement; however, the Dark mage in the Abyss will. It is possible to receive a free replacement by contacting the Dark mage via the Astral Contact spell.

The small pouch is the smallest of the five essence pouches .

Unlike the other pouches, the small pouch does not degrade from use.
5510:
Medium pouches are bags that can hold 6 rune , pure , daeyalt , or guardian essence for use in the Runecraft skill . This item requires level 25 Runecraft to use, and it is not possible to boost your Runecrafting level in order to use it at lower levels. This item is dropped by Abyssal monsters . It is also a reward from the Temple of the Eye quest if one hasn't been obtained prior.

This is the fourth best essence pouch that can be obtained.

After it has been used to store 270 essence (or approximately 45 full uses), the pouch will degrade and hold only 3 essence. Further uses degrade the capacity even more, and it will eventually disintegrate completely , and must be reacquired thereafter. Like other essence pouches, the Medium pouch does not degrade if the player is wearing a Runecraft cape or max cape when filling it.

To repair the pouch so it can hold the maximum of six essence again, you must speak to the Dark mage located in the centre of the Abyss . Cordelia is also able to repair essence pouches at a cost of one abyssal pearl , though this service requires 25 abyssal pearls to unlock first.

Essence contained in the pouch when it's dropped will be lost. A message will pop up and tell the player: "The contents of the pouch fell out as you dropped it!". The exception to this is dying with a pouch that still contains essence. If you recover your pouch from looting your gravestone or from Death , it will still contain the same amount of essence as before.

5516:
The elemental talisman is a talisman that allows players to enter the elemental runic altars to craft elemental runes .

The talisman can be combined with a gold tiara to make an elemental tiara for 40 Runecraft experience at an elemental altar, by using the tiara on it. This makes the talisman disappear, but the elemental tiara can be used in just the same way and can be worn on the head, saving an inventory space when crafting elemental runes. Note: This cannot be done whilst in the Guardians of the rift minigame.

It cannot be used as the talisman ingredient required for crafting combination runes .
5518:
The scrying orb is an item used in the Enter the Abyss miniquest , given by the Mage of Zamorak located in the south-east section of Varrock , in the Zamorak church. This item has a one time use for the sole purpose of this mini-quest and is henceforth never used.

The scrying orb needs to be filled with magic energy by teleporting to the Rune essence mine . Having the orb in the player's inventory while being teleported to the rune essence mine will partially fill it, while teleporting from 3 different locations to the rune essence mine will fill the orb entirely. Once players give the orb back to the mage, they never use the orb again.

Should the player die with the orb in their inventory or destroy it, the orb will be lost. However, when acquiring a new one from the Mage of Zamorak, the quest progress will be saved and it is not needed to return to the essence mine again. If a fully charged orb is lost, the quest progress is still saved, but you will be given an unfilled orb which can be filled by teleporting to the rune essence mine from Aubury close by.

The book can be gained from the Mage of Zamorak north of Edgeville after completing the Enter the Abyss miniquest . If the book is lost, a player may speak to the dark mage in the Abyss for a replacement, or may take one from the bookcase in a player-owned house .
5521:
The binding necklace is an enchanted emerald necklace that gives the wearer a 100% success rate in making combination runes through the Runecraft skill. It has 16 uses (one use is one click on an altar) and will be destroyed once all are used. It has a right-click "check" option that shows how many charges are left.

Similar to a ring of recoil , binding necklace charges are stored per player, not per necklace. Thus if the player sells or casts High Level Alchemy on a necklace with 1 charge remaining, the next necklace the player equips will still have only 1 charge. The player can right-click to "destroy" a binding necklace, destroying it and restoring the next binding necklace the player equips to 16 charges. This can be useful when a necklace drops to 1 charge left and a player is crafting runes in pairs, where a player can destroy a second necklace in their inventory and the equipped one will regain charges.

Players with 27 Magic or higher can make it by casting Lvl-2 Enchant on an Emerald necklace . It can also be obtained as a drop by the monsters in the Abyss .

Prior to an update , the binding necklace was one of only two pieces of jewellery to change their appearance slightly upon being enchanted, the other being the amulet of fury .

A Tiara mould is used in conjunction with a silver or gold bar to make tiaras in a furnace , via the Crafting skill. A tiara mould can be bought from crafting stores in Al Kharid , Rimmington , Sophanem , or Civitas illa Fortis for 100-150 coins .

Tiaras can then be used to make elemental tiaras in the Runecraft skill, and are a good way of training Runecraft without the need for talismans. A tiara is an item that can be created at a furnace from a silver bar along with a tiara mould and level 23 Crafting , granting 52.5 Crafting experience.

They are a purely cosmetic head slot item, though they can be turned into a talisman tiara, used in the Runecraft skill, acting as an equipable talisman ( head slot ), saving an inventory space over a normal talisman. It also allows the player to enter a particular runic altar by left-clicking on the corresponding mysterious ruins, saving time.

To create a talisman tiara, the player must have a tiara and the corresponding talisman in their inventory , and use the talisman or tiara on the altar of that particular rune. For example, a player who wishes to create an air tiara must enter the Air Altar ruins, and use the tiara on the altar with an air talisman in their inventory. The talisman itself is lost in the process. Tiaras cannot be imbued during Guardians of the Rift as attempting to enter an altar during the minigame with a tiara in your inventory will result in the chat dialog, "You should leave your tiara behind. There's no telling what the rift will do to it."

The rogue kit can be obtained as a reward from the Rogues' Den minigame . When used, it can be made into a chisel , rope , tinderbox , or spade . Once used, it cannot be changed back.

There is a 3/8 [ 1 ] chance of obtaining a Rogue Kit when a player successfully cracks the safe at the end of the Rogues' Den maze.

The main use of this item would be in cases where you're doing something like a quest , where you might not be sure what items you might need, but one of the above items might end up being useful. It can also be used to save bank space by taking up one slot instead of four.

One advantage of rogue kits is that they stack in inventory, so a player can carry a large number while only using up one slot. This can be useful for areas where a player needs to use up more than two ropes to get through (so that they only need to use up two inventory slots), or for quests that take place far from banks and require multiple of these items, but also encourage the player to take plenty of food. A specific example would be the Shilo Village quest, where all four items are needed, while you also need to defend yourself against undead ones .

It provides a small prayer bonus that matches that of a helm of Neitiznot, while retaining the defensive bonuses of a mithril full helm, and is commonly used during Slayer tasks that require the use of protection prayers, as the armour reduces the drain of prayer points.

The Hourglass is a quest item used only in Recruitment Drive . It is found on the table in Sir Tinley 's trial.

It serves no purpose in the quest. It can be taken before talking to Sir Tinley and after completing the patience test.

Duplicates can be drop tricked to obtain another. After leaving the room, all copies in the inventory are deleted.
5614: The Magic carpet is an animation item that is temporarily wielded by the player when using a magic carpet . Because the item is technically wielded in the weapon slot, originally players could not carry any weapons when using the carpet. Its inventory sprite has the appearance of a knife, as it was never meant to be seen in the inventory.
5615: Shaikahan bonemeal is an item that is used for worship at the Ectofuntus. It consists of a pot filled with shaikahan bones that have been crushed in the bone grinder at the Ectofuntus.
5616:
The bronze arrow is an arrow made of bronze. These arrows are the weakest type of arrows in Old School RuneScape and are compatible with most bows. As with most arrows, they can be poisoned.

In order to create this item players must first smelt bronze bars. Then using a hammer and anvil, the player must turn the bar into bronze arrowtips. Creating the bronze bar has no Smithing requirement, while a player must have level 5 Smithing to create the arrowheads. Then players should cut logs, and using a knife, turn them into arrow shafts. After attaching feathers to the arrow shafts (creating headless arrows) players can then use the arrowheads on the headless arrows to create bronze arrows. This entire process requires level 1 Fletching.

In addition, arrows can be purchased from a variety of general and archery stores.
5617:
Iron arrows are stronger than bronze arrows , and are compatible with most bows . Iron arrows can be made at level 15 Fletching by using 15 iron arrowtips on 15 headless arrows , granting 37.5 Fletching experience . As with most arrows , they can be poisoned .

Iron arrows can be purchased from Lowe's Archery Emporium in Varrock .
5618:
Steel arrows are stronger than iron arrows, and can be used with any standard bow of oak or stronger. Steel arrows can be made at level 30 Fletching by using 15 steel arrowtips on 15 headless arrows, granting 75 Fletching experience. As with most arrows, they can be poisoned.

Ava's accumulator (from the Animal Magnetism quest) generates steel arrows in the ammo slot, and also randomly attracts items into your inventory.

Steel arrows can be purchased from Lowe's Archery Emporium in Varrock, or Brian's Archery Supplies in Rimmington.
5619:
Mithril arrows are arrows made of mithril , are stackable, and can be used with any standard bow of willow or stronger. Stronger than steel arrows , mithril arrows can be made at level 45 Fletching by using mithril arrowtips on headless arrows . Doing so grants 112.5 experience for every batch of 15 arrows made. As with most arrows , they can be poisoned .

Mithril arrows can be purchased from Lowe's Archery Emporium in Varrock , or Brian's Archery Supplies in Rimmington .
5620:
Adamant arrows are stronger than mithril arrows , and can be used by any standard bow of maple or stronger. They can be made at level 60 Fletching by using 15 adamant arrowtips on 15 headless arrows , granting 150 Fletching experience . As with most arrows , they can be poisoned .

They are the best arrows available to free-to-play players.

Adamant arrows can be purchased from Lowe's Archery Emporium in Varrock , or Brian's Archery Supplies in Rimmington .
5621:

5628:
Bronze darts are Ranged throwing weapons made from bronze that are only available to members . Bronze darts only require level 1 Ranged to wield. They can be obtained by either using the Smithing and Fletching skills or trading with another player. Bronze darts can be poisoned and can be wielded with a shield or god book for protection.

Players can smith bronze bars into bronze dart tips with level 4 Smithing after completion of The Tourist Trap . Each bronze bar creates 10 bronze dart tips and gives the player 12.5 Smithing experience. Feathers then must be added with at least level 10 Fletching to create the bronze darts. This step does not require the quest to be completed. 1.8 Fletching experience is rewarded per bronze dart.

Darts are among the fastest weapons in the game (along with throwing knives ), and are commonly used for player-killing , training Ranged, or tagging enemies for barraging.
5629:
Iron darts are Ranged throwing weapons made from iron. Iron darts can be wielded at level 1 Ranged. They can be obtained by using the Smithing and Fletching skills or trading with another player. Iron darts can be poisoned and can be wielded with a shield or god book for protection.

To create iron darts the player must have completed the Tourist Trap quest and have at least level 19 Smithing and level 22 Fletching. Players can smith iron bars into iron dart tips. Each iron bar creates 10 iron dart tips and gives the player 25 Smithing experience. Feathers then must be added to create the iron darts. 3.8 Fletching experience is rewarded per iron dart fletched.
5630:
Steel darts are Ranged throwing weapons. To wield steel darts, players must have at least level 5 Ranged. They can be obtained by either using the Smithing and Fletching skills or trading with another player. Steel darts can be poisoned and can be wielded with a shield or god book for protection.

To create steel darts, the player must have completed the Tourist Trap quest and have at least level 34 Smithing and level 37 Fletching. Each steel bar will create 10 steel dart tips and the player will receive 37.5 Smithing experience. When feathers are added the player will receive 10 steel darts and 7.5 Fletching experience per steel dart.

Steel darts have almost the same stats and speed as iron knives , which are often used for Ranged training at lower levels - however, they are far cheaper in price than iron knives due to people training Fletching.

A steel dart is one of the possible items requested by the rowdy dwarf during the Forgettable Tale quest.
5631: Black darts are ranged throwing weapons. To wield black darts, players must have at least level 10 Ranged . Black darts cannot be made with the Fletching skill and instead are obtained through monster drops. The only monsters to drop black darts are Burthorpe soldiers . This makes black darts rather rare and hard to obtain. Black darts can be poisoned and they can be wielded with a shield or god book for protection.
5632:
Mithril darts are Ranged throwing weapons made from mithril that are only available to members. Mithril darts require level 20 Ranged to wield. They can be obtained by either using the Smithing and Fletching skills or trading with another player. Mithril darts can be poisoned and can be wielded with a shield or god book for protection.

Mithril darts are one of the most cost effective Ranged training weapons for lower level players, as they have an extremely quick rate of fire and cost very little compared to similar training methods like throwing knives or arrows. They can be bought in large numbers from the Grand Exchange, costing less than half of what similar tier ranged ammunition costs.

To create mithril darts the player must have completed The Tourist Trap quest and have at least level 54 Smithing and level 52 Fletching. Players can smith mithril bars into mithril dart tips. Each mithril bar creates 10 mithril dart tips and gives the player 50 Smithing experience. Feathers or Stripy Feathers then must be added to create the mithril darts. 11.2 Fletching experience is rewarded per mithril dart.
5633:
Adamant darts are Ranged throwing weapons. To wield the player must have at least 30 Ranged. They can be obtained by either using the Smithing and Fletching skills or trading with another player. Adamant darts can be poisoned and can be wielded with a shield or god book for protection.

To make adamant darts, the player must have completed the Tourist Trap quest and have at least 74 Smithing and 67 Fletching. Each adamant bar will create 10 adamant dart tips and the player will receive 62.5 Smithing experience. When feathers are added the player will receive 10 adamant darts and 15 Fletching experience per adamant dart.
5634:
Rune darts are throwing weapons requiring level 40 Ranged to wield. They are created by combining rune dart tips with feathers . Rune darts can be poisoned and can be wielded with a shield or god book for protection.

To create rune darts the player must have completed the Tourist Trap quest and have at least level 89 Smithing and level 81 Fletching . Players can smith rune bars into rune dart tips. Each rune bar creates 10 rune dart tips and gives the player 75 Smithing experience . Feathers then must be added to create the rune darts. 18.8 Fletching experience is rewarded per rune dart.

Smithing and fletching 10 rune darts while in Varrock is required to complete the Elite Varrock Diary . Fletching a rune dart is required to complete a master clue scroll skill challenge assigned by Sherlock .

They can be poisoned and can be wielded with a shield or god book for protection.

Throwing knives are among the fastest weapons in the game (along with darts ), and are commonly used for PKing or training Ranged.

Despite having lower ranged strength, rune knives in particular are sometimes used over dragon knives in PKing since their throwing animation can be cancelled earlier, allowing users to be more mobile and unpredictable while attacking.
5668:
The iron dagger is a dagger stronger than the bronze dagger. Players can make an iron dagger with the Smithing skill at level 15 using 1 iron bar, giving the player 25 Smithing experience. Members can poison this weapon, giving them an advantage in combat. Players can purchase this dagger from the Varrock Swordshop. There are also several spawn points throughout the map. As with most daggers, it can be poisoned.

Players with at least level 32 Thieving can get an iron dagger (p) by pickpocketing Rogues. Rogues are located south-west of the deep Wilderness Mage Arena.

It is superior in accuracy to the bronze sword, but inferior in strength. As it is a common and inexpensive item, an iron dagger is more likely to be obtained by new players than other iron weaponry. It is often used by low level ironman accounts to kill higher-leveled enemies with poison.
5670: The bronze dagger is the most basic dagger in Old School RuneScape , and can be made at an anvil using the Smithing skill. This requires one bronze bar and a hammer , and yields 12.5 Smithing experience . There are no level requirements to create or wield a bronze dagger; like many melee weapons, it can be poisoned .
5672:

As with most daggers, this weapon can be poisoned. Players can purchase this dagger from the Varrock Swordshop.

The dragon dagger is the second-strongest dagger available in Old School RuneScape , behind the abyssal dagger . It can be wielded by players with at least 60 Attack after completion of the Lost City quest. As with most daggers, it can be poisoned .

If casting either of the alchemy spells on a dragon dagger, use a cleaning cloth on poisoned versions to make more profit, as the value of the unpoisoned dagger is higher than any of the poisoned versions: 18,000 coins compared to 14,400 coins .

5704:
The bronze spear is a two-handed melee weapon made from bronze and is the weakest spear in Old School RuneScape . Spears are members -only weapons. Bronze spears can also be used to create a scarecrow .

Bronze spears can be easily obtained from low-level monsters such as goblins . There is a bronze spear spawn in the Haunted Mine on the second level near other assorted bronze equipment. A (kp) version can be bought from Tamayu after finishing the Tai Bwo Wannai Trio quest. Using the Smithing skill, players can create bronze spears. However, players must have begun Barbarian Smithing training to be able to smith these spears. It can also be found by digging at Level 3 digging spots at the Digsite , with a specimen brush , specimen jar and trowel in the inventory, or bought from the Fortis Blacksmith .

Like most spears, the bronze spear can be poisoned .
5706: The iron spear is a members-only two-handed melee weapon. An iron spear can be obtained by buying one from the Fortis Blacksmith, buying one from another player, or receiving it as a monster drop. The only way it can be created using the Smithing skill is through Barbarian Training after completing Tai Bwo Wannai Trio. It can be poisoned.
5708: The steel spear is a two-handed melee weapon that requires 5 Attack to wield. It can be bought from the Mount Karuulm Weapon Shop or Fortis Blacksmith , or obtained as a drop from monsters. Players who have started learning Barbarian Smithing and have level 35 Smithing may produce a spear at a Barbarian anvil from one steel bar and one willow log , receiving 75 Smithing experience . Smithing spears at the Barbarian anvil requires completion of Tai Bwo Wannai Trio . Like most spears , it can be poisoned .
5710: The mithril spear is a two-handed melee weapon made from mithril requiring 20 Attack to wield. Mithril spears are a members-only weapon. It can be bought from the Mount Karuulm Weapon Shop or Fortis Blacksmith, or obtained as a drop from monsters. Using the Smithing skill, players can create mithril spears on one of the barbarian anvils in either Otto's Grotto or Barbarian Village. However, players must have begun Barbarian Smithing training to be able to smith these spears. Like most spears, the mithril spear can be poisoned.
5712: The adamant spear is a two-handed members '-only melee weapon requiring 30 Attack to wield. It can be bought from the Mount Karuulm Weapon Shop or Fortis Blacksmith , or obtained as a drop from monsters. Using the Smithing skill, players can create adamant spears with level 75 Smithing This requires 1 adamantite bar and 1 yew log . However, players must have begun Barbarian Smithing training to be able to smith these spears. Like most spears, the adamant spear can be poisoned . Smithing an adamant spear at the anvil at Otto's Grotto is a requirement for the Kandarin Hard Diary .
5714:
The rune spear is a two-handed melee weapon requiring 40 Attack to wield. Unlike most other rune equipment , rune spears are members -only. Rune spears can be created at a barbarian anvil with 90 Smithing , requiring one runite bar and one magic log , as well as partial completion of the Barbarian Training miniquest . Like most spears, the rune spear can be poisoned .

A rune spear is also a requirement for a hard clue scroll . Ironmen can acquire it by completing Tai Bwo Wannai Trio for a rune spear (kp) then using a cleaning cloth on it, or by buying it from Mount Karuulm Weapon Shop .

This item is a rare drop from the rare drop table . Wearing a ring of wealth will increase the chances of receiving one from the rare drop table.
5716:
The dragon spear is a two-handed melee weapon that requires level 60 Attack to wield. It does not require the completion of a quest to equip. Like most spears, it can be poisoned.

The spear is a rare drop from both the rare and gem drop tables. On the gem drop table, the spear will only drop if the Legends' Quest has been completed, otherwise a talisman will be dropped in its place. However, the rare drop table does not require the quest's completion in order to be able to receive it as a drop. Wearing a ring of wealth will increase the chances of receiving one from both tables.

Goraks fought in the Gorak Plane while wearing a ring of wealth are more likely to drop the dragon spear than any other monster, with a drop rate of 1 in 325. Brutal black dragons are also frequent droppers of dragon spears, dropping it directly with a drop rate of 1 in 512 (while also having access to the rare drop table so they drop it slightly more common than this overall).

The spear is primarily used for player killing scenarios; outside of this, it is sought after by ironmen, as two elite clue steps require it.

As with most dragon equipment, the dragon spear cannot be made from raw materials using the Smithing skill.
