6301:
Burnt spider is the result of accidentally burning a spider on stick . The burn rate while cooking these will decrease as players reach higher Cooking levels, stopping entirely at level 48.

The burnt spider has no use whatsoever. Like most other burnt food, it is tradeable to other players but not on the Grand Exchange .
6303:
A burnt spider on shaft is the result of accidentally burning a spider on shaft . The burn rate while cooking these will decrease as players reach higher Cooking levels, stopping entirely at level 48.

The burnt spider has no use whatsoever. Like most other burnt food, it is tradeable to other players but not on the Grand Exchange .
6305:
Skewer sticks are made by cutting a thatching spar from Tai Bwo Wannai Cleanup minigame with a machete . Spider carcasses can be put on the sticks to make spiders on stick . Cooking a spider on a stick is an achievement in the Karamja Diary .

Cutting any thatching spar gives 3-6 skewer sticks.
6306: Trading sticks are the main currency of the jungle village of Tai Bwo Wannai on Karamja. They can be received by participating in the Tai Bwo Wannai Cleanup minigame, selling items to Gabooty's Tai Bwo Wannai Cooperative, or killing Karamja-related monsters such as jogres.
6311:
Gout tubers are a rare seed and food obtained from Tai Bwo Wannai Cleanup . It can be planted in a herb patch requiring 29 Farming and completion of Eadgar's Ruse to grow goutweeds . Due to its rarity, it is often only used for the medium Karamja Diary task of trading Safta Doc a gout tuber, 3 specific unnoted gems , and trading sticks for a gem machete . It cannot be planted at the disease-free Troll Stronghold herb patch, nor the patch at Weiss . Although gout tubers may be planted, they cannot be stored in the Seed vault or a Seed box . As with other herbs, it is not possible to pay a nearby gardener to watch over goutweed plants, nor will a fully-grown white lily plant protect them from disease.

Goutweed can be traded to Sanfew in Taverley , for a random herb per goutweed. Growing goutweed to trade with Sanfew is not recommended. The herbs received from Sanfew are random and gout tubers are very costly compared to standard herb seeds. If goutweed itself is needed, players should obtain it from the cellar at the Troll Stronghold due to the tuber's rarity and high trade value for its use in the medium Karamja Diary .

Gout tubers are edible. When eaten, a gout tuber heals 12 Hitpoints and restores 50 run energy. Eating one results in the message " You eat the tuber. Hmmm, peculiar taste! It heals some run energy. It heals some health anyway. "

Gout tubers will be turned to rotten food if you are attacked by a Ghast in the Mort Myre swamp .
6313:
The opal machete is a machete which cuts at a faster rate than a normal machete , but is still outclassed by jade and red topaz machetes . It has no requirements to wield, though cutting light , medium , and dense jungle requires 10, 20, and 35 Woodcutting to harvest respectively.

It can be obtained either from Gabooty's store with 600 trading sticks (500 if you are wearing any tier of the Karamja gloves ), looting a ninja impling , or bringing 300 trading sticks, 3 cut or uncut opals, and 1 gout tuber to Safta Doc in Tai Bwo Wannai . The opal machete can be used as a weapon but is primarily used to cut jungle in the Tai Bwo Wannai Cleanup minigame .
6315:
A jade machete can be used to repair the Tai Bwo Wannai gates. It is the second-highest tier of machete, outclassed only by the red topaz machete.

It may be obtained by purchasing it from Safta Doc in northern Tai Bwo Wannai Village with items, or from Gabooty's Cooperative store in the village gates for 1,200 trading sticks (1,000 if you are wearing any tier of the Karamja gloves). You will need to get one from Safta Doc for the Karamja Achievement Diary, by exchanging a Gout Tuber, 3 cut/uncut jade and 600 trading sticks.
6317:
The red topaz machete is a tribal weapon that can be used to chop Jungle on Karamja . It is the highest tier of machete, and offers the best chance to successfully cut through the jungles.

It can also be used as a weak low level weapon. The machete can be bought from Gabooty 's shop after the completion of the quest Jungle Potion . This can be found in the Tai Bwo Wannai Village on Karamja . Gabooty trades the machete for 2,400 trading sticks (or 2,000 if you are wearing karamja gloves 1 ). Additionally, Safta Doc trades 1,200 trading sticks, a gout tuber , and three red topaz for the machete. The red topaz can be either cut or uncut.
6319:
A proboscis (plural proboscises or proboscides) is an item dropped by mosquitoes encountered during the Tai Bwo Wannai Cleanup minigame. It is used to inject sulliuscep mushrooms in the Tar Swamp with fungicide spray, causing them to die and respawn in another location.

This was most often done when the sulliuscep is found in a location where the player is easily exposed to Tar Monsters. After an update, most sulliuscep are out of range of any tar monsters.

It can also be one of the randomly selected items that the player must take to Filliman Tarlock in order to make the magic secateurs used in Fairytale I - Growing Pains.

Completion of the Jungle Potion quest is required to access the Tai Bwo Wannai Cleanup minigame and obtain this item. Alternatively, it can be purchased from the Grand Exchange.

Proboscides can also be obtained by killing mosquitoes spawned by other players playing the minigame (also works as an ironman), bypassing the requirement to complete Jungle Potion.
6322:
A snakeskin body is snakeskin armour worn in the body slot available to pay-to-play rangers . To wear a snakeskin body, a player must have 30 Ranged and 30 Defence .

This item can be stored in the armour case of a costume room , as part of the snakeskin armour set. Ultimate Ironmen will be unable to retrieve individual pieces until the full set is stored.
6324:
Snakeskin chaps are snakeskin armour worn in the legwear slot available to pay-to-play rangers . To wear snakeskin chaps, a player must have 30 Ranged and 30 Defence . Snakeskin chaps are very popular amongst low/mid-level rangers, because of their low requirements and lack of an affordable upgrade. However, studded chaps are preferred over snakeskin chaps, as studded chaps has only a 20 Ranged requirement and provides the same attack bonuses and more defensive bonuses. The only trade-off is that snakeskin chaps are 1 kg lighter than studded chaps, weighing 3 kg.

This item can be stored in the armour case of a costume room , as part of the snakeskin armour set. Ultimate Ironmen will be unable to retrieve individual pieces until the full set is stored.

Mahogany logs are logs obtained from Woodcutting mahogany trees with a Woodcutting level of 50, and they yield 125 experience when cut. Players can burn these logs with the Firemaking skill for 157.5 experience at level 50 or above.

Players training Construction can bring mahogany logs to a sawmill to get a mahogany plank at a cost of 1,500 coins each. Alternatively, the Lunar spell Plank Make can allow players to convert them to planks at a lower cost, but at the expense of runes .

Simultaneously making 20 planks from mahogany logs is required to complete the medium Varrock Diary .

In addition to other sources listed below, mahogany logs can be effectively "purchased" by Managing Miscellania , unless the player is an Ultimate ironman . Miscellania 's effective GP/resource rates aren't completely straightforward, since some money is spent on other resources. Assuming the player also has completed Royal Trouble , 10 workers are put on mahogany trees, the maximum value of 75,000 is deducted from the treasury each day, bird nests and the 25,000 that gets invested in other resources are ignored, the kingdom returns 223 mahogany logs per day at a cost of 50,000 , or 224.20 per log.
6333:
Teak logs are obtained through the Woodcutting skill by cutting teaks with a Woodcutting level of 35, yielding 85 experience when cut. These trees can be found in Tai Bwo Wannai, the Ruins of Uzer, Kharazi Jungle, Ape Atoll, in the woodland south and west of Castle Wars, islands north-east of Mos Le'Harmless, Miscellania (although you cannot chop and keep the logs here), Isle of Souls, Locus Oasis, and Prifddinas.

The most unrestricted place to obtain teak logs is a single tree south-west of Castle Wars, accessible by a ring of dueling. If you have access to the fairy rings, BKP will teleport you slightly closer to the tree spot. Just walk west of the fairy ring - you could also choose to bank your logs at the Shayzien Encampment through fairy ring DJR (it is 83 tiles to the bank at the Encampment, from the Teak Tree, while walking to the Castle Wars Bank is 152 tiles).

Once players have access to Fossil Island, and have a Farming level of 35, they are able to plant up to three teak trees in the hardwood farming patch, which is much closer to a bank than Castle Wars.

While players can burn these logs with the Firemaking skill, they are mainly used in Construction. Members can bring teak logs to a sawmill to make teak planks at a cost of 500 coins each. Alternatively, the Lunar spell Plank Make can allow players to convert them to planks at a lower cost, but at the expense of runes. Once you have a demon butler, the fastest way to make planks is to give them to your butler to send to the sawmill, teleport to a bank to re-stock your inventory and repeat. Upwards of 7,000 planks per hour can be made using this method.

These logs can be burned starting at level 35 Firemaking for 105 experience each.

Players can use a knife on teak logs to create a teak stock at level 46 Fletching for 27 experience. This is one of several tick manipulation options.

With the introduction of Sailing, new teak trees can be found on The Great Conch island, with 45 Sailing and partial completion of Troubled Tortugans quest. A bank deposit box is located 69 tiles away from the nearest teak tree, along with a nearby fairy ring, CJQ.

"Tax relief" was the name originally given to an unobtainable item that existed in the game cache. It was created to replace the noted version of the man speak amulet from the Evil Bob random event. Since items could not be fully removed once created, it was added in a hidden update in 2005 to fill this slot. The actual item was just a copy of a pink skirt.

If players attempted to view the tax relief in game by using cheating software, they would be given a hex edit detected instead.

In RuneScape 2, the item later became viewable via Quick Chat, causing much confusion. It was deleted from the game cache in 2018, being replaced by barbed arrows.

An oak blackjack(o) is a members-only melee weapon mainly used to lure/knockout NPCs. You must have an Attack and Thieving level of 10 to wield this blackjack. To obtain one, the player must have completed the blackjack section of the Rogue Trader minigame.

There are three NPCs that can be lured/knocked out with this blackjack: villagers, bandits and Menaphite Thugs, all located in Pollnivneach. However for luring/knocking out these NPCs, the player must have the right Thieving level: level 30, 45, and 65, respectively. When fighting with a blackjack, there is a slight chance that it will stun the opponent.

Firstly, the player uses the Lure function of the blackjack to lead the unsuspecting NPC to a house, and can then Knock out the NPC. Once unconscious, the player can pickpocket the victim. If done quickly one can pickpocket multiple times in a row.

The white rose seed is a quest item given to the player during the Garden of Tranquillity quest by Brother Althric. In order to obtain the seeds the player must throw away or destroy their Ring of Charos since Brother Althric believes it to be an evil device. Once disposed of, the player can simply pick seeds from the roses behind the Monastery north of Barbarian Village.

It is advisable to use the Ring of Charos on the well in Edgeville instead of using other methods to dispose of it. After receiving the seeds, it can be re-obtained by using a fishing rod with the well.

The rose seeds then need to be planted in Queen Ellamaria's garden behind Varrock Palace.

She will tell the player that the white tree is dying and the only way to save it is to grow a cutting from one of its branches.

The cutting should be taken from the tree on top of Ice Mountain with secateurs, put into a plant pot filled with soil, water it with a watering can and left to grow. Once large enough the sapling can be transplanted into Queen Ellamaria's garden behind Varrock Palace.

Currently, players could cut from the Ice Mountain white tree even after completing the quest. They could even plant it in a plant pot and water it, but it would never grow into a sapling, and cannot be planted into a wood or fruit tree patch, so it would just be a waste of plant pots.

The white tree shoot is a quest item used in the Garden of Tranquillity quest. The player must speak to the gardener Dantaera just east of Catherby with the Ring of Charos(a) equipped. She will tell the player that the white tree is dying and the only way to save it is to grow a cutting from one of its branches.

The cutting should be taken from the tree on top of Ice Mountain with secateurs, put into a plant pot filled with soil, water it with a watering can and left to grow. Once large enough the sapling can be transplanted into Queen Ellamaria's garden behind Varrock Palace.

Currently, players could cut from the Ice Mountain white tree even after completing the quest. They could even plant it in a plant pot and water it, but it would never grow into a sapling, and cannot be planted into a wood or fruit tree patch, so it would just be a waste of plant pots.
6464: The white tree sapling is a quest item used in the Garden of Tranquillity quest. It is grown from a white tree shoot and can be transplanted into the White Tree patch in Queen Ellamaria's garden behind Varrock Palace.
6465:
The ring of Charos is a magical ring that charms certain NPCs when worn, unlocking different dialogue options and benefits. Charos, the creator of the ring, used it to enhance his prowess as a diplomat and convince the weak-minded to do his bidding. The Wise Old Man says that anyone who uses the ring must already possess some kind of diplomatic skill for it to work.

The unactivated form is awarded upon completion of Creature of Fenkenstrain. This version of the ring can only be used to deceive werewolves into believing the wearer is one of them; wearing it is necessary to access the Werewolf Agility Course. Near the beginning of the Garden of Tranquillity quest, the Wise Old Man activates it into the ring of Charos(a), allowing the player to charm and convince other people into helping you. Finishing Garden of Tranquility is NOT required to use the activated form of the ring.

The ring is lost upon death. If lost, it can be recovered by pickpocketing Dr Fenkenstrain. After Creature of Fenkenstrain, he resides on the top floor of Fenkenstrain's Castle; partway through The Great Brain Robbery, he permanently moves to the basement of the Harmony Island windmill. Note that if the player throws the ring into the Edgeville well during Garden of Tranquillity, another one cannot be claimed from Fenkenstrain during the quest, and the only way to get it back is to use a fishing rod on the well. Once the ring is activated for the first time, it will always be activated when recovered, and the original version becomes unobtainable.
6466:
Rune shards can be made by using rune essence or pure essence with a hammer to crack them into small pieces. The shards can then be ground down into rune dust .

Rune shards and rune dust feature in the Garden of Tranquillity quest, where it is revealed that adding the essence to a plant cure potion enhances its potency. This potion is then used to successfully treat the badly diseased vines in Bernald 's garden behind his house in Taverley .
6467:
Rune dust can be made by using a hammer or a chisel on a rune essence or pure essence stone to crack them into rune shards , and then grinding these down in a pestle and mortar .

Rune shards and rune dust appear in the Garden of Tranquillity quest, when rune dust must be added to a plant cure potion to revive some badly damaged vines in Bernald 's garden behind the bar in Burthorpe .
6468: Plant cure is a strengthened form of plant cure used during Garden of Tranquillity to cure the Burthorpe Vines. It is created by mixing rune dust with regular plant cure.
6469:
White tree fruit is a food item acquired by picking the white tree in the garden at Varrock Palace, after completion of the Garden of Tranquillity quest. The tree grows one fruit approximately every 5 minutes and can hold up to 4 fruit at a time. Picking one grants 12 Farming experience.

When eaten, white tree fruit restore 5-10% run energy and heal 3 health.

Due to being non-tradeable unlike other fruit, they cannot be turned into banknotes neither by tool leprechaun nor at a bank.

White tree fruit can be used as an ingredient when making supercompost. It can also be fed to the raccoon on Vatrachos Island in exchange for a medallion fragment.
6470:
Compost potions are made by mixing harralander and volcanic ash in a vial of water . Doing so requires level 22 Herblore and gives 60 experience.

A compost potion is one of the quest rewards after completing Garden of Tranquillity , and can be purchased with 5,000 reward points from participating in the Nightmare Zone minigame .

Players can use a dose of compost potion on a bucket of compost to make it into supercompost, or use a dose on a full compost bin to obtain 15 buckets of supercompost instead. It can also be used on Big Compost Bin which turns all 30 buckets of compost into super with a single dose, thus doubling the potion's benefit.

The trolley is a quest item given to the player during the Garden of Tranquillity quest by Queen Ellamaria. The player must use the trolley to transport two heavy statues from Falador and Lumbridge to her garden behind Varrock Palace. The first is by the crossroads just north of the White Knights' Castle in Falador. The second is on the south pillar of the archway into Lumbridge Castle.

To move a statue the player must use the trolley on it. The player will pull the statue onto the trolley and it can then be pushed by standing next to it and using the action menu. Other players can see the statue (or trolley only if the player has completed the quest or is moving the statue) being moved.

Once the quest is complete and the statues are in the garden; the player will lose the trolley and the two statues will no longer appear in the spot they once were leaving just plinths behind.
6479:
The list is a quest item given to the player by Queen Ellamaria at the start of the Garden of Tranquillity quest. It contains a list of flowers the plants that the player must grow in her garden behind Varrock Palace .

To grow all of the plants the player must obtain the following seeds:

The seeds are given to the player by various NPCs for performing tasks during the quest. See the main Garden of Tranquillity walkthrough for complete instructions on each task.

6522:
Toktz-xil-ul, also known as obsidian throwing rings, are a one-handed thrown weapon that require level 60 Ranged. They are quite powerful, having stats equivalent to a magic shortbow in conjunction with rune arrows, making them one of the more powerful thrown weapons. Because of this, and the fact that they can be equipped with a shield, they are seen in PvP scenarios quite often even after the introduction of dragon knives. However, they are significantly more expensive than rune arrows, making them less practical for general use. It is part of the set of obsidian weapons.

25 of these are required to build an obsidian fence at level 83 Construction in the Superior garden of a player-owned house.

This weapon has an attack range of 7 on rapid, and 9 on long range.
6523:
The toktz-xil-ak, also known as the obsidian splitsword or obby sword, is a one-handed stab sword requiring an Attack level of 60 to wield. It has stats similar to a rune longsword but with a faster attack speed of 4 ticks. It is part of the set of obsidian weapons.

When correctly used, the obsidian sword is one of the best weapons used for training Strength, especially for those who do not want to complete the master quest Monkey Madness I for use of the dragon scimitar.

When a berserker necklace is equipped, this weapon gains a 20% damage boost. It is also affected by the obsidian armour (helmet, platebody, and platelegs) which will increase the melee attack and melee strength by 10%. The damage bonus does stack with the berserker necklace.
6524: The toktz-ket-xil is an obsidian shield requiring 60 Defence to wield. Its defensive stats are equal to a granite shield's stats with an additional +5 Strength bonus; it also weighs less. It has lower Melee defence bonuses than a rune kiteshield, but higher Ranged defence. Compared to the rune defender, it has the same strength bonus but swaps Melee accuracy bonuses for higher defensive bonuses.
6525:
The toktz-xil-ek (also known as the obsidian knife or obsidian dagger) is a one-handed slash sword that requires 60 Attack to wield. Despite often being referred to as a dagger, the toktz-xil-ek is not a stab sword, has no magic attack bonus, and cannot be poisoned. It is part of the set of obsidian weapons.

Players can buy the toktz-xil-ek at the weapons store in Mor Ul Rek for 37,500 Tokkul. This weapon cannot be made using the Crafting and/or Smithing skills.

When a Berserker necklace is equipped, this weapon gains a 20% damage boost. It is also affected by the Obsidian armour (helmet, platebody and platelegs) which will increase the melee attack and melee strength by 10%. The damage bonus does stack with the Berserker necklace.

Buying this item from the store does not unlock the collection log. The drop must be obtained via TzHaar-Xil.
6526:
A toktz-mej-tal (also known as an obsidian staff) is a two-handed staff wielded by the TzHaar-Mej, and can be obtained as a very rare drop from them. Level 60 Magic and Attack are required to equip it. As well as being able to cast Magic spells, it can be sufficiently used as a melee weapon due to its significant crush and strength bonuses. It is part of the set of obsidian weapons.

It is one of the only magic weapons that requires two hands to equip, the others being the Gauntlet-exclusive Crystal and Corrupted staves, the Blue moon spear, and Tumeken's shadow.

Ten of these are used to build an obsidian fence at level 83 Construction in a player's Superior garden.
6527:
The Tzhaar-ket-em (also known as the obsidian mace ) is a one-handed blunt weapon requiring an Attack level of 60 to wield. Though it's commonly thought of as mace , it is not a spiked weapon and has no prayer bonus. It is slightly stronger and more accurate than the dragon mace , but has a slower attack speed and lacks any special attack . It is part of the set of obsidian weapons .

When a Berserker necklace is equipped, this weapon gains a 20% damage boost. It is also affected by the Obsidian armour ( helmet , platebody , and platelegs ) which will increase the melee attack and melee strength by 10%. The damage bonus does stack with the Berserker necklace.

Unlike other obsidian weapons, Tzhaar-ket-em can only be obtained from TzHaar-Hur-Tel's Equipment Store .
6528:
The Tzhaar-ket-om , also known as the obsidian maul , is a two-handed blunt weapon that requires a Strength level of 60 to wield. It is affected by the Berserker necklace , receiving a 20% damage increase when the necklace is worn. It is also affected by the Obsidian armour ( helmet , platebody and platelegs ) which will increase the melee attack and melee strength by 10%. These damage bonuses do stack with each other. It is part of the set of obsidian weapons .

Two of these are used to build an obsidian fence at level 83 Construction in a player's superior garden .

The maul is used commonly by Obsidian maulers in player-killing because the only requirement is a Strength level of 60, which makes it possible to have a low Combat level while being able to deal high amounts of damage. However, one major drawback of this weapon is its poor attack speed .

With Karamja Gloves 1 or higher, players can purchase the maul by selling 7223 chaos runes to TzHaar-Mej-Roh's Rune Store .

Players can attach a Tzhaar-ket-om ornament kit , obtained from hard Treasure Trails , to create a Tzhaar-ket-om (t) . This is only cosmetic, and does not affect the maul's stat bonuses. It can be dismantled, returning the maul and ornament kit.
6529:
TokKul is the currency of Mor Ul Rek. It is made from obsidian and cannot be created by players. As it is a currency, TokKul dropped by monsters can be automatically collected if the player is wearing a ring of wealth.

TokKul is made out of the corpses of the TzHaar, as stated in the 17th Postbag from the Hedge letter. When asked why players cannot trade TokKul, TzHaar-Hur-Lek responded:
6541:
The mouse toy is a fun weapon obtained from Bob the Cat after completion of the quest A Tail of Two Cats. Occasionally, if the player wields the toy and has a pet cat following them, the cat will perform a pouncing animation at it.

The attack animation is similar to the abyssal whip. When it is used to attack, it makes the same noise as a rubber chicken "whacking" someone. This item is not commonly seen, as its damage and accuracy bonuses are noticeably poor.

If lost after the completion of A Tail of Two Cats, the mouse toy can be re-obtained by talking to Bob the Cat with an amulet of catspeak equipped. A quick way to find Bob is to hop worlds at the anvils south of the west bank in Varrock, as he can often be found there.

If lost after the completion of Dragon Slayer II, the mouse toy can be re-obtained by searching the closed chest in Unferth's house east of the castle in Burthorpe.
6542: The present is an item obtained upon completion of the A Tail of Two Cats quest. The present, when opened, yields a mouse toy , which can be used to play with your cat , and two antique lamps , which grant 2,500 experience each in a chosen skill that is above level 30.
6543:
The antique lamp is an item obtained from opening the present after completing the A Tail of Two Cats quest . Two are given to the player, and each lamp grants 2,500 experience in a skill of the player's choosing, given that the skill is over level 30.

The same lamp is also received from the Fairy Queen after completing Fairytale II - Cure a Queen .
6544:
The enchanted catspeak amulet is an amulet worn in the neck slot obtained during A Tail of Two Cats by handing over a regular catspeak amulet and 5 death runes to Hild in Burthorpe. Like the unenchanted version, you can speak to cats while wearing it. The main difference is that it can also be used to locate Bob the Cat's general direction. To do so, right click the amulet, use the "Open" option (or the "Locate" option if equipped) which will open a compass-like interface in the shape of a cat, and turn the compass clockwise or anti-clockwise by clicking on the whiskers until the eyes are lit and the cat's mouth starts moving.

After the events of Dragon Slayer II, opening the amulet simply results in the message, "You look at the amulet and take a moment to remember your fallen friend."

If the amulet is lost, you will have to visit the Sphinx in Sophanem if you don't have a spare regular amulet (your cat must be following you when you talk to the Sphinx), and pay Hild another 5 death runes and your catspeak amulet to get it enchanted again. Unlike the regular amulet, you can only hold one enchanted catspeak amulet at any time.
6545:
Chores is a quest item that players obtain from Bob the Jagex Cat as part of A Tail of Two Cats. It contains a list of five tasks that players must do for Unferth as part of the quest.

Each task is crossed off as the player completes it.

The five tasks are:

Tidy house - involves only making Unferth's bed by clicking on it

Warm human - involves using logs and a tinderbox on Unferth's fireplace

Feed human - involves using a chocolate cake and a bucket of milk on Unferth's table

Tidy human - involves using shears on Unferth to cut his hair

Tend garden - involves using a rake on Unferth's Farming patch, then growing four potato seeds in it; these do not require compost or water, but take approximately thirty minutes to grow
6546: Recipe is an item that players can find in Unferth 's bookcase during A Tail of Two Cats . The recipe is for a chocolate cake , and serves as a hint that this is the food players should provide him with.
6547:
The doctor's hat is used during A Tail of Two Cats to convince Unferth that you are a doctor. It is obtained from the Apothecary.

If a player gets a nurse hat during the quest and later wants to get the doctor's hat, or vice versa, they can destroy their current hat and talk to the Apothecary to choose which hat they want. Players cannot own both hats at the same time.
6548:
The nurse hat is an item obtained from A Tail of Two Cats . During the quest, the hat is given to the player by the Apothecary in Varrock . It is used as part of a disguise to fool Unferth . Players can choose between a doctor's hat or a Nurse's hat.

After the player has finished the quest, they can return to the apothecary and receive a new hat if their original has been lost.
6549:
A lazy cat is a special variant of a pet cat , which players gain access to by completing the Ratcatchers quest . After completion, players can speak to Felkrash to have her train their overgrown cat into a wily cat . After a random amount of time, usually under an hour, regardless of the amount of interactions performed, a wily cat will become a lazy cat. Lazy cats cannot catch kalphite larvae or butterflies like wily cats can, and they have around a base 33% success rate at catching rats and hell-rats, which increases with their activity level. Players can only have one wily or lazy cat at a time.

Lazy cats can be trained back into wily cats by having them catch a random amount of rats . Other kinds of activity, such as letting the cat play with a ball of wool , or stroking it, will not help a lazy cat get back into shape.

Lazy cats have a hidden "happiness" status, which can result in 3 different sets of standard dialogue depending on whether the cat is happy, content, or unhappy. A lazy cat's happiness decreases when it is not given attention for an extended period of time, similarly to raising kittens . A content or unhappy cat's mood can be improved through stroking and playing with the cat. It can also be improved by taking the cat rat catching.

A wily cat is a special variant of a pet cat , which players gain access to by completing the Ratcatchers quest . After completion, players can speak to Felkrash to have her train their overgrown cat into a wily cat. ( Warning : After training your overgrown cat to be a wily cat, you will start from zero for the number of rats caught for the cat training medal . Wily cats are also ineligible for the medal.)

Wily cats are the best hunters of any cat, with a base success rate of 50% plus an additional success roll which increases based on their activity level, capping at an additional 50% success roll. When fighting hell-rat behemoths , they have higher health, get hit less often, and have twice the DPS of a regular cat. In addition, they can also catch kalphite larvae and butterflies (as well as Hunter butterflies , though this yields no experience ). Wily cats do not require food of any kind (except when fighting hell-rat behemoths).

Players are only allowed to have one wily or lazy cat at a time, in addition to one kitten or adult cat, and as many overgrown cats as they wish. You may have multiple wily cats if you first store your existing wily cat in your menagerie before training another.

Wily cats have a hidden "happiness" status, which can result in 3 different sets of standard dialogue depending on whether the cat is happy, content, or unhappy. A wily cat's happiness decreases when it is not given attention for an extended period of time, similarly to raising kittens . A content or unhappy cat's mood can be improved through stroking and playing with the cat. It can also be improved by taking the cat rat catching.

In addition, they can also catch kalphite larvae and butterflies (as well as Hunter butterflies , though this yields no experience ). Wily cats do not require food of any kind (except when fighting hell-rat behemoths).

Players are only allowed to have one wily or lazy cat at a time, in addition to one kitten or adult cat, and as many overgrown cats as they wish. You may have multiple wily cats if you first store your existing wily cat in your menagerie before training another.

Wily cats have a hidden "happiness" status, which can result in 3 different sets of standard dialogue depending on whether the cat is happy, content, or unhappy. A wily cat's happiness decreases when it is not given attention for an extended period of time, similarly to raising kittens . A content or unhappy cat's mood can be improved through stroking and playing with the cat. It can also be improved by taking the cat rat catching.

Ahab's beer is a glass of beer in the Port Sarim pub, The Rusty Anchor . It is unobtainable , even through telegrabbing .

When the "take" option is selected, Ahab yells at the player, Oi matey, leave my beer alone! . Attempting to telegrab the beer results in a chatbox message stating I can't use Telekinetic Grab on this object.
6562:
"Double helix" was the name originally given to an unobtainable item that exists in the game cache. It was created to replace the noted form of bronze fire arrows . Since items could not be fully removed once created, it was added in a hidden update in 2005 to fill this slot. The actual item was just a copy of a pink skirt.

If players attempted to view the double helix in game by using cheating software, they would be given a hex edit detected instead.

In RuneScape 2 , the item later became viewable via Quick Chat, causing much confusion. It was deleted from the game cache in 2017, being replaced by Buchu seeds .

Two more double helixes were briefly added to the game in 2005, serving as placeholders for the mud battlestaff and the mystic mud staff before release.

6568:
The obsidian cape is a piece of the Obsidian armour. Due to its lack of requirements and high defensive bonuses, it is a popular choice for players who lack a fire cape or a Cape of Accomplishment. It is one of few capes to count as warm clothing at the Wintertodt, although for this purpose some players may instead opt for the free, easily obtainable clue hunter cloak.

A reversed colour version may be obtained as a master clue scroll reward from Treasure Trails, which is statistically identical but the colours are inverted; it is red with black trim, as opposed to black with a red trim.

The cape of skulls provides equal bonuses while having the advantage of weighing 1.361 kg less, with the expense of a higher cost and that it gives the player a PK skull when equipped. The Tortugan shield is another good defensive cape that is considerably easier to acquire, particularly for ironman players.

This item can be stored in the cape rack of a costume room.
6570:
The fire cape is a melee cape obtained as a reward for completing the TzHaar Fight Cave . It is the second best melee cape in the game, outclassed only by the infernal cape . In order to obtain the fire cape, players must survive all waves of TzHaar Fight Caves and defeat TzTok-Jad . Note that the cape will not be awarded should both the player and TzTok-Jad die simultaneously, even though the boss log will count the kill. The player must be taken out of the cave by the game recognising TzTok-Jad's death; if they are removed from the cave due to dying, the game considers the player to have failed the challenge.

A fire cape must be shown to TzHaar-Ket guards around the centre of the city to allow further access to Mor Ul Rek . This does not consume the fire cape. However, to enter the Inferno , a fire cape must be sacrificed by giving it to TzHaar-Ket-Keh . This is a one-time fee.

If the player dies a PvP death and the fire cape is unprotected, it will remain in the player's inventory; however, the item will be in a broken, unusable state and must be repaired by using it on Perdu and paying him 150,000 coins .

When worn, players are granted the fiery attribute and will therefore receive additional damage in PvP from the special effects of Pearl bolts (e) and Pearl dragon bolts (e) .
6571:
An uncut onyx is the second rarest gem in Old School RuneScape , behind zenyte . It can be cut with a chisel at level 67 Crafting , granting 167.5 experience . This makes a cut onyx , which can be used to make very powerful jewellery . The cut onyx can also be used with a zenyte shard to create an uncut zenyte .

It can be purchased from TzHaar-Hur-Lek's Ore and Gem Store for 300,000 Tokkul (or 260,000 with any pair of Karamja gloves ). Purchasing an uncut onyx does not register as a drop for the collection log . A common method to obtain this Tokkul as an ironman involves selling chaos runes to TzHaar-Mej-Roh's Rune Store ; assuming a fully overstocked shop, this requires 28,889 chaos runes or 14,445 death runes with Karamja gloves.

There is also an extremely small chance of getting it from a bag full of gems . Each bag has 40 gems with each individual one having a 1/100,000,000 chance of being an onyx, making the chance per bag approximately 1/2,500,000. [ 1 ]
6573:
An onyx is the second rarest gem in Old School RuneScape , behind zenyte (which is created from an onyx and a zenyte shard ). Cutting an uncut onyx with a chisel requires level 67 Crafting and yields 167.5 experience . It can then be made into onyx jewellery by using a furnace along with a gold bar and a mould . Onyx can also be cut into 24 onyx bolt tips , though this is not recommended due to the bolt tips being worth significantly less than the onyx.

In order to create an uncut zenyte , a cut onyx must be fused with a zenyte shard in the wall of flames of the Temple of Marimbo Dungeon while holding a zombie monkey greegree (either variant). Doing so grants 15 crafting experience and gives the message: You reach into the extremely hot flames and fuse the zenyte and onyx together, forming an uncut zenyte.

Using a zenyte shard on a cut onyx gives the message: Only the intense heat of the flame pits beneath Ape Atoll can fuse the zenyte and onyx together.

Six of these are used to build a volcanic theme at level 85 Construction in a player's superior garden . In addition, one is used to build an obsidian decorative bench at level 98 Construction .

The onyx ring is made by using a gold bar, an onyx, and a ring mould on a furnace. It requires a Crafting level of 67 and provides 115 Crafting experience when made.

The onyx ring can be enchanted into a ring of stone through the use of the Lvl-6 Enchant spell at level 87 Magic, requiring 20 fire runes, 20 earth runes, and 1 cosmic rune.

An onyx necklace can be enchanted into a berserker necklace with the Lvl-6 Enchant standard spell which requires 87 Magic, a cosmic rune, 20 earth runes, and 20 fire runes.
6579:
An onyx amulet (u) is the unstrung version of the regular onyx amulet. It is made by using a gold bar on a furnace, while having a cut onyx and an amulet mould in the inventory.

Level 90 Crafting is required to make one, and it grants 165 experience. When used with a ball of wool, it becomes an onyx amulet, giving 4 experience. After it is strung, it can be enchanted into an amulet of fury, which requires level 87 Magic and yields 97 experience.
6581:
The Onyx amulet is made by using an onyx and a gold bar on a furnace with an amulet mould in your inventory to create an onyx amulet (u) . This requires a Crafting level of 90 and provides 165 Crafting experience when made. The amulet must then be strung before wearing by using a ball of wool or the String Jewellery spell from the Lunar spellbook . Stringing provides an additional 4 Crafting experience.

The Onyx amulet can be enchanted into an amulet of fury through the use of the Lvl-6 Enchant spell which requires level 87 Magic , or an enchant onyx tablet made from a lectern in a player-owned house .
6583: The ring of stone is an enchanted onyx ring . It can change the avatar of the player to look like that of a stone or empty Mining rock. If the player moves while under the effect, the effect will end. If another player mouses over or right-clicks on the player-turned-rock, the normal options will appear ("Walk here (Player name)," "Follow (Player name)," etc.).

The amulet of fury is one of the most powerful amulets available in Old School RuneScape, having equivalent attack bonuses to the amulet of glory with superior defensive, strength, and prayer bonuses, but without the ability to teleport the player. It can be made by enchanting an onyx amulet using Lvl-6 Enchant, requiring a Magic level of 87.

While it is generally regarded as the most versatile amulet with the best all-around bonuses, several amulets surpass it in certain areas.

A blood shard can be combined with the amulet to create an amulet of blood fury, which has a 20% chance of passively healing the player 30% of the damage they deal only while using melee. Its stats remain the same.

The amulet of fury can be decorated with a fury ornament kit. This produces an amulet of fury (or) but does not change its bonuses.

The colour wheel is a quest item in Mourning's End Part II and Song of the Elves . Although it plays no direct part in the quests, it can be used as a guide to the crystal puzzles in the Temple of Light and the library of Prifddinas as it provides clues to what colour of light needs to be sent to what part of the temple in order to unlock various doors there.

Red, green, and blue are the primary colours of the additive (projected) colour system, while cyan, magenta, and yellow are subtractive (reflected) colours. In the quest you will find various doors which have two colours attached to them, you are required to use prisms, mirrors and coloured crystals to direct a beam of light which is the correct colour to the various doors to unlock them. The doors will only unlock when they are hit with a beam of light which is complementary on the colour wheel. So for instance, the magenta door must be unlocked with a green beam of light.

The complements used in this spectrum of light are Magenta and Green, Cyan and Red, and Yellow and Blue.

If lost, it can be re-obtained by searching the dead guard slumped against the wall by the crystal dispenser in the temple of light, or by searching the pack by the crystal dispenser in the library.
6639: The hand mirror is a quest item used in the Mourning's End Part II and the Song of the Elves quest. It is obtained by pulling a lever in the Temple of Light near the start of the quest and is needed to solve the light puzzle in the Temple. As the player progresses through the puzzle they are rewarded with more mirrors in order to unlock more complicated parts of the puzzle. The mirrors redirect light to the place it needs to go if you put it at the right angle.
6640:
The red crystal is an unobtainable crystal released alongside the Mourning's End Part II quest. It was likely intended to be used during the light puzzle to recolour the light beams red.

It was presumably scrapped as it would make the puzzles requiring a red beam of light too easy. In the actual puzzle, red light can only be formed by passing yellow light through the magenta crystal.
6641: The yellow crystal is used in Mourning's End Part II to change the light beams colour to yellow. It is obtained by pulling a lever in the Temple of Light near the start of the quest and is needed to solve the light puzzle in the Temple.
6642:
The green crystal is an unobtainable item released alongside the Mourning's End Part II quest . Presumably it would have been used in one of the light puzzles in the Temple of Light .

It can be seen in the chatbox when searching the Pillar of light with a green crystal stuck inside it.
6643:
The cyan crystal is a quest item used in the Mourning's End Part II quest. It is obtained by solving the first part of the light puzzle in the Temple of Light, found upon searching the chest in the blue room. It is needed in order to progress further through the puzzle.

Interestingly, whenever you attempt to alchemise the crystal with any alchemy spell, elven magic forbids it and a message will appear saying "You can't do that to elven crystal!".

Upon finishing the quest, the cyan crystal is the only remaining piece of the puzzle left in the player's inventory.

Furthermore, trying to bank it will result in the message: "Some of your items cannot be stored in the bank.", so it is recommended to destroy it, as it has no further use.

You can leave it in a pillar before completing the quest, certainly it is not possible afterwards, attempting to gives the message "The Temple of Light's safeguards are working fine for now, so I'd best not meddle with them." Destroying it gives the message "Resetting the light maze will generate a new crystal".
6644: The blue crystal is a quest item used in the Mourning's End Part II quest. It is obtained by solving part of the light puzzle in the Temple of Light and is needed in order to progress further through the puzzle.
6645:
The magenta crystal is an unobtainable item released alongside the Mourning's End Part II quest. Presumably, it would have been used in one of the light puzzles in the Temple of Light.

One of the pillars of light has a magenta crystal stuck inside it; however, it is inaccessible and cannot be inspected, unlike the green crystal pillar.
6646:
The horizontal fractured crystal is an item used in Mourning's End Part II. It is the first fractured crystal obtained in a chest during the quest. It splits a southbound light into a west-, south- and east-bound light. It used to open the magenta and yellow doors.

The vertical fractured crystal is the second fractured crystal obtained in a chest during the quest. It splits a west-bound light into a north-, west- and south-bound light. It is used to open the cyan and black doors.

The fractured crystals act like beam splitters and allow a beam of light to be split into three separate beams. Each crystal splits the light in different directions and must be used in a specific combination in order to be able to solve the puzzle.
6647:

6648:
The item list is a quest item given to the player during the Mourning's End Part II quest by a dwarf named Thorgel at the end of the puzzle in the Temple of Light . Thorgel will give the player a Death talisman if the player delivers all of the items on the list to him.

There are 50 items on the list in total, so players must make a minimum of two trips to deliver them all. Players should remember to turn the mirror towards the cyan door if they're travelling through the Temple of Light to Thorgel, otherwise they will lock themselves out.

Note that it's possible to completely skip having to get the death talisman, and therefore having to do Thorgel's item list, by utilizing a Catalytic talisman to access the death altar instead. This is especially useful for ironmen, who may want to grind Guardians of the Rift in hopes of obtaining the catalytic talisman before doing the quest.
6649:
Edern's journal, or Journal of Nissyen Edern, can be found by searching the dead guard that is located outside the Temple of Light.

Through nine daily entries, the mourner Nissyen Edern wrote about joining the Death Guard, being deployed to West Ardougne, participating in the plague hoax, and investigating the tunnel to the Temple of Light.

After the quest, it can be found in the bookcase of your player-owned house or in the Grand Library in Prifddinas after completion of Song of the Elves.
6650: The blackened crystal is a quest item used in the Mourning's End Part II quest. It is obtained by using a chisel on a large black rock in the Temple of Light at the start of the quest. The player must give the crystal to Arianwyn, who will then turn it into a newly made crystal, which is needed to complete the final part of the quest. If a player has lost their blackened crystal, they must carve a new piece from the giant black crystal in order to get it back.
6651:
The newly made crystal is a quest item used in the Mourning's End Part II quest. It is obtained by using a chisel on a large black rock in the Temple of Light at the start of the quest and then giving this to Eluned after talking to Arianwyn . He will then turn it into an uncharged crystal which must be charged on the Death Altar in order to be able to seal the Temple for 1,000 years.

If lost, it can be reobtained directly from Arianwyn without needing to chisel the rock again.
6652:

6653:
The crystal trinket is a reward from Arianwyn after completing Mourning's End Part II. It is used to enter the Temple of Light after the quest. For players who have not completed Song of the Elves, this also requires mourner gear or a slayer ring since the entrance is via the Mourner headquarters' basement in West Ardougne. Players will still need the trinket after completing Song of the Elves.

If players lose it, they can obtain another from Arianwyn in Lletya. During and after Song of the Elves, it is instead found in a chest on the east side of the ground floor in Lletya in the main building.

If you try to enter the temple after completing the quest without the trinket, players will be bounced back and get the message "A strange force blocks your path." This is not necessary when crafting death runes through the Abyss, the Underground Pass, or through Guardians of the Rift.
6654:
The Camo top is a possible reward item from the Drill Demon random event.

This item can be stored in the fancy dress box of a costume room, as part of the Camo Outfit set. Ultimate Ironmen will be unable to retrieve individual pieces until the full set is stored.
6655:
Camo bottoms are a possible reward from the Drill Demon random event .

This item can be stored in the fancy dress box of a costume room , as part of the Camo Outfit set. Ultimate Ironmen will be unable to retrieve individual pieces until the full set is stored.
6656:
The camo helmet is a possible reward from the Drill Demon random event.

This item can be stored in the fancy dress box of a costume room, as part of the camo outfit set. Ultimate Ironmen will be unable to retrieve individual pieces until the full set is stored.
6657:
The Camo top is an unobtainable version of the Camo top obtained from the Drill Demon random event. Originally, all pieces of Camo were tradeable, and could be turned into banknotes. However, due to players selling the pieces for very expensive prices (some up to several million) they were made untradeable 2 weeks later. Any noted versions existing ingame were transformed into this unique stackable variant.

As this change occurred prior to August 2007, the item has never been obtainable in Old School RuneScape.

6660:
The Fishing explosive is an interface item that can be seen in the Slayer skill guide representing the Fishing explosive

The actual item cannot be obtained by players.
6661:
The Mogre is an interface item that can be seen in the Slayer skill guide representing the Mogre

The actual item cannot be obtained by players.
6662: A broken fishing rod is found at Mudskipper Point , near the forlorn boot . At this time it has no use and cannot be repaired. It is possible that the rod may have belonged to a Mogre victim, (such as Skippy ), given that the Mogres live nearby.
6663:
A forlorn boot can be found at Mudskipper Point near the broken fishing rod .

Players can return the boot to Skippy . This action results in him accepting the item and declaring, Thanks! Now I have two right boots! Players are able to give Skippy the boot repeatedly, but his response is always the same.
6664:
A fishing explosive is a consumable piece of Slayer equipment purchased from any Slayer master . It can lure mogres out of the water by using it on any of the three Ominous Fishing Spots in Mudskipper Point .

It can also be used to instantly awaken the Kraken boss by using it on the large whirlpool.
6665:
The mudskipper hat is an uncommon cosmetic item dropped by Mogres , which require 32 Slayer and completion of the mogre miniquest , or ocean Mogres in order to obtain. It is worn in the head slot and gives no bonuses. They are occasionally worn with flippers , another uncommon item dropped by both types of Mogres .

It can be stored in a magic wardrobe in a player's costume room .
6666:
Flippers are an uncommon drop from mogres and sea mogres, which require 32 Slayer to kill. They are worn in the footwear slot and allow players to 'run' while in the underwater area beneath Fossil Island. Once the player enters the water wearing flippers, the ability to run remains active even if the player switches to other footwear.

If a weapon is equipped, you will not be able to 'run' while swimming. You must also be under 28 kg.

They can be stored in a magic wardrobe in a player's costume room. They can also be stored in a tackle box.

Flippers can be made into dark flippers by talking to Patchy on Mos Le'Harmless while carrying a dark claw and 500 coins.
6667:
A fishbowl is an item that can be created with level 42 Crafting or received as a drop from Mogres . It can be filled with water and then with seaweed . With a filled fishbowl in the inventory, a tiny net can be purchased from Harry in Catherby for 10 gold which can then be used to catch a fish in the aquarium to get a pet fish . This is one of the tasks in the Easy Kandarin Diary .

It is also used in the Recipe for Disaster quest, in which players make it into a fishbowl helmet . This is worn in the helm slot and allows the player to go diving near Port Khazard .

It is also used in the Rum Deal quest, in which players receive a Fishbowl and net , which can be dismantled into a Fishbowl and a Big fishing net in order to obtain a fishbowl without having to go obtain molten glass first, which can be convenient for ironmen .

Fishbowls are sometimes used to train Magic with the Lunar spell Humidify , which fills any container in the player's inventory with water. Because the left-click option for a water-filled fishbowl is to empty it, the spell can be repeatedly cast with ease.

6670:
A pet fish may be obtained from Harry's Fishing Shop in Catherby by using a tiny net to fish in one of aquarium fishing spots inside the shop. For a player to be able to fish in the aquarium, the player must have a fishbowl containing water and seaweed in their inventory. Catching a pet fish gives 1 Fishing experience.

Pet fish eat fish food . A box of fish food can be found on the 1 st floor [ UK ] 2 nd floor [ US ] of Draynor Manor . Players can also make fish food by adding ground guam and ground seaweed to an empty fish food box .

There are three different types of pet fish. It is possible to own multiple types of pet fish at the same time and to have more than one fish of the same colour. The type of fish received is dependent on the player's Fishing level. At level 99, players have a 40% chance of catching a bluefish, 40% chance of catching a greenfish, and a 20% chance of receiving a spinefish. [ 1 ] Players must have at least level 70 Fishing to be able to obtain the orange (spinefish) variant.

Pet fish can be stored in a player-owned house menagerie . When dropping it in any other way, a message will pop up saying "If you drop your fishbowl it will break!", after which the player can choose to "Drop it regardless" or to "Keep hold".

6673:
A fishbowl and net is created by using a big fishing net with an empty fishbowl . You can then untangle the fishbowl from the net, to get the separate components. It is used during Rum Deal to catch sluglings .

It cannot be stored in the tackle box .
6674: A tiny net is used to obtain a pet fish, can be stored in a tackle box, and can be purchased from Harry in Catherby for 10 gold, provided the player has a fishbowl filled with both water and seaweed in their inventory. When meeting this criteria, a dialogue option about getting a fish and buying a tiny net becomes an option. A Fishing level of 10 or higher is required. Obtaining a pet fish from Harry is required for the Easy Kandarin Diary.
6675: An empty fish food box may be obtained from Harry in Catherby if a player has a fishbowl filled with either water, seaweed, or a pet fish in their inventory. Adding ground guam and ground seaweed to the box will turn it into fish food. Along with the fish food box spawn in Draynor Manor, it is currently the only way to obtain fish food.
6677: Guam in a box is made by adding ground guam to an empty fish food box . To obtain an empty box, players must talk to Harry in Catherby with a filled fishbowl in their inventory. To make the ground guam, the player must use a guam leaf with a pestle and mortar . Adding ground seaweed then turns it into fish food which can be fed to a player's pet fish . This is currently the only way to obtain fish food, other than picking it up in Draynor Manor . Making it provides no experience in any skills.
6678:
Guam in a box? is an unobtainable item added to the game with the release of pet fish . It is identical to the real Guam in a box , except with a different name and usable by free to play players.

It is unknown what purpose, if any, the item was intended to serve.
6679: Seaweed in a box is made by adding ground seaweed to an empty fish food box. To obtain an empty box, players must talk to Harry in Catherby with a filled fishbowl in their inventory. To make the ground seaweed, the player must use seaweed with a pestle and mortar. Adding ground guam then turns it into fish food which can be fed to a player's pet fish. This is currently the only way to obtain fish food, other than picking it up in Draynor Manor. Making it provides no experience in any skills.
6680:
Seaweed in a box? is an unobtainable item added to the game with the release of pet fish. It is identical to the real Seaweed in a box, except with a different name and usable by free to play players.

It is unknown what purpose, if any, the item was intended to serve.
6681:
Ground guam is made by using a pestle and mortar on a guam leaf. It is used to make fish food by combining it with ground seaweed on an empty box.

Ground guam cannot be used to make potions, such as attack potions.

With a pestle and mortar in your inventory and a Herblore level of 19, you can use a ground guam on a stack of (at least 15) swamp tar to make 15 guam tar, granting 30 Herblore experience.
6683: Ground seaweed is seaweed that has been ground with a pestle and mortar. It may then be combined with ground guam by using both on an empty fish food box to make fish food. The fish food is for pet fish.
6685:
A Saradomin brew is made by mixing toadflax and a crushed bird's nest in a vial of water , giving 180 Herblore experience. This requires level 81 Herblore.

Each dose of a Saradomin brew temporarily lowers Strength , Attack , Magic , and Ranged by 10% + 2 of their current levels, and raises Hitpoints by 15% + 2 and Defence by 20% + 2 of their base levels, all rounded down. This can boost the player's Hitpoints and Defence above their base level by up to the amount restored. Saradomin brews are frequently used alongside super restore potions which restore the drained offensive stats and can leave the player with overhealed hitpoints and a temporarily boosted defence level greater than they would gain from a super defence potion .

Depending on skill levels, one dose of super restore is enough to restore lost stats from two or three doses of Saradomin brew, or up to four doses of brew if the player's stats were boosted beforehand (as with a super combat potion ). At skill levels 90 and higher, a super restore will only fully restore lost stats from two doses of Saradomin brew.

Saradomin brews can restore far more Hitpoints per inventory slot (a maximum of 64 at or above 94 hitpoints) than any other item except purple sweets . Saradomin brews are often used in lengthy combat encounters with bosses or at raids where inventory space is limited, as well as being commonly used in player killing .

Creating a Saradomin brew in the Falador east bank is needed to complete the Elite Falador Diary .
