6693:
A Crushed nest is an item created by using a pestle and mortar on an empty bird nest. It is the secondary ingredient in a Saradomin brew.

Wesley in Nardah can crush unnoted or noted herblore secondary items for 50 coins per item.
6696:
Ice coolers can be purchased from any Slayer master , and are used to finish off desert lizards that have less than 5 Hitpoints . When used, the lizard shudders and collapses from the freezing water, consuming the ice cooler. Using an ice cooler on a desert lizard with 5 or more Hitpoints has no effect but will still consume an ice cooler. It is recommended to bring an excess due to the possibility of wasting coolers.

They can also be used to craft empty fish crates , used in Sailing deep sea trawling .

Sulphur Lizards and Grimy Lizards do not require ice coolers to finish off.
6697:
A pat of butter is a food ingredient made with a Cooking skill of 38. Players can make one by churning a bucket of milk, which gives 40.5 Cooking experience, or a pot of cream, which gives 22.5 Cooking experience, in a dairy churn.

A pat of butter is used by adding it to a baked potato to make a potato with butter. After adding the butter, players can then add additional toppings.
6699:
Burnt potato is the result of accidentally burning a raw potato while attempting to make a baked potato . The burn rate while cooking these will decrease as players reach higher Cooking levels, stopping entirely at level 41.

The burnt potato has no use whatsoever. Like most other burnt food, it is tradeable to other players but not on the Grand Exchange .
6701:
A baked potato is a type of food that heals 4 Hitpoints when eaten. It can be obtained by baking a potato on a cooking range, requiring level 7 Cooking and granting 15 experience when successful. Potatoes cannot be cooked on fires.

Players may burn the potato, resulting in a burnt potato. Players burn potatoes less at higher levels, and will stop burning them entirely at Cooking level 41.
6703:
A potato with butter is a food item and cooking ingredient that heals 14 Hitpoints when eaten and is consumed in one bite. It can be made with a Cooking level of 39 by using a baked potato on a pat of butter or a pat of not garlic butter . Doing so grants 40 Cooking experience and does not require use of a fire or range .

A potato with butter can be combined with various other toppings like tuna and corn or mushroom & onion to make food that restores more hitpoints .
6705:
Potato with cheese is a food item that heals 16 Hitpoints when eaten and is consumed in one bite. It can be made with a Cooking level of 47 by using a piece of cheese on a potato with butter . Doing so grants 40 Cooking experience and does not require the use of a fire or range .

They are also sold by Lidio in the Warriors' Guild who has a stock of 10.

It is a popular food choice among mid-level players due to its low cost, alongside reasonable accessibility at the Warriors' Guild.
6707:
The Null amulet was an unobtainable item originally created as a placeholder for the Camulet .

While various camels were added to the game files on 24 October 2005, alongside members of Ali Morrisane Commercial Enterprises Ltd. , the camels could not be found anywhere in-game. The Null amulet was also added to the game files, but was unobtainable. Eventually on 23 January 2006, the amulet was replaced by the Camulet , and camels now appeared. It is possible, therefore, that the Camulet was originally intended to be a reward from a quest or miniquest with Ali Morrisane's associates, who currently serve no purpose in-game.

As the Null amulet was removed long before August 2007, it has never been present in Old School RuneScape .
6709:
The Fever spider is an interface item that can be seen in the Slayer skill guide representing the Fever spider

The actual item cannot be obtained by players.
6710:
Blindweed seed is a quest item that the player must grow during the Rum Deal quest . It is planted in the Blindweed farming patch on the south-eastern part of Braindeath Island . Players do not need a watering can or a form of compost after planting the blindweed seed.

A nearby gardener will not watch over your growing blindweed, but blindweed cannot become diseased.

When harvested it yields blindweed , which is the first ingredient of the unsanitary swill that the player must make during the quest. Planting a blindweed seed grants 32 Farming experience and harvesting the blindweed grants 45 Farming experience.
6711: Blindweed is a quest item grown by the player during the Rum Deal quest, and is grown by planting a blindweed seed in the Farming patch on Braindeath Island . The plant is one of the ingredients of the unsanitary swill , which the player must make during the quest.
6712:
The Bucket of water is a quest item used during the Rum Deal quest. It is different to an ordinary bucket of water in that it must be filled from a stagnant lake near Braindeath Island Volcano , on Braindeath Island . The symbol of the stagnant lake is the normal symbol for a water source but has a bit of grey in it.

The bucket of water is then used to make the unsanitary swill that the player needs to continue the quest. Trying to obtain it after the quest will result in the message You do not need any more of that stuff! .
6713: The wrench is a quest item used during the Rum Deal quest. It is given to players by Captain Braindeath. Players must then take it to Davey on the ground floor of the rum factory on Braindeath Island to have it blessed, turning it into a holy wrench. It can then be used to exorcise the possessed controls on the 1st floor of the brewery to release a level 150 evil spirit that must be killed.
6714:
The holy wrench is a reward for partially completing the Rum Deal quest. If players have it in their inventory when they drink or share a prayer potion, prayer mix, super restore potion, super restore mix, blighted super restore, or Sanfew serum, they will regain additional Prayer points, depending on their Prayer level. The wrench does not work with Moonlight moths nor its mixes.

When held in the player's inventory, the holy wrench increases the amount of Prayer points restored when drinking a dose of certain prayer restoring potions by an additional 2% of your prayer level. This means that each dose of a potion will restore 27% or 32% of your prayer on top of the base restore of 7, 8, or 4, instead of 25% or 30%. All numbers are rounded down to the closest integer.

Both the Prayer cape and the ring of the gods (i) provide the same effect as the holy wrench; however, the effects do not stack. Prayer regeneration potions, moonlight moths, moonlight moth mixes, Moonlight potions, Ancient brews, Forgotten brews, and Zamorak brews do not benefit from this effect.

If lost, the holy wrench can be re-obtained by talking to Davey in the brewery on Braindeath Island. You will not be able to receive another holy wrench if you already have one in your inventory or your bank. Multiple wrenches may be obtained via the drop trick method.

The holy wrench is required to imbue the ring of the gods into the ring of the gods (i), along with the appropriate amount of Nightmare Zone reward points, Soul Wars Zeal, or a scroll of imbuing from the Emir's Arena. This does not consume the wrench.
6715:
Sluglings are a quest item used during the Rum Deal quest. They are believed to be young sea slugs, as confirmed by Captain Braindeath.

Players catch sluglings by using a fishbowl and net in a fishing spot on Braindeath Island. They are one of the ingredients of the unsanitary swill that the player must make during the quest. Players are not awarded any Fishing experience when catching sluglings.

After the quest, any sluglings remaining in inventory will disappear, and an attempt to fish for sluglings triggers the response, "You have no need to do that any more."

They appear to have mind-controlling properties. Using them on Captain Braindeath triggers dialogue where the player says the sluglings are telling them to do "bad things", prompting Braindeath to stomp on them to release the player from their hypnotic trance.
6716:
Karamthulhu are a squid-like species that are sometimes obtained while fishing for slugs during the Rum Deal quest . They are also dropped by zombie pirates and zombie swabs on Braindeath Island .

Karamthulhus can be used during Rum Deal in addition to sluglings to make unsanitary swill . After the quest, any Karamthulhus remaining in the inventory will disappear, and an attempt to fish for them triggers the response, "You have no need to do that any more." Players will still be able to obtain a Karamthulhu as a drop from the aforementioned zombie pirates and swabs after having completed the quest.
6717: Karamthulhu is an unobtainable item released alongside the Rum Deal quest . It is very similar to the obtainable karamthulhu item, but has a different inventory icon, value, and examine text. While its examine text suggests it was intended to be linked to the unreleased Karamthulhu pet , the pet NPC was linked to the obtainable karamthulhu item instead, leaving the purpose of this one unknown.
6718:
The fever spider body is a quest item used during the Rum Deal quest. It can only be obtained by killing a fever spider in the basement of the rum factory on Braindeath Island and is one of the ingredients of the unsanitary swill that the player must make during the quest.

This cannot be used on an arrow shaft or thatch spar to produce a spider on shaft or spider on stick.
6719: Unsanitary swill , sometimes referred to as 'rum' , is a player made quest item brewed during the Rum Deal quest . It is made by adding blindweed , stagnant water , sluglings , and a fever spider body to a brewing device on Braindeath Island . It is used on Captain Donnie who doesn't become drunk, but he does tell you the name ' Rabid Jack '.
6720:
Slayer gloves are a piece of Slayer equipment used to fight fever spiders , and require a Slayer level of 42 to be worn. If the gloves are not equipped, the spiders will damage the player for 12.5% of their base hitpoints, as well as inflict disease . When worn, they resemble a lighter brown hue similar to that of normal leather gloves .

They can be purchased from any Slayer Master for 200 coins .
6721:
A rusty scimitar is a scimitar that has turned rusty. Rusty scimitars are dropped by zombie pirates, Sorebones, or zombie swabs. It can be taken to Tindel Marchant, along with 100 coins, to clean it and turn it into a scimitar up to mithril.

It cannot be used on a whetstone or armour stand in a player-owned house.
6722:
Zombie heads can be obtained by completing one of the Halloween events that occur once per year. This also rewards the player with all other holiday items associated with Halloween.

Previously, they were obtainable during the 2013 Rare Drops event (from 26 August to 2 September ) as part of a rare item drop .

If destroyed, a replacement can be obtained from Diango in Draynor Village or from the toy box of a costume room . A lost zombie head can also be recovered by digging in the Lumbridge Swamp with a spade .
6724:
The seercull is a Fremennik bow that requires a Ranged level of 50 to wield, and fires arrows up to Amethyst . Compared to a magic shortbow , it has a slower rate of fire and a different special attack which is more effective against mages. In addition, its normal and rapid fire attacks have one more range than that of a shortbow , and its long range attack is equivalent to that of a composite bow . It is a comparable weapon to the Magic comp bow .

The name can be attributed to the combination of the word seer (another word for "mage" or "wizard") and the word cull (another word for "kill"), in other words, the mage-killer . This is a fitting name because of the effect of its special attack and its examine text.
6728: Dagannoth-king bonemeal is an item that is used for worship at the Ectofuntus. It consists of a pot filled with dagannoth bones that have been crushed in the bone grinder at the Ectofuntus.
6729:
Dagannoth bones are bones dropped by Dagannoth Rex, Dagannoth Prime, and Dagannoth Supreme. They are not obtained as drops from regular Dagannoth, who only drop standard bones.

Dagannoth bones give 125 Prayer experience when buried. This can be increased by offering the bones in different ways:

375 XP when casting Sinister Offering.

375 XP when offered at the sacred bone burner after the appropriate faith level has been achieved.

437.5 XP when offered at a gilded altar with two burners lit.

500 XP when offered at the Ectofuntus in the form of dagannoth bonemeal.

500 XP when blessed and broken down into blessed bone shards and offered at the libation bowl, or 600 XP when offered with a jug of blessed sunfire wine. Virilis outside the altar will exchange noted bones for 10 coins each.

875 XP on average when offered at the Chaos Temple in the Wilderness. Each offering gives 437.5 XP, which is the same as the gilded altars with two burners lit, but with an additional 50% chance to not consume the bones.

Dagannoth bones cannot be turned into peaches via the Bones to Peaches spell.

If players have completed the elite Fremennik Diary, the bones will be dropped as bank notes. This can be disabled or re-enabled by talking to Thorodin.
6731:
The Seers ring is one of the four Fremennik rings , and is dropped by the Dagannoth Prime in the Waterbirth Island Dungeon .

It can be imbued using 650,000 Nightmare Zone reward points or 325,000 with the hard tier of Combat Achievements , 260 Soul Wars Zeal Tokens , or a Scroll of Imbuing , purchased for 200 Emir's Arena reward points, which doubles the magic attack and defence bonuses, and increases the magic damage bonus from 0.2% to 0.5%.

Players can use a chisel on the seers ring to create a seers icon after completing Desert Treasure II . This process requires 80 Crafting (boostable), and is part of the process for creating the magus ring .
6733:
The archers ring is one of the Fremennik rings and is dropped by the Dagannoth Supreme in the Waterbirth Island Dungeon. It increases the player's ranged accuracy and ranged defence when worn.

It can be imbued using 650,000 Nightmare Zone reward points or 325,000 with the hard tier of Combat Achievements, 260 Soul Wars Zeal Tokens, or a Scroll of Imbuing, purchased for 200 Emir's Arena reward points, which doubles its bonuses.

Players can use a chisel on the archers ring to create an archer icon after completing Desert Treasure II. This process requires 80 Crafting (boostable), and is part of the process for creating the venator ring.
6735:
The warrior ring is one of the four Fremennik rings and is dropped by Dagannoth Rex . The Fremennik rings are among the few rings that provide combat stat bonuses.

It can be imbued using 650,000 Nightmare Zone reward points or 325,000 with the hard tier of Combat Achievements , 260 Soul Wars Zeal Tokens , or a Scroll of Imbuing , purchased for 200 Emir's Arena reward points, which doubles its bonuses.

Players can use a chisel on the warrior ring to create a warrior icon after completing Desert Treasure II . This process requires 80 Crafting (boostable), and is part of the process for creating the bellator ring .
6737:
The berserker ring is the strength bonus variant of the Fremennik rings and is dropped by Dagannoth Rex in the Waterbirth Island Dungeon. The Fremennik rings are some of the very few rings to give stat bonuses. Group Ironmen who do not have individual prestige require at least 1 Dagannoth Rex kill before they are able to wear this item.

It can be imbued into a berserker ring (i), doubling its bonuses, by using 650,000 Nightmare Zone reward points or 325,000 with the hard tier of Combat Achievements, 260 Soul Wars Zeal Tokens, or a scroll of imbuing purchased for 200 Emir's Arena reward points.

The berserker ring is one of a handful of rings that provide a strength bonus. Thus, it is commonly used in melee setups because strength bonus raises the player's maximum hit, which is usually more beneficial than accuracy for lowering kill times.

The ring makes the biggest difference when facing monsters with low Defence, but in general even against higher defence targets it will provide better DPS than rings which only provide accuracy bonuses. In specific situations where long-term DPS is not a concern (for example special attacks or boss mechanics), if crush accuracy is needed the Tyrannical ring should be used; for slash accuracy a warrior or bellator ring should be used.

Players can use a chisel on the berserker ring to create a berserker icon after completing Desert Treasure II. This process requires 80 Crafting (boostable), and is part of the process for creating the ultor ring.
6739:
The dragon axe is the second best axe in the game after its direct upgrade, the crystal axe , and is tied with the 3rd Age axe . It is 10% more efficient at chopping logs than the rune axe . [ 1 ]

Like all axes, it is both a weapon (requiring 60 Attack to wield) and a tool (requiring 61 Woodcutting to use).

As with most dragon equipment , the dragon axe cannot be made from raw materials using the Smithing skill.
6741:
A broken dragon axe was a dragon axe that has been broken by an ent from a random event. It can be fixed at Bob's axe shop in Lumbridge for 1,800 coins.

If the broken axe was equipped before being broken, it will remain in the weapon slot. Once unequipped, it cannot be equipped again.

After an update on 11 September 2014 making random events optional, all existing broken axes were automatically repaired.
6743:
The dragon axe head is an unobtainable item that was originally used in the axe handle random event. The axe head would become detached from the player's axe while Woodcutting . To fix their axe, players had to collect the axe head off the ground and reattach it to the axe handle .

As dragon axes were worth over 2 million at the time, players who were not paying constant attention risked substantial losses. Curiously, although a special version of the Dragon axe handle was added in 2006, it was still possible to combine a Dragon axe head and a regular Axe handle.

A similar event used to happen to players while Mining , but with a pickaxe head and pickaxe handle .

Axe heads were removed in an update on 17 July 2007, prior to the release of Old School RuneScape, so have never been obtainable.
6745:
Silverlight is a magical sword used in Demon Slayer and Shadow of the Storm . It is a demonbane sword that is very effective against demonic creatures. As it is a silver weapon , it is also effective against most vampyres . It is obtained by bringing the three Silverlight keys to Sir Prysin during Demon Slayer.

In Demon Slayer, it is used to defeat Delrith . In Shadow of the Storm, it is dyed black using black dye , and later transforms into Darklight when it gets stained with the blood of Agrith-Naar .

It can be mounted on the wall in the quest hall of a player-owned house .
6746:
Darklight is a quest item used in Shadow of the Storm . It is a demonbane weapon created from the sword Silverlight . In that quest, it transformed into Darklight after being used to slay the demon Agrith-Naar , which coats it in his blood.

Both Silverlight and Darklight can be mounted on the wall of a Quest Hall in a player-owned house at 42 Construction .

If lost, Darklight can be reclaimed from Sir Prysin for a cost of 1,000 coins.
6747:
The demonic sigil mould is used to make demonic sigils , which are used in the Shadow of the Storm . Players may obtain a sigil mould from Jennifer , a disciple of Denath , who can be found in the demonic throne room under the Ruins of Uzer .

To make a Demonic sigil, players must have 30 crafting and use a silver bar on a furnace whilst having a sigil mould in their inventory. The sigil is used to summon the demon, Agrith-Naar , in order to defeat him.

The demonic sigil mould is kept after completing Shadow of the Storm, however it can no longer be used to make a sigil, with the response: " There is no need to make another sigil now you have defeated Agrith-Naar. " If lost, it cannot be reobtained.
6748:
The demonic sigil is featured heavily in the Shadow of the Storm quest. The player using it must chant a combination of the words as shown in the Demonic tome to summon the demon Agrith-Naar. If a player does not take the sigils provided during the quest, more can be made by using a silver bar on a furnace with a Demonic sigil mould in their inventory. This item cannot be made after the quest is complete, even if the player still has the mould.

The demonic sigil is kept after completing the quest and with it, the emote can be used to chant the five words in any order you want. This has no effect and does not summon demons, even if the chant is in the correct order.
6749:
The demonic tome , or The Confession of Ellemar , is found during the Shadow of the Storm quest. It's the final confession of Ellemar , a Saradominist mage who, while studying some of the dark arts, summoned a powerful demon from the Infernal Dimensions .

One of its most important uses is that it contains a chant that is needed to "summon" the demon Agrith-Naar (but actually returns him to his realm) during the quest. The chant differs from player to player, but the words used are: Tarren, Caldar, Camerinthum, Agrith-Naar, and Nahudu.

The same chant spoken backwards truly summons the demon at the end of the quest.

After the quest, this book can be found on the shelves in player-owned houses .
6750:
A black desert shirt is an item of clothing that players may find useful when doing the Shadow of the Storm quest . They can make it by using black dye on a normal desert shirt . This can also be done with a desert robe to create a black desert robe .

The quest requires players to be wearing at least three black garments, in order to look evil. Players may already be wearing a desert shirt (since the main part of the quest takes place in the Kharidian Desert ), and black mushrooms can be found locally.

This makes it a convenient choice to make the ink and use it to dye the shirt, though players will also need an empty vial and a pestle and mortar with them.

The black desert robes will not protect players from the desert heat effect. This is stated in a warning message shown when attempting to dye them.
6752:
A black desert robe is an item of clothing that players may find useful when doing the Shadow of the Storm quest . They can make it by using black dye on a normal desert robe . This can also be done with a desert shirt to create a black desert shirt .

The quest requires players to be wearing at least three black garments, in order to look evil. Players may already be wearing a set of desert robes (since the main part of the quest takes place in the Kharidian Desert ), and black mushrooms can be found locally.

This makes it a convenient choice to make the ink and use it to dye the robes, though players will also need an empty vial and a pestle and mortar with them.

The black desert robes will not protect players from the desert heat effect. This is stated in a warning message shown when attempting to dye them.
6754:
The enchanted key is a quest item that is used to locate treasure rather than unlocking things. This key is featured in the Making History quest . It is also used in The Enchanted Key miniquest to locate additional rewards after completing the quest. Once the miniquest is completed, the key disappears.

If the key is destroyed before completing all the treasures, another key can be obtained from the Silver Merchant for 500 coins . However, if the player has received and since destroyed the steel key ring , they will need to re-obtain the ring before the merchant will sell them the key.

This key can be placed on the steel key ring . Note, if placed on your key ring its name changes to "Key" with the description "Key to find hidden treasure!".
6755:
Drozal's Journal is a book that players find in a chest during the quest Making History. After completing the quest, they can find it in the bookcase of their player-owned houses.

The journal details the private thoughts of a Zamorakian individual called Drozal, who never appears in the game. His entries span a period of at least 60 days (see below), and give an overview of his somewhat evil behaviour. This includes poisoning the drinking water of the people of Ardougne (this seems to refer specifically to West Ardougne), causing them to break out in boils.

Since the entries are dated, this journal in itself also tells us the names of two (probably consecutive) months in the world of Gielinor. These are "Bennath" (which has at least 32 days) and "Raktuber" (which has at least 28 days).
6756:
The letter is an item given to the player by Jorral in the outpost north of West Ardougne to deliver to King Lathas of East Ardougne during Making History .

The contents of this letter ask the king not to demolish the outpost as planned. In return for delivering this letter, the king will give the player another letter to deliver back to Jorral.
6757: The letter is a quest item given to the player by King Lathas of Ardougne during the Making History quest. It is given to the player to deliver to Jorral in the outpost outside of north-east Ardougne as a response to the letter that Jorral asks the player to deliver to the king. The contents of this letter guarantee that the outpost will not be demolished by the king.
6758:
The scroll from the Making History quest contains a history of the outpost outside the north-west corner of Ardougne. The scroll is obtained by talking to Droalak, a ghost who lives in Port Phasmatys, and giving his wife Melina a sapphire amulet.

The scroll must then be taken back to the outpost and given to Jorral.
6759: The chest is a quest item used during Making History . To obtain the chest, a player must rub an Enchanted key to find the location where the chest is buried, which is an area south of the Observatory and north of Castle Wars . The key will be steaming hot when the player is standing on the spot where the buried chest lies. Once the player has dug up the chest with a spade , the key is used on the chest to open it and get Drozal's journal .
6760:
The Guthix mjolnir is a two-handed weapon . There are no level requirements to wield this item. To obtain one, a player can either find it during The Enchanted Key miniquest or trade with another player.

Each mjolnir can only be obtained once per account, as the Enchanted key will disintegrate after the player finds all of the treasure. Once this happens, the key cannot be re-obtained.

As its name implies, the Guthix mjolnir is affiliated with the god Guthix . It is tipped with a symbol associated with Guthix, the Tear of Guthix.
6762:
The Saradomin mjolnir is a two-handed weapon . There are no level requirements to wield this item. To obtain one, a player can either find it during The Enchanted Key miniquest or trade with another player.

Each mjolnir can only be obtained once per account, as the Enchanted key will disintegrate after the player finds all of the treasure. Once this happens, the key cannot be re-obtained.

As its name implies, the Saradomin mjolnir is affiliated with the god Saradomin . It is tipped with a symbol associated with Saradomin.

It can be equipped for protection against the Saradomin followers in the God Wars Dungeon .
6764:
The Zamorak mjolnir is a two-handed weapon . There are no level requirements to wield this item. To obtain one, a player can either find it during The Enchanted Key miniquest or trade with another player.

Each mjolnir can only be obtained once per account, as the Enchanted key will disintegrate after the player finds all of the treasure. Once this happens, the key cannot be re-obtained.

As its name implies, the Zamorak mjolnir is affiliated with the god Zamorak . It is tipped with Zamorak's symbol of horns.

It can be equipped for protection against the Zamorakian followers in the God Wars Dungeon .
6766:
Cat antipoison is created by the Apothecary from a bucket of milk , marrentill and unicorn horn dust . It is used in the Ratcatchers quest for curing Pox 's poison. This item can only be obtained during the quest.

This potion uses the same ingredients as normal antipoison , except that milk replaces the vial of water .
6767:
The Book is an item that players gain as part of the Ratcatchers quest. It explains the concept of the Rat Pits activity.

Since the item is not needed for the quest, it cannot be considered a quest item. After completing Ratcatchers, players can find this book in the bookcase of their player-owned house .
6768:
Poisoned cheese is used in the Ratcatchers quest to poison rats in 4 rat holes in the warehouse in the south-west corner of South-east Varrock. It is created by using rat poison on cheese.

When attempting to eat it, the player's character will state: "Um... let me think about this one. No! That would be stupid." Due to it not being consumable, it has no use outside of the quest.

Attempting to place the poisoned cheese in a rat hole after the completion of the quest would result in the message "Putting things in poisoned rat holes isn't my idea of fun."

Using it on a Rat trap (near the Rat Pits) will yield a message in your chatbox saying that it's an over kill and normal cheese will work fine.
6769: The music scroll is used to tell you which notes to play on the snake charm during the final part of the Ratcatchers quest.
6770:
Directions are an item given to the player by Jimmy Dazzler during the Ratcatchers quest. They are used to locate a house in which the player must deal with a rat problem. Choosing to follow them results in the player being teleported instantly to their current checkpoint, initially just inside the garden gates. They cannot be used outside of Ardougne , with your character saying, "These directions are from Ardougne, it would be much easier to find the place if I left from there."

After completion of the quest, players can no longer gain access to the house again, with your character saying, "I don't want to go there again. I barely managed to get out unseen."
6771: A pot of weeds is a quest item used during the Ratcatchers quest. It is made by adding normal farming weeds to an empty pot. Using a tinderbox on the pot will turn it into a smouldering pot, which can then be used to smoke out rats from their holes during the Smokin' Joe section of the quest.
6772:
A smouldering pot is a quest item used in the Ratcatchers quest. It is created by using a tinderbox on a pot of weeds. The player can then use it to help Smokin' Joe clear out rats from their holes.

Smokin' Joe offers his own pot for the player to use. But due to the green phlegm that Joe has coughed up into the pot, the player refuses and decides to make their own smouldering pot for use.

After helping Smokin' Joe, the smouldering pot becomes useless and can be safely disposed of.
6773:
The rat pole is a two-handed weapon that players obtain during the Ratcatchers quest. Players who lose their rat pole can obtain a new empty one by talking to Phingspet and Grimesquit.

Players can attach up to six dead rats to the pole. To attach a rat, the player must first be wielding the pole, and not just have it in their inventory. The player must use their cat to catch rats. When the cat catches a rat, the player has the option to put the rat on the pole. An adult cat or wily cat is recommended for this, as they have a much better success rate than kittens. The rat pole is ineffective as a weapon, serving mostly as a cosmetic item.

6780:
The Menaphite thug is an interface item that can be seen in the Thieving skill guide, representing Menaphite Thugs.

Skill guides are in fact inventories containing a series of items. In order to represent NPCs or scenery in a skill guide, examinable items had to be created for each.

The actual item cannot be obtained by players.
6781:
Bandits are interface items that can be seen in the Thieving skill guide, representing Bandits.

Skill guides are in fact inventories containing a series of items. In order to represent NPCs or scenery in a skill guide, examinable items had to be created for each.

The actual items cannot be obtained by players.
6782:
Bandits are interface items that can be seen in the Thieving skill guide, representing Bandits.

The actual items cannot be obtained by players.
6785:
The Statuette is an icon of the goddess Elidinis and is obtained during the Spirits of the Elid quest. The statuette is said to have been made by Elidinis herself and was given to Nardarine, future founder of Nardah who swore loyalty to Elidinis, after Elidinis offered to save her from the desert heat.

The statuette must be retrieved from the evil genie in the crevice to the west of Nardah. The genie will give the player the statuette if they present him with the sole of the mayor of Nardah.

Once the statuette is returned to the Elidinis Statuette, players may recharge their Prayer there to receive +2 bonus Prayer points as well as a boost to hitpoints, and their special attack energy and run energy will be fully restored as well. Any poison or venom the player has will also be cured.
6786:
The Robe of Elidinis (top) is a robe top that is required in the Spirits of the Elid quest. The robes are created by using a needle on the torn robes found in the shrine in Nardah during or after the quest. The player must wear the robes in order to enter the Water Ravine Dungeon farther north along the River Elid . After the quest, players may use the robes to continue to access the dungeon, although few do.

You can get a new set of robes by searching the cupboard again for the torn robes and then remaking them with needle and thread. You cannot get another set of torn robes if you already have a set of torn robes or Robes of Elidinis in your possession (including in the bank). However, you can use the Drop trick to get extra sets by dropping your robes before searching the cupboard. This gets you a new set of torn robes, which you can mend when you wish.

Wearing the robe top will delay the onset of desert heat by 12 seconds.
6787:
The Robe of Elidinis (bottom) is a robe bottom that is required in the Spirits of the Elid quest. The robes are created by using a needle on the torn robes found in the shrine in Nardah during or after the quest. The player must wear the robes in order to enter the Water Ravine Dungeon farther north along the River Elid .

You can get a new set of robes by searching the cupboard again for the torn robes and then remaking them with needle and thread. You cannot get another set of torn robes if you already have a set of torn robes or robe of Elidinis in your possession (including in the bank). 6794:
Choc-ice can be bought from a local vendor named Rokuh in Nardah, who runs Rok's Chocs Box. They are sold for 30 coins each, and heal 7 Hitpoints when eaten. If a bar of choc-ice is brought while venturing through the desert, it will automatically be consumed when the desert heat sets in, providing both its healing effect as well as quenching the player's thirst. That said, manually eating choc-ice does not reset nor delay the onset of desert heat. Choc-ice can nevertheless come in handy as an alternative to bringing waterskins to the desert. Although waterskins are refillable and provide up to 4 uses each, choc-ice has the advantages of being essentially weightless and serving a dual purpose as a food. This can be particularly useful when scaling the Agility Pyramid.

Waterskins have priority over choc-ices when under the influence of desert heat, and will be consumed first if the player is carrying both in their inventory. Bars of choc-ice can also occasionally melt while in the desert, regardless of any other measures taken to combat the heat, prompting the message: Your choc ice evaporates in the desert heat.

Choc-ices were invented by Rokuh, who sold them to the people of Nardah when their town had become cursed and they could no longer draw water from its wells. Rokuh bought a box imbued with a powerful ice spell, ensuring its contents would never melt, even under the harsh desert sun. He used this magical box (possibly an ice cooler) to store his new invention: a confection made of an iced cream coated with a layer of chocolate, which he called choc-ice. Even after the curse has been lifted from Nardah upon completion of the Spirits of the Elid, its inhabitants remain eager consumers of the treat.

Karamel, an enemy from Recipe for Disaster, drops a choc-ice when she is killed.
6796:

Trying to pick it up via Telekinetic Grab results in the Genie yelling "Hey, no casting spells on my house!"

Bring this scroll to Larxus in the basement of Champions' Guild. Go down the Champion Statue and through the portcullis to fight the Earth Warrior Champion as part of the Champions' Challenge minigame. During the fight, players cannot use prayers of any kind. The skeleton champion scroll is an extremely rare drop from skeletons . It contains a challenge from the Skeleton Champion . In order to be eligible to receive the scroll, players must have at least 32 quest points and be on a members world.

By bringing this scroll to Larxus in the basement of Champions' Guild , players may fight the Skeleton Champion as part of the Champions' Challenge minigame . During the fight, players can only use ranged attacks.

Players wanting to obtain this scroll may wish to prioritise getting the Lesser demon champion scroll first, because when cannoning demons in the Crandor and Karamja Dungeon , occasionally skeletons may be killed as well. It is recommended to turn on collection log notifications in the settings, as to not miss these drops. Additionally, this champion scroll may also be obtained by killing Skeletons in the Barrows dungeons, meaning that collection log hunters may wish to prioritise the Barrows collection log over the Skeleton log. The same applies to Vet'ion and Calvar'ion , which are also able to drop the scroll. It should be noted that both Barrows and the mentioned Wilderness bosses make grinding for this challenge scroll significantly longer, though.

Some of the best locations for cannoning skeletons include the Bone Yard , which is a multicombat area with 14 spread out skeleton spawns in the Wilderness , or the Digsite Dungeon , which is a single-combat area with 10 skeleton spawns. Alternatively, for players wishing to train their Magic or Ranged , the Ape Atoll Dungeon may serve as a useful location for obtaining this scroll, by killing them with Chinchompas or Barrage spells .

Like all champion scrolls, this scroll will be removed from the player's inventory once the challenge has been completed. It is however possible to keep the scroll by dropping it before entering the arena and defeating the champion, then picking it up after the challenge has been completed.

The Graveyard of Shadows in the Wilderness is the best spot for obtaining the scroll, due to the amount of zombies that reside there. While the area is not multicombat , a cannon may be used to speed up kills. Avoid carrying decent gear/cannonballs as player killers may appear.

A good place outside the Wilderness to collect this scroll is the basement of the Wizards' Guild in Yanille (requires level 66 Magic ; boosts allowed). The zombies are in an inaccessible cage and need to be fought with magic or ranged. Runes for Telekinetic Grab are also needed to collect the scroll if it drops here. Players also looking for hard clues can leverage the aggressive and burst-able armoured zombies in Zemouregal's Base , or the stronger variants in Zemouregal's Fort .

6817: The slender blade is an item used in Devious Minds . To create it, the player must take a mithril 2h sword to Doric 's shack just north of Falador and east of Taverley, and use it on the whetstone there. A Smithing level of 65 is required to perform this task. Adding a bow string to it with 50 Fletching turns the blade into a bow-sword ; doing so grants 50 Fletching experience.
6818:
The bow-sword is required in the Devious Minds quest , for the monk at the Paterdomus Temple on the way to Canifis . According to the monk, they learned of the weapon from someone came from the "lands to the far east" , as the design originated from there.

Although the bow sword offers a wield option, the player unfortunately can't wield it, as attempting to do so produces an exclamation that "It's a bow and a sword...how am I supposed to use this?!" Asking the monk to teach the player how to use it produces the comment that "it's a foreign weapon" and "perhaps later" one of their warriors can teach them.

To make the bow-sword, players need to use a mithril 2h sword on Doric 's whetstone, directly east of Taverley to produce a slender blade , then adding a bow string to it. This entire process requires 65 Smithing and 50 Fletching . Players should take care not to die with this item, as it is lost on death and must be created again.

The bow-sword is later used by the assassin to kill several Monks of Entrana and snatch the relic.

The assassin makes further appearances during Secrets of the North and Desert Treasure II - The Fallen Empire , using the bow-sword to fend off his opponents.
6819: The large pouch is created when using the orb on a regular large pouch during the Devious Minds quest. It is used as a teleport beacon for a mysterious character later known as the Assassin to steal a relic from the Entrana church. This item is lost on death.
6820:
The relic is an unobtainable item seen in the cutscene during Devious Minds. Players doing the quest unwittingly help an assassin reach Entrana, at which point he slays the monks who were protecting it and steals it. After the theft, the High Priest tells the player to inform Sir Tiffy Cashien of the events. Sir Tiffy tells the player that he will be "in touch" later. It appears to have a star of Saradomin carved on it.

The item briefly appears on the floor during the cutscene after being dropped by a Monk, before it is taken by the Assassin. However, it cannot be taken by the player.

It is revealed during Desert Treasure II that the relic is one of the three artefacts Azzanadra had been searching for in order to contact Zaros, alongside the Strange icon and the Frostenhorn. The relic has presumably been destroyed by Sliske after the events of Devious Minds.
6821:
An orb is given to the player by the hooded monk near Paterdomus during the Devious Minds quest. The player must put it into a large or colossal pouch to be able to smuggle it to Entrana, and even then they must use the Abyss to enter the Law Altar to be able to enter Entrana. While it is possible to remove the orb from the pouch on Entrana (or elsewhere), the player will not be able to place it on the altar except in the pouch.

Late towards the end of the quest, the player discovers that the orb is, in fact, a teleport beacon used by an assassin to infiltrate Entrana and attack a congregation of Monks of Saradomin during a special ceremony.

The orb is always lost upon death.

Blue marionettes are holiday items that can be obtained as a reward from Christmas events that occur once per year.

Previously, they were obtainable during the 2013 Rare Drops event (from 28 July to 5 August ) as part of a rare item drop . Additionally, during the 2013 Christmas event , after obtaining the various Christmas hats and scarves from Diango 's workshop, players could take five boxes of baubles to a huge tree in the centre of Varrock to acquire all three marionettes.

If destroyed, a replacement can be obtained from Diango in Draynor Village or from the toy box of a costume room , as part of the 2005: Marrionette set. Ultimate Ironmen will be unable to retrieve individual pieces until the full set is stored.

The marionette can be operated to do 4 different moves, which are jump, walk, dance, and bow.

A peach is an untradeable fruit that restores 8 Hitpoints when eaten. It can only be created by casting Bones to Peaches or a bones to peaches tablet on bones . To cast Bones to Peaches, players must unlock the spell as a reward from the Mage Training Arena .

Due to offering a technically-unlimited food source, peaches are commonly used on long training or bossing trips far from a bank , such as in the God Wars Dungeon .

Peaches can also be used in place of bananas in the Creature Graveyard , giving double the amount of pizazz points .

When creating 27 peaches at once using a mud staff and buying bones , the resulting food costs 48.37 per peach and 6.05 per hitpoint healed.

Spells are a series of unobtainable items that exist in the game cache. Presumably, they are used in the Spellbook interface. While originally a Spell item existed for every magic spell, since 2014 this has not been necessary.

In an update in 2018 which reworked the Spellbook, the original scroll appearance of the items was removed.
6885:
The progress hat is a magical, talking hat used to keep track of the player's pizazz points obtained from the Mage Training Arena. If lost, another one can be obtained for free from the Entrance Guardian.

The player can talk to the hat to check the number of points they have in each activity. It replies with a grumpy attitude but will tell the player anyway. The hat has a maximum point storage limit, as follows:

8,000 Graveyard Pizazz Points

8,000 Telekinetic Pizazz Points

16,000 Alchemist Pizazz Points

32,000 Enchantment Pizazz Points

Note that destroying the hat will not cause the player to lose their pizazz points.

6888:
The guardian statue was an item used in the Telekinetic Theatre mazes of the Mage Training Arena. Unlike other items, casting Telekinetic Grab on the guardian statue did not pick it up to the inventory; instead, it moved the item as far as it could towards the player before it hits an obstacle. The spell needed to be cast on the statue to solve the mazes.

The statue had 2 options: observe, which turned the camera into a top-down view of the whole maze, and reset, which returned the statue to its starting point. When the statue reached the end point, it turns into a Maze Guardian which can be used to start the next puzzle.

After an update to make the Telekinetic Theatre room faster, this item no longer exists. Instead, the NPC is used in the puzzle and is moved, rather than the still statue.

A mage's book is a book in the shield slot, requiring 60 Magic to wield. It is tied with the ancient wyvern shield for the third-best Magic attack bonus in the shield slot, behind the arcane spirit shield and the Elidinis' ward (f), but it has no Melee or Ranged defensive bonuses. The mage's book is popular among combat pures because there is no required Defence level. It gives a Magic damage bonus of 2%.

It can be obtained by playing the Mage Training Arena minigame for:

It is the most expensive reward available from the Mage Training Arena minigame. It takes 5.3 hours on average to acquire the mage's book when playing efficiently and using the best spells. Acquiring the book yields a profit of 3,356,160 while using the appropriate staves.

An orb is an item used in the Enchanting Chamber of the Mage Training Arena. They can be made by casting an enchant jewellery spell on icosahedrons, cylinders, cubes, pentamids, and dragonstones found within the chamber. If the player leaves the Enchanting Chamber, all orbs will disappear from their inventory.

Orbs can be deposited in the hole in the centre of the chamber. Every 20 orbs deposited will reward the player with three blood, death, or cosmic runes.
6903:
Dragonstones can be found in the Enchanting Chamber of the Mage Training Arena . They cannot be taken outside of the chamber. They provide pizazz points when any enchantment spell is used on them.

Six dragonstones spawn around the room every five minutes, which players can enchant at any level. Additionally, there is a 1/32 chance of finding a dragonstone when searching a pile of shapes. The stones give more bonus pizazz points depending on the level of enchantment the player uses. Points gained per dragonstone is equal to two times the enchantment level used; therefore, the maximum points available for enchanting one of the six dragonstones is 14 (using Lvl-7 Enchant ).
6904: Animals' bones are obtained and used in the Creature Graveyard of the Mage Training Arena. Bones to Bananas or Bones to Peaches must be cast on them after grabbing them from piles of bones within the arena. On the in-game interface, the number next to the bones indicates how many fruit will be made from each bone when casting either spell. The resulting fruit can be eaten to recover Hitpoints or deposited in the food chutes for pizazz points. Every 16 fruit deposited yields 1 pizazz point and one water, earth, nature, death, or blood rune.

6908: The beginner wand is a one-handed staff , and the weakest of the wands , requiring 45 Magic to wield. It can be obtained by either exchanging pizazz points at the Mage Training Arena or buying one from another player.
6910: The apprentice wand is a one-handed staff and wand that can be wielded with 50 Magic . It can be obtained by either exchanging pizazz points at the Mage Training Arena or buying one from another player.

6914:
The master wand is a one-handed staff and wand requiring 60 Magic to wield. It can be obtained by either exchanging pizazz points at the Mage Training Arena or buying one from another player. It is one of ten weapons able to autocast Ancient Magicks , and one of only four weapons able to autocast both Ancient Magicks and Arceuus combat spells . This means the wand is able to autocast the Ancient, Arceuus, and Standard spellbooks.

A master wand can be upgraded to a Kodai wand if the player has a Kodai insignia , obtained from the Chambers of Xeric .

Infinity boots are magical boots with the third highest Magic attack and Magic defence bonuses available, below the Avernic Treads and Eternal boots . They require 50 Magic and 25 Defence to equip.

Their Magic attack bonus is tied with Aranea boots , while their Magic defence bonus is tied with the silly jester boots , bloodbark boots , pegasian boots , and boots of brimstone .

They can be obtained by playing the Mage Training Arena minigame for:

Infinity boots can be combined with an eternal crystal to create a pair of Eternal boots (requiring level 60 in Runecraft and Magic ), which have increased stats and remain tradeable. The process cannot be reversed.

This item can be stored in the magic wardrobe of a costume room , as part of the Infinity Robes set. Ultimate Ironmen will be unable to retrieve individual pieces until the full set is stored.

As magic equipment, they are generally only recommended if player doesn't have access to the Dragon gloves or the Tormented bracelet , since the former are far cheaper and have identical magic attack and defence bonuses, and the latter provides much higher magic attack and magic strength bonuses.

6945: The sandy hand is an item from The Hand in the Sand quest . It is actually the severed hand of a now deceased wizard scholar named Clarence . If it is lost or destroyed, another can be obtained from Bert .
6946: A beer soaked hand is obtained during The Hand in the Sand quest by giving a sandy hand to the Guard Captain in the Dragon Inn in Yanille . He will drop it in his beer, turning it into a beer-soaked hand.
6947:
Bert's rota is a copy of Bert's working schedule. Bert gives it to the player during The Hand in the Sand quest.

Notice that the rota quotes Bert's wages in "gps", presumably short for gold pieces. This is an alternative term for coins, which is commonly used amongst players but rarely used in official Old School RuneScape text.
6948: Sandy's rota is a quest item found by the player during the Hand in the Sand quest . It contains Bert 's original work schedule. It can be found in Brimhaven on Sandy 's desk.
6949: A magic scroll is an item used in The Hand in the Sand quest. Bert finds it in his house, and after taking it to Zavistic Rarve , the player learns that it is a mind-altering scroll, which caused Bert to not notice when his work schedule was changed but his pay had not been increased.
6950:

Activating the orb when not besides Sandy will trigger the "Nothing interesting happens!" instead of the usual "Nothing interesting happens."

6952: Truth serum is a special potion obtained during The Hand in the Sand quest. Players are able to make it by using a rose-tinted lens on the unfinished truth serum potion on the counter in Betty's Magic Emporium in Port Sarim.
6953: Bottled water is given to the player by Betty in Port Sarim during the Hand in the Sand quest. It is used to make a pink dye, which is needed to make the rose-tinted lens required for the truth serum that is to be used on Sandy.
6954: Redberry juice is a quest item made by the player during the Hand in the Sand quest by adding redberries to a flask of bottled water . The addition of white berries then turns this into pink dye .
6955:
Pink dye is a members -only dye. It is initially created as part of The Hand in the Sand quest by using redberries and white berries on bottled water . It can then be used on a lantern lens to make a rose-tinted lens , which is also required for the While Guthix Sleeps quest.

After completing The Hand in the Sand, players can buy more of it from Betty in the Magic Shop in Port Sarim for 20 coins each. The dye does not appear in her usual store, and can only be bought through dialogue with her.

Pink dyes can be used as an ingredient to train Construction and Farming through building Zen themes , costing only 3GP/XP and giving up to 252k experience per hour in both Construction and Farming. Buying a full inventory of pink dyes from Betty and depositing at the Port Sarim deposit box takes between 1 minute and 45 seconds up to 2 minutes, obtaining up to 800-925 pink dyes per hour.

Pink dye cannot be used to dye a blue or black skirt into a pink skirt .
6956: A rose-tinted lens is a quest item used in The Hand in the Sand and While Guthix Sleeps. Players make it by using pink dye on a lantern lens. Pink dye can only be obtained from Betty in Port Sarim for 20 coins. The lens cannot be made after both quests have been completed, attempting to do so gives the message You have no need for a rose-tinted lens right now.
6957: The Wizard's head is an item used in The Hand in the Sand quest . It belonged to Clarence who was a young wizard in the Wizards' Guild . The head still has a blue wizard's hat on it.
6958: Sand is an item that forms part of The Hand in the Sand quest, and has no use other than that. Players obtain the sand by pickpocketing Sandy as part of the quest. They later give it to Betty to form part of the truth serum.
6959:
A pink cape is a coloured capes which can only be made using pink dye on another coloured cape. Unlike the other coloured capes, it is members -only.

Pink dye is initially made in The Hand in the Sand for a truth serum, by combining redberries and white berries in bottled water . However, Betty in Port Sarim sells it for 20 coins after completing the quest .
6961:
A baguette is a possible reward from the Sandwich lady random event. It is a food item that heals 6 hitpoints when eaten.

Before an update, it was used by the sandwich lady as a "weapon". If a player did not respond to her for some time or chose a wrong food, she would hit them with a baguette, causing the player to be knocked out and then teleported to a random location. Following the update, the sandwich lady no longer punishes players if they ignore her or choose the wrong food item.

The baguette in the form of a weapon was later introduced to players as the stale baguette, a rare item obtainable only from a mystery box. The stale baguette was later also made available as a rare replacement for the baguette from the sandwich lady.
6962:
A triangle sandwich is a food item that heals 6 hitpoints when eaten. It can be obtained from the Sandwich lady random event or by pickpocketing the Tower of Life construction workers: 'Black-eye' , 'Gummy' , 'No fingers' , and 'The Guns' . Notably, Rogue equipment does not give double loot when obtaining this item via pickpocketing. Alternatively, some crates inside the Tower of Life can be searched or telekinetic grab can be used on the sandwich spawn in the Woodcutting Guild .

A triangle sandwich can be placed into a satchel .
6963:
A roll is a possible reward from the Sandwich lady random event . It is a food item that heals 6 hitpoints when eaten.

Although its appearance was updated, the corresponding item in the sandwich lady's food tray still uses its old appearance that resembles bread .
6964:
"Waste disposal" was the name originally given to an unobtainable item that existed in the game cache. It was created to replace the noted form of the shrimps from Tutorial Island . Since items could not be fully removed once created, it was added in a hidden update in 2005 to fill this slot. The actual item was just a copy of a pink skirt.

If players attempted to view the waste disposal in game by using cheating software, they would be given a hex edit detected instead.

Later in 2006, four more waste disposals were added to replace the noted forms of the roll , square sandwich , triangle sandwich , and baguette .

They were all deleted from the game cache in 2006, being replaced by the dragon chainbody, coins, dragon med helm, abyssal whip, and shark from My Arm's Big Adventure .
6965: A square sandwich is a possible reward from the Sandwich lady random event. It is a food item that heals 6 hitpoints when eaten.
6966:
The Prison key is part of the random event involving Prison Pete . It is obtained by popping one of the balloon animals . Although it has a "return" option, the player automatically walks back to Prison Pete after he tells them to. If the correct balloon animal has been popped, this key will unlock one of the barriers. If not, another barrier will be added for you to unlock. Five barriers is the maximum amount. If the key is dropped it will vanish and the player must pop another balloon animal to get a new one.

In order to get the correct key, a player must pull the lever to find out which balloon animal they should pop. They should then pop the animal that looks exactly the same as the image you see after pulling the lever. This will ensure the key fits.

6970:
The pyramid top is an artefact found at the top of the Agility Pyramid course. To obtain it, players have to go through a series of obstacles to reach the top. Once at the highest point on the pyramid, the pyramid top can be seen above the exit doorway. To reach it, climb the climbing rocks at the side of the doorway. Then proceed around the top level and you will arrive at the centre of the south face of the pyramid.

Since the pyramid is situated in the Kharidian Desert , players will be affected by the desert heat , thus bringing waterskins , a circlet of water , or desert amulet 4 is recommended.

Simon Templeton will buy pyramid tops from the player for 10,000 coins each. Using them on Simon will allow you to sell them faster.
6971:
Sandstone is an item that can only be mined from sandstone rocks, requiring level 35 Mining. Sandstone rocks can be found in the quarry south of Bandit Camp, at the Necropolis mine in the Necropolis, and at the Cape Conch mine on The Great Conch island. The first two areas are subject to desert heat, so players mining there need waterskins, the circlet of water, or the Desert amulet 4 to avoid taking damage.

Sandstone respawns quickly, so a player can mine continuously at a group of only 3-4 rocks. Thus, it can be quickly mined for fast experience. When sandstone is mined, the player randomly receives one of four possible sizes of sandstone blocks. The sandstone can be used at the Sandstorm grinder, found just west of the Quarry, to convert un-noted into buckets of sand. The amount of sand produced per sandstone varies, as larger chunks provide more sand. This comes at the cost of 50 per bucket of sand produced, and the player is required to supply their own (noted or un-noted) buckets. While using Sandstorm, it is highly recommended that players bring stamina potions or other energy restoring items, as the player will likely run out of energy when running to deposit.

Players can use 3-tick mining (3t4s) to dramatically increase sandstone yield and experience gained, though it is significantly more intensive. Buckets of sand per hour tends to range from 3000–4500 when mined normally, or 5000–6500 when using tick manipulation, depending on the player's focus and proficiency.

To increase sandstone yield, it is recommended to wear the following mining enhancers, as they have the chance to activate while mining sandstone:

Expert mining gloves guarantees one extra sandstone is obtained from the rock before it depletes.

Celestial ring and Varrock armour 2 or higher gives a 10% chance to mine an extra sandstone of the same size, and can be used together.

Mining cape gives a 5% chance to mine an extra sandstone of the same size.

See recommended equipment for more info.

Sandstone is used in the quest Enakhra's Lament to make part of Lazim's statue: 32kg for the base, and 20kg for the body. Using a chisel, sandstone can be split into smaller pieces. One 10kg block can be split into two 5kg blocks, one 5kg block can be split into two 2kg blocks and 1kg block, and one 2kg block can be split into two 1kg blocks. Attempting to use a chisel on a 1kg block displays the message This block of sandstone is too small to be worth splitting into smaller ones.

6979:
Granite is a rock mined from granite rocks , requiring 45 Mining . Granite rocks can be found in the quarry south of Bandit Camp , at the Necropolis mine in the Necropolis , and at the Cape Conch mine on The Great Conch island. The first two areas are subject to desert heat , so players mining there need waterskins , the circlet of water , or the Desert amulet 4 to avoid taking damage.

A piece of granite (any size) is required in the quest King's Ransom , and two 5kg pieces of granite are required in the quest Enakhra's Lament . In a player-owned house , five pieces of granite (5kg) can be used to upgrade an outdoor menagerie to a volcanic habitat, or two pieces of granite (5kg) can be used to build a volcanic theme in a superior garden . A piece of granite (any size) can be used to recolour the mining pet, the Rock golem .

Unlike sandstone , larger pieces of granite cannot be chiseled down into smaller pieces. Attempting to chisel a 5kg piece outside of Enakhra's Lament displays the message You don't need to craft the granite into anything. , and attempting to chisel down a 1kg or 2kg piece displays the message This block of granite is too small to craft into anything.

Sandstone (20kg) is a quest item used during the Enakhra's Lament quest. It is obtained by speaking to Lazim in the desert south of the Bandit Camp and then giving exactly 20 kg of individual sandstone blocks. The blocks can be mined from the quarry immediately south-west of Lazim.

After giving the blocks to Lazim he will magically join them to create the 20 kg block. The player can then use a chisel on this to make the sandstone body for the statue needed in the quest.
6986: Sandstone (32kg) is a quest item used during the Enakhra's Lament quest. It is obtained by speaking to Lazim in the desert south of the Bandit Camp and then giving exactly 32 kg of individual sandstone blocks. The blocks can be mined from the quarry immediately south-west of Lazim. After giving the blocks to Lazim he will magically join them to create the 32 kg block. The player can then use a chisel on this to make the sandstone base for the statue needed in the quest.
6987:
The sandstone body is a quest item used during the Enakhra's Lament quest. It is obtained by using a chisel to carve the 20kg block of sandstone given to the player by Lazim in the desert south of the Bandit Camp.

The body can then be positioned on top of the sandstone base that the player made earlier in the quest.
6988:
The sandstone base is a quest item used during the Enakhra's Lament quest. It is obtained by using a chisel to carve the 32kg block of sandstone given to the player by Lazim in the desert south of the Bandit Camp.

The base can then be positioned on the floor near Lazim ready to put the sandstone body on top.
6989: The stone head is a quest item used during Enakhra's Lament. It is made by using a chisel on a 5 kg piece of granite. This item cannot be reobtained after Enakhra's Lament is completed.

6997:
The stone left arm is a quest item found in the Enakhra's Lament quest. It is obtained by searching a statue made by the player after it has been dropped through the roof of the underground temple in the desert near the Bandit Camp. Repeatedly searching the statue will also yield a stone right arm, a stone left leg and a stone right leg.

The limbs are used to unlock doors in the underground temple in order to continue the quest.

The item cannot be reclaimed after completion of Enakhra's Lament. If it is destroyed after the quest without having been used to unlock the corresponding door, the door will remain permanently locked.

7001: The Camel mould (p) is a quest item used during the Enakhra's Lament quest. The (p) means positive mould. It is obtained by using a piece of soft clay in a cavity on the pedestal on the upper floor of the underground temple south of the Bandit Camp . The mould can then be used to carve a new stone head from a block of granite . The player should then insert the head into the cavity on the pedestal in order to continue the quest.
7002:
The stone head is a quest item used during the Enakhra's Lament quest. It is made by using a chisel on a piece of granite while the camel mould (p) is in the player's inventory.

The head can then be inserted into the cavity on top of the pedestal on the upper floor of the underground temple south of the Bandit Camp.
7003:
The camel mask is a hat that can be made during and after the Enakhra's Lament quest, although it plays no role in the quest itself. It gives no stat bonuses, and is merely worn for aesthetic purposes.

Players can make one by going to the middle floor of Enakhra's Temple and using a single piece of soft clay on the pedestal in the middle of the room. There is no limit to how many masks you can own.
7004: The Chisel is an animation item released with Enakhra's Lament. It is temporarily wielded during several animations in which the player holds a chisel in their right hand. Aside from this, it cannot be obtained.
7050:
The Swarm is an interface item that can be seen in the Slayer skill guide representing the Harpie Bug Swarm

The actual item cannot be obtained by players.
7051:
The lit bug lantern is an item used in the Slayer skill. It requires level 33 Slayer to wield and must be equipped in order to fight Harpie Bug Swarms .

Level 33 Firemaking and a tinderbox are required to light the unlit lantern. Bug lanterns are worn in the shield slot , but only lit lanterns are effective against Harpie Bug Swarms for completing slayer tasks.

Only the extinguished lantern is tradeable. The version purchased from Slayer masters is unlit by default.

The bug lantern does not qualify as a light source , however it does count as warm clothing while fighting Wintertodt . It can also be used as a lantern for lantern harpooning .

7054:
A chilli potato is a food item that heals 14 hitpoints, identical to the potato with butter used to make it. It is made by combining a potato with butter and a bowl of chilli con carne, which requires 41 Cooking.

Due to its difficulty to obtain, the chilli potato is not a commonly cooked or eaten item unless received as a monster drop. Similar foods such as potato with cheese heal more and are easier to obtain.
7056:
The egg potato is a food item that can be made by players by combining an egg and tomato topping with a potato with butter . This requires a Cooking level of 51, granting 45 Cooking experience, and heals 16 hitpoints. Creating all ingredients from scratch and using them to create an egg potato grants 196.5 Cooking experience.

It is worth noting that potato with cheese provides the same amount of healing, and requires fewer ingredients to make.
7058:
A mushroom potato is food that heals 20 Hitpoints when consumed. 64 Cooking is required to make them by adding mushroom & onion to a potato with butter yielding 55 Cooking experience , 270.5 experience if made from scratch.

Mushroom potatoes are among the highest-healing single-bite food items in the game, but the time required to prepare them from scratch is substantial. Sharks heal the same amount, but weigh 30% more. Tuna potatoes are a more commonly used alternative, as they heal 22 Hitpoints and are simpler to produce, requiring two fewer steps.

Mushroom potatoes are common drops from the Grotesque Guardians and Kree'arra 's bodyguards, making them useful to increase the number of kills that can be done without leaving the boss and banking (especially useful at Kree'arra, due to the time required to access the boss room).
7060:
The tuna potato is a type of food that restores 22 Hitpoints when eaten. It can be obtained by following the steps to combine various items (listed below). To follow all the preparation steps requires level 68 Cooking and grants 10 Cooking experience for a grand total of 309.5 Cooking experience (all the necessary steps).

The tuna potato is the second highest instant-health single consumption food, behind the marlin , alongside the dark crab , anglerfish , bluefin and manta ray . The tuna potato has the lowest Cooking requirement of these, but has the highest weight and is tedious to mass-produce. For a comparison to other items that provide healing, see food .
7062: Chilli con carne is a food that heals 5 Hitpoints. It can be used with a potato with butter to create a chilli potato at level 41 Cooking, providing 165.5 Cooking experience.
7064:
Egg and tomato is a food and cooking ingredient. It can be created by players with a cooking level of 23 by combining a scrambled egg with a tomato . This does not require a knife or range . Consuming it heals for 8 hitpoints.

At level 51 Cooking , it can be combined with a potato with butter to make an egg potato . Doing so provides 45 Cooking experience and does not require a range or fire .
7066:
Mushroom & onion can be created by players with level 57 Cooking . The full process of making mushroom & onion gives 120 experience, but the final step gives none. Eating Mushroom & onion restores 11 hitpoints .

To make mushroom and onion, obtain a knife , mushroom , onion , and two bowls :

Mushroom and onion may be added to a potato with butter to make mushroom potato .
7068:
Tuna and corn is food and a cooking ingredient that can only be created by members with a Cooking level of 67. It can be created by using a bowl of sweetcorn on cooked tuna with a Fletching knife equipped, or while a knife is in your inventory, or by adding cooked sweetcorn to a bowl of chopped tuna , or by using a bowl of sweetcorn on chopped tuna.

It heals 13 hitpoints . Making all ingredients for tuna and corn from scratch provides you with 204 Cooking experience.

It is mostly used as one of the final ingredients for a tuna potato , which heals 22 hitpoints . To make a tuna potato , use a tuna and corn with a potato with butter at level 68 Cooking .
7070: Minced meat is made by using cooked meat on a bowl while having a knife in your inventory. It can be eaten to restore 2 Hitpoints . Minced meat can be made into spicy minced meat by using a shaker of gnome spice or spice on it, which can then be used as bait for catching carnivorous chinchompas . Alternatively, spicy sauce can be used on minced meat to make chilli con carne .
7072:
Spicy sauce is a food and cooking ingredient. It is made by combining chopped garlic with Gnome spice. (Spice or Evil Dave's Spices do not work.) Doing so requires a Cooking level of 9 and grants 25 Cooking experience. When eaten, it heals 2 hit points.

It is commonly used with cooked meat to create chilli con carne at a Cooking level of 11. Doing so provides no experience but the chilli con carne may be combined with a potato with butter at level 41 to create a chilli potato for 15 experience.
7074:
A bowl of chopped garlic is a cooking ingredient that cannot be eaten. It can be made by using a bowl on garlic while a knife is in inventory. It grants no Cooking experience but does not require any Cooking levels to make.

Rather than being edible as a food, chopped garlic instead may be combined with gnome spice to make spicy sauce. To do so, simply use the chopped garlic on a shaker of gnome spice. Creating spicy sauce grants 25 Cooking experience.
7076:
An uncooked egg is a cooking ingredient that players can make by using an egg on a bowl . This food item cannot be eaten.

At level 13 Cooking , a player can cook an uncooked egg on a range or fire . This produces a scrambled egg and grants 50 Cooking experience . The scrambled egg can either be eaten or combined with a tomato to make egg and tomato topping, used in making an egg potato .
7078:
Scrambled eggs are a type of food that restores 5 Hitpoints when eaten. It can be obtained by cooking an uncooked egg on cooking range or fire, requiring level 13 Cooking and granting 50 experience when successful. Players may burn the egg while cooking one, resulting in a burnt egg; the burn rate while cooking these will decrease as players reach higher Cooking levels. It will stop burning entirely at Cooking level 48 on both ranges and fires.

At level 23 Cooking, it can also be combined with a tomato to make egg and tomato topping, which provides no experience but does provide one of the two final ingredients for an egg potato.

Due to all the ingredients being available in a player-owned house kitchen, it can be made by the player that owns the house (POH) (not by a Butler) when battling others in a combat ring.
7080:
Sliced mushrooms are a cooking ingredient made by using a bowl with a mushroom while a knife is in inventory. This grants no Cooking experience but requires no Cooking level .

They can be cooked on a fire or range at a Cooking level of 46 to make Fried mushrooms for 60 Cooking experience . If burnt, the sliced mushrooms instead become worthless burnt mushrooms .
7082:
Fried mushrooms are a type of food that can be obtained by cooking sliced mushrooms on a fire or cooking range, requiring level 46 Cooking and granting 60 experience when successful. Players may burn the mushrooms while cooking one, resulting in a burnt mushroom; the burn rate while cooking these will decrease as players reach higher Cooking levels. It will stop burning entirely at level 90 Cooking on both ranges and fires. When eaten, fried mushrooms heals 5 Hitpoints.

As a cooking ingredient, they can be combined with fried onions to create mushroom & onion at level 57 Cooking. Mushroom and onion can be used at level 64 with a potato with butter to create mushroom potatoes for 55 experience.
7084:
Fried onions are a type of food that can be obtained by cooking chopped onions on a fire or cooking range, requiring level 42 Cooking and granting 60 experience when successful. Players may burn the onions while cooking one, resulting in a burnt onion; the burn rate while cooking these will decrease as players reach higher Cooking levels. It will stop burning entirely at Cooking level 77 on both ranges and fires. When eaten, fried onions heal 5 hitpoints.

It is more commonly used as an ingredient to create mushroom & onion topping by combining it with fried mushrooms at a Cooking level of 57. This does not grant any Cooking experience, but in turn mushroom & onion can be used at level 64 with a potato with butter to create a mushroom potato for 55 experience.
7086: Chopped tuna is created by using a bowl on a cooked tuna with a knife in your inventory. This action does not grant Cooking experience. It is edible and heals 10 Hitpoints, the same as regular tuna. Its other use is as an ingredient in the much sought after Tuna potato. It can be combined with a cooked sweetcorn to form tuna and corn without a knife in your inventory.
7088:
A bowl of sweetcorn (in game name "Sweetcorn") is both food and a cooking ingredient. It can be made by using a bowl on a cooked sweetcorn ; this does not require a knife , nor does it provide any Cooking experience . As food , when eaten, it provides healing identical to cooked sweetcorn , namely 1+10% of total hitpoints, rounded down. A bowl of sweetcorn is called "Sweetcorn" in-game. This may cause confusion among players as raw sweetcorn has the same in-game name.

Its primary use is as an ingredient in making tuna and corn . At level 67 Cooking, with a knife in inventory, members can use a bowl of sweetcorn with cooked tuna to create tuna and corn. This mixture heals 13 hitpoints when eaten, but is usually added to a potato with butter at level 68 Cooking to create a tuna potato that heals 22 hitpoints .
7090:
Burnt egg is the result of accidentally burning an uncooked egg while attempting to make scrambled egg . The burn rate while cooking these will decrease as players reach higher Cooking levels, stopping entirely at level 48.

The burnt egg has no use whatsoever, although it can be emptied to reclaim a bowl . Like most other burnt food, it is tradeable to other players but not on the Grand Exchange .
7092:
Burnt onion is the result of accidentally burning a chopped onion while attempting to make a fried onions . The burn rate while cooking these will decrease as players reach higher Cooking levels, stopping entirely at level 77.

The burnt onion has no use whatsoever, although it can be emptied to reclaim a bowl . Like most other burnt food, it is tradeable to other players but not on the Grand Exchange .
7094:
Burnt mushroom is the result of accidentally burning sliced mushrooms while attempting to make fried mushrooms . The burn rate while cooking these will decrease as players reach higher Cooking levels, stopping entirely at level 90.

The burnt mushroom has no use whatsoever, although it can be emptied to reclaim a bowl . Like most other burnt food, it is tradeable to other players but not on the Grand Exchange .
