7566:
A raw jubbly is obtained by killing a jubbly bird or jubster during, or after, the Recipe for Disaster quest (after having begun saving Skrach Uglogwee).

It can be cooked with 41 Cooking on the spit located near Rantz or the one located at Jiggig. Cooking a raw jubbly yields 160 experience and produces a cooked jubbly. There is no level that Jubbly will "stop burning" except indirectly at 99 Cooking via a Cooking skill cape or a Max Cape.

Raw jubbly is also used in Creature Creation together with a raw lobster to make a jubster.
7568:
Cooked jubbly is an ogre delicacy obtained by cooking raw jubbly on the spitroast located near Rantz in Feldip Hills or the one located at Jiggig, requiring level 41 Cooking and granting 160 experience when successful. Players may burn the jubbly while cooking one, resulting in burnt jubbly; the burn rate while cooking these will decrease as players reach higher Cooking levels.

Eating cooked jubbly will heal 15 Hitpoints, and one is required to complete the Skrach Uglogwee subquest for Recipe for Disaster.
7570:
Burnt jubbly is the result of accidentally burning a raw jubbly while attempting to make a cooked jubbly. Cooking a cooked jubbly requires 41 Cooking, and burning it will become less common with a higher Cooking level. It must be cooked on an ogre spit-roast.

The burnt jubbly has no use whatsoever. Like most other burnt food, it is tradeable to other players but not on the Grand Exchange. Many burnt food collectors find this item more valuable than some other burnt items.
7572:
A red banana is a type of banana found on a tree on the west side of the Ape Atoll . The only way to pick a red banana is to use a rope on the red banana tree while wearing a gorilla greegree . It is used for Freeing King Awowogei in the Recipe for Disaster quest to make a stuffed snake dish fit for a monkey king. It also heals 5 hitpoints if eaten.

After freeing King Awowogei , you can no longer pick the red bananas. When you eat a red banana, you get a message, "You eat the red banana. It's tastier than your average banana."

The red banana can be turned into a sliced red banana by using a knife or any bladed weapon on it. The sliced red banana is used in the Recipe for Disaster quest to stuff the snake used to free King Awowogei . It has no other purpose than to stuff the king's snake, or to use for food while fighting an enemy.

You can only pick a red banana after investigating King Awowogei in the Lumbridge dining room. You are only allowed to pick one at a time, but more can be obtained through the drop trick .
7573:
Tchiki monkey nuts are used in, and only available during, the Freeing King Awowogei subquest of Recipe for Disaster. They are picked from a Tchiki nut bush on the Ape Atoll Agility Course. There is a hole in the ground, inside a partial hut after the rope swing. Climb down the rope to the nut bush, you may only pick one at a time.

They are different from regular monkey nuts. They can be helpful to those who need to heal when doing the Ape Atoll Agility Course. They heal 5 hitpoints, and can be ground with a pestle and mortar to create Tchiki nut paste.

If you return to the three wise monkeys with the nuts and speak to them, Mizaru will swiftly take and eat them, forcing you to go obtain more (this only happens once).

They are considered a delicacy amongst Monkeys, and many legends surround them. One such legend suggests that they are the thing that gave monkeys their superior intelligence, another suggests that they are the food of choice of the Monkey Gods.
7574:
A sliced red banana is the result of using a knife or any bladed weapon on a red banana . When eaten, the sliced red banana heals 5 Hitpoints ; the same amount as the original fruit. The message box also states "You eat the sliced red banana. Yum.".

Sliced red banana used in preparing the snake for King Awowogei during Recipe for Disaster . After the quest is complete, there is no further use for red bananas, nor can any more of them be obtained.
7575:
Tchiki nut paste is made by grinding tchiki monkey nuts with a pestle and mortar. Tchiki nut paste is one of the ingredients of stuffed snake, made in the Freeing King Awowogei subquest of Recipe for Disaster.

Tchiki nut paste heals 5 hitpoints when eaten, giving a message "You eat the Tchiki monkey nut paste. It sticks to the roof of your mouth."
7576:
A snake corpse is used as a cooking ingredient for the food you prepare for Awowogei during the Freeing King Awowogei subquest of Recipe for Disaster. Adding Tchiki nut paste and red banana slices result in a stuffed snake.

It is a guaranteed drop from Big Snakes after starting the subquest. Outside of the quest, it has no use, as the Tchiki monkey nuts cannot be retrieved after the quest.
7577:
The raw stuffed snake is used for Freeing King Awowogei in the Recipe for Disaster quest. It is made from stuffing a snake corpse with a sliced red banana and Tchiki nut paste. The player must then cook it into a stuffed snake on the snake-shaped rock below the Temple of Marimbo.

You must have level 70 Cooking to cook the snake below the pyre.

In the event a player attempts to add unprepared ingredients into the snake, they will end up with an odd stuffed snake.
7578: The odd stuffed snake is created by adding unprepared ingredients to a snake (i.e. an unsliced banana and/or unground nuts ). Had the ingredients been prepared, the result would be a raw stuffed snake .
7579:
A stuffed snake is made during the Freeing King Awowogei subquest of Recipe for Disaster, and requires level 70 Cooking to make. It is made from stuffing a snake corpse (obtained by killing a Big Snake) with a sliced red banana and tchiki nut paste to obtain a raw stuffed snake and then cooked on the snake-shaped rock in dungeon below Temple of Marimbo. A stuffed snake heals 20 Hitpoints. After completion of Freeing King Awowogei, players can no longer procure the ingredients for a stuffed snake, but can cook more from those left over from the quest.

It is suggested to prepare at least three since there is approximately a 1/4 chance to burn the snake on each attempt at level 70 Cooking. The cooked snake is given to King Awowogei to complete his portion of the quest.

When eaten a message in the chatbox will appear, stating You eat the stuffed snake—it's quite a meal! It tastes like chicken.
7580:
A snake over-cooked is the result of accidentally burning a raw stuffed snake while trying to make a stuffed snake in the Temple of Marimbo Dungeon during the Awowogei section of Recipe for Disaster .

Cooking the snake requires 70 Cooking , and burning it becomes less likely at higher levels. It is one of three burnt food items (along with the ruined chompy and spider on shaft ) that do not have "burnt" in their names.
7581:
A hellcat is a special cosmetic variant of a normal cat that can be accessed after starting the Freeing Evil Dave sub-quest of Recipe for Disaster . During the quest, players must visit Evil Dave in his mother 's basement. There they must use their cat to kill hell-rats , which have stolen his mother 's special coloured spices which are needed to make the spicy stew to free him. After your cat catches seven rats, it will become corrupt by the demonic nature of the rats and will suddenly transform into a hellcat. [ 1 ] Alternatively, killing the hell-rat behemoth seven times will yield the same result. Kittens on the other hand, have a chance to turn into hell-kittens on any hell-rat catch.

Note that any existing hellcats may need to be placed in a menagerie, or transformed back in to an ordinary cat, in order for subsequent cats to be transformed. A hellcat can be turned back into a normal cat of the same colour it was before the conversion at any time by feeding it a bucket of milk .

A cat at any stage of growth can be a hellcat, and a cat that has become a hellcat will continue to age as normal. [ 2 ] To get an overgrown hellcat, you must either grow a regular hellcat into one (by having it following you for another 5-6 hours), or have an overgrown cat kill seven hell-rat behemoths. Players who have completed Ratcatchers can also get wily and lazy hellcats, either by using their regular wily or lazy cats to catch Hell-Rats, or by taking an overgrown hellcat to Felkrash and having her train it into a wily hellcat.

7619:
Spells are a series of unobtainable items that exist in the game cache. Presumably, they are used in the Spellbook interface. While originally a Spell item existed for every magic spell, since 2014 this has not been necessary.

In an update in 2018 which reworked the Spellbook, the original scroll appearance of the items was removed.
7622:
The bucket of rubble is a quest item made by the player during the In Aid of the Myreque quest. It is made by mining the rubble using a pickaxe in the basement of the bar in Burgh de Rott , and then using a spade or a pot on the remaining bits of rubble with a bucket in the player's inventory. To empty it, players either have to empty it next to the rubble pile outside the bar, or anywhere outside Burgh de Rott. It has no use after the quest.

There are 15 rubble rocks in the basement and a single bucket can hold three bits of rubble, meaning it will take 5 buckets filled in total to clear all of the rubble.
7624:

7628:
A plaster fragment is found in the In Aid of the Myreque quest when clearing the rubble in the basement of the pub in Burgh de Rott . If the player has no room for it, they will put it into a bucket of rubble and will have to find it in the rubble pile outside of the pub. This is also where it can be found again if the player loses it.

This item depicts the slaying of a vampyre by somebody using the rod of Ivandis , and gives the player a hint of the ingredients required for a Guthix balance potion.
7629:
The dusty scroll is an item that players might uncover whilst clearing rubble during the In Aid of the Myreque quest. It is a letter from Sialathin to his girlfriend Lantania, promising her that they will escape over the River Salve. Once destroyed, it can be reobtained from the rubble pile behind the inn in Burgh de Rott.

This item is not required for the quest.
7630:
The crate is an item that players use while doing the In Aid of the Myreque quest, specifically while restocking the general store in Burgh de Rott . It is obtained from Aurel to hold the items he requires. Those items are ten bronze axes , ten raw mackerel or raw snails and three tinderboxes .

Despite having a destroy option, it can be placed on a table.
7632:
The temple library key is a quest item obtained during the In Aid of the Myreque quest . It is used to access a secret room under the Mausoleum of the Paterdomus , the Temple of Saradomin on the River Salve . Drezel has the key and is located in room containing the secret trapdoor to the library.

This key cannot be put on the Steel key ring acquired from completion of One Small Favour . Once the trapdoor is unlocked, however, it remains unlocked, so there is no need to keep the key afterwards. Using the key on the keyhole after the quest will remove access to the trapdoor, and if destroyed, cannot be retrieved by talking to Drezel, meaning the player is no longer able to enter the temple's library.
7633: The sleeping seven is a book found during In Aid of the Myreque, written by Keorgius Feryis. After the quest, it is available in the bookcase of a player-owned house, or from a bookcase in the Paterdomus Temple Library.
7634:
Histories of the Hallowland is a book found during In Aid of the Myreque . As its name implies, the content of this book is mostly a history of Morytania . It does also raise questions about the origin of Lord Lowerniel Vergidiyad Drakan .

After the quest, players can find this book in the bookcase of a player-owned house , or in a bookcase in the Paterdomus Temple Library.
7635:
Modern day Morytania is a book obtained from a bookcase within the Paterdomus Temple Library during the In Aid of the Myreque quest.

Its content mostly documents the geography of Morytania , listing place names and locations relative to each other. It also warns about dangers such as ghasts in Mort Myre Swamp .

It can be obtained after the quest from bookcase of a player-owned house , or the bookcase within the Paterdomus Temple Library.
7636: Rod dust is what is left behind after using up the 10 charges of a Rod of Ivandis . It remains equipped when the Rod of Ivandis loses its final charge, however after unequipping it cannot be re-equipped. It has no equipment stats, and functions identically to barehanded combat. It has no use at all.
7637:
A silvthrill rod is an item made by using a silver bar , mithril bar , and a sapphire on a furnace with a rod mould in the inventory. It is then enchanted with Lvl-1 Enchant , and dipped it into the River Salve , with a rope , via the well underneath Paterdomus and it will become a rod of Ivandis .

An Enchant sapphire or opal tablet cannot be used to enchant the rod; the Standard spellbook spell must be cast by the player.

As a rod of Ivandis, the weapon has 10 charges in the form of a special attack used to freeze vampyres , allowing you to use a Guthix balance potion on them. If a Guthix balance potion is used, the vampyre will either be destroyed, become angry (stronger, but vulnerable to all attacks) or they will be returned to human form.

It is used during the In Aid of the Myreque quest.

It is used during the In Aid of the Myreque quest.
7639:
The rod of Ivandis is a staff created during the In Aid of the Myreque quest . As a silver weapon, it increases damage against vampyres by 10%. It is also one of the weapons that is capable of killing tier 2 vampyres. Being in the staff weapon category, it can autocast spells. It can only autocast from the Standard Spellbook . Its special attack can be used to fully defeat Vampyre Juveniles and Vampyre Juvinates , at the cost of one of its 10 charges. After all charges are used, it turns into rod dust .

The rod is created by casting Lvl-1 Enchant on a silvthrill rod and then dipping the enchanted rod into the well at Paterdomus using a rope . A silvthrill rod can be created by using a sapphire , mithril bar , and silver bar on a furnace with a rod mould in the inventory .

The rod of Ivandis features in A Taste of Hope , in which it is used along with a chain and an enchanted emerald sickle (b) to make the Ivandis flail . The rod given to Veliaf at the end of In Aid of the Myreque can be reclaimed from him during A Taste of Hope for this purpose. Veliaf will not have a replacement if the rod is lost.

The Ivandis flail and its upgraded versions, the blisterwood flail and the hallowed flail , are some of the only weapons capable of damaging Vyrewatch . The weapon is a reconstruction of the one used by Ivandis Seergaze , one of the Seven Priestly Warriors .
7640:
The rod of Ivandis is a staff created during the In Aid of the Myreque quest . As a silver weapon, it increases damage against vampyres by 10%. It is also one of the weapons that is capable of killing tier 2 vampyres. Being in the staff weapon category, it can autocast spells. It can only autocast from the Standard Spellbook . Its special attack can be used to fully defeat Vampyre Juveniles and Vampyre Juvinates , at the cost of one of its 10 charges. After all charges are used, it turns into rod dust .

The rod is created by casting Lvl-1 Enchant on a silvthrill rod and then dipping the enchanted rod into the well at Paterdomus using a rope . A silvthrill rod can be created by using a sapphire , mithril bar , and silver bar on a furnace with a rod mould in the inventory .

The rod of Ivandis features in A Taste of Hope , in which it is used along with a chain and an enchanted emerald sickle (b) to make the Ivandis flail . The rod given to Veliaf at the end of In Aid of the Myreque can be reclaimed from him during A Taste of Hope for this purpose. Veliaf will not have a replacement if the rod is lost.

The Ivandis flail and its upgraded versions, the blisterwood flail and the hallowed flail , are some of the only weapons capable of damaging Vyrewatch . The weapon is a reconstruction of the one used by Ivandis Seergaze , one of the Seven Priestly Warriors .

7649:
The rod mould is an item first made by the player during the In Aid of the Myreque quest to craft the silvthrill rod , which later becomes the Rod of Ivandis . It can still be used to create silvthrill rods after completing the quest.

It is made by using a piece of soft clay on the coffin of Ivandis Seergaze , under the Hair of the Dog pub in Canifis . After entering the basement of the pub, the coffin is located in the first cave entrance after walking through the secret door. The player can repeat this after the quest to create a new mould, should they lose the one they made during the quest.
7650:
Silver dust can be obtained by grinding a silver bar in the bone grinder in the Ectofuntus. Unlike most ground ingredients in Herblore, silver cannot be ground down by a pestle and mortar. It is an ingredient for the Guthix balance potion, used on several types of Vampyre.

Silver dust is also used in While Guthix Sleeps, as it must be placed on the statue of balance within the Ancient Guthixian Temple along with the other Guthix balance ingredients to receive a balance dolmen.
7652:
A Guthix balance (unf) is an unfinished Guthix balance . To make Guthix balance, players must have started In Aid of the Myreque and have at least level 22 Herblore .

They are made by adding garlic to a restore potion (which is made adding harralander and red spider's eggs to a vial of water ). This gives 25 Herblore experience. Silver dust should be added to the unfinished potion to make a Guthix balance, also giving 25 experience.

Garlic can be added to restore potion of any dosage; i.e., 1-4 doses. The dosage of the unfinished potion, and finished guthix balance, will be dependent on the original dosage of the restore potion. The number of doses for these unfinished potions is not shown in their names, although it will be for the finished potion. The experience for adding the ingredients is the same, independent of the dosage.

For maximum efficiency, it is recommended that restore potions are decanted into 4-dose potions before Guthix balance potions are created. Alternatively, if being made from scratch for the experience, decanting the potions into 1-dose potions would earn more experience at the cost of more materials. It is generally recommended to only make the unfinished variant if one is an ironman, as garlic is trivial to obtain compared to silver dust, which can drastically increase the time it takes to finish. Rather than a "Make-x" menu like most potions, Guthix balance can be made as fast as the player can click. Despite the low XP per potion, one can gain upwards of 125k Herblore XP/hr with moderate focus and a good stockpile of materials.

7660:
Guthix balance potions are modified restore potions used against frozen Vampyre Juveniles and Juvinates . After freezing the vampyre with the Rod of Ivandis , Ivandis flail , or blisterwood flail and using a dose of the potion on them, one of three outcomes may happen: the vampyre will either be destroyed (16% chance), become feral (16% chance), or be returned to human form (68% chance). [ 1 ] The player cannot drink the potion; it is used exclusively against vampyre juveniles and juvinates.

To make this potion, add garlic to a restore potion (made from harralander and red spiders' eggs ) to make the unfinished potion . Then add some silver dust (made by using a silver bar on the grinder at the Ectofuntus ) to complete the potion. This costs 790 coins if buying the 4 dose restore potion, garlic, and silver dust. The potion cannot be made until the player defeats Gadderanks in In Aid of the Myreque and talks to him to learn how to create the potion.

Rather than a "Make-x" menu like most potions, Guthix balance can be made as fast as the player can click. Despite the low XP per potion, one can gain upwards of 125,000 Herblore experience per hour with moderate focus and a good stockpile of materials.

It is a medium task in the Morytania Diary to make a Guthix balance potion while in Morytania .

7668:
The gadderhammer is a two-handed members-only maul. There are no combat requirements for wielding the gadderhammer. To obtain the gadderhammer the player must defeat Gadderanks during In Aid of the Myreque. Even though it can be purchased from another player or the Grand Exchange, it cannot be wielded until Gadderanks is defeated.

This weapon cannot be made using the Smithing skill. It has a very similar appearance and combat animation to the granite maul, and stats similar to an Adamant warhammer.

If lost, the gadderhammer can be bought from Burgh de Rott's general store owner, Aurel, for 3,000 coins.

The gadderhammer does extra damage against shades (similar to the keris versus kalphites), possessing a 25% damage bonus against shades as well as a 5% chance to deal double damage. The bonus damage when employed against shades stacks with the benefits provided by a salve amulet (e) and Void Knight equipment.

Despite its name, the gadderhammer does not act as a replacement for a hammer, unlike the Imcando hammer.
7671:
Boxing gloves are items that can only be obtained from a glove rack in a player-owned house. They come in two different colours: red and blue. They are categorically a claw weapon, and deal a max hit of 12 to other players in the boxing ring. Other gloves cannot be worn while wielding the boxing gloves, and anything worn in the glove slot will be automatically unequipped when putting them on.

When walking with these equipped your character holds them up to their face in a typical boxing stance. They are the only weapon that can be used in a boxing ring in a player's Combat Room, and they are destroyed if a player tries to leave a house with them. Fighting with them in a player-owned house is their only use.

7675:
Wooden sword is a basic weapon that can only be obtained and used within player-owned houses . They are found on the weapons rack in a player's Combat Room for use in that room. Its stats are identical to those of a bronze sword .

Upon leaving the house with a wooden sword, it will disappear.
7676:
A wooden shield can be found in the weapons rack of a player-owned house . It provides no bonuses.

This shield is obtainable through the Construction skill . Players require at least 35 Construction to build a fencing ring , and subsequently need to be able to construct a 'Level 2 Weapons rack' (44 Construction) to obtain this shield from their own house. However, it may be retrieved from another player's weapons rack.

Upon dropping or leaving the player's house, it is destroyed.
7677: The treasure stone is an item used in treasure hunts inside player-owned houses. Its sole purpose is to tell a player how close they are to the hidden Treasure fairy. The item disappears from the player's inventory when they leave the house.
7678: A prize key is obtained after a player wins a game in a Player-owned house (if prizes are offered in the game). It is used to open prize chests that may be found in Games rooms.
7679:
A pugel is the weapon you use on the balance beam , a form of the combat ring in player-owned houses .

It has no wield option, but when stepping on a balance beam, a second pugel will be wielded while the original remains in the player's inventory. The pugel provides no bonuses, and its attack options are the same as when the player is unarmed.

A pugel stick can be obtained by searching an extra weapons rack in a player-owned house. The pugel is a tradeable item within the POH, but disappears once a player leaves the house.
7681:
The Game book, titled Party Pete's Bumper Book of Games, is found on the bookshelves in player-owned houses. It features guides to all of the games the player can make and play if they have a Games room or Combat Room.

The guides include:

Hangman

Fairy Treasure Hunt

Mimic-the-Jester

Elemental balance

Attack stone

Ranging Games (including stick-and-hoop, dartboard and archery game)

Combat (on combat rings)

Prizes (on treasure chests)
7682:
The Hoop is an unobtainable item added with the release of Construction . Although it cannot be obtained, it appears in the animation when throwing at a hoop and stick in the Games room .

It was presumably originally intended to be an obtainable item, that players would have to collect before they could use the hoop and stick. This was removed and players can instead use the hoop and stick at any time.
7684:
The dart is an unobtainable item added with the release of Construction . Although it cannot be obtained, it appears in the animation when throwing at a dartboard in the games room .

It was presumably originally intended to be an obtainable item, that players would have to collect before they could use the dartboard. This was removed and players can instead use the dartboard at any time.
7686:
The Bow and arrow is an unobtainable item that would have been added alongside Construction . Presumably, it would have been used for the Archery target in the Games room . Its player model and examine description are conflicting, as while the player view model and the name features an actual bow and arrow, the examine and the inventory appearance describe an arrow only.

Most likely it was designed to be an obtainable item, that players would have to collect before they could use the Archery target. This was removed, and players are required to bring their own bow and arrows instead.

Unlike the Hoop or Dart , which can still be seen in the animations for their respective games, the bow and arrow does not appear at all in Old School RuneScape .
7688: A kettle is an item used to make a cup of tea in the kitchen of a player-owned house, allowing the player to temporarily boost Construction by up to 3 levels. An infinite number can be taken from any type of kitchen shelf. Players may use this item on a water source to produce a full kettle. If the player leaves the house this item will disappear from their inventory.
7690:
A full kettle is an item used to make a cup of tea in the kitchen of a player-owned house , allowing the player to temporarily boost Construction by up to 3 levels. To make this item, players must use a kettle on a sink or other water source inside a player-owned house. Players can then use this item on a range to produce a hot kettle . Complete directions on how to make tea can be found here .

Note: If a player leaves the house in any way, the item will disappear from their inventory.
7691:
A hot kettle is an item used to make a cup of tea in the kitchen of a player-owned house allowing the player to temporarily boost Construction by up to 3 levels. A player can obtain this item by placing a full kettle on a range and then removing the kettle from the range. Requiring level 20 Cooking , players can use a hot kettle with a teapot with leaves in order to make a pot of tea and gain 52 experience. Complete directions on how to make tea can be found here .

Note: If a player leaves the house in any way, then this item will disappear from their inventory.
7692:
A pot of tea is an item used to make a cup of tea in the kitchen of a player-owned house allowing the player to temporarily boost Construction by up to 3 levels. Players can obtain this item by using a hot kettle with a teapot with leaves. When made, a pot of tea has four doses. Players must use the pot of tea on a clay cup, porcelain cup, or a trimmed porcelain cup producing a cup of tea to make the tea drinkable. Complete directions on how to make tea can be found here.

Note: If a player leaves the house in any way, then this item will disappear from their inventory.

A pot of tea comes in three different colours depending on the shelf that the teapot was taken from. A clay teapot can be taken from Wooden shelves 1 (6 Construction), Wooden shelves 2 (12 Construction), and Oak shelves 1 (34 Construction). Despite the different teapots, the boost only depends on the type of cup used.

Wooden shelves 1

Wooden shelves 2

Oak shelves 1

Players can also ask their servant to serve tea, and if the best shelves in your kitchen are one of those, the servant will serve this type of tea.

Tea from player-owned houses can not be put into a tea flask. If a player leaves the house in any way, then this item will disappear from their inventory.

7752:

It also cannot be used to make a cider barrel (flatpack) .

7756:
The Paintbrush is an unobtainable item that appears in the game's code but does not spawn anywhere, that would have been added alongside Construction .

Presumably, it was intended for use on a banner easel in a Player-owned house Workshop ; it can be seen in unused animations for this purpose. Identical paintbrushes can be seen lying next to the banner easel and the shield easel .

It is possible that the paintbrush was intended to be an obtainable item rather than merely used in an animation, given that it can be turned into banknotes. However, it lacks a proper inventory sprite suggesting it was scrapped early in development.
7758: The Rusty sword is an animation item released with Construction. It is temporarily wielded by the player during an animation when repairing a Rusty sword in the Workshop of a Player-owned house. Aside from this, the item cannot be obtained.
7759: The toy soldier is a wind-up toy made at a Crafting table 3 or 4 in the Workshop of a player-owned house, requiring a clockwork and a regular plank. Level 13 Crafting is needed to assemble the soldier, granting 15 experience. Once wound up, he can be released to walk around the immediate area.
7761: The toy soldier is a wind-up toy made at a Crafting table 3 or 4 in the Workshop of a player-owned house, requiring a clockwork and a regular plank. Level 13 Crafting is needed to assemble the soldier, granting 15 experience. Once wound up, he can be released to walk around the immediate area.
7763:
The toy doll is a clockwork toy. Players can make it at a crafting table 3 in the Workshop of a player-owned house, requiring a clockwork mechanism and a regular plank. A Crafting level of 18 is needed to construct the doll, giving 15 experience points.

Once wound up, the doll may be released to wander around the immediate area. Catching it will yield the player 2.5 Agility experience, though only the player who released it is able to do this. The toy doll also turns around at walls most of the time, while the toy soldier hits the wall and falls over.

Warning: This item is commonly used for scamming, as there are certain areas in the game which do not allow clockwork toys to be released. If a player has an inventory full of toy dolls which cannot be released, they are unable to pick up any more items, effectively locking their inventory.

7767:
The toy mouse is a clockwork item that players can wind up and release, whereupon it will move around on the floor. If the player can catch it before it stops moving, they will gain 3 Agility experience. Despite being a members item, members used to be able to use it on a non-members server. However, this is no longer possible.

Members can make a toy mouse at a crafting table 4 (Construction level 42) in the workshop of a player-owned house. They need level 33 Crafting to construct the mouse, and gain 15 experience in doing so. The raw materials needed are a clockwork (made from a steel bar at any crafting table) and one ordinary plank. Toy mice can also be picked up by Ava's accumulator; the chance of this occurring is 1/2,000.

Cats can chase these clockwork mice. If they catch them they will eat them and the clockwork mouse will be lost.

7771:
The toy cat or clockwork cat is made at a Crafting table 4 in the workshop of a player-owned house, from a clockwork and a regular plank. The toy cat differs from the wooden cat, a quest item which can also be made in the workshop.

A Crafting level of 85 is needed to construct the cat, giving 15 experience points.

The cat may be "released" to follow players around like any regular cat. However, it cannot be fed, catch rats, be petted, be spoken to or be used as a substitute for a real cat in quests. Similarly, the cat may be stored in a pet house in the menagerie of a player-owned house. The clockwork cat does not require any maintenance and will only disappear in the event of the owner's death. If the player attempts to release the cat on a free to play world, they will receive a game message stating "Toy cats do not function on free worlds. If you drop it it will break." and prompt the player to "Drop the cat anyway" or "Keep hold of it". Dropping the cat results in "The toy cat smashes onto the ground".

Toy cats are the only type of pet which can be traded with another player. In addition, players do not have to complete the Gertrude's Cat quest in order to have the clockwork cat follow them.
7773:
Branch is an item obtained by using a knife or an axe on a spiny bush , giving between 2 and 4 branches. They have no use, and are removed from the inventory upon teleporting.

Prior to the removal of the bog event in Temple Trekking , they were used on the bog to see whether it's firm or not.
7774:
Reward tokens are unobtainable items that could originally be obtained from the Temple Trekking minigame. They provided similar rewards to the present day Reward token, but could only be obtained by escorting villagers from Burgh de Rott to the Paterdomus. Players would then have to travel back to Burgh de Rott bank to exchange the token.

In 2007, the minigame was updated with the addition of Burgh de Rott Ramble. They were superseded by new reward tokens which can be exchanged anywhere. As this change occurred prior to August 2007, the original tokens have never been obtainable in Old School RuneScape.

7777: A long vine is a player-made item used to cross a river in Temple Trekking . To make this, players must use a knife on a nearby set of hanging vines to obtain three short vines . The three vine sections are combined by using them on each other, forming a long vine which is then lassoed over a swamp tree to form a rope swing to cross the river. The long vine is lost in process, and therefore cannot be taken outside of the minigame .
7778: A short vine is a player-made item used to cross a river in Temple Trekking . Using a knife on a nearby set of hanging vines yields three short vines. The three vine sections are combined to form a long vine which is then lassoed over a swamp tree to form a rope swing to cross the river.
7779:
A Fishing tome is potential reward from the Temple Trekking minigame , in which players bring followers to Paterdomus or Burgh de Rott .

At the end of a trek, players receive a reward token , which can be exchanged for a number of rewards; should players select the "XP tome" reward option, they will receive a tome granting experience in either Agility , Firemaking , Fishing , Mining , Slayer , Thieving , or Woodcutting , with an equal (one in seven) chance of receiving each tome.

The Fishing tome grants Fishing experience once read. The colour of the tome depends upon the level of the reward token. A higher level reward token will give more Fishing experience.

7800:
Snail shells are dropped by giant snails during the Temple Trekking minigame. These are the default shells; there's also a small chance the snails will drop the perfect snail shell.

This type of snail shell cannot be used to create a snail helmet, and can instead be sold to Barlak in Dorgesh-Kaan for 600 coins.
7801:
Snake hides are obtained from Swamp snakes from the Temple Trekking minigame. When killed, a swamp snake becomes a dead swamp snake, and a player may use a knife on these remains to obtain 2 to 5 snake hides.

The snake hide can be tanned into snakeskin by a tanner, at a cost of 20 coins. Tanners can be found in Al Kharid, the Ranging Guild, Canifis, Forthos Dungeon and the Crafting Guild. Members can craft the snakeskins into snakeskin armour.
7803:
The yin yang amulet is a cosmetic amulet that can be purchased from the Makeover Mage for 100 coins. The amulet is a replica of the one the Makeover Mage uses to change the gender of players.

According to the Makeover Mage, they found the amulet after killing a nest of gazulibirds, and asked Doric to make non-magical copies of the amulet as a result of player requests to obtain the amulet as an item.
7804:
The ancient mjolnir is an unobtainable item that was released alongside A Soul's Bane. Although the name would suggest that it was intended as a reward for treasure hunting with the enchanted key, it is most likely that the mjolnir was supposed to be either a reward from the quest, or a fifth Anger weapon.

It is possible that A Soul's Bane was originally intended to serve as a sequel to The Dig Site. Tolna's Rift is located very close to Senntisten, while Tolna states that he encountered the ruins of an ancient civilisation who used to worship a god, watched over by an evil power. The pattern on the ancient mjolnir matches the one found in the Senntisten temple; therefore it is possible that the mjolnir would have been the original reward from the quest.

For unknown reasons, the mjolnir was ultimately not released, and therefore has never been obtainable in Old School RuneScape.
7806: The anger sword is a weapon obtained during the quest A Soul's Bane used to kill Angry unicorns . The anger sword is one of four weapons to choose from the weapon rack while completing the Anger Room in Tolna's Rift. This weapon cannot be taken from the room, and has a special ability that will automatically activate upon filling the Anger Bar. This special ability will send energy out to all NPCs in the room, instantly killing them.
7807: Anger battleaxe is an item that is used only during A Soul's Bane quest . It is used to kill Angry goblins , and the apparent damage it does is the player's normal damage multiplied by 10, meaning that you will hit three digits frequently. Unfortunately the player won't get any experience when using it. It is found from the weapon rack in the rage room, and cannot be taken out of the room.

7810:
A jug of vinegar can be bought from Fortunato in Draynor Village for 1 coin after starting the Rag and Bone Man I quest ( Note: If you do not see Jug of vinegar in his shop, talk to Fortunato and ask about vinegar). When decanted into an empty pot it becomes a pot of vinegar and an empty jug . Bones from various creatures around Gielinor can then be added to the pot (one bone per pot) and boiled over the fire outside the Odd Old Man 's house. This will clean the bones and they can then be given to the old man to complete the quest.

A total of 35 jugs of vinegar are needed for Rag and Bone Man I (8) as well as Rag and Bone Man II (27).
7811: A pot of vinegar can be made by pouring a jug of vinegar into an empty pot. During the Rag and Bone Man I quest various bones that are dropped from creatures around Gielinor can be added to the pot (one bone per pot, 8 pots total) and boiled over the fire outside the Odd Old Man's house. This will clean the bones and they can then be given to the old man to complete the quest (you don't have to bring them all together in the quest though).
7812:
The goblin skull is a bone dropped by goblins that is on the Odd Old Man's wish-list during the Rag and Bone Man I quest. It must be put in a pot of vinegar, making a bone in vinegar, which then must be boiled on the pot-boiler to produce a polished goblin skull. The polished bone can then be handed in to the Odd Old Man.

After the quest is complete, it is no longer possible to obtain this item.

It is made by using certain one-time drop bones (such as a wolf bone ) with a pot of vinegar . Due to the fact that each bone in vinegar contains a different bone, they do not stack in the inventory or bank.

All the bones in vinegar look identical, but the examine text differs for each one. For example:

Take care not to accidentally empty the pot during your quest or when cleaning the bones. You will be left with only the empty pot , forcing you to retrieve the bone all over again.
7913: The vulture wing is an item on the Odd Old Man 's wish list during Rag and Bone Man II . It is dropped by vultures . After the quest is completed you can no longer obtain this as a drop. The bone must be put into a pot of vinegar and boiled to create a polished vulture wing before giving it to the Odd Old Man.
7914: The jackal bone is an item on the Odd Old Man's wish list during Rag and Bone Man II. It is dropped by jackals. After the quest is completed you can no longer obtain this as a drop. The bone must be put into a pot of vinegar and boiled to create a polished jackal bone before giving it to the Odd Old Man.

7917:
The ram skull helm is a helmet given as a reward, alongside the bonesack , for completing Rag and Bone Man II . If lost, the Odd Old Man will offer a replacement for free.

It requires 30 Defence to wear. The helmet's stats are nearly identical to those of an adamant full helmet , the only differences being the lack of negative Magic attack and defence bonuses , and a slightly higher Ranged accuracy.
7918:
The bonesack is a large sack filled with bones worn in the cape slot . Alongside the ram skull helm , it is given to the player as a reward for completing Rag and Bone Man II . If lost, the Odd Old Man will offer a replacement for free.

Despite appearing to hold bones, the bonesack cannot store any bones.

Due to the item's defensive bonuses it's considered to be armour and you will be denied passage to Entrana while possessing it.
7919:
A bottle of wine can be thieved from the Draynor Village wine stall at 22 Thieving or bought from Fortunato. It is a common loot when thieving from the stall. It heals 14 Hitpoints when consumed, and temporarily lowers Attack by 3.

Players often like to thieve bottles from the stall, then either wait a while or trade with a friend to sell them back to the stall. Because they are worth so much from the store, this allows players to get a decent amount of money using this method.

Some players also use the stolen bottles of wine (and jugs of wine) as means of healing when pickpocketing Master Farmers or stealing from the various stalls in the market. Because bottles of wine heal a good amount of hitpoints, this method allows for an easy-to-use, practically unlimited supply of food.

When consumed, a player will receive an empty wine bottle, which is untradeable and can only be sold to Fortunato for 2 coins. Simply drop it to discard it, or use it on Fortunato to sell it.
7921:
An empty wine bottle is the by-product of drinking a bottle of wine. It cannot be refilled in any way, so therefore it is essentially a useless item.

Fortunato in Draynor Market buys back all empty wine bottles for 2 coins a piece. This option, however, does not come up in any dialogue; you must use the empty wine bottle on him.
7922:
The Al Kharid flyer is an item given by Ali the Leaflet Dropper. He is located at the northern entrance of Al Kharid just above the Al Kharid mine.

On free-to-play worlds, it can be used to access the shop of Ali Morrisane by using the flyer on him. When opening the store this way, one sees members items, but is not able to buy those. Besides this, the flyer is useless.
7927:
The Easter ring is an untradeable item which, when worn, turns the player into an Easter egg. It can be obtained by completing one of the Easter holiday events that occur once per year. This also rewards the player with all other holiday items associated with Easter.

The colour of the Easter egg that the player turns into is based on their current location. [ 1 ] Previously, the ring would randomly pick a colour to transform the player into.

Previously, they were obtainable during the 2013 Rare Drops event (from 28 July to 5 August ) as part of a rare item drop .

If destroyed, a replacement can be obtained from Diango in Draynor Village or from the toy box of a costume room .
7928:
Easter eggs could be dug up out of holes in the ground south of Falador during the 2014 Easter event. They came in six varieties: chocolate (blue with red spots), toffee (green with blue stripes), orange (red with yellow trim), caramel (pink with blue trim), nougat (yellow with red circles), and a very special carrot flavoured egg (blue with bunny head print). Eating them would display the message Mmm... [name of flavour]., with the flavour depending on which type of egg you ate.

By eating one of the special carrot eggs while standing on a hole, players could enter an underground maze filled with hypnotised bunnies. During the event, the Easter Bunny asked the player to help deliver ten eggs to children.

7934:
Field rations can be bought from the Void Knight General Store in the Pest Control hub or Jennifer's General Supplies in Shayzien. They can be eaten to restore 10 hitpoints, making them effectively equivalent to tuna.

Field rations are not commonly used by players either in Pest Control or beyond. Healing is not typically a priority in Pest Control because there is no penalty for death and players respawn immediately with their health and prayer replenished. Outside of Pest Control, there are simply cheaper and more effective alternatives available in greater quantities.
7936:
Pure essence is a raw material used in the Runecraft skill to make all types of runes . They can create the same runes as rune essence as well as cosmic , chaos , astral , nature , law , death , blood , wrath , and any combination runes . Pure essence does not provide any bonus over rune essence when crafting runes lower than cosmic runes; they are however much cheaper.

Unlike runes, pure essence does not stack. Essence pouches can be used to transport additional essence, when collecting or using pure essence to craft runes. Pure essence is one of the most commonly traded items in Old School RuneScape , due to its very high demand by runecrafters.
7938:
" Bob " was the name of an unobtainable item that could previously be found in the cache. It was released alongside pure essence , and was supposed to be an item used in more advanced Runecrafting named "Large essence". For unknown reasons, the large essence was not initially added to the game.

It was graphically updated in 2006 with the release of Lunar Diplomacy , suggesting it may have been planned to be used when Runecrafting astral runes .

The item was removed in 2016 and replaced by dark essence fragments , which are used to craft blood and soul runes.
7939:
Tortoise shells are dropped by tortoises , who can drop up to three shells at a time per kill. They can be sold to Barlak in Dorgesh-Kaan for 600 coins . The shells must be unnoted in order to sell them to Barlak.

Barlak does NOT grant any Crafting experience for this item. He will only grant Crafting experience for perfect shells , a rarer counterpart to tortoise shells.
7941: An iron sheet is made by placing an Iron bar into the press at the Piscatoris Fishing Colony furnace building. It is used to repair the colony wall during the quest Swan Song. It has no further uses after the quest, and can be sold to Franklin Caranos for 20 coins after the quest. It can be made using the Smithing skill, which grants 20 Smithing experience.
7942:
Fresh monkfish are caught during Swan Song. Fresh monkfish heal 1 hitpoint when successfully cooked and then consumed.

Like regular monkfish, players need a Fishing level of 62 to catch fresh monkfish, but using boosts such as a fishing potions at 59 or an admiral pie at 57 may be used.

During the quest, Arnold Lydspor asks players to refill the fishing colony's food stocks. Players must catch and successfully cook five fresh monkfish. Catching a few extra in case some burn while cooking is not a bad idea, as even players with 99 Cooking may burn them. However it is not recommended that players train Fishing during the quest, as these quest-specific fresh monkfish only provide 1 experience for catching and 10 experience for cooking. If eaten players will heal 1 hitpoint and receive the message: It's so fresh that it's got no flavour, and it doesn't heal much health either.
7943:

7944:
Raw monkfish are fish that can be caught with a Fishing level of at least 62 and small fishing net , granting 120 Fishing experience points per fish. Monkfish fishing spots can be found at Piscatoris Fishing Colony (near fairy ring A K Q ) and in the nearby ocean accessible via sailing a raft ; both spots require the completion of Swan Song to fish from.

Monkfish give 10 more Fishing experience per catch than sharks , are caught much faster, and can be fished at a lower Fishing level than raw sharks . This makes fishing for monkfish a very efficient way of levelling up. In addition, cooked monkfish are lighter , so players engaging in a lot of running can run longer carrying monkfish versus carrying sharks. The only downsides are that sharks are more valuable, give more Cooking experience (although that does not matter if the raw fish are sold) and heal more when eating the cooked variant.

Raw monkfish can be cooked at level 62 Cooking, and yield 150 experience if they are successfully cooked. Players will stop burning monkfish at level 92 normally on a fire, 90 normally on a range, 88 with cooking gauntlets , 86 with cooking gauntlets on a range, and 82 with the gauntlets at Hosidius Kitchen before the elite diary bonus. Cooking monkfish gives approximately 200,000 experience per hour at level 90 with no/few burns.

Catching and cooking a monkfish is needed for the hard Western Provinces Diary .
7946:
Monkfish is a type of fish that restores 16 Hitpoints when eaten.

It can be obtained by cooking raw monkfish on a fire or cooking range , requiring level 62 Cooking and granting 150 experience when successful. When cooking there is a chance to fail, resulting in a burnt monkfish . The burn rate decreases as the player's Cooking level increases, and it will stop burning entirely at Cooking level 90 on ranges and level 92 on fires.

When eaten, the message You eat the monkfish. It heals some health. is displayed.

While the Swan Song quest must be completed to fish raw monkfish, there is no such requirement for cooking them.

Catching and cooking a monkfish is a requirement for the hard Western Provinces Diary .
7948:
Burnt monkfish is the result of accidentally burning a fresh or raw monkfish while attempting to make a monkfish . The burn rate while cooking these will decrease as players reach higher Cooking levels, stopping entirely at level 92; wearing cooking gauntlets will stop them from burning at level 87 instead.

The burnt monkfish has no use whatsoever. Like most other burnt food, it is tradeable to other players but not on the Grand Exchange .
7950:
Bone seeds are obtained during and after the Swan Song quest. To obtain the item, one must talk to Malignius Mortifer with an airtight pot (consists of a pot and a pot lid ) in the inventory. When opened a non-attackable Skeleton Mage will appear, perform a random emote , and then die. The animation occurs randomly on 1 tile away from the player.

Players may only own one pot of bone seeds at a time. Dropping the pot of bone seed will result in the magic of the bone seeds escaping from the pot. They cannot be used around Malignius Mortifier, as he will request the player move further away before opening them.
7951:
Herman's book, titled Dionysius: A Legend in his own Lifetime, can be obtained from the bookcase in a player-owned house after the quest Swan Song, or from Herman's desk in the Piscatoris Fishing Colony.

It is a biography of Dionysius, also known as the Wise Old Man. Although it is very brief and many pages are missing, it details several significant events in his life, including his early life in the city of Varrock and some of his more notable actions during his adventures. It also explains some of the legacies he left behind; for example, the reason Saniboch demands payment for access to Brimhaven Dungeon is because Dionysius visited Karamja during his adventures and told one of the villages to do so.
7952:
Axe handles were items created through a random event that caused axe heads to fly off whilst Woodcutting . Heads and handles were either re-attached or deleted to prevent them from becoming discontinued items.

Dragon axes were included in this event. As they were worth over 2 million at the time, players who were not paying constant attention risked substantial losses. Curiously, although a special version of the Dragon axe handle was added in 2006, it was still possible to combine a Dragon axe head and a regular Axe handle.

Axe handles were removed in an update on 17 July 2007 , prior to the release of Old School RuneScape , so they have never been obtainable.
7954:
Burnt shrimp is the result of accidentally burning a raw shrimp while attempting to make a shrimp . The burn rate while cooking these will decrease as players reach higher Cooking levels, stopping entirely at level 34.

The burnt shrimp has no use whatsoever. Like most other burnt food, it is tradeable to other players but not on the Grand Exchange .
7956:
The casket (also known as One-Eyed Hector's chest ) is a quest item reward in Pirate's Treasure . It is found by digging with a spade next to the statue of Saradomin in Falador Park .

A gardener will spawn and attack the player who digs there. The gardener can be killed or despawned by running away. Afterwards, dig in that location again to obtain the casket and complete the quest. It was buried by One-Eyed Hector and the pirate message leads the player to the location of the treasure. The casket can only be obtained one time.

It can be opened to receive 450 coins , a gold ring , and an emerald .
7957:
The White apron is an unobtainable item that can be seen hanging on the wall of Gerrant's Fishy Business. If the player picks it up, they will be given a regular white apron instead. It is therefore designed to serve as an infinite source of aprons, but the actual hanging apron cannot be obtained by the player.

Trying to obtain the white apron via telekinetic grab does not work, with a message stating "It seems to be firmly on the hook. I cannot get that this way."
7958: The Mining prop is a quest item found during the Royal Trouble quest. It is given to the player by a dwarf called Donal in the dungeons of Miscellania castle. The player must use the prop to hold open a crack in the rocks that allows passage deeper into the dungeons. If you use a Tinderbox with it, the message "The tunnel will collapse if you do that!" will appear.
7959: The heavy box is a quest item found during the Royal Trouble quest. It is obtained by killing the Giant Sea Snake encountered at the end of the quest. The box must then be taken to Queen Sigrid to receive a letter that has to be delivered to King Vargas . The box will then stay in your inventory as an empty box - which has no further use.
7960: The empty box is what the player is left with after they hand the contents of the heavy box to Queen Sigrid on Etceteria during the quest Royal Trouble . After the quest is complete, it has no use and can be discarded.
7961:
The burnt diary is a book that acts as a quest item in the Royal Trouble quest . The title of the book (visible when reading it) may variably be Charred diary , Armod's Charred Diary , or Armod's Burnt Diary . It seems to change as the quest progresses, though the item name remains the same.

Players find the pages of the book in the remains of fires in the tunnels beneath Miscellania and Etceteria during the quest. Players put them together to make this book. The item's examine text also seems to change to reflect how many of the five pages the player has found so far.

The diary reveals that Armod and his friends have been causing all the trouble between the two kingdoms. He and his friends intended to cause a war, and then act as peacemakers in reconciling them. This is because they have been unable to complete The Fremennik Trials .

If lost, the book can be reclaimed from a bookcase within a player-owned house .

7966: The letter is used in the Royal Trouble quest . After the player returns the Heavy box full of stolen Etceterian goods, which Queen Sigrid falsely accused King Vargas of stealing, she writes this letter as a formal apology and asks the player to deliver it to Vargas. Players who attempt to read it will be given a choice of whether to proceed or not, since the letter is not addressed to them, however there is no consequence for reading it. It reads:
7967: The engine is a quest item found during the Royal Trouble quest. It is used to repair the lift that takes the player further into the dungeons beneath Miscellania castle. It is also the last item needed to fix the lift. Once the engine has been placed on the engine platform, the player must add 5 coal to it in order to restore the lift to a fully working state.
7968:
The Scroll is given to the player by King Vargas during Royal Trouble. It identifies the players as the official Regent of Miscellania, which allows them access to the Miscellania & Etceteria Dungeon. It is collected by the dungeon guard as the player enters it for the first time, after which players cannot get it again.

The scroll quotes, I, King Vargas, proclaim that the bearer of this scroll is the Regent of Miscellania.
7969:
The pulley beam is a quest item found during the Royal Trouble quest. It is used to repair the lift that takes the player further into the dungeons beneath Miscellania castle.

Combining a beam with a pulley beam turns it into a long pulley beam , and combining this with another beam turns it into a longer pulley beam .
7970:
The long pulley beam is a quest item found during the Royal Trouble quest. It is used to repair the lift that takes the player further into the dungeons beneath Miscellania castle.

Combining a beam with a pulley beam turns it into a long pulley beam, and combining this with another beam turns it into a longer pulley beam .
7971:
The longer pulley beam is a quest item obtained during the Royal Trouble quest. It is used to repair the lift that takes the player further into the dungeons beneath Miscellania castle.

Combining a beam with a pulley beam turns it into a long pulley beam , and combining this with another beam turns it into a longer pulley beam.
7972:
A lift manual, or AMCE Lift-In-A-Box User Manual, is obtained during the Royal Trouble quest. It is a guide to using the Lift-In-A-Box system, which is being used by a number of dwarves in their efforts to expand the caves beneath Miscellania. The Lift-In-A-Box is a product of Ali Morrisane Commercial Enterprises Ltd., one of the many projects of famed entrepreneur Ali Morrisane.

It can be obtained again from the table in the dungeon if lost.

It cannot be stored in nor retrieved from the bookcase of a player-owned house.
7973:
A beam is found during the Royal Trouble quest. It is used to repair the lift that takes the player further into the dungeons beneath Miscellania castle.

Combining a beam with a pulley beam turns it into a long pulley beam , and combining this with another beam turns it into a longer pulley beam .
7974:
The servant bell is an unobtainable item added to the game with the release of Construction. It is identical in every respect to the grail bell, except the name is different. It is possible that it would have been used to summon servants but was removed before launch.

Alternatively, it may have been intended to represent servants in the Construction skill guide. Bizarrely, the grail bell is used for this purpose instead.
7975:
A crawling hand is a rare drop from Crawling Hands , requiring 5 Slayer to kill. It can be stuffed at the Taxidermist in Canifis by using the item on her and paying 1,000 coins, returning a stuffed crawling hand . When players take it to her, she will tell players "That's a very fine crawling hand."

Once stuffed, it can be mounted at a teak , mahogany , or gilded display within the skill hall in a player-owned house , granting 31 Construction and 261 Slayer experience .

The hand can alternatively be sacrificed to the Dark Altar north of Arceuus , granting 2,500 Prayer experience.
7976:
A cockatrice head is a rare drop from cockatrices and moonlight cockatrices, requiring 25 Slayer to kill. It can be stuffed at the Taxidermist in Canifis by using the item on her and paying 2,000 coins, returning a stuffed cockatrice head. When players take it to her, she will tell players "A cockatrice! Beautiful, isn't it? Look at the plumage!"

Once stuffed, it can be mounted at a teak, mahogany, or gilded display within the skill hall in a player-owned house, granting 44 Construction and 294 Slayer experience.

The head can alternatively be sacrificed to the Dark Altar north of Arceuus, granting 2,500 Prayer experience.
7977:
A basilisk head is a rare drop from basilisks and basilisk knights , requiring 40 and 60 Slayer to kill respectively. It can be stuffed at the Taxidermist in Canifis by using the item on her and paying 4,000 coins, returning a stuffed basilisk head . When players take it to her, she will tell players "My, he's a scary-looking fellow, isn't it? He'll look good on your wall!"

Once stuffed, it can be mounted at a teak , mahogany , or gilded display within the skill hall in a player-owned house , granting 63 Construction and 343 Slayer experience .

The head can alternatively be sacrificed to the Dark Altar north of Arceuus , granting 2,500 Prayer experience.
7978:
A kurask head is a rare drop from kurasks, requiring 70 Slayer to kill. It can be stuffed at the Taxidermist in Canifis by using the item on her and paying 6,000 coins, returning a stuffed kurask head. When players take it to the taxidermist, she will tell players "A kurask? Splendid! Look at those horns!"

Once stuffed, it can be mounted at a mahogany or gilded display within the skill hall in a player-owned house, granting 77 Construction and 657 Slayer experience. Alternatively, the head can be sacrificed to the Dark Altar north of Arceuus, granting 2,500 Prayer experience.

Lastly, the kurask head or stuffed kurask head can be used to enhance the ornate undead combat dummy, enabling it to act as a monster that can only be damaged by leaf-bladed weapons.
7979:
An abyssal head is a rare drop from abyssal demons , requiring 85 Slayer to kill. Players may also obtain an abyssal head by placing an unsired at the Font of Consumption; this has a 5/64 chance, and as an unsired is a 1/100 drop, this effectively makes it a 1/1,280 drop per Abyssal Sire kill.

Abyssal heads can be stuffed at the Taxidermist in Canifis by using the item on her and paying 12,000 coins, returning a stuffed abyssal head . When players take it to her, she will tell players "Goodness, an abyssal demon! See how it's still glowing? I'll have to use some magic to preserve that."

Once stuffed, it can be mounted at a mahogany or gilded display within the skill hall in a player-owned house , granting 109 Construction and 889 Slayer experience . Alternatively, the head can be sacrificed to the Dark Altar north of Arceuus , granting 2,500 Prayer experience.

Lastly, the head can be combined with a slayer helmet or slayer helmet (i) to create a red slayer helmet or red slayer helmet (i) , respectively. Doing so requires purchasing the ability Unholy Helmet for 1,000 Slayer reward points .
7980:
Kbd heads are a rare drop from the King Black Dragon . It can be stuffed at the Taxidermist in Canifis by using the item on her and paying 50,000 coins, returning a stuffed kbd heads . When players take it to the her, she will tell players "Three?! This must be a King Black Dragon! I'll have to get out my heavy duty tools -- this skin's as tough as iron!"

Once stuffed, it can be mounted at a gilded display within the skill hall in a player-owned house , granting 223 Construction alongside 200 Attack , Strength , Defence , Magic , and Ranged experience , with players being given the option to decline the combat experience before mounting the heads.

Alternatively, the head can be sacrificed to the Dark Altar north of Arceuus , granting 2,500 Prayer experience. However, players with level 90 Magic can instead opt to use a knife on the heads to obtain three ensouled dragon heads , which will give a total of 4,680 Prayer experience by casting Master Reanimation on each of the heads.

The head can also be combined with a slayer helmet (or imbued) to create a black slayer helmet ; doing so requires purchasing the ability King Black Bonnet for 1,000 Slayer reward points . After claiming the hard tier rewards from the Combat Achievements system, the heads can additionally be combined with the dragon hunter crossbow to create a black variant .
7981:
The Kq head is a rare drop from the Kalphite Queen . It can be stuffed at the Taxidermist in Canifis by using the item on her and paying 50,000 coins, returning a stuffed kq head . When players take it to her, she will tell players "That must be the biggest kalphite I've ever seen! Preserving insects is always tricky. I'll have to be careful..."

Once stuffed, it can be mounted at a gilded display within the skill hall in a player-owned house , granting 223 Construction alongside 200 Attack , Strength , Defence , Magic , and Ranged experience , with players being given the option to decline the combat experience before mounting the heads. Talking to a mounted kalphite queen head in your POH is a task in the Elite Desert Diary . Alternatively, the head can be sacrificed to the Dark Altar north of Arceuus , granting 2,500 Prayer experience.

Lastly, the head can be combined with a slayer helmet or slayer helmet (i) to create a green slayer helmet or green slayer helmet (i) , respectively. Doing so requires purchasing the ability Kalphite Khat for 1,000 Slayer reward points .

A big bass is an abnormally large bass caught while fishing at any big net/harpoon fishing spot, requiring 46 Fishing to catch. Players have a 1/1,000 to receive a big bass in place of a raw bass; catching one results in the game message You catch an enormous bass! instead of the usual You catch a raw bass. If fishing with a fish barrel, a big bass will be placed into the inventory. Additionally, big bass cannot be cooked.

It can be stuffed at the taxidermist in Canifis by using the item on her and paying 1,000 coins, returning a stuffed big bass. When players take it to her, she will tell players "That's a mighty fine sea bass you've caught there." Once stuffed, it can be mounted at an oak, teak or mahogany display within the skill hall in a player-owned house, granting 31 Construction and 151 Fishing experience.

The benefits of Rada's blessing and spirit flakes will cause two big basses to be caught at once if either item activates. The extra big bass will not be counted in the collection log if this happens.

8007:
The Varrock teleport is a magic tablet that can be broken by players to teleport to Varrock . Players can create this item on any regular lectern as long as they have 1 law rune , 3 air runes , 1 fire rune , and 1 soft clay and at least level 25 Magic , giving 35 experience .

This tablet can be made regardless of the player's current spellbook .

As with all tablets, the player does not need to have the required Magic level to cast the spell in order to use the tablet, and the player does not receive any Magic experience upon using the tablet.

Players who have completed the Medium Varrock Diary can switch the location of the teleport to the Grand Exchange by right-clicking the teleport tablet or spell and changing the destination. This applies to all further Varrock Teleport tablets, until the player changes it back, not just the one they are currently using.
8008:
The Lumbridge teleport is a magic tablet that can be broken by players to teleport to the Lumbridge Castle courtyard.

Players can create this item on either an Eagle lectern , Teak eagle lectern , or Mahogany eagle lectern as long as they have 1 law rune , 3 air runes , 1 earth rune , and 1 soft clay and at least level 31 Magic .
8009:
The Falador teleport is a magic tablet that can be broken by players to teleport to Falador .

Players can create this item on an eagle lectern , a teak eagle lectern , or a mahogany eagle lectern . To make it, level 37 Magic , 1 law rune , 3 air runes , 1 water rune , and 1 soft clay is required, which grants 48 experience. A single Falador tablet can be obtained from Marlo's crate , a reward from the Daddy's Home miniquest.

This tablet can be made and used regardless of the player's current spellbook . The user does not need the relevant Magic level to use the tablet, which shares the same rule with all tablets not including Ardougne tablet , house tablet , and Watchtower teleport , as they require quests or having a player-owned house .
8010:
The Camelot teleport is a magic tablet that can be broken by players to teleport to Camelot .

Players can create this item on a Teak eagle lectern , a Mahogany eagle lectern , or a Marble Lectern as long as they have 1 law rune , 5 air runes , and 1 soft clay and at least level 45 Magic , granting 55.5 experience. In addition to using air runes, a player may also use a staff of air to reduce the cost and allow for an extra inventory slot.

This tablet can be made regardless of the player's current spellbook . As with all tablets, the user does not need to have the relevant Magic level to use this tablet.
8011:
The Ardougne teleport is a magic tablet that can be broken by players to teleport to East Ardougne . Using the tablet requires completion of Plague City , however, players do not have to read the Ardougne teleport scroll to use the tablet.

Players with level 51 Magic can create this item on a Teak eagle lectern or better in a player-owned house . This requires 2 law runes , 2 water runes , and 1 soft clay . Creating a tablet grants 61 Magic experience, the same as casting the Ardougne Teleport spell. Elemental staves can be substituted for runes and are recommended when making teleport tablets in large groups at a time.

As with all teleport tablets, using an Ardougne teleport tablet does not grant any experience.
8012:
The Watchtower teleport is a magic tablet that can be broken by players to teleport to the Watchtower . Using the tablet requires completion of the Watchtower quest .

Players can create this item on a mahogany eagle or marble lectern as long as they have 2 law runes , 2 earth runes , 1 soft clay and level 58 Magic , and completion of the Watchtower quest. Elemental staves can be substituted for runes and are recommended when making teleport tablets in large amounts at a time.
8013:
The teleport to house is a magic tablet that can be broken by players to teleport to their player-owned house . Players can right-click to choose whether they teleport inside or outside of their house.

Players can create this item on a mahogany eagle lectern (requiring 67 Construction ) or marble lectern (77) as long as they have 1 law rune , 1 air rune , 1 earth rune , and 1 soft clay and at least level 40 Magic . Combination runes and staves can be used, allowing for two spaces to be freed by using a dust staff . You gain 30 Magic experience for each tablet you create, and each tablet takes 4 ticks (2.4 seconds) to make.

This tablet can be made regardless of the player's current spellbook . As with all tablets (except for the Ardougne teletab ), the user does not need to have the relevant Magic level to use it. All tablets, including this one are an efficient method of earning money and Magic experience. They are very popular with players, as they take up 1 inventory space, making a good 1-click teleport and great for tablet making/Construction training. A good strategy for making tablets is to carry law runes, noted soft clay and coins while wielding a dust staff; make the tablets at a player-owned house in Rimmington , and use Phials to un-note the soft clay for 5 coins per note, then repeat the process.
8014:
The bones to bananas tablet is an item that can be used by any player to change normal bones and big bones into bananas .

Players can create this item on either a demon , teak demon , mahogany demon or marble lectern as long as they have 1 nature rune , 2 earth runes , 2 water runes , and 1 soft clay and at least level 15 Magic . Using a mud battlestaff , staff of earth , or staff of water can make this more cost-effective. The spell is transferred to a piece of soft clay at a lectern in the Study of a player-owned house , creating a magic tablet. The experience for casting the spell is gained at the time the tablet is created.

This tablet can be made regardless of the player's current spellbook .
8015:
Bones to peaches is a tablet that can be used to cast the Bones to Peaches spell. Unlocking the spell from the Mage Training Arena is not required to use the tablet, and as with all magic tablets, the requirements for the appropriate Magic level and runes also do not apply. Using the tablet grants no experience.

The tablet is particularly useful for players who have not unlocked the spell, for players wishing to save inventory space by bringing them instead of the runes required to cast the spell, or for situations where another spellbook is more useful and would still want to cast Bones to Peaches.

The tablets are created on a mahogany demon lectern (or better) in the study of a player-owned house , requiring the player to have 60 Magic and to have unlocked the spell from the Mage Training Arena. Crafting a tablet requires 2 nature runes , 4 earth runes , 4 water runes , and 1 soft clay , granting 35.5 Magic experience. Tablets can be made regardless of which spellbook the player is using. Elemental staves can save runes when creating tablets to make the process more cost-effective.

The tablet cannot be used for the Lumbridge & Draynor Diary task of converting bones to peaches in Al Kharid palace . The tablet also cannot be used inside the Creature Graveyard in the Mage Training Arena unless the Bones to Peaches spell has already been unlocked, players who have not unlocked Bones to Peaches and use the tablet in the Creature Graveyard will be given the message: You have to unlock that spell to use it inside of Mage Training Arena.

When using the tablet, the sound of the spell and the sound of a tablet being broken are played simultaneously; the animation when using the tablet is identical to casting the spell itself.
8016:
An enchant sapphire or opal tablet is the magic tablet version of the Lvl-1 Enchant spell. It can be used by any player to enchant sapphire or opal jewellery. As with all magic tablets, using this tablet does not have a Magic level requirement and grants no experience.

The tablet cannot be used to enchant the silvthrill rod during In Aid of the Myreque , nor can it be used to enchant portal frames within the Hallowed Sepulchre .

This tablet can be made regardless of the player's current spell book. Using a Staff of air can reduce the cost of casting the spell.

This can be an efficient, and somewhat cheap, way to level up Magic, providing one owns a Lava battlestaff ; the staff will quickly pay for itself.

An oak staircase can be built in the rug space and stair space of the skill hall , quest hall , and dungeon in a player-owned house . It requires 27 Construction to build and gives 680 experience when built. The player must have a hammer and a saw in their inventory to build it.

The direction that non-spiral staircases face when built can be chosen from any angle that the room is built, as all rooms, after selection and prior to building, can be rotated with all of the room's hotspots visible. By default, the stairs will slope down away from the direction it is built, and must be rotated clockwise or anticlockwise twice in order to face the player.

Other complications associated with staircases involve adding rooms, or changing the staircase.

A staircase added to a skill hall on the regular level will prompt you to build it "Up" or "Down". When building an "Up" staircase, then attempting to climb the staircase, the construction interface will ask if you want to add a room at the top of the staircase. The rooms available at the top are either a quest hall or a skill hall. If the player builds a "Down" staircase, there is an additional option of building a dungeon stairs room downstairs.

A Rune heraldic helm is a decorative helmet with the colours of the Arrav symbol. Players can paint them on a pluming stand , shield easel , or banner easel in a player-owned house 's Workshop at level 38 Crafting with a Rune full helm and the appropriate crest from Sir Renitee in the White Knights' Castle .

Players need to complete the Shield of Arrav quest in order to create the helm. Players can use a stand or easel in another player's house if they do not have one in theirs.

If a player is killed by another player , the helm will convert into a rune full helm if it is not protected upon death.

A crystal ball flatpack is an unobtainable item . It was most likely intended to be released alongside Construction as a flatpackable version of the crystal ball , but was scrapped before launch for unknown reasons, alongside other flatpackable versions of various furniture in the Study .

Upon the release of the Grand Exchange , players were able to submit buy offers for these items, but as they cannot be made in the workshop 's workbench , the offers were never completed.

When asked about these items in a Q&A stream on 24 March 2016 [ 1 ] , Jagex Moderator Mod John C gave the following response:

While most other flatpacks from the study were removed from the Grand Exchange in an update on 14 April 2016 , the three crystal balls continue to be listed.

Players need to complete the Shield of Arrav quest in order to create the helm. Players can use a stand or easel in another player's house if they do not have one in theirs.

If a player is killed by another player, the helm will convert into a steel full helm if it is not protected upon death.

Players must pay 500,000 coins instead of the normal 5,000 in order to have their crest symbolised as a money bag. Players can use a stand or easel in another player's house if they do not have one in theirs.

If a player is killed by another player, the helm will convert into a steel full helm if it is not protected upon death.

It is visually somewhat similar to a bronze full helm (g).
