8778:
Oak planks are a type of plank in the Construction skill. Each plank gives 60 Construction experience when used.

A single oak plank is worth on average of ~175 experience when used in novice Mahogany Homes contracts (including completion bonus), and 150 experience when used to fix the broken bridges in the Hallowed Sepulchre, also requiring mithril nails.

Oak planks are most commonly obtained from hunting Eclectic implings, fighting Vet'ion/Calvar'ion, and as a common reward from elite clue scrolls.
8780: Teak planks are a type of plank used in the Construction skill to make moderately high level furniture. Each plank gives 90 experience when used in a player-owned house, 123.3 experience when used to make mounted mythical capes, an average of 280.35 experience when used in adept Mahogany Homes contracts (including completion bonus), and 67.5 experience when used to make teak repair kits. Teak planks are worth 225 experience when used to fix the broken bridges in the Hallowed Sepulchre, also requiring adamantite nails.
8782:
Mahogany planks are the highest level planks used in the Construction skill , used to make some of the highest-level furniture. Each plank gives 140 experience when used in a player-owned house , 105 experience when used to build mahogany repair kits , an average of 346.1 experience when used in expert Mahogany Homes contracts (including completion bonus), and 350 experience when used to fix the broken bridges in the Hallowed Sepulchre .

The lowest construction level required to build something in your player-owned house is 40, for either a tip jar or mahogany bookcase .
8784: Gold leaf is an item used in Construction , yielding 300 Construction experience per leaf used when building many decorative items for a player-owned house . It is also used for master STASH units . It can be bought from the Stonemason in south-western Keldagrim or Metla in Stonecutter Outpost for 130,000 coins . It cannot be made by players.
8786: Marble blocks are used in the Construction skill. They can only be bought in Keldagrim from the Stonemason , or in Stonecutter Outpost from Metla for 325,000 coins . Unlike limestone bricks , marble blocks cannot be made by players. Marble blocks are commonly used to build high-level furniture and decorations in a player-owned house , yielding 500 experience per block used.
8788:
A Magic stone is used in the Construction and Sailing skills to build very high level items in player-owned houses and boats; it is also used in the construction of bank chests on various islands accessible through Sailing.

It is available from the Stonemason in south-western Keldagrim or Metla in Stonecutter Outpost for 975,000 coins each.
8790:
A bolt of cloth is used in the Construction skill to build objects such as wooden beds, curtains, and also rugs. Bolts of cloth can be purchased from a Sawmill Operator for 650 coins and provide 15 Construction experience each when used.

One bolt of cloth is used in the quest Making Friends with My Arm, and five are used in the Daddy's Home miniquest.
8792: Clockwork can be made on a Crafting table 2 or better in the Workshop of a Player-owned house. A Clockwork requires a steel bar and level 8 Crafting to make and gives 15 Crafting experience.
8794:
A saw is a tool that can be purchased from the sawmill operator at the Lumber Yard located north-east of Varrock for 13 coins. It is used along with a hammer in the Construction skill to create furniture . A saw spawn can be found in the Varrock estate agent 's house, and they can also be obtained from a tool store .

The Crystal saw , a reward from completing The Eyes of Glouphrie , is functionally identical to the normal saw, but with the added bonus that it allows players to build furniture up to three levels above their Construction level when building furniture that requires both a hammer and a saw.

While the saw cannot be equipped, there is an equipable variant purchased with points earned from Mahogany Homes called Amy's saw .
8796:
The Limestone brick was an unobtainable item released with Construction . It was identical to the real Limestone brick .

Its purpose is unknown, but it was possibly created to be a new item sold at Razmire Builders Merchants. In the same way that the Timber beam was added to replace the now-valuable Plank at the store, this version of the Limestone brick may have intended to be only usable in Shades of Mort'ton .

With the Construction expansion in 2016 , the Limestone brick was deleted from the cache.
8828:
Spells are a series of unobtainable items that exist in the game cache. Presumably, they are used in the Spellbook interface. While originally a Spell item existed for every magic spell, since 2014 this has not been necessary.

In an update in 2018 which reworked the Spellbook, the original scroll appearance of the items was removed.
8837: Timber beams are used in the Shades of Mort'ton quest and Shades of Mort'ton minigame. The beams can be used in place of planks during the minigame. They have no further use outside the quest and minigame.
8839:
The Void Knight top is a piece of Void Knight equipment . It can be bought from a Void Knight for 250 Void Knight commendation points through the Pest Control mini game, although a player must have at least 42 Attack , Strength , Defence , Hitpoints , Ranged , and Magic , along with 22 Prayer to buy and wear one.

It is worn in combination with the other pieces of Void Knight Armour to achieve the designated set effect, depending on which helm is worn. This chestpiece does not interfere with Ava's devices . Unlike the Void knight robe , the Void knight top doesn't have more Magic Defence than its blessed d'hide counterparts (+45, as opposed to a blessed d'hide body's +50).

It can be upgraded into an Elite void top for 200 Void Knight commendation points, although a player must have completed the hard Western Provinces Diary tasks to be able to upgrade it. The top can also be given to the Dodgy Squire in exchange for 200 Void Knight commendation points.

If the player dies a PvP death at level 20 Wilderness or below and the item is unprotected, it will remain in the player's inventory; however, the item will be in a broken, unusable state and must be repaired by using it on Perdu and paying him 180,000 coins .

If the player dies a PvP death above level 20 Wilderness and the item is unprotected, it will be converted to coins. To prevent this, a Trouver parchment and a payment of 500,000 coins can be given to Perdu in order to permanently lock the item. The locked item will remain in the player's inventory; however, the item will be in a mangled, unusable state and must be repaired by using it on Perdu and paying him 500,000 coins.
8840:
The Void Knight robe is a piece of Void Knight equipment . It can be bought from a Void Knight for 250 Void Knight commendation points through the Pest Control minigame, although a player must have at least 42 Attack , Strength , Defence , Hitpoints , Ranged , and Magic , along with 22 Prayer to buy and wear one.

It is worn in combination with the other pieces of Void Knight Armour to achieve the designated set effect, depending on which helm is worn.

It can be upgraded into an Elite void robe for 200 Void Knight commendation points, although a player must have completed the hard Western Provinces Diary tasks to be able to upgrade it. The robe can also be given to the Dodgy Squire in exchange for 200 Void Knight commendation points.

The robe is notable for having a high magic defence bonus, higher than that of blessed and black dragonhide chaps , without having any negative attack bonuses in addition to being non-degradable. The void robe bottom can therefore be a decent alternative to Karil's leatherskirt in melee gear setups aiming to maximise defence against magic.

If the player dies a PvP death at level 20 Wilderness or below and the item is unprotected, it will remain in the player's inventory; however, the item will be in a broken, unusable state and must be repaired by using it on Perdu and paying him 180,000 coins .
8841:
The Void Knight mace can be bought from a Void Knight for 250 commendation points , although a player must have 42 Attack , Strength , Defence , Hitpoints , Ranged , and Magic , along with 22 Prayer . The mace can be used to autocast Claws of Guthix , Crumble Undead , and the Wave and Surge spells . To cast Claws of Guthix, the player must have cast the spell 100 times in the Wilderness Mage Arena . Note that the Void knight mace does not count towards the four pieces needed for the void set effect .

Its stats are relatively close to that of the rune mace , with the main difference being its 20% slower attack speed . It also has +2 bonus in Stab, Slash, and Crush attack, as well as Stab, Slash, Crush, Magic, and Ranged defence, as well as a relative +2 Strength and Prayer bonus compared to the rune mace. Due to its role as one of the weapons to cast Claws of Guthix, it also has a +8 Magic attack bonus. These stats make it one of the only melee weapons in game to have a positive ranged defence bonus, other than the Lunar staff , with +1, and the dragon spear and Zamorakian spear , with +5 and +13, respectively. Unlike other maces, it only has crushing attack styles. Alongside croziers , the hallowed flail , and the 3rd Age druidic staff , it has the highest Prayer bonus of all one-handed weapons.

While Claws of Guthix can be cast and autocast while wearing an imbued Saradomin cape or imbued Zamorak cape , an appropriate cape ( Guthix cape or its imbued variant) must still be worn to receive the damage boost from Charge .

If the player dies a PvP death and the item is unprotected, it will remain in the player's inventory; however, the item will be in a broken, unusable state and must be repaired by using it on Perdu and paying him 20,000 coins .

The mace can also be given to the Dodgy Squire in exchange for 200 Void Knight commendation points.

This item can be stored in the armour case of a costume room , as part of the Void Knight Elite armour set or the Void Knight armour set. Ultimate Ironmen will be unable to retrieve individual pieces until the full set is stored.

The bronze defender is the weakest defender . It is similar to a dagger, but held in the off-hand in place of a shield. The bronze defender is dropped by cyclopes on the top floor of the Warriors' Guild . Entry to the Cyclops room requires a minimum of 100 Warrior guild tokens .

If the player dies to a PvP death and the bronze defender is not one of the player's protected items, it will remain in the player's inventory, but will become broken , which means the item is unusable and must be repaired with 1,000 coins by using the item on Perdu .
8845:
The iron defender is a defender made of iron. It is dropped by any of the Cyclops on the top floor of the Warriors' Guild, but only once players have obtained a bronze defender. It is one of the two defenders that does not provide a strength bonus, along with the bronze defender.

If the player dies to a PvP death and the iron defender is not one of the player's protected items, it will remain in the player's inventory, but will become broken, which means the item is unusable and must be repaired with 2,000 coins by using the item on Perdu.
8846:
The steel defender is the third weakest defender . It is similar to a dagger, but held in the off-hand in place of a shield. It requires 5 Attack and 5 Defence to wield. The steel defender is dropped by Cyclopes on the top floor of the Warriors' Guild , but only once you have obtained an iron defender .

If the player dies to a PvP death and the steel defender is not one of the player's protected items, it will remain in the player's inventory, but will become broken , which means the item is unusable and must be repaired with 2,500 coins by using the item on Perdu .
8847:
The black defender is a defender made of black metal. It is similar to a dagger, but held in the off-hand in place of a shield. It requires 10 Attack and 10 Defence to wield. The black defender is dropped by Cyclopes on the top floor of the Warriors' Guild , but only once you have obtained a steel defender .

If the player dies to a PvP death and the black defender is not one of the player's protected items, it will remain in the player's inventory, but will become broken , which means the item is unusable and must be repaired with 5,000 coins by using the item on Perdu .

The black defender does not count as an "evil" item in Shadow of the Storm despite its colour.
8848:
The mithril defender is a defender made of mithril. It can be obtained by killing cyclopes on the top floor of the Warriors' Guild, but only if you have a black defender in your inventory or if you have shown a black defender to Kamfreena. It is held in the shield slot and requires 20 Attack and Defence to wield.

If the player dies to a PvP death and the mithril defender is not one of the player's protected items, it will remain in the player's inventory, but will become broken, which means the item is unusable and must be repaired with 15,000 coins by using the item on Perdu.
8849:
The adamant defender is a defender made out of adamant . It can be obtained by killing cyclopes on the top floor of the Warriors' Guild with a mithril defender in the inventory or after you have shown a mithril defender to Kamfreena . It is held in the shield slot and requires 30 Attack and Defence to wield.

If the player dies to a PvP death and the adamant defender is not one of the player's protected items, it will remain in the player's inventory, but will become broken , which means the item is unusable and must be repaired with 25,000 coins by using the item on Perdu .
8850:
The rune defender is the 3rd strongest defender . It is used for its attack bonus and is held in the off-hand in place of a shield . It requires 40 Attack and 40 Defence to wield. The rune defender is dropped by cyclopes on the top floor of the Warriors' Guild after showing an adamant defender or better as the player enters the room.

The rune defender's slash and crush defensive bonuses are the same as a black kiteshield , but its stab defence bonus is slightly less than an adamant square shield . However, it is much more commonly used for its melee bonuses, as it gives the same bonus to strength as the toktz-ket-xil (obsidian shield) and has melee attack bonuses. A rune defender is commonly combined with weapons such as a dragon scimitar or an abyssal whip as a result.

The defender is popular among players of higher combat levels due to its offensive stats. It can be considered to be the third best off-hand item for melee training, only beaten by the dragon defender and Avernic defender , and is commonly used in PvP situations as re-obtaining a rune defender is easier than re-obtaining a dragon or Avernic one.

If the player dies to a PvP death and the rune defender is not one of the player's protected items, it will remain in the player's inventory, but will become broken , which means the item is unusable and must be repaired with 35,000 coins by using the item on Perdu . Any ornament kit on the item will also be lost on death.

Players can attach a Rune defender ornament kit , obtained from hard Treasure Trails , to create a Rune defender (t) . This is only cosmetic, and does not affect the defender's stat bonuses. It can be dismantled, returning the defender and ornament kit.

Warrior guild tokens are obtained by participating in various activities found in the Warriors' Guild . They are used to gain entry to the 2 nd floor [ UK ] 3 rd floor [ US ] Cyclops chamber and basement areas, where they can be killed for a chance to drop defenders . To enter the area, players need a minimum of 100 tokens in their inventory.

Upon entry, 10 tokens are taken from your inventory immediately. With every minute spent inside one of the cyclops rooms, 10 tokens will crumble away. When you run out of tokens, you are asked to leave, and if you stay, you will be forcefully teleported out in another minute.
8856:
The defensive shield is a two-handed Shield used during the Warriors' Guild catapult activity . It is acquired by talking to Gamfred on the 1 st floor [ UK ] 2 nd floor [ US ] of the Warriors' Guild. It can only be equipped while standing on the target in the activity room, and moving away from that square will unequip the shield. This activity is a slower tactic of obtaining warrior guild tokens compared to killing Animated Armour .

The shield has 4 defensive options: stab, blunt, slash and magic. Successfully defending against the correct attack type awards a player with 10 Defence experience and 1 warrior guild token . While the shield is equipped, the defensive options interface will appear automatically. The quest, prayer, magic, options, emotes, and music menus will be hidden.

An 18lb shot is an item used in the shot put room, one of the activities that can be found in the Warriors' Guild. The shot put room is located on the 1st floor in the north-east corner of the guild. The northern lane in this room contains a pile of 18lb shot, while the southern lane contains a pile of 22lb shot. For each shot made with these balls, players will receive tokens equal to the distance plus one, whereas shots made with the 22lb shot will reward tokens equal to the distance plus three.

The actual 18lb shot item appears on the ground after being thrown by the player. However, it cannot be obtained; when trying to pick it up, the referee will say "Hey! The Dorgeshuun crossbow is a crossbow requiring level 28 Ranged to equip. It is often used to train Ranged at low to medium levels, due to it having several advantages over similar crossbows with the same level requirements. It has the same attack bonus as an iron crossbow . It has an attack speed that is one tick faster than most other crossbows, and it is able to fire bone bolts , which are significantly cheaper than most other ammunition of similar strength. The fact it is a crossbow also gives it an advantage over shortbows , allowing the use of the shield slot for defensive or offensive purposes. Despite the bone bolts being roughly equivalent to iron bolts in ranged strength, the Dorgeshuun crossbow's faster attack speed means that its damage-per-second output when firing bone bolts is comparable to that of a regular crossbow firing steel or even mithril bolts (depending on the player's exact Ranged level).

It can be bought from Nardok in the Dorgeshuun Mines after the completion of The Lost Tribe quest. Completion of this quest is not required to equip it, however, meaning it can be purchased from other players and used without completing this quest. It can fire metal bolts up to iron, except silver bolts , and is the only crossbow that can use bone bolts . Note, however, that bolts containing unique tips and their (e) variants are not able to be fired from it.

This crossbow is the only crossbow with an attack speed of 5. This makes it 1 tick faster than most crossbows - it is only slower than the Karil's crossbow , the hunters' crossbow , and its upgraded variant, the hunter's sunlight crossbow , which all have an attack speed of 4. It should be noted that the Karil's crossbow is two-handed.

Weighing only 2.267kg, it is also the lightest crossbow in the game, making it ideal to use along with the mithril grapple when conservation of run energy is necessary, such as in the Hallowed Sepulchre .
8882:
Bone bolts are ammunition that can be bought after completion of The Lost Tribe quest. They can only be used with the Dorgeshuun crossbow, a popular choice for training ranged due to its faster speed than regular crossbows. Unlike other ammunition, it requires 28 Ranged to equip.

Due to their low price and ease of access from Nardok's Bone Weapons, having a base price of only 3 coins each, bone bolts are generally considered a very cost-effective method of training Ranged at lower levels. Assuming non-stop use of the Dorgeshuun crossbow on rapid, the player can fire 1,500 bolts per hour, which only costs 10,500 coins per hour if buying the bolts from the Grand Exchange.

Despite the bone bolts being roughly equivalent to iron bolts in ranged strength, the Dorgeshuun crossbow's faster attack speed means that its damage-per-second output when firing bone bolts is comparable to that of a regular crossbow firing steel or even mithril bolts (depending on the player's exact Ranged level).

If not buying the bolts from the Grand Exchange, buying bone bolt packs is recommended in order to save costs, since the cost per bolt can rapidly increase when buying the bolts individually. As with other bolts, their ranged strength is higher than most arrows with similar level requirements. The Dorgeshuun crossbow is 1 tick (0.6 seconds) slower to fire than shortbows, which balances out the higher strength of the bolts.

Despite not being made of metal, bone bolts do function with Ava's devices obtained from the completion of Animal Magnetism.
8887:
Zanik is an unobtainable item that may be placed into the player's inventory when Zanik is following the player during Death to the Dorgeshuun, Another Slice of H.A.M., and Land of the Goblins. Zanik technically functions as a pet during these quests, although the item version is never meant to be seen.

Three different versions exist in Death to the Dorgeshuun. Aside from the default variant, there are versions for when Zanik is wearing H.A.M. robes, and during the final showdown when she equips a Dorgeshuun crossbow. A fourth variant was added with Another Slice of H.A.M.

This item only exists as every follower NPC is required to be tied to an item. If the items are ever obtained however, dropping them will just cause the item to appear on the floor, rather than causing the pet to reappear.

8890: Coins in the Mage Training Arena are produced by using alchemy spells ( High Level Alchemy or Low Level Alchemy ) in the alchemist's section of the minigame. 8901:
The black mask is a unique mask worn in the head slot. The mask has the same stats as a black med helm . It provides a player 16.67% [ 1 ] Attack and Strength boost against all monsters on the player's current Slayer task . It requires 20 Strength, 10 Defence , and 40 Combat to equip.

The black mask is a rare drop from cave horrors . Killing them requires 58 Slayer and completion of the Cabin Fever quest to access the island they live on, Mos Le'Harmless .

When charged, the mask has a passive ability to lower an attacking monster's Defence by 2 + 7% rounded down, using one charge in the process. In order for the mask to activate the following requirement must be met:

There is a 1/10 chance to attempt triggering the effect. [ 2 ] If it succeeds, then it rolls your magic accuracy vs the NPC's magic defence. [ 3 ] Once the mask has been drained of all 10 charges, there is no way to recharge it; however, the Attack and Strength boosts remain.

For 1,250,000 Nightmare Zone points or 625,000 with the hard tier of Combat Achievements , 500 Soul Wars Zeal Tokens , or a scroll of imbuing purchased for 200 PvP Arena points , players can imbue a black mask, making it into a black mask (i) , which provides a 15% Ranged and Magic accuracy and damage boost in addition to its melee boost. Imbuing a charged black mask gives an imbued version with the same number of charges, though the imbued version loses charges similarly to the unimbued mask.

The black mask is a rare drop from cave horrors . Killing them requires 58 Slayer and completion of the Cabin Fever quest to access the island they live on, Mos Le'Harmless .

When charged, the mask has a passive ability to lower an attacking monster's Defence by 2 + 7% rounded down, using one charge in the process. In order for the mask to activate the following requirement must be met:

There is a 1/10 chance to attempt triggering the effect. [ 2 ] If it succeeds, then it rolls your magic accuracy vs the NPC's magic defence. [ 3 ] Once the mask has been drained of all 10 charges, there is no way to recharge it; however, the Attack and Strength boosts remain.

For 1,250,000 Nightmare Zone points or 625,000 with the hard tier of Combat Achievements , 500 Soul Wars Zeal Tokens , or a scroll of imbuing purchased for 200 PvP Arena points , players can imbue a black mask, making it into a black mask (i) , which provides a 15% Ranged and Magic accuracy and damage boost in addition to its melee boost. Imbuing a charged black mask gives an imbued version with the same number of charges, though the imbued version loses charges similarly to the unimbued mask.

The witchwood icon is a piece of Slayer equipment used to decrease the effectiveness of the screams of Cave horrors found in the Mos Le'Harmless Cave . The icon is worn around the neck and requires a Slayer level of 35 to equip, although players must have 58 Slayer to be able to kill cave horrors.

If the icon is not worn, the special scream attack from cave horrors is guaranteed to deal 10% of the player's total Hitpoints . Wearing the icon does not negate all damage from the scream, it instead causes the scream attack to roll as a regular attack. Jungle horrors do not use the special scream attack, as such, the icon is not necessary to fight them.

It can be purchased from any Slayer Master for 900 coins but cannot be traded with other players. The Slayer Masters created these from witchwood trees , an extinct species of tree that once grew in Gielinor .

Protect from Melee also provides complete protection against screams, serving as an acceptable substitution for the icon.

The crabclaw hook is made by talking to Patchy on Mos Le'Harmless while carrying a crab claw and pirate's hook . It costs 500 coins to sew together and 600 to separate them. The crabclaw and hook occupy only the glove slot when worn.

While players cannot equip claws whilst having a crab claw equipped, players can do so whilst wearing crabclaw hooks.

The crabclaw hook cannot be used in place of the crab claw for the elite clue emote step on Wintumber Island or stored in the respective elite STASH unit.

When wearing the crabclaw hook, players can perform an enhanced crab dance emote, which adds additional light and confetti effects.
8930:
The pipe section is an item used in the Trouble Brewing minigame to repair sabotaged bamboo pipes and water pumps . At the start of each game, 10 pipe sections are stocked in the tool workbench , and crafted pipe sections can be used on the workbench to store them within it.

Pipe sections can be crafted by using a regular log on the large workbench . Logs can be gathered from the log store within your team's base, or by chopping down the various trees around your base with an axe . Scrapey tree logs cannot be crafted into pipe sections. Creating a pipe section rewards 12.5 crafting experience, and using it to repair something rewards the same amount.

It can take up to three patches to repair a hopper, depending on how long it was on fire for. At the start of each game, 10 lumber patches are stocked in the tool workbench , and crafted lumber patches can be used on the workbench to store them within it.

Lumber patches can be crafted by using a regular log on the large workbench . Logs can be gathered from the log store within your team's base, or by chopping down the various trees around your base with an axe . Scrapey tree logs cannot be crafted into lumber patches. Creating a lumber patch rewards 12.5 crafting experience, and using it to repair a hopper rewards the same amount.
8934: Scrapey tree logs are items used in the Trouble Brewing minigame. They can be obtained by chopping the scrapey trees found within the brewing area. To use the logs to produce rum, players must use a knife on them, which will yield scrapey bark. Doing so has a 1/50 chance to cause the player to become diseased.

Blue flowers are an item obtained within the Trouble Brewing minigame. Blue flowers and red flowers are found in the minigame outside the opposite team's base. Team members must collect their team's coloured flowers and place them in the kettle in order to make their team's coloured water which is then used as an ingredient in the rum.

Players can only carry 5 flowers at a time, attempting to gather more will yield the message: You have plenty of those.

These flowers cannot be taken out of the minigame but are tradeable within, and have a trade value of 1 coin. This item cannot be picked up using Telekinetic Grab, attempting to do so will yield the message: I can't use Telekinetic Grab on this object.

Upon drinking the rum, the player will become intoxicated and collapse, after which point they will awaken outside the lobby of the minigame. The rum can not be consumed beyond level 20 Wilderness .

Attempting to drink the rum while already at Trouble Brewing will result in the message: It hardly seems worth drinking the 'rum' here.

A monkey is used in Trouble Brewing to gather bitternuts. They are found in the island in between the two bases, and they can be caught awarding the player with 15 Agility and Hunter experience. To use it to obtain bitternuts, a bowl of red water or a bowl of blue water must be used on the monkey, making it a red monkey or a blue monkey. The dyed monkey can then be used on a Bitternut Tree, and it will throw down a bitternut to the player after some time if the player is within range of the tree. If a monkey from the opposing team is in the tree as well, the two monkeys will fight, only one will throw down a bitternut, and the other will disappear.

With completion of Monkey Madness II or a m'speak amulet, the player can "Anger the monkey" or "Caution the monkey" when talking to it. An angry monkey will grab the nut quickly, but will always lose a fight if there is one. A cautious monkey will take longer to grab the nut, but will always win the fight. A player can have a maximum of two monkeys, and a team can have a maximum of twelve. If the player chooses to release the monkey, a level 1 Monkey will spawn.

Pieces of eight were a currency earned from the Trouble Brewing minigame used to buy rewards from Honest Jimmy's House of Stuff. During a game of Trouble Brewing, each resource deposited (i.e. buckets of water, bowls of coloured water, etc.) and opponent equipment burned (i.e. pipes, pump, etc.) would result in a piece of eight being awarded at the end of the game, up to 100 pieces of eight. Each bottle of rum deposited by the player's team gave 2 extra pieces to each player on the team at the end of the game. Pieces of eight awarded for bottling rum did not count towards the 100 pieces of eight limit for resources and sabotage, making it possible for players to earn more than 100 pieces of eight in a single game.

The amount received at the end of a game was not dependent on who was winning.

It took approximately 8 hours to complete a full outfit, the average amount earned was 100+ with each match being 20 minutes long.

In total, 39,590 pieces of eight were required to buy everything in the shop. It was not possible to sell items back to the store, so in order to fill out the collection log, at least this amount of pieces of eight were needed.

Pieces of eight were discontinued in an update on 23 May 2024, and any players with the original pieces of eight had it automatically converted to a virtual currency also named pieces of eight that is stored as a variable on a player's account. A "Count" option was also added to the original item to convert any leftover pieces into the new virtual currency.

8972: A bowl of red water is an item obtained within the minigame Trouble Brewing. It is made by using a bowl on the kettle with red flowers in it. 8976:
Bitternuts are items used in the Trouble Brewing minigame. Players can obtain the nuts from the bitternut trees found within the minigame on Mos Le'Harmless using monkeys, which are caught in the same area.

In order to retrieve a bitternut, the player must first dye a monkey in the colour of their team using red water or blue water, obtained by using either red or blue flowers on the kettle in your team's base and then using an empty bowl on the kettle. They then can use the monkey with the Bitternut Tree.

Additionally, if you have a Monkeyspeak amulet or have completed Monkey Madness II, you can alter the strategy used. You can choose to either make the monkey angry by taunting it, or caution him. By making him angry, he'll be more inclined to get up the tree as fast as possible and start pelting you with bitternuts, speeding up the time before you get a nut. If you tell him to be careful, he'll take a little bit longer, but will be more aware of other monkeys and will be more likely to win in a confrontation. This is also the most complicated task in Trouble Brewing.

Players may only have 2 bitternuts in their inventory at one time. If the player attempts to gather more while having two in their inventory already, the monkey will return home without giving the player another bitternut. When obtained players are granted 50 Hunter experience. Bitternuts can be used on the team's hopper, gaining 200 Cooking experience in the process.

According to Varrock Museum, monkeys on both Karamja and Mos Le'Harmless are very fond of bitternuts, although the nuts can only be found by players on Mos Le'Harmless.
8977: Scrapey bark is used in the Trouble Brewing minigame. Players may obtain bark by using a knife with the scrapey tree logs obtained from chopping scrapey trees, granting 50 Fletching experience. Doing so has a 1/50 chance to cause the player to become diseased. They must then be placed in their corresponding factory hopper, and doing so will provide the player with 100 Cooking experience.
8979:
A bridge section is an item used in the Trouble Brewing minigame that will repair bridges damaged by fires. It can take up to three bridge sections to repair a bridge, depending on how long it was on fire for. At the start of each game, 10 bridge sections are stocked in the tool workbench , and crafted bridge sections can be used on the workbench to store them within it.

Bridge sections can be crafted by using a regular log on the large workbench . Logs can be gathered from the log store within your team's base, or by chopping down the various trees around your base with an axe . Scrapey tree logs cannot be crafted into bridge sections. Creating a bridge section rewards 12.5 crafting experience, and using it to repair a bridge rewards the same amount.
8981:
Sweetgrubs are insects used during Trouble Brewing , and are a key ingredient in the brewing of rum within the minigame , serving as a substitute to the sluglings that Braindeath 'rum' uses. They have a "gag-inducing" aftertaste, but are otherwise quite sweet, hence the name. [ 1 ] Sweetgrubs live in large Sweetgrub Mounds found on both sides of the Trouble Brewing facility.

Raw rat meat can be used on the mounds to collect sweetgrubs, with 40 Hunter experience being awarded for each sweetgrub successfully collected. When attempting to draw out some sweetgrubs from a mound, there is a 1/5 chance that the mound will empty out and collapse. [ 2 ] Players will have to find another mound or wait for it to fill again.

If the mound does not collapse after the player uses their meat on it, there is a further 1/5 chance that a swarm of sweetflies will be drawn out instead. No one can gather more sweetgrubs from the mound while there are still sweetflies present.
8986: The Bucket is an animation item released with Trouble Brewing . It is temporarily wielded by the player during an animation. Aside from this, it cannot be obtained.

8988:
The stuff is purchased from Honest Jimmy's House of Stuff with 50 pieces of eight from the Trouble Brewing minigame on Mos Le'Harmless . Access to the minigame and shop requires completion of the Cabin Fever quest . "The stuff" apparently contains some questionable and/or toxic content, as it has been banned by the Cooks' Guild of Varrock . However, it does not actually cause any negative side effects when used in brewing .

The stuff is used in brewing when making ales after placing two buckets of water and two barley malt into the fermenting vat . After adding it, the specific ale ingredient and ale yeast are also put in. The odds of brewing a mature ale increases. The chances of ale maturing naturally is 5%, but adding the stuff increases this chance to 64%. [ 1 ] However, using it can cause brewing to take up to 7 days instead of the usual 1-1½ days.
8989: The brewin' guide can be obtained near the Trouble Brewing minigame and describes how to play the game. Once obtained, it can be reclaimed from a bookcase within a player-owned house .
8990: Brewin' guides are an unobtainable item. They can be found around Trouble Brewing and have a "Take" option. However, when taken they will give a copy of the real Brewin' guide instead, and the item will not despawn. Therefore, while they serve as an infinite source of Brewin' guides, the item itself is unobtainable. On March 30th 2022 there was a brief glitch that allowed players to telegrab the books, however this was shortly hotfixed.

9004:

9005:
Fancy boots are a pair of low level boots with stats identical to bronze boots (except weighing significantly less), fighting boots and fancier boots . They are obtained from the Cradle of Life on the fourth level of the Stronghold of Security dungeon provided the player's account has two-factor authentication enabled. They are used by new or free-to-play players, as the centre of each level rewards a combined total of 10,000 coins along with the choice between fancy boots, fighting boots or fancier boots (at the fourth and final level).

If the player dies (including in PvP) and the boots are unprotected, it will be sent to the gravestone . When lost, they can be reclaimed for free from the Cradle of Life . Multiple pairs can be claimed and owned at the same time.

They used to be the best melee boots in free-to-play, but have since been surpassed by all of the Castle Wars decorative boots , especially the decorative boots (gold) due to their Strength bonus . The high requirement of 400 castle wars tickets causes the fancy boots to still be popular, due to its nonexistent cost.

This item can be stored in the armour case of a costume room .

9007:
A right skull half is one of 4 parts needed to make a skull sceptre, and can be found by killing a minotaur on the first level of the Stronghold of Security, the Vault of War. These minotaurs can be either low or high level and are not aggressive. It is combined with a left skull half to make a strange skull. Doing so will result in a chatbox message stating: "The two halves of the skull fit perfectly, they appear to have a fixing point, perhaps they are to be mounted on something?" It cannot be traded, bought or sold. It is a fairly uncommon drop, as are the other pieces of the sceptre. It seems to have the highest drop rate of any of the pieces of the sceptre. You can also get more than one skull half at a time, without using the drop trick. Interestingly, the skull half looks like that of an ankou, while the left skull halves dropped by Ankou seem to be minotaur skulls.

Skull sceptre pieces can be crushed with a chisel to yield bone fragments, or used on a skull sceptre (i) to add to its current charges. When chiseled, the right skull half will provide a base quantity of three bone fragments, increasing by one for each Varrock diary tier the player has completed.
9008:
The left skull half is part of the skull sceptre. The left skull half is used with the right skull half to obtain a strange skull. Doing so will result in a chatbox message stating: "The two halves of the skull fit perfectly, they appear to have a fixing point, perhaps they are to be mounted on something?" It is dropped by ankou on the fourth level of the Stronghold of Security. The left skull half cannot be traded or withdrawn as a noted item from the bank. Either skull half is more difficult to obtain than the other parts of the sceptre. The left skull half takes the most effort to obtain from all of the pieces, due to the difficulty in killing ankou compared to the weaker monsters which drop pieces of the skull sceptre.

The skull half looks like part of a minotaur skull, while, oddly, the right half would look more like an ankou's skull, and is dropped by minotaurs, possibly indicating fighting between the two monsters.

Skull sceptre pieces can be crushed with a chisel to yield bone fragments, or combined to a skull sceptre (i) to add to its current charges. When chiseled, the left skull half will provide a base quantity of five bone fragments, increasing by one for each Varrock diary tier the player has completed.
9009:
The Strange skull is an item that players can use with a runed sceptre to make a skull sceptre. It appears to be half an animal skull attached to half a human skull.

Players make the strange skull by combining a right skull half with a left skull half. Right halves, which resemble and most likely are halves of ankou skulls, are dropped by minotaurs, while left halves, resembling half of a minotaur's skull, are dropped by ankou. Minotaurs are found only in the Stronghold of Security, while ankou can be found in the Stronghold of Security, the Stronghold Slayer Cave and The Forgotten Cemetery.

The skull sceptre, when formed from its 4 components, teleports the user to the mines in Barbarian Village, just above the Stronghold of Security. A new sceptre may be formed by combining the right skull half, left skull half, bottom of sceptre, and top of sceptre. Only one skull sceptre may be created at one time, but a player may own as many strange skulls, runed sceptres, skull halves and sceptre halves as one wishes.

Skull sceptre pieces can be crushed with a chisel to yield bone fragments, or combined to a skull sceptre (i) to add to its current charges. When chiseled, the strange skull will provide a base quantity of eight bone fragments, increasing by two for each Varrock diary tier the player has completed.

The top of sceptre is a part of the runed sceptre and eventually the skull sceptre . It is dropped by Catablepon on the third level of the Stronghold of Security . Combining it with the bottom of sceptre makes the runed sceptre . Using it with a chisel makes bone fragments , 3 if none of the Varrock Diary is complete and 4, 5, 6, or 7 respectively depending on which tier of the diary is complete. Bone fragments can be added to a Skull sceptre (i) to add one charge per bone fragment.

After combining a message in chatbox will state: "The two halves of the Sceptre fit perfectly. The Sceptre appears to be designed to have something on top." The Stronghold of Security is the dungeon beneath Barbarian Village , to the west of Varrock and east of the Dwarven Mine .

The skull sceptre is obtained by combining monsters drops from within the Stronghold of Security, as explained below.

It can be used to teleport to the entrance of the Stronghold in Barbarian Village, and members can use it to autocast Arceuus combat spells. Unlike the imbued version, this version cannot autocast crumble undead, and it also breaks when all the teleport charges are depleted.

Its teleport may be used up to level 20 Wilderness.

Gorak claws are common drops by goraks . Using a set of claws with a pestle and mortar creates gorak claw powder , which is the secondary ingredient used in making the magic essence potion .

Because both ingredients of the magic essence potion are free, gorak claws could theoretically be useful for players who cannot afford to make potions with expensive ingredients, or who don't have access to herbs . However, because goraks are so powerful and prayer cannot be used against them, this method is rarely feasible.
9017:
A star flower is a special type of flower that only grows in the cosmic entity's plane (accessible via the fairy ring coordinates C K P ). They can be used during and after the Fairytale II - Cure a Queen quest to create a magic essence potion.

Picking the flower requires 49 Farming . At 57 Herblore it can be added to a vial of water to create a magic essence (unf) , to which gorak claw powder can be added to create the magic essence potion, granting 130 Herblore experience.

When first arriving on this plane no starflowers will be available, but they will start to bloom within a minute of arriving. The flowers grow faster the more players are present.

Attempting to pick another star flower with one already in the inventory results in the message You already have a Star flower, you don't need another one. . Despite this, the drop trick can be utilised to obtain several flowers. Alternatively, players may bring multiple vials of water, add a star flower to one to create a magic essence (unf), then pick up another one without having to use the drop trick. The drop trick method is not necessary after completion of Fairytale II, as players may obtain multiple flowers in a single inventory after the quest.

Star flowers cannot be used to create imp repellent .

Gorak claw powder is gained during Fairytale II - Cure a Queen by grinding a Gorak claw using a pestle and mortar , and is used in the production of a magic essence . It can also be obtained and used the same way after the quest.

Gorak claws are obtained by killing Goraks , which can be found through the fairy rings (code D I R ) or in the God Wars Dungeon .
9019: A Magic essence (unf) is an unfinished potion made at 57 Herblore by using a star flower on a vial of water . In part 2, you need to pickpocket Fairy Godfather to get them, which requires a level of 40 Thieving . The secateurs from A Fairy Tale I and A Fairy Tale II quests are two different items.

These secateurs cannot be wielded, or used as normal secateurs; they are purely a quest item.

You cannot obtain multiple secateurs while one is in your inventory or bank. However, through the drop trick , it is possible to obtain multiple secateurs during Fairytale II.

If the Queen's secateurs are lost before talking to the Fairy Godfather at the end of Fairytale I - Growing Pains , they can be reobtained by entering the gap in the wall next to the Cosmic Altar into the tunnels where you fought Tanglefoot . The secateurs will appear in your inventory upon squeezing through the gap .

9044:
The pharaoh's sceptre is a discontinued item that previously had similar functionality to its modern incarnation . It was changed with the update that introduced Beneath Cursed Sands . In that update, the sceptre was updated to hold a vastly increased number of charges, and now functions in a manner similar to Xeric's talisman . It held 3 charges by default, increased to 4 charges after the Easy Desert Diary , 5 after the Medium Desert Diary , 6 after the Hard Desert Diary , and 8 after the Elite Desert Diary .

After the game update on 27 April 2022 , some existing pharaoh's sceptres were automatically converted to the new item. However, players who had this item in storage at the time of the update kept the original item, albeit with updated menu options; the only menu option besides " Drop " is "Convert", which converts it into a normal pharaoh's sceptre . There is no longer any other use for the item.

Locust meat is dropped by locusts in the city of Sophanem . It heals three hitpoints . Locust meat may not be cooked using the Cooking skill, but can be eaten right after killing a locust.

Red goblin mails cannot be sold nor traded, and therefore has no value. It can only occupy space in the inventory or bank . However, the dye and the goblin mail are tradeable.

The emerald lantern is a light source . It is used during the Lunar Diplomacy quest and is created by using the emerald lens with a bullseye lantern or a bullseye lantern (unf) .

If created from a bullseye lantern (unf), it will require lamp oil to be lit with a tinderbox . To fix this mistake during the quest, there is an easy way to pull the Emerald Lens back out of the lantern by using a Sapphire (with completion of Tears of Guthix ) or a Lantern lens on the bullseye lantern.

Level 49 Firemaking is required to light it. It is similar to the sapphire lantern , but unlike the sapphire lantern it is not made using a cut gem. If lost, the emerald lens can be recovered by speaking to the Cabin boy who can be found slightly north-west of the Lunar Isle bank .

If created from a bullseye lantern (unf), it will require lamp oil to be lit with a tinderbox . To fix this mistake during the quest, there is an easy way to pull the Emerald Lens back out of the lantern by using a Sapphire (with completion of Tears of Guthix ) or a Lantern lens on the bullseye lantern.

Level 49 Firemaking is required to light it. It is similar to the sapphire lantern , but unlike the sapphire lantern it is not made using a cut gem. If lost, the emerald lens can be recovered by speaking to the Cabin boy who can be found slightly north-west of the Lunar Isle bank .
9066:
The emerald lens is a quest item obtained from the Cabin boy during Lunar Diplomacy and is used to expose all the markings left on the ship by the Moon Clan .

It is used on a bullseye lantern or bullseye lantern (unf) to receive an emerald lantern , similar to a sapphire lantern . After Lunar Diplomacy is completed, this item can be discarded.
9067:
Dream logs are ethereal logs obtained whilst cutting Dream trees during the Lunar Diplomacy quest . They cannot be burned or fletched.

It is possible to remove dream logs from the Dream World by dying with Protect Item active while carrying nothing else, however they cannot be banked.

Interacting with them outside of the Dream World (e.g: attempting to drop them) deletes all copies from the player’s inventory.
9068: The Moonclan helm is part of the Moonclan robes set. It can be purchased from the clothing store on Lunar Isle during or after the Lunar Diplomacy quest. It can be stored in a magic wardrobe in a player-owned house.
9069: The Moonclan hat is part of the Moonclan robes set. It can be purchased from the clothing store on Lunar Isle during or after Lunar Diplomacy . It can be stored in a magic wardrobe in a player-owned house.
9070: The Moonclan armour is part of the Moonclan robes set. It can be bought from the clothing shop on Lunar Isle during or after Lunar Diplomacy . It can be stored in a magic wardrobe in a player-owned house.
9071: The Moonclan skirt is part of the Moonclan robes set. It can be purchased from the clothing store on Lunar Isle during or after Lunar Diplomacy . It can be stored in a magic wardrobe in a player-owned house.
9072: Moonclan gloves are part of the Moonclan robes set. They can be purchased from the clothing store on Lunar Isle during or after Lunar Diplomacy . It can be stored in a magic wardrobe in a player-owned house.
9073: Moonclan boots of the Moonclan robes set are purchased from the Moon Clan Fine Clothes clothes shop on Lunar Isle during or after Lunar Diplomacy . They can be stored in a magic wardrobe in the costume room of a player-owned house .
9074: The Moonclan cape is part of the Moonclan robes set. It can be purchased from the clothing store on Lunar Isle during or after Lunar Diplomacy . It is currently the only cape to have a negative defence bonus for any style, and one of two capes to have a negative attack bonus in any style (the other being the mixed hide cape ). It can be stored in a magic wardrobe in a player-owned house.
9075:
Astral runes are runes used in all Lunar Spells . Astral runes require level 40 Runecraft to craft. They may be crafted by using pure essence at the Astral Altar on Lunar Isle after the completion of Lunar Diplomacy . 8.7 Runecraft experience is gained per essence used. At level 82 Runecraft, players will receive two astral runes per pure essence used.

Astral runes may not be crafted via the Abyss . There is no talisman needed to access the Astral Altar, making it and the Soul Altar the only runic altars that do not have a talisman associated with them. However, the Soul Altar can be reached through the Abyss, unlike the Astral Altar.

Astral runes may also be purchased at Baba Yaga's Magic Shop after completion of Lunar Diplomacy, located north of the bank on Lunar Isle . The shop stocks 250 astral runes. Players must have a Seal of passage equipped or in their inventory when attempting to trade with Baba Yaga or they'll be thrown off the island unless they have completed the Elite tier of the Fremennik Diary .
9076: Lunar ore is an ore that can be mined at level 60 Mining from the stalagmites in the western part of the caves underneath Lunar Isle during and after the Lunar Diplomacy quest . It can be smelted at a furnace or via the Superheat Item spell into a lunar bar , one of which is needed to make a lunar helm , and another three to make the V sigil during The Fremennik Exiles .
9077:
A lunar bar is a bar of refined lunar ore . It is created by smelting lunar ore, which can be mined from the stalagmites in the western part of the caves underneath Lunar Isle .

During Lunar Diplomacy , one bar is needed to make a lunar helm . During The Fremennik Exiles , three lunar bars are needed to make the V sigil .

During Fremennik Exiles, the fastest way to make lunar bars is to use the Superheat Item spell, then head over to Seers' Village and use the lunar bars on the anvil there.
9078:
The Moonclan manual, or The Basics of Magic, tells the history of how the Astral Altar came to exist and some of the history of the origin of magic in Gielinor .

It also tells the story of the Fremennik V------- who discovered the rune essence . Unfortunately, some of the words have been omitted by the Moon Clan in an effort to keep some things secret.

A player can buy the book for one coin from Baba Yaga on the Lunar Isle . Afterward, it is in a bookcase in a player's house .

It is worth noting that wearing a Seal of passage is required to buy a Moonclan manual prior to the completion of the Fremennik Elite Diary .
9079:
A suqah tooth is obtained as a drop from the Suqah that live on Lunar Isle. It can be used with a pestle and mortar to turn it into a ground tooth, which is used in making the Waking Sleep Potion during the Lunar Diplomacy quest and used in Farming as one of the items needed to pay a gardener to look after a player's spirit tree patch.

Suqah teeth cannot be noted.
9080: Suqah hide is obtained as a drop from the Suqah . It is used in making the Lunar armour for the Lunar Diplomacy quest. The Suqah hide must first be tanned into Suqah leather by Rimae Sirsalis . This is only possible during the quest.
9081:
Suqah leather is obtained by tanning suqah hide at Rimae Sirsalis for 100 coins per hide. These hides, when used with a thread and needle, can be used to create lunar torsos, lunar legs, lunar boots, and lunar gloves.

After one has finished the Lunar Diplomacy quest, they cannot craft lunar equipment from suqah leather. If one loses some of their lunar equipment, one can only recover them from the Oneiromancer or Perdu. This item therefore becomes useless after the quest.
9082: A ground tooth is made by using a suqah tooth with a pestle and mortar . It is used in farming as part of the payment for protecting a spirit tree , along with five monkey nuts and a monkey bar . Ground tooth is also used in the making of the Waking sleep vial during the Lunar Diplomacy quest. The ground tooth is not tradeable and suqah teeth may only be obtained by killing suqah on Lunar Isle . According to Yulf Squecks , many gnomes enjoy eating this item.
9083:
A seal of passage is a neckwear slot item that is required to be worn or held in the inventory in order to talk to or trade with anyone on Lunar Isle, except for 'Birds-Eye' Jack, the banker available after Dream Mentor. Without it, players attempting to speak with anyone will be forcibly teleported from Lunar Isle back to Rellekka.

The seal of passage is obtained at the beginning of the Lunar Diplomacy quest by talking to Brundt the Chieftain in the longhall in Rellekka. He will replace it for free if the player destroys it or loses it. If the seal is lost during the Fremennik Exiles quest, players must talk to Brundt in the woods south-east of Rellekka (rather than in the longhall) to reobtain it.

It is always lost on death. Because of this, it is recommended for players planning to return to Lunar Isle via Rellekka to destroy their seal of passage after each visit, as they can get a free replacement from Brundt if they do not have one banked (Rellekka is a long way from a bank if a player forgets their seal). If The Fremennik Isles is started, Maria Gunnars will transport the player to Neitiznot where there is a bank to use.

Players who have completed the Fremennik Elite Diaries will no longer need to hold or wear a seal of passage in order to speak to the residents of Lunar Isle.
9084:
The lunar staff is a magic weapon and piece of lunar equipment , requiring 65 Magic and 40 Defence to wield. It is created during Lunar Diplomacy by using a dramen staff on the air , fire , water , and earth altars (in that order). This cannot be done after Lunar Diplomacy is completed, however.

As an enhanced dramen staff, the lunar staff can similarly be used to access Zanaris and the fairy ring network. This can be done even before completing Lunar Diplomacy if the player retrieved their staff back from the Oneiromancer , or if the player made copies and gave one of them to her.

While it has slightly better stats than the dramen staff, it also has a slower attack speed , making it generally a worse melee weapon. Notably however, the lunar staff provides +3 prayer bonus , while the dramen staff provides no prayer bonus.

As with all lunar equipment, it is always lost on death , even though it is an untradeable item. Priestess Zul-Gwenwynig won't recover the staff if the player dies with it while fighting Zulrah . For this reason a dramen staff is often preferable.

If the player loses their staff, they can obtain one from the Oneiromancer for 30,000 (or for free if lost before the quest is completed); this requires a seal of passage or completion of the elite Fremennik diary otherwise the player will be teleported off the island. Players may also obtain a replacement staff from Perdu for 60,000 .
9085: The empty vial is an item obtained during the Lunar Diplomacy quest, from Baba Yaga. It is the only vial that can contain a Waking Sleep Potion. This vial can only be used during Lunar Diplomacy, not for the Potion of Shared Dreaming or any other potion made during Herblore. The vial has no further use once the quest is completed.
9086: A vial of water is a quest item obtained during the Lunar Diplomacy quest . It is made by using an empty vial on a water source . A guam leaf or marrentill is used on it to make a guam vial or marr vial respectively.
9087:
The waking sleep vial is made by using ground tooth with a guam-marr vial. It is a potion used to access the Dream World in the Lunar Diplomacy quest by pouring it on the magic kindling yielding a soaked kindling. When that is lit on fire it transports the player to the Dream World. Pouring it out leaves an empty vial and has no further use once the quest is completed.

Before completing Lunar Diplomacy, collecting empty vials allows for affordable, but time consuming, Herblore training. After giving the lunar equipment set and waking sleep vial to the Oneiromancer, and getting back with magic kindling, use the potion on the kindling, drop the kindling and ask for another potion and kindling. The resulting empty vials can only be filled with water during the quest, however, Guam and Marrentill can still be added to filled vials of water after the quest has been completed.
9088:
A guam vial is made by using a guam leaf on a vial of water (Lunar Diplomacy) , yielding 84 Herblore experience . It is an early step in creating the waking sleep potion in the Lunar Diplomacy quest . Then a marrentill can be added to make a guam-marr vial .

Alternatively, a marr vial can be made and a guam leaf can be added to make the same product.
9089:
A marr vial is made by using a marrentill on a vial of water (Lunar Diplomacy), yielding 84 Herblore experience. It is an early step in creating the waking sleep potion in the Lunar Diplomacy quest. Then a guam leaf can be added to make a guam-marr vial.

Alternatively, a guam vial can be made and a marrentill can be added to make the same product.
9090: The guam-marr vial is made by using a marrentill on a guam vial or a guam leaf on a marr vial , yielding a guam-marr vial and 84 Herblore experience . Adding a ground tooth is the next step in making the waking sleep potion required for the Lunar Diplomacy quest .
9091:
Lunar staff - pt1 is made by using a dramen staff on the Air Altar during the Lunar Diplomacy quest. After using the staff on the Fire Altar , Water Altar and Earth Altar , in that order, it becomes a lunar staff . An unfinished lunar staff at any stage of completion will still function as a regular dramen staff when using fairy rings and entering the shed to Zanaris in the Lumbridge Swamp .

After the quest is complete, lunar staves can no longer be made through this process.
9092:
Lunar staff - pt2 is made by using a dramen staff on the Air Altar and Fire Altar during the Lunar Diplomacy quest. After using the staff on the Water Altar and Earth Altar (in that order), it becomes a lunar staff . An unfinished lunar staff at any stage of completion will still function as a regular dramen staff when using fairy rings and entering the shed to Zanaris in the Lumbridge Swamp .

After the quest is complete, lunar staves can no longer be made through this process.
9093:
Lunar staff - pt3 is made by using a dramen staff on the Air Altar, Fire Altar and Water Altar (in that order) during the Lunar Diplomacy quest. After using the staff on the Earth Altar, it becomes a lunar staff. An unfinished lunar staff at any stage of completion will still function as a regular dramen staff when using fairy rings and entering the shed to Zanaris in the Lumbridge Swamp.

After the quest is complete, lunar staves can no longer be made through this process.
9094:
Kindling is used in the Lunar Diplomacy quest. The Oneiromancer gives the player magic kindling to use in the ceremony to travel to the Dream World .

The Oneiromancer tells the player the magic kindling is from the first magic tree that ever grew.

The player uses the Waking Sleep Potion on the kindling to make Soaked kindling . The player then places the Soaked kindling on the lit Ceremonial Brazier to enter the land of dreams. If the player leaves the Dream World or has to log out, more kindling can be obtained from the Oneiromancer . If the player has an extra set of Lunar equipment stored in their house , they may enter a dialogue loop where they ask for another set of armour and the Oneiromancer refuses them before they can ask for more kindling. This is resolved by removing the armour and having it in your inventory while speaking to the Oneiromancer.

Using the potion on the kindling prints the message You soak the kindling with the potion. .
9095: A soaked kindling is used in the Lunar Diplomacy quest. The player creates a soaked kindling by using waking sleep vial on a kindling. The player then places the soaked kindling on the lit ceremonial brazier to enter the Dream World.
9096:
The lunar helm is a piece of lunar equipment worn in the head slot . 65 Magic and 40 Defence are required to wear the lunar helm. It is statistically similar to a splitbark helm . The lunar helm is created during the Lunar Diplomacy quest by using a lunar bar on an anvil while the player has a hammer , granting 25 Smithing experience.

A lunar bar is created by using a lunar ore on a furnace, lunar ores can be mined from stalagmites found in the cave at the north-east end of the Lunar Isle . The lunar helm may also be bought for 15,000 coins from the Oneiromancer after a player has completed the Lunar Diplomacy quest if the player has lost their helm. The lunar helm is the only piece of lunar equipment that can be remade after the quest. It can be stored in a magic wardrobe in a player-owned house.

As with all lunar equipment, it is always lost on death.
9097:
The lunar torso is a piece of lunar equipment worn in the body slot. 65 Magic and 40 Defence are required to wear the lunar torso. The lunar torso is created during the Lunar Diplomacy quest by using a needle and thread on Suqah leather, but it may be bought from the Oneiromancer after a player has completed the quest for a price of 120,000 coins. It may also be purchased from Perdu for 140,000 coins. It can be stored in a magic wardrobe in a player-owned house.

As with all lunar equipment, it is always lost on death.
9098:
Lunar legs are a piece of Lunar equipment worn in the legwear slot . 65 Magic and 40 Defence are required to wear them. Lunar legs are created during the Lunar Diplomacy quest by using a needle and thread on suqah leather , but they may also be bought from the Oneiromancer after a player has completed the quest for a price of 80,000 coins . It can be stored in a magic wardrobe in a player-owned house.

As with all lunar equipment, it is always lost on death.
9099:
Lunar gloves are a piece of lunar equipment worn in the hand slot . 65 Magic and 40 Defence are required to wear lunar gloves. Lunar gloves are created during the Lunar Diplomacy quest by using a needle and thread on suqah leather , but they may also be bought from the Oneiromancer after a player has completed the quest. This is one of the more useful items of the lunar set, as it has a quite good magic attack bonus, fitting between Mystic gloves and Infinity gloves . It can be stored in a magic wardrobe in a player-owned house.

As with all lunar equipment, it is always lost on death.
9100:
Lunar boots are a piece of lunar equipment worn in the footwear slot . 65 Magic and 40 Defence are required to wear lunar boots. Lunar boots are created during the Lunar Diplomacy quest by using a needle and thread on suqah leather , but they may also be bought from the Oneiromancer after a player has completed the quest for 10,000 coins . It can be stored in a magic wardrobe in a player-owned house.

As with all lunar equipment, it is always lost on death.
9101:
The lunar cape is the cape of the lunar equipment set, requiring 65 Magic and 40 Defence to equip. During the Lunar Diplomacy quest , Pauline Polaris gives it to the player once they correctly guess her name, Jane Blud-Hagic-Maid. After the quest is completed it is purchased from the Oneiromancer or Perdu 's Lost Property shop . It can be stored in a magic wardrobe in a player-owned house.

As with all lunar equipment, it is always lost on death.
9102:
The lunar amulet is a piece of lunar equipment worn in the neckwear slot . The lunar amulet is given to players by Meteora , located on the south side of the Lunar Isle , during the Lunar Diplomacy quest if they can find her tiara by killing suqahs . The lunar amulet may also be bought from the Oneiromancer after a player has completed the quest. It can be stored in a magic wardrobe in a player-owned house.

As with all lunar equipment, it is always lost on death.
9103:
A special tiara is an item dropped by one of the Suqahs found on Lunar Isle during the Lunar Diplomacy quest. This tiara belongs to Meteora , who lost it to the Suqahs. Meteora will exchange the Lunar amulet , if the player returns her tiara to her.

Despite the destroy text stating the Oneiromancer may provide another tiara, there is no dialogue branch that does this. Instead, the player will need to kill Suqahs to reobtain the tiara.
9104:
The lunar ring is a piece of lunar equipment worn in the ring slot . The lunar ring can be obtained during the Lunar Diplomacy quest, and its location is revealed to players through a riddle told by Selene , located near the centre of the Lunar Isle . A player must take a spade and travel outside the south side of the village to the east until they come to a bridge, and over that bridge is a blue flower which the player must dig on top of. The lunar ring may also be bought from the Oneiromancer after a player has completed the quest, however if you don't own the other lunar equipment you will have to purchase those first. It can be stored in a magic wardrobe in a player-owned house.

Compared to other quest rewards, the lunar ring has the same magic bonus as the beacon ring , and 3 less magic bonus than the ring of shadows .

As with all lunar equipment, it is always lost on death. If the player loses their ring, they can obtain one from the Oneiromancer for 2,000 (or for free if lost before the quest is completed); this requires a seal of passage or completion of the elite Fremennik diary or the player will be teleported off the island. Players may also obtain a replacement ring from Perdu for 8,000 .
9106:
The astral tiara is an unobtainable item that was released alongside Lunar Diplomacy . As the Astral Altar did not require a talisman or tiara to enter, it was never made obtainable.

Bizarrely, no astral talisman was created to accompany it. It is possible therefore that the astral tiara would have been included as a purely cosmetic item, but the idea was scrapped before launch.
9107:
Spells are a series of unobtainable items that exist in the game cache. Presumably, they are used in the Spellbook interface. While originally a Spell item existed for every magic spell, since 2014 this has not been necessary.

In an update in 2018 which reworked the Spellbook, the original scroll appearance of the items was removed.
