9139:
Blurite bolts are the second weakest type of bolts. They are stronger than bronze bolts but weaker than iron bolts . They can only be fired from at least a blurite crossbow or better. As with most bolts , they can be poisoned , however this will prevent the addition of bolt tips .

Blurite bolts cannot be bought, and can only be created by players. First, in order to make blurite bolts, a player must smith unfinished blurite bolts . This requires a Smithing level of 8, and for each blurite bar that player smiths they will get 10 unfinished blurite bolts and 17 Smithing experience . Then a player must attach flights to the bolts. Attaching flights to each bolt requires a Fletching level of 24 and 1 feather , granting 1 Fletching experience per bolt.

Blurite bolts may be tipped with jade . A player must first have a Fletching level of 26 and take a cut jade and use a chisel with it to make 12 jade bolt tips , granting 2 Fletching experience. Attaching jade bolt tips also requires a Fletching level of 26, and for each jade bolt tip attached to a blurite bolt, a player is granted 2.4 Fletching experience. Once the jade bolt tips have been attached, the blurite bolts become jade bolts . Jade bolts can then be enchanted to become jade bolts (e) .
9140:
Iron bolts are the third-weakest bolts, stronger than blurite bolts. Iron bolts may be shot from iron or better crossbows. As with most bolts, they can be poisoned, however this will prevent the addition of bolt tips.

Iron bolts may be created by players. First, a player must smith unfinished iron bolts. This requires a Smithing level of 18, and for each iron bar a player smiths they will get 10 unfinished iron bolts and 25 Smithing experience. Then a player must attach flights to the bolts. Attaching flights to each bolt requires a Fletching level of 39 and 1 feather, granting 1.5 Fletching experience per bolt.

Iron bolts may be tipped with pearl. To tip the bolts with pearl, a player must have a Fletching level of 41 and use pearl bolt tips with the iron bolts, granting 3.2 Fletching experience for each pearl bolt tip attached and making the iron bolts into pearl bolts. Pearl bolts can then be enchanted; more information on enchanting them is available under pearl bolts.
9141:
Steel bolts are the fourth available bolt, just after iron bolts and before mithril bolts . Steel bolts may be shot from a steel crossbow or better. As with most bolts , they can be poisoned , however this will prevent the addition of bolt tips .

Steel bolts may be smithed by first making steel bolts(unf) . This requires a Smithing level of 33 and a steel bar . Each bar will make 10 unfinished steel bolts and grant 37.5 Smithing experience . Attaching feathers to each bolt requires a Fletching level of 46, and will grant 3.5 Fletching experience per bolt. At 48 Fletching , red topaz bolt tips can be attached to create red topaz bolts .
9142:
Mithril bolts are a ranged projectile which are fired from a mithril crossbow or higher. Level 36 Ranged is required to equip them. As with most bolts, they can be poisoned, however this will prevent the addition of bolt tips.

To create mithril bolts, a player must first smith unfinished mithril bolts by using a mithril bar on an anvil while carrying a hammer. This requires a Smithing level of 53, and for each mithril bar that player smiths, they will get 10 unfinished mithril bolts and 50 Smithing experience. Then, a player must attach feathers to the bolts. Attaching feathers to each bolt requires a Fletching level of 54 and 1 feather, granting 5 Fletching experience per bolt.

Mithril bolts may be tipped with sapphire, emerald, or a grapple. To tip the bolts with sapphire, a player must have a Fletching level of 56 and use sapphire bolt tips with the mithril bolts, granting 4.7 Fletching experience for each sapphire bolt tip attached and making the mithril bolts into sapphire bolts. To tip the bolts with emerald, a player must have a Fletching level of 58 and use emerald bolt tips with the mithril bolts, granting 5.5 Fletching experience for each emerald bolt tip attached and making the mithril bolts into Emerald bolts. To tip a bolt with a grapple, a player must use a mithril grapple tip on the mithril bolt, granting 11 Fletching experience, and also a rope, making a mithril grapple.

They are commonly used for Ranged training due to them being modestly priced with a good damage output.
9143:
Adamant bolts are a ranged projectile that can be fired from an adamant crossbow or higher, effectively requiring 46 Ranged to use. As with most bolts , they can be poisoned , however this will prevent the addition of bolt tips .

Adamant bolts can be smithed at level 73 Smithing using an adamantite bar , creating 10 adamant bolts(unf) per bar. Level 61 Fletching is required to complete the bolts. When adding feathers , every set of ten bolts yields 70 experience. Players can also choose to attach ruby or diamond bolt tips at level 63 and 65 Fletching, respectively, and then enchant the bolts to make ruby bolts (e) or diamond bolts (e) , which are useful for boss fights.

Ironmen who lack the 73 Smithing requirement may receive adamant bolts as an uncommon drop from iron dragons (1/21.33) and skeletal wyverns (1/42.67), or as rewards from the Hallowed Sepulchre , Soul Wars , and Gnome Restaurant . An alternative for players with 55 Slayer and 61 Ranged is broad bolts , as these are equally strong. However, broad bolts require a rune crossbow or higher to use.
9144:
Runite bolts (or rune bolts) are a type of crossbow ammo. They can be fired using a rune, dragon, dragon hunter, Armadyl, or Zaryte crossbow. Runite bolts provide +115 Ranged strength, making them tied with amethyst broad bolts for fourth strongest type of crossbow ammunition in the game, being surpassed by dragon bolts, onyx-tipped, and dragonstone-tipped rune bolts which provide +122, +120, and +117 respectively. They require a Ranged level of 61 to equip.

Runite bolts can be made by first smithing runite bolts (unf). This requires a Smithing level of 88 and a runite bar. Each bar will make 10 unfinished runite bolts and grant 75 Smithing experience. Attaching feathers to each bolt requires a Fletching level of 69, granting 10 Fletching experience per bolt. As with most bolts, they can be poisoned, however this will prevent the addition of bolt tips.

Unlike all other runite equipment in the game, runite bolts do not use the shorthand 'rune' in their name.
9145:
Silver bolts are ranged ammunition that can be fired from iron crossbows or better. They have a Ranged Strength bonus higher than blurite bolts but lower than iron bolts.

To produce silver bolts, players with at least 21 Crafting must use a silver bar on a furnace with a bolt mould in their inventory. This will return 10 unfeathered silver bolts and 50 Crafting experience. Attaching feathers to the bolts with 43 Fletching will complete them and grant the player 25 Fletching experience.

They are a type of silver weaponry and are one of the few ammo types able to be used to effectively kill Vampyre Juvinates.
9174:
A bronze crossbow is the weakest metal crossbow in the game. It requires a Ranged level of 1 to wield, and can only fire bronze bolts . It has an attack range of 7, increased to 9 with long range.

Bronze crossbows can be made through the Fletching skill at level 9; a player must first cut a wooden stock for the crossbow from logs , granting 6 Fletching experience . Then, a player must add bronze limbs to the stock with a hammer in their inventory, granting 12 experience and making an unstrung bronze crossbow . Finally, a player must string the crossbow with a crossbow string , granting 6 experience. Creating a bronze crossbow from raw materials grants 24 Fletching experience in total.

An unlimited supply of bronze crossbows can be found via a crate located in Armadyl's Eyrie , due south of the grapple spot. However, the player requires a crossbow to access the Eyrie. The " drop trick " can be utilised here to obtain multiple bronze crossbows, as players can only retrieve a bronze crossbow from this crate if they do not already have a crossbow of any kind on their character, be it in their inventory or equipped.

You are also able to obtain up to 3 bronze crossbows every day by searching the Fletching cape , as long as you are not currently in a PvP Arena duel.
9176:
A blurite crossbow is a crossbow stronger than the bronze crossbow but weaker than the iron crossbow . It requires 16 Ranged to wield and can only fire bronze or blurite bolts . It has an attack range of 7, increased to 9 with long range.

Blurite crossbows require 24 Fletching to be made. An oak stock must be fletched from oak logs , yielding 16 Fletching experience , then blurite limbs must be attached to the stock with a hammer , yielding 32 Fletching experience and an unstrung blurite crossbow . Finally, the crossbow must be strung with a crossbow string , yielding 16 experience. In total, making a blurite crossbow yields 64 Fletching experience.

The Knight's Sword quest must be completed before a player can create this crossbow.
9177:
An iron crossbow is a crossbow stronger than the blurite crossbow but weaker than the steel crossbow. It requires a Ranged level of 26 to wield, and can use bolts up to and including iron bolts. It has an attack range of 7, increased to 9 with long range.

Iron crossbows can be made through the Fletching skill at level 39; a player must first cut a willow stock for the crossbow from willow logs, granting 22 Fletching experience. Then, a player must add iron limbs to the stock with a hammer in their inventory, granting 44 experience and making an unstrung iron crossbow. Finally, a player must string the crossbow with a crossbow string, granting 22 experience. Creating an iron crossbow from raw materials grants 88 Fletching experience in total.
9179:
A steel crossbow is a crossbow stronger than the iron crossbow but weaker than the mithril crossbow . It requires a Ranged level of 31 to wield, and can use bolts up to and including steel bolts . It has an attack range of 7 increased to 9 with longrange.

Steel crossbows can be made through the Fletching skill at level 46; a player must first cut a teak stock for the crossbow from teak logs , granting 27 Fletching experience . Then, a player must add steel limbs to the stock with a hammer in their inventory, granting 54 experience and making an unstrung steel crossbow . Finally, a player must string the crossbow with a crossbow string , granting 27 experience. Creating a steel crossbow from raw materials grants 108 Fletching experience in total.
9181:
A mithril crossbow is a crossbow that is stronger than the steel crossbow but weaker than the adamant crossbow. It requires a Ranged level of 36 to wield, and can fire bolts up to and including mithril bolts. It has an attack range of 7 increased to 9 with longrange.

Mithril crossbows can be made through the Fletching skill at level 54; a player must first cut a maple stock for the crossbow from maple logs, granting 32 Fletching experience. Then, a player must add mithril limbs to the stock with a hammer in their inventory, granting 64 experience and making an unstrung mithril crossbow. Finally, a player must string the crossbow with a crossbow string, granting 32 experience. Creating a mithril crossbow from raw materials grants 128 Fletching experience in total.
9183:
An adamant crossbow is a crossbow that is stronger than the mithril crossbow but weaker than the rune crossbow . It requires a Ranged level of 46 to wield, and can fire bolts up to and including adamant bolts . It has an attack range of 7 increased to 9 with longrange.

Adamant crossbows can be made through the Fletching skill at level 61; a player must first cut a mahogany stock for the crossbow from mahogany logs , granting 41 Fletching experience . Then, a player must add adamantite limbs to the stock with a hammer in their inventory, granting 82 experience and making an unstrung adamant crossbow . Finally, a player must string the crossbow with a crossbow string , granting 41 experience. Creating an adamant crossbow from raw materials grants 164 Fletching experience in total.
9185:
The rune crossbow is a crossbow that is stronger than the adamant crossbow but weaker than the dragon crossbow. It requires a Ranged level of 61 to wield, and can fire up to and including runite bolts. It is one-handed so it can be equipped alongside a shield, such as an anti-dragon shield or god book. It has an attack range of 7 increased to 9 with longrange.

Rune crossbows can be made through the Fletching skill at level 69; a player must first cut a yew stock for the crossbow from yew logs, granting 50 Fletching experience. Then, a player must add runite limbs to the stock with a hammer in their inventory, granting 100 experience and making an unstrung rune crossbow. Finally, a player must string the crossbow with a crossbow string, granting 50 experience. Creating a rune crossbow from raw materials grants 200 Fletching experience in total, and doing so within Witchaven and/or Yanille is a task for the elite Ardougne Diary.

Ironmen may obtain a rune crossbow by defeating the crazy archaeologist. The rune crossbow is commonly used among ironmen and low-level players for Slayer tasks, and for TzHaar Fight Cave, due to the ease of obtaining broad bolts and the ability to equip a shield. For Slayer tasks, a magic shortbow with rune or amethyst arrows is often a stronger weapon.

The rune crossbow is commonly used even for high-level content due to its ability to fire ruby and diamond bolts. The dragon, Armadyl, Zaryte, and dragon hunter crossbows are stronger alternatives.

Using a Shattered relics variety ornament kit on the crossbow will change its appearance into that of an rune crossbow (or).
9187:
Jade bolt tips are attached to the tips of blurite bolts or dragon bolts and can then be enchanted. Once jade bolt tips have been attached to the bolts, they become jade bolts and jade dragon bolts respectively.

Jade bolt tips can be created through the Fletching skill. A player must have a Fletching level of 26 and take a cut jade and use a chisel with it to make 12 jade bolt tips, granting 2 Fletching experience.

Attaching jade bolt tips to blurite bolts requires a Fletching level of 26, and for each jade bolt tip attached to a blurite bolt, a player is granted 2.4 Fletching experience. Attaching jade bolt tips to dragon bolts requires a Fletching level of 84, granting 2.4 Fletching experience per bolt.
9188:
Red topaz bolt tips are attached to the tips of steel and dragon bolts, which can then be enchanted. Once red topaz bolt tips have been attached to steel or dragon bolts, they become topaz bolts and topaz dragon bolts, respectively.

Red topaz bolt tips can be created through the Fletching skill. A player must have a Fletching level of 48 and take a cut red topaz and use a chisel with it to make 12 red topaz bolt tips. Attaching red topaz bolt tips to steel bolts also requires 48 Fletching, and gives 4 experience.
9189:
Sapphire bolt tips are attached to the tips of mithril and dragon bolts, which can then be enchanted. Once sapphire bolt tips have been attached to mithril or dragon bolts, they become sapphire bolts and sapphire dragon bolts, respectively.

Sapphire bolt tips can be created through the Fletching skill. A player must have a Fletching level of 56 and take a cut sapphire and use a chisel with it to make 12 sapphire bolt tips, giving 4 experience per gem.
9190:
Emerald bolt tips are attached to the tips of mithril and dragon bolts , which can then be enchanted . Once emerald bolt tips have been attached to mithril or dragon bolts, they become emerald bolts and emerald dragon bolts , respectively.

Emerald bolt tips can be created through the Fletching skill. A player must have a Fletching level of 58 and take a cut emerald and use a chisel with it to make 12 Emerald bolt tips, giving 5.5 experience.
9191:
Ruby bolt tips are attached to the tips of adamant and dragon bolts, which can then be enchanted. Once ruby bolt tips have been attached to adamant or dragon bolts, they become ruby bolts and ruby dragon bolts, respectively.

Ruby bolt tips can be created through the Fletching skill. A player must have a Fletching level of 63 and take a ruby and use a chisel with it to make 12 ruby bolt tips, yielding 6.3 experience per gem.
9192:
Diamond bolt tips can be attached to adamantite bolts or dragon bolts, and can then be enchanted. Once diamond bolt tips have been attached, the bolts become diamond bolts or diamond dragon bolts, respectively.

Diamond bolt tips can be created through the Fletching skill. A player must have a Fletching level of 65 and take a cut diamond and use a chisel with it to make 12 diamond bolt tips, giving 7 experience.
9193:
Dragonstone bolt tips are attached to the tips of runite and dragon bolts , which can then be enchanted . Once dragonstone bolt tips have been attached to runite or dragon bolts, they become dragonstone bolts and dragonstone dragon bolts , respectively.

Dragonstone bolt tips can be created through the Fletching skill. One must have 71 Fletching and take a cut dragonstone and use a chisel with it to make 12 dragonstone bolt tips, granting 8.2 Fletching experience per dragonstone. To avoid misclicking, players will receive a message to confirm cutting the dragonstone into bolt tips. There is a "Make - x" option for this, and it takes about 70 seconds per inventory of cut gems chiselled into tips.

Attaching dragonstone bolt tips to runite bolts to make dragonstone bolts also requires 71 Fletching, and gives 8.2 experience for each dragonstone bolt tip attached to a runite bolt.
9194:
Onyx bolt tips are attached to the tips of runite bolts to create onyx bolts, or to dragon bolts to create dragon onyx bolts, which can then be enchanted to make onyx bolts (e) and onyx dragon bolts (e), respectively.

Onyx bolt tips can be created through the Fletching skill. A player must have a Fletching level of 73 and take a cut onyx and use a chisel with it to make 24 onyx bolt tips. This is not recommended because the gem itself is worth far more than the bolt tips. Instead, it's recommended to collect them as drops from various monsters, or fish infernal eels.

Attaching onyx bolt tips also requires a Fletching level of 73, and for each onyx bolt tip attached to a runite bolt, the player is granted 9.4 Fletching experience.

Onyx bolt tips can also be obtained from stone chests, ninja implings, infernal eels, and elite Treasure Trails.
9236:
Opal bolts (e) are opal bolts which have been enchanted through use of the Enchant Crossbow Bolt (Opal) spell, which requires level 4 Magic, 1 cosmic rune, 2 air runes, and 10 opal bolts which to enchant per cast of the spell.

Opal bolts are crafted by gem-tipping bronze bolts with opal bolt tips.
9237: Jade bolts (e) are blurite bolts tipped with enchanted jade. Jade bolts can be enchanted into enchanted jade bolts through the spell Enchant Crossbow Bolt (Jade) by a player with level 14 Magic. The spell enchants 10 jade bolts at a time. These bolts are untradeable.
9238: Enchanted pearl bolts are iron bolts tipped with enchanted Pearl bolt tips made from Oyster pearls . Pearl bolts can be enchanted into enchanted pearl bolts through the spell Enchant Crossbow Bolt (Pearl) by a player with 24 Magic . The spell enchants 10 pearl bolts at a time and requires 1 Cosmic rune and 2 Water runes to be present in their inventory.
9239: Topaz bolts (e) are steel bolts tipped with enchanted red topaz. Topaz bolts can be enchanted through the spell Enchant Crossbow Bolt (Red Topaz) by a player with level 29 Magic. The spell enchants 10 red topaz bolts at a time.
9240: Sapphire bolts (e) are mithril bolts tipped with enchanted sapphire. Sapphire bolts can be enchanted through the spell Enchant Crossbow Bolt (Sapphire) by a player with level 7 Magic. The spell enchants 10 sapphire bolts at a time.
9241: Emerald bolts (e) are mithril bolts tipped with enchanted emerald . Emerald bolts can be enchanted through the spell Enchant Crossbow Bolt (Emerald) by a player with level 27 Magic . The spell enchants 10 emerald bolts at a time. Like mithril and emerald bolts, firing them requires a mithril crossbow , or better.
9242: Ruby bolts (e) are adamant bolts that have been enchanted after having been tipped with ruby bolt tips . Ruby bolts can be enchanted with the spell Enchant Crossbow Bolt (Ruby) by a player with level 49 Magic , requiring 46 Ranged to wield. The spell enchants 10 ruby bolts at a time and uses 1 blood rune , 1 cosmic rune , and 5 fire runes .
9243: Diamond bolts (e) are adamant bolts tipped with enchanted diamond . Diamond bolts can be enchanted by using the spell Enchant Crossbow Bolt (Diamond) by a player with 57 Magic . The spell enchants 10 diamond bolts per cast and uses 2 law runes , 1 cosmic rune , and 10 earth runes .
9244: Dragonstone bolts (e) are runite bolts tipped with enchanted dragonstone. Dragonstone bolts can be enchanted through the spell Enchant Crossbow Bolt (Dragonstone) by a player with level 68 Magic. The spell enchants 10 dragonstone bolts at a time. They require 61 Ranged to wield. Dragonstone bolts (e) can be purchased from Justine located at the Last Man Standing Minigame in Ferox Enclave, who sells 20 for 3 points.
9245: Onyx bolts (e) are rune bolts tipped with enchanted onyx. Onyx bolts can be enchanted through the spell Enchant Crossbow Bolt (Onyx) by a player with level 87 Magic. The spell enchants 10 onyx bolts at a time. These bolts are rarely used due to their cost, but are often fletched and enchanted by ironman players for their High Level Alchemy value. Additionally, they require a Ranged level of 61 to wield.

To tip the bolts with sapphire, a player must have a Fletching level of 56 and use sapphire bolt tips with the mithril bolts, granting 4.7 Fletching experience for each sapphire bolt tip attached and making the mithril bolts into sapphire bolts. To tip the bolts with emerald, a player must have a Fletching level of 58 and use emerald bolt tips with the mithril bolts, granting 5.5 Fletching experience for each emerald bolt tip attached and making the mithril bolts into Emerald bolts. To tip a bolt with a grapple, a player must use a mithril grapple tip on the mithril bolt, granting 11 Fletching experience, and also a rope, making a mithril grapple.

They are commonly used for Ranged training due to them being modestly priced with a good damage output.
9297:
Adamant bolts are a ranged projectile that can be fired from an adamant crossbow or higher, effectively requiring 46 Ranged to use. As with most bolts , they can be poisoned , however this will prevent the addition of bolt tips .

Adamant bolts can be smithed at level 73 Smithing using an adamantite bar , creating 10 adamant bolts(unf) per bar. Level 61 Fletching is required to complete the bolts. When adding feathers , every set of ten bolts yields 70 experience. Players can also choose to attach ruby or diamond bolt tips at level 63 and 65 Fletching, respectively, and then enchant the bolts to make ruby bolts (e) or diamond bolts (e) , which are useful for boss fights.

Ironmen who lack the 73 Smithing requirement may receive adamant bolts as an uncommon drop from iron dragons (1/21.33) and skeletal wyverns (1/42.67), or as rewards from the Hallowed Sepulchre , Soul Wars , and Gnome Restaurant . An alternative for players with 55 Slayer and 61 Ranged is broad bolts , as these are equally strong. However, broad bolts require a rune crossbow or higher to use.
9298:
Runite bolts (or rune bolts) are a type of crossbow ammo. They can be fired using a rune, dragon, dragon hunter, Armadyl, or Zaryte crossbow. Runite bolts provide +115 Ranged strength, making them tied with amethyst broad bolts for fourth strongest type of crossbow ammunition in the game, being surpassed by dragon bolts, onyx-tipped, and dragonstone-tipped rune bolts which provide +122, +120, and +117 respectively. They require a Ranged level of 61 to equip.

Runite bolts can be made by first smithing runite bolts (unf). This requires a Smithing level of 88 and a runite bar. Each bar will make 10 unfinished runite bolts and grant 75 Smithing experience. Attaching feathers to each bolt requires a Fletching level of 69, granting 10 Fletching experience per bolt. As with most bolts, they can be poisoned, however this will prevent the addition of bolt tips.

Unlike all other runite equipment in the game, runite bolts do not use the shorthand 'rune' in their name.
9299:
Silver bolts are ranged ammunition that can be fired from iron crossbows or better. They have a Ranged Strength bonus higher than blurite bolts but lower than iron bolts.

To produce silver bolts, players with at least 21 Crafting must use a silver bar on a furnace with a bolt mould in their inventory. This will return 10 unfeathered silver bolts and 50 Crafting experience. Attaching feathers to the bolts with 43 Fletching will complete them and grant the player 25 Fletching experience.

They are a type of silver weaponry and are one of the few ammo types able to be used to effectively kill Vampyre Juvinates.

This requires a Smithing level of 8, and for each blurite bar that player smiths they will get 10 unfinished blurite bolts and 17 Smithing experience . Then a player must attach flights to the bolts. Once the jade bolt tips have been attached, the blurite bolts become jade bolts . Jade bolts can then be enchanted to become jade bolts (e) .

Grapples are wielded in the ammo slot and used with a crossbow . Sometimes grapples may break (although rarely) so it is a good idea to have more than one available.

The mith grapple is an item carried in the ammunition slot , used together with any crossbow (excluding the love crossbow , light , and heavy ballistae ) to grapple across certain Agility shortcuts . Both items must be equipped. Using these crossbow shortcuts is a requirement for a number of achievement diary tasks . As well as the required Agility level, players will also need a certain Ranged and Strength level to use them. Armadyl 's section of the God Wars Dungeon is the sole exception, as it only requires 70 Ranged.

There is a 1/25 chance of the grapple being destroyed upon usage; when this occurs, the message box states " After untying the rope, you find that your grapple is broken and useless. ". [ 1 ] The mith grapple will never be destroyed within the Hallowed Sepulchre or while doing the Shayzien Agility Course .

The grapple can be made by attaching a mith grapple tip to a mithril bolt to create a mith grapple (unf) , requiring 59 Fletching , then using the unfinished grapple on a rope . The tip can be smelted using a mithril bar , requiring 59 Smithing .

The grapple is also dropped by a number of monsters found in the Ancient Cavern , which may be accessed after completing the first part of Barbarian Firemaking , requiring level 35 Firemaking .

An unlimited supply of mith grapples can be found via a crate located in Armadyl's Eyrie , due south of the grapple spot. A mith grapple is required to access this crate. The " drop trick " can be utilised here to obtain multiple grapples, as players can only retrieve a mith grapple from this crate if they do not already have one equipped or in their inventory.

9433:
A bolt pouch allows a player to carry multiple kinds of bolts in one inventory slot, including bolt racks, as well as mith grapples, and swap between two types of bolts mid-combat. It can be purchased for 1,500 from Hirko, who runs the crossbow shop in Keldagrim on the east side of the river. Players must ask Hirko about ammo in order to be given the option to purchase a pouch; it cannot be bought in Hirko's normal shop.

Within the bolt pouch, there are four slots that can each hold 10,000 bolts of a single type, or one mith grapple. To store items in the pouch, players must use them on the pouch. Left-clicking on the pouch will open an interface showing what bolts are in the pouch and what the player has equipped in their ammo and extra ammo slots. Bolts can be moved between slots via left click and dragging.

In addition to storing ammo, the bolt pouch allows players to seamlessly swap between their equipped ammo and one extra ammo slot. This can be done via left click from the Worn Equipment tab without interrupting the player's current action, including attacking enemies. This does not work with non-ammo items, such as Ghommal's penny or Rada's blessing - these items can only be equipped in the primary ammo slot, and switching ammo from the extra slot into the primary slot will unequip them.

If the player has Dizana's quiver equipped or in their inventory it will disable the bolt pouch's functionality to swap between their equipped ammo and the extra ammo in the bolt pouch. The Worn Equipment tab will not show the extra ammo in the bolt pouch—only the ammo in the quiver. If the player attempts to move ammo from the bolt pouch into their ammunition slot using the bolt pouch interface, it will not work, and a message will warn the player You cannot change ammo from your bolt pouch with Dizana's quiver on your person.

Attempting to use an alchemy spell on the bolt pouch fails and results in the message The dwarven pouch resists your magic. appearing in the chatbox.

The bolt pouch is never one of protected items kept in the inventory on death. In PvM death it always goes to the gravestone where it may be reclaimed with its contents preserved. In PvP death, it is always destroyed and its contents are dropped to the killer.

If an Ultimate Ironman loses the bolt pouch on death, either through despawning from a pve deathpile or being wiped from an item retrieval service, its contents will be preserved and can be reclaimed by buying a new bolt pouch from Hirko.

The bolt pouch is not obtainable on Deadman Mode worlds.

Making a runite crossbow (u) within Witchaven and/or Yanille is required for completing one of the elite Ardougne Diary tasks.
9467: A blurite bar is a bar of refined blurite . It can be created through the Smithing skill at level 13 by using blurite ore on a furnace or level 10 by using Superheat Item on the ore, granting 8 Smithing experience . A blurite bar can be smithed on an anvil , through the Smithing skill to create blurite bolts (unf) for use in the creation of blurite bolts , or blurite limbs for use in the creation of a blurite crossbow and also to complete a task in the Falador Easy Diary when smithed on Doric 's anvil.
9468:
Sawdust appears at a player's feet after asking the Sawmill operator to convert logs into planks . It currently has no use.

Its addition to the game was alluded to a day after its release in Postbag from the Hedge issue 9 . When a player asked the sawmill operator how he explained the loss of weight when making planks, the operator responded that the weight loss was caused by the sawdust created when making said planks. He then goes on to say that he has to pay quite a lot to have the sawdust disposed of as he cannot just leave it lying around, before starting to wonder to himself if that is truly the case, implying that the sawmill operator was considering no longer paying money to have the sawdust disposed of. [ 1 ]

The operator used to wander around freely, south of the Lumber Yard , which would cause many spawns of sawdust. Now the sawmill operator only works in a shed, in the Lumber Yard itself and the Woodcutting Guild , meaning these locations only provide two spawns for sawdust. With the addition of Prifddinas and the Sawmill Operator there, there are more spawns as the operator can saw planks from many sides, provided the player is quick enough to trade for planks before being forced to walk south of the operator.

When created, it can be picked up by ironmen even when made by other players milling logs. This serves no practical purpose to do, however, as sawdust has no use.
9469:
The grand seed pod is a single-use teleport item that can be obtained as a rare reward from Wingstone , Penwie , Brambickle , and Professor Manglethorp in the Gnome Restaurant minigame . [ 1 ] [ 2 ] Seed pods are stackable. They can take players to the Grand Tree , and have two right-click options: launch and squash.

Launching the seed pod will take players to the top floor of the Grand Tree , through Captain Lamdoo and a glider, but it can only be used outdoors. This option will also give the player 100 Farming experience. Squashing the seed will take players to the Grand Tree (to the ground floor by King Narnode Shareen ) faster than Launching it, but the Farming experience will not be given, and will temporarily drain their Farming skill by 5 levels.

Unlike most teleports, which stop working above level 20 Wilderness, the Grand seed pod is among the few items whose teleports can still be used up to level 30 Wilderness.

The upgraded version of this item, the Royal seed pod , is obtained upon completion of Monkey Madness II , and has unlimited charges. It does not offer the Launch option and does not affect Farming (experience or level drain).

This item was once commonly used to lure players. Although scams involving this item have fallen out of favour, players should still exercise caution when the grand seed pod is involved. Most of these lures involve the victim dropping valuable items and then proceeding to Squash or Launch the pod.
9470: The gnome scarf is a possible reward from the Gnome Restaurant activity. Players have a 1/17 chance of receiving this from Captain Daerkin and Captain Ninto . [ 1 ] The scarf has no stats, but it can function as warm clothing in Wintertodt reducing damage taken, and is the only tradeable neck slot item to do so. It is often used for fashion purposes.
9472:
Gnome goggles are a possible reward from the Gnome Restaurant minigame. Players have a 1/17 chance to obtain them as a reward from Captain Daerkin or Captain Ninto , which are accessible with hard deliveries. [ 1 ] The gnome goggles are part of the gnome pilot set which also includes the gnome scarf .

Goggles can be combined with the Bomber cap from the Enlightened Journey quest by talking with Auguste , resulting in a Cap and goggles . As the cap and goggles can be stored, though not the goggles themselves, this provides a means of storing the goggles in the armour case (as part of the bomber jacket costume ).
9474:
Reward tokens are received for gaining at least 12 credits in the Gnome Restaurant minigame . It can be used at any time to summon a mounted terrorchick gnome bearing gnome cuisine . A player may only have one reward token at a time, but when used, it grants the player one food item for every 12 credits the player has, for up to 10 free items of gnome food. This makes it useful for exploring dungeons and other dangerous areas as it provides up to 10 pieces of food in just one inventory slot. Depending on which food you get, you can heal 5 to 15 HP per food for a potential total of 50 to 150 HP (although the drinks can have negative effects on skills such as strength and attack ). While it can be brought to the Barbarian Assault minigame, it can not be used there.

If a reward token is destroyed, the credits are not destroyed and a player can talk to Gianne jnr. to get a new token. If the mounted terrorchick gnome cannot reach the player and eventually despawns, the amassed credits will still be retained.

Once the player has filled their reward token by obtaining a total of 120 credits, the dialogue from Gianne jnr. will change while getting a new job. This (unintentionally) allows players to recycle their newly given job without penalty by right-clicking Gianne jnr.'s "Get job" option before moving on to subsequent dialogue.

Mint cake is a food item that, when eaten, will restore a player's run energy by 50%. Mint cakes restore more energy per consumption than any other item using only one click (outside of the Agility cape). When eaten, it gives the message Mmm ... minty. You feel energized! [ sic ] .

A mint cake can be obtained as a tip from Brambickle , Wingstone , and Penwie in the Gnome Restaurant minigame . [ 1 ] A one-off mint cake can also be obtained during or after The Path of Glouphrie by giving Longramble a tangled toad's legs , though receiving one this way does not register it in the collection log .

Creating weird gloop will result in a game message in the chatbox stating " You mix the rune dust into the tree sap. It doesn't look quite right. "

A crystal saw is an item made from a crystal saw seed by invoking a singing bowl in either Brimstail's cave or Prifddinas . The seed is awarded to players who complete The Eyes of Glouphrie quest.

When in the inventory, the saw allows the player to build furniture up to 3 levels higher than their current Construction level. Note that this boost only works on furniture that requires both a saw and a hammer to make ( STASH units, Fire Pits , and Shipbuilding included); as such, the saw cannot assist in building new rooms or planting flowers in a garden . This bonus stacks with all other visible boosts to Construction , making it possible to build items up to 8 levels higher than the player's current Construction level when used in conjunction with a +5 boost from spicy stew . However, given the erratic nature of spicy stew boosts, it is more common for players to combine it with a trimmed cup of tea for a +6 boost.

If players lose or destroy the saw, they can get it back by talking to Brimstail in his cave and selecting his first dialogue option. He will not give players a seed if they have either the seed or the saw in the bank or inventory. The saw is destroyed upon death.

The saw can be used to boost your construction level for Sailing Facilities and core boat parts , despite the latter not requiring a saw. When used to construct core boat parts the crystal saw will not lose any charges.

The saw cannot be used to get higher-level contracts in Mahogany Homes .

If the player loses the seed or the saw, they can speak to Brimstail and select the "Hello, just wanted a chat." chat option to obtain another seed.

9646: The castle sketch 1 is a quest item made during the Darkness of Hallowvale quest. It is made by using a piece of charcoal on a sheet of papyrus while standing on the north side of the castle at the north end of Meiyerditch . The sketch must be given to Safalaan along with castle sketch 2 and castle sketch 3 to complete the intelligence-gathering part of the quest.
9647:
The castle sketch 2 is a quest item made during the Darkness of Hallowvale quest . It is made by using a piece of charcoal on a sheet of papyrus while standing on the west side of the castle at the north end of Meiyerditch . The sketch must be given to Safalaan , along with the castle sketch 1 and castle sketch 3 , to complete the intelligence-gathering part of the quest.

When the player attempts to make this sketch for the first time, they will be interrupted by a cutscene with Vanstrom Klause , Vanescula Drakan and her brother, Ranis Drakan . After this, the player will finish their sketch.
9648:
The castle sketch 3 is a quest item made during the Darkness of Hallowvale quest. It is a sketch of the southern part of Castle Drakan . It is made by using a piece of charcoal on a sheet of papyrus while standing on the South side of the castle (just a few steps west from where Safalaan give you the mission to sketch out the castle) at the north end of Meiyerditch . The sketch must be given to Safalaan along with castle sketch 1 and castle sketch 2 to complete the intelligence-gathering part of the quest.

When the player attempts to make this sketch for the first time, they will be interrupted by a cutscene with Vanstrom Klause . After this, Vanstrom attacks the player, but they are saved by Sarius Guile . Note that the player still has not finished the sketch after this cutscene as they were interrupted .
9649: The message is a quest item used during the Darkness of Hallowvale . It is found by using a knife on a fireplace in a building near the centre of Meiyerditch after giving Safalaan three sketches of the castle in the north part of town. It is reobtainable from the same place even after the completion of the quest.
9650:
The blood tithe pouch is an unobtainable item released with Darkness of Hallowvale. It presumably would have been an item that players would have obtained during the quest.

A similar item can be seen served by a vyrewatch to Vanescula Drakan and Ranis Drakan during a cutscene in Darkness of Hallowvale. It is not possible to obtain the item in-game.
9651: A large ornate key is used in Darkness of Hallowvale quest. It can be found by using a knife on the portrait in Meiyerditch. If used on the vampyre statue in the house with the tapestry, it will open a door that leads to the Haemalchemy book.
9652:
Haemalchemy volume 1 is a book that gives details on what the Vampyres are experimenting with. It must be telegrabbed in the Meiyerditch Laboratories to be obtained. It is given to Safalaan at the end of the Darkness of Hallowvale quest.

Haemalchemy, when broken down by definition, is the study of transmuting or modifying blood.

If a player attempts to read the book on haemalchemy, they will get the message, "This book seems far too complex to you at the moment." While the exact contents of the book are a mystery, it is known that a majority of the book is written in the vampyric language and that it details their usage of haemalchemy in an attempt to increase the amount of blood received from tithing a human and in strengthening their immunity to conventional weaponry.
9653:
The sealed message is obtained during the Darkness of Hallowvale quest. It is a sealed letter written by Safalaan to be delivered to Veliaf. Attempting to read it gives the message "The message is sealed and addressed to Veliaf. It would be rude of you to open it."

Once delivered, the player discovers that it is really a commendation letter from the "highest ranking member of the Myreque", and Veliaf then makes the player a full member of the Myreque.
9654: A door key is used in Darkness of Hallowvale to continue on the Myreque 's trail in Meiyerditch . It is found by searching some pots and is used to open the door adjacent to it. Once used, it disappears and cannot be recovered.
9655: The ladder top is a quest item found during the Darkness of Hallowvale quest while trying to cross Meiyerditch without being spotted by the Vyrewatch. It is used to extend a broken ladder to allow the player access to the upper level of a building which is on the route through the town.
9656:
The tome of experience is received from Veliaf Hurtz on completion of the Darkness of Hallowvale quest . Reading it opens a window to select the skill a player wishes to advance. The player must be at least level 30 in their chosen skill.

It has three chapters which provide 2000 experience each. After confirming, the player receives the message " You read a fascinating chapter and earn experience! You have been awarded 2,000 (skill) experience! " After the third reading, the book disappears and the player receives the message " The book crumbles into a dust cloud of knowledge. "

This item cannot be banked.

If lost or destroyed, the tome can be reclaimed by talking to Veliaf Hurtz in the Myreque Hideout under Burgh de Rott , or from the chest in the same hideout after completing A Taste of Hope .

9659:
Buckets of water are unobtainable items that can be found throughout Meiyerditch . Attempting to take them results in the chatbox message I really do not want to go anywhere near that! It stinks! , and attempting to cast Telekinetic Grab results in the chatbox message I really don't want to waste runes grabbing this item .

Based on the message given in the chatbox, it can be assumed that the bucket contains urine or stagnant liquids.
9660:
Buckets are unobtainable items that can be found throughout Meiyerditch . Attempting to take them results in the chatbox message I really do not want to go anywhere near that! It stinks! , and attempting to cast Telekinetic Grab results in the chatbox message I really don't want to waste runes grabbing this item .

Based on the message given in the chatbox, it can be assumed that the bucket contains excrement or rotten food.
9662:
The useless key is an unobtainable item released alongside A Taste of Hope , created to replace the discontinued shortcut key . Two versions of the key were created to replace the standard and bank placeholder versions of the shortcut key. While the useless key was never meant to be seen by players, it inadvertently became visible as the bank placeholders were not wiped from the game. [ 1 ] Therefore, any players who had created a bank placeholder of the shortcut key saw the useless key takes its place.

The placeholders were removed over a year later in an update on 13 June 2019.
9665: The torch is an animation item released with the rework of the Sea Slug. It is temporarily wielded by the player in an animation where they scare away a Fisherman or a Sea Slug with a lit torch. Aside from this, the item cannot be obtained.
9666:
A proselyte harness m can be obtained after completing the Slug Menace quest by buying it from Sir Tiffy Cashien in Falador. It may be opened to obtain Proselyte armour.

The set contains: Proselyte sallet, Proselyte hauberk, and the Proselyte cuisse.
9668: An initiate harness m can be obtained after completing the Recruitment Drive quest by buying it from Sir Tiffy Cashien in Falador. It may be opened to obtain initiate armour. Once opened it cannot be recreated by a Grand Exchange Clerk.
9670:
A proselyte harness f can be obtained after completing the Slug Menace quest by buying it from Sir Tiffy Cashien in Falador. It may be opened to obtain proselyte armour.

The set contains: proselyte sallet, proselyte hauberk, and the proselyte tasset.
9672:
The proselyte sallet is a piece of Temple Knight Armour that requires 30 Defence , 20 Prayer , and completion of The Slug Menace quest to equip. It is only exceeded by the god mitres and sunfire fanatic helm in Prayer bonus for the helmet slot.

It has the exact same bonuses as an Adamant full helm , except that it offers +4 Prayer bonus. Like other Proselyte equipment, it is white with a dark-gold trim.

This piece of armour cannot be made using the Smithing skill. Although this armour is trimmed, it cannot be obtained from any Treasure Trail .

This item can be stored in the armour case of a costume room , as part of the proselyte armour set. Ultimate Ironmen will be unable to retrieve individual pieces until the full set is stored.
9674:
The proselyte hauberk is a piece of Temple Knight Armour that requires 30 Defence, 20 Prayer, and completion of The Slug Menace quest to equip. It shares the second highest Prayer bonus of any body slot equipment with the 3rd Age druidic robe top and the Elite black platebody, only beaten by the Sunfire fanatic cuirass. It has similar bonuses to those of an Adamant platebody with a +8 Prayer bonus, and is slightly lighter. Oddly enough, it does not stop Ava's devices from gathering arrows.

Like other Proselyte equipment, it is white with a dark-gold trim.

This piece of armour cannot be made using the Smithing skill. Although this armour is trimmed, it cannot be obtained from any Treasure Trail.

This item can be stored in the armour case of a costume room, as part of the proselyte armour set. Ultimate Ironmen will be unable to retrieve individual pieces until the full set is stored.
9676:
The proselyte cuisse is a piece of Temple Knight Armour that requires 30 Defence, 20 Prayer, and completion of The Slug Menace quest to equip. Along with its tasset counterpart, it is tied with the 3rd Age druidic robe bottoms and the Zealot's robe bottom for the second highest Prayer bonus of any leg slot equipment, beaten only by the Sunfire fanatic chausses.

It has the same bonuses as Adamant platelegs, except that it offers +6 Prayer bonus and weighs less. Like other Proselyte equipment, it is white with a dark-gold trim.

This piece of armour cannot be made using the Smithing skill. Although this armour is trimmed, it cannot be obtained from any Treasure Trail.

This item can be stored in the armour case of a costume room, as part of the proselyte armour set. Ultimate Ironmen will be unable to retrieve individual pieces until the full set is stored.
9678:

It has the exact same bonuses as an Adamant plateskirt , except that it offers +6 Prayer bonus and weighs less. Like other Proselyte equipment, it is white with a dark-gold trim.

This item can be stored in the armour case of a costume room , as part of the proselyte armour set. Ultimate Ironmen will be unable to retrieve individual pieces until the full set is stored.
9680: Sea slug glue is a quest item used in The Slug Menace quest . It is made by giving a dead sea slug to Bailey on the Fishing Platform near Witchaven . The glue is used to join together the three fragments of Page 3 of Maledict's holy book, which is used later in the quest.
9681:
The commorb v2 is a quest item used in the Slug Menace quest. It is made by giving Sir Tiffy Cashien a normal commorb. During the quest it was used to contact Savant for help in solving the mystery of the slug infestation.

After completing the quest, if the player does not have a commorb v2 in their bank or inventory, Sir Tiffy Cashien will give the player a new one immediately after talking to him.
9682:
The door transcription is a quest item used in the Slug Menace quest. It is given to the player by Savant after using the Commorb v2 to scan the markings on a mysterious door in the newly discovered shrine underneath Witchaven .

If you happen to lose your door transcription, you can get it back by using the Playback option on the Commorb v2 and looking at your current assignment.
9683: The dead sea slug is a quest item used in the Slug Menace quest. It is found on the floor in the newly discovered shrine under Witchaven, and is given to Bailey on the Fishing Platform in order to make sea slug glue during the quest.
9684:
Page 1 is a quest item used in the Slug Menace quest. It is found by searching the study desk in the Mayor's house in Witchaven. The page is used in conjunction with Page 2 and Page 3 of Brother Maledict's holy book in order to determine how to make the special runes needed to open a mysterious door in the newly discovered shrine beneath Witchaven.

In the quest, the player was tricked by sea slug possessed citizens that it will help shut Mother Mallum's door, but in reality, frees her.
9685: Page 2 is a quest item used in the Slug Menace quest. It is given to the player by Ezekial Lovecraft, the owner of the fishing store in Witchaven. The page is used in conjunction with Page 1 and Page 3 of Brother Maledict's holy book in order to determine how to make the special runes needed to open a mysterious door in the newly discovered shrine beneath Witchaven.
9686: Page 3 is a quest item used in the Slug Menace quest. It is given to the player by Col. O'Niall in the form of three Fragments which the player must glue together using sea slug glue . The page is used in conjunction with Page 1 and Page 2 of Brother Maledict 's holy book in order to determine how to make the special runes needed to open a mysterious door in the newly discovered shrine beneath Witchaven .
9687: Fragment 1 is a quest item used in the Slug Menace quest. It is given to the player by Col. O'Niall, along with Fragment 2 and Fragment 3. The player must glue the fragments together using sea slug glue and doing a small jigsaw puzzle to form Page 3 of Maledict's holy book. This page is used in conjunction with Page 1 and Page 2 of the book in order to determine how to make the special runes needed to open a mysterious door in the newly discovered shrine beneath Witchaven.
9688: Fragment 2 is a quest item used in the Slug Menace quest. It is given to the player by Col. O'Niall, along with Fragment 1 and Fragment 3. The player must glue the fragments together using sea slug glue and doing a small jigsaw puzzle to form Page 3 of Maledict's holy book. This page is used in conjunction with Page 1 and Page 2 of the book in order to determine how to make the special runes needed to open a mysterious door in the newly discovered shrine beneath Witchaven.
9689: Fragment 3 is a quest item used in the Slug Menace quest. It is given to the player by Col. O'Niall, along with fragment 2 and fragment 1. The player must glue the fragments together using sea slug glue and doing a small jigsaw puzzle to form Page 3 of Maledict's holy book. This page is used in conjunction with page 1 and page 2 of the book in order to determine how to make the special runes needed to open a mysterious door in the newly discovered shrine beneath Witchaven.
9690:
The blank water rune is a quest item used in The Slug Menace . It is made by right-clicking on Page 2 of Brother Maledict 's holy book and choosing the "shape water" option with a rune essence or pure essence in the inventory. During this process the player must also make a blank air rune , a blank earth rune , a blank fire rune , and a blank mind rune using page 1 and page 3 . The player needs a chisel in their inventory to make these runes.

Make more than one blank because you can fail while chiselling the shape of the rune and/or binding it with the element of the rune.

When used on the Water Altar in the usual way it turns into a special water rune , which is needed later in the quest. This item is lost upon death with all the others blank runes aswell.
9691: A water rune is a special type of water rune used during The Slug Menace . It is made by using a blank water rune on the Water Altar in the normal way and is used to unlock a mysterious door in the newly discovered shrine beneath Witchaven . Sometimes the blank water rune can break while trying to fuse it with the Water Altar. In order to unlock the door the player must also have made a special air rune , a special earth rune , a special fire rune , and a special mind rune . Unlike normal water runes, this cannot be used to cast a spell.
9692:
The blank air rune is a quest item used in The Slug Menace . It is made by right-clicking on Page 1 of Brother Maledict 's holy book and choosing the "shape air" option with a rune essence or pure essence in the inventory. During this process the player must also make a blank water rune , a blank earth rune , a blank fire rune , and a blank mind rune using page 2 and page 3 . The player needs a chisel in their inventory to make these runes. Make more than one blank because you can fail while chiselling the shape of the rune, and/or binding it with the element of the rune.

When used on the Air Altar in the usual way it turns into a special air rune which is needed later in the quest. This item is lost upon death with all the others blank runes aswell.
9693:
An air rune is a special type of air rune used during The Slug Menace quest. It is made by using a blank air rune on the Air Altar in the normal way and is used to unlock a mysterious door in the newly discovered shrine beneath Witchaven.

In order to unlock the door, the player must also have made a special earth rune, a special fire rune, a special mind rune, and a special water rune.

It cannot replace a normal air rune during spells.
9694:
The blank earth rune is a quest item used in The Slug Menace . It is made by right-clicking on Page 1 of Brother Maledict 's holy book and choosing the "shape earth" option with a rune essence or pure essence in the inventory. During this process the player must also make a blank air rune , a blank water rune , a blank fire rune , and a blank mind rune using page 2 and page 3 . The player needs a chisel in their inventory to make these runes.

Make more than one blank because you can fail while chiselling the shape of the rune, and/or binding it with the element of the rune.

When used on an Earth Altar in the usual way it turns into a special earth rune which is needed later in the quest. This item is lost upon death with all the others blank runes aswell.
9695: An earth rune is a special type of earth rune used during The Slug Menace. It is made by using a blank earth rune on the Earth Altar, yielding 2 Runecraft experience regardless of whether the essence is successfully empowered or not. This experience is given even if It is used to unlock a mysterious door in the newly discovered shrine beneath Witchaven. In order to unlock the door the player must also have made a special air rune, a special fire rune, a special mind rune and a special water rune. It is made by using one of the three pages that are found during the quest. You must have one or more rune essence as there is the chance that you might shatter the essence creating "rune shards". Unlike normal earth runes, this cannot be used to cast a spell.
9696:
The blank mind rune is a quest item used in The Slug Menace . It is made by right-clicking on Page 3 of Brother Maledict 's holy book and choosing the "shape mind" option with a rune essence or pure essence in the inventory. During this process the player must also make a blank air rune , a blank earth rune , a blank fire rune , and a blank water rune using page 1 and page 2 . The player needs a chisel in their inventory to make these runes. It is recommended that players make more than one blank because players can fail while chiselling the shape of the rune, as well as when binding it with the element of the rune.

When used on a Mind Altar in the usual way it turns into a special mind rune which is needed later in the quest. This item is lost upon death with all the others blank runes aswell.
9697: A mind rune is a special type of mind rune used during The Slug Menace. Unlike normal mind runes, this cannot be used to cast a spell.

9702: The stick is an animation item added alongside the skill tutors update. It is temporarily wielded by the player during the animation for casting Lumbridge Home Teleport . Aside from this, it cannot be obtained.
9703:
A Training sword is a beginner weapon . It has identical stats to a bronze sword .

It is obtained for free along with a training shield from the Melee combat tutor , just south of the Lumbridge General Store . It can be replaced if lost, but only one can be obtained at a time. Due to the accessibility, this sword is ideal for players who are new to the game and have just finished Tutorial Island .
9704: The training shield is a beginner's item. The shield has an appearance similar to a white decorative shield and has the same bonuses as a wooden shield , though it weighs significantly more. It can be obtained for free from the melee combat tutor east of Lumbridge Castle . Players are only allowed one shield at any time.
9705: The training bow can be obtained from the Ranged combat tutor in Lumbridge . As it only requires a Ranged level of 1 to wield, it can be used by all players. It can only fire training arrows , which are given to players in sets of 25 by the tutor. It has the same stats as a shortbow .
9706:
Training arrows are arrows given by the ranged combat tutor . They can only be fired using a training bow . The combat stats of the arrows are equivalent to bronze arrows but are less used due to the fact that they can only be fired by a training bow .

Training arrows can be collected from the ranged combat tutor (east of Lumbridge Castle ), along with a training bow, every 30 minutes. Although technically the player cannot claim more than 25, arrows on the ground do not count towards that limit. This means that a player can shoot the arrows without picking them up, claim an extra 25 arrows, and then pick up the fired ones from the ground, obtaining more than 25 in total.

The time limit is shared with the magic combat tutor , meaning runes must not have been collected from the magic combat tutor in the past 30 minutes to be able to receive training arrows.
9712:
Spells are a series of unobtainable items that exist in the game cache. Presumably, they are used in the Spellbook interface. While originally a Spell item existed for every magic spell, since 2014 this has not been necessary.

In an update in 2018 which reworked the Spellbook, the original scroll appearance of the items was removed.
9715:
The slashed book is a quest item used in Elemental Workshop I. It is made by using a knife or any slashweapon on a battered book. Additionally, it can be found by searching the bookcase where the battered book was originally found, only after creating a slashed book for the first time.

It is used to make elemental shields or mind shields.

The slashed book (or the battered book) may be one of the items on the item list, given by Thorgel, that is needed to receive a death talisman during or after Mourning's End II; however, it is not needed to finish the quest as long as you already have a death talisman or catalytic talisman.

Duplicates can be drop tricked by searching the bookcase to obtain another only after the player has created a slashed book. Duplicates can be obtained after completing the quest.
9716: Rocks are an unobtainable item released with the rework of Elemental Workshop I . Their internal name of "Rock remains" suggest they would have been left behind when killing an Earth elemental . However, both forms of the Earth elemental continue to drop the standard elemental rock , and this item cannot be obtained.
9717:
The Beaten book or the Book of the Elemental Helm begins the Elemental Workshop II quest. It can be found in the Digsite's Exam Centre library south-east of Varrock, or in your POH bookcase after completing the quest (Book of the Elemental Helm), and has a scroll inside it as a bookmark. This scroll helps find the key to get into a lower level of the workshop.

To make a mind helmet for the quest you must have this book in your inventory after which the book serves no purpose beyond reading (other than use for Kandarin Medium Diary). If the book is lost or destroyed prior to completion of the quest, another may be obtained by searching the Exam Centre's library again after dropping the scroll obtained from the book.
9718: The crane schematic is an item used in the Elemental Workshop II quest . It includes instructions on how to make a crane claw from elemental metal . This item is gained by searching one of two crates near the entrance to the Elemental Workshop II quest room.
9719:
The lever schematic is an item that can be obtained during the Elemental Workshop II quest from the same crate as the claw schematic.

This is a clue as to the correct solution to the pipe connection puzzle in the junction box. It shows that the middle pipe going to the lever, top-right in the interface of the junction box, provides incoming water that is then directed by the lever down one of the other 2 pipes and on to the press. In combination with how the pipes are plumbed into the back of the junction box, this means that the top-right pipe end in the interface must be connected to the large water supply pipe, top-middle in the interface and that the other 2 pipes coming from the lever, bottom-right and bottom-middle in the interface must be connected to the 2 pipes going to the press, top-left and bottom-left in the interface. Given these constraints, there is only one possible solution.
9720: The crane claw is a quest item made in the Elemental Workshop II quest . It is made from elemental metal , requiring 20 Smithing , yielding 20 Smithing experience . It is used to repair the crane.
9721:
The scroll is used in the Elemental Workshop II quest. It is used for locating the pipe that contains a key.

In the Elemental Workshop II quest, players must use this scroll to guide them to the pipe that contains the key which unlocks the second level of the workshop.

To re-obtain it after it is lost, you must find the beaten book again at the Exam Centre and read it (you cannot already have a scroll in your inventory or bank.) The Beaten Book is found on a bookshelf in the south-east corner of the Exam Centre (the north-eastern bookshelf, facing north.) It is, however, useless to re-obtain it.
9722: A key is an item used in the Elemental Workshop II quest. It is found by walking the path described on the scroll and searching the machinery. It is used to open the hatch to the second level of the workshop.
9723: The pipe is an item used during Elemental Workshop II in the Elemental Workshop in Seers' Village . The pipe is found in one of the crates in the workshop. It is used to repair the piping in the water tank, which is needed so the machine can produce a primed mind bar .
9724: A large cog is an item used in the Elemental Workshop II quest. It is found by searching the catwalk and downstairs in the secondary Elemental Workshop, and the location is random for each player. It can be used, along with the small cog and medium cog , to repair the wind tunnel, by placing it on the right-hand pin on the east side of the room.
9725: Medium cog is an item used in the Elemental Workshop II quest. It is found by searching upstairs and downstairs in the secondary Elemental Workshop, and the location is random for each player. It can be used, along with the large cog and small cog, to repair the wind tunnel by placing it on the lower-left pin on the east side of the room.
9726: A small cog is an item used in the Elemental Workshop II quest. It is found by searching upstairs and downstairs in the second area of Elemental Workshop, and the location is random for each player. It can be used, along with the large cog and medium cog, to repair the wind tunnel, by placing it on the upper-left pin on the east side of the room.
9727: A primed bar is an elemental metal that has undergone several processes making it receptive to magical forces formed by machines in the basement of the Elemental Workshop . They can be turned into primed mind bars .
9728:
Primed mind bars are made during and after the Elemental Workshop II quest in the Elemental Workshop in Seers' Village . The bar may be created by placing a primed bar into the extractor gun found in the mind room and operating the machinery. Doing so will temporarily reduce the player's Magic level by 20.

The bar may be smithed into a mind shield with a slashed book or a mind helmet with a beaten book , by using it on the workbench in the first level of the Elemental Workshop.
9729:
The elemental helmet is magical headwear that can be made after completing the Elemental Workshop II quest. The helmet is created by using an elemental metal on a workbench within the Elemental Workshop with a beaten book in the player's inventory. This requires level 20 Smithing and grants 20 experience.

Although the helmet can be traded between players, it can only be equipped by those who have completed Elemental Workshop II.
9731:
A mind shield is an upgraded version of the elemental shield, offering an additional +3 magic defence bonus over the latter. It is made during and after the Elemental Workshop II quest in the elemental workshop dungeon.

Making the shield requires 30 Smithing, a primed mind bar, a hammer, and a slashed book in the inventory. Right-click the "Smith" option on a workbench in the elemental workshop to smith the shield, which grants the player 30 Smithing experience. Equipping a mind shield requires completion of Elemental Workshop II.

The Defence cape is a Cape of Accomplishment that players can purchase only when they've reached level 99 in the Defence skill . It can be bought from Harlan , the Melee combat tutor, for 99,000 coins from where he resides, close to the Lumbridge general store .

Like all skill capes , the Defence cape gives +9 to all defensive stats , and also a +4 bonus to prayer if it is trimmed, which requires a separate skill at level 99. The cape is automatically trimmed if this condition is met.

When the defence cape is equipped, players can enable the cape to act as a ring of life . This option is toggle-able, and can be enabled/disabled by the player at any given time. When the effect occurs, the wearer will receive the message Your cape saves you. . Upon completion of the medium Ardougne diary , the respawn point of this effect can be toggled to Ardougne . However, an actual death will result in the player respawning to their respawn point .

As it acts like a ring of life, it is one of the few items whose teleports will work up to level 30 Wilderness, while most other means of teleportation will not work above level 20 Wilderness.

This item can be stored in the cape rack of a costume room , as part of the Defence cape set, along with the hood . Ultimate Ironmen will be unable to retrieve individual pieces until the full set is stored.

The ranging cape is a Cape of Accomplishment awarded to players who have achieved 99 Ranged . The skillcape and its respective hood can be bought from Aaron the Armour salesman in the Ranging Guild for 99,000 coins.

Like all skill capes , the Ranging cape gives +9 to all defensive stats, and also a +4 bonus to prayer if it is trimmed, which requires a separate skill at level 99. The cape is automatically trimmed if this condition is met.

When the ranging cape is equipped, it grants players the ammo-saving effects of Ava's accumulator . Completion of Animal Magnetism is not required to benefit from this perk. [ 1 ] By default, the cape will only provide the 72% ammo-saving effect of the accumulator, not the improved 80% savings of Ava's assembler . However, Vorkath's head can be used on the cape to increase its ammo-saving rate to 80% to match the assembler (an assembler cannot be used as a substitute). This consumes the head, and will upgrade all ranging and max capes currently in possession or purchased in the future. Note that upgrading the cape does not give it the ranged strength and accuracy bonuses of Ava's assembler.

Like Ava's devices, the ranging cape is affected by metallic interference .

The ranging cape will also collect miscellaneous steel items (or mithril items after it has been upgraded with a Vorkath's head) into the player's inventory; as with the Ava's devices this can be disabled with the right-click Commune option.

The Hitpoints cape is a Cape of Accomplishment that can be bought from Surgeon General Tafani in the Emir's Arena hospital after achieving level 99 in the Hitpoints skill . The skillcape and its corresponding hood can be purchased for 99,000 coins . The skillcape has a white colour and red stripes if trimmed.

Like all skill capes , the Hitpoints cape gives +9 to all defensive stats , and also a +4 bonus to prayer if it is trimmed, which requires a separate skill at level 99. The cape is automatically trimmed if this condition is met.

When the Hitpoints cape is equipped, the player's natural Hitpoints regeneration rate is doubled to 2 Hitpoints per minute instead of the natural rate of 1 Hitpoint per minute. This does not stack with the Rapid Heal prayer , but does stack with the regen bracelet to regenerate 4 Hitpoints per minute.

Utilising the worn boost effect on the cape will instantly give you +1 health point. This can be used once per minute.

On the mobile and Official Client the effect is visible in the form of a second blue sector around the player's hitpoints orb . This blue sector is only visible when its cooldown is less than that of the natural regeneration segment (otherwise it will be hidden behind it). The blue regeneration bar is functionally independent from your natural regeneration bar, and cannot be influenced by external factors such as Rapid heal (though Rapid Heal can still be used to offset your natural regeneration to better match that of the blue regeneration bar for optimal healing). Despite not stacking with the Rapid Heal prayer , the prayer causes the blue regeneration bar to completely disappear, though it does not reset.

The Agility cape is the only piece of the graceful set that can be purchased with coins.

9774:
The Herblore cape, otherwise known as the Skillcape of Herblore, is a Cape of Accomplishment that may only be acquired and worn by players who have achieved the maximum level in the Herblore skill, 99. Once players have trained to this level, they may purchase the cape from Kaqemeex the druid, located in the druid circle of Taverley - slightly north of the eastern end of the witch's house - for which a fee of 99,000 coins is charged. When this fee is paid, the player receives both the cape and the matching hood. Herblore capes are a dark green colour, and have a yellow-gold trim for players who have more than one 99.

Like all skillcapes, the Herblore cape gives +9 to all defensive stats, and also a +4 bonus to prayer if it is trimmed, which requires a second skill of 99. The cape is automatically trimmed if this condition is met.

Players can search the Herblore cape to obtain a pestle and mortar. In addition, while the cape is equipped, grimy herbs can be used to create unfinished potions; doing so gives the experience of cleaning the herb. Zahur in Nardah will create unfinished potions for 200 coins each when the player has the cape equipped, the same perk from completing the Hard Desert Diary, though this will still only work with clean herbs.

This item can be stored in the cape rack of a costume room, as part of the Herblore cape set, along with the hood. Ultimate Ironmen will be unable to retrieve individual pieces until the full set is stored.

As of 1 August 2026, there are 168,336 players that have achieved level 99 in Herblore.

A Fletching cape can be purchased for 99,000 coins from Hickton at Catherby by players who have achieved level 99 Fletching. It is the Cape of Accomplishment for the Fletching skill. Like all other skill capes, it can temporarily boost your Fletching level by one. Fletching capes are of a slightly saturated teal colour and have a gold trim if the player has more than one level 99 skill.

Players can search the cape and obtain a mithril grapple and bronze crossbow three times per day. This does not work in duels.

The Fletching cape has a niche use where its perk can be utilised when entering Armadyl's Eyrie in the God Wars Dungeon if the player does not need a crossbow to fight Kree'arra. This is done by dropping two supplies, searching the cape, equipping the crossbow and grapple, grappling across, dropping two more supplies on the other side, grappling back, picking up the original two supplies, grappling back across, un-equip and drop the crossbow and grapple, and finally picking up the second set of two supplies.

This item can be stored in the cape rack of a costume room, as part of the Fletching cape set, along with the hood. Ultimate Ironmen will be unable to retrieve individual pieces until the full set is stored.

A Slayer cape is the Cape of Accomplishment for players who have achieved level 99 in the Slayer skill. The cape can be purchased for 99,000 coins from Duradel (or Kuradal after completion of While Guthix Sleeps ), in Shilo Village . Slayer capes are black in colour, and have a red trim if the player has more than one level 99 skill. As Duradel is in Shilo Village, players must have completed the Shilo Village quest in order to buy the cape.

Like all skill capes , the Slayer cape gives +9 to all defensive stats, and also a +4 bonus to prayer if it is trimmed, which requires a separate skill at level 99. The cape is automatically trimmed if this condition is met.

When the Slayer cape is equipped or in the inventory , there is a 10% chance of being given the option to have their previous Slayer task reassigned by the same Slayer Master the player got their last task from, either in person or through the Astral Contact spell. [ 1 ] If activated on a boss task, the assigned boss can potentially be a different one.

When the cape effect activates on Konar quo Maten 's tasks, she will retain the same location as with the old task. On Mortimer 's tasks, the modifier of the task is retained.

Showing the cape to a master also bypasses combat level restrictions on tasks for lower-levelled accounts. When activated after skipping a task, they will offer the last task that was assigned, rather than the last one that was completed. If using Slayer Rewards#Task Storage , you can receive the same task you have stored, but the Slayer skillcape perk will not apply.

9789:
A Construct. cape or Construction cape is the Cape of Accomplishment for the Construction skill . It can be purchased for 99,000 coins alongside the Construction hood from any Estate agent by players who have achieved skill mastery (level 99) in the Construction skill.

Like all skill capes , the Construction cape gives +9 to all defensive stats , and also a +4 bonus to prayer if it is trimmed, which requires a separate skill at level 99. The cape is automatically trimmed if this condition is met.

When the construction cape is equipped or in the inventory, it provides unlimited teleports to the player's own house and to house portals , which are located in Rimmington , Taverley , Pollnivneach , Hosidius , Rellekka , Aldarin , Brimhaven , Yanille , and Prifddinas . All teleports are available regardless of where a player's house is located. This perk provides nearly the same destinations as redirected teleport to house tablets , with the only exception being Trollheim as there is no house portal there. This allows the player to freely relocate their house without having to consider its utility as a teleport destination.

When using the Tele to POH right-click function, the player character will always be placed just north of the exit portal in their house, or just outside the house portal , depending on their house teleport settings. If multiple exit portals exist in the player's house, the teleport function will prioritise the one that was built last.

This item can be stored in the cape rack of a costume room , as part of the Construction cape set, along with the hood . Ultimate Ironmen will be unable to retrieve individual pieces until the full set is stored. It can also be displayed on a cape hanger in the achievement gallery , from which the owner of the house can access its right-click teleports.

Like all skill capes , the Cooking cape gives +9 to all defensive stats , and also a +4 bonus to prayer if it is trimmed, which requires a separate skill at level 99. The cape is automatically trimmed if this condition is met.

When the Cooking cape is equipped, players will never burn food. The only exception to this is raw oomlie , which is impossible to successfully cook. It can also be used in place of a chef's hat or varrock armour 3 / 4 to enter the Cooking Guild .

This item can be stored in the cape rack of a costume room , as part of the Cooking cape set, along with the hood . Ultimate Ironmen will be unable to retrieve individual pieces until the full set is stored.

As of 1 August 2026, there are 481,041 players that have achieved level 99 in Cooking.
