A Woodcutting cape can be purchased from Wilfred (found south of the furnace in Lumbridge ) for 99,000 coins and comes with the Woodcutting hood only for players who have achieved level 99 Woodcutting .

Like all skill capes , the Woodcutting cape gives +9 to all defensive stats, and also a +4 bonus to prayer if it is trimmed, which requires a separate skill at level 99. The cape is automatically trimmed if this condition is met.

When a Woodcutting cape is equipped, players will have an additional 10% chance of a bird nest falling while chopping trees. [ 1 ] This boost does not apply to clue nests , only ring , egg , and seed nests . [ 2 ]

The Woodcutting cape can be stored in a Forestry kit or basket that has been expanded by way of a cape pouch , allowing you to receive its bird nest boosting effects while wearing either of those instead. Merely carrying a Forestry kit or basket is not sufficient to benefit from the effects of a Woodcutting cape stored inside; it must be equipped.

It should be noted that boosting past level 99 Woodcutting does not have an effect on the rate at which players receive logs. [ 3 ] Therefore, the +1 boost a player gains when equipping the skillcape - as well as any other boosts, such as the dragon / infernal axe special attack - aren't necessary when woodcutting.

The Farming cape can be purchased for 99,000 coins alongside the Farming hood from Martin the Master Gardener at Draynor Village by players who have achieved skill mastery (level 99) in Farming. It is the Cape of Accomplishment for the Farming skill.

Like all skill capes, the Farming cape gives +9 to all defensive stats, and also a +4 bonus to prayer if it is trimmed, which requires a separate skill at level 99. The cape is automatically trimmed if this condition is met.

When the Farming cape is equipped, herb patches will have a 5% increase to the base chance to save harvest lives and gain extra herbs. This effect stacks additively with the magic secateurs. It also provides unlimited teleports to the Farming Guild in the Kebos Lowlands. Unlike the magic secateurs, this cape does not increase yield when harvesting herbs off a herbiboar.

Like all skillcapes, equipping the cape or using the "Boost" option in the equipment menu temporarily boosts Farming by +1, up to 100. This only affects the yield of belladonna, as limpwurt plants require a boost to 101 for additional yield. Unequipping the cape will remove the boost. This boost cannot be used to restore temporary skill drains.

This item can be stored in the cape rack of a costume room, as part of the Farming cape set, along with the hood. Ultimate Ironmen will be unable to retrieve individual pieces until the full set is stored.

The cape is noteworthy for providing an unlimited, wearable teleport that brings the player to the Farming Guild. The teleport location is close to both a bank, between 16 and 18 tiles, and a spirit tree, between 24 and 26 tiles, and therefore provides quick access to both the Grand Exchange and a player's house, as well as other locations.

As of 1 August 2026, there are 381,592 players that have achieved level 99 in Farming.

9813:
The quest point cape is a cape of accomplishment that can be obtained by players who have completed all quests (excluding miniquests ). The cape, along with the quest point hood , can be purchased from the Wise Old Man in Draynor Village for 99,000 coins . To trim the cape, players must complete all achievement diaries , thus earning them the achievement diary cape as well.

Should a new quest be released, the cape will be unequipped, and the player will not be able to equip or operate it until the new quest is completed. If the player's inventory is full, the cape will be banked instead. In the event that their inventory and bank are both full, the cape will be lost , and will have to be re-purchased from the Wise Old Man.

The cape is a popular goal for ironmen due to its quick teleport to a fairy ring . Additionally, performing the quest cape emote in the Wise Old Man 's house is an elite task in the Lumbridge & Draynor Diary . The emote can also be used at the top of Falador Castle for a task in the elite Falador Diary .

Unlike skill hiscores, there is no official way to track the number of players who currently own the cape; it must be shared by Jagex. In February 2020, there were 61,766 current members who had obtained the quest point cape. [ 1 ]

This item can be stored in the cape rack of a costume room , as part of the Quest point cape set, along with the hood . Ultimate Ironmen will be unable to retrieve individual pieces until the full set is stored. Players who own a quest cape but no longer have all quests completed will find they cannot store the cape until they re-complete all quests. However, quest capes that were already mounted on the cape rack prior to new quests becoming available will remain on the rack. Quest capes on cape racks therefore represent that the home owner at one point or another had attained all available quest points at the time of mounting.

The goutweedy lump is a quest item found during the My Arm's Big Adventure quest. At the start of the quest, My Arm the troll asks the player to obtain it from the cauldron at Death Plateau so that he can grow fresh supplies of the herb at the Troll Stronghold .

According to My Arm, a man was cooked by the troll cooks on Death Plateau, Ash and Dung . While searching his trousers they found something that had similar properties to goutweed, but was not goutweed ( gout tuber ) so they threw it into the cooking pot along with their captive. When he finished cooking and they ate him they discovered that he was flavoured like Goutweed.
9902:
Hardy gout tubers are obtained during the My Arm's Big Adventure quest from Murcaily . They cannot be dug up or planted in a herb patch. A single tuber is given to the player after obtaining 60% favour, but is immediately replaced by a handful of tubers by Murcaily after My Arm goes on a rampage.

They are given to My Arm towards the end of the quest, before the final fight with the Baby Roc and Giant Roc .

If lost, the manual can be reclaimed from My Arm (before Making Friends with My Arm) or Drunken Dwarf's Leg, or from a bookcase within a player-owned house.

When loaded with a white destabiliser , shooting a possessed toy would reveal a coloured poltergeist that could then be defeated by loading the corresponding destabiliser and shooting again.

9919: The Evil root was an item found during the 2013 Halloween event by cutting roots from the Haunted Tree , requiring an axe . If 10 of them were given to Diango , he would reward the player with a Jack lantern mask .

If destroyed, a replacement can be obtained from Diango in Draynor Village or from the toy box of a costume room .

9932:
Auguste's sapling is given during the Enlightened Journey quest by Auguste to grow into a willow tree in order to obtain Willow branches to build the basket of the balloon for the Balloon transport system. The branches can also be cut off any existing willow tree in a farming patch or obtained by trading with other players. If the sapling is lost before it is planted, another can be purchased from Auguste for 30,000 coins. However, as a willow seed costs 58 coins, this option is only reasonable for ironmen who are unwilling or unable to obtain a seed by other methods.

Auguste gives the player the sapling for free, only the first time. With it, he also gives the player a basket of apples, to pay a gardener to watch over it. Growing this sapling to a willow tree takes 4 hours. The sapling cannot be re-obtained after completing the quest, and cannot be stored in the seed vault.
9933: A balloon structure is used in the Enlightened Journey quest. It is made by using papyrus with a ball of wool . It can be made into an origami balloon by adding an unlit candle . The origami balloon can be lit so it flies away. Players can still craft this item after they have completed the quest .
9934:
An origami balloon is a smaller version of a hot air balloon made during the Enlightened Journey quest to test the scientific principles of a hot air balloon. It will end up being burnt.

The Origami balloon can be made by players who have reached the point in the quest in which they are made. Dyes can be applied to the balloon as well. It will produce the same result and burn after a short distance flight (if there are no obstacles in front of the balloon, it will fly farther; otherwise, it will burn down before it reaches an obstacle).

Making an origami balloon provides 35 Crafting experience.

All of the necessary parts, with the exception of papyrus , can be found in the dwarven city of Keldagrim . The city's general store , Gunslik's Assorted Items stocks candles, as well as tinderboxes. On the east side of the city, in the marketplace, the Carefree Crafting Stall stocks balls of wool. Papyrus can be bought in Shilo Village , Al Kharid or East Ardougne , found in a cupboard on the ground floor of the White Knights' Castle , and dye can be made in Pollnivneach and Draynor Village or purchased in Lletya .

The sandbag is a quest item used during Enlightened Journey as an anchor for the air balloon. It is made by using a sack on a sand pit or a bucket of sand. Players can use a bucket on the sandbag to make it into a bucket of sand.

For non-ironmen accounts, the sandbag can be obtained quite easily with the use of the Grand Exchange. A bucket of sand can be used on the sack to make the sandbag even before starting the quest. Players can also make the sandbag after quest completion, although there is no further use for this at present.
9944:
The bomber jacket is one of two items of clothing that form the Bomber jacket costume, the other being the Bomber cap. Players obtain the set after completing Enlightened Journey. If lost, the jacket can be retrieved again from Auguste on Entrana. It can be used as warm clothing at Wintertodt.

This item can be stored in the armour case of a costume room, as part of the Bomber jacket costume set. Ultimate Ironmen will be unable to retrieve individual pieces until the full set is stored.
9945:
The bomber cap and the bomber jacket form the bomber jacket costume, which is a reward for completing the Enlightened Journey Quest. If lost on death, a replacement can be claimed from Auguste in Entrana.

The bomber cap can be combined with the gnome goggles from the Gnome Restaurant minigame into a cap and goggles by talking with Auguste on Entrana.

It can be used as warm clothing for the Wintertodt.

This item can be stored in the armour case of a costume room, as part of the Bomber jacket costume set. Ultimate Ironmen will be unable to retrieve individual pieces until the full set is stored.
9946:
Cap and goggles are a combination of gnome goggles , obtained during Gnome Restaurant , and the bomber cap reward from the Enlightened Journey quest . The items can be combined by talking with Auguste on the island of Entrana . To separate the combined cap and goggles, right click and choose "split".

If you die with this item, the goggles will disappear.

The cap and goggles can be used as warm clothing for the Wintertodt .

This item can be stored in the armour case of a costume room , as part of the Bomber jacket costume set. Ultimate Ironmen will be unable to retrieve individual pieces until the full set is stored.
9947: The old red disk is a quest item used in The Fremennik Trials quest. It is found during Peer the Seer 's part of the quest while searching upstairs in his house. It is found by studying the mounted unicorn head. The disk is used on an abstract mural downstairs in his house in order to obtain a vase lid needed to complete Peer's challenge.
9948:
The Hunter cape is the Cape of Accomplishment for the Hunter skill and can be purchased for 99,000 coins alongside the Hunter hood from the Hunting expert located in the Feldip Hills , by players who have achieved level 99 .

Like all skill capes , the Hunter cape gives +9 to all defensive stats , and also a +4 bonus to prayer if it is trimmed, which requires a separate skill at level 99. The cape is automatically trimmed if this condition is met.

The cape provides five teleports per day which can be used to travel to the carnivorous chinchompas in the Feldip Hunter area or the black chinchompas in the Wilderness Hunter area . A third teleport to the Hunter Guild can be unlocked by bringing a cape, worn or in the inventory, to Guildmaster Apatura at the guild. Unlike the previous teleports, the guild teleport has no limit on the number of daily teleports.

This item can be stored in the cape rack of a costume room , as part of the Hunter cape set, along with the hood . Ultimate Ironmen will be unable to retrieve individual pieces until the full set is stored.

This item can also be stored in the Huntsman's kit .

The Hunter hood is the skillcape hood associated with having achieved skill mastery in the Hunter skill . Players may buy the hood alongside the Hunter cape from Hunting expert in the Feldip Hunter area for 99,000 coins , providing that they have level 99 Hunter, although the hood and the cape may not be purchased separately. The hood itself provides absolutely no offensive or defensive bonuses and may be worn for purely aesthetic purposes.

While the hood is bought with the skillcape, it is not needed to perform the emote associated with it; the skillcape is the only essential item.

Should players lose the hood, they may reclaim it from the hunting expert for free.

This item can be stored in the cape rack of a costume room , as part of the Hunter cape set. Ultimate Ironmen will be unable to retrieve individual pieces until the full set is stored.

9978:
Raw bird meat can be obtained from Hunter birds and bird houses . It can be skewered with an iron spit to make skewered bird meat , which can then be cooked on a fire to make roast bird meat , requiring 11 Cooking and 20 Firemaking , granting 62 Cooking experience.

Despite being obtained from Hunter creatures, bird meat is not considered a Hunter meat and so cannot be used to recharge a quetzal whistle or stored in a meat pouch .
9980:
Roast bird meat are a type of food that can be obtained by cooking skewered bird meat on a fire , requiring level 11 Cooking and granting 62.5 experience when successful. Cooking the skewered bird meat also requires level 20 Firemaking , though it does not give any Firemaking experience.

Players may burn the meat while cooking one, resulting in burnt bird meat ; the burn rate while cooking these will decrease as players reach higher Cooking levels. It will stop burning entirely at Cooking level 99.

When eaten, roast bird meat heals 6 hitpoints.
9982:
Burnt bird meat is the result of accidentally burning raw bird meat while attempting to make roast bird meat . The burn rate while cooking these will decrease as players reach higher Cooking levels, stopping entirely at level 99.

The burnt bird meat has no use whatsoever. Like most other burnt food, it is tradeable to other players but not on the Grand Exchange .
9984: Skewered bird meat is created when an iron spit is used on raw bird meat . The skewered bird meat can then be cooked on a fire to create roast bird meat , granting 62.5 Cooking experience and requiring 11 Cooking.
9986:
Raw beast meat is dropped by kebbits that are tracked and caught using a noose wand and the Hunter skill . It can be added to the Small meat pouch and Large meat pouch , but not used to recharge any of the Quetzal whistles .

Level 21 Cooking and 20 Firemaking is needed to cook raw beast meat. It can be skewered with an iron spit to make skewered beast , which can then be cooked on a fire to make roast beast meat , which gives 82.5 Cooking experience.
9988:
Roast beast meat are a type of food that can be obtained by cooking a skewered beast on a fire , requiring level 21 Cooking and granting 82.5 experience when successful. Players may burn the meat while cooking one, resulting in burnt beast meat ; the burn rate while cooking these will decrease as players reach higher Cooking levels. It will stop burning entirely at Cooking level 99.

When eaten, roast beast meat heals 8 hitpoints .
9990:
Burnt beast meat is the result of accidentally burning skewered beast while attempting to make roast beast meat . The burn rate while cooking these will decrease as players reach higher Cooking levels, stopping entirely at level 99.

The burnt beast meat has no use whatsoever. Like most other burnt food, it is tradeable to other players but not on the Grand Exchange .
9992: Skewered beast is a raw food created by using raw beast meat on an iron spit . It can be cooked only on a fire to make roasted beast meat .
9994:
Spicy tomatoes are created by using a tomato with a bowl when the player has a knife in their inventory , and using spice or gnome spice on the bowl of chopped tomatoes . When creating spicy tomatoes only spice is needed to add to the bottom most chopped tomato, as the spice is actually added to the closest tomato to the first inventory slot. They can then be used on a set box trap as bait for the Hunter skill. They may also be eaten and they heal 2 hitpoints .

Spicy chopped tomatoes are a very uncommon item. They are rarely made due to their complexity, but they are intended to be used as bait for chinchompas . It is not recommended to use bait; in fact, not using bait is much faster and does not require constant bank trips.
9996:
Spicy minced meat is created by using spice or gnome spice on a bowl of minced meat. Minced meat is made by using Cooked meat on a bowl while having a knife in your inventory. Eating spicy minced meat will heal three hitpoints.

They can be used as bait for carnivorous and black chinchompas, but chinchompas can be caught fine without the bait. This, alongside the fact that spicy minced meat is not stackable, makes them impractical for hunting.
9998:
Hunter potions are potions that boost your Hunter level by 3. Players with at least 53 Herblore can make this potion. The required ingredients are one clean avantoe and kebbit teeth dust. 120 Herblore experience is given per potion made. A player can obtain kebbit teeth dust by using a pestle and mortar on kebbit teeth. These teeth are loot from hunting sabre-toothed kebbits.

After Barbarian Herblore Training is completed, caviar can be added to a hunter potion(2) to produce a hunting mix. This requires 58 Herblore and provides 40 Herblore experience. A hunting mix has 2 doses, each of which heals 6 Hitpoints in addition to the normal hunter potion boost.

After Barbarian Herblore Training is completed, caviar can be added to a hunter potion(2) to produce a hunting mix. This requires 58 Herblore and provides 40 Herblore experience. A hunting mix has 2 doses, each of which heals 6 Hitpoints in addition to the normal hunter potion boost.
10006:
A bird snare is a type of trap used in the Hunter skill. The bird snaring technique is used to catch several birds . With the required Hunter level, the player may set up a bird snare and wait for a bird to approach the trap.

If the prey is successfully caught, the snare will trap the bird, and the player will have the option to "check" the trap. If not successful, the trap will still snap, and the player will have to reset it. A bird snare will not catch birds if the user is standing directly on the bird snare.

Smoking a trap will increase the catch rate by +2%. [ 1 ] Due to the low increase of the catch rate, most players believe that smoking traps doesn't justify the extra actions it takes.

Bird snares may be bought from Aleck's Hunter Emporium in Yanille , the Nardah Hunter Shop in Nardah , or Imia's Supplies in the Hunter Guild . One can also be obtained for free by searching the south-western crate in Hugor 's house at Land's End (multiple snares can be obtained by dropping the snare and searching again).

Bird snares are also obtainable from a Hunter kit , the only way native to the Fremennik region to acquire one and necessary to complete the Fremennik Diary .
10008:
A box trap is a type of trap used in the Hunter skill to catch ferrets, embertailed jerboas and chinchompas. Using a box trap requires the specific Hunter level needed for the prey, as well as partial completion of the Eagles' Peak quest.

Whenever prey passes a trap, it has a chance of either being caught in the trap or evading it. If the prey is successfully caught, the box trap will close in around the animal and start shaking, at which point the player will have the option to "check" the trap for loot and experience. If the prey evades the trap, the trap will simply close, at which point the player will have to reset it.

Box traps may be bought from Aleck's Hunter Emporium in Yanille, the Nardah Hunter Shop in Nardah, or Imia's Supplies in the Hunter Guild. One can also be obtained for free by searching the crate adjacent to the bookcases in the north-western house at Land's End. They can also be obtained from Hunter kits.

A butterfly net is an item used in the Hunter skill. It is wielded to capture implings, and butterflies or moths throughout Gielinor and Puro-Puro, and bats in the Chambers of Xeric. Catching an impling without an impling jar will automatically loot it, and catching a butterfly or moth without a butterfly jar will automatically release it. A jar is required to keep them for later use.

The magic butterfly net is an upgraded butterfly net that requires 17 Hunter to obtain, and increases the player's chances of capturing butterflies, implings, and bats by about 7.8%.

Butterfly nets and jars may be bought from Aleck's Hunter Emporium. in Yanille, the Nardah Hunter Shop in Nardah, or Imia's Supplies in the Hunter Guild. Alternatively, they can also be obtained from a hunter kit, which is obtained by casting the Hunter Kit spell on the Lunar spellbook, requiring a Magic level of 71. A butterfly net can also be obtained for free from a crate in the north-east corner of Lan the Butcher's house at Land's End.

Elnock Inquisitor located inside Puro-Puro will give you a starter set consisting of 1 butterfly net, 7 impling jars, and an impling scroll.

Players can right-click this net to open the Impling Tracker, which tracks how many implings they've caught both in Puro-Puro and the surface world.
10012: A butterfly jar is used to contain captured butterflies or moths with the Hunter skill. These jars can also be turned into impling jars by treating them with imp repellent. Butterfly jars cannot be used to hold implings. They can be created by using one charge of a jar generator or bought in four different Hunter shops in Gielinor (in Yanille, Nardah, the Hunter Guild, and The Great Conch).

A black warlock is a members-only item that can be made by catching a black warlock whilst they have a butterfly jar in their inventory . This requires level 45 Hunter to do so with a butterfly net or a magic butterfly net , or level 55 Hunter without, and gives 54 experience points. They can be found in the southern to middle part of the Feldip Hunter area and in the Farming Guild 's Advanced tier.

Once caught, players can right-click "Release" the filled butterfly jar to boost their Strength by 4 + 15% of their Strength level (rounded down). In a multi-combat zone , the item may be used on another player to share the effect with them and up to three players within a 5x5 area of the target. Players must have Accept Aid toggled on to receive the boost. The empty butterfly jar will remain in the inventory after use.

With a pestle and mortar , players can combine the butterfly with raw hunter meat to create black warlock mix (2) .

This requires level 35 Hunter using a (magic) butterfly net and gives 44 experience points. Players with level 45 Hunter can catch them barehanded. These butterflies can be found in Weiss, the Rellekka Hunter area, outside the Farming Guild, or on Mons Gratia.

Once caught, players can right-click "Release" the filled butterfly jar to restore 15 hitpoints. Players must have Accept Aid toggled on to receive the healing. The empty butterfly jar will remain in the inventory after use.

With a pestle and mortar, players can combine the jarred butterfly with raw hunter meat to create snowy knight mix (2). Unlike other hunter's mixes, the snowy knight mix has a reduced "per-use" effect than the jarred butterfly, but has a greater overall effect (restoring only 8 hitpoints per use, with a total of 16 across two doses).

The Falconer's glove is used in the Hunter skill in the falconry hunting technique in the Piscatoris falconry area , which is located east of the Piscatoris Hunter Area . While wearing the glove, a player has a gyr falcon on their hand which they can send to catch spotted kebbits , dark kebbits and dashing kebbits . While wearing the glove, players cannot wear any other gloves , bracelets , weapons or shields .

A player can temporarily borrow the glove and falcon from Matthias for a fee of 500 coins, and it will be taken away from the player when they leave the fenced area. The fee must be paid every time the player returns to the area later to hunt more kebbits. Alternatively, players may pay a one-time fee of 500,000 coins for unlimited free glove rentals in the future. Players don't need to worry about logging out with the glove on, it will remain with them when they log back in.

When attempting to leave the area with the glove equipped, the player will state "I should return the glove I borrowed from the falconer before leaving.". Attempting to remove the glove yourself, will give the message You should speak to Matthias to get this removed safely. . Teleporting bypasses this restriction with the text As you leave, Matthias' falcon flies back to him.

A magic box is a type of trap used in the Hunter skill. The magic box trapping technique is used to catch imps . With 71 Hunter, the player may set up a magic box. When an imp passes the trap, it may be caught, but only when the player is not standing on the trap.

If the prey is successfully caught, the magic box will enclose the imp inside the box. Doing this creates an Imp-in-a-box , which can be used to bank 2 items or stacks of items, although it cannot be used while in combat or above level 30 Wilderness .

Adding bait (any bead ) to a trap will increase the catch rate by +3%. [ 1 ] It is not possible to smoke magic boxes, unlike other hunter traps, to increase the catch rate. Doing so yields the message, Imps steal so many human items, they're unlikely to be worried by human smells. Due to the low increase of the catch rate, as well as the impracticality and cost of bringing beads to bait the traps, it is generally considered not worth baiting the trap.

Magic boxes, as well as magic imp box packs containing 100 magic boxes, may be bought from Aleck's Hunter Emporium. in Yanille , the Nardah Hunter Shop. in Nardah , or Imia's Supplies in the Hunter Guild .

Having a magic box in your inventory prevents you from entering the Puro-Puro mini-game . Since magic boxes can be stored inside the Huntsman's kit , players can store the magic box before going inside the Puro-Puro mini-game. Players who attempt to activate the magic box within the mini-game will receive the message, You can't set up a trap here.

An imp-in-a-box is made by catching an imp with a magic box . It can be used to send items from anywhere to the bank .

It is used by right-clicking on it and choosing "Bank Imp-in-a-box"; then, a window will come up where the items to be sent to the bank can be selected (be careful to not click twice quickly, because items can move after clicking on the first one). Alternatively, simply use an item on the box for it to be sent to your bank. This method is a quick way for players with higher Hunter levels (71 required to catch imps) to quickly bank items. The imp will agree to take two items or stacks from the player to the bank in exchange for its freedom; however, it will refuse to do so in the following areas or scenarios:

The imp will also refuse to bank a player's looting bag , even outside of the Wilderness . If it is not one of the protected items , the imp-in-a-box is converted to a magic box upon death in the Wilderness.

Imps-in-boxes can be stored in the huntsman's kit . Having an imp-in-a-box in your inventory prevents you from entering the Puro-Puro mini-game .

Note that while the box can be used to send two items to the bank, it will be labelled Imp-in-a-box(2) ; when one has already been used, it will be labelled Imp-in-a-box(1) and when both have been used, it will revert to magic box .

A Teasing stick is used in Hunter to catch Spined larupia, Horned graahk, Sabre-toothed kyatt, sunlight antelope, and moonlight antelope. While carrying the teasing stick, players are able to "tease" these animals. This makes them aggressive toward the player, allowing players to lure them into a Pitfall trap.

Players with low combat levels should be wary of damage taken from the animals.

The teasing stick can first be used at level 31 Hunter to catch spined larupia, but there is no hunter requirement for having one. It can be purchased from Aleck's Hunter Emporium. in Yanille, Nardah Hunter Shop in Nardah, or Imia's Supplies in the Hunter Guild.

A teasing stick is one of several items that can be obtained from a Hunter kit, which is created by casting the Lunar spell Hunter Kit (spell).

A teasing stick also spawns on the west coast of Karamja, near the horned graahk area.

A Hunter's spear also functions as a teasing stick and can be equipped to save an inventory space.

A rabbit snare is a type of trap used in the Hunter skill. The rabbit snaring technique is used to catch white rabbits. With 27 Hunter, completion of the Eagles' Peak quest, and a ferret in the inventory, the player may set up a rabbit snare and flush a rabbit hole to trap a white rabbit. When the rabbit passes the trap, it gets caught.

To use a rabbit snare, set it up on a path that a rabbit could take while going from a rabbit hole to another rabbit hole. Then, while a ferret is in the inventory, select the "flush" option on the rabbit hole. The ferret will run in and hopefully run the rabbit into the snare. Note: the ferret may run away, so it is advised to bring multiple ferrets.

Rabbit snares can be bought for 18 coins from Aleck's Hunter Emporium. in Yanille, the Nardah Hunter Shop in Nardah, or 19 coins from Imia's Supplies within the Hunter Guild. Rabbit snares can also be found in a Hunter kit, obtained by casting Hunter Kit (spell) (1 per kit).

Chinchompas are one-handed, multi-target, stackable Ranged weapons requiring level 45 Ranged to wield. Chinchompas can be obtained by box trapping grey chinchompas in the Piscatoris Hunter area, the Kourend Woodland, or on the Isle of Souls. This requires 53 Hunter and completion of the Eagles' Peak quest, and will give the player 198.4 Hunter experience per catch. They have a catch rate of about 146/255 at 53 Hunter and a guaranteed chance to catch at 95 Hunter. To use chinchompas in combat, they must be wielded in the weapons slot. Chinchompas are thrown like darts or throwing knives; however, they explode on impact. In PvM, they can hit up to 11 targets in a 3x3 area. In PvP, the cap is 9 targets. They cannot be picked up again from the ground after being thrown, and Ava's device does not return them.

When throwing a chinchompa at a group, the accuracy roll is based on the targeted NPC. If you miss on this target, you will miss on all targets. If you hit on this target, you will hit on all targets. The damage rolls are done independently per target. The max hit for the targeted NPC is calculated normally, however the max hit used for the damage roll on the additional targets is the max hit for the initial target with the boosts from Salve and Avarice removed. The accuracy roll made on the initial target uses the 'heavy' ranged defence for determining the opponent's defence roll.

Fuses are used to describe the attack speed for throwing chinchompas. It is just another name for the conventional styles of ranged training.

Short fuse (accurate): 4 ticks

Medium fuse (rapid): 3 ticks

Long fuse (longrange): 4 ticks
10034:
Red chinchompas are one-handed multi-target stackable Ranged weapons requiring level 55 Ranged to wield. Red chinchompas can be obtained by box trapping carnivorous chinchompas , requiring 63 Hunter and completion of the Eagles' Peak quest.

To use chinchompas in combat , they must be wielded in the weapons slot . Red chinchompas are thrown like darts or throwing knives ; however, they explode on impact. In PvM , they can hit up to 11 targets in a 3x3 area. In PvP , the cap is 9 targets. They cannot be picked up again from the ground after being thrown and Ava's device does not return them. In multiple target attacks, the chinchompa simply rolls at the target's defence values; if it hits, then all other nearby targets are also hit, regardless of their Defence level and ranged defence bonuses. If it misses, then none of the targets take damage. The accuracy roll made on the initial target uses the 'heavy' ranged defence for determining the opponent's defence roll. [ 1 ]

Using red chinchompas is widely regarded as the second fastest way to train Ranged and Hitpoints ; however, this method is very costly. Catching red chinchompas is also popular among high-level Hunters as it gives fast experience and is profitable.

Fuses are used to describe the attack speed for throwing chinchompas. It is just another name for the conventional styles of ranged training.

10075:
Gloves of silence are a pair of thieving gloves requiring 54 Hunter to wear. When worn, the gloves increase your success chance while pickpocketing by 5%, eventually breaking after 62 failed pickpockets.

To make the gloves, players must bring two unnoted Dark kebbit furs from the Piscatoris falconry area (level 57 Hunter) and 600 coins to the Fancy Clothes Store in Varrock , to Pellem in the Hunter Guild , or to Prifddinas' Seamstress . Before they break, the gloves can be repaired by using one dark kebbit fur on them, while having one spool of thread , a knife , and a needle in your inventory; repairing them requires level 64 Crafting but does not grant any experience .

After completing the medium Ardougne diaries , the gloves become ineffective when used in Ardougne and will not degrade, as the 10% increased chance of success the diary provides is higher than that of the gloves and both bonuses do not stack. [ 1 ] Upon completion of the hard Ardougne diaries, this extends to the rest of Gielinor and the gloves become completely obsolete. This effect does not require an Ardougne cloak of any tier to be worn.

Players with access to rogue equipment (minimum of 50 Agility and 50 Thieving to obtain) may choose to forgo using the gloves of silence, as wearing the full rogue set guarantees double rewards for pickpocketing. If wearing the gloves instead of the Rogue gloves with the rest of the rogue set, you instead have a 60% chance to double pickpocketing loot (since you lose both the 15% chance from the gloves and the 25% full set bonus), and therefore receive ~20% less loot, while gaining more XP per hour due to less failures. Due to stun timers on failed pickpocketing being longer than the action of pickpocketing itself, the 5% increased success rate results in 7-25% increased XP rates from pickpocketing, depending on base pickpocketing chance.
10077:
Spiky vambraces are leather armour worn on the forearms, most commonly by low-level warriors, and often rangers (as there is no magic penalty), in place of leather vambraces . They have the same stats as leather vambraces, except for a +2 Strength bonus. To make spiky vambraces, use kebbit claws on leather vambraces. This grants 6 Crafting experience . Level 32 Crafting is required to make any vambraces into spiked vambraces.

Like the leather vambraces they are created from, this variant also has no skill requirements to be worn.
10079:
Green spiky vambraces is a piece of Ranged armour worn in the gloves slot. They are created by using kebbit claws with green dragonhide vambraces which requires a crafting level of 32. The difference in stats between spiked and non-spiked vambraces is a bonus to strength of +2 and a slight increase in physical defence for the spiked ones.

Like the green dragonhide vambraces they are created from, this variant also requires 40 Ranged to be worn.
10081:
Blue spiky vambraces are blue dragonhide armour worn in the hand slot. They are created by using Kebbit claws with blue dragonhide vambraces. The spiked vambraces gain very small defensive bonuses and a bonus to melee strength of +2.

Like the blue dragonhide vambraces they are created from, this variant also requires 50 Ranged to be worn.
10083:
Red spiky vambraces are red dragonhide vambraces with kebbit claws attached, which requires 32 Crafting to do and grants 5.8 Crafting experience. Kebbit claws can be gained using the Hunter skill. Red spiked vambraces can also be obtained by looting an eclectic impling that has been caught. The difference in stats between spiked and non-spiked vambraces is a bonus to strength of +2 and a slight increase in physical defence for the spiked ones.

Like the red dragonhide vambraces they are created from, this variant also requires 60 Ranged to be worn.
10085:
Black spiky vambraces are black dragonhide vambraces with kebbit claws attached. The difference in stats between spiked and non-spiked vambraces is a bonus to strength of +2 and a slight increase in melee defence for the spiked ones.

Like the black dragonhide vambraces they are created from, this variant also requires 70 Ranged to be worn.

Kebbit claws can be gained using the Hunter skill or from trading another player.
10087:
A stripy feather is a drop from the tropical wagtail bird caught using the Hunter skill . Level 19 Hunter and at least one bird snare are needed to catch these birds in the Feldip Hunter area . These feathers may be used with a fly fishing rod to catch rainbow fish , with 38 Fishing , in rivers of Gielinor , and in place of regular feathers in Fletching . It can be stored in a tackle box .

They can be sold to the Fancy Dress Shop for 8 coins each.
10088:
A red feather is a drop from the crimson swift bird caught using the Hunter skill. Level 1 Hunter and at least one bird snare are needed to catch these birds in the Feldip Hunter area .

Red feathers, along with all coloured feathers gathered from the Hunter skill, can be used in place of regular white feathers in the Fletching skill. Despite the difference, the arrows still come out with white feathers and are used as normal arrows. However, they can not be used for fly fishing. They can be sold to the Varrock Fancy Dress Shop for 4 coins each.
10089:
A blue feather is a drop from the Cerulean twitch bird caught using the Hunter skill. Level 11 Hunter and at least one bird snare are needed to catch these birds in the Rellekka Hunter area.

Blue feathers, along with all coloured feathers gathered from the Hunter skill, can be used in place of regular white feathers with the Fletching skill. Despite the difference, the arrows still come out with white feathers and are used as normal arrows. They can be sold to the Varrock Fancy Clothes Store for 6 coins each. They cannot be used for fly fishing.
10090:
A yellow feather is an item dropped the golden warbler bird caught using the Hunter skill. Level 5 Hunter and at least one bird snare are needed to catch these birds in the Uzer Hunter area.

Yellow feathers, along with all coloured feathers gathered from the Hunter skill, can be used in place of regular white feathers for the Fletching skill. Despite the difference, the bolts and arrows created still come out with white feathers and have no extra properties. These feathers cannot be used for fly fishing. They are colourful and can be sold at the Varrock Fancy Dress Shop for 5 coins each.
10091:
Orange feathers are a drop from the Copper longtail bird caught using the Hunter skill. Level 9 Hunter and at least one bird snare are needed to catch these birds in the Piscatoris Hunter area .

Orange feathers, along with all coloured feathers gathered from the Hunter skill, can be used in place of regular white feathers with the Fletching skill. Despite the difference, bolts and arrows created still come out with white feathers and have no extra properties. These feathers cannot be used for fly fishing. They are colourful and can be sold at the Varrock Fancy Dress Shop .
10092:
A ferret is an item used with a rabbit snare in order to hunt white rabbits in the Piscatoris Hunter area . Players can obtain a ferret by catching a wild ferret using a box trap slightly south-west of the southern rabbit holes. Once caught, the player can use a ferret to flush out a white rabbit from its hole and towards a waiting rabbit snare. A ferret is caught during the quest Eagles' Peak to be given to Charlie .

There is a small chance of a ferret escaping from the player once caught, forcing the player to catch another one to continue hunting rabbits. The chance to keep the ferret scales with Hunter level, ranging from around an 80.9% chance at level 27, up to a 100% chance at level 99. [ 1 ]
10093:
Tatty larupia fur is obtained when trapping a spined larupia, found in the Feldip Hunter area. This fur, along with 200 coins, can be turned into either the larupia top and larupia legs by one of the Custom Fur Clothing vendors. It cannot be made into a larupia hat, which requires normal larupia fur. Level 28 Hunter is required to wear the larupia hunter gear set.

Tatty larupia fur, like all tatty furs, cannot be stored in a fur pouch or used during Golem crafting.
10095:
Larupia fur is a common item obtained by hunting Spined larupias (requires Level 31 Hunter) in the Feldip Hunter area. It can be used to create all pieces of larupia hunter gear. Only the full larupia fur may be used to make the headgear of larupia hunter gear. It can be used to dress golems in the golem crafting activity.

Although it can be used for any piece of larupia hunter gear, tatty larupia fur also works for the body and legs but drops more often and is far less expensive. As a result, players often only use the full fur for headdresses.
10097:
Tatty graahk fur is obtained when trapping a horned graahk, found in the Karamja Hunter area. This fur, along with 200 coins, can be turned into either a graahk top or graahk legs by one of the Custom Fur Clothing vendors. It cannot be used to make the graahk headdress, which requires normal graahk fur. Level 38 Hunter is required to wear the graahk hunter gear set.

Tatty graahk fur, like all tatty furs, cannot be stored in a fur pouch or used during Golem crafting.
10099:
Graahk fur can be obtained by trapping Horned graahks on Karamja. The fur comes in two variants; perfect and tatty . Both variants can be taken to the Fancy Dress Shop in Varrock , to Pellem in the Hunter Guild , or Prifddinas' Seamstress in Prifddinas to be made into various articles of clothing. The tatty fur can only be made into Graahk tops and Graahk legs , and the perfect fur is used for the Graahk headdress . It can be used to dress golems in the golem crafting activity.

Furs can also be sold to merchants in East Ardougne and Rellekka .

The ratio of getting graahk fur to tatty graahk fur is based on one's Hunter level.
10101:
Tatty kyatt fur is obtained when trapping a sabre-toothed kyatt, found in the Rellekka Hunter area. This fur, along with 200 coins, can be turned into either a kyatt top or kyatt legs by one of the Custom Fur Clothing vendors. It cannot be used to make the hat, which requires normal kyatt fur. Level 52 Hunter is required to wear the kyatt hunter gear set.

Tatty kyatt fur, like all tatty furs, cannot be stored in a fur pouch or used during Golem crafting.
10103: Kyatt fur is sometimes obtained by pit trapping a Sabre-toothed kyatt in the polar/snow hunting region, although Tatty kyatt fur is more often obtained. Level 55 Hunter is required. The fur can be taken to the Fancy Clothes Store owner in Varrock, who will turn it into a hat, top, or legs for some coins. Wearing the set of kyatt camouflage does not increase the player's hunting abilities, however when wearing the full set you receive 60% less damage from hunter creatures. Level 52 Hunter is required to wear the set. It can be used to dress golems in the golem crafting activity.
10105:
Kebbit spikes are obtained through the Hunter skill, by deadfall trapping prickly kebbits , or by trading with other players. At level 32 Fletching , a chisel can be used with the spike to make twelve kebbit bolts per spike, and gives 6 experience. Kebbit bolts are used as ammunition for the Hunter's crossbow .

Players can also bring a kebbit spike and 20 coins to Leon , located inside Aleck's Hunter Emporium in Yanille , who will exchange it for 12 kebbit bolts.
10107:
Long kebbit spikes are loot obtained from tracking Razor-backed kebbits , which requires a Hunter level of 49. With a Fletching level of 42, a chisel can be used on a spike to create 12 Long kebbit bolts . Long kebbit bolts can only be fired from a hunters' crossbow .

Players can also bring a long kebbit spike and 40 coins to Leon , located inside Aleck's Hunter Emporium in Yanille , who will exchange it for 12 long kebbit bolts.
10109:
Kebbit teeth are dropped from Sabre-toothed kebbits after a successful deadfall trapping. The teeth can be used with a pestle and mortar to create Kebbit teeth dust , which is used to make a Hunter potion in the Herblore skill.

The Herblore Hunting potion info refers to Kebbit teeth dust as 'ground sabre-toothed Kebbit teeth'. These are the same item.
10111: Kebbit teeth dust is obtained by grinding kebbit teeth , obtained by deadfalling a sabre-toothed kebbit at level 51 Hunter, with a pestle and mortar . The dust is a secondary ingredient for the Hunter potion , which can be created at level 53 Herblore .
10113: Kebbit claws are obtained from wild kebbits caught with deadfall traps in either the Piscatoris Hunter area or Auburnvale , requiring 23 Hunter . They can be attached to any leather or regular dragonhide vambraces (excluding blessed , gilded , snakeskin and third age ) making spiked vambraces . These add a +2 strength bonus to all vambraces and in the cases of the dragonhide versions a slight increase in physical defensive bonuses as well.
10115:
Dark kebbit fur is a type of fur obtained from dark kebbits , which are caught using the Hunter skill. Dark kebbits can be hunted with level 57 Hunter in the Piscatoris falconry area after renting a falcon from Matthias for 500 coins .

Two dark kebbit furs can be taken to the Fancy Clothes Store in Varrock or Pellem at the Hunter Guild , where the shop owner will charge 600 coins to turn the furs into a pair of gloves of silence , or used along with a needle and thread to repair an existing pair of the gloves, requiring 64 Crafting . The gloves require level 54 Hunter to wear, and lower the wearer's chance of getting caught while pickpocketing by 5%, however this is rendered obsolete after completing and claiming the rewards from the hard Ardougne Diary , or when using Rogue equipment to thieve. It can be used to dress golems in the golem crafting activity.
10117: Polar kebbit fur is an item obtained after successfully tracking a polar kebbit and catching it with a noose wand . Polar kebbit fur may be used to make polar camouflage gear by taking two furs and 20 coins per piece to the Fancy Dress Store in south-east Varrock . However, it cannot be used with needles and thread . It can be used to dress golems in the golem crafting activity.
10119:
Feldip weasel fur is dropped by feldip weasels , which are found south of the Feldip Hills . Players require a Hunter level of 7 in order to capture these creatures. The fur may be made into jungle camouflage gear at Tailor's Fancy Clothes Store in south-eastern Varrock . It takes 2 of these furs and 20 coins in order to make one part of the two piece outfit. A total of 4 pieces of fur and 40 coins will make the full set.

Hunter camouflage gear is mostly cosmetic and does not increase catch rates. However, it is weight-reducing clothing . It can be used to dress golems in the golem crafting activity.
10121: Common kebbit fur is obtained by tracking common kebbits in the Piscatoris Hunter area. Take 4 common kebbit furs and 40 coins to the Fancy Clothes Store in Varrock to create Wood camouflage gear. It can be used to dress golems in the golem crafting activity.
10123: Desert devil fur is the fur from a dead Desert Devil used to make Desert camouflage gear . This outfit does not decrease your chances of being seen by animals while hunting. It can be used to dress golems in the golem crafting activity.
10125:
Spotted kebbit fur is a type of fur obtained from spotted kebbits, which are caught using the Hunter skill. Spotted kebbits can be hunted with level 43 Hunter in the Piscatoris falconry area after renting a falcon from Matthias for 500 coins.

Two spotted kebbit furs can be taken to the Fancy Clothes Store in Varrock or Pellem at the Hunter Guild, where the shop owner will charge 400 coins to turn the furs into a spotted cape. The cape requires level 40 Hunter to wear, reduces the wearer's weight by 2.267 kg. It can be used to dress golems in the golem crafting activity.
10127:
Dashing kebbit fur is a type of fur obtained from dashing kebbits , which are caught using the Hunter skill. Dashing kebbits can be hunted with level 69 Hunter in the Piscatoris falconry area after renting a falcon from Matthias for 500 coins .

Two dashing kebbit furs can be brought to the Fancy Clothes Store in Varrock or Pellem at the Hunter Guild , where the shop owner will charge 800 coins to turn the furs into a spottier cape ; doing so is a task for the hard Varrock Diary . The cape requires level 66 Hunter to wear, and reduces the wearer's weight by 4.5 kg.

It can be used to dress golems in the golem crafting activity.
10129: A barb-tail harpoon is a weapon obtained after successfully trapping a barb-tailed kebbit, which requires 33 Hunter to catch. It is special as it functions as a wieldable harpoon in Fishing. Its ability to be wielded makes it a more convenient option for early-game players as it saves one inventory space and does not have a minimum Attack level requirement, unlike the highly sought after dragon harpoon. It also cannot be taken away by the tide while subduing Tempoross if the player fails to tether themselves to the mast. It can be stored in a tackle box.
10132:
A strung rabbit foot is made by using a ball of wool with a rabbit foot , which requires level 37 Crafting and gives 4 experience; players must have level 24 Hunter to wear the strung rabbit foot. Rabbit feet can be obtained by snaring rabbits . Players must have completed the Eagles' Peak quest to be able to snare rabbits.

If worn whilst woodcutting, bird nest drops are slightly less likely to contain seeds, and slightly more likely to contain bird's eggs or rings [ 1 ] (changing the rate from 3/100 to 3/95 [ 2 ] ). If worn whilst looting bird houses , bird nest drops are slightly less likely to be empty nests, and slightly more likely to contain eggs or rings. [ 3 ] In practice, wearing the strung rabbit foot lowers the average coin value of a bird nest, so it is only recommended to wear it if actively hunting for egg nests .

For activities that can directly award empty nests, e.g. bird house trapping , up to 10 nest rolls are performed with a chance of getting an empty nest. For successful rolls, the chance is 65/100 for an empty nest. Wearing a strung rabbit foot removes 5 empty nest slots, making the chance 60/95, and improving the chance of getting ring or egg nests instead.

The benefits of wearing a strung rabbit foot stack with the effect of wearing a pair of twitcher's gloves . [ 4 ]

Since redwood trees and sulliusceps only drop clue nests , wearing the strung rabbit foot has no effect when chopping these trees.
10134:
A rabbit foot is received through the hunter skill by snaring a rabbit. It can be made into a strung rabbit foot at level 37 Crafting by using a ball of wool on it.

When worn, the rabbit foot increases the chance that nests received from cutting trees or emptying birdhouses will contain a bird's egg, from the usual chance of 3/100 to 3/95.
10136: Rainbow fish is a type of fish that restores 11 Hitpoints when eaten. It can be obtained by cooking raw rainbow fish on a fire or cooking range, requiring level 35 Cooking and granting 110 experience when successful. When cooking there is a chance to fail, resulting in a burnt rainbow fish. The burn rate decreases as the player's Cooking level increases, and it will stop burning entirely at Cooking level 63.
10138:
A raw rainbow fish can be caught by players with 38 Fishing . They are caught with a fly fishing rod at a river fishing spot (such as the one near Barbarian Village or in Shilo Village ), using stripy feathers (obtained via the Hunter skill) as bait. Each one caught grants 80 Fishing experience .

Raw rainbow fish can be used in the Hunter skill as optional bait for barb-tailed kebbits in the Feldip Hunter area . Catching a barb-tailed kebbit requires level 33 Hunter and yields 168 Hunter experience.

Players can also cook it on a range or a fire to make a cooked rainbow fish , which heals 11 Hitpoints when eaten. Doing so requires 35 Cooking and grants 110 Cooking experience. With 63 Cooking or higher it is impossible to burn the fish.

Although they reward more Fishing experience when caught than salmon or trout , they are much slower to catch and as such are not recommended to be caught purely for experience.
10140:
Burnt rainbow fish is the result of accidentally burning a raw rainbow fish while attempting to make a rainbow fish . The burn rate while cooking these will decrease as players reach higher Cooking levels, stopping entirely at level 64.

The burnt rainbow fish has no use whatsoever. Like most other burnt food, it is tradeable to other players but not on the Grand Exchange .
10142:
Guam tar is an item used as food, or "ammunition", for swamp lizards when used as a weapon. It is also optionally used as bait for hunting swamp lizards to increase the catch rate by 3%.

Guam tar can be made at level 19 Herblore by using 15 swamp tar on a guam leaf or ground guam , whilst having a pestle and mortar in the inventory. This process yields 15 guam tar, and grants 30 Herblore experience.
10143:
Marrentill tar is an item used as food, or "ammunition", for orange salamanders when used as a weapon. It is also optionally used as bait for hunting orange salamanders to increase the catch rate by 3%.

Marrentill tar can be made at level 31 Herblore by using 15 swamp tar on a marrentill, whilst having a pestle and mortar in the inventory. This process yields 15 marrentill tar, and grants 42.5 Herblore experience.
10144:
Tarromin tar is an item used as food, or "ammunition", for red salamanders when used as a weapon. It is also optionally used as bait for hunting red salamanders to increase the catch rate by 3%.

Tarromin tar can be made at level 39 Herblore by using 15 swamp tar on a tarromin , whilst having a pestle and mortar in the inventory. This process yields 15 tarromin tar, and grants 55 Herblore experience.
10145:
Harralander tar is an item used as food, or "ammunition", for black salamanders when used as a weapon. It is also optionally used as bait for hunting black salamanders to increase the catch rate by 3%.

Harralander tar can be made at level 44 Herblore by using 15 swamp tar on a harralander, whilst having a pestle and mortar in the inventory. This process yields 15 harralander tar, and grants 72.5 Herblore experience.
10146:
The orange salamander is the fourth strongest salamander weapon . Once the Hunter creature is caught using the Hunter skill, they become weapons. The orange salamander requires level 50 Ranged , 50 Attack , and 50 Magic to wield and is a two-handed weapon. Marrentill tar is used as ammunition for the salamander.

Despite being able to perform Magic and Ranged attacks, this weapon requires the user to be in the opponent's melee distance to attack, potentially reducing the practicality of the two attack styles. However, it can be used to attack enemies from behind fences, and can also attack enemies in diagonal squares, meaning that safespotting is still possible.

They require 47 Hunter to catch, and give 224 Hunter experience when caught. A small fishing net and a rope is used to set up the traps that catch salamanders. They can be caught in the Uzer hunter area , the Necropolis hunter area , and the Great Conch 's Abalone Cliffs .

When using the Scorch (Slash) and Blaze (Magic) attack styles, the attack speed is 5. When using the Flare (Range) attack style, the attack speed is 4, which is similar in concept to the Rapid style of most ranged weapons, and it will use standard [ 1 ] ranged defence, similar to bows .

Warning: This is a live creature; if unprotected it will run away when you die . Should this happen, you will need to buy or catch a new one.
10147:
The red salamander is the third strongest salamander and can be caught using a net trap and the Hunter skill at level 59. It requires level 60 Ranged, 60 Attack, and 60 Magic to wield.

Despite being able to perform Magic and Ranged attacks, this weapon requires the user to be in the opponent's melee distance to attack, potentially reducing the practicality of the two attack styles. However, it can be used to attack enemies from behind fences, and can also attack enemies in diagonal squares, meaning that safespotting is still possible.

Tarromin tar is used as ammo for the salamander. Tarromin tar can be made by using tarromin with swamp tar along with 39 Herblore. However, this weapon's proprietary ammo is consumed on use, much like bolt racks.

When using the Scorch (Slash) and Blaze (Magic) attack styles, the attack speed is 5. When using the Flare (Range) attack style, the attack speed is 4, which is similar in concept to the Rapid style of most ranged weapons, and it will use standard ranged defence, similar to bows.

Warning: This is a live creature; if unprotected it will run away when you die. Should this happen, you will need to buy or catch a new one.
10148:
The black salamander is the second strongest salamander that can be caught using the Hunter skill at level 67 Hunter, giving 319 experience per catch. They can be found north-east of the Chaos Temple.

It is a two-handed weapon that requires level 70 Attack, Magic, and Ranged to wield, and can be used to train Strength, Magic, and Ranged. Harralander tar is used as ammunition for the salamander.

Despite being able to perform Magic and Ranged attacks, this weapon requires the user to be in the opponent's melee distance to attack, potentially reducing the practicality of the two attack styles. However, it can be used to attack enemies from behind fences, and can also attack enemies in diagonal squares, meaning that safespotting is still possible.

When using the Scorch (Slash) and Blaze (Magic) attack styles, the attack speed is 5. When using the Flare (Range) attack style, the attack speed is 4, which is similar in concept to the Rapid style of most ranged weapons, and it will use standard ranged defence, similar to bows.

Warning: This is a live creature; if unprotected it will run away when you die. Should this happen, you will need to buy or catch a new one.
10149:
The swamp lizard is a two-handed Ranged weapon requiring level 30 in Attack, Ranged, and Magic to wield. The required ammunition for the swamp lizard is Guam tar.

Despite being able to perform Magic and Ranged attacks, this weapon requires the user to be in the opponent's melee distance to attack, potentially reducing the practicality of the two attack styles. However, it can be used to attack enemies from behind fences, and can also attack enemies in diagonal squares, meaning that safespotting is still possible.

Swamp lizards may be obtained by trapping swamp lizards east of Canifis using net traps, requiring level 29 Hunter, or by trading with other players. Successfully catching a Swamp Lizard grants 152 Hunter experience.

When using the Scorch (Slash) and Blaze (Magic) attack styles, the attack speed is 5. When using the Flare (Range) attack style, the attack speed is 4, which is similar in concept to the Rapid style of most ranged weapons, and it will use standard ranged defence, similar to bows.

In its melee mode, the swamp lizard has a chance of inflicting poison starting at 6 damage.

Warning: This is a live creature; if unprotected it will run away when you die. Should this happen, you will need to buy or catch a new one.
10150:
The noose wand is used in the Hunter skill to catch kebbits while tracking. The kebbits caught through tracking are polar kebbits, common kebbits, feldip weasels, desert devils, and razor-backed kebbits.

Once a kebbit has been tracked down, the player must equip the wand to catch it; without the noose wand, a Kebbit will simply be scared off. The noose wand serves no purpose when hunting Herbiboar. The noose wand can also be used to slice bananas.

This item can be bought from the Hunter shops in Yanille, Nardah, and the Hunters' Guild for 4 or 5 coins. The level 71 spell Hunter Kit from the lunar spellbook also gives a noose wand, among other hunter items. Casting Hunter Kit requires the completion of both the Lunar Diplomacy and Dream Mentor quests.
10156:
The hunters' crossbow is a crossbow that requires 50 Ranged to wield. It possesses a firing speed of 3 ticks on rapid, equivalent to that of a shortbow. It can only use kebbit bolts and long kebbit bolts as ammunition. Players with at least 74 Fletching can upgrade the hunters' crossbow into the hunters' sunlight crossbow by using a sunlight antelope antler on it while having a chisel in their inventory.

The hunters' crossbow can be bought from Leon for 1,300 coins at the Leon's Prototype Crossbow shop in Yanille. It cannot be crafted by players.

Like the Armadyl crossbow, it has an attack range of 8 tiles. Longrange increases the attack range by 2.
10158:
Kebbit bolts are ammunition used in tandem with the hunters' crossbow . They can be made at level 32 Fletching by using a chisel on a kebbit spike . Doing so will produce twelve bolts from every one spike, giving 5.8 experience each action.

As they are stackable, it may prove beneficial to carry a chisel in the inventory whilst hunting prickly kebbits , in order to free up inventory space.

Kebbit bolts can also be acquired from Leon , inside Aleck's Hunter Emporium in Yanille . He gives 12 kebbit bolts in exchange for one kebbit spike and 20 coins.
10159: Long kebbit-tipped hunting bolts are ranged ammunition for the hunters' crossbow . They are made from long kebbit spikes . Use a chisel on a long kebbit spike to create twelve long kebbit bolts. This requires 42 Fletching and gives 7.9 Fletching experience per long kebbit spike.
10167: Eagle feathers are used in the Eagles' Peak quest to make the eagle cape . They can be picked from the giant feathers scattered around the Eagles' Peak Dungeon . After the quest, they remain obtainable and can be used to make additional eagle capes, but serve no other purpose.
10171: The eagle cape is a quest item used in the Eagles' Peak quest . Additional eagle cape and fake beak combos can be obtained from the fancy-dress shop owner when he is supplied with 5 eagle feathers , 1 swamp tar , yellow dye and 25 coins .
10172: A fake beak is an item needed for Eagles' Peak quest along with the eagle cape to make a convincing disguise. It is made by taking Yellow dye and Swamp tar to the Fancy Dress Shop . It is used to prevent players from taking damage from the mother eagle. Additional eagle cape and fake beak combos can be obtained from the fancy-dress shop owner when he is supplied with 5 eagle feathers , 1 swamp tar , yellow dye and 25 coins .
10173:
The Bird book (properly titled William Oddity's Guide to the Avian ) is a book that players find as part of the Eagles' Peak quest. It is written by William Oddity , an expert on hunting.

It provides a short commentary on several birds that players can hunt via the Hunter skill, namely the crimson swift , the cerulean twitch , the golden warbler , the tropical wagtail , and the copper longtail .

However, it also gives vague information about the elusive giant eagle , and hints at the existence of the eagle transport system and the location of the secret hidden entrance to the Eagles' Peak Dungeon .

After completing the quest, players can only find this book in the bookcase of their player-owned house ; the stack of books it was originally found in during the quest can no longer be searched.
10174:
The metal feather is a quest item obtained during the Eagles' Peak quest , and is used to open the door leading into the dungeon atop Eagles' Peak .

Players can find the metal feather inside the bird book the first time and in the stack of books after. Both the bird book and the stack of books can be found inside a tent at the northern base of Eagles' Peak.

Once the quest is complete, the metal feather is rendered useless and can be destroyed; you cannot reobtain the feather after the quest is complete as the books are no longer searchable.

During the quest, it can be reobtained from the camp-site at the base of Eagles' Peak if destroyed.
10175:
The golden feather is a quest item used in the Eagles' Peak quest. It is found on a pedestal inside the caves under Eagles' Peak.

The player must use the golden feather along with a bronze feather and silver feather in order to open a locked door that leads deeper into the caves. The feather can also be obtained after the quest and multiple copies can be obtained by banking the duplicates.
10176: The silver feather is a quest item used in the Eagles' Peak quest. It is found on a pedestal inside some caves under Eagles' Peak . The player must use the silver feather along with a bronze feather and a golden feather in order to open a locked door that leads deeper into the caves. The feather can be reobtained after the quest and multiple copies can be obtained by banking the duplicates.
10177:
The bronze feather is a quest item used in the Eagles' Peak quest. It is found on a pedestal inside some caves under Eagles' Peak . When a player attempts to take it, a net trap will lift the feather upwards. The player must then operate the winches in order to lower it. It is not possible to obtain it without setting off the trap.

The player must use the bronze feather along with a silver feather and a golden feather in order to open a locked door that leads deeper into the caves. The feather can be reobtained after the quest and multiple copies can be obtained by banking the duplicates.
10178:
Odd bird seed is a quest item used in the Eagles' Peak quest. It is found by searching the birdseed holder inside some caves under Eagles Peak mountain and is used to navigate a small maze containing statues of eagles. It can be obtained even after the quest.

Placing the bird seed at the appropriate locations will cause the statues to move, allowing the player to access different parts of the maze. At the end of the maze the player obtains a golden feather which, along with a bronze feather and a silver feather , obtained earlier in the quest, is used to open a locked door that leads deeper into the caves.
10179:
The feathered journal is a book that players will find as part of the Eagles' Peak quest.

The book is the journal of the criminal Arthur Artimus, and documents the rise and fall of his gang. The gang was known in local folk tales as "the bandits of the golden claw" (according to the bird book ), though this may not have been the gang's real name.

Artimus's accomplices included Armen, Davey, and Barakur. Barakur was an expert on mechanisms, and it was he who set up the entrance mechanism to the dungeon under the mountain. The gang had intended to use the dungeon as a hideout whilst they plotted to rob the Tree Gnome Stronghold . They did rob the stronghold, but with only limited success; Armen's pet kebbit hampered their efforts.

They did eventually tame an eagle well enough to use it as a transport system . They flew it over East Ardougne , where they stole some bread from a market stall using a fishing net.

The gang's demise ultimately came when they chose to ignore the Mysterious Old Man who apparently appeared as part of a random event .

Willow composite bows are a reward from Easy Treasure Trails . It requires a Ranged level of 20 to use and can fire up to mithril arrows . The attack range of the willow composite bow is ten squares.

The willow composite bow cannot be made using the Fletching skill. It can, however, be obtained through trading with another player.

This item can be stored in the treasure chest of a costume room , provided that the interface of the corresponding clue tier is opened before attempting to store the item. Alternatively, the item can be used on the opened treasure chest to insert it without viewing the interface.
10282:
The yew composite bow is a bow that requires level 40 Ranged to equip. Yew comp bows can be obtained from completing a medium difficulty Treasure Trail . The yew comp bow is essentially an upgraded yew longbow with a one tick faster attack speed and slightly improved accuracy.

This item can be stored in the treasure chest of a costume room , provided that the interface of the corresponding clue tier is opened before attempting to store the item. Alternatively, the item can be used on the opened treasure chest to insert it without viewing the interface.
10284:
The magic comp bow requires level 50 Ranged to wield, and can fire arrows up to amethyst . It is slightly quicker and more accurate than a magic longbow , and features the same special attack . Magic comp bows can be obtained as a reward for completing a hard Treasure Trail . This item can be stored in the treasure chest of a costume room , provided that the interface of the corresponding clue tier is opened before attempting to store the item. Alternatively, the item can be used on the opened treasure chest to insert it without viewing the interface.

Composite bows can be fired from 10 squares away at both rapid and long range styles; this combination of speed and distance is matched only by the crystal bow , scorching bow , and bow of Faerdhinen . Where long attack distance is ideal, a magic comp bow could suffice as a non-degradable alternative to the crystal bow.

Purple firelighters are a possible reward from Treasure Trails. They create purple logs when used with regular logs.

In addition, players can use 250 purple firelighters on a Phoenix to recolour it purple.
10327:
White firelighters are a possible reward from Treasure Trails . They create white logs when used with regular logs .

In addition, players can use 250 white firelighters on a Phoenix to recolour it white.
10328:
White logs are created by using logs with a white firelighter , a possible reward from any tier of clue scroll . When burned they create a white fire , yielding 50 Firemaking experience , which is 10 more than regular logs . Additionally, every attempt to make a white fire is successful, unlike with regular fire.

These logs are not logs cut from a white tree .

White logs can be added to the Odd Old Man 's pot-boiler , but the resulting fire will be normal and the logs will be lost.
10329:
Purple logs are created by using logs with a purple firelighter, a possible reward from any tier of clue scroll. When burned they create a purple fire, yielding 50 Firemaking experience, which is 10 more than regular logs. Additionally, every attempt to make a purple fire is successful, unlike with regular fire.

Note: Purple logs can be added to the Odd Old Man's pot-boiler, but the resulting fire will be normal and the logs will be lost.

10354:
The amulet of glory (t) (or trimmed amulet of glory) is a cosmetic variant of the regular amulet of glory. Players can receive this item as a reward from hard Treasure Trails at a chance of 1/1,625 per slot. Aside from appearance, it has the same functions and stat bonuses as a regular amulet of glory (including gem mining as long as it is charged).

This item can be stored in the treasure chest of a costume room, provided that the interface of the corresponding clue tier is opened before attempting to store the item. Alternatively, the item can be used on the opened treasure chest to insert it without viewing the interface. However, unlike its regular counterpart, it cannot be mounted in a Quest Hall.

For Ironmen completing treasure trails, this can NOT be used as an uncharged amulet of glory - only a regular amulet of glory may be used, obtained either through crafting one at level 80, catching a dragon impling at level 83 Hunter, or by completing other treasure trails.

Heroes' Quest is required to charge the amulet at the Fountain of Rune. Like the regular amulet of glory, there is a 1 in 25,000 chance that it will transmute into an amulet of eternal glory when charged at the Fountain of Rune, causing it to provide unlimited teleports rather than the usual six. This will cause it to lose its trimmed status.
