The Guthix stole is part of the Guthix vestment set and can be obtained by completing hard Treasure Trails. To wear one, the player needs at least 60 Prayer.

This item can be stored in the treasure chest of a costume room, provided that the interface of the corresponding clue tier is opened before attempting to store the item. Alternatively, the item can be used on the opened treasure chest to insert it without viewing the interface, as part of the Guthix vestment set. Ultimate Ironmen will be unable to retrieve individual pieces until the full set is stored.
10474:
The Zamorak stole is part of the Zamorak vestment set and can be obtained by completing hard Treasure Trails. To wear one, the player needs at least 60 Prayer. It will count as a Zamorakian item within the God Wars Dungeon.

This item can be stored in the treasure chest of a costume room, provided that the interface of the corresponding clue tier is opened before attempting to store the item. Alternatively, the item can be used on the opened treasure chest to insert it without viewing the interface, as part of the Zamorak vestment set. Ultimate Ironmen will be unable to retrieve individual pieces until the full set is stored.
10476:
Purple sweets are a stackable food item that are earned from all levels of Treasure Trails , except beginner . They are the only stackable food item in the game, restoring 1–3 Hitpoints and 10% run energy per sweets eaten.

Due to their high price and low amount healed, they are rarely used as conventional food. Due to being stackable, they are often used for activities with constant tick eating and to restore run energy instead of stamina potions to save inventory space.

When eaten, the message You eat the sweets. The sugary goodness heals some energy. is displayed.
10485: The Scroll is an animation item released with the rework of Watchtower . It is temporarily wielded by the player during an animation where they read the Spell scroll , unlocking the Watchtower Teleport . Aside from this, the item cannot be obtained.
10486:
The Empty sack is an animation item added to the game with Animal Magnetism. It is wielded by Malcolm during a cutscene in which he attempts to catch an Undead chicken for the player.

It may have originally been intended for players to obtain this item first, then give it to Malcolm to use.
10487:
An undead chicken is obtained during the quest Animal Magnetism from Malcolm who lives just west of the Ectofuntus by paying him 10 ectotokens per chicken. It is widely considered a 'fun' weapon , and shares its stats with a range of other such weapons.

This weapon can be bought during or after the quest for 10 Ecto-tokens .

Equipping the weapon causes the chicken to emit a short scream.
10488: Selected iron is a quest item used in the Animal Magnetism quest. The player must give the Witch in Draynor Manor five regular iron bars and she will then return the bar that is most suitable for turning into a bar magnet . The player must then take this bar to the mine near Rimmington and hit the bar with a hammer , making sure to face in the north direction, to turn it into a bar magnet. This will grant the player a token amount of Smithing experience .
10489:
A bar magnet is a quest item used in the Animal Magnetism quest. It is one of the items Ava asks the player to obtain in order to make an arrow making contraption - either Ava's attractor or Ava's accumulator depending on the player's Ranged level.

To make the bar magnet, the player must talk to the witch in Draynor Manor who will instruct the player to visit the mines near Rimmington and hit a selected iron with a hammer while facing north.
10490:
Undead twigs can be obtained by chopping undead trees outside Draynor Manor with a blessed axe during or after the Animal Magnetism quest. They have no use outside of this quest. It may take several attempts before some twigs are acquired, as there is a chance of failing to cut the tree properly.

Ordinary woodcutting axes will not be able to cut the undead tree , as they will "bounce off the bark" of the undead tree.

Each twig procured gives 5 Woodcutting experience.
10491:
The blessed axe is an axe made by Turael by giving him a mithril axe and a holy symbol , which requires completing the Animal Magnetism quest up until the point Ava suggests talking to him. Talking to Turael after this step will then make it. It is used to chop undead twigs from the undead trees within the vicinity of Draynor Manor . Turael will make additional blessed axes if the required materials are brought to him again in Burthorpe .

As the axe possesses a silver blade, it can damage vampyres .

The blessed axe does not retain the functionality of the mithril axe used to create it; it cannot be used to chop anything but undead trees. It does not require an Attack level to wield. The only statistical difference is the blessed axe has a +2 Prayer bonus the mithril axe does not.

Despite being made with a holy symbol, the blessed axe does not count as a Saradomin item for God Wars Dungeon when equipped.
10492: The research notes are a quest item obtained during the Animal Magnetism quest . They are given to the player by Ava in Draynor Manor toward the end of the quest, and the player must perform a simple mini-game to translate the notes into something Ava can understand. Once this is complete, the player can give Ava a container which she will then fashion into Ava's attractor or Ava's accumulator depending on the player's Ranged level.
10493: Translated notes are used in the Animal Magnetism quest. They are made by decoding the research notes by doing a puzzle. Ava uses them to make an accumulator or attractor .
10494: A pattern is an item that players obtain from Ava as part of Animal Magnetism . They must use it with polished buttons and hard leather to make a container . This container can then be given to Ava to receive Ava's attractor .
10495: A container is an item that players create as part of Animal Magnetism. They make it by combining a pattern with polished buttons and hard leather. They then give it to Ava, who turns it into Ava's attractor. The container is important in finishing the quest and is the structure of the whole attractor.
10496:
Polished buttons are obtained by polishing regular buttons . When polished, one receives 5 Crafting experience.

One may get the buttons by pickpocketing H.A.M. members , digging in the Level-1 or Level-3 digsite east of Varrock , opening Ogre coffins , or by inspecting the Port Khazard trawler net after participating in the Fishing Trawler .

They are used in the Animal Magnetism quest.
10498:
Ava's attractor is an item awarded to the player by completing the quest Animal Magnetism if the player is below level 50 Ranged. It is equipped in the cape slot, can pick up a player's ranged ammunition after they fire it, and every 3.5 minutes, will attract an assortment of metal ammunition.

It also provides a ranged attack bonus. It can also generate iron arrows into the player's ammo slot if it's empty or there are iron arrows in it. Like all of Ava's devices, the attractor won't work when metal torso armour is worn, as this will cause 'interference'. A list of metal torso armour that does not interfere with Ava's attractor can be found here.

Ava will upgrade it to Ava's accumulator after the Animal Magnetism quest, provided the player has 50 Ranged. 75 steel arrows must also be paid to Ava.

The breakdown of the ammo recovery rate is as follows:

Break on impact: 20%

Drop onto floor: 20%

Recovered automatically: 60%
10499:
Ava's accumulator is an item awarded to the player by completing the quest Animal Magnetism if the player is level 50 Ranged or above (players below 50 Ranged will instead receive Ava's attractor). It is equipped in the cape slot, can pick up a player's ranged ammunition after they fire it, and every 3.5 minutes, will attract an assortment of metal ammunition. The accumulator gives the fourth best Ranged attack bonus for the cape slot.

Like all of Ava's devices, the accumulator will not work when metal torso armour (Ahrim's top included) is worn, as this will cause 'interference'. A list of metal torso armour that does not interfere with Ava's accumulator can be found here.

Ava (found in Draynor Manor) will upgrade the attractor for anyone who obtains 50 Ranged after the quest for a price of 75 steel arrows, along with either 999 coins or an attractor (If you bring both coins and an attractor, the attractor will be used). It can also be purchased from Perdu after getting level 50 Ranged, even without first obtaining one from Ava. After that, it can be upgraded to Ava's assembler (upon completion of Dragon Slayer II) for Vorkath's head and 75 mithril arrows, as well as 4,999 coins or an Accumulator.

Upon dying, if it is not an item kept on death, it will be stored in the player's grave until reclaimed. If not reclaimed within an hour, it can be reacquired by speaking with Ava and purchased for 999 coins and 75 steel arrows. Multiple devices may be possessed at the same time.

As with Ava's other devices, Ava's accumulator can be used on both Lanthus in the Castle Wars lobby and Nomad in the Soul Wars lobby to permanently activate the effect in the minigames.

The Ava's accumulator can also be combined with the max cape to change its appearance by turning it into the accumulator max cape.

Lastly, the breakdown of the ammo recovery rate is as listed:

Break on impact: 20%

Drop onto floor: 8%

Recovered automatically: 72%
10500:
The crone-made amulet is an altered ghostspeak amulet used in Animal Magnetism.

Players obtain it by talking to the Old Crone with a ghostspeak amulet and at least one empty slot in their inventory. The old crone will use a hair from Alice (which players do not need to obtain - the old crone finds it on their clothes) to create a special copy of the ghostspeak amulet.

Only Malcolm (the farmer north-west of Port Phasmatys) can use it, and even then he can only talk to his wife Alice. The purpose of all this is so Alice could get his bank PIN and receive her inheritance.

Players attempting to equip this amulet on themselves receive the message: "Your ghostliness isn't ethereal enough to wear this. Perhaps you should wait a few hundred years or so?"
10501: Snowballs are stackable projectiles originally used in the 2013 Christmas Event . They were used to pelt Gublinchs and other players throughout the event. They may also be obtained by operating a reindeer hat or snow globe , obtained during Christmas events . Snowballs will not melt after Christmas events.
10506: Gublinch shards were part of the 2013 Christmas event. They were obtained when a player throws a snowball at a Gublinch and froze it. The frozen Gublinch could then be placed into cages on Musa Point to get a reward.
10507:
The reindeer hat is an untradeable cosmetic item obtained by completing one of the Christmas holiday events that occur once per year. This also rewards the player with all other holiday items associated with Christmas.

If destroyed, a replacement can be obtained from Diango in Draynor Village or from the toy box of a costume room .

An emote is performed by using the "prance" option on the hat while it is worn. This spawns a snow pile under the player, which snowballs can be picked from, and melts soon after. It is commonly used in free to play for tick-manipulation.

In snow-restricted areas, the message in the chatbox will instead state This is not an appropriate place to play with your hat! . The hat cannot also be operated while sitting down prompting the message You can't operate the hat while you're sitting down. .

Previously, they were obtainable during the 2013 Rare Drops event (from 14 July to 21 July ) as part of a rare item drop .
10508:
A wintumber tree is a holiday item that can be planted in a player-owned house. It can be obtained by completing one of the Christmas holiday events that occur once per year. This also rewards the player with all other holiday items associated with Christmas. The tree is untradeable and may be planted on any free non-hotspot space in the Garden or on any free outdoor space of a player-owned house. If lost or destroyed, the player can obtain another from Diango in Draynor Village.

Attempting to plant the tree anywhere besides the garden of your player-owned house prints the message You can only plant the wintumber tree in the garden of your player-owned house. Attempting to dig up a wintumber tree in someone else's house prints the message You can't dig up the owner's wintumber tree! How unfestive!

Previously, they were obtainable during the 2013 Rare Drops event (from 5 August to 12 August) as part of a rare item drop.

10531:
A green egg is used in Barbarian Assault to damage penance monsters. If loaded into the egg launcher and shot at penance creatures, it will deal 1 damage and poison the target. If shot at a Penance Runner, Penance Fighter, or Penance Ranger, the poison will hit every 3 seconds a total of 5 times unless healed. If shot at a Penance Healer, the poison will hit every 18 seconds a total of 5 times. Green egg poison is in addition to poisoned food damage, and will not reset, reduce, or delay damage. A maximum of five green eggs may be loaded into the egg launcher at any given time. Both egg launchers share the same reserve of eggs.

Green eggs tend to be used when no red eggs are available, as they deal less damage and can only damage one enemy at a time.
10532:
A red egg is used in Barbarian Assault to damage penance monsters. If loaded into the egg launcher and shot at penance creatures, it will explode and deal 3 damage to the primary target, and 0 to 1 damage to any penance monster within 3 squares of the primary target. A maximum of five red eggs may be loaded into the egg launcher at any given time. Both egg launchers share the same reserve of eggs.

Red eggs are most commonly used against stray Penance Runners. They are also very effective against clumps of Penance Healers.
10533:
Blue eggs are used in Barbarian Assault to stun penance monsters. If loaded into an egg launcher and shot at penance creatures, a blue egg will stun its target for 6 seconds. During this time, the monster will not move, and cannot be targeted with food, weapons or the egg launcher. A maximum of five blue eggs may be loaded into the egg launcher at any given time. Both egg launchers share the same reserve of eggs.

Blue eggs are rarely used in the minigame due to the fact that firing one will render its target temporarily unattackable (and, in the case of healers, unable to be poisoned). However, they can still be useful for slowing down Penance runners from reaching the southern cave entrance should they manage to get past the player(s) who are assigned the Defender role.
10534: A yellow egg is used in the final wave of Barbarian Assault and is the first step in creating an Omega egg. It is found on the ground by the collector during wave 10. It must be passed on to the healer to make a poisoned egg.
10535: A poisoned egg is used in the final wave of Barbarian Assault. It is made by using a yellow egg, which is dropped by the Penance Queen in the 10th wave, on the poison crater. The yellow egg must be received from the collector and dunked in poison craters by the healer. It must then be passed on to the attacker to make a spiked/pois. egg.
10536: A spiked/pois. egg is used in the final wave of Barbarian Assault . It is made by using spikes on a poisoned egg . The poisoned egg must be received from the healer and have spikes added by the attacker. It must then be passed on to the defender to make an omega egg .
10537:
The omega egg is used during the last wave of the Barbarian Assault minigame to defeat the Penance Queen . The omega egg is launched using the egg launcher . This is the only way the queen can be damaged and defeated. Each hit with the omega egg deals 30-39 damage.

The omega egg can only be shot if the wave's runners , fighters , healers , and rangers have been defeated.
10538: A defender horn is used in Barbarian Assault to tell the healer what to do. The choices to tell the healer are poisoned tofu , poisoned worms , and poisoned meat . It is received when starting Barbarian Assault and becoming a defender.
10539: Poisoned tofu is used in Barbarian Assault to hurt Penance Healers. The healer needs to use the poisoned tofu on the penance healer. This will cause 4 damage, and poison the healer for 4 damage. Unlike regular monsters, the Penance Healer ticks poison damage every 3 seconds.
10540: Poisoned worms are used in Barbarian Assault to hurt Penance Healers. The healer needs to use the poisoned worms on the penance healer. This will cause 4 damage, and poison the healer for 4 damage. Unlike regular monsters, the Penance Healer ticks poison damage every 3 seconds.
10541: Poisoned meat is used in Barbarian Assault to hurt Penance Healers. The healer needs to use the poisoned meat on the penance healer. This will cause 4 damage, and poison the healer for 4 damage. Unlike regular monsters, the Penance Healer ticks poison damage every 3 seconds.
10542: Healing vials are used in Barbarian Assault by the Healer to heal teammates. It is made by getting an empty healing vial from the Healer item machine and taking it to the Healer spring . The amount it heals varies by the healer level the player has.
10543: Healing vials are used in Barbarian Assault by the Healer to heal teammates. It is made by getting an empty healing vial from the Healer item machine and taking it to the Healer spring . The amount it heals varies by the healer level the player has.
10544: Healing vials are used in Barbarian Assault by the Healer to heal teammates. It is made by getting an empty healing vial from the Healer item machine and taking it to the Healer spring . The amount it heals varies by the healer level the player has.

10547:
The healer hat is a possible reward item from Barbarian Assault and requires 45 Defence to wear. Players who have killed the Penance Queen and have 275 Honour points in each of the four roles can purchase the hat from Commander Connad , located on the main floor of the Barbarian Outpost . The hat is part of the penance set , all parts of which are available from Barbarian Assault.

Its stats are very similar to the farseer helm . Both require 45 Defence and offer +6 magic attack bonus with attack penalties of -5 to all other styles. However, the healer hat has a slightly higher (+1) magic defence bonus at the cost of lower melee defence (-2 to stab, slash, and crush).

If the player dies a PvP death and the item is unprotected, it will remain in the player's inventory; however, the item will be in a broken, unusable state and must be repaired by using it on Perdu and paying him 45,000 coins .

This item can be stored in the armour case of a costume room .
10548:
The fighter hat is a piece of members-only armour that requires 45 Defence to wear, and is obtained through the Barbarian Assault minigame. Players with 275 honour points in each role and who have killed the Penance Queen can purchase the hat from Commander Connad, located on the ground floor of the Barbarian Outpost.

The fighter hat is sometimes used in place of the warrior helm and berserker helm. The warrior helm provides slightly better defensive bonuses, but offers an attack bonus to slash only, while the fighter hat also provides attack bonuses to stab and crush. In fact, the +5 stab attack bonus makes the fighter hat the best-in-slot item for stab attack. The berserker helm has slightly better defensive bonuses and provides a strength bonus (+3), but provides no melee attack bonuses. The fighter hat is a popular choice among obsidian maulers that are unable to obtain the Inquisitor's great helm.

If the player dies a PvP death and the item is unprotected, it will remain in the player's inventory; however, the item will be in a broken, unusable state and must be repaired by using it on Perdu and paying him 45,000 coins.

This item can be stored in the armour case of a costume room.
10549:
The runner hat is a piece of members-only armour that requires 45 Defence and is rewarded from the Barbarian Assault minigame. Players with 275 Honour points in all four roles and who have killed the Penance Queen can purchase the hat from Commander Connad, located on the ground floor of the Barbarian Outpost.

Compared to other helmets requiring 45 Defence, the Runner hat lacks attack bonuses. The stats for the hat are closely similar to equipment requiring 40 Defence. The Runner hat provides a slightly higher magic defence bonus (+1) compared to the that of the rune full helm (-1), and lacks a negative attack bonus for ranged and magic. The runner hat has a weight of only 1 kg, whilst most other helmets weigh at least 2 kg if not more. It is mostly used by players who want to show their prestige in Barbarian Assault.

If the player dies a PvP death and the item is unprotected, it will remain in the player's inventory; however, the item will be in a broken, unusable state and must be repaired by using it on Perdu and paying him 40,005 coins.

This item can be stored in the armour case of a costume room.
10550:
A ranger hat is a piece of headgear available as a reward from Barbarian Assault . It resembles the head of a Penance Ranger .

Equipping the hat requires level 45 Defence . Players who have killed the Penance Queen and have 275 honour points in all four roles can purchase a Ranger hat from Commander Connad , who is located on the ground floor [ UK ] 1 st floor [ US ] of the Barbarian Outpost . In terms of Ranged attack bonus, it has 2 more than a Snakeskin bandana , the same as a Spined helm , and 2 less than a Robin Hood hat .

If the player dies a PvP death and the item is unprotected, it will remain in the player's inventory; however, the item will be in a broken, unusable state and must be repaired by using it on Perdu and paying him 45,000 coins .

This item can be stored in the armour case of a costume room .
10551:
The fighter torso (called the Penance torso in the Barbarian Assault Reward Shop) is armour that requires 40 Defence to equip and is a reward from the Barbarian Assault minigame. It can be purchased from Commander Connad for 375 honour points in all four roles, and one Penance Queen kill. It can be sold back to Connad for 300 honour points in all four roles by using it on him.

If the player dies a PvP death at level 20 Wilderness or below and the item is unprotected, it will remain in the player's inventory; however, the item will be in a broken, unusable state and must be repaired by using it on Perdu and paying him 150,000 coins.

If the player dies a PvP death above level 20 Wilderness and the item is unprotected, it will be converted to coins. To prevent this, a Trouver parchment and a payment of 500,000 coins can be given to Perdu in order to permanently lock the item. The locked item will remain in the player's inventory; however, the item will be in a mangled, unusable state and must be repaired by using it on Perdu and paying him 500,000 coins.

Note: It is possible to obtain at any level, but low level players may struggle specifically with the attacker role.

This item can be stored in the armour case of a costume room.
10552:
Runner boots (called the Penance boots in the Barbarian Assault Reward Shop) are boots obtained from Barbarian Assault, requiring 40 Defence to wear. The boots can be obtained by exchanging 100 Honour Points in each role from the Barbarian Assault minigame, and does not require the Penance Queen to be killed.

The runner boots are not often used for combat purposes because of their poor stats. Runner boots provide a small attack bonus to magic (+1) and ranged (+1) but have defence bonuses similar to that of black boots, which only require 10 Defence. The boots also lack a strength bonus like that provided by climbing boots, rune boots, spiked manacles, and dragon boots. The boots are often used instead to show prestige in Barbarian Assault.

This item can be stored in the armour case of a costume room.
10553:
Penance gloves are gloves obtained from Barbarian Assault , requiring 40 Defence to wear. Players with 150 honour points in each of the four roles can purchase the gloves by speaking to Commander Connad , located on the main floor of the Barbarian Outpost . Players do not have to kill the Penance Queen to obtain the gloves.

Penance gloves provide 4.535 kg in weight reduction , along with modest defensive bonuses.

These gloves can be taken to Entrana .

This item can be stored in the armour case of a costume room .

However, the red d'hide chaps does not require 40 Defence to wear like the Penance skirt does.

10556:
Attacker icon is an item worn in the jaw slot, a back-end Worn Equipment slot system where facial hair is placed [ 1 ] while playing Barbarian Assault . It shows that the player is an attacker indicated by the red circle around them with the attacker symbol. When a game of Barbarian Assault finishes, the icon is removed.

Having a higher level in the Attacker role, which can be done via Commander Connad or choosing to do so immediately after a game, allows players to deal bonus damage to penance monsters.
10557:
Collector icon is an item worn in the jaw slot, a back-end Worn Equipment slot system where facial hair is placed [ 1 ] while playing Barbarian Assault . It shows that the player is a collector indicated by the yellow circle around them with the collector symbol. When a game of Barbarian Assault finishes, the icon is removed.

Having a higher level in the Collector role, which can be done via Commander Connad or choosing to do so immediately after a game, allows the collection bag to hold more eggs, and an increased chance of success when converting eggs.
10558:
Defender icon is an item worn in the jaw slot, a back-end Worn Equipment slot system where facial hair is placed [ 1 ] while playing Barbarian Assault . It shows that the player is a defender indicated by the blue circle around them with the defender symbol. When a game of Barbarian Assault finishes, the icon is removed.

Having a higher level in the Defender role, which can be done via Commander Connad or choosing to do so immediately after a game, allows players to have an increased luring range when luring Penance Runners .
10559:
Healer icon is an item worn in the jaw slot, a back-end Worn Equipment slot system where facial hair is placed [ 1 ] while playing Barbarian Assault . It shows that the player is a healer indicated by the green circle around them with the healer symbol. When a game of Barbarian Assault finishes, the icon is removed.

Having a higher level in the Healer role, which can be done via Commander Connad or choosing to do so immediately after a game, allows players to heal more hitpoints per healing vial dose.
10560: A collector horn is used in Barbarian Assault to tell the attacker what style to use. It is received when starting Barbarian Assault and becoming a collector.
10561:
Spikes can only be found in the Barbarian Assault minigame on the 10th wave. The person designated as the Attacker must take them from the petrified mushrooms found around the area.

They are to be used upon an Omega egg . Any spare spikes are automatically removed from the inventory upon leaving the Barbarian Assault cavern.
10562:
The Queen help book or Queen help is obtained during the Barbarian Assault minigame after The Final Battle tutorial with Captain Cain .

If players destroy the book, it can be reclaimed from Captain Cain after viewing the same tutorial. It is also available in a bookcase of a player-owned house .
10563: No eggs is an unobtainable item released along with Barbarian Assault, used on the Barbarian Assault in-game interface to represent that no eggs of a particular colour have been deposited.
10564:
The granite body is a piece of body armour that requires 50 Defence and 50 Strength to wear. Players who have killed the Penance Queen can purchase it from Commander Connad , located on the ground floor of the Barbarian Outpost , for 95,000 coins . It is the only reward from the Barbarian Assault minigame that is not obtained with honour points .

The granite body is the most commonly used piece of the granite armour set, being similar in price to the rune platebody while providing better defensive bonuses. While the granite helm and granite boots similarly outclass their rune counterparts, the latter is significantly more expensive and the former competes with the more common Fremennik helmets .

Even though it is seen as low-level armour, the granite body has slightly higher defensive bonuses than the Fighter torso , except the slash defence, which is 1 lower. However, the granite body's lack of a strength bonus means the fighter torso is more commonly used for slayer tasks and general melee training, where maximizing one's damage output outweighs defensive bonuses. Compared to the dragon chainbody , the granite body provides better range defence and stab defence but is weaker by 9 and 19 points in slash and crush respectively. The granite body does not interfere with Ava's devices, this combined with its modest ranged penalty can make it a decent choice for Range Tank in PvM.

Purchasing and equipping a granite body is a requirement for the hard Kandarin diary . It must be purchased from Commander Connad to meet the requirement for the task, requiring the player kill the Penance Queen at least once.
10566: The Fire cape is an animation item that is temporarily equipped by the player when travelling through a Fairy ring while wearing a Fire cape . It is impossible for the game to render animated textures as transparent; therefore, this non-animated fire cape is equipped during the animation. Aside from this, the item is unobtainable.
10567:
The "Thingy" was the name of seven unobtainable items that could previously be found in the game cache.

Originally, it was intended that the Sapphire amulet would give players the ability to teleport to the Barbarian Outpost , holding 8 charges. The standard sapphire amulet would have been converted into the 8 charge version, while the thingys were added for variants that had 1-7 charges. Upon the release of Barbarian Assault , this feature was added to the Games necklace instead.

In RuneScape , the item briefly became viewable in the Grand Exchange. When asked about this, a Jagex Moderator claimed the item was just a joke:

The Thingys were gradually removed from the game, with the last being replaced by a Healer icon in 2019. As a result, they have never been obtainable in Old School RuneScape .

10581:
The keris is a one-handed stab sword and dagger dropped by the Giant Scarab toward the end of the Contact! quest, and is the precursor to the keris partisan. It deals 33% bonus damage against all kalphites and scabarites, and has a 1/51 chance of puncturing a hole in their exoskeleton, dealing triple damage. When the special effect occurs, the chatbox will display the game message: You slip your dagger through a gap in the creature's chitin, landing a vicious blow. This message is not displayed if the effect deals less than 10 damage, which can cause the activation frequency to appear lower than it is in reality.

The keris requires 50 Attack to wield. Like most daggers, it can be poisoned. It has offensive melee stats similar to the dragon dagger albeit slightly weaker. Its +2 prayer bonus makes it one of the three daggers to provide one, the others being Wolfbane with +5 and the white dagger with +1. It is needed to kill a locust rider for a Hard Desert Diary task.

It is lost on death if it is not protected, and can be retrieved from Osman, (or Selim, after Beneath Cursed Sands), for a fee of 20,000. Alternatively, it can be reclaimed from Perdu for a fee of 25,000.

10586:
A combat lamp is a quest reward for completing the Contact! quest. It grants two experience boosts in combat skills of the player's choice. If the lamp is lost or destroyed before experience is gained from it, it can be reclaimed from the Sophanem High Priest .

This lamp can be banked.

It grants two wishes of 7,000 experience each to any of the following skills :
10587:
Tarn's diary , or The Diary of Tarn Razorlor , is a book that chronicles how Tarn came to be in the dungeon where he is and how he got involved in the dark arts of necromancy . Additionally, the book contains some magic elements: when used with a Salve amulet or an imbued salve amulet, it will enchant it and increase the benefits gained to a 20% boost in strength and accuracy against the undead .

The diary can initially be found on the table in the room just past where the player fights Tarn in Lair of Tarn Razorlor . After completing the miniquest, the lair does not need to be navigated again, as the diary can be re-obtained from the bookcase of the player's house under the name The Diary of Tarn Razorlor .
10588:
The salve amulet (e) is the enchanted form of the salve amulet , granting a 20% increase (from 16.67%) in the wearer's Attack and Strength when fighting undead monsters .

The salve amulet is enchanted by using Tarn's diary on it, acquired as part of the Lair of Tarn Razorlor miniquest. An easy way to obtain the diary is by teleporting directly to Tarn's Lair using a Slayer ring . After the miniquest, players can quickly reclaim the diary from a bookcase in a player-owned house under the name The Diary of Tarn Razorlor .
10589:
Granite helm is a helmet that can be obtained by killing terror dogs or from High Level Gambles at Barbarian Assault . 50 Strength and 50 Defence are required to equip the helm. It has slightly better stats than the rune full helm but slightly worse stats than the dragon med helm .

The granite helm has superior ranged defensive stats compared to rune and dragon (but inferior to the dragon full helm ). This also applies to other pieces of granite equipment.
10591:
The Terror dog is an interface item that can be seen in the Slayer skill guide representing the Terror dog

The actual item cannot be obtained by players.
10592:
Penguin bongos are a quest item made and used in the Cold War quest .

They are made by using a mahogany plank with soft leather . During the quest, they are given to the penguin Ping . Afterward, it is possible to make them again, and play them while dressed as a penguin.
10593:
Cowbells are available from any dairy cow, if a player has started the Cold War quest and has 15 Thieving. Stealing a cowbell provides 16 Thieving experience. In Zanaris, the dairy cow will have a conversation with you about the bell, and will give it to you.

This item is required during the Cold War quest, but additional cowbells may be thieved afterwards. They may be used (played) as long as the player is wearing their clockwork suit.
10594:
A clockwork book can be found in the bookcase of a player-owned house. It is given to you by Larry during the Cold War quest.

The book itself contains notes and instructions on making clockwork toys and a note from Larry on how to make the penguin suit. It is needed if you wish to build the penguin suit in Cold War.

If lost, it can be reclaimed from Larry at Ardougne Zoo, or from a bookcase within a player-owned house.
10595:
The clockwork suit (or Penguin suit) is made during and after the Cold War quest. It is made on a Crafting table 3 in the workshop of a player-owned house with a clockwork, a plank, and silk, by selecting the Clockwork toy option, followed by Clockwork penguin.

With the suit, the player can become a penguin by talking to Larry while at the iceberg (or by using Larry's "Tuxedo-time" right-click option). Larry can be found at the Ardougne Zoo, the pier south of the Rellekka Hunter area near fairy ring DKS, the penguin iceberg, and the Lumbridge sheep farm. Note that in order to wear the suit, players must not have anything in the weapon, shield and cape slots. This is the only way to wear the clockwork suit.

Wearing the suit opens up a possibility of performing 8 unique penguin emotes. The suit is required in order to access the Penguin agility course on the Penguin Outpost.

The Clockwork Suit can be wound and released, like the toy mouse can. You can then catch it for 3 Agility experience. Players will not be able to retrieve the suit if they release the suit first and then teleport away from it.

The suit is also required for a master clue cryptic step.

For collectors, be cautious after the quest's end. Noodle, who trades you this, is no longer present afterward, making this item unobtainable if lost.

Sarachnis chitin were an item that could be dropped by monsters in the Forthos Dungeon. To be eligible to receive them, players must have talked to Sir Pear Visor in the centre of the Old School Museum beneath the Falador Party Room, and have agreed to help him. After agreeing to help him, a message appeared in the player's chatbox stating: You have enabled additional drops from activities across the game. To disable these speak to Sir Pear Visor in the Falador museum.

The item was given to Sir Pear Visor as part of the community goals for global contributions toward the Old School Museum expansion; the 'Check-Progress' option on the item will open the museum expansion's contributions interface. Upon the goal being reached, the item became unobtainable.

1/15 from Sarachnis

1/80 from baby red dragons

1/100 from temple spiders

10808: Arctic pyre logs may be used during the Shades of Mort'ton minigame to cremate the remains of Loar , Phrin , and Riyl Shades . They require level 47 Firemaking to light and grant 158 Firemaking experience when used to cremate a shade (237 with Morytania Diary 4 complete).
10810:
Arctic pine logs are cut from arctic pine trees , found on the island of Neitiznot and south-west of Rellekka . A Woodcutting level of 54 is required to cut them, giving 40 experience per log; 42 Firemaking is needed to make a fire using these type of logs, granting 125 experience per log. A Woodcutting level of 56 is required to split these logs.

They are also used to make Neitiznot shields , requiring a level of 56 in Woodcutting. Two of these logs, a bronze nail , and a rope are required to make one, granting 34 Crafting experience.

Players can also use the logs on a woodcutting stump to make split logs for the quest The Fremennik Isles .
10812:
Split logs are made from arctic pine logs when they are used on a woodcutting stump . The logs require level 56 Woodcutting to split, giving 5 Woodcutting experience per log split, or 140 per inventory. Players wearing Lumberjack clothing will receive the appropriate bonus experience. It takes 50 seconds to convert an entire inventory of arctic pine logs to split logs.

Split logs are used to repair the bridges in the quest The Fremennik Isles . Apart from training Woodcutting, they have no other use.
10814:
Hair is a drop obtained by killing yaks outside the village of Neitiznot . Players can use it on a spinning wheel to make rope using the Crafting skill. Making a rope requires level 30 Crafting and grants 25 Crafting experience .

The players who paid Vanligga Gastfrihet 's taxes during or after The Fremennik Isles can buy them from her shop (located north of the longhall in Jatizso ) for a price starting at 2 coins each with a stock of 50. She is very close to a bank, so purchasing hair from her is a faster method of obtaining than killing yaks.
10816:
Raw yak meat is an uncooked food . It becomes cooked meat when successfully cooked, granting 30 Cooking experience.

It can be obtained by killing a Yak on Neitiznot or by trading with the shop Contraband yak produce on Jatizso . The shop is convenient due to its proximity to a bank.
10818:
Yak-hides are a 100% drop from yaks . They can be cured for 5 coins by Thakkrad Sigmundson on Neitiznot . Cured yak-hide can be crafted into yak-hide legs and yak-hide bodies with the use of a needle and thread .

After partially completing The Fremennik Isles quest , players can also buy yak-hides from Contraband yak produce in central Jatizso .
10820:
Cured yak-hides are obtained by taking a yak-hide to Thakkrad Sigmundson on Neitiznot and paying him 5 coins to cure it. They can also be bought from the Contraband yak produce store on Jatizso starting at 110 coins each.

Cured yak-hides can be crafted into yak-hide legs and yak-hide bodies with the use of a needle and thread . Yak-hide legs require one cured yak-hide and 43 Crafting , while yak-hide bodies require two cured yak-hides and 46 Crafting. Each item gives 32 Crafting experience upon creation, which is unusual, as usually when crafting with hides the experience granted is based on the amount of hides used.
10822:
The Yak-hide armour is a piece of member's only armour . A Defence level of 20 is required to wear the top. It is part of the Yak-hide armour set, with the other part being the legs .

Yak-hide armour counts as warm clothing for the Wintertodt .
10824:
Yak hide armour are pieces of members only armour. Level 20 Defence is required to wear them. Yak hide legs have a +2 Ranged attack bonus compared to green d'hide chaps . It is part of the Yak-hide armour set, with the other part being the top .

Yak-hide armour counts as warm clothing for the Wintertodt .
10826:
The Neitiznot shield, also commonly called the Fremennik roundshield, is a shield made of wood that requires level 25 Defence to wield. It can be made during and after completion of The Fremennik Isles quest with level 56 Woodcutting on the woodcutting stump near the bank in Neitiznot. This requires two arctic pine logs, a bronze nail, a rope, and a hammer in the inventory. Making the shield grants 34 Crafting experience.

Although this shield can only be created after reaching a certain point in The Fremennik Isles quest, it is not a wielding requirement, and it can be worn by players who have not started the quest.

It has a slightly higher ranged and crush defence compared to the adamant kiteshield, but much lower slash and stab defence. It also lowers ranged attack and magic attack more than the adamant kiteshield. Therefore, it is not commonly used by players with 30 or higher Defence. It is, however, a safe alternative to players who have 25 Defence, as its defensive stats are comparably higher than those of the mithril kiteshield.

This shield also reduces the maximum damage taken from rocks thrown by ice troll females and thrower trolls from 6 to 2, as well as reducing the maximum hit of the Ice Troll King's throwing rock attacks from 7 to 2.
10828:
The Helm of Neitiznot is a helmet awarded to players upon completing The Fremennik Isles quest and requires a Defence level of 55 to wear. While it is tradeable, players may only equip the helm if they have completed The Fremennik Isles quest.

Its stats are roughly akin to those of a berserker helm . However, the helm of Neitiznot has an additional +3 prayer bonus, +1 crush and +3 magic defence bonuses, and does not possess negative magic and ranged attack bonuses. The helmet's substantial bonuses, along with it being non-degradable and cheap, make it one of the most frequently used helmets.

Additional helms can be obtained from Mawnis Burowgar for 50,000 coins. Alternatively, for those who do not wish to travel to Neitiznot , Perdu will return the helm to players for 95,000 coins.
10829:
The Documents are an unobtainable item added to the cache alongside The Fremennik Isles. They have an option to "Open", while their examine states they must be taken to Ali Morrisane in Al Kharid.

The documents' internal name suggest they formed part of a trade agreement, while the Royal decree is referred to as a "receipt", despite not serving this purpose. At the same time, many unused models can be found depicting crates of armour, swords, and battleaxes. It is possible therefore that there was a cut subplot in the quest which involved trading Jatizso products with Ali Morrisane.
10830: The royal decree is given to you by King Gjuki Sorvott IV to give to Mawnis Burowgar. This document is quest item from The Fremennik Isles quest. The Royal decree is an issue for better relations with Neitiznot, and Jatizso. The document cannot be banked, as a magical force prevents the player from doing so.
10831: The empty tax bag is used during The Fremennik Isles quest for collecting taxes from the shopkeepers and more inhabitants of Jatizso. While collecting taxes, it will become a light tax bag, then a normal tax bag, and finally a hefty tax bag. Tax bags cannot be banked, as "a magical force prevents you from banking this item!"
10832: The light tax bag is used during The Fremennik Isles quest for collecting taxes from the shopkeepers and more inhabitants of Jatizso. It is originally an empty tax bag, then as more taxes are collected it becomes a light tax bag, then a normal tax bag, and finally a hefty tax bag.
10833: The normal tax bag is used during The Fremennik Isles quest for collecting taxes from the shopkeepers and more inhabitants of Jatizso. It is originally an empty tax bag, then as more taxes are collected it becomes a light tax bag, then a normal tax bag, and finally a hefty tax bag.
10834: The hefty tax bag is used during The Fremennik Isles quest for collecting taxes from the shopkeepers and more inhabitants of Jatizso . It is originally an empty tax bag , then as more taxes are collected it becomes a light tax bag , then a normal tax bag , and finally a hefty tax bag.
10835:
The bulging taxbag is an item that is unobtainable via normal gameplay. During The Fremennik Isles, in the part of the quest where players collect taxes for King Gjuki Sorvott IV, the tax bag becomes bulging when they collect at least 33,000 coins in taxes from the citizens of Jatizso. However, players can only collect a maximum of 29,000 coins in taxes, resulting in a hefty tax bag.

For the tax bag to become bulging, players must perform an exploit:

Destroy the tax bag, and filling the inventory entirely.

Attempt to collect taxes from Vanligga Gastfrihet, and offer to pay her taxes with your own coins. As you have no space in your inventory, a tax bag is placed in your bank containing the taxes you paid for her.

As the flag that tracks whether Vanligga's taxes has been paid or not is not set when paying her taxes in this manner, players can keep paying her taxes until the tax bag in the bank is bulging.
10836:

10842:
The Decapitated head is the severed head of the Ice Troll King , whom players slay as part of The Fremennik Isles .

Players must decapitate the Ice Troll King after killing him - they do not gain the head in their inventory automatically. They should then take the head to Mawnis Burowgar in Neitiznot .

Unusually (even for a quest item ), players cannot deposit this item in a bank . If the head is lost prior to completion of the quest, another can be obtained by reentering the Ice Troll Caves. In this scenario, upon entering the caves the player will be returned to the location of the Ice Troll King's corpse without having to pass through the first part of the cave.
10844:
Spring sq'irks are obtained through the Sorceress's Garden minigame. They are picked off of the sq'irk tree in the spring maze, requiring 25 Thieving to enter. Picking a spring sq'irk gives 40 Farming experience, and teleports the player to the fountain in the inner garden.

Players can use a pestle and mortar and an empty beer glass with 4 spring sq'irks to make spring sq'irkjuice. The spring sq'irkjuice gives 1,350 Thieving experience when given to Osman (or Selim after completing Beneath Cursed Sands), or can be consumed to boost Thieving by 1.
10845:
Summer sq'irks are obtained through the Sorceress's Garden minigame. They are picked off of the Sq'irk tree in the Summer maze. Doing so gives 60 Farming experience and teleports the player to the fountain in the inner garden.

With 2 summer sq'irks in your inventory along with a pestle and mortar and an empty beer glass you can make Summer sq'irkjuice .

Summer sq'irkjuice gives 3,000 Thieving experience when given to Osman (or Selim after completing Beneath Cursed Sands ).
10846:
Autumn sq'irks are obtained through the Sorceress's Garden minigame. They are picked off of the Sq'irk tree in the Autumn maze. Doing so gives 50 Farming experience and teleports the player to the fountain in the inner garden.

With 3 autumn sq'irks in your inventory along with a pestle and mortar and an empty beer glass, you can make Autumn sq'irkjuice.

Autumn sq'irkjuice gives 2,350 Thieving experience when given to Osman (or Selim after completing Beneath Cursed Sands).
10847:
Winter sq'irks are obtained through the Sorceress's Garden minigame. They are picked off of the Sq'irk tree in the Winter maze. Doing so gives 30 Farming experience and teleports the player to the fountain in the inner garden.

With 5 winter sq'irks in your inventory along with a pestle and mortar and an empty beer glass you can make Winter sq'irkjuice.

Winter sq'irkjuice gives 350 Thieving experience when given to Osman (or Selim after completing Beneath Cursed Sands).
10848:
Spring sq'irkjuice is made from spring sq'irks, found in the Sorceress's Garden minigame. Level 25 Thieving is required to access the spring garden. To make the juice, pick 4 spring sq'irks and use them with a pestle and mortar while having a beer glass in your inventory.

Picking the spring sq'irk gives 40 Farming experience.

Drinking the spring sq'irkjuice will restore 10% of your energy and give you a Thieving bonus of +1.

You can also give the spring sq'irkjuice to Osman (or Selim after completing Beneath Cursed Sands) for 1,350 Thieving experience.

Players wishing to gain fast levels in Thieving need only give Osman 40 glasses of spring sq'irkjuice to go from level 25 to level 45 Thieving. Progressing to the next available sq'irkjuice provides better experience with fewer required sq'irks per drink.
10849:
Summer sq'irkjuice is made from summer sq'irks , found in the Sorceress's Garden minigame. Level 65 Thieving is required to access the summer garden. To make the juice, pick 2 summer sq'irks and use them with a pestle and mortar while having a beer glass in your inventory which can be obtained on the shelves in the Sorceress 's house.

Turning in summer sq'irkjuice provides 84,000 Thieving experience per inventory, the highest of all sq'irkjuices.
10850:
Autumn sq'irkjuice is made from autumn sq'irks, found in the Sorceress's Garden minigame. Level 45 Thieving is required to access the autumn garden. To make the juice, pick 3 autumn sq'irks and use them with a pestle and mortar while having a beer glass in your inventory. In the autumn garden, you will also find a herb bush that allows you to pick two herbs at a time.

Picking the autumn sq'irk gives 50 Farming experience.

Drinking the autumn sq'irkjuice will restore 15% of your energy and give you a Thieving bonus of +2

You can also give the autumn sq'irkjuice to Osman (or Selim after completing Beneath Cursed Sands) for 2,350 Thieving experience.
10851:
Winter sq'irkjuice is made from winter sq'irks, found in the Sorceress's Garden minigame. No Thieving level is required to access the winter garden. To make the juice, pick 5 winter sq'irks and use them with a pestle and mortar while having a beer glass in your inventory. In the winter garden, you will also find a herb bush that allows you to pick two herbs at a time.

Picking the winter sq'irk gives 30 Farming experience.

Drinking the winter sq'irkjuice will restore 5% of your energy.

You can also give the juice to Osman (or Selim after completing Beneath Cursed Sands) for 350 Thieving experience.

The winter sq'irkjuice does not provide a temporary boost to Thieving unlike other sq'irkjuice variants, which makes drinking it almost entirely pointless over handing it in for experience.

10856: Sin seer's note is given by Sin Seer in Seers' Village during The General's Shadow miniquest. 10857: A severed leg is an item given by General Khazard during The General's Shadow miniquest. It is used to distract Bouncer after getting him to low health so the player can kill him at the end of the miniquest.
10858:
The shadow sword is a two-handed sword obtained as a reward from The General's Shadow mini-quest. The sword matches the ghostly robes set, though it cannot be stored alongside the robes in the costume room of a player-owned house .

The shadow sword has the same stats as a black 2h sword , with additional Magic attack and defence bonuses.

If lost, the sword can be reclaimed by speaking to the ghost in the room where you fought Bouncer's ghost (accessible through a crack on the south wall of the north-eastern room in the Goblin Cave , just east of the Fishing Guild entrance). A ghostspeak amulet (or Morytania legs 2 or better) must be worn in order to talk to the ghost.

The ghost will not give you a second copy if you already have one in your inventory or bank. The only way to obtain multiple copies at the same time is to first deposit one in the master STASH unit in the south-east corner of Zamorak's Fortress .

Note: Despite being untradeable, the shadow sword will always be lost on death, unless it's one of the three (or four with Protect Item ) items protected on death. It will also not appear on the ground, meaning you will have to reclaim it.
10859:
A tea flask is a container item that can store up to 5 cups of plain tea. Tea may be drunk directly from the flask restoring 3 Hitpoints and temporarily boosting Attack by 2 + 2% (rounded down). Upon consuming the tea, the player will exclaim Ahhh, tea is so refreshing.. The tea flask may also be used on an empty cup to fill it. Tea flasks cannot be filled with damiana tea, nettle tea, or tea from a player-owned house.

Tea flasks can be obtained through Creature Creation, a solo activity that involves creating unique hybrid monsters and killing them for their drops. The tea flask may be obtained from any of the hybrid monsters.

Like satchels, they do not stack in the bank even if they have matching contents, and cannot be placed in Group storage.

10884: A fuse is used during The Great Brain Robbery to blow open the door of the monastery. The fuse is found in a locker on the ground floor of the ship beached on Harmony Island. It is identical to the fuse used in Cabin Fever.
10885:
The Keg is an item that can be found on the crashed ship on Harmony Island . During The Great Brain Robbery , it serves as an infinite source of kegs needed to complete the quest. This keg however is intended to be an unobtainable dummy item, similar to the tinderbox on the ship.

10886: The Prayer book is an animation item released with The Great Brain Robbery . It is temporarily wielded by the player during an animation for using the Prayer book to cure poison. Aside from this, it cannot be obtained.
10887:
The barrelchest anchor is a two-handed spiked weapon and quest item acquired in The Great Brain Robbery . 60 Attack and 40 Strength are required to wield it. It is obtained after killing Barrelchest .

Players receive this item in a broken state and must pay Smith on the docks of Mos Le'Harmless a fee of 230,000 coins to repair the anchor ( Book o' Piracy is needed to properly speak with Smith). If the anchor is lost, players can retrieve another damaged anchor from Brother Tranquility or purchase a repaired one from Perdu for 290,000 coins. Similar to the Bearhead , players do not need to complete The Great Brain Robbery in order to use or reclaim the Barrelchest anchor.

The anchor has a soft requirement of 50 Prayer in order to start The Great Brain Robbery . Many combat pures may still opt to complete the quest as Smite requires 52 Prayer.

The barrelchest anchor's stats are almost equal to those of Dharok's greataxe . It is well known as a PKing weapon, used in combos such as anchor to Granite maul specials .

It can be upgraded to the Barrelchest anchor (bh) with a Barrelchest anchor imbue scroll , which has a +10 increased crush and strength bonus and a +15% increase to the special attack's damage. The upgraded version can only be used for PvP in the Bounty Hunter minigame , Castle Wars , Clan Wars and Soul Wars however.

The anchor has a soft requirement of 50 Prayer in order to start The Great Brain Robbery . Many combat pures may still opt to complete the quest as Smite requires 52 Prayer.

The barrelchest anchor's stats are almost equal to those of Dharok's greataxe . It is well known as a PKing weapon, used in combos such as anchor to Granite maul specials .

It can be upgraded to the Barrelchest anchor (bh) with a Barrelchest anchor imbue scroll , which has a +10 increased crush and strength bonus and a +15% increase to the special attack's damage. The upgraded version can only be used for PvP in the Bounty Hunter minigame , Castle Wars , Clan Wars and Soul Wars however.
10889:
The blessed lamp is a reward obtained by completing the Great Brain Robbery quest. It gives 5,000 experience in a chosen skill above level 30. Players may reclaim their blessed lamp from Brother Tranquility if they lose it before gaining the experience from it.

This lamp can be banked. It is also worth noting that if your inventory is full, the lamp will not be placed in the inventory.
10890:
The prayer book is a reward from the The Great Brain Robbery quest . By right clicking on it while wearing a holy symbol or hallowed symbol , the player can use Prayer to cure poison at the cost of some prayer points (see #Usages ). This can also be done via clicking the hitpoints orb, though potions will be prioritised. Sometimes the poison will only be partially cured if you run out of prayer points .

If lost, the prayer book can be reclaimed in the Edgeville Monastery on the ground floor [ UK ] 1 st floor [ US ] on the south-western bookcase. The book can also be found on the bookcase in a player-owned house under the title, "Prayer of Deliverance from Poisons".

Although this book has a 'destroy' option, it is possible to get more than one copy. This can be done by keeping the book in your bank while you obtain a new one from your player-owned house bookcase.

The prayer book is always lost on death.
10891:
A wooden cat is a toy that can be made using the Crafting skill, after partial completion of the quest The Great Brain Robbery. During the quest, 10 of them are needed to fool Rufus the meat trader into thinking they're real cats. After speaking to Rufus and watching a cutscene, you will be granted the ability to make wooden cats.

They can be made on the crafting table in your house with a regular wooden plank and one piece of fur (werewolf fur, bear fur or grey wolf fur) gaining you 15 Crafting experience. Attempting to use any fur from a Hunter creature will result in the message: "The only fur you have is too nice to waste on these cats. You should try something else."

When doing The Great Brain Robbery quest and it doesn't show up on the clockwork bench to make it, make sure you have progressed far enough in the quest.
10893:
The cranial clamp is used by Dr Fenkenstrain in The Great Brain Robbery quest along with some bell jars , a pair of brain tongs and some skull staples .

This equipment is used to perform brain transplants on the zombified monks in Mos Le'Harmless in order to restore them to their normal form.
10894: Brain tongs are used by Dr Fenkenstrain in The Great Brain Robbery quest along with some bell jars, a cranial clamp and some skull staples. This equipment is used to perform brain transplants on the zombified monks in Mos Le'Harmless in order to restore them to their normal form.
10895: Bell jars are used by Dr Fenkenstrain in The Great Brain Robbery quest along with a pair of brain tongs , a cranial clamp and some skull staples . This equipment is used to perform brain transplants on the zombified monks in Mos Le'Harmless in order to restore them to their normal form.
10896:
The wolf whistle is a quest item given to the player by Rufus during the The Great Brain Robbery quest.

It is used to call Rufus to Fenkenstrain's Castle to collect a box of wooden cats (which also contains Dr Fenkenstrain for delivery to Mos Le'Harmless ).

Multiple whistles can be obtained by dropping one and asking Rufus for more. All existing whistles (including the banked ones) will be removed upon summoning Rufus for the crate inspection.
10897:
The shipping order is a quest item used in The Great Brain Robbery . It is given to the player to attach to what is supposedly a crate of live cats, but actually contains Dr Fenkenstrain and a collection of wooden cats instead. When the player uses the shipping list on the crate it is teleported to Mos Le'Harmless .

Multiple items can be obtained by dropping the shipping order and asking Rufus for another. All existing copies (including the banked ones) will disappear after using the shipping order on the crate.
10898:
A keg is an item used in the The Great Brain Robbery quest. It is filled with gunpowder and is used to blow up a door open to the monastery on Harmony Island in order to get inside.

During the quest, four kegs spawn on the upper level of the zombie pirate's ship on Harmony Island . After the quest, they cannot be picked up.

For collectors, entering the monastery boss fight will remove the keg and fuse from your inventory.
10899: Crate parts are given to the player by Rufus in Canifis during The Great Brain Robbery quest. They are used to build a crate in Fenkenstrain's Castle which the player must then fill with wooden cats . Dr Fenkenstrain will then climb into this crate to be shipped to Mos Le'Harmless as he is allergic to teleporting. However, the plot is made waste when the whole crate is teleported.
10904:
Skull staples are used by Dr Fenkenstrain in The Great Brain Robbery quest along with a pair of brain tongs, bell jars and a cranial clamp. This equipment is used to perform brain transplants on the zombified monks in Mos Le'Harmless in order to restore them to their normal form.

Strangely, if a group of skull staples are examined, the examine text will still be "one skull staple."

10925:
Sanfew serum is a potion invented by the druid Sanfew that combines the properties of the super restore , superantipoison , and Relicym's balm . It restores 4 + 30% of the player's base level (rounded down) per dose in all skills except Hitpoints , provides 6 minutes of immunity to poison , and provides 15 minutes of immunity to disease .

Sanfew serums can also be used on nail beasts , which can deal 20-40 damage per dose and grants melee experience . This requires the player to have no weapons equipped; if they do, it will automatically be unequipped if there is space in their inventory .

Sanfew serum is made by adding, in order, unicorn horn dust , clean snake weed , and nail beast nails to an already made super restore . Partially completed Sanfew serums are called mixture - step 1 and step 2 , but are not drinkable in these forms. Level 65 Herblore and completion of Zogre Flesh Eaters is required in order to make this potion.

96 Herblore experience is given for a completed 1-dose Sanfew serum, 128 experience for a 2-dose serum, 160 experience for a 3-dose serum, and 192 experience for a 4-dose serum. Or more simply, the total experience given can be calculated with: E x p e r i e n c e = 32 × D o s e s + 64

As Sanfew serums' higher price often makes super restores and prayer potions more cost efficient for restoring prayer, Sanfew serums are notably useful in situations where prayer restoration as well as poison protection are needed and inventory space is limited, such as Dagannoth Kings , as it fulfills the two requirements in one inventory space. Similarly, Sanfew serums are effective for fighting The Nightmare as they offer the same utility against parasites as Relicym's balm while also offering prayer restoration.

The lumberjack boots are a part of the lumberjack clothing set that can be purchased from the Forestry Shop for 1,000 anima-infused bark , 100 noted maple logs , and 200 noted yew logs . These logs can be bought on the Grand Exchange for 23,500 . It is also dropped by undead lumberjacks in the Temple Trekking minigame . They increase experience by 0.2% when Woodcutting . This is increased to +2.5% when wearing the whole set.

This item can be stored in the armour case of a costume room , as part of the Lumberjack Costume set. Ultimate Ironmen will be unable to retrieve individual pieces until the full set is stored. It can also be stored in the Forestry kit with a Clothes pouch in order to receive the outfit's benefits without having to wear them. However, bonuses from other outfits, such as the graceful outfit , will override the clothes pouch if worn.

10950:
Skull staples are an unobtainable item. They were added in March 2007 under the name Loot bag (230k).

On release, the barrelchest anchor could originally be dropped by players, and was very popular in player-killing. A week after the update, the drop mechanics were changed so that a player who died with the anchor would lose the item, and drop 230,000 coins instead. The loot bag was presumably created in order to fulfil this purpose.

However, it is unclear if the item could ever actually be obtained by players; at the time players reported receiving a stack of coins instead, and the Loot bag does not have any way to redeem the coins inside.

In any event, this mechanic was removed from the game a week later, after players realised they could die on purpose to receive 230k coins and then repair the anchor for only 50k. The Loot bag was deleted, and its name and examine were changed to that of the Skull staple, another item used during The Great Brain Robbery.

The frog-leather body is a piece of frog-leather armour that can be bought from Reldak's Leather Armour in the market place of Dorgesh-Kaan. It can also be looted from Dorgesh-Kaan average chests, specifically from the chests in Zanik's house, which require 52 Thieving to unlock. Frog-leather armour cannot be created through the Crafting skill.

Wearing the body requires level 25 in Defence and Ranged.
10956:
Frog-leather chaps are a piece of frog-leather armour that can be bought from Reldak's Leather Armour in the market place of Dorgesh-Kaan. It can also be looted from the Dorgesh-Kaan average chests, specifically from the chests in Zanik's house, which require 52 Thieving to unlock. Frog-leather armour cannot be created through the Crafting skill.

Wearing the chaps requires level 25 in Defence and Ranged. Despite having lower requirements to equip, studded chaps have better stats than frog-leather chaps.
10958:
Frog-leather boots are a piece of frog-leather armour that can be bought from Reldak's Leather Armour in the market place of Dorgesh-Kaan. Frog-leather armour cannot be created through the Crafting skill.

Wearing the boots requires level 25 in Defence and Ranged.
10960: Green gloop soup is a food that can be bought from Turgok in Dorgesh-Kaan. Turgok calls it 'Cave slime soup'. Presumably the poisonous substances from the cave slime are removed or treated before serving. Eating it will heal 2 Hitpoints. It can also be pickpocketed from the cave goblins in Dorgesh-Kaan.
10961: Frogspawn gumbo is a delicacy of the Dorgeshuun. It can be acquired in three ways: selling food to gourmets in Dorgesh-Kaan, purchasing it for 10 coins from Markog in Dorgesh-Kaan, or pickpocketing cave goblins. It heals 2 hitpoints when eaten. This food can be handy when pickpocketing cave goblins, as it provides a fast way of healing the player when injured from failed pickpocketing attempts.
10962:
Frogburgers are a hamburger-like dish popular amongst the Dorgeshuun. The dish itself is relatively simple, consisting of big frog meat inside a sliced bun. When eaten, frogburgers heal 2 hitpoints.

Frogburgers can be acquired by buying them from Durgok for 10 coins or by pickpocketing cave goblins. This food can be handy when pickpocketing cave goblins, as it provides a fast way of healing the player when injured from failed pickpocketing attempts.

Should players speak to the spit goblin near the sand pit in Dorgesh-Kaan, they may ask if the goblin will give them some of the frog meat being cooked. The goblin will reply that players can buy frogburgers at the market, implying that they are currently popular.
10963: Coated frogs' legs are Dorgeshuun cuisine. They can be obtained by pickpocketing cave goblins or purchasing them from Tindar at the Dorgesh-Kaan marketplace. They heal 2 hitpoints when eaten.
10964:
Bat shish kebabs are a delicacy amongst the Dorgeshuun cave goblins. The local goblins make them by first killing giant bats and skewering them on a stick or rod. They heal 2 Hitpoints .

Bat shish kebabs can be purchased in the cave goblin capital of Dorgesh-Kaan from one of the many merchants in the marketplace for 10 coins . They can also be stolen from some of the local cave goblins, which requires level 36 Thieving .
10965: Fingers are a traditional Dorgeshuun dish. They comprise of several wall beast fingers, served in a sauce made from subterranean ferns found in the area of Dorgesh-Kaan . They can be bought from the food merchants in Dorgesh-Kaan. They can also be obtained by pickpocketing cave goblins within Dorgesh-Kaan. Fingers heal 2 hitpoints when consumed.
10966:
Grubs à la mode is a dish eaten by the Dorgeshuun . They appear to be cave bug larva or a similar type of grub, served cold. The term à la mode has a French etymology.

Grubs à la mode heal 2 hitpoints when eaten, and boost Cooking by 1. They can only be obtained by selling food to gourmets in Dorgesh-Kaan market. Sometimes, when the player sells an item, the gourmet will give the player a Dorgeshuun dish in addition to coins .
10967:
Roast frog is a basic but popular dish eaten by the Dorgeshuun cave goblins of Dorgesh-Kaan . It is created by roasting a frog on a spit over an open fire. An example of this can be seen in southern Dorgesh-Kaan, where the spit goblin roasts big frogs .

Roasted frog can be obtained by trading with gourmets in the Dorgesh-Kaan market, as a random reward in addition to the coins received when selling food. It heals 2 Hitpoints when eaten. They also give a temporary Cooking boost of +1.
10968: Mushrooms are a dish eaten by the Dorgeshuun . They can be obtained at random by selling food to Gourmets in Dorgesh-Kaan . When eaten, they heal 2 Hitpoints . They also give a temporary Cooking boost of +1.
10969:
Fillets, also known as cave crawler fillets, are a delicacy of the Dorgeshuun. They consist of grilled slices of cave crawler, usually served on a decorative platter. The poisonous parts of the crawler are presumably removed or treated before serving.

Fillets can be obtained by trading with various shopkeepers in the Dorgesh-Kaan marketplace. They heal 2 hitpoints when eaten. They also give a temporary Cooking boost of +1.
10970:
Loach is a dish enjoyed by the Dorgeshuun cave goblins. It is a simple dish, consisting of a steamed locally-caught loach, referred to by some as a goblin fish.

Loach heal 3 hitpoints when eaten and can only be received at random when trading with gourmets in the Dorgesh-Kaan marketplace. They also give a temporary Cooking boost of +1.
10971:
Eel sushi is a traditional dish of the Dorgeshuun cave goblins. It consists of a raw cave/slimy eel wrapped in swamp weed. It cannot be made by players.

Eel sushi can be obtained randomly when selling food to Gourmets in Dorgesh-Kaan. Unlike most other Dorgeshuun cuisine, it heals 10 Hitpoints when eaten. They also give a temporary Cooking boost of +1.
10972:
The Dorgesh-kaan sphere teleports the player to a random location within Dorgesh-Kaan . They can be purchased and used upon completion of the Death to the Dorgeshuun quest . The sphere is consumed upon use and does not work beyond level 20 Wilderness .

Oldak , the cave goblin professor, will construct these spheres for the player if they provide him with 2 law runes and 1 molten glass (which can be noted). Players with at least 52 Thieving can also steal the spheres from Oldak's chest using a lockpick .
10973:
Light orbs can be used to fix magical lamps in Dorgesh-Kaan. Level 52 Crafting and Firemaking is needed to fix a lamp, giving 500 Crafting experience and 500 Firemaking experience. When a player has replaced 50 light orbs they will receive the message "You have replaced 50 orbs and have gained extra experience." The bonus received is 2,500 Crafting and Firemaking experience. This can be repeated indefinitely.

Broken lamps are found on all three floors. The large street lamps throughout Dorgesh-Kaan never need replacing. Broken lamps can be hard to distinguish from a distance. There are always ten broken lamps, and once one is fixed, a new one will break. Broken lamps are unique to each player and are the same for the player no matter what world the player is on.

In addition to attaching cave goblin wire to empty light orbs via the Crafting skill (requires 87 Crafting, granting 104 experience), complete light orbs are sometimes obtained from Dorgesh-Kaan Average Chests, specifically from the chest on the 2nd floor in Oldak's house. Empty orbs are obtained by looting a chest only slightly more frequently than completed light orbs.

A light orb is needed for a Sherlock elite clue scroll step, and one must be crafted for a master clue scroll.
10975: The spanner is an item used in the Dorgesh-Kaan Agility Course . It may be received from Turgall in the Dorgesh-Kaan South Dungeon . It is used to remove machine parts from the station at the end of the course.
10976:
A long bone is a drop from various monsters , typically those that also drop big bones , at a nearly universal rate of 1/400. [ 1 ] It can also drop as a regular drop from both the crazy and deranged archaeologists at a much higher rate.

After completion of Death to the Dorgeshuun , long bones may be sold to Barlak in Dorgesh-Kaan for 1,000 coins each. If the player has level 30 Construction [ not boostable ] and a player-owned house , Barlak will also grant 4,500 Construction experience per bone. The Carpenter's outfit set effect does not apply to the Construction experience rewarded. Note that Barlak will automatically take all of your long bones, including those in your bank, so it is not necessary to have any bones in your inventory.

Long bones can be buried for 15.1 Prayer experience, but this is not recommended. Burying a long bone in the Catacombs of Kourend will restore 2 prayer points, the same as big bones .

The bonecrusher will not automatically bury the bone, allowing the player to pick it up. Bones to Bananas and Bones to Peaches will not convert long bones. Long bones cannot be used on the Exposed altar in The Teomat . Long bones cannot be sacrificed with Sinister Offering , giving the message You could find something better to do with your special bone.

It would take 2,894 long bones to level Construction from 30 to 99.
10977:
A curved bone is an item dropped by any monster that drops big bones or giant bones , as well as Venenatis and Sotetseg . Curved bones are dropped at a universal rate of 1/5,012.5. [ 1 ]

Curved bones may be sold to Barlak , a Dorgesh-Kaan cave goblin, for 2,000 coins each. Dorgesh-Kaan can be accessed after the quest Death to the Dorgeshuun . The player will also be given a lecture on Construction , granting 6,750 Construction experience , as long as their Construction level is at least 30. If the player were to gain the same amount of experience by oak planks , it would cost them 45,337 coins , which can be considered as an extra theoretical value of a curved bone. Handing in bones does not grant any experience under level 30 Construction.

Curved bones can be buried, but this is not recommended as they only give 15.1 experience for each bone buried.

The bonecrusher will not automatically bury the bone, allowing the player to pick it up. Bones to Bananas and Bones to Peaches will not convert curved bones into fruit. Curved bones cannot be sacrificed with Sinister Offering , giving the message You could find something better to do with your special bone.

It would take 1,930 curved bones to go from level 30 to 99 Construction.
10978:
Swamp weed is a plant dropped by two Slayer monsters, Cave bugs and Molanisks , in the Dorgesh-Kaan South Dungeon . One of the uses is to cook it on a range for soda ash . Players can also catch it with a net while fishing for Frog spawn in Lumbridge Swamp Caves , giving 1 experience point. Swamp weeds are not stackable.

Swamp weed is also used by the Dorgeshuun cave goblins as a common cooking ingredient, as it is one of the few green plants that grow in or near Dorgesh-Kaan . An example of this can be seen in eel sushi , in which swamp weed is wrapped around raw cave eel or raw slimy eel .
10980:
Empty light orbs can be made with level 87 Crafting by blowing molten glass, granting 70 experience. Attaching a cave goblin wire to an empty orb creates a light orb, which gives 104 Crafting experience when the wire and empty light orb are combined. The light orb can be used to repair broken lamps in Dorgesh-Kaan for Firemaking and Crafting experience.

Empty light orbs cannot be traded. Coupled with the purchase cost or slow rate of collection of cave goblin wire, light orbs are an undesirable Crafting training method.
10981:
Cave goblin wire is a type of metal wire invented by the Dorgeshuun cave goblins. It is used primarily in their lighting system, which runs throughout their entire city of Dorgesh-Kaan .

Cave goblin wire is used in light orbs , which can be made by players using the glassblowing section of the Crafting skill or by stealing from various chests in Dorgesh-Kaan. The wire must then be added to the empty light orb to create a filament, allowing the light orb to function in a similar fashion to a light bulb, which grants the player 104 Crafting experience. The completed orb can then be used to replace broken sections of the magical Dorgeshuun lighting system.

Cave goblin wire is needed to make a light orb to complete a Sherlock 's master clue step, and the resulting light orb is used to complete an elite clue step.

Cave goblin wire can be obtained three ways, all of which are through the use of the Thieving skill. Completing the elite Lumbridge diary will double how much cave goblin wire is received.

10998:
