The actual item cannot be obtained by players.
10999: The goblin book is an item that is an uncommon drop from goblins . After completing the Another Slice of H.A.M. quest , members can re-obtain it from the bookcase in their player-owned houses , under the name The Book of the Big High War God .
11001:
Dagon'hai history (also known as The Fall of the Dagon'hai or History of the Dagon'hai ) is a book found in the Varrock library. It can be found in the north-east corner of the room (the two bookcases placed south, with the book in the western bookcase). It tells of the fall of the Dagon'hai and is used in the quest What Lies Below . After the quest it can also be found in a bookcase in a player-owned house .

After What Lies Below , the player can take this book to Historian Minas on the 1 st floor [ UK ] 2 nd floor [ US ] of the Varrock Museum to receive 5 kudos .
11002:
Sin'keth's diary is a quest item used only in What Lies Below quest. It is obtained from Surok Magis along with the wand. It is diary of the former leader of the Dagon'hai and shows the place of the Tunnel of Chaos. The examine text implies that Surok is a descendant or relative of the diary's owner.

After completing the quest, players can find it in one of the bookcases in the north-east corner of the Varrock Palace library.
11003:
An empty folder is a quest item used only in What Lies Below . It is given to the player by Rat Burgiss to store the paperwork that he asks the player to recover from outlaws in their camp west of Varrock palace.

As you add Rat's papers to it, it will become a used folder . When all five papers are added, it becomes a full folder .

When handing in the full folder to Rat, any excess papers are also removed from the player's inventory.
11006: A used folder is an item used in the What Lies Below quest . It is obtained by filling an empty folder with Rat's papers , which are dropped by Outlaws . Once the folder is filled with 5 papers, it becomes a full folder .
11007:
A full folder is a quest item used only in What Lies Below quest . It contains 5 of Rat's pages , which are obtained by killing Outlaws . It is obtained from Rat Burgiss at the start of the quest as an empty folder . As pages are added to the empty folder, it first becomes a used folder and when 5 pages are added it becomes a full folder.

When handing in the full folder to Rat, any excess papers are also removed from the player's inventory.
11008:
Rat's paper is a quest item used only during the quest What Lies Below. The player obtains the paper by killing outlaws in the camp west of Varrock and east of Edgeville. Once the player has obtained five papers they can be put in the empty folder given by Rat Burgiss to create a full folder.

When the player chooses the Read Rat's paper option, it reads: The piece of paper appears to contain lots of facts and figures. They look like accounts and lists of items. You're not sure what they all mean.

When handing in the full folder to Rat, any excess papers are also removed from the player's inventory.
11009: The letter to Surok is an item used in the What Lies Below quest. It is obtained from Rat Burgiss after he is given the full folder . The letter must be delivered to Surok Magis . The letter is written in a hard to read font , though the message is in English.
11010: Surok's letter is a quest item used in the What Lies Below quest. It is obtained from Surok Magis after the infused wand and a bowl are given to him. It must be delivered to Rat Burgiss.
11011:
Zaff's instructions is a members-only quest item used only in What Lies Below. It is obtained from Zaff, and gives instructions for using the beacon ring. It serves no purposes other than to inform players about how to operate the beacon ring.

Simply click 'Operate' (either when it is worn or in your inventory), and Zaff will come by to stop Surok Magis once King Roald has no Health in his bar ('red barred'). If you use it before you are supposed to in the quest you will get a message saying "You shouldn't call Zaff until you need to" and will not be allowed to use it again until you need to. If you lose them, you can go back to Zaff to get them back.
11012: The wand is a members-only quest item used only in What Lies Below quest. It is obtained from Surok Magis along with Sin'keth's diary. It must be infused with 15 chaos runes at Chaos Altar to turn it into infused wand. Then it must be returned to Surok Magis.
11013: The infused wand is an item used during What Lies Below. It is obtained by infusing the normal wand at the Chaos Altar with 15 chaos runes. The infused wand is then given to Surok Magis to progress in the quest.
11014:
A beacon ring is a ring used in the What Lies Below Quest . It is obtained from Zaff and is used to summon him during the quest. After the quest, the ring can no longer summon Zaff and the Operate option becomes unuseable; attempting the option results in the message Zaff has removed the summon charges from the ring. It will not summon him again.

Players can regain this ring for free from Zaff if they lose it, making it a free alternative to the Seers' ring , albeit with a much lower magic attack stat. The ring is similar in stats to the Lunar ring , but has 1 less Magic defence. It can also be re-purchased from Perdu for 6,000 coins.

Chicken feet are an untradeable cosmetic item. It is part of the chicken outfit , which can be obtained by completing one of the Easter holiday events that occur once per year. This also rewards the player with all other holiday items associated with Easter.

If the "Flap" emote has been unlocked from the Stronghold of Security , when wearing all the pieces of the set, players can do an enhanced "Flap" emote where their character lifts off the ground slightly as if flying.

Previously, they were obtainable during the 2013 Rare Drops event (from 19 August to 26 August ) as part of a rare item drop .

If destroyed, a replacement can be obtained from Diango in Draynor Village or from the toy box of a costume room , as part of the 2007: Chicken Suit set. Ultimate Ironmen will be unable to retrieve individual pieces until the full set is stored.

11023: The Magic egg was an item obtained during the 2013 Easter event . When eaten, the message Mmm...yummy. would be displayed in chat, and it turned the player into a rabbit for a brief period of time, or for longer if near the entrance to Nigel 's farm. If a player had not already learned the "Bunny-hop" emote , they would learn it upon eating this item.
11024: The Rabbit mould was an item used in 2013 Easter event. It was obtained from part of the rabbit hole where players can only enter after completing the first part of the event. It was given to Easter Bunny to claim rest of the reward.

Chocolate chunks were used in the 2013 Easter event . They could be obtained by smashing chocolate kebbits and were given to the Easter Bunny for part of the reward. To smash them, the player used the Easter eggs on it by bowling them.

They are non-tradeable and may not be banked - if a player attempts to deposit some in a bank , the message "A magical force prevents you from banking this item!" appears in the chat window .

After the event ended, all chocolate chunks turned into chocolate dust .
11026:
Chocolate kebbits were an item obtained during the 2013 Easter event . Players had to "Grab" these enchanted kebbits from the ground as they hopped around in a rabbit hole.

When 10 chocolate kebbits were placed in the kebbit chute, they could be crushed into chocolate chunks using eggs in the bowling room.

It has an "Eat" option, but cannot be eaten and instead gives the message "I'm not going to eat that! It's wiggling.". It is also stackable, and if the player chooses to drop it, one kebbit would be let loose on the ground and run away (even through walls, in some cases). If you tried to drop it outside of the rabbit hole, a message would appear stating "The chocolate kebbit refuses to budge from your pack."

11031: Damp planks are quest items from Olaf's Quest , obtained from Olaf Hradson . During the quest, they are used on the embers beside Olaf with a tinderbox to light it, giving Olaf some place to warm up. Besides this, they have no other use.
11032: The crude carving is a quest item used during Olaf's Quest. It is made by Olaf Hradson when the player presents him with some windswept logs from the windswept tree near where Olaf is. 11034:
Sven's last map is a quest item from Olaf's Quest. It shows the location of Brine Rat Cavern, which players can only access by digging at the X with a spade. The spot is next to the tree on the mountain.

Olaf Hradson gives you this map. It belonged to his grandfather, Sven the Helmsman. The map is not required to enter the Brine Rat Cavern after the quest and may be safely discarded.
11035: Windswept logs are quest items in Olaf's Quest obtained by using an axe on the windswept tree east of Olaf Hradson. Attempting to light them with a tinderbox gives the message: "These are for Olaf, so I shouldn't burn them."
11036:
The parchment is a reward for completing Olaf's Quest . It is obtained by searching the chest at the end of the quest, and tells of additional treasure ships that sank in the area, however this additional treasure is currently unavailable.

The first time you read it, the following messages are displayed in the chatbox: The scroll tells you that there were more ships washed up, further out to sea. Better yet, they were apparently carrying the better part of the treasure!

It is likely that the parchment will play a role in the upcoming sequel quest The Graveyard .
11037:
The brine sabre is a one-handed weapon that requires 40 Attack to wield. It is dropped by brine rats in the small cave accessed during Olaf's Quest. The brine sabre is a slightly better alternative to a rune scimitar, boasting 2 higher strength and slash attack bonuses when compared to the former. However, it is significantly more expensive due to the fact it is only dropped by the rarely-killed brine rat at a low rate.

Brine sabres can finish off rockslugs without the use of a bag of salt. It is also one of the few weapons that can be used to kill lobstrosities.

Attempting to Telekinetic Grab the key whilst in the dungeon will fail, with a message claiming the salty air interferes with the spell.

The Rotten barrel is an unobtainable item found in the Brine Rat Cavern .

The item has a "Take" option, however this will give a regular Rotten barrel instead, and the item will not despawn. Therefore, it serves as an infinite source of rotten barrels for players.

Players cannot pick up the rotten barrel with Telekinetic grab , as a message states "Oh dear, it looks like the salt air is interfering with the spell."
11045: Rotten barrels are found in the Brine Rat Cavern near Rellekka . The player uses two of these with six ropes to build a makeshift bridge to cross the river during Olaf's Quest .
11046:

The item has a "Take" option - however, this will give the standard rope instead, and the item will not despawn. Therefore, it is designed to serve as an infinite source of rope. 11048:
The armour shard is a quest item used during the Another Slice of H.A.M. quest. It is one of the six artefacts obtained during the first stage of the quest by digging in the unfinished train tunnel in Dorgesh-Kaan using a trowel.

When the artefacts are cleaned using a specimen brush, one of them will turn into the armour shard. This must be given to Tegdak the goblin along with the other cleaned artefacts (a shield fragment, a helmet fragment, a sword fragment, and an ancient mace).

Players cannot cast alchemy spells on them. If a player attempts to do so, the chatbox will state "This ancient artefact resists your magic."

The artefacts can be cleaned by using a specimen brush and will then turn into one of the following items: a shield fragment, a helmet fragment, an axe head, a sword fragment, an ancient mace or an armour shard. These items must be given to Tegdak the goblin.

Players cannot cast alchemy spells on them. If a player attempts to do so, the chatbox will state "This ancient artefact resists your magic."

The goblin village sphere sphere teleports the player to a random location within the Goblin Village. They can be purchased and used upon completion of the Another Slice of H.A.M. quest, and are identical in appearance to plain of mud spheres. The sphere is consumed upon use and does not work beyond level 20 Wilderness.

Oldak, the cave goblin professor, will construct these spheres for the player if they provide him with 2 law runes and 1 molten glass (which can be noted).

Unlike Dorgesh-kaan spheres, they cannot be thieved from Oldak's chest.
11061:
The ancient mace is a weapon that can be acquired during the Another Slice of H.A.M. quest, when the player helps the Dorgeshuun archaeology team uncover ancient artefacts in the train tunnel from the Third Age . It's found that the mace was bestowed to Bandos ' strongest goblin warriors during the God Wars to siphon favour of their enemies' god from their users. [ 1 ] Although tradeable, it cannot be wielded until after a certain point in the quest; attempting to do so results in the message, You must have received that mace in Another Slice of H.A.M to wield it.

The ancient mace has stats in between those of a black mace and mithril mace (but with a 1 tick slower attack speed) and requires level 15 Attack and level 25 Prayer to wield. In addition, it can be equipped for protection against the Bandosian followers in the God Wars Dungeon .

If lost during the quest, it can be retrieved from General Bentnoze and General Wartface for 1,000 coins . After the quest, it can be retrieved from Tegdak for 1,000 coins, north-east of the Dorgesh-Kaan marketplace.
11062:
Zanik is an unobtainable item that may be placed into the player's inventory when Zanik is following the player during Death to the Dorgeshuun, Another Slice of H.A.M., and Land of the Goblins. Zanik technically functions as a pet during these quests, although the item version is never meant to be seen.

Three different versions exist in Death to the Dorgeshuun. Aside from the default variant, there are versions for when Zanik is wearing H.A.M. robes, and during the final showdown when she equips a Dorgeshuun crossbow. A fourth variant was added with Another Slice of H.A.M.

This item only exists as every follower NPC is required to be tied to an item. If the items are ever obtained however, dropping them will just cause the item to appear on the floor, rather than causing the pet to reappear.
11065: A bracelet mould allows a player to make bracelets through the Crafting skill out of silver bars, gold bars, and possibly gems by using them on a furnace. A minimum Crafting level of 7 is needed to make bracelets. It can be obtained at the Crafting Guild and some crafting stores. It can also be obtained in your house if you have a tool store 4 in your workshop.
11067: The Black bracelet is an interface item. It can be seen in the interface for crafting jewellery. If the player does not have the correct gem to craft a bracelet, the black bracelet appears in its place as a greyed out version.
11069:
The Gold bracelet is made by using a gold bar on a furnace . It requires a Crafting level of 7 and gives 25 experience when made. It offers no combat bonuses when worn.

It is commonly used as a High Alchemy item because it is very cheap and very easy to make. Due to the high price of gold ore , players who want to buy materials to make these are advised to buy gold bars directly rather than purchasing gold ore and smelting their own bars.
11072:
The sapphire bracelet is made by using a gold bar, a sapphire and a bracelet mould on a furnace. It requires a Crafting level of 23 and gives 60 experience when made. It offers no combat bonuses when worn.

Players can convert this item into a bracelet of clay by casting the spell Lvl-1 Enchant on it, requiring level 7 Magic and grants 17.5 Magic experience.
11074:
A bracelet of clay allows players to mine soft clay instead of hard clay. It is made by enchanting a sapphire bracelet with the Lvl-1 Enchant spell.

A single bracelet can mine 28 soft clay, after which it disintegrates. The player can check how many more soft clay it can mine by equipping it and then right-clicking "check." The number of charges is stored per player, not per bracelet, so equipping another bracelet will not reset the number of charges a player has.

The bracelet can be useful for making magic tablets in a player-owned house, as the Rimmington and Hosidius mines both contain clay and are very close to a house portal.

When mining soft clay rocks in the Trahaearn mine, the bracelet of clay allows players to mine two soft clay at once.
11076:
An emerald bracelet is made by using a gold bar , an emerald , and a bracelet mould on a furnace . It requires level 30 Crafting and provides 65 Crafting experience when made. It offers no combat bonuses when worn.

An emerald bracelet can be enchanted into a Castle wars bracelet using the Lvl-2 Enchant spell by players with level 27 Magic , granting 37 experience.
11079:
A Castle Wars bracelet is a bracelet that aids the player in Castle Wars . It is obtained by casting Lvl-2 Enchant on an emerald bracelet .

When players are wielding this item at the moment they enter the game, they do an extra 20% damage against a bearer of a flag and bandages heal 50% more. Players only need to be wearing it up until the time the game starts. After that, the charge is already given, and the player can switch to any item to be worn in the hand slot . Players instead may opt to give bracelets to Lanthus to have a charge used automatically when a game is started without needing to wear one at all.

The bracelet can have a maximum of 3 charges. Each game will use up one charge, and after all charges are gone it will be destroyed. The number of charges remaining is displayed in brackets in the item name.

Members can enchant the ruby bracelet into an inoculation bracelet by casting Lvl-3 Enchant on it. Doing so requires level 49 Magic and grants 59 Magic experience.
11088:
An inoculation bracelet is a ruby bracelet enchanted using the Lvl-3 Enchant spell. Wearing the bracelet requires completion of Zogre Flesh Eaters, otherwise the player will receive the message You need to have completed the Zogre Flesh Eaters quest to wear a bracelet of inoculation.

When equipped, it protects the wearer from a total of 275 disease damage. This includes the negative stat bonus "damage." Players still get diseased, but it reduces the damage normally taken from the disease to 0. It degrades to dust once its protection has been depleted. It may also be right-click checked while worn to find out how many more points of disease damage protection it will provide.

This bracelet is quite useful in combination with Relicym's balm when killing Skogres and Zogres, as well as for the Trouble Brewing minigame. The bracelet can also be useful when fighting the Maggot King, allowing the player to avoid damage from the disease pools it drops.
11090:
Phoenix necklaces are necklaces that automatically restore the wearer's Hitpoints by 30% of maximum if they drop to 20% of the maximum or below. They only have one use, after which they are destroyed.

In addition to restoring health, the phoenix necklace also clears out any pending attacks on the player from the attack buffer. This negates any pending damage from delayed attacks such as spells and arrows from afar. This also notably works on certain multi-hit special attacks , such as those from dragon claws and dark bows , where if one of the multi-hits triggers the effect, it will cancel the damage from subsequent multi-hits. The phoenix necklace is often brought in PvP as a gear switch to counter these special attacks finishers.

If the user's hitpoints drop below 10% in one hit after being above 20%, and the player is also wearing a ring of life , then the phoenix necklace is activated first. Self-inflicted damage such as guzzling a dwarven rock cake will also cause it to activate.

Players can make one by enchanting a diamond necklace with the Lvl-4 Enchant spell. This requires level 57 Magic , 10 earth runes , and 1 cosmic rune and grants 67 Magic experience.

In legacy duels within Emir's Arena and in Tombs of Amascut the phoenix necklace is considered food . Therefore, it will produce no effect if the "No Food" option is toggled during a duel or if the “On a Diet” invocation is active. Phoenix necklaces cannot be used in Bounty Hunter .

It can be enchanted at level 68 Magic into a combat bracelet.
11118:
The combat bracelet is a dragonstone bracelet that has been enchanted by the Lvl-5 Enchant spell.

A combat bracelet can be recharged at the totem pole in the Legends' Guild , or at the Fountain of Uhld in the Myths' Guild , or by casting Recharge Dragonstone , giving it four charges. Players who have completed Legends' Quest can also recharge it at the Fountain of Rune , giving it six charges.

The bracelet provides useful teleports to combat-related guilds . The bracelet also informs its wearer of their current Slayer task count every 10 kills (i.e. "You still need to kill x0 monsters to complete your current Slayer assignment"). This feature only works if the bracelet is charged.

Like other dragonstone jewellery, it is one of the few items whose teleports will work up to level 30 Wilderness, while most other means of teleportation will not work above level 20 Wilderness.

The bracelet also provides combat bonuses comparable to those of mithril gloves from the Culinaromancer's Chest . Compared to mithril gloves, the bracelet has +1 attack bonuses and -1 defensive bonuses in all attack styles except magic .

The berserker necklace is an onyx necklace enchanted by the Lvl-6 Enchant spell. When worn, it increases the amount of damage the wearer does when wielding an obsidian melee weapon (Toktz-xil-ak, Tzhaar-ket-om, Tzhaar-ket-em, or Toktz-xil-ek) by 20%. However, in exchange it lowers the wearer's melee accuracy and the player's defences against all combat styles. This bonus stacks with the bonus provided from wearing the Obsidian armour set (helmet, platebody, and platelegs). It also stacks with slayer helmet and Void Knight equipment.

Players can attach a Berserker necklace ornament kit, obtained from hard Treasure Trails, to create a Berserker necklace (or). This is only cosmetic, and does not affect the necklace's stat bonuses. It can be dismantled, returning the necklace and ornament kit.
11130:
The onyx bracelet is made by using a gold bar, an onyx, and a bracelet mould on a furnace a with Crafting level of 84, earning 125 experience. It is the bracelet of the second highest gem quality in the game, behind zenyte.

The bracelet has no bonuses of any kind until enchanted. If it is enchanted using the level 87 spell Lvl-6 Enchant (earning 97 Magic experience), it becomes a regen bracelet, which adds combat bonuses and doubles the natural restoration of Hitpoints.
11133:
The regen bracelet is an enchanted bracelet that is worn in the hand slot . It is created by casting Lvl-6 Enchant on an onyx bracelet , requiring level 87 Magic and granting 97 Magic experience .

When worn, it doubles the player's natural Hitpoints regeneration amount, healing 2 Hitpoints per minute instead of the standard 1 Hitpoint per minute. The effect of the regen bracelet stacks with either the Rapid Heal prayer or with the Hitpoints cape (which do not stack with each other); using either of these in conjunction with a regen bracelet effectively quadruples the natural rate of Hitpoint regeneration, increasing it to 2 Hitpoints per 30 seconds. This is a very helpful perk during activities that deal low amounts of continuous damage, reducing the need to bank frequently or rely on outside sources of healing. Examples of activities where it is helpful include fighting weak but accurate NPCs , doing Pyramid Plunder , subduing the Wintertodt (doubles warmth regeneration), chopping Sulliusceps , mining in the Volcanic Mine , or fighting Zalcano .

In addition, the offensive and defensive bonuses provided by the bracelet are better than those of the combat bracelet and mithril gloves . This, combined with the fact that it has no requirements to equip, makes it the best-in-slot melee hand slot item for players with 1 Defence .

The easy lamp grants 1,000 experience in a skill of the player's choosing with no level requirement.

The medium lamp grants 5,000 experience in a skill of the player's choosing, given that the skill is over level 30.

The hard lamp grants 10,000 experience in a skill of the player's choosing, given that the skill is over level 40.

Completing the elite Karamja diary gives the regular elite Antique lamp.

11151:
The dream vial is obtained in the Dream Mentor and Dragon Slayer II quests. The Oneiromancer gives the player an empty Dream vial.

To make the potion, the player fills the Dream vial (empty) with water to create a Dream vial (water) - The easiest way to fill the vial after obtaining it is in the house south-west of the bank on Lunar Isle . Next, add a Goutweed (either grown through Farming or stolen at the Troll Stronghold ) to create a Dream vial (herb). Finally add ground astral rune (use a hammer on an astral rune , then crush the shards into dust with a pestle and mortar ) to make the Potion of Shared Dreaming .

With the potion, the player can travel to a Dream World in Dream Mentor or Dragon Slayer II, and sort out either Cyrisus's fear of combat in Dream Mentor, or Bob's past in Dragon Slayer II, where the player faces high-levelled monsters representing the respective quests' issues.

Warning: The dream vial is lost upon death and you will need to acquire a new one.

11154:
The dream potion is used in both the Dream Mentor and Dragon Slayer II quests. The Oneiromancer tells the player that the potion will send them to the Dream World to attempt to combat either Cyrisus ' fears, or Bob the cat 's past. The potion puts the player in the NPC's dream and binds the two subconsciouses together.

With the two minds melded as one, the Oneiromancer says both characters need each other to survive. If one dies, both die, "just as if you were killed by a monster in the wild", the Oneiromancer cautions.

During the Dream Mentor quest, you give the Dream potion to Cyrisus, who puts it on the brazier used in the Lunar Diplomacy quest. You then light the burner and are transported to Cyrisus's dream, where you have to conquer his fear of combat by fighting four monsters: The Inadequacy , The Everlasting , The Untouchable and The Illusive .

During Dragon Slayer II quest, you must first light the brazier, then add the potion onto the flaming pyre. You will be in a different dream world, where you must defeat Robert the Strong in combat.

Warning : If you die while carrying the Dream potion, it is lost and you will need to create a new one.
11155: Ground astral rune is a quest item used in both the Dream Mentor and Dragon Slayer II quests to make a dream potion. It is created by using an astral rune on a hammer, and subsequently using the resulting astral rune shards on a pestle and mortar. The item has no use outside of these quests. This item is lost upon death.
11156: Astral rune shards are a quest item used in both the Dream Mentor and Dragon Slayer II quests. They are created by using an astral rune on a hammer in one's inventory. The shards can then be ground down to dust with a pestle and mortar to create ground astral rune , which is an ingredient for the shared dream potion needed in the quests.
11157:
The dreamy lamp is a reward for completing the Dream Mentor quest. It grants one wish of 15,000 experience to any of the following skills:

If destroyed, you can get another from the Oneiromancer on Lunar Isle. It can be banked.
11158:
Cyrisus's chest is an item used in Dream Mentor to carry Cyrisus's armour to him from the bank, to aid in restoring Cyrisus's Armament meter to 100%. It is obtained from 'Bird's-Eye' Jack who works at the Lunar Isle bank since the player has started the quest and has gotten Cyrisus on his feet.

Much like Cyrisus's bank, the items inside the chest cannot be obtained in any way by opening or destroying it.

If a player attempts to cast alchemy spells on it, the chatbox will state You can't do that to the property of the bank.
11159: A Hunter kit is an item that is produced from casting the Lunar spell Hunter Kit . A single one-time Hunter kit can also be obtained from the Feldip Hills and Relleka hunting experts . It contains 8 items in total.
11164:
The Restored shield is an unobtainable item released with the rework of Shield of Arrav . Presumably it would have been formed by combining the two halves of the Broken shield , but this is impossible as the player can only ever have one.

It was replaced with the Shield of Arrav with the release of Defender of Varrock .
11165:
The Phoenix crossbows are two unobtainable items released with the rework of Shield of Arrav . They are identical to the regular Phoenix crossbow . Since the quest requires Black Arm Gang members to steal two phoenix crossbows, it is possible that these would have been quest-specific variants. Therefore, players would have been unable to complete this portion of the quest by simply buying phoenix crossbows from another player. However, they were ultimately never added.

The first crossbow can be seen on the quest's reward scroll.

11169: The Newspaper is an unobtainable item added with the graphical update of Varrock . It is identical to the Newspaper that can be bought from Benny in Varrock square. Internally, it is referred to as "Newspaper 1" as opposed to the obtainable "Newspaper 2". Presumably, it would have played some role in Shield of Arrav .
11171:
A newspaper is a readable item that tells about the different going-ons in and around Varrock at that time. Players can purchase an issue for 50 coins from Benny in Varrock Square . Benny's shouts reveal that it is called the Varrock Herald. Buying a newspaper is required for the Easy Varrock Diary .

This item cannot be traded on the Grand Exchange .
11173:
Half certificates are used during the Shield of Arrav quest . When a player returns their half of the Shield to Curator Haig Halen of the Varrock Museum , they will receive one half of the certificate, depending on whether they joined the Phoenix Gang or the Black Arm Gang . There are two different certificate halves. Once combined, one can not trade the full certificate . The full certificate must be given to King Roald to complete the Shield of Arrav quest.

The player who joined the Phoenix Gang will receive 2 left halves, and the player who joined the Black Arm Gang will receive 2 right halves.

11175:
An uncleaned find is a rock obtained in the Varrock Museum specimen cleaning activity. The specimens are obtainable from the rock piles within the activity. Players need to use it on a specimen table to reveal the archaeological artefact inside (see the list below). The cleaning activity can be done after finishing The Dig Site quest.

Players can take part in the cleaning activity in the south fenced-off corner of the museum. The tools necessary to do so can be found on the tool rack hanging on the wall. Players can then show the artefact to one of the archaeologists in the room, who will then tell them what to do with the item. Certain items are eligible for being displayed in the display cases. Other items can be put in the storage crates. On average, this results in 3-5 antique lamps per hour, depending on your efficiency.

Note: To keep copies of any items that can be turned in, the drop trick must be used. Handing them in removes any duplicates from the player's inventory and bank, and are unobtainable after being handed in.
11176:
Arrowheads are an item that players can find by cleaning an uncleaned find as part of the Varrock Museum activity. Unlike arrowtips, players cannot add them to headless arrows to make arrows. The arrowheads have no use, but you can put them in the crate by the southernmost door for a small reward, like a pot, or a bowl.

They are made of crude bronze and are extremely old, likely being from the Third Age. They were used by the Zarosians of Senntisten.

Often, players new to the Varrock museum misinterpret the arrowheads to be arrowtips, which members may use in Fletching. However, when they try to connect the arrowheads with headless arrows, nothing interesting happens.
11177:
Jewellery is an item that players can randomly obtain by cleaning an uncleaned find at the Varrock Museum. Players cannot wear this jewellery, and it has no use outside the Varrock Museum minigame.

The jewellery appears to include a gold holy symbol, which players can only make from silver. The jewellery also includes a gold tiara, a gold ring, and a strung gold amulet. Because it includes a Saradominist symbol, it is believed to be from the ruins of Saranthium as opposed to Senntisten, which was earlier and of Zarosian religion.

When players find this item, the message they see includes the word "jewelry", which is the American spelling of the word "jewellery". This goes against Jagex's usual policy of using British spellings.

It may be shown to one of the six archaeologists in the room to receive 5 coins, after which the player comments: "Must have been worth a lot in his days!"

Players might prefer to put it in the storage crate instead for a random reward, usually worth more than 5 coins.
11178:
Pottery is obtained in the Varrock Museum activity when cleaning Uncleaned finds . According to the archaeologists in the cleaning area, the pottery was made by Zaros worshippers. They say the pottery reinforces the evidence that Varrock was occupied by Zarosians before Saradominists .

The player places the pottery in display case 22 (which is directly in front of the stairs that go to the basement) to be rewarded with 10 kudos . Note that this display case is already occupied with other pottery instead of a note card. Unlike the other 4 finds, this one is not accompanied by a chatbox notification and can be deposited in the storage crates without warning.

The text accompanying the exhibit in the museum reads as follows:
11179:
The old coin is obtained in the Varrock Museum activity when cleaning uncleaned finds. When a player returns the old coin to display case 45 (ground floor, southern-most row, second from the left. Directly to the north-east of the soil layers display), they are rewarded with 10 kudos. Because it has a symbol to Saradomin and writing mentioning Saranthium, it is believed to be from the ruins of Saranthium as opposed to Senntisten, which was earlier and of Zarosian religion.

Turning in the coin causes all copies to be removed from the player's inventory and bank, as well as no long appear when cleaning uncleaned finds. In order to keep a copy, the drop trick must be used.
11180:
The ancient coin is a coin with the symbol of Zamorak . Players may find this whilst working in the excavational area of the Varrock Museum by cleaning uncleaned finds . When a player returns it to display case 44 (ground floor, middle row, case to the west), they are rewarded with 10 kudos . It cannot be obtained after it is returned to its display case.

This coin is interesting because it is Zamorakian , from the time when the city was named Senntisten , before the Saradominists took over and renamed it Saranthium . This suggests that sometime during the God Wars followers of Zamorak controlled this city.

Turning in the coin causes all copies to be removed from the player's inventory and bank , as well as no long appear when cleaning uncleaned finds. In order to keep a copy, the drop trick must be used.
11181:
The ancient symbol is an old symbol of Saradomin . Players may find this whilst working in the excavational area of the Varrock Museum by cleaning uncleaned finds .

The ancient symbol looks like an eroded holy symbol without the string. Players cannot string this symbol with a ball of wool , and it has no use except as part of the miniquest .

Players should place it in display case 37 ( ground floor [ UK ] 1 st floor [ US ] ). Case 37 is located on the second row from the south in the centre of the row. Its information reads: "This small symbol was used as a decoration on the Saradominist altars throughout the city. Two or three examples have been found, but this is the best. Worked in blue-enamelled iron, it has not survived the ages well. We believe this to be from the early years when the city was still being built."

Because it is a symbol to Saradomin, it is believed to be from the ruins of Saranthium as opposed to Senntisten , which was an earlier settlement on the same location and of Zarosian religion.

Turning in the symbol causes all copies to be removed from the player's inventory and bank , as well as no long appear when cleaning uncleaned finds. In order to keep a copy, the drop trick must be used.
11182:
The old symbol is obtained from the Varrock Museum activity by cleaning uncleaned finds . Players can return it to display case 36 ( ground floor [ UK ] 1 st floor [ US ] , southern-most row, second from the east. Display is directly west of the Ancient Talisman display.) to be rewarded with 10 kudos . The symbol cannot be strung with a ball of wool , and it has no other use.

Turning in the symbol causes all copies to be removed from the player's inventory and bank , as well as the symbol no longer appearing when cleaning uncleaned finds. In order to keep a copy, the drop trick must be used.
11183:
An old chipped vase is an item that players may find whilst cleaning Uncleaned finds in the Varrock Museum (after completing The Dig Site).

It has no use, except in the Varrock Museum miniquest. It is a common find even then, and of little value to the archaeologists there. Because it has a symbol to Saradomin, it is believed to be from the ruins of Saranthium as opposed to Senntisten, which was earlier and of Zarosian religion. You need to put it in the storage crate as it has no use for your reward.
11184: The Museum map is a small map of the Varrock Museum . It can be obtained for free from the various larger maps hanging around the walls in the museum and the information booth on the ground floor [ UK ] 1 st floor [ US ] .

Infinite can be obtained as a possible reward from cleaning: 500xp in a skill of at least 10.

Three from giving information about the quests Making History, Merlin's Crystal, and Shield of Arrav: 1,000xp in a skill of at least level 20.

Giving information about the Defender of Varrock awards one antique lamp granting 5,000xp in a skill of at least 30.

Giving information about the Curse of the Empty Lord awards one antique lamp granting 10,000xp in a skill of at least 50.

11190:
A digsite pendant is a ruby necklace that has been enchanted using the Lvl-3 Enchant spell. It requires completion of The Dig Site quest and the spell learnt from one of the archaeologists in Varrock Museum to make or use. Digsite pendants cannot be recharged and crumble to dust when all charges have been used.

Unlike most gold jewellery , this necklace cannot be enchanted until the spell has been learnt from one of the archaeologists cleaning finds at the Varrock Museum . To learn how to enchant a ruby necklace, a player must first participate in the museum's specimen cleaning activity (located on the ground floor [ UK ] 1 st floor [ US ] floor of the museum) until a clean necklace is discovered from the uncleaned finds ; the chance of this is 1/51. Giving the clean necklace to any of the archaeologists in the Varrock museum’s cleaning area will prompt them to teach the player how to replicate the enchantment spell, which requires either 49 Magic or an enchant ruby or topaz tablet.

When enchanted, the pendant can be used to teleport to the north of the Digsite , west of the canal barge . The number of charges on an individual pendant is suffixed to the item's name. For example, an unused pendant is named "Digsite pendant (5)". When all five teleports have been used, the pendant will crumble away. Players can cast an alchemy spell on it when only 1 charge is left to minimise costs.

Once the quest Bone Voyage has been completed, a pendant of any amount of charges can be used on the southern strange machine (the one displaying a book with symbols) at the House on the Hill , north of the Museum Camp in Fossil Island . This gives the player an extra teleport option to the House on the Hill when using any digsite pendant. Once Dragon Slayer II has been completed, a teleport to Lithkren can be unlocked by using a digsite pendant on the strange machinery north of the rune dragons . Each teleport option can be unbound by using a pendant on the machine again.

At 82 Construction , a curator's medallion can be mounted in a player-owned house portal nexus room, creating a mounted digsite pendant . The mounted version of the pendant will allow unlimited teleports to the same locations as the normal unmounted version.

11195:
A clean necklace is obtained by cleaning uncleaned finds at the specimen table in the Varrock Museum , requiring completion of The Dig Site quest . Its drop rate is 1/51. [ 1 ] The necklace may be worn and it is identical to a ruby necklace when worn.

Obtaining it requires quickly clicking specimen rocks to get uncleaned finds, cleaning them, then dropping everything for more uncleaned finds unless the player needs kudos or rarely an antique lamp yielding 500 experience .

Once found, when talking to one of the archaeologists in the area the player will learn how to enchant ruby necklaces to make Digsite pendants .

Note: The clean necklace (including duplicates obtained via drop trick ) will be removed from the player's inventory and bank and afterwards will become unobtainable. In order to keep a duplicate, the player should drop one of the necklaces and turn the other one in.

To check if the clean necklace has been found already, cast Lvl-3 Enchant or use an enchant ruby or topaz tablet on a ruby necklace. Attempting to enchant a ruby necklace before learning about the clean necklace results in the game message: "You have not yet discovered the secret to enchanting ruby necklaces."
11196: The griffin feather is a quest item obtained during the Grim Tales quest. The player must steal it from Grimgnash , the griffin that lives on the east side of White Wolf Mountain . In order to obtain the feather, the player has to first send Grimgnash to sleep with a most horrid bedtime story. The feather must then be taken to Sylas in Taverley along with Rupert's helmet in order to exchange them for some magic beans .
11197: Miazrqa's pendant was given to her by her mother and is of great sentimental value to Miazrqa . The player is asked to retrieve the pendant from a mouse which stole it from her at the witch's house in Taverley . To claim it back the player must first shrink themselves with a shrink-me-quick potion in order to be able to follow the mouse down its hole, and find the pendant on the ground inside. In return for getting the pendant back, Miazrqa will release Rupert from the tower he is being held captive in.
11198:
The music sheet is a quest item used during the Grim Tales quest. It is obtained by searching the music stand in the witch's house basement in Taverley, after passing an electrified gate while wearing leather gloves. The sheet shows how to play the piano in a special combination that will open a secret compartment in the piano to reveal a shrinking recipe, a to-do list and 2 shrunk ogleroots.

If lost, players may climb up the ladder and re-enter the basement to retrieve another music sheet.
11199:
Rupert's helmet is an item obtained during Grim Tales. The helmet is owned by Rupert the Beard, who will provide it after being freed from the tower. The helmet must then be taken to Sylas in Taverley along with a griffin feather in order to exchange them for some magic beans.

After the quest, an equipable version called the dwarven helmet is given as a reward.
11200:
The dwarven helmet is obtained as a reward for completing the quest Grim Tales . A Defence level of 50, as well as completion of the quest Grim Tales , is required in order to wear the dwarven helmet.

The dwarven helmet has similar stats to a rune full helm , though it is worth noting that it has a +6 crush attack bonus, making it the third highest for crush attack bonus after the zombie helmet and Inquisitor's great helm . It is also unusual for being a melee helmet with a magic defence bonus.

Additional helmets can be obtained by talking to Rupert the Beard beside Miazrqa 's tower, where he was kept prisoner during Grim Tales (between Goblin Village and Ice Mountain ), and paying him 60,000 coins. Alternatively, Perdu will return the helmet to players for 115,000 coins.

It is somewhat popular to wear when fighting Vet'ion , Sarachnis , and The Nightmare , due to its cheap cost and crush attack bonus.

Equipping the helmet inside the Dwarven Mine is a requirement for the hard Falador Diary .
11202:
The shrinking recipe is a quest item used during the Grim Tales quest. It is obtained by playing a special tune on the piano in the basement of the witch's house in Taverley. Playing the correct tune reveals a secret compartment in the piano which contains the recipe, a to-do list and 2 shrunk ogleroot.

The recipe requires a tarromin to be added to a vial of water followed by a shrunk ogleroot to make a shrink-me-quick potion. The potion can then be consumed by the player to allow them to enter a mouse hole in the witch's house to retrieve Miazrqa's pendant from a mouse that stole it from Miazrqa.
11203: The to-do list is a quest item obtained during the Grim Tales quest. It is obtained by playing the tune written on a music sheet on the piano in the basement of the witch's house in Taverley . Playing the correct tune reveals a secret compartment in the piano which contains a shrinking recipe , the to-do list and 2 shrunk ogleroots .
11204:
The shrink-me-quick is a quest item used during the Grim Tales quest. It is created by adding a tarromin to a vial of water, and then adding a shrunk ogleroot. The potion can then be drunk by the player in order to go through a mouse hole in the witch's house in Taverley in order to recover Miazrqa's pendant from a mouse that stole it. The potion can still be made and used after completion of the quest.

The potion is made through the Herblore skill, and requires a level of 52, and gives 6 experience when made. Players may use boosts such as Greenman's Ale.
11205:
Shrunk ogleroot can be found in the witch's house in Taverley by playing the piano, as part of the Grim Tales quest, or as a drop from an Experiment No.2 down the manhole near the entrance to the witch's house. Although they have an "Eat" option, shrunk ogleroots may not be eaten, attempting to do so will result in the message "You attempt to take a bite out of the ogleroot. It tastes vile and you immediately spit it out.".

This is the second ingredient of shrink-me-quick potion used during Grim Tales quest.
11210:
The golden goblin is a quest item used in the Grim Tales quest, acquired after killing a cloud giant named Glod found atop a giant beanstalk.

According to legend the statue was once a greedy goblin named Gubblebak who was overseeing the smelting of molten gold when his goblin workers mutinied on him. He tripped and fell into the vat of gold, and although he managed to escape he was still coated with the metal. He then jumped into a water trough, hardening the layer of gold and encasing him as the statue he is today.

The cloud giant, Glod, somehow managed to get the golden goblin and must be killed in order to get the goblin and bring it to Sylas in Taverley to complete Grim Tales.
11211:
Magic beans are a quest item used during the Grim Tales . They are given to the player by Sylas , an old man in Taverley who will exchange them for a griffin feather and Rupert's helmet . The beans can then be planted in a special farming patch in Taverley to grow a giant beanstalk. This patch has a nearby sign that when examined says that on the patch farming is prohibited.

The beans can't be planted with Barbarian farming [ confirmation needed ] , therefore needing the seed dibber for the beans to be planted.
11212:
Dragon arrows are the strongest type of non- seeking arrow in the game. They are only usable with the dark bow , twisted bow , venator bow , scorching bow , and the 3rd Age bow . As with most arrows , they can be poisoned .

They can be created through the Fletching skill at level 90 by using dragon arrowtips on headless arrows , granting 15 Fletching experience per arrow made. 15 arrows can be made at a time, giving 225 Fletching experience.

When used with a dark bow , dragon arrows will enhance its special attack .
11217:
Dragon fire arrows are dragon arrows wrapped in an oily cloth , which are then lit by using them on a tinderbox . They, along with any other fire arrow , are primarily used to pierce the guide rope in the Underground Pass to lower the bridge so that a player may walk across.

They have the same ranged strength as regular dragon arrows .

11230:
Dragon darts are a type of Ranged throwing weapons. Dragon darts require level 60 Ranged to wield. They can be obtained by using the Fletching skill, trading with another player, or via dragon implings . Dragon darts can be poisoned and can be wielded with a shield or god book for protection, or added into a toxic blowpipe .

To create dragon darts the player must have at least level 95 Fletching. Players must obtain dragon dart tips (these cannot be smithed ) and then attach feathers to the dart tips. 250 Fletching experience is given per set of dragon darts created.

Fletching some dragon darts while in the Bedabin Camp is required to complete the Elite Desert Diary .

11232:
Dragon dart tips are used in the making of dragon darts . At level 95 Fletching , they can be made into dragon darts by adding feathers . Fletching a set of 10 will provide 250 experience.

Making dragon darts is the fastest method of training Fletching, with rates approaching 2,250,000 experience per hour if the player is fast and attentive enough. However, due to their price and limited supply, this is usually nonviable for long-term training.

Dragon dart tips are required for the Elite Desert Diary .

11235:
The dark bow is a two-handed ranged weapon that requires level 60 in Ranged to wield. It can only be obtained as a drop from dark beasts and their superior variant, night beasts. With an attack speed of 9 (5.4 seconds), and 8 on rapid (4.8 seconds), this bow stands out as the slowest weapon in the game. It fires two arrows per attack which roll independent accuracy checks. It has the maximum possible attack range of 10, so the longrange attack style will not increase its attack range.

Assuming that the weapon is set to the rapid attack style, the dark bow has a firing time of 2.4 seconds per arrow, whereas a shortbow such as the magic shortbow (i) takes only 1.8. Because of this, the dark bow is only fairly popular for player killing. It has one of the highest max hits of any weapons in the game by means of special attack, along with the crystal halberd and dragon dagger, although the twisted bow and Dharok's greataxe can hit harder with regular attacks, and the dragon 2h sword and Dinh's bulwark are able to deal more total damage with their special attack.

By using a Dark bow imbue scroll, the player can empower the dark bow into a Dark bow (bh), improving the item's stats and special attack. However, you can only use the Dark bow (bh) specifically in Daimon's Crater.

Each arrow fired has an independent chance to be saved by an Ava's device, and the bow may also be fired with only one arrow equipped.
11237: Dragon arrowtips are arrowtips that are used to create dragon arrows at level 90 Fletching . Fletching a set of 15 dragon arrows yields 225 Fletching experience . Dragon Arrowtips can also be obtained by trading in Venator fangs .
11238:
A baby impling jar is the result of successfully catching a baby impling , while also having an empty impling jar . Baby impling jars are not that commonly looted because of the low value of the loot. Instead, the jar can be traded in singularly to Elnock Inquisitor for 3 empty impling jars. This allows the player to collect 3 more higher level implings for them to loot.

You can trade 3 of this jar, along with two young impling jars and one gourmet impling jar to Elnock for a vial of imp repellent .
11240:
The young impling jar is the result of successfully catching a Young impling, whilst also having an empty impling jar. Young impling jars are not that commonly looted because of the low value of the loot. Instead, the jar can be traded in singularly to Elnock Inquisitor for 3 empty impling jars. This allows the player to collect 3 more higher level implings for them to loot.

If a player catches an impling without an empty impling jar, they will automatically receive the loot instead.

You can trade two of this jar, along with three baby impling jars and one Gourmet impling jar to Elnock for a vial of Imp repellent.
11242:
A gourmet impling jar is the result of successfully catching a Gourmet impling , while also having an empty impling jar . It requires 28 Hunter to catch a gourmet impling.

This jar can be traded in singularly to Elnock Inquisitor for 3 empty impling jars.

One gourmet impling jar, along with three baby impling jars and two young impling jars , can be traded to Elnock for a vial of Imp repellent . Alternatively, three gourmet impling jars, along with two earth impling jars and one essence impling jar , can be traded for a magic butterfly net .
11244:
An earth impling jar is the result of successfully catching an Earth impling while having an empty impling jar . It requires 36 Hunter to catch an earth impling.

This jar can be traded in individually to Elnock Inquisitor for 3 empty impling jars.

Players can also trade Elnock two Earth impling jars along with three Gourmet impling jars and one Essence impling jar for a magic butterfly net .
11246:
An essence impling jar is the result of successfully catching an essence impling , while also having an empty impling jar . It requires 42 Hunter to catch an essence impling.

This jar can be traded in singularly to Elnock Inquisitor for 3 empty impling jars.

One essence impling jar of this jar, along with three gourmet impling jars and two earth impling jars , can be traded to Elnock for a magic butterfly net . Alternatively, players can trade three of this jar, two eclectic impling jars and one nature impling jar for a jar generator .
11248:
An eclectic impling jar is the result of successfully catching an eclectic impling in the Impetuous Impulses minigame .

This jar can be traded in singularly to Elnock Inquisitor for 3 empty impling jars, but this is not recommended due to its high value.

You can trade two of this jar, three essence impling jars and one nature impling jar for a jar generator .
11250:
The nature impling jar is the result of successfully catching a Nature impling , while also having an empty impling jar . A player needs level 58 Hunter to catch them.

This jar can be traded in singularly to Elnock Inquisitor for 3 empty impling jars, but this is not recommended due to its high value.

You can trade one of these jars as well as three essence impling jars and two eclectic impling jar for a jar generator .
11252:
A magpie impling jar is obtained as the result of successfully catching a Magpie impling , while also having an empty impling jar . A Hunter level of 65 is required to catch magpie implings.

This jar can be traded in singly to Elnock Inquisitor for 3 empty impling jars, but this is not recommended due to its high value.
11254:
A ninja impling jar is obtained as the result of successfully catching a Ninja impling, while also having an empty impling jar in your inventory. A Hunter level of 74 is required to catch ninja implings.

This jar can be traded in singularly to Elnock Inquisitor for 3 empty impling jars, but this is not recommended due to its high value.
11256:
The dragon impling jar is the result of successfully catching a dragon impling, requiring level 83 Hunter. The dragon impling is second only to the Lucky impling as the rarest and most difficult to catch impling in Impetuous Impulses.

As can be done with all impling jars, the dragon impling jar can be traded in singularly to Elnock Inquisitor for three empty impling jars. This is not recommended, due to the fact that dragon impling jars are worth vastly more than three empty jars.

The market value of dragon impling jars is considerably more than all but a few of the possible loot items from it, notably dragon darts or dragon dart tips. Their price is high due to the chance of said expensive items, the rarity of the dragon impling itself, as well as players opening dragon impling jars for elite clue scrolls. Clue hunters will buy implings in bulk for the ability to obtain clues faster than any other method in the game for a high cost. You can't take dragon impling jars onto Entrana, as looting them may give you weapons.
11258:
The jar generator can be obtained from Elnock Inquisitor , and can be used to create either butterfly jars or impling jars . Only one jar generator can be owned at a time, and the player must use up or destroy their current generator before obtaining another. Attempting to obtain another while the player has one will lead to the choice to recharge the currently-owned generator instead, which costs the same as buying a new one. It is always lost upon death.

In order to receive the generator, the player must trade Elnock:

The jar generator begins with 100% charge. 3% charge is consumed when creating impling jars, and 1% when creating butterfly jars. When a jar generator runs out of charge, it disappears. Jar generators are very useful because they can hold 33 impling jars and one butterfly jar, or 100 butterfly jars, in one inventory slot.
11259:
A magic butterfly net is an item used in the Hunter skill. 17 Hunter is required to access Puro-Puro to obtain it. Like the butterfly net , it can be wielded to capture implings , butterflies, moths , and bats throughout Gielinor and Puro-Puro , but with an increased capture chance of approximately 7.8% (20/256) . [ 1 ] [ 2 ] Catching an impling without an impling jar will automatically loot it, and catching a butterfly or moth without a butterfly jar will automatically release it (unless the player is in Puro-Puro ). A jar is required to keep them for later use.

Players can right-click this net to open the Impling Tracker , tracking the combined number of implings caught in both Puro-Puro and the surface world.

A magic butterfly net can be obtained by trading Elnock Inquisitor for the following impling jars (can be made or purchased from other players):

Warning: This item is always lost upon death and will need to be reobtained, unless it is stored in the huntsman's kit .
11260:
An impling jar is a butterfly jar treated with Imp Repellent. These jars are used to catch implings in both the Impetuous Impulses minigame and all over Gielinor. Impling jars cannot be used to catch butterflies. When opening a caught impling in a jar, the jar has a 10% chance of being destroyed.

Players can receive a one-time-only donation of 7 impling jars (as well as a butterfly net and impling scroll) from Elnock Inquisitor by asking him for some spare equipment.
11262:
Imp repellent is an undrinkable potion with two uses when capturing implings :

It is made by combining anchovy oil with marigolds , rosemary , nasturtiums , or any of the flowers grown from a mithril seed , such as assorted flowers . Elnock Inquisitor will exchange 3 baby impling jars , 2 young impling jars , and 1 gourmet impling jar for one imp repellent in Elnock's Exchange .
11264: Anchovy oil is made by using eight anchovy paste on an empty vial with a sieve in the inventory (using the items in any different order does not work). It is used to make imp repellent when combined with marigolds, rosemary, nasturtiums, or flowers grown from mithril seeds.
11266: Anchovy paste is made by crushing anchovies with a pestle and mortar. It is used to make anchovy oil, an ingredient in imp repellent, by using eight anchovy paste on an empty vial with a sieve in the inventory (in this specific order; using the items in any other order results in nothing interesting happening).
11273: The impling scroll is given to the player by Elnock Inquisitor to aid them in the Impetuous Impulses minigame. The scroll can only be used in Puro-Puro. When clicked, the scroll shows how many of each kind of implings one currently has captured (and in their possession).
11279: Elvarg's head is a quest item obtained during Dragon Slayer I. Players receive it when they defeat Elvarg and automatically decapitate her. The player does not need to deliver it to Oziach to complete the quest. If it is in the player's bank when they finish the quest it will disappear.
11280:
A cavalier mask is a black cavalier and a highwayman mask assembled together. To obtain one, take both items to Patchy on Mos Le'Harmless, who will charge 500 coins to assemble it and 600 coins to disassemble. The black cavalier and highwayman mask are received from hard and easy Treasure Trails, respectively.

This item can be stored in the treasure chest of a costume room, provided that the interface of the corresponding clue tier is opened before attempting to store the item. Alternatively, the item can be used on the opened treasure chest to insert it without viewing the interface.
11282:
A beret mask is a black beret and a mime mask assembled together. To obtain one, take both items to Patchy on Mos Le'Harmless , who will charge 500 coins to assemble it and 600 coins to disassemble. The mime mask is received from the mime random event and the black beret from easy Treasure Trails .

This item can be stored in the treasure chest of a costume room , provided that the interface of the corresponding clue tier is opened before attempting to store the item. Alternatively, the item can be used on the opened treasure chest to insert it without viewing the interface.
11283:
A dragonfire shield is an upgraded anti-dragon shield , and one of the best shields in the game behind the elysian spirit shield and Dinh's bulwark . Equipping it requires 75 Defence and having started Dragon Slayer I . It retains the same dragonfire protection as the anti-dragon shield and it also provides partial protection against the icy breath of wyverns , like the dragonfire ward , elemental shield , and mind shield .

When uncharged, it is tradeable and offers slightly more defensive bonuses than a mithril sq shield , however, each charge it gains increases melee defensive bonuses and the range defensive bonus by 1 for a total of +50 at maximum for those four defensive stats. To charge the shield, dragonfire needs to be absorbed from dragonfire or icy breath attacks while it is equipped. Bottled dragonbreath can also be used to charge the shield.

11286:
The draconic visage is a very rare item obtained from many high-levelled dragons , as well as Skeletal Wyverns . It was supposedly created by the Dragonkin as a way to channel dragonfire . [ 1 ]

Players with 90 Smithing (can be boosted) can combine an anti-dragon shield with a draconic visage at an anvil to create a dragonfire shield . Doing so grants 2,000 Smithing experience . If the player doesn't have the required Smithing level, they can take the draconic visage to Oziach in Edgeville , who will assist in creating the shield for a payment of 1,250,000 coins . Completion of the quest Dragon Slayer I is required for Oziach to make the shield.

The following dragons or wyverns do NOT drop the draconic visage: baby dragons , green dragons , blue dragons , red dragons , brutal green dragons , bronze dragons , revenant dragons , Fossil Island wyverns and quest bosses like Elvarg and Galvek . For a list of dragons that do drop the draconic visage, see the 'item sources' section.
11323:
The barbarian rod is a heavier version of the fishing rod used during the Fishing portion of Barbarian Training . When you start that portion of the training Otto Godblessed will let you take this fishing rod from underneath the bed in his cabin; if you lose or drop it, get another from the bed. It uses fishing bait , feathers , fish offcuts , roe , or caviar as bait. It is the only fishing rod capable of catching leaping trout , leaping salmon and leaping sturgeon , except for the equippable version, the Pearl Barbarian Rod . It can only be used in the fishing spots at Otto's Grotto , and Mount Quidamortem in the Kebos Lowlands . Since barbarian fishing gives marginal Strength and Agility experience with each catch, it is more efficient than other training methods such as fly fishing.

The equipable version of the barbarian rod, the pearl barbarian rod , can be bought with molch pearls from Alry the Angler .
11324:
Roe is a food and ingredient used in the Barbarian Herblore to make Barbarian mixes . It can be obtained by using a knife to cut open Leaping salmon and Leaping trout , which are caught through Barbarian fishing with the Barbarian rod . The chance of receiving roe will scale with Cooking level, and depends on which fish is being cut.

Roe can be used with the respective two dose potions to make Attack mix , Strength mix , Restore mix , Antipoison mix , and Relicym's mix . All other Barbarian mixes require caviar as the additional ingredient. Roe can also be eaten to restore 3 hitpoints or used as bait to catch more fish while Barbarian fishing.

Players training fishing can either deposit the roe at a nearby bank such as the Bank Chest at Barbarian Assault for later use, or use the roe along with the fish offcuts as baits for more Barbarian fishing. Roe is only used as bait when there are no other fishing bait types or offcuts in the inventory.
11326:
Caviar is a food and enhancing ingredient used in the Barbarian Herblore to make Barbarian mixes . Caviar can be used to mix with all potions, as opposed to roe , which cannot be used with potions from Energy and up. It can also be eaten on its own to heal 5 Hitpoints . It can be obtained when players cut open the leaping sturgeon , obtained through Barbarian Fishing , with a knife, granting 15 Cooking experience. The chance of receiving caviar from leaping sturgeon scales with Cooking level, with a 1/80 chance at level 1 Cooking, and a 100% chance at level 80.

Caviar can be used as bait while fishing at Baxtorian Falls and Mount Quidamortem , along with fish offcuts and roe, but only when there is no other usable bait in your inventory. Caviar cannot be mixed with any other ingredients with the Cooking skill to create a new type of food.

Mixing caviar with a ranging potion(2) is a master clue skill challenge from Sherlock .
11328:
Leaping trout is a fish which requires 48 Fishing , 15 Strength , and 15 Agility to be caught, providing 50 Fishing experience, 5 Strength experience, and 5 Agility experience. It can be caught at Otto's Grotto or Mount Quidamortem with a barbarian rod and suitable bait after starting the Barbarian Training miniquest .

The order in which bait is consumed from the inventory is: fish offcuts , fishing bait , feathers , roe , then caviar .

While it cannot be cooked, it can be gutted with a knife , providing a chance of receiving roe and fish offcuts. There's a 1/150 (0.7%) chance of receiving roe with level 1 Cooking, and 99/150 (66%) chance at level 99, scaling linearly in between. [ 1 ] If the player successfully receives roe, they will be rewarded with 10 Cooking experience and a further 1/2 chance of receiving fish offcuts as well. The roe and offcuts serve as bait, allowing the player to optionally save some feathers.
11330:
Leaping salmon is a fish which requires 58 Fishing , 30 Strength , and 30 Agility to be caught, providing 70 Fishing experience, 6 Strength experience, and 6 Agility experience. It can be caught at Otto's Grotto or Mount Quidamortem with a barbarian rod and suitable bait after starting the Barbarian Training miniquest .

The order in which bait is consumed from the inventory is: fish offcuts , fishing bait , feathers , roe , then caviar .

While it cannot be cooked, it can be gutted with a knife , providing a chance of receiving roe and fish offcuts. There's a 1/80 (1.25%) chance of receiving roe with level 1 Cooking, and 100% chance at level 80, scaling linearly in between. [ 1 ] If the player successfully receives roe, they will be rewarded with 10 Cooking experience and a further 3/4 chance of receiving fish offcuts as well. The roe and offcuts serve as bait, allowing the player to optionally save some feathers.
11332:
Leaping sturgeon is a fish which requires 70 Fishing , 45 Strength , and 45 Agility to be caught, providing 80 Fishing experience, 7 Strength experience, and 7 Agility experience. It can be caught at Otto's Grotto or Mount Quidamortem with a barbarian rod and suitable bait after starting the Barbarian Training miniquest .

The order in which bait is consumed from the inventory is: fish offcuts , fishing bait , feathers , roe , then caviar .

While it cannot be cooked, it can be gutted with a knife , providing a chance of receiving caviar and fish offcuts. There's a 1/80 (1.25%) chance of receiving caviar with level 1 Cooking and 100% chance at level 80, scaling linearly in between. [ 1 ] If the player successfully receives caviar, they will be rewarded with 15 Cooking experience and a further 5/6 chance of receiving fish offcuts as well. This is the only leaping fish to give caviar (which is sturgeon roe). The caviar and offcuts serve as bait, allowing the player to optionally save some feathers.
11334:
Fish offcuts are a form of fishing bait created by using a knife on most types of raw fish. Using a knife on certain high level raw fish will yield fine fish offcuts instead. Like other baits, they can be stored in a tackle box.

When used as bait for Barbarian Fishing, fish offcuts will be prioritised over other types of bait in your inventory (followed by fishing bait, feathers, roe, and caviar in that order).

Offcuts can also be used as a substitute for king worms when feeding the cormorant in aerial fishing. When aerial fishing, there is a 50% chance for a fish chunk to be consumed after every third catch. If it is not consumed on the third, it is guaranteed to be consumed on the fourth, meaning each chunk is consumed every 3.5 catches on average.

Offcuts can be used to bait shimmering, giant krill and haddock shoals while deep sea trawling. Players or crewmates can prepare them at a chum station facility on a boat, and spread them into the sea. They can also be used to bait crab traps.
11335:
The dragon full helm is a helmet that requires 60 Defence to equip. The dragon full helm gives better defence bonuses than its medium helm counterpart. Due to its high price, and lack of prayer or strength bonuses, it is more often used as a sign of wealth, rather than in combat.

A dragon full helm can be combined with a dragon full helm ornament kit to make a gold-trimmed dragon full helm (g) . This cosmetic enhancement won't change the stats in any way.

It is considered a piece of the dragon armour set.
11337:
Mangled bones are obtained in the Ancient Cavern , either from certain monsters or rummaging the skeletons found on the ground. If rummaging a skeleton, at least 2 inventory slots must be free because of the random chance of finding an ancient page ; otherwise, the bones will "disintegrate". The chance of obtaining a mangled bone from a skeleton is 11/202. [ 1 ]

Unlike other types of bones, mangled bones cannot be buried, and as such a bonecrusher will not activate when receiving them.

Mangled bones do NOT work for completing the Firemaking section of the Barbarian Training miniquest ; only chewed bones work.

With any type of logs , an axe , and a tinderbox , players can use it on the burnt space (pyre site) to make a pyre ship . When burned, this will release a level 166 ferocious barbarian spirit , which must be killed to receive a reward. However, players cannot receive a dragon full helm , as it is only obtainable from chewed bone pyre ships or as a drop from mithril dragons .
11338:
Chewed bones are obtained exclusively as a drop from mithril dragons in the Ancient Cavern at a rate of 3/128. No other monsters in the Ancient Cavern will drop chewed bones, and looting the skeletons won't give chewed bones either (only mangled bones ). The bones can be burnt on a pyre ship for rewards, including the dragon full helm .

Burning chewed bones on a pyre ship constructed with magic logs is a requirement for the elite Kandarin Diary ; using another type of log will not complete the task.
11339:
My notes is a book given during the Barbarian Training miniquest by Otto Godblessed. It records entries from ancient pages which are sometimes obtained when rummaging barbarian skeletons or as monster drops in the Ancient Cavern. It can be stored in the bookcase of a Player-owned house, where it is called "Records from my discoveries beneath the lake".

Rummaging skeletons gives a 1/13 chance of receiving an ancient page, while the spirits and skeletons have a 5/128 (1/25.6) chance of dropping them. In addition, mithril dragons have a 1/64 chance of dropping them. Brutal green dragons do not drop the pages. You can receive duplicate ancient pages from all drop sources, and you do not have to have the book in your inventory to add the pages.
11340:
Barbarian skills was a book that players could obtain from Otto Godblessed when embarking on Barbarian Training , which was removed alongside the update to rework Barbarian Training into a miniquest . [ 1 ]

The book detailed the proper ways to use a number of skills the barbarians have honed over the centuries, containing instructions on Fishing with a barbarian rod , fishing without a harpoon , and lighting a fire without a tinderbox (by using a bow on logs ).

If lost, it could be reobtained from Otto Godblessed or from the bookcase of a player-owned house if the player had previously stored it there.

11367: The bronze hasta is a one-handed melee members -only weapon , similar to the spear . It is the weakest hasta in Old School RuneScape . To wield this weapon, players need to have completed the Barbarian Training miniquest up through the Smithing section. To obtain a bronze hasta the player can either create one using the Smithing skill or trade with another player. It can be poisoned .
11369: The iron hasta is a one-handed melee weapon , similar to the spear . To wield this weapon, players need to have completed the Barbarian Training miniquest through the Smithing section. Although hastae offer negative defensive bonuses, the fact that they can be used with a shield or defender provides more defence than a normal spear. To obtain an iron hasta the player can either create one using the Smithing skill or trade with another player. It can be poisoned .

11427:
The fish vial is an unobtainable item that was presumably intended to be used in Barbarian Herblore . The examine suggests it would have been made by crushing roe or caviar into a vial.

A book of knowledge is the reward from Surprise Exam random events. Reading it grants experience equivalent to 15 times the level of the selected skill, 50% more than a genie lamp's 10 times multiplier. Two books of knowledge cannot be obtained at once, however it is still possible to get a second Surprise Exam random event. The player will receive an item instead. Possible rewards include an uncut gem, loop half of key, cosmic talisman, or coins.

If no inventory space is available, the book will be put on floor, but once picked up it cannot be dropped. Attempting to bank a book of knowledge yields the message: "A magical force prevents you from banking this item!".

The book is lost upon death.

The glassblowing book is a book that players can obtain from the reception at the Observatory north of Castle Wars, in the house west of the furnace on Entrana, or from a bookcase in a player-owned house, but only after it has already been picked up once before.

The book was written by Fritz the Glassblower, who also teaches the player how to make glass on Entrana. It explains in-depth the art of glassblowing involving blowing air into molten glass, which is part of the Crafting skill.
11663:
The Void mage helm is a piece of Void Knight equipment . It can be bought from a Void Knight for 200 commendation points , if the player has at least 42 Attack , Strength , Defence , Hitpoints , Ranged , and Magic , and 22 Prayer to buy and wear one. It is worn in combination with the other pieces of Void Knight Armour ( Void knight top , Void knight robe , and Void knight gloves ) to achieve the designated set effect. The Void knight mace is not required for the bonus.

The Void mage set gives a +45% to magic accuracy. This typically provides less accuracy and defensive bonuses than Ahrim's robes , but can be easily switched with the other Void sets. If wearing Elite Void Knight robes , the set gives an additional 5% increase to magic damage.

The effective magic attack bonus can be calculated as 1.45 x + 28.8 , where x is the total equipment magic attack bonus when wearing the Void mage set. For example, if you have a magic attack bonus of +16 while also wearing the Void mage set (which provides no bonus), the effective bonus becomes +52 taking into account the set effect. When wearing several best-in-slot pieces of magical gear, the accuracy of the Void mage set can surpass Ahrim's robes with the same gear.

If the player dies a PvP death at level 20 Wilderness or below and the item is unprotected, it will remain in the player's inventory; however, the item will be in a broken, unusable state and must be repaired by using it on Perdu and paying him 160,000 coins .

If the player dies a PvP death above level 20 Wilderness and the item is unprotected, it will be converted to coins. To prevent this, a Trouver parchment and a payment of 500,000 coins can be given to Perdu in order to permanently lock the item. The locked item will remain in the player's inventory; however, the item will be in a mangled, unusable state and must be repaired by using it on Perdu and paying him 500,000 coins.

The Void ranger helm is a piece of Void Knight equipment obtained as a reward from the Pest Control minigame. It can be bought from a Void Knight for 200 commendation points ; players also must have at least 42 Attack , Strength , Defence , Hitpoints , Ranged , Magic and 22 Prayer to buy and wear one.

If worn alongside the other three equipment pieces ( Void knight top , Void knight robe and Void knight gloves ), the Void ranger helm grants the player a 10% boost to Ranged damage (12.5% with Elite equipment ) and a 10% boost to Ranged accuracy. The Void knight mace is not required for the bonus.

It should be noted that while void knight armour significantly increases Ranged output against targets which are lacking in Defence, the substantial attack bonus provided by regular ranged armour makes the latter more effective against stronger opponents such as bosses.
