12795:
The steam battlestaff (or) is a steam battlestaff with a steam staff upgrade kit attached to it. The kit gives no additional bonuses, and is only used to add aesthetics to the staff. It costs 616,843 for both the parts to make the steam battlestaff (or).

While the staff is untradeable in its ornamented state, it can be reverted anytime, returning the steam battlestaff. However, the kit will not be returned.

If a player dies with the staff and it is not one of the player's protected items, the staff will revert to its default appearance, and players must use another steam staff upgrade kit to enhance its appearance again.
12796:
The mystic steam staff (or) is a mystic steam staff with a steam staff upgrade kit attached to it. The kit gives no additional bonuses, and is only used to add aesthetics to the staff. It costs 666,403 coins for both the parts to make the steam staff (or). The staff provides unlimited amounts of water and fire runes as well as the autocast option when equipped.

This staff can be also be created after the completion of the quest Scorpion Catcher by taking a steam battlestaff (or) and 40,000 coins to Thormac . After completion of the Hard Kandarin Diary and Elite Kandarin Diary , Thormac will only require 30,000 or 20,000 coins respectively.

While the staff is untradeable in its ornamented state, it can be reverted anytime, returning the mystic steam staff. However, the kit will not be returned.

If a player dies with the staff and it is not one of the player's protected items, the staff will revert to its default appearance, and players must use another steam staff upgrade kit to enhance its appearance again.
12797:
The dragon pickaxe (upgraded) is a dragon pickaxe with a dragon pickaxe upgrade kit attached to it. The kit gives no additional bonuses, and is only used to add aesthetics to the pickaxe. It costs 1,214,841 coins for both the parts to make the cosmetic dragon pickaxe.

While the pickaxe is untradeable in its ornamented state, it can be reverted anytime, returning the dragon pickaxe. However, the kit will not be returned.

If a player dies with the pickaxe and it is not one of the player's protected items, the pickaxe will revert to its default appearance, and players must use another dragon pickaxe upgrade kit to enhance its appearance again.
12798:
The steam staff upgrade kit is an item which can be used on the steam battlestaff or its mystic counterpart to create the steam battlestaff (or) or the mystic steam staff (or), which alters the staff's appearance, and is a purely cosmetic addition.

It can be purchased at Justine's stuff for the Last Shopper Standing for 13 Last Man Standing points.

Upon using the upgrade kit, the upgraded steam battlestaff becomes untradeable and the kit is consumed. The staff may be reverted to a staff again by selecting the "revert" option. The upgrade kit will not be returned upon reverting the ornate steam staff.
12800:
The dragon pickaxe upgrade kit is an item that can be used on the dragon pickaxe to create the dragon pickaxe (upgraded), which alters solely the pickaxe's appearance, and does not modify any stats.

It can be purchased at Justine's stuff for the Last Shopper Standing for 14 Last Man Standing points.

Upon using the upgrade kit, the upgraded dragon pickaxe becomes untradeable and the kit is consumed. The pickaxe may be reverted to a dragon pickaxe again by selecting the "revert" option. The upgrade kit will not be returned upon reverting the upgraded dragon pickaxe.
12802:
Ward upgrade kit is an item which can be used on either the odium ward or malediction ward to create the odium ward (or) and malediction ward (or), respectively. The kit simply alters the ward's appearance, and is a purely cosmetic addition.

It can be purchased at Justine's stuff for the Last Shopper Standing for 20 Last Man Standing points.

Upon using the upgrade kit, the upgraded ward becomes untradeable and the kit is consumed. The ward may be reverted to a tradeable version again by selecting the "revert" option. The upgrade kit will not be returned upon reverting the upgraded ward.
12804:
Saradomin's tear is a crystalised tear that is said to have been shed by Saradomin himself, created when he wept over the wounds of Commander Zilyana, who became seriously injured in the Battle of Annakarl during the God Wars.

It can be purchased from Justine's stuff for the Last Shopper Standing for 150 Last Man Standing points.

When attached to a Saradomin sword, it creates Saradomin's blessed sword, which adds +18 to slash attack and +6 to strength bonus. 75 Attack is required to wield Saradomin's blessed sword. Like the abyssal tentacle, it will consume the Saradomin sword after it has dealt 10,000 hits, leaving players with Saradomin's tear upon fully degrading.

When using the items on each other, there will be a warning message that states A blessed Saradomin sword is untradeable, with an Attack requirement of 75. After 10,000 hits, the sword crumbles to dust, and you get the Tear back.
12806:
The malediction ward (or) is a malediction ward with a ward upgrade kit attached to it. The kit gives no additional bonuses, and is only used to add aesthetics to the ward. It costs 3,109,635 for both the parts to make the malediction ward (or).

While the ward is untradeable in its ornamented state, it can be reverted anytime, returning the malediction ward. However, the kit will not be returned.

If a player dies with the ward and it is not one of the player's protected items, the ward will revert to its default appearance, and players must use another ward upgrade kit to enhance its appearance again.
12807:
The odium ward (or) is an odium ward with a ward upgrade kit attached to it. The kit gives no additional bonuses, and is only used to add aesthetics to the ward. It costs 3,950,490 for both the parts to make the odium ward (or).

While the ward is untradeable in its ornamented state, it can be reverted anytime, returning the odium ward. However, the kit will not be returned.

If a player dies with the ward and it is not one of the player's protected items, the ward will revert to its default appearance, and players must use another ward upgrade kit to enhance its appearance again. Ultimate Ironmen will instead keep the shield in its ornamented state.
12808:
Saradomin's blessed sword is a degradable two-handed sword which requires 75 Attack to wield. It is created by combining Saradomin's tear with the Saradomin sword. The blessed sword has +18 Slash and +6 Strength more than the normal variant.

If the sword is not protected upon death, it will fully degrade into Saradomin's tear. However, if it is protected on death, it will remain in its regular state as Saradomin's blessed sword.
12809:
Saradomin's blessed sword is a degradable two-handed sword which requires 75 Attack to wield. It is created by combining Saradomin's tear with the Saradomin sword. The blessed sword has +18 Slash and +6 Strength more than the normal variant.

If the sword is not protected upon death, it will fully degrade into Saradomin's tear. However, if it is protected on death, it will remain in its regular state as Saradomin's blessed sword.
12810: The ironman helm is a full helm obtainable only by players who chose to be a standard ironman in Ironman Mode . It is obtained by speaking to Adam after leaving Tutorial Island , after choosing to be a standard ironman.
12811: The ironman platebody is a platebody obtainable only by players who chose to be a standard ironman in Ironman Mode . It is obtained by speaking to Adam after leaving Tutorial Island , after choosing to be a standard ironman. Fittingly, it has equivalent stats to an iron platebody , which is the best melee armour a starting player can use.
12812: Ironman platelegs are obtainable only by players who chose to be a standard ironman in Ironman Mode . They can be obtained by speaking to Adam after leaving Tutorial Island , after choosing to be a standard ironman.
12813: The Ultimate ironman helm is a full helm obtainable only by players who chose to be an Ultimate ironman in Ironman Mode. It is obtained by speaking to Adam after leaving Tutorial Island, after choosing to be an Ultimate ironman.
12814: The Ultimate ironman platebody is a platebody obtainable only by players who chose to be an Ultimate ironman in Ironman Mode. It is obtained by speaking to Adam after leaving Tutorial Island, after choosing to be an Ultimate ironman.
12815: Ultimate ironman platelegs are obtainable only by players who chose to be an ultimate ironman in Ironman Mode. They can be obtained by speaking to Adam after leaving Tutorial Island, after choosing to be an ultimate ironman.
12816:
The pet dark core is a pet dropped by the Corporeal Beast. It is the dark energy core that is summoned during the fight with the Corporeal Beast. Players can right click "Metamorphosis" to change between the dark core and the Corporeal Critter, which is a smaller version of the Corporeal Beast.

When a player receives the pet, it will automatically try to appear as their follower. At the same time, a message in the chatbox will state You have a funny feeling like you're being followed. However, if a player receives a pet while having a follower out (for example, a cat), it will be placed into their inventory. When this occurs, the message in the chatbox will instead state You feel something weird sneaking into your backpack.

If a player's inventory is full and they have a follower already, they will not receive the pet; it must instead be claimed from Probita in East Ardougne.

On death, if a player loses their pet (as a follower or in your inventory) it will wander around the area for 30 seconds before despawning. Even if the player returns in time, the pet cannot be picked up, and can be reclaimed from Probita.
12817:
The elysian spirit shield requires 75 Defence and 75 Prayer to wield.

It is made by attaching an elysian sigil, a rare drop from the Corporeal Beast, to a blessed spirit shield using a hammer at an anvil; this process requires 90 Prayer and 85 Smithing. Players without the required skill levels to create the shield may ask Abbot Langley in the Edgeville Monastery to combine the sigil and the blessed spirit shield, for a fee of 1,500,000 coins.

This shield has superior Melee and Ranged defence bonuses compared to the arcane and spectral spirit shields, as well as a powerful passive effect. It has the highest crush defence in the shield slot. In terms of mitigating damage taken, the elysian spirit shield is one of the most powerful shields in Old School RuneScape.
12819: The elysian sigil can be attached to a blessed spirit shield to make an elysian spirit shield. To attach the sigil to the blessed spirit shield, players need 90 Prayer and 85 Smithing. It is a very rare drop from the Corporeal Beast. Players without the required skill levels to create the shield may ask Abbot Langley in the Edgeville Monastery to combine the sigil and the blessed spirit shield, for a fee of 1,500,000 coins.
12821:
The spectral spirit shield is a shield which requires 75 Defence, 70 Prayer and 65 Magic to wield.

It is made by attaching a spectral sigil, a rare drop from the Corporeal Beast, to a blessed spirit shield using a hammer at an anvil; this process requires 90 Prayer and 85 Smithing. Players without the required skill levels to create the shield may ask Abbot Langley in the Edgeville Monastery to combine the sigil and the blessed spirit shield, for a fee of 1,500,000 coins.

The shield's melee and ranged defensive bonuses are identical to the blessed spirit shield, but has a magic defence bonus of +30, the highest of any shield in the game. Its counterpart, the arcane spirit shield, instead provides a magic attack bonus of +20. The spectral spirit shield also has a unique passive effect.
12823: The spectral sigil can be attached to a blessed spirit shield to make a spectral spirit shield. To attach the sigil to the blessed spirit shield, players need 90 Prayer and 85 Smithing. It is made by using the sigil on an anvil, while having a hammer and a blessed spirit shield in the inventory. Alternatively, players can ask Abbot Langley to attach it for 1,500,000 coins. It is a rare drop from the Corporeal Beast.
12825:
The arcane spirit shield requires 75 Defence, 65 Magic and 70 Prayer to wield.

It is made by attaching an arcane sigil, a rare drop from the Corporeal Beast, to a blessed spirit shield using a hammer at an anvil; this process requires 90 Prayer and 85 Smithing. Players without the required skill levels to create the shield may ask Abbot Langley in the Edgeville Monastery to combine the sigil and the blessed spirit shield, for a fee of 1,500,000 coins.

Abbot Langley can also remove the sigil from the shield, though this destroys the blessed spirit shield; this is usually done in order to use the sigil to fortify Elidinis' ward into an Elidinis' ward (f).

The shield's defensive bonuses are identical to the blessed spirit shield, but provides an additional Magic attack bonus of +20 and Magic damage bonus of +3%. Its counterpart, the spectral spirit shield, instead provides a Magic defence bonus of +30 and a unique passive effect.
12827:
The arcane sigil is an item obtained as a rare drop from the Corporeal Beast. It can be attached to a blessed spirit shield to create an arcane spirit shield, as well as an Elidinis' ward to create Elidinis' ward (f).

Creating an arcane spirit shield requires level 90 Prayer and 85 Smithing. Alternatively, players can ask Abbot Langley to create it for them for 1,500,000 coins.

Meanwhile, fortifying Elidinis' ward requires level 90 Prayer and 90 Smithing, as well as 10,000 soul runes. Unlike the arcane spirit shield, Abbot Langley cannot help players to fortify the ward, though he can remove the sigil from an arcane spirit shield, destroying the blessed spirit shield in the process.
12829:
The spirit shield is obtained as a drop from the Corporeal Beast. It requires 45 Defence and 55 Prayer to wield.

Stats-wise, this unblessed spirit shield is comparable with the rune kiteshield and the obsidian shield, arguably being somewhere in between, along with carrying no attack penalties for Ranged and Magic users.

The spirit shield can be combined with a holy elixir, with 85 Prayer, to make a blessed spirit shield. The blessed spirit shield can then be modified by attaching spirit sigils to create the enhanced spirit shields.
12831:
The blessed spirit shield requires 70 Defence and 60 Prayer to wield. To make this shield, players must use a holy elixir with a normal spirit shield, which requires 85 Prayer. Ironmen may note this level cannot be boosted as prayer boosts do not affect the base level. Once blessed, players may apply spirit sigils to enhance the shield. Attaching a sigil onto the shield requires 90 Prayer and 85 Smithing.

This shield's stats are comparable to the stats of the arcane and spectral spirit shield. It differs only in lacking the higher magic attack and defence stats of the enhanced shields. This shield is a good choice for any player using melee because of its substantial defence bonuses and prayer bonus. Its crush defence bonus is also one point higher than that of a completely charged Dragonfire shield. Players who use Magic or Ranged may also find this shield useful due to its lack of negative stats.
12833:
The holy elixir is an item that players can use to bless a spirit shield , making it a blessed spirit shield , requiring level 85 Prayer . It is a rare drop from the Corporeal Beast .

After the shield has been blessed, an arcane , spectral , or elysian sigil can be attached to it to create an arcane , spectral , or elysian spirit shield , respectively.
12835: The community pumpkin is an unobtainable item added to the cache during the 2014 Halloween event, but was never used during the event.
12836: The Grim reaper's diary was obtained during the 2014 Halloween event . It directed players where to place the items found in the lounge area. It could not be taken out of Grim Reaper's house while doing the event.
12837: The Grim robe was an item used in the 2014 Halloween event , which took place in the Grim Reaper 's house. Players found this in the cabinet and then had to relocate it to the fireplace.
12838: A will and testament was an item found on the fireplace in the Grim Reaper 's house, and then relocated to the sofa in the 2014 Halloween event . It apparently is from the Servants' Guild , as the Last Will and Testament of the 1,000th servant that the Grim Reaper hired.
12839: Human bones were an item needed to be found in the Fish tank, and then relocated to the chest in the 2014 Halloween event . These as well as several other items were to be moved to the chest before moving onto the next stage of the event.
12840: The Servant's skull was an item that was used during the 2014 Halloween event. The Grim Reaper had a task for players to find his servant that went missing shortly after. He notices this when spider webs were starting to build up around the house. The Grim Reaper asks you to go to the backyard (which was a maze) and try to locate him. After traversing through the maze, you eventually find the servants skull. The skull had to be brought back in order to give word about the servant's "unexpected" death.
12841: The hourglass was an item that was found on the shelves and then needed to be relocated to the fishtank in the 2014 Halloween event .
12842: The Scythe sharpener was an item used in the 2014 Halloween event . This Halloween event consisted of doing 3 different chores for the Grim Reaper including one chore where items needed to be found and properly placed in a specific place and that is where the scythe sharpener comes in. The sharpener was found in the bookcase, and then relocated to the cabinet.
12843: A Human eye was an item from the 2014 Halloween event . It was part of a task in which the player would find various items in the Grim Reaper 's living room and would have to put them in the correct places. The eye was found under the Reaper's sofa and was meant to be placed on his shelf.
12844: The voice potion was an item that was involved in the 2014 Halloween event , during which the player completed a series of chores meant for the Grim Reaper 's late assistant. It was found by searching the fireplace, and it needed to be placed on the bookshelf. The potion in question could not be used by players.
12845:
The Grim reaper hood is a cosmetic head slot item originally rewarded to players upon completion of the 2014 Halloween event .

If destroyed, a replacement can be obtained from Diango in Draynor Village or from the toy box of a costume room . However, instead of being listed as a 2014 item, it is listed as a 2007 item, likely due to the fact the 2014 Halloween event was mostly present in the August 2007 Archive of RuneScape as the RuneScape 2 2007 Halloween event .
12846:
The target teleport scroll is an item that can be read to unlock the Teleport to Target spell, which requires level 85 in Magic to use.

It can be purchased at Justine's stuff for the Last Shopper Standing for 250 Last Man Standing points, or at the Bounty Hunter Store for 500 Bounty Hunter points. There will be a confirmation message when the player attempts to read the scroll.
12848:
The granite maul is a two-handed melee weapon that requires 50 Strength and Attack to wield. They are dropped by gargoyles (75 Slayer required), which are in the Slayer Tower .

Players can use a granite clamp to cosmetically enhance the granite maul. This causes the maul to become untradeable, and the clamp is not returned upon reverting the maul back to its original state.

Players can use an ornate maul handle to enhance the granite maul into a granite maul (ornate handle) , which reduces its special attack cost from 60% to 50%.

The granite clamp and ornate handle are obtained from Justine's stuff for the Last Shopper Standing .
12849:
The granite clamp is an item that can be used on the granite maul or granite maul (ornate handle) to alter the maul's appearance. It is a purely cosmetic addition.

The clamp can be purchased at Justine's stuff for the Last Shopper Standing for 25 Last Man Standing points.

Upon using the clamp, the maul becomes untradeable and the kit is consumed. The maul may be reverted to a granite maul again by selecting the "revert" option. The clamp will not be returned upon reverting the ornate granite maul.

The ornate maul handle , which reduces the maul's special attack cost to 50%, can be used before and after attaching the granite clamp.
12851: The Amulet of the Damned is an amulet that provides extra buffs to Barrows equipment . It can be obtained from silver and gold shade chests found in the Shade Catacombs . The amulet has the same bonuses as an amulet of glory .
12853: The Amulet of the Damned is an amulet that provides extra buffs to Barrows equipment . It can be obtained from silver and gold shade chests found in the Shade Catacombs . The amulet has the same bonuses as an amulet of glory .
12854:
The Flamtaer bag is a bag that can store supplies used in the Shades of Mort'ton minigame . It is obtained from any chest (except bronze) in the Shade Catacombs . Players can only own one Flamtaer bag at any given time.

The Flamtaer bag is able to store up to 60 timber beams , 60 limestone bricks , and 500 swamp paste , which can be withdrawn at any time using the "Empty" option. Items inside the bag will be automatically used without needing to withdraw them when repairing temple walls in the Shades of Mort'ton minigame.

As a limestone brick container , the bag can also be useful when building certain items in a player-owned house . If using the bag in this manner, the items must be emptied from the bag before they can be used to build furniture.

On death, the Flamtaer bag is lost along with its contents.
12855:
The Hunter's honour is a cosmetic hat that can be claimed from Corrupted Warriors in Ferox Enclave or Daimon's Crater, once players obtain one target kill in the Bounty Hunter minigame.

The hat alters its appearance depending on the number of target kills (assigned target kills in the Bounty Hunter minigame) and rogue kills (non-target kills on Bounty Hunter worlds) the player has; the Hunter's honour is chosen if the player has more target kills than rogue kills, and the Rogue's revenge is chosen if the player has more rogue kills than target kills.
12856:
The Rogue's revenge is a cosmetic hat that can be claimed from Corrupted Warriors in Ferox Enclave or Daimon's Crater , once players has more non target kills than target kills, and at least 1 target kill.

The hat alters its appearance depending on the amount of target kills (assigned target kills in the Bounty Hunter minigame) and rogue kills (non-target kills on Bounty Hunter worlds) the player has; the Hunter's honour is chosen if the player has more target kills than rogue kills, and the Rogue's revenge is chosen if the player has more rogue kills than target kills.

The trident of the swamp is a one-handed powered staff requiring 78 Magic to wield. It is a direct upgrade of the trident of the seas , made with level 59 Crafting by using a magic fang on it with a chisel , which is a reversible process. However, unlike its predecessor, the trident can only be listed for sale on the Grand Exchange when it is fully uncharged.

The trident possesses a passive effect wherein successful hits with either the built-in spell or a manually-cast combat spell have a 25% chance of inflicting venom on the opponent. If the player is wearing a serpentine helm , the chance is increased to 100% if the target is a monster. If using a manually-cast spell, the staff must contain at least one charge for it to be able to apply venom, although this will not use up any charges.

Additionally, the trident of the swamp has the same effect in drift net fishing as the merfolk trident , though it does not have the ability to hold pufferfish charges (convenient for breathing underwater ).

The trident of the swamp is a popular weapon choice for applying venom among combat pures who do not want to get 75 Attack for the toxic staff of the dead .

12902:
The toxic staff of the dead is a one-handed bladed staff made by using a magic fang on a staff of the dead, requiring 59 Crafting to do so. This process is reversible, provided that the staff is uncharged. It also requires 75 Attack and 75 Magic to wield.

Aside from increased stats, the toxic staff shares the same features as the regular staff of the dead, with one extra benefit; players using combat spells when wielding the staff have a 25% chance of inflicting venom on their opponent. However, if the opponent is an NPC and the serpentine helm is worn in conjunction with the staff, there is a 100% chance of envenoming them. The player can also envenom opponents using the staff's melee attack.

The staff can be turned into the Toxic staff (Deadman) by using it on Nigel if the Annihilation weapon scroll has been previously used on him.

12905:
Anti-venom is a potion that instantly cures venom and poison . It provides immunity to poison for 12 minutes and immunity to venom for 36-54 seconds.

Players can make this potion at 87 Herblore by using Zulrah's scales on an Antidote++ . Five scales are needed per dose of antidote++, so 20 scales will be needed to create a four-dose Anti-venom. This grants 30 Herblore experience per dose.

Anti-venom is used to create anti-venom+ , which cures poison and venom and provides immunity to venom for three minutes. This can be done by adding a clean torstol into it, requiring 94 Herblore and granting 125 Herblore experience.

Ten anti-venom(4) potions are among the required materials for building an ornate rejuvenation pool .

Creating an anti-venom potion whilst standing in the Horseshoe Mine is required to complete the Elite Karamja Diary . Creating an anti-venom potion is required to complete a master clue scroll skill challenge assigned by Sherlock .

12921:
The Pet Snakeling is a pet dropped by Zulrah. It resembles the appearance of the snakelings that Zulrah summons during the fight. Players can right click "Metamorphosis" to change it between its normal, magma, or tanzanite form.

When a player receives the pet, it will automatically try to appear as their follower. At the same time, a message in the chatbox will state You have a funny feeling like you're being followed. However, if a player receives a pet while having a follower out (for example, a cat), it will be placed into their inventory. When this occurs, the message in the chatbox will instead state You feel something weird sneaking into your backpack.

If a player's inventory is full and they have a follower already, they will not receive the pet; it must instead be claimed from Probita in East Ardougne.

On death, if a player loses their pet (as a follower or in your inventory) it will wander around the area for 30 seconds before despawning. Even if the player returns in time, the pet cannot be picked up, and can be reclaimed from Probita.
12922:
The tanzanite fang is obtained from killing Zulrah . It can be used with a chisel to create the toxic blowpipe (empty) , requiring level 78 Fletching and granting 120 experience.

Players can dismantle the fang to receive 20,000 Zulrah's scales , resulting in a loss of −6,313,281 coins .
12924:
The toxic blowpipe is a blowpipe that requires 75 Ranged to wield. Like all blowpipes, it is a two-handed weapon. It can be made by using a chisel on a tanzanite fang, which requires 78 Fletching. Players using the blowpipe have a 25% chance of inflicting venom on their opponent with attacks or manually-cast combat spells. However, if the opponent is an NPC and the serpentine helm is worn in conjunction with the blowpipe, there is a 100% chance of envenoming them.

The base attack speed of the toxic blowpipe varies; in player versus monster encounters, its attack speed is 3, or equal to darts. During player versus player combat, its attack speed is 4, or equal to a shortbow. In addition, its attack range is +2 higher than that of throwing darts, at 5 by default. Longrange increases attack range by 2.

If the blowpipe is not protected upon death, all scale and dart charges will appear on the floor alongside the blowpipe. If the blowpipe IS protected upon death, ALL scale and dart charges will be maintained when you respawn. This makes it an effective weapon for ranging in the Wilderness as the weapon and the ammo is contained in one high-value item slot, being very effective at the Revenant Caves for those who are not skulled. The blowpipe is only tradeable when uncharged (empty).

Players can dismantle an uncharged blowpipe to receive 20,000 Zulrah's scales, resulting in a loss of −6,515,732 coins.

Players can toggle whether picked up ammunition is automatically reloaded into the blowpipe or remains in the inventory by talking to the Ranged combat tutor or by toggling the "ammo-picking behaviour" checkbox in the in-game settings.

12929:
The serpentine helm is a degradable helmet made at level 52 Crafting by using a chisel on a serpentine visage, giving the player 120 Crafting experience. The helmet requires 75 Defence to wear. Its defensive bonuses are comparable to those of the Barrows helmets, without the prayer bonus that Verac's helm offers. It has the fourth highest strength bonus of all helmets, although its high cost of use makes other helmets more feasible for general training.

If a player dies with the helmet in PvP and it is not protected, any scales that were used to charge it will appear on the floor along with the uncharged helmet.

The serpentine helm is only tradeable when uncharged. In addition, players can dismantle an uncharged helm to receive 20,000 Zulrah's scales, resulting in a profit of −29,031 coins.

12932:
The magic fang is obtained from killing Zulrah . With level 59 Crafting , it can be used with a chisel and either a staff of the dead or an uncharged trident of the seas to create the toxic staff of the dead or trident of the swamp , respectively.

The magic fang can be safely removed after being attached, as long as the item it is attached to is uncharged.

Players can dismantle the fang to receive 20,000 Zulrah's scales , resulting in a profit of 47,714 coins .
12934:
Zulrah's scales are items used to charge serpentine helms, toxic blowpipes, toxic staves of the dead, and tridents of the swamp. It can also be used to create anti-venom at 87 Herblore by using them on an Antidote++, with 5 scales used per dose.

They are primarily obtained as a drop from Zulrah. They can also be obtained by dissecting sacred eels with a knife, which requires level 72 in Cooking and level 87 in Fishing. A player's Cooking level affects how many scales are received when they are dissected.

In addition, players can receive 20,000 scales from dismantling the following items:

Tanzanite fang

Toxic blowpipe (empty)

Serpentine visage

Serpentine helm (uncharged)

Magic fang

On average, each Zulrah kill will provide 220 scales, or 337 if including scales gained by dismantling the aforementioned drops.
12935:
Ohn's diary is found by searching a crate east of the High Priestess Zul-Harcinqa, after speaking to her. It is written by Ohn, and provides a backstory on how the tribe of Zul-Andra came to be.

If lost, it can be reclaimed from the crate east of the High Priestess, or from a bookcase within a player-owned house.
12936:
The jar of swamp is a rare drop from Zulrah .

The jar can be used on a boss lair display in a player's Achievement Gallery to have a display of Zulrah. Doing so requires having defeated Zulrah at least once.
12938:
Zul-andra teleport scrolls are consumable teleport scrolls that teleport the player to Zul-Andra. They can be obtained from defeating Zulrah.

This scroll is only usable after completing the Regicide quest. Attempting to use the scroll without meeting the requirements displays the game message: You need to complete the Regicide quest before you can teleport to Zul-Andra.
12939:
The Pet Snakeling is a pet dropped by Zulrah. It resembles the appearance of the snakelings that Zulrah summons during the fight. Players can right click "Metamorphosis" to change it between its normal, magma, or tanzanite form.

When a player receives the pet, it will automatically try to appear as their follower. At the same time, a message in the chatbox will state You have a funny feeling like you're being followed. However, if a player receives a pet while having a follower out (for example, a cat), it will be placed into their inventory. When this occurs, the message in the chatbox will instead state You feel something weird sneaking into your backpack.

If a player's inventory is full and they have a follower already, they will not receive the pet; it must instead be claimed from Probita in East Ardougne.

On death, if a player loses their pet (as a follower or in your inventory) it will wander around the area for 30 seconds before despawning. Even if the player returns in time, the pet cannot be picked up, and can be reclaimed from Probita.

The dragon defender is the second strongest defender , behind the Avernic defender . It is used for its attack and strength bonus and is held in the shield slot. It requires level 60 Defence to equip.

The dragon defender can only be obtained from the stronger level 106 Cyclopes found exclusively in the Warrior Guild 's basement. To enter the basement for the first time, a player must show a rune defender to Lorelai , who will then grant them permanent access. Warrior Guild tokens are still required for time spent inside the basement unless the player has an Attack Cape equipped. Players can obtain a dragon defender without having a rune defender in their bank. [ 1 ] Players can obtain the dragon defender without having 60 Defence . [ 2 ]

Its melee defensive bonuses are comparable to those of an adamant square shield , with slight differences. Its strength bonus is surpassed by both the dragonfire shield and the Avernic defender , which give +7 and +8 strength bonuses, respectively. However, the dragon defender is more commonly used than either of these for melee training, due to its superior melee attack bonuses over the dragonfire shield and the overall rarity of the Avernic defender .

If the player dies to a PvP death and the dragon defender is not one of the player's protected items, it will remain in the player's inventory, but will become broken , which means the item is unusable and must be repaired with 240,000 coins by using the item on Perdu .

The quest point cape is a cape of accomplishment that can be obtained by players who have completed all quests (excluding miniquests ). The cape, along with the quest point hood , can be purchased from the Wise Old Man in Draynor Village for 99,000 coins . To trim the cape, players must complete all achievement diaries , thus earning them the achievement diary cape as well.

Should a new quest be released, the cape will be unequipped, and the player will not be able to equip or operate it until the new quest is completed. If the player's inventory is full, the cape will be banked instead. In the event that their inventory and bank are both full, the cape will be lost , and will have to be re-purchased from the Wise Old Man.

The cape is a popular goal for ironmen due to its quick teleport to a fairy ring . Additionally, performing the quest cape emote in the Wise Old Man 's house is an elite task in the Lumbridge & Draynor Diary . The emote can also be used at the top of Falador Castle for a task in the elite Falador Diary .

Unlike skill hiscores, there is no official way to track the number of players who currently own the cape; it must be shared by Jagex. In February 2020, there were 61,766 current members who had obtained the quest point cape. [ 1 ]

This item can be stored in the cape rack of a costume room , as part of the Quest point cape set, along with the hood . Ultimate Ironmen will be unable to retrieve individual pieces until the full set is stored. Players who own a quest cape but no longer have all quests completed will find they cannot store the cape until they re-complete all quests. However, quest capes that were already mounted on the cape rack prior to new quests becoming available will remain on the rack. Quest capes on cape racks therefore represent that the home owner at one point or another had attained all available quest points at the time of mounting.
13069:
The achievement diary cape can be obtained by players who have completed all Achievement Diaries. It can be purchased along with its hood for 99,000 coins, from Twiggy O'Korn in Draynor Village. The cape becomes trimmed after completion of all quests, as do the quest cape and music cape after completing all diaries. The cape is notable for providing teleports to all diary masters, and offering a close bank teleport, and options that are useful for optimal Runecrafting and Farming runs.

If a new quest is released, the cape will untrim itself, and will not be able to be re-trimmed until the player completes it. Unlike skillcapes, the achievement diary cape can be trimmed and untrimmed at will, provided that the player meets the requirements. The cape provides a +4 prayer bonus, regardless of whether or not it is trimmed. Untrimmed skill capes will not be trimmed from trimming the achievement diary cape. Obtaining the music cape is not necessary to trim the diary cape.

This item can be stored in the cape rack of a costume room, as part of the achievement diary cape set, along with the hood. Ultimate Ironmen will be unable to retrieve individual pieces until the full set is stored.
13070:
The achievement diary hood is the skillcape hood associated with having completed all Achievement Diaries. Players may buy the hood alongside the Achievement diary cape (t) from the Twiggy O'Korn in Draynor for 99,000 coins. The hood itself provides absolutely no offensive or defensive bonuses and may be worn for purely aesthetic purposes.

While the hood is bought with the skillcape, it is not needed to perform the emote associated with it; the skillcape is the only essential item.

This item can be stored in the cape rack of a costume room, as part of the Achievement diary cape set. Ultimate Ironmen will be unable to retrieve individual pieces until the full set is stored.

Should players lose the hood, they may reclaim it from Twiggy for free.

The Chompy chick is a pet that can be received as a rare drop from chompy birds (not jubbly birds), and can only be obtained by players who have completed the elite Western Provinces diary and received its rewards. There is a chance to receive the pet when the chompy bird is killed and when it is plucked.

When a player receives the pet, it will automatically try to appear as their follower. At the same time, a message in the chatbox will state You have a funny feeling like you're being followed. However, if a player receives a pet while having a follower out (for example, a cat), it will be placed into their inventory. When this occurs, the message in the chatbox will instead state You feel something weird sneaking into your backpack.

If a player's inventory is full and they have a follower already, they will not receive the pet; it must instead be claimed from Probita in East Ardougne.

On death, if a player loses their pet (as a follower or in your inventory) it will wander around the area for 30 seconds before despawning. Even if the player returns in time, the pet cannot be picked up, and can be reclaimed from Probita.
13072:
The elite Void top is a piece of Elite Void Knight equipment . It can be upgraded from a Void knight top for 200 Void Knight commendation points by speaking to the Elite Void Knight , although a player must have completed the Hard Western Provinces Diary to be able to upgrade it. It is worn in combination with the other pieces of Void Knight Armour to achieve the designated set effect, depending on which helm is worn. The stats are the same as the Void knight top , but with a +3 prayer bonus , as well as a +2.5% damage boost to Ranged and +5% damage boost to Magic when worn with the Elite void robe .

If the player dies a PvP death at level 20 Wilderness or below and the item is unprotected, it will remain in the player's inventory; however, the item will be in a broken, unusable state and must be repaired by using it on Perdu and paying him 250,000 coins .

If the player dies a PvP death above level 20 Wilderness and the item is unprotected, it will be converted to coins. To prevent this, a Trouver parchment and a payment of 500,000 coins can be given to Perdu in order to permanently lock the item. The locked item will remain in the player's inventory; however, the item will be in a mangled, unusable state and must be repaired by using it on Perdu and paying him 500,000 coins.

This item can be stored in the armour case of a costume room , as part of the Void Knight Elite armour set. Ultimate Ironmen will be unable to retrieve individual pieces until the full set is stored.

The top can also be given to the Dodgy Squire in exchange for 360 Void Knight commendation points.
13073:
An elite void robe is a piece of Elite Void Knight equipment . It can be upgraded from a void knight robe for 200 Void Knight commendation points by speaking to the Elite Void Knight , although the hard Western Provinces Diary must be completed to upgrade it. When worn in combination with the other pieces of Void Knight armour, there is a set effect that depends on which void helm is worn. Compared to the void knight robe , it has an additional +3 prayer bonus and a +2.5% damage boost to Ranged and +5% damage boost to Mage when worn with the elite void top .

If the player dies a PvP death at level 20 Wilderness or below and the item is unprotected, it will remain in the player's inventory; however, the item will be in a broken, unusable state and must be repaired by using it on Perdu and paying him 250,000 coins .

If the player dies a PvP death above level 20 Wilderness and the item is unprotected, it will be converted to coins. To prevent this, a Trouver parchment and a payment of 500,000 coins can be given to Perdu in order to permanently lock the item. The locked item will remain in the player's inventory; however, the item will be in a mangled, unusable state and must be repaired by using it on Perdu and paying him 500,000 coins.

This item can be stored in the armour case of a costume room , as part of the Void Knight Elite armour set. Ultimate Ironmen will be unable to retrieve individual pieces until the full set is stored.

The robe can also be given to the Dodgy Squire in exchange for 360 Void Knight commendation points.
13074:
The pharaoh's sceptre is a discontinued item that previously had similar functionality to its modern incarnation . It was changed with the update that introduced Beneath Cursed Sands . In that update, the sceptre was updated to hold a vastly increased number of charges, and now functions in a manner similar to Xeric's talisman . It held 3 charges by default, increased to 4 charges after the Easy Desert Diary , 5 after the Medium Desert Diary , 6 after the Hard Desert Diary , and 8 after the Elite Desert Diary .

After the game update on 27 April 2022 , some existing pharaoh's sceptres were automatically converted to the new item. However, players who had this item in storage at the time of the update kept the original item, albeit with updated menu options; the only menu option besides " Drop " is "Convert", which converts it into a normal pharaoh's sceptre . There is no longer any other use for the item.

13079:
The enchanted lyre is acquired in The Fremennik Trials quest . It is used in the quest to perform in the longhall to get Olaf the Bard 's vote for the player to become a Fremennik . The lyre can be made by using an axe to cut a branch from the swaying tree east of Rellekka , and then using a knife on the branch to obtain an unstrung lyre , then attaching spun golden fleece . This part needs 25 Fletching . Alternatively, players may receive one as a drop from Lanzig , Borrokar , or Freidir in their huts in the south-eastern area of the village.

After the quest, the player can enchant their normal lyre into an enchanted lyre by charging it with Fossegrimen to be used as a teleport to Rellekka . When the hard Fremennik Diary is completed, the enchanted lyre can also teleport to Waterbirth Island , and gains the ability to teleport to Jatizso and Neitiznot after completion of the elite Fremennik Diary .

It required completion of the Hard Western Provinces Diary to wield, as well as 70 Attack , 35 Strength and 50 Agility .

13091:
The crystal halberd was a degradable two-handed weapon made from elven crystal . It required completion of the Hard Western Provinces Diary to wield, as well as 70 Attack , 35 Strength and 50 Agility .

These crystal halberds functioned differently to the present day Crystal halberd . They would degrade over time with use, and their stats would gradually decrease as the halberd degraded.

With the release of Song of the Elves , all existing Crystal halberds reverted into Crystal weapon seeds . As a result, these items are currently unobtainable; however, they remain in the game files.

13102:
A teleport crystal is a small crystal which can teleport a player to the elven village of Lletya (and Prifddinas upon completion of the Song of the Elves quest). Both teleports are reasonably close to a bank, and the Lletya teleport is close to a fruit tree patch and an altar.

The crystal has four teleport charges when initially received and, when used up, becomes a crystal teleport seed. It can then be recharged by Eluned for 150–750 coins; she will recharge the crystal for the player when it's out of charges; upon completing the Hard Western Provinces Diary, she can enchant 5 instead of 3 charges. Players may possess multiple teleport crystals at the same time. After the completion of the Song of the Elves quest, crystals can be charged by Eluned in south-west Prifddinas or by the elven scout at Eluned's former locations. You can find her location in Eluned#Finding Eluned

Crystal teleport seeds can be obtained as a common drop from Elf warriors and Elf guards. Note that these are only dropped by the elves found in Lletya and Prifddinas, as the elves in the Iorwerth Camp will not drop it. Players are also required to at least have started Mourning's End Part I, though 50 Thieving is not required to obtain it. Elf warriors may drop it with one charge or no charges at all.

After Song of the Elves, players can craft an eternal teleport crystal to allow unlimited teleports. Eternal teleport crystals are crafted from the rarer enhanced crystal teleport seed rather than the common crystal teleport seeds.
13103: Karamja gloves 4 are a reward for completing the Elite Karamja Diary tasks. The gloves can be claimed by talking to Pirate Jackie the Fruit found in Brimhaven, near the entrance to the Brimhaven Agility Arena, and can be retrieved from her for free if lost. Multiple pairs of gloves can be obtained for free. Alternatively, players can purchase a pair from Perdu for 200 coins should they lose them.
13104: Varrock armour 1 is a reward from completing the easy Varrock Diary . The armour is received from Toby in Varrock and can be retrieved from him for free if lost. The general stats of Varrock armour 1 are the same as a steel platebody , apart from +5 higher relative ranged attack (-10 vs. -15) and a weight of only 1 kg. The item has no Defence requirement, and can be re-obtained for free. This makes it a desirable option for 1 Defence Pures (particularly when using Melee ) and lower level Abyss runecrafters . Unlike most platebodies , it does not interfere with Ava's devices .
13105: Varrock armour 2 is a reward from completing the medium Varrock Diary . The armour is received from Toby in Varrock and can be retrieved from him for free if lost. Its stats are almost identical to those of a black platebody , but significantly lighter while providing a higher range bonus.
13106: Varrock armour 3 is a reward from completing the hard Varrock Diary . The armour is received from Toby in Varrock and can be retrieved from him for free if lost. Its stats are almost identical to those of a mithril platebody , but significantly lighter while providing a higher range bonus.
13107: Varrock armour 4 is a reward from completing the elite Varrock Diary . The armour is received from Toby in Varrock and can be retrieved from him for free if lost. Multiple can be obtained for free. Its stats are almost identical to those of a adamant platebody , but it's significantly lighter and the range bonus of -10 is less of a penalty than the -15 for the adamant platebody.
13108:
The Wilderness sword 1 is a reward from completing the easy Wilderness Diary given to you by the Lesser Fanatic in Edgeville . If lost, it can be retrieved from him for free, or from Perdu for a fee.

Its stats are identical to an iron sword .
13109:
The Wilderness sword 2 is an Achievement Diary reward for completing the medium Wilderness Diary given by the Lesser Fanatic in Edgeville and can be reclaimed from him for free if lost.

Its stats are identical to a steel sword .
13110:
The Wilderness sword 3 is a reward from completing the hard Wilderness Diary tasks given to you by the Lesser Fanatic in Edgeville , and can be retrieved from him for free if lost.

Its stats are identical to the mithril sword , except that the Wilderness sword 3 weighs more.
13111:
The Wilderness sword 4 is a reward from completing the elite Wilderness Diary tasks given to you by the Lesser Fanatic in Edgeville , and can be retrieved from him for free if lost. Multiple swords can be obtained for free.

Its stats are identical to the adamant sword besides a lower weight, which makes it a rather inefficient weapon when compared to the skills and costs required to acquire it. The sword does not need to be equipped or held in the inventory to benefit from its Diary bonuses.

Because Desert Treasure I (and consequently the Waterfall Quest ) is necessary to complete the diary, it is not obtainable on 1 Attack pures .
13112: The Morytania legs 1 are a reward for completing all of the easy tasks in the Morytania Diary and speaking to Le-sabrè in Canifis . Its defensive bonuses are equivalent to iron platelegs , but with a lower Ranged attack penalty.
13113: The Morytania legs 2 are a reward for completing all of the medium Morytania Diary tasks and speaking to Le-sabrè in Canifis . Its defensive bonuses are equivalent to steel platelegs , but with a lower Ranged attack penalty.
13114:
The Morytania legs 3 is a reward for completing all of the tasks in the hard Morytania Diary and speaking to Le-sabre in Canifis . Its defensive bonuses are equivalent to mithril platelegs , but with a lower Ranged attack penalty.

These legs offer unlimited teleports to Burgh de Rott , which is relatively close to a bank and a useful item to have for those who do the Barrows minigame .
13115: The Morytania legs 4 are a reward for completing all of the elite Morytania Diary tasks and speaking to Le-sabrè in Canifis , and can be retrieved from her for free if lost. Multiple pairs can be obtained for free. Its defensive bonuses are equivalent to adamant platelegs , but weigh less and have a lower Ranged attack penalty.
13116:
The bonecrusher is a reward from the hard Morytania Diary . Players can obtain a bonecrusher from a ghost disciple in the Ectofuntus building whilst wearing a Ghostspeak amulet (or Morytania legs ).

When charged with ecto-tokens and carried in the inventory, the bonecrusher will automatically crush bones dropped by monsters on death. This grants the player half the Prayer experience they would have received from burying the bones themselves, or the full amount if the elite Morytania Diary is completed, and consumes one charge. The effect can be toggled with the right-click "Activity" option. A good method to obtain consistent charges is to offer the free bonemeal and buckets of slime from Robin that are given daily as part of the Morytania diary rewards .

The bonecrusher will also work on bones placed into the inventory by Hunter creatures that do so, such as those located in the Piscatoris falconry area . However, the bonecrusher does not crush bones obtained as a tertiary drop. This includes drops such as long and curved bones . Bones dropped as notes are also not affected by the bonecrusher.

Bones crushed with the bonecrusher in the Catacombs of Kourend will trigger the catacombs' Prayer restoration effect. Bones crushed while wearing a dragonbone necklace will also trigger its Prayer restoration effect. Note that these two effects do not stack with each other.

The bonecrusher can be combined with the dragonbone necklace and a hydra tail to create the bonecrusher necklace , which combines the effects of both the dragonbone necklace and the bonecrusher. Players cannot have both a bonecrusher necklace and a bonecrusher simultaneously.
13117: The Falador shield 1 is a reward from completing the easy Falador Diary tasks given to you by Sir Rebral in the White Knights' Castle courtyard and can be retrieved from him for free if lost. Its defensive bonuses are equivalent to an Iron kiteshield , except it has an added Prayer bonus and higher Ranged attack bonus.
13118: The Falador shield 2 is a reward from completing the medium Falador Diary tasks given to you by Sir Rebral in the White Knights' Castle courtyard and can be retrieved from him for free if lost. Its defensive bonuses are equivalent to a Steel kiteshield , except it has an added Prayer bonus and higher Ranged attack bonus.
13119: The Falador shield 3 is a reward from completing the hard Falador Diary tasks given to you by Sir Rebral in the White Knights' Castle courtyard and can be retrieved from him for free if lost. Its defensive bonuses are equivalent to a Mithril kiteshield , except it has an added Prayer bonus, a higher Ranged attack bonus, and weighs more.
13120: The Falador shield 4 is a reward from completing the elite Falador Diary tasks given to you by Sir Rebral in the White Knights' Castle courtyard and can be retrieved from him for free if lost. Multiple shields can be obtained for free. Its defensive bonuses are equivalent to an Adamant kiteshield , except it has an added Prayer bonus, a higher Ranged attack bonus, and weighs less.
13121:
The Ardougne cloak 1 is a reward from completing the easy Ardougne Diary given to you by Two-pints in the Flying Horse Inn at East Ardougne , and can be retrieved from her for free if lost.

This cape's teleport can be used with the nearby spirit tree or fairy ring for quick transportation with low requirements.
13122: The Ardougne cloak 2 is a reward for completing the medium Ardougne Diary given to you by Two-pints in the Flying Horse Inn in East Ardougne , and can be retrieved from her for free if lost.
13123: The Ardougne cloak 3 is a reward from completing the hard Ardougne Diary given to you by Two-pints in the Flying Horse Inn in East Ardougne , and can be retrieved from her for free if lost.
13124:
The Ardougne cloak 4 is a reward from completing the elite Ardougne Diary given to you by Two-pints in the Flying Horse Inn in East Ardougne , and can be retrieved from her for free if lost. Multiple capes can be obtained for free.

This cape currently offers the highest stab bonus in the cape slot . It is often used by players when fighting the Corporeal Beast , as well as Wilderness bosses where the free expendable nature of the cape and its Prayer bonus prove useful.

A Max cape can be combined with this cloak to create an Ardougne max cape , serving as a cosmetic upgrade.
13125:
The Explorer's ring 1 is a reward for completing all of the easy tasks in the Lumbridge & Draynor Diary and speaking to Hatius Cosaintus in Lumbridge .

Whenever the energy restore function is used, a message appears in the player's chatbox displaying how many uses are left for that day.

The Check option will send a chatbox message with the amount of energy restores and alchemy casts remaining for that day.
13126:
The Explorer's ring 2 is a reward from completing the medium Lumbridge & Draynor Diary . The ring is received from Hatius Cosaintus in Lumbridge , and can be retrieved from him for free if lost.

Whenever the teleport or energy restore functions are used, a message appears in the player's chatbox displaying how many uses are left for that day.

Upgrading from an Explorer's ring 1 resets the number of energy restore charges, but does not reset alchemy charges in the Explorer's ring 2, regardless of how many charges were left in the former.

The Check option will send a chatbox message with the amount of energy restores, teleports, and alchemy casts remaining for that day.
13127:
The explorer's ring 3 is a reward from completing the hard Lumbridge & Draynor Diary . The ring is received from Hatius Cosaintus in Lumbridge , and can be retrieved from him for free if lost.

Whenever the energy restore function is used, a message appears in the player's chatbox displaying how many uses are left for that day. Upgrading from an explorer's ring 2 resets the number of energy restore charges in the explorer's ring 3, regardless of how many charges were left in the former. The number of low alchemy charges is not reset. The Check option will send a chatbox message with the amount of energy restores and alchemy casts remaining for that day.
13128:
The Explorer's ring 4 is a reward from completing the elite Lumbridge & Draynor Diary . It is received from Hatius Cosaintus in Lumbridge , and can be retrieved from him for free if lost. Multiple rings can be obtained for free.

The Check option will send a chatbox message with the amount of energy restores, teleports, and alchemy casts remaining for that day.
13129: The Fremennik sea boots 1 are a piece of footwear obtained by completing the easy Fremennik Diary . The boots are given out by Thorodin , and can be reclaimed from him if lost. Its stats are identical to that of Iron boots , however the Fremennik sea boots 1 weigh less.
13130: Fremennik sea boots 2 are the reward for completing the medium Fremennik Diary . They are given by Thorodin south of Rellekka , and can be retrieved from him for free if lost. The boots have equivalent bonuses to steel boots , however the Fremennik sea boots 2 weigh less.
13131:
The Fremennik sea boots 3 are a reward for completing the hard Fremennik Diary tasks given to you by Thorodin , south of Rellekka , and can be retrieved from him for free if lost.

They have the same stats as Black boots , but are lighter.
13132: The Fremennik sea boots 4 is a reward from completing the elite Fremennik Diary tasks given to you by Thorodin in Rellekka and can be retrieved from him for free if lost. Multiple pairs of boots can be obtained for free. Their bonuses are equivalent to Adamant boots , with the exception of the Fremennik sea boots having a higher magic and ranged attack and weighing less.
13133: The desert amulet 1 is a reward from completing the easy Desert Diary . The amulet is received from Jarr at Shantay Pass , and can be retrieved from him for free if lost. The amulet is completely cosmetic as none of the diary rewards require the amulet to be worn and the amulet has no stats.
13134: The desert amulet 2 is a reward from completing the medium Desert Diary . The amulet is received from Jarr at Shantay Pass , and can be retrieved from him for free if lost.
13135: The desert amulet 3 is a reward from completing the hard Desert Diary . The amulet is received from Jarr at Shantay Pass , and can be retrieved from him for free if lost.
13136:
The desert amulet 4 is a reward from completing the elite Desert Diary . The amulet is received from Jarr at Shantay Pass , and can be retrieved from him for free if lost. Multiple amulets can be obtained for free. It provides unlimited Nardah teleports which take the player within close proximity of the Elidinis Statuette , which completely heals the player from damage and poison and offers restoration to run energy , prayer points , and special attack when worshipped.

The Venenatis spiderling is a pet dropped by Venenatis and Spindel , and is a much smaller version of it. Players can right click " Metamorphosis " to change between its regular and legacy forms, the latter which uses the former appearance of the pet prior to 25 January 2023.

When a player receives the pet, it will automatically try to appear as their follower. At the same time, a message in the chatbox will state You have a funny feeling like you're being followed. However, if a player receives a pet while having a follower out (for example, a cat ), it will be placed into their inventory . When this occurs, the message in the chatbox will instead state You feel something weird sneaking into your backpack.

If a player's inventory is full and they have a follower already, they will not receive the pet; it must instead be claimed from Probita in East Ardougne .

On death , if a player loses their pet (as a follower or in your inventory) it will wander around the area for 30 seconds before despawning. Even if the player returns in time, the pet cannot be picked up, and can be reclaimed from Probita.

13190:
An old school bond , commonly referred to as a bond, is an item that allows a player to pay for membership , both for Old School RuneScape and RuneScape 3 , on their account. Bonds can be purchased from Jagex for real-world money or in RuneScape for in-game money, keeping RuneScape as a free-to-play game. Bonds can be redeemed in-game for membership or traded with other players for coins or items, providing a means for players to buy membership with in-game items or (indirectly) in-game items with real-world money. Bonds are the only item that can be obtained in-game through a purchase with real-world money.

When bought with real-world money from Jagex , tradeable bonds are added to the bond pouch. These bonds may be traded with other players, sold on the Grand Exchange , or used on another player to donate it to them for free, including on ironmen players. Any of these transfers makes the bond untradeable and unable to be donated.

Players can convert untradeable bonds into tradeable bonds again by choosing the "Convert" option and paying 10% of a tradeable bond's current Grand Exchange value ( 1,184,402 coins ). The total cost of buying and converting a bond (e.g. to buy a gift bond with GP) is 13,028,419 coins . Conversely, the net value of converting and then selling a gifted bond is 10,659,615 coins . Buying a bond with GP and then immediately re-selling it is usually not profitable due to the conversion fees, though it can be profitable to buy one, convert it, and then re-sell it much later.

Players can store up to 100 bonds (tradeable, untradeable, or a mix of both) in their bond pouch. This is a feature of each player's Old School RuneScape account rather than an in-game item, and can be accessed via the Account Management interface. Attempting to buy more from the in-game interface whilst it is full will result in a game message stating Your bonds pouch is full. Please empty it before buying more. However, players can continue to buy additional bonds via the game's website, albeit they will not be given until there is sufficient space within the bond pouch when the player next logs in; a game message accompanies this, stating Your Bond Pouch is too full to hold your recent purchase. The game will try again next time you log in, if there is space then.

Bonds can never be dropped, destroyed, alchemised , or sold in shops . They are always kept on death , even when inside the Wilderness . The only way a player can get rid of a bond, other than by using it, is by trading it or feeding it to an abyssal leech .

The tanzanite helm retains the stats and abilities of the serpentine helm, the only difference being the appearance of the helmet. Like the regular helm, it cannot be equipped if it is uncharged, except when it fully degrades while being worn. The ring of the gods (i) is an upgraded version of the regular ring of the gods . It is imbued as a reward from the Nightmare Zone , costing 650,000 reward points or 325,000 with the hard tier of Combat Achievements , at Soul Wars for 260 Zeal Tokens , or by using a scroll of imbuing purchased from the Emir's Arena . Imbuing the ring also requires having a holy wrench in the inventory, though it does not consume it. The Prayer cape does not act as a substitute for imbuing the ring.

The imbued version incorporates the holy wrench's benefit of increasing prayer points restored from some prayer potions when it is equipped, and also provides an extra +4 prayer bonus compared to the regular version. The increased prayer restoration effect of the ring of the gods, Prayer cape and holy wrench do not stack . Unlike the Prayer cape and holy wrench, ring of the gods (i) must be worn to activate the prayer restoration effect and does not work when in the player's inventory.

13204:
Platinum tokens are a currency that can be obtained by using coins on any banker , exchanging for a static rate of 1,000 coins per token.

Platinum tokens can be used to replace large amounts of coins, especially more than the stack limit of 2,147,483,647 , due to the guaranteed exchange rate. This is useful for storing or trading for amounts higher than the limit. They can only be used for trading with players and not buying from, for example, a shop. For example, if the street value of an item is 4 billion coins, players can instead trade 4 million platinum tokens for the item, or use a combination of coins and tokens to equal the same amount. Taking this into account, 2,147,483,647 tokens equals 2,147,483,647,000 , which would increase the "true" limit for a stack of coins to 2,149,631,130,647 coins , which is just over 2 trillion coins.

Five platinum tokens are needed to build the tip jar in a player-owned house .

If destroyed, a replacement can be obtained from Diango in Draynor Village or from the toy box of a costume room , as part of the 2015: Toy Animals set. Ultimate Ironmen will be unable to retrieve individual pieces until the full set is stored.
13219: Stones were obtained by mining rock in the southern area of the WWF conservation area during the Big Cats & WWF holiday event. 75 in total were required to build a bridge for Humroc.
13220:
Farming helper - do not add! was an unobtainable item added alongside the Big Cats & WWF event. Presumably, it was used by Jagex moderators to test the Farming mechanics of the event. It had a right click option of "Cheat".

Despite the very clear instructions in the item's name, it was ultimately added to the game and not removed until the end of the event.
13221:
The music cape is a cape of accomplishment , obtainable by players who have unlocked all non-holiday music tracks. It is purchased from Olaf the Bard in Rellekka for 99,000 coins , granting players the cape, hood , and Air Guitar emote . The cape grants unlimited teleports to Falo the Bard , making it useful for master clue scrolls .

To trim the music cape, the player must also unlock all holiday event tracks, and have completed all quests and Achievement Diaries . After meeting the requirements, the player can right-click the cape and select the Trim option. The trimmed cape can be reverted back to the untrimmed version by selecting the Untrim option.

Should new, non-holiday songs be released, the cape will be unequipped, with the player unable to re-equip or operate it until the songs are unlocked. If a player's inventory is full, the cape will be banked ; if their bank is full, the cape will be destroyed.

This item can be stored in the cape rack of a costume room , as part of the music cape set, along with the hood . Ultimate Ironmen will be unable to retrieve individual pieces until the full set is stored.

13223:
The Music hood is the skillcape hood associated with having unlocked all non-holiday music tracks. Players may buy the hood alongside the Music cape from Olaf the Bard in Rellekka for 99,000 coins . The hood itself provides absolutely no offensive or defensive bonuses and may be worn for purely aesthetic purposes. It is the only non-black skillcape hood that is black on the inside.

While the hood is bought with the skillcape, it is not needed to perform the Air Guitar emote associated with it; the music cape's emote is unique in that it can be performed without wearing the cape.

13225:
The TzRek-Jad (translated as Baby Fire Elemental ) is a pet that can be obtained via defeating TzTok-Jad in the TzHaar Fight Cave . It is a much smaller version of TzTok-Jad . Players are twice as likely to receive the pet upon defeating TzTok-Jad if they are assigned to defeat it on a Slayer task. In addition, players may exchange their fire capes by speaking to TzHaar-Mej-Jal for a 1/200 chance of obtaining TzRek-Jad. Provided a player defeats TzTok-Jad while on a Slayer task for a 1/100 chance of the pet and hands in their cape, the overall chance of receiving the pet from either the boss or the cape is approximately 1/67.

Players who have completed all six of TzHaar-Ket-Rak's Challenges can right click " Metamorphosis " to change between the TzRek-Jad and JalRek-Jad, which is a smaller version of JalTok-Jad . Attempting to change the pet's appearance before completing the challenges will result in the chatbox stating " You must have completed TzHaar-Ket-Rak's Challenges to do that. "

When a player receives the pet, it will automatically try to appear as their follower. At the same time, a message in the chatbox will state You have a funny feeling like you're being followed. However, if a player receives a pet while having a follower out (for example, a cat ), it will be placed into their inventory . When this occurs, the message in the chatbox will instead state You feel something weird sneaking into your backpack.

If a player's inventory is full and they have a follower already, they will not receive the pet; it must instead be claimed from Probita in East Ardougne .

On death , if a player loses their pet (as a follower or in your inventory) it will wander around the area for 30 seconds before despawning. Even if the player returns in time, the pet cannot be picked up, and can be reclaimed from Probita.
13226:
A herb sack is an item that can be bought from Slayer masters for 750 Slayer reward points or from Farmer Gricoller's Rewards for 250 Tithe Farm points.

Buying one requires level 58 in Herblore (cannot be boosted) and allows the player to store up to 30 of each of the grimy normal herbs, for a total of 450 stored. A full herb sack is worth 1,077,150. Players cannot store noted or cleaned herbs in the herb sack.

The herb sack can be upgraded into the silklined herb sack, which can store up to 100 of each grimy herb. This requires using a pristine spider silk on the standard version to permanently upgrade it. The silklined herb sack is practical for farming due to the expanded capacity.

The herb sack can be manually filled by using the left-click 'Fill' option, which will deposit any grimy herbs from your inventory, unless it is full. It can be opened or closed with the right-click options 'Open' or 'Close' respectively. An open sack will automatically deposit any grimy herbs that are picked up by the player, as well as those harvested from a herb patch and Herbiboars, provided there is space for it. A closed sack will not automatically deposit herbs.

The 'Empty' option deposits herbs into the inventory, starting from the lowest level herb, and with the bank open it will deposit all of the contents into the bank. Using the 'Check' option will list all currently stored herbs within it in the chat box. Using the 'Check' option while the sack is empty will result in the messages You look in your herb sack and see: The herb sack is empty.

The herb sack is useful for killing monsters that often drop valuable herbs, such as chaos druids, flesh crawlers, aberrant spectres, and deviant spectres, since it only takes up one inventory slot. The herb sack can also be used when lighting incense burners during open altar house parties, reducing the frequency of banking or unnoting Marrentill at Phials. The base version is generally not practical for farming since it has a limit of 30 of each type, and the Tool Leprechaun can note your produce (both grimy or cleaned).

Herbs stored in the sack are not lost upon death. Herbs will stay in the herb sack upon death, unless the player has untoggled this setting. Even if the herb sack is one of the items kept on PvP death, the herbs inside the herb sack are NOT kept on death when killed by a player.
13227: The eternal crystal is an add-on dropped by Cerberus. When used with a pair of infinity boots, eternal boots will be created. This process cannot be reversed, and requires level 60 in Runecraft and Magic (boosts cannot be used), granting 200 experience in both skills.
13229:
The pegasian crystal is an add-on dropped by Cerberus . When used with a pair of ranger boots , Pegasian boots will be created. This process cannot be reversed, and requires level 60 in Runecraft and Magic (boosts cannot be used), granting 200 experience in both skills.

The crystal is inexpensive compared to the other crystals dropped by Cerberus. This is due to the small supply of Ranger boots available in the game.
13231: The primordial crystal is an add-on dropped by Cerberus . When used with a pair of dragon boots , primordial boots will be created. This process cannot be reversed, and requires level 60 in Runecraft and Magic (boosts cannot be used), granting 200 experience in both skills.
13233:
A smouldering stone is a stone dropped by Cerberus and, much more rarely, hellhounds. It can be used to upgrade the dragon axe, dragon harpoon, and dragon pickaxe into the infernal axe, infernal harpoon, and infernal pickaxe, respectively. These infernal tools have a 1/3 chance to instantly process and destroy a resource (using a charge and granting half of the normal processing experience gained in Firemaking, Cooking, and Smithing, respectively), begin with 5,000 charges, and will function as their dragon variant when all charges are depleted. Another smouldering stone or another dragon tool of that type must be used to recharge it. At current Grand Exchange prices, one charge costs approximately 644.77 coins.

Skills cannot be boosted to create infernal tools using the smouldering stone; the player must have the required base levels of either 85 Firemaking for the infernal axe, 85 Smithing for the infernal pickaxe, or 85 Cooking and 75 Fishing for the infernal harpoon. The conversion process is permanent, and the upgraded tools are untradeable.

When dropped by a hellhound, a message will appear in the player's chatbox: Something hot drops from the body of your vanquished foe.
13235:
Eternal boots are boots that require level 75 Magic and Defence to wear. They currently have the second highest Magic attack bonus and Magic defence of any pair of boots, behind the Avernic treads. They have a Magic damage bonus of 1%.

They can be created by using an eternal crystal with a pair of infinity boots. This process cannot be reversed, and requires level 60 in Runecraft and Magic (boosts cannot be used), granting 200 experience in both skills. Unlike the infinity boots, the eternal boots cannot be stored in the player owned house.
13237:
Pegasian boots are boots that require level 75 Ranged and Defence to wear. They currently have the 2nd highest ranged attack bonus of any pair of boots.

They can be created by using a pegasian crystal with a pair of ranger boots . This process cannot be reversed, and requires level 60 in Runecraft and Magic (boosts cannot be used), granting 200 experience in both skills.
13239:
Primordial boots are boots that require level 75 Strength and Defence to wear. Primordial boots provide the second highest strength bonus of any pair of boots in game, surpassed only by avernic treads that have primordial boots added to them.

They can be created by using a primordial crystal with a pair of dragon boots . This process cannot be reversed, and requires level 60 in Runecraft and Magic (boosts cannot be used), granting 200 experience in both skills.

When compared to dragon boots , primordial boots grant very similar bonuses, but the upgrade provides +1 additional melee strength bonus and +2 additional attack bonus to all melee styles, as well as an average of +5 additional defence bonus against all melee styles, at the cost of -1 magic attack bonus.
13241:
The infernal axe is a special type of axe that is created by using a smouldering stone on a dragon axe , requiring 61 Woodcutting [ not boostable ] and 85 Firemaking [ not boostable ] to create. Creating the axe grants 350 Firemaking and 200 Woodcutting experience.

While chopping a tree with the infernal axe in the inventory or equipped, there is a 1/3 chance that the logs will be consumed as they are chopped, giving half of the Firemaking experience that would usually be gained by burning them the normal way. For example, redwood logs that are burnt by the infernal axe (which does not require level 90 Firemaking) will grant 175 Firemaking experience rather than the 350 experience that is granted by burning it normally. Experience gained from logs burnt by the infernal axe is increased by the Pyromancer outfit bonus.

The infernal axe does not consume bruma roots within the Wintertodt , sulliuscep mushrooms, or celastrus bark , instead acting as a regular dragon axe when cutting these trees. When chopping infected roots , it will only consume charges when a log is burned, and will not burn demonic tears .

The infernal axe cannot be reverted back to a tradeable dragon axe or smouldering stone. If lost on death in level 20 or higher Wilderness , it is converted to 11,976 coins .

13243:
The infernal pickaxe is a special pickaxe that requires level 61 Mining to use and 60 Attack to wield. It is created by using a smouldering stone on a dragon pickaxe , requiring level 85 Smithing [ not boostable ] to create, and starts with 5,000 charges. Doing so grants 200 Mining experience and 350 Smithing experience.

Mining rocks with it equipped or in the inventory will give a 1/3 (33%) chance for the ore to automatically combust. This will destroy the ore, using one charge and granting roughly half of the Smithing experience based on the amount that would usually be gained when creating a bar from the ore. For rocks that cannot be smelted, Smithing experience will be gained based on the level required to mine the rock. At some mining spots, such as Motherlode Mine , Volcanic Mine , amethyst , gem rocks , crashed stars , dense runestone , or punishment rocks , the infernal pickaxe does not consume ores and acts as a regular dragon pickaxe.

Players can only use the standard, tradeable dragon pickaxe to create the infernal pickaxe; attempting to use other variants will result the chatbox stating " The cosmetically upgraded pickaxe is too beautiful to convert into an infernal pickaxe. "

The infernal pickaxe possesses the same special attack as the dragon pickaxe, which will boost a player's Mining level by 3. This consumes 100% special attack energy.

When mining in the Mining Guild , unidentified minerals can still be obtained when this effect consumes an ore.

13252: A sack pack is an item pack containing 100 empty sacks . They can be bought from any farming shop .
