Players can cast Lvl-7 Enchant on a zenyte necklace to enchant it into a necklace of anguish . This requires level 93 Magic and grants 110 Magic experience.
19538:
The zenyte ring is made by using a gold bar , a zenyte , and a ring mould on a furnace with a Crafting level of 89. Doing so gives the player 150 experience in Crafting.

Players can cast Lvl-7 Enchant on a zenyte ring to enchant it into a ring of suffering . This requires level 93 Magic and grants 110 Magic experience.
19541:
The zenyte amulet is made by using a ball of wool or casting the String Jewellery spell on a zenyte amulet (u) , which has no requirements and grants 4 Crafting experience. The unstrung zenyte amulet is created by using a gold bar and a zenyte on a furnace with an amulet mould in the inventory. This requires a Crafting level of 98 and provides 200 Crafting experience when made.

Players can cast Lvl-7 Enchant on a zenyte amulet to enchant it into an amulet of torture . This requires level 93 Magic and grants 110 Magic experience.
19544:
The tormented bracelet is an enchanted zenyte bracelet that requires a Hitpoints of 75 to equip. It is the second best magic item worn in the hand slot, behind the confliction gauntlets , providing the second greatest magic attack bonus, as well as a 5% bonus to magical damage . This effect stacks with other boosts.

Players can make a tormented bracelet by enchanting a zenyte bracelet with the Lvl-7 Enchant spell. This requires level 93 Magic , 20 soul runes , 20 blood runes , and 1 cosmic rune , and grants 110 Magic experience.

Players can attach a tormented ornament kit , obtained from master Treasure Trails , to create a tormented bracelet (or) . This is only cosmetic, and does not affect the bracelet's stat bonuses. It can be dismantled, returning the bracelet and ornament kit.

A tormented bracelet can be combined with a Mokhaiotl cloth and 10,000 demon tears to create the confliction gauntlets , requiring 83 Crafting and 70 Smithing . This process is irreversible.
19547:
The necklace of anguish is a necklace made by enchanting a zenyte necklace with the Lvl-7 Enchant spell. Requiring level 75 Hitpoints to equip, it is a purely offensive neck slot item, offering the second best-in-slot Ranged attack and Ranged Strength bonus.

Players can attach an anguish ornament kit, obtained from master clue scrolls, to create a necklace of anguish (or). This is only cosmetic, and does not affect the necklace's stat bonuses. It can be dismantled, returning the necklace and ornament kit.

Players can attach an etched elder venator fang to create the best-in-slot necklace, the necklace of rupture.
19550:
The ring of suffering is an enchanted zenyte ring , requiring a Hitpoints level of 75 to be equipped. It is the best-in-slot all-around defensive ring, only beaten by its imbued variant , the steel ring for melee defence, and the granite ring for ranged defence. This ring can be imbued into a ring of suffering (i) using 725,000 Nightmare Zone reward points, 300 Zeal Tokens from Soul Wars , or a scroll of imbuing (which can be purchased for 200 Emir's Arena reward points). With completion of the hard tier of Combat Achievements , these costs are halved to 362,500 Nightmare Zone reward points and 150 Zeal Tokens from Soul Wars. A ring of suffering (i) has double the bonuses of a non-imbued ring.

Players can make one by enchanting a zenyte ring with the Lvl-7 Enchant spell. This requires level 93 Magic , 20 soul runes , 20 blood runes , and 1 cosmic rune and grants 110 Magic experience.

The ring can also be charged with noted and unnoted rings of recoil to give it the recoil effect, renaming the item to ring of suffering (r) . Each ring of recoil provides 40 charges. A maximum of 100,000 charges can be stored, equivalent to 2,500 rings and costing 2,350,000 . Players can configure the charges while the ring is in their bank by right-clicking on Configure-Charges, as long as players have the required materials. Note that if the ring is discharged, the rings stored will not be refunded. The ring of recoil effect is toggle-able, so players may disable it as to not waste it during training and instead use it in activities such as fighting Zulrah and in PvP combat, where the effect may prove more useful. Charges are not lost upon death. While charged, the ring is untradeable.
19553:
The amulet of torture is an enchanted zenyte amulet requiring level 75 Hitpoints to equip. It is made by enchanting a zenyte amulet with the Lvl-7 Enchant spell, which requires level 93 Magic and grants 110 Magic experience.

As a purely offensive amulet, it gives the second highest melee attack and strength bonuses of any neck slot item, outclassed only by the amulet of rancour , where the amulet of torture is used in its creation.

Players can attach a torture ornament kit , obtained from master clue scrolls , to create an amulet of torture (or) . This is purely cosmetic, and does not affect the amulet's stat bonuses. It can be dismantled, returning the amulet and ornament kit.
19556:
Monkey is an item obtainable after the completion of Monkey Madness II. Players can get this item by searching the westernmost crate at the Crash Site Cavern entrance. Upon doing so, a dialogue box will appear in chat stating, "There's a sweet little monkey hiding in the warm crate. You gently pick it up."

Players are able to release the monkey via right-click, prompting a dialogue box to appear stating, "The monkey scampers back to the warmth of its crate." If players wish to retrieve the monkey again, they will have to search the crate back at the Crash Site Cavern entrance. Because the monkey is classed as an item rather than a pet, it cannot be stored in the menagerie of a player-owned house.

Players are also able to transform the monkey via right-click into several other variants upon completing a number of laps at the Ape Atoll Agility Course. Note that laps are only tracked upon completion of Monkey Madness II.

If the player owns an untransformed monkey and searches the crate again, the chatbox will state, "The crate is empty." However, if the player has transformed their monkey into any other variant, they will be able to grab more monkeys and transform them into all of the other variants.
19558:
Nieve is an item that may be placed into the player's inventory when Nieve is following them during Chapter IV of Monkey Madness II . Dropping it will cause Nieve to follow the player, much like a pet does.

The circumstances in which it may be forced into the inventory is unknown, although the item may have been created as a failsafe measure in the event of a glitch.
19559:
The elysian spirit shield is an item which can be retrieved from Nieve's remains during Monkey Madness II after Glough becomes mutated. The shield disintegrated as a result of Glough's devastating attack on the Slayer master.

It serves as a joke item, as the real shield is widely coveted among high level players. There are no uses for the ruined shield, and it cannot be deposited into a bank. The ruined shield is always lost on death.
19560: A charged onyx is an item obtained from a device in Glough's laboratory during Monkey Madness II. It is used with a chisel to create a deconstructed onyx, reversing the energy flow from the device and corrupting Glough's mutagen.
19562: A deconstructed onyx is an item obtained during Monkey Madness II by using a charged onyx on a chisel. It is to be placed into the device at the northern end of the laboratory, reversing the energy flow from the device and corrupting Glough's mutagen.
19564:
The royal seed pod is rewarded to the player by King Narnode Shareen after completing Monkey Madness II. Like the grand seed pod, this item can be used to teleport the player to the Grand Tree. Unlike the grand seed pod, the royal seed pod is not consumed upon use and never runs out of charges. When successfully teleporting with the royal seed pod, the message The Royal seed pod teleports you to the Grand Tree. will be displayed.

Unlike most teleports, which stop working above level 20 Wilderness, the royal seed pod is among the few items whose teleports can still be used up to level 30 Wilderness; as an easily replaceable item with a one-click teleport, many players prefer the royal seed pod for emergency escape. A 3-tick teleport delay is applied in the Revenant Caves and Wilderness boss lairs before completion of the Wilderness hard diary.

Additional pods may be purchased from King Narnode Shareen for 2 coins each.
19566:
The bronze key is found during the Monkey Madness II quest in Kruk's Dungeon , found on the upper floor of the dungeon in the agility portion of the maze. It is used to access the Bronze Door north-west of the chest in order to progress further into the dungeon.

Duplicates of the key can be obtained by searching the chest again, and opening the door consumes a key, so getting duplicates is recommended. It cannot be added to the steel key ring . This key is the agility route's counterpart to the combat damaged key and the combat scratched key .
19567: The Combat scarred key is an unobtainable item released with Monkey Madness II. Presumably, it would have been found in the maze in Kruk's Dungeon, like the Combat scratched key and Combat damaged key. The key would have been obtained from a chest as part of a scrapped third route featuring agility and thieving puzzles, which can be seen ingame but is inaccessible.
19568: A combat scratched key is a key obtained from the closed chest found in the tank route of the Monkey Madness II maze dungeon under Ape Atoll. This key can only be obtained by players who must follow the outer (southern) route. Players who follow the inner route will instead obtain a combat damaged key. These two keys are the tank route's counterpart to the agility route's bronze key.
19569: A combat damaged key is a key obtained from the closed chest found in the tank route of the Monkey Madness II maze dungeon under Ape Atoll . This key can only be obtained by players who must follow the inner route. Players who follow the outer (southern) route will instead obtain a combat scratched key . These two keys are the tank route's counterpart to the agility route's bronze key .
19570: Bronze javelin tips are items that can be made at level 6 Smithing, granting 5 javelin tips and 12.5 experience per bronze bar . They can be fletched into bronze javelins at level 3 Fletching when used with javelin shafts , which are made by using regular logs with a knife , granting 15 experience per 15 javelins made.
19572: Iron javelin tips are items that can be made at level 21 Smithing, granting 5 javelin tips and 25 experience per iron bar . They can be fletched into iron javelins at level 17 Fletching when used with javelin shafts , which are made by using regular logs with a knife , granting 30 experience per 15 javelins made.
19574: Steel javelin tips are items that can be made at level 36 Smithing, granting 5 javelin tips and 37.5 experience per steel bar . They can be fletched into steel javelins at level 32 Fletching when used with javelin shafts , which are made by using regular logs with a knife , granting 75 experience per 15 javelins made.
19576: Mithril javelin tips are items that can be made at level 56 Smithing, granting 5 javelin tips and 50 experience per mithril bar . They can be fletched into mithril javelins at level 47 Fletching when used with javelin shafts , which are made by using regular logs with a knife , granting 120 experience per 15 javelins made.
19578: Adamant javelin tips are items that can be made at level 76 Smithing, granting 5 javelin tips and 62.5 experience per adamantite bar . They can be fletched into adamant javelins at level 62 Fletching when used with javelin shafts , which are made by using regular logs with a knife , granting 150 experience per 15 javelins made.
19580:
Rune javelin tips are items that can be made at level 91 Smithing, granting 5 javelin tips and 75 experience per runite bar. They can be fletched into rune javelins at level 77 Fletching when used with javelin shafts, which are made by using regular logs with a knife, granting 187.5 experience per 15 javelins made. However, fletching javelins decreases the resale and alchemy values significantly.

As a standalone item, rune javelin tips are a profitable way to use high alchemy due to their low cost on the Grand Exchange, which easily offsets the price of Nature runes when converting them into coins.
19582:
Dragon javelin tips are attached to javelin shafts to make dragon javelins, requiring 92 Fletching, and yielding 225 Fletching experience per 15 javelins made.

In order to obtain them as a drop from most sources (e.g dragons and dragon implings), players must have completed Monkey Madness II, or they will not be dropped at all. The only exceptions to this rule are Scorpia and the Desert Treasure II bosses.

As with most dragon equipment, dragon javelin tips cannot be made from raw materials using the Smithing skill.
19584:
Javelin shafts are made by using a knife on logs , requiring 3 Fletching , yielding 15 javelin shafts and 5 Fletching experience .

Attaching javelin tips to javelin shafts will make javelins . Unlike arrows, javelins do not need to be feathered .
19586:
A light frame is a rare drop from demonic gorillas and tortured gorillas, which can be fought after the Monkey Madness II quest in the Crash Site Cavern.

They are a component in creating light ballistae. They must be attached to ballista limbs to create an incomplete light ballista. Doing so requires level 47 in Fletching, granting 15 experience in the process.
19589:
A heavy frame is a rare drop from demonic gorillas and tortured gorillas , which can be fought after the Monkey Madness II quest in the Crash Site Cavern .

They are a component in creating heavy ballista . They must be attached to ballista limbs to create an incomplete heavy ballista . Doing so requires level 72 in fletching , granting 30 experience in the process.
19592:
Ballista limbs are a component in making heavy or light ballistae . It is dropped by demonic gorillas and tortured gorillas in the Crash Site Cavern .

Ballista limbs can be attached to a light frame or a heavy frame to create an incomplete light ballista or incomplete heavy ballista , respectively. Attaching a light frame requires level 47 Fletching , granting 15 experience. Attaching a heavy frame requires level 72 Fletching, granting 30 experience.
19595: The incomplete light ballista is an item obtained by attaching ballista limbs to a light frame with a Fletching level of 47, granting 15 experience in the process. It is then attached with a ballista spring to create an unstrung light ballista, granting an additional 15 experience.
19598: The incomplete heavy ballista is an item obtained by attaching ballista limbs to a heavy frame with a Fletching level of 72, granting 30 experience in the process. It is then attached with a ballista spring to create an unstrung heavy ballista, granting an additional 30 experience.
19601:
Ballista springs are a component in making heavy or light ballistae . It is dropped by demonic gorillas and tortured gorillas in the Crash Site Cavern .

Ballista springs can be attached to an incomplete light or heavy ballista to create an unstrung light or heavy ballista , respectively. Attaching a light one requires level 47 Fletching , granting 15 experience. Attaching a heavy one requires level 72 Fletching, granting 30 experience.
19604: An unstrung light ballista is made by using a ballista spring with incomplete light ballista , requiring 47 Fletching , and yielding 15 Fletching experience . Attaching a monkey tail to it makes a light ballista , requiring 47 Fletching, and yielding 300 Fletching experience.
19607: An unstrung heavy ballista is made by using a ballista spring with incomplete heavy ballista , requiring 72 Fletching and yielding 30 Fletching experience . Attaching a monkey tail to it makes a heavy ballista , requiring 72 Fletching and yielding 600 Fletching experience.
19610:
Monkey tails are used to create heavy and light ballistae . They are dropped by demonic gorillas and tortured gorillas in the Crash Site Cavern . [ 1 ] They can also be received as a very rare drop (1 in 5,000) from hunting maniacal monkeys with a deadfall trap in Kruk's Dungeon , prompting the message You've caught a monkey's tail. Other than the missing monkey, it's in perfect condition!

Monkey tails can be attached to an unstrung light ballista to create a light ballista , requiring 47 Fletching and granting 300 experience.

Monkey tails can be attached to an unstrung heavy ballista to create a heavy ballista , requiring 72 Fletching and granting 600 experience.
19613:
The Arceuus library teleport is a magic tablet that can be broken by players to teleport north of the Grand Library of Great Kourend.

Players can create this item on the Arceuus lectern in the Ouditor's house with 1 law rune, 2 earth runes, and at least level 6 Magic while being on the Arceuus spellbook. In addition, a dark essence block is required to substitute soft clay.

The player does not need to have the relevant Magic level to use the tablet, which shares the same rule with all tablets and the player will not receive any experience, although making the teleport tablet does give 10 experience in Magic.
19615:
The Draynor manor teleport is a magic tablet that can be broken by players to teleport to Draynor Manor .

Players can create this item on the Arceuus lectern in the Ouditor 's house with 1 law rune , 1 earth rune , 1 water rune , and level 17 Magic while being on the Arceuus spellbook . In addition, a dark essence block is required to substitute soft clay .

The player does not need to have the relevant Magic level to use the tablet, which shares the same rule with all tablets and the player will not receive any experience , although making the teleport tablet does give 16 experience in Magic.
19617:
The Mind altar teleport is a magic tablet that can be broken by players to teleport to the entrance of the Mind Altar .

Players can create this item on the Arceuus lectern in the Ouditor 's house with 1 law rune , 2 mind runes , and level 28 Magic while being on the Arceuus spellbook . In addition, a dark essence block is required to substitute soft clay .

The player does not need to have the relevant Magic level to use the tablet, which shares the same rule with all tablets and the player will not receive any experience , although making the teleport tablet does give 22 experience in Magic.
19619:
The Salve graveyard teleport is a magic tablet that can be broken by players to teleport to the River Salve graveyard, by the ghouls at the entrance to Mort Myre Swamp .

If the player has not completed the Priest in Peril quest and spoke to Drezel before entering Morytania , they will receive a message in the chatbox stating You must have completed Priest in Peril and received Drezel's warning to cast this spell.

Players can create this item on the Arceuus lectern in the Ouditor 's house with 1 law rune , 2 soul runes , and level 40 Magic while being on the Arceuus spellbook . In addition, a dark essence block is required to substitute soft clay . Making the teleport tablet grants 30 experience in Magic.

The player does not need to have the required spellbook or Magic level in order to use this tablet, but using the tablet does not grant any experience.
19621:
The Fenkenstrain's castle teleport is a magic tablet that can be broken by players to teleport to Fenkenstrain's Castle .

Players can create this item on the Arceuus lectern in the Ouditor 's house with 1 law rune , 1 earth rune , 1 soul rune , and level 48 Magic while being on the Arceuus spellbook . In addition, a dark essence block is required to substitute soft clay .

The player does not need to have the relevant Magic level to use the tablet, which shares the same rule with all tablets and the player will not receive any experience , although making the teleport tablet does give 50 experience in Magic. The player needs to have completed Priest in Peril and have received Drezel's warning in order to use this tablet.
19623:
The West ardougne teleport is a magic tablet that can be broken by players to teleport to West Ardougne . Completion of Biohazard is required to use this tablet.

Players can create this item on the Arceuus lectern in the Ouditor 's house with 2 law runes , 2 soul runes , and level 61 Magic while being on the Arceuus spellbook . In addition, a dark essence block is required to substitute soft clay .

The player does not need to have the relevant Magic level to use the tablet, which shares the same rule with all tablets and the player will not receive any experience , although making the teleport tablet does give 68 experience in Magic.
19625:
The Harmony island teleport is a magic tablet that can be broken by players to teleport to Harmony Island. Completion of The Great Brain Robbery is required to use this tablet.

Players can create this item on the Arceuus lectern in the Ouditor's house with 1 law rune, 1 soul rune, 1 nature rune, and level 65 Magic while being on the Arceuus spellbook. A dark essence block is also required. Making the teleport tablet grants 74 Magic experience.

Completion of The Great Brain Robbery is required to use this tablet but the quest is not required to create the tablet. The player does not otherwise need to have the Magic level to cast the spell in order to use the tablet, but will not receive any experience for doing so.

The tablet is useful for players that have completed the elite tier of the Morytania Diary so that they can access the Harmony Island herb patch without having to switch away from the Lunar Spellbook, which is often used during farm runs.
19627:
Cemetery teleport is a magic tablet that can be broken by players to teleport to The Forgotten Cemetery in level 31 Wilderness .

Because this tablet teleports players to the Wilderness, a warning will appear upon clicking the "Break" option on the tablet. This can be toggled by right-clicking the "Configure" option.

Players with 71 Magic can create this item on the Arceuus lectern in the Ouditor 's house with 1 law rune , 1 soul rune , 1 blood rune , and a dark essence block instead of the soft clay normally required for teleport tablets. Making the teleport tablet grants 82 Magic experience .

As with all magic tablets, players do not need to have the relevant Magic level to use this tablet, and will not receive any experience for doing so.
19629:
The Barrows teleport is a magic tablet that can be broken by players to teleport to the Barrows. To use this tablet, the user must have completed the Priest in Peril quest and must have passed through the barrier to Morytania at least once.

Players with 83 Magic and the Arceuus spellbook active can create this item on the Arceuus lectern in the Ouditor's house with 2 law runes, 2 soul runes, 1 blood rune, and a dark essence block (instead of the soft clay required for standard spellbook magic tablets). Making this tablet grants 90 Magic experience, the same as if casting the spell.

As with all magic tablets, there is no Magic level requirement to use this tablet, and no Magic experience is granted for using it.

Making a Barrows tablet is one of the challenges assigned by Sherlock for a master clue step.
19631:
The Ape atoll teleport is a magic tablet that can be broken by players to teleport to the Ape Atoll Dungeon . Completion of Monkey Madness I is required to use this tablet. Neither the post-quest 10th squad training from Daero nor Freeing King Awowogei Recipe for Disaster subquest need to be completed.

Players with level 90 Magic can create this item on the Arceuus lectern in the Ouditor 's house if they have the Arceuus spellbook enabled. This requires 2 law runes , 2 soul runes , 2 blood runes , and a dark essence block instead of the soft clay required for most magic tablets. Making the tablet grants 100 Magic experience, the same as casting the Ape Atoll Teleport spell. It is not required to have Monkey Madness I completed in order to make a tablet.

As with all magic tablets, the player does not need to have the relevant Magic level to use the tablet, but using the tablet does not grant the player any experience.

Creating an Ape Atoll teleport tablet is a task for the elite Kourend & Kebos Diary .
19634:
The soul bearer is an item that sends all of the ensouled heads from their inventory to the player's bank. To use the soul bearer, the player must pick up the ensouled head(s) and select the 'Fill' option on the Soul Bearer. It is obtained from the Bear Your Soul miniquest after the Key Master repairs the damaged soul bearer .

The soul bearer is an ancient artefact that draws souls from one place to another, enabling them to travel within the River of Souls across the dimensions.

Each ensouled head costs one charge. Charging the soul bearer costs one blood rune and one soul rune per charge ( 738 ). Players can configure the charges while the soul bearer is in their bank by right-clicking on Configure-Charges, as long as players have the required materials. The soul bearer can hold 1,000 charges ( 738,000 ) and charges can be removed at any time by using the Uncharge right-click option.

If a player loses the soul bearer, they can acquire another one by using a spade to dig in the Arceuus church crypt again.

Ultimate ironmen cannot use the soul bearer.
19636:
The damaged soul bearer is an item found during the Bear Your Soul miniquest . It is found in the crypts of the Arceuus church after speaking to Aretha while having the Soul Journey book in their possession.

It is brought to the Key Master to repair it to a soul bearer .
19637:
Soul Journey is a book written by Aretha . It can be found in the Grand Library in Arceuus . Professor Gracklebone , Sam , and Villia may ask the player to find this book for them, in which their location is random and changes every 80-100 minutes. Upon handing in the book to the player's customer, a book of arcane knowledge is rewarded.

Players cannot perform a drop trick to obtain more books, as they will disappear once dropped; this is done to prevent the player from obtaining multiple copies in order to gain experience books quicker by having the book readily available after a customer asks for it.

The book speaks about the River of Souls and its role in Great Kourend's perception of the afterlife, along with excerpts from past experiences involving the Key Master 's acceptance in the role of guarding Cerberus . It also mentions the soul bearer , an ancient artefact.

After reading the book for the first time, the chatbox will state The book referred to an artefact being buried in Kourend, but the author did not specify where it was buried. Maybe you could persuade her to change her mind. This begins the Bear Your Soul miniquest .
19639:
The black Slayer helmet is a piece of equipment that is worn in the helmet slot. It is a cosmetic upgrade to the Slayer helmet .

It can be created by adding an unstuffed Kbd heads after purchasing the ability King black bonnet for 1,000 Slayer reward points from any Slayer master . This is reversible, and the head will be returned to the inventory along with the slayer helmet's components. If a player loses the black slayer helmet in a PvP death, the Kbd heads will be placed in their gravestone.
19641:
The black Slayer helmet (i) is a piece of equipment that is worn in the helmet slot. It is a cosmetic upgrade to the Slayer helmet (i) .

It can be created by adding an unstuffed Kbd heads after purchasing the ability King black bonnet for 1,000 Slayer reward points from any Slayer master . This is reversable, and the head will be returned to the inventory along with the slayer helmet's components. If a player loses the black slayer helmet (i) in a PvP death, the Kbd heads will be placed in their gravestone.
19643:
The green Slayer helmet is a piece of equipment that is worn in the helmet slot. It is a cosmetic upgrade to the Slayer helmet .

It can be created by adding an unstuffed Kq head (a tattered kq head will not work) after purchasing the ability Kalphite khat for 1,000 Slayer reward points from any Slayer master . This is reversible, and the head will be returned to the inventory along with the slayer helmet's components. If a player loses the green slayer helmet in a PvP death, the Kq head will be placed in their gravestone.
19645:

This is reversible, and the head will be returned to the inventory along with the slayer helmet's components. If a player loses the green slayer helmet (i) in a PvP death, the Kq head will be placed in their gravestone.
19647:
The red Slayer helmet is a piece of equipment that is worn in the helmet slot. It is a cosmetic upgrade to the Slayer helmet.

It can be created by adding an unstuffed abyssal demon head after purchasing the ability Unholy helmet for 1,000 Slayer reward points from any Slayer master. This is reversible, and the head will be returned to the inventory along with the slayer helmet's components. If a player loses the red slayer helmet in a PvP death, the abyssal demon head will be placed in their gravestone.
19649:
The red Slayer helmet (i) is a piece of equipment that is worn in the helmet slot. It is a cosmetic upgrade to the Slayer helmet (i).

It can be created by adding an unstuffed abyssal demon head after purchasing the ability Unholy helmet for 1,000 Slayer reward points from any Slayer master. This is reversible, and the head will be returned to the inventory along with the slayer helmet's components. If a player loses the red slayer helmet (i) in a PvP death, the abyssal demon head will be placed in their gravestone.
19651: The Hosidius teleport is a magic tablet that can be broken by players to teleport just outside the Hosidius house portal . It can be created at level 25 Construction by using a scroll of redirection on a teleport to house tablet.
19653:
A golovanova fruit top is an ingredient used in the Cooking skill to make botanical pies , a food item used to boost Herblore by 4 levels.

It can only be obtained by stealing from fruit stalls in Hosidius . This requires level 25 Thieving .
19656: An uncooked botanical pie is made by adding a Golovanova fruit top to a Pie shell . It can be baked with level 52 Cooking to make a botanical pie , granting 180 Cooking experience when successfully baked.
19659:
Botanical pie is a type of pie that restores 14 Hitpoints in total, 2 bites each healing for 7. It also temporarily boosts Herblore by 4, the second highest boost available, and the highest reliable boost. A pie dish will remain after both bites are consumed.

It can be created by baking an uncooked botanical pie on a cooking range , requiring level 52 Cooking and granting 180 experience when successful. When cooking there is a chance to fail, resulting in burnt pie . The burn rate decreases as the player's Cooking level increases. Botanical pie is one of a number of foods with a reduced burn rate while using the Lumbridge Castle range with Cook's Assistant completed. It will stop burning entirely at Cooking level 84, or 52 when using the Lumbridge range. Alternatively, casting the Bake Pie spell from the lunar spellbook will always create a pie without burning it.
19662:
Botanical pie is a type of pie that restores 14 Hitpoints in total, 2 bites each healing for 7. It also temporarily boosts Herblore by 4, the second highest boost available, and the highest reliable boost. A pie dish will remain after both bites are consumed.

It can be created by baking an uncooked botanical pie on a cooking range , requiring level 52 Cooking and granting 180 experience when successful. When cooking there is a chance to fail, resulting in burnt pie . The burn rate decreases as the player's Cooking level increases. Botanical pie is one of a number of foods with a reduced burn rate while using the Lumbridge Castle range with Cook's Assistant completed. It will stop burning entirely at Cooking level 84, or 52 when using the Lumbridge range. Alternatively, casting the Bake Pie spell from the lunar spellbook will always create a pie without burning it.
19665:
A damaged monkey tail is an item obtained from hunting maniacal monkeys. It is a Monkey tail which has been damaged during the hunting process, and as such it cannot be used to string ballistae .

With level 10 Crafting , a damaged monkey tail can be used with a knife in order to create sinew , granting 15 experience in doing so.
19668:
Minecart control scrolls were instructions given to the player by Miriam. They were used to set up the Lovakengj Minecart Network. They were given to Loinur, Mogrim, Traxi, Raeli, and Stuliette to complete the network. The scrolls were removed on 10 January 2024 after an update removing any requirements to use the Lovakengj Minecart Network.

Players could use the Check option to find out the locations of the NPCs.
19669:
Redwood logs are logs received from cutting redwoods , which are found in the Woodcutting Guild or can be grown from a redwood sapling in the Farming Guild (with level 90 Farming ). They require a Woodcutting level of 90 to chop and yield 380 Woodcutting experience per log.

Redwood logs can be burnt with a Firemaking level of 90, giving 350 experience per log. They can be fletched into 105 arrow shafts , a redwood shield , or a redwood hiking staff . They are also used in creation of redwood pyre logs , redwood bird house , building a redwood fence in the superior garden of a player-owned house , lighting the Abyssal lantern (requiring 90 Firemaking), or to craft a perfected quetzal whistle .
19672: Redwood pyre logs are created by using a sacred oil (4) on redwood logs , granting 20 Firemaking experience. They are used during the Shades of Mort'ton minigame to cremate the remains of all shades, and are among the only two types of pyre logs (alongside rosewood pyre logs ) that can be used to cremate Urium remains . They require level 95 Firemaking to ignite, and grant 500 Firemaking experience when used to cremate a shade (750 with Morytania Diary 4 complete).
19675:
Arclight is a demonbane weapon requiring level 75 Attack to wield. An upgraded variant of Darklight , Arclight features an enhanced passive effect in addition to modest improvements in attack bonus and speed.

If Arclight is lost, it can be replaced by paying Sir Prysin 1,000 coins for Darklight and enhancing it with ancient shards again. Players can possess multiple copies of Arclight.

After reading Duradel's notes , at level 74 Smithing , players can use either a fully charged or infused Arclight with a tormented synapse to upgrade the weapon to Emberlight .
19677: Ancient shards are obtained from monsters found within the Catacombs of Kourend (excluding ghosts ). Ancient shards are also used to charge Arclight. One shard provides 333 charges, three shards provide 1,000 charges; up to a maximum of 10,000. 19685:
The dark totem is an item that can be created by combining the dark totem base , dark totem middle , and dark totem top . The totem pieces are dropped in that order and duplicates drop after all three are obtained. It is used on the altar in the centre of the Catacombs of Kourend to access the lower level of the catacombs to fight Skotizo . The totem is consumed when using it on the altar regardless of the outcome of the fight.

All three components can be found by killing monsters (excluding ghosts) in the Catacombs of Kourend and in the Giants' Den . Superior slayer monsters have a 100% chance of dropping a totem piece; all others have a chance equal to 1 / ( 500 − H ) , where H is the monster's Hitpoints . Since the improvement in drop rate as monster HP increases is very small, dark totem pieces can be most quickly obtained by killing low HP monsters within the catacombs, such as hill giants.

Assembling the dark totem results in a chatbox message stating You bring the totem pieces together with a click. It looks kind of like an arcane key and pulses with dark power in your hand.

A fully-assembled dark totem can also be rarely obtained from Skotizo .

The Helm of Raedwald is obtained from completing the fifth, final clue during the Crack the Clue event. It is part of the clue hunter outfit . This item has the same stat bonuses as an iron full helm . Unlike the other parts of the clue hunter outfit, it is not considered warm clothing for the purposes of Wintertodt .

In order to obtain the helmet, the player must dig between the four iron rocks by the cave entrance east of the Clock Tower while having a spade , a nature rune , a superantipoison with one dose remaining, and a pair of leather boots .

This item can be stored in the armour case of a costume room .

The Helm of Raedwald was not found until just over a year (377 days) after the fourth clue was made available, alongside several hints given by Jagex Moderators , on 18 July 2017 . An additional sentence was added to the examine text with an update the same week to commemorate the first player that found it, Pikachu Yip .

The amulet of eternal glory is a special dragonstone amulet possessing identical stats and features of a regular amulet of glory, except it has unlimited teleport charges instead of the regular four or six maximum charges. However, it cannot be mounted in a player-owned house.

It is made (only after completion of Heroes Quest) while charging amulets of glory (including the trimmed variant) with fewer than six charges at the Fountain of Rune in the Wilderness. Each amulet recharged has a 1 in 25,000 chance to be turned into an amulet of eternal glory. When this occurs, a message in the chatbox will appear, stating: "The power of the fountain is transferred into an amulet of eternal glory. It will now have unlimited charges."

Like other dragonstone jewellery, it is one of the few items whose teleports will work up to level 30 Wilderness, while most other means of teleportation will not work above level 20 Wilderness.

As with the regular charged amulet of glory, it retains the passive effect which increases chance to mine gems and gem rocks.
19710:
The ring of suffering (i) is an upgraded version of the regular ring of suffering . It can be imbued as a reward from the Nightmare Zone , costing 725,000 reward points or 362,500 with the hard tier of Combat Achievements , at Soul Wars for 300 Zeal Tokens , or by using a scroll of imbuing purchased from Emir's Arena for 200 points. Its stats are double those of the ring of suffering.

The ring can also be charged with rings of recoil to give it the recoil effect, renaming the item to ring of suffering (ri) . Each ring of recoil provides 40 charges, assuming the ring of recoil has not been drained prior. A maximum of 100,000 charges can be stored, equivalent to 2,500 rings, at a cost of 2,350,000 coins . Players can configure the charges while the ring is in their bank by right-clicking on Configure-Charges, as long as players have the required materials. If a player uncharged the ring, the recoil rings stored will not be refunded. The ring of recoil effect is toggle-able, so players may disable it as to not waste it during training and instead use it in activities such as fighting Zulrah , or in PvP combat, where the effect may prove more useful. Charges are not lost upon death.

If not protected, dying to another player will cause the imbued ring to lose its imbued status, however the player will be reimbursed the Nightmare Zone points , Zeal Tokens or Scroll of imbuing to re-imbue it via the aforementioned methods. Dying to a monster will not remove its imbued effect.

The occult necklace (or) is an occult necklace with an occult ornament kit attached to it. The attached ornament kit gives no additional bonuses, and is only used to add aesthetics to the necklace. It costs 3,338,698 for both the parts to make the occult necklace (or).

A double eye patch is an item that is obtained by paying Patchy to sew together a left and right eye patch , resembling a pair of sunglasses. This item can be stored in the mahogany treasure chest of a costume room under master tier. Alternatively, the item can be used on the opened treasure chest to insert it without viewing the interface.

The Bloodhound is a pet that can be received as a rare reward from master Treasure Trails at a rate of 1/1,000. Using a set of bones on the bloodhound will result in the chatbox message You give the dog the bone - it eats it.

When a player receives the pet, it will automatically try to appear as their follower. At the same time, a message in the chatbox will state You have a funny feeling like you're being followed. However, if a player receives a pet while having a follower out (for example, a cat), it will be placed into their inventory. When this occurs, the message in the chatbox will instead state You feel something weird sneaking into your backpack.

If a player's inventory is full and they have a follower already, they will not receive the pet; it must instead be claimed from Probita in East Ardougne.

On death, if a player loses their pet (as a follower or in your inventory) it will wander around the area for 30 seconds before despawning. Even if the player returns in time, the pet cannot be picked up, but can be reclaimed from Probita.

19812:
A key is an item needed to unlock a chest or drawer during a Treasure Trail.

There will be a clue telling you where to get it. The key is a drop only when carrying the clue scroll. It disappears when used to open the chest or drawer. Keys are non-tradeable objects, specific to the player who finds them. They are used on all levels of treasure trails.

It is possible to obtain more than one key using the drop trick. However, after taking a clue from the chest/drawer, the key won't open it again, and the player gets a message: "The chest (or drawer) is locked." Keys obtained this way from the same clue will still remain in the bank; however, keys obtained from different clues will not stack.

19836:
A reward casket (master) is received after completing the final clue of a master clue scroll trail, and contains the final reward for the trail. Opening the reward casket is required for treasure trail completion to be tracked on the HiScores and collection log .

The player can possess unlimited amounts of reward caskets up to the stack limit . Players are eligible to receive more clue scrolls regardless of how many reward caskets are in the player's posession.
19837:
Torn clue scrolls are parts of the next clue scroll step during a master clue . Solving each part of a three-part master cryptic clue gives a torn clue scroll, which can be combined to continue the treasure trail .

Note for Ultimate Ironmen: When dying with a torn clue scroll, the pieces will drop to the ground. However, torn clue scrolls will be destroyed upon attempting to pick them up, and the player will receive the chatbox message "The torn clue scroll disintegrates".

Torn clue scrolls are always kept on death, whether protected or not, as it is an untradeable item. If not protected it will go to the gravestone. In the Wilderness a clue box can be brought if the player prefers an unprotected clue scroll to remain in their inventory upon death. Note that the box will always be lost.

In clue juggling , torn clue scrolls can only be juggled with another clue which also has 3 parts needed to solve it. Attempting to combine the clue scroll parts after swapping out the clue scroll in your inventory with a different master clue that only requires 1 action (e.g. a Falo the Bard clue) results in the parts being discarded, forcing the player to gather them again.

Challenge scrolls are riddles given to players by an NPC during a Treasure Trail. Challenge scrolls appear in medium, hard, and elite clue steps. Players must solve the challenge scroll in order to advance in their Treasure Trail. The challenge scroll is not a separate step in the Treasure Trail.

The questions for the challenge scrolls are always the same. Players do not have to read the challenge scroll in order to answer the question. Players only need to talk to the NPC again after receiving the scroll to answer the answer. There are no penalties for incorrect answers.

It features sounds of a zombie 's defensive sounds when the player attacks an opponent, and sounds of a zombie's death when wielded, unwielded and stored into a mahogany treasure chest .

A cyclops head is a piece of headgear obtained as a reward from hard Treasure Trails. It has no combat bonuses, and is used only for aesthetics.

This item can be stored in the treasure chest of a costume room, provided that the interface of the corresponding clue tier is opened before attempting to store the item. Alternatively, the item can be used on the opened treasure chest to insert it without viewing the interface.
19918:
The nunchaku is a two-handed weapon that can be received as a reward from hard Treasure Trails .

It has stats comparable to an iron warhammer , albeit with 3 more strength bonus. It is also a two-handed weapon, meaning players cannot use a shield at the same time.

This item can be stored in the treasure chest of a costume room , provided that the interface of the corresponding clue tier is opened before attempting to store the item. Alternatively, the item can be used on the opened treasure chest to insert it without viewing the interface.

A strange device is an item used in the Hot & Cold challenge of a beginner or master clue .

The beginner clue strange device can be obtained by talking to Reldo in the Varrock Palace library, while the master clue strange device can be obtained by talking to Jorral in the outpost north-west of West Ardougne . The player must have an active clue step directing them to one of Reldo or Jorral to obtain a strange device, but once obtained it does not need to be returned and can be kept in the bank. Note that one must have completed Making History before Jorral will give them a strange device for a master clue.

The strange device changes temperature as the player moves about. Its temperature is based on the distance of the treasure from the player, measured in the number of steps it would take to reach the treasure, ignoring any obstacles. The warmer the key gets, the closer the player is to the treasure.

Clicking "Feel Strange device " gives information on its temperature. If using the strange device obtained from Jorral used for master clues, this will deal 3-8 damage to the player each time , which can be fatal . If you do not have an active master clue with a hot & cold step, the device will be inactive, and using it will not damage you.

A list of possible locations can be found here .

The charge dragonstone jewellery scroll is a consumable scroll obtained as a reward from all levels of Treasure Trails, excluding beginner clue scrolls. In order to use the scroll, players must first have completed the Heroes' Quest.

The scroll allows a player to charge any amulet of glory, combat bracelet, and skills necklace with 4 charges, although the former requires completion of Heroes' Quest and the latter two can only be charged after completion of the Legends' Quest. One scroll will charge all uncharged and partially charged unnoted jewellery in the inventory, as well as any equipped jewellery.

This item cannot charge the ring of wealth; only the Fountain of Rune in the deep Wilderness can do so.

The gnomish firelighter is an item obtainable by completing medium Treasure Trails . It may be charged with any one colour of gnomish firelighters at a time. Like other firelighters, it also increases the chance of a log to be successfully burned, additionally giving an extra 10 Firemaking experience per log when charged.

The maximum number of charges is 1,000.

While charged, it can be used with any set of standard logs in the same manner as one would use a tinderbox with any other set of logs to produce the same colour of fire as the firelighters it is charged with. One charge is used up for every coloured fire created.

If another colour is desired, one may simply uncharge the firelighter at any time; this will return any unused firelighters and free the device up to be charged with another style of firelighter.

Gnomish firelighters do not function as a tinderbox when out of charges, and only standard logs may be used to create coloured fires.

Puzzle boxes can be obtained by doing hard, elite, and master Treasure Trails . Before you are able to continue with your clue scroll, you will have to complete the puzzle.

A puzzle box is always scrambled 101 times before being handed to the player, by randomly sliding a piece into the empty position starting from the solved state. [ 1 ]

If you have a duplicate puzzle box, (obtained by a method such as the Drop trick ) in your inventory or bank after completing the clue, you cannot obtain another clue.

The fire cape is a melee cape obtained as a reward for completing the TzHaar Fight Cave . It is the second best melee cape in the game, outclassed only by the infernal cape . In order to obtain the fire cape, players must survive all waves of TzHaar Fight Caves and defeat TzTok-Jad . Note that the cape will not be awarded should both the player and TzTok-Jad die simultaneously, even though the boss log will count the kill. The player must be taken out of the cave by the game recognising TzTok-Jad's death; if they are removed from the cave due to dying, the game considers the player to have failed the challenge.

A fire cape must be shown to TzHaar-Ket guards around the centre of the city to allow further access to Mor Ul Rek . This does not consume the fire cape. However, to enter the Inferno , a fire cape must be sacrificed by giving it to TzHaar-Ket-Keh . This is a one-time fee.

If the player dies a PvP death and the fire cape is unprotected, it will remain in the player's inventory; however, the item will be in a broken, unusable state and must be repaired by using it on Perdu and paying him 150,000 coins .

When worn, players are granted the fiery attribute and will therefore receive additional damage in PvP from the special effects of Pearl bolts (e) and Pearl dragon bolts (e) .

The fire max cape is the result of combining a fire cape with a max cape , during which the max hood required to be in the player's inventory will automatically convert to the fire max hood .

Like the other max cape variants (a max cape combined with another cape slot item), the fire max cape does not have the max cape's stats or perks with the following exceptions when worn:

The max cape and fire cape can be separated by using a knife on the cape. Mac will also buy back a max cape, along with its variants, for 1,900,800 coins each. He will return the secondary item any max cape variant was combined with upon doing so.

If the player dies a PvP death and the item is unprotected, it will remain in the player's inventory; however, the item will be in a broken, unusable state and must be repaired by using it on Perdu and paying him 150,000 coins .

A fire max cape cannot be gambled for a chance at TzRek-Jad .

The bronze defender is the weakest defender . It is similar to a dagger, but held in the off-hand in place of a shield. The bronze defender is dropped by cyclopes on the top floor of the Warriors' Guild . Entry to the Cyclops room requires a minimum of 100 Warrior guild tokens .

If the player dies to a PvP death and the bronze defender is not one of the player's protected items, it will remain in the player's inventory, but will become broken , which means the item is unusable and must be repaired with 1,000 coins by using the item on Perdu .
20451:
The iron defender is a defender made of iron. It is dropped by any of the Cyclops on the top floor of the Warriors' Guild, but only once players have obtained a bronze defender. It is one of the two defenders that does not provide a strength bonus, along with the bronze defender.

If the player dies to a PvP death and the iron defender is not one of the player's protected items, it will remain in the player's inventory, but will become broken, which means the item is unusable and must be repaired with 2,000 coins by using the item on Perdu.

If the player dies to a PvP death and the steel defender is not one of the player's protected items, it will remain in the player's inventory, but will become broken , which means the item is unusable and must be repaired with 2,500 coins by using the item on Perdu .

If the player dies to a PvP death and the black defender is not one of the player's protected items, it will remain in the player's inventory, but will become broken , which means the item is unusable and must be repaired with 5,000 coins by using the item on Perdu .

20457:
The mithril defender is a defender made of mithril. It can be obtained by killing cyclopes on the top floor of the Warriors' Guild, but only if you have a black defender in your inventory or if you have shown a black defender to Kamfreena. It is held in the shield slot and requires 20 Attack and Defence to wield.

If the player dies to a PvP death and the mithril defender is not one of the player's protected items, it will remain in the player's inventory, but will become broken, which means the item is unusable and must be repaired with 15,000 coins by using the item on Perdu.
20459:
The adamant defender is a defender made out of adamant . It can be obtained by killing cyclopes on the top floor of the Warriors' Guild with a mithril defender in the inventory or after you have shown a mithril defender to Kamfreena . It is held in the shield slot and requires 30 Attack and Defence to wield.

If the player dies to a PvP death and the adamant defender is not one of the player's protected items, it will remain in the player's inventory, but will become broken , which means the item is unusable and must be repaired with 25,000 coins by using the item on Perdu .
20461:
The rune defender is the 3rd strongest defender . It is used for its attack bonus and is held in the off-hand in place of a shield . It requires 40 Attack and 40 Defence to wield. The rune defender is dropped by cyclopes on the top floor of the Warriors' Guild after showing an adamant defender or better as the player enters the room.

The rune defender's slash and crush defensive bonuses are the same as a black kiteshield , but its stab defence bonus is slightly less than an adamant square shield . However, it is much more commonly used for its melee bonuses, as it gives the same bonus to strength as the toktz-ket-xil (obsidian shield) and has melee attack bonuses. A rune defender is commonly combined with weapons such as a dragon scimitar or an abyssal whip as a result.

The defender is popular among players of higher combat levels due to its offensive stats. It can be considered to be the third best off-hand item for melee training, only beaten by the dragon defender and Avernic defender , and is commonly used in PvP situations as re-obtaining a rune defender is easier than re-obtaining a dragon or Avernic one.

If the player dies to a PvP death and the rune defender is not one of the player's protected items, it will remain in the player's inventory, but will become broken , which means the item is unusable and must be repaired with 35,000 coins by using the item on Perdu . Any ornament kit on the item will also be lost on death.

Players can attach a Rune defender ornament kit , obtained from hard Treasure Trails , to create a Rune defender (t) . This is only cosmetic, and does not affect the defender's stat bonuses. It can be dismantled, returning the defender and ornament kit.
20463:
The dragon defender is the second strongest defender , behind the Avernic defender . It is used for its attack and strength bonus and is held in the shield slot. It requires level 60 Defence to equip.

The dragon defender can only be obtained from the stronger level 106 Cyclopes found exclusively in the Warrior Guild 's basement. To enter the basement for the first time, a player must show a rune defender to Lorelai , who will then grant them permanent access. Warrior Guild tokens are still required for time spent inside the basement unless the player has an Attack Cape equipped. Players can obtain a dragon defender without having a rune defender in their bank. [ 1 ] Players can obtain the dragon defender without having 60 Defence . [ 2 ]

Its melee defensive bonuses are comparable to those of an adamant square shield , with slight differences. Its strength bonus is surpassed by both the dragonfire shield and the Avernic defender , which give +7 and +8 strength bonuses, respectively. However, the dragon defender is more commonly used than either of these for melee training, due to its superior melee attack bonuses over the dragonfire shield and the overall rarity of the Avernic defender .

If the player dies to a PvP death and the dragon defender is not one of the player's protected items, it will remain in the player's inventory, but will become broken , which means the item is unusable and must be repaired with 240,000 coins by using the item on Perdu .
20465:
The Void Knight top is a piece of Void Knight equipment . It can be bought from a Void Knight for 250 Void Knight commendation points through the Pest Control mini game, although a player must have at least 42 Attack , Strength , Defence , Hitpoints , Ranged , and Magic , along with 22 Prayer to buy and wear one.

It is worn in combination with the other pieces of Void Knight Armour to achieve the designated set effect, depending on which helm is worn. This chestpiece does not interfere with Ava's devices . Unlike the Void knight robe , the Void knight top doesn't have more Magic Defence than its blessed d'hide counterparts (+45, as opposed to a blessed d'hide body's +50).

It can be upgraded into an Elite void top for 200 Void Knight commendation points, although a player must have completed the hard Western Provinces Diary tasks to be able to upgrade it. The top can also be given to the Dodgy Squire in exchange for 200 Void Knight commendation points.

If the player dies a PvP death at level 20 Wilderness or below and the item is unprotected, it will remain in the player's inventory; however, the item will be in a broken, unusable state and must be repaired by using it on Perdu and paying him 180,000 coins .

If the player dies a PvP death above level 20 Wilderness and the item is unprotected, it will be converted to coins. To prevent this, a Trouver parchment and a payment of 500,000 coins can be given to Perdu in order to permanently lock the item. The locked item will remain in the player's inventory; however, the item will be in a mangled, unusable state and must be repaired by using it on Perdu and paying him 500,000 coins.
20467:
The elite Void top is a piece of Elite Void Knight equipment . It can be upgraded from a Void knight top for 200 Void Knight commendation points by speaking to the Elite Void Knight , although a player must have completed the Hard Western Provinces Diary to be able to upgrade it. It is worn in combination with the other pieces of Void Knight Armour to achieve the designated set effect, depending on which helm is worn. The stats are the same as the Void knight top , but with a +3 prayer bonus , as well as a +2.5% damage boost to Ranged and +5% damage boost to Magic when worn with the Elite void robe .

If the player dies a PvP death at level 20 Wilderness or below and the item is unprotected, it will remain in the player's inventory; however, the item will be in a broken, unusable state and must be repaired by using it on Perdu and paying him 250,000 coins .

If the player dies a PvP death above level 20 Wilderness and the item is unprotected, it will be converted to coins. To prevent this, a Trouver parchment and a payment of 500,000 coins can be given to Perdu in order to permanently lock the item. The locked item will remain in the player's inventory; however, the item will be in a mangled, unusable state and must be repaired by using it on Perdu and paying him 500,000 coins.

This item can be stored in the armour case of a costume room , as part of the Void Knight Elite armour set. Ultimate Ironmen will be unable to retrieve individual pieces until the full set is stored.

The top can also be given to the Dodgy Squire in exchange for 360 Void Knight commendation points.
20469:

It can be bought from a Void Knight for 250 Void Knight commendation points through the Pest Control minigame, although a player must have at least 42 Attack , Strength , Defence , Hitpoints , Ranged , and Magic , along with 22 Prayer to buy and wear one.

It is worn in combination with the other pieces of Void Knight Armour to achieve the designated set effect, depending on which helm is worn.

It can be upgraded into an Elite void robe for 200 Void Knight commendation points, although a player must have completed the hard Western Provinces Diary tasks to be able to upgrade it. The robe can also be given to the Dodgy Squire in exchange for 200 Void Knight commendation points.

The robe is notable for having a high magic defence bonus, higher than that of blessed and black dragonhide chaps , without having any negative attack bonuses in addition to being non-degradable. The void robe bottom can therefore be a decent alternative to Karil's leatherskirt in melee gear setups aiming to maximise defence against magic.

If the player dies a PvP death at level 20 Wilderness or below and the item is unprotected, it will remain in the player's inventory; however, the item will be in a broken, unusable state and must be repaired by using it on Perdu and paying him 180,000 coins .

It can be upgraded from a void knight robe for 200 Void Knight commendation points by speaking to the Elite Void Knight , although the hard Western Provinces Diary must be completed to upgrade it. When worn in combination with the other pieces of Void Knight armour, there is a set effect that depends on which void helm is worn. Compared to the void knight robe , it has an additional +3 prayer bonus and a +2.5% damage boost to Ranged and +5% damage boost to Mage when worn with the elite void top .

If the player dies a PvP death at level 20 Wilderness or below and the item is unprotected, it will remain in the player's inventory; however, the item will be in a broken, unusable state and must be repaired by using it on Perdu and paying him 250,000 coins .

This item can be stored in the armour case of a costume room , as part of the Void Knight Elite armour set. Ultimate Ironmen will be unable to retrieve individual pieces until the full set is stored.

The robe can also be given to the Dodgy Squire in exchange for 360 Void Knight commendation points.
20473:
The Void Knight mace can be bought from a Void Knight for 250 commendation points , although a player must have 42 Attack , Strength , Defence , Hitpoints , Ranged , and Magic , along with 22 Prayer . The mace can be used to autocast Claws of Guthix , Crumble Undead , and the Wave and Surge spells . To cast Claws of Guthix, the player must have cast the spell 100 times in the Wilderness Mage Arena . Note that the Void knight mace does not count towards the four pieces needed for the void set effect .

Its stats are relatively close to that of the rune mace , with the main difference being its 20% slower attack speed . It also has +2 bonus in Stab, Slash, and Crush attack, as well as Stab, Slash, Crush, Magic, and Ranged defence, as well as a relative +2 Strength and Prayer bonus compared to the rune mace. Due to its role as one of the weapons to cast Claws of Guthix, it also has a +8 Magic attack bonus. These stats make it one of the only melee weapons in game to have a positive ranged defence bonus, other than the Lunar staff , with +1, and the dragon spear and Zamorakian spear , with +5 and +13, respectively. Unlike other maces, it only has crushing attack styles. Alongside croziers , the hallowed flail , and the 3rd Age druidic staff , it has the highest Prayer bonus of all one-handed weapons.

While Claws of Guthix can be cast and autocast while wearing an imbued Saradomin cape or imbued Zamorak cape , an appropriate cape ( Guthix cape or its imbued variant) must still be worn to receive the damage boost from Charge .

If the player dies a PvP death and the item is unprotected, it will remain in the player's inventory; however, the item will be in a broken, unusable state and must be repaired by using it on Perdu and paying him 20,000 coins .

The mace can also be given to the Dodgy Squire in exchange for 200 Void Knight commendation points.

Void Knight gloves are a piece of Void Knight equipment . They can be bought from a Void Knight for 150 commendations , although a player must have at least 42 Attack , Strength , Defence , Hitpoints , Ranged , and Magic , along with 22 Prayer to buy and wear them. The gloves can also be given to the Dodgy Squire in exchange for 120 Void Knight commendation points.

If the player dies a PvP death at level 20 Wilderness or below and the item is unprotected, it will remain in the player's inventory; however, the item will be in a broken, unusable state and must be repaired by using it on Perdu and paying him 120,000 coins .

If the player dies a PvP death above level 20 Wilderness and the item is unprotected, it will be converted to coins. To prevent this, a Trouver parchment and a payment of 500,000 coins can be given to Perdu in order to permanently lock the item. The locked item will remain in the player's inventory; however, the item will be in a mangled, unusable state and must be repaired by using it on Perdu and paying him 500,000 coins.

This item can be stored in the armour case of a costume room , as part of the Void Knight Elite armour set or the Void Knight armour set. Ultimate Ironmen will be unable to retrieve individual pieces until the full set is stored.
20477:
The Void mage helm is a piece of Void Knight equipment . It can be bought from a Void Knight for 200 commendation points , if the player has at least 42 Attack , Strength , Defence , Hitpoints , Ranged , and Magic , and 22 Prayer to buy and wear one. It is worn in combination with the other pieces of Void Knight Armour ( Void knight top , Void knight robe , and Void knight gloves ) to achieve the designated set effect. The Void knight mace is not required for the bonus.

The Void mage set gives a +45% to magic accuracy. This typically provides less accuracy and defensive bonuses than Ahrim's robes , but can be easily switched with the other Void sets. If wearing Elite Void Knight robes , the set gives an additional 5% increase to magic damage.

The effective magic attack bonus can be calculated as 1.45 x + 28.8 , where x is the total equipment magic attack bonus when wearing the Void mage set. For example, if you have a magic attack bonus of +16 while also wearing the Void mage set (which provides no bonus), the effective bonus becomes +52 taking into account the set effect. When wearing several best-in-slot pieces of magical gear, the accuracy of the Void mage set can surpass Ahrim's robes with the same gear.

The Void ranger helm is a piece of Void Knight equipment obtained as a reward from the Pest Control minigame. It can be bought from a Void Knight for 200 commendation points ; players also must have at least 42 Attack , Strength , Defence , Hitpoints , Ranged , Magic and 22 Prayer to buy and wear one.

If worn alongside the other three equipment pieces ( Void knight top , Void knight robe and Void knight gloves ), the Void ranger helm grants the player a 10% boost to Ranged damage (12.5% with Elite equipment ) and a 10% boost to Ranged accuracy. The fighter hat is a piece of members-only armour that requires 45 Defence to wear, and is obtained through the Barbarian Assault minigame. Players with 275 honour points in each role and who have killed the Penance Queen can purchase the hat from Commander Connad, located on the ground floor of the Barbarian Outpost.

The fighter hat is sometimes used in place of the warrior helm and berserker helm. The warrior helm provides slightly better defensive bonuses, but offers an attack bonus to slash only, while the fighter hat also provides attack bonuses to stab and crush. In fact, the +5 stab attack bonus makes the fighter hat the best-in-slot item for stab attack. The berserker helm has slightly better defensive bonuses and provides a strength bonus (+3), but provides no melee attack bonuses. The fighter hat is a popular choice among obsidian maulers that are unable to obtain the Inquisitor's great helm.

If the player dies a PvP death and the item is unprotected, it will remain in the player's inventory; however, the item will be in a broken, unusable state and must be repaired by using it on Perdu and paying him 45,000 coins.

This item can be stored in the armour case of a costume room.

The bank filler is an item found exclusively within a player's bank , and cannot be withdrawn. It fills the entire player's bank, with the amount filled dependent on the number of bank spaces remaining.

The bank can be filled with bank fillers by enabling them in the bank settings menu on the top left corner of the interface. Players can remove the desired amount of bank fillers from their bank by right-clicking a bank filler.

Having a bank full of filler items allows players to decide which items they want deposited when using the Deposit inventory or Deposit worn items buttons. For example, if players are crafting leather items, they can remove the needle and thread from their bank, enable the bank fillers, and be able to use the Deposit inventory button without having to consistently withdraw the needle and thread.

For the placeholder functionality of the bank, please see here .

Rune arrow packs are purchased from a vending shrine for 10 survival tokens during a game of Last Man Standing.

Opening the pack gives the player 50 rune arrows.
20608: The bloodier key is an item that is automatically placed in the player's inventory when they kill another player with five or fewer players remaining during a game of Last Man Standing. The key allows the player to loot a chest to access an upgraded loot table containing Ancient Warriors' weapons, Lightbearer, and the Voidwaker.
20609: Fairy enchantment are purchased from Fairy Fixit's Fairy Enchantment after completing Fairytale II - Cure a Queen for 100 coins. They are required in planting fairy rings or spirit tree & fairy ring within a player's Superior garden.
20611: Ancient signets can be freely obtained by speaking to Eblis after the completion of Desert Treasure I . They are required in building ancient altars or occult altars within a player's Achievement Gallery .
20613:
Lunar signets are purchased from Baba Yaga's Magic Shop for 2 coins, after completing Lunar Diplomacy . They are required in building lunar altars or occult altars within a player's Achievement Gallery .

It is worth noting that a seal of passage is required to buy a lunar signet prior to the completion of the Fremennik Elite Diary .
20615: Arceuus signets are obtained by speaking to Tyss. They are required in building dark altars or occult altars within a player's Achievement Gallery.

20620:
The occult altar can be built in the altar space of the achievement gallery in a player-owned house. It requires 90 Construction to build and gives 3,445 experience when built. The player must have a hammer and a saw in their inventory to build it.

Players can switch their spellbook to one of the following: the Arceuus spellbook, Lunar spellbook, standard spellbook, or Ancient Magicks. Other players can use the altar, provided they have the requirements to access those spellbooks.

In order to build the occult altar, players must right-click upgrade from the altar they have built, with the required materials dependent on the altar built. For example, upgrading the Ancient altar to the occult altar will require 1 lunar signet, 10,000 astral runes, 1 Arceuus signet, 5,000 blood runes, and 5,000 soul runes.

The crystal saw boost is applicable, making the minimum requirement level 82 Construction with a +5 boost from an orange spicy stew.

For the Dark altar and Lunar altar, although the recipes list that Pharaoh's sceptre (uncharged) can be used, a sceptre with any charge level will be acceptable.
