20655:
The ring of suffering is an enchanted zenyte ring , requiring a Hitpoints level of 75 to be equipped. It is the best-in-slot all-around defensive ring, only beaten by its imbued variant , the steel ring for melee defence, and the granite ring for ranged defence. This ring can be imbued into a ring of suffering (i) using 725,000 Nightmare Zone reward points, 300 Zeal Tokens from Soul Wars , or a scroll of imbuing (which can be purchased for 200 Emir's Arena reward points). With completion of the hard tier of Combat Achievements , these costs are halved to 362,500 Nightmare Zone reward points and 150 Zeal Tokens from Soul Wars. A ring of suffering (i) has double the bonuses of a non-imbued ring.

Players can make one by enchanting a zenyte ring with the Lvl-7 Enchant spell. This requires level 93 Magic , 20 soul runes , 20 blood runes , and 1 cosmic rune and grants 110 Magic experience.

The ring can also be charged with noted and unnoted rings of recoil to give it the recoil effect, renaming the item to ring of suffering (r) . Each ring of recoil provides 40 charges. A maximum of 100,000 charges can be stored, equivalent to 2,500 rings and costing 2,350,000 . Players can configure the charges while the ring is in their bank by right-clicking on Configure-Charges, as long as players have the required materials. Note that if the ring is discharged, the rings stored will not be refunded. The ring of recoil effect is toggle-able, so players may disable it as to not waste it during training and instead use it in activities such as fighting Zulrah and in PvP combat, where the effect may prove more useful. Charges are not lost upon death. While charged, the ring is untradeable.
20657:
The ring of suffering (i) is an upgraded version of the regular ring of suffering . It can be imbued as a reward from the Nightmare Zone , costing 725,000 reward points or 362,500 with the hard tier of Combat Achievements , at Soul Wars for 300 Zeal Tokens , or by using a scroll of imbuing purchased from Emir's Arena for 200 points. Its stats are double those of the ring of suffering.

The ring can also be charged with rings of recoil to give it the recoil effect, renaming the item to ring of suffering (ri) . Each ring of recoil provides 40 charges, assuming the ring of recoil has not been drained prior. A maximum of 100,000 charges can be stored, equivalent to 2,500 rings, at a cost of 2,350,000 coins . Players can configure the charges while the ring is in their bank by right-clicking on Configure-Charges, as long as players have the required materials. If a player uncharged the ring, the recoil rings stored will not be refunded. The ring of recoil effect is toggle-able, so players may disable it as to not waste it during training and instead use it in activities such as fighting Zulrah , or in PvP combat, where the effect may prove more useful. Charges are not lost upon death.

If not protected, dying to another player will cause the imbued ring to lose its imbued status, however the player will be reimbursed the Nightmare Zone points , Zeal Tokens or Scroll of imbuing to re-imbue it via the aforementioned methods. Dying to a monster will not remove its imbued effect.
20659:
The giant squirrel is a skilling pet that can be obtained after completion of an Agility course, as well as from tagging marked ticket dispensers within the Brimhaven Agility Arena.

When a player receives the pet, it will automatically try to appear as their follower. At the same time, a message in the chatbox will state You have a funny feeling like you're being followed. However, if a player receives a pet while having a follower out (for example, a cat), it will be placed into their inventory. When this occurs, the message in the chatbox will instead state You feel something weird sneaking into your backpack.

If a player's inventory is full and they have a follower already, they will not receive the pet; it must instead be claimed from Probita in East Ardougne.

On death, if a player loses their pet (as a follower or in your inventory) it will wander around the area for 30 seconds before despawning. Even if the player returns in time, the pet cannot be picked up, and can be reclaimed from Probita.
20661:
The tangleroot is a skilling pet that can be obtained when checking the health (for patches that have this option, like fruit trees) or when harvesting the final crop (for patches without a "Check-health" option) of a farming patch. It may also be obtained while playing the Tithe Farm minigame or from killing the Hespori. The chances of getting it are dependent on the player's Farming level and the crop the player is harvesting.

When a player receives the pet, it will automatically try to appear as their follower. At the same time, a message in the chatbox will state You have a funny feeling like you're being followed. However, if a player receives a pet while having a follower out (for example, a cat), it will be placed into their inventory. When this occurs, the message in the chatbox will instead state You feel something weird sneaking into your backpack.

Unlike pets such as the rock golem, an incoming farming resource such as a herb or hespori seed will take precedence over the farming pet. If the player already has a follower and the remaining inventory slots are then filled by an incoming farming resource, the player will not receive the pet and must instead claim it from Probita in East Ardougne. Should the player obtain the pet while harvesting giant seaweed, the pet will not be lost upon drowning.

On death, if a player loses their pet (as a follower or in your inventory) it will wander around the area for 30 seconds before despawning. Even if the player returns in time, the pet cannot be picked up, and can be reclaimed from Probita. If a seed has been used on tangleroot and is lost upon death, the pet will revert to its original form and the player must use another seed on it upon reclaim.
20663:
Rocky is a skilling pet that can be obtained when training the Thieving skill. This includes stealing from stalls, pickpocketing from NPCs, picking fruit in the Sorceress's Garden , and looting grand gold chests within Pyramid Plunder . The chances of getting it are dependent on the player's Thieving level, and the person/object the player is stealing from.

When a player receives the pet, it will automatically try to appear as their follower. At the same time, a message in the chatbox will state You have a funny feeling like you're being followed. However, if a player receives a pet while having a follower out (for example, a cat ), it will be placed into their inventory . When this occurs, the message in the chatbox will instead state You feel something weird sneaking into your backpack.

If a player's inventory is full and they have a follower already, they will not receive the pet; it must instead be claimed from Probita in East Ardougne .

On death , if a player loses their pet (as a follower or in your inventory) it will wander around the area for 30 seconds before despawning. Even if the player returns in time, the pet cannot be picked up, and can be reclaimed from Probita.
20665:
The rift guardian is a members-only skilling pet that can be obtained while training Runecraft. The chances of getting it are dependent on the player's Runecraft level, the rune the player is crafting, and the number of essence used. Upon using the Guardian's eye on it, which is purchased from the Guardians of the Rift reward shop for 3,000 abyssal pearls, players unlock a permanent metamorphosis option to turn it into the Greatish guardian.

When a player receives the pet, it will automatically try to appear as their follower. At the same time, a message in the chatbox will state You have a funny feeling like you're being followed. However, if a player receives a pet while having a follower out (for example, a cat), it will be placed into their inventory. When this occurs, the message in the chatbox will instead state You feel something weird sneaking into your backpack.

When runecrafting using dark essence fragments, the pet is given after they are removed and the runes are given back. This means if there is not already some of the runes to be crafted in the inventory, and the rest of the inventory is full, and a pet is already following the player, the rift guardian will not be given; it must instead be claimed from Probita in East Ardougne.

On death, if a player loses their pet (as a follower or in your inventory) it will wander around the area for 30 seconds before despawning. Even if the player returns in time, the pet cannot be picked up, and can be reclaimed from Probita.

When this occurs, the message in the chatbox will instead state You feel something weird sneaking into your backpack.

When runecrafting using dark essence fragments, the pet is given after they are removed and the runes are given back. This means if there is not already some of the runes to be crafted in the inventory, and the rest of the inventory is full, and a pet is already following the player, the rift guardian will not be given; it must instead be claimed from Probita in East Ardougne.

On death, if a player loses their pet (as a follower or in your inventory) it will wander around the area for 30 seconds before despawning. Even if the player returns in time, the pet cannot be picked up, and can be reclaimed from Probita.

20693:
The Phoenix is a pet that can be received from looting the Reward Cart , from which rewards are obtained by subduing the Wintertodt with at least 500 points.

When a player receives the pet, it will automatically try to appear as their follower. At the same time, a message in the chatbox will state You have a funny feeling like you're being followed. However, if a player receives a pet while having a follower out (for example, a cat ), it will be placed into their inventory . When this occurs, the message in the chatbox will instead state You feel something weird sneaking into your backpack.

On death , if a player loses their pet (as a follower or in your inventory) it will wander around the area for 30 seconds before despawning. Even if the player returns in time, the pet cannot be picked up, and can be reclaimed from Probita .

Though the Wintertodt is classified as a boss rather than a skilling activity, the phoenix is fifteen times more common at 200 million Firemaking experience.
20695:
A bruma root is obtained by chopping bruma roots found in the four corners of the Wintertodt's prison north of the Wintertodt Camp. The experience given is equal to 0.3 times the player's Woodcutting level. They cannot be taken out of the prison.

It is burned in a brazier which drains the Wintertodt's energy, granting Firemaking experience equal to 3x the player's level per log. These can be fletched into bruma kindlings, which give 3.8x the player's Firemaking level in experience, roughly 27% more. The fletching knife works on the bruma roots, speeding up the rate at which they are fletched.
20696:
A bruma kindling is obtained by using a knife on a bruma root, granting Fletching experience appropriate to the player's level. The Fletching experience given is equal to 0.6 times the player's Fletching level.

It is used to burn the braziers, found in the four corners of the Wintertodt's prison, to drain the Wintertodt's energy, granting Firemaking experience appropriate to the player's level. Bruma kindlings give approximately 27% more Firemaking experience than using bruma roots on the brazier, 3.8 times the player's Firemaking level. When using the Fletching knife, the fletching time is reduced by 1 tick starting from the second action onward. This represents an average fletching speed increase of 15-30% depending on Wintertodt attacks, most likely around 20%.
20697:
A rejuvenation potion (unf) is an unfinished potion obtained from the crate found in the Wintertodt's prison north of the Wintertodt Camp.

It is used to make the rejuvenation potion by adding a bruma herb, earning Herblore experience appropriate to the player's level.
20698: Bruma herbs are obtained from picking Sprouting Roots found within the lobby and the east and west side of the Wintertodt's prison. They are used on a rejuvenation potion (unf) to create a rejuvenation potion, yielding Herblore experience equal to 10% of the player's Herblore level. They can be used to heal the pyromancers and to restore player's warmth during a game of Wintertodt.
20699:
Rejuvenation potions are created by adding a bruma herb to a rejuvenation potion (unf), earning Herblore experience equal to the player's Herblore level divided by 10.

Each potion holds 4 doses and are used to heal the pyromancers found in the Wintertodt's prison. Using a dose on a pyromancer heals them fully and grants the player 75 points towards a reward cart roll when subduing the Wintertodt. A single dose will fully heal any pyromancer, including those that have been incapacitated. When healing pyromancers, a dose will be consumed from the potion with the fewest doses remaining.

You are able to drink this potion to restore 30% of your own warmth.

Brew'ma can create the potions for the player if they wish not to do it themselves or haven't completed Druidic Ritual, provided the player gives them the ingredients.

Attempting to create this potion outside of the Wintertodt's prison results in the message You can only do that within the influence of the Bruma tree. appearing in the chatbox.

20703:
A supply crate was a reward item given for subduing the Wintertodt after earning at least 500 points. It was replaced by the Reward Cart , but existing supply crates were not deleted and can still be opened or kept. It can reward many useful items for skilling such as ores, logs, herbs, seeds, gems, and fish. The supply crate also gives the opportunity for items only obtainable through defeating the Wintertodt, such as the tome of fire , pyromancer outfit , and the phoenix pet.

Opening it will give players two rolls on the reward table. For every 500 points earned after the initial 500, another reward is added to the crate. With 13,500 points or above, players will receive 28 reward rolls, the maximum from any single supply crate. Beyond this point, earning extra points does not increase the number of rewards from a supply crate.

Players can exchange excess Wintertodt-unique items (excluding burnt pages and the phoenix ) with Ignisia for an extra supply crate or 50 burnt pages. While it is not possible to receive unique items from an extra supply crate, the player may still receive a dragon axe . Tomes of fire may also be exchanged for 250 burnt pages. It is recommended for ironmen to keep 3 warm gloves and 3 bruma torches since this is the maximum and any further rolls for the two will result in a roll for a magic seed or torstol seeds. Players without account restrictions may wish to exchange them for burnt pages instead, as the combined market value of the pages is often higher than that of the seeds.
20704:
The pyromancer garb is a possible reward from the Reward Cart upon subduing the Wintertodt . The garb provides a 0.8% Firemaking experience boost. This is increased to 2.5% when wearing the full pyromancer outfit . Players can also trade in extra pieces for an extra supply crate or 50 burnt pages via Ignisia .

It can be stored in a magic wardrobe in a player-owned house. It is also a piece of warm clothing .
20706:
The pyromancer robe is a possible reward from the Reward Cart upon subduing the Wintertodt . The robe provides a 0.6% Firemaking experience boost. This is increased to 2.5% when wearing the full pyromancer outfit . Players can also trade in extra pieces for an extra supply crate or 50 burnt pages via Ignisia .

It can be stored in a magic wardrobe in a player-owned house. It is also a piece of warm clothing .
20708:
The pyromancer hood is a possible reward from the Reward Cart upon subduing the Wintertodt . The hood provides a 0.4% Firemaking experience boost. This is increased to 2.5% when wearing the full pyromancer outfit . Players can also trade in extra pieces for an extra supply crate or 50 burnt pages via Ignisia .

It can be stored in a magic wardrobe in a player-owned house. It is also a piece of warm clothing .
20710:
The pyromancer boots are a possible reward from the Reward Cart upon subduing the Wintertodt . The boots provide a 0.2% Firemaking experience boost. When wearing the full pyromancer outfit , the set bonus is 2.5%. Players can also trade in extra pieces for an extra supply crate or 50 burnt pages via Ignisia .

According to the outfit drop priority of the reward cart , the boots are always the last piece dropped to complete the pyromancer outfit. If the pyromancer robe has been filled in its proper STASH unit , they will not receive the boots, but another robe instead (See the reward cart's unique drop table for more information on the mechanics).

It can be stored in a magic wardrobe in a player-owned house. It is also a piece of warm clothing .
20712:
Warm gloves are obtained as a reward from the Reward Cart by contributing in the subduing of the Wintertodt.

Although they match the appearance of the Pyromancer outfit, they do not count towards the set bonus. They only provide warmth while subduing the Wintertodt, which reduces the damage taken. This item can be stored in the magic wardrobe of a costume room.

Players can also trade in warm gloves for an extra supply crate or 50 burnt pages via Ignisia.

If the player has three pairs of warm gloves in their bank and/or inventory, the reward cart will instead give a magic seed when it would have given gloves. Currently the Grand Exchange price of 50 burnt pages is 328,150 and the price of a magic seed is 71,233.

The gloves do not work as protection when picking Belladonna.
20714:
The tome of fire is a book held in place of a shield that is a possible reward from the reward cart upon subduing the Wintertodt . The tome of fire requires level 50 in Magic to wield.

The tome is only tradeable when empty. When it is empty, its only function is its magic attack and magic defence equipment bonuses.

Empty tomes can be traded in for 250 burnt pages per tome (value of 1,640,750 ) by speaking to Ignisia .

This item counts as a warm item at the Wintertodt.

If lost to another player in a dangerous PVP death, all charges inside will be converted into pages and dropped for the killer alongside the empty tome.
20716:
The tome of fire is a book held in place of a shield that is a possible reward from the reward cart upon subduing the Wintertodt . The tome of fire requires level 50 in Magic to wield.

The tome is only tradeable when empty. When it is empty, its only function is its magic attack and magic defence equipment bonuses.

Empty tomes can be traded in for 250 burnt pages per tome (value of 1,640,750 ) by speaking to Ignisia .

This item counts as a warm item at the Wintertodt.

If lost to another player in a dangerous PVP death, all charges inside will be converted into pages and dropped for the killer alongside the empty tome.
20718:
Burnt pages are a possible reward from the Reward Cart upon subduing the Wintertodt , or created at the Book of Eternal Flame with desiccated pages and level 50 Runecraft . They are used to charge the tome of fire , which gives it additional effects.

Each burnt page adds 20 charges to the tome, and one charge is consumed when an elemental fire spell is cast with the tome equipped. Players may remove the pages from the tome should they wish to do so.

Empty tomes of fire can be traded in for 250 burnt pages by speaking to Ignisia , while pieces of the Pyromancer outfit give 50 pages per piece (with 250 pages being given if exchanging a full set). The bruma torch and warm gloves will also give 50 burnt pages each when exchanged with Ignisia .
20720:
The bruma torch is a possible reward from the Reward Cart after subduing the Wintertodt. When worn during the Wintertodt boss fight, it acts as a warm clothing item, and it can also be used as a replacement for a tinderbox for the purpose of lighting braziers, regardless of whether the torch is equipped or in the player's inventory.

Around the game world, the torch acts as a light source that can be equipped, but does not function as a tinderbox. It has no possibility of triggering the explosions in the Lumbridge Swamp Caves. It can also be used in place of a lit torch when smoking traps.

Players can trade in bruma torches for an extra supply crate or 50 burnt pages via Ignisia. If a player has three bruma torches in their bank and/or inventory and/or Magic wardrobe in a POH, searching the reward cart will give 2-3 torstol seeds when it would have given another torch. Currently the Grand Exchange price of 50 burnt pages is 328,150 and the price of a torstol seed is 15,311.

It is generally more beneficial to exchange spare torches for 50 burnt pages, unless you are an ironman who wishes to receive torstol seeds. Note Wintertodt's unique rewards cannot be received from the extra supply crate.

The torch can be swapped via the "Swap" option, converting it to its off-hand variant so that it can be equipped in the shield slot. Both versions are storable in the magic wardrobe.

This item can be stored in the magic wardrobe of a costume room.
20722:
The emerald lantern is a light source . It is used during the Lunar Diplomacy quest and is created by using the emerald lens with a bullseye lantern or a bullseye lantern (unf) .

If created from a bullseye lantern (unf), it will require lamp oil to be lit with a tinderbox . To fix this mistake during the quest, there is an easy way to pull the Emerald Lens back out of the lantern by using a Sapphire (with completion of Tears of Guthix ) or a Lantern lens on the bullseye lantern.

Level 49 Firemaking is required to light it. It is similar to the sapphire lantern , but unlike the sapphire lantern it is not made using a cut gem. If lost, the emerald lens can be recovered by speaking to the Cabin boy who can be found slightly north-west of the Lunar Isle bank .
20724:
The imbued heart is a magic-boosting item dropped by superior slayer monsters , which are rare encounters unlocked after purchasing the unlock Bigger and Badder for 50 Slayer reward points from any Slayer master .

Players can use the Invigorate option on the heart to temporarily increase their Magic level by 1 + 10% of the player's level, rounded down. It can be activated an infinite number of times, but it can only be activated once every seven minutes per player, regardless of how many imbued hearts are owned. Attempting to use the Invigorate option while it is on cooldown will result in the chatbox message The heart is still drained of its power. Judging by how it feels, it will be ready in around X minutes.

The cooldown resets on death, even in safe minigames such as Castle Wars . The quickest way a player can reset the cooldown is by travelling back and forth through the Clan Wars free-for-all (white) portal , or by drinking from the Pool of Refreshment (which also removes buffed levels), both located in the Ferox Enclave .

Players cannot bring the imbued heart into legacy duels within the Emir's Arena to gain an advantage in magical duels if the "no potions" option is enabled.

An imbued heart can be upgraded to a saturated heart by adding 150,000 ancient essence to it, increasing the Magic boost by +3, making the boost not gradually drain (like divine potions ) and reducing the cooldown from 7 minutes to 5 minutes. Doing so is non-reversible.
20727:
The leaf-bladed battleaxe is a one-handed axe requiring an Attack level of 65 and a Slayer level of 55 to wield. It is one of three melee weapons used to harm turoths and kurasks , the others being the leaf-bladed spear and sword . When fighting these monsters with the battleaxe, it has an added 17.5% damage, stacking with the Slayer helmet .

It is dropped by kurasks , located in the Fremennik Slayer Dungeon , the Iorwerth Dungeon , and the Kurask lair on Laguna Aurorae .
20730:
A mist battlestaff is a mist elemental staff which provides unlimited amounts of air and water runes as well as the autocast option when equipped. It requires 30 Attack and 30 Magic to wield.

The mystic mist staff is an even stronger alternative, providing better melee and magic stat bonuses. It is obtained by taking the mist battlestaff and 40,000 to Thormac . (Reduced to 30,000 or 20,000 with completion of the hard and elite Kandarin diaries respectively.)

The staff is obtainable as a potential drop from superior slayer monsters and waterfiends .
20733:
The mystic mist staff is an elemental staff requiring 40 Attack and 40 Magic to wield. In addition to increased Melee and Magic Attack bonuses, the staff provides unlimited amounts of air and water runes as well as the autocast option when equipped.

This staff can be created after the completion of the quest Scorpion Catcher by taking a mist battlestaff and 40,000 to Thormac. After completion of the Hard Kandarin Diary and Elite Kandarin Diary, Thormac will only require 30,000 or 20,000 respectively.

It can also be obtained through other players and bought on the Grand Exchange.
20736:
A dust battlestaff is a dust elemental staff which provides unlimited amounts of air and earth runes as well as the autocast option when equipped. It requires 30 Attack and 30 Magic to wield.

The mystic dust staff is an even stronger alternative, providing better melee and magic stat bonuses. It is obtained by taking the dust battlestaff and 40,000 to Thormac. (Reduced to 30,000 or 20,000 with completion of the hard and elite Kandarin diaries respectively.)

The staff is obtainable as a potential drop from superior slayer monsters and dust devils.
20739:
The mystic dust staff is an elemental staff requiring 40 Attack and 40 Magic to wield. In addition to increased Melee and Magic Attack bonuses, the staff provides unlimited amounts of air and earth runes as well as the autocast option when equipped.

This staff can be created after the completion of the quest Scorpion Catcher by taking a dust battlestaff and 40,000 to Thormac . After completion of the Hard Kandarin Diary and Elite Kandarin Diary , Thormac will only require 30,000 or 20,000 respectively.
20742:
An empty jug pack is an item pack containing 100 noted jugs.

These packs can be bought at general stores for 140-182 coins each depending on the stock available, with the highest stocks being The Lighthouse Store, Bandit Bargains, and Ifaba's General Store, all of which stock eight packs. Additionally, the Culinaromancer's Chest stocks eight packs once eight subquests have been completed.

They are not sold at the Bedabin Camp, Catherby, East Ardougne, West Ardougne, Shantay Pass, Tai Bwo Wannai, and Shilo Village general stores.
20745:
The Combat dummy is an interface item that can be seen in the Construction skill guide representing the Combat dummy .

The actual item cannot be obtained by players.
20746:
The Undead combat dummy is an interface item that can be seen in the Construction skill guide representing the Undead combat dummy .

The actual item cannot be obtained by players.
20747:
Bologa's blessing is an item that can only be purchased from Farmer Gricoller's Tithe Farm shop for 1 point per 20 blessings. The blessing allows players to pick Zamorak's grapes instead of grapes from the vinery and from grapevines, consuming one blessing per grape picked.

Before being able to purchase blessings from Gricoller, players must pay 75,000 coins to Bologa, his youngest granddaughter, while wearing an item affiliated with Zamorak and no other god affiliated items. Bologa's blessing requires level 50 Prayer and 65 Cooking to unlock and use.

The blessing is invented by Bologa, who explains that as the grapes are severed from the stem, it creates a brief moment of vulnerability where the unholy power from the blessing can infest it with Zamorakian magic. However, she also adds that this volatile, chaotic power makes players more likely to get a smaller harvest of grapes.

The blessing will make grape farming much more profitable, as grapes are usually inexpensive and can only be sold for 70 coins, while Zamorak's grapes will sell for much higher at 1,822 coins, so if one intends to farm grapes, it is much better to farm with the blessing than without, as profits will be increased by almost 1,752 coins per harvest.
20749:
Zamorak's grapes are a special type of grape that can be obtained by players through harvesting grapes in the Hosidius vinery while having Bologa's blessings in their inventory. One blessing is consumed for every grape picked from the vine patch.

Zamorak's grapes cannot be consumed on their own; instead they are a Cooking ingredient used in making wine of Zamorak at level 65 Cooking by using them on a jug of water.

The success rate for turning Zamorak's grapes into wine of Zamorak is ~50% at 65 Cooking which increases linearly until you can no longer fail at 98 Cooking. If unsuccessful, a jug of bad wine will be made instead.
20752:
Zamorak's unfermented wine is made by using Zamorak's grapes on a jug of water. This requires 65 Cooking.

After about twelve seconds, the wine will ferment into a wine of Zamorak or a jug of bad wine, giving 200 Cooking experience if successfully fermented. It can then be used as a secondary ingredient to create ranging, and bastion potions.
20754:
A giant key grants players access to Obor 's lair in the Hill Giant section of the Edgeville Dungeon . The key is not consumed when unlocking access to Obor's lair for the first time.

It is consumed when used to unlock the chest inside Obor's lair. It is possible to hold more than one giant key at once.

For hill giants located in the Wilderness, the drop rate is doubled to 1/64.

With a Giantsoul amulet and Desert amulet 4 , players can kill Obor 120+ times per hour when using burning claws, giving approximately 8 keys per hour.
20756:
The hill giant club is a two-handed melee weapon requiring 40 Attack to equip. It is currently the best-in-slot weapon for crush bonuses in free-to-play , possessing very similar stats to a rune 2h sword but with the slash and crush bonuses swapped, though the rune 2h sword has a slightly higher slash bonus than the crush bonus of the club.

It can be obtained by opening the chest in Obor 's lair, which requires first killing Obor then using a giant key . Keys can be obtained from Obor, the chest itself, or hill giants , of which the ones in the Wilderness have the highest chance to drop a key.

This weapon is commonly used in free-to-play PvP activities as a knockout weapon, especially during the so-called risk fights , as well as safe activities such as Clan Wars and Castle Wars . It is notable for being more accurate against opponents in full rune armour than the rune 2h sword . It can be used as a slash weapon for cutting spider webs.
20760:
The Ardougne max cape is the result of combining the Ardougne cloak 4 with a max cape , during which the max hood required to be in the player's inventory will automatically convert to the Ardougne max hood .

Like the other max cape variants (a max cape combined with another cape slot item), the Ardougne max cape does not have the max cape's stats or perks; it only acts as a cosmetic upgrade to the Ardougne cloak 4 with the following exceptions when worn:

The max cape and ardougne cloak 4 can be separated by using a knife on the cape. Mac will also buy back a max cape, along with its variants, for 1,900,800 coins each. He will return the secondary item any max cape variant was combined with upon doing so.

Unlike the Ardougne cloak 4, the Ardougne max cape can be stored on the cape hanger in a player-owned house .

On a PvP death, it is always kept in the inventory, even if not protected. If the player is skulled and has the Protect Item prayer active, both the max cape and their most valuable item will be kept. Otherwise, on death from causes outside of the wilderness, if it is not one of your protected items, it goes to your grave .
20764:
The Ardougne max hood is a hood created by using an Ardougne cloak 4 on a max cape . When the Ardougne max cape is created, the max hood that is required to be in the player's inventory during the cape's creation is automatically converted to the Ardougne max hood.

If players are refunding the Ardougne max cape via Mac , the player must also have the Ardougne max hood in their inventory.

Should players lose the hood, they may reclaim it from Mac for free.
20766: The Manor key is an item that is found in a barrel west of the manor during the Misthalin Mystery quest . It is used to open the doors to the manor. After which, it is consumed and no longer needed.
20767: The Ruby key is an item that was found in a slashed painting during the Misthalin Mystery quest . It is used to open the eastern doors to the manor.
20768: The emerald key is an item that was found in the piano in the north-eastern corner during the Misthalin Mystery quest . It is used to open the door with the emerald doorknob.
20769: The sapphire key is an item that was found in the fireplace in the eastern room during the Misthalin Mystery quest. It is used to open the door with the sapphire doorknob.
20770: The Notes are an item that was found by the library doors during Misthalin Mystery . It contains a riddle.
20771: The Notes are an item that was found in the back of the manor during Misthalin Mystery . It contains a riddle.
20772: The Notes are an item that was found outside the kitchen doors during Misthalin Mystery . It contains a riddle.

20779:
The Hunting knife is obtained as a reward from the 2016 Halloween event, as well as subsequent Halloween events. Running while having the knife equipped uses a different animation. It is considered a fun weapon.

Its -100 Strength bonus makes it the weakest weapon melee weapon in the game, tied with the cursed goblin hammer, carrot sword, and nutcracker staff. If the user's Strength bonus is -64 or less, it will never deal damage.

When wielded, a "Slash" option will appear on other players. Picking this option will cause the player to hit the other player. Similarly to the rubber chicken, the hit is just an animation and no damage is dealt, nor does it count as entering combat. You also have a chance to miss with the knife and have it drop to the floor, and the message You drop your hunting knife on the floor! will appear in the chatbox.

If destroyed, a replacement can be obtained from Diango in Draynor Village or from the toy box of a costume room, as part of the 2016: Masked Killer set. Ultimate Ironmen will be unable to retrieve individual pieces until the full set is stored.
20781: The killer's knife is a quest item in the Misthalin Mystery quest . It is obtained during the confrontation with Abigale and used to attack her.
20782:
The Bandos godsword is an unobtainable weapon that appears during the Misthalin Mystery quest. It is modelled after the Bandos godsword, but unlike the regular version of the item, the one during the quest only serves as an unobtainable decoration. It was added in case players were ever able to obtain the godsword using glitches, and it is in unequipable, untradeable and it has an alchemy value of 0 coins, rendering this item useless in the hands of any potential player that might obtain it.

During the quest, the sword is first seen in the kitchen with Mandy, where it is placed on a table. At the end of the quest, Mandy uses the sword to slay Abigale after she is revealed to be the Killer.

The item was originally introduced in the 2016 Halloween event, which had the same storyline as the Misthalin Mystery quest.
20784:
Dragon claws from Last Man Standing is a minigame-exclusive variant of the normal dragon claws . It has no requirements to wield and is part of the Max/Med starting loadout in the minigame. For the Zerker and 1 Def Pure builds, it can be obtained from opening the chests with a bloody key or bloodier key , or looting the crates that spawn at random locations on the map. It is dropped on death to whoever killed you.

Dragon claws are notable for their special attack, which can deal a lot of damage in quick succession.
20786:
The ring of wealth (i) is an imbued ring of wealth created with a ring of wealth scroll and 50,000 coins . The imbued ring has all the functions of a ring of wealth with an additional effect of doubling the player's chance of getting a clue scroll from monsters and skilling activities in the Wilderness (excluding beginner clue scrolls ). This effect applies regardless of where the player is whenever they kill a monster in the Wilderness. [ 1 ]

If you die with the ring, regardless if it is an item kept on death , the imbue will be removed from the ring and converted to 50,000 coins . In a PvP death, the coins appear in the inventory of the player who killed you; in a PvM death, the coins will instead go to your grave . It should also be noted that attempting to drop the ring whilst in PvP combat will result in the message "You must wait a few seconds before dropping this item."

Like other dragonstone jewellery, it can be charged to provide teleports, albeit only at the Fountain of Rune .

Extra supply crates are obtained by exchanging certain items to Ignisia. Unlike regular pulls from the reward cart, these typically only come with one roll on the drop table.

The items players can exchange are:

Note that players cannot receive these items from the exchanged crates, nor can they receive burnt pages or the Phoenix pet. Receiving a dragon axe is possible.

Handing in a full set of the pyromancer outfit (hood, garb, legs, and boots) will give players an extra supply crate with five rolls on the drop table rather than the regular one. This is a bonus of one when compared to handing in the components individually.
20792:
The Hardcore ironman helm is a full helm obtainable only by players who chose to be a Hardcore Ironman in Ironman Mode . It is obtained by speaking to Adam after leaving Tutorial Island , after choosing to be a Hardcore Ironman. It has stats equivalent to an iron full helm , but with one third of the weight.

If the player loses their Hardcore Ironman status, the item is deleted and cannot be reclaimed.
20794:
The Hardcore ironman platebody is obtainable only by players who chose to be a Hardcore ironman in Ironman Mode . It is obtained by speaking to Adam after leaving Tutorial Island , after choosing to be a Hardcore ironman. It has stats identical to an iron platebody , but weighs half as much.

If the player loses their Hardcore Ironman status, the item is deleted and cannot be reclaimed.
20796:
Hardcore ironman platelegs are obtainable only by players who chose to be a Hardcore ironman in Ironman Mode . They can be obtained by speaking to Adam after leaving Tutorial Island , after choosing to be a Hardcore ironman. It has stats identical to iron platelegs , but weighs half as much.

If the player loses their Hardcore Ironman status, the item is deleted and cannot be reclaimed.
20798:
The smelly journal is a book found in the Fishing Hamlet east of the Wintertodt Camp . It is found in the south-westernmost building.

The journal speaks about a group of Fremenniks from Rellekka who wished to travel west, and details their experiences.

The journal is written for an individual named Lensa. Despite this, using the journal on Lensa of Jatizso or Lensa of Rellekka results in nothing.
20799:
Kindlings are obtained from chopping saplings found within the Chambers of Xeric . They are used to light fires and as fuel for the braziers in the ice demon 's lair.

Kindling works on a timer system, which is affected by the icefiends which spawn inside of the room, as well as a weighting system. Each kindling gives 36 points, while lighting the brazier gives 32 points.

The yield per successful chop from a sapling is scaled to the player's Woodcutting level, up to a maximum of eight. The experience gained also varies, scaling based on the amount of kindling received. Kindling is stackable, but having 28 or more in your inventory will prevent you from chopping more saplings . This can be circumvented by dropping kindling to chop more and picking up the dropped kindling.
20800: Empty gourd vial are obtained from picking gourd trees found in resource rooms within the Chambers of Xeric. They must then be filled with water, by using them on geysers, to create a water-filled gourd vial, which is used to make potions within the Chambers.
20801: Water-filled gourd vials are obtained from using empty gourd vials on geysers found in resource rooms in the Chambers of Xeric. They act as vials of water within the Chambers, and are used to brew potions.
20802: The red bouncy ball is an item used during the 2016 Christmas event . It can be obtained by obtaining a deflated red bouncy ball in the crates near Ulina and Dylan , and then using it on the bellows to inflate it.
20804: A green bouncy ball was used during the 2016 Christmas event . It could be obtained by inflating with bellows a deflated green bouncy ball , found in the crates near Ulina and Dylan .

20826: The green paper hat is an item used during the 2016 Christmas event . It can be made by using a blank paper hat on a green paint cauldron.

The snow globe is obtained as a reward from the 2016 Christmas event , as well as subsequent Christmas events. Its design is based off the original snowglobe obtained from the 2007 Christmas event, in which players obtained a snowglobe with a replica of Lumbridge Castle inside it. When shaken, the snowglobe would play a softer version of the song Harmony , create a pile of snow , and fill the player's inventory with snow .

When creating a pile of snow, if a pile already exists within that map square (8x8 game square ), the new one needs to be created in another one.

If destroyed, a replacement can be obtained from Diango in Draynor Village or from the toy box of a costume room .

20851:
The Olmlet is a pet obtained from the Chambers of Xeric . It is a much smaller version of the Great Olm , with its body fully visible. Players have a 1/53 chance of receiving the pet when they receive an item from the unique drop table after killing the Great Olm.

The olmlet is able to metamorphose into five other pets which are smaller versions of the other bosses encountered inside the Chambers of Xeric, which requires using metamorphic dust on it. The dust can be acquired from the Chambers' Challenge Mode version and clearing it under a specific time.

When a player receives the pet, it will automatically try to appear as their follower. At the same time, a message in the chatbox will state You have a funny feeling like you're being followed. However, if a player receives a pet while having a follower out (for example, a cat ), it will be placed into their inventory . When this occurs, the message in the chatbox will instead state You feel something weird sneaking into your backpack.

If a player's inventory is full and they have a follower already, they will not receive the pet; it must instead be claimed from Probita in East Ardougne .

On death , if a player loses their pet (as a follower or in your inventory) it will wander around the area for 30 seconds before despawning. Even if the player returns in time, the pet cannot be picked up, and can be reclaimed from Probita.

20884: The keystone crystal is obtained from the other side of the tightrope in the tightrope room within the Chambers of Xeric . The crystal is required to disable the glowing barrier leading deeper into the chambers. Once it is used on the barrier, it is consumed as it dispels it, killing off any deathly rangers and mages still alive at the time.

20886:
The creature keeper's journal is a book that is found by searching the corpse of the creature keeper in the Chambers of Xeric .

The book details the creature keeper's experiences with the scavengers, comparing them to skavids found in Gu'Tanoth .

If lost, it can be reclaimed by searching the creature keeper, or from a bookcase within a player-owned house .
20888:
Nistirio's manifesto is a book that appears on the ground after defeating Vasa Nistirio in the Chambers of Xeric.

The manifesto details the origin of Vasa Nistirio, Xeric's former High Priest, and how he managed to harness the power of the crystals within the Chambers.

If lost, it can be reclaimed by defeating Vasa Nistirio, or from a bookcase within a player-owned house.
20890:
Tekton's journal is a book that appears on the ground after defeating Tekton in the Chambers of Xeric.

The journal details Tekton's experiences in serving Xeric as his artisan, and how he attained his current form. He only refers to himself in the third person.

If lost, it can be reclaimed by defeating Tekton, or from a bookcase within a player-owned house.
20892: Medivaemia blossom are obtained from picking the medivaemia roots in Vespula's lair within the Chambers of Xeric. They are used to feed the lux grubs so that their health does not reach zero.
20893:

The notes detail Xeric 's first encounter with the abyss and Vespula .

If lost, it can be reclaimed by defeating Vespula, or from a bookcase within a player-owned house , in which the book's title is Notes on Transdimensional Travel.
20895:
The vanguard judgement is a book that appears on the ground after defeating the Vanguard in the Chambers of Xeric.

The book details the origins of the Vanguard, three elite commanders of Xeric's army during his reign over Great Kourend.

If lost, it can be reclaimed by defeating the Vanguard, or from a bookcase within a player-owned house, in which the book's title is Judgement of the Vanguard.
20897:
The houndmaster's diary is a book that appears on the ground after defeating the muttadiles in the Chambers of Xeric .

The book details a houndmaster's exploits with the dogs in the Chambers, and the experiments that he and Xeric began to perform on them.

If lost, it can be reclaimed by defeating the muttadiles, or from a bookcase within a player-owned house .
20899:
The dark journal is a book found in the ancient chest after defeating the Great Olm in the Chambers of Xeric .

The journal, written by a Xerician High Priest, details their completed development of the Chambers and their encounter with the Great Olm, referring to it as the "Guardian in the Deep".

If lost, it can be reclaimed from the ancient chest after defeating the Great Olm, or from a bookcase within a player-owned house .
20901: Grimy noxifer is a herb found within the Chambers of Xeric . It can be grown with a Farming level of 55, by planting noxifer seeds in herb patches found within resource rooms. It must be cleaned into noxifer before it can be used to brew potions, and requires 60 Herblore to be cleaned.
20902:
Noxifer is a herb found within the Chambers of Xeric by cleaning a grimy noxifer . It can be grown with a Farming level of 55, by planting noxifer seeds in herb patches found within resource rooms. 60 Herblore is required to clean the grimy herb.

Unlike other potions, a secondary ingredient must be present in the player's inventory before it can be used on a water-filled gourd vial to create the potions listed below.
20903:

It can be planted in a resource room in the Chambers to grow noxifer .

20961:
A prayer enhance (-) is a potion made and used within the Chambers of Xeric . Each dose gradually restores the player's Prayer points for either 275 seconds (4 minutes and 35 seconds) or 290 seconds (4 minutes and 50 seconds). The duration appears to vary between players: those who receive a chatbox warning that the effect is about to expire receive the 290-second duration, while those who do not receive the warning receive the 275-second duration.

The potion is made at level 52 Herblore by using a buchu leaf on a water-filled gourd vial while carrying a cicely in the inventory. This produces a four-dose potion and grants 13.5 Herblore experience.

It is the weakest variant of the prayer enhance potions, alongside the standard prayer enhance and the stronger prayer enhance (+) . Like the other variants, it cannot be taken outside the Chambers of Xeric.

20997:
The twisted bow is a rare reward from the Chambers of Xeric that requires a Ranged level of 85 to wield. It can fire any type of arrow, including dragon arrows . The twisted bow is extremely valuable due to its unmatched power against monsters with a high Magic level or accuracy bonus, such as Commander Zilyana and TzKal-Zuk .

Similar to the crystal bow , the bow has an attack range of 10 tiles. As all attacks have a maximum of 10 range, longrange does not provide any attack distance benefit but may still be used to gain Defence XP.
21000:
The twisted buckler is a ranged-class shield that is obtained as a possible reward from the Chambers of Xeric, requiring level 75 Ranged and Defence to equip.

The buckler currently offers the best Ranged Attack and Ranged Strength bonus for the shield slot in the game. It also has some of the best Magic defence in its slot, beaten only by the dragonfire ward and spectral spirit shield. Its melee defence bonuses are comparable to an adamant sq shield.
21003:
The elder maul is a two-handed crush weapon that requires Attack and Strength levels of 75 to wield. It can be obtained as a possible reward from the Chambers of Xeric.

It is the highest tier crush weapon available in Old School RuneScape. It overtakes the godswords as the weapon with the highest strength bonus. Despite the strength bonus, the abyssal bludgeon often has higher overall damage output against low-defence monsters because of its quicker attack speed, making it only useful in places such as Tekton. Because of its high strength bonus, it is often used as a finisher in player killing.

Although its normal attack has fairly limited use cases, its special attack surpasses that of the dragon warhammer and is best in slot for many bossing encounters and raids that utilise defence reduction including the Corporeal Beast, the Chambers of Xeric, and the Theatre of Blood.

As with the dragon warhammer, it too can be used as a substitute for a regular hammer when banging the big door at the entrance of Bandos' Stronghold in the God Wars Dungeon, as well as in the Chambers of Xeric to stun Jewelled Crabs and build any storage chest (with the required mallignum root planks and Construction level).
21006:
The Kodai wand is a one-handed staff and the strongest wand in Old School RuneScape . Requiring 80 Magic to wield, it is able to autocast Ancient Magicks , standard spells , and Arceuus combat spells , and provides unlimited water runes when equipped.

When casting a water spell with both the Kodai wand and tome of water equipped, the accuracy and damage bonuses from the tome are used while also using soaked page charges.

Passive effect: The wand has a 15% chance of negating rune costs when casting an offensive spell.

The wand is created by using a Kodai insignia , obtained as a reward at the end of the Chambers of Xeric , on a master wand . When creating the wand, the chatbox will state Power shoots down the length of the wand, empowering it with the darkness of Xeric's Kodai wizards. This process cannot be reverted.
21009:
The dragon sword is a one-handed stab weapon obtained as a rare drop from wyrms or lost ironwood crates , and requires 60 Attack to wield. It has the highest stab attack bonus of the standard shortswords , and the third highest stab attack bonus of all shortswords. The dragon sword provides 2 less stab attack than the leaf-bladed sword , but provides 13 more strength bonus .

As with most dragon equipment , the dragon sword cannot be made from raw materials using the Smithing skill.
21012:
The dragon hunter crossbow is a one-handed crossbow and dragonbane weapon obtained as a possible reward from the Chambers of Xeric, requiring 70 Ranged to wield. It can fire up to and including dragon bolts. The crossbow has an attack range of 7, and the longrange combat style will increase it by 2.

After claiming the hard tier rewards from the Combat Achievements system, the dragon hunter crossbow can be combined with kbd heads to create a black variant. Similarly, a turquoise variant can be made with Vorkath's head after claiming the elite tier rewards.

The dragon hunter crossbow's dragonbane passive effect is its 30% increase in ranged accuracy and 25% increase in damage when fighting draconic creatures, such as dragons and wyverns. However, Elvarg and revenant dragons are not affected by this bonus. This stacks additively with the Slayer helm (i), but multiplicatively with Void Knight equipment and salve amulets.

Other than the dragonbane effect, the dragon hunter crossbow is near identical to the dragon crossbow, but lacking a special attack and having 1 higher ranged bonus.
21015:
Dinh's bulwark is a two-handed shield created by Dinh , a Lovakengj smith of unparalleled skill. It requires 75 Attack and Defence to wield and is obtained as a rare reward from the Chambers of Xeric .

As the strongest shield in-game (barring any passive effects ), it is often equipped alongside magically defensive armour (such as black dragonhide armour ) while doing non-combat activities in the Wilderness to defend against player killing and/or dangerous monsters. As a two-handed shield, the bulwark is also capable of attacking opponents. In order to attack with the bulwark, it must be set to the pummel option. This also allows it to perform its special attack.

Players wielding the bulwark will not be able to cast any combat spells; players attempting to do so will receive the message " Your bulwark gets in the way ". When in defensive mode, the dwarf multicannon will not fire, but it will still rotate, with a filterable message stating " Your bulwark shuns your cowardliness; stopping your cannon from firing. "

21027:
The dark relic is a possible reward from the Chambers of Xeric . It has a Commune option which will result in the chat box stating A dark power emanates from the relic. You sense that this power can be directed.

Upon communing with the relic, the player may choose a skill in which to receive experience . If the chosen skill is one of the skills used in the Chambers of Xeric – combat skills, Mining , Woodcutting , Herblore , Farming , Hunter , Cooking , Fishing , Thieving , Firemaking , or Agility – the player will receive 150 times their level in that skill as experience. If the chosen skill is not on this list, the player will instead only receive 50 times the corresponding skill level as experience. Construction is not included in the list of skills that receive an additional experience bonus, despite it being used to build storage units .
21028:
The dragon harpoon is a wieldable harpoon that requires 61 Fishing to use and 60 Attack to wield. The harpoon gives the player a 20% increased catch rate compared to the regular harpoon, reduced to 5% at Tempoross. Its combat stats are comparable to the dragon dagger, but it is 1 tick slower. It can be stored in a tackle box.

As with most dragon equipment, the dragon harpoon cannot be made from raw materials using the Smithing skill.
21031:
The infernal harpoon is a special non-tradeable harpoon created by using a smouldering stone on a dragon harpoon , requiring 75 Fishing [ not boostable ] and 85 Cooking [ not boostable ] to craft. This cannot be boosted. It is non-reversible and grants 350 Cooking and 200 Fishing experience. It can be stored in a tackle box .

Fish caught with a charged harpoon have a 1/3 (33%) chance to be cooked and destroyed instantly, granting half of the Cooking experience that would normally be gained from cooking the fish otherwise. Harpoonfish caught within the Tempoross minigame are not destroyed when cooked, making it a popular upgrade that saves 3 ticks (1.8 seconds) per fish. The harpoon will not consume big fish, such as the big shark . [ 1 ] Fishing training methods using tick manipulation also can use the infernal harpoon to avoid dropping 1/3rd of the fish caught.

Since it cannot revert to its components and cannot be traded, if lost on death in level 20 or higher Wilderness it is converted to 11,000 .

If all 5,000 charges are used on raw sharks , 525,000 Cooking experience will be gained which would save about 2 hours of cooking and destroy 3,685,000 in fish.

When using the infernal harpoon at leaping harpoonfish spots at Tempoross , or when using it with Rada's blessing and/or spirit flakes , the extra fish has a separate independent chance to be cooked.

21140:
Efaritay's aid is a topaz ring enchanted via the Lvl-3 Enchant spell. When worn, it improves the player's effectiveness against vampyric creatures by increasing the damage dealt to them by 10% and accuracy by 15% (stackable with the Black mask(i)/Slayer helmet(i)). Additionally, it allows non-silver weaponry to be used against Tier 2 vampyres, albeit dealing half their usual damage.

A ring will provide 200 charges before shattering, though players may also use the right-click "Break" option ahead of time, in order to start from fresh with the next ring. One charge is consumed per attack while Efaritay's aid is equipped, provided the attack was a successful hit against a relevant target. Ring charges will not be consumed when attacking a monster that is not vampyric. Given the cost of the ring, each charge costs around 9.4 coins.

The warning Your ring has 10 charges left. will be displayed when the ring has 10 charges remaining. When the ring breaks, the message Your ring crumbles to dust. will be displayed.

The ring is named after Efaritay Hallow, who is the former ruler of the kingdom of Hallowvale, which was conquered by vampyres and is today known as Morytania.
21143:
A dodgy necklace is an opal necklace enchanted via the Lvl-1 Enchant spell.

While equipped, the necklace provides a 25% chance to prevent the player from being stunned and damaged while pickpocketing NPCs. The necklace begins with 10 charges; one charge is consumed each time the necklace successfully prevents damage. When the last charge is consumed, the necklace crumbles to dust. This stacks multiplicatively with the spell Shadow Veil, where Shadow Veil will attempt to avoid the stun first for a total of 36.25% chance to not take damage from a failed pickpocket. As the player cannot fail a pickpocket attempt on a knocked out NPC, damage taken during blackjacking can only be received by failing a knockout; as such, a dodgy necklace will have no effect on blackjacking.

As in the case of other enchanted items of jewellery (such as the ring of forging), the charges stored on this necklace are specific to the player, not the item itself. This means that players will lose a dodgy necklace after 10 uses irrespective of the particular one they have equipped, and all dodgy necklaces will show the same charge when checked.

Depending on the NPC being pickpocketed, one necklace can prevent 10 to 50 damage and 40 to 60 seconds of being stunned.

The necklace of passage is a jade necklace enchanted via the Lvl-2 Enchant spell requiring a Magic level of 27. Right-clicking the necklace in your inventory and selecting "rub", or right-clicking it while equipped will allow the player to teleport to one of four possible locations. Using the necklace to teleport will consume a charge. After all five charges are used, the necklace will disintegrate into dust.

When teleporting using the necklace, the message You rub the necklace... will be displayed, followed by a message with the number of charges remaining, ex. Your necklace of passage has three uses left. If using the last charge on the necklace, the message Your necklace of passage crumbles away. will be displayed instead.

Equipping the necklace yields no stat bonuses so wearing it is purely cosmetic or to conserve inventory space.

The necklace of passage is one of the few pieces of teleportation jewellery excluded from jewellery boxes, so players must retain a necklace if they wish to utilise its features.

A necklace of faith is a topaz necklace enchanted via the Lvl-3 Enchant spell.

When worn, the necklace will restore the wearer's prayer points by 25% of Prayer level if their hitpoints drop below 20% of their maximum. Once the effect takes place, the necklace will degrade to dust. However, if the player is reduced to zero hitpoints from above 20%, the necklace will have no effect and the player will die as usual.

If Redemption is active while the necklace is worn and the player is reduced to below 10% hitpoints from above 20% in one hit, the necklace of faith will trigger first, restoring prayer points which are immediately consumed by Redemption. As the healing from Redemption is not dependent on current prayer points, this would effectively make the necklace of faith's effect useless.
21160:
An amulet of bounty is an opal amulet enchanted via the Lvl-1 Enchant spell.

The amulet begins with 10 charges. When equipped, there is a 25% chance to use one seed instead of three when planting them in allotment patches, consuming 1 charge. After all charges are used, the amulet will crumble to dust.

Similar to a ring of recoil, amulet of bounty charges are accounted per player, not per amulet. Thus if the player sells or casts High Level Alchemy on an amulet with 1 charge remaining, the next amulet the player equips will still have only 1 charge. The player can right-click to "break" an amulet of bounty, destroying it and restoring the next amulet of bounty the player equips to 10 charges.

It's not possible to exploit the effect by holding only 1 seed in the inventory.
21163:
An amulet of chemistry is a jade amulet enchanted via the Lvl-2 Enchant spell.

Each amulet begins with 5 charges. While the amulet is equipped, there is a 5% chance that you will create a 4-dose potion rather than a 3-dose potion when brewing potions (but with no extra experience), which consumes one charge. Once all of the amulet's charges are used up, the amulet crumbles to dust. When the amulet crumbles to dust, the player will either continue making potions or stop depending on the choice selected in the Options menu of the amulet. Each amulet lasts for an average of 100 potions made.

Similar to a ring of recoil, amulet of chemistry charges are stored per player, not per amulet. Thus if the player gets rid of an amulet with 1 charge remaining, the next amulet the player equips will still have only 1 charge. The player can right-click and "break" an amulet of chemistry, destroying it and restoring the next amulet of chemistry the player equips to 5 charges.

The amulet of chemistry can also be used to charge the upgraded variant, the Alchemist's amulet, with an additional 5 charges for a total of 10 charges per amulet.

21177:
The expeditious bracelet is an opal bracelet enchanted with the Lvl-1 Enchant spell.

When worn, the bracelet provides a 25% chance for a monster killed to count as two kills toward the player's Slayer task without granting additional experience. The use of this is to speed up Slayer tasks the player does not particularly like doing. This effect is the inverse of the effect of the bracelet of slaughter . The bracelet only needs to be worn at the moment the monster is slain (more specifically, when the Slayer experience drop appears) for the effect to occur, so for the rest of the fight, players may wear other bracelets or gloves such as Barrows gloves .

All expeditious bracelets share the same pool of 30 charges, with a charge consumed every time the worn effect is activated. (It is possible for a charge to be consumed on the last kill of a Slayer task.) When the last charge is consumed, the number of charges will reset to 30, and the worn bracelet will disappear. Dropping or alching a bracelet will not reset the shared charges; the only way to reset the charges at will is to use the right-click "break" option to sacrifice a bracelet early. In addition, the elite Combat Achievements rewards add a 10% chance for the bracelet to regenerate rather than disappearing, allowing it to be used for another set of charges.

The number of charges for a given task can be estimated as C = x 5 , where C is the charges required and x is the assigned Slayer count.

For example, an assigned Slayer count of 180 results in: C = 180 5 = 36 .
21180:
A Flamtaer bracelet is a jade bracelet enchanted via the Lvl-2 Enchant spell.

When equipped, each build at the Shades of Mort'ton temple increases the Sancticity at a higher rate, allowing players to create Serum 208 and Sacred oil faster. The bracelet will provide 80 charges before disappearing; one charge is depleted as a player completes a repair. Building the temple solo with a Flamtaer hammer and a few Flamtaer bracelets is possible.

The bracelet is still useful once the temple is built, as you generate around 75% more Sanctity when repairing whilst it is equipped. When paired with a Flamtaer Hammer, players in the Shades of Mort'on themed world can generate enough sancticity to convert about one and a half full inventories of 4-dose olive oils into sacred oil before the bracelet runs out of charges.
21183:
A bracelet of slaughter is a topaz bracelet enchanted via the Lvl-3 Enchant spell.

When worn, there is a 25% chance for a Slayer task kill to not count as a kill towards it, but still granting the appropriate Slayer experience (excluding TzTok-Jad and TzKal-Zuk). This results in Slayer tasks lasting 33.3% longer on average. This effect is the inverse of the expeditious bracelets effect. Note that the bracelet needs to be worn only for the tick the Slayer XP drop appears for the effect to occur. This means that for the rest of the fight, other bracelets or gloves can be worn such as the Barrows gloves. The effects of the bracelet make it an ideal switch choice when completing desirable tasks, primarily bosses when inventory space is not an issue.

All bracelets of slaughter share the same pool of 30 charges, with a charge consumed every time the worn effect is activated. When the last charge is consumed, the number of charges will reset to 30, and the worn bracelet will disappear. Dropping or alching a bracelet will not reset the shared charges; the only way to reset the charges at will is to use the right-click "break" option to sacrifice a bracelet early. In addition, the elite Combat Achievements rewards add a 10% chance for the bracelet to regenerate rather than disappearing, allowing it to be used for another set of charges.

On average, you will need 1 charge per 3 assigned monsters. So, an estimate of the number of charges can be calculated as C=x3 , where C is the charges required and x is the assigned slayer count. For example, an assigned slayer count of 132 results in: C=1323=44.

Players can estimate the number of bracelets required per task by dividing the number of charges required by 30 and rounding up. In this example, the number of bracelets required is ⌈4430⌉=⌈1.46⌉=2, so the player will need 2 bracelets of slaughter. You can also simply divide the assigned slayer count by 90 to receive the same answer.

At the current price of the bracelet, the price per extra kill is about 63.83.

21187:
The rock golem is a members-only skilling pet that can be obtained while training Mining . The chances of getting it are dependent on the player's Mining level, and the time it takes to gather a resource.

When a player receives the pet, it will automatically try to appear as their follower. At the same time, a message in the chatbox will state You have a funny feeling like you're being followed. However, if a player receives a pet while having a follower out (for example, a cat ), it will be placed into their inventory . When this occurs, the message in the chatbox will instead state You feel something weird sneaking into your backpack. This message also occurs if there is one last inventory space while the player already has a pet following them, in which case the pet will appear in the inventory instead and the resource dropped to the ground. [ 1 ]

On death, if a player loses their pet (as a follower or in your inventory) it will wander around for 30 seconds before disappearing completely. It can then be reclaimed from Probita in East Ardougne for no cost.

A lava battlestaff (or) is a lava battlestaff with a lava staff upgrade kit attached to it. The kit gives no additional bonuses, and is only used to add aesthetics to the staff. It costs 579,054 for both the parts to make the lava battlestaff (or).

While the staff is untradeable in its ornamented state, it can be reverted anytime, returning the lava battlestaff. However, the kit will not be returned.

If a player dies with the staff and it is not one of the player's protected items, the staff will revert to its default appearance, and players must use another lava staff upgrade kit to enhance its appearance again.
21200:
The mystic lava staff (or) is a mystic lava staff with a lava staff upgrade kit attached to it. The kit gives no additional bonuses, and is only used to add aesthetics to the staff. It costs 595,784 for both the parts to make the lava staff (or).

This staff can be also be created after the completion of the quest Scorpion Catcher by taking a lava battlestaff (or) and 40,000 to Thormac . After completion of the Hard Kandarin Diary and Elite Kandarin Diary , Thormac will only require 30,000 or 20,000 respectively.

While the staff is untradeable in its ornamented state, it can be reverted anytime, returning the mystic lava staff. However, the kit will not be returned.

If a player dies with the staff and it is not one of the player's protected items, the staff will revert to its default appearance, and players must use another lava staff upgrade kit to enhance its appearance again.

Upon using the upgrade kit, the upgraded lava battlestaff becomes untradeable and the kit is consumed. The staff may be reverted to a staff again by selecting the "revert" option. The upgrade kit will not be returned upon reverting the ornate lava staff.

21255:
The slayer's staff (e) is an upgraded version of the slayer's staff , obtained by using a slayer's enchantment on it. It requires 75 Magic and 55 Slayer to wield. It can be used to cast Magic Dart like the normal version of the staff.

Upon enchanting the staff, it becomes untradeable and gains 2,500 charges. Once the charges run out, it will revert to a regular Slayer's staff, and an additional Slayer's enchantment must be used on it.

Using the staff increases the damage dealt by Magic Dart when attacking a Slayer monster the player is assigned to kill. Specifically, the max hit of Magic Dart when using the slayer's staff (e) increases from ⌊ M a g i c L e v e l × 1 10 ⌋ + 10 to ⌊ M a g i c L e v e l × 1 6 ⌋ + 13 . This stacks with other magic-damage boosts like the occult necklace , tormented bracelet , and black mask (i) / slayer helmet (i) . Each cast of Magic Dart consumes 1 charge from the staff if the spell hits. If the spell does not hit, no charges will be consumed. Charges are also not consumed (and damage is not boosted) when casting Magic Dart on a monster that is not a current Slayer assignment.
21257:
The Slayer's enchantment is a parchment that is used on a Slayer's staff to enchant it into a Slayer's staff (e) with 2,500 charges. Once the charges run out, it reverts to a basic Slayer's staff.

Using the enchantment increases the max hit of Magic Dart whilst using the staff from ⌊MagicLevel×110⌋+10 to ⌊MagicLevel×16⌋+13. The enchanted Slayer's staff requires 75 Magic and 55 Slayer to wield, which is a significant difference from the basic Slayer's staff requirement of level 50 Magic and level 55 Slayer.

It is dropped by monsters in the Wilderness while on a Slayer task given by Krystilia.
21259:
The enchanted scroll is a quest item used only in Client of Kourend . It is obtained from Veos at the start of the quest.

A feather must be used on it to obtain an enchanted quill .

Duplicates can be banked by talking to Veos to obtain another. After giving Veos the scroll and quill, all copies in the bank are deleted. This item cannot leave a placeholder.
21260:
The enchanted quill is a quest item used only in Client of Kourend . It is made by using a feather on an enchanted scroll .

It is to write on the enchanted scroll so the client can see what the player is writing without any visible writing.

Duplicates can be obtained by banking the first one to obtain another. After giving Veos the scroll and quill, all copies in the inventory and bank are deleted. This item cannot leave a placeholder. If a player tries to make another quill while already having one in their inventory, a message will appear saying that "there's no need to make another". If a player tries to use the quill on an enchanted scroll, then a message appears saying that "you can't create another quill... by using the quill on the scroll."
21261:
The mysterious orb is a quest item used only in Client of Kourend . It is obtained from Veos after returning the enchanted scroll and quill to him.

It must be taken to the Dark Altar to be activated. Once the orb is activated near the Dark Altar, it will shatter into broken glass . If a player activates the orb anywhere else, a message appears stating that the orb is unresponsive.

Duplicates can be obtained by banking the first one to obtain another. After completing the quest, all copies in the inventory and bank are deleted.
21262:
The antique lamp is a quest item reward in Client of Kourend . It grants 500 experience in a skill of the player's choosing.

The lamps cannot be banked. However, if the player prefers to use them at a later date, they can be destroyed and reclaimed from Veos or Cabin Boy Herbert whenever the player wishes to do so.

It can only be obtained once players offer to help them recover the collar after using wolf bones on Veos , and cannot be deposited into a bank . Multiple can be obtained; however, upon completing the task, duplicates are removed.
