21859:
The Wise old man's santa hat is an untradeable event item rewarded after completing a Christmas event. It appears to be a combination santa hat and blue party hat.

If destroyed, a replacement can be obtained from Diango in Draynor Village or from the toy box of a costume room.
21861: Enchanted curtains is an item obtained from the Wise Old Man during the 2017 Christmas event . It is used on a snowball obtained outside the grotto to turn it into enchanted snowy curtains .
21862: Enchanted snowy curtains is an item obtained by using a snowball on some enchanted curtains during the 2017 Christmas event . It is given to Iffie in order to create the snow imp costume .
21863:
The Wise old man's teleport tablet is an item obtained during the 2017 Christmas event. It is given to the player so that they can return conveniently to the Land of Snow once they have made the snow imp costume.

Unlike most event items, if this item is destroyed during the event, it cannot be reobtained, and players must return to the Land of Snow by speaking to the Wise Old Man in his house.
21864: Snow sprites are obtained in the Land of Snow, outside Santa's Grotto during the 2017 Christmas event . They can only be caught with a fine mesh net equipped, and three are required in order to light up Dolph 's nose.
21865:
The Fine mesh net is an item obtained in Santa's Grotto during the 2017 Christmas event. It is used to catch Snow Sprites to light up Dolph's nose.

After the event is completed, it was automatically taken away from the player. However, players could reobtain it by revisiting the Land of Snow via speaking to the Wise Old Man after completing the event. After the event ended, it was automatically deleted from every player.

It cannot be used as a net for butterflies or implings, even if it is reobtained after the event.
21866: The Santa suit is obtained from the wardrobe in Santa's Grotto during the 2017 Christmas event . It is used on the washer furnace after it has been fuelled to produce a wet Santa suit .
21867: The Santa suit (wet) is obtained during the 2017 Christmas event by using a Santa suit on the washer furnace after it has been fuelled. The wet suit is to be used on a fuelled dryer furnace to produce a dry Santa suit .
21868: The Santa suit (dry) is obtained during the 2017 Christmas event by using a wet Santa suit on the dryer furnace after it has been fuelled. The dry suit is to be given to the Wise Old Man so that he can dress up as Santa.
21869: Logs and kindling are obtained in Santa 's Grotto during the 2017 Christmas event . Two are used to light up the washer and dryer furnaces in order to shrink the Santa suit for the Wise Old Man .
21870: The Promissory note is obtained during the 2017 Christmas event by using the desk while having Santa's seal. It is given to Diango as payment for the toys the Wise Old Man requires.
21871: Santa's seal is obtained during the 2017 Christmas event by searching the shelf within Santa's vault. It is used to sign the promissory note .
21872: The Vault key is obtained during the 2017 Christmas event by searching the plant in the south-west corner of Santa's Grotto. It is used to open the vault to obtain Santa's seal .
21873: An empty sack is obtained from Santa's Grotto during the 2017 Christmas event. It is used to fill the toys that the Foreman gives to the player.
21874: A bulging sack is obtained from the Foreman during the 2017 Christmas event. It is given to the Wise Old Man so that he can deliver the presents.
21875:
A Kristmas kebab is obtained during the 2017 Christmas event by searching the kebab meat cooker in Santa's Grotto.

When a player eats the kebab, a message will appear in the chatbox, stating The warmth of the meat and Christmas spices suffuse your mouth, it tastes somewhat like reindeer. Zero health is regained.

The examine text spells donner incorrectly, with the actual spelling being doner. This may imply that Donner, one of Santa's reindeers, was cooked into a kebab, as he is not found with the other reindeer. This is reinforced by speaking to Dolph after relighting his nose, in which he exclaims I'd rather end up like Donner than have another sprite shoved where the sun don't shine!
21880:
Wrath runes are the highest level runes in Old School RuneScape. Released alongside the Dragon Slayer II quest, they are used for surge spells, which are the strongest elemental spells in the standard spellbook, and offering spells in the Arceuus spellbook.

Wrath runes can be made with 95 Runecraft at the Wrath Altar by using pure essence or daeyalt essence on it, providing 8 or 12 Runecraft experience each, respectively. Scarred extracts can also be used to increase the quantity of crafted wrath runes by 60 per pure essence, requiring partial completion of Desert Treasure II - The Fallen Empire and access to the Scar essence mine.

Access to the Wrath Altar requires completion of the Dragon Slayer II quest. To enter the Wrath Altar, the player needs a wrath talisman or tiara, catalytic talisman or tiara, or a Runecraft cape. The Wrath Altar can be reached by entering the statue in the Myths' Guild and going west then south in the dungeon, through the blue dragons and entering the crevice in the southern wall, ending up on an island with the altar ruins.

Wrath runes cannot be obtained via the Ourania Altar and the altar cannot be accessed via the Abyss.
21882:
Dragon armour set (lg) is an item obtained by exchanging a set of items with a Grand Exchange clerk via their right-click "Sets" option and clicking on the appropriate item set within the Item Sets interface.

Sets are commonly used to reduce the amount of bank space taken up.
21885:
Dragon armour set (sk) is an item obtained by exchanging a set of items with a Grand Exchange clerk via their right-click "sets" option and clicking on the appropriate item set within the Item Sets interface.

Sets are commonly used to reduce the amount of bank space taken up.
21888:
The turquoise Slayer helmet is a piece of equipment that is worn in the helmet slot. It is a cosmetic upgrade to the Slayer helmet .

It can be created by adding Vorkath's head after purchasing the ability Undead Head for 1,000 Slayer reward points from any Slayer master . This is reversible, and the head will be returned to the inventory along with the slayer helmet's components. If a player loses the turquoise slayer helmet in a PvP death, Vorkath's head will be placed in their gravestone.
21890:
The turquoise Slayer helmet (i) is a piece of equipment that is worn in the helmet slot. It is a cosmetic upgrade to the Slayer helmet (i) .

It can be created by adding Vorkath's head after purchasing the ability Undead Head for 1,000 Slayer reward points from any Slayer master . This is reversible, and the head will be returned to the inventory along with the slayer helmet's components. If a player loses the turquoise slayer helmet (i) in a PvP death, Vorkath's head will be placed in their gravestone.
21892:
The dragon platebody is an armour used in melee and the strongest of all standard platebodies. It requires 60 Defence and completion of the quest Dragon Slayer I to equip.

It offers some of the highest bonuses of any non-degradable armour in the game, providing higher slash and stab defence than the Bandos chestplate. For melee use it is a direct upgrade to the dragon chainbody in every stat except crush, with the chainbody having +1 crush defence more than the platebody. Despite its high defensive bonuses however, the dragon platebody lacks a strength bonus, making it less commonly used for general melee training.

Players with level 90 Smithing can make one by using a dragon chainbody, dragon metal lump, and dragon metal shard at the Dragon Forge, granting 2,000 experience.

A dragon platebody ornament kit, obtained from master clue scrolls, can be attached to create a gold-trimmed dragon platebody (g). This is only cosmetic, and does not affect the platebody's stat bonuses. It can be dismantled, returning the platebody and ornament kit.

It is considered a piece of the dragon armour set.
21895:
A dragon kiteshield is a kiteshield made by combining a dragon sq shield , dragon metal shard , and dragon metal slice at the Dragon Forge after the completion of Dragon Slayer II . This process requires a hammer and 75 Smithing , granting 1,000 Smithing experience . The dragon kiteshield does not require Legends' Quest to wield, despite being created from the dragon sq shield. Like other dragon equipment , it requires 60 Defence to wield.

Just like the dragon sq shield, the dragon kiteshield does not protect against dragonfire .

Players can attach a dragon kiteshield ornament kit , obtained from master clue scrolls , to create a gold-trimmed dragon kiteshield (g) . This marginally increases the kiteshield's Ranged attack bonus (from -3 to -2), but is otherwise cosmetic. It can be dismantled, returning the kiteshield and ornament kit.
21898:
The Assembler max cape is the result of combining Ava's assembler with a max cape , during which the max hood required to be in the player's inventory will automatically convert to the assembler max hood .

Like the other max cape variants (a max cape combined with another cape slot item), the assembler max cape does not have the max cape's stats or perks; it only acts as a cosmetic upgrade to Ava's assembler with the following exceptions when worn:

The max cape and assembler can be separated by using a knife on the cape. Mac will also buy back a max cape, along with its variants, for 1,900,800 coins each. He will return the secondary item any max cape variant was combined with upon doing so.

Turning the Ava's assembler into an assembler max cape is the only way for ultimate ironmen to store one, as it counts as a max cape on the cape rack.

If the player dies a PvP death and the item is unprotected, it will remain in the player's inventory; however, the item will be in a broken, unusable state and must be repaired by using it on Perdu and paying him 240,000 coins .
21900:
Assembler max hood is a hood created by using Ava's assembler on a max cape . When the assembler max cape is created, the max hood that is required to be in the player's inventory during the cape's creation is automatically converted to the assembler max hood.

If players are refunding the assembler max cape via Mac , the player must also have the assembler max hood in their inventory.

Should players lose the hood, they may reclaim it from Mac for free.
21902:
The dragon crossbow is a crossbow that is stronger than the rune crossbow . It requires a Ranged level of 64 to wield, and can fire bolts up to dragon bolts . It has an attack range of 7 increased to 9 with longrange.

Dragon crossbows can be made through the Fletching skill at level 78; a player must first cut a magic stock for the crossbow from magic logs , granting 70 Fletching experience . Then, a player must add dragon limbs to the stock with a hammer in their inventory, granting 135 experience and making an unstrung dragon crossbow . Finally, they must string the crossbow with a crossbow string , granting 70 experience. Creating a dragon crossbow from raw materials grants 275 Fletching experience in total. A dragon crossbow can be changed cosmetically by using a Bounty hunter ornament kit on it to become a dragon crossbow (cr) . The ornament kit can be obtained by participating in Bounty Hunter and earning 50 Bounty Hunter Points needed to purchase one from the Bounty Hunter Store .
21905:
Dragon bolts are a type of crossbow ammo that can only be fired from a dragon crossbow, Armadyl crossbow, dragon hunter crossbow, or Zaryte crossbow. Additionally, they require a Ranged level of 64 to wield. As with most bolts, they can be poisoned, however this will prevent the addition of bolt tips.

They can only be obtained by using feathers on unfinished dragon bolts. Doing so requires level 84 in Fletching and grants 12 experience per bolt.

Bolt tips of any kind, excluding amethyst, can be added to dragon bolts and then enchanted to obtain enchanted bolts that possess the ranged strength of dragon bolts.
21907:
Vorkath's head is an item dropped by Vorkath. The head has various uses, such as being used to upgrade Ava's accumulator, as a cosmetic upgrade to the Slayer helmet, or sacrificed for Prayer experience. For any given kill, the drop rate of the head is 1/50, with the exception of the 50th kill, when the drop is guaranteed.

Players can take the head along with 75 mithril arrows, and either Ava's accumulator or 4,999 coins (for a new device), to Ava in Draynor Manor to obtain Ava's assembler, which gives increased stats and improved ammo return. Players can also use the head on a ranging or max cape to give the enhanced ammo-returning effect to those capes. Additionally, players can bring the assembler and Dizana's quiver to Ava to grant the quiver the ammo-returning effect.
21909:
Vorkath's stuffed head is obtained by bringing Vorkath's head and 50,000 coins to the taxidermist in Canifis; this process is reversible by selecting the "Unstuff" option on the item.

Once stuffed, it can be mounted at a gilded display within the skill hall in a player-owned house with level 82 Construction, granting 223 Construction alongside 200 Attack, Strength, Defence, Magic, and Ranged experience, with players being given the option to decline the combat experience before mounting the heads.
21911:
The Rune dragon is an interface item that can be seen in the Construction skill guide representing the Rune dragon .

The actual item cannot be obtained by players.
21912:
The Mounted Vorkath head is an interface item that can be seen in the Construction skill guide representing the Vorkath's head (mounted) .

The actual item cannot be obtained by players.
21913:
The Mythical cape (mounted) is an interface item that can be seen in the Construction skill guide representing the mythical cape .

The actual item cannot be obtained by players.
21914:
Ava's assembler is the upgraded version of Ava's accumulator that requires level 70 Ranged to equip. The assembler gives the second best Ranged attack bonus for the cape slot and is one of the few cape slot items that provides a Ranged Strength bonus. To obtain the assembler, players must take 75 mithril arrows, Ava's accumulator (or 4,999 coins), and Vorkath's head (which can only be obtained by killing Vorkath after completion of Dragon Slayer II) to Ava in Draynor Manor.

Like all of Ava's devices, the assembler does not work when metal torso armour is worn, as this will cause 'interference'; this includes most melee armour as well as Ahrim's robetop. A list of metal torso armour that does not interfere with Ava's assembler can be found here.

Similar to its predecessors, it can randomly gather mithril ranged equipment. It also has an 80% chance of saving ammunition compared to the accumulator's 72%. As the remaining 20% chance is for the ammunition breaking, the assembler will never drop any ammo on the ground.

The breakdown of the ammo recovery rate is as listed:

Break on impact: 20%

Recovered automatically: 80%

The appearance of the assembler can be ornamented using a Masori crafting kit to match that of the Masori armour. It is solely a cosmetic upgrade and does not change its stats.

21921: A dragon crossbow (u) is made by using a magic stock with dragon limbs , requiring 78 Fletching and yielding 135 Fletching experience . Attaching a crossbow string to it makes a dragon crossbow , also requiring 78 Fletching and yielding an additional 70 Fletching experience.
21924:
Dragon bolts are a type of crossbow ammo that can only be fired from a dragon crossbow, Armadyl crossbow, dragon hunter crossbow, or Zaryte crossbow. Additionally, they require a Ranged level of 64 to wield. As with most bolts, they can be poisoned, however this will prevent the addition of bolt tips.

They can only be obtained by using feathers on unfinished dragon bolts. Doing so requires level 84 in Fletching and grants 12 experience per bolt.

Bolt tips of any kind, excluding amethyst, can be added to dragon bolts and then enchanted to obtain enchanted bolts that possess the ranged strength of dragon bolts.

21975:
Crushed superior dragon bones are a secondary ingredient used to create super antifire potions, which require level 92 Herblore to make. They can be obtained by using a pestle and mortar with superior dragon bones, which in turn can be obtained by killing Vorkath or frost dragons.

They can be stored in a reagent pouch while superior dragon bones cannot, which can allow saving inventory space when fighting Vorkath repeatedly.
21978:
A super antifire potion is a potion made with Herblore that provides complete immunity to regular dragonfire for three minutes, as well as partially blocking the stronger dragonfire of Galvek and Vorkath. It may only be used after starting Dragon Slayer I.

It can be made by a player with 92 Herblore by adding crushed superior dragon bones to an antifire potion, which grants 130 Herblore experience. With 98 Herblore, the super antifire potion can be upgraded to an extended super antifire with lava scale shards.

To be able to create super antifire potions, the process must first be learned by speaking to Primula, who can be found on the 1st floor inside the Myths' Guild, which requires completion of Dragon Slayer II to enter.

It will completely block the King Black Dragon's standard dragonfire, but not at all his special dragonfires, which can still hit up to 50, so pairing this potion with an anti-dragon shield is recommended. Given that there is no difference in damage taken between using an anti-dragon shield + (regular) antifire potion versus using an anti-dragon shield + super antifire potion, it's actually better to use a regular antifire potion for this boss, given that its effect lasts twice as long per dose. For more information, read the dragonfire page.

After Barbarian Herblore Training is completed, caviar can be added to a super antifire potion(2) to produce a super antifire mix. This requires 98 Herblore and provides 70 Herblore experience. A super antifire mix has 2 doses, each of which heals 6 Hitpoints in addition to the usual super antifire behaviour.

21990:
The rift guardian is a members-only skilling pet that can be obtained while training Runecraft. The chances of getting it are dependent on the player's Runecraft level, the rune the player is crafting, and the number of essence used. Upon using the Guardian's eye on it, which is purchased from the Guardians of the Rift reward shop for 3,000 abyssal pearls, players unlock a permanent metamorphosis option to turn it into the Greatish guardian.

When a player receives the pet, it will automatically try to appear as their follower. At the same time, a message in the chatbox will state You have a funny feeling like you're being followed. However, if a player receives a pet while having a follower out (for example, a cat), it will be placed into their inventory. When this occurs, the message in the chatbox will instead state You feel something weird sneaking into your backpack.

When runecrafting using dark essence fragments, the pet is given after they are removed and the runes are given back. This means if there is not already some of the runes to be crafted in the inventory, and the rest of the inventory is full, and a pet is already following the player, the rift guardian will not be given; it must instead be claimed from Probita in East Ardougne.

On death, if a player loses their pet (as a follower or in your inventory) it will wander around the area for 30 seconds before despawning. Even if the player returns in time, the pet cannot be picked up, and can be reclaimed from Probita.
21992:
Vorki is a pet dropped by Vorkath. It is a much smaller version of Vorkath.

When a player receives the pet, it will automatically try to appear as their follower. At the same time, a message in the chatbox will state You have a funny feeling like you're being followed. However, if a player receives a pet while having a follower out (for example, a cat), it will be placed into their inventory. When this occurs, the message in the chatbox will instead state You feel something weird sneaking into your backpack.

If a player's inventory is full and they have a follower already, they will not receive the pet; it must instead be claimed from Probita in East Ardougne.

On death, if a player loses their pet (as a follower or in your inventory) it will wander around the area for 30 seconds before despawning. Even if the player returns in time, the pet cannot be picked up, and can be reclaimed from Probita.
21994:
Super antifire mix is a barbarian potion that provides 3 minutes of complete dragonfire protection and heals 6 Hitpoints. It is made by adding caviar to a super antifire potion(2), requiring level 98 Herblore and giving 70 experience. This mix can only be created after completing the Herblore part of Barbarian training with Otto Godblessed, and it may only be used after starting Dragon Slayer I.

Drinking a sip of the potion gives the message "You drink the lumpy potion". If the player drinks all doses or empties the potion, it will become a regular empty vial.

22002:
The dragonfire ward is a ranged shield requiring a Ranged level of 70 and a Defence level of 75 to equip, as well as having started Dragon Slayer I . It offers the second highest Ranged Attack and Ranged Strength bonus for the shield slot in the game, only beaten by the twisted buckler .

The ward offers two special characteristics: it acts like a regular anti-dragon shield in terms of dragonfire protection, and it provides partial protection against the icy breath of wyverns , like the elemental , mind , and dragonfire shields . This immunity does not extend to draconic creatures capable of producing a similar effect ( KBD , Vorkath , etc).

22006:
A skeletal visage is an item obtained as a very rare drop from Vorkath .

Players with 90 Smithing (can be boosted) can combine an anti-dragon shield with a skeletal visage to create a dragonfire ward . Doing so requires a hammer and grants 2,000 Smithing experience . If the player doesn't have the required Smithing level, they can take the skeletal visage to Oziach in Edgeville , who will assist in creating the shield for a payment of 1,250,000 coins . Completion of the quest Dragon Slayer I is required for Oziach to make the shield.
22009:
Map pieces are obtainable from multiple locations on the House on the Hill during the Dragon Slayer II quest. 24 pieces can be merged into a map that leads the player to Lithkren.

There are five on a stone chest in the basement.

There are three on a stone chest at the top floor.

There are four in the fungi next to the staircase outside.

There are seven scraps in a hook briar south of the house.

There are five on a mushtree just east of the house, near the strange stone.

22033:
Aivas' diary can be obtained in the dungeon beneath Lithkren by searching Aivas' charred corpse next to the ancient doors.

The diary describes the events that resulted in the discovery of Lithkren by the humans, which led to the battle on Lithkren, which Aivas led alongside Robert the Strong, Camorra Shayzien and Tristan Corvo.

If lost, it can be reclaimed from Aivas' corpse, or from a bookcase within a player-owned house.
22035:
Varrock census records can be obtained from a bookcase in the Varrock Palace Library . It is to be given to Reldo so that he can determine where the descendants of Tristan may possibly reside.

Upon reading the census records, a chat box message will appear, stating The book contains page after page of census records. You're sure it makes for a thrilling read, but you have better things to be getting on with. Maybe Reldo can read it for you instead.
22037:
Malumac's journal is a journal that can be found by searching a skeleton in the south-west corner of the Karamjan Temple found in the Kharazi Jungle .

The journal, written by Malumac , a member of an elite expeditionary group led by Skotizo and operating under Zamorak 's direct orders, details the group's goal to retrieve a powerful artefact in an underground temple beneath the Kharazi Jungle.

If lost, it can be reclaimed from Malumac's corpse, or from a bookcase within a player-owned house .
22039:
Ablenkian's escape is a book that can be found in the library of the Myths' Guild after completing Dragon Slayer II .

The book tells of a Dragon rider named Ablenkian , who along with all the other dragon riders, were branded traitors by both Zarosian and Zamorakians at the end of the Second Age , and was presumably killed by Ripper Demons .

If lost, it can be reclaimed from the Myths' Guild library, or from a bookcase within a player-owned house .
22041:
Imcandoria's fall is a book found in the library of the Myths' Guild after completing Dragon Slayer II . The book can be used on Freja , who transcribed the original text, as well as Thurgo , one of the last known Imcando dwarves .

The book, written by Highseer Gulbrand of the Isle of Garmr , details the fall of Imcandoria . The text was originally inscribed in rock paper in an extremely heavy tome and was loosely translated based on old trade scrolls written by early Fremennik tribes on the isle.

If lost, it can be reclaimed from the Myths' Guild library or from a bookcase within a player-owned house .
22043:
Imafore's betrayal is a book that can be found in the library of the Myths' Guild after completing Dragon Slayer II.

The book describes the events that led to Great Kourend's declaration of war against Varlamore.

If lost, it can be reclaimed from the Myths' Guild library, or from a bookcase within a player-owned house.
22045:
Lutwidge and the Moonfly is a poem written by a bard named Shudersque that can be found in the library of the Myths' Guild after completing Dragon Slayer II.

The poem describes the encounter between Lutwidge and the Moonfly. If players speak to Lutwidge about his grand feats, he will tell players that the poem's telling of the battle is a little embellished and rife with errors. If players have the poem in their inventory, he will also tell them that the sword was actually bathed in the sap of a yew tree, rather than sheep's blood.

If lost, it can be reclaimed from the Myths' Guild library, or from a bookcase within a player-owned house.
22047:
Serafina, or The Tale of Serafina is a book written by James Locke that can be found in the library of the Myths' Guild after completing Dragon Slayer II.

The book speaks of the Tale of Serafina, in which she takes on the Theatre of Blood and survived all of the challenges within, and was granted freedom from the blood tithes as her reward. However, it is discovered during the quest A Taste of Hope and in her diary that the tale was simply a ruse to instill false hope into the citizens of Meiyerditch so that they could provide entertainment for the vampyres.

If lost, it can be reclaimed from the Myths' Guild library, or from a bookcase within a player-owned house.
22049:
The weeping is a book written by Herbert Dunwich that can be found in the library of the Myths' Guild after completing Dragon Slayer II .

According to Mod Raven , who added the story in-game, The Weeping is simply "a sinister story with a sinister monster-y thing in it... it's a horror story basically."

If lost, it can be reclaimed from the Myths' Guild library, or from a bookcase within a player-owned house .
22051:
Old notes can be obtained during the Dragon Slayer II quest. The notes are written by Zorgoth , a dragonkin , noting his experiments to enhance the strength and aggressiveness of dragons in order to turn the tide on the war on humanity during the Fourth Age .

One of these notes can be found in the small laboratory in Crandor hidden in the north-east corner of Elvarg 's lair. Six additional notes can be found in the laboratory underneath Ungael , and seven are found in the Lithkren Vault , of which four can only be obtained after completion of Dragon Slayer II .

The notes from Ungael and the Lithkren Vault can be combined into a single book by using all notes from the same location on each other, creating the Ungael lab notes and Lithkren vault notes , respectively.

22079:
An Inert locator orb can be obtained by using two molten glass and a dragonstone with a glassblowing pipe. It is to be given to Ava so she can create a locator orb for the player.

Note after the quest, if lost, players do not need to make another orb - they simply go to see Ava in Draynor Manor, using option 3, for a replacement.
22081:
A locator orb is an item obtained by giving Ava an inert locator orb during Dragon Slayer II. After some adjustments, she will give you a locator orb to track down the Morytania dragon key piece.

Each use of this orb will reduce a player's health by 10 hitpoints down to a minimum of 1 hitpoint and cannot kill the player, similar to a dwarven rock cake. The message The locator orb is unstable and hurts you as you use it. will be displayed when used in this way. Because of this, it can be beneficial to use in combination with the Dharok's armour set. This method can also be used effectively in Nightmare Zone as it does not affect a player's absorption count.

If lost or manually "destroyed", the player can speak to Ava about "a key" for another one. After completion of Dragon Slayer II, the chat option changes with the player asking directly for more orbs instead.

Like the Dwarven rock cake, players may own multiple locator orbs at a time.
22083:
The Robert bust is obtained in Camorra's crypt on the bottom level of the Shayzien Crypts.

The bust, along with those of Camorra, Tristan Corvo, and Aivas, are used to solve a riddle to obtain Camorra's dragon key piece.
22084:
The Camorra bust is obtained in her crypt on the bottom level of the Shayzien Crypts.

The bust, along with those of Robert the Strong, Tristan Corvo, and Aivas, are used to solve a riddle to obtain Camorra's dragon key piece.
22085:

22086:

The bust, along with those of Robert the Strong, Camorra, and Tristan Corvo, are used to solve a riddle to obtain Camorra's dragon key piece.
22087:
The dragon key is a key made out of Orikalkum that is reforged during the Dragon Slayer II quest. After a player has collected all four dragon key pieces, they must be brought to the Ancient Cavern to be forged into the complete key. It is then used on the ancient doors underneath Lithkren to open the Lithkren Vault.

This item was dropped by a slain dragonkin during the assault on Lithkren in the Fourth Age by Robert the Strong, Aivas, Camorra, and Tristan. Fearing what the key may have opened, the heroes decided to split it into four pieces and hid them throughout the world.
22088: Dragon key pieces are items which can be found throughout the Dragon Slayer II quest.
22089: Dragon key pieces are items which can be found throughout the Dragon Slayer II quest.
22090: Dragon key pieces are items which can be found throughout the Dragon Slayer II quest.
22091: Dragon key pieces are items which can be found throughout the Dragon Slayer II quest.
22092:
The dragon key is an unobtainable item that can be seen in a cutscene during Dragon Slayer II . It is dropped by a slain dragonkin during the assault on Lithkren in the Fourth Age by Robert the Strong , Aivas , Camorra , and Tristan .

While the key appears visually identical to the real dragon key used to open the Lithkren Vault , it is in reality a different version of the item to prevent sequence breaking in case a player somehow manages to access the cutscene and take the item.
22093:
The ancient key is an item which can be found in the locked room in the dragonkin laboratory underneath Ungael during the Dragon Slayer II quest.

In this laboratory, six old notes can be found by searching various ancient machinery, a door can be found to the east, as well as a lever to the south-west. Once pulled, there's a limited amount of time that the doors stays open so players must be quick in order to enter the room. In this room they will find a stone chest containing the ancient key as well as a Dragon key piece .

The key is later used to unlock the mithril door in the Ancient Cavern .
22094: A water container can be found in a crate when sailing to Ungael during Dragon Slayer II . It is used to douse fires that appear on the Fremennik ship. It doesn't need to be refilled and has unlimited uses.
22095: Swamp paste can be found in a crate when sailing to Ungael during Dragon Slayer II. It is used to fill leaks that appear on the Fremennik ship during the dragon assault.
22096: Revitalisation potions can be found in a crate on Brundt 's ship when sailing to Ungael during Dragon Slayer II . They are used to heal injured Fremennik warriors if they get hit with dragon fire.
22097:
A dragon metal shard is an item that can be purchased from the Myths' Guild Armoury for 1,800,000 coins, which requires the completion of Dragon Slayer II to access.

The shard can be used alongside a dragon metal slice and a dragon sq shield to create a dragon kiteshield . Doing so requires level 75 Smithing , and grants the player 1,000 experience.

Alternatively, it can be used alongside a dragon metal lump and a dragon chainbody to create a dragon platebody . This requires level 90 in Smithing , and grants the player 2,000 experience.
22100:
The dragon metal slice is an item dropped exclusively by adamant dragons .

The slice, along with a dragon metal shard and a dragon sq shield , is used to create a dragon kiteshield . Doing so requires level 75 in Smithing , and grants the player 1,000 experience.
22103: Dragon metal lumps are dropped by rune dragons . The lump, along with a dragon metal shard and a dragon chainbody , is used to create a dragon platebody . Doing so requires level 90 in Smithing and grants the player 2,000 experience.
22106:
The jar of decay is a rare drop from Vorkath who can be found on the island of Ungael .

The jar can be used on a boss lair display in a player's achievement gallery to have a display of Vorkath. Doing so requires killing his more difficult form after completion of Dragon Slayer II at least once.
22109:
Ava's assembler is the upgraded version of Ava's accumulator that requires level 70 Ranged to equip. The assembler gives the second best Ranged attack bonus for the cape slot and is one of the few cape slot items that provides a Ranged Strength bonus. To obtain the assembler, players must take 75 mithril arrows, Ava's accumulator (or 4,999 coins), and Vorkath's head (which can only be obtained by killing Vorkath after completion of Dragon Slayer II) to Ava in Draynor Manor.

Like all of Ava's devices, the assembler does not work when metal torso armour is worn, as this will cause 'interference'; this includes most melee armour as well as Ahrim's robetop. A list of metal torso armour that does not interfere with Ava's assembler can be found here.

Similar to its predecessors, it can randomly gather mithril ranged equipment. It also has an 80% chance of saving ammunition compared to the accumulator's 72%. As the remaining 20% chance is for the ammunition breaking, the assembler will never drop any ammo on the ground.

The breakdown of the ammo recovery rate is as listed:

Break on impact: 20%

Recovered automatically: 80%

The appearance of the assembler can be ornamented using a Masori crafting kit to match that of the Masori armour. It is solely a cosmetic upgrade and does not change its stats.
22111:
The dragonbone necklace is a necklace that is dropped exclusively by Vorkath . Wearing the necklace requires level 70 in Prayer , and currently offers the highest Prayer bonus of any piece of equipment available in Old School RuneScape .

When worn, it will restore Prayer points as bones are buried (even if buried via the bonecrusher ). This effect does not stack with the Catacombs of Kourend Prayer restoration effect, and does not grant Prayer points for scattering demonic ashes .

The dragonbone necklace can be combined with the bonecrusher and a hydra tail to create the bonecrusher necklace , which combines the effects of both the dragonbone necklace and the bonecrusher.

The amount of points restored are as follows:
22114:
The mythical cape is a cape that can only be worn by those who have completed the Dragon Slayer II quest .

It can be purchased from Jack at the Mythical Cape Store on the top floor of the Myths' Guild for 10,000 coins . The cape provides unlimited free teleports to the guild. The mythical cape has the highest crush attack bonus of any cape slot item in Old School RuneScape , providing a +6 bonus.

This item can be stored in the cape rack of a costume room . It may also be mounted in the Quest Hall in the Guild trophy space , or the cape hanger in the Achievement Gallery , of a player-owned house . While mounted, the player can use it to teleport to the Myths' Guild.
22116: Superior dragon bonemeal is an item that is used for worship at the Ectofuntus . It consists of a pot filled with superior dragon bones that have been crushed in the bone grinder at the Ectofuntus.
22118:
The wrath talisman is a talisman that allows players to enter the Wrath Altar where wrath runes are crafted. The Wrath Altar is located south of the Myths' Guild, which can be accessed after completing Dragon Slayer II. Making wrath runes requires level 95 Runecraft.

The talisman can be combined with a tiara to make a wrath tiara for 52.5 Runecraft experience at the Wrath Altar, by using the tiara on the altar. This makes the talisman disappear, but the wrath tiara can be used in just the same way and can be worn on the head, saving an inventory space when crafting wrath runes.
22121:
A wrath tiara is a head slot item used in Runecraft. It is created at the Wrath Altar by using a tiara or wrath talisman on the altar with both in your inventory. This consumes the wrath talisman and yields 52.5 Runecraft experience.

While a wrath tiara is equipped, the mysterious ruins to the Wrath Altar have a left-click "Enter" option, freeing up an inventory slot that the wrath talisman would otherwise occupy.
22124:
Superior dragon bones are obtained as a guaranteed drop from killing Vorkath and as an uncommon drop from killing frost dragons . They can be crushed with a pestle and mortar to create crushed superior dragon bones , which is a secondary ingredient in super antifire potions , requiring level 92 Herblore to create.

Unlike other types of bones, superior dragon bones require a Prayer level of 70 (unboostable) to use, and give 150 Prayer experience when buried. This can be increased by offering the bones in different ways:

Superior dragon bones provide the most Prayer experience of any bone in the game, but they are very expensive, making them the top-tier choice for efficient training when cost is not a concern. When used at a gilded altar , they require 38.84 coins per experience, while regular dragon bones use 13.05 coins per experience. As such, the most economical use is as a secondary for making super antifire potions .
22127:
An adamant kiteshield is a decorative kiteshield with the symbol of Arrav . Players can paint them on a shield easel or banner easel in a player-owned house 's Workshop at level 43 Crafting with an adamant kiteshield and the appropriate crest from Sir Renitee in the White Knights' Castle .

Players must have completed the Shield of Arrav quest in order to create the kiteshield. Players can use an easel in another player's house if they do not have one in theirs.

If a player is killed by another player , the shield will convert into an adamant kiteshield if it is not protected upon death.

A maple bird house is used to set bird house traps on Fossil Island requiring 44 Hunter. It can be made at 45 Crafting using maple logs on a clockwork with a chisel and hammer yielding 35 experience.

Once placed in a bird house space, it becomes a maple birdhouse trap.

Bird houses must be baited with 10 hop seeds (5 if Wildblood), 10 allotment seeds, 10 flower seeds, 10 low level herb seeds (guam, marrentill, tarromin, harralander), or 5 high level herb seeds (ranarr and above). After approximately 50 minutes when the birdhouse is full, it can be emptied, granting 369 Hunter experience.

22207:
Glistening tears are a form of currency found in the Underwater Agility and Thieving training activity, located in the Underwater section of Fossil Island. Glistening tears can be exchanged with Mairin for experience in Agility, Thieving, or both, and are obtained by looting chests and clams during the activity. Glistening tears are always obtained alongside a mermaid's tear. Approximately 150 tears are obtainable per hour.

The most efficient way of exchanging glistening tears is selecting both skills. While it gives less experience in an individual skill, its value is higher than training the two skills independently, due to Agility being proportionally slower to train.

Players can only exchange a maximum of 700 glistening tears at once; if players exchange them for experience with more than 700 glistening tears in the inventory, the excess will be discarded. In addition, they cannot be deposited into a bank.

Choosing Agility and Thieving, the experience granted by each Glistening Tear is defined by the following equations; When exchanging for one skill, experience is multiplied by 1.5:

EA⌊0.1⌋=3×A2×910150=0.018×A2 ET⌊0.1⌋ =11×T2×910150=0.066×T2

EA is Agility experience; ET is Thieving experience; A is Agility level; T is Thieving level.

Based on 150 tears per hour.
22208: Wrath runes are a variant of normal wrath runes which can be obtained from the Attacker item machine when playing the Attacker role in Barbarian Assault. To prevent any glitches where players may be able to take runes outside of the minigame and sell them for profit, the machine gives untradeable runes that have no value. Normally, they will disappear if the player attempts to take them outside.
22209:
An extended super antifire potion is a potion that provides complete immunity against dragonfire for exactly six minutes (24 minutes per 4-dose potion). However, the potion's effects will not work on Galvek's attacks, nor will it work on the King Black Dragon's poisonous/shocking/freezing dragonbreath. It will also block Vorkath's attacks only partially. It may only be used after starting Dragon Slayer I.

To be able to create extended super antifire potions, like regular super antifire, the process must first be learned by speaking to Primula, who can be found on the 1st floor inside the Myths' Guild, which requires completion of Dragon Slayer II to enter.

It can be made by a player with 98 Herblore by mixing a regular super antifire and lava scale shards, which grants 40 Herblore experience per shard added, or 160 Herblore experience if they put in four shards into a 4-dosed potion. One dose is created per shard, so four shards will be needed to create a four-dosed extended antifire. Alternatively, it can be made by mixing a 4-dose extended antifire with crushed superior dragon bones, which grants 180 Herblore experience.

Players with 99 Herblore can mix caviar into a 2-dose extended super antifire to create an extended super antifire mix.

Players will get a warning in their chatbox when the potion is about to wear off: "Your super antifire potion is about to expire." Then they will get another message when it has worn off, approximately 15 seconds after the initial warning: "Your super antifire potion has expired." This allows you to keep track of how long you have until you have to drink again.

Bullet arrows are a special set of arrows obtained from the Attacker item machine during a game of Barbarian Assault. It is only obtainable by players if they are assigned the Attacker role, and are used to harm Penance Fighters and Rangers when they are weak to the Controlled/Bullet/Wind styles, which the Collector will call.

The feather's colours match the colour of the magic spell element that the fighters and rangers are weak to, which makes it easy to know which arrow should be equipped once the Collector has made the correct call.

The dragon boots ornament kit is a possible reward from hard Treasure Trails. It is purely decorative, and can be attached to a pair of dragon boots, making it a pair of dragon boots (g).

Once attached, the ornamented item becomes untradeable, but the kit can be detached from the item and sold.
22234:
The dragon boots (g) are dragon boots with a dragon boots ornament kit attached to it. The attached ornament kit gives no additional bonuses, and is only used to add aesthetics to the boots. It costs 221,016 for both the parts to make the dragon boots (g).

While the boots are untradeable in its ornamented state, it can be dismantled anytime, returning the tradeable boots and ornament kit.

This item can be stored in the treasure chest of a costume room, provided that the interface of the corresponding clue tier is opened before attempting to store the item. Alternatively, the item can be used on the opened treasure chest to insert it without viewing the interface.

Once attached, the ornamented item becomes untradeable, but the kit can be detached from the item and sold.
22249:
The necklace of anguish (or) is a necklace of anguish with an anguish ornament kit attached to it. The attached ornament kit gives no additional bonuses, and is only used to add aesthetics to the necklace. It costs 20,129,998 for both the parts to make the necklace of anguish (or).

While the amulet is untradeable in its ornamented state, it can be dismantled anytime, returning the tradeable amulet and ornament kit.

Many players purchase the ornament kit for the purpose of making the item untradeable, thus allowing the player to always keep it on death against NPCs.

The trident of the seas (e) is a one-handed powered staff that requires 75 Magic to wield. If a player dies with the trident, only the uncharged trident will appear on the floor (if it's not protected on death ).

The trident of the swamp (e) is a one-handed powered staff that requires 78 Magic to wield. It is an enhanced version of the regular trident of the swamp obtained by giving Lieve McCracken 10 kraken tentacles , costing 2,573,340 coins . It holds 20,000 charges, rather than the 2,500 charges of the unenhanced version. Like the unenhanced version, it is only tradeable when it is fully uncharged.

To fully charge an enhanced trident, it would cost 9,520,000 coins , requiring one death rune, one chaos rune, 5 fire runes, and a Zulrah scale per charge. Players can configure the charges while the trident is in their bank by right-clicking on Configure-Charges, as long as players have the required materials.

If lost on death, any scales that were used to charge the trident will appear on the floor along with the uncharged trident.

The staff of light is a one-handed bladed staff which requires 75 Attack and 75 Magic to wield. It is created by using Saradomin's light on a staff of the dead. This process is irreversible.

The staff of light inherits all of the staff of the dead's effects. The only differences between them is that the staff of light autocasts the Saradomin Strike god spell rather than the Flames of Zamorak god spell, and is unable to autocast Arceuus combat spells. In addition, it counts as both a Saradominist and a Zamorakian item while in the God Wars Dungeon and in the Desert Bandit Camp.

The staff of light cannot be upgraded with a magic fang to provide the additional magic attack bonus and toxic effect given to the toxic staff of the dead.

The ancient medallion is a drop obtained from revenants found in the Revenant Caves.

The statuette cannot be given to him in Edgeville. A chisel can be used on the ancient medallion to break it into 8,000 revenant ether.

Much like the bracelet of ethereum, the medallion is always lost on death, even if it is the only item in the player's inventory.

22316:
The prop sword is a weapon first obtained as a reward from the 2018 Birthday event. It is the iconic sword seen in the logo of RuneScape from 2001 to 2007.

While equipped, players can right-click the sword in the Equipment Stats interface to perform an emote, in which players assume a fencing position and slash the air to create the letters "RS", the acronym for "RuneScape".

Despite being a sword, its combat styles are the same as those of a warhammer. It offers very large attack penalties and is nearly useless as an actual weapon. As such, it is allowed during "fun weapon" fights in legacy duels within the Emir's Arena.

When wielded, a "Slash" option will appear on other players. Picking this option will cause the player to slash their target. The hit is just an animation and no damage is dealt, nor does it count as entering combat. There is a chance that players may "fumble" the sword, dropping it to the ground where it must be picked up.

If destroyed, a replacement can be obtained from Diango in Draynor Village or from the toy box of a costume room.
22318:
The pet dark core is a pet dropped by the Corporeal Beast. It is the dark energy core that is summoned during the fight with the Corporeal Beast. Players can right click "Metamorphosis" to change between the dark core and the Corporeal Critter, which is a smaller version of the Corporeal Beast.

When a player receives the pet, it will automatically try to appear as their follower. At the same time, a message in the chatbox will state You have a funny feeling like you're being followed. However, if a player receives a pet while having a follower out (for example, a cat), it will be placed into their inventory. When this occurs, the message in the chatbox will instead state You feel something weird sneaking into your backpack.

If a player's inventory is full and they have a follower already, they will not receive the pet; it must instead be claimed from Probita in East Ardougne.

On death, if a player loses their pet (as a follower or in your inventory) it will wander around the area for 30 seconds before despawning. Even if the player returns in time, the pet cannot be picked up, and can be reclaimed from Probita.
22319:
The Jal-Nib-Rek (roughly translated as Foreign Nibbler Baby/Young ) is a Jal-Nib dropped by TzKal-Zuk upon completion of the Inferno . The standard drop rate is 1/100, but this is increased to 1/75 if TzKal-Zuk is defeated while on a Slayer task. Players may also exchange their infernal capes by speaking to TzHaar-Ket-Keh for a 1/100 chance of obtaining the pet. Providing a player defeats TzKal-Zuk while on a slayer task for a 1/75 chance of the pet, and hands in their cape, the overall chance of receiving the pet from either the boss or the cape is approximately 1/43.

Players can right click " Metamorphosis " to change between the Jal-Nib and TzRek-Zuk, which is a smaller version of TzKal-Zuk.

The champion's lamp is an item obtained from the Chest of Champions in the north side of the Champions' Challenge area after defeating a champion.

Rubbing the lamp awards the player ten times the experience that is given immediately after a champion's defeat. For example, rubbing a lamp obtained after defeating the Hobgoblin Champion will award players with 2,320 Hitpoints and Slayer experience. Players will receive a confirmation message before gaining the experience.

The lamp cannot be banked. If players were to somehow lose the lamp, it can be reclaimed from the Chest of Champions.

The Scythe of vitur is a slash weapon requiring 75 Attack and Strength to wield. It is only available from the supplies table in an unrestricted world as a test weapon for players. As it was a test weapon, the graphics were used as a placeholder, using a pink scythe .

The scythe can hit up to three enemies once in a 1x3 arc in front of the player. Each hit can also hit large creatures up to three times in the same attack. The scythe can only hit a maximum of three NPCs and can only hit a maximum of three times. The first hit deals 100% damage, the 2nd deals 50% and the 3rd deals 25%. Each attack, regardless of which enemy is the player's primary target, is rolled independently based on their attack bonuses versus the NPCs defence bonuses.

The Justiciar faceguard is a helmet requiring 75 Defence to equip, and is part of the Justiciar armour set. When the full set of Justiciar armour is equipped, the player gains a set effect : all combat damage taken is reduced (except in PvP ). The exact formula for the amount of damage reduced is b o n u s 3000 , where bonus is the player's defence bonus for that particular style. For example, if an enemy was using a crush style attack, and the player has a crush defence bonus of +450, then 15% of the damage (450/3,000) is reduced.

The oculus orb is an item which allows players to have total control over the camera, an ability which is useful for content creators. The orb can be purchased from Diango's Toy Store in Draynor Village for 60 coins or claimed for free from Diango's Holiday Item Retrieval.

It has a Scry option that lets the player more freely control the viewpoint of game client, making it possible to not have it centred on the player character as it does normally. However, players cannot use it while in combat , and can only see as far as the game has loaded, meaning the orb cannot see players and non-player characters beyond their normal field of vision. In addition, interface elements and all environmental overlays (such as the water overlay that appears when players travel underwater ) are removed when players use the orb.

Not only can the oculus orb be used for making videos and taking screenshots, it can also be used for taking a closer look at areas which players either cannot access, could formerly access but can no longer do so (the former King Black Dragon Lair , which is in the Temple of Ikov ), or ones which are unrelated to the area the player is currently standing in and are only visited via completely different methods (the Mime random event area, which can be seen with the orb if scrying from Iban's throne room after completing Underground Pass ).

The orb cannot be used on Old School RuneScape Mobile . Attempting to do so results in the chat message Scrying is not available on this platform.
22365:
The Shayzien favour certificate was a quest reward for completing Tale of the Righteous. Reading this granted the player 10% Shayzien favour, where there would be a confirmation message before doing so. Should the player have wished to use it some other time, they could destroy it (if bank space was an issue) and reclaim it from Lord Shiro Shayzien.

The certificate was removed alongside the entire Kourend Favour system on 10 January 2024 with the release of Children of the Sun.
22366: The cyan crystal is an unobtainable item that can only be seen on the reward scroll of the quest Tale of the Righteous, and cannot actually be obtained by players.
22367:
The Kourend favour certificate was a quest reward for completing Client of Kourend . Reading this granted the player 20% favour towards a city of their choosing, where there would be a confirmation message before doing so. Should the player have wished to use it some other time, they could destroy it (if bank space was an issue) and reclaim it from Veos in Port Piscarilius . This item could not leave a placeholder.

If the player had not started gaining Piscarilius favour, it was recommended to use the certificate to bypass the first 20% favour there, as it was costly and time consuming requiring three planks and nine nails per 0.5% favour gained.

The certificate was removed alongside the entire Kourend Favour system on 10 January 2024 with the release of Children of the Sun .
22368:
Bryophyta's staff is a staff requiring level 30 Attack and Magic to wield.

It can be obtained by paying 50,000 coins to Zaff , in central Varrock , with a Bryophyta's essence in your inventory. Members with 62 Crafting can make one, by using the essence on a battlestaff or vice versa. In both cases, the essence will be consumed, along with any battlestaff.

The staff can be charged with up to 1,000 nature runes . While the staff is equipped, it acts as if the player is holding the charged number of nature runes. When equipped and charged, it has a 1/15 chance to save a single charge, whenever a spell requiring nature runes is cast. Players can configure the charges while the weapon is in their bank by right-clicking on Configure-Charges, as long as players have the required materials.

The staff is untradeable while it has any charges. Players can use a right-click option to remove all of the staff's charges, but the nature runes stored within it are not returned. In addition, if the player dies with a charged staff, all charges except one will be lost. Ultimate ironmen do not keep additional charges on death.

The staff can be used along with a tome of fire to increase profits with High Level Alchemy ; however, it takes several thousand spell casts to negate any resale tax, and hundreds of thousands more to pay for the staff alone.

Bryophyta's essence is an item obtained from Bryophyta's chest , and can be used with a battlestaff with 62 Crafting to create an uncharged Bryophyta's staff .

Free-to-play players, or those without the required Crafting level to create the staff, may bring the essence to Zaff in central Varrock to do so, for a fee of 50,000 coins.
22374:
A mossy key grants players access to Bryophyta 's lair in the moss giant section of the Varrock Sewers and unlocks Bryophyta's chest after defeating her.

A key is consumed when looting the chest, and one key is also required to access Bryophyta's lair for the first time, after which the lair can be freely entered. The key is not consumed when unlocking access to Bryophyta's lair for the first time. Additionally, five keys are needed in order to complete the Bryophyta Champion combat achievement as the achievement kill count is increased upon looting the chest. It is possible to hold more than one mossy key at once.

The drop rate of mossy keys is 1/150 from moss giants, 1/120 from Iorwerth Dungeon moss giants , and 1/100 from Wilderness moss giants. However, while on a moss giant Slayer task , the drop rate is increased to 1/75 from regular moss giants, and 1/40 from Iorwerth Dungeon moss giants (due to an additional task-only drop at a rate of 1/60).

This drop rate increase does not remain when killing moss giants outside of the Wilderness when on a Wilderness Slayer task. [ 1 ] Boosts to the drop rate do not stack with each other, meaning that if a moss giant is killed in the Wilderness as part of a Slayer task, the rate remains at 1/75. [ 2 ] The increased drop rate in the Wilderness is also extended to free-to-play accounts, and the Slayer task boost may still apply in free-to-play worlds in the event an account had a moss giant task when their membership lapsed. [ 3 ] [ confirmation needed ]
22376:
The Olmlet is a pet obtained from the Chambers of Xeric . It is a much smaller version of the Great Olm , with its body fully visible. Players have a 1/53 chance of receiving the pet when they receive an item from the unique drop table after killing the Great Olm.

The olmlet is able to metamorphose into five other pets which are smaller versions of the other bosses encountered inside the Chambers of Xeric, which requires using metamorphic dust on it. The dust can be acquired from the Chambers' Challenge Mode version and clearing it under a specific time.

When a player receives the pet, it will automatically try to appear as their follower. At the same time, a message in the chatbox will state You have a funny feeling like you're being followed. However, if a player receives a pet while having a follower out (for example, a cat ), it will be placed into their inventory . When this occurs, the message in the chatbox will instead state You feel something weird sneaking into your backpack.

If a player's inventory is full and they have a follower already, they will not receive the pet; it must instead be claimed from Probita in East Ardougne .

On death , if a player loses their pet (as a follower or in your inventory) it will wander around the area for 30 seconds before despawning. Even if the player returns in time, the pet cannot be picked up, and can be reclaimed from Probita.

22388:

This item can be stored in the cape rack of a costume room . It can also be mounted on a cape hanger in an Achievement Gallery .
22390:
Xeric's warrior is a cosmetic cape that can be obtained from Captain Rimor by the entrance to the Chambers of Xeric after completing 500 Chambers of Xeric in Challenge Mode .

This item can be stored in the cape rack of a costume room . It can also be mounted on a cape hanger in an Achievement Gallery .
22392:
Xeric's sentinel is a cosmetic cape that can be obtained from Captain Rimor by the entrance to the Chambers of Xeric after completing 1,000 Chambers of Xeric in Challenge Mode .

This item can be stored in the cape rack of a costume room . It can also be mounted on a cape hanger in an Achievement Gallery .
22394:
Xeric's general is a cosmetic cape that can be obtained from Captain Rimor by the entrance to the Chambers of Xeric after completing 1,500 Chambers of Xeric in Challenge Mode .

This item can be stored in the cape rack of a costume room . It can also be mounted on a cape hanger in an Achievement Gallery .
22396:

This item can be stored in the cape rack of a costume room . It can also be mounted on a cape hanger in an Achievement Gallery .
22398:
The Ivandis flail is a one-handed staff created by the player during A Taste of Hope from a chain , an enchanted emerald sickle (b) and the rod of Ivandis . The flail requires an Attack level of 40 to wield. It is a silver weapon and can deal full damage to vampyres of all tiers and gives a 20% damage bonus against them. [ 1 ] It can also autocast standard spellbook spells.

This flail is effective in damaging and killing the vyrewatch because, despite their sufficient mind-reading ability to predict attacks and avoid damage, the flail is incredibly unpredictable and random. The sickle head further increases the unpredictability of the weapon. Thus, attackers do not hit the Vyrewatch in the intended way, rendering their mind-reading useless. [ 2 ]

The flail retains the ability to cast Bloom from the silver sickle (b). This versatility lets a player kill ghasts , vampyre juvinates and vyrewatch with a single weapon.

While players can make a flail themselves after the quest, it is much easier to purchase one from Vertida Sefalatis for 20,000 coins in the old Myreque Hideout under Old Man Ral 's home or from Perdu for 30,000 coins from the Lost Property shop . During Sins of the Father , an Ivandis flail is used to create a blisterwood flail in the hideout.
22400:
Drakan's medallion is a reward from the quest A Taste of Hope. It allows unlimited teleportation to Ver Sinhaza, Darkmeyer (after completion of Sins of the Father), and the Sisterhood Sanctuary under Slepe (after using a Slepey tablet on it, which is a 1/25 drop from Phosani's Nightmare), and to Castle Drakan (after partial completion of The Blood Moon Rises). Players cannot teleport past level 20 Wilderness.

The main purpose of the medallion is for easy teleportation to the Theatre of Blood. In addition, the teleport location is decently close to a bank, making the medallion an easier to obtain but less effective alternative to the Crafting cape.

Apart from access to a bank, the destination of Ver Sinhaza offers a convenient full replenishment option by entering the Theatre of Blood and resigning the fight at the end of the hallway through the vyre orator present before entering the boss room.

Players can get an infinite amount of medallions from Kael Forshaw (or Ivan Strom after completing Sins of the Father) in the old Myreque Hideout under the trapdoor in the northern room of Old Man Ral's home. After beginning The Blood Moon Rises, players must instead speak to Old Man Ral in his house for more medallions free of charge. After completing The Blood Moon Rises, players can retrieve amulets from either Old Man Ral or Ivan Strom (now in the Paterdomus Temple). Alternatively, players can purchase one from Perdu for 30,000 coins.
22402: The mysterious herb is a herb obtained from Serafina's home during A Taste of Hope. It is used to create the potion and blood potion, along with some mysterious crushed meat.
22403: The mysterious meat is obtained from Serafina's home during A Taste of Hope. It is crushed with a pestle and mortar to create mysterious crushed meat, which is the second ingredient used to create the potion and blood potion.
22404: The mysterious crushed meat is obtained from Serafina's home during A Taste of Hope. It is obtained by crushing mysterious meat with a pestle and mortar. It is the second ingredient used to create the potion and blood potion.
22405: The vial of blood is obtained during A Taste of Hope by giving Safalaan an empty vial . The vial contains his blood, which is used to create a blood potion .
22406: The unfinished blood potion is obtained during A Taste of Hope by using the mysterious herb with a vial of blood. A mysterious crushed meat is then added to it to create a blood potion.
22407: The blood potion is obtained during A Taste of Hope by using the mysterious herb with a vial of blood , then adding mysterious crushed meat to the Unfinished blood potion . It is to be used on the door in Serafina's home, which will open this time.
22408: The unfinished potion is obtained during A Taste of Hope by using the mysterious herb with a vial of water . A mysterious crushed meat is then added to it to create a potion .
22409: The potion is obtained during A Taste of Hope by using the mysterious herb with a vial of water , then adding mysterious crushed meat to the unfinished potion . It is to be used on the door in Serafina's home.
22410: The old notes is obtained during A Taste of Hope by searching the chest behind the door in Serafina's home.
22411:
The old diary is obtained by searching the bed next to the staircase in Serafina's home. It can be obtained as early as partial completion of Darkness of Hallowvale after gaining access to the route to the Sanguinesti Meiyerditch hideout, however its contents are mostly relevant for the quest A Taste of Hope.

Written by Serafina's brother, the diary describes Ranis Drakan and Serafina making a deal to cure her brother of his illness, which players find out later in the quest was transforming him into the abomination. The same story, but from Serafina's perspective, can be read in her diary.

If lost, it can be reclaimed from Serafina's home or from a bookcase within a player-owned house.
22413: Flaygian's notes are obtained during A Taste of Hope. They are the results of Flaygian Screwte's effort to translate the Haemalchemy book that the player found during Darkness of Hallowvale. It contains some notes about the vampyre's immunities, and Screwte's theories on how to overcome them.
22414: The chain was obtained from a crate in the old Myreque Hideout under Old Man Ral's house during A Taste of Hope. It was used to link the enchanted emerald sickle (b) and the rod of Ivandis to create the Ivandis flail. It was replaced by an identical looking chain with the release of Sailing.
22415:
The tome of experience is received from Safalaan on completion of A Taste of Hope . Reading it opens a window to select the skill a player wishes to advance. The player must be at least level 35 in their chosen skill. In the event this item is lost or destroyed after the completion of A Taste of Hope and during or after Sins of the Father , players may reclaim this item from Ivan Strom in Old Man Ral 's house in Meyerditch after finishing Sins of the Father . After progressing far enough into The Blood Moon Rises , it is reclaimed from Old Man Ral instead.

It has three chapters which provide 2,500 experience each. After confirming, the player receives the message " You read a fascinating chapter and earn experience! You have been awarded 2,500 (skill) experience! " After the third reading, the book disappears and the player receives the message " The book crumbles into a dust cloud of knowledge. "

This item cannot be banked.
22416:
The Turncloak can be found in upper floor of the Crombwick Manor, which is accessed through the Sisterhood Sanctuary.

The book is written from the perspective of Phosani, the Justiciar of the Wolf, and describes her and her companions Insela and Otrava surrendering their squadron, pledging allegiance to Lord Drakan and betraying Saradomin during the God Wars.

This book cannot be stored in a player-owned house bookcase.
22418:
Explosive Discovery can be found on the 2 nd floor [ UK ] 3 rd floor [ US ] in the church of Slepe . It was presumably written by Insela , a ballistics expert and one of the founders of the Sisterhood .

This book cannot be stored in a player-owned house bookcase .
22420:
The bloody grimoire is an old book that can be found in the Sisterhood Sanctuary. It can only be obtained by using the Telekinetic Grab spell to reach it.

The book is authored by Otrava, a member of the Sisterhood. It describes the author's discovery of a damaged version of the Senntisten Scriptures from their slain enemies, and details how they used their newfound knowledge of blood magic to create blood potions; namely, the bastion and battlemage potions.

In addition, the book lists two more recipes for a 'totality potion' and 'vigour potion' that were crossed out due to instability and a lack of ingredients, respectively.

This book cannot be stored in a player-owned house bookcase.
22422:
The Elixir of Everlasting is a scroll containing the formula to the fabled elixir created by Otrava , a high-ranking member of the Sisterhood and its divine healer. It can be obtained by using an old key on the chest on the 2 nd floor [ UK ] 3 rd floor [ US ] of church in Slepe .

While the Elixir of Everlasting is able to extend the drinker's life indefinitely, it had the side effect of causing the drinker to sleep for longer periods of time, until they eventually become trapped in an eternal slumber, never to wake up.

Phosani , along with other high-ranking members of the Sisterhood , drank this without knowing of its side effects, and fell into a deep sleep. Realising the consequences of messing with the natural order, the people of modern-day Slepe (its original name currently unknown), in accordance to the laws set by Phosani, moved the sleeping members of the Sisterhood deep into the Sanctuary with all their possessions and hid the formula itself away to prevent others from suffering its side effects.

Despite this, several notes about the elixir remain in the Sisterhood Sanctuary, albeit most of them have been scribbled over the top with hastily written warnings. Daer Krand , who is performing research on the elixir within the Sanctuary, is currently attempting to recreate it.

During Sins of the Father , it is discovered that Kroy , a vampyre herbalist, found the formula and recreated it. Alongside Damien Leucurte , a vampyre noble, the both of them used the elixir on Slepe's townsfolk by mixing it with their local beverage, Bloody Bracer , causing the town's second Sleeper Plague, in order to perform blood tithes on them as the sleeping victims only require a fraction of the blood compared to an awake human due to an increased vampyre population and dwindling blood supply.
22424:
Buried Alive is an old piece of parchment received from Hameln the Jester in the Slepe church.

The scroll documents the high-ranked members of the Sisterhood being moved deeper into the Sisterhood Sanctuary, who did not wake after a fortnight (two weeks). This was done in accordance to the laws set by Phosani, the Sisterhood's founder.

This scroll cannot be stored in a player-owned house bookcase.
22426:
The deed is received from a table in the eastern room of the Crombwick Manor's ground floor, which is accessed through the Sisterhood Sanctuary.

The deed, signed by Lord Drakan himself on the 38th of Septober on the 661st Year of the Fourth Age, certifies that the Sleepers Manor (known today as the Crombwick Manor) is now owned by Ichabod Crombwick as a commemoration for his loyalty to the Drakans.

The deed cannot be stored in a player-owned house bookcase.
22428:
The Old key is an item that can be found in the north-western room of the Sisterhood Sanctuary, north of Kroy's laboratory, which is locked and inaccessible until his death during Sins of the Father.

It is used to open the large chest found on the 2nd floor of church in Slepe, which contains the Elixir of Everlasting, a scroll containing the formula for an ancient potion said to be able to extend the drinker's life indefinitely.
22430:
The bloody bracer is a type of ale that restores 2 Hitpoints and drains Prayer by 4% + 2. The bloody bracer may heal you above your maximum Hitpoints once. Upon drinking the ale, a message in the chatbox will state The tincture tastes great, but you feel an evil within you stir..

It is purchasable at the Rat & Bat in the town of Slepe. Unlike other ales, it cannot be created through brewing.
22433:
The emerald sickle (b) is an item obtained by using an emerald on a silver sickle (b) after starting A Taste of Hope. It can be enchanted into an enchanted emerald sickle (b) by casting Lvl-2 Enchant on it.

The sickle has a right-click "bloom" option which can be used next to rotten logs, branches, or bushes in Mort Myre swamp to obtain Mort myre fungi , stems , and pears . These items can be used to fill the Druid pouch which allows the player to fight Ghasts . Bloom can also be cast on dead vines in the Ancient Guthixian Temple to grow them into flowering vines which can be picked to obtain a vine flower .

It can also be used to harm Vampyres and Vampyre Juvinates , but this is not recommended due to its weak stats.
22435:
The enchanted emerald sickle (b) is an item obtained by using an emerald on a silver sickle (b) , then casting Lvl-2 Enchant on the resulting emerald sickle (b) . It is to be used on a rod of Ivandis while having a chain in the inventory to create the Ivandis flail .

The sickle retains the right-click "bloom" option from the silver sickle (b) , which can be used next to rotten logs, branches, or bushes in Mort Myre swamp to obtain Mort myre fungi , stems , and pears . These items can be used to fill the Druid pouch which allows the player to fight Ghasts . Bloom can also be cast on dead vines in the Ancient Guthixian Temple to grow them into flowering vines which can be picked to obtain a vine flower .

It can also be used to harm Vampyres and Vampyre Juvinates , but this is not recommended due to its weak stats.
22437:
The rotten carrot is an item available only to Jagex Moderators , similar to the rotten potato , egg and cabbage .

Using the rotten carrot on an account will instantly kill them and show an interface with the account's bank and inventory contents, which will be teleported to the user's bank.

It is used for the Bot Busting stream on the Old School RuneScape Twitch channel, which began at 8pm BST/3pm EST on Saturday June 16th, 2018.
22438:
Justiciar armour set is an item obtained by exchanging a set of items with a Grand Exchange clerk via their right-click "Sets" option and clicking on the appropriate item set within the Item Sets interface.

It is commonly made in order to conveniently sell all three components of Justiciar armour at once.
22441:
The Avernic defender is a defender wielded in the shield slot, requiring 70 Attack and Defence to wield. It is obtained by combining a dragon defender with an Avernic defender hilt. This process can be reversed to return the dragon defender, but the hilt will be destroyed in the process. This defender boasts the highest strength bonus of any shield slot equipment, being 1 higher than the dragonfire shield. It also has the highest melee attack bonuses of any shield slot equipment. The defensive bonuses are comparable to that of an adamant kiteshield.

Ghommal's hilt 5 or 6 can be attached to it, creating Ghommal's avernic defender 5 or 6 respectively, giving the bonuses of the Avernic defender and the additional benefits of the hilt. This process is reversible, returning both the hilt and the defender.

Avernic weaponry was common amongst Zarosian forces in the Second Age, crafted by Avernic demon smiths in the liquid fires of Infernus. Today, they are incredibly rare, and Verzik Vitur's Avernic defender is one of the few to remain, a relic from her time in the service of Zaros. Due to its age, the full defender has been destroyed, and only the hilt remains.

If the player dies to a PvP death and the avernic defender is not one of the player's protected items, it will remain in the player's inventory, but will become broken, which means the item is unusable and must be repaired with 600,000 coins by using the item on Perdu. The game values the defender at 600,000 GP when determining which items to protect.
22443: A cadantine blood potion (unf) is an unfinished potion made via the Herblore skill. Players make it by using a cadantine on a vial of blood.
22446:
Vials of blood are obtained as drops from the Theatre of Blood or made by squeezing 50 blood sacs into a vial. It is used as the base instead of a vial of water when creating bastion and battlemage potions .

It is also used to charge the Scythe of Vitur , with each vial of blood, along with 200 blood runes , providing 100 charges. It can be charged by depositing the items into the vyre well in Ver Sinhaza or Darkmeyer and using the Scythe of Vitur on it.

Vials of blood may also be used to pay the aranei scout near the portal to Castle Drakan to move the player's grave near to them, if they had died whilst fighting the Maggot King . Depending on the current prices of vials of blood, this may be the most cost-effective way to pay.
