22473:
Lil' Zik is a pet that can be obtained from completing the Theatre of Blood . It is a much smaller version of Verzik Vitur 's final form. Players have a chance of receiving the pet when looting the monumental chests in Verzik's treasure vault. The drop rate is dependent on the player's performance in the raid, unaffected by that of teammates, ranging from 1/650 to 1/6,500 in regular raids and ranging from 1/500 to 1/5,000 in Hard Mode raids. The maximum rate is reached with 10 individual points (which are invisible to the players; the maximum per player is 32, or 18 if not including the MVP bonuses for each room). [ 1 ] The highest rate is reached by dying no more than twice per raid, with more deaths allowed if the player deals the most damage in some rooms, assuming participation in each room.

Lil' Zik is able to metamorphose into five other pets which are smaller versions of the other bosses encountered in the Theatre of Blood, which requires using Sanguine dust on it. The dust can be acquired from the Theatre's Hard Mode version and clearing it under a specific time.

When a player receives the pet, it will automatically try to appear as their follower. At the same time, a message in the chatbox will state You have a funny feeling like you're being followed. However, if a player receives a pet while having a follower out (for example, a cat ), it will be placed into their inventory . When this occurs, the message in the chatbox will instead state You feel something weird sneaking into your backpack.

If a player's inventory is full and they have a follower already, they will not receive the pet; it must instead be claimed from Probita in East Ardougne .

On death , if a player loses their pet (as a follower or in your inventory) it will wander around the area for 30 seconds before despawning. Even if the player returns in time, the pet cannot be picked up, and can be reclaimed from Probita.
22475: Messages can be found within the Theatre of Blood in the supply chests between bosses. The text is randomly generated depending on how well or poorly the player performed. A message can also be obtained from the Monumental chest when the player finishes a raid with a score of 0.
22477:
The Avernic defender hilt is an add-on that can be received as a reward from the Theatre of Blood. When used with a dragon defender, the Avernic defender will be created after a confirmation message. This process can be reversed, but the hilt will not be returned.

Avernic weaponry was common amongst Zarosian forces in the Second Age, crafted by Avernic demon smiths in the liquid fires of Infernus. Today, they are incredibly rare, and Verzik Vitur's Avernic defender is one of the few to remain, a relic from her time in the service of Zaros. Due to its age, the full defender has been destroyed, and only the hilt remains.

When the hilt is inspected, the chatbox message states You raise the hilt, inspecting each section carefully. It looks as though it could combine with a powerful parrying dagger.
22481:
The Sanguinesti staff is a one-handed powered staff requiring 82 Magic to wield, available as a rare drop from the Theatre of Blood . Like most powered staves, it is only tradeable when it is fully uncharged. Named after the Sanguinesti region , the staff was crafted by Lord Lowerniel Drakan himself, and was given to Lady Verzik Vitur as a gift for her assistance in the Misthalin–Morytania War . [ 1 ]

The Sanguinesti staff can be combined with a holy ornament kit to make a Saradomin -themed holy Sanguinesti staff . Though its stats do not change, it makes it usable as a Saradomin item in the God Wars Dungeon .

The staff's charge cannot be used against another player in dangerous PvP, only safe minigames.
22486:
The Scythe of Vitur is a two-handed slash weapon requiring 80 Attack and 90 Strength to wield, available as a rare drop from the Theatre of Blood . The scythe is extremely valuable due to its immense power against most large monsters. It is only tradeable when fully uncharged.

The Scythe of Vitur was once wielded by the founder of House Vitur, a vampyre now worshipped as a god. [ 1 ]

Although the Scythe of Vitur has a stab bonus, it does not have a Stab combat style.

22504:
Serafina's diary is an old diary that appears on the ground after defeating The Maiden of Sugadinti in the Theatre of Blood. It can also be obtained from the grand bookshelves in Verzik Vitur's treasure vault beneath her throne room, accessed after her defeat.

The book details the personal thoughts of Serafina, and explains how she was transformed into The Maiden of Sugadinti. The same story, but from her brother's perspective, can be read in his diary.

If lost, it can be reclaimed by defeating The Maiden of Sugadinti, or from a bookcase within a player-owned house.
22506:
The Butcher is a book that appears on the ground after defeating the Pestilent Bloat in the Theatre of Blood. It can also be obtained from the grand bookshelves in Verzik Vitur's treasure vault beneath her throne room, accessed after her defeat.

The book details how the Pestilent Bloat came to be, being created by an erratic vampyre known as "The Butcher" using the body parts of different races such as ogres and cyclopes.

If lost, it can be reclaimed by defeating the Pestilent Bloat, or from a bookcase within a player-owned house.
22508:
Arachnids of Vampyrium is a book that appears on the ground after defeating the Nylocas Vasilias in the Theatre of Blood . It can also be obtained from the grand bookshelves in Verzik Vitur 's treasure vault beneath her throne room, accessed after her defeat.

The book gives details about the various species of nylocas , and tells how they were brought from Vampyrium , the vampyre's homeworld.

If lost, it can be reclaimed by defeating the Nylocas Vasilias, or from a bookcase within a player-owned house .
22510:
The Shadow Realm is a book that appears on the ground after defeating Sotetseg in the Theatre of Blood. It can also be obtained from the grand bookshelves in Verzik Vitur's treasure vault beneath her throne room, accessed after her defeat.

The book details the experiments performed on Sotetseg and how the author manipulated it to travel into the Shadow Realm.

If lost, it can be reclaimed by defeating Sotetseg, or from a bookcase within a player-owned house.
22512:
The Wild Hunt is a journal that appears on the ground after defeating Xarpus in the Theatre of Blood. It can also be obtained from the grand bookshelves in Verzik Vitur's treasure vault beneath her throne room, accessed after her defeat.

The journal is written by Lowerniel Drakan, and it tells of his desire to hunt down the Yarasa Xarpus from his homeworld of Vampyrium.

If lost, it can be reclaimed by defeating Xarpus, or from a bookcase within a player-owned house.
22514:
Verzik Vitur - Patient Record are a set of medical notes that appear on the ground after defeating Verzik Vitur in the Theatre of Blood. It can also be obtained from the grand bookshelves in her treasure vault beneath her throne room, accessed after her defeat.

The patient record, written by Vulcan Orvoros, contains medical notes on Verzik Vitur, detailing a sickness she was infected with after a nylocas bite. In A Night at the Theatre it is revealed that the bite was actually a result of a prototype nylocas biting her when she presented it to Ranis Drakan, which injected a parasite that eventually matured into the Nylocas Queen and killed her, before the Queen ordered him killed too.

If lost, it can be reclaimed by defeating Verzik Vitur, or from a bookcase within a player-owned house.
22516:
The Dawnbringer is a powered staff obtained from the skeleton next to the entrance to Verzik Vitur's throne room in the Theatre of Blood. When a player takes the staff from the skeleton, a chatbox message will state You find the Dawnbringer; you feel a pulse of energy burst through it.

Used to break Verzik Vitur's shield during the first phase of the final fight against her, the Dawnbringer ignores accuracy rolls, meaning the player will always deal successful hits, even when at or below -64 Magic attack bonus.

After her shield is destroyed, the Dawnbringer will crumble to dust. When this occurs, a message in the chatbox will state The weapon falls apart in your hand as Verzik's shield is destroyed.
22517:
Escape crystals are a consumable teleport item that can be equipped in the ring slot . It can be purchased from Rick in the 1 st floor [ UK ] 2 nd floor [ US ] of the Wizards' Tower , as well as from the Mysterious Stranger in Ver Sinhaza , for 75,000 coins.

The crystal acts similarly to a respawn teleport , teleporting players away from various activities, which Hardcore ironmen/group ironmen may consider as dangerous upon death:

Players can also use the crystal on their group members to activate them, allowing teleportation of teammates out of danger in an instant. To enable this, players must right-click the crystal and select "Configure", then choose the first option. Both players must have a crystal for this to work, and both crystals will be consumed in the process.

Additionally, the crystal can be configured to auto-activate upon taking damage (including zeros) after a specified time of inactivity (ranging from 2 to 300 seconds) via the "Configure" option; in this case, inactivity is defined as any time the player is not typing, clicking/tapping within the game, moving/zooming the camera, or moving the mouse. [ 1 ] For example, if players configure the timer to 30 seconds, they will automatically be teleported away from the aforementioned activities upon taking damage after being inactive for at least 30 seconds. However, if the player has just logged in or hopped worlds and takes damage, the escape crystal will activate immediately even if the inactivity timer has not elapsed. This function will apply in The Gauntlet if the crystal was in the player's inventory upon entry, and is configured to auto-activate.

The crystal will NOT activate while the player is moving. If the inactive time is reached at any point during movement, the crystal will activate when the player stops moving.
22519:
Cabbages are a series of unobtainable items. Presumably, they are used in order to track the status of players being able to purchase exclusive content. However, it is unknown how they are used in this regard.

Two cabbages were added in June 2018, with "Buy" and "Unbuy" versions, with the release of the Purple skin exclusive to Twitch Prime

A cabbage was added in November 2019, to track points earned in the Twisted League, and presumably determining access to the Leagues Reward Shop

Another cabbage was added on 5 December 2019, with the overhaul of the Leagues Reward Shop, tracking "negative points"

Four cabbages were added in October 2020, presumably used during the Trailblazer League

Two cabbages were added in January 2022, presumably used during the Shattered Relics League

22521:
A coin pouch is an item obtained from pickpocketing certain NPCs, which contains several coins depending on the NPC it was obtained from. To obtain the coins from them, players can simply click their stack of coin pouches to open them all at once, or they can right-click them to open one at a time. They cannot be traded or banked.

Up to 28 coin pouches can stack in a player's inventory, after which the player must open them to collect the coins inside before being able to pickpocket more. This limit can be increased by completing the Ardougne Diary, where it increases to 56, 84, and 140 after completing the Medium, Hard, and Elite diaries, respectively.

Coin pouches have different variants depending on who the player pickpocketed it from; for example, a coin pouch from pickpocketing guards does not stack with pouches from pickpocketing Ardougne knights. NPCs who are pickpocketed via blackjacking yield coins directly while they are knocked out instead of coin pouches. If rogue equipment is used to receive double the loot from pickpocketing, only one coin pouch is obtained (containing the normal amount) while the other half is obtained directly as coins.

Viggora's chainmace is a one-handed spiked weapon that can be received as a drop from revenants found within the Revenant Caves . It was once owned by Viggora , the only human among the generals of Zaros during the Second Age . After his death, it was claimed by a follower of Zamorak, and was extensively used during the God Wars . This item counts as a Zamorakian item in the God Wars Dungeon .

The chainmace requires an Attack level of 60 to wield and has bonuses similar to the dragon scimitar , with the chainmace using crush attack styles rather than slash . Although it can be used in its uncharged form, it has a powerful passive effect within the Wilderness when charged with revenant ether .

Due to the damage increase of the passive effect, the chainmace is a popular item used for PvM within the Wilderness such as Wilderness Slayer tasks and killing revenants .

The chainmace can be upgraded to an ursine chainmace by attaching the claws of Callisto to it, requiring level 85 Smithing or paying Andros Mai 500,000 coins. Players can also dismantle an uncharged chainmace to receive 7,500 revenant ether , resulting in 1,305,000 coins and a loss of −3,105,985 coins .

After his death, it was claimed by a follower of Zamorak, and was extensively used during the God Wars . This item counts as a Zamorakian item in the God Wars Dungeon .

The chainmace requires an Attack level of 60 to wield and has bonuses similar to the dragon scimitar , with the chainmace using crush attack styles rather than slash . Although it can be used in its uncharged form, it has a powerful passive effect within the Wilderness when charged with revenant ether .

Due to the damage increase of the passive effect, the chainmace is a popular item used for PvM within the Wilderness such as Wilderness Slayer tasks and killing revenants .

The chainmace can be upgraded to an ursine chainmace by attaching the claws of Callisto to it, requiring level 85 Smithing or paying Andros Mai 500,000 coins. Players can also dismantle an uncharged chainmace to receive 7,500 revenant ether , resulting in 1,305,000 coins and a loss of −3,105,985 coins .
22547:
Craw's bow is a shortbow once owned by Craw , one of the more formidable followers among Armadyl 's forces during the God Wars . It can be received as a drop from revenants found within the Revenant Caves . This item counts as an Armadyl item in the God Wars Dungeon .

The bow requires a Ranged level of 60 to wield, and shares the same bonuses as the magic shortbow (i) with the ranged strength of dragon arrows , although it does not have a special attack . It has to be charged with revenant ether to be fired, but it does provide its own ammo, rolling damage against an NPC's standard ranged defence. It also has a powerful passive effect within the Wilderness .

The bow's fired shots are coated in a yellow-orange aura, similar to the crystal bow. The bow has an attack range of 9. Longrange increases attack range by 1.

The bow can be upgraded to a webweaver bow by attaching the fangs of Venenatis to it, requiring level 85 Fletching or paying Derse Venator 500,000 coins. Players can also dismantle an uncharged bow to receive 7,500 revenant ether , resulting in a loss of −13,624,019 coins .

Thammaron's sceptre is a powered staff requiring 60 Magic to wield, available as a drop from revenants . Like most powered staves, it is only tradeable when it is fully uncharged. It was once owned by Thammaron , a Tsutsaroth demon who was one of Zamorak 's most trusted allies during the reign of Zaros , and later one of his key generals during the God Wars . This item counts as a Zamorakian item in the God Wars Dungeon .

The sceptre shares the same magic attack bonus as the trident of the seas , and has a powerful passive effect within the Wilderness when charged with revenant ether . In addition, unlike other powered staves, the sceptre can attack players outside of minigames . The sceptre also has a "Swap" option that allows players to switch it to Thammaron's sceptre (a) , which is a variant that can autocast offensive combat spells from the standard spellbook (including Flames of Zamorak ) and the Ancient Magicks .

The sceptre can be upgraded to an accursed sceptre by attaching the skull of Vet'ion to it, requiring level 85 Crafting or paying Phabelle Bile 500,000 coins . Players can also dismantle an uncharged sceptre to receive 7,500 revenant ether , resulting in 1,305,000 coins and a loss of −1,438,765 coins .

22557:
The amulet of avarice is an amulet that can be received as a drop from revenants found within the Revenant Caves. The amulet has the same combat bonuses as the amulet of glory, but has an additional 20% increase in accuracy and damage when fighting revenants, similar to a Salve amulet. The effects of the amulet do not stack with the Slayer helmet (i).

When worn, all drops received from NPCs within the Revenant Caves, Wilderness Slayer Cave and Chaos Temple will be in the form of bank notes, except for secondary supply rolls and uniques. However, equipping the amulet will cause the player to become skulled, similar to the cape of skulls. Attempting to equip the amulet gives a warning telling the player that this will happen. The skull cannot be removed until the amulet is unequipped, after which it behaves like a normal PK skull and disappears after twenty minutes. This behaviour is different from the cape of skulls, which will only keep the skull active for 20 minutes from the moment of equipping.

It is worth noting that while skulled (regardless of the source of the skull, except for the skull given by a high-risk PvP world), unique drops from revenants have their drop rate nearly doubled.

Wearing the amulet while looting a Zombie Pirate's Locker will note the drops other than the teleport anchoring scroll.

If the amulet is worn while killing the Revenant maledictus as a top-damaging player, they will obtain the Forinthry Surge skull for 30 minutes, a variant that provides an additional 15% accuracy and damage boost when fighting revenants. Taking off the amulet will automatically remove this buff.
22586:
The looting bag is a storage bag that can hold up to 28 stacks of any item. Only one looting bag can be in a player's possession at a time.

Tradeable items can only be stored whilst in the Wilderness, including the Ferox Enclave, by using them on the looting bag or via the looting bag's "Deposit" option. Stackable items like runes, arrows, or noted items stack in the looting bag as they would in the inventory. The bag may also be used in certain locations outside the Wilderness on PvP worlds. The contents of a looting bag cannot be recovered outside of a bank without destroying it or dying.
22588: The old man's coffin can be built inside the Wise Old Man's house during the quest Making Friends with My Arm. It is used to put the Wise Old Man's "corpse" inside to make My Arm think the player killed him, resulting in an old man's coffin. It requires 35 Construction to build and gives 715 experience when built. The player must have a hammer and a saw in their inventory to build it.
22589:
The reduced cadava potion is made by the Apothecary during the quest Making Friends with My Arm by giving him a cadava berry , requesting a variant of the cadava potion appropriate for the Wise Old Man 's age. When given to the Wise Old Man he uses it to pretend to be dead for My Arm .

Attempting to drink the potion yields the chatbox message " However bad the day's been, drinking this is unlikely to make it better. "

Once the Wise Old Man drinks the potion, he collapses, and the player puts him in a coffin to prove My Arm "killed" the Wise Old Man.
22590:
Goat dung is an item used in the quest Making Friends with My Arm . It is obtained by using a bucket on a pile of goat poo in the north-easternmost building in Weiss .

It is given to Snowflake to fertilise two herb patches in Weiss: one for the Weiss trolls to grow goutweed , and another for players to use after the quest, which, like the Troll Stronghold herb patch, will never be diseased .
22591:
The Weiss fire notes, or Odd Mushroom's Notes, are obtained during the Making Friends with My Arm quest. They are Odd Mushroom 's old notes describing the various types of fires that can be made by combining salts found in Weiss .

After completion of Making Friends with My Arm , the notes can be given to Burntmeat in the Troll Stronghold kitchen . In exchange, Wolfbone will fill the player's inventory with burnt meat .

If lost, it can be reclaimed from Snowflake or from a bookcase within a player-owned house .
22593:
Te salt is a type of salt that can be mined from te salt rocks in the Salt Mine beneath Weiss after the completion of Making Friends with My Arm. Along with Urt salt and Efh salt, it can be used to light fire pits that provide benefits (such as a permanent light source), and it is also used to create icy and stony basalts. Mining Te salt requires 72 Mining and is mined in chunks of 2-7 scaling with the player's level, granting the player 5 experience per salt mined. Mining enhancers do not work here.

A total of 1100 Te salt is required to construct all the permanent fires available (1 dehumidification, 3 eternal light, 1 nourishment, 1 unseasonal warmth). 100 Te salt is required to attune each portal to Weiss or Troll Stronghold in a Portal Chamber in a Player Owned House (for a total of 200 for both portals), and 1000 Te salt is required to attune a Portal Nexus to either (for a total of 2000 for both portals).Players will also need 250 Te, Efh, and Urt salts to build an Eternal brazier on each of their boats. Assuming the brazier is built on 5 boats (the current maximum), 1250 of each salt would be needed in total.

Icy basalt is an item that can be used to teleport to Weiss, near the herb patches. Using it to teleport consumes the icy basalt. It may only be used after finishing Making Friends with My Arm.

To create an icy basalt, players must use a basalt with 3 efh salt and 1 te salt.

This teleport can be incorporated into a portal within a Portal Chamber using 100 times the required resources (300 efh salt, 100 te salt, and 100 basalt), or in a Portal Nexus using 1,000 times the required resources (3,000 efh salt, 1,000 te salt, and 1,000 basalt).

Note: The resources for icy basalt (efh salt, te salt, and basalt) must be used for the portal chamber, not the created item.
22601:
Stony basalt is an item that can be used to teleport to the Troll Stronghold entrance, below the climbing rocks shortcut . The stony basalt is consumed when it is used to teleport. It may only be used after completing Making Friends with My Arm .

To create stony basalt, players must use 1 basalt with 3 urt salt and 1 te salt .

With level 73 Agility and the completion of the Hard Fremennik Diary , an option to teleport to the Stronghold roof is unlocked, past the climbing rocks shortcut . This alternate destination works like all Agility shortcuts, you may boost to pass the check, although being drained when you otherwise meet the requirement will still put you on the roof.

This teleport can be incorporated into a portal within a Portal Chamber using 100 times the required resources (300 urt salt, 100 te salt, and 100 basalt), or in a Portal Nexus using 1,000 times the required resources (3,000 urt salt, 1,000 te salt, and 1,000 basalt).

Note: The resources for Stony basalt (urt salt, te salt, and basalt) must be used for the portal chamber, not the created item.
22603:
Basalt is a rock that can be mined from basalt rocks in the Salt Mine beneath Weiss after the completion of Making Friends with My Arm. It requires level 72 Mining and grants 5 Mining experience. Mining enhancers do not work here.

It can be used with te salt, along with urt or efh salts to create icy basalt and stony basalt. 200 Basalt is required to attune a portal to both (100 each) Troll Stronghold and Weiss in a Portal Chamber in a Player Owned House, and 2000 Basalt is required to attune a Portal Nexus with both teleports (1000 each). Basalt rocks have a 1/7 chance of being depleted each time they are mined.

Snowflake, who is located just outside the mine entrance, is able to note any basalt you have mined for free.

The pet smoke devil is a pet dropped by the Thermonuclear smoke devil. It is a much smaller version of the (Thermonuclear) smoke devil. Players can right click "Metamorphosis" to change between the regular smoke devil and the thermonuclear smoke devil.

When a player receives the pet, it will automatically try to appear as their follower. At the same time, a message in the chatbox will state You have a funny feeling like you're being followed. However, if a player receives a pet while having a follower out (for example, a cat), it will be placed into their inventory. When this occurs, the message in the chatbox will instead state You feel something weird sneaking into your backpack.

If a player's inventory is full and they have a follower already, they will not receive the pet; it must instead be claimed from Probita in East Ardougne.

On death, if a player loses their pet (as a follower or in your inventory) it will wander around the area for 30 seconds before despawning. Even if the player returns in time, the pet cannot be picked up, and can be reclaimed from Probita.

22671:
The tattered Kalphite Queen head is an item dropped by the Kalphite Queen . Players are guaranteed to receive one for their 256th Kalphite Queen kill; players who already had 256 kills before the tattered head's release will receive it on their next kill instead.

It can be stuffed at the Taxidermist in Canifis by using the item on her and paying 50,000 coins, returning a stuffed tattered kq head . When players take it to her, she will tell players "That's not the most impressive head I've seen but I think I can just about manage this one. Preserving insects is always tricky. I'll have to be careful..."

Once stuffed, it can be mounted at a gilded display within the skill hall in a player-owned house , granting 223 Construction alongside 200 Attack , Strength , Defence , Magic , and Ranged experience , with players being given the option to decline the combat experience before mounting the heads.

Unlike the normal kq head , the tattered head's only use is to be stuffed and mounted, as talking to it is part of the Desert Elite Achievement Diary . As such, it cannot be used to create the green slayer helmet or be sacrificed to the Dark Altar .

If a player dies or teleports out while the Kalphite Queen is killed on the 256th kill, the player will not receive the drop and will be unable to obtain the Kq head (tattered).

Eek is a small spider that plays a part in the 2018 Halloween event. She can be found in the small graveyard north of the church next to Rimmington and Port Sarim. She understands humans, due to spiders spending much of their time in human settlements. She got her name from the scared exclamation "eek", as it was a sound she liked. After the player completes the event, Eric gives Eek to the player.

Completing any subsequent Halloween event will allow players to obtain Eek.

Eek can be wielded in the weapon slot, and is classified as a fun weapon in legacy duels within the Emir's Arena because she gives the wielding player negative bonuses. Players have the right-click option of Talk-to, in which a random conversation takes place between the player and Eek.

If destroyed, a replacement can be obtained from Diango in Draynor Village or from the toy box of a costume room.

A curator's medallion is used to build a mounted digsite pendant within a player-owned house portal nexus room. It is obtained from Curator Haig Halen , after having discovered the digsite pendant in the Varrock Museum , in exchange for 1 digsite pendant of any charge, 250 cut rubies , 500 fire runes (combination runes will not work), and 100 cosmic runes . The clean necklace must be found before you are given the option to deposit rubies.

Curator Haig Halen accepts noted rubies and any amount of rubies up to 250. The digsite pendant and the runes will not be accepted until the rubies have been delivered or the player has enough in their inventory to satisfy the remaining quantity. The remaining rubies (minimum of 1), digsite pendant, and runes must all be delivered at the same time, as the final rubies will not be accepted without the rest of the required items. The ability to deliver rubies piecemeal mostly benefits Ultimate Ironmen who do not have access to the noting facilities of a bank.

The medallion is lost on death , even though it is an untradeable item.

The medallion will be lost permanently if destroyed. A new medallion can be claimed from Curator Haig Halen by exchanging another digsite pendant and the required rubies , fire runes and cosmic runes . As such, Ultimate Ironmen are strongly recommended to ensure they have the appropriate Construction level to add it to their player-owned house before claiming a medallion.
22711:
The collection log is a book that players can receive from The Collector near the stairs in the Varrock Museum 's ground floor [ UK ] 1 st floor [ US ] . It records nearly every unique drop the player has obtained from various content in Old School RuneScape . The player does not need to have claimed a collection log for it to start tracking drops.

Drops obtained prior to its release are not automatically recorded for any player, excluding untradeable items (such as pets ) provided that they can be tracked by the game; for example, long bones the player had traded to Barlak or buried before the log's release were not added to it, but any long bones in the player's possession were added. Ironman players are able to add some items collected prior to the release by using the item on the collection log item; this does not apply to Group Ironman players. Using an ineligible or already logged item on the collection log gives the message Your collection log has already accounted for that item.

Each entry in the log is tracked by the item itself, not where it was obtained. This means that collection log item slots can be shared across multiple pages. For example, obtaining a dragon pickaxe from the Chaos Elemental will also log it under other bosses that drop it, such as Callisto and the King Black Dragon .

There is a cap on the amount each item can be tracked, depending on the item in question. For example, Zulrah's scales will only be tracked up to 65,535 and bracelets of ethereum up to 250.

It can be stored in a bookcase within a player-owned house , and can also be accessed from the adventurer's log within a player's Achievement Gallery and the Character Summary interface.

Dragon hastae are obtained as loot from the brimstone chest, which requires a brimstone key to open. The dragon hasta is obtained in broken form and can be repaired for free by showing it to Otto Godblessed (the repair does not require Barbarian Smithing).

Like most hastae, it provides negative defensive bonuses, but when equipped with a shield, the combined defence bonuses will be higher than those provided by the dragon spear.

The Ikkle Hydra is a pet dropped by the Alchemical Hydra, and is a much smaller version of the Hydra. Players may change the pet's appearance via the "Metamorphosis" option to its green, blue, red, or black appearance (with the respective amount of heads like in the boss encounter).

When a player receives the pet, it will automatically try to appear as their follower. At the same time, a message in the chatbox will state You have a funny feeling like you're being followed. However, if a player receives a pet while having a follower out (for example, a cat), it will be placed into their inventory. When this occurs, the message in the chatbox will instead state You feel something weird sneaking into your backpack.

If a player's inventory is full and they have a follower already, they will not receive the pet; it must instead be claimed from Probita in East Ardougne.

On death, if a player loses their pet (as a follower or in your inventory) it will wander around the area for 30 seconds before despawning. Even if the player returns in time, the pet cannot be picked up, and can be reclaimed from Probita.

Wyrm bones are the remains obtained from killing wyrms, which give 50 Prayer experience when buried. This can be increased by offering the bones in different ways:

150 XP when casting Sinister Offering.

150 XP when offered at the sacred bone burner after the appropriate faith level has been achieved.

175 XP when offered at a gilded altar with two burners lit.

200 XP when offered at the Ectofuntus in the form of wyrm bonemeal.

210 XP when blessed and broken down into blessed bone shards and offered at the libation bowl, or 252 XP when offered with a jug of blessed sunfire wine. Virilis outside the altar will exchange noted bones for 10 coins each.

350 XP on average when offered at the Chaos Temple in the Wilderness. Each offering gives 175 XP, which is the same as the gilded altar with two burners lit, but with an additional 50% chance to not consume the bones.

Burying them while wearing a dragonbone necklace will restore 3 prayer points.

280 XP when offered at a gilded altar with two burners lit.

320 XP when offered at the Ectofuntus in the form of drake bonemeal.

335 XP when blessed and broken down into blessed bone shards and offered at the libation bowl, or 402 XP when offered with a jug of blessed sunfire wine. Virilis outside the altar will exchange noted bones for 10 coins each.

22789: An uncooked dragonfruit pie is a pie made by adding a dragonfruit to a pie shell . It can be baked with level 73 Cooking to make a dragonfruit pie , granting 220 Cooking experience when successfully baked.
22792:
Dragonfruit pie is a type of pie that restores 20 Hitpoints in total, 2 bites each healing for 10. It also temporarily boosts Fletching by 4, the second highest boost available, and the highest reliable boost. A pie dish will remain after both bites are consumed.

It can be created by baking a uncooked dragonfruit pie on a cooking range , requiring level 73 Cooking and granting 220 experience when successful. When cooking there is a chance to fail, resulting in burnt pie . The burn rate decreases as the player's Cooking level increases. Dragonfruit pies never stop burning altogether even at level 99, unless the player is wearing a Cooking cape or using the Hosidius kitchen . Alternatively, casting the Bake Pie spell from the lunar spellbook will always create a pie without burning it.

A bird nest with seeds can be found while woodcutting most types of trees , as well as several other activities. Bird nests may contain tree or fruit tree seeds , and also provide an empty nest . The chance of getting a bird nest from a tree is 1/256 each time you would normally get a log, regardless of the type of tree.

If a nest appears while a player is cutting a tree, a chirping sound will usually be heard, and the player will get a message in the chat box stating, A bird's nest falls out of the tree. The nest is dropped on the ground and will despawn after 2 minutes if not picked up. Redwood trees do not drop seed nests, and instead only drop clue nests .

When woodcutting , a roll is done to determine the type of nest the player will receive. The table contains 100 slots: 3/100 egg nest (one for each colour), 32/100 ring nest , 65/100 seed nest. When wearing a strung rabbit foot , five seed slots are removed, making the chances 3/95 for bird's egg, 32/95 for ring and 60/95 for seeds. [ 1 ] Twitcher's gloves also increase the chance to receive a particular type of nest by approximately 20%.

During bird house trapping , at most 1 seed nest is awarded per birdhouse. The chance of getting a seed nest is improved with higher Hunter level, but is not affected by the tier of birdhouse.

Seed nests are also rewarded from Managing Miscellania when subjects are tasked with collecting maple, teak or mahogany logs.

Wyson will accept noted mole claws and mole skins, and will reward nest boxes if there isn't enough room in the inventory for all the nests.

Cormorant's glove is an item required for Aerial Fishing that can obtained for free by speaking to Alry the Angler on Molch island . Levels 35 Hunter and 43 Fishing are required to receive the glove and begin using it to catch bluegill , common tench , mottled eel , and greater siren . Alongside the fish, players can also catch Molch pearls which can then be traded to Alry for a number of items which can assist in standard fishing.

In order to use the cormorant's glove, players must have appropriate food in their inventory to keep the bird fed. King worms can be found scattered around the island to use for this purpose. Alternatively, the player may bring a knife to the island or pick up the one that spawns there and butcher any fish caught there into fish offcuts . The player receives 1 fish offcut from butchering any of the Molch island fish. Fine fish offcuts may also be used.

22818:
Fish chunks were a product of cutting open a bluegill, common tench, mottled eel, or greater siren using a knife. They could be stored in a tackle box. Fish chunks were used as a substitute for King worms when feeding the cormorant in aerial fishing. Cutting the fish has no skill requirements, but provides a small amount of Cooking experience. When catching fish, there is a 50% chance for a fish chunk to be consumed after every third catch. If it is not consumed on the third, it is guaranteed to be consumed on the fourth, meaning each chunk is consumed every 3.5 catches on average.

As part of the Sailing technical pre-release, all fish chunks were converted into fish offcuts, which now also function as food for the cormorant in aerial fishing.
22820:
Molch pearls are a stackable item which can be obtained while Aerial fishing. Each catch has a 1/66.6 to 1/50 chance of giving Molch pearls in addition to the player's catch, which scales based on the player's Fishing and Hunter levels. Players can also exchange a golden tench with Alry the Angler for 100 Molch pearls. They can be stored in a tackle box.

Molch pearls can be traded to Alry in his shop, Alry the Angler's Angling Accessories on Molch Island for equipable versions of fishing rods, pieces of the Angler's outfit, as well as for the fish sack.
22826:
Bluegill are fish that can be caught on Molch Island using the Cormorant's glove . Requiring 43 Fishing and 35 Hunter to catch, they provide 11.5 Fishing experience and 16.5 Hunter experience.

Before attempting to fish them, players must speak with Alry the Angler to obtain the Cormorant's glove . This item functions similarly to the Falconer's glove used in the hunter skill. Players must click on rapidly moving fishing spots and can obtain a variety of fish, including the bluegill.

Bluegill require no bait to catch directly, however King worms are initially required to feed the cormorant. Once caught, a knife can be used to cut the bluegill to obtain stackable fish offcuts which can be used as a substitute for the king worms. Cutting the fish provides 3.5 Cooking experience.

Catching a Bluegill on Lake Molch is a requirement of the medium Kourend & Kebos Diary .
22829:
Common tench are fish that can be caught on Molch island using the Cormorant's glove. Requiring 56 Fishing and 51 Hunter to catch, they provide 40 fishing experience and 45 hunter experience.

Before attempting to fish them, players must speak with Alry the Angler to obtain the Cormorant's glove. This item functions similarly to the Falconer's glove used in the hunter skill. Players must click on rapidly moving fishing spots and can obtain a variety of fish, including the Common tench.

Common tench require no bait to catch directly, however King worms are initially required to feed the cormorant. After caught, a knife can be used to cut the tench to obtain stackable Fish offcuts which can be used as a substitute for the king worms. Cutting the fish provides 10 Cooking experience.
22832:
Mottled eel are fish that can be caught on Molch island using the Cormorant's glove . Requiring 73 Fishing and 68 Hunter to catch, they provide 65 fishing experience and 90 hunter experience.

Before attempting to fish them, players must speak with Alry the Angler to obtain the Cormorant's glove . This item functions similarly to the Falconer's glove used in the hunter skill. Players must click on rapidly moving fishing spots and can obtain a variety of fish, including the Mottled eel.

Mottled eel require no bait to catch directly, however the cormorant is initially required to be fed either with fish offcuts or King worms , the latter of which are easily found in the island. After catching a Mottled eel, a knife can be used to cut the eel to obtain stackable fish offcuts which can be used as a substitute for the king worms. Cutting the fish provides 20 Cooking experience.
22835:
Greater siren are aquatic creatures that can be caught on Molch island using the Cormorant's glove . Requiring 91 Fishing and 87 Hunter to catch, they provide 100 fishing experience and 130 hunter experience.

Before attempting to fish them, players must speak with Alry the Angler to obtain the Cormorant's glove . This item functions similarly to the Falconer's glove used in the hunter skill. Players must click on rapidly moving fishing spots and can obtain a variety of fish, including the Greater siren.

Greater siren require no bait to catch directly, however King worms or fish offcuts are initially required to feed the cormorant. When caught, a knife can be used to cut the siren to obtain stackable fish offcuts which can be used as a substitute for the king worms. Cutting the siren provides 25 Cooking experience.
22838:
The fish sack is an item that can be purchased for 500 Molch pearls from Alry the Angler on Molch Island. The Fish sack is worn in place of a cape and has minor defence bonuses.

Players can combine the fish sack with a fish barrel to create the fish sack barrel, which is an equipable version of the fish barrel. There is no confirmation message when this occurs, but it can be split apart by selecting the "Dismantle" option after right-clicking "Configure".

This item can be stored in the magic wardrobe of a costume room. However, if the player already has a fish sack barrel stored, it cannot be stored, instead receiving the message "The store already contains an equivalent item".
22840:
The golden tench is a very rare equipable fish obtained from aerial fishing at Lake Molch at a rate of 1/20,000. [ 1 ] When a player receives the tench, a message in the chatbox will state: The cormorant has brought you a very strange tench. , or The cormorant is about to eat a strange tench before you quickly yank it out of its mouth. if the player has the option to feed the cormorant whole fish enabled. Unlike other catches in Lake Molch , the golden tench cannot be cut using a knife . The golden tench will be dropped on the ground if a player's inventory is full.

Equipping the golden tench allows players to whack other players by right-clicking on them, just like with the stale baguette or the rubber chicken . Unlike the chicken, the tench cannot be fumbled, and thus is never forcefully dropped on the ground. Multiple golden tenches can be kept at a time, or players can speak to Alry the Angler to exchange it for 100 Molch pearls .

The benefits of Rada's blessing and spirit flakes will cause two golden tench to be caught at once if either item activates. [ 2 ] The extra golden tench will not be counted in the collection log if this happens. If your inventory is full when the effect activates, you will not receive the extra tench.

This item can be stored in the magic wardrobe of a costume room .
22842:
A pearl barbarian rod is an item that can be purchased for 150 Molch pearls from Alry the Angler on Molch island . It is an equipable version of the Barbarian rod , and can only be purchased if the relevant part of the Barbarian Training miniquest is completed with Otto Godblessed . It can only be used in the fishing spots at Otto's Grotto , and Mount Quidamortem in the Kebos Lowlands . Since barbarian fishing gives marginal Strength and Agility experience with each catch, it is more efficient than other training methods such as fly fishing.

This item can be stored in the magic wardrobe of a costume room . It can also be stored in a Tackle box .
22844:
A pearl fly fishing rod is an equipable version of the fly fishing rod . It is purchased for 120 Molch pearls from Alry the Angler on Molch island . This rod can be used to fish for trout , salmon (both with feathers ), and rainbow fish (with stripy feathers ).

The pearl fly fishing rod can only be obtained by members, but can be equipped and used in a free to play world.

This item can be stored in the magic wardrobe of a costume room . It can also be stored in a Tackle box .
22846:
A pearl fishing rod is an item that can be purchased for 100 Molch pearls from Alry the Angler on Molch island . It is an equipable version of the fishing rod .

To use this fishing rod, one will need fishing bait ( sandworms or Diabolic worms for anglerfish ) to catch fish. Players can also add blamish oil to create an oily pearl fishing rod to catch lava and infernal eels . This process can be reverted with a cleaning cloth .

The pearl fishing rod can only be obtained by members but can be equipped and used in a free to play world.

This item can be stored in the magic wardrobe of a costume room . It can also be stored in a Tackle box .

The following fish are caught with a pearl fishing rod:

22856:
Celastrus saplings are saplings that can be used to grow celastrus trees at level 85 Farming .

They can be made by planting a celastrus seed in a filled plant pot , with a gardening trowel in your inventory, and then watering the celastrus seedling with a watering can or by using Humidify . When watered, the seedling will sprout into a sapling in one crop cycle (0-5 minutes).

Planting the sapling in the celastrus patch in the Farming Guild , with a spade in your inventory, will give 204 Farming experience. It will grow into a celastrus tree after 800 minutes (13 hours and 20 minutes), which gives 14,130 Farming experience.

Players can ask the gardener to protect their tree from disease whilst it grows, which requires payment of 8 potato cacti . This payment can be noted.

Players should use ultracompost to increase the celastrus bark yield when the tree is harvested.
22859:
Redwood saplings are saplings that can be used to grow redwood trees at 90 Farming . They are made by planting a redwood seed in a filled plant pot , with a gardening trowel in your inventory, then watering the redwood seedling with a watering can or by casting Humidify . When watered, the seedling will sprout into a sapling in one crop cycle (0-5 minutes).

Planting the sapling in the redwood tree patch in the Farming Guild , requiring a spade, yields 230 Farming experience. It will grow into a redwood tree after 6,400 minutes (4 days, 10 hours, and 40 minutes), and yields 22,450 Farming experience when checked.

Players can ask the gardener to protect their tree from disease whilst it grows, which requires payment of 6 dragonfruits . This payment can be noted.

Once the tree has fully grown, it can be cut down like a regular redwood tree, as it will regrow unlike other self-grown log giving trees. This method of cutting redwoods may be preferable for players looking to AFK more, as you don't compete with other players and the bank deposit is closer. However; you will lose out on the Woodcutting Guild's invisible +7 boost to Woodcutting , making it slightly slower overall.

It is not possible for players to clear the redwood tree patch; Alexandra must be paid 2,000 coins to clear it.
22862: Dragonfruit seedlings are the result of planting a dragonfruit tree seed in a plant pot with a gardening trowel . Once watered, these seedlings will take approximately 5 minutes to grow into a dragonfruit sapling . 81 Farming is needed to plant the seed. When it has grown, players may place it in a fruit tree patch to grow a dragonfruit tree . Players can pay 15 coconuts for the farmer to look after it.

22866:

They can be made by planting a dragonfruit tree seed in a filled plant pot , with a gardening trowel in your inventory, and then watering the dragonfruit seedling with a watering can or by using Humidify . When watered, the seedling will sprout into a sapling in one crop cycle (0-5 minutes).

Players can ask the gardener to protect their tree from disease whilst it grows, which requires payment of 15 coconuts . This payment can be noted.
22869:
Celastrus seeds are a type of seed requiring level 85 Farming to plant, and can only be planted in the celastrus patch within the third tier of the Farming Guild . They can be obtained from bird nests , monster drops, Pest Control , the Hespori , the brimstone chest , Larran's big chest , or by completing farming contracts .

A celastrus seed, when planted in a plant pot , watered, allowed to sprout into a sapling , and then planted in a Celastrus patch, may grow into a celastrus tree . A nearby gardener named Taylor will watch over a player's growing Celastrus tree for 8 potato cacti .

Once fully grown, it can be harvested for celastrus bark , which then can be fletched into a battlestaff with level 40 Fletching. The amount of bark harvested from a fully grown Celastrus tree is random, much like the harvesting of herbs, with a minimum number of three lives to ensure a guaranteed amount each harvest. Using compost of any kind or growing an attas plant will increase the average yield. [ 1 ] Once harvested, players must chop down the tree and clear the patch with a spade in order to plant another celastrus sapling.
22871:
Redwood tree seeds are seeds used in the Farming skill. At level 90 Farming [ boostable ] , redwood seeds may be planted in plant pots with a gardening trowel and watered to become redwood saplings . They can be obtained from bird nests , monster drops, the brimstone chest , Larran's big chest or by completing farming contracts .

After planting the sapling in a redwood tree patch found in the Farming Guild and waiting for it to fully grow, which takes over four days (106.7 hours), the plant will grow into a redwood tree which can be cut to yield redwood logs (and grant Woodcutting experience ). Planting the redwood sapling yields 230 experience, and checking its health gives 22,450 experience. Alexandra will look after a player's redwood patch in exchange for 6 dragonfruits .

When cut down, the tree will automatically regrow after a period of time. Players cannot clear the patch on their own; they must pay Alexandra 2,000 coins to do so.

One seed can be used on the skilling pet Tangleroot to change its appearance.
22873:
Potato cactus seeds are a type of seed that can be planted in a cactus patch found in Al Kharid or the Farming Guild. They require level 64 Farming to plant and produce a potato cactus. Growth time is approximately 70 minutes. Players can harvest potato cacti from the mature plant.

Potato cactus seeds can be obtained as drops from various monsters, in seed packs awarded from farming contracts, or by pickpocketing a master farmer.

A nearby gardener will watch over your growing potato cactus plant in exchange for 8 snape grass.
22875:
Hespori seeds are a type of seed requiring level 65 Farming to plant, and that can only be planted in the Hespori patch with a seed dibber in the cave found in the west wing of the Farming Guild . They can be randomly obtained from checking the health of fully grown trees , bushes or cacti , from the last harvest of a regular plant such as herbs , hops , allotments , flowers , mushrooms , cacti , giant seaweed , coral , or from completing farming contracts . [ 1 ]

When fully grown, it will grow into the Hespori , a demi-boss that can be defeated for 12,600 Farming experience. It is not necessary to water or compost a Hespori plant, nor does it need protection from disease . It takes 22–32 hours to grow, depending on when it was planted. The flower behind the cave entrance will be in bloom when the Hespori plant is fully grown.

Players can speak to Arno if they wish to stop randomly receiving Hespori seeds as they harvest, clear, or check the health of their crops around Gielinor.

Hespori seeds are most commonly dropped from plants grown in Special patches ; players looking to fight Hespori more often should consider growing cactus , nightshade , mushrooms and giant seaweed. Giant seaweed is a popular choice as the seaweed spores are easily obtainable, grow quickly, and have a 1/15 chance to drop a Hespori seed; similar to the Tangleroot, this is rolled on the last harvesting attempt. [ 2 ]

If the player has no room in their inventory, they will not receive a Hespori seed. In most cases, the chance of receiving a Hespori seed is 500 times the base chance of the Tangleroot . [ 3 ] At 99 Farming, the effective chance of Tangleroot per Hespori seeds received is between 1/252.2 [ 4 ] and 1/497.3 [ 5 ] . Note this is outside Tithe farm and does not account for Hespori seeds received from seed packs .
22877:
Dragonfruit tree seeds are the highest level fruit tree patch seeds . At 81 Farming , a dragonfruit tree seed can be planted in a plant pot to make a dragonfruit seedling , which grows into a dragonfruit sapling ; the sapling can be planted in a fruit tree patch to be grown into a dragonfruit tree . Dragonfruit trees, when fully grown, bear dragonfruit .

A nearby gardener will watch over your growing dragonfruit tree at the cost of 15 coconuts .

Dragonfruit trees, like all fruit trees, ideally take six 160-minute farming cycles to fully grow, but certain factors can delay this. Dragonfruit trees are usually fully grown within 24 hours, however.

Dragonfruit tree seeds may be found rarely in a bird nest , which can be obtained randomly while Woodcutting , emptying Birdhouses or from Managing Miscellania . They can also be obtained via farming contracts from the Farming Guild , as loot from opening the brimstone chest , Larran's small or big chest or as rare drops from the Hespori , alchemical hydra , demonic gorillas , lizardman shamans , and Vorkath .

One seed can be used on the skilling pet Tangleroot to change its appearance.
22879:
Snape grass seeds can be planted at level 61 Farming . 3 seeds are sown in an allotment patch to grow snape grass plants , which yield snape grass : a Herblore secondary ingredient . They take 1 hour and 10 minutes to grow.

A nearby gardener will watch over growing snape grass plants for 5 jangerberries . Fully grown white lilies in a nearby flower patch will also protect the snape grass from disease .

These seeds can be stolen from master farmers . They may also be obtained from various monsters , Farming Guild seed packs , and the Wintertodt reward cart .

The amulet of bounty is useful for saving snape grass seeds, providing a saving of 23,274 coins per charge.

8 snape grass are needed to protect growing potato cactus .
22881:

From the moment the seed is planted, the attas plant will increase the yield of player's farming patches worldwide, by increasing the chance to save a harvest life by 5%. [ 1 ] This effect stacks with other similar chance-to-save boosts, such as the magic secateurs and the Farming cape . The plant will provide this effect for approximately 3.5 days (8 x 640 mins) before dying. The next growth stage will occur in approximately 2 hours and 42 minutes (refresh) . After refreshing, when this timer indicates 10 hours and 40 minutes, this signifies a Farming tick just occurred. Due to the Farming tick varying between accounts, it is recommended to wait another 15 minutes, after it says 10 hours and 25 minutes.

Once the Attas plant reaches its eighth growth stage (~74 hours after planting), it will begin to take on a withered appearance, indicating the plant will die in the next growth stage, though the benefits will remain until death. In order to reap the Attas plant's benefits again, players must clear the anima patch and plant another Attas seed. The plant cannot be resurrected with the Resurrect Crops spell. Players can remove the plant before the plant dies by using a spade on the anima patch, being prompted "are you sure you want to dig up this patch?"
22883:

22885:
Kronos seeds are a type of anima seed requiring level 76 Farming to plant. They are obtained exclusively from the Hespori , and can only be planted in the anima patch within the intermediate tier of the Farming Guild . Planting a kronos seed gives 100 Farming experience .

From the moment the seed is planted, the kronos plant provides a chance for all Farming patches worldwide (excluding kronos itself) to skip a growth stage during their next growth cycle ; this chance is shared between all farming patches of that growth cycle. For example, if a 20 minute growth cycle is skipped, both herb and bush patches (which advance a growth stage every 20 minutes) will skip a growth stage. Multiple growth stages can be skipped in the same Farming tick.

Kronos plant can also speed up some other processes tied to the Farming clock, such as the rate at which berries, fruit, or cactus spines regrow after they've been picked. [ 1 ] That said, neither fermenting vats nor compost bins benefit from the effects of a kronos plant. [ 2 ] [ 3 ]

22887:
White lily seeds can be planted in a flower patch at level 58 Farming to yield a white lily . When fully grown, it protects all neighbouring allotments from disease .

A nearby gardener will not watch over a growing white lily plant . It is recommended to use ultracompost when planting them.

They can be obtained as a drop from the Hespori , from a seed pack bought from Tithe Farm , or bought from other players.

Using one seed on the Tangleroot pet will change its appearance to a white lily variant .
22929:
A dragonfruit is obtained from a dragonfruit tree , which can be grown from a dragonfruit sapling in a fruit tree patch , provided that one has level 81 Farming . Players can pay a gardener a fee of 15 coconuts to watch over the tree while it grows. A fully grown dragonfruit tree grows one dragonfruit per 30 minutes up to a maximum of six per tree.

When eaten, a dragonfruit heals 10 hitpoints . They are an ingredient in dragonfruit pies , which require level 73 Cooking to bake and boost a player's Fletching level by 4 when eaten.

Ten dragonfruits can also be used on a vial to create bottled dragonbreath , which can be used on a sulphur vent on Mount Karuulm to "power" it (this process will burn the player for 2 damage if they are not wearing ice gloves ). Once powered, it can be used on a dragonfire shield or ward to fully charge it instantly.

Players may pay 6 dragonfruits to Alexandra in the Farming Guild to have her look after a planted redwood tree . Players can also pay a gardener 8 dragonfruits to look after a planted rosewood tree .
22932:
White lilies are flowers that can be harvested from a flower patch after planting white lily seeds . Fully grown white lilies protect all neighbouring allotments from disease .

White lilies have very limited practical uses after being harvested. The most productive use of white lilies (once harvested) is to add them to a compost bin to make supercompost .
22935:
Celastrus bark is a type of wood harvested from a celastrus tree . The bark can be fletched into a battlestaff using a knife with level 40 Fletching , granting 80 Fletching experience.

One celastrus tree produces a minimum of 3 bark, where each harvest has a chance of using up one of the "lives" of the celastrus patch, much like harvesting herb patches . Similar to other variable-yield patches, the yield of celastrus bark can be increased by using magic secateurs , [ 1 ] supercompost , ultracompost , attas seed , [ 2 ] and having higher Farming levels. Nature offerings do not increase the yield of celastrus bark, however.

Celastrus bark can also be used for tick manipulation training on a 4-tick cycle to receive greatly improved experience rates. An expanded explanation on tick manipulation and celastrus bark's use case can be found on that page.
22938:
The Kronos plant is an interface item that can be seen in the Farming skill guide representing the Kronos plant .

The actual item cannot be obtained by players.
22939:
The Iasor plant is an interface item that can be seen in the Farming skill guide representing the Iasor plant .

The actual item cannot be obtained by players.
22940:
The Attas plant is an interface item that can be seen in the Farming skill guide representing the Attas plant .

The actual item cannot be obtained by players.

22943: Rada's blessing 2 is an Achievement diary reward for completing all medium Kourend & Kebos Diary tasks. It is given by Elise in the Kourend Castle courtyard, and can be retrieved for free if lost. It can be stored in a tackle box.
22945: Rada's blessing 3 is an Achievement diary reward for completing all hard Kourend & Kebos Diary tasks. It is given by Elise in the Kourend Castle courtyard, and can be retrieved for free if lost. It can be stored in a tackle box.
22947:
Rada's blessing 4 is an Achievement diary reward for completing all elite Kourend & Kebos Diary tasks. It is given by Elise in the Kourend Castle courtyard, and can be retrieved for free if lost. Multiple can be obtained for free. Players can also trade with Perdu who sells blessings for 200 coins each, this is especially handy if buying bulk as Perdu allows the player to buy a full inventory at once. It can be stored in a tackle box.

Rada's blessing 4 gives the best-in-slot prayer bonus for the ammunition slot at +2, surpassing god blessings.
22949:
The Battlefront teleport is a magic tablet that can be broken by players to teleport to the ancient grave just outside the Battlefront in the Kebos Lowlands .

Players with 23 Magic and the Arceuus spellbook enabled can create this item on the Arceuus lectern in the Ouditor 's house with 1 law rune , 1 earth rune , 1 fire rune , and a dark essence block instead of the soft clay required for most magic tablets. This grants 19 Magic experience .

As with all magic tablets, the player does not need to have the relevant Magic level to use the tablet, but will not receive any experience for using it.
22951:
Boots of Brimstone are a piece of Slayer equipment worn in the foot slot. A Slayer level of 44, along with level 70 in Defence , Magic , and Ranged is required to wear them.

They can be created by using a drake's claw on the boots of stone , and can protect the wearer from the extremely hot ground within the Karuulm Slayer Dungeon .

These boots have the second highest stab attack bonus, as well as the third-highest magic defence in the footwear slot, tied with the silly jester boots , bloodbark boots , infinity boots , and pegasian boots . Because these boots have no negative bonuses, positive attack and defence bonuses in both ranged and magic, and decent melee defensive bonuses, these boots are an excellent choice for activities that require use of mage and range styles such as Zulrah . They are a poor choice for activities which require melee due to the absence of any strength bonus.
22954:
Devout boots are a pair of footwear requiring level 60 in Prayer to wear. They can be created by using a drake's tooth on a pair of holy sandals. This process can be reversed using the dismantle option.

They have the best prayer bonus for the footwear slot at +5, a bonus of +1 over the Echo boots. They also count as a Saradomin item for the God Wars Dungeon and the Bandit Camp. Unlike the holy sandals they are made from, the devout boots cannot be stored in the player owned house.
22957: A drake's claw is an item obtained from drakes found within the Karuulm Slayer Dungeon. It can be combined with the boots of stone to create the boots of brimstone, which has increased stats and can also protect players from the extremely hot ground within the dungeon.
22960:
The drake tooth is an item obtained from drakes found within the Karuulm Slayer Dungeon. It can be combined with the holy sandals to create devout boots, which require level 60 Prayer to wear and increase the prayer bonus from +3 to +5.

A confirmation message appears when attempting to create the devout boots, asking if the player would like to proceed with the alchemical combination. Should the player confirm, the chatbox will state You successfully combine the Holy sandals and Drake's tooth to create Devout boots.
22963: A broken dragon hasta is a broken form of the dragon hasta and can be received as loot from the brimstone chest . Players can show the broken dragon hasta to Otto Godblessed for a free repair. Players do not have to learn Barbarian Smithing via the Barbarian Training miniquest to do this. Players do however need to have completed the smithing portion of the miniquest in order to wield the repaired hasta.
22966:
The hydra's claw is an item dropped by the Alchemical Hydra. It can be combined with the Zamorakian hasta to create the dragon hunter lance.

When attempting to create the dragon hunter lance, a warning will appear in the chatbox stating that the process cannot be reversed, and a confirmation will appear afterwards asking if players would like to proceed with the alchemical combination.
22969:
The Hydra's heart is an item dropped by hydras and the Alchemical Hydra. It can be combined with the Hydra's eye and fang to create the brimstone ring.

Much like abyssal bludgeons, players will not receive duplicate pieces until they have all three Hydra body parts. For example, if a player has obtained a Hydra's heart, they are guaranteed to get either a fang or eye next time.

When attempting to create the brimstone ring, a warning will appear in the chatbox stating that the process cannot be reversed, and a confirmation will appear afterwards asking if players would like to proceed with the combination. Should the player confirm, the chatbox will state You successfully combine the Hydra Heart, the Hydra Eye, and the Hydra Fang to create the Brimstone Ring.
22971:

22973:

22975:
A brimstone ring is a ring created by combining three untradeable components — the hydra's eye , fang , and heart ; players cannot receive a duplicate of these until obtaining each of the other pieces.

The ring provides the combined offensive and defensive stats of the archers , berserker , warrior , seers , treasonous , and tyrannical rings , though it cannot be imbued.

The ring also has a passive effect when worn that improves its effectiveness to rival the seers ring (i) when using Magic. Each time the player attacks using a spell or magical attack ( powered staves included), there is a 25% chance that the target's defensive roll will be reduced by 10% for that attack. [ 1 ] When this occurs, there will be a game chat message Your attack ignored 10% of your opponent's magic defence. Note the reduction doesn't affect multiple targets when barraging or hitting multiple opponents. The effect is limited to the single intended target you select.
22978:
The dragon hunter lance is a one-handed spear and dragonbane weapon created by using a hydra claw on a Zamorakian hasta. Equipping the lance requires level 78 Attack as well as completion of the Firemaking (not the pyre step), Fishing, and Smithing sections of the Barbarian Training miniquest.

The lance's dragonbane passive effect is its 20% increased accuracy and damage when fighting draconic creatures, such as dragons, wyverns, and the Great Olm (but excluding Elvarg and revenant dragons). This stacks multiplicatively with both Void Knight equipment and the Slayer helm (i).

Like the Zamorakian hasta, it will act as a Zamorak item within the God Wars Dungeon; though the lance lacks the hasta's prayer and defensive bonuses and special attack, while sporting a lower strength bonus.

When attempting to create the dragon hunter lance, a warning will appear in the chatbox stating that the process cannot be reversed, and a confirmation will appear afterwards asking if players would like to proceed with the alchemical combination. Should the player confirm, the chatbox will state: You successfully combine the Hydra claw and the Zamorakian hasta to create the Dragon hunter lance.
22981:
The ferocious gloves are a pair of melee gloves requiring level 80 Attack and Defence to equip. They are the best-in-slot offensive gloves for melee, surpassing Barrows gloves . However, they provide no defensive stats, and have a negative ranged and magic attack bonuses, making them less effective when using multiple attack styles.

The gloves are untradeable, but can be made from a piece of hydra leather , costing 10,077,686 on the Grand Exchange . To craft the gloves, player must bring the leather and a hammer to the northern part of the Lithkren Vault , and use the leather on the machinery south-west of the pool. In order to revert the gloves back to leather form, simply use the machinery again while holding a hammer and the gloves. Players must complete Dragon Slayer II to access the vault.
22983:
Hydra leather is dropped by the Alchemical Hydra . It is used to make ferocious gloves , by placing it on the piece of machinery just south-west of the large pool in Lithkren Vault , requiring Dragon Slayer II and a hammer . The gloves can be reverted to leather using the same machinery.

When Hydra leather is inspected, the chatbox message states This leather looks pretty tough to work with... Maybe the dragonkin had a way. When the gloves are created, the chatbox message states By feeding the tough to work leather through the machine, you manage to form a pair of gloves .
22986:
The bonecrusher necklace is a necklace that can be created by combining the bonecrusher and dragonbone necklace with a hydra tail . It requires level 70 in Prayer to equip and shares its best in slot +12 prayer bonus with the dragonbone necklace.

The necklace possesses the effects of both the bonecrusher and the dragonbone necklace, being able to automatically crush bones while restoring prayer, saving an inventory slot. Like the bonecrusher , the necklace must be charged with ecto-tokens (25 charges per token). It can be charged quickly using the free bonemeal and buckets of slime from Robin given daily as part of the hard Morytania diary rewards . The prayer restoration effect does not stack with the Catacombs of Kourend prayer restoration effect. When unequipped, the bonecrusher necklace behaves like an ordinary bonecrusher, granting Prayer experience but no restoration.

The bones crushed can include those from monsters killed traditionally, but can also include those killed using hunter methods such as deadfall traps.

When killed in PvP, the bonecrusher necklace and its charges are kept when protected. When unprotected, only the bonecrusher is kept with the charges, the hydra tail and dragonbone necklace are always dropped to the killer.

The amount of points restored are as follows:
22988: The hydra tail is an item dropped by hydras and the Alchemical Hydra . It can be combined with the dragonbone necklace and bonecrusher to create the bonecrusher necklace , which combines the effects of both. There will be a confirmation message before combining them; this can be reversed.
22991:
The stone tablet is a tablet found in a stone chest in the south-east corner of the Lizardman Temple . It records the construction of the temple.

When read, the player will read it aloud and make their own commentary.
22993:
A seed pack is an item received from Guildmaster Jane as a reward for completing a farming contract , or purchased from Farmer Gricoller for 30 Tithe Farm points.

Taking from a seed pack rewards the player with seeds based on the pack's tier. The player may keep taking seeds until all seeds have been removed. [ 1 ]

Each seed pack has a tier from 1 to 5, with 5 being the highest, which determines the quantity and value of the seeds received (see table below). Low-tier packs can be received from completing Easy contracts such as growing potatoes, and high-tier packs can be received from completing Hard contracts such as growing a magic tree .

Seed packs purchased from Farmer Gricoller are equivalent to tier 3, with the addition of white lily seeds to its drop table.

Upon death the seed pack will always be destroyed.
22994:
A bottomless compost bucket is a drop from the Hespori, which can be filled with compost, supercompost, or ultracompost. Tool Leprechauns will store one of them in its own slot.

Despite being called a bottomless compost bucket, it can only hold a maximum of 10,000 uses of a single type of compost. With each bucket of compost added, it gains two charges, effectively doubling the use of a single bucket of compost. It can be filled with up to 5,000 buckets at a time. It can be filled from a compost bin or from other noted or unnoted buckets of compost. If buckets of compost are used to fill the bottomless compost bucket, empty buckets are returned to the player in the same noted/unnoted form. Compost in the bottomless bucket can only be used to fertilise farming patches and cannot be put back into empty buckets, only discarded.

The doubling effect means that if used exclusively for ultracompost, the bottomless compost bucket will pay for itself after fertilising 2,110 farming patches.

The bottomless compost bucket is tradeable only when empty, which can be done via the right-click option to empty the bucket.

Bottled dragonbreath is an item obtained from using ten dragonfruit on a vial. Having done so, it becomes an unpowered bottled dragonbreath. To charge it, players must use it on a sulphur vent on Mount Karuulm (one is found outside the bank). Players will take a small amount of damage (2 Hitpoints) during the process if they are not wearing ice gloves or smiths gloves (i).

Once powered, it can be used on a dragonfire shield or ward to instantly charge them to full, consuming the item. The ancient wyvern shield cannot be charged with bottled dragon breath.

23047: The mystic hat (dusk) is a part of the dusk Mystic robes set worn in the head slot. Mystic hats come in many colours but all share the same bonuses, and all mystic items require 40 Magic and 20 Defence to wear. It can be stored in a magic wardrobe in a player-owned house.

23062:
The nest box is an item that holds bird nests. It can be obtained from trading in noted mole claws or mole skins to Wyson the gardener who can be found in Falador Park.

There are three different types of nest boxes.

Nest box (seeds) - Contains birds nests with seeds in them.

Nest box (ring) - Contains bird nests with rings in them.

Nest box (empty) - Contains bird nests with nothing in them.

Each box will contain various amounts of nests depending on what each nest contains.

If you have nest boxes on you, trading more mole parts into Wyson will not result in the bird nests being added to the existing boxes. Rather, you will get a separate additional set of boxes.
23064:
The jar of chemicals is a rare drop from the Alchemical Hydra that can be found in the Karuulm Slayer Dungeon .

The jar can be used on a boss lair display in a player's Achievement Gallery to have a display of the Alchemical Hydra's final form. Doing so requires killing it at least once.

23071:
The ancient casket is a quest item used only in X Marks the Spot. It is found after digging in Draynor Village's pig pen. It contains the treasure that Veos is seeking, and giving it to him will complete the quest.

When players dig it up, the chatbox will state "You dig up an Ancient Casket. As you do, you hear a faint whispering. You can't make out what it says though..." and your character will believe it was just the wind.

If players attempt to open the casket, they will say "I don't think Veos would want me to open his treasure. I should take it to him. If I remember right, he's docked at the northernmost pier in Port Sarim."

When asked about the contents of the casket, Veos will reply shiftily, saying "Oh err... Nothing important. Just something that might be of use to me back in Great Kourend."
23072:
The antique lamp is an item obtained from Veos after completing the X Marks the Spot quest. It grants 300 experience in a skill of the player's choosing.

The lamp cannot be banked. However, if the player prefers to use it at a later date, they can destroy it and simply reclaim it from Veos when they want to use it.
23073:
The hydra Slayer helmet is a piece of equipment that is worn in the helmet slot. It is a cosmetic upgrade to the Slayer helmet .

It can be created by adding Alchemical hydra heads after purchasing the ability Use more head for 1,000 Slayer reward points from any Slayer master . This is reversible, and the heads will be returned to the inventory along with the slayer helmet's components. If a player loses the hydra slayer helmet in a PvP death, the alchemical hydra heads will be placed in their gravestone.
23075:
The hydra Slayer helmet (i) is a piece of equipment that is worn in the helmet slot. It is a cosmetic upgrade to the Slayer helmet (i) .

It can be created by adding Alchemical hydra heads after purchasing the ability Use more head for 1,000 Slayer reward points from any Slayer master . This is reversible, and the heads will be returned to the inventory along with the slayer helmet's components. If a player loses the hydra slayer helmet (i) in a PvP death, the alchemical hydra heads will be placed in their gravestone.
23077:
Alchemical hydra heads are a rare drop from the Alchemical Hydra . They can be stuffed at the taxidermist in Canifis by using the item on her and paying 50,000 coins, returning stuffed hydra heads . When shown the heads, she will say, "This hydra looks like it might fall to pieces soon. I'll have to be careful to preserve it properly."

Once stuffed, Alchemical hydra heads can be mounted at a gilded display within the skill hall in a player-owned house , granting 223 Construction alongside 200 Attack , Strength , Defence , Magic , and Ranged experience , although players are given the option to decline the combat experience. Alternatively, the heads can be sacrificed to the Dark Altar north of Arceuus , granting 2,500 Prayer experience.

Lastly, the heads can be combined with a slayer helmet (or imbued) to create a hydra slayer helmet ; doing so requires purchasing the ability Use More Head for 1,000 Slayer reward points .
23079:
Stuffed hydra heads are obtained by bringing alchemical hydra heads and 50,000 coins to the taxidermist in Canifis; this process is reversible by selecting the "Unstuff" option on the item.

Once stuffed, it can be mounted at a gilded display within the skill hall in a player-owned house with level 82 Construction, granting 223 Construction alongside 200 Attack, Strength, Defence, Magic, and Ranged experience, with players being given the option to decline the combat experience before mounting the heads.
23081:
