23082:
The antique lamp is a reward from A Kingdom Divided , two of which are received from Commander Fullore upon completing the quest . Each lamp grants 10,000 experience in a skill of the player's choosing, given that the skill is over level 40.

The lamp cannot be banked. However, if the player prefers to use it at a later date, it can be destroyed and reclaimed from Commander Fullore whenever the player wishes to do so. If you die with it in inventory Commander Fullore will grant the lamps.

Players who have completed the removed Architectural Alliance miniquest prior to 10 January 2024 without claiming an antique lamp as their reward can still do so.

For monsters with combat level L smaller than level 100, the probability follows the curve [ 2 ]

Additionally, if the monster has a Slayer level requirement, there is a 20% boost in the drop probability. [ 3 ]

23091:
Ornate gloves are obtained from completing the first clue during the Crack the Clue II event. They are part of the ornate armour set, and are obtainable only once if you already have them in your inventory or bank. If you happen to accidentally destroy them, you will need to discover them again.

They are obtained alongside the ornate boots .

In order to obtain/reobtain the boots and gloves, the player must dig just south-east of Rimmington near Skippy with a pie dish in their inventory.

Its stats are identical to those of Leather gloves .

This item can be stored in the armour case of a costume room , as part of the Ornate armour set. Ultimate Ironmen will be unable to retrieve individual pieces until the full set is stored.
23093:
Ornate boots are obtained from completing the first clue during the Crack the Clue II event. They are part of the ornate armour set, and are obtainable only once if you already have them in your inventory or bank. If you happen to accidentally destroy them, you will need to discover them again.

They are obtained alongside the ornate gloves , and have stats identical to leather boots .

This item can be stored in the armour case of a costume room , as part of the Ornate armour set. Ultimate Ironmen will be unable to retrieve individual pieces until the full set is stored.
23095:
The ornate legs are obtained from completing a clue during the Crack the Clue II event. Giving the same bonuses as iron platelegs , they are part of the ornate armour set, and are obtainable only once if you already have them in your inventory or bank. If you happen to accidentally destroy them, you will need to discover them again.

In order to obtain/reobtain the legs, the player must dig East (Near blue flower) of the entrance to the Air Altar south of Falador with a raw herring in their inventory.

The ornate legs are a required item to solve Step 3 (Match-Catch) and Step 5 (Start-South-Numbers) of Crack the Clue III .

This item can be stored in the armour case of a costume room , as part of the Ornate armour set. Ultimate Ironmen will be unable to retrieve individual pieces until the full set is stored.

It is part of the ornate armour set, and is obtainable only once if you already have it in your inventory or bank. If you happen to accidentally destroy it, you will need to discover it again. A strange device is an item used in the Hot & Cold challenge of a beginner or master clue .

The beginner clue strange device can be obtained by talking to Reldo in the Varrock Palace library, while the master clue strange device can be obtained by talking to Jorral in the outpost north-west of West Ardougne . The player must have an active clue step directing them to one of Reldo or Jorral to obtain a strange device, but once obtained it does not need to be returned and can be kept in the bank. Note that one must have completed Making History before Jorral will give them a strange device for a master clue.

The strange device changes temperature as the player moves about. Its temperature is based on the distance of the treasure from the player, measured in the number of steps it would take to reach the treasure, ignoring any obstacles. The warmer the key gets, the closer the player is to the treasure.

Clicking "Feel Strange device " gives information on its temperature. If using the strange device obtained from Jorral used for master clues, this will deal 3-8 damage to the player each time , which can be fatal . If you do not have an active master clue with a hot & cold step, the device will be inactive, and using it will not damage you.

A list of possible locations can be found here .
23184:
The Mimic is an item that may be obtained when attempting to open an elite or master reward casket . In order to be eligible to obtain it, players must first speak to the strange casket upstairs in Watson's house in Hosidius to enable the chance of a reward casket turning into the Mimic; attempting to open an elite or master reward casket for the first time before speaking to the strange casket will direct players to the strange casket if they say they want Mimic encounters. An elite reward casket has a 1/35 chance of being a mimic, while master reward caskets have a 1/15 chance. [ 1 ] There is a dry protection that guarantees your first Mimic encounter on either the 10th master reward casket or 25th elite reward casket, if you have Mimic encounters enabled.

When obtained, a message in the chatbox will state The chest turned out to be the Mimic! . Attempting to open the Mimic before defeating the Mimic boss gives the message "Visit the Strange Casket, upstairs in Watson's house in Hosidius, to attempt the Mimic's challenge.".

Once a player obtains the Mimic, they can return to the strange casket to challenge The Mimic . When the player defeats the Mimic, they must leave in order to open the mimic chest and receive their reward. If a player attempts to open the mimic chest while in the Mimic's fight area, the chatbox will state "It'd be bad taste to try opening that in here."

If a player tries to open another elite or master reward casket with a Mimic in the player's inventory, the chatbox will warn the player "You already have a Mimic, and cannot be given another one. Do you wish to open the casket anyway?" [ 2 ] However, if the Mimic is dropped on the ground, the player may obtain more Mimics. Just like clue scrolls, Mimics can be juggled , staying on the ground for an hour before despawning. As such the player may opt to juggle Mimics if opening a lot of caskets. Once done, the player can pick up all Mimics at once, since there is no restriction against carrying several Mimics.

The Mimic cannot be deposited into a bank. If players try to bank it, the chatbox will state "A magical force prevents you from banking this item!"

Watson teleport scrolls are consumable teleport scrolls that teleport the player to Watson's house in Hosidius. They are obtained by exchanging empty master scroll books with Watson. Each book given will reward the player with 10-20 scrolls.

There are no requirements to use this teleport. Notably, this teleport can be used without requiring the player to have visited Kourend before, unlike other teleports such as the Hosidius teleport or the games necklace teleport to the Wintertodt Camp.

Players use these scrolls to access Watson's home, where they can quickly turn in clue scrolls in exchange for a master clue scroll, or to reach The Mimic upstairs more quickly. They can also use them as a one-click stackable teleport to Hosidius in general.
23389:
Spiked manacles are a rare reward obtained from medium Treasure Trails . They are tied with aranea boots for the best-in-slot strength bonus for footwear that has no requirements to equip. It has equivalent strength bonus to dragon boots and aranea boots , all of which are only surpassed by primordial boots and the avernic treads , though without any of the defensive bonuses.

In comparison to climbing boots , which also have no Defence requirement to equip, Spiked manacles have +2 higher strength bonus. However, Spiked manacles have some negative bonuses whereas the Climbing boots have none, and Climbing boots also offer +2 Slash and +2 Crush melee defence bonuses. Aranea boots have slight Ranged and Magic attack bonuses, no negative defence bonuses, and 1 Prayer bonus, making them slightly better than spiked manacles.

The Giant easter egg is a cosmetic reward obtained from the 2019 Easter event , as well as subsequent Easter events. When wielded, players will be given a unique animation of them struggling to carry the egg. The egg has a unique Easter dance emote that can be used by right clicking on the item.

After the event, a hammer can be used on the giant easter egg to find the bunnyman mask . Holding the giant easter egg causes the Bunny Man to have different dialogue, which hints at the use of a hammer.

If the player attempts to use the easter egg in a PvP zone they will receive the message "Perhaps you should play with your egg somewhere safer."

If destroyed, a replacement can be obtained from Diango in Draynor Village or from the toy box of a costume room .
23448:
The bunnyman mask is an untradeable cosmetic item that is worn by the Bunny Man. During the 2019 Easter event, it was obtained by using a hammer on the giant easter egg; subsequent events simply reward the player with the mask.

If destroyed, a replacement can be obtained from Diango in Draynor Village or from the toy box of a costume room.
23450: Dried cocoa is an item used during the 2019 Easter event . It can be found by talking to the Travelling merchant and delivering him the crate of baskets . The crate of baskets can be found by talking to the Shop keeper in the Al Kharid general store. The dried cocoa is then given to the Easter Bunny .
23451: Hosidius milk is an item used during the 2019 Easter event . It is obtained by talking to the Lumbridge Cook and answering a riddle. The item is then given to the Easter Bunny .
23452: Special spices were used during the 2019 Easter event. They could be found by bringing Martin the Master Gardener some fine red silk. This was created by bringing fine silk and a tomato to Aggie, who would dye the silk red. The special spices could then be brought to the Easter Bunny to progress in the event.
23453: Crate of baskets is an item used during the 2019 Easter event. It can be found by talking to the Shop keeper in the Al Kharid General Store. The crate of baskets is requested by the Travelling merchant and can be exchanged with him for dried cocoa. The dried cocoa is then given to the Easter Bunny to progress in the event.
23454: Fine silk is an item used during the 2019 Easter event . It can be found by talking to Martin the Master Gardener in Draynor Village . The fine silk is then given to Aggie along with a tomato to create fine red silk . The red silk can then be exchanged with Martin for the special spices .
23455: Fine red silk is an item used during the 2019 Easter event. It can be found by bringing fine silk and a tomato to Aggie, who will dye the silk red. The red silk can then be brought back to Martin to receive the special spices.
23456: Chocolate mixture(u) is an item used during the 2019 Easter event . The mixture is given by the Easter bunny after bringing him the special spices , hosidius milk , and dried cocoa . The mixture needs to be brought to Party Pete in the Falador Party Room , because the Easter bunny's mixing machine has run out of fuel and he can not mix the mixture properly himself. Party Pete is able to turn the mixture into choco serum by dancing. The choco serum can then be brought back to the Easter bunny.
23457: Choco serum is an item used during the 2019 Easter event. The serum is needed by the Easter bunny to fuel his Easter machines. The serum is created by bringing the chocolate mixture(u) to Party Pete in Falador, who is able to mix the mixture by dancing.
23458: An enchanted lyre(i) is an enchanted lyre that contains infinite teleport charges to Rellekka . When the hard Fremennik Diary is completed, the lyre can also teleport to Waterbirth Island , and gains the ability to teleport to Jatizso and Neitiznot after completion of the elite Fremennik Diary .

The Archaic emblems are former discontinued items that could be obtained as a reward from Bounty Hunter. Originally, the Tier 1 and 10 Mysterious emblems received were tradeable and could be turned into banknotes. In 2019, Bounty Hunter was reworked; the Mysterious emblems were converted into Archaic emblems and made untradeable. Any player who had one in banknote form was given this unique discontinued variant; it was identical to the real Archaic emblems, except stackable.

In 2021, all Archaic emblems were removed from the game with the closure of the Bounty Hunter Reward Shop. While the normal versions can still be obtained during Deadman Mode, the stackable variants are now gone entirely.
23489:
This Wine of Zamorak is an unobtainable variant of the Wine of Zamorak that can be found in the Deep Wilderness Dungeon. Unlike the normal item, this version is scripted to respawn much faster than normal, and to give the wine in banknote form after the completion of the Wilderness Hard diary.

The item is unobtainable, as it cannot be picked up directly from the table. Casting Telekinetic grab on it will give the regular wine of Zamorak instead.
23490:
Larran's key is a key obtained from killing monsters while on a Slayer task given by Krystilia. It is used to open Larran's small and big chests.

The exact odds of receiving a key scales with the monster's Combat level. For levels 1-80, the probability follows a curve between 1/1972 at level 1 to 1/100 at level 80. For levels 81 or higher, the odds are between 1/99 and 1/50, scaling linearly and capping at level 350, as reflected in the equation below.

If it concerns a Slayer monster (meaning it requires a certain Slayer level to kill), the drop chance is increased by 20%. In addition, any monster killed within the Wilderness Slayer Cave has a further 15% increased chance to drop a key. Superior slayer monsters that spawn as part of Krystilia's tasks will always drop a key on death.

The probability P of obtaining a key when killing a monster with combat level L is given by:

P={1⌊310×(80−L)2⌋+100if L∈(0,80]1⌊−527×L⌋+115if L∈(80,350]150L∈(350,∞)

Larran's keys are always dropped on player death, even if there are fewer than 3 items kept on death. If killed by another player, keys are lost to the killer. If killed in PvM, the keys always go to your gravestone.
23495:
Sraracha is a pet dropped by Sarachnis, and is a much smaller version of the boss. Players can right click "Metamorphosis" to change its form, providing they have used an orange or blue egg sac to unlock its other coloured forms.

When a player receives the pet, it will automatically try to appear as their follower. At the same time, a message in the chatbox will state You have a funny feeling like you're being followed. However, if a player receives a pet while having a follower out (for example, a cat), it will be placed into their inventory. When this occurs, the message in the chatbox will instead state You feel something weird sneaking into your backpack.

If a player's inventory is full and they have a follower already, they will not receive the pet; it must instead be claimed from Probita in East Ardougne.

On death, if a player loses their pet (as a follower or in your inventory) it will wander around the area for 30 seconds before despawning. Even if the player returns in time, the pet cannot be picked up, and can be reclaimed from Probita.
23497:
The temple coin is an old coin that is obtained from Olbertus in the Forthos Dungeon , either by trading him five unnoted cut dragonstones or by attempting to kill him.

If players choose to kill him, he will transform into a level-186 Shaeded Beast , who will curse the Altar of the Sun and render it unusable until 200 eligible types of dragon bones are offered to the Sacred Bone Burner in the central chamber (see here ), which removes the curse and reverts it into a normal altar that restores prayer points.

However, if players choose to hand him the five unnoted cut dragonstones , then only 100 eligible types of dragon bones will be needed. Therefore this second option is recommended over fighting him.

The coin is used on the Stone Relief in the Crypt of the Moon in order to unlock the chamber containing the Sacred Bone Burner and Eodan . The Crypt of the Moon is located in the long northern room full of Undead Druids , immediately east of the entrance. After entering the central chamber through the Stone Relief, the coin is consumed, and the chamber is permanently unlocked. Inside the chamber, there is a lever which unlocks the gate on the south wall of the room, allowing easy travel between the red dragons and the chamber.

It is lost upon death, however it can be retrieved from Olbertus without having to fight him again or pay five dragonstones.
23499:
The grubby key is a key obtained from killing monsters within the Forthos Dungeon . It is used to open the Grubby Chest .

Brother Aimeri will give the player a key in exchange for spare pristine spider silks .
23502:
The temple key is a key obtained in the Forthos Dungeon that unlocks the eastern and western Temple Doors within the dungeon. The key only needs to be in the inventory when entering the gates for the first time, after which the doors will be permanently unlocked.

Obtaining the key requires offering a certain number of baby , lava , superior , or regular dragon bones on the sacred bone burner . To access the bone burner, the temple coin must be obtained from Olbertus , either by killing him or by bribing him with 5 dragonstones . This coin then needs to be used on the stone relief in the Crypt of the Moon.

If Olbertus is bribed with dragonstones, only 100 bones have to be offered on the burner, but if Olbertus is defeated instead, the number of bones to be offered is increased to 200. After access to the burner has been obtained, a lever can be pulled at the western side of the room, in order to unlock the gate to the south of the burner.

If lost, the key can be re-obtained from Brother Aimeri .

This key cannot be placed on the steel key ring .
23504:
The Tome of the Moon is a book obtained during the miniquest In Search of Knowledge by searching the north-eastern Temple Library bookshelves within the Forthos Dungeon . Initially empty, players must fill four Tattered moon pages that are received as drops from monsters within the dungeon.

The tome contains the teachings of Ranul , the god of the moon.

If lost, it can be reclaimed from the north-eastern bookshelves in the Temple Library, or from a bookcase within a player-owned house if the tome has been fully restored. Any pages that were previously filled before the book was lost will be present in the reclaimed book.
23506:
The tome of the Sun is a book obtained during the miniquest In Search of Knowledge by searching the south-eastern Temple Library bookshelves within the Forthos Dungeon . Initially empty, players must fill four Tattered sun pages that are received as drops from monsters within the dungeon.

The tome contains the teachings of Ralos , the god of the sun.

If lost, it can be reclaimed from the south-eastern bookshelves in the Temple Library, or from a bookcase within a player-owned house if the tome has been fully restored. Any pages that were previously filled before the book was lost will be present in the reclaimed book.
23508:
The tome of the Temple is a book obtained during the miniquest In Search of Knowledge by searching the south-western Temple Library bookshelves within the Forthos Dungeon . Initially empty, players must fill four Tattered temple pages that are received as drops from monsters within the dungeon.

The tome details the various features of the Forthos Dungeon, referred to in the tome as the Temple to Ranul/Ralos, and their original uses. The last page of the tome contains an entry by a follower of Ranul , whose followers have become corrupted and fanatical after meeting a dark wizard, who is either Xeric or one of his followers; it is purposely left open to interpretation.

If lost, it can be reclaimed from the south-western bookshelves in the Temple Library, or from a bookcase within a player-owned house if the tome has been fully restored. Any pages that were previously filled before the book was lost will be present in the reclaimed book.

This means opening a full giant egg sac results in a profit of 1,566 .

The red spiders' eggs are placed into your inventory as items ( not as notes ), and the giant egg sac (full) becomes the untradeable giant egg sac.

Once opened, the untradeable giant egg sac has a Remove-eggs option which will remove red spiders' eggs from the sac and place them in free inventory slots.

The Mask of Ranul is worn by the Undead Druids in the Forthos Dungeon and can be received from them as a drop.

If worn while inspecting the campfire at Shipwreck Cove, Chosen Aluinus will appear and give the message Hmm... Such potential. Such a waste.... He seems to go on a minute cooldown before appearing again.

Like most items obtained in the Forthos Dungeon , it can be used on Brother Aimeri for some additional dialogue.
23528:
Sarachnis cudgel is a one-handed crush weapon dropped by Sarachnis, requiring level 65 Attack to equip. The weapon appears to be made from several of Sarachnis' legs bound together by her webs.

The cudgel has slightly better crush and strength bonuses than Viggora's chainmace and slightly lower bonuses than the Leaf-bladed battleaxe, although with a faster attack speed than the latter. This makes it a good crush weapon which does not degrade or require a charge.

23567:
A super restore is a potion found in the Last Man Standing minigame that restores all player stats that have been lowered, including Prayer , but not including Hitpoints .

The restore value obtained per dose is 8 + 25% of the player's base level (round down) in each of the affected skills . For example, a player with 84 Thieving and 63 Smithing would restore both 29 points of Thieving and 23 points of Smithing for each dose consumed. The maximum amount of points that can be restored with this potion is 32 at level 96. This means that a super restore potion will restore 1 more Prayer point per dose than a prayer potion . Unlike normal super restores , these lack an "Empty" option.

23575:
A Saradomin brew is a potion found in the Last Man Standing minigame .

Each dose of a Saradomin brew temporarily raises Hitpoints by 15% + 2 and Defence by 20% + 2, both rounded down, and can boost a player's Hitpoints above their maximum Hitpoints level by up to the amount healed. It also temporarily lowers Strength , Attack , Magic and Ranged by 10% + 2. Players typically use super restore potions along with Saradomin brews to offset their stat reduction effect, as one dose of super restore is enough to restore lost stats from three doses of Saradomin brew, or up to four doses of brew if the player's stats were boosted beforehand (as with a super combat potion ). Unlike normal Saradomin brews , these lack an "Empty" option.

Dharok's platelegs from Last Man Standing is a minigame-exclusive variant of the normal Dharok's platelegs. It can be obtained (along with the rest of the set) from opening the chests with a bloody key or bloodier key, or looting the crates that spawn at random locations on the map. It can be looted from other players as it always drops on death.

As it is part of Dharok's barrows set, if Dharok's platelegs is worn along with all of the other pieces of equipment in Dharok's barrows set, the player gains a special effect. Attacks do more damage as the player's hitpoints decrease, up to 98.9% bonus damage with 1 hitpoint remaining with 99 max.

In the minigame, the set is highly valued as it can deliver devastating damage to unsuspecting opponents not using Protect from Melee. However, it requires players to stay at low health, making it risky to use effectively. It also makes players vulnerable to magical attacks, since the full set is required for the effect and it provides negative magical defence.

For more details on the mechanics and strategies for this equipment, see the set page.

Enchanted diamond bolts from Last Man Standing are a minigame-exclusive variant of the normal Enchanted diamond bolts . 5,000 of them are available as part of the starting loadout.

Enchanted diamond bolts have a 10% chance of triggering the Armour Piercing effect. This increases the max hit (and thus damage) by 15% and ignores your opponent's Defence and your own accuracy for the hit it activates on. [ 1 ] [ 2 ] [ 3 ] [ 4 ] Not only is your range accuracy ignored when the spec activates, so is your range level, so if your stats are reduced (e.g. by brewing down), you will still roll with guaranteed accuracy and 0-115% of your usual max hit. [ 5 ] A twinkling sound can be heard when this activates.

If the player has completed the hard Kandarin Diary , there is a 10% increase of the likelihood that the special effect of an enchanted bolt will occur, giving enchanted diamond bolts an overall 11% chance of the special effect activating. [ 6 ] This effect is active in Last Man Standing . [ 7 ]

23659:
Crystal saplings are used to grow crystal trees , with 74 Farming .

They can be made by planting a crystal acorn in a filled plant pot , with a gardening trowel in your inventory, and then watering the crystal seedling with a watering can or by using Humidify . When watered, the seedling will sprout into a sapling in one crop cycle (0-5 minutes).

Planting the sapling in the crystal tree patch in the Crwys district in north-east Prifddinas , with a spade in your inventory, will give 180 Farming experience. It will grow into a crystal tree after 480 minutes (8 hours), which gives 13,240 Farming experience.

The crystal tree cannot become diseased .

Players should use ultracompost to increase the crystal shard yield from 16-20 to 28-32 when the tree is cut down.
23661:
Crystal acorns are seeds used in the Farming skill. At level 74 Farming , crystal acorns may be planted in plant pots with a gardening trowel and watered to become crystal saplings . They can be obtained as a reward from the Elven Crystal Chest , by catching crystal implings or from trading crystal weapon , armour , and tool seeds to Pennant in Prifddinas . Pennant exchanges one acorn in return for any one seed, except for Enhanced crystal teleport seed .

After planting the sapling in the crystal tree patch found in Prifddinas and waiting for it to fully grow, which takes about eight hours, the plant will grow into a crystal tree which can be cut to yield crystal shards . Planting the crystal sapling yields 126 experience, and checking its health gives 13,240 experience. Crystal trees cannot become diseased.

Harvesting crystal trees grants 28-32 crystal shards if ultracompost is used. Other types of compost will yield fewer shards, down to 16-20 with no compost. Magic secateurs have no effect. [ 1 ] Players can also receive bird nests after chopping the tree down.

One acorn can be used on the skilling pet Tangleroot to change its appearance.
23667:
The dragonstone armour set is an item obtained by exchanging a set of items with a Grand Exchange clerk via their right-click "Sets" option and clicking on the appropriate item set within the Item Sets interface.

23670: Iwan's flyer is an item obtained from The Gauntlet when dying after dealing minimal damage. The flyer advertises the shop Iwan's Maces , run by Iwan in northern Prifddinas . Using the item on Iwan has no effect; it has no use whatsoever.
23673:
The crystal axe is an item used in Woodcutting . It requires level 71 Woodcutting and Song of the Elves to create and use, with 50 Agility and 70 Attack required to wield it. It possesses the same special attack as the dragon axe , and gives the player a 15% increase in efficiency chopping logs over the rune axe , surpassing the 10% increase of the dragon axe. This makes the crystal axe approximately 4.5% faster than the dragon axe.

Players can create a crystal axe via a singing bowl by combining a dragon axe, 120 crystal shards and a crystal tool seed . Doing so requires level 76 Smithing [ boostable ] and 76 Crafting [ boostable ] to sing the crystal, and grants 6,000 experience in both skills. Players can configure the charges while the axe is in their bank by right-clicking on Configure-Charges, as long as players have the required materials. If the player does not meet the Smithing and Crafting requirements, they can have Conwenna or Reese sing the crystal for them for an extra 60 crystal shards, for a total of 180.

After creation, the player can revert the crystal axe into a dragon axe. This process returns the crystal tool seed and the dragon axe to the player, but all crystal shards used to create or charge the axe are lost.

A dangerous death in PvP causes the crystal axe to revert to a dragon axe, which will then be dropped for the killer. All crystal shards will be lost should this happen.

A charged crystal pickaxe provides a chance to mine an ore every three ticks (with an additional 1/4 chance to reduce this to two ticks); excluding waiting for ores to respawn or having to move to a new resource, the crystal pickaxe is effectively a 3.03% increase in overall mining speed compared to a dragon pickaxe or 9.09% compared to a rune pickaxe . An uncharged crystal pickaxe has the same mining capabilities as a dragon pickaxe.

Players can create a crystal pickaxe via a singing bowl by combining a dragon pickaxe , 120 crystal shards , and a crystal tool seed . Doing so requires level 76 Smithing and Crafting to sing the crystal (the levels can be boosted ), and grants 6,000 experience in both skills. Players can configure the charges while the pickaxe is in their bank by right-clicking on Configure-Charges, as long as players have the required materials. If the player does not meet the Smithing and Crafting requirements, they can have Conwenna or Reese sing the crystal for them for an extra 60 crystal shards, for a total of 180.

A dangerous death in PvP causes the crystal pickaxe to revert to a dragon pickaxe, which will then be dropped for the killer. All crystal shards will be lost should this happen.

The divine super combat potion is a stat-boosting potion that increases the player's Attack, Strength, and Defence level by 5 + 15% for 5 minutes. During these 5 minutes, the player's Attack, Strength, and Defence levels will not drain below the maximum boost of the potion. Although natural stat drain is disabled, a player's stats can still be decreased or increased by the use of other spells and potions.

Once the 5 minutes are over, any stats normally boosted by the potion will be reduced back to their base level; Preserve does not affect the duration of the potion. Drinking this potion will also damage the player by 10 Hitpoints. Trying to drink the potion with 10 Hitpoints or less will instead prompt the message: You need more than 10 hitpoints to survive the power of a divine potion.

Players are unable to cast Boost Potion Share to share the effect across a group of players.

It is created by using crystal dust on a super combat potion, requiring 97 Herblore.

Mixing divine super combat potions yields 0.5 experience per dose.

23757:
The Youngllef is a pet received from the reward chest in the Gauntlet. It is a smaller version of the Crystalline Hunllef. Upon completion of the Corrupted Gauntlet, players unlock the right click "Metamorphosis" option to change between the regular Youngllef and the corrupted Youngllef variant. The pet will always be received in the regular form, even if it is obtained from the Corrupted Gauntlet.

When a player receives the pet, it will automatically try to appear as their follower. At the same time, a message in the chatbox will state You have a funny feeling like you're being followed. However, if a player receives a pet while having a follower out (for example, a cat), it will be placed into their inventory. When this occurs, the message in the chatbox will instead state You feel something weird sneaking into your backpack.

If a player's inventory is full and they have a follower already, they will not receive the pet; it must instead be claimed from Probita in East Ardougne.

On death, if a player loses their pet (as a follower or in your inventory) it will wander around the area for 30 seconds before despawning. The pet cannot be picked up and instead must be reclaimed from Probita.

23762:
The crystal harpoon is an untradeable harpoon created via crystal singing after finishing Song of the Elves . It requires 71 Fishing , 70 Attack , and 50 Agility to wield and degrades during use like other crystal equipment . It can be stored in a tackle box .

While fishing, the charged harpoon provides a 35% increased catch rate over the regular harpoon (a 12.5% increase compared with the dragon harpoon ) , the highest for all harpoons. This effect only works on fish that utilise the harpoon (sharks etc). Whilst fighting Tempoross , an additional effect transforms 1/3 of caught fish into crystallised harpoonfish , which grant 20% more Fishing experience when used as ammunition. The crystal harpoon only provides a 10% increased catch chance at Tempoross, rather than 35%.

Players can create a crystal harpoon via a singing bowl by combining a dragon harpoon, 120 crystal shards , and a crystal tool seed . Singing the crystal requires 76 Smithing and 76 Crafting , which can be boosted , and grants 6,000 experience in both skills. Players may bypass the skill requirements by having Conwenna or Reese sing the crystal for an additional 60 crystal shards, bringing the total to 180.

The harpoon is created with 10,000 charges and a charge is consumed for every fish caught. Crystal shards can be used to recharge the harpoon, each providing 100 charges up to a maximum of 20,000. Players can configure the charges while the harpoon is in their bank by right-clicking on Configure-Charges, as long as players have the required materials.

A dangerous death in PvP causes the crystal harpoon to revert to a dragon harpoon, which will then be dropped for the killer. All crystal shards will be lost should this happen.

The crystal harpoon is an untradeable harpoon created via crystal singing after finishing Song of the Elves . It requires 71 Fishing , 70 Attack , and 50 Agility to wield and degrades during use like other crystal equipment . It can be stored in a tackle box .

While fishing, the charged harpoon provides a 35% increased catch rate over the regular harpoon (a 12.5% increase compared with the dragon harpoon ) , the highest for all harpoons. This effect only works on fish that utilise the harpoon (sharks etc). Whilst fighting Tempoross , an additional effect transforms 1/3 of caught fish into crystallised harpoonfish , which grant 20% more Fishing experience when used as ammunition. The crystal harpoon only provides a 10% increased catch chance at Tempoross, rather than 35%.

Players can create a crystal harpoon via a singing bowl by combining a dragon harpoon, 120 crystal shards , and a crystal tool seed . Singing the crystal requires 76 Smithing and 76 Crafting , which can be boosted , and grants 6,000 experience in both skills. Players may bypass the skill requirements by having Conwenna or Reese sing the crystal for an additional 60 crystal shards, bringing the total to 180.

The harpoon is created with 10,000 charges and a charge is consumed for every fish caught. Crystal shards can be used to recharge the harpoon, each providing 100 charges up to a maximum of 20,000. Players can configure the charges while the harpoon is in their bank by right-clicking on Configure-Charges, as long as players have the required materials.

A dangerous death in PvP causes the crystal harpoon to revert to a dragon harpoon, which will then be dropped for the killer. All crystal shards will be lost should this happen.

The Ardougne knight helm is a quest item used in Song of the Elves . It is made by using red dye on a steel full helm to emulate the equipment of a Knight of Ardougne . It has no Defence requirement to wear, and has identical stats to an iron full helm .

This item can be stored in the armour case of a costume room , as part of the Ardougne knight armour set. Ultimate Ironmen will be unable to retrieve individual pieces until the full set is stored.

The Ardougne knight platebody is a quest item from Song of the Elves . An Ardougne knight tabard is obtained by Alrena for a purple dye and some silk , which is then combined with a steel platebody to obtain this item.

If the Ardougne knight tabard or platebody is lost, Alrena will give out a new tabard for free.

The defensive bonuses of this item are equivalent to those of an iron platebody , despite the item requiring a steel platebody to create. However, it can be equipped even at level 1 Defence .

This item can be stored in the armour case of a costume room , as part of the Ardougne knight armour set. Ultimate Ironmen will be unable to retrieve individual pieces until the full set is stored.

The Ardougne knight platelegs is a piece of equipment used in Song of the Elves . It shares the same bonuses as iron platelegs . It is impossible to obtain for players with the required Defence level to wear steel platelegs , even if deboosting Defence level.

This item can be stored in the armour case of a costume room , as part of the Ardougne knight armour set. Ultimate Ironmen will be unable to retrieve individual pieces until the full set is stored. If lost, a pair of steel platelegs can be used instead to store in the armour case.

The staff has a max hit of 31, regardless of level. [ 1 ]
23900:
A perfected crystal staff is a powered staff that can be created in the Gauntlet from an attuned crystal staff and a crystal orb .

In total, a player will require 50 crystal shards , a weapon frame , and a crystal orb to create the perfected crystal staff.

The staff has a max hit of 39, regardless of level. [ 1 ] This is increased to 40 by the Mystic Vigour and Augury prayers.
23901: A basic crystal bow is a weapon that can be created in the Gauntlet , made from a weapon frame . It can be upgraded into an attuned crystal bow by using 50 crystal shards.
23902: An attuned crystal bow is a weapon that can be created in the Gauntlet , made from 50 crystal shards and a basic crystal bow . It can be upgraded into a perfected crystal bow by using a crystalline bowstring .
23903:
A perfected crystal bow is a weapon that can be created in the Gauntlet, made from an attuned crystal bow and a crystalline bowstring.

In total, a player will require 50 crystal shards, a weapon frame, and a crystalline bowstring to create the perfected crystal bow.
23904:
Teleport crystal is a single-use item received when starting the Gauntlet. It teleports players back to the starting room.

Additional crystals can be created with 50 crystal shards.
23905:
Tephra are fragmental materials mined from rock formations within Zalcano 's prison beneath Prifddinas , granting 35 Mining experience per tephra mined. Rock formations that are glowing will yield tephra at a much faster rate. The Varrock armour 's double ore mining effect works here as well. Both the celestial ring and celestial signet (when charged) can give multiple tephra per mining action. As with all other suitable ore, a charge will be lost from the ring whether or not additional tephra is mined.

These are refined in the furnace to the east to create refined tephra , then imbued at the altar to create imbued tephra , which is used to deal damage to Zalcano's stone armour.

There is a 1/65 chance that 1-3 crystal shards will be obtained while mining tephra.

Casting Superheat Item does not work. The Infernal pickaxe does not work on tephra.
23906: Refined tephra is obtained by using tephra mined within Zalcano 's prison on the furnace in the east, granting 10 Smithing experience per refined tephra. Players must then imbue them at the altar to create imbued tephra , which is used to deal damage to Zalcano's stone armour.
23907:
Imbued tephra is obtained by imbuing refined tephra at the Seren altar in the western end of Zalcano 's prison. It can also be obtained from golems that Zalcano occasionally summons.

The imbued tephra is the only item that can deal damage to Zalcano while she is still standing; the damage dealt is scaled based on the player's Smithing and Runecraft levels. In addition, if she has summoned demonic symbols around the prison, the blue symbols will increase the damage dealt. Players can either attack Zalcano directly while having the imbued tephra in their inventory to use them, or equip and throw them at her.
23908:
The Zalcano shard is an item dropped by Zalcano. It can be used on the dragon pickaxe to create the dragon pickaxe (or), which alters its appearance. It is solely a cosmetic upgrade and does not change the stats.

The shard is the second cosmetic add-on for the dragon pickaxe, after the dragon pickaxe upgrade kit. However, unlike the upgrade kit, it will not be destroyed should players revert the dragon pickaxe to its regular appearance.
23911:
The crystal crown is a purely cosmetic crown purchasable from the Lliann's Wares in Prifddinas's Ithell district for 250,000,000 coins. The crown is untradeable, and it cannot be alchemised or sold back to Lliann's shop.

It should be noted that Lliann's Wares initially carries three crowns in stock. Each crown in stock is set to resupply after as many game ticks as it costs (250 million), which can take several years. However, like all other shops, the stock refreshes back to three crowns after server restarts, such as maintenance or game updates. Due to the low number of players wishing to buy crystal crowns, the restock time should not be a concern.

The crown’s colours, based on that of the Ithell Clan, may be changed to other colours of the Elven Clans. The crystals needed to do so can be bought from the same store for 500,000 coins each. It can also be reverted to the Ithell Clan's colour by using the crystal of Ithell on any variant of the crystal crown.
23913:

23943:
The elven signet is a unique ring obtainable only from crystal implings. When worn, it offers a 10% chance to not use a charge when using crystal equipment, excluding the blade of Saeldor and the bow of Faerdhinen.

The signet can be combined with a celestial ring at a singing bowl, alongside 100 crystal shards and 1,000 stardust, to create the celestial signet, which combines the effects of both. Doing so requires level 70 Smithing and Crafting; if the player does not meet the Smithing and Crafting requirements, they can have Conwenna or Reese sing the crystal for them for an extra 50 crystal shards, for a total of 150.
23946:
The eternal teleport crystal is an item that can be used to teleport to Lletya and Prifddinas, in a similar fashion to the teleport crystal, but with infinite charges. You cannot obtain it before completing Song of the Elves.

Players can create an eternal teleport crystal via a singing bowl by combining an enhanced crystal teleport seed and 100 crystal shards. Doing so requires level 80 Smithing and Crafting to sing the crystal (the levels can be boosted), and grants 5,000 experience in both skills. If the player does not meet the Smithing and Crafting requirements, they can have Conwenna or Reese sing the crystal for them for an extra 50 crystal shards, for a total of 150, you are also not granted the experience if made for you.
23948:
Elven dawn is a type of ale that restores 1 Hitpoint and temporarily boosts Agility by 1 while draining Strength by 1.

It is purchasable at the Hefin Inn in Prifddinas. Unlike other ales, it cannot be created through brewing.
23951:
The enhanced crystal key is an upgraded version of the regular crystal key that is used to open the Elven Crystal Chest in the upper level of the Tower of Voices in Prifddinas.

Players can create an enhanced crystal key via a singing bowl by combining a crystal key and 10 crystal shards. Doing so requires level 80 Smithing and Crafting to sing the crystal (the levels can be boosted), and grants 500 experience in both skills. If the player does not meet the Smithing and Crafting requirements, they can have Conwenna or Reese sing the crystal for them for an extra 5 crystal shards, for a total of 15.

The rewards from the Elven Crystal Chest include one uncut dragonstone and various other items that are generally worth more than the rewards from the regular crystal chest in Taverley.

The average drop value of the chest is 51,133. Additionally, an average of ~3.77 crystal shards and a low amount of crystal acorns is expected.

If the player manually buys the required crystal shards, each shard will cost 21,612.59 them through the cheapest option, purchasing Enhanced crystal teleport seeds on the Grand Exchange and selling the seeds to Amrod, and the expected loss from opening the chest would be −103,452.77. If growing the received crystal acorns from the chest into crystal trees with ultracompost, the expected loss is −14,872.07 instead.
23953:
The crystal tool seed is an elven crystal that can be turned into the crystal axe , crystal harpoon , or crystal pickaxe , using 120 crystal shards and the dragon counterpart on a singing bowl . It can be obtained as a drop from Zalcano .

The crystal tools start off at 10,000 charges and degrades, like other crystal equipment . One charge is depleted for each time an item is obtained using the tool, with some exceptions for particular uses of the axe and pickaxe where the crystal version has no additional benefit (duplicates from items such as the Varrock armour do not deplete an extra charge). The player may add charges with crystal shards , with each shard granting 100 charges, up to a maximum of 20,000 charges. Dismantling a crystal tool will return the dragon equivalent and crystal tool seed to the player and doing so will lose all crystal shard charges that were previously loaded.

Players can also exchange the tool seed for 100 crystal shards by speaking to Amrod in Prifddinas ' Hefin Inn .

A dangerous death in PvP causes the crystal tools to revert to their dragon equivalents which will then be dropped for the killer. All crystal shards will be lost as well.
23956:
The crystal armour seed is an elven crystal that can be turned into crystal armour at a singing bowl . Completing the Gauntlet will yield a chance of gaining these seeds and combining them with crystal shards can be used to create the armour pieces.

Players can also exchange the armour seed for 250 crystal shards by speaking to Amrod in Prifddinas ' Hefin Inn . The seed can additionally be traded to Pennant in Prifddinas for one crystal acorn .
23959:
The enhanced crystal teleport seed is a crystal seed that can be used with 100 crystal shards at a singing bowl to create an eternal teleport crystal—which functions as a teleport crystal with unlimited teleport charges.

If the player does not meet the 80 Smithing and 80 Crafting requirements, they can have Conwenna or Reese sing the crystal for them for an extra 50 crystal shards, for a total of 150.

Players can also exchange the enhanced crystal teleport seed for 150 crystal shards by speaking to Amrod in Prifddinas' Hefin Inn. They must be unnoted.

Note: The effect of the rogue equipment does apply to this item; the player will have a chance to receive two enhanced seeds if they are wearing parts of the outfit, with it guaranteed if the full set is worn.
23962:
Crystal shards are items that can be obtained through participating in various activities within Prifddinas , or obtained during sailing using the crystal extractor .

These are necessary to create and charge various crystal equipment through crystal singing , can be used to create enhanced crystal keys for the Elven Crystal Chest , and can be crushed into crystal dust which is used to make divine potions . Each crystal shard added onto a piece of crystal equipment provides 100 charges, up to a maximum of 20,000.
23964:
Crystal dust is a Herblore tertiary ingredient used for creating divine potions. Divine potions provide the same level of stat boosts as the base potion they are made from, but stay boosted to their maximum for 5 minutes instead of the boost reducing by one level per minute as normal potions do.

Crystal dust can be made by using a pestle and mortar on crystal shards, to create 10 dust per shard. One dust is used per dose (similar to amylase crystals in stamina potions); therefore, a single shard provides enough dust to create two and a half full divine potions.
23971:
A crystal helm is a piece of crystal armour requiring level 70 Defence and 50 Agility to equip. When equipped, a 2.5% damage bonus and 5% accuracy bonus is applied when using the crystal bow or Bow of Faerdhinen . This bonus stacks additively with the crystal legs and crystal body 's bonuses, for a total of 15% damage and 30% accuracy.

Players can create a crystal helm via a singing bowl by combining 50 crystal shards and a crystal armour seed . Doing so requires level 70 Smithing and Crafting to sing the crystal (the levels can be boosted ), and grants 2,500 experience in both skills. Players can configure the charges while the helm is in their bank by right-clicking on Configure-Charges, as long as players have the required materials. If the player does not meet the Smithing and Crafting requirements, they can have Conwenna or Reese sing the crystal for them for an extra 60 crystal shards, for a total of 110.

The helm's colours may also be changed to other colours of the Elven Clans by buying crystals from Lliann's Wares in Prifddinas , which cost 500,000 coins each. It can also be reverted to its original colour by using the crystal of Meilyr on any variant of the helm.

If lost to another player in a dangerous PVP death, the crystal helm will revert to a crystal armour seed, which will then be dropped for the killer. All crystal shards will be lost should this happen. If the crystal helm is protected on death, the helmet will be kept, and will not lose any charges- similar to a blowpipe or trident.

Players can configure the charges while the crystal body is in their bank by right-clicking on Configure-Charges, as long as players have the required materials. If the player does not meet the Smithing and Crafting requirements, they can have Conwenna or Reese sing the crystal for them for an extra 60 crystal shards, for a total of 210.

The body's colours may also be changed to other colours of the Elven Clans by buying crystals from Lliann's Wares in Prifddinas , which cost 500,000 coins each. It can also be reverted to its original colour by using the crystal of Meilyr on any variant of the body.

If lost to another player in a dangerous PVP death, the crystal body will revert to 3 crystal armour seeds, which will then be dropped for the killer. All crystal shards will be lost should this happen. If the crystal body is protected on death, the body will be kept, and will not lose any charges- similar to a blowpipe or trident.

When combined with an imbued slayer helmet , the damage bonus from crystal armour pieces is multiplied by the 15% ranged damage boost from the helmet. Assuming players are wearing both the crystal body and legs, this results in a damage bonus of approximately 29.375%.

23983:
The crystal bow is a powerful degradable bow available after a player completes the Roving Elves quest, and a possible reward from this quest along with the crystal shield . The crystal bow may be made from enchanted elven crystals . To wield the crystal bow, a player must have 70 Ranged , 50 Agility and have completed the Roving Elves quest. The crystal bow benefits from damage and accuracy boosts when crystal armour is equipped.

A crystal bow is created when an elf sings to a crystal weapon seed and enchants it into a bow. The most prominent elf with this talent is Ilfeen , who will perform this service for players for a price. However, she can only do this with a weapon seed; partially charged bows should be reverted to their seed form (using the right-click menu in the inventory) to be converted back into a bow.

Because it is blessed by the elven goddess Seren , the crystal bow does not require any arrows to use, as it generates its own when fired. The bow's fired shots are coated in a green aura, similar to Craw's bow , and rolls damage against an NPC's standard ranged defence.

The crystal bow can be considered the penultimate bow in the composite bow family, before the bow of Faerdhinen . It shares the same 10-square attack range on any style as well as a 4-tick attack speed on rapid, placing it between popular ranged weapons like the shortbow (3-tick) and crossbow (5-tick).

The crystal bow is required to complete the Hard Western Provinces Diary . It is also used for two master clue steps: an emote step and as a possible item to show Falo the Bard .

23987:
The crystal halberd is a degradable two-handed polearm made from a crystal weapon seed . It requires completion of the Hard Western Provinces Diary to wield, as well as 70 Attack , 35 Strength and 50 Agility .

In order to obtain a crystal halberd (with 2,500 charges), one must talk to Islwyn who will offer to sell a crystal halberd for 750,000 coins. Alternatively, one can take a crystal weapon seed to Ilfeen to be recharged into a crystal halberd with 2,500 charges starting at a price of 750,000 coins, lowering by 150,000 each time afterwards, eventually reaching a recharge price of 150,000 coins.

With access to Prifddinas and completion of the Hard Western Provinces Diary , the singing bowl can be used with 78 Crafting and Smithing and 40 crystal shards to turn a crystal weapon seed into a crystal halberd. Players without the stat requirements can speak to Conwenna or Reese and have them create the crystal halberd for you for 20 additional crystal shards.

The crystal halberd is significantly more powerful than a dragon halberd , making it a good choice as a melee safespot weapon.

The crystal halberd can deal full damage to the Corporeal Beast , despite not being a spear, but it must be on the stab attack style.

The crystal shield is a powerful degradable shield available after a player completes the Roving Elves quest, and a possible reward from this quest along with the Crystal bow . The crystal shield may be made from enchanted elven crystals . To wield the crystal shield, a player must have 70 Defence , 50 Agility , and have completed the Roving Elves quest.

It can be made by combining 40 crystal shards with one crystal weapon seed at a singing bowl in Prifddinas . It can be considered similar to Barrows equipment due to its substantial power and expensive repair costs. The blade of Saeldor is a one-handed slash sword that once belonged to Saeldor, an elite elven warrior, that can be created from an enhanced crystal weapon seed. Requiring level 80 Attack to wield, it provides the highest slash bonus out of any one-handed weapon for its attack speed, and is tied with the two-handed Saradomin's blessed sword for highest slash bonus of any weapon for its speed (although using any sort of defender makes the blade a superior choice). It is considered the best one-handed slash weapon in the game and one of the strongest one-handed melee weapons, along with the Ghrazi rapier and the Inquisitor's mace; though these weapons are weaker than Osmumten's fang against high-defence, stab-susceptible monsters.

On unprotected death in PvP, the inactive blade is dropped, and all shards used to charge it will be lost. In PvM on the other hand, all current charges will be kept upon death.

24049:
Crazed scribbles , or The Diary of Randas , is a book written by Randas , found in the Grand Library in Prifddinas .

Prior to obtaining it from the Grand Library, it can only be read by talking to Koftik at the bridge at the beginning of the Underground Pass during the Underground Pass quest.

If lost, it can be reclaimed from any bookshelf in the Grand Library, or from a bookcase within a player-owned house .
24051:
A Dear Friend is a book found in the Grand Library in Prifddinas, which requires completion of Song of the Elves to access.

The book is written before the First Age prior to the elves' arrival on Gielinor from their homeworld Tarddiad. It describes the experiences of Caron and his wife's encounter with a Hunllef cub, the elves' natural predator, on Tarddiad.

If lost, it can be reclaimed from any bookshelf in the Grand Library, or from a bookcase within a player-owned house.
24053:
On Leprechauns is a book found in the Grand Library in Prifddinas , which requires completion of Song of the Elves to access.

The short book describes a possible sinister side to the Tool Leprechauns that hold a player's farming tools.

If lost, it can be reclaimed from any bookshelf in the Grand Library, or from a bookcase within a player-owned house .
24055:
The bloody diary is a book found in the Grand Library in Prifddinas, which requires completion of Song of the Elves to access.

The diary was written during the War of the Five Houses 200 years ago by an unnamed adventurer from Hosidius. However, most of the pages have been stained in blood and cannot be read by the player.

The few entries that remain unstained describes the adventurer's return to Great Kourend after the war, some of his adventures in Varlamore, as well as nearly discovering how to create Arclight.

If lost, it can be reclaimed from any bookshelf in the Grand Library, or from a bookcase within a player-owned house.
24057:
The Eight Clans is a hymn found in the Grand Library in Prifddinas, which requires completion of Song of the Elves to access.

The hymn sings of the eight Elven Clans and their specialties.

If lost, it can be reclaimed from any bookshelf in the Grand Library, or from a bookcase within a player-owned house.
24059:
Gollwyn's final statement is a book found in the Grand Library in Prifddinas , which requires completion of Song of the Elves to access.

The book is written by Gollwyn , Arianwyn 's father, and describes his experiences during the battle between Lord Iorwerth 's forces and Baxtorian 's soldiers during The Great Divide.

If lost, it can be reclaimed from any bookshelf in the Grand Library, or from a bookcase within a player-owned house .
24061:
Niff & Harry is a poem found in the Grand Library in Prifddinas , which requires completion of Song of the Elves to access.

The poem describes an encounter between Niff Delfingus, a nurse who was said to be able to cure any illness, and a human named Sir Harry the Hero. It is not known whether the Harry referred to in the poem is the same Sir Harry encountered in the Underground Pass .

If lost, it can be reclaimed from any bookshelf in the Grand Library, or from a bookcase within a player-owned house .
24063:
Soggy journal is a book found in the Grand Library in Prifddinas, which requires completion of Song of the Elves to access.

The journal is written by a pirate named Blunderguts, and describes his experiences sailing from Port Sarim to the Western Ocean.

If lost, it can be reclaimed from any bookshelf in the Grand Library, or from a bookcase within a player-owned house.
24065:

If lost, it can be reclaimed from any bookshelf in the Grand Library, or from a bookcase within a player-owned house .
24067:

If lost, it can be reclaimed from any bookshelf in the Grand Library, or from a bookcase within a player-owned house .
24069:
The Truth Behind the Myth (excerpt) is a book found in the Grand Library in Prifddinas, which requires completion of Song of the Elves to access.

The excerpt written is from a book about Camorra Shayzien, a famous heroine during the Fourth Age, and ponders about why her slaying of Garak was considered a more impressive feat than her heroic acts with Robert the Strong during the Dragonkin Conflicts.

If lost, it can be reclaimed from any bookshelf in the Grand Library, or from a bookcase within a player-owned house.

The book contains three short tales surrounding Mynydd, the mountain that towers over the village of Gwenith.

If lost, it can be reclaimed from any bookshelf in the Grand Library, or from a bookcase within a player-owned house.
24123:
The crystal bow is a powerful degradable bow available after a player completes the Roving Elves quest, and a possible reward from this quest along with the crystal shield . The crystal bow may be made from enchanted elven crystals . To wield the crystal bow, a player must have 70 Ranged , 50 Agility and have completed the Roving Elves quest. The crystal bow benefits from damage and accuracy boosts when crystal armour is equipped.

A crystal bow is created when an elf sings to a crystal weapon seed and enchants it into a bow. The most prominent elf with this talent is Ilfeen , who will perform this service for players for a price. However, she can only do this with a weapon seed; partially charged bows should be reverted to their seed form (using the right-click menu in the inventory) to be converted back into a bow.

Because it is blessed by the elven goddess Seren , the crystal bow does not require any arrows to use, as it generates its own when fired. The bow's fired shots are coated in a green aura, similar to Craw's bow , and rolls damage against an NPC's standard ranged defence.

The crystal bow can be considered the penultimate bow in the composite bow family, before the bow of Faerdhinen . It shares the same 10-square attack range on any style as well as a 4-tick attack speed on rapid, placing it between popular ranged weapons like the shortbow (3-tick) and crossbow (5-tick).

The crystal bow is required to complete the Hard Western Provinces Diary . It is also used for two master clue steps: an emote step and as a possible item to show Falo the Bard .
24125:
The crystal halberd is a degradable two-handed polearm made from a crystal weapon seed . It requires completion of the Hard Western Provinces Diary to wield, as well as 70 Attack , 35 Strength and 50 Agility .

In order to obtain a crystal halberd (with 2,500 charges), one must talk to Islwyn who will offer to sell a crystal halberd for 750,000 coins. Alternatively, one can take a crystal weapon seed to Ilfeen to be recharged into a crystal halberd with 2,500 charges starting at a price of 750,000 coins, lowering by 150,000 each time afterwards, eventually reaching a recharge price of 150,000 coins.

With access to Prifddinas and completion of the Hard Western Provinces Diary , the singing bowl can be used with 78 Crafting and Smithing and 40 crystal shards to turn a crystal weapon seed into a crystal halberd. Players without the stat requirements can speak to Conwenna or Reese and have them create the crystal halberd for you for 20 additional crystal shards.

The crystal halberd is significantly more powerful than a dragon halberd , making it a good choice as a melee safespot weapon.

The crystal halberd can deal full damage to the Corporeal Beast , despite not being a spear, but it must be on the stab attack style.
24127:
The crystal shield is a powerful degradable shield available after a player completes the Roving Elves quest, and a possible reward from this quest along with the Crystal bow . The crystal shield may be made from enchanted elven crystals . To wield the crystal shield, a player must have 70 Defence , 50 Agility , and have completed the Roving Elves quest.

It can be made by combining 40 crystal shards with one crystal weapon seed at a singing bowl in Prifddinas . Alternatively, the crystal shield can be purchased from Islwyn for 750,000 coins even if the player chose the crystal bow as their initial quest reward for completing Roving Elves. It can be considered similar to Barrows equipment due to its substantial power and expensive repair costs. The crystal shield's melee defence bonuses are comparable to those of a dragon square shield . However, its ranged defence bonus is the highest of any one-handed shield.
24130: The combat path starter kit is an item obtained from Adventurer Jon for free after starting the combat path of the Adventure Paths. It contains an assortment of combat-related items.
24131: Combat path voucher is an item obtained from Adventurer Jon by completing tasks in the Adventure Paths' Combat Path. It can be used to claim rewards from various NPCs in Varrock. Players can read the voucher to see a list of items they can still claim. Upon claiming the last reward, that NPC will take the voucher from the player.
24132:
The Marble lectern is an interface item that can be seen in the Construction skill guide representing the Marble lectern .

The actual item cannot be obtained by players.
24133:
The infernal max cape is the result of combining an infernal cape with a max cape , during which the max hood is required to be in the player's inventory and will automatically be converted to the infernal max hood .

Like the other max cape variants (a max cape combined with another cape slot item), the infernal max cape does not have the max cape's stats or perks; it only acts as a cosmetic upgrade to the infernal cape with the following exceptions when worn:

The max cape and infernal cape can be separated by using a knife on the cape. Mac will also buy back a max cape, along with its variants, for 1,900,800 coins each. He will return the secondary item any max cape variant was combined with upon doing so.

If the player dies a PvP death at level 20 Wilderness or below and the item is unprotected, it will remain in the player's inventory; however, the item will be in a broken, unusable state and must be repaired by using it on Perdu and paying him 225,000 coins .

If the player dies a PvP death above level 20 Wilderness and the item is unprotected, it will be converted to coins. To prevent this, a Trouver parchment and a payment of 500,000 coins can be given to Perdu in order to permanently lock the item. The locked item will remain in the player's inventory; however, the item will be in a mangled, unusable state and must be repaired by using it on Perdu and paying him 500,000 coins.
24134:
The fire max cape is the result of combining a fire cape with a max cape , during which the max hood required to be in the player's inventory will automatically convert to the fire max hood .

Like the other max cape variants (a max cape combined with another cape slot item), the fire max cape does not have the max cape's stats or perks with the following exceptions when worn:

The max cape and fire cape can be separated by using a knife on the cape. Mac will also buy back a max cape, along with its variants, for 1,900,800 coins each. He will return the secondary item any max cape variant was combined with upon doing so.

If the player dies a PvP death and the item is unprotected, it will remain in the player's inventory; however, the item will be in a broken, unusable state and must be repaired by using it on Perdu and paying him 150,000 coins .

A fire max cape cannot be gambled for a chance at TzRek-Jad .
24135:
The Assembler max cape is the result of combining Ava's assembler with a max cape , during which the max hood required to be in the player's inventory will automatically convert to the assembler max hood .

Like the other max cape variants (a max cape combined with another cape slot item), the assembler max cape does not have the max cape's stats or perks; it only acts as a cosmetic upgrade to Ava's assembler with the following exceptions when worn:

The max cape and assembler can be separated by using a knife on the cape. Mac will also buy back a max cape, along with its variants, for 1,900,800 coins each. He will return the secondary item any max cape variant was combined with upon doing so.

Turning the Ava's assembler into an assembler max cape is the only way for ultimate ironmen to store one, as it counts as a max cape on the cape rack.

If the player dies a PvP death and the item is unprotected, it will remain in the player's inventory; however, the item will be in a broken, unusable state and must be repaired by using it on Perdu and paying him 240,000 coins .
24136:
The bronze defender is the weakest defender . It is similar to a dagger, but held in the off-hand in place of a shield. The bronze defender is dropped by cyclopes on the top floor of the Warriors' Guild . Entry to the Cyclops room requires a minimum of 100 Warrior guild tokens .

If the player dies to a PvP death and the bronze defender is not one of the player's protected items, it will remain in the player's inventory, but will become broken , which means the item is unusable and must be repaired with 1,000 coins by using the item on Perdu .
24137:
The iron defender is a defender made of iron. It is dropped by any of the Cyclops on the top floor of the Warriors' Guild, but only once players have obtained a bronze defender. It is one of the two defenders that does not provide a strength bonus, along with the bronze defender.

If the player dies to a PvP death and the iron defender is not one of the player's protected items, it will remain in the player's inventory, but will become broken, which means the item is unusable and must be repaired with 2,000 coins by using the item on Perdu.
24138:
The steel defender is the third weakest defender . It is similar to a dagger, but held in the off-hand in place of a shield. It requires 5 Attack and 5 Defence to wield. The steel defender is dropped by Cyclopes on the top floor of the Warriors' Guild , but only once you have obtained an iron defender .

If the player dies to a PvP death and the steel defender is not one of the player's protected items, it will remain in the player's inventory, but will become broken , which means the item is unusable and must be repaired with 2,500 coins by using the item on Perdu .
24139:
The black defender is a defender made of black metal. It is similar to a dagger, but held in the off-hand in place of a shield. It requires 10 Attack and 10 Defence to wield. The black defender is dropped by Cyclopes on the top floor of the Warriors' Guild , but only once you have obtained a steel defender .

If the player dies to a PvP death and the black defender is not one of the player's protected items, it will remain in the player's inventory, but will become broken , which means the item is unusable and must be repaired with 5,000 coins by using the item on Perdu .

The black defender does not count as an "evil" item in Shadow of the Storm despite its colour.
24140:
The mithril defender is a defender made of mithril. It can be obtained by killing cyclopes on the top floor of the Warriors' Guild, but only if you have a black defender in your inventory or if you have shown a black defender to Kamfreena. It is held in the shield slot and requires 20 Attack and Defence to wield.

If the player dies to a PvP death and the mithril defender is not one of the player's protected items, it will remain in the player's inventory, but will become broken, which means the item is unusable and must be repaired with 15,000 coins by using the item on Perdu.
24141:
The adamant defender is a defender made out of adamant . It can be obtained by killing cyclopes on the top floor of the Warriors' Guild with a mithril defender in the inventory or after you have shown a mithril defender to Kamfreena . It is held in the shield slot and requires 30 Attack and Defence to wield.

If the player dies to a PvP death and the adamant defender is not one of the player's protected items, it will remain in the player's inventory, but will become broken , which means the item is unusable and must be repaired with 25,000 coins by using the item on Perdu .
24142:
The rune defender is the 3rd strongest defender . It is used for its attack bonus and is held in the off-hand in place of a shield . It requires 40 Attack and 40 Defence to wield. The rune defender is dropped by cyclopes on the top floor of the Warriors' Guild after showing an adamant defender or better as the player enters the room.

The rune defender's slash and crush defensive bonuses are the same as a black kiteshield , but its stab defence bonus is slightly less than an adamant square shield . However, it is much more commonly used for its melee bonuses, as it gives the same bonus to strength as the toktz-ket-xil (obsidian shield) and has melee attack bonuses. A rune defender is commonly combined with weapons such as a dragon scimitar or an abyssal whip as a result.

The defender is popular among players of higher combat levels due to its offensive stats. It can be considered to be the third best off-hand item for melee training, only beaten by the dragon defender and Avernic defender , and is commonly used in PvP situations as re-obtaining a rune defender is easier than re-obtaining a dragon or Avernic one.

If the player dies to a PvP death and the rune defender is not one of the player's protected items, it will remain in the player's inventory, but will become broken , which means the item is unusable and must be repaired with 35,000 coins by using the item on Perdu . Any ornament kit on the item will also be lost on death.

Players can attach a Rune defender ornament kit , obtained from hard Treasure Trails , to create a Rune defender (t) . This is only cosmetic, and does not affect the defender's stat bonuses. It can be dismantled, returning the defender and ornament kit.
24143:
The dragon defender is the second strongest defender , behind the Avernic defender . It is used for its attack and strength bonus and is held in the shield slot. It requires level 60 Defence to equip.

The dragon defender can only be obtained from the stronger level 106 Cyclopes found exclusively in the Warrior Guild 's basement. To enter the basement for the first time, a player must show a rune defender to Lorelai , who will then grant them permanent access. Warrior Guild tokens are still required for time spent inside the basement unless the player has an Attack Cape equipped. Players can obtain a dragon defender without having a rune defender in their bank. [ 1 ] Players can obtain the dragon defender without having 60 Defence . [ 2 ]

Its melee defensive bonuses are comparable to those of an adamant square shield , with slight differences. Its strength bonus is surpassed by both the dragonfire shield and the Avernic defender , which give +7 and +8 strength bonuses, respectively. However, the dragon defender is more commonly used than either of these for melee training, due to its superior melee attack bonuses over the dragonfire shield and the overall rarity of the Avernic defender .

If the player dies to a PvP death and the dragon defender is not one of the player's protected items, it will remain in the player's inventory, but will become broken , which means the item is unusable and must be repaired with 240,000 coins by using the item on Perdu .
24144:
The staff of balance is a one-handed bladed staff which requires 75 Attack and 75 Magic to wield. It is created by bringing a Guthixian icon and a staff of the dead to Juna in the Chasm of Tears. This process is irreversible.

The staff of balance inherits all of the staff of the dead's effects. The only differences between them is that the staff of balance autocasts the Claws of Guthix god spell rather than the Flames of Zamorak god spell, and is unable to autocast Arceuus combat spells. In addition, it counts as a Zamorakian item while in the God Wars Dungeon and in the Desert Bandit Camp.

The staff of balance cannot be upgraded with a magic fang to provide the additional magic attack bonus and toxic effect given to the toxic staff of the dead.

If the player dies a PvP death and the item is unprotected, it will remain in the player's inventory; however, the item will be in a broken, unusable state and must be repaired by using it on Perdu and paying him 25,000 coins .

This item can be stored in the armour case of a costume room .

24151:

The defensive bonuses of the halo are similar to those of a black full helm, excluding negative attack bonuses. In addition, the halo gives prayer bonus and magic defence while the full helm does not.

The defensive bonuses of the halo are similar to those of a black full helm , excluding negative attack bonuses. In addition, the halo gives prayer bonus and magic defence while the full helm does not.

The fighter hat is sometimes used in place of the warrior helm and berserker helm. The Void Knight mace can be bought from a Void Knight for 250 commendation points , although a player must have 42 Attack , Strength , Defence , Hitpoints , Ranged , and Magic , along with 22 Prayer . The mace can be used to autocast Claws of Guthix , Crumble Undead , and the Wave and Surge spells . To cast Claws of Guthix, the player must have cast the spell 100 times in the Wilderness Mage Arena . Note that the Void knight mace does not count towards the four pieces needed for the void set effect .

Its stats are relatively close to that of the rune mace , with the main difference being its 20% slower attack speed . It also has +2 bonus in Stab, Slash, and Crush attack, as well as Stab, Slash, Crush, Magic, and Ranged defence, as well as a relative +2 Strength and Prayer bonus compared to the rune mace. Due to its role as one of the weapons to cast Claws of Guthix, it also has a +8 Magic attack bonus. These stats make it one of the only melee weapons in game to have a positive ranged defence bonus, other than the Lunar staff , with +1, and the dragon spear and Zamorakian spear , with +5 and +13, respectively. Unlike other maces, it only has crushing attack styles. Alongside croziers , the hallowed flail , and the 3rd Age druidic staff , it has the highest Prayer bonus of all one-handed weapons.

While Claws of Guthix can be cast and autocast while wearing an imbued Saradomin cape or imbued Zamorak cape , an appropriate cape ( Guthix cape or its imbued variant) must still be worn to receive the damage boost from Charge .

It is worn in combination with the other pieces of Void Knight Armour ( Void knight top , Void knight robe , and Void knight gloves ) to achieve the designated set effect. The Void knight mace is not required for the bonus.

The Void mage set gives a +45% to magic accuracy. This typically provides less accuracy and defensive bonuses than Ahrim's robes , but can be easily switched with the other Void sets. If wearing Elite Void Knight robes , the set gives an additional 5% increase to magic damage.

The effective magic attack bonus can be calculated as 1.45 x + 28.8 , where x is the total equipment magic attack bonus when wearing the Void mage set. For example, if you have a magic attack bonus of +16 while also wearing the Void mage set (which provides no bonus), the effective bonus becomes +52 taking into account the set effect. When wearing several best-in-slot pieces of magical gear, the accuracy of the Void mage set can surpass Ahrim's robes with the same gear.
