The Avernic defender is a defender wielded in the shield slot, requiring 70 Attack and Defence to wield. It is obtained by combining a dragon defender with an Avernic defender hilt. This process can be reversed to return the dragon defender, but the hilt will be destroyed in the process. This defender boasts the highest strength bonus of any shield slot equipment, being 1 higher than the dragonfire shield. It also has the highest melee attack bonuses of any shield slot equipment. The defensive bonuses are comparable to that of an adamant kiteshield.

Ghommal's hilt 5 or 6 can be attached to it, creating Ghommal's avernic defender 5 or 6 respectively, giving the bonuses of the Avernic defender and the additional benefits of the hilt. This process is reversible, returning both the hilt and the defender.

Avernic weaponry was common amongst Zarosian forces in the Second Age, crafted by Avernic demon smiths in the liquid fires of Infernus. Today, they are incredibly rare, and Verzik Vitur's Avernic defender is one of the few to remain, a relic from her time in the service of Zaros. Due to its age, the full defender has been destroyed, and only the hilt remains.

If the player dies to a PvP death and the avernic defender is not one of the player's protected items, it will remain in the player's inventory, but will become broken, which means the item is unusable and must be repaired with 600,000 coins by using the item on Perdu. The game values the defender at 600,000 GP when determining which items to protect.

Players will need to give the parchment and pay 500,000 to Perdu for each item they lock; multiple items can be locked simultaneously, but will require additional parchments for each one.

24219:
The Swift blade is a one-handed weapon purchased from Justine's stuff for the Last Shopper Standing for 350 Last Man Standing points.

It is one of the only four melee weapons with an attack speed of 3, with the other ones being the ham joint , goblin paint cannon , and mystic cards , with the latter two also being two handed weapons only. The swift blade also exclusively uses Stab and Slash attack styles whereas the others use Crush , and the mystic cards have negative combat stat bonuses whereas the others have no bonuses.

Due to having no Attack level requirement, the Swift blade is the best-in-slot weapon for training Defence pures and combines well with the stab bonus given by the Ardougne cloaks .

This item is also commonly used in the Theatre of Blood for the Nylocas room because of its fast attack speed. It is preferred over the Goblin paint cannon and the Ham joint because its attack styles are not shared with the dragon warhammer , allowing players to keep the dragon warhammer on an accurate attack style, while having the swift blade on an aggressive style. In addition, the swift blade is slightly more accurate than a ham joint when used with a defender , as defenders have +2 higher stab accuracy compared to crush.

This item can be stored in the armour case of a costume room .
24222:
Ava's assembler is the upgraded version of Ava's accumulator that requires level 70 Ranged to equip. The assembler gives the second best Ranged attack bonus for the cape slot and is one of the few cape slot items that provides a Ranged Strength bonus. To obtain the assembler, players must take 75 mithril arrows, Ava's accumulator (or 4,999 coins), and Vorkath's head (which can only be obtained by killing Vorkath after completion of Dragon Slayer II) to Ava in Draynor Manor.

Like all of Ava's devices, the assembler does not work when metal torso armour is worn, as this will cause 'interference'; this includes most melee armour as well as Ahrim's robetop. A list of metal torso armour that does not interfere with Ava's assembler can be found here.

Similar to its predecessors, it can randomly gather mithril ranged equipment. It also has an 80% chance of saving ammunition compared to the accumulator's 72%. As the remaining 20% chance is for the ammunition breaking, the assembler will never drop any ammo on the ground.

The breakdown of the ammo recovery rate is as listed:

Break on impact: 20%

Recovered automatically: 80%

The appearance of the assembler can be ornamented using a Masori crafting kit to match that of the Masori armour. It is solely a cosmetic upgrade and does not change its stats.
24223:
The fire cape is a melee cape obtained as a reward for completing the TzHaar Fight Cave . It is the second best melee cape in the game, outclassed only by the infernal cape . In order to obtain the fire cape, players must survive all waves of TzHaar Fight Caves and defeat TzTok-Jad . Note that the cape will not be awarded should both the player and TzTok-Jad die simultaneously, even though the boss log will count the kill. The player must be taken out of the cave by the game recognising TzTok-Jad's death; if they are removed from the cave due to dying, the game considers the player to have failed the challenge.

A fire cape must be shown to TzHaar-Ket guards around the centre of the city to allow further access to Mor Ul Rek . This does not consume the fire cape. However, to enter the Inferno , a fire cape must be sacrificed by giving it to TzHaar-Ket-Keh . This is a one-time fee.

If the player dies a PvP death and the fire cape is unprotected, it will remain in the player's inventory; however, the item will be in a broken, unusable state and must be repaired by using it on Perdu and paying him 150,000 coins .

When worn, players are granted the fiery attribute and will therefore receive additional damage in PvP from the special effects of Pearl bolts (e) and Pearl dragon bolts (e) .
24224:
The infernal cape is the most powerful melee cape in terms of overall bonuses, awarded for defeating TzKal-Zuk in the Inferno . It surpasses its predecessor, the fire cape , boasting greater melee attack and strength bonuses, along with slightly higher defensive bonuses. In spite of this, it is still surpassed by the Ardougne cloaks 3 and 4 in stab attack and prayer bonuses, and by the mythical cape in crush attack.

An infernal cape can be exchanged for a chance of obtaining the Jal-Nib-Rek pet by speaking to TzHaar-Ket-Keh . Like killing TzKal-Zuk , there is a 1/100 chance of obtaining the pet this way. If the player already has the pet, capes cannot be exchanged.

An infernal cape can be combined with the max cape to change its appearance by turning it into the infernal max cape .

As of 1 August 2026, there are 170,755 accounts that have obtained an infernal cape.

If the player dies a PvP death at level 20 Wilderness or below and the item is unprotected, it will remain in the player's inventory; however, the item will be in a broken, unusable state and must be repaired by using it on Perdu and paying him 225,000 coins .
24225:
The ornate granite maul is a granite maul with an ornate maul handle attached to it. The handle enhances the granite maul by reducing its special attack cost from 60% to 50%. The handle is effectively consumed by this process, as while the maul can be reverted, the process will destroy the handle. The ornate handle is obtained from Justine's Stuff for the Last Shopper Standing .

A granite clamp can be added to the maul to adjust its appearance. The clamp gives no additional bonuses, and is only used to add aesthetics to the maul. While untradeable, the maul can be reverted to its tradeable state at any time using the right-click "Revert" option; however, the clamp will be destroyed upon doing so.

When this weapon is lost on death in PvP, it is converted to 90% of Grand Exchange price of the granite maul and the ornate maul handle.

If a player dies with the clamped maul and it is not one of the player's protected items, the maul will revert to its default appearance, and players must use another granite clamp to enhance its appearance again.

The cape, like most untradeable equipment, is automatically protected upon death in dangerous PvM scenarios outside of the Wilderness , and likewise is always protected upon safe deaths and services that offer an item reclaim function (such as Zulrah via Priestess Zul-Gwenwynig and the Grotesque Guardians via the magical chest).

If the player dies a PvP death and the item is unprotected, it will remain in the player's inventory; however, the item will be in a broken, unusable state and must be repaired by using it on Perdu and paying him 96,000 coins .

The imbued Zamorak cape can be combined with the max cape to change its appearance by turning it into the imbued Zamorak max cape .
24251:
The Wilderness crabs teleport is a magic tablet that can be broken to teleport the player to the dark crab fishing spots in level 33 eastern Wilderness , a single-way combat zone south-east of Venenatis .

Because this tablet teleports players to the Wilderness, a warning will appear upon clicking the "Break" option on the tablet. This can be toggled by right-clicking the "Configure" option.

It is purchased at Justine's stuff for the Last Shopper Standing for one point.
24253: Clue scroll (elite) is a coordinate clue obtained from elite Treasure Trails.
24254:
A fang is an item found during the The Fremennik Exiles quest, obtained by searching the rocks west of the sandpit in Rellekka . It is given to Freygerd along with the unsealed letter and venom gland as evidence of basilisks plotting to attack Rellekka.

The item's model appears to be based off the magic fang , without the purple orb.
24255: A Venom gland is an item used in The Fremennik Exiles quest. It can be found in some crates south of the house that is south of the sandpit in Rellekka. It is given to Freygerd along with the fang and an unsealed letter as evidence of basilisks plotting to attack Rellekka.
24256: The unsealed letter is an item used in The Fremennik Exiles quest. It is obtained by killing a Basilisk Youngling that comes out after the player searches the sandpit in Rellekka . It is given to Freygerd along with the fang and venom gland as evidence of basilisks plotting to attack Rellekka, and if the player has not read it, it is returned by Brundt the Chieftain .
24257: The unsealed letter is an item used in The Fremennik Exiles quest. It is obtained by killing a Basilisk Youngling that comes out after the player searches the sandpit in Rellekka . It is given to Freygerd along with the fang and venom gland as evidence of basilisks plotting to attack Rellekka, and if the player has not read it, it is returned by Brundt the Chieftain .
24258: The V sigil is an item used in The Fremennik Exiles quest. It is obtained by using three lunar bars on an anvil along with a hammer , granting 25 Smithing experience. It can be enchanted into the V sigil (e) by bringing it to Fossegrimmen south of Rellekka .
24259: The V sigil (e) is an item used in The Fremennik Exiles quest. It is obtained by bringing a V sigil to Fossegrimmen located south of Rellekka . It can be combined with lunar glass , a polishing rock and a fremennik shield to create V's shield .
24260: Molten glass (i) is an item used in The Fremennik Exiles quest. It is obtained by bringing molten glass to Baba Yaga on Lunar Isle. It can be turned into Lunar glass by using it on the Astral Altar along with 100 astral runes.
24261: Lunar glass is an item used in The Fremennik Exiles quest. It is obtained by using a molten glass (i) on the Astral Altar along with 100 astral runes . With a glassblowing pipe in the player's inventory, it can be used with the V sigil (e) , polishing rock , and a fremennik shield to create V's shield .
24262: The Polishing rock is an item used in The Fremennik Exiles quest. It can be obtained by dropping a pet rock into the large geyser north-west of the Mountain Camp , then fishing it out with a fishing rod while equipping ice gloves .
24263:
Ballad of the Basilisk is a scroll containing the lyrics to the song Ballad of the Basilisk . It is found by searching some boxes outside the Rellekka Longhall Bar , against its north wall.

If lost, it can be reclaimed from the boxes behind the Longhall or from a bookcase within a player-owned house .
24265:
V's shield is a shield created during The Fremennik Exiles quest. It is a recreation of the shield owned by the legendary warrior V . It requires 40 Defence and 60 Slayer to wield.

It acts as a mirror shield when fighting basilisks , basilisk knights , and cockatrice . It has stronger defensive stats than the mirror shield, on par with an Adamant kiteshield but positive magic defence and without negative stats.

If lost, it can be reobtained from Brundt the Chieftain in Rellekka 's longhall for 50,000 . Multiple shields can be obtained via the drop trick .

24268:
The basilisk jaw is a unique drop from basilisk knights . It can be combined with the helm of Neitiznot , after the completion of The Fremennik Exiles , to create an untradeable Neitiznot faceguard . Doing so requires asking Olaf the Bard for stories about basilisk jaws while having it in their inventory. Completion of The Fremennik Exiles is also required to equip the helmet.

If players are on a Slayer task for basilisks, the drop rate of the basilisk jaw is improved from 1/5,000 to 1/1,000. [ 1 ]

Upon inspecting the jaw, a message appears in the chatbox stating " It's the jaw of a Basilisk Knight. Perhaps Olaf the Bard knows a good story about it." If a player attempts to use the jaw on the helm of Neitiznot before speaking to Olaf the Bard , a message appears in the chatbox stating " You're not quite sure how to do that. Perhaps Olaf the Bard can help. He's likely to know a good story about Basilisk Jaws."
24271:
The Neitiznot faceguard is an upgraded helm of Neitiznot that requires 70 Defence and completion of The Fremennik Exiles to wear. In addition to offering increased defensive bonuses, its strength bonus is doubled, giving it the second highest of any helmet, tied with Oathplate helm and behind the torva full helm.

It can be made by combining a helm of Neitiznot and a basilisk jaw after asking Olaf the Bard for stories about basilisk jaws while having it in their inventory.

The helmet is untradeable, but can be freely reverted at any time. If lost in PvP, it will revert to the normal helm of Neitiznot and basilisk jaw.
24276:
The Basilisk knight is an interface item that can be seen in the Slayer skill guide representing the Basilisk knight .

The actual item cannot be obtained by players.
24277:
A mysterious emblem was an item that was purchasable from the Emblem Trader, which a player could upgrade by killing the player's assigned target on the official Bounty Hunter world whilst having a mysterious emblem in their inventory. However, their opponent must also have had a mysterious emblem of the same tier in order for it to be upgraded. If a player is holding multiple emblems, only the highest tier emblem will be upgraded.

Emblems were always lost upon death; players were willing to risk their emblem to either receive an emblem in another player's possession or to upgrade their own. For example, if a player was killed and had a tier 4 emblem in their inventory, the target's emblem will be destroyed upon death, and the victor's emblem would have been upgraded to tier 5.

Players were not able to drop Mysterious emblems. Unlike most items, mysterious emblems had a seven second timer before being destroyed, in order to prevent players from destroying them mid-combat to deny their killer the emblem as loot.

24288: The Dagon'hai hat is a piece of magic armour obtained as a rare loot from Larran's big chest . It is part of the Dagon'hai robes set, and requires level 70 Magic and 40 Defence to wear. It can be stored in a magic wardrobe in a player-owned house.
24291: The Dagon'hai robe top is a piece of magic armour obtained as a rare loot from Larran's big chest . It is part of the Dagon'hai robes set, and requires level 70 Magic and 40 Defence to wear. It can be stored in a magic wardrobe in a player-owned house.
24294: The Dagon'hai robe bottom is a piece of magic armour obtained as a rare loot from Larran's big chest . It is part of the Dagon'hai robes set, and requires level 70 Magic and 40 Defence to wear. It can be stored in a magic wardrobe in a player-owned house.
24297:
The White bed sheets are an item used during the 2019 Halloween event. They are obtained from the bed in the house north of Bob's Axe shop. Using a knife on the bed sheets produces the 5 items in the spooky outfit.

Attempting to grab a second pair of sheets produces the message "You already have some sheets, try cutting some holes to make a costume!". After this, attempting to gather more sheets produces the message "You already have the full costume!"

Before getting to the appropriate part of the event and after completion, attempting to take the sheets from the bed causes the player to say in the chatbox "Why would I do that?"
24298:
Smoke powder is an item used during the 2019 Halloween event . It can be found in a sack of black powder directly south of the Lumbridge furnace . It is used inside the Lumbridge General Store with a tinderbox to create a Smoke Bomb on the ground. The smoke from the bomb distracts the shopkeepers so that you can steal the shiny glass from the table.

Attempting to pick up more than one provides the message "You already have some powder in your inventory." Attempting to ignite it outside the Lumbridge general store provides the message "You should plant that inside the Lumbridge general store!" Attempting to ignite it inside the Lumbridge general store without a tinderbox prompts a chatbox with the message "I need a tinderbox to light his, maybe my new friend has one."

Before getting to the appropriate part of the event and after completion, attempting to take the smoke powder from the Black powder sack causes the player to say in the chatbox "Why would I want that?"
24299:
Shiny glass is an item used during the 2019 Halloween event . It is found inside the Lumbridge General Store on a table. The shopkeeper will prevent it from being picked up unless the store has been filled with smoke from the smoke powder , and it can also not be telegrabbed. The shiny glass must be stolen and given to the goblins Snailneck and Grasslegs to complete the event.

Before getting to the appropriate part of the event and after completion, attempting to take the shiny glass from the table causes the player to say in the chatbox "Why would I steal that?"
24300:
The spooky hood is a cosmetic reward from the 2019 Halloween event . It is part of the spooky outfit , and can be obtained as a reward from the Halloween events that occur once per year. It can be used on the swampy sink outside the toolshed in the Lumbridge Swamp , or on the Ectofuntus outside Port Phasmatys to unlock the spookier hood .

It is meant to mimic the bedsheet obtained during the Ghosts Ahoy quest , which players have often requested that it be wearable outside Port Phasmatys but cannot due to restricted interaction checks in the game code.

If destroyed, a replacement can be obtained from Diango in Draynor Village or from the toy box of a costume room , as part of the 2019: Spooky Costume set. Ultimate Ironmen will be unable to retrieve individual pieces until the full set is stored.

24329:
A bounty crate was an item that contained an assortment of supplies that are commonly used in player killing activities. In order to purchase it from the Bounty Hunter Shop for 7 Bounty Hunter points, players required a combat level of 50. In addition, ironmen must have had the requirements to obtain the item for themselves. If the crate rolled an item the player did not meet the requirements for, a lower-level item was rolled instead. Ironmen were also unable to obtain Mysterious Emblems from the crate. It is unknown how this affected the probabilities of rolling the other items.

Players could buy up to a maximum of five crates, and could purchase an additional five for every target killed in Bounty Hunter.

With Bounty Hunter's rework in 2023, the crates have since been superseded by their tiered counterparts.
24331:
The birthday cake is an item obtained from the large cakes in Varrock Square in commemoration of the first anniversary of Old School RuneScape Mobile . Eating the cake heals six hitpoints . There is no limit to the number of slices players can take from the fountain, aside from inventory size. While they are tradeable, they cannot be sold on the Grand Exchange .

Taking a slice from the fountain for the first time after logging in causes the chatbox to display a message: "You can take this slice of cake just about anywhere with you, just like OSRS Mobile!"

Players using the desktop client can right-click the cake and click the "Learn-more" option, which prompts a confirmation message to open this link in the player's browser. If players select the "Learn-more" option on the mobile version, the chatbox will state "You are currently playing on mobile. You seem to know what you are doing!"
24333:
Dagon'hai robes set is an item obtained by exchanging a set of items with a Grand Exchange clerk via their right-click "Sets" option and clicking on the appropriate item set within the Item Sets interface.

It is commonly made in order to conveniently sell all three components of the Dagon'hai robes at once.
24336:
The Target teleport is a magic tablet that can be broken by players to teleport to their assigned target. They can be purchased at Justine's stuff for the Last Shopper Standing for 1 Last Man Standing point after reading a Target teleport scroll .

In order to be able to use the tablet, players must have unlocked Teleport to Target via reading the Target teleport scroll . In addition, the restrictions for casting the teleport spell also apply to the tablet. The tablet can be received as a monster drop regardless of whether the Target teleport scroll has been read.

This item can be stored in the magic wardrobe of a costume room .
24340:

24361:
A beginner scroll box is a Scroll box that gives players a beginner clue scroll when opened. Upon completion of X Marks the Spot , scroll boxes are obtained in place of clue scrolls, and are stackable up to a certain limit depending on the number of beginner clue completions.

If a clue scroll is already in the player's inventory or bank, players will receive the message, The clue box refuses to open - you already have a clue.

The rune pouch is an item that can store 16,000 of three types of runes (except runes found in the Nightmare Zone). Players can cast spells using the runes stored in the pouch, so a rune pouch saves inventory space. With a thread of Elidinis and level 75 crafting, the rune pouch can be upgraded (with a needle) to a divine rune pouch. Players cannot own more than one rune pouch.

If players die a PvP death while carrying a rune pouch in any level Wilderness or in a PvP world, they will lose the rune pouch, unless it has been locked via use of a trouver parchment. It should be noted that the Trouver parchment does not protect runes stored within a Rune pouch upon PvP death.

If players die a PvM death anywhere, including any level Wilderness, the rune pouch is always sent to a gravestone or item retrieval service, unless it has been locked via use of a trouver parchment. Locked rune pouches are kept in the inventory upon PvM death, instead.

The Inquisitor's mace is a one-handed crush weapon requiring 80 Attack to wield. Received as a drop from The Nightmare , it has bonuses nearly identical to the Ghrazi rapier and blade of Saeldor , acting as the crush variant of these weapons, with an additional +3 Strength bonus and +2 Prayer bonus.

Once belonging to Phosani , a former Saradominist Justiciar and one of the founders of Slepe , the Inquisitor's mace had remained sealed in the Sisterhood Sanctuary deep beneath Slepe until The Nightmare's arrival unearthed it. [ 1 ]

The Inquisitor's mace, along with the pieces of Inquisitor's armour , counts as a Zamorakian item in God Wars Dungeon , providing God-related Protection . The mace can be used to train all the combat stats (Attack, Strength, Defence) while on crush whereas most other melee weapons have singular strengths.

The Nightmare staff is a one-handed staff that can be received as a drop from The Nightmare . Requiring level 72 Magic and 50 Hitpoints to wield, it can autocast offensive standard spells as well as Ancient Magicks .

Once belonging to the shamans of Ashihama , its true name has since been lost to the world, and is now associated with The Nightmare. [ 1 ] It gives a 15% bonus in magic damage .

Players can attach three different orbs to the Nightmare staff, giving it differing effects, increasing the magic requirement to 82, and making it untradeable:

The upgraded staves can be reverted to their tradeable components at any time.
24423:
The harmonised Nightmare staff is a one-handed staff that is created by attaching a harmonised orb to the Nightmare staff . Requiring level 82 Magic and 50 Hitpoints to wield, it can autocast offensive standard spells , but cannot autocast any other spells (including Ancient Magicks and the Arceuus spellbook ) unlike its other variants. Like the Nightmare staff it gives a 15% bonus in magic damage . The upgraded staff is untradeable, but it can be reverted to its tradeable components at any time. If lost on death in the Wilderness , the killer will receive the staff and the orb.

When casting offensive spells from the standard spellbook, the harmonised Nightmare staff reduces the cast time from 5 (3.0s) to 4 (2.4s) ticks, equal to most powered staves . The 4-tick spell speed only applies when autocasting. Manually casting spells with the staff equipped will result in a 5-tick attack speed. Unlike powered staves, the harmonised Nightmare staff can be used against other players in dangerous PvP scenarios, as it is not classified as a powered staff.

Due to the increased casting speed, the harmonised Nightmare staff allows standard combat spells to have damage output competitive with the powered staves; casting Fire Surge with the staff along with a charged tome of fire is particularly effective against monsters weak to magic, such as Zulrah , The Nightmare 's pillars, and Kraken , albeit without the passive healing and venom provided by the Sanguinesti staff and trident of the swamp respectively.

In PvP, the increased attack speed is notable for enabling the stacking of damage from spells and melee weapon special attacks on the same tick, such as Fire Surge into Armadyl godsword special attack, something that slower attack speed staves cannot do.

A herb sack is an item that can be bought from Slayer masters for 750 Slayer reward points or from Farmer Gricoller's Rewards for 250 Tithe Farm points.

Buying one requires level 58 in Herblore (cannot be boosted) and allows the player to store up to 30 of each of the grimy normal herbs, for a total of 450 stored. A full herb sack is worth 1,077,150. Players cannot store noted or cleaned herbs in the herb sack.

The herb sack can be upgraded into the silklined herb sack, which can store up to 100 of each grimy herb. This requires using a pristine spider silk on the standard version to permanently upgrade it. The silklined herb sack is practical for farming due to the expanded capacity.

The herb sack can be manually filled by using the left-click 'Fill' option, which will deposit any grimy herbs from your inventory, unless it is full. It can be opened or closed with the right-click options 'Open' or 'Close' respectively. An open sack will automatically deposit any grimy herbs that are picked up by the player, as well as those harvested from a herb patch and Herbiboars, provided there is space for it. A closed sack will not automatically deposit herbs.

The 'Empty' option deposits herbs into the inventory, starting from the lowest level herb, and with the bank open it will deposit all of the contents into the bank. Using the 'Check' option will list all currently stored herbs within it in the chat box. Using the 'Check' option while the sack is empty will result in the messages You look in your herb sack and see: The herb sack is empty.

The herb sack is useful for killing monsters that often drop valuable herbs, such as chaos druids, flesh crawlers, aberrant spectres, and deviant spectres, since it only takes up one inventory slot. The herb sack can also be used when lighting incense burners during open altar house parties, reducing the frequency of banking or unnoting Marrentill at Phials. The base version is generally not practical for farming since it has a limit of 30 of each type, and the Tool Leprechaun can note your produce (both grimy or cleaned).

Herbs stored in the sack are not lost upon death. Herbs will stay in the herb sack upon death, unless the player has untoggled this setting. Even if the herb sack is one of the items kept on PvP death, the herbs inside the herb sack are NOT kept on death when killed by a player.
24479:
The Spice rack is an interface item that can be seen in the Construction skill guide representing the Spice rack.

The actual item cannot be obtained by players.
24480:
The coal bag is a reward purchasable from Prospector Percy's Nugget Shop for 100 golden nuggets . The coal bag holds up to 27 pieces of coal (36 if a Smithing cape is equipped). When smelting or superheating , coal in the bag will be used after the coal in the inventory . It is refillable just like essence pouches , though unlike an essence pouch, it does not degrade . This is useful for both mining and smithing as it effectively doubles the amount of coal a player can carry and thus the number of bars a player can make per inventory of ore. Coal placed inside the bag will not add additional weight to your character until removed from the coal bag.

Players can right-click to open the bag, which will have coal that the player mines from coal rocks be automatically placed inside the bag, providing there is space for it.

Alternatively, players can hold-shift and left-click to empty the coal bag without the need to right-click, if " shift click to drop items " is enabled in the settings.

Only one coal bag may be in the player's possession at any time. It cannot be traded or dropped but it can be destroyed if it is empty. Players may sell their coal bag back to Percy in exchange for golden nuggets equal to 80% of its original cost (80 golden nuggets ).

Warning: Attempting to use alchemy spells on the coal bag will destroy it regardless of whether or not there was any coal in it.
24481:
The gem bag is a gem container purchasable from Prospector Percy's Nugget Shop for 100 golden nuggets . It can hold 60 of each (300 total) uncut gems of the following types:

A full gem bag is worth 1,129,980 . To deposit a gem, players can use the gem with the gem bag or left-click the bag to store all uncut gems in their inventory. This will produce a game message saying, You add the gem[s] to your bag. Players can empty the bag via a right-click option or by shift-clicking the bag (if they have shift-click item dropping enabled) in their inventory or whilst their bank is open.

Ultimate Ironmen get an additional interface when emptying their gem pouch that allows them to choose the type of gem and the quantity to withdraw.

Players can "open" the bag via a right-click option. Whilst open, any gems that the player picks up off the ground or obtains during Mining and Thieving are automatically placed inside the bag, if there is enough space. Players will receive a game message confirming the open gem bag automatically stored the gem saying, You put it straight into your open gem bag.

Players may only own one gem bag at a time. On death , the gem bag does not lose its contents. Players who no longer want their gem bag can sell it back to Percy for 80% of the original cost.
24482:
The seed box is an item that can store up to 2,147,483,647 seeds of six different types. It is purchased from Farmer Gricoller at the Tithe Farm for 250 points. This item can be used directly on a farming patch . Using the box on a patch will automatically plant the first applicable seed of that patch's type, which can be reordered. Players can right-click to open the box, which will have seeds that the player picks up be automatically placed inside the box, provided there is space for it.

Although frags and mushroom spores are not taxonomically seeds, they can still be stored in the seed box.

Like Gricoller's can , players can only own one seed box at a time. It is useful to bring to Slayer tasks and bosses which drop a large variety of seeds commonly, such as nechryael , to save inventory space. Ultimate Ironman players may find the seed box very useful, as it saves up to five inventory spaces while training Farming and Herblore .

It is also useful to bring while shipwreck salvaging due to the number of seeds and frags different shipwrecks provide, particularly at large shipwrecks and merchant shipwrecks . Seeds gained from sorting salvage do not automatically go into an opened seed box.
24483:
The Phoenix is a pet that can be received from looting the Reward Cart , from which rewards are obtained by subduing the Wintertodt with at least 500 points.

When a player receives the pet, it will automatically try to appear as their follower. At the same time, a message in the chatbox will state You have a funny feeling like you're being followed. However, if a player receives a pet while having a follower out (for example, a cat ), it will be placed into their inventory . When this occurs, the message in the chatbox will instead state You feel something weird sneaking into your backpack.

On death , if a player loses their pet (as a follower or in your inventory) it will wander around the area for 30 seconds before despawning. Even if the player returns in time, the pet cannot be picked up, and can be reclaimed from Probita .

Though the Wintertodt is classified as a boss rather than a skilling activity, the phoenix is fifteen times more common at 200 million Firemaking experience.

24488:
Inquisitor's armour set is an item obtained by exchanging a set of items with a Grand Exchange clerk via their right-click "Sets" option and clicking on the appropriate item set within the Item Sets interface.

It is commonly made in order to conveniently sell all three components of the Inquisitor's armour at once.
24491:
The Little Nightmare is a pet that can be obtained by defeating The Nightmare or Phosani's Nightmare. It is a much smaller version of her. The pet has a 1/800 drop rate in the original encounter, decreasing for every additional player in the room when the fight started: 1/1600 in a duo, 1/2400 in a trio, 1/3200 in a 4-man and 1/4000 in a 5-or-higher-man encounter. At Phosani's Nightmare, the pet has a flat 1/1400 drop rate.

The Little Nightmare is able to metamorphose into a little parasite. For Little Nightmare to be able to do so, players must use the Parasitic Egg on her, a drop acquired from Phosani's Nightmare.

When a player receives the pet, it will automatically try to appear as their follower. At the same time, a message in the chatbox will state You have a funny feeling like you're being followed. However, if a player receives a pet while having a follower out (for example, a cat), it will be placed into their inventory. When this occurs, the message in the chatbox will instead state You feel something weird sneaking into your backpack.

If a player's inventory is full and they have a follower already, they will not receive the pet; it must instead be claimed from Probita in East Ardougne.

On death, if a player loses their pet (as a follower or in your inventory) it will wander around the area for 30 seconds before despawning. Even if the player returns in time, the pet cannot be picked up, and can be reclaimed from Probita.
24493: Clue scroll (hard) is an anagram clue obtained from hard Treasure Trails .
24495:
The jar of dreams is a rare drop from The Nightmare found in the Sisterhood Sanctuary .

The jar can be used on a boss lair display in a player's Achievement Gallery to have a display of The Nightmare. Doing so requires killing it at least once.
24511:
The harmonised orb is an item obtained as a rare drop from The Nightmare. It can be used on a Nightmare staff to upgrade it to the harmonised Nightmare staff.

Once belonging to the shamans of Ashihama, the orb was used by the shamans to adapt the Nightmare staff, its true name long since lost to the world, to any task, which gave them complete power over the island until the arrival of The Nightmare.
24514:
The volatile orb is an item obtained as a rare drop from The Nightmare. It can be used on a Nightmare staff to upgrade it to the volatile Nightmare staff.

Once belonging to the shamans of Ashihama, the orb was used by the shamans to adapt the Nightmare staff, its true name long since lost to the world, to any task, which gave them complete power over the island until the arrival of The Nightmare.
24517:
The eldritch orb is an item obtained as a rare drop from The Nightmare. It can be used on a Nightmare staff to upgrade it to the eldritch Nightmare staff.

Once belonging to the shamans of Ashihama, the orb was used by the shamans to adapt the Nightmare staff, its true name long since lost to the world, to any task, which gave them complete power over the island until the arrival of The Nightmare.
24520:
The victor's cape (1000) is a cosmetic cape that can be obtained from Justine's stuff for the Last Shopper Standing after obtaining 1,000 non-casual wins in the minigame.

This item can be stored in the cape rack of a costume room .
24522:
Cat ears are a head-slot cosmetic obtained as a reward from the 2020 Birthday event. They have a right-click 'chase' option which allows players to chase Hell-Rats, which will turn them into hell cat ears.

If destroyed, a replacement can be obtained from Diango in Draynor Village or from the toy box of a costume room.
24523: Death's coffer is an unobtainable item released with Death's Office. It appears in the chatbox when the player cannot afford the fees to reclaim items from Death's coffer, or tries to sacrifice items that are too cheap. The actual item however cannot be obtained.
24524: The Gravestones are two unobtainable items. They can be seen in the chatbox when choosing which style of Grave to select in Death's Office. The actual items however cannot be obtained.
24525:

If destroyed, a replacement can be obtained from Diango in Draynor Village or from the toy box of a costume room.
24527:
Hell cat ears are a head-slot cosmetic obtained as a reward from the 2020 Birthday event . They can be obtained by using the right-click 'chase' option of regular cat ears while near Hell-Rats .

While the hell cat ears are a free-to-play item, there is currently no known way to transform the cat ears into hell cat ears on a free-to-play world .

If destroyed, a replacement can be obtained from Diango in Draynor Village or from the toy box of a costume room .
24528: The Lamp of the Gatherer is an item obtained from Adventurer Jon by completing tasks in the Adventure Paths' Gatherer Path. It grants 150 experience in either Fishing, Mining or Woodcutting.
24529:
Harmony is a book found in the Grand Library in Prifddinas, which requires completion of Song of the Elves to access.

The book, written by the leader of Clan Iorwerth, Aenwyn Iorwerth, takes place shortly before the elves and their goddess, Seren, left Tarddiad, the elven homeworld, for Gielinor during the First Age. The book details Aenwyn's refusal to leave Tarddiad and the conversation she has with Seren regarding said matter.

If lost, it can be reclaimed from any bookshelf in the Grand Library, or from a bookcase within a player-owned house.
24531:
The runner hat is a piece of members-only armour that requires 45 Defence and is rewarded from the Barbarian Assault minigame. Players with 275 Honour points in all four roles and who have killed the Penance Queen can purchase the hat from Commander Connad, located on the ground floor of the Barbarian Outpost.

Compared to other helmets requiring 45 Defence, the Runner hat lacks attack bonuses. The stats for the hat are closely similar to equipment requiring 40 Defence. The Runner hat provides a slightly higher magic defence bonus (+1) compared to the that of the rune full helm (-1), and lacks a negative attack bonus for ranged and magic. The runner hat has a weight of only 1 kg, whilst most other helmets weigh at least 2 kg if not more. It is mostly used by players who want to show their prestige in Barbarian Assault.

If the player dies a PvP death and the item is unprotected, it will remain in the player's inventory; however, the item will be in a broken, unusable state and must be repaired by using it on Perdu and paying him 40,005 coins.

This item can be stored in the armour case of a costume room.

24534:
Mithril seeds from Last Man Standing are a minigame-exclusive variant of the normal Mithril seeds. It can be obtained from opening the chests with a bloody key or bloodier key, or looting the crates that spawn at random locations on the map. It can be looted from other players as it always drops on death. Additionally, they disappear upon leaving the minigame.

On planting the seeds, the player will move one adjacent square then be given the option to pick the flowers. Picking the flowers produces one of nine different colours of flowers.

While seemingly useless at first, they are often used in PVP to move while frozen in place, as the seeds force the player to move one tile. This is useful when fighting opponents who take advantage of your inability to move by standing on top of your character, where your character cannot hit them. They may do this inbetween attacks to prevent you from fighting back, or as a safe place to eat multiple times.
24535:
The magic egg ball is an item first obtained as a reward from the 2020 Easter event . It acts as a real-life Magic 8-Ball , but with RuneScape-themed questions.

If destroyed, a replacement can be obtained from Diango in Draynor Village or from the toy box of a costume room .

Players are able to ask the egg any of the following questions:
24537:
The carrot sword is a fun weapon first obtained as a reward from the 2020 Easter event. It is classified as a fun weapon in legacy duels within the Emir's Arena because it gives the player negative bonuses.

Its -100 Strength bonus makes it the weakest weapon melee weapon in the game, tied with the cursed goblin hammer, hunting knife, and nutcracker staff. If the user's strength bonus is -64 or less, it will never deal damage.

If destroyed, a replacement can be obtained from Diango in Draynor Village or from the toy box of a costume room, as part of the 2020: Easter Carrot Swords set. Ultimate Ironmen will be unable to retrieve individual pieces until the full set is stored.
24539:
The '24-carat' sword is a fun weapon first obtained as a reward from the 2020 Easter event by using the carrot sword on the paint buckets at the top of Duke Rabbacio's castle. Upon doing so, a message in the chatbox states You dunk your sword into the paint turning it into a 24 Carot Gold Sword!

It is classified as a fun weapon in legacy duels within the Emir's Arena because it gives the player negative bonuses.

If destroyed, a replacement can be obtained from Diango in Draynor Village or from the toy box of a costume room, as part of the 2020: Easter Carrot Swords set. Ultimate Ironmen will be unable to retrieve individual pieces until the full set is stored.
24541:
The painted fake magic egg is an item obtained during the 2020 Easter event by dipping an unpainted fake magic egg in paint buckets found on top of the Castle in Bunbridge .

The player must try to deceive Duke Rabbacio to replace his Magic Egg with the fake one by asking the magic egg if it itself is the fake one.
24542: The unpainted fake magic egg is an item created during the 2020 Easter event by using a conch shell on a broken egg. It is used on paint buckets found on the top of the Castle in Bunbridge to create the painted fake magic egg.
24543: The conch shell was an item found on south-west side of Bunbridge in the 2020 Easter event . It was formerly used on a broken egg to create an unpainted fake magic egg .
24544: The broken egg is an item obtained during the 2020 Easter event , from Farmer Maggot 's farm on the north-east side of Bunbridge . It is used on a conch shell to create an unpainted fake magic egg .
24545: The dummy portal item is an unobtainable item which shows the portal inside The Disappointing Gelt 's hat. It is only seen in-game via a chatbox message.
24546: The carrot was an orange item used for the post-2020 Easter event pseudo-quest, The Rabbit's Assistant. It was found on a table in a house south of the Rabbit Realm Castle, and is one of three ingredients players must give the Rabbit Chef.
24547: The broken goat horn is an item used for the post- 2020 Easter event quest, The Restless Goat. It is found on the beach in the Rabbit Realm's east coast, and is used to put Viktor the Restless Goat to rest.
24549:
The cake is an item that is used for the post- 2020 Easter event pseudo-quest, The Rabbit's Assistant . It can be found at the Rabbit campfire at the north-west corner of Bunbridge , and is one of three ingredients players must give the Rabbit Chef .

While it shares the same appearance and examine as a regular cake , it cannot be eaten.
24551:
The blade of Saeldor (c) is a corrupted version of the blade of Saeldor that does not degrade, with its appearance altered to resemble the corrupted crystal seen within the Corrupted Gauntlet. The blade's colours may be changed to other colours of the Elven Clans by buying crystals from Lliann's Wares in Prifddinas, which cost 500,000 coins each. It can also be reverted to its original colour by using the crystal of Hefin on any variant of the corrupted blade.

The blade can be upgraded by bringing it and 1,000 crystal shards to a singing bowl. Doing so requires level 82 Smithing and Crafting (the levels can be boosted), and grants no experience. If the player does not meet the Smithing and Crafting requirements, they can have Conwenna or Reese sing the crystal for them for an extra 500 crystal shards. Excess charges in the blade will be taken into account; for example, a fully charged blade (20,000 charges) will only cost 800 crystal shards to upgrade. Upon creating the corrupted blade, the chatbox message states "With the help of the crystal bowl, you sing a dark song which corrupts the crystals."

While untradeable, the blade can be uncharged, but the crystal shards used to upgrade it will not be returned.

Like its regular variant, the blade requires level 80 Attack to wield, and provides the highest slash bonus out of any one-handed weapon for its attack speed, surpassing the abyssal tentacle as the best slash weapon. It is tied with the Ghrazi rapier as the second strongest one-handed melee weapon in the game, after the Inquisitor's mace, although it is outperformed by the Scythe of Vitur against large monsters.
24554:
The Pyromancer set is an unobtainable item seen in-game via a chatbox interface when giving Ignisia unique items from the Reward Cart in exchange for extra supply crates or burnt pages .

Players who exchange a full set of the Pyromancer outfit for burnt pages will receive 250 burnt pages rather than the 200 pages given when exchanging individual pieces of the outfit.
24555:
The tangleroot is a skilling pet that can be obtained when checking the health (for patches that have this option, like fruit trees) or when harvesting the final crop (for patches without a "Check-health" option) of a farming patch. It may also be obtained while playing the Tithe Farm minigame or from killing the Hespori. The chances of getting it are dependent on the player's Farming level and the crop the player is harvesting.

When a player receives the pet, it will automatically try to appear as their follower. At the same time, a message in the chatbox will state You have a funny feeling like you're being followed. However, if a player receives a pet while having a follower out (for example, a cat), it will be placed into their inventory. When this occurs, the message in the chatbox will instead state You feel something weird sneaking into your backpack.

Unlike pets such as the rock golem, an incoming farming resource such as a herb or hespori seed will take precedence over the farming pet. If the player already has a follower and the remaining inventory slots are then filled by an incoming farming resource, the player will not receive the pet and must instead claim it from Probita in East Ardougne. Should the player obtain the pet while harvesting giant seaweed, the pet will not be lost upon drowning.

On death, if a player loses their pet (as a follower or in your inventory) it will wander around the area for 30 seconds before despawning. Even if the player returns in time, the pet cannot be picked up, and can be reclaimed from Probita. If a seed has been used on tangleroot and is lost upon death, the pet will revert to its original form and the player must use another seed on it upon reclaim.

24565:
Antique emblems are rewards from the Bounty Hunter Minigame . Unlike their previous version , they can only be obtained by killing your target in the Wilderness on Bounty Hunter worlds. There is also a chance for the emblem to upgrade to the next Tier when killing other Players. The chance of upgrading an emblem can be increased, by killing higher level Targets, carrying higher level emblems, and by killing your Target in Hotspots . There is also a silent cooldown that caps the rate at which players can receive Emblems, similar to the system used for marks of grace . There is also a maximum cap of 10 Bounty Hunter rewards you can gain each day. A reward is considered either a newly dropped Tier 1 Antique emblem or one of the Antique emblems in your inventory being upgraded upon killing an opponent.

Antique emblems of all tiers can be traded to the Emblem trader in Edgeville for points in the Bounty Hunter Shop .

A Tier 10 Antique emblem can also be mounted in your Player-owned house 's Achievement gallery hotspot to create a Mounted emblem .

24585:
A looting bag note is an item that can be purchased at Justine's stuff for the Last Shopper Standing for 1 Last Man Standing point. It can be used on a banker or bank booth/chest in exchange for a looting bag.

As players cannot own more than one looting bag, looting bag notes can act as backup bags should the player lose their looting bag.

When read, the note reads: The Bank of RuneScape promises to pay the bearer, on demand, one Looting Bag, provided the bearer is eligible to receive one. Use this Note on a bank booth to exchange it.
24587:
A rune pouch note is an item that can be purchased at Justine's stuff for the Last Shopper Standing for 75 Last Man Standing points. It can be used on a banker, Grand Exchange Clerk, or bank booth/chest in exchange for a rune pouch.

As players cannot own more than one rune pouch, rune pouch notes can act as backup pouches should the player lose their rune pouch. In addition, they are tradeable, whereas rune pouches themselves are not.
24589:
A blighted manta ray is a manta ray variant that can only be eaten inside the Wilderness, Ferox Enclave, Mage Arena bank, PvP worlds, Castle Wars lobby, and Clan Wars. 15 can be purchased at Justine's stuff for the Last Shopper Standing for 1 Last Man Standing point or at the Soul Wars Reward Shop for 10 Zeal Tokens.

Blighted manta rays heal 22 Hitpoints, and are considered to be among the best foods in the game.

Attempting to eat the manta ray outside the Wilderness prints the message The blighted manta ray can be eaten only in the Wilderness.
24592:
Blighted anglerfish are a variant of anglerfish that can only be eaten while inside the Wilderness, Ferox Enclave, Mage Arena bank, PvP Worlds, Castle Wars lobby, and Clan Wars. 15 can be purchased at Justine's stuff for the Last Shopper Standing for 1 Last Man Standing point or at the Soul Wars Reward Shop for 10 Zeal Tokens.

Similarly to anglerfish, blighted anglerfish can heal above maximum Hitpoints (making the maximum Hitpoints possible 121). Overheal does not apply if the player has been attacked or damaged (including zeroes) inside a PvP area within the past 16 ticks (9.6s), whether from a player, monster, or environmental source. There is a small exception: when fighting an NPC in a single-way or singles-plus combat area, you can overheal as soon as the NPC dies rather than waiting 16 ticks.
24595:
Blighted karambwan are a variant of cooked karambwan that can only be eaten while inside the Wilderness, Ferox Enclave, Mage Arena bank, PvP worlds, Castle Wars lobby, and Clan Wars healing 18 hitpoints. 12 can be purchased at Justine's stuff for the Last Shopper Standing for 1 Last Man Standing point or at the Soul Wars Reward Shop for 10 Zeal Tokens.

Unlike most other food, they can be consumed nearly instantly with no delay after consuming another food item, known as "combo eating"; this makes them a favourable item for player killing. The "combo eating" tactic can be enhanced further by drinking a dose of saradomin brew alongside a karambwan and the base food item, enabling a player to heal over 50 hitpoints very rapidly.

Attempting to eat the karambwan outside the Wilderness prints the message The blighted karambwan can be eaten only in the Wilderness.
24598:
Blighted super restore potions are a variant of super restore potion that can only be drunk while inside the Wilderness, Ferox Enclave, Mage Arena bank, PvP worlds, Castle Wars, and Clan Wars. If a Prayer cape or ring of the gods (i) is equipped, or if a Prayer cape or holy wrench is in the player's inventory, the Prayer restore increases to 8 + 27% of the player's current Prayer level, rounded down. This does not affect the rate of restoration of stats other than Prayer.

4 can be purchased at Justine's stuff for the Last Shopper Standing for 1 Last Man Standing point or at the Soul Wars Reward Shop for 10 Zeal Tokens. Unlike other potions, only the 4-dose variant is purchasable on the Grand Exchange.

Attempting to drink the potion outside the Wilderness prints the message The blighted potion can be used only in the Wilderness. However, the potion will act like a regular super restore potion in PvP worlds, which can be useful for Ironman accounts with limited access to prayer-restoring potions.

24607:
Blighted ancient ice sacks are an item that allows players to cast any ice spell within their Magic level without needing the runes for it. However, it can only be used inside the Wilderness, Ferox Enclave, Mage Arena bank, PvP worlds, Castle Wars, Clan Wars, and Soul Wars, and the Ancient Magicks spellbook must be active.

30 can be purchased at Justine's stuff for the Last Shopper Standing for 1 Last Man Standing point or at the Soul Wars Reward Shop for 10 Zeal Tokens.

Blighted ancient ice sacks function like runes, meaning having one in the inventory allows an ice spell to be cast via the spellbook. This also means autocasting with Ancient Magicks staves is an option.
24609:
Blighted bind sacks were an item that allowed players to cast Bind without needing the runes for it. However, it can only be used inside the Wilderness while on the standard spellbook.

300 could be purchased at Justine's stuff for the Last Shopper Standing for 1 Last Man Standing point or from Soul Wars Reward Shop for 10 zeal tokens.

Upon its removal, blighted entangle sack was given its function.
24611:
Blighted snare sacks were an item that allowed players to cast Snare without needing the runes for it. However, it could only be used inside the Wilderness while on the standard spellbook.

150 could be purchased at Justine's stuff for the Last Shopper Standing for 1 Last Man Standing point or at the Soul Wars Reward Shop for 10 zeal tokens.

Upon its removal, blighted entangle sack was given its function.
24613:
A blighted entangle sack is an item that allows players to cast Entangle, Snare, or Bind without needing the runes for it. However, it can only be used inside the Wilderness, Ferox Enclave, Mage Arena bank, PvP worlds, Castle Wars, Clan Wars, and Soul Wars, while on the standard spellbook. It is consumed upon cast, regardless of a successful hit.

A sack of 70 casts can be purchased at Justine's stuff for the Last Shopper Standing for 1 Last Man Standing point. They can also be purchased from Nomad with 10 Zeal Tokens earned from Soul Wars.
24615:
A blighted teleport spell sack is an item that allows players to cast Tele Block and Teleport to Target without needing the runes for it. However, it can only be used inside the Wilderness , and the spells still require level 85 Magic . Tele Block still requires using the Standard spellbook . It is consumed upon use.

50 can be purchased at Justine's stuff for the Last Shopper Standing for 1 Last Man Standing point or at the Soul Wars Reward Shop for 10 Zeal Tokens .
24617:
Vesta's blighted longsword is an untradeable sword that can be purchased at Justine's stuff for the Last Shopper Standing for 300 Last Man Standing points. It requires 75 Attack both to wield it and to purchase it from the reward shop.

The sword is inactive upon purchase, and must be activated by using 50,000,000 coins on it. Once activated, it becomes equipable, sharing the same stats and special attack as its other variants. However, the blighted longsword can only be used on a Bounty Hunter world while in the Wilderness, or on any world within the following locations: inside Daimon's Crater, Castle Wars, Clan Wars, Soul Wars, the TzHaar Fight Pit, and both the player-owned house and Clan Hall combat rings. This restriction applies to both PvM and PvP combat activities.

If the owner of this sword dies with it in PvP, the sword is lost on death and dropped as 50,000,000 coins if not one of the player's protected items. This is also the case while partaking in the Bounty Hunter activity, unlike the mini-game specific version of Vesta's longsword, which is kept in its inactive form on death.

In regards to Items Kept on Death, the activated Vesta's blighted longsword has a value of 50,000,000 coins. It cannot be uncharged to return the coins once activated; you must die in the Wilderness with it to return the coins, but the sword will be lost in the process.

24623:
The divine battlemage potion is a stat-boosting potion that increases the player's Magic level by 4, and the player's Defence level by 5 + 15% of the player's Defence level for 5 minutes. During these 5 minutes, the player's Magic and Defence levels will not drain below the maximum boost of the potion. Although natural stat drain is disabled, a player's stats can still be decreased or increased by the use of other spells and potions.

Once the 5 minutes are over, any stats normally boosted by the potion will be reduced back to their base level; Preserve does not affect the duration of the potion. Drinking this potion will also damage the player by 10 Hitpoints. Trying to drink the potion with less than 11 Hitpoints will instead prompt the message: You need more than 10 hitpoints to survive the power of a divine potion.

Players are unable to cast Boost Potion Share to share the effect across a group of players.

It is created by using crystal dust on a battlemage potion, requiring 86 Herblore.

Mixing divine battlemage potions yields 0.5 experience per dose.

24650:
Logs are a unique variant of logs that can only be obtained on Tutorial Island . They are obtained by cutting down a Tutorial Island tree . The Survival Expert teaches the player how to cut down the trees using a bronze axe; they must obtain some logs and burn them in order to proceed to the next part of the tutorial.

A second variant of the logs can be obtained from the alternate Tutorial Island available to some players in 2020.
24652:
Raw shrimps are a unique variant of raw shrimps that can only be obtained on Tutorial Island. They are obtained by fishing at a Tutorial Island fishing spot. The Survival Expert teaches the player how to fish for shrimp using a small fishing net; they must catch and cook some shrimp in order to proceed to the next part of the tutorial.

A second variant of the raw shrimps could be obtained from the alternate Tutorial Island available to some players in 2020.
24655:
Bones are a unique variant of bones that can only be obtained on Tutorial Island . They can be obtained by killing Giant rats , but this is not required to progress in the tutorial.

A second variant of the bones could be obtained from the alternate Tutorial Island available to some players in 2020.
24656:
The Olmlet is a pet obtained from the Chambers of Xeric . It is a much smaller version of the Great Olm , with its body fully visible. Players have a 1/53 chance of receiving the pet when they receive an item from the unique drop table after killing the Great Olm.

The olmlet is able to metamorphose into five other pets which are smaller versions of the other bosses encountered inside the Chambers of Xeric, which requires using metamorphic dust on it. The dust can be acquired from the Chambers' Challenge Mode version and clearing it under a specific time.

When a player receives the pet, it will automatically try to appear as their follower. At the same time, a message in the chatbox will state You have a funny feeling like you're being followed. However, if a player receives a pet while having a follower out (for example, a cat ), it will be placed into their inventory . When this occurs, the message in the chatbox will instead state You feel something weird sneaking into your backpack.

If a player's inventory is full and they have a follower already, they will not receive the pet; it must instead be claimed from Probita in East Ardougne .

On death , if a player loses their pet (as a follower or in your inventory) it will wander around the area for 30 seconds before despawning. Even if the player returns in time, the pet cannot be picked up, and can be reclaimed from Probita.
24658:
The Olmlet is a pet obtained from the Chambers of Xeric . It is a much smaller version of the Great Olm , with its body fully visible. Players have a 1/53 chance of receiving the pet when they receive an item from the unique drop table after killing the Great Olm.

The olmlet is able to metamorphose into five other pets which are smaller versions of the other bosses encountered inside the Chambers of Xeric, which requires using metamorphic dust on it. The dust can be acquired from the Chambers' Challenge Mode version and clearing it under a specific time.

When a player receives the pet, it will automatically try to appear as their follower. At the same time, a message in the chatbox will state You have a funny feeling like you're being followed. However, if a player receives a pet while having a follower out (for example, a cat ), it will be placed into their inventory . When this occurs, the message in the chatbox will instead state You feel something weird sneaking into your backpack.

If a player's inventory is full and they have a follower already, they will not receive the pet; it must instead be claimed from Probita in East Ardougne .

On death , if a player loses their pet (as a follower or in your inventory) it will wander around the area for 30 seconds before despawning. Even if the player returns in time, the pet cannot be picked up, and can be reclaimed from Probita.
24660:
Massive storage units can be built in resource rooms within the Chambers of Xeric . It allows players to store, for the duration of the raid, 1,500 items that are found only within the Chambers and 120 of the player's personal items. It requires a Construction level of 99 in order to build.

Note: Players who leave the Chambers with their personal items still stored in the storage units can retrieve them from the private storage unit next to the bank chest on the Mountain. The private storage unit must be emptied before players re-enter the Chambers of Xeric.
