Soft clay pack is an item pack containing 100 noted soft clay. It is obtainable from Prospector Percy's Nugget Shop in the Motherlode Mine for 10 golden nuggets, from Belona's Mining Guild Mineral Exchange for 10 unidentified minerals, or from Dusuri's Star Shop for 150 stardust.

When purchasing clay packs, gold nuggets and minerals are worth 1,160, and stardust is worth 77.33.

The packs are exclusive to the stores they are bought from and therefore cannot be sold to another store in exchange for a different currency.

Essence packs are an unobtainable item which contain 100 pure essence when opened. There are two variants of this item, the first being a generic item pack intended to be purchased with coins , and the second intended to be purchased with stardust via Dusuri's Star Shop .

Essence packs were offered as a purchasable item from Dusuri's Star Shop in the Shooting Stars poll , though it only received 73.4% support, 1.6% short of the votes required to pass. As the developer creating Shooting Stars was unaware of the first version's existence, a second version of the item was created and subsequently removed from the shop after the item failed to pass the poll, which is why two variants of the item exist.

A bag full of gems is a bag that contains an assortment of 40 noted uncut gems . These bags are obtainable from Prospector Percy's Nugget Shop for 40 golden nuggets , from Belona 's Mining Guild Mineral Exchange for 20 unidentified minerals , or from Dusuri's Star Shop for 300 stardust .

The chances of an individual gem being an uncut onyx is 1/100,000,000, making the chance per bag approximately 1/2,500,000. In terms of probability, this makes it one of the rarest drops in the game. [ 1 ]

Obtaining the uncut onyx from a bag full of gems does produce an entry in the Collection Log .

The bags are exclusive to the stores they are bought from and therefore cannot be sold to another store in exchange for a different currency.

The celestial ring is a mining enhancer from the Shooting Stars activity, purchased from Dusuri's Star Shop for 2,000 stardust .

Whether or not the ring is charged, it provides players an invisible +4 boost to Mining ; this stacks with both visible and invisible boosts. This bonus does not allow the player to receive ores higher than their level range or deal more damage within the Path of Het puzzle room.

The ring can be combined with an elven signet at a singing bowl , alongside 100 crystal shards and 1,000 stardust , to create the celestial signet , which combines the effects of both. Doing so requires level 70 Smithing and Crafting ; if the player does not meet the Smithing and Crafting requirements, they can have Conwenna or Reese sing the crystal for them for an extra 50 crystal shards, for a total of 150.

The celestial signet is a mining enhancer that possesses the effects of the celestial ring and the elven signet . Players can create one via a singing bowl by combining a celestial ring, elven signet, 100 crystal shards , and 1,000 stardust . Doing so requires level 70 Smithing and Crafting to sing the crystal (the levels can be boosted ), and grants 5,000 experience in both skills. If the player does not meet the Smithing and Crafting requirements, they can have Conwenna or Reese sing the crystal for them for an extra 50 crystal shards, for a total of 150.

Players can configure the charges while the signet is in their bank by right-clicking on Configure-Charges, as long as players have the required materials.

Players can charge the ring with stardust, with each one added giving one charge (up to a maximum of 10,000). Crystal shards cannot be used. Uncharging the signet will return all charges that were remaining in the ring.

25561:
A stuffed big harpoonfish is obtained by bringing a big harpoonfish and 3,500 coins to the taxidermist in Canifis ; this process is reversible by selecting the "Unstuff" option on the item.

At level 66 Construction , it can be mounted at a teak or mahogany display within the skill hall in a player-owned house , granting 59 Construction and 239 Fishing experience .

To mount the stuffed big harpoonfish, enter building mode in your Player-owned house and first build a fishing trophy space (not to be confused with the head trophy space ) in your skill hall . Once built, use the stuffed fish on the display. With the new menu open, right click the stuffed fish in your inventory and select "mount."

Raw harpoonfish are fish that can be fished from fishing spots in Tempoross Cove. During the fight with Tempoross, they are used as ammunition for harpoonfish cannons. They can be cooked at the shrine, which allows them to drain Tempoross' energy more than raw ones. Catching a harpoonfish grants 5 points during the Tempoross fight.

Note: You can use Tempoross harpoonfish in order to perform the initial bare-handed fishing task from Otto Godblessed.
25565:
Harpoonfish are obtained by cooking raw harpoonfish. They are used as ammunition for the harpoonfish cannons during the fight against Tempoross. Cooked harpoonfish drain Tempoross' energy more than raw harpoonfish, as well as giving more points. They cannot be burnt.

According to the Spirit anglers research notes, "cooking the Harpoonfish, while doing nothing for the edibility, does harden the bill, making them even more effective when used as ammunition."
25566:
Crystallised harpoonfish are fish that can be fished from fishing spots in Tempoross Cove. While fishing with a crystal harpoon, there is a 1 in 3 chance that players will catch a crystallised harpoonfish instead of a raw one.

During the fight with Tempoross, they are used as ammunition for harpoonfish cannons. Crystallised harpoonfish drains Tempoross' energy as much as raw ones, and cannot be cooked. While this means players will get fewer points over the course of the fight, players will instead receive 20% more Fishing experience from using them as ammunition.

Spirit anglers research notes is a book found by searching the book table in the small ruined building in the centre of the Ruins of Unkah.

The research notes contain the Spirit Angler's theories and observations on Tempoross.
25571: Damp eggs are found in a crate in the south-west corner of the large ruined temple in the Ruins of Unkah . The crate can be distinguished by it being the only crate in the ruins with a "Search" option. The damp egg cannot be used as a substitute for regular eggs in Cooking .
25574:
The tome of water is a book held in place of a shield that is a possible reward from Tempoross . The tome of water requires level 50 in Magic to wield.

The tome is only tradeable when empty. When it is empty its only function is its magic attack and magic defence equipment bonuses.

Empty tomes can be traded in for 25 soaked pages per tome (value of 75,900 ) by speaking to the retired sailor . Non- ironmen players are recommended to sell excess tomes on the Grand Exchange instead, as they are far more valuable when sold to other players.

25578:
Soaked pages are a possible catch from fishing at the reward pool with the reward permits from subduing Tempoross, or created at the Book of Storms with desiccated pages and level 50 Runecraft. They are used to charge the tome of water, which gives it additional effects.

Each soaked page adds 20 charges to the tome, and one charge is consumed when any combat spell from the standard spellbook requiring water runes is cast with the tome equipped. Each consumed charge increases damaging spells' accuracy and damage by 10%, non-damaging spells' accuracy by 20%, and curse spells' stat drain effects by 50%. Casting non-combat standard spells, or any spell from other spellbooks requiring water runes, will provide infinite runes and not consume any charges, including Ice spells. Players may remove the pages from the tome should they wish to do so.

An empty tome of water, fish barrel, tackle box, or big harpoonfish can be traded in to the Retired sailor for 25 soaked pages each.
25580:
The tackle box can be obtained from fishing at the reward pool with the reward permits gained from subduing Tempoross, or purchased from Flakes 'n' Flotsam for 6,000 spirit flakes. The tackle box can be used to store various fishing equipment. It is not possible to use the items whilst they are in the tackle box; for example, players must still have a fishing rod and Sandworms in their inventory to fish Anglerfish even if they have a tackle box with the items stored in their inventory. Additionally, items cannot be stored in the tackle box while in noted form.

While the bank interface is open and the tackle box is in the inventory, players can select the "Use" right-click option to automatically have all unnoted supported items in the inventory deposited into the tackle box. Noted items will not be stored in the tackle box this way.

On a PvP death, tradeable items stored in the tackle box (such as bait) are saved as long as the tackle box is one of the protected items.

Players may have more than one tackle box at the same time, despite the reward pool having a duplicate prevention, by purchasing them from Flakes 'n' Flotsam. However, the items will share their inventory.
25582:
The fish barrel is an item that can be obtained from the reward pool in the Ruins of Unkah after defeating Tempoross, or purchased from Flakes 'n' Flotsam for 6,000 spirit flakes. The barrel is able to store a combined total of 28 raw fish of any type except for harpoonfish (from Tempoross), stackable fish, trophy fish, and fish caught in the Chambers of Xeric, Ruins of Camdozaal, or Neypotzli. Players can right-click to open the barrel, which will have raw fish that the player acquires be automatically placed inside the barrel, providing there is space for it. Players can check the contents of the barrel by selecting the "Check" right-click option, which tells the amount and type of raw fish the player has inside. Note that the "Destroy" right-click option will destroy the barrel itself, not the content inside.

When the barrel is full, players can only empty it at a bank or a bank deposit box, similar to looting bags; for Ultimate Ironmen, fish can be withdrawn by using the barrel on an appropriate bank stand. When this occurs, players will get a message in the chatbox stating: "The barrel is full. It may be emptied at a bank."

Upon death to an NPC, the barrel will drop to the ground with all of its contents still stored. It is also always kept on death if killed by another player in the Wilderness. This makes the fish barrel especially useful if fishing raw dark crabs from the Resource Area, as any fish stored in the barrel will be kept on death and denied to potential player killers, since the barrel is protected above dark crabs and dark fishing bait.

Players can combine the barrel with a fish sack to create the fish sack barrel, which is an equipable version of the fish barrel. There is no confirmation message when this occurs, but it can be split apart by selecting the "Dismantle" option after right-clicking "Configure".

Players may have more than one barrel at the same time, despite the reward pool having a duplicate prevention, by purchasing them from Flakes 'n' Flotsam. However, the items will share their inventory.

25585:
The fish sack barrel is made by using a fish sack on a fish barrel. It is an equipable version of the fish barrel and has the same functions; players can use the right-click options "Open" and "Close" to open and close the barrel, respectively. When opened, any raw fish that the player picks up or catches will automatically be placed inside the barrel, provided there is space for it.

Rather than a right-click "Check" option that the fish barrel has, the fish sack barrel has a right-click "Configure" option that prompts the player to either check the barrel's contents or to dismantle the item, which splits the item back into a fish sack and fish barrel.

For Ultimate Ironmen, fish can be withdrawn by using the barrel on an appropriate bank stand.

This item can be stored in the magic wardrobe of a costume room. However, if the player already has a fish sack stored, it cannot be stored, instead receiving the message "The store already contains an equivalent item".

25588:
Spirit flakes are a fishing enhancer item received from looting the reward pool after defeating Tempoross. They can be stored in a tackle box.

They are used in Fishing to give a 50% chance of yielding double catch everywhere (with some exceptions), at the cost of one flake per fish caught, although no additional experience is given. This effect stacks with Rada's blessing allowing for an additional 2%-8% chance of catching double the fish, depending on which tier of the Kourend & Kebos Diary the player has completed.

When using the infernal harpoon with spirit flakes, any extra fish caught has a separate independent chance to be cooked.

Players will always lose a flake per fish caught, regardless of whether they get a single or double catch. Spirit flakes do not increase the rate at which bait is consumed, nor replace the need for other forms of bait. For example, catching trout/salmon via fly fishing will still require feathers in addition to spirit flakes. Non-fish catches (for example, seaweed, leather gloves, and leather boots) and tertiary items such as big fish are also eligible for the spirit flakes' double catch effect.

Spirit flakes cannot activate with only one empty inventory slot remaining as it would not be able to fit a second fish.

1,200 spirit flakes can be exchanged to upgrade a piece of the angler's outfit to its spirit version by talking to Gita Prymes (4,800 spirit flakes for the full set). Additionally 3,000 spirit flakes can be used on the heron pet to change it into the great blue heron. 6,000 Spirit flakes can be used to purchase the fish barrel and tackle box from Flakes 'n' Flotsam (12,000 for the both).

Player who wish to spend their extra spirit flakes without fishing can trade them at Flakes 'n' Flotsam for either extra barrels or tackle boxes and exchange them at the retired sailor for 25 soaked pages, making each spirit flake worth 12.65.
25590: Caskets are a possible catch from fishing at the reward pool with the reward permits gained from subduing Tempoross .

The heron is a members-only skilling pet that can be obtained while training Fishing. The chances of getting it are dependent on the player's Fishing level, and the time it takes to gather a resource.

A heron can be turned into a great blue heron by feeding it 3,000 spirit flakes. The recolouring can be reversed by feeding the great blue heron any raw fish, while one spirit flake can be used to turn it back to blue.

When a player receives the pet, it will automatically try to appear as their follower. At the same time, a message in the chatbox will state You have a funny feeling like you're being followed. However, if a player receives a pet while having a follower out (for example, a cat), it will be placed into their inventory. When this occurs, the message in the chatbox will instead state You feel something weird sneaking into your backpack. This message also occurs if there is one last inventory space while the player already has a pet following them, in which case the pet will appear in the inventory instead and the resource dropped to the ground.

On death, if a player loses their pet (as a follower or in your inventory) it will wander around for 30 seconds before disappearing completely. It can then be reclaimed from Probita in East Ardougne.

Gregg's eastdoor is an item that can be obtained from participating in any Easter event, and was first obtained from the 2021 Easter event. It is a two-handed fun weapon, with a similar equipped stance to the Dinh's bulwark. However, it does not share its attack styles with the Bulwark, instead having regular blunt attack styles.

Gregg's eastdoor has the lowest attack speed out of any fun weapon, but is outclassed by the cursed goblin hammer in terms of dealing the least damage.

If destroyed, a replacement can be obtained from Diango in Draynor Village or from the toy box of a costume room.

If destroyed, a replacement can be obtained from Diango in Draynor Village or from the toy box of a costume room.

A heat-proof vessel is a water container given to the player by Petrified Pete upon entering the Volcanic Mine . It can be equipped in the weapon slot. It has 36 uses per game, and can be used to throw water onto the lava, creating platforms which players can walk on. These platforms will melt after 90 seconds, giving players limited time to stand on them. If players remain on the hardened lava when it melts, they will fall into the lava, taking massive damage.

The water can only be thrown while the player is facing north, east, south, and west. Additionally, the water canteen can be right-clicked to open a dialogue box to throw water in a specified direction, or right-clicked while it is equipped to select the direction the player wants to throw it at.

Players can pay Petrified Pete 10,000 Volcanic Mine points to have him upgrade their vessel to hold more water, increasing the number of uses per game from 36 to 72. The Collection Log and Petrified Pete's Ore Shop interfaces refer to this upgrade as "Large water container".

25625:
The Barronite mace is a crush melee weapon that can be obtained within the Ruins of Camdozaal, requiring 40 Attack to wield. Its bonuses are comparable to that of a rune mace, but it provides higher melee strength and crush accuracy bonuses at the cost of a lower prayer bonus. It also has a 15% damage and accuracy bonus against golems, including those within the dungeon. Unlike regular metal maces, the barronite mace offers blunt rather than spiked attack styles, which means it can only be used for crush attacks, despite having a notable stab accuracy bonus. For free-to-play and low level players, this mace is a good alternative to the rune scimitar when fighting golems thanks to its golembane effect and it is the second-best free-to-play weapon in most other situations, outperforming the rune sword in both strength and attack bonus. For those with membership, the golembane effect stacks with the black mask or slayer helmet effect while on a Gargoyle slayer task.

When lost during PvM, the mace goes to the gravestone and does not require repair. In a PvP death, the mace will be broken and will require 10,500 coins fee to be repaired, while the killer will receive 10,500 coins as additional loot.

The mace can be crafted by handing 3 distinct pieces of the mace to Ramarno along with 1,500 barronite shards. Note that the shards already stored in the Sacred Forge shop will not count towards these 1,500; one would have to Empty the forge to get the shards back. Activating the luck buff from Ramarno for 3,000 Barronite shards will give a 5% boost of getting the following 3 parts. The required pieces include:

Barronite guard, obtained from killing golems within the dungeon.

Barronite head, obtained from crushing barronite deposits.

Barronite handle, obtained from fishing within the dungeon.

The mace can be exchanged for 500 Barronite shards by showing it to Ramarno.
25631:
A steak sandwich is a food item that heals 6 Hitpoints and can be made during Below Ice Mountain. It is made by using bread on cooked meat with a knife in the inventory after learning the recipe from the cook in the Blue Moon Inn near Varrock's south gate.

It is given to Marley to convince him to meet up with Willow. If the player has not yet given a sandwich to Marley, there will be a confirmation dialogue if the player tries to eat it.

More sandwiches can be made during and after the quest. If the player uses the knife on the bread but has not yet learned the recipe and has started the Freeing Pirate Pete subquest of Recipe For Disaster, they will turn the bread into breadcrumbs instead of making a sandwich.
25633:
The Imcando hammer is a wieldable variant of a hammer mostly used for Smithing , Crafting , or Construction . It can be obtained through smashing barronite deposits on the barronite crusher in the Ruins of Camdozaal after completing the Below Ice Mountain quest .

When first obtained, the hammer will be in a broken state. The broken hammer can be fixed by using it on Ramarno , who will repair it for 1,250 barronite shards. Once repaired, it can be used as a hammer, both while equipped and unequipped, in any way that a normal hammer can be used.

The Imcando hammer is especially useful in a few situations:

The hammer can be swapped via the "Swap" option, converting it to its off-hand variant so that it can be equipped in the shield slot . This allows it to be equipped alongside Amy's saw , a mist battlestaff , an equippable harpoon , or a pickaxe when doing the aforementioned activities.

This item can be stored in the magic wardrobe of a costume room . Both the normal and off-hand variant can be stored in the magic wardrobe at the same time. Unwanted broken hammers can be exchanged at Ramarno for 350 barronite shards, while the fixed hammer can be exchanged for 500 barronite shards.
25635:
The barronite head is one of the three parts of the barronite mace, obtained from smashing barronite deposits on the Barronite Crusher in the Ruins of Camdozaal's next to Ramarno. When obtained, the message There's a Barronite Head inside! will be displayed.

Alongside 1,500 barronite shards, a barronite guard, and barronite handle, it can be restored to a barronite mace by Ramarno. Alternatively, the head can be exchanged for 100 barronite shards by showing it to Ramarno, or it can be turned into coins via alchemy spells if extra shards are not needed.

Activating the Charm of Luck buff from Ramarno for 3,000 barronite shards will give a 5% boost of getting this item.
25637:
The barronite handle is one of the three parts of the barronite mace, found while fishing at a fishing spot in the Ruins of Camdozaal. When obtained, the message You fished out a Barronite Handle! will be displayed. Note that the handle cannot be obtained from the frogspawn fishing spots in Camdozaal.

Alongside 1,500 barronite shards, a barronite head, and barronite guard, it can be restored to a barronite mace by Ramarno. Alternatively, the handle can be exchanged for 100 barronite shards by showing it to Ramarno, or it can be turned into coins via alchemy spells if extra shards are not needed.

The fastest way to obtain a barronite handle is small net fishing. Offering fish to the altar does not provide any rolls on the drop table, so if only seeking the handle, it is more efficient to just drop the fish and continue fishing.

Activating the Charm of Luck buff from Ramarno for 3,000 barronite shards will give a 5% boost of getting this item.

The Imcando hammer is a wieldable variant of a hammer mostly used for Smithing , Crafting , or Construction . It can be obtained through smashing barronite deposits on the barronite crusher in the Ruins of Camdozaal after completing the Below Ice Mountain quest .

When first obtained, the hammer will be in a broken state. The broken hammer can be fixed by using it on Ramarno , who will repair it for 1,250 barronite shards. Once repaired, it can be used as a hammer, both while equipped and unequipped, in any way that a normal hammer can be used.

The Imcando hammer is especially useful in a few situations:

The hammer can be swapped via the "Swap" option, converting it to its off-hand variant so that it can be equipped in the shield slot . This allows it to be equipped alongside Amy's saw , a mist battlestaff , an equippable harpoon , or a pickaxe when doing the aforementioned activities.

This item can be stored in the magic wardrobe of a costume room . Both the normal and off-hand variant can be stored in the magic wardrobe at the same time. Unwanted broken hammers can be exchanged at Ramarno for 350 barronite shards, while the fixed hammer can be exchanged for 500 barronite shards.

Simple lockboxes are boxes found within the Camdozaal Vault , typically found closer towards the vault's exit. Players must exit the vault before the one minute timer runs out to keep their lockboxes; otherwise, they will lose all lockboxes they have acquired whilst inside. Lockboxes the player was carrying before entering the vault will not be lost.

Simple lockboxes have a 1/25 chance to roll the gear drop table, which contains weapons and armour ranging from iron to adamant. The gear sub-table can only be rolled once per lockbox, with any subsequent hits to it being rerolled until a "standard" item is awarded instead.

Raw guppies are a type of fish found only at fishing spots within the Ruins of Camdozaal. In order to catch this fish, players require level 7 in Fishing and a small fishing net. Each catch grants 8 Fishing experience.

Unlike other fish, guppies are not eaten and are instead prepared at the preparation table for ritual offerings at the mysterious altar, requiring level 7 Cooking and granting 12 experience when successful. Players may ruin the guppy during preparation, resulting in a ruined guppy; the chance of failure while preparing these will decrease as players reach higher Cooking levels.

Guppies stop being ruined at 42 Cooking. However, players can reduce this to 36 Cooking if they purchase the Preparation buff from Ramarno's Shard Exchange for 2500 Barronite shards.

Raw guppies cannot be fed to a kitten and will not be stolen by the naughty gull.

Barronite shards are collected throughout the Ruins of Camdozaal, below the Ice Mountain. They are the fuel for the Sacred Forge and are thus currency for Ramarno's Shard Exchange, which has several different buffs that apply when performing actions inside the ruins.

Four to six shards are gained per mining action, which can also occasionally yield a barronite deposit that can be crushed on the anvil near Ramarno for more shards.

Barronite shards can also be stored in the Sacred Forge, either directly or by using the shards on Ramarno. While stored in the forge, the shards can be used as fuel to gain entrance to the Camdozaal Vault or spent in Ramarno's Shard Exchange. Upon entering the Camdozaal Vault, 750 Barronite shards are deducted from the Sacred Forge.

A barronite mace can be crafted by handing a barronite guard, a barronite head, a barronite handle, and 1,500 Barronite shards to Ramarno. Shards stored in the Sacred Forge will not count towards this.

Members can use a broken Imcando hammer on Ramarno to repair it at a cost of 1,250 Barronite shards. As with the mace, shards already stored in the Sacred Forge will not count towards this.

Buying all 5 permanent buffs from Ramarno's Shard Exchange, crafting one barronite mace, and repairing one Imcando hammer requires 15,750 barronite shards in total.
25684:
Barronite deposits are found whilst mining barronite rocks within the Ruins of Camdozaal. Each deposit mined yields 32 Mining experience. Mining barronite does not consume celestial ring charges, but the +4 invisible Mining boost still applies.

Using them on the Barronite Crusher anvil, near Ramarno, with a hammer yields 30 Smithing experience and various rewards, including barronite shards.

The globe can be handed to Curator Haig Halen at the Varrock Museum for 1 Kudos and 200 coins. Players will receive 100 coins for additional ancient globes. When given to the curator for the first time, he will comment " This Ancient globe seems to show new constellations. What a discovery! "

Mind cores are the corrupted cores of Mind Golems, imbued with the power of the Mind Altar. They can be used in place of rune or pure essence, but only for crafting mind runes. Each core gives 55 Runecraft experience and 11 mind runes.

Like regular essence, the amount of mind runes crafted will increase with the player's Runecraft level; for example, each mind core will craft 55 mind runes at level 56 Runecraft.

Golem cores cannot be placed in essence pouches. If players attempt to store them in one, a chatbox message will appear, stating The golem core is too big to fit in an essence pouch.

The Charm of Luck buff purchasable from Ramarno's Shard Exchange does affect the drop chance of the core.
25698:

Like regular essence, the amount of body runes crafted will increase with the player's Runecraft level; for example, each body core will craft 33 body runes at level 92 Runecraft.

Golem cores cannot be placed in essence pouches . If players attempt to store them in one, a chatbox message will appear, stating The golem core is too big to fit in an essence pouch.

25700:
Chaos cores are the corrupted cores of Chaos Golems, imbued with the power of the Chaos Altar. They can be used in place of pure essence, but only for crafting chaos runes. They act as if the player was carrying eleven essence instead of one, meaning each core gives 85 Runecraft experience and 11 chaos runes or 2,380 Runecraft experience and 308 chaos runes for a complete inventory.

Like regular essence, the amount of chaos runes crafted will increase with the player's Runecraft level; each chaos core will craft 22 chaos runes at level 74 Runecraft.

Golem cores cannot be placed in essence pouches. If players attempt to store them in one, a chatbox message will appear, stating "The golem core is too big to fit in an essence pouch." Furthermore, cores cannot be taken through the altar portals at Guardians of the Rift.

The Charm of Luck buff purchasable from Ramarno's Shard Exchange does affect the drop chance of the core.

A chaos core is used in the quest Defender of Varrock on a Barronite deposit to create an Imbued barronite.

Ungael lab notes are a compilation of old notes obtained from the laboratory beneath Ungael . Players must have all six old notes from the laboratory in order to combine them.

Written by Zorgoth , a dragonkin , the notes contain comments on his experiments to enhance the strength and aggressiveness of dragons in order to turn the tide on the war on humanity during the Fourth Age . The notes on Ungael indicate that Zorgoth had begun switching to blue dragons for his experiments, resulting in the creation of his vorkath , a word for "pathetic failure" in the Dragonkin language. In addition, he speculates that the Stone of Jas or a similar artefact may have once been present on the island, as he could sense its residual energy.

If lost, it can be reclaimed from a bookcase within a player-owned house .
25704:
Lithkren vault notes are a compilation of old notes obtained from the Lithkren Vault. Players must have all seven old notes from the Lithkren Vault in order to combine them, four of which can only be obtained after completion of Dragon Slayer II.

Written by Zorgoth, a dragonkin, the notes were first written during the attack on Lithkren in the Dragonkin Conflicts, and more written after he became trapped inside the vault. The notes contain comments on his experiments to create his ultimate weapon, Galvek, alongside exploration of a side project that resulted in the creation of the adamant and rune dragons.

If lost, it can be reclaimed from a bookcase within a player-owned house.

The dusty note is an item found by searching the skeleton in the south-west part of the Tower of Magic prison during Tale of the Righteous. Although the item is optional, it provides instructions on how to solve the puzzle to open the gates that lead the player to the skeleton with the "investigate" option.

After investigating the skeleton, it will yield the message, "You notice some writing carved into the floor beside the skeleton: 'Lizards on the mountain. Do not trust the King. The altar is a lie.' " In a previous update, investigating the skeleton would instead give the player a dusty note with the message about the lizards being on the mountain and the king being untrustworthy instead of the current dusty note with the puzzle's instructions. The note can be kept after the quest, but it can no longer be reobtained as it serves no purpose beyond the quest.

Regular runes could not be used for this purpose since they are stackable, and therefore stack quantities would display next to each piece on the board. The actual items cannot be obtained by players.

Clan vexillums are banners that players can obtain from the Clerk in the Clan Hub . Players must be in a clan to claim a clan vexillum and clan cloak . Unlike clan vexillums in RuneScape 3 , clan vexillums in Old School RuneScape cannot be placed on the ground for others to see, nor do they have any teleport options.

Bandages are a consumable item obtainable during the Theatre of Blood entry mode . They restore 20 hitpoints, 29 [ confirmation needed ] prayer points, and 20% run energy when consumed. They also cure poison, boost the player's combat stats, and provide the effect of a stamina potion .

Bandages act as a food item, and therefore delay the player's next attack when consumed during combat. They can be combo eaten with potions and/or cooked karambwan .

10 bandages can be claimed from the rewards chest after defeating the Pestilent Bloat and another 10 become available after defeating Sotetseg . The chest can only contain a maximum of 10 bandages, so uncollected bandages are deleted.

Stat boosts to Attack, Strength and Defence are one level lower than the corresponding super potion, and are calculated with: ⌊ S k i l l L e v e l × 15 100 ⌋ + 4

Ranged boost is equal to a ranging potion , and is calculated with: ⌊ S k i l l L e v e l × 1 10 ⌋ + 4
25731:
The holy Sanguinesti staff is a Sanguinesti staff with a holy ornament kit attached to it. The ornament kit gives no additional stat bonuses, but it will make the staff count as a Saradomin item in the God Wars Dungeon.

The holy Sanguinesti staff retains all the properties that the original variant has, such as its passive effect and its built-in spell, which still requires blood runes to charge.

While the staff is untradeable in its ornamented and charged state, it can be dismantled anytime, returning the ornament kit and staff. If a player loses the holy Sanguinesti staff in a PvP death, the holy ornament kit will be placed in their gravestone.

25748:
Lil' Zik is a pet that can be obtained from completing the Theatre of Blood . It is a much smaller version of Verzik Vitur 's final form. Players have a chance of receiving the pet when looting the monumental chests in Verzik's treasure vault. The drop rate is dependent on the player's performance in the raid, unaffected by that of teammates, ranging from 1/650 to 1/6,500 in regular raids and ranging from 1/500 to 1/5,000 in Hard Mode raids. The maximum rate is reached with 10 individual points (which are invisible to the players; the maximum per player is 32, or 18 if not including the MVP bonuses for each room). [ 1 ] The highest rate is reached by dying no more than twice per raid, with more deaths allowed if the player deals the most damage in some rooms, assuming participation in each room.

Lil' Zik is able to metamorphose into five other pets which are smaller versions of the other bosses encountered in the Theatre of Blood, which requires using Sanguine dust on it. The dust can be acquired from the Theatre's Hard Mode version and clearing it under a specific time.

When a player receives the pet, it will automatically try to appear as their follower. At the same time, a message in the chatbox will state You have a funny feeling like you're being followed. However, if a player receives a pet while having a follower out (for example, a cat ), it will be placed into their inventory . When this occurs, the message in the chatbox will instead state You feel something weird sneaking into your backpack.

If a player's inventory is full and they have a follower already, they will not receive the pet; it must instead be claimed from Probita in East Ardougne .

On death , if a player loses their pet (as a follower or in your inventory) it will wander around the area for 30 seconds before despawning. Even if the player returns in time, the pet cannot be picked up, and can be reclaimed from Probita.

Fiendish ashes are a 100% drop from imps and fiends. They give 10 Prayer experience when scattered, or 30 when offered via the Demonic Offering spell. It cannot be offered at the Chaos Temple or in player-owned house altars.

The Ash sanctifier will automatically purify these demonic ashes for 5 experience if the Hard Kourend & Kebos Diary has been completed and 10 experience if the Elite Kourend & Kebos Diary is completed. It is NOT recommended to use the Ash sanctifier on demonic creatures dropping these ashes as it is not cost effective.
25769:
Vile ashes are demonic ashes dropped by lesser demons , greater demons , hellhounds , bloodvelds , and mutated bloodvelds . The ashes give 25 Prayer experience when scattered normally. Members can get 75 experience when offered via the Demonic Offering spell. Ashes cannot be offered at the Ectofuntus , Chaos Temple , or at player-owned house altars .

The ash sanctifier will automatically purify these demonic ashes for 12.5 experience if the Hard Kourend & Kebos Diary has been completed and 25 experience if the Elite Kourend & Kebos Diary is completed.
25772:
Malicious ashes are a 100% drop from black demons , nechryael , and demonic gorillas . They give 65 Prayer experience when scattered, or 195 when offered via the Demonic Offering spell. It cannot be offered at the Chaos Temple or in player-owned house altars .

The ash sanctifier will automatically purify these demonic ashes for 32.5 experience if the Hard Kourend & Kebos Diary has been completed and 65 experience if the Elite Kourend & Kebos Diary is completed.
25775:
Abyssal ashes are a 100% drop from abyssal demons and the Abyssal Sire . They give 85 Prayer experience when scattered, or 255 when offered via the Demonic Offering spell. Three can be offered per cast at a time for 765 xp per cast. With a rune pouch, it requires 9 casts to clear an inventory. It cannot be offered at the Chaos Temple or in player-owned house altars .

The ash sanctifier will automatically purify these demonic ashes for 42.5 experience if the Hard Kourend & Kebos Diary has been completed, and 85 experience if the Elite Kourend & Kebos Diary is completed.
25778:
Infernal ashes are a 100% drop from various high-leveled demons . They give 110 Prayer experience when scattered, or 330 when offered via the Demonic Offering spell. It cannot be offered at the Chaos Temple or in player-owned house altars .

The ash sanctifier will automatically purify these demonic ashes for 55 experience if the Hard Kourend & Kebos Diary has been completed and 110 experience if the Elite Kourend & Kebos Diary is completed.
25781:
The ash sanctifier is a reward from completing the Hard Kourend & Kebos Diary , where players can then claim it from Tyss near the Dark Altar . To use it, it must be charged with death runes , gaining 10 charges per death rune at a cost of 19 coins per charge. The charge limit is 2,147,483,647. Players can configure the charges while the sanctifier is in their bank by right-clicking on Configure-Charges, as long as players have the required materials. Un-charging it will return the unused death runes.

When charged and carried in the inventory, the ash sanctifier will automatically purify demonic ashes that are dropped from demonic creatures upon death, granting the player half the Prayer experience they would have received from scattering the ashes themselves, or the full amount if the Elite Kourend & Kebos Diary is completed, consuming one charge in the process. This effect can be toggled with the right-click "Activity" option.

It is always kept on PvM Death. Should the player die in PvP and it is not one of their protected items, it will be sent to a gravestone . In all cases, the ash sanctifier will retain all of its charges.

The ash sanctifier will not affect bones . For this, use the Bonecrusher or Bonecrusher necklace . For spectral creatures that do not drop ashes or bones, use the Ectoplasmator .

Challenge scrolls are riddles given to players by an NPC during a Treasure Trail. Challenge scrolls appear in medium, hard, and elite clue steps. Players must solve the challenge scroll in order to advance in their Treasure Trail. The challenge scroll is not a separate step in the Treasure Trail.

The questions for the challenge scrolls are always the same. Players do not have to read the challenge scroll in order to answer the question. Players only need to talk to the NPC again after receiving the scroll to answer the answer. There are no penalties for incorrect answers.

The broken redirector is the device that players destroy during the quest The Ascent of Arceuus , in which it was responsible for redirecting energy from the Dark Altar , causing loss in power from the Dark Altar among the Citizens of Arceuus and the death of Thana .

It is obtained from Lord Trobin Arceuus during A Kingdom Divided , and is given to the Tasakaal in order to have them inspect it, where players discover the device was created by Xamphur , who had Councillor Andrews place the device nearby.

The broken redirector can be reclaimed from Lord Trobin Arceuus at Xeric's Lookout during the quest A Kingdom Divided .

25816:
The Shayzien journal is an old journal written by King Shayzien VII, who ruled Great Kourend from the 32nd to 37th decade. Recovered from the Tower of Magic during the uprising against Xeric at the end of the Age of Strife , it was sent via parcel by an unknown party to Phileas Rimor 's house, and kickstarts the events of the quest Tale of the Righteous .

During A Kingdom Divided , the journal is recovered from Lord Kandur Hosidius ' hidden office at the request of Lord Shiro Shayzien . It is revealed later in the quest that it was Lord Hosidius who had acquired the journal and sent the parcel to Phileas, while the journal players took from his office was actually just a copy with many bits removed.

When read, the chatbox message states The old journal seems to have been bound shut somehow. Maybe Lord Shayzien will know what to do with it.

The Royal Accord of Twill is the document that declared the transition of authority from the Council of Elders to the Royal Lords of the five Houses of Great Kourend , and details the rotation of succession between them.

According to the book, The Envoy to Varlamore , the document was lost at sea when it was being transported to the Grand Museum of Civitas illa Fortis , the capital of Varlamore . The Accord can be read, and a transcript of it is found in a book of the same name . Upon inspecting the original Accord, the chatbox will display a message stating Despite its age, the scroll is in near perfect condition. It's likely that some sort of magic was used to ensure it remained preserved .

The document is recovered during The Depths of Despair , and is given to Lord Kandur Hosidius at the end of the quest , who uses the original copy to push for a new Accord for Kourend's return to royal rule during A Kingdom Divided , and is safely stored in the Library Historical Archive after the quest.
25818:
The Book of the Dead is an equipable book obtained as a reward from completing A Kingdom Divided . Having it equipped or in the player's inventory is required when casting resurrection spells .

The book is an improved version of Kharedst's memoirs , and offers the same teleports. The book offers as an additional 150 charges over the memoirs, resulting in a maximum of 250 charges if all five of the pages from the original Kourend quests have been added.

If lost, the book can be reclaimed from Commander Fullore on the ground floor of the Kourend Castle . Additional copies can be purchased from Perdu for 9,500 coins each.
25820:
The antique lamp is a reward from A Kingdom Divided , two of which are received from Commander Fullore upon completing the quest . Each lamp grants 10,000 experience in a skill of the player's choosing, given that the skill is over level 40.

The lamp cannot be banked. However, if the player prefers to use it at a later date, it can be destroyed and reclaimed from Commander Fullore whenever the player wishes to do so. If you die with it in inventory Commander Fullore will grant the lamps.

Players who have completed the removed Architectural Alliance miniquest prior to 10 January 2024 without claiming an antique lamp as their reward can still do so.
25822: A protest banner is an item used during the quest A Kingdom Divided . Players can get this item by taking one from the pile outside Sophia Hughes ' house in Kingstown without needing to start the quest.
25824:
Research notes are a set of notes found in the south-easternmost table in Xamphur 's lab within the Lizardman Temple .

The notes appear to be Xamphur's research into the Dark Altar and the artefact known as as the Soul Stone . He notes that the energy of the Dark Altar matches the energy found on the Isle of Souls . He also questions if the Soul Stone is the Stone of Jas , but deems it unlikely.
25826:
The Lizardkicker is a type of ale that temporarily boosts Ranged by 4 while draining Strength and Magic by 2 + 4%. Unlike other ales, it cannot be created through brewing.

It can be purchased at The Cloak and Stagger in the city of Shayzien.

Upon drinking the ale, a message in the chatbox will state You drink the Lizardkicker. It tastes like swampwater, but you feel like your eyesight has improved slightly.
25829: An old note can be found in the Secluded Chapel south of the Giant Pit .
25831:
The Shayzia military orders is a letter obtained from searching the Broken altar in the Shayzia Ruin , just north-east of Shayzien .

The letter, addressed to Captain Tebell in Shayzia , is written by General Lern during the early days of the War of the Five Houses , detailing the removal of King Agata IV from the throne and the movements of the other four Houses of Kourend.
25833: Raw boar meat can be obtained by killing boars , found in the woods west of Kourend Castle and south of The Node . It can be cooked at level 1 Cooking , granting 30 Cooking experience if successful. After successfully cooking it, it will simply be cooked meat , while burning it will result in burnt meat (burning can be achieved at any level by cooking it twice). The raw boar meat can also be made into sinew at level 1 Cooking by using it on a range.
25836:
The Little Nightmare is a pet that can be obtained by defeating The Nightmare or Phosani's Nightmare. It is a much smaller version of her. The pet has a 1/800 drop rate in the original encounter, decreasing for every additional player in the room when the fight started: 1/1600 in a duo, 1/2400 in a trio, 1/3200 in a 4-man and 1/4000 in a 5-or-higher-man encounter. At Phosani's Nightmare, the pet has a flat 1/1400 drop rate.

The Little Nightmare is able to metamorphose into a little parasite. For Little Nightmare to be able to do so, players must use the Parasitic Egg on her, a drop acquired from Phosani's Nightmare.

When a player receives the pet, it will automatically try to appear as their follower. At the same time, a message in the chatbox will state You have a funny feeling like you're being followed. However, if a player receives a pet while having a follower out (for example, a cat), it will be placed into their inventory. When this occurs, the message in the chatbox will instead state You feel something weird sneaking into your backpack.

If a player's inventory is full and they have a follower already, they will not receive the pet; it must instead be claimed from Probita in East Ardougne.

On death, if a player loses their pet (as a follower or in your inventory) it will wander around the area for 30 seconds before despawning. Even if the player returns in time, the pet cannot be picked up, and can be reclaimed from Probita.
25837:

25838: The parasitic egg is a reward from defeating Phosani's Nightmare . Players may use the egg on the Little Nightmare to allow it to metamorphose into a parasite version of the pet.

Amethyst darts are Ranged throwing weapons. To wield them, the player must have at least 50 Ranged. They can be obtained by using the Mining , Crafting , and Fletching skills or trading with other players. Amethyst darts can be poisoned and are one-handed, so they can be wielded with a shield or god book for protection. To fletch amethyst darts, the player must have at least 90 Fletching. Amethyst dart tips are combined with feathers , awarding 21 Fletching experience per dart.

Amethyst dart tips can be crafted from amethyst , creating 8 amethyst dart tips and earning 60 Crafting experience for each mineral.

Amethyst darts have a +2 higher Ranged strength bonus compared to rune darts . The strongest dart type, dragon darts , have a +7 higher Ranged strength bonus advantage over amethyst darts. However, dragon darts are much more costly to use.

The enhanced crystal weapon seed is an enhanced version of the crystal weapon seed that can be obtained as a rare drop from the Gauntlet. With level 82 Smithing and Crafting (the levels can be boosted), it can be sung into either the Blade of Saeldor or Bow of Faerdhinen at a singing bowl. If the player does not meet the Smithing and Crafting requirements, they can have Conwenna or Reese sing the crystal for them for an extra 50 crystal shards, for a total of 150.

It can also be obtained by reverting the inactive blade or bow at a singing bowl. Reverting an inactive blade or bow requires 250 crystal shards, 82 Smithing and 82 Crafting. Conwenna and Reese can also revert the inactive blade or bow for players who don't meet the level requirements, costing an additional 125 shards, for a total of 375. There is no confirmation screen on the reversion menu.

Players can also exchange the enhanced weapon seed for 1,500 crystal shards by speaking to Amrod in Prifddinas' Hefin Inn.
25862:
The bow of Faerdhinen is a magical bow that once belonged to Faerdhinen , an elite elven warrior. It is created from an enhanced crystal weapon seed . Requiring level 80 Ranged and 70 Agility to wield, it provides the highest Ranged Attack and Ranged Strength bonus out of any weapon for its attack speed .

Like the crystal bow , the bow of Faerdhinen does not require any arrows to use, as it generates its own when fired. The bow also benefits from improved damage and accuracy when crystal armour is equipped, with each piece granting additional bonuses - up to a total of 15% damage and 30% accuracy when the full set is equipped.

On unprotected death in PvP , the inactive bow is dropped, and all shards used to charge it will be lost. In a PvM or protected on PvP death, all current charges are kept.

The bow of Faerdhinen (c) is a corrupted version of the Bow of Faerdhinen that does not degrade , with its appearance altered to resemble the corrupted crystal seen within the Corrupted Gauntlet . The bow's colours may be changed to other colours of the Elven Clans by buying crystals from Lliann's Wares in Prifddinas , which cost 500,000 coins each. It can also be reverted to its original colour by using the crystal of Hefin on any variant of the corrupted bow.

The bow can be upgraded by bringing it and 2,000 crystal shards to a singing bowl . Doing so requires level 82 Smithing and Crafting (the levels can be boosted ), and grants no experience. If the player does not meet the Smithing and Crafting requirements, they can have Conwenna or Reese sing the crystal in their stead for an extra 1,000 crystal shards. Excess charges in the bow will be taken into account; for example, a newly created bow with 10,000 charges will require 1,900 crystal shards to corrupt and a fully charged bow will only cost 1,800 crystal shards to upgrade.

Alternatively, the Bow of Faerdhinen can be corrupted passively through use: every 100 shots fired from the bow contributes 1 shard worth of progress toward the 1,900-shard corruption requirement. Once this cumulative amount is reached, the bow can be corrupted at the singing bowl with the level requirements or have Conwenna corrupt it for you for the 1000 shard price. Any combination of progress towards corruption, charges in the bow, and crystal shards can be used to meet the crystal shard requirement to corrupt the bow.

Upon creating the corrupted bow, the chatbox message states " With the help of the crystal bowl, you sing a dark song which corrupts the crystals. "

While untradeable, the bow can be uncharged, but the crystal shards used to upgrade it will not be returned.

The Masori chestplate is a piece of armour requiring 80 Ranged , 70 Hitpoints , and 30 Defence to equip, and is part of the Masori armour set. It is only available from the supplies table in an unrestricted world as a test armour for players. It is one of the proposed rewards for the Tombs of Amascut raid.

The Masori chestplate makes use of the Low Life status effect, where if players have less than 40% of their health, its Ranged Attack bonus is increased to +43, and its Ranged Strength bonus increased to +4. In addition, players also have a 3% chance to dodge an incoming attack, negating damage from any non- typeless attack; this is increased to a total of 8% when wearing the full armour set.

25973:
The Masori amulet was an amulet requiring 80 Ranged, 70 Hitpoints, and 30 Defence to equip, and was part of the Masori armour set. It was only available from the supplies table in an unrestricted world as a test armour for players. It was one of the proposed rewards for the Tombs of Amascut raid.

The Masori amulet made use of the Low Life status effect, where if players had less than 40% of their health, its Ranged Attack bonus would be increased to +17, and its Ranged Strength bonus increased to +7.

Wearing the Masori amulet would result in players taking damage for 15% of their health every three ticks (1.8 seconds); players would be warned that this would occur upon attempting to wear the amulet. This damage would persist until the player has less than 40% of their health, where the Low Life status will take effect.
25975:
The Lightbearer is a ring available from the supplies table in an unrestricted world as a test item for players. It is one of the proposed rewards for the Tombs of Amascut raid.

Having no requirements to wear, the ring regenerates the player's special attack energy twice as fast (approximately 15 seconds per 10%, or 150 seconds per 100%). Unequipping the ring will cause the special attack energy restoration timer to reset.
25979:
The Keris partisan is a one-handed melee weapon requiring 70 Attack to equip. It is only available from the supplies table in an unrestricted world as a test item for players, and is one of the proposed rewards for completing Beneath Cursed Sands.

The Keris partisan retains the effects of the Keris, dealing 33% bonus damage against all Kalphites and Scabarites, alongside a 1/51 chance of puncturing a hole in their exoskeleton, dealing triple damage. When this special effect occurs, the chatbox will display the message You slip your weapon through a gap in the creature's chitin, landing a vicious blow.

Players can attach three different jewels to the Keris partisan to give it differing effects within the Tombs of Amascut; this increases the requirement to wield them to 80 Attack. However, only the Keris partisan of breaching is available to test in the beta.

Eye of the Corrupter - Adds a damage-over-time effect to attacked enemies. Players won't be able to stack this effect multiple times onto a single NPC, but will be able to apply it to multiple NPCs at once.

Jewel of the Sun - Applies a debuff to attacked NPCs, which causes them to take higher damage for a sustained period of time.

Breach of the Scarab - Adds a 33% accuracy bonus against Kalphites and Scabarites.
25981:
The Keris partisan of breaching is a one-handed spear requiring 80 Attack to equip. It is only available from the supplies table in an unrestricted world as a test item for players, and is one of the proposed rewards for the Tombs of Amascut raid.

The Keris partisan of breaching is upgraded from the Keris partisan, which adds a 33% accuracy bonus against Kalphites and Scabarites, in addition to the original effects of Keris.
25983:
Elidinis' broken ward is a broken magical shield that is one of the proposed rewards for the Tombs of Amascut raid. It is restored into Elidinis' ward by attaching an arcane sigil to the broken ward, requiring level 90 Prayer , 90 Smithing , and 10,000 soul runes , granting 260 experience in both skills in the process. Players without the required skill levels to create the shield may ask Abbot Langley in the Edgeville Monastery to create the ward, for a fee of 20,000,000 coins.

Upon restoring Elidinis' ward, the chatbox states You fuse your Arcane sigil to Elidinis' broken ward, returning it to its former glory.

The restored ward is untradeable, but it can be dismantled to return the sigil and broken ward. However, the soul runes will not be returned.
25985:
Elidinis' ward is a restored magical shield requiring 80 Magic , Defence , and Prayer to equip. Belonging to the goddess Elidinis herself, the ward was given to Pharaoh Osmumten before disappearing to mourn the loss of her husband Tumeken at the end of the Kharidian–Zarosian War .

It is only available from the supplies table in an unrestricted world as a test item for players, and is one of the proposed rewards for the Tombs of Amascut raid. Its defence bonuses are identical to the arcane spirit shield , however it provides +5 more Magic Attack bonus and a 5% magic damage bonus, along with +1 Prayer bonus.

The ward is made by attaching an arcane sigil to the broken ward , requiring level 90 Prayer , 90 Smithing , and 10,000 soul runes , granting 260 experience in both skills in the process. Players without the required skill levels to create the shield may ask Abbot Langley in the Edgeville Monastery to create the ward, for a fee of 20,000,000 coins.

The restored ward is untradeable, but it can be dismantled to return the sigil and broken ward. However, the soul runes will not be returned.
25987:
Tumeken's heka was a proposed powered wand requiring 85 Magic to equip. It belonged to Tumeken , the head of the Menaphite Pantheon , and was given to Pharaoh Osmumten by Elidinis after his sacrifice that ended the Kharidian–Zarosian War . It was only available from the supplies table in an unrestricted world as a test item for players, and was one of the proposed rewards for the Tombs of Amascut raid.

Although Tumeken's heka passed its poll , it was proposed to be replaced by the Shadow of Tumeken in a poll blog two months later, due to continued player feedback on the desire for a magic weapon that would "redefine Magic as a combat style just as the Scythe [of Vitur] and Twisted Bow did." It was then polled in the Tombs of Amascut Reward Changes poll with the caveat that the heka would be replaced with the Shadow of Tumeken if it passed the poll; this came to pass with 90.9% support.

In order to use the wand's magic spell, it must be charged with soul and chaos runes , holding up to 20,000 charges when fully charged. Each cast requires 1 soul rune and 3 chaos runes, costing 697 coins per cast. The total cost to fully charge the wand with 20,000 soul and 60,000 chaos runes is 13,940,000 coins . Players can uncharge the wand whenever and wherever they choose, getting all of their runes back.

The Masori headdress is a piece of armour requiring 80 Ranged , 70 Hitpoints , and 30 Defence to equip, and is part of the Masori armour set. It is only available from the supplies table in an unrestricted world as a test armour for players. It is one of the proposed rewards for the Tombs of Amascut raid.

The Masori headdress makes use of the Low Life status effect, where if players have less than 40% of their health, its Ranged Attack bonus is increased to +12, and its Ranged Strength bonus increased to +1. In addition, players also have a 2% chance to dodge an incoming attack, negating damage from any non- typeless attack; this is increased to a total of 8% when wearing the full armour set.
26219:
Osmumten's fang is a stab sword requiring 82 Attack to equip. It is only available from the supplies table in an unrestricted world as a test item for players, and is one of the proposed rewards for the Tombs of Amascut raid .

It comes with a unique ability that aims to make it effective against targets with a high Defence level. This involves using a different formula to determine damage rolls; unlike other weapons that roll zero to max damage upon a successful hit , the fang uses the following formula for damage rolls: ( M a x H i t * 0.15 ) − [ M a x H i t − ( M a x H i t * 0.15 ) ]

For example, if the fang's true max hit was 60, it would roll 9 to 51 damage upon a successful hit.

Zaryte vambraces are a pair of non-degradeable vambraces requiring 80 Ranged and 50 Defence to wear. One of the proposed rewards from Nex, they are only available from the supplies table in a tournament world as a test item for players. The vambraces are the best-in-slot offensive gloves for rangers, surpassing Barrows gloves as well as being the only hands slot item to offer a Ranged Strength bonus.

When worn, Zaryte vambraces allow the Zaryte bow's passive effect to hit up to three targets within two tiles of the main target, instead of one additional target. As a Zarosian item, it will also grant god protection towards Zarosian NPCs in the God Wars Dungeon.
26237:
The Zaryte bow was a two-handed ranged weapon that would have required level 80 in Ranged to wield. It was one of the proposed rewards from Nex, and was only available from the supplies table in a tournament world as a test weapon for players. As a Zarosian item, it would have granted god protection towards Zarosian NPCs in the God Wars Dungeon.

The Zaryte bow has an attack range of nine, and is able to fire any type of arrow. In addition, the bow does not degrade, though it possesses a passive effect that consumes charges, similar to how an uncharged infernal axe acts as a regular a dragon axe.

The Zaryte bow was ultimately shelved and replaced by the Zaryte crossbow as a reward from Nex before being polled. With the later release of the Phantom Muspah, the venator bow was added to the game, with a similar design to the Zaryte bow.

The pumpkin pie is an unobtainable item used during the 2021 Halloween event . In order to distract the Cook in the Blue Moon Inn , the player orders this meal and loudly insults the food, causing the chef to leave the kitchen.

Although the item can be seen on a table during the cutscene, it cannot actually be obtained. Ending the cutscene with an empty inventory slot will cause the player to receive a pie dish .

The item could originally be bought and sold on the Grand Exchange due to an oversight, but was never listed on the Grand Exchange Database . Some people were able to obtain the Pumpkin pie through glitches, and sell it for very high prices. As a result of this exploit, it was made untradeable in a hotfix, then delisted from the Grand Exchange altogether.

With the end of the event, the pie was removed from the inventories of any players who still had them. However, they were not removed from any uncollected Grand Exchange offers, and are therefore still in the game.

An ancient brew is a potion made by using nihil dust on an unfinished dwarf weed potion, requiring 85 Herblore, yielding an ancient brew(3) and 190 Herblore experience.

A dose of ancient brew boosts the player's Magic level by 2 + 5% of their base Magic level, as well as restoring prayer points equal to 2 + 10% of their base Prayer level (with the ability to restore up to 5% over the player's base Prayer level). However, it will also drain the player's Attack, Strength, and Defence levels by 2 + 10% of their current levels.

An ancient brew can be upgraded into a forgotten brew by combining it with 20 ancient essence per dose, requiring 91 Herblore and yielding 145 Herblore experience (36.25 experience per dose).

After Barbarian Herblore Training, caviar can be added to a 2-dose ancient brew, requiring 92 Herblore, yielding an ancient mix and 63 Herblore experience. An ancient mix has 2 doses, with the same effects when consumed, and heals 6 Hitpoints.

Nexling is a pet dropped by Nex . It is a much smaller version of her.

When a player receives the pet, it will automatically try to appear as their follower. At the same time, a message in the chatbox will state You have a funny feeling like you're being followed. However, if a player receives a pet while having a follower out (for example, a cat ), it will be placed into their inventory . When this occurs, the message in the chatbox will instead state You feel something weird sneaking into your backpack.

If a player's inventory is full and they have a follower already, they will not receive the pet; it must instead be claimed from Probita in East Ardougne .

On death , if a player loses their pet (as a follower or in your inventory) it will wander around the area for 30 seconds before despawning. Even if the player returns in time, the pet cannot be picked up, and can be reclaimed from Probita.

26370:
The ancient hilt is a rare drop from Nex , in the God Wars Dungeon . Its design bears the Zarosian symbol, and was created under Nex's orders after her escape from the Ancient Prison . Though the hilt was created, it never saw usage as the four armies of the gods joined forces to imprison Nex once more before the weapon could be completed. [ 1 ]

When attached to a completed godsword blade , which can be created by combining the three Godsword shards , it creates the ancient godsword .
26372: The nihil horn is an item dropped by Nex . It is used to upgrade an Armadyl crossbow to a Zaryte crossbow , alongside 250 nihil shards .
26374:
The Zaryte crossbow is a ranged weapon that requires a Ranged level of 80 to wield, and can fire up to dragon bolts. The crossbow has an attack range of 8, and the longrange combat style will increase it by 2. It is only outclassed by the dragon hunter crossbow when fighting draconic monsters. This item counts as a Zaros item in the God Wars Dungeon.

The crossbow itself is crafted by attaching a nihil horn, obtained as a rare drop from Nex, with an Armadyl crossbow and 250 nihil shards. The Zaryte crossbow counts as a Zarosian item, but not as an Armadylean item in the God Wars Dungeon. In addition, the crossbow possesses a special attack as well as a passive effect, both of which synergise extremely well with the effects of enchanted bolts.

The Zaryte crossbow is primarily used for its special attack, which can deal a guaranteed 110 damage when used with ruby bolts (e) against high-health enemies. Additionally, it is the strongest weapon against non-draconic enemies weak to heavy Ranged attacks, such as the Leviathan.

The Torva full helm is part of the Torva armour set, requiring 80 Defence to wear. The helmet boasts the highest strength bonus of any helmet, being 2 higher than the Neitiznot faceguard and 3 higher than the serpentine helm . As a Zarosian -aligned item, Torva armour will give Zarosian protection within the God Wars Dungeon .

The helmet is created by combining a damaged Torva full helm, obtained as a drop from Nex , with one Bandosian component . This process requires level 90 Smithing , and is not reversible.
26378:
The Torva platebody is part of the Torva armour set, requiring 80 Defence to wear. The platebody boasts the highest strength bonus of any body slot equipment, being 2 higher than the oathplate chest , Bandos chestplate , Inquisitor's hauberk , fighter torso , and blood moon chestplate . As a Zarosian -aligned item, Torva armour will give Zarosian protection within the God Wars Dungeon .

The platebody is created by combining a damaged Torva platebody, obtained as a drop from Nex , with two Bandosian components . This process requires level 90 Smithing , drains the player's Strength and Prayer level temporarily, and is not reversible.

The platelegs are created by combining damaged Torva platelegs, obtained as a drop from Nex, with two Bandosian components. This process requires level 90 Smithing, and is not reversible.

26388:
Ecumenical key shards are an item dropped by Nex. 50 of these shards can be combined to create an ecumenical key, which allows entry to the chambers of the God Wars Dungeon bosses without having to obtain the 40 kill count normally required.

Players are limited to having three ecumenical keys at a time; completing the Medium and Hard Wilderness Diary increases this limit to four and five, respectively. As such, players who have the maximum number of ecumenical keys in their possession cannot combine additional shards until they have used a key. This does, however, mean that Ecumenical key shards are effectively a means of bypassing this restriction, since the player can have an essentially unlimited number of shards in their possession.
26390:
Blood essence is an item dropped by certain NPCs in the Ancient Prison , a possible reward from the Tombs of Amascut , as well as a potential reward when opening an intricate pouch . When one is activated, it becomes untradeable. While activated and in the inventory, it will give a 50% chance to craft an extra blood rune per pure essence , daeyalt essence , guardian essence or dark essence fragment for no additional experience. The bonus runes granted stack additively with other multipliers such as the Raiments of the Eye or runic extracts . Only one blood essence may be active at a time. If the player tries to activate a second blood essence, they will receive the message You can only have one active blood essence at a time. Each blood essence can craft an extra 1,000 blood runes before being destroyed. Blood essence works in Guardians of the Rift , however, the additional blood runes crafted will not provide additional catalytic guardian stones . Blood essence does not provide benefit nor consume charges at the Ourania Altar .

For Ultimate Ironman , the activated blood essence is destroyed upon death, and cannot be recovered from an Item Retrieval Service .

Each charge will on average last two essences. After using up all 1,000 charges, the player will have gained 47,600 experience when using dark essence, or 21,000 experience when using pure essence, and 4,200 blood runes provided the Raiments of the Eye were worn.

As a blood rune costs 356 coins , each blood essence could add an additional 356,000 coins in total. At current blood essence and blood rune prices, one can expect to earn 269,972 coins for every blood essence consumed. If using blood essence from level 77 to 99, a total of 242 blood essence would be consumed doing Zeah runecrafting for an additional 65,333,224 coins profit, while using pure essence would consume 550 blood essence for an additional 148,484,600 coins profit.

When an activated blood essence is checked by the player, they will receive the message Your blood essence has X charges remaining.

26394: Bandosian components are an item used to restore damaged Torva armour dropped by Nex . They are made by breaking down a Bandos chestplate or Bandos tassets at the ancient forge in the Ancient Prison . Breaking down a chestplate gives three components whereas the tassets give two.
26419:
Cabbages are a series of unobtainable items. Presumably, they are used in order to track the status of players being able to purchase exclusive content. However, it is unknown how they are used in this regard.

Two cabbages were added in June 2018, with "Buy" and "Unbuy" versions, with the release of the Purple skin exclusive to Twitch Prime

A cabbage was added in November 2019, to track points earned in the Twisted League, and presumably determining access to the Leagues Reward Shop

Another cabbage was added on 5 December 2019, with the overhaul of the Leagues Reward Shop, tracking "negative points"

Four cabbages were added in October 2020, presumably used during the Trailblazer League

Two cabbages were added in January 2022, presumably used during the Shattered Relics League

Whilst in its ornamented state, the top can be reverted anytime, returning the void knight top and kit.

If the player dies a PvP death at level 20 Wilderness or below and the item is unprotected, it will remain in the player's inventory; however, the item will be in a broken, unusable state and must be repaired by using it on Perdu and paying him 180,000 coins . They can be purchased after the Land of the Goblins quest , and are identical in appearance to Goblin village spheres . The sphere is consumed upon use and does not work beyond level 20 Wilderness . A skills necklace 's teleport to the Fishing Guild can be used in place of the sphere, as it brings players just outside of the Goblin Cave.

Oldak , the cave goblin professor, will construct these spheres for the player if they provide him with 2 law runes and 1 molten glass (which can be noted).

Unlike Dorgesh-kaan spheres , they cannot be thieved from Oldak's chest .

It is given to Aggie, the witch in Draynor Village, as a bleaching agent to remove the dye from goblin mail and turn it white.

The potion's effects will wear off if "in direct sunlight", the player wears something other than a goblin mail, teleports, or if the player attacks something. It requires 47 Herblore to make the 3-dose potion and yields 55 experience.

The Slayer helmet (i) , requiring a Defence level of 10 to wear, is a piece of equipment that is worn in the helmet slot. It provides the bonuses of multiple pieces of protective and beneficial Slayer equipment. It functions in the same manner as its unimbued variant (with the 16.67% Melee bonus), except that it also provides an extra 15% boost to Ranged accuracy and Ranged damage, and a 15% boost to Magic accuracy and Magic damage, against monsters assigned as the player's Slayer task.

It has defensive bonuses equivalent to the rune full helm , with the exception of providing +11 higher relative magic defence (+10 vs. -1) as well as positive Magic and Ranged attack bonuses. It will prevent infection from Nex 's virus attack, and can be used as warm clothing for Wintertodt .

Players can imbue the Slayer helmet using either 1,250,000 Nightmare Zone reward points (625,000 when the hard tier of Combat Achievements are complete), 500 Soul Wars Zeal Tokens , or by using a scroll of imbuing purchased from the Emir's Arena . The scroll can be used on the black mask before assembling the Slayer helmet or on the Slayer helmet itself.

If an imbued Slayer helmet is disassembled, then it will return an imbued black mask, along with the other components. The black mask (i) can be uncharged to return (depending on the original imbuing method) the scroll of imbuing, or a full refund of the Nightmare Zone reward points or Soul Wars zeal tokens used to purchase it.

For players with undead Slayer tasks , the boosts given by the Salve amulet or Salve amulet (e) do not stack with the effects of a Slayer helmet (i), and the amulet's boosts will take priority over the helmet's.

The granite ring (i) is an imbued version of the regular granite ring from the Nightmare Zone and Soul Wars minigames . It requires 50 Defence and 50 Strength to equip. The imbue upgrade costs either 500,000 Nightmare Zone points or 250,000 with the hard tier of Combat Achievements , 200 Zeal Tokens , or by using a scroll of imbuing purchased from the Emir's Arena .

The upgrade doubles all defensive bonuses, including the negative Magic defence bonus.

If not protected, dying to another player will cause the imbued ring to lose its imbued status, but the player will be reimbursed the Nightmare Zone points , Zeal Tokens or Scroll of imbuing to re-imbue it via the aforementioned methods. Dying to a monster will not remove its imbued effect.

The ring of suffering (i) is an upgraded version of the regular ring of suffering . It can be imbued as a reward from the Nightmare Zone , costing 725,000 reward points or 362,500 with the hard tier of Combat Achievements , at Soul Wars for 300 Zeal Tokens , or by using a scroll of imbuing purchased from Emir's Arena for 200 points. Its stats are double those of the ring of suffering.

The ring can also be charged with rings of recoil to give it the recoil effect, renaming the item to ring of suffering (ri) . Each ring of recoil provides 40 charges, assuming the ring of recoil has not been drained prior. A maximum of 100,000 charges can be stored, equivalent to 2,500 rings, at a cost of 2,350,000 coins . Players can configure the charges while the ring is in their bank by right-clicking on Configure-Charges, as long as players have the required materials. If a player uncharged the ring, the recoil rings stored will not be refunded. The ring of recoil effect is toggle-able, so players may disable it as to not waste it during training and instead use it in activities such as fighting Zulrah , or in PvP combat, where the effect may prove more useful. Charges are not lost upon death.

If not protected, dying to another player will cause the imbued ring to lose its imbued status, however the player will be reimbursed the Nightmare Zone points , Zeal Tokens or Scroll of imbuing to re-imbue it via the aforementioned methods. Dying to a monster will not remove its imbued effect.

The Salve amulet (i) is the imbued form of the salve amulet , granting an additional 16.67% [ 1 ] increase in the wearer's ranged accuracy and damage, as well as a 15% increase for magic , when fighting undead monsters .

The salve amulet is imbued by using either 800,000 Nightmare Zone points (halved upon completing the hard combat achievements ), 320 Soul Wars Zeal Tokens , or by using a scroll of imbuing on the amulet. Amulets imbued through the latter two methods do not count for completing the Ardougne Diary task. [ 2 ] Furthermore, amulets imbued at one location cannot be refunded at a different location.

The ring of the gods (i) is an upgraded version of the regular ring of the gods . It is imbued as a reward from the Nightmare Zone , costing 650,000 reward points or 325,000 with the hard tier of Combat Achievements , at Soul Wars for 260 Zeal Tokens , or by using a scroll of imbuing purchased from the Emir's Arena . Imbuing the ring also requires having a holy wrench in the inventory, though it does not consume it. The Prayer cape does not act as a substitute for imbuing the ring.

The imbued version incorporates the holy wrench's benefit of increasing prayer points restored from some prayer potions when it is equipped, and also provides an extra +4 prayer bonus compared to the regular version. The increased prayer restoration effect of the ring of the gods, Prayer cape and holy wrench do not stack . Unlike the Prayer cape and holy wrench, ring of the gods (i) must be worn to activate the prayer restoration effect and does not work when in the player's inventory.
