26782:
The Salve amulet(ei) is the enchanted and imbued form of the salve amulet , granting a 20% increase in the wearer's accuracy and damage for melee , ranged , and magic when fighting undead monsters .

The salve amulet's bonuses against the undead do not stack with the black mask and slayer helmet's on-task bonuses; wearing both will only apply the bonuses of the salve amulet (ei). The salve amulet also does not have an effect on the dwarf multicannon 's accuracy. [ 1 ] However, the bonuses of Void Knight equipment do stack with the salve amulet. Additionally, the amulet's effects apply to all targets when using multi-hitting melee weapons in a multicombat area , such as the Scythe of Vitur and the special attack of the dragon 2h sword , but not for multi-hitting magic and ranged attacks (ex. chinchompas and burst spells ).
26784:
The colossal pouch is the largest of the five essence pouches and can hold up to 40 rune , pure , daeyalt , or guardian essence for use in the Runecraft skill . The pouch is made by using an abyssal needle to stitch together a small , medium , large , and giant pouch , which requires the unboosted levels of 25 Runecraft and 56 Crafting . [ 1 ] The pouches must be in their non-degraded state to be used in crafting.

Players cannot receive additional essence pouches if they own a colossal pouch. Should the player lose their colossal pouch, they must use a regular needle on the Rewards Guardian to obtain another abyssal needle, as well as reacquire the pouches.

When players create a colossal pouch, the chatbox will state You attempt to stitch together all of the pouches. It's difficult, but you eventually craft a strange, kind of gross, fleshy container. It seems capable of storing up to X essence. , with X being the capacity depending on your Runecraft level. Attempting to make a colossal pouch without the required Crafting level will give the message You need level 56 Crafting to even attempt stitching these together. .

During the Devious Minds quest , a colossal pouch can be used to hold an orb . The pouch is not lost when used for the quest, stating " The colossal pouch was so strong that it survived the blast from the glowing orb. "

26788: A gold tiara is an item that members can create at a furnace from a gold bar along with a tiara mould and level 42 Crafting, granting 35 Crafting experience. They are a purely cosmetic head slot item, though they can be turned into an elemental or catalytic tiara, by bringing a gold tiara and either talisman to the appropriate runic altar. The talisman itself is lost in the process. Both gold and normal tiaras cannot be imbued during Guardians of the Rift.
26792:
Abyssal pearls are items obtained from the Rewards Guardian after completing a round of Guardians of the Rift . They are used to purchase items from Temple Supplies , the shop run by Apprentice Felix near the entrance to the minigame. The rewards are helpful items for training Runecraft , including the Raiments of the Eye outfit pieces costing 1,350 abyssal pearls. The average number of abyssal pearls per search is 2.14 (2.41 when exchanging lanterns and dyes), [ 1 ] thus making 630 (or 560 when exchanging special items) the average number of searches required to complete the full Raiments of the Eye set if no duplicate items or excess dyes are traded in. [ 2 ] While abyssal pearls cannot be traded or exchanged for coins, 400 pearls can be used to purchase a ring of the elements from Temple Supplies, which puts the value of an abyssal pearl at 1,593.57 .

Players may also sell abyssal lanterns to Apprentice Felix for 100 pearls, and abyssal dyes for 50 pearls. Players may also pay Apprentice Cordelia 1 pearl to repair their essence pouches in place of the Dark Mage , after unlocking the service for an initial 25 pearls. Lastly, players can use 25 pearls on the Rewards Guardian for an additional loot roll.
26798:
The catalytic talisman is a talisman that can be received as a drop from the Rewards Guardian, using points earned while playing Guardians of the Rift. It allows players to access any catalytic runic altar, providing the player has completed the quests to access some of them.

The talisman can be combined with a gold tiara to make a catalytic tiara for 60 Runecraft experience at a catalytic altar, by using the tiara on it. This consumes the talisman, but the catalytic tiara can be used in just the same way and can be worn on the head, saving an inventory space when crafting catalytic runes. Creating the tiara cannot be done whilst playing the Guardians of the Rift minigame.

The talisman (and the tiara) can be used to access the Death Altar during Mourning's End Part II to skip completing Thorgel's item list.

Though it has a locate option, using it will give the message "Nothing interesting happens."
26801:
A catalytic tiara is a head slot item used in Runecraft. It is created at any catalytic runic altar (except for the Astral Altar, Soul Altar or Kourend's Blood Altar) by using a gold tiara or catalytic talisman on the altar with both in your inventory. This consumes the catalytic talisman and yields 60 Runecraft experience. As with all other tiaras, catalytic runic altars accessed through Guardians of the Rift cannot be used for imbuing.

The Catalytic runes are: Cosmic runes, Mind runes, Body runes, Chaos runes, Nature runes, Law runes, Death runes, Blood runes, Soul runes and Wrath runes.

While a catalytic tiara is equipped, the mysterious ruins to catalytic altars have a left-click "Enter" option, freeing up an inventory slot that the catalytic talisman would otherwise occupy.

A catalytic tiara, or any other imbued tiaras, may also be used on the Hat of the Eye in order to make the hat function as the tiara that was attuned to it.

The tiara (or the talisman) can be used to access the Death Altar during Mourning's End Part II to skip completing Thorgel's item list.
26804:
An elemental tiara is a head slot item used in Runecraft . It is created at any elemental runic altar by using a gold tiara or elemental talisman on the altar with both in your inventory. This consumes the elemental talisman and yields 40 Runecraft experience . As with all other tiaras, elemental runic altars accessed via Guardians of the Rift cannot be used for imbuement.

While an elemental tiara is equipped, the mysterious ruins to elemental altars have a left-click " Enter " option, freeing up an inventory slot that the elemental talisman would otherwise occupy.

An elemental tiara, or any other imbued tiaras , may also be used on the Hat of the Eye in order to make the hat function as the tiara that was attuned to it.
26807:
Abyssal green dye is an item that allows one piece of the raiments of the eye to be recoloured to a green variant. It is a one time use per item, therefore a total of three are needed to recolour a full set, with optionally two more for the Amulet of the Eye and the lost bag .

Excess green dyes can be exchanged for an abyssal red or abyssal blue dye by using it on Apprentice Felix ; however, doing so does not count towards unlocking the respective slots in the collection log . Players may also choose to exchange the dye with Apprentice Felix for 50 abyssal pearls instead.

26813:
The abyssal needle is an item that can be obtained from the Rewards Guardian after completing a round of Guardians of the Rift . It can also be purchased from the Temple Supplies shop for 750 abyssal pearls .

Players with level 56 Crafting [ not boostable ] and 25 Runecraft [ not boostable ] can use the needle to stitch together the small , medium , large , and giant pouches into a colossal pouch , which stores up to 40 rune , pure , daeyalt , or guardian essence . The pouches must be in their non-degraded state to be used in crafting. Upon crafting the colossal pouch, the abyssal needle is consumed.

The maximum essence held by the pouch scales with the player's Runecraft level.

Should the player lose their colossal pouch or abyssal needle, they may use a regular needle on the Rewards Guardian to obtain another abyssal needle.
26815:
The ring of the elements is an item purchased from the Guardians of the Rift reward shop for 400 abyssal pearls . It teleports players near the elemental runic altars . It also counts as a piece of warm clothing at Wintertodt , regardless of charge. When charged, the ring is untradeable.

The ring is charged by using one of each elemental rune ( air , earth , fire , water ) and one law rune together on the ring, costing 148 per teleport. The ring can hold up to 10,000 charges, costing 1,480,000 to fully charge. The number of charges is tracked by player, meaning a second ring owned by the player will have the same number of charges as the first. Players can receive the runes back through the ring's right-click "Uncharge" option while at almost any bank .

26820: The Guardian's eye is an item that transforms the rift guardian pet into a greatish guardian, unlocking it as a permanent metamorphosis option and consuming the item in the process. It is purchased from the Guardians of the Rift reward shop for 3,000 abyssal pearls.
26822:
The abyssal lantern is an item worn in the shield slot that can be obtained from the Rewards Guardian after completing a round of Guardians of the Rift . It can also be purchased from the Temple Supplies reward shop or Apprentice Felix via dialogue for 1,500 abyssal pearls .

Players with the appropriate Firemaking level and a tinderbox can use six logs of a certain type ( normal , oak , willow , maple , yew , blisterwood , magic , or redwood ) on the lantern to light it, which gives varying benefits for runecrafting when worn. The Firemaking level requirement cannot be boosted, and no Firemaking experience is gained. Coloured logs can be used in place of normal logs, though they give the same effects.

In addition to the benefits provided when runecrafting, the lit lantern serves as an equipable light source . It also works as a lantern for lantern harpooning .

Players cannot light a lantern if they already have another one lit.

Any extra abyssal lanterns the player has can be exchanged with Apprentice Felix for 100 abyssal pearls .

The abyssal lantern is an item worn in the shield slot that can be obtained from the Rewards Guardian after completing a round of Guardians of the Rift . It can also be purchased from the Temple Supplies reward shop or Apprentice Felix via dialogue for 1,500 abyssal pearls .

Players with the appropriate Firemaking level and a tinderbox can use six logs of a certain type ( normal , oak , willow , maple , yew , blisterwood , magic , or redwood ) on the lantern to light it, which gives varying benefits for runecrafting when worn. The Firemaking level requirement cannot be boosted, and no Firemaking experience is gained. Coloured logs can be used in place of normal logs, though they give the same effects.

In addition to the benefits provided when runecrafting, the lit lantern serves as an equipable light source . It also works as a lantern for lantern harpooning .

Players cannot light a lantern if they already have another one lit.

Any extra abyssal lanterns the player has can be exchanged with Apprentice Felix for 100 abyssal pearls .

26850:
The Hat of the Eye is a part of the Raiments of the Eye set, purchased from the Guardians of the Rift reward shop for 400 abyssal pearls. It grants 10% more runes when Runecrafting, and is increased to 60% when the full set is worn.

The hat can be recoloured using abyssal dye (received from the Rewards Guardian) to a red, blue, or green colour scheme.

Players can attune imbued tiaras to the Hat of the Eye to allow it to function as one. This includes the catalytic tiara and the elemental tiara, allowing access to multiple altars simultaneously. All copies of the Hat of the Eye, including those of a different colour, will then be attuned to that tiara (including those stored in the magic wardrobe). The tiara is not consumed in this manner, and the attunement can be freely switched by using a different tiara. Players can use the hat's right-click "Check" option to see which type of tiara it is currently attuned to.

This item can be stored in the magic wardrobe of a costume room, as part of the Raiments of the Eye sets. Ultimate Ironmen will be unable to retrieve individual pieces until the full set is stored.

26876:
Atlax's diary is a book that may be received from the Rewards Guardian after a game of Guardians of the Rift .

Written by Atlax , the diary details their experiences exploring the Temple of the Eye while working for Pharana. Pharana, in turn, was asked to clear the site by Justiciar Aliya following the battle that occurred when a rift to the scar was opened . While exploring the temple, Atlax documents several discoveries, including a cache of Eye amulets and a mysterious stone guardian tasked with protecting the temple.

The book can also be found in the bookcases in a player-owned house if the player has previously read the book.
26878: Guardian fragments are remnants of rune guardians that are mined during the Guardians of the Rift minigame. They can be used on the workbench at the Temple of the Eye to create guardian essence, which are then crafted upon runic altars to create elemental or catalytic guardian stones.
26879: Guardian essence is an item obtained during the Guardians of the Rift minigame. Guardian essence can be stored in essence pouches. This item can be obtained by using guardian fragments on the workbench in the Guardians of the Rift minigame. Alternatively, this item can be obtained by mining the huge guardian remains or fallen guardians which provide essence rather than fragments like the other guardian remains.
26880:
Catalytic guardian stones are items used to power-up the Great Guardian during a game of Guardians of the Rift, alongside elemental guardian stones and polyelemental guardian stones.

They are obtained by imbuing guardian essence at a catalytic runic altar, accessible directly by entering an active Portal Guardian. This is a 1:1 ratio of essence to stones. The Raiments of the Eye set does not offer additional bonuses.

Players are granted 5 Runecraft experience and 2 catalytic energy per catalytic guardian stone used to power-up the Great Guardian.

Mind, Body, Cosmic, Chaos, Nature, Law, Death and Blood Runes give Catalytic Energy.
26881:
Elemental guardian stones are items used to power-up the Great Guardian during a game of Guardians of the Rift, alongside catalytic guardian stones and polyelemental guardian stones.

They are obtained by imbuing guardian essence at an elemental runic altar, accessible directly by entering an active Portal Guardian.

Players are granted 5 Runecraft experience and 2 elemental energy per elemental guardian stone used to power-up the Great Guardian.

Air, Water, Earth and Fire Runes give Elemental Energy.
26882:
Uncharged cells are an item obtained during the Guardians of the Rift minigame. They are charged by imbuing them at a runic altar, accessible directly by entering an active Portal Guardian. The type of charge it holds is dependent on the runic altar it is charged at.

When inspected, the chatbox will state "An uncharged magical cell built to hold runic energy."
26883:
Weak cells are an item obtained during the Guardians of the Rift minigame. Players can obtain one from the table by the entrance, or by imbuing an uncharged cell at the Air, Mind, or Body Altar, which are accessible directly by entering the active Portal Guardians of that type.

The weak cell can be used alongside a chisel to create weak elemental and catalytic guardians or placed on an inactive cell tile to create weak barriers, or reinforce an existing barrier.

When inspected, the chatbox will state "A magical cell charged with a small amount of runic energy."
26884:
Medium cells are an item obtained during the Guardians of the Rift minigame. Players can obtain one by imbuing an uncharged cell at the Water, Cosmic, or Chaos Altar, which are accessible directly by entering the active Portal Guardians of that type.

The medium cell can be used alongside a chisel to create medium elemental and catalytic guardians, be placed on a weak cell tile to create medium barriers, or reinforce an existing barrier.

When inspected, the chatbox will state A magical cell charged with a moderate amount of runic energy.
26885:
Strong cells are an item obtained during the Guardians of the Rift minigame . Players can obtain one by imbuing an uncharged cell at the Earth , Nature , or Law Altar , which are accessible directly by entering the active Portal Guardians of that type.

The strong cell can be used alongside a chisel to create strong elemental and catalytic guardians , be placed on a medium cell tile to create strong barriers , or reinforce an existing barrier.

When inspected, the chatbox will state "A magical cell charged with a high amount of runic energy."
26886:
Overcharged cells are items obtained during the Guardians of the Rift minigame. Players can obtain one by imbuing an uncharged cell at the Fire, Death, or Blood Altar, which are accessible directly by entering the active Portal Guardians of that type.

The overcharged cell can be used alongside a chisel to create overcharged elemental and catalytic guardians. They can also be placed on a strong cell tile to create overcharged barriers, or reinforce existing ones.

When inspected, the chatbox will display a message similar to the cell's examine text, describing the cell as "a magical cell charged with an immense amount of runic energy."
26887:
Air portal talismans are items that can be obtained during the Guardians of the Rift minigame , by imbuing guardian essence or charging uncharged cells at the Air Altar . Upon receiving one, a message in the chatbox will state " You discover a strange talisman during the runecrafting process! "

Portal talismans have a 1/250 chance of being acquired per guardian essence crafted, or 1/200 if players have a maple abyssal lantern equipped; [ 1 ] [ 2 ] this chance is rolled until the player receives one.

The portal talisman can be used to enter the Guardian of Air to access the Air Altar, even if it is inactive. Doing so consumes the talisman, unless the Guardian of Air is currently active. Portal talismans cannot be kept after the game ends, so it is recommended to use them whenever possible.

Players can right-click "Toggle-talisman" on the Guardian of Air to toggle whether they wish to receive portal talismans or not from crafting at the Air Altar.

When inspected, the chatbox will state "A talisman bound to a runic altar. Presenting this to the respective portal guardian will return you there."

26899:
The rift guardian is a members-only skilling pet that can be obtained while training Runecraft. The chances of getting it are dependent on the player's Runecraft level, the rune the player is crafting, and the number of essence used. Upon using the Guardian's eye on it, which is purchased from the Guardians of the Rift reward shop for 3,000 abyssal pearls, players unlock a permanent metamorphosis option to turn it into the Greatish guardian.

When a player receives the pet, it will automatically try to appear as their follower. At the same time, a message in the chatbox will state You have a funny feeling like you're being followed. However, if a player receives a pet while having a follower out (for example, a cat), it will be placed into their inventory. When this occurs, the message in the chatbox will instead state You feel something weird sneaking into your backpack.

When runecrafting using dark essence fragments, the pet is given after they are removed and the runes are given back. This means if there is not already some of the runes to be crafted in the inventory, and the rest of the inventory is full, and a pet is already following the player, the rift guardian will not be given; it must instead be claimed from Probita in East Ardougne.

On death, if a player loses their pet (as a follower or in your inventory) it will wander around the area for 30 seconds before despawning. Even if the player returns in time, the pet cannot be picked up, and can be reclaimed from Probita.
26901:
Abyssal protector is a pet that can be obtained from the Rewards Guardian. It is a much smaller version of the Abyssal guardians found within the Guardians of the Rift minigame.

When a player receives the pet, it will automatically try to appear as their follower. At the same time, a message in the chatbox will state You have a funny feeling like you're being followed. However, if a player receives a pet while having a follower out (for example, a cat), it will be placed into their inventory. When this occurs, the message in the chatbox will instead state You feel something weird sneaking into your backpack.

If a player's inventory is full and they have a follower already, they will not receive the pet; it must instead be claimed from Probita in East Ardougne.

On death, if a player loses their pet (as a follower or in your inventory) it will wander around the area for 30 seconds before despawning. Even if the player returns in time, the pet cannot be picked up, and can be reclaimed from Probita.
26903:
The eye amulet is obtained during the quest Temple of the Eye. The player is requested to bring this item to the Mage of Zamorak in Varrock at the Altar of Zamorak to have him trace the object. The eye on the amulet is said to be the symbol of the Order of Wizards and gives off abyssal energy. The Mage of Zamorak will tell the player more about the amulet in exchange for a bucket of water and a Strong cup of tea.

Later in the quest, the player discovers from Wizard Persten that the amulet is related to a teleportation matrix and that a Transmission Spell has been cast upon the amulet, thereby allowing the Z.M.I to track the user of the amulet. In response to this, Wizard Persten alters the spell on the amulet to provide the Z.M.I with false information.

If the amulet is lost upon death, a new one can be acquired by speaking to Wizard Persten.
26904: A strong cup of tea is an item obtained from the Tea Seller during the quest Temple of the Eye at the request of Herbert, the Mage of Zamorak . The Tea Seller tells the player the strong cups of tea that he gives Herbert are in actuality regular cups of tea, and he chooses not to tell him to keep him happy.
26905:
The abyssal incantation is an item obtained during the quest Temple of the Eye , written down by the Dark Mage . This item should be taken to Wizard Persten north of Al Kharid who then goes on to recommend you take it to Archmage Sedridor in the Wizards' Tower .

Sedridor notes that the incantation is written on thin flesh rather than parchment; when speaking to Herbert after the quest, he tells players that it is most likely flesh from an abyssal creature.
26906:
The colossal pouch is created when using the orb on a regular colossal pouch during the Devious Minds quest. It is used as a teleport beacon for a mysterious character later known as the Assassin to steal a relic from the Entrana church.

Note that unlike the large pouch , the colossal pouch is not lost during the quest. After the cutscene where the relic is stolen, the game chat will state The colossal pouch was so strong that it survived the blast from the glowing orb.
26908: The intricate pouch is an item that can be obtained from the Rewards Guardian after completing a game of Guardians of the Rift . It can be opened to obtain a reward.
26910: The tarnished locket is an item that can be obtained from an intricate pouch , which can be received from the Rewards Guardian after completing a round of Guardians of the Rift . After inspecting it, players can give the locket to Phileas the Lumbridge Guide in exchange for the Amulet of the Eye . If the locket is lost before turning it in, it can be reclaimed from Apprentice Felix .
26912:
The lost bag is a cape slot item that can be obtained from an intricate pouch, which can be received from the Rewards Guardian after completing a round of Guardians of the Rift. It has no stat bonuses and is purely cosmetic.

The bag can be recoloured using abyssal dye (received from the Rewards Guardian) to a red, blue, or green colour scheme.

If the bag is destroyed, another can be obtained from Apprentice Felix. If the bag was recoloured before it was destroyed, then it will still be recoloured when it is reclaimed.

As it is dropped at a 1/60 rate from an intricate pouch, which in its place has a drop rate of 1/28 to 1/25, the effective drop rate of the lost bag ranges from 1/1500 to 1/1680 searches.
26914:
The amulet of the Eye is an item that allows unlimited teleportation to the Temple of the Eye , just south of the portal . It is obtained by inspecting the tarnished locket and then showing it to Phileas the Lumbridge Guide .

The amulet can be recoloured using Abyssal dye (received from the Rewards Guardian ) to a red, blue, or green colour scheme.

The amulet provides unlimited teleports to the Temple of the Eye and can be used as a banking method with low requirements.

Players can reclaim the amulet from the Lumbridge Guide should it be lost. If the amulet was recoloured before it was destroyed, then it will still be recoloured when it is reclaimed. If players wish to reclaim multiple amulets, they can do so by attempting to destroy the amulet on a Free-to-play world, which drops the amulet to the ground, allowing players to reclaim another and also pick up the dropped one.

When trading the locket for the amulet, the Lumbridge Guide provides a little backstory for the item. Phileas explains that the amulet had long been in the possession of his family, whose members had been initiated into the Order of Wizards for generations. [ 1 ] The eye-shaped amulet displays the symbol of the Order of Wizards, which long ago built and oversaw the Temple of the Eye with the aim of protecting a powerful artefact. [ 2 ] The order had long since given up this task, leading the history of its symbol to become obscured, until the player is able to confirm its origins after re-discovering the temple.
26916: The Special hot sauce is obtained from Ali Morrisane in the 2022 Easter event . It has a right-click "Drink" option, though attempting to do so results in the player saying " I definitely do not want to drink any of this! " The special hot sauce cannot be put in the bank.
26917: The special super hot kebab is obtained from Karim after giving him the special hot sauce in the 2022 Easter event. It has a right-click "Eat" option, though attempting to do so results in the player saying "Nope, I am not going to eat that!" The special super hot kebab cannot be banked.
26918: The secret report is obtained from the Suspicious crate after giving him the Special super hot kebab in the 2022 Easter event .
26919:
A big bucket is obtained from the Easter Bunny after talking to him about the choc-ice in the 2022 Easter event. It is used on a camel to obtain a Big bucket of camel milk, which is needed to create camel ice cream during the event.

The big bucket cannot be put in the bank.
26920:
Big bucket of camel milk is an item obtained during the 2022 Easter event. It is obtained by using a big bucket on either Alice, Cam, or Elly the Camel.

The bucket has a right-click "Drink" option, though attempting to do so results in the player saying "I don't think I actually want to drink that. I need it for the ice cream!"

Emptying the bucket prints the message "You empty the contents of the bucket on the floor. What a waste of camel milk!" and leaves the player with an empty big bucket. The big bucket of camel milk cannot be banked.
26921: Big bucket of frozen camel milk is an item obtained during the 2022 Easter event . It is only seen by players during a cutscene where Phoebe Kay freezes the big bucket of camel milk outside Ferox Enclave .
26924:
Magical cleaning potion is an item obtained during the 2022 Easter event . It is used to clean the dirty vat . According to Ali Morrisane , this potion is the very same one used during the 2021 Christmas event .

The bottle has a right-click "Drink" option, though attempting to do so results in the player saying " As good as this smells, I need to use this to clean the tanning vat. "
26925: Cooler is an item obtained during the 2022 Easter event after asking the Suspicious crate for one. The cooler is used to hold an easter egg and ice cream easter egg in order to transport them to the Shantay Pass to perform a melting experiment. The eggs can only be removed from the cooler when standing in the Shantay Pass, which begins the experiment.
26926: Easter egg is an item obtained during the 2022 Easter event. It is used alongside the ice cream easter egg to test the its durability under the desert heat. The normal Easter egg will melt into a melted easter egg in the process.
26927:
Melted easter egg is an item obtained during the 2022 Easter event. It is the result of melting an easter egg during the Shantay Pass experiment, or from the ice cream easter egg melting when talking to the Easter Bunny at the end of the event. Upon finishing the event, all remaining easter eggs in the inventory will melt.

When eaten, it heals 1 Hitpoint, resulting in the following game message:

You eat the melted Easter egg...

...It tastes lovely and heals some health.

If you eat the melted easter egg with full health, the message is slightly different:

You eat the melted Easter egg...

...It tastes lovely.

Although useless, players were able to keep melted easter eggs after completion of the event. With the end of the event, all melted easter eggs were removed from the inventories of any players who still had them.
26928: Ice cream easter egg is an item obtained during the 2022 Easter event . It is made of a normal easter egg filled with camel milk ice cream, intended to keep the chocolate from melting in the desert heat. The ice cream easter egg doesn't melt during the Shantay Pass experiment, but melts into a melted easter egg when talking to the Easter Bunny at the end of the event.
26929: Blunt scimitars can be obtained by talking to Zeke during the 2022 Easter event . They can be used to create the churning machine .
26930: Washing line is an item obtained after searching the pile of junk during the 2022 Easter event . It can be used to create the churning machine .
26931: Tanning wheel is an item obtained after searching the pile of junk during the 2022 Easter event. It can be used to create the churning machine.
26932: Vat (dirty) is an item obtained after searching the pile of junk during the 2022 Easter event . It must be cleaned using the magical cleaning potion to obtain a clean vat . The clean vat is then used to create a churning machine needed to create camel milk ice cream.
26933: Vat (cleaned) is an item obtained after using the magical cleaning potion on a vat (dirty) during the 2022 Easter event . It can be used to create the churning machine .
26934: Wooden pole is an item obtained after searching the pile of junk during the 2022 Easter event . It can be used to create the churning machine .
26935: Churning machine is an item obtained after combining the blunt scimitars , tanning wheel , cleaned vat , washing line , and wooden pole during the 2022 Easter event .
26936: Frozen churning machine is an item obtained during the 2022 Easter event . It is created during a cutscene in the wilderness when Phoebe Kay freezes the churning machine by casting a freezing spell. The frozen churning machine is placed on the dirty ground in Al Kharid in order to prepare camel milk ice cream.
26937:
The Easter hat is an item that can be obtained from participating in any Easter event , and was first obtained from the 2022 Easter event .

If destroyed, a replacement can be obtained from Diango in Draynor Village or from the toy box of a costume room .
26939:
The crate ring is an item that can be obtained from participating in any Easter event , and was first obtained from the 2022 Easter event . When equipped, the player's model transforms into a crate. While this effect is active, the player cannot move, or the player's model will return to normal.

While in crate form, if another player right clicks on the player disguised as a crate, the normal options will appear (i.e. "Walk here Username", "Follow Username", etc.) Upon equipping the ring, the player will receive the message You hide inside the crate. Sneaky!

If destroyed, a replacement can be obtained from Diango in Draynor Village or from the toy box of a costume room .
26941:
Polyelemental guardian stones are items used to power-up the Great Guardian during a game of Guardians of the Rift , alongside elemental , catalytic , and polycatalytic guardian stones.

They are obtained by crafting combination runes when imbuing guardian essence at an elemental runic altar , accessible directly by entering an active Portal Guardian.

Players are granted 5 Runecraft experience and 3 elemental energy (instead of the normal 2) per polyelemental guardian stone used to power-up the Great Guardian.

Mist , Dust , Mud , Smoke , Steam , and Lava Runes give Polyelemental Energy.
26942: Message is a quest item that players receive from Jamila upon talking to her to start Beneath Cursed Sands .
26943: Clue scroll (elite) is a music clue obtained from elite Treasure Trails.
26944: Clue scroll (elite) is an coordinate clue obtained from elite Treasure Trails .

The pharaoh's sceptre is a polestaff found during the Pyramid Plunder minigame in Sophanem , from the golden chests and sarcophagi . It requires 30 Attack and 30 Magic to wield.

The sceptre provides teleports to each of the great pyramids of the Kharidian Desert , using a charge to do so. By default, the sceptre holds three charges. Players who have progressed in the Desert Diary have their sceptre hold more charges; up to 10 with the easy diary, 25 with the medium diary, 50 with the hard diary, and 100 with the elite diary.

It is one of only a few teleports that work up to level 30 Wilderness, while most other means of teleportation will not work above level 20 Wilderness.

26952: The scarab mould is an item obtained from the chest during the quest Beneath Cursed Sands . It is used to craft a scarab emblem from an iron bar.
26953:
The scarab emblem is an item obtained during the quest Beneath Cursed Sands . The emblem depicts Scabaras , one of the four minor gods of the Menaphite Pantheon .

The iron emblem is obtained by using an iron bar on the furnace in the Ruins of Ullek whilst having a scarab mould , whilst the gold emblem is used to solve a puzzle to progress in the tomb below the ruins.
26954:
The stone tablet is an item obtained during the quest Beneath Cursed Sands , from searching the well in the Ruins of Ullek .

The tablet, carved during the God Wars , contains the code to the buried chest mentioned in the message.
26955:
The chest is an item obtained during the quest Beneath Cursed Sands . It is found by digging the southernmost ritual pillar just south-west of the climbing steps in the Ruins of Ullek .

The chest has a seven digit lock, which is deciphered from the stone tablet , being 1118513. The code is derived from the name of Akhem, as per the text on the tablet. Each letter is converted to their position in the alphabet, that is: 1, 11, 8, 5 and 13.

26957:
The human emblem is an item obtained during the quest Beneath Cursed Sands . The emblem depicts Het , one of the four minor gods of the Menaphite Pantheon .

The human emblem, along with the scarab , baboon , and crocodile emblem , are used to solve a puzzle in the tomb below the Ruins of Ullek .
26958:
The baboon emblem is an item obtained during the quest Beneath Cursed Sands . The emblem depicts Apmeken , one of the four minor gods of the Menaphite Pantheon .

The baboon emblem, along with the scarab , crocodile , and human emblem , are used to solve a puzzle in the tomb below the Ruins of Ullek .
26959:
The crocodile emblem is an item obtained during the quest Beneath Cursed Sands. The emblem depicts Crondis, one of the four minor gods of the Menaphite Pantheon.

26960: The rusty key is an item obtained during the quest Beneath Cursed Sands, in an urn behind Mehhar's sarcophagus. It is used to access the upper chamber of the tomb below the Ruins of Ullek.
26961: The lily of the Elid is an item obtained during the quest Beneath Cursed Sands . It is picked from the lily on a small island directly west of Nardah .
26962: The cure crate is an item obtained from Zahur during the quest Beneath Cursed Sands . It contains the cure to the plague in Sophanem .
26963:
Odd spectacles are an item found on a table at Maisa 's camp between Sophanem and the Ruins of Ullek during the quest Beneath Cursed Sands . They have no stat bonuses and are completely cosmetic.

Before her graphical update, Maisa wore them during her encounter with the player in Contact! .
26965: The bottle of 'tonic' is an item that can be obtained from a table at Maisa 's camp between Sophanem and the Ruins of Ullek during the quest Beneath Cursed Sands . It has no apparent use.
26967:
The circlet of water is an item obtained from Maisa as a reward for completing the quest Beneath Cursed Sands . Wearing it will delay the onset of desert heat by 12 seconds.

The circlet, which acts as an equipable waterskin , is charged with five water runes per charge, and can hold up to 500,000 charges. One charge is consumed whenever the player would have needed to drink water due to the effects of desert heat . The circlet can be uncharged to regain the runes. The circlet must be equipped in order for the effects to work.

The maximum time between drinks is 132 seconds (costing 28 charges per hour).

If lost, it can be reclaimed from the High Priest of Sophanem for 10,000 coins . Additionally, if the free one was not received due to a full inventory at the end of the quest and Into the Tombs has been started, it can be claimed from the High Priest.

The desert amulet 4 , which requires completion of the elite Desert Diary , also provides 100% protection against desert heat when worn but doesn't require upkeep.

The lion helm was removed the next week, as it was not intended to be released yet and was not obtainable through any means.

26990:
The amulet of the Eye is an item that allows unlimited teleportation to the Temple of the Eye , just south of the portal . It is obtained by inspecting the tarnished locket and then showing it to Phileas the Lumbridge Guide .

The amulet can be recoloured using Abyssal dye (received from the Rewards Guardian ) to a red, blue, or green colour scheme.

The amulet provides unlimited teleports to the Temple of the Eye and can be used as a banking method with low requirements.

Players can reclaim the amulet from the Lumbridge Guide should it be lost. If the amulet was recoloured before it was destroyed, then it will still be recoloured when it is reclaimed. If players wish to reclaim multiple amulets, they can do so by attempting to destroy the amulet on a Free-to-play world, which drops the amulet to the ground, allowing players to reclaim another and also pick up the dropped one.

When trading the locket for the amulet, the Lumbridge Guide provides a little backstory for the item. Phileas explains that the amulet had long been in the possession of his family, whose members had been initiated into the Order of Wizards for generations. [ 1 ] The eye-shaped amulet displays the symbol of the Order of Wizards, which long ago built and oversaw the Temple of the Eye with the aim of protecting a powerful artefact. [ 2 ] The order had long since given up this task, leading the history of its symbol to become obscured, until the player is able to confirm its origins after re-discovering the temple.

An ensouled hellhound head is an item which can be dropped by hellhounds and Cerberus . It is used to gain Prayer experience by using the level 72 Magic spell Expert Reanimation from the Arceuus spellbook using 3 nature runes , 1 blood rune , and 2 soul runes . When a player reanimates an ensouled hellhound head, a reanimated hellhound will appear and grant 1,200 Prayer experience after being killed.

Ensouled heads can be reanimated anywhere as long as the head is on the ground within the 31x31 area centred on its initial drop location and has not been put into the bank , trade screen, Grand Exchange , or price checker . [ 1 ] [ 2 ] Otherwise, it must be taken to the Dark Altar in Arceuus to be reanimated.

27000:
The Void knight top (or) is a Void knight top with a Shattered relics void ornament kit added onto it. The kit gives no additional bonuses, and is only used to add aesthetics to the top.

Whilst in its ornamented state, the top can be reverted anytime, returning the void knight top and kit.

If the player dies a PvP death at level 20 Wilderness or below and the item is unprotected, it will remain in the player's inventory; however, the item will be in a broken, unusable state and must be repaired by using it on Perdu and paying him 180,000 coins . The ornament kit is lost to the killer.

If the player dies a PvP death above level 20 Wilderness and the item is unprotected, it will be converted to coins. To prevent this, a Trouver parchment and a payment of 500,000 coins can be given to Perdu in order to permanently lock the item. The locked item will remain in the player's inventory; however, the item will be in a mangled, unusable state and must be repaired by using it on Perdu and paying him 500,000 coins. The ornament kit is lost to the killer.

This item can be stored in the armour case of a costume room , as part of the Void Knight (Shattered Relics) set. Ultimate Ironmen will be unable to retrieve individual pieces until the full set is stored.

27010: A preform is an unfinished giant's sword made during the Sleeping Giants quest and the Giants' Foundry minigame. It is automatically equipped, and can only be unequipped by taking it to the preform storage in the northern part of the foundry. This means an unwanted preform cannot be simply gotten rid of; either the sword must be completed, damaged by messing up the process (this is the fastest method), or it must be stored forever.
27012:
The double ammo mould is an item that makes cannonballs twice as fast compared to a regular ammo mould , making 8 cannonballs rather than 4 (and using 2 metal bars rather than 1) per action.

It can be purchased from the Giants' Foundry reward shop for 2,000 Foundry Reputation if Dwarf Cannon is complete. On average, using Steel-Mithril longswords with only optimal moulds (requiring up to 81 Smithing ), obtaining a double ammo mould takes around 75 minutes of gameplay. With only default moulds, it takes 15 minutes more.

This mould can also be used to create the gold cannonball used in the Between a Rock... quest.

With 87 Sailing , the Ancient Furnace can be accessed within the Grimstone Dungeon and used to smelt cannonballs at double speed.
27014:
Kovac's grog is a type of ale that restores 1 Hitpoint and temporarily boosts Smithing by 4 while draining Attack , Ranged , and Magic by 2. This provides the second highest Smithing boost available, surpassing the mature dwarven stout's 2-level boost. Furthermore, this is a reliable boost, unlike orange spicy stew which may boost or drain the player by up to 5 levels when 3 dashes of orange spice are added.

It can be purchased from the Giants' Foundry reward shop for 300 Foundry Reputation . Each serving of Kovac's grog is worth 100,492 coins , or 334.97 coins per Reputation point.

Upon drinking the grog, a message in the chatbox will state You drink Kovac's grog. It tastes like giants' feet.

This item cannot be traded back to the shop for Foundry Reputation. Ironman players are presented with an Easter egg message if they try to exchange the grog for Foundry Reputation.
27017:
Smithing catalyst is a consumable item purchased from the Giants' Foundry reward shop for 15 Foundry Reputation .

They are used when smelting bars at a furnace , or using the Superheat Item spell, to halve the amount of coal required per bar, whilst simultaneously providing double experience per bar consuming the catalyst in the process. The catalyst only works for bars that are produced using coal. The experience doubling effect works at the Blast Furnace , but it does not reduce the amount of coal needed any further.

Based on the opportunity cost of using Foundry Reputation to buy catalyst instead of Kovac's grog to sell on the Grand Exchange , each Smithing catalyst costs 5,024.6 coins .
27019:
Ore packs are an item purchased from the Giants' Foundry reward shop for 200 Foundry Reputation. A pack contains 30 noted ores which could be any combination of the following (mainly coal): coal, iron ore, mithril ore, adamantite ore, and runite ore.

The distribution of ore types found in a pack is not influenced by Mining level in any way.
27021:
The colossal blade is a two-handed sword purchased from the Giants' Foundry reward shop for 5,000 Foundry Reputation , requiring level 60 Attack to wield.

The colossal blade's stats are similar to those of the barrelchest anchor , with a slightly higher slash bonus than the anchor's crush bonus. Although it lacks a special attack , it has a passive effect to make up for it on larger size monsters. The blade also has much lower requirements compared to the barrelchest anchor, which also requires 40 Strength , in addition to 50 Prayer and 40 Ranged for completion of The Great Brain Robbery quest. Due to this, the blade can be used as a substitute for the anchor on low Prayer, 60 Attack, player killing builds. The 16, 31, and 44 Prayer builds for example, will benefit from this.

The colossal blade only has to be unlocked once; if lost in any situation, it can be re-obtained from Perdu for 300,000 as long as you do not have another copy of this item. If lost in PVP, the item will drop as 225,000 for the killer.

The elder maul (or) is a cosmetic variant of the elder maul with an elder maul ornament kit added to it. It can be dismantled at any time, returning both parts back to the player. It is a two-handed crush weapon that requires Attack and Strength levels of 75 to wield.

Along with the non-cosmetic variant, it is the highest tier crush weapon available. It overtakes the godswords as the weapon with the highest strength bonus. Despite the strength bonus, the abyssal bludgeon often has higher overall damage output against low-defence monsters because of its quicker attack speed, making it only useful in places such as Tekton. Because of its high strength bonus, it is often used as a finisher in player killing. The colour of the ornament kit matches that of the Bandos armour set.

27202:
A Menaphite remedy is a stat renewal potion that restores 6 + 16% of the player's combat stats (excluding prayer) every 15 seconds, over the course of 5 minutes. This can be used to effectively negate the stat-draining effects of Saradomin brews and Armadyl Brews, but will also cancel out standard stat boosts.

It can be made by a player with 88 Herblore by adding a Lily of the Sands to an unfinished dwarf weed potion. This grants the player 200 Herblore experience.

Although this potion will restore combat stats if they are below their base level, it will not boost your combat stats back up if they were previously boosted.

Additionally, consuming this potion will remove all divine effects of existing boosts, such as from the saturated heart or a divine super combat potion, making them tick down at the usual rate of -1 level per 60 seconds (90 if praying Preserve).

This property can prolong the usefulness of these boosts by consuming the remedy at any point before the boost runs out. A stat boosted by a divine effect will return to its base level after the divine effect expires, but removing it with the Menaphite remedy will retain the boosted stat, allowing it to tick down normally.

If new divine boosts are applied after the remedy has been consumed, they will correctly apply their divine status. This strategy can be useful at a bank to prepare for scenarios where the player's stats are frequently lowered, such as Nex, where Saradomin brews are often used. This allows the player to benefit from the stat restoration of the Menaphite remedy while retaining the benefits of their divine potions or saturated heart.

The Masori mask is obtained as a rare drop from the Tombs of Amascut . It is part of the Masori armour set, and requires level 80 Ranged and 30 Defence to equip. As with the rest of the armour set, the mask boasts the highest ranged attack bonus of any item in the head slot .

The mask can be upgraded into a fortified variant by attaching an Armadylean plate onto it, increasing the Defence level to equip it to level 80. This process requires level 90 Crafting , and is not reversible.

This item can be stored in the armour case of a costume room , as part of the Masori armour set. Ultimate Ironmen will be unable to retrieve individual pieces until the full set is stored.

Osmumten's fang (or) is a cosmetic variant of Osmumten's fang with a cursed phalanx attached to it. It retains all the effects of the original variant.

In order to receive the cursed phalanx, players must complete a Tombs of Amascut raid at level 500+ with zero deaths for all party members. If a player loses Osmumten's fang (or) in a PvP death, the cursed phalanx will be placed in their gravestone.
27248:
The cursed phalanx is an ornament kit received from the Tombs of Amascut that can be used on Osmumten's fang to create Osmumten's fang (or) , which alters its appearance. It is solely a cosmetic upgrade and does not change the stats.

In order to receive one from the reward chest , players must complete a raid at level 500+ with zero deaths for all party members.

If a player already owns a cursed phalanx or has a Osmumten's fang (or), they will not be able to obtain another one from the rewards chest. All available items must be dropped on the ground prior to opening the chest in order to receive multiple phalanxes.

It is possible to receive the combat achievement Amascut's Remnant without receiving the cursed phalanx by defeating the boss, dying, and regenerating one HP all on the same tick.
27251:
Elidinis' ward (f) is a magical shield requiring 80 Magic , Defence , and Prayer to equip. The fortified ward provides an additional 2% magic damage , 5 Magic Attack and 1 Prayer over the arcane spirit shield . Its defence bonuses are identical to the arcane spirit shield.

The ward is fortified by attaching an arcane sigil to Elidinis' ward , requiring level 90 Prayer , 90 Smithing , and 10,000 soul runes , granting 260 experience in both skills in the process. Boosts can be used for the Prayer and Smithing level requirements to fortify the ward; players cannot pay Abbot Langley to fortify it for them, though he can remove the sigil from an arcane spirit shield. Upon fortifying Elidinis' ward, the chatbox states " You fuse your Arcane sigil to Elidinis' ward, returning it to its former glory."

The fortified ward is untradeable, but it can be dismantled to return the sigil and ward. However, the soul runes will not be returned.

A Menaphite ornament kit can be attached to the ward to create Elidinis' ward (or) , a cosmetic variant of the ward.
27253:
Elidinis' ward (or) is a cosmetic variant of Elidinis' ward (f) with a Menaphite ornament kit added to it. The ward's colours are based on that of the Jaltevas Pyramid , where the Tombs of Amascut raid takes place.

In order to receive the Menaphite ornament kit, players must complete a raid at level 425+ with zero deaths for all party members. If a player loses Elidinis' ward (or) in a PvP death, the Menaphite ornament kit will be placed in their gravestone.
27255:
The Menaphite ornament kit is an ornament kit that can be used on Elidinis' ward (f) to create Elidinis' ward (or), which alters its appearance. It is solely a cosmetic upgrade and does not change its stats.

In order to receive one from the reward chest, players must complete a raid at level 425 (or higher) with zero deaths for all party members.

Despite having a high alchemy value of 60,000 coins, Menaphite ornament kits cannot be alched.

Tumeken's shadow is a two-handed powered staff requiring 85 Magic to wield, and is only available as a rare drop from the Tombs of Amascut . The staff is extremely valuable as, when matched with other high-end magic gear, it excels with its damage and immense accuracy even against magic-resistant monsters. Like most powered staves, it is only tradeable when it is fully uncharged.

Powered by the sun itself, the staff was created by the god Tumeken using an unknown artefact during the Kharidian–Zarosian War as a means to fight back against the invading force of the Zarosian Empire . [ 1 ] Tumeken also used it to create Tumeken's Warden and Elidinis' Warden , two massive automata imbued with the divine essence of himself and his wife Elidinis . [ 2 ] After Tumeken sacrificed himself to end the war, Elidinis gifted the weapon as well as her own ward to Osmumten before leaving to mourn her family.

As with all powered staves other than Thammaron's sceptre and the accursed sceptre , Tumeken's shadow is not able to use its built-in spell against other players outside of minigames.

The thread of Elidinis is an uncommon reward from the rewards chest within the Tombs of Amascut . Players with 75 Crafting [ boostable ] can use the thread on a rune pouch with a needle in their inventory to create a divine rune pouch , which can store four types of runes instead of three. This process can be reversed to return both items.

The base rate of receiving the thread is 1/10. To mitigate bad luck , the rate is scaled linearly with the number of raid completions, up to a maximum of 3/10 upon completing 15 raids. [ 1 ] Once the player gets their first thread, the drop rate is decreased to 1/50. [ 2 ] [ 3 ] Additionally, players can buy the thread from Perdu for 350,000 coins if they have obtained it from the Tombs of Amascut at least once.

Note: This item is destroyed on death.
27281:
The divine rune pouch is an upgraded variant of the rune pouch, which holds four types of runes instead of three. Each rune can be stacked up to 16,000, the same as a normal rune pouch. The pouch is made by using a needle or costume needle to stitch together a thread of Elidinis and the rune pouch, which requires level 75 Crafting to do; boosts will work.

The pouch can be reverted to its base components, returning the thread and pouch. When reverting the pouch, if the player has a rune in the 4th slot they will be warned all of the runes in that slot will be lost, even if there are only 3 unique runes in the pouch. If players die to other players while carrying a divine rune pouch in the Wilderness or in a PvP world, they will lose it, unless it has been locked via use of a trouver parchment. It should be noted that the Trouver parchment does not protect runes stored within a Divine rune pouch upon death.

The Breach of the Scarab is an untradeable jewel that can be obtained as a reward from the Tombs of Amascut .

The jewel can be attached to the Keris partisan to create the Keris partisan of breaching , providing a 33% accuracy boost against all Kalphites and Scabarites .

Unlike the other three jeweled Keris partisans, the Keris partisan of breaching's passive effect can be used outside the Tombs of Amascut.
27285:
The Eye of the Corruptor is an untradeable jewel that can be obtained as a reward from the Tombs of Amascut.

The jewel can be attached to the Keris partisan to create the Keris partisan of corruption, whose special attack can only be used within the Tombs of Amascut.
27287:
The keris partisan of corruption is a one-handed spear requiring 80 Attack to equip. It is made by attaching the Eye of the Corruptor on the keris partisan, granting it a special attack which can only be used within the Tombs of Amascut raid. As with the keris partisan, weapon poisons cannot be applied to the partisan.

The keris partisan of corruption retains the effects of the keris partisan, dealing 33% bonus damage against all kalphites and scabarites, alongside a 1/51 chance of finding a gap in their exoskeleton, dealing triple damage. When this special effect occurs, the chatbox will display the message: You slip your weapon through a gap in the creature's chitin, landing a vicious blow.
27289:
The Jewel of the Sun is an untradeable jewel that can be obtained as a reward from the Tombs of Amascut.

The jewel can be attached to the keris partisan to create the keris partisan of the sun, whose special attack can only be used within the Tombs of Amascut.
27291:
The keris partisan of the sun is a one-handed spear requiring 80 Attack to equip. It is made by attaching the jewel of the sun to the keris partisan, granting it a special attack and two unique passive effects that only apply within the Tombs of Amascut raid:

providing a 25% increase to accuracy for targets with less than 25% health

healing the player for 12 Hitpoints upon killing a target at the cost of 5 prayer points; this effect can overheal players up to 12 Hitpoints above their base Hitpoints level

The keris partisan of the sun retains the effects of the keris partisan, dealing 33% bonus damage against all kalphites and scabarites, alongside a 1/51 chance of puncturing a hole in their exoskeleton, dealing triple damage. When this special effect occurs, the chatbox will display the message: You slip your weapon through a gap in the creature's chitin, landing a vicious blow.

As with the keris partisan, weapon poisons cannot be applied to the partisan.
27293: Caches of runes can be obtained from the reward chest within the Tombs of Amascut. It can be opened to receive runes. Based on the value of the runes, the value of the cache can range from 95,000 coins to 1,146,000 coins each.
27295:
A water container is an item obtained in the Path of Crondis within the Tombs of Amascut , where it is used to water the Palm of Resourcefulness in the centre of the challenge room.

To fill it with water, players must obtain water from the waterfalls in the area, whilst avoiding the obstacles in order to minimise water spilling out of the container. Humidify has no effect on this water container.

When the player is hit by an obstacle, the water container will be reduced by 50% of the current level. There is a slight chance that the contents will be reduced by 16% of the current level, rather than 50%. This will stack effectively infinitely, with the current capacity never being reduced below 1% in the game chat.

If a crocodile successfully bites the player, the water container will also be reduced by 50%. Once it's under 15% capacity, successful crocodile bites will reduce the capacity by 10%.
27296: Mirrors are an item obtained in the Path of Het within the Tombs of Amascut . They are used to reflect the energy beams shot by the caster statue .
27297: Neutralising potions are an item obtained in the Path of Apmeken within the Tombs of Amascut . They are poured into the holes in the floor indicated by Apmeken's Sight to neutralise the dangerous fumes that can damage players if left unchecked. In groups, they are also used to cleanse a player of corruption in the challenge room.
27298:
Maisa's message is given to the player by a messenger, who appears to players who've completed the Beneath Cursed Sands quest prior to 24 August 2022, indicating the beginning of the Into the Tombs miniquest.

Players who've completed Beneath Cursed Sands after 24 August 2022 will simply be able to begin the miniquest by entering the Jaltevas Pyramid, and thus cannot ever obtain Maisa's message.
27299:
The antique lamp is an item obtained from Maisa after completing the Into the Tombs miniquest. It grants 50,000 experience in a combat skill of the player's choosing (except Prayer), given that the skill is over level 60.

If destroyed or lost before completion of the miniquest, players can reclaim it by talking to Maisa. Otherwise, players can search the crate in the Tombs of Amascut raid lobby post-miniquest.

27314:

27339:
Liquid adrenaline is an item that can be obtained from the supplies bag within the Tombs of Amascut . It can only be used within the raid.

Drinking it will reduce energy costs for special attacks by half for 150 seconds. This is best used with highly-damaging special attacks, such as those of the dragon claws , as it reduces the cost to only 25% energy per special attack. This reduction will still apply if Overly Draining is enabled, causing all special attacks to cost 50% energy instead of 100%.

It is also worth noting that the player's special attack bar energy is actually out of 1000, meaning no rounding is applied (e.g. a 75% special attack will use 37.5%, rather than being rounded to 37 or 38%).

27347:
Ambrosia is an item that can be obtained from the supplies bag within the Tombs of Amascut . Drinking it will completely restore and boost Hitpoints and Prayer , as well as replenish run energy . In addition, it also acts as a dose of antidote++ (curing venom and poison , while providing immunity to them for 36 seconds and 12 minutes respectively).

Ambrosia is a strong emergency item due to the benefits it provides in one click. It is recommended to use this item as a last resort when hitpoints, prayer, and energy are as low as possible to maximise the benefit obtained from it.

27351:
Honey locust is a stackable food given to players who have failed a challenge or boss room in the Tombs of Amascut. The player can consume it to heal 20 Hitpoints, with overhealing. It will also restore prayer points equal to a dose of prayer potion (7 + 25% of the player's current Prayer level, rounded down), and restore depleted combat stats equal to a dose of super restore (8 + 25% of the player's base level rounded down).

Honey locusts are a catch-up mechanic to ensure that enough supplies are available for subsequent attempts, unless the "On a Diet" invocation is enabled. The quantity given seems to vary according to the room failed; failing the final encounter typically provides more food than the previous paths.

In Expert Mode, if the player has a number of locusts greater than the amount given upon dying (e.g. more than 2 locusts at 300 Raid Level), upon consuming a honey locust their stack size will be reset to 1 with the message Some of your honey locusts fly away under the immense pressure of the tomb.
27352:
Tumeken's Guardian is a pet that can be obtained from completing the Tombs of Amascut . It is a much smaller version of Tumeken's Warden . Players have a chance of receiving the pet when looting the reward chest in the burial chamber. It is possible for it to be obtained in Entry mode, although at a much lower rate.

When a player receives the pet, it will automatically try to appear as their follower. At the same time, a message in the chatbox will state You have a funny feeling like you're being followed. However, if a player receives a pet while having a follower out (for example, a cat ), it will be placed into their inventory . When this occurs, the message in the chatbox will instead state You feel something weird sneaking into your backpack.

If a player's inventory is full and they have a follower already, they will not receive the pet; it must instead be claimed from Probita in East Ardougne .

On death , if a player loses their pet (as a follower or in your inventory) it will wander around the area for 30 seconds before despawning. Even if the player returns in time, the pet cannot be picked up, and can be reclaimed from Probita.

Masori armour set (f) is an item obtained by exchanging a set of items with a Grand Exchange clerk via their right-click "Sets" option and clicking on the appropriate item set within the Item Sets interface.

It is commonly made in order to conveniently sell all three components of the fortified Masori armour at once.
27358: Tome of fire from Last Man Standing is a minigame-exclusive variant of the normal tome of fire . It has no requirements to wield and is a selectable offhand item in the starting loadout in the minigame.
27359:
The Masori assembler is a cosmetic variant of Ava's assembler with a Masori crafting kit added to it. The assembler's colours are based on that of the Masori armour.

The assembler can also be combined with the max cape to change its appearance further by turning it into the Masori assembler max cape. A needle is required in order to create and dismantle the Masori assembler.

If the player dies a PvP death and the item is unprotected, it will remain in the player's inventory; however, the item will be in a broken, unusable state and must be repaired by using it on Perdu and paying him 240,000 coins. The Masori crafting kit will be placed in their gravestone.
27361:
The Masori assembler max cape is the result of combining a Masori assembler with a max cape, or by using a Masori crafting kit on an Assembler max cape, during which the max hood required to be in the player's inventory will automatically convert to the Masori assembler max hood.

Like the other max cape variants (a max cape combined with another cape slot item), the Masori assembler max cape does not have the max cape's stats or perks; it only acts as a cosmetic upgrade to Ava's assembler with the following exceptions when worn:

It acts as a Cooking cape to allow access to the Cooks' Guild without a chef's hat, golden chef's hat, Varrock armour 3 or 4

It acts as a Crafting cape to allow access to the Crafting Guild without a brown apron or golden apron

It acts as a Runecraft cape to prevent essence pouches from degrading (but does not allow access to runic altars)

It acts as a Firemaking cape to work as a piece of warm clothing

It can be used to perform the Skill Cape emote.

The max cape and masori assembler can be separated by using a knife on the cape. Mac will also buy back a max cape, along with its variants, for 1,900,800 coins each. He will return the secondary item any max cape variant was combined with upon doing so.

If the player dies a PvP death and the item is unprotected, it will remain in the player's inventory; however, the item will be in a broken, unusable state and must be repaired by using it on Perdu and paying him 240,000 coins. The Masori crafting kit will be placed in their gravestone.

27368:
The dawn scarab egg is an item that is acquired by using a bucket of water on a scarab dung . Doing so requires having spoken to the Bank Camel after completing the miniquest Into the Tombs .

It is given to the High Priest of Scabaras beneath the Ruins of Ullek for safekeeping, as part of obtaining the ancient key from the Bank Camel .
27369:
The ancient key is an item obtained from the Bank Camel after properly dealing with certain items dropped by the four bosses in the Tombs of Amascut .

The key is used to enter the strange tablet and open the strange chest in order to acquire the mask of rebirth .

Upon death, the ancient key will be lost.
27370:
The mask of rebirth is a cosmetic mask obtained from the strange chest in the hidden room in Osmumten's burial chamber inside the Tombs of Amascut raid, which is accessed by using the ancient key on the strange tablet on the western side of the burial chamber.

It resembles the mask worn by Amascut, although with added cat ears to the mask. Its name refers to the fact that Amascut was the goddess of rebirth prior to becoming corrupted as the Devourer.

This item can be stored in the magic wardrobe of a costume room.
27372:
The Masori crafting kit is an ornament kit obtained from the Tombs of Amascut that can be used on an Ava's assembler or an Assembler max cape along with a needle or costume needle to create a Masori assembler or Masori assembler max cape , respectively. This alters its appearance to match the appearance of Masori armour . It is solely a cosmetic upgrade and does not change the stats.

In order to receive one from the Tombs of Amascut reward chest , players must complete a raid at level 350+ with zero deaths for all party members while also scoring at least 1500 points. Additionally, if a player is already in possession of a Masori crafting kit or Masori assembler, it is not possible to receive another without dropping the item on the ground before opening the reward chest.

Once the kit is used on an Ava's assembler, it can be separated again by using a needle or costume needle on the Masori assembler. This cannot be done for the Masori assembler max cape or the locked version of the assembler, however.

However, if a player receives a pet while having a follower out (for example, a cat ), it will be placed into their inventory . When this occurs, the message in the chatbox will instead state You feel something weird sneaking into your backpack.

If a player's inventory is full and they have a follower already, they will not receive the pet; it must instead be claimed from Probita in East Ardougne .

On death , if a player loses their pet (as a follower or in your inventory) it will wander around the area for 30 seconds before despawning. Even if the player returns in time, the pet cannot be picked up, and can be reclaimed from Probita.

27416:
The speedy teleport scroll is a consumable item purchased for 600 Quest Speedrunning reward points from the Speedrunning Reward Shop, and can be freely reclaimed once purchased. It can be used to unlock a speedrunning-themed Home Teleport animation override. To enable it, players can right click "Animation" on the Home Teleport spell icon in their spellbook and select "Speedy". The speedy home teleport is slightly faster than other home teleport animation overrides, which results in a casting time of only 18 ticks (10.8 seconds) as opposed to the standard 24 ticks (14.4 seconds).

When the player reads the scroll, the chatbox message states This scroll details an incantation which unlocks the Speedy Home Teleport animation. Would you like to learn the incantation? This will consume the scroll.

If a player reads the scroll while already having unlocked the animation, the chatbox message will state This scroll details an incantation which unlocks the Speedy Home Teleport animation. However, you have already unlocked this animation.

The bronze speedrun trophy is an item that can be claimed from Eliza by beating the bronze speedrun time for all available quests in the Quest Speedrunning game mode.

Should a new quest be released for speedrunning, the trophy will be unequipped and the player cannot equip it until the new quest is completed. If the player's inventory is full, the trophy will be banked instead. If the player's inventory and bank are full, the trophy will be destroyed, with the chatbox message appearing upon logging in: " Some new quests have been made available on Speedrunning Worlds. As such, the Speedrun Trophy you had equipped has been destroyed. You can obtain another from Eliza in Varrock Square. "

Dynamite(p) is an item made by using three cave nightshade on a pot of dynamite . When lit with a tinderbox , it will detonate and hit an attackable NPC standing on it after 5 ticks (3 seconds), with a 25% chance of inflicting poison if the target took damage (providing they aren't immune). For larger NPCs, the dynamite must be lit on the south-westernmost tile of the NPC.

Only one poison dynamite can be lit at a time, and it will only hit the target if its in a multicombat area , or if its a single target and the player is actively in combat with it.

The damage dealt via poison dynamite scales with the player's Firemaking level, with the accuracy roll based on the player's highest accuracy stat and the target's corresponding defensive stat.

The treat cauldron is a holiday reward received from completing the 2022 and 2023 Halloween event. It can be changed into various styles, each appearing more and more filled than the last. In addition, it has an emote that can be performed whilst equipped.

Players may also use the cauldron's "Check" option to display the total amount of treats deposited by all players during the event, as well as the personal amount deposited.

During the 2022 and 2023 Halloween event, it was used to trick-or-treat with various NPCs, store collected treats, and deposit treats into the Great Cauldron. The cauldron held a maximum of 8,000 treats. When attempting to put more treats in when the cauldron is full gives the message, Your Treat cauldron is full and can't hold any more treats.

If destroyed, a replacement can be obtained from Diango in Draynor Village or from the toy box of a costume room.

The terrifying charm is an item made by combining the bruised banana , old wool , smelly sock , and spooky egg , all of which can be found by rummaging through the spooky cauldron . When the player makes one, a game message in the chatbox states You combine the questionable items together to create something that could scare Death himself!

When equipped during the 2022 or 2023 Halloween events , "trick-or-treating" NPCs will always result in the player receiving five treats. However, the terrifying charm is destroyed after three uses. With the end of the event, players can still assemble terrifying charms, though they have no use and do not stack in a bank. As this is an ammunition slot item, it is not visible on the player model when equipped.
27485:
The bruised banana is an item that may be obtained by rummaging through the spooky cauldron and taking "something squishy". It is used alongside the old wool, smelly sock, and spooky egg to create the terrifying charm, which are used in the 2022 and 2023 Halloween events.

The bruised banana has an "Eat" option, which gives a game message in the chatbox stating You eat the Bruised banana. It's slimy and not at all delicious. Eating it does not restore health and it cannot be cut with a knife.

During the 2022 and 2023 Halloween event, it was randomly obtained by trick-or-treating men, women, and guards.

27509:
The divine rune pouch is an upgraded variant of the rune pouch, which holds four types of runes instead of three. Each rune can be stacked up to 16,000, the same as a normal rune pouch. The pouch is made by using a needle or costume needle to stitch together a thread of Elidinis and the rune pouch, which requires level 75 Crafting to do; boosts will work.

The pouch can be reverted to its base components, returning the thread and pouch. When reverting the pouch, if the player has a rune in the 4th slot they will be warned all of the runes in that slot will be lost, even if there are only 3 unique runes in the pouch. If players die to other players while carrying a divine rune pouch in the Wilderness or in a PvP world, they will lose it, unless it has been locked via use of a trouver parchment. It should be noted that the Trouver parchment does not protect runes stored within a Divine rune pouch upon death.
27511:
Kasonde's journal is an item found by searching the tent east of the large chasm at the southern end of the Kebos Lowlands . Receiving the journal begins The Garden of Death quest.

Written by Kasonde Shaw , the journal tells about a group named the Old Ones , who were once an ancient race that inhabited what is today the Kingdom of Varlamore , and suggests lizardmen architecture was derived from those of the Old Ones.

The notes can be stored in and retrieved from the bookcase in a player-owned house .
27513: Word translations is an item obtained during The Garden of Death by reading the stone tablet in the dungeon south-east of Mount Quidamortem .
27515: Dirty notes are items obtained throughout the dungeons visited during The Garden of Death . They are written by Kasonde Shaw .

27518:
A warning note is an item upon completing the translation of the stone tablet found in the dungeon beneath the Ruins of Morra during The Garden of Death.

It is written by Kasonde Shaw, who players discover was several steps ahead of them during the quest, and assumes they must have come to the same conclusion as them: that the Old Ones were the first ones to perform soul transference, rather than the Citizens of Arceuus.
27519:
Stone tablets are items obtained during The Garden of Death , where players find them throughout the dungeons built by the Old Ones , an ancient race who inhabited modern-day Varlamore .

The tablets can be read, and are automatically translated as players find new translations during and after the quest via the word translations scroll. When read, translated words in blue indicate that the word is incorrect in context, whilst words in green indicate the word is correct in context.

The only untranslatable phrase is "Zema-Tal" in the last tablet found. Though players infer "Tal" to mean life or soul, "Zema" is not translatable during the quest, but is instead revealed during The Heart of Darkness to mean together, people, and one. With the context of both words and the discovery of the Stranglewood during Desert Treasure II - The Fallen Empire , one possible meaning of Zema-Tal may be what the Old Ones called themselves (ex. Zema-Tal tepat -> We [the Old Ones are] destroyed).

The antique lamp is an item obtained from Radimus Erkle after completing Legends' Quest. Four are given to the player, and each grants 30,000 experience each in four skills of their choice: Attack, Defence, Strength, Hitpoints, Prayer, Magic, Woodcutting, Crafting, Smithing, Herblore, Agility, and Thieving.

The lamps cannot be banked. However, if the player prefers to use them at a later date, they can be destroyed and reclaimed from Radimus whenever the player wishes to do so.
27544:
Ghommal's lucky penny is an item equipped in the ammunition slot, obtained from Ghommal or Laidee Gnonock after claiming the master tier rewards from the Combat Achievements system.

When equipped, it offers a 5% chance to not use a charge when using items that consume charges (such as jewellery and weapons). When equipped in conjunction with an elven or celestial signet , both items will roll independently at a chance to not use a charge while using a piece of crystal equipment . [ 1 ]

If you drop down to the elite tier from the master tier, the item is not deleted, but it cannot be equipped until the master tier is unlocked again. Attempting to equip it without having the master tier displays the message You need to have unlocked the Master tier of Combat Achievement rewards to use this item. .

Ghommal's Avernic defender 5 is an Avernic defender with Ghommal's hilt 5 attached to it. The defender retains the benefits given by the hilt and the bonuses given by the Avernic defender.

The defender can be dismantled any time, returning the defender and the hilt.

If the player dies to a PvP death and the avernic defender is not one of the player's protected items, it will remain in the player's inventory, but will become broken , which means the item is unusable and must be repaired with 600,000 coins by using the item on Perdu .

If you drop down to the elite tier from the master tier, the defender cannot be equipped until either it is dismantled, or the master tier is unlocked again. Attempting to equip it without having the master tier displays the message You need to have completed the Master tier of Combat Achievement rewards to use this item. , and attempting to combine a Ghommal's hilt 5 with an Avernic defender displays the message You need to have completed the Master tier of Combat Achievements to combine a Ghommal's hilt 5. .
