Muphin is a pet dropped by the Phantom Muspah , and is a much smaller version of it. Players can right click " Metamorphosis " to change between its ranged, melee, and shielded forms, providing they have used a charged ice on it to unlock the latter two forms.

When a player receives the pet, it will automatically try to appear as their follower. At the same time, a message in the chatbox will state You have a funny feeling like you're being followed.

However, if a player receives a pet while having a follower out (for example, a cat ), it will be placed into their inventory . When this occurs, the message in the chatbox will instead state You feel something weird sneaking into your backpack.

If a player's inventory is full and they have a follower already, they will not receive the pet; it must instead be claimed from Probita in East Ardougne .

On death , if a player loses their pet (as a follower or in your inventory) it will wander around the area for 30 seconds before despawning. Even if the player returns in time, the pet cannot be picked up, and can be reclaimed from Probita.

The venator bow is a two-handed ranged weapon that was once used by the venators, who were hunters and scouts that served the Zarosian Empire . Requiring level 80 in Ranged to wield, it is made by combining five venator shards . It can fire any type of arrow, including dragon arrows , and has an attack range of 6 (8 when using the "Longrange" combat style).

The bow can be charged with ancient essence to gain a unique passive effect that consumes charges, although the uncharged version can still be used as a regular bow. The passive effect enables the bow to be used against multiple targets with one attack, with the arrow bouncing up to two other nearby monsters.

27616:
Ancient essence is a drop received from defeating the Phantom Muspah . It can also be obtained by mining ancient essence crystals in the Ghorrock Dungeon with 75 Mining , granting 13.5 Mining experience. It is used to create the saturated heart and forgotten brews . It is also used to charge the Venator bow to use its passive effect .

Ancient essence can also be obtained by breaking down ancient icons and venator shards . Ancient icons give 5,000 essence, while venator shards give 50,000 essence.

A total of 150,000 Ancient essence is required to saturate the Imbued heart into a Saturated heart .

When mining the essence, it can be found in one of 3 spots in the wall just south of the entrance to the Phantom Muspah fight. Only one spot will be active, switching between spots randomly with possibly 60 to 90 seconds between each movement, similar to daeyalt essence rocks . Gems can also be obtained while mining, as is the case with most mines.

Mining enhancers have no effect on crystals, however, the Crystal pickaxe's effect does, therefore mining crystals with a charged crystal pickaxe will consume charges.
27622: The frozen cache is a drop received from defeating the Phantom Muspah . When opened, it gives a reward from the Muspah's drop table.
27624:
The ancient sceptre is an upgraded version of the Ancient staff that requires level 70 Magic , 60 Strength , 50 Attack , as well as completion of Secrets of the North to wield. It is made by bringing the untradeable Ancient icon and staff to Eblis . This combination process is irreversible.

The ancient sceptre, like its predecessor, can be used to autocast spells from the Ancient Magicks and standard spellbook . Unlike the ancient staff, the ancient sceptre provides a 10% Magic damage bonus, as well as a passive effect that increases the effects of Ancient Magicks by 10%. This passive effect does not increase the Magic damage bonus.

As a Zarosian item , it will also grant god protection towards Zarosian NPCs in the God Wars Dungeon .

If the player dies a PvP death and the item is unprotected, it is reverted to an ancient staff that is dropped for the killer, and the ancient icon disappears. To prevent this, a Trouver parchment and a payment of 500,000 coins can be given to Perdu in order to permanently lock the item. The locked item will remain in the player's inventory; however, the item will be in a mangled, unusable state and must be repaired by using it on Perdu and paying him 500,000 coins.

A forgotten brew is a potion made by using 20 ancient essence per dose on an ancient brew , requiring 91 Herblore and giving 36 Herblore experience per dose (145 for a 4-dose potion) in the process.

A dose of forgotten brew boosts the player's Magic level by 3 + 8% of their base Magic level, as well as restoring prayer points equal to 2 + 10% of their base Prayer level (with the ability to restore up to 5% over the player's base Prayer level). However, it will also drain the player's Attack , Strength , and Defence levels by 2 + 10% of their current levels.

27641:
The saturated heart is an upgraded version of the imbued heart , created by combining it with 150,000 ancient essence . This process is non-reversible.

The heart grants a 5-minute temporary boost that increases the player's Magic level by 4 + 10% of their level, rounded down (compared to the imbued heart's 1 + 10% boost). In addition, the player's Magic level will not drain below the maximum boost of the heart when used, though it can still be decreased by the use of certain potions or by attacks from an opponent. After five minutes, the player's Magic level will return to normal.

The saturated heart has a five minute cooldown, 2 minutes shorter than the imbued heart ; however players cannot use both simultaneously.

On average, 196 Phantom Muspah would need to be killed to saturate the heart, assuming the player does not break down any uniques. If they do, it would instead take 110 kills, on average.
27643:
Charged ice is a tertiary drop from the Phantom Muspah, guaranteed as a drop if it is killed in under three minutes. It is used on a Muphin to allow it to metamorphose into its melee and shielded forms. Once used on Muphin, it cannot be obtained again, even if the player gets another kill under three minutes.

One way to quicken kill times is to use only a crossbow, relying on the effects of enchanted ruby bolts during its melee and ranged phases, enchanted sapphire bolts during its shielded phase, and enchanted diamond bolts for its post-shield phase. A Zaryte crossbow or Armadyl crossbow is recommended for this, due to their special attacks affecting enchanted bolts (the Zaryte crossbow guarantees activation and passively strengthens its effects, while the Armadyl crossbow doubles base chance of activation). Players who can afford both a tumeken's shadow and twisted bow can easily make the time without having to rely on bolt activation.

Although valued at 10,000, the charged ice's clan loot broadcast values it at 500,000.
27645:
The mystic cards are an equipable set of cards obtained by redeeming the code v1r354cqu1r173und0 from Diango in Draynor Village , via the right-click "Redeem-code" option.

The cards are awarded upon completing the final step of the Runestone Basalt ARG clue-hunting event, which was released alongside the launch of the Shattered Relics League . The appearance of the mystic cards is styled after the tarot cards that could be found perched on the three runestone basalt pillars during that league, which would instantly fade away once interacted with. Diango's dialogue upon redeeming the code implies that The Sage gave him the mystic cards to hold until someone completed the event.

It is one of only four melee weapons with an attack speed of 3, with the other ones being the goblin paint cannon , swift blade , and ham joint , with the former two being two handed weapons only, and the latter two being one-handed weapons that may be equipped along with a shield-slot item. The swift blade also exclusively uses Stab and Slash attack styles whereas the others use Crush , and the mystic cards have negative combat stat bonuses whereas the others have no bonuses.

For this reason, it is a purely cosmetic item and cannot be used to train any melee combat skills. For that, players are forced to choose from the previously mentioned crush-based two-handed goblin paint cannon , or crush-based single-handed ham joint . If a stab or slash-weapon is needed then the one-handed swift blade may be used instead.

Whilst having the Mystic cards equipped, other players will have a right-click "Duel" option listed in their right-click choose option menu. Doing this will result in the player throwing a card towards the target, though of course this deals no damage.

The accursed sceptre is a powered staff requiring 70 Magic to wield. It is a direct upgrade of Thammaron's sceptre, made with level 85 Crafting by using the Skull of Vet'ion on the Thammaron's sceptre (note that this process is reversible). Players without the required level to combine the items may ask Phabelle Bile in Ferox Enclave to do so instead, for a fee of 500,000 coins. The item counts as a Zamorakian item in the God Wars Dungeon. Like most powered staves, it is only tradeable when it is fully uncharged.

The Voidwaker is a melee weapon that requires level 75 Attack to wield. It is acquired by providing the Voidwaker blade , hilt , and gem to Madam Sikaro in the Ferox Enclave Dungeon , who will reassemble the weapon for a fee of 500,000 coins . The three parts are obtained separately as rare drops from Vet'ion , Callisto , and Venenatis (or their lesser counterparts) respectively. Its base stats are roughly comparable to an abyssal whip , and it has one of the most powerful damaging special attacks of any weapon in the game.

Attempting to combine the pieces on your own displays the message You don't think you have the skills to reassemble this weapon yourself. .
27693: Ore packs are an item purchased from the Volcanic Mine reward shop for 4,000 points. A pack contains an assortment of ores such that their total point value, had they been purchased directly from the shop instead, never exceeds 3,300. Since the packs always cost more points than their contents, they should never be purchased except by players looking to obtain a broken dragon pickaxe which they drop at a rate of 1/100 openings.
27695:
A broken dragon pickaxe is a rare loot from opening ore packs from the Volcanic Mine reward shop .

It can be repaired back to a dragon pickaxe by speaking to Nurmof in the Dwarven Mine , for a fee of 2,500,000 coins . Repairing a broken dragon pickaxe does not increase the count for a collection log slot for a dragon pickaxe.

Although it has a 'Wield' option, it is not wieldable; this option instead prompts the dialogue: I should get this repaired before I try and use it. Maybe Petrified Pete will know someone who can help.

When receiving the pickaxe from an ore pack, the message You find something unexpected in the ore pack... it's a broken pickaxe! will be displayed.

The diamond speedrun trophy is an item that can be claimed from Eliza by beating the diamond speedrun time for all available quests in the Quest Speedrunning game mode. When equipped, the trophy can be right-clicked to perform the Trophy Emote.

Should a new quest be released for speedrunning, the trophy will be unequipped and the player cannot equip it until the new quest is completed. If the player's inventory is full, the trophy will be banked instead. If the player's inventory and bank are full, the trophy will be destroyed, with the chatbox message appearing upon logging in: " Some new quests have been made available on Speedrunning Worlds. As such, the Speedrun Trophy you had equipped has been destroyed. You can obtain another from Eliza in Varrock Square. "

By selecting the "Swap" option on the sceptre, players can switch between the regular sceptre (a powered staff ) and the autocasting sceptre, which can autocast offensive combat spells from the standard spellbook (including Flames of Zamorak ) and the Ancient Magicks .

Nightshade , also known as belladonna , is a stackable variant of cave nightshade that can be harvested from the Draynor Manor and Auburnvale belladonna patches after planting belladonna seeds . It is used in Herblore to make weapon poison(++) or as an addition to dynamite for poison dynamite .

Players can eat nightshade, but this is not recommended in most situations. When eaten, the player will say, "Ahhhh! What have I done!" in a dialogue box, and take up to 15 damage (damage taken scales with the player's current Hitpoints ). Additionally, the message You eat the nightshade... The nightshade was highly poisonous. will be displayed. Like most self-damaging items, it is impossible for the player to kill themselves with it. ( Note: It is possible for players to eat this without losing health; if the player were to accidentally eat the nightshade, they can teleport away to avoid losing any hitpoints, provided they don't click "Continue" on the dialogue text.)

Damage taken is given by the following formula:

D a m a g e ( H i t p o i n t s ) = { 15 , if H i t p o i n t s ≥ 20 ⌊ H i t p o i n t s 2 ⌋ if H i t p o i n t s < 20

Harvesting nightshade is a task in the hard Lumbridge and Draynor Diary .

Vesta's chainbody (bh) is a piece of armour requiring 78 Defence to wear, and is purchased from the Bounty Hunter Store for 600 Bounty Hunter points. When worn alongside Vesta's plateskirt (bh), the accuracy of melee special attacks are increased by 15%. It can be converted into its corrupted variant by speaking to a Corrupted Warrior.

As with all Ancient Warriors' equipment from Bounty Hunter, it is initially purchased in inactive form and must be charged with 5,000,000 coins before it can be used by the player. In addition, it can only be used within Daimon's Crater, Castle Wars, Clan Wars, Soul Wars, the TzHaar Fight Pit, and both the player-owned house and Clan Hall combat rings; attempting to attack anything outside the listed areas will result in the player being interrupted from doing so.

Upon dying in PvP, the coins used to activate the item are given to the killer, and players are left with the inactive variant.

27853:
The dark bow (bh) is a two-handed ranged weapon that requires level 60 in Ranged to wield. Proposed as a reward for the 2023 Bounty Hunter minigame rework, it is available from the supplies table in a beta world as a test armour for the Bounty Hunter Rewards Beta.

The imbued bow has +105 Ranged attack, instead of the regular bow's +95, and uses 45% of the special bar when performing the special attack, instead of the regular bow's 55%. In addition, the minimum hit from the special attack is increased from 5 to 7 for non-dragon arrows, and 8 to 10 for dragon arrows. The special attack's damage also rolls between the minimum and maximum damage, rather than zero to max. Lastly, when the dark bow (bh) performs an attack, both arrows hit the target simultaneously instead of having a short delay between the hitsplats.

This item can only be used in player killing; attempting to attack an NPC will result in the player being interrupted from doing so.

The giant bronze dagger is a reward obtained from the 2023 Easter event , as well as subsequent Easter events. Despite its size, its stats are equivalent to the normal-sized bronze dagger , except it weighs much more and is categorically a 2h sword . When wielded, players will be given a unique animation akin to that of the colossal blade .

If destroyed, a replacement can be obtained from Diango in Draynor Village or from the toy box of a costume room .

Attempting to use it outside of Treasure Trails results in the game message This spade is only sturdy enough for certain loose soil often found on the trail of treasure.

If destroyed, a replacement can be obtained from Diango in Draynor Village or from the toy box of a costume room .

28067:
The fighter torso (or) is a cosmetic variant of the fighter torso with a bounty hunter ornament kit added to it.

If the player dies a PvP death at level 20 Wilderness or below and the item is unprotected, it will remain in the player's inventory; however, the item will be in a broken, unusable state and must be repaired by using it on Perdu and paying him 150,000 coins. The ornament kit will be placed in their gravestone.

If the player dies a PvP death above level 20 Wilderness and the item is unprotected, it will be converted to coins. To prevent this, a Trouver parchment and a payment of 500,000 coins can be given to Perdu in order to permanently lock the item. The locked item will remain in the player's inventory; however, the item will be in a mangled, unusable state and must be repaired by using it on Perdu and paying him 500,000 coins. The ornament kit will be placed in their gravestone.

Unlike its base variant, it cannot be stored in the storage space of a costume room.

28108:
The rainbow scarf is a neck slot item originally introduced as a reward from Gilbert for completing the Gilbert's Colours event in 2017. It can either be purchased from Diango's Toy Store for 120 coins , or obtained freely from Gilbert in the flower field south-east of Barbarian Village .

There are nine unique versions of the scarf representing different variants of sexual orientation or gender identity , whose colours can be changed at any time by right-clicking the "Change" option on the scarf. When switched to another style other than the pride (rainbow) style, the item is renamed to a colourful scarf .

It can be used as warm clothing for the Wintertodt. Note that the scarf is always destroyed on death; you will need to reacquire it if you die while fighting the Wintertodt.

If destroyed, a replacement can be obtained from Diango in Draynor Village or from the toy box of a costume room .

28128:
The love crossbow is a fun weapon unlocked by speaking to Gilbert in the flower field south-east of Barbarian Village, after which it can be obtained from Diango or retrieved from a toy box built in the costume room. It was originally received as a reward for completing the 2023 Pride event.

Despite resembling a crossbow, it is in fact a two-handed melee weapon, and as such cannot be used to fire bolts or mith grapples. Like the goblin paint cannon, ham joint, swift blade, and mystic cards, the love crossbow is one of the few melee weapons to possess an attack speed of 3. However, due to hefty offensive penalties similar to those of the mystic cards, it is not advised to train with it.

Whilst having the crossbow equipped, other players will have a right-click "Enamour" option listed in their choose option menu. Doing this will result in the player firing a "love" bolt towards the target, causing hearts to appear around the player and their target. This deals no damage, and can only be done if the target is at least one tile away from the player.
28130:
The strange icon is an item obtained from the Barrows chest after defeating all six Barrows brothers during the miniquest His Faithful Servants . At the end of the miniquest the icon is given to the Strange Old Man , who disintegrates it by casting a spell. [ 1 ]

Looting the icon while not having enough inventory space will cause the icon to be destroyed, requiring the completion of another Barrows run in order to obtain another.

It is revealed during Desert Treasure II that the relic is one of the three artefacts Azzanadra had been searching for in order to contact Zaros , alongside the relic and the Frostenhorn .
28132:
The dusty lamp is an item obtained from the Strange Old Man after completing the miniquest His Faithful Servants. It grants 20,000 Prayer experience when rubbed; there is no minimum Prayer level required to use it.

The lamp cannot be banked. However, if the player prefers to use it at a later date, it can be destroyed and reclaimed from the Strange Old Man whenever the player wishes to do so.
28133:
The crypt map is an item obtained from the Strange Old Man after completing the miniquest His Faithful Servants .

The "Study" option on the item will permanently reveal the minimap whilst inside the Barrows crypt. After this, the crypt map is destroyed.
28134:
Anima-infused bark is the primary currency used in the Forestry Shop, which are earned by completing Forestry events that occasionally occur whilst Woodcutting or by rummaging Vale offerings. While free-to-play players can obtain this item, the only item which can be purchased from the Friendly Forester is the felling axe handle (and the felling axe it creates is members-only); all other rewards are only available for members.

Anima-infused bark can be stored inside the Forestry kit, alongside various tools, gear, and leaves.

One anima bark is valued at 201.42 coins when purchasing the felling axe handle from the Forestry Shop, and 211.53 coins when purchasing sawmill vouchers.
28136:
The Forestry kit is an item worn in the cape slot used to store a variety of Forestry -related items, such as anima-infused bark and tree leaves. It can be obtained for free from the Forestry Shop in Draynor Village , Prifddinas , Seers' Village , or Nemus Retreat . The Forestry kit is required for players to spawn events , meaning at least one player chopping the tree needs to either be wearing one or have one in their inventory.

Players can quickly empty the contents of the kit by right-clicking "Use" on the item whilst the bank interface is open. This empties the contents into the inventory, which can then be deposited into the bank.

The contents of the Forestry kit are accessible from any Forestry kit in the player's possession, but if the player destroys their last kit, all contents will be lost. Ultimate Ironmen however, can safely deathpile and allow the kit to despawn without losing its contents.

This item can be stored in the magic wardrobe of a costume room .
28138:
The funky shaped log is an item that is used on the beaver pet (and consumed) in order to permanently allow it to metamorphose into a variety of log-based colours.

It is purchased from the Forestry Shop for 15,000 anima-infused bark, as well as 500 noted oak, willow, teak, maple, mahogany, arctic pine, yew, magic, and redwood logs. Players (excluding Ultimate Ironmen) who have not used it on a beaver can sell the log back to the shop to get 80% of its cost in bark and logs back.

After consuming the funky shaped log, in order to change the colour of the beaver pet, the player needs to use the corresponding log on it. If the beaver has been recoloured and the player then metamorphs it to either the fox or the pheasant, then the beaver will return to the default colour when changed back.
28140:
A log basket is an item that allows players to store a combined total of 28 logs of any type. The basket can be purchased from the Forestry Shop for 300 noted oak logs , 300 noted willow logs , and 5,000 anima-infused bark . Players (excluding Ultimate Ironmen ) can sell the basket back to the rewards shop for an 80% return of the cost to purchase. The basket must be closed before being sold back.

This item can be stored in the magic wardrobe of a costume room .
28141: Forester's tea was an item during the Forestry Open Beta update that could be brewed using different types of leaves and roots, providing boosts to production and gathering skills. Players can add up to ten of these, in any combination they wish. Jagex cited player feedback as the primary reason for not introducing forester's tea into the game, stating the system would add an "unnecessary amount of complexity to a skill whose roots are very simple and easy to understand for all players." 28157:
Forester's rations are a stackable item used in Woodcutting . When in the inventory or stored in a Forestry kit , a player wielding or having a felling axe in their inventory (as the highest or equal-highest-tier axe, if multiple axes are carried) will receive 10% more Woodcutting experience each time they successfully chop a tree and gain a 20% chance not to receive a log. One ration is consumed each time a tree is successfully chopped with a felling axe (meaning Woodcutting experience is received), whether or not logs are gathered. When this happens, a game message in the chatbox will state You consume a Forester's ration to fuel a mighty chop. You strike a clean cut without gathering any material.

Sulliusceps are also affected by Forester's rations in the same way as trees that grant logs.

Additionally, if your run energy is under 90%, there is a 30% chance of consuming a forester's ration to restore 20% of your run energy when successfully chopping a tree. Both regular axes and felling axes can trigger this effect. When this happens, a game message in the chatbox will state You consume a Forester's ration and feel energised. if chopping with a regular axe or The Forester's ration restores some of your energy. if chopping with a felling axe.
28159:
The secateurs blade is an item purchased from the Forestry Shop for 20 anima-infused bark, as well as 10 noted oak logs and 5 noted willow logs. These logs can be bought on the Grand Exchange for 515.

With level 35 Woodcutting and Smithing, players can create secateurs attachments by combining the blade and an iron bar; each set will produce 50 attachments.
28161:
Secateurs attachments are a stackable item used in Woodcutting. While in the inventory or stored in a forestry kit, when players receive a leaf from cutting trees (a 1/4 chance for every log cut, regardless of Woodcutting level), a secateurs attachment is consumed and an additional second leaf is obtained.

They can be created by using a secateurs blade, purchased from the Forestry Shop, on an iron bar. This requires level 35 Woodcutting and Smithing, granting 32 Crafting experience; each set will produce 50 attachments.

They will not be consumed when failing to roll for a leaf, nor are they consumed from chopping trees that do not have a corresponding leaf, such as camphor, ironwood, or rosewood trees.
28163:
The clothes pouch is an item that needs to be attached to the Forestry kit or basket (irreversible process) to allow the player to store the lumberjack or Forestry outfit to receive the outfit's benefits without having to wear them. Players can receive a partial amount of Woodcutting experience if at least one piece of either the lumberjack or Forestry outfit is placed inside. The upgraded Forestry kit must be equipped or in the player's inventory to receive the bonus. Players who have achieved level 99 Woodcutting can store both the clothes and cape pouches inside the Forestry kit.

They can be created by using a piece of leather on the clothes pouch blueprint with a thread in the inventory. Doing so requires level 50 Woodcutting and Crafting, and the blueprint is consumed in the process. The kit does not change any interface options when the clothes pouch is attached to the Forestry kit.

If the forestry basket is destroyed while the clothes pouch is attached, new forestry kits from the forestry shop will come with the clothes pouch (with any clothing sets) already installed, along with any set stored with anima-infused bark ghost banked. However, the log basket and brace are lost and must be reacquired.

While the clothes pouch item itself weighs 1kg, when attached to the Forestry kit and with an outfit stored, the Forestry kit weighs 0 kg when worn.
28166:
The clothes pouch blueprint is an item purchased from the Forestry Shop for 10,000 anima-infused bark, as well as 300 noted willow and maple logs. These logs can be bought on the Grand Exchange for 9,600.

With level 50 Woodcutting and Crafting, players can craft a clothes pouch by using a piece of leather on the blueprint whilst having thread in the inventory.
28169:
The forestry top is a cosmetic variant of the lumberjack top , purchased from the Forestry Shop for 1,250 anima-infused bark , the lumberjack top, and 60 noted oak , willow , teak , maple , mahogany , arctic pine , yew , magic , and redwood logs .

Like the lumberjack top, the forestry top provides a +0.8% boost in Woodcutting experience, and is increased to +2.5% when the full forestry outfit is worn.

This item can be stored in the armour case of a costume room , as part of the Lumberjack Costume: Forestry set. Ultimate Ironmen will be unable to retrieve individual pieces until the full set is stored. It can also be stored in the Forestry kit with a Clothes pouch in order to receive the outfit's benefits without having to wear them. However, bonuses from other outfits, such as the graceful outfit , will override the clothes pouch if worn.

The felling axe handle is an item used in the process of creating felling axes . Using the handle on any regular axe within a 3x3 area of an anvil, including through walls, with a hammer in the inventory will irreversibly turn it into a felling axe. The felling axe handle is available from the Forestry Shop for 10,000 anima-infused bark and 500 noted oak logs . These logs can be bought on the Grand Exchange for 20,500 . While this item is free-to-play obtainable, the felling axes it creates are members-only .

Felling axes take priority over other axes when used to chop trees, even if you're wielding a normal axe.
28179:
Leprechaun charms were a stackable item used in Woodcutting . When in the inventory or stored in a Forestry kit , there was a chance of spawning a Woodcutting Leprechaun , depositing logs to the player's bank. If the player's charm was consumed after attracting the Leprechaun, he also acted as a Bank Deposit Box . The chance of this occurring was scaled on the number of players present. When a charm was consumed, a game message in the chatbox stated: Your charm has attracted a Leprechaun.

They were created by combining a clover insignia , purchased from the Forestry Shop , with an emerald and ball of wool . This required level 70 Woodcutting , 70 Crafting , and 35 Farming ; each set produced 10 charms.
28181:
Clover insignias were an item purchased from the Forestry Shop for 200 anima-infused bark and 15 noted oak logs.

With level 70 Woodcutting, 70 Crafting, and 35 Farming, players created leprechaun charms by using the insignia with an emerald and ball of wool; each set produced 10 charms.
28183:
Mulch is an item used during the Struggling sapling Forestry event , where players must create the right combination of resource piles to feed the struggling sapling . These resource piles include droppings , green leaves , rotting leaves , splintered bark , and wild mushrooms .

Players can use the mulch's "check" option to see which ingredients are currently used in it. In addition, the "History" option shows players an interface of the struggling sapling 's health, as well as the best and most recent combination of mulch discovered during the event. Note that this interface is identical to the "Inspect" option on the struggling sapling.
28184:
Bees on a stick was a stackable item used in Woodcutting. When in the inventory or stored in a Forestry kit, there was a chance of the flowering tree event appearing. The chance of this occurring was scaled based on the number of players present; when a stick was consumed, a game message in the chatbox stated, Your Bee on a stick buzzes excitedly as it detects pollen-rich plants nearby., and the player will receive roughly double the anima-infused bark for each pollination as well as double bark rewarded at the end of the event.

It was created by combining powdered pollen, purchased from the Forestry Shop, with logs and a ball of wool. This required being next to a beehive, as well as level 35 Woodcutting and 50 Hunter; each set produced 10 sticks.
28190:
Powdered pollen was an item purchased from the Forestry Shop for 300 anima-infused bark and 15 noted willow logs .

With level 35 Woodcutting and 50 Hunter , players created bees on a stick by combining powdered pollen with logs and a ball of wool , whilst being next to a beehive ( beehives built by the player could not be used). Each set of the aforementioned items produced 10 sticks.
28192: Strange pollen is an item used during the flowering tree event, where players must transfer it to a specific pair of flowering bushes to pollinate them.
28193:
An unfired cup is made by using soft clay on a potter's wheel , requiring level 3 Crafting and granting 8.5 experience. One piece of soft clay will produce four unfired cups.

It is then made into an empty cup by placing it into a pottery oven , granting 8.5 Crafting experience. Unlike shaping the clay, firing it has no Crafting level requirement. At lower levels, an unfired cup can crack in the oven, destroying the cup and granting no experience.
28196:
The bronze felling axe is a type of felling axe requiring an Attack level of 1 to be equipped, and a Woodcutting level of 1 to be used. Players can create the axe by using a felling axe handle on a bronze axe while having a hammer in their inventory and standing next to an anvil ; this process is irreversible , but the felling axe itself remains tradeable.

Bronze felling axes will chop at the same speed as a normal bronze axe. If the player is carrying forester's rations however (either in the inventory or inside a forestry kit ), they will receive 10% more Woodcutting experience each time they successfully chop a tree and gain a 20% chance not to receive logs when chopping trees (or tree roots in the Rising Roots forestry event), at the cost of consuming one ration. This also results in a 20% chance to not receive anima-infused bark from tree roots.

If the player has no rations on their person, the felling axe will function like a regular bronze axe.

28220:
The crystal felling axe is a type of felling axe requiring a level of 70 Attack and 50 Agility to be equipped respectively, and a Woodcutting level of 71 to be used. Players can create the axe by either using a felling axe handle on a crystal axe while standing near a singing bowl, or by using the singing bowl directly with a dragon felling axe, a crystal tool seed, and 120 crystal shards. Doing so requires level 76 Smithing[boostable] and 76 Crafting[boostable] to sing the crystal, and grants 6,000 experience in both skills. Players can configure the charges while the axe is in their bank by right-clicking on Configure-Charges, as long as players have the required materials. If the player does not meet the Smithing and Crafting requirements, they can have Conwenna or Reese sing the crystal for them for an extra 60 crystal shards, for a total of 180.

Applying the felling handle to the axe is irreversible: a one-handed axe upgraded into a felling axe can never revert to being one-handed. However, the standard process of reverting crystal to dragon does apply, meaning a crystal felling axe can be reverted into a dragon felling axe (while losing all crystal shards used to make and charge it). The crystal felling axe will start off with 10,000 charges, unless a previously used crystal axe was used in its creation, in which case it will instead inherit the remaining charges from that axe.

Crystal felling axes will chop at the same speed as a normal crystal axe, possessing the same special attack as the dragon axe, giving the player a 15% increase in efficiency over the rune axe, surpassing the 10% increase of the dragon axe. This makes the crystal felling axe approximately 4.5% faster than the dragon felling axe.

If the player is carrying forester's rations however (in the inventory or inside a forestry kit), they will receive 10% more Woodcutting experience per each log and gain a 20% chance not to receive logs when chopping trees (or tree roots in the Rising Roots forestry event), at the cost of consuming one ration. This also results in a 20% chance to not receive anima-infused bark from tree roots.

If the player has no rations on their person, the felling axe will function like a regular crystal axe.

28229:
The beaver is a members-only skilling pet that can be obtained while training Woodcutting. A strange sound is heard when you obtain the beaver while Woodcutting. The chances of getting it are dependent on the player's Woodcutting level, the base drop chance for a given tree, and the rate of successfully chopping logs.

When a player receives the pet, it will automatically try to appear as their follower. At the same time, a message in the chatbox will state You have a funny feeling like you're being followed. However, if a player receives a pet while having a follower out (for example, a cat), it will be placed into their inventory. When this occurs, the message in the chatbox will instead state You feel something weird sneaking into your backpack. This message also occurs if there is one last inventory space while the player already has a pet following them, in which case the pet will appear in the inventory instead and the resource dropped to the ground.

On death, if a player loses their pet (as a follower or in your inventory) it will wander around for 30 seconds before disappearing completely. It can then be reclaimed from Probita in East Ardougne for no cost.

28238:
The blood ancient sceptre is a sceptre requiring 75 Magic , 60 Strength , and 50 Attack to wield. It is made by attaching the blood quartz , dropped by Vardorvis , to the ancient sceptre ; this process can be reversed, allowing players to switch between quartzes as desired.

Like its predecessor, it will increase the effects of Ancient Magicks by 10%, with the added effect of Blood spells being able to overheal up to 10% over the player's base Hitpoints .

The blood ancient sceptre finds practical use in the Inferno for improved Blood Barrages at the end of waves, to start the next wave at up to 108 Hitpoints, as well as against God Wars Dungeon boss bodyguards in between boss kills.

If the player dies a PvP death at level 20 Wilderness or below and the item is unprotected, it will remain in the player's inventory; however, the item will be in a broken, unusable state and must be repaired by using it on Perdu and paying him 260,849 coins . The price is defined as 200,000 coins plus the current guide price of an ancient staff .

If the player dies a PvP death above level 20 Wilderness and the item is unprotected, it will be converted to coins. To prevent this, a Trouver parchment and a payment of 500,000 coins can be given to Perdu in order to permanently lock the item. The locked item will remain in the player's inventory; however, the item will be in a mangled, unusable state and must be repaired by using it on Perdu and paying him 500,000 coins.

The ultor ring is one of four ancient rings which currently boasts the highest strength bonus of any ring, surpassing the imbued berserker ring by +4. It cannot be equipped in the Lassar Undercity .

When charged, the ring can teleport players to the Ancient Vault ; additional teleports to the Ghorrock Dungeon , the Scar , the Lassar Undercity , and the Stranglewood can be unlocked by using tablets received as drops from Duke Sucellus , The Leviathan , The Whisperer , and Vardorvis respectively on the ring. It may contain a maximum of 1,000 charges (costing 1,054,000 coins to fully charge, or 1,054 coins per teleport). Players can configure the charges while the ring is in their bank by right-clicking on Configure-Charges, as long as players have the required materials. Uncharging the ring does refund the runes.

If lost, another can be obtained from the Mysterious Bandit in the Ancient Vault for 75,000 coins. Multiple rings can be purchased from the bandit.

Despite the ring's connections with Zaros' generals, it does not provide Zarosian god protection in the God Wars Dungeon .

In PvP death, the ring turns into 75,000 coins regardless of Wilderness location. Any charges in the ring will be lost along with the ring itself.

28336:
The ancient blood ornament kit is an item obtained by defeating the awakened variants of the Leviathan, the Whisperer, Vardorvis, and Duke Sucellus. To obtain the item, the player must kill all four bosses at least once in their awakened state, with the kit being awarded from the final awakened boss.

It is used on Torva armour pieces to cosmetically enhance them. While the kit itself has unlimited uses, players must use 20,000 blood runes to convert each armour piece.

If the ancient blood ornament kit is lost by any means (such as destroying it or dying before being able to pick it up) it can be regained by killing any of the four awakened bosses.
28338:
The Soulreaper axe is a two-handed axe that requires 80 Attack and Strength to wield. It is created by combining four untradeable components, obtained as drops from The Leviathan , The Whisperer , Vardorvis , and Duke Sucellus , alongside 2,000 blood runes and level 75 Magic (which cannot be boosted).

Despite being made from items dropped by prominent Zarosians , the item itself does not grant god protection towards Zarosian NPCs in the God Wars Dungeon .
28341:
Musca mushrooms are an item used during the fight with Duke Sucellus . They are picked from musca mushrooms found at the east side of the asylum, past the extremities .

They are ground into musca powder , which are mixed in the Fermentation Vat alongside arder powder and salax salt to create arder-musca poisons to wake the Duke.

You will get more powder from each mushroom with a higher Herblore level. 2 potions require 3 mushrooms below 80 herblore, and 2 mushrooms at level 80 or higher.
28342:
Musca powder is the result of using a pestle and mortar on a musca mushroom , where between five and six powders are given per mushroom with the amount being tied to your Herblore level. The amount of powder produced is based on the equation ⌊ l e v e l − 20 10 ⌋ , and is capped between 1 and 6 powders. Due to the required 62 Herblore for Desert Treasure II , the only amounts players will normally see are 4, 5, and 6 powders. 80 Herblore will give the player the max amount of powder. Six are mixed in the asylum's Fermentation Vat , alongside six Arder powder and six Salax salt , to create one Arder-musca poison , which are used to wake Duke Sucellus .

Musca powder can also be fed to Duke Sucellus to deal 5 damage to him, requiring 40 powder total to awaken the boss.

The blackstone fragment is a modified shard of the ancient pillar found in the Lassar Undercity. During the quest, it is used to instantly leave the Shadow Realm within the Lassar Undercity upon activating it. It can be also used to recall the shadow blocker, revitalising idol, and anima portal back to the player's inventory from wherever they were placed.

The fragment must also be in the player's inventory during the fight against The Whisperer, as it is used at various points in the fight where her attacks must be countered from within the Shadow Realm; the player will be prompted to activate it when it begins glowing yellow. Without the fragment, the player will refuse to fight her.

If players lose the fragment, it can be re-obtained by speaking to Ketla, or from Ketla's workbench in the Residential District, located in the building just north of the Western Residential District teleporter.

28390: Barricades are an item obtained during Desert Treasure II . They are used to protect Kasonde and the player from the horde of strangled converging toward them. 28392:
Satchels are an item obtained during Desert Treasure II . They are used to protect Kasonde and the player from the horde of strangled converging toward them. By placing them on the ground, the player can use a detonator to blow up the strangled within a 7x7 area around the satchel.

If the player is in the explosion radius, they will take damage equal to 33% of their Hitpoints level. This damage can kill the player, resulting in an unsafe death where items are sent to a gravestone. Satchels will damage Kasonde, but cannot deal a killing blow against him. Satchels will not damage barricades placed by the player, nor can satchels damage Strangled through barricades.

Unlike most items with a "Destroy" option, there is no confirmation message when attempting to destroy a satchel.
28393: The detonator is an item obtained during Desert Treasure II. It is used to protect Kasonde and the player from the horde of strangled converging toward them; by placing satchels on the ground, the player can use the detonator to blow up the strangled within its vicinity.

The stink bomb can be obtained by searching a stone chest in The Stranglewood , where players first meet Kasonde .

When set off, a stink bomb will attract the nearest strangled to the location it was set off to help keep them away from the player. A game message will state You set off a stink bomb. It smells as bad as you'd expect.

Stink bombs have a maximum range of ten squares, forming a 21x21 tile attraction area centred on the square where the bomb is set off.
28473:
The blood ancient sceptre is a sceptre requiring 75 Magic , 60 Strength , and 50 Attack to wield. It is made by attaching the blood quartz , dropped by Vardorvis , to the ancient sceptre ; this process can be reversed, allowing players to switch between quartzes as desired.

Like its predecessor, it will increase the effects of Ancient Magicks by 10%, with the added effect of Blood spells being able to overheal up to 10% over the player's base Hitpoints .

The blood ancient sceptre finds practical use in the Inferno for improved Blood Barrages at the end of waves, to start the next wave at up to 108 Hitpoints, as well as against God Wars Dungeon boss bodyguards in between boss kills.

If the player dies a PvP death at level 20 Wilderness or below and the item is unprotected, it will remain in the player's inventory; however, the item will be in a broken, unusable state and must be repaired by using it on Perdu and paying him 260,849 coins . The price is defined as 200,000 coins plus the current guide price of an ancient staff .

If the player dies a PvP death above level 20 Wilderness and the item is unprotected, it will be converted to coins. To prevent this, a Trouver parchment and a payment of 500,000 coins can be given to Perdu in order to permanently lock the item. The locked item will remain in the player's inventory; however, the item will be in a mangled, unusable state and must be repaired by using it on Perdu and paying him 500,000 coins.

The trinket of vengeance is an item in Deadman Mode and its seasonal variants Apocalypse and Armageddon which casts the Vengeance spell. Though it has no requirements to use, it retains the 30 second casting cooldown that the spell has.

Like the sigils , trinkets are dropped by most monsters (via the Deadman Mode drop table ) and are tradeable on the Grand Exchange .

This trinket is not accessible in Deadman: Annihilation . In Deadman: All Stars Season 3 , a version of the trinket that had only two charges before being destroyed was available.
28564:
The trinket of fairies is an item in Deadman Mode that allows players to remotely access fairy rings , spirit trees , and tool leprechauns that they have access to. The trinket cannot be used beyond level 30 Wilderness .

It can be acquired as a drop from monsters found during breaches .
28567:
The trinket of advanced weaponry is an item in Deadman Mode that can be opened to give one of eight corrupted weapons, which are weaker versions of existing weapons. It cannot be opened if there is a player or obstacle in the way that would block the animation of opening it, and attempting to do so gives the message You must have nothing surrounding you to open this trinket. .

It can be acquired as a drop from monsters found during breaches , as well as from looting the Deadman's chest .
28570:
The trinket of undead is an item in Deadman Mode that allows players to summon a special thrall of the player's choice, being either TzRek-Zuk , the Kalphite Princess , or Wisp . These thralls function the same as greater thralls, functioning as a melee, ranged, or magic thrall respectively. Though the trinket has no requirements to use, it does have a 10 second cooldown.

Being identical to regular greater thralls, the trinket's thralls always deal successful hits , with the damage roll ranging from 0-3. The damage roll can be increased to 0-15 with the sigil of the augmented thrall .

It can be acquired as a drop from monsters found during breaches , as well as from looting the Deadman's chest .
28573:
The chest key is an item obtained during The Path of Glouphrie , found by searching the silver chest in the north-west corner of the storeroom of the Tree Gnome Village dungeon . It is obtained alongside Yewnock's notes .

The key is used to unlock the gold chest , which contains the strongroom key . Once the chest has been unlocked, the chest key can no longer be obtained.
28574:
The strongroom key is an item obtained during The Path of Glouphrie , found by opening the gold chest in the storeroom of the Tree Gnome Village dungeon .

It is used to open the gates in the western side of the storeroom to access Yewnock's machine. Once the gate has been unlocked the key can no longer be obtained.

If lost, it can be reobtained after the quest by searching the gold chest in the Tree Gnome Village Dungeon for a crystal chime seed.

The notes can be stored in and retrieved from the bookcase in a player-owned house.

The warped sceptre is a powered staff requiring 62 Magic to wield, available as a drop from warped terrorbirds or warped tortoises with level 56 Slayer . Like most powered staves, it is only tradeable when it is fully uncharged.

Its cast speed gives it an improved damage output compared to the Iban's staff (at 81 or higher Magic), but less than the trident of the seas . This is particularly useful for midgame ironmen players who are unable to kill Cave krakens . Additionally, the fact that the runes it uses are stored within the staff makes it useful over the Iban's staff (which doesn't store runes) when inventory slots are scarce.

On death in the wilderness, if you have the sceptre as one of your protected items, it will not lose charges. The built-in spell cannot be used against other players in the wilderness.

28591: Tainted essence chunks are an item that is obtained from mining amalgamations in the Scar essence mine. These are deposited into Ventriculus openings, with each chunk providing five tainted essence, which can then be processed in two ways: the first is to clean it via the essence orifice, converting two tainted essence into one noted pure essence. The second way - acquiring runic extracts from the extract orifice - requires having deposited a certain amount of coins into Hagus' coffer, depending on the type of extract they wish to acquire:
28593:
Warped extracts are a catalyst used in runecrafting when crafting elemental, mind, and body runes, by giving 250 extra runes per extract.

The extract can be obtained in the Scar essence mine from the extract orifice by depositing tainted essence chunks into a ventriculus opening, and having 1,250 coins within Hagus' coffer to convert the tainted essence into a warped extract.

As warped extracts result in a cost of 5 coins for each rune crafted, it is suited for Ironman players who plan to use the runes for themselves.

If players happen to make too many extracts, they can be refunded for 90% of their original cost by taking them to Hagus in the Scar.
28595:
Twisted extracts are a catalyst used in runecrafting when crafting chaos, cosmic, combination runes (except aether), and sunfire runes, by giving 60 extra runes per extract.

The extract can be obtained in the Scar essence mine from the extract orifice by depositing tainted essence chunks into a ventriculus opening, and having 6,000 coins within Hagus' coffer to convert the tainted essence into a twisted extract.

Because using twisted extracts result in a cost of 100 coins for each rune crafted, it is not recommended to use extracts as a means of making money; rather, it is intended for Ironman players who plan to use the runes for themselves.

When using twisted extracts to craft combination runes without the use of a binding necklace, extracts will only be consumed for successfully created runes. In other words, a rune that fails to combine will not also delete a twisted extract.

If players happen to make too many extracts, they can be refunded for 90% of their original cost by taking them to Hagus in the Scar.

Sunfire runes require an additional twisted extract for each base multiplied rune crafted. For example, if a player can craft 3 sunfire runes per essence at 98 Runecraft, 3 twisted extract are needed per essence. Each rune created will receive the bonus multiplier provided by the extract. For the previous example, 183 sunfire runes will be created per essence.
28597:
Mangled extracts are a catalyst used in runecrafting when crafting nature , law , astral , and death runes , by giving 60 extra runes per extract.

The extract can be obtained in the Scar essence mine from the extract orifice by depositing tainted essence chunks into a ventriculus opening , and having 12,000 coins within Hagus ' coffer to convert the tainted essence into a mangled extract.

Because using mangled extracts result in a cost of 200 coins for each rune crafted, it is not recommended to use extracts as a means of making money; rather, it is intended for Ironman players who plan to use the runes for themselves.

If players happen to make too many extracts, they can be refunded for 90% of their original cost by taking them to Hagus in the Scar.
28599:
Scarred extracts are a catalyst used in runecrafting when crafting blood , soul , aether , and wrath runes , by giving 60 extra runes per extract.

The extract can be obtained in the Scar essence mine from the extract orifice by depositing tainted essence chunks into a ventriculus opening , and having 24,000 coins within Hagus ' coffer to convert the tainted essence into a scarred extract.

Because using scarred extracts results in a cost of 400 coins for each rune crafted, it is not recommended to use extracts as a means of making money; rather, it is intended for ironman players who plan to use the runes for themselves.

When used in combination with a blood essence , their effects stack additively: both the essence and the extract will act on the base number of blood runes crafted. [ 1 ]

Scarred extracts can be used at either the traditional runecrafting altars , or at the Zeah blood or soul altars .

The cape pouch is an item purchased from the Forestry Shop for 2,500 anima-infused bark . This pouch is used on the Forestry kit or Forestry basket with level 99 Woodcutting, allowing the player to store the Woodcutting cape within, to receive the skillcape benefits whilst wearing the Forestry kit instead to save an extra inventory slot.

When used on a Forestry kit or basket with level 99 Woodcutting, a message in the chatbox will state You expand your Forestry kit/basket to be able to hold a Woodcutting cape. If the player does not have level 99 Woodcutting, it will state You need level 99 Woodcutting to expand your Forestry kit/basket with this. When the cape pouch is attached to the Forestry kit, it does not change any interface options. Players can also store both the cape and the clothes pouches in their Forestry kit. To access the Woodcutting cape, use the "View" option.

Unlike the clothes pouch upgrade, the Forestry kit or basket must be equipped to receive the benefits of a Woodcutting cape stored inside; merely carrying it in the inventory is not sufficient. [ 1 ]

Players can sell the pouch back to the shop to get 80% of its cost back (2,000 bark).

Pheasant tail feathers are an item used to create the pheasant costume . Players can use a needle and thread to create the outfit; 15 feathers are required per piece, for a total of 60 to create the full outfit.

There is a fixed 50% [ 1 ] chance of obtaining one from Pheasant Nests as part of the Pheasant Control Forestry event . Excess feathers can be sold to the Friendly Forester for 5 anima-infused bark each.
28626:
The fox whistle is a rare reward from the Poachers Forestry event. It is used on the beaver pet to allow it to metamorphose into a fox. It is consumed in the process.

There is a 1/30 chance to retrieve a fox whistle at the end of the event, provided a player is eligible to receive the full rewards of the event (meaning the player disarmed at least 1 trap). Upon receiving one, it will be placed in the inventory (or on the ground if it is full), and a game message in the chatbox will state Well done, you've saved the fox from the poachers! The fox has left you a gift... You feel a connection to the fox as if it wishes to travel with you....

Alternatively, players can purchase the fox whistle for 75,000 anima bark from the Forestry Shop. It can also be sold to the Forestry Shop for 250 anima-infused bark.

Sawmill vouchers are an item purchased from the Forestry Shop . 10 can be purchased for 150 anima-infused bark . The voucher can be redeemed for an extra plank per log at a sawmill , or when using the Plank Make spell. Players must have sufficient space in their inventory or plank sack to do so, or the vouchers will not be used, with the excess logs that cannot be converted into 2 planks (due to lack of inventory space) being converted into 1 plank (without using a voucher) instead, which is more costly for the player.

Sawmill vouchers cannot be used by butlers when asking them to convert logs into planks.
28630:
Twitcher's gloves are an item purchased from the Forestry Shop for 5,000 anima-infused bark and 500 noted willow logs .

Whilst equipped, the player will have a 20% increased chance to receive a specific type of bird nest whenever they receive one from Woodcutting ; the player can right-click "Settings" on the gloves to specify which type: Ring , Egg , Seed , or Clue . This effect stacks with the effects of a strung rabbit foot . [ 1 ] Additionally, although redwood trees only yield clue nests when cut, the gloves can still increase the chance of getting clue nests. [ 2 ]

The effect of the gloves does not apply during bird house trapping .

When purchasing these gloves, you receive a chatbox message stating "Remember, you must wear these gloves to receive their bonus."

There is a fixed chance of 1/30 to receive the petal garland upon completing at least one step of the ritual, [ 1 ] provided the player was eligible for the full rewards of the event. [ 2 ] When receiving one, a game message in the chatbox will state The Dryad also hands you a Petal garland.

It can be sold to the Forestry Shop for 150 anima-infused bark .

When retrieving eggs for an event that players did not trigger, a spoon was consumed on the first pheasant egg but no chatbox message appeared.

They were created by combining an egg cushion, purchased from the Forestry Shop, with a limestone and a chisel. This required level 35 Crafting and 25 Woodcutting; each set produced 10 spoons.

Using a Padded spoon increased the amount of anima-infused bark the player receives by almost double, as well as increasing the chance to find pheasant tail feathers.
28659:
Egg cushions were an item purchased from the Forestry Shop for 300 anima-infused bark and 15 noted maple logs .

With level 25 Woodcutting and 35 Crafting , players created padded spoons by using the cushion with limestone and a chisel ; each set produced 10 spoons.
28661:
Pheasant eggs can be retrieved from empty pheasant nests during the Pheasant Control Forestry event . Players can give pheasant eggs to the Freaky Forester for Woodcutting and Thieving experience and anima-infused bark . Players may only carry one egg at a time.

Players may also find themselves at the end of an event with an egg still left in their inventory (different from the golden pheasant egg , which is a transmog for the beaver pet ). As there is no way to bank or sell the egg to the Friendly Forester , the item should either be destroyed or kept until the next pheasant event.
28663:
The Golden pheasant egg is a rare reward from the Pheasant Control Forestry event. It is used on the beaver pet to allow it to metamorphose into a pheasant. It is consumed in the process.

Unlike the fox whistle, the golden pheasant egg can be obtained mid-way through the event rather than only at the end. Alternatively, the golden pheasant egg can be purchased for 75,000 anima bark from the Forestry Shop.

There is a chance to retrieve a golden pheasant egg from a pheasant nest, provided a player is eligible to receive the reward from the event; the rate is approximately 1/1500 for every regular pheasant egg retrieved. Upon receiving one, it will be placed in the inventory (or on the ground if it is full), and a game message in the chatbox will state You feel a connection to the pheasants as if one wishes to travel with you...

The golden pheasant egg can be turned in to the Friendly Forester for 250 anima-infused bark.

Only one roll for the golden pheasant egg is made upon looting a pheasant nest, after which no more rolls are given until the regular pheasant egg is turned in to the Freaky Forester. As such, repeatedly destroying regular pheasant eggs will not increase one's chance of receiving the drop.
28665:
Trap disarmers were a stackable item used in Woodcutting . When in the inventory or stored in a Forestry kit , there was a chance of the Poachers Forestry event appearing. The chance of this occurring scaled based on the number of players present; when a disarmer is consumed while training Woodcutting, a game message in the chatbox stated Poachers suddenly jump out of the trees as a fox rushes by. You unpack your Trap disarmer in preparation. When disarming traps for an event that players did not trigger, a disarmer will be consumed on the first trap, and a game message in the chatbox stated You unpack your Trap disarmer.

Completing the Poacher event with a trap disarmer provided roughly 2.5 times the amount of rewarded anima-infused bark .

They were created by combining a trap disarmer blueprint , purchased from the Forestry Shop , with an iron bar and bronze wire . This required being next to an anvil with a hammer , as well as level 15 Woodcutting and 16 Hunter ; each set produced 10 disarmers.
28667:
Trap disarmer blueprints were an item purchased from the Forestry Shop for 300 anima-infused bark and 15 noted willow logs .

With level 15 Woodcutting and 16 Hunter , players created trap disarmers at an anvil with a hammer by combining a bronze wire and iron bar ; each set produced 10 disarmers.
28669:
The pheasant is a variant of the beaver pet that can be permanently unlocked by using the golden pheasant egg , a rare reward from the Pheasant Control Forestry event , on the beaver. Once unlocked, the pheasant can be freely transformed between the beaver and pheasant versions, as well as the fox if that variant has been unlocked as well. If the beaver has been recoloured and the player metamorphs to either the fox or the pheasant and then back into the beaver, then the beaver will revert back into the default colour.

On death, if a player loses their pet (as a follower or in your inventory) it will wander around for 30 seconds before disappearing completely. It can then be reclaimed from Probita in East Ardougne for no cost.
28670:
The fox is a variant of the beaver pet that can be permanently unlocked by using the fox whistle, a rare reward from the Poachers Forestry event, on the beaver. Once unlocked, the fox can be freely transformed between the beaver and fox versions, as well as the pheasant if that variant has been unlocked as well. If the beaver has been recoloured and the player metamorphs to either the fox or the pheasant and then back into the beaver, then the beaver will revert back into the default colour.

On death, if a player loses their pet (as a follower or in your inventory) it will wander around for 30 seconds before disappearing completely. It can then be reclaimed from Probita in East Ardougne for no cost.
28671:
The web cloak is a cosmetic reward from the 2023 Halloween event . It can be obtained as a reward from the Halloween events that occur once per year.

The web cloak has a right click "Change" option that transforms the cape into a cobweb cape .

If destroyed, a replacement can be obtained from Diango in Draynor Village or from the toy box of a costume room .
28672:
Fancier boots are a fusion of fancy boots and fighting boots that are obtained from the Cradle of Life on the fourth level of the Stronghold of Security dungeon, provided the player's account is a Jagex Account and has two-factor authentication enabled.

They have identical stats to fancy boots and fighting boots and are purely a cosmetic change.

If the player dies (including in PvP) and the boots are unprotected, it will be sent to the gravestone . When lost, they can be reclaimed for free from the Cradle of Life . Multiple pairs can be claimed and owned at the same time.

This item can be stored in the armour case of a costume room .
28674:
Sturdy beehive parts is an item that can be obtained as a reward from the Beehive Forestry event. Ten beehive parts are required to build a beehive in the garden and formal garden in a player-owned house.

There is a 2/3 chance of receiving a set of parts upon building a complete beehive. Upon receiving one, it will be placed in the inventory (or on the ground if it is full), and a game message in the chatbox will state The temporary beehive was made so well you take some parts for building a permanent hive.

Excess parts can be sold to the Friendly Forester for 25 anima-infused bark each.
28676:
Beehives can be built in the garden (hotspots big plant space 1 and big plant space 2) or the formal garden (hotspots big plant, big plant 2) of a player-owned house. It requires level 1 Construction to build alongside 10 sturdy beehive parts. Removing the beehive will return all ten parts back to the player.

Beehives have a "Release-bees" option that will release agitated bees, who will simply roam around the player-owned house.

Players cannot obtain a bucket of wax from these beehives.

28682:
Dinh's blazing bulwark is a Dinh's bulwark with a Trailblazer reloaded bulwark ornament kit added onto it. The kit gives no additional bonuses, and is only used to add aesthetics to the bulwark.

Whilst in its ornamented state, the item can be reverted anytime, returning the bulwark and kit.

The bulwark resembles the Ancestral Glyph found within the Inferno .
28684:
The Trailblazer reloaded bulwark ornament kit is an ornament kit that changes the appearance of Dinh's bulwark to Dinh's blazing bulwark . This process can be reverted at any time returning the item and ornament kit.

It can be purchased from the Leagues Reward Shop for 10,000 League Points.
28687:

To add the kit, players must empty the blowpipe of Zulrah's scales and darts . Players can configure the charges while the blowpipe is in their bank by right-clicking on Configure-Charges, as long as players have the required materials.

Whilst in its ornamented state, the item can be reverted anytime, returning the blowpipe and kit.

28693: The Trailblazer reloaded alchemy scroll is a consumable item purchased from the Leagues Reward Shop for 2,000 League points. It can be used to unlock a Trailblazer Reloaded -themed alchemy spell animation override . To enable it, players can right click "Animation" on either the Low Level Alchemy or High Level Alchemy icon in the standard spellbook and select "Leagues IV - Trailblazer Reloaded".
28696:

It can be used to unlock a Trailblazer Reloaded -themed Vengeance animation override . To enable it, players can right click "Animation" on the Vengeance spell icon in the lunar spellbook and select "Leagues IV - Trailblazer Reloaded".

The scroll does not affect Vengeance Other 's animation.
28699:
The Trailblazer reloaded death scroll is a consumable item purchased from the Leagues Reward Shop for 3,000 League points. It can be used to unlock a Trailblazer Reloaded -themed death animation override . To enable it, players must visit Death and ask him to change how you die.

When the player reads the scroll, the chatbox message states This scroll contains the ability to override your Death animation. Would you like to read the scroll? Upon reading the scroll, it is consumed, and the chatbox message states You feel empowered by the scroll and unlock the Leagues IV: Trailblazer Reloaded Death animation . This can be changed by speaking to Death inside his office.
28702:
The Trailblazer reloaded banner is a cosmetic reward representing the Trailblazer Reloaded League , which costs 500 League points from the Leagues Reward Shop .

The banner can be displayed by using it on furniture built in the League hall 's banner stand space . Ultimate Ironmen can use this as a storage mechanism, but since a player may only build one league hall, only one league banner can be stored in a POH .
28705:
The Trailblazer reloaded home teleport scroll is a consumable item purchased from the Leagues Reward Shop for 1,000 League points. It can be used to unlock a Trailblazer Reloaded-themed Home Teleport animation override. To enable it, players can right click "Animation" on the Home Teleport spell icon in their spellbook and select "Leagues IV - Trailblazer Reloaded".

When the player reads the scroll, the chatbox message states This scroll contains an incantation which will unlock a new home teleport animation. Would you like to learn the incantation? (Warning: This will consume the scroll.)

If a player reads the scroll while already having unlocked the animation, the chatbox message will state This scroll contains an incantation which unlocks the Leagues IV - Trailblazer Reloaded home teleport animation. However you have already unlocked this animation.
28708: The Trailblazer reloaded rejuvenation pool scroll is a consumable item purchased from the Leagues Reward Shop for 9,000 League points. It can be used on an ornate rejuvenation pool to change its appearance to a fiery-themed pool. Reverting the ornate rejuvenation pool to its original appearance will return the scroll.

28765:
The Globetrotter pendant is an item obtained within the Trailblazer Reloaded League, which allows players to teleport to a large number of teleport locations from teleport jewellery and spellbooks, providing that they are able to access the region, and cannot be used above level 20 Wilderness.

It is obtained at a bank upon unlocking the Globetrotter relic. For an interactive map of destinations, see here.

If lost or destroyed, the Globetrotter pendant can be reclaimed from The Sage.
28767:
The banker's note is an item in the Grid Master community event from the Banker's Note relic, unlocked by completing the Corrupted Gauntlet .

It allows players to use note -able items on it to turn them into banknotes or unnote them. The "Activate" option allows players to note and un-note items in one action with a quantity of the player's choosing, though an item must first be used on the banker's note in order for this to work.

If lost or destroyed, the banker's note can be reclaimed from The Sage .
28769:
The minion whistle is an item obtained during the Demonic Pacts League, given to players who picked the tier 8 Minion relic.

The whistle allows players to summon a powerful minion which lasts for 30 minutes. The minion will cast an AoE attack if the player's target is weakest to range or magic and is in a multi-combat area.

The base minion's stats are:

Min hit: 3

Max hit: 10

Attack speed: 1.8

Accuracy: 45,000

Up to 5 equippable Zamorak-aligned items can be used on the whistle to consume them, increasing the minion's max hit by 2 per unique item, up to a total of 20.

The minion whistle can be retrieved from the Leagues Tutor in Yama's Lair if lost.
28771:
The Searing boots are footwear obtained during the Demonic Pacts League, given to players who picked the Hotfoot relic.

Players wearing the boots earn 10+⌊(AgilityLvl*23)⌋ Agility experience roughly every 10 ticks as they run before applying any League multipliers. For players to be eligible to gain experience as they run, the greaves simply check if the player has moved 2 game squares in 1 tick. This means that diagonal moves around objects will not count towards experience despite of technically taking 2 steps.

Although renamed for the Demonic Pacts League, the boots have made past appearances as the Sage's greaves.
28773:
The Sage's axe is an item obtained during the Demonic Pacts League , given to players upon unlocking the Executioner relic .

With a maximum attack range of 6 tiles (8 on longrange), the Sage's axe will instantly kill targets who have less than 20% of their health remaining. However, NPCs who take reduced damage from ranged attacks will still take reduced damage when using the Sage's axe; for example, the Kraken only takes 1/7th ranged damage. Additionally, the axe does not work against Yama or the Gemstone Crab .

If lost or destroyed, the Sage's axe can be reclaimed from the Leagues Tutor in Yama's Lair .
28775:
The Ruinous powers is an item obtained within the Trailblazer Reloaded League , given to players at a bank upon unlocking the Ruinous Powers relic .

The item allows players to alternate between the standard prayer book and the Ruinous Powers prayer book. If lost or destroyed, the Ruinous powers can be reclaimed from The Sage .

This item may be equipped and used as an alternative to the Ancient Staff or the Ancient Sceptre to grant a negative prayer bonus in order to complete the master clue step for Abbot Langley .

In the God Wars Dungeon , this item did not provide protection against Zaros' troops when worn, despite the large symbol of Zaros on the book's cover.
