28790:
The Kourend castle teleport is a magic tablet that can be broken by players to teleport to the Kourend Castle courtyard, by the statue of King Rada I. Using the tablet requires completion of the quest Client of Kourend .

Players can create this item on a teak eagle lectern , a mahogany eagle lectern , or a marble lectern with 2 law runes , 1 water rune , 1 fire rune , and 1 soft clay and at least level 48 Magic , granting 58 experience.

This tablet can be made regardless of the player's current spellbook . As with all tablets, the user does not need to have the relevant Magic level to use this tablet.
28792:
The bone mace is a weapon requiring level 50 Attack to wield. It is made by combining a rune mace with Scurrius' spine at an anvil , requiring a hammer and level 35 Smithing to do so; players without the required level can alternatively pay Historian Aldo 50,000 coins to create it on their behalf. The mace has almost identical stats to the dragon mace , missing only the 5 prayer bonus .

As a rat bone weapon , it is effective against all types of rats by adding 10 damage to the player's maximum hit . [ 1 ] Additionally, it has no attack cooldown when attacking the giant rats that Scurrius summons. The mace cannot be used against any other type of monster (including manual cast spells ); doing so will yield the game message You can only use this weapon against rats.
28794:
The bone shortbow is a weapon requiring level 50 Ranged to wield. It is made by combining a yew shortbow with Scurrius' spine , requiring a knife and level 35 Fletching to do so; players without the required level can alternatively pay Historian Aldo 50,000 coins to create it on their behalf. The bow has identical offensive stats to the magic shortbow , and can fire up to amethyst arrows .

As a rat bone weapon , it is effective against all types of rats by adding 10 damage to the player's maximum hit . [ 1 ] The shortbow cannot be used against any other type of monster (including manually cast spells ); doing so will yield the game message You can only use this weapon against rats. Additionally, this weapon has no attack cooldown when attacking the giant rats that Scurrius summons.
28796:
The bone staff is a powered staff requiring level 50 Magic to wield. It is made by combining a battlestaff with Scurrius' spine alongside 1,000 chaos runes , requiring a chisel and level 35 Crafting to do so; players without the required level can alternatively pay Historian Aldo 50,000 coins to create it on their behalf. The chaos runes are not consumed but are used to give the bone staff an initial 1,000 charges.

In order to use the staff's magic spell, it must be charged with chaos runes , holding up to 20,000 charges when fully charged. Each cast requires one chaos rune, costing 105 coins . Uncharging the staff returns all remaining runes back. Additionally, unlike other powered staves, the bone staff's built-in spell gives 35 base Magic experience on a successful hit.

As a rat bone weapon , it is effective against all types of rats by adding 10 damage to the player's maximum hit . [ 1 ] The staff cannot be used against any other type of monster (including manual cast spells ); doing so will yield the game message You can only use this weapon against rats. Additionally, this weapon has no attack cooldown when attacking the giant rats that Scurrius summons.
28798:
Scurrius' spine is an uncommon drop from Scurrius . It can be combined with various weapons to create rat bone weapons .

Excess spines can be given to Historian Aldo outside the boss area in exchange for an antique lamp giving 5,000 experience in either Attack , Strength , Defence , Hitpoints , Magic , Ranged , or 3,500 experience in Prayer .
28800: The antique lamp is an item obtained from Historian Aldo by giving him Scurrius' spine. When rubbed, it grants 5,000 experience in a combat skill of the player's choosing (except Prayer, which gives 3,500).
28801:
Scurry is a pet dropped by Scurrius . It is a much smaller version of Scurrius. When spoken to, it has three distinct personalities: Scurry , the main (melee) rat, Chewy , the ranged rat, and Nibbles , the mage rat.

When a player receives the pet, it will automatically try to appear as their follower. At the same time, a message in the chatbox will state You have a funny feeling like you're being followed. However, if a player receives a pet while having a follower out (for example, a cat ), it will be placed into their inventory . When this occurs, the message in the chatbox will instead state You feel something weird sneaking into your backpack.

If a player's inventory is full and they have a follower already, they will not receive the pet; it must instead be claimed from Probita in East Ardougne .

On death , if a player loses their pet (as a follower or in your inventory) it will wander around the area for 30 seconds before despawning. Even if the player returns in time, the pet cannot be picked up, and can be reclaimed from Probita.
28803:
A grubby key is obtained during Defender of Varrock , where it is used to permanently unlock access to Zemouregal's Base .

Elias White will prevent the player from destroying the key while following them and, instead, offers to hold onto the key for them. Elias won't return the key if given to him and will later use it to open the trapdoor found during the quest for the player.
28804:
Bottles are obtained during Defender of Varrock within Zemouregal's Base , where they are used to collect red mist from defeated armoured zombies in order to obtain a bottle of mist .

After the quest, the item has no use and can be safely dropped.
28805:
A bottle of mist is obtained during Defender of Varrock within Zemouregal's Base , where it is used to bypass a door's security system.

It is acquired by using a bottle on red mist that appears after defeating an armoured zombie . Additional mist cannot be acquired after the quest although any in the player's bank will be kept. While the empty bottles can still be picked up, attempting to collect more mist is prevented and the following message is displayed: You don't need any more mist.
28806:
Imbued barronite is obtained during Defender of Varrock , where it is used on the Sacred Forge to access the Imcando Dream Theatre.

It is acquired by using a chaos core on a barronite deposit . The item cannot be created after using it to visit the Dream Theatre and completing the cutscene. Any duplicates of this item will be removed at the end of the quest.
28807:
The Shield of Arrav is an artefact that once belonged to Arrav , a legendary hero from the Fourth Age who defended Avarrocka from the necromancer Zemouregal , a Zamorakian Mahjarrat .

According to the The Legend of Arrav , the shield is remarkably strong and has the power to crumble undead to dust, which would be proven true when Zemouregal attempted a second invasion in the Fifth Age .
28808: List of elders is obtained during Defender of Varrock, found in the Varrock Palace Library by the scrolls near the flipped table. It lists the founding elders of Avarrocka, and is cross referenced with the Varrock Census to find their living descendants.
28809:
Elias white is an item that may be placed into the player's inventory when Elias White is following them during Defender of Varrock . Dropping it will cause him to follow the player, much like a pet does.

Because he cannot be picked up normally, the follower item is not intended to be received by players, but is used as a failsafe measure in the event that the Elias White follower is forced into the player's backpack.
28810:
The zombie axe is a one-handed axe that requires 65 Attack to wield. It is created by taking a broken zombie axe , obtained as a drop from armoured zombies , to an anvil and repairing it with 70 Smithing .

The axe's strength bonus and slash attack stats are higher than any other one-handed weapon, while its crush attack bonus is only surpassed by the dragon warhammer and inquisitor's mace (not counting PVP-only weapons). Coupled with its 5- tick attack speed, the axe does slightly less average damage than the dragon scimitar against enemies with low to semi-low defence. However, against enemies weak to crush or enemies with higher defence, such as a gargoyle , the axe can potentially deal even more average damage than an abyssal whip . This is particularly useful for midgame ironman players who do not have level 85 Slayer to kill abyssal demons .

The zombie axe has +105 slash bonus which always slashes webs successfully like the Wilderness sword 1 , making it a convenient weapon of choice for ironmen to slay Sarachnis .

The zombie axe counts as an axe for fixing bridges when doing Temple Trekking .
28813: The broken zombie axe is the broken version of the zombie axe. It is dropped by armoured zombies in Zemouregal's Base, and by their higher-level variants in Zemouregal's Fort. Players with 70 Smithing can repair the axe at an anvil with a hammer in the inventory; boosts can be used. Repairing the axe grants the player 500 Smithing experience.
28816: The stone tablet is an item obtained during The Curse of Arrav in the tunnels beneath Zemouregal's Fort , and is one of four tablets made by Lamistard , who dug the tunnels in an attempt to avoid being chosen as a sacrifice in the Mahjarrat 's rituals.
28817: The granite tablet is an item obtained during The Curse of Arrav in the tunnels beneath Zemouregal's Fort, and is one of four tablets made by Lamistard, who dug the tunnels in an attempt to avoid being chosen as a sacrifice in the Mahjarrat's rituals.
28818: The slate tablet is an item obtained during The Curse of Arrav in the tunnels beneath Zemouregal's Fort, and is one of four tablets made by Lamistard, who dug the tunnels in an attempt to avoid being chosen as a sacrifice in the Mahjarrat's rituals.
28819: The shale tablet is an item obtained during The Curse of Arrav in the tunnels beneath Zemouregal's Fort, and is one of four tablets made by Lamistard, who dug the tunnels in an attempt to avoid being chosen as a sacrifice in the Mahjarrat's rituals.
28820:
The antique lamp is an item obtained from the Varrock Museum upon giving Historian Minas various information for their displays:

Infinite can be obtained as a possible reward from cleaning: 500xp in a skill of at least 10.

Three from giving information about the quests Making History, Merlin's Crystal, and Shield of Arrav: 1,000xp in a skill of at least level 20.

Giving information about the Defender of Varrock awards one antique lamp granting 5,000xp in a skill of at least 30.

Giving information about the Curse of the Empty Lord awards one antique lamp granting 10,000xp in a skill of at least 50.
28821:
The Wealthy citizen is an interface item that can be seen in the Thieving and Pickpocketing subsections of the Thieving skill guide. The item represents the Wealthy citizen.

The actual item cannot be obtained by players.
28822:
A coin pouch is an item obtained from pickpocketing certain NPCs, which contains several coins depending on the NPC it was obtained from. To obtain the coins from them, players can simply click their stack of coin pouches to open them all at once, or they can right-click them to open one at a time. They cannot be traded or banked.

Up to 28 coin pouches can stack in a player's inventory, after which the player must open them to collect the coins inside before being able to pickpocket more. This limit can be increased by completing the Ardougne Diary, where it increases to 56, 84, and 140 after completing the Medium, Hard, and Elite diaries, respectively.

Coin pouches have different variants depending on who the player pickpocketed it from; for example, a coin pouch from pickpocketing guards does not stack with pouches from pickpocketing Ardougne knights. NPCs who are pickpocketed via blackjacking yield coins directly while they are knocked out instead of coin pouches. If rogue equipment is used to receive double the loot from pickpocketing, only one coin pouch is obtained (containing the normal amount) while the other half is obtained directly as coins.
28824:
The Civitas illa Fortis teleport is a magic tablet that can be broken by players to teleport to Civitas illa Fortis . Using the tablet requires completion of Twilight's Promise .

Players with level 54 Magic can create this item on a Mahogany eagle lectern or better in a player-owned house . This requires 2 law runes , 1 fire rune , 1 earth rune , and 1 soft clay . Creating a tablet grants 64 Magic experience, the same as casting the Civitas illa Fortis Teleport spell. Elemental staves can be substituted for runes and are recommended when making teleport tablets in large groups at a time.

As with all teleport tablets, using a Civitas illa Fortis teleport tablet does not grant any experience.
28828:
Blessed Dizana's quiver is an upgraded variant of Dizana's quiver , made by using it on a Shrine of Ralos while having a total of 150,000 sunfire splinters and a Dizana's quiver in the player's inventory. Charging the quiver with sunfire splinters contributes to the required amount of splinters to upgrade.

The blessed quiver permanently gains the effects of Dizana's Sunfire , where an additional +1 Ranged Strength and +10 Ranged accuracy is applied to stored arrows and bolts - essentially acting as a variant of the original with unlimited charges. The upgraded variant also retains its level 75 Ranged requirement to equip.

It can also be combined with the max cape to change its appearance by turning it into Dizana's max cape .
28830:
Dizana's max cape is the result of combining blessed Dizana's quiver with a max cape, during which the max hood required to be in the player's inventory will automatically convert to Dizana's max hood.

Like the other max cape variants (a max cape combined with another cape slot item), Dizana's max cape does not have the max cape's stats or perks; it only acts as a cosmetic upgrade to blessed Dizana's quiver with the following exceptions when worn:

It acts as a Cooking cape to allow access to the Cooks' Guild without a chef's hat, golden chef's hat, Varrock armour 3 or 4

It acts as a Crafting cape to allow access to the Crafting Guild without a brown apron or golden apron

It acts as a Runecraft cape to prevent essence pouches from degrading (but does not allow access to runic altars)

It acts as a Firemaking cape to work as a piece of warm clothing

It can be used to perform the Skill Cape emote.

The cape retains the perks of the blessed Dizana's quiver.

The max cape and quiver can be separated by using a knife on the cape. Mac will also buy back a max cape, along with its variants, for 1,900,800 coins each. He will return the secondary item any max cape variant was combined with upon doing so.

If the player dies a PvP death at level 20 Wilderness or below and the item is unprotected, it will remain in the player's inventory; however, the item will be in a broken, unusable state and must be repaired by using it on Perdu and paying him 400,000 coins.

If the player dies a PvP death above level 20 Wilderness and the item is unprotected, it will be converted to coins. To prevent this, a Trouver parchment and a payment of 500,000 coins can be given to Perdu in order to permanently lock the item. The locked item will remain in the player's inventory; however, the item will be in a mangled, unusable state and must be repaired by using it on Perdu and paying him 500,000 coins.
28831:
Immature tecu salamanders are young tecu salamanders that are caught as part of the Hunter skill. They have no use and cannot be used as a weapon.

Unlike other salamanders , which are caught and able to be used as weapons from the get go, tecu salamanders are often caught at this immature stage; to use one as a weapon, players must catch a fully grown tecu salamander instead, which are a much rarer catch.
28834:
The tecu salamander is the strongest salamander that can be caught using a net trap and the Hunter skill at level 79, granting 344 Hunter experience, which can be found south-east of Ralos' Rise. Catching a matured tecu salamander is rare, as players often receive immature tecu salamanders instead; when an adult is captured, a message in the game chat will state The salamander is fully grown, you could use this as a weapon.

Tecu salamanders require level 80 Attack, Magic, and Ranged to wield. Irit tar is used as ammunition for the salamander. It is the best salamander to use for the two salamander-required Combat Achievements: The Worst Ranged Weapon and More than just a ranged weapon.

Despite being able to perform Magic and Ranged attacks, this weapon requires the user to be in the opponent's melee distance to attack, potentially reducing the practicality of the two attack styles. However, it can be used to attack enemies from behind fences, and can also attack enemies in diagonal squares, meaning that safespotting is still possible.

When using the Scorch (Slash) and Blaze (Magic) attack styles, the attack speed is 5. When using the Flare (Range) attack style, the attack speed is 4, which is similar in concept to the Rapid style of most ranged weapons, and it will use standard ranged defence, similar to bows.

Warning: This is a live creature; if unprotected it will run away when you die. Should this happen, you will need to buy or catch a new one.
28837:
Irit tar is an item used as food, or "ammunition", for tecu salamanders when used as a weapon. It can be made at level 55 Herblore by using 15 swamp tar on an irit leaf , whilst having a pestle and mortar in the inventory. This process yields 15 irit tar, and grants 85 Herblore experience.

Although the Hunter skill guide in-game states that it can optionally be used as bait for hunting tecu salamanders to increase the catch rate by 3%, this has not actually been implemented.
28839:
The wood camo top is a members only piece of wood camouflage gear . To make one, bring two common kebbit furs and 20 coins to the Fancy Clothes Store in Varrock , to Pellem in the Hunter Guild , or to Prifddinas' Seamstress .

When worn, it reduces weight by 3 kg. Additionally, though the examine claims so, it does not affect the trapping of hunter creatures .

This item can be stored in the armour case of a costume room , as part of the Camouflage gear: Woodland set. Ultimate Ironmen will be unable to retrieve individual pieces until the full set is stored.

28869:
The hunters' sunlight crossbow is an upgraded variant of the hunters' crossbow that requires level 66 Ranged and 50 Hunter to use. It is made with level 74 Fletching by using a sunlight antelope antler on the hunters' crossbow with a chisel in inventory.

The crossbow uses sunlight or moonlight antler bolts, and works with grapples. Despite being an upgrade from the hunter's crossbow, it cannot be used to fire kebbit or long kebbit bolts.

As with other crossbows, the bolts fired from it roll against the enemy's heavy ranged defence, tying it with Karil's crossbow and chinchompas as the fastest firing weapons to do so. Like the hunters' crossbow, it possesses an attack speed of 4 (3 on rapid), equal to a shortbow and faster than most other crossbows.

Due to its quick attack speed and the high strength bonus of its bolts, it is very effective against enemies where a crossbow is desirable but enchanted bolts are not needed.
28872:
Sunlight antler bolts are ranged ammunition for the hunters' sunlight crossbow, requiring 66 Ranged to use. They can be created at level 62 Fletching by using a chisel on a sunlight antelope antler; each antler produces 12 bolts and 10 Fletching experience.

Unlike other arrows and bolts, weapon poison is not able to be applied to them.

Despite not being made of metal, sunlight antler bolts do function with Ava's devices obtained from the completion of Animal Magnetism.
28878:
Moonlight antler bolts are ranged ammunition for the hunters' sunlight crossbow, effectively requiring 66 Ranged to use. They can be created at level 72 Fletching by using a chisel on a moonlight antelope antler; each antler produces 12 bolts and rewards 12.1 Fletching experience.

Unlike other arrows and bolts, moonlight antler bolts cannot be coated with weapon poison.

Despite not being made of metal, moonlight antler bolts do function with Ava's devices obtained from the completion of Animal Magnetism.
28890:
A sunlight moth is an item that is obtained from catching sunlight moths, which requires level 65 Hunter and a butterfly net and jar. Players with level 75 Hunter can catch sunlight moths barehanded.

Once caught, players can right-click "Release" the filled butterfly jar to restore 6 + 20% of a player's reduced stats (excluding Prayer), as well as 8 Hitpoints (as of December 21st, 2025, the sunlight moth does not restore lowered sailing levels). In a multi-combat zone, the item may be used on another player to share the effect with them and up to three players within a 5x5 area of the target. Players must have Accept Aid toggled on to receive the effect. The empty butterfly jar will remain in the inventory after use.

With a pestle and mortar, players can combine the moth with raw hunter meat to create sunlight moth mix (2).
28893:
A moonlight moth is an item that is obtained from catching moonlight moths, which require level 75 Hunter and a butterfly net and jar. Players with level 85 Hunter can catch moonlight moths barehanded.

Once caught, players can right-click "Release" the filled butterfly jar to restore 22 Prayer points. In a multi-combat zone, the item may be used on another player to share the effect with them and up to three players within a 5x5 area of the target if the players have Accept Aid toggled on. The empty butterfly jar will remain in the inventory after use. For Group Ironmen, the moonlight moth cannot be shared, while the Moonlight moth mix can.

The effect of the holy wrench does not apply to this item.

With a pestle and mortar, players can combine a Moonlight Moth with raw hunter meat to create moonlight moth mix (2).
28896:
Rum is a drink that can be purchased from Atlazora's Rest and The Flaming Arrow , which are both found in Civitas illa Fortis . It is also frequently found in mid-level salvage .

When drunk, it boosts the player's Strength by 1 + 5% of their base level, rounded down, restores 5 Hitpoints , and drains Attack by 3 + 2% of their current level, rounded down.
28899:
Wyrmling bones are the remains obtained from killing wyrmlings, which give 21 Prayer experience when buried. This can be increased by offering the bones in different ways:

63 XP when casting Sinister Offering.

63 XP when offered at the Sacred Bone Burner after the appropriate faith level has been achieved.

73.5 XP when offered at a gilded altar with two burners lit or at the Chaos Temple. The Temple additionally has a 50% chance to not deplete the bones; effectively doubling the XP to 147 per bone.

105 XP when blessed and broken down into blessed bone shards and offered at the libation bowl, or 126 XP when offered with a jug of blessed sunfire wine. Virilis outside the altar will exchange noted bones for 10 coins each.

120 XP when offered at the Ectofuntus in the form of baby dragon bonemeal.

28919:
The Tonalztics of Ralos is a one-handed thrown weapon that requires level 75 Ranged to equip, obtained by participating in the Fortis Colosseum . Unlike most thrown weapons , it is not stackable and effectively provides unlimited "ammo," though it has an additional effect when charged with Sunfire splinters . The weapon rolls against a monster's light ranged defence.

When charged, the weapon will hit twice , with two independent damage rolls and an attack range of 7 tiles (9 on longrange). Uncharged, the weapon hits a target once for 0-75% of the player's maximum ranged hit , with a slightly worse attack range of 6 tiles (8 on longrange). It can hold a maximum of 20,000 charges. One charge is consumed per throw, whether or not the special attack is used, and regardless of the amount of hits that land. Players can configure the charges while the weapon is in their bank by right-clicking on Configure-Charges, as long as players have the required materials.

Sunfire splinters can be obtained from participating in the Fortis Colosseum , hunting sunlight antelope , defeating the Hueycoatl and opening Chest (moon key) . They are used for various items:

Dizana's quivers can be exchanged for 4,000 sunfire splinters by talking to Minimus . The average number of Sunfire splinters gained per successful Colosseum run is 2,014.62, not including exchanging the additional quivers from completion.
28929:
Sunfire runes are a type of rune created by using fire runes , along with sunfire splinters and pure / daeyalt essence , at a Shrine of Ralos . Doing so requires level 33 Runecraft , with the output being doubled at level 49, and tripled at level 98.

As a superior variant of the fire rune, any successful hit with offensive fire spells will deal a minimum of 10% of the player's max hit. If the player has a source of infinite fire runes equipped (e.g. twinflame staff ) and casts a fire spell with sunfire runes in their inventory, the sunfire runes are still consumed and still grant their minimum hit effect.

Though not advisable due to the cost per rune, they can be used in place of fire runes for non-combat spells such as teleporting or High Level Alchemy .

100 sunfire runes can also be used on burnt pages to create searing pages , which can be used on a tome of fire to give it the same effect.
28931:
Searing pages are an upgraded variant of burnt pages made by adding 100 sunfire runes to one page. When used on a tome of fire to charge it, the tome gains a 10% minimum hit on their target when casting any standard spellbook's fire spells. However, the minimum hit is based on the player’s maximum hit before the tome’s 10% damage boost is applied. For example, a player with a pre-tome maximum hit of 19 would have a minimum hit of 1 when using sunfire runes. If the player equips a tome charged with searing pages, the maximum hit will be boosted to 20, but the minimum hit will remain 1.

Each searing page adds 20 charges to the tome, and one charge is consumed when an elemental fire spell is cast with the tome equipped. Players may remove the pages from the tome should they wish to do so.

Searing pages are more cost-effective for Fire Wave/Surge when using Sunfire runes. Fire Wave consumes 7 fire runes per cast. One searing page (20 charges) therefore replaces 140 fire runes, saving 40 Sunfire runes (28%). Fire Surge consumes 10 fire runes per cast. One searing page (20 charges) therefore replaces 200 fire runes, saving 100 Sunfire runes (50%).

Echo crystals are a drop received from participating in the Fortis Colosseum . It is used on a pair of guardian boots to create echo boots , which gives it an additional +2 prayer bonus and a passive recoil effect.

Each echo crystal added to the boots gives it 6,000 recoil charges.
28945:
Echo boots are an enhanced pair of guardian boots which require level 75 Defence to wear. They are made by combining the boots with an echo crystal , a rare drop from participating in the Fortis Colosseum . Compared to its predecessor, it gives an additional +2 prayer bonus and a passive effect in which the boots deal 1 recoil damage to any target that damages the player, limited to a 3x3 square centered on the player. This effectively restricts recoiled targets to only those in melee range.

Each echo crystal will add 6,000 charges to the recoil effect (costing 481.11 per charge), up to a maximum of 60,000. The recoil effect can be toggled via the boots' "Toggle-activity" option, allowing players to disable it as to not waste it during casual training, and instead use it in activities where the effect may prove more useful. The "Revert" option reverts the echo boots back into guardian boots, though this will not return any echo crystals, regardless of whether or not any recoil charges were used. Players can configure the charges while the boots are in their bank by right-clicking on Configure-Charges, as long as players have the required materials.

Like the Bandos and guardian boots used in their creation, they will render followers of Bandos unaggressive to the wearer in the God Wars Dungeon .

Smol Heredit is a pet that can be obtained from completing the Fortis Colosseum after defeating Sol Heredit. Players have a 1/200 chance of obtaining him. Alternatively, players can exchange Dizana's quiver to Minimus for another 1/200 chance to obtain him. Unlike other boss pets, Smol Heredit is considered a main drop and will be shown accordingly on the colosseum interface upon reaching the final wave.

When a player receives the pet, it will automatically try to appear as their follower. At the same time, a message in the chatbox will state You have a funny feeling like you're being followed. However, if a player receives a pet while having a follower out (for example, a cat), it will be placed into their inventory. When this occurs, the message in the chatbox will instead state You feel something weird sneaking into your backpack.

If a player's inventory is full and they have a follower already, they will not receive the pet; it must instead be claimed from Probita in East Ardougne.

On death, if a player loses their pet (as a follower or in your inventory) it will wander around the area for 30 seconds before despawning. Even if the player returns in time, the pet cannot be picked up, and can be reclaimed from Probita.

Atlatl darts are ammunition used exclusively by the eclipse atlatl , which is obtained as a possible reward from the Lunar Chest in Neypotzli . Alternatively the darts can be crafted, requiring level 74 Fletching , Headless atlatl dart and Atlatl dart tips . Ironmen additionally require 54 Slayer in order to obtain broken antlers , which are required to make the dart tips.

The atlatl dart has no bonuses as the eclipse atlatl uses the player's melee strength bonus to deal damage.

Despite being called darts , atlatl darts cannot be loaded into the toxic blowpipe , and they deal standard ranged damage. [ 1 ]

Despite being equipped in the ammo slot, they can not be stored in Dizana's quiver . Attempting to do so displays the following message: "You have nothing in your worn quiver to fill your Dizana's Quiver with."

Atlatl darts are compatible with Ava's devices , however the Ranged strength bonus on them will not affect their damage, making other capes like a Fire cape more preferable if not concerned with saving the darts.
28997:
The dual macuahuitl (in English pronounced roughly mah-KUA-weetl) is a non-degradable two-handed spiked weapon that requires level 70 Attack and 75 Strength to equip, which is obtained as a possible reward from the Lunar Chest in Neypotzli .

The weapon hits twice per attack , spaced 1 game tick apart when attacking monsters, and dealing damage in two hitsplats , with both hitsplats having their max hit halved. If the player has an odd maximum hit , the first hit's maximum damage will be rounded down and the second hit's will be rounded up, e.g. a maximum hit of 25 will be split into two maximum hits of 12 and 13.

Each hitsplat has its own accuracy check. However, unlike other two-hit weapons like Torag's hammers or sulphur blades , where both checks are independent (either can hit or miss without affecting the other, equivalent to two separate hits with a single-hit weapon), the Dual macuahuitl checks the two hits sequentially, and the second check will only proceed if the first succeeds.

If the first accuracy check succeeds, damage will be rolled for the first hit, and a second accuracy check will then be performed for the second hit. If the first accuracy check fails, the second check will not proceed at all, and both hits will deal no damage. As a result, one "half" of the weapon's DPS functions normally, while the other "half" is reduced due to requiring both accuracy checks to succeed.

This is an intentional design [ 1 ] to push the weapon into a niche against targets with lower Defence levels and mirrors the attacks of the Moons of Peril , which check accuracy in the same way.
29000:
The eclipse atlatl is a non-degradable two-handed ranged weapon that requires level 75 Ranged, 50 Attack, and 50 Strength to equip. It can be obtained as a possible reward from the Lunar Chest in Neypotzli. It uses atlatl darts as ammunition, which can be collected by Ava's devices.

Despite not being strung and using a “throwing” attack animation, the atlatl is categorically a bow and not a thrown weapon, and therefore deals standard-type damage.

Its max hit is determined by the player's melee strength bonus, while accuracy is still based on their ranged bonus, which is a unique mechanic among ranged weapons.

The atlatl's max hit mechanic means it pairs unusually with other equipment; endgame ranged gear is not best-in-slot as usual. Instead, the atlatl performs better against low-defence enemies when used in conjunction with high-strength equipment (e.g. amulet of strength, dragon boots), while end-game tribrid equipment such as Barrows gloves, amulet of fury, and aranea boots will usually outperform specialised ranged gear against high-defence enemies.

Though the atlatl's max hit is based on visible boosts to the player's Strength level (including potions), it does not benefit from melee prayers. Ranged prayers boost both accuracy and damage. Additionally, it uses the melee bonuses from the slayer helmet and salve amulets, but gains increased damage from Void Knight equipment whilst wearing the void ranger helm rather than the void melee helm.

When using the rapid attack style, up to 2,000 darts may be fired per hour. This makes the cost per hour 51,600 with Ava's assembler, 72,240 with Ava's accumulator if not picking up used ammo, or 258,000 if choosing to use a different cape for more damage, such as the Infernal cape.

The attack speed of the Atlatl varies; in player versus monster encounters, its base attack speed is 4, or equal to shortbows. During player versus player combat, its base attack speed is 5, unless the full Eclipse armour set is worn.
29004:
The eclipse moon chestplate is an item that requires level 75 Ranged and 50 Defence to equip, which is obtained as a possible reward from the Lunar Chest in Neypotzli.

As with all Moon equipment it is degradeable, much like Barrows equipment. The armour starts at 3000 charges and loses 1 charge for every 54 seconds in combat, meaning it lasts for 45 hours of continuous combat before breaking. Having an NPC such as Bob and Dunstan repair it costs 1,500,000 coins when fully broken, while repairing it yourself at an armour stand adds a discount of 7,500 coins per Smithing level, reducing the price to 757,500 coins at level 99.

The chestplate, along with all other Eclipse moon armour, functions as a very capable hybrid armour, with its strength bonuses and relatively high ranged bonuses. This is useful in situations where it is desireable to bring fewer armour switches, while still being effective in multiple styles.

As with all Moon equipment it is degradeable, much like Barrows equipment. The armour starts at 3000 charges and loses 1 charge for every 54 seconds in combat, meaning it lasts for 45 hours of continuous combat before breaking. Having an NPC such as Bob and Dunstan repair it costs 1,500,000 coins when fully broken, while repairing it yourself at an armour stand adds a discount of 7,500 coins per Smithing level, reducing the price to 757,500 coins at level 99.

29076:
Raw moss lizards are items obtained from catching Moss Lizards found within the Earthbound Cavern in Neypotzli . During Perilous Moons , players must catch one and use a knife on it to obtain a moss lizard tail .

Players with level 30 Cooking can cook moss lizards to obtain a cooked moss lizard . Up to three cuts of meat can be obtained from cooking one, with the chance depending on the player's Cooking level.

When leaving Neypotzli, this item is removed from the player's inventory with the message: The resources from Neypotzli fizzle to dust as they are severed from its magic.
29077:
Cooked moss lizard is a type of food obtained by cooking raw moss lizards at the campsites within Neypotzli after partial completion of Perilous Moons. It can be used as food whilst fighting the Moons of Peril.

Level 30 Cooking is required to cook moss lizards, and up to three cuts of meat can be obtained from cooking one, with the chance depending on the player's Cooking level.

The amount of Hitpoints restored is 1/3rd of the player's Cooking level or 1/2 of their Hunter level, whichever heals less, rounded down.

When leaving Neypotzli, this item is removed from the player's inventory with the message: The resources from Neypotzli fizzle to dust as they are severed from its magic.
29078:
Moonlight grubs are items collected from grubby saplings found within the Earthbound and Streambound Caverns in Neypotzli. During Perilous Moons, players must collect one and use a pestle and mortar on it to obtain moonlight grub paste.

When leaving Neypotzli, this item is removed from the player's inventory with the message: The resources from Neypotzli fizzle to dust as they are severed from its magic.

This item is used as the icon for moonlight potions on the in-game Herblore skill guide, despite the uncrushed grubs not being a reagent for the potion.
29079:
Moonlight grub paste is made by using a pestle and mortar on moonlight grubs, which are picked from grubby saplings within Neypotzli. Players can sometimes receive multiple paste from one grub, depending on their Herblore level.

Moonlight grub paste can be combined with a vial of water to create moonlight potions, which can be used as a potion whilst fighting the Moons of Peril to provide melee skill boosts and prayer restoration. Players may create an extra dose of potion, with the chance depending on the player's Herblore level.

Additionally, one moonlight grub paste is requested by Eyatlalli during Perilous Moons.

When leaving Neypotzli this item is removed from the player's inventory with the message: The resources from Neypotzli fizzle to dust as they are severed from its magic.
29080:
A moonlight potion is a potion created by adding moonlight grub paste to a vial of water. A dose of the moonlight potion provides a temporary skill boost to Attack, Strength, Defence, as well as restoring prayer points; the values of the boost vary depending on the player's Herblore level.

The potion can have 2-4 doses on creation, with chances of each varying depending on the player's Herblore level.

The potion cannot be taken out of Neypotzli. Doing so will revert the potion into a vial of water and the player will receive following message: The resources from Neypotzli fizzle to dust as they are severed from its magic.

Unlike prayer potions, moonlights potions do not benefit from the effects of the Holy wrench.

29084:
Sulphur blades are a two-handed weapon that requires level 55 Attack to wield, obtained as a rare drop from sulphur nagua in Neypotzli . Like their crush and stab equivalents, the glacial temotli and earthbound tecpatl , it performs two independently rolled hits per attack . The maximum damage of each hit is determined by calculating the combined max hit as normal and dividing it by two. If the combined max hit is odd, one max hit is rounded up while the other is rounded down (e.g., 45 → 22 + 23).

Their stats are nearly identical to the dragon scimitar , trading 2 strength bonus for 5 more slash accuracy, although the scimitar paired with a defender is considerably stronger.

As sulphur blades deal damage in two hitsplats, they are very good for training combat on sulphur nagua due to them taking an additional 4 minimum damage for each hitsplat. Additionally, moonlight potions are easy to make nearby and can be used to provide prayer points and melee stat boosts.
29087:
Sulphurous essence is an item dropped by sulphur nagua in Neypotzli . They can be given to Eyatlalli for 50 Runecraft experience each after completing Perilous Moons .

Leaving Neypotzli will cause any sulphurous essence in the player's inventory to be removed, accompanied by the message The resources from Neypotzli fizzle to dust as they are severed from its magic. . However, players can drop their essence before leaving and pick it up again after returning if they are fast enough.

It is always lost on death, even if reclaiming from the gravestone within the ruins.
29088:
Calcified deposit is an item that can occasionally be obtained from mining calcified rocks in the Cam Torum mine .

It can be crushed with a hammer by using it on an anvil , producing blessed bone shards or calcified moths . This process provides 1 Smithing experience and takes 3 ticks per deposit. On average, each deposit gives 7.5 shards.
29090:
Calcified moths are a single-use item that can teleport players to Cam Torum .

They require partial completion of Perilous Moons to use, up through killing the Sulphur Nagua to receive permission to enter the city. They cannot be used beyond level 20 Wilderness . When crushed, a game message in the chatbox will state You crush the moth, releasing the energy inside...

They are obtained by using a calcified deposit on any anvil with a hammer ; the rate of obtaining them from a calcified deposit is 1 in 4.

Despite having a high alchemy value of 6,000 coins, calcified moths cannot be alched. However, they can be sold to general stores for 4,000 to 6,000 coins, depending on the store.
29098: Not meat is an unobtainable item that dropped from sabre-toothed kebbits for about an hour after the addition of Varlamore. The item could originally be bought and sold on the Grand Exchange, but was never listed on the Grand Exchange Database. About an hour after the update, the item was removed from the inventories of any players who still had them. However, they were not removed from any uncollected Grand Exchange offers, nor were they removed from the private storage units in the Chambers of Xeric. As such, they are still in the game.

29128:
Cooked wild kebbit is a type of hunter meat that restores a total of 8 Hitpoints when eaten, 4 are restored immediately, 4 are restored after a delay of 7 ticks (4.2s). Eating another hunter meat too quickly will waste any pending healing, as the most recent delayed heal will replace older effects that have not completed yet. Standard foods and potions do not interrupt this pending heal.

It can be obtained by cooking raw wild kebbit on a fire or cooking range , requiring level 23 Cooking and granting 73 experience when successful. When cooking there is a chance to fail, resulting in burnt kebbit . The burn rate decreases as the player's Cooking level increases, and it will stop burning entirely at Cooking level 50 on both ranges and fires.
29131:
Cooked barb-tailed kebbit is a type of hunter meat that restores a total of 12 Hitpoints when eaten, 7 are restored immediately, 5 are restored after a delay of 7 ticks (4.2s). Eating another hunter meat too quickly will waste any pending healing, as the most recent delayed heal will replace older effects that have not completed yet. Standard foods and potions do not interrupt this pending heal.

It can be obtained by cooking raw barb-tailed kebbit on a fire or cooking range , requiring level 32 Cooking and granting 106 experience when successful. When cooking there is a chance to fail, resulting in burnt kebbit . The burn rate decreases as the player's Cooking level increases, and it will stop burning entirely at Cooking level 63 on both ranges and fires.
29134:
Cooked dashing kebbit is a type of hunter meat that restores a total of 23 Hitpoints when eaten, 13 are restored immediately, 10 are restored after a delay of 7 ticks (4.2s). The secondary heal also restores 10 points of run energy. Eating another hunter meat too quickly will waste any pending healing, as the most recent delayed heal will replace older effects that have not completed yet. Standard foods and potions do not interrupt this pending heal.

It can be obtained by cooking raw dashing kebbit on a fire or cooking range, requiring level 82 Cooking and granting 215 experience when successful. 50 Hunters' Rumours must be completed before they may be cooked. When cooking there is a chance to fail, resulting in burnt kebbit. The burn rate decreases as the player's Cooking level increases. Cooked dashing kebbit never stop burning altogether even at level 99, unless the player is wearing a Cooking cape.

Dashing kebbit is the third-highest healing single consumption food, surpassing the dark crab, bluefin, anglerfish, tuna potato, and manta ray, but is surpassed by cooked moonlight antelope and marlin. Dashing kebbit heals 23 health, but part of the healing is delayed, making it not always practical. Cooked moonlight antelope also has delayed healing, heals 26 health, and also cures poison when eaten. The other foods heal the full 22 Hitpoints instantly, anglerfish can heal the player above their base Hitpoints, and bluefin also restores 5 Prayer points.

Standard foods and potions do not interrupt this pending heal.

The burn rate decreases as the player's Cooking level increases, and it will stop burning entirely at Cooking level 92 on ranges and level 93 on fires.

Eating another hunter meat too quickly will waste any pending healing, as the most recent delayed heal will replace older effects that have not completed yet. Standard foods and potions do not interrupt this pending heal.

It can be obtained by cooking raw sunlight antelope on a fire or cooking range , requiring level 68 Cooking and granting 175 experience when successful. 50 Hunters' Rumours must be completed before they may be cooked. When cooking, there is a chance to fail, resulting in burnt antelope . The burn rate decreases as the player's Cooking level increases, and it will stop burning entirely on ranges at level 95.
29143:
Cooked moonlight antelope is a type of hunter meat that restores a total of 26 Hitpoints when eaten, 14 are restored immediately, 12 are restored after a delay of 7 ticks (4.2s). The secondary heal also cures poison and reduces venom to poison. Eating another hunter meat too quickly will waste any pending healing, as the most recent delayed heal will replace older effects that have not completed yet. Standard foods and potions do not interrupt this pending heal.

It can be obtained by cooking raw moonlight antelope on a fire or cooking range, requiring level 92 Cooking and granting 220 experience when successful. 50 Hunters' Rumours must be completed before they may be cooked. When cooking there is a chance to fail, resulting in burnt antelope. The burn rate decreases as the player's Cooking level increases. Moonlight antelope will never stop burning altogether even at level 99, unless the player is wearing a Cooking cape.

Moonlight antelope is the highest-healing single-consumption food, surpassing the marlin and cooked dashing kebbit. Moonlight antelope heals 26 health, but part of the healing is delayed, making it sometimes impractical. Dashing kebbit also has delayed healing, but heals only 23, and restores 10 run energy when eaten. Marlin heals 24 instantly, while others such as manta rays heal 22 instantly.
29146:
Cooked larupia is a type of hunter meat that restores a total of 11 Hitpoints when eaten, 6 are restored immediately, 5 are restored after a delay of 7 ticks (4.2s). Eating another hunter meat too quickly will waste any pending healing, as the most recent delayed heal will replace older effects that have not completed yet. Standard foods and potions do not interrupt this pending heal.

It can be obtained by cooking raw larupia on a fire or cooking range, requiring level 31 Cooking and granting 92 experience when successful. When cooking there is a chance to fail, resulting in a burnt large beast. The burn rate decreases as the player's Cooking level increases, and it will stop burning entirely at Cooking level 59 on both ranges and fires.
29149:
Cooked graahk is a type of hunter meat that restores a total of 14 Hitpoints when eaten, 8 are restored immediately, 6 are restored after a delay of 7 ticks (4.2s). Eating another hunter meat too quickly will waste any pending healing, as the most recent delayed heal will replace older effects that have not completed yet. Standard foods and potions do not interrupt this pending heal.

It can be obtained by cooking raw graahk on a fire or cooking range, requiring level 41 Cooking and granting 124 experience when successful. 25 Hunters' Rumours must be completed before they may be cooked. When cooking there is a chance to fail, resulting in burnt large beast. The burn rate decreases as the player's Cooking level increases, and it will stop burning entirely at Cooking level 75.
29152:
Cooked kyatt is a type of hunter meat that restores a total of 17 Hitpoints when eaten, 9 are restored immediately, 8 are restored after a delay of 7 ticks (4.2s). Eating another hunter meat too quickly will waste any pending healing, as the most recent delayed heal will replace older effects that have not completed yet. Standard foods and potions do not interrupt this pending heal.

It can be obtained by cooking raw kyatt on a fire or cooking range, requiring level 51 Cooking and granting 143 experience when successful. 25 Hunters' Rumours must be completed before they may be cooked. When cooking there is a chance to fail, resulting in burnt large beast. The burn rate decreases as the player's Cooking level increases, and it will stop burning entirely at Cooking level 80 on ranges and level 86 on fires.
29155:
Burnt kebbit is the result of accidentally burning either raw wild kebbit, raw barb-tailed kebbit, or raw dashing kebbit. The burn rate while cooking these will decrease as players reach higher Cooking levels.

The burnt kebbit has no use whatsoever. Like most other burnt food, it is tradeable to other players but not on the Grand Exchange.
29157:
Burnt large beast is the result of accidentally burning either raw larupia, raw graahk, or raw kyatt. The burn rate while cooking these will decrease as players reach higher Cooking levels.

The burnt large beast has no use whatsoever. Like most other burnt food, it is tradeable to other players but not on the Grand Exchange.
29159:
Burnt antelope is the result of accidentally burning either raw sunlight antelope or raw moonlight antelope . The burn rate while cooking these will decrease as players reach higher Cooking levels.

The burnt antelope has no use whatsoever. Like most other burnt food, it is tradeable to other players but not on the Grand Exchange .
29161:
Burnt fox meat is the result of accidentally burning a raw pyre fox while attempting to cook pyre fox meat. The burn rate while cooking these will decrease as players reach higher Cooking levels, stopping entirely at level 92 on ranges and level 93 on fires.

The burnt fox meat has no use whatsoever. Like most other burnt food, it is tradeable to other players but not on the Grand Exchange.
29163:
Fox fur is a type of hunter fur obtained from pyre foxes, requiring level 57 Hunter to hunt.

It can be used to craft small meat pouches at level 35 Crafting, or be used in crafting mixed hide legs at level 71 Crafting. It can be used to dress golems in the golem crafting activity.
29166:
A Jerboa tail is an item obtained from embertailed jerboas , requiring level 39 Hunter to hunt.

It can optionally be used as bait when hunting pyre foxes , which gives a 3% bonus to catch rate. Combined with a lit Torch used on the trap gives an extra 2% bonus, for a total of 5%. This stacks with the Guild hunter outfit bonus.

Five jerboa tails are also used with a knife , teak logs , and five hunter spear tips to create five hunter's spears .

During At First Light , it is also used to create a makeshift poultice for Guild Hunter Fox , as well as for repairing the bed of Guild Hunter Kiko .
29168:
Sunlight antelope antlers are obtained from hunting sunlight antelopes (requiring level 72 Hunter ) in the far east of the Avium Savannah .

It is used to upgrade a hunters' crossbow to a hunters' sunlight crossbow with level 74 Fletching , as well as be used to create 12 sunlight antler bolts per antler with level 62 Fletching. Both products require having a chisel .
29171:
Moonlight antelope antlers are obtained from hunting moonlight antelopes (requiring level 91 Hunter ) found south of the Hunter Guild pub.

Each antler is used along with a chisel to create 12 moonlight antler bolts with level 72 Fletching .
29174:
Moonlight antelope fur is a type of hunter fur obtained from moonlight antelopes, requiring level 91 Hunter to hunt.

Currently, it is only used for finishing a golem as a part of golem crafting. Otherwise, it can be sold to Pellem's Fur Store, Durrik's Goods or the Fortis Fur Stall.
29177:
Sunlight antelope fur is a type of hunter fur obtained from Sunlight antelopes, requiring level 72 Hunter to hunt.

It can be used to craft large meat pouches at level 65 Crafting, or be used in crafting mixed hide boots and mixed hide tops at level 69 and 72 Crafting, respectively. It can be used to dress golems in the golem crafting activity.
29180:
A sapphire glacialis mix is a type of hunter's mix that players can drink to boost their Defence level by 4 + 15% of their Defence level, rounded down. If drunk in a multicombat area, up to three players who are standing within two tiles of the drinker will receive the same boost, provided that they have Accept Aid toggled on.

They are made by using a jarred sapphire glacialis with certain meats acquired from hunter creatures; doing so requires a pestle and mortar, and does not appear to have any skill requirements associated to mix them.
29183:
A snowy knight mix is a type of hunter's mix that players can drink to restore 8 Hitpoints per dose (16 hitpoints total). If drunk in a multicombat area, up to three players who are standing within two tiles of the drinker will also be healed, provided that they have Accept Aid toggled on.

The snowy knight mix is the only hunter's mix that has a weaker per-use effect than releasing the moth or butterfly directly. The jarred snowy knight is a single-use item that restores 15 hitpoints in a single action, whereas the hunter mix restores a total of 16 hitpoints across two actions.

They are made by using a jarred snowy knight with certain meats acquired from hunter creatures; doing so requires a pestle and mortar, and does not appear to have any skill requirements associated to mix them.
29186:
A ruby harvest mix is a type of hunter's mix that players can drink to boost their Attack level by 4 + 15% of their Attack level, rounded down. If drunk in a multicombat area , up to three players who are standing within two tiles of the drinker will receive the same boost, provided that they have Accept Aid toggled on.

They are made by using a jarred ruby harvest with certain meats acquired from hunter creatures ; doing so requires a pestle and mortar , and does not appear to have any skill requirements associated to mix them.
29189:
A black warlock mix is a type of hunter's mix that players can drink to boost their Strength level by 4 + 15% of their Strength level, rounded down. If drunk in a multicombat area , up to three players who are standing within two tiles of the drinker will receive the same boost, provided that they have Accept Aid toggled on.

They are made by using a jarred black warlock with certain raw meats (cooked meat will not work) acquired from hunter creatures ; doing so requires a pestle and mortar , and does not appear to have any skill requirements associated to mix them.
29192:
A sunlight moth mix is a type of hunter's mix that players can drink to restore 6 + 20% of their reduced stats, as well as 8 Hitpoints, but not including Prayer. If consumed in a multicombat area, up to three players who are standing within two tiles of the drinker will receive the same effect, provided that they have Accept Aid toggled on. This effectively works as a cheaper restore potion, without requiring either Herblore levels or ingredients.

They are made by using a jarred sunlight moth with certain meats acquired from hunter creatures; doing so requires a pestle and mortar, and does not appear to have any skill requirements associated to mix them.

Similar to Guthix rest, sunlight moth mix effectively functions as a potion, meaning players can use them to heal during combat without delaying their attacks. This makes them particularly useful for healing when attempting to kill bosses as quickly as possible for certain combat achievements, especially when intentionally taking damage with vengeance and rings of recoil.
29195:
A moonlight moth mix is a type of hunter's mix that players can drink to restore 22 Prayer points per dose. The effect of the holy wrench does not apply to this item.

If drunk in a multicombat area, up to three players who are standing within two tiles of the drinker will receive the same effect, provided that they have Accept Aid toggled on. This effectively works as a cheaper Prayer potion, without requiring either Herblore levels or ingredients. For Group Ironmen, the moonlight moth mix can be shared, while the non-mix variant cannot.

They are made by using a jarred moonlight moth with hunter meat acquired from hunter creatures; doing so requires a pestle and mortar, and does not have any skill requirements associated to mix them.

A quick way for Ironmen to obtain raw hunter meat is by catching dashing kebbits in the Piscatoris falconry area.

Players with level 30 Cooking can cook raw bream to obtain a cooked bream . Up to two bream can be cooked in a single action, with the chance depending on the player's Cooking level.
29217:
Cooked Bream are a type of fish obtained by cooking raw bream at the campsites within Neypotzli after completion of Perilous Moons . It can be used as food whilst fighting the Moons of Peril .

The amount of Hitpoints restored is 1/3rd of the player's Cooking level or Fishing level, whichever skill is the lowest.

When leaving Neypotzli, this item is removed from the player's inventory with the message: The resources from Neypotzli fizzle to dust as they are severed from its magic.

29242:
Basic hunters' loot sacks are a reward for successfully completing novice Hunters' Rumours assigned by Huntmaster Gilman.

Opening them rolls 5 times on the loot table; however, unlike other hunters' loot sacks, the basic sack does not drop enhanced quetzal whistle blueprints, huntsman's kits, or pieces of the guild hunter outfit.
29244:
Adept hunters' loot sacks are a reward for successfully completing adept Hunters' Rumours assigned by Guild Hunter Cervus or Ornus.

Opening them rolls 7 times for resources, and also has a chance to reward the enhanced quetzal whistle blueprint, the huntsman's kit, and pieces of the guild hunter outfit.
29246:
Expert hunters' loot sacks are a reward for successfully completing expert Hunters' Rumours assigned by Guild Hunter Aco or Teco.

Opening them rolls 9 times for resources, and also has a chance to reward the enhanced quetzal whistle blueprint, the huntsman's kit, and pieces of the guild hunter outfit. Expert and master sacks also drop perfected quetzal whistle blueprints, and rarely the Quetzin pet.
29248:
Master hunters' loot sacks are a reward for successfully completing master Hunters' Rumours assigned by Guild Hunter Wolf.

Opening them rolls 11 times for resources, and also has a chance to reward the enhanced quetzal whistle blueprint, the huntsman's kit, and pieces of the guild hunter outfit. Master and expert sacks also drop perfected quetzal whistle blueprints, and rarely the Quetzin pet.

Upon completing 10 Hunters' Rumours, players can obtain one for free from Soar Leader Pitri; subsequent blueprints will cost 500 coins.
29253:
Enhanced quetzal whistle blueprints are used to craft enhanced quetzal whistles, alongside a basic quetzal whistle, yew logs and a knife.

Enhanced blueprints can be obtained from hunters' loot sacks or purchased from other players. An untradeable variant, the torn enhanced quetzal whistle blueprint, can be obtained from any hunters' loot sack upon completing 100 Hunters' Rumours.

Enhanced blueprints can be traded in to Guild Scribe Verity for a supply loot sack.

Perfected blueprints can be traded in to Guild Scribe Verity for a supply loot sack .

29271:
A basic quetzal whistle is a teleportation item that takes players to any built Quetzal Transport System landing site. When the teleport function is clicked, it will open the transport interface. It cannot be used beyond level 20 Wilderness.

The whistle is made via the right-click "Craft" option on a basic quetzal whistle blueprint, whilst having willow logs and a knife in the inventory. The blueprints are initially obtained for free from Soar Leader Pitri after completing 10 Hunters' Rumours, with subsequent blueprints costing 500 coins. Players can then craft and charge more whistles, carrying or storing away as many as they'd like.

The basic whistle can hold up to 5 charges, but can be upgraded to an enhanced quetzal whistle, which holds up to 20. The "Check" option will display a message containing the whistle's remaining charges, e.g. Your quetzal whistle has 4 charges remaining.. Lastly, the "Rumour" option on the whistle will remind players of their active rumour, e.g. Your current rumour target is a grey chinchompa. You'll need to bring back some of its fur. Cervus was the source of the rumour..

Quetzal whistles may be used to teleport to any built landing site in the Quetzal Transport System without needing to unlock Renu during Twilight's Promise.

There is an option in the game settings to configure the quetzal whether to open a map or directly teleport you to the guild. The tickbox for this can be found under the Gameplay section.

A perfected quetzal whistle is a teleportation item that takes players to any built Quetzal Transport System landing site. When the teleport function is clicked, it will open the transport interface. It cannot be used beyond level 20 Wilderness .

The whistle is made via the right-click "Craft" option on a perfected quetzal whistle blueprint , whilst having an enhanced quetzal whistle , redwood logs , and a knife in the inventory. The blueprints can be obtained from hunters' loot sacks or purchased from other players; players who have completed 250 Hunters' Rumours without ever getting a perfected whistle blueprint will receive an untradeable torn variant from their next hunters' loot sack to be used in crafting the whistle for themselves. Any charges on the enhanced whistle will be transferred to the perfected whistle.

The perfected whistle holds up to 50 charges. The "Check" option will display a message containing the whistle's remaining charges, ex. Your quetzal whistle has 4 charges remaining. . Lastly, the "Rumour" option on the whistle will remind players of their active rumour, ex. Your current rumour target is a grey chinchompa. You'll need to bring back some of its fur. Cervus was the source of the rumour. .

Quetzal whistles may be used to teleport to any built landing site in the Quetzal Transport System without needing to unlock Renu during Twilight's Promise .

There is an option in the game settings to configure the quetzal whether to open a map or directly teleport you to the guild. The tickbox for this can be found under the Gameplay section.
29277:
Trapper's tipple is a type of ale that temporarily boosts Hunter by 2 while draining Strength by 1 and Attack by 2.

It is purchasable from Huntmaster Gilman, who runs The Burrow pub in the Hunter Guild, requiring a minimum Hunter level of 46 (not boostable) to access. Three spawns can also be found on the tables inside the Burrow. Unlike other ales, it cannot be created through brewing.

Upon drinking the ale, a message in the chatbox will state You drink the Trapper's Tipple and feel ready to catch some creatures. You feel less able to fight said creatures.
29280:
A mixed hide top is a part of the mixed hide armour set, requiring level 60 Ranged and 50 Defence to wear. It provides bonuses that are meant to complement the hunter's spear . It is the only chestpiece with a stab attack bonus, which can also make it uniquely effective against high defence enemies with a stab weakness, especially considering that it only has two less strength bonus than accessible alternatives like a Fighter torso .

Players with level 72 Crafting can create the top with a mixed hide base and two sunlight antelope furs , alongside a needle and thread (or a costume needle ). Players without the required level may instead pay 20,000 coins to Pellem at the Hunter Guild to make one on their behalf, whilst providing the aforementioned fur (you do not need to provide the mixed hide base).

This item can be stored in the armour case of a costume room , as part of the mixed hide armour set. Ultimate Ironmen will be unable to retrieve individual pieces until the full set is stored.
29283:
Mixed hide legs are part of the mixed hide armour set, requiring level 60 Ranged to wear. It provides bonuses that are meant to complement the hunter's spear . However, because of the added stab bonus, this item may be preferable to the Bandos tassets in situations where the additional 2 Strength bonus does not grant a max hit.

Players with level 71 Crafting can create the legs with a mixed hide base and three fox furs , alongside a needle and thread (or a costume needle ). Players without the required level may instead pay 20,000 coins to Pellem at the Hunter Guild to make one on their behalf, whilst providing the aforementioned fur (you do not need to provide the mixed hide base).

This item can be stored in the armour case of a costume room , as part of the mixed hide armour set. Ultimate Ironmen will be unable to retrieve individual pieces until the full set is stored.
29286:
Mixed hide boots are part of the mixed hide armour set, requiring level 60 Ranged and 50 Defence to wear. It provides bonuses that complement the hunter's spear .

Players with level 69 Crafting can create the boots with a mixed hide base and one sunlight antelope fur , alongside a needle and thread . Players without the required level may instead pay 17,500 coins to Pellem at the Hunter Guild to make one on their behalf, whilst providing the aforementioned fur (you do not need to provide the mixed hide base).

This item can be stored in the armour case of a costume room , as part of the mixed hide armour set. Ultimate Ironmen will be unable to retrieve individual pieces until the full set is stored.

Compared to the climbing boots , which are also strength-bonus-giving boots, mixed hide boots have extra defence bonuses, as well as some ranged attack bonus. However, they have much higher requirements to equip, and provide negative magic attack bonus.
29289:
A mixed hide cape is a part of the mixed hide armour set, requiring level 60 Ranged and 50 Defence to wear. It provides bonuses that complement the hunter's spear .

Players with level 68 Crafting can create the cape with a mixed hide base and a jaguar fur , alongside a needle and thread . Players without the required level may instead pay 20,000 coins to Pellem at the Hunter Guild to make one on their behalf, whilst providing the aforementioned fur (you do not need to provide the mixed hide base).

This is the only tradeable cape to provide a strength bonus. Because of this, it may be desirable for those who cannot earn a Fire cape . It is also notable for being the only cape slot item to have a negative magic attack bonus.

This item can be stored in the armour case of a costume room , as part of the mixed hide armour set. Ultimate Ironmen will be unable to retrieve individual pieces until the full set is stored.
29292: A mixed hide base is an item purchased from Pellem's Fur Store at the Hunter Guild . A needle can be used on it to craft mixed hide armour ; a total of four pieces are needed to create a full set of mixed hide armour, with one used for each piece.
29295:
The small meat pouch is an item that can store up to 14 pieces of hunter meat . It is made with level 35 Crafting from 4 fox fur , as well as a needle and thread ; doing so grants 30 Crafting experience.

Players can right-click to open the pouch, which will have hunter meats that the player acquires to be automatically placed inside the pouch, provided there is space for it. Players can check the contents of the pouch by selecting the "Check" right-click option, which tells the number of meats the player has inside. The pouch does not store raw bird meat , despite being acquired from hunting. Players may empty the pouch by right-clicking "Empty" on the item within a bank , whilst the bank or deposit box interface is open, or on the top floor of the Hunters' Guild. However, players cannot empty their meat pouches into their inventory whilst inside both Mor Ul Rek 's outer and inner parts of the city.

It can be upgraded into a large meat pouch with 65 Crafting and 3 sunlight antelope fur . If you already own a large meat pouch, the items stored by a small pouch will overwrite those pouches during this process and may delete items from the game.

The pouch shares its inventory with every small meat pouch you own. This means creating multiple pouches will not let you store more meat. If you have multiple pouches in your inventory, and destroy any of the other small meat pouches, all contents throughout your inventory and bank will be removed (You can however use a large meat pouch to store meat and craft multiple small meat pouches during a Pyre fox Hunters' Rumours and cast High Level Alchemy to make 1,800 coins every 4 fox fur you get). If you cast High Level Alchemy on a small meat pouch full of meat and then craft a new one the meat will remain in the pouch.
29297:
The large meat pouch is an item that can store up to 28 pieces of hunter meat . It is made with level 65 Crafting by upgrading a small meat pouch with 3 sunlight antelope fur as well as a needle and thread , granting 60 Crafting experience. A costume needle can also be used in place of the regular needle and thread. The small meat pouch must be closed before the player can upgrade it.

Players can right-click to open the pouch. Whilst open, hunter meats obtained from hunting will automatically go into the pouch if there is enough space. Players can check the number of meats inside with the right-click "Check" option.

The large meat pouch can only be emptied within a bank or while on the top floor of the Hunters' Guild. The meats can be emptied into the inventory or into the bank (if the bank or deposit box interface is open) via the right-click "Empty" option or by shift-clicking the pouch (if shift-click item dropping is enabled). The pouch cannot be emptied into the inventory at these banks:

The pouch shares its inventory with every meat pouch the player owns. Creating multiple pouches will not let the player store more meat. If the player destroys any of the pouches, all the meats inside will be removed.
29299:

29305:
The hunter's spear is a thrown weapon that requires level 55 Ranged and 30 Strength to equip. Compared to other ranged weapons, the player's melee strength bonuses are used when determining the amount of ranged damage dealt to a target. Ava's devices do work on these.

The hunter's spear when equipped also acts like a teasing stick and provides a 5% increased chance for teased creatures to walk into a pitfall trap. The spear must be equipped before being able to tease creatures. Teasing creatures does not consume the spear. Despite being a thrown weapon, it cannot be used to tease creatures from a distance, though it may be used to hunt stymphikes in place of makeshift spears (although it seems Ava's devices do not work while hunting stymphikes). The hunter's spear can be stored in the Huntsman's kit.

Additionally, it will not be consumed when attacking chinchompas to speed up and reset their spawns when Hunting.
29307:
Quetzal feed is a possible reward from completing Hunters' Rumours at the Hunter Guild. Ten are needed to build a landing site for the Quetzal Transport System. It may also be used to recharge the Quetzal whistle's teleports by 1. If quetzal feed is in the inventory when recharging the whistle, it may be lost.

A total of 60 quetzal feeds is required in order to build all landing sites.
29309:
The huntsman's kit can be obtained from hunters' loot sacks, which are received as rewards upon completing Hunters' Rumours. The huntsman's kit can be used to store various hunting equipment, though they cannot be used whilst stored.

The kit has a maximum capacity of up to 32 different types of items that can be stored at once, so it is unable to contain all types of storable items at one time.

Items stored in the kit are not lost upon death, even against players in the Wilderness, and remain stored when reclaimed. Only one kit can be owned at a time.

The kit can be given to Verity for a master-level hunters' loot sack which excludes uniques, although it can only be subsequently reobtained by receiving it again.

The kit will empty from the last slot in the kit.

Because the huntsman's kit stores imps-in-boxes, it can be taken to extended combat to effectively serve as an unlimited deposit box.
29311:
Hunter spear tips are an item used in crafting hunter's spears that are obtainable from hunters' loot sacks, which are received as rewards upon completing Hunters' Rumours.

Players with level 60 Fletching (unboostable) can use a knife to create hunter's spears from five jerboa tails, a teak log, and five hunter spear tips. Spears are always crafted in batches of five, so a minimum of 5 spear tips must be used.
29317:
The tattered request note is obtained by speaking to Guildmaster Apatura after completing 50 Hunters' Rumours .

It can be reclaimed by searching the bookshelf upstairs in her quarters.
29319: The guild history excerpt is obtained by speaking to Guildmaster Apatura after completing 100 Hunters' Rumours.
29321:
Apatura's note is a document offering information on how Apatura came to be guildmaster of the Hunter Guild .

After completing 150 Hunters' Rumours , players can speak to Apatura to receive her key , which unlocks the guildmaster's chest containing the note.
29323:
Apatura's key is obtained by speaking to Guildmaster Apatura after completing 150 Hunters' Rumours .

It is used to unlock the guildmaster's chest a floor above her quarters, which contains Apatura's note .
29325:
House keys can be obtained from pickpocketing wealthy citizens in Civitas illa Fortis at 50 Thieving . They can also be fished from the fishing spot within the park using a big fishing net .

At level 50 Thieving , house keys can be used in stealing valuables . A Thieving activity located in Civitas illa Fortis where players enter Victor's , Caius ', or Lavinia's houses while they are unoccupied in order to steal valuables , after which they are consumed upon use.

Wearing a full set of rogue equipment doubles the number of house keys stolen from wealthy citizens.

Despite Oriana suggesting that the player uses them before they break, house keys do not actually break over time. They do, however, break in the door when used.
29328:
The House keys is an interface item that can be seen in the Thieving skill guide representing house keys .

The actual item cannot be obtained by players.
29332:
Valuables are acquired by stealing valuables from wealthy citizens' houses in Civitas illa Fortis . Found inside chests, wardrobes, and jewellery cases, valuables are stackable and will continue to be looted without clicking again for a time, granting 45 Thieving experience per valuable. Rogue equipment will not double the valuables obtained.

Occasionally, a flashing arrow will appear above one of the objects in the house, indicated by a game message in the chatbox stating You notice something shine somewhere else in the house. . These indicate that the player can get a one-time reward of 630 Thieving experience and 14 valuables from it.

Though considered as contraband in Varlamore , players may break them down with a chisel to obtain 125 blessed bone shards (similar to that of blessed superior dragon bones at 121 blessed bone shards) and 5 Crafting experience.

29344:
Blessed bones are the blessed form of bones obtained by using them on the exposed altar on the summit of Ralos' Rise . They are broken down with a chisel to obtain 4 blessed bone shards and 5 Crafting experience, which can then be sacrificed at the libation bowl at the Teomat .

As each shard sacrificed gives 5 Prayer experience, each blessed bone gives 20 Prayer experience overall. If using a jug of blessed sunfire wine at the libation bowl instead of a regular jug of blessed wine , this is increased to 6 Prayer experience per shard, or 24 Prayer experience per bone.

Players looking to bless bones in bulk may talk to Virilis , found at the base of the exposed altar, to unnote any type of bones for a fee of 10 coins per bone.

As each shard sacrificed gives 5 Prayer experience, each sun-kissed bones gives 225 Prayer experience overall.
