30310:
The base plans are an item obtained from searching the tapestry in Zemouregal's Fort during The Curse of Arrav, alongside the base key. They are given to Elias White, who uses them to formulate a plan to retrieve Arrav's heart, which is guarded under heavy security in the inner section of Zemouregal's Base.

Studing the plans will give a chatbox message stating "These appear to be complex plans for Zemouregal's Base in Silvarea. Maybe Elias can help you interpret them."
30311: The base key is an item obtained from searching the tapestry in Zemouregal's Fort during The Curse of Arrav, alongside the base plans. They are used to enter the inner section of Zemouregal's Base, where Arrav's heart is located.

Pre-filled with sacred oil, players must then study the mural south of the chamber, which depicts the items required to preserve Arrav 's heart: three dwellberries and a ring of life .

After The Curse of Arrav , another can still be obtained by searching the shelves in the mastaba.

Arrav's axe is an animation item that is temporarily wielded by the player when they counter Arrav's flying axe attack during the fight against him in The Curse of Arrav. Aside from this, it cannot actually be obtained.

Oddly, his axe, which is said to have been left behind by accident before he journeyed on his quest for the legendary shield, is seen in the Large Display at the outpost after completion of the Making History quest.
30321:
The zombie helmet is a crush-focused piece of headgear that requires 50 Strength and Defence to equip. It is created by taking a broken zombie helmet , which can be obtained as a drop from armoured zombies in Zemouregal's Fort , to an anvil and repairing it. Doing so requires level 70 Smithing .

The zombie helmet is one of a small number of helmets with a crush attack bonus, lying between the dwarven helmet (+6) and the inquisitor's great helm (+10). It has the best defensive bonuses of any crush-focused helm, but lacks the melee strength bonus, and prayer bonus of the inquisitor's great helm.
30324: The broken zombie helmet is the broken version of the zombie helmet, and is dropped by armoured zombies found within Zemouregal's Fort. Players with 70 Smithing can repair the helmet at an anvil with a hammer in the inventory, or boosted from level 65 with an orange spicy stew. Repairing the helmet grants the player 500 Smithing experience.

Dust is an item obtained from searching the northern skeleton in the ground level of the Uzer Mastaba, in the tunnel connecting to it. The skeleton will not give more dust when searched if the player already has dust in their inventory.

Dust can also be rarely obtained by searching the barrels and bookcases in the basement of the Twilight Temple.

It currently has no use, but is notably purchasable by free-to-play players on the Grand Exchange despite being only obtainable from members sources.

30359:
The leprechaun's vault is an item that was obtainable during the Raging Echoes League , given to players upon unlocking the Overgrown relic .

The leprechaun's vault allows players to access their seed vault from anywhere in the world.

If lost or destroyed, the leprechaun's vault can be reclaimed from The Sage .
30361:
The banker's briefcase is an item that can be obtained during Demonic Pacts League from the Bank Heist relic. The briefcase is equipped to the cape slot .

The item allows players to teleport to any bank , bank chest , or bank deposit box , providing that the destination is in a region the player has unlocked.

This item ignores Wilderness teleport restrictions.

If lost or destroyed, the banker's briefcase can be reclaimed from the Leagues Tutor in Yama's Lair .
30363:
The clue compass is an item that was obtainable during the Raging Echoes League , given to players upon unlocking the Clue Compass relic . The compass is equipped to the ammo slot.

The item allows players to teleport to any STASH unit (with the exception of 3 in Varlamore near the Twilight Temple ), and Falo the Bard , provided that the destination is in a region the player has unlocked. The player may also teleport to the location of the clue step they have last read.

This item ignores wilderness teleport restrictions.

For Falo the Bard clue steps, "use" the clue compass on Falo the Bard to fulfil the item requirement.

This item also acts as a light source .

The dogsword was a Godsword combining the effects of all 5 godswords. It was an unlock in the Grid Master community event, unlocked by completing all tasks in column 1. As with all godsword variants, it requires level 75 Attack to wield.

It counts as a god item towards all factions in the God Wars Dungeon.
30369:
The sunlight spear is a two-handed weapon that was a reward from completing all column 6 tasks in Grid Master. Every time the player attacks using the spear, they will gain a "Sunlight Stack", which can be stacked up to 20. Players will lose a Sunlight Stack if they have not attacked for 50 ticks (30 seconds). Additionally, teleporting will reset the Sunlight Stacks to zero.

Despite the name, the Sunlight Spear is considered a Stab Sword and will not complete the Combat Achievement I Brought Mine Too for killing Sol Heredit with a spear.
30371:
The devil's element is an offhand magic item that can be obtained from the echo thermonuclear smoke devil in the Demonic Pacts League.

The devil's element has a passive effect that adds a 30% elemental weakness against all elements in addition to any existing weaknesses.

Like the Shadowflame Quadrant, this item provides unlimited air, water, earth, and fire runes when equipped.
30373:
The drygore blowpipe is a two-handed light ranged weapon that can be obtained during Demonic Pacts League by defeating Echo Kalphite Queen .

Similar to Osmumten's fang , it has a passive effect which provides two independent accuracy rolls; if either is higher than the opponent's original defence roll, the attack is a successful hit . Each attack also has a 25% chance to inflict burn on the target.

Unlike the toxic blowpipe , the drygore blowpipe does not have a ranged requirement to wield, although it still inherits the reduced attack speed in PvP (3 on Rapid).

When loaded with darts , the drygore blowpipe has an extra +10 Ranged Strength . The Drygore blowpipe cannot be loaded with poisoned darts, attempting to do so results in the message "You can't use that kind of dart."

30380:
The Gloves of the Damned are a pair of gloves that were obtainable during the Grid Master community event by completing all tasks in row 6. They provide combat bonuses identical to Barrows gloves .

Wearing the gloves counts as wearing an Amulet of the Damned for Barrows equipment while strengthening both the equipment's base set effects and their amulet of the damned additions. The gloves' effect does not require or stack with an amulet of the damned. [ 1 ]
30382:
The thousand-dragon ward was an unlock in the Grid Master community event , unlocked by completing all tasks in column 7.

While equipped, the player is immune to a number of status effects and attacks, including poison , venom , dragonfire (except from drakes ), icy breath , swamp decay , disease , desert heat , and chill stat-drains. This immunity also applies to more specific damage sources, such as Nex's ice prison , the Karuulm Slayer Dungeon floor, and poison gas clouds . Note that this will NOT prevent damage from Echo King Black Dragon's venom attack, but will prevent the venom status effect from being applied. The ward does not provide immunity to stat drain effect from basilisks .
30384:
The crystal blessing is an echo item that can be obtained from Echo Corrupted Hunllef during the Demonic Pacts League . Equipped in the ammunition slot, the blessing expands the accuracy and damage bonus from crystal armour (which is usually only applied to the crystal bow and Bow of Faerdhinen ) to all melee weapons (including barehanded attacks) and all magic powered weapons.

Additionally, the blessing provides +2% magic damage and +20 Magic attack bonus per crystal armour piece equipped (this is additive with the negative magic attack bonuses from the crystal armour pieces themselves; as the full crystal armour set has a negative magic attack bonus of -40 by default, equipping the blessing along with all three pieces of crystal armour will result in a total magic attack bonus of +20).
30386: The sunlit bracers are gloves that were rewarded when completing all column six tasks in Grid Master. The bracers have a passive effect which doubles any base healing received, including from the amulet of blood fury, blood spells, and Guthan the Infested's equipment, but doesn't double modifiers like bloodbark armour. They will protect the wearer from nettles.
30388:
The thunder khopesh was an unlock in the Grid Master community event . After the player builds a demonic throne in their player-owned house , the player is given the thunder khopesh.

It has a passive effect that grants standard, successful hits a 20% chance to summon a delayed lightning bolt at the target's location, damaging enemies in a 3x3 area for up to 50% of the player's max hit. The lightning bolt will be summoned at the centre of the target's location at the time the effect was triggered.

The lightning does not roll accuracy checks, but it is possible for enemies to move out of the effect between the attack triggering and the attack striking, causing them to avoid the damage entirely. No experience is gained from the damage dealt by the lightning bolts.

It is a corpbane weapon, meaning it does full damage to the Corporeal Beast .
30390:
Nature's reprisal is a two-handed weapon that was dropped from the Echo variant of the Hespori during the Raging Echoes League. Similar to salamanders, it is able to attack with all three combat styles, with the added benefit of an expanded attack range, even when using melee.

The reprisal is charged with 1 nature and 5 earth runes, and it can hold up to 5,000 charges.

The drop has a 1/15 chance to drop from Hespori, and players will always receive a nature's reprisal on their 30th Hespori (Echo) kill.

30402: The raids megarare voucher is an item obtainable during the Demonic Pacts League. When a player normally rolls a megarare item as a drop from any of the three raids (Chambers of Xeric, Theatre of Blood, and Tombs of Amascut), they will instead receive a megarare voucher. The voucher can then be given to the Leagues Tutor in Yama's Lair to redeem any of the three megarare items (twisted bow, scythe of Vitur, or Tumeken's shadow) from any of the three raids, rather than being limited to the megarare item of that particular raid. 30495:
The spirit tree & fairy ring can be built in the teleport space of the superior garden in a player-owned house. It requires 95 Construction, 83 Farming, and a watering can to build and when built, it gives 885 Construction and Farming experience. Players can teleport to other fairy rings and spirit trees using this teleportation space. Other players can use the tree-ring, provided they have met the requirements to do so. This does not count towards the number of spirit trees a player may own.

A set of goblin decorations can be used on the tree to make a Christmas-themed spiritual fairy tree, or a Raging echoes spirit tree scroll to make a Raging Echoes League-themed tree. Using a spade on the tree while in building mode allows the player to rotate it. The Raging echoes spirit tree scroll can be removed by attempting to remove the spirit tree in build mode.

The minimum levels a spirit tree & fairy ring can be built at are 90 Construction (with use of a spicy stew) and 78 Farming (also with the use of a spicy stew). A crystal saw cannot be used. Otherwise, the alternative is making 2 superior gardens and planting the tree and fairy ring separately, which requires level 75 Construction and 85 Construction respectively.

Compared with an ordinary fairy ring in a player-owned-house, the spirit tree & fairy ring does not have a right-click favourites menu. The loss of this feature may be a reason to prefer a separate ring and tree as opposed to the combined version.
30496:
A spirit tree can be built in the teleport space of the superior garden in a player-owned house. It requires 75 Construction, 83 Farming, and a watering can. Both skills requirements are boostable, however the crystal saw will not work. When built, it gives 350 Construction and Farming experience.

A set of goblin decorations can be used on the tree to make a Christmas-themed spirit tree, or a Raging echoes spirit tree scroll to make a Raging Echoes League-themed tree. Using a spade on the tree while in building mode allows the player to rotate it.

Trees can be planted without completing Tree Gnome Village, but can not be used to teleport to or from other spirit trees before completing the quest. Other players can also use the tree, provided they have completed the quest.

Protecting the sapling is not needed to build the spirit tree in the player-owned house, and it does not count towards the number of spirit trees a player may own.

The spirit tree grows immediately and may be used for travel directly after planting. Removing the spirit tree does not return the spirit sapling or seed.
30497:
The crystalline portal nexus can be built in the portal nexus space of the portal nexus in a player-owned house. It requires 92 Construction to build and gives 2,600 experience when built. The player must have a hammer and a saw in their inventory to build it, meaning it can be built at 84 construction through the use of a crystal saw and a +5 spicy stew boost.

The crystalline portal nexus can be directed to forty-one locations of a player's choosing, in which each destination directed requires 1,000 times the required runes for casting the teleport spell. Refer to the Adding a teleport page for estimated rune cost per teleport and relevant information on upgrading.

The crystalline portal nexus can be redecorated into a Raging Echoes League-themed portal nexus by using the Raging echoes nexus scroll on it.
30498:
A marble portal can be built in the Portal space of the Portal Chamber in a player-owned house . It requires 80 Construction to build and gives 1,500 experience when built. The player must have a hammer and a saw in their inventory to build it.

It can be assigned to teleport the player to various locations, such as Varrock or Falador. To do so, a payment of 100 times the required runes for casting the teleport spell is required.

Removing an old portal frame to upgrade it to a better one will not delete the teleport. The teleport will automatically be reassigned to the new frame.

The marble portal can be redecorated into a Raging Echoes League -themed portal by using the Raging echoes portal scroll on it.
30499:
A scrying pool can be built in the Centrepiece space of the Portal Chamber in a player-owned house . It requires 80 Construction to build and gives 2,000 experience when built.

The scrying pool can be used to see the areas where players' portals would take them. This excludes locations in the Wilderness , where it would instead state the amount of players within the vicinity in the chatbox.

When creating teleports, location 1 is the portal to the left of the door when walking into the portal chamber. Location 2 is directly opposite of the door. Location 3 is the portal to the right of the door when walking into the portal chamber.

Lastly, it can be redecorated into a Raging Echoes League -themed pool by using the Raging echoes scrying pool scroll on it.

Bran is a pet dropped by the Royal Titans. It is a much smaller version of Branda the Fire Queen. Players can right click "Metamorphosis" to change between Bran and Ric, a smaller version of Eldric the Ice King.

When a player receives the pet, it will automatically try to appear as their follower. At the same time, a message in the chatbox will state You have a funny feeling like you're being followed. However, if a player receives a pet while having a follower out (for example, a cat), it will be placed into their inventory. When this occurs, the message in the chatbox will instead state You feel something weird sneaking into your backpack.

If a player's inventory is full and they have a follower already, they will not receive the pet; it must instead be claimed from Probita in East Ardougne.

On death, if a player loses their pet (as a follower or in your inventory) it will wander around the area for 30 seconds before despawning. Even if the player returns in time, the pet cannot be picked up, and can be reclaimed from Probita.

30634:
The twinflame staff is a one-handed staff requiring level 60 Magic to wield. It is made by combining a battlestaff with the fire element staff crown and ice element staff crown , obtained from looting Branda the Fire Queen and Eldric the Ice King respectively. It acts as an infinite source of fire and water runes when casting spells, like the steam battlestaff .

The staff has an attack and cast speed of 6. It provides a 10% increase in accuracy and damage when casting spells from the standard spellbook , and will automatically cast the appropriate elemental spell for an NPC with a different elemental weakness than what the player is autocasting, provided that the player has the required runes and Magic level for the selected spell. For example, a player with level 75 Magic attacking a moss giant with Wind Wave will instead cast Fire Wave .

When attacking the walls during the Royal Titans fight, if a player has death runes in their inventory and is auto-casting Wave spells , the walls will be attacked using the relevant Blast spell for each type of wall, saving blood runes throughout multiple kills.

Additionally, when casting elemental spells (excluding Strike and Surge spells), the staff will fire off two spells at once ; the second hit will land one tick after the first, dealing 40% of the damage dealt by the first, rounded down. Note that the second spell does not give Magic or Hitpoints experience, nor consume runes or any additional charges from the tome of fire or its other variants.

Taking into account the slower attack speed, the additional hit, and the 10% damage bonus, the twinflame staff has an effective damage bonus of 28% for standard spellbook spells. Compared to other autocasting staves, it will typically outperform most options other than the dragon hunter wand (against dragons) and harmonised Nightmare staff until 95 Magic, when Surge spells are at their full power. Compared to powered staves , it is a stronger option for most enemies without an elemental weakness until ~80 Magic. Against opponents with an elemental weakness, it can outperform most powered staves other than the Tumeken's shadow .

The giantsoul amulet is an amulet that can be obtained as an untradeable drop from looting either Branda the Fire Queen or Eldric the Ice King . When charged, it provides teleports to the entrances of the lairs of Bryophyta , Obor , and the Royal Titans .

The amulet is charged by using one set of big bones (which can be noted) and one law rune on the amulet and can contain a maximum of 16,000 charges (costing 5,776,000 to fully charge, or 361 per teleport). Unlike similar items such as Xeric's talisman and Pendant of Ates , the giantsoul amulet cannot be uncharged to return the bones and runes.

Bryophyta's teleport is a short distance from an agility shortcut next to Vannaka , making the Giantsoul amulet useful for mid-level Slayer as well as Treasure Trails steps that require talking to Vannaka.

Should you die while fighting the titans, the amulet will always be retained as an additional inventory item, providing easy access to your gravestone just outside the tunnel entrance.

Players can get duplicate amulets, which can be exchanged with the Odd Old Man for 30 noted big bones each, worth a total of 7,050 on the Grand Exchange.

Accumulation charms are dropped by breach bosses and monsters with a combat level of at least 200 in the permanent version Deadman Mode. It must be kept in the player's inventory or looting bag for it to function.

The charm offers the following benefits:

Clue scroll drop rates, chinchompa captures, and resources from Mining, Fishing, Woodcutting, and Farming are tripled. This also triples the experience rates of these activities.

The amount of runes produced during Runecrafting are multiplied by five.

Use the Toggle option on the item to receive planks instead of logs when Woodcutting. Planks are only received outside of guarded areas; otherwise, you will continue to receive logs. Coins will be automatically removed from your inventory when receiving planks based upon the plank conversion rates at the sawmill. This rate is 50% of the normal price, but is tripled due to receiving 3 planks. For example, when receiving 3 oak planks, 375 coins will be paid instead of 750 coins. It is not possible to use sawmill vouchers in this process.

The charm synergizes well with stockpiling charm as its effect removes the need for banking that would become a problem with gathering resources at triple the speed. Items that consume charges such as bracelet of clay only use up one charge while still providing the item's effect on all three gathered resources.

When the charm is used with shark lures to fish for raw sharks, you will receive the full experience from catching two additional sharks, but the initial catch will still suffer reduced experience; the total amount of Fishing experience will be at least 1100 under the standard 5x experience rate.

The rune pouch is a special version of the rune pouch automatically given to the player during a game of Castle Wars.

This version of the pouch provides access to all existing runes, allowing players to cast specific spells on any spellbook. These spells include:

Standard spellbook: Wind Strike, Bind, Snare, Entangle, Saradomin Strike, Claws of Guthix, Flames of Zamorak, and more.

Ancient Magicks: Blood Barrage, Ice Barrage, Smoke Burst, and other PvP-relevant spells.

Lunar spellbook: Vengeance, Vengeance Other, Spellbook Swap, Humidify, and Energy Transfer.

Arceuus spellbook: Ghostly Grasp, Vile Vigour, Mark of Darkness, Skeletal Grasp, Undead Grasp, Corruption spells, and Ward of Arceuus.

Spells that require specific equipment, such as god spells, still require the equipment to be equipped. Non-PvP utility spells are restricted within Castle Wars. Demon dung is an item that may be received upon defeating Yama in a duo encounter with less than 375 damage dealt towards him. Despite appearing useless, it can be used as an alternative to ultracompost , although it is much harder to obtain, and cannot be added to a bottomless compost bucket .

30750:

30763:
The forgotten lockbox is a drop received from defeating Yama that can be opened to obtain a reward.

Each forgotten lockbox yields an average of approximately 3.23 oathplate shards and 28.54 dragon darts . When the respective reward is rolled, it yields an average of approximately 11.82 oathplate shards or 104.55 dragon darts. Based on the lockbox's drop rate of 1/33 from Yama, lockboxes account for approximately 0.098 oathplate shards and 0.865 dragon darts per Yama kill.
30765:
Oathplate shards are an uncommon drop from Yama used to create infernal nuggets, which can then be turned into oathplate armour. Nuggets can be created with level 83 Smithing by combining 5 oathplate shards with 28 crushed infernal shale.

In total, 450 oathplate shards must be combined with 2,520 crushed infernal shale to make 9 infernal plates in order to smith any individual piece of oathplate armour. Buying 450 oathplate shards costs 78,354,900 and 2,520 crushed infernal shale 1,023,120, making the full cost of smithing a piece of armour 79,378,020.

The average Yama kill will drop 0.8075 oathplate shards (including lockboxes), meaning that a player can expect to have enough shards to craft a piece of oathplate armour every 557 solo kills.

A piece of oathplate armour can be broken down at the Ancient Forge inside the Ancient Prison in the God Wars Dungeon for 50 oathplate shards.
30767: Baby umbral coral was an item in the Sailing alpha game files. It seems to have been intended to be planted in a coral patch to grow umbral coral at level 75 Farming . In the beta it was removed and umbral frags were added, likely as a replacement.
30771:
Aether catalysts are an item dropped by Yama , The Leviathan , the Abyssal Sire and the Doom of Mokhaiotl , which are used to create aether runes , a combination of cosmic and soul runes .

Crafting aether runes requires level 90 Runecraft . As the true Soul Altar and soul talisman are not accessible to the player, the Cosmic Altar , soul runes , and the Magic Imbue spell must be used.

One aether catalyst is required for each aether rune crafted; this means that using Raiments of the Eye and scarred extracts to increase the yield of aether runes will still require one catalyst per rune.
30773:
Diabolic worms are a fishing enhancer item, which are a superior alternative to sandworms for fishing raw anglerfish. They are dropped by Yama.

Using diabolic worms as bait will increase the skilling success rate of catching anglerfish; upon its consumption, the player's next 'catch' roll has a 50% chance to occur a tick faster. However, these benefits come at a cost of reducing the experience gained per anglerfish from 120 to 79.2.

At level 99 Fishing, your chance of a successful anglerfish catch increases from 14% up to 40%.

Diabolic worms can be stored inside a tackle box.
30775:

They can be obtained from defeating Yama and by opening dossiers . On average, Yama drops one teleport scroll approximately every 2.91 kills, including via dossiers.

There are no requirements to use this teleport.

Upon creating a piece of radiant oathplate armour, a chatbox message appears stating " The sigil violently draws power from the runes, sending a burst of blue flame out and peeling back the old darkened metal. "
30795: A barrel of demonic tallow is an uncommon drop from Yama that can be emptied to receive 100 demonic tallow , an ingredient for surge potions . Partially emptying it converts it into a partially empty barrel that cannot be traded.
30798: A barrel of demonic tallow is an uncommon drop from Yama that can be emptied to receive 100 demonic tallow , an ingredient for surge potions . Partially emptying it converts it into a partially empty barrel that cannot be traded.

30803: Dossiers are a drop from Yama . They can be opened to obtain a contract , chasm teleport scrolls , or a rite of vile transference . The Rite of Vile Transference is guaranteed from the first Dossier opened with at least 100 Yama kill count.
30806:
The rite of vile transference is a scroll which when read will permanently upgrade the Death Charge spell to restore special attack energy from two targets per cast instead of one.

The rite is obtained as a drop from Yama himself through opening dossiers . Players have a 1/15 chance of obtaining the rite when opening a dossier; as the dossier is a 1/12.1 drop, this effectively makes the overall rate around 1/181.5 assuming a solo kill, as the dossier drop rate scales with contribution.

Additionally, the rite possesses a bad luck mitigation mechanic where the first dossier the player opens after reaching 100 Yama victories will guarantee the rite as loot. As the dossier can be deposited into the bank, wary players can opt to hold off on opening a dossier until they reach 100 victories.
30808:
Jim's wet cloth is an item obtainable from Jim the imp on the lower floor of the Chasm of Fire in the infernal shale resource area. Using the wipe option of the cloth will start an animation where the character wipes their forehead with the cloth.

By using a specific tick manipulation rhythm (as shown in the video to the left/above), infernal shale rocks can be mined much more efficiently. The character will wipe their forehead then mine the rock after a 1 tick (0.6s) delay as indicated by a different mining animation. An example of the rhythm would be:

1st tick: click cloth,

2nd tick: move to rock,

3rd tick: click rock.

If while attempting to perform tick manipulation, the player clicks on the rock too soon, the player will receive the message You can't swing a pickaxe whilst wiping your forehead!

When leaving the infernal shale resource area, the cloth will disappear with a message stating The imp takes back his cloth, as per your contract.
30810:
Contract of glyphic attenuation is a contract used to challenge Yama to a more difficult fight for the bottom piece of the purifying sigil . It can be dropped by Yama himself through opening dossiers , or via black , greater , and lesser demons in the Chasm of Fire after the player has agreed to Yama's terms by speaking to him after A Kingdom Divided .

To obtain this contract from the demons in the Chasm of Fire, the final blow must come from special attacks . The drop rate will 5x while the yellow sigil is active above their heads. Players can speak to the Disciple of Yama outside the chasm to learn about which sigil is currently active.

The contract is consumed upon starting the fight, although if successful the challenger will receive the contract again as a drop. Yama will not drop standard loot upon completion of this contract.

30842: Tortugan vessel is an item in the Sailing alpha .
30843:
Aether runes are combination runes that count as two separate runes: one cosmic rune and one soul rune . Thus, any spell requiring one cosmic rune, one soul rune, or both will spend only one aether rune.

Aether runes can be used to cast Death Charge , Dark Demonbane , and summon thralls with just four runes (aether, blood , death , and fire runes ), meaning the divine rune pouch can hold all runes required for these three spells.

Aether runes are also required to create radiant oathplate armour : 2,500 runes are consumed for each armour piece converted, requiring a total of 7,500 aether runes to create a full set of radiant oathplate armour.

They can be created with level 90 Runecraft using an aether catalyst .

Compared to using soul and cosmic runes separately, using a single aether rune costs 269 more.
30844: Tortugan sacred vessel is an item in the Sailing alpha .
30846:
Infernal shale is an ore that can be mined in the Chasm of Fire with level 78 Mining , granting between 13.2 and 100 experience. It can be crushed into crushed infernal shale with a hammer and a chisel, which is necessary for the creation of oathplate armour .

The shale can be acquired by three different mining methods:

Each infernal shale can be crushed into 1–3 crushed infernal shale. When crushing them, it is recommended to do so with 9 or fewer shale in the inventory – in this case, the expected yield from each shale is 1.7 crushed shale, but with 10 or more in the inventory, the expected yield is only 1.4 crushed shale.

Crushing the shale provides no experience, and it will not automatically process, so each infernal shale must be individually clicked. Repeatedly using a chisel on the very last shale in the inventory is the easiest way to process infernal shale.

The Imcando hammer is an acceptable kind of hammer while equipped or in the inventory.
30848:
Crushed infernal shale is made by crushing infernal shale with a hammer and chisel, and is used to create infernal nuggets, which can then be turned into oathplate armour. Nuggets can be created with level 83 Smithing by combining 28 crushed infernal shale with 5 oathplate shards.

In total, 2,520 crushed infernal shale must be combined with 450 oathplate shards to make 9 infernal plates in order to smith any individual piece of oathplate armour.

Crushing the shale provides no experience, and it will not automatically process, so each infernal shale must be individually clicked. Repeatedly using a chisel on the very last shale in the inventory is the easiest way to process infernal shale.

The Imcando hammer is an acceptable kind of hammer while equipped or in the inventory.
30854:
An infernal blend is an item used in the process of creating infernal plates . They can be created with level 83 Smithing by combining 28 crushed infernal shale with 5 oathplate shards using the furnace located in the mining area on the lower level of the Chasm of Fire .

The blend must be quenched in the nearby pool of ichor in order to turn it into an infernal nugget , although it is possible for the blend to become malformed if the player takes the blend out too early. Players can only have one infernal blend in their inventory at a time, attempting to make a second blend while already carrying one gives the message You should quench your infernal blend first. .
30856:
A malformed infernal blend is the result of making a mistake during the quenching process of creating infernal nuggets , either by retrieving the item too quickly or stepping away when the item finishes. The message You withdraw the infernal blend too early, it looks malformed. appears if the player retrieves it too quickly, while the message The ichor bubbles over and spits out your malformed infernal blend. appears if the player is not standing next to the pool of ichor.

Putting the malformed blend back into the furnace reverts it to an infernal blend , allowing the user to retry the quenching process.
30858:
Infernal nuggets are used to create infernal plates , which can then be turned into oathplate armour . They are created with level 83 Smithing by combining 28 crushed infernal shale with 5 oathplate shards using the furnace located in the mining area on the lower level of the Chasm of Fire . 10 infernal nuggets are required per infernal plate.

In total, 2,520 crushed infernal shale must be combined with 450 oathplate shards to make 9 infernal plates in order to smith any individual piece of oathplate armour .
30860:
A cooled infernal chunk is a piece of infernal chunk that cools upon leaving the mining area on the lower level of the Chasm of Fire .

Putting the cooled chunk back into the furnace heats it back to normal, allowing the user to resume the process of creating an infernal plate .
30861: Cursed gold keel parts is an item in the Sailing alpha .
30862:

30864:

30887:
Polycatalytic guardian stones are items used to power-up the Great Guardian during a game of Guardians of the Rift , alongside elemental , polyelemental , and catalytic guardian stones.

They are obtained by crafting combination runes when imbuing guardian essence at a catalytic runic altar , accessible directly by entering an active Portal Guardian.

Players are granted 5 Runecraft experience and 3 catalytic energy (instead of the normal 2) per polycatalytic guardian stone used to power-up the Great Guardian.

Currently, only Aether runes give Polycatalytic Energy.
30888:
Yami is a pet dropped by Yama. It is a much smaller version of him.

When a player receives the pet, it will automatically try to appear as their follower; Unlike other pets, Yami will initially spawn in front of Yama's throne with a cloud of smoke similar to those of imps, saying Oh no. At the same time, a message in the chatbox will state You have a funny feeling like you're being followed. However, if a player receives a pet while having a follower out (for example, a cat), it will be placed into their inventory. When this occurs, the message in the chatbox will instead state You feel something weird sneaking into your backpack.

If a player's inventory is full and they have a follower already, they will not receive the pet; it must instead be claimed from Probita in East Ardougne.

On death, if a player loses their pet (as a follower or in your inventory) it will wander around the area for 30 seconds before despawning. Even if the player returns in time, the pet cannot be picked up, and can be reclaimed from Probita.
30890: The rotten turnip is an item similar to the rotten potato that is used to assist with developing plugins. It is not currently accessible and is only known to exist in the cache .
30891:
The keris partisan of Amascut is a one-handed spear requiring Attack level 80 to wield. It is created by combining a jewel of Amascut with a keris partisan. The upgrade greatly enhances the weapon's stats when used inside the Tombs of Amascut. If fighting kalphites or scabarites, this variant has a damage bonus of 15%, down from the base weapon's 33%. It retains the 1/51 chance to deal triple damage against these targets, however.

The upgrade increases the stab bonus and strength bonus to +108 and +67, respectively (up from +58 and +45). This combination makes the weapon more suitable for general use in the raid, allowing it to be effective against a wide array of enemies. This makes it a possible choice for a primary weapon, with its effectiveness surpassing the Zamorakian hasta for this purpose. The Keris partisan of Amascut is particularly useful for players who have not yet obtained Osmumten's fang, including Ironmen. It isn't ideal for higher invocations, however.

As with other variants, weapon poisons cannot be applied to the keris partisan of Amascut.
30893:
The jewel of Amascut is an untradeable jewel that can be obtained as a reward from the Tombs of Amascut.

The jewel can be attached to the keris partisan to create the keris partisan of Amascut, which has increased stats and a passive effect when used within the Tombs of Amascut. Outside the Tombs of Amascut it functions as a keris partisan.
30895:
The steel ring is an item dropped by the deranged archaeologist . It has no requirements to equip and is the best-in-slot melee defensive ring, surpassing the ring of suffering (i) . However, it has no Magic defence, Ranged defence, or Prayer bonuses.

It may be a more useful option for players who cannot afford a ring of suffering, or require better melee tanking equipment for encounters where they won't be attacked with other styles like the Moons of Peril . Other rings that provide offensive bonuses will usually perform better, but the steel ring can be useful for earlier in account progression, as the deranged archaeologist has very low requirements to defeat.

Unlike gold rings , it cannot be made with the Crafting skill using a ring mould at a furnace .
30898:
Giant bones are a larger variant of big bones dropped by Obor and Bryophyta on members worlds. Unlike most items, which only have a "Take" option on the ground, the item additionally has a "Bury" option, which when selected prompts a confirmation message whether the player wishes to receive 150 Prayer experience and can be permanently disabled by selecting "Yes, don't ask me again". This confirmation message is shared with bull bones, and toggling it off for one of the bones toggles it off for both.

Selecting the "Take" option results in a game message in the chatbox stating I don't think those will fit in my backpack..., nor can Telekinetic Grab be cast on it. The bonecrusher will still automatically bury them, however.

The experience boost provided by chewed bones does not apply to giant bones.

As they cannot be picked up, they cannot be used for alternative Prayer training methods, such as the gilded altar or the deep Wilderness chaos altar.
30900:
Shark lures are a fishing enhancer item, which is used as bait to improve the success rate of catching raw sharks. The configured amount of lures will always be consumed per raw shark caught. Shark lures can be stored inside a tackle box.

Shark lures can be used at 1, 3, or 5 at a time for further improved rates per lure, with diminishing experience per lure used at a time. When the effect of this item is combined with the accumulation charm in Deadman Mode, however, the additional experience from receiving two extra raw sharks is not reduced.

It is dropped from certain bosses and chests that drop large quantities of food, a portion of which was replaced with shark lure drops.

Using shark lures decreases the drop rate of the Heron pet, making it rarer.

Their increased catching speed makes fishing with them one of the best methods of obtaining moon key loop halves and the big shark.

30950: The canvas piece is an item obtained during The Final Dawn , in which players must find a key inside the drawers within Augur Metzli's chambers to unlock the chest that holds the canvas piece. 30951: A key is obtained during The Final Dawn by searching the drawers in backroom of the Twilight Temple basement, past the Emissary Enforcer. This key is used to unlock the nearby drawer that contains a canvas piece.
30952:
Stone tablets are items obtained during The Final Dawn , found in Mokhaiotl after defeating Augur Metzli . Both tablets, like the stone tablet found in Tapoyauik , were written by human refugees assisting the Old Ones in preserving their knowledge and history before their extinction.

The first tablet is found by searching the skeleton downstairs immediately west from where players defeat Metzli, depicting the process in creating the moon puzzle.

The second one is found by searching the skeleton by the entrance leading to the Doom of Mokhaiotl 's den, which can only be searched after Prince Itzla and Furia's departure, revealing that Mokhaiotl was destroyed by something during its construction. Based on available context, Tapoyauik appears to have been constructed before Mokhaiotl's destruction.
30953:
A stone tablet can be found in Mokhaiotl , via searching a skeleton opposite the scoreboard just before the gap leading to the Doom of Mokhaiotl .

Reading it reveals a list of players who presumably helped playtest the boss.

30955:
The Arkan blade is a one-handed melee weapon requiring 60 Attack to wield. Belonging to Prince Itzla's grandfather, [ 1 ] it is obtained from him as a reward for completing The Final Dawn .

It has 64 strength bonus, comparable in strength to the dragon scimitar 's 66, but with a slightly raised slash bonus of 70 compared to 67, and a vastly higher stab bonus of 55 compared to 8.

If lost, the blade can be reclaimed from Prince Itzla at the Sunrise Palace for 250,000 coins . It is currently not possible to obtain multiple blades, as any dropped blades are deleted upon repurchasing, despite losing the coins. If lost in a PvP death, it is converted into 250,000 coins for the killer.
30957: Earthbound tecpatl are a two-handed stab sword that require level 55 Attack to wield, obtained as a rare drop from earthen nagua in the Tonali Cavern. Like their crush and slash equivalents, the glacial temotli and sulphur blades, it performs two independently rolled hits per attack. The maximum damage of each hit is determined by calculating the combined max hit as normal and dividing it by two. If the combined max hit is odd, one max hit is rounded up while the other is rounded down (e.g., 45 → 22 + 23). As a multi-hit weapon, it is especially useful against monsters that have negative flat armour, such as Nagua, since all successful hits will do an extra damage to them.
30960:
The antique lamp is a reward from The Final Dawn quest. The lamp grants 55,000 experience to any combat skill, including Prayer. You must have at least level 40 in the skill you wish to gain experience in.

The lamp cannot be banked. However, if the player prefers to use it at a later date, it can be destroyed and reclaimed from Prince Itzla whenever the player wishes to do so.
30961: A keystone fragment is an item given to the player by Eyatlalli during The Final Dawn . It acts as a connection to the prototype version of the icosahedron found in a hidden room within Neypotzli , in which the player uses it as a guide to locate its entrance.
30962: Kuhu essence are runestones obtained within the ruins beneath the Crypt of Tonali during The Final Dawn , found by searching urns around the sun puzzle room area. They are used to imbue the altars to complete the puzzle.
30963: Ancient roots are obtained during The Final Dawn inside the moon puzzle room in the ruins beneath the Crypt of Tonali. They are chopped from the roots found in the room using a knife blade and can be cut into root kindling, used to complete the puzzle.
30964:
Root kindling is an item obtained during The Final Dawn , being the result of cutting ancient roots with a knife blade .

They are used in the moon puzzle room within the ruins beneath the Crypt of Tonali , being offered to the moon statue; the correct amounts must be offered in order to complete the puzzle, which are based on the total number of lit braziers.
30965: A knife blade is obtained within the ruins beneath the Crypt of Tonali during The Final Dawn, found by searching old tools in the moon puzzle room area. They are used to obtain ancient roots and cutting them into root kindling, which are used to complete the puzzle.
30966:
Ancient teleporters are items that can be found by searching the chest right next to the lift platform between the Crypt of Tonali and the Ruins of Mokhaiotl after completion of The Final Dawn .

The two teleporters can be placed anywhere in the area, even between floors, as long as they are placed within 30 tiles of each other. Once a pair has been placed, the Tonali Teleporters can be used to transport players to the other instantly. Should players wish to relocate the teleporters, they may simply pick one up and right-click "Recall" to obtain the other.

The teleporters are useful in speeding up travel to Ruins of Mokhaiotl by placing one teleporter on the tile where players arrive via lift platform, and another further north. It can also be used for quicker access to specific areas of the cavern; for example, to the central area where multiple earthen nagua and moonlight moths are found together.
30967: A large egg is an item obtained during the quest Scrambled! as a possible replacement for Humphrey Dumphrey . It is rejected by King's men, due to it being too small compared to the original Humphrey Dumphrey.
30968: A dragon egg is an item obtained during the quest Scrambled! as a possible replacement for Humphrey Dumphrey . It is rejected by King's men due to its innate heat, which causes the paint on the egg to melt.
30969: Jaguar egg is an item obtained during the quest Scrambled! as a possible replacement for Humphrey Dumphrey. It is received from the pile of eggs east of Tal Teklan. It is chosen as the replacement, though it, the large egg, and the dragon egg all fall off of the wall and break, forcing the player to reassemble the remains of the original Humphrey Dumphrey.
30970:
Humphrey Dumphrey is a fragile egg of unknown parentage, though most closely resembling a jaguar egg , and the best friend of Alan . In the Scrambled! quest, the player is tasked with babysitting Humphrey while Alan is away preparing a feast. After the quest, he can be obtained as a pet by talking to him at Tal Teok .

Humphrey goes by many aliases, and every character seems to know him by a different name. After the quest, however, the player may choose to collect him at which point he identifies himself simply as "Egg."

Egg can be interacted with, though conversations with him tend to be one-sided, perhaps due to his shy nature and reluctance to come out of his shell. Egg generally maintains a sunny disposition, smiling at all times, but seems to grimace when spoken to.

He may also be held carefully in both hands. The player runs with a unique animation when wielding him, apparently taking extra precautions not to drop him, though he also functions as a crush weapon with the player raising him up and smashing him down on their enemies.

Egg will happily live in the cat basket or menagerie of a player-owned house . When dropped inside a house, he will responsibly stay in his spot, patiently waiting for the player to come back.
30973:
Alan's bones are the remains of what was once Alan the tourist, which are obtainable after the completion of the Scrambled! quest.

There are a number of unique interactions with Alan's bones:

Can be blessed at the exposed altar to turn them into Alan's blessed bones

Can be given to Rosie at the South Falador farm, Floki north of Land's End, Molossus, Lola, and Xolo in Varlamore, or stray dogs in Varrock. Doing so yields the chat messages You give the dog Alan's bones. followed by It happily gnaws on them, but something feels wrong about all of this.

Can be used to distract the dog in The Final Dawn. Doing so yields the message "The dog takes Alan's bones. Something doesn't feel quite right about this, but the dog seems happy enough. He quickly calms down and gives your hand a little lick."

Can be crushed using the bone grinder into Alan's bonemeal.

Should the player be in possession of the Bonecrusher or its necklace variant at the time of quest completion, the bones will be automatically buried; It is important to make sure neither of these items are on their person as Alan dies, should the player desire to keep them.
30975:
Alan's bonemeal is made using Alan's bones after completing the quest, Scrambled!, with the bone grinder at the Ectofuntus.

It can be used to worship Ectofuntus alongside a bucket of slime to claim 5 ecto-tokens.
30977: Damiana leaves can be picked from damiana shrubs south east of Tal Teklan . They can be added to a bowl of water to create damiana water , which when boiled creates damiana tea .
30979: Damiana water is created by adding damiana leaves to a Bowl of water . It can be boiled at a fire or range in order to create damiana tea , or drunk as-is to restore 1 Hitpoint.
30981:
Damiana tea is tea made of damiana leaves . It can be created by boiling damiana water at a fire or range. Drinking damiana tea, either from a bowl or cup, restores 4 hitpoints and 6 run energy .

A bowl of damiana tea can be transferred to an empty cup to create a cup of damiana tea . It can also be used with a bucket of milk to get milky damiana tea .

This particular kind of tea cannot be added to a tea flask and cannot be given to the Panning guide during The Dig Site quest.
30983:
Milky damiana tea is created by using a bucket of milk on a bowl of damiana tea . Drinking damiana tea, either from the bowl or from the cup, restores 4 hitpoints and 6 run energy.

This particular kind of tea cannot be added to a tea flask and cannot be given to the Panning guide during The Dig Site quest.
30985:
A cup of damiana tea can be created by using a bowl of damiana tea on an empty cup. Drinking damiana tea restores 4 hitpoints and 6 run energy.

This particular kind of tea cannot be added to a tea flask and cannot be used in place of a regular cup of tea for the Panning guide during The Dig Site quest.
30986: Portable weather station (rusty) was an item in the Sailing alpha . By using anti-rust tonic it was changed into the Portable weather station .
30987:
A cup of milky damiana tea is the result of using a bucket of milk on a cup of damiana tea. Drinking milky damiana tea restores 4 hitpoints and 6 run energy.

This particular kind of tea cannot be added to a tea flask and cannot be used in place of a regular cup of tea for the Panning guide during The Dig Site quest.
30989: Acatzin's axe is an axe belonging to Acatzin, given to the player by the blacksmith in Tal Teklan as part of the Scrambled! quest. It is initially broken, but the player repairs it on the blacksmith's whetstone.
30990: Acatzin's axe is an axe belonging to Acatzin, given to the player by the blacksmith in Tal Teklan as part of the Scrambled! quest. It is initially broken, but the player repairs it on the blacksmith's whetstone.
30998: Atlatl dart tips are used in fletching Atlatl darts . They are made by using a chisel on broken antlers , which are dropped by Custodian stalkers , yielding 100 dart tips per antler.
30999: Premium fish offcuts were an item in the March 2025 Sailing Alpha and June 2025 Sailing Beta . They were created by using a knife on raw bluefin and raw marlin , and could be used to bait shoals of fish while deep sea trawling . Players or crewmates could prepare them at an advanced chum station facility on a boat , and spread them into the sea. They could also be used to bait crab traps .

31010: Headless atlatl darts are used in Fletching atlatl darts . Attaching atlatl dart tips (obtained by breaking down broken antlers with a chisel) to headless atlatl darts requires 74 Fletching and grants 20 experience.
31016:
Sacraments of Ent Folk is a book that players can receive from Ranulph in Auburnvale upon completion of the miniquest Vale Totems .

If lost, it can also be retrieved from a bookcase in a player-owned house .
31018:
An ent seed is a rare item that can be obtained while chopping certain types of trees throughout Varlamore , including in Auburn Valley , the Tlati Rainforest , Aldarin , the Avium Savannah , and the Custodia Mountains . The types of trees that may yield a seed are oak , willow , maple , teak , mahogany , yew , magic , and trees planted in the Locus Oasis hardwood tree patch . Regular and dead trees do not provide ent seeds.

Ent seeds can be exchanged for a bird nest by using them on ents in Auburn Valley. Players can receive a ring nest , bird's egg nest , seed nest , or clue nest (which is replaced with an empty nest and scroll box if X Marks the Spot has been completed).

Ent seeds cannot be stored in a seed box , the seed vault , or be used to bait bird houses .
31024:
The greenman carving is an item created with a greenman mask , five ent branches , and one set of yew logs It requires 79 Fletching to produce, granting 70 Fletching experience.

It is used to build a greenman carving in either a dining room , combat room , or throne room in a player-owned house . Removing a built carving will return it to the player's inventory.
31027:
The greenman statue is an item created with a greenman mask , five ent branches , and one set of maple logs . It requires 53 Fletching to produce, granting 55 Fletching experience.

It is used to build a greenman statue in either a normal garden or formal garden in a player-owned house . Removing a built statue will return it to the player's inventory.
31030:
The greenman carving can be built in the decoration space of a dining room , combat room , or throne room in a player-owned house . It has no requirements to build, nor does it give any experience. The player must have a hammer and a saw in their inventory to build it.

If the furniture is removed, players will receive their greenman carving back, allowing them to sell it if they so wish.
31031:
The greenman statue can be built in a garden or formal garden in a player-owned house . It has no requirements to build, nor does it give any experience. The player must have a hammer and a saw in their inventory to build it.

Within the garden , it can be built in the centrepiece space , Big Plant space 1 , and Big Plant space 2 hotspots. Within the formal garden , it can only be built in the centrepiece space.

If the furniture is removed, players will receive their greenman statue back, allowing them to sell it if they so wish.
31032:
An ent branch is an item received from the Vale Totems minigame , which can be obtained as common loot from rummaging through Vale offerings , or bought directly from Vale Research Exchange for 20 research points .

Ent branches are primarily used to fletch atlatl dart shafts , yielding 100 shafts per branch. When using the "Make-all" option to fletch them into dart shafts, it will fletch 28 branches at a time. They are also used to create a greenman statue or greenman carving to place in a player-owned house .
31033:
Raw gracefish was an item in the Sailing alpha.

31034:
The greenman mask is a cosmetic reward from the Vale Totems minigame , which can be obtained from rummaging through Vale offerings at a rate of 1/500, or bought directly from Vale Research Exchange for 500 research points . Ironmen (including group ironmen , despite them being able to trade the mask with fellow group members) with spare masks can trade them in to Ranulph for 125 Vale research points.

Its style can be changed to match various logs by using 300 of their corresponding tree leaves on it. This grants 20 Fletching experience and permanently unlocks that style, allowing players to freely switch between appearances on any mask item once unlocked.

The greenman mask can also be used to create a greenman statue and greenman carving to place in a player-owned house .

This item can be stored in the magic wardrobe of a costume room .

The fletching knife is an equippable version of a knife obtained as reward from the Vale Totems minigame. It can be found at a rate of 1/333.3 while rummaging through Vale offerings or purchased from Ranulph's Vale Research Exchange for 350 research points. Spare fletching knives can be exchanged for 175 Vale research points.

The fletching knife reduces the time to complete various Fletching actions by 1 tick for all but the first item being fletched. For example, fletching unstrung bows becomes a 2-tick action instead of a 3-tick action, meaning that approximately 2,700 bows can be fletched per hour instead of 1,800. This effect is active whether it is in the inventory or equipped in the off-hand slot, though the wielder will still need a knife in their inventory to use on logs to initiate the cutting.

It can also perform all the functions of a regular knife such as cutting food items, slashing webs, and setting up Hunter traps (including while equipped). Due to the first item being cut with the normal speed, the fletching knife cannot be used to speed up tick manipulation.

This item can be stored in the magic wardrobe of a costume room.
31045:
A bale of flax is an item received from the Vale Totems minigame, which can be obtained as common loot from rummaging through vale offerings. Unpacking a bale of flax yields 25 unnoted flax. With the bank interface opened, players can unpack all bales of flax in their inventory directly to the bank.

Unpacking a bale of flax will display the message You unpack a bale of flax.. Unpacking a bale of flax to the player inventory yields 25 unnoted flax. If the player has less than 25 empty inventory spaces, the message You need at least 25 empty space to unpack the flax. will be displayed instead.

This item can be used to very quickly spin flax when used in combination with the bow string spool, either at a spinning wheel or with the Spin Flax spell. Assuming a fully upgraded spool, roughly 40 bowstrings per minute can be spun if using the Seers' Village spinning wheel with the medium Kandarin Diary completed. If doing an activity that does not require any inventory spaces, such as Rooftop Agility Courses, bales of flax can be used to train Crafting and Magic while training, by bringing a rune pouch with runes for Spin Flax and the bow string spool.
31047: Dirty arrowtips are a possible reward from rummaging through vale offerings which are obtained from the Vale Totems minigame. Cleaning dirty arrowtips consumes 50 of them at a time and yields arrowtips ranging from steel to dragon (excluding amethyst).
31049: A redwood hiking staff is a one-handed crush weapon made from a knife and one set of redwood logs . Despite the fact that it is a staff, the redwood hiking staff has no magical ability and cannot autocast any spells. Its primary use is to be used as a totem decoration during the Vale Totems minigame .
31052:
The bow string spool is a reward from the Vale Totems minigame , which can be obtained from rummaging through Vale offerings at a rate of 1/200, or bought directly from Vale Research Exchange for 250 research points . Spare spools can be combined to increase the capacity of the spool, or they can be traded in to Ranulph for 125 Vale research points.

The spool, when added with bow strings , can be used on an unfinished bow to string them, allowing the player to string 27 bows per inventory rather than 14. Additionally, it will automatically fill up with bow strings as they get spun from flax, providing the spool has not reached its maximum capacity.

The amount of string stored on the spool is tied to the player's account rather than the individual item, so even if the item is lost the charges are not.

Unlike the fletching knife , it cannot be stored in the costume room of a player-owned house .

31081:
The antler guard is a tribrid shield slot item dropped by mature and elder custodian stalkers .

Requiring only level 50 Prayer to wield, its melee bonuses sit between an adamant and rune defender , ranged bonus between an unholy book and book of law , and magic bonus between that of an elemental tome and book of darkness . It shares the same strength bonus as a rune defender. Additionally, it has +2 ranged strength bonus and +5 prayer bonus. However, the main drawback of the guard is that it penalises all defence bonuses, so it is only recommended when players are not expected to be hit often.
31084: Alchemist's signet is a drop from elder custodian stalkers that can be used to open the chest next to the staircase downstairs in the Alchemical Society 's headquarters, where the Mastering Mixology minigame is played. 60 Herblore [ not boostable ] is required to gain access to the basement. The chest contains a variety of useful Herblore supplies, including herbs , herb seeds , and secondaries . The signet is consumed once the chest is opened.

Avernic treads are boots that require level 80 in Defence, Strength, Ranged, and Magic to wear. They are dropped in their base form by the Doom of Mokhaiotl, and can be upgraded into stronger variants.

In their base form, the treads already surpass each of the primordial, eternal, and pegasian boots in accuracy and most defensive bonuses as well as providing a ranged strength bonus. However, they have slightly less strength bonus than the primordial boots and no prayer bonus compared to aranea boots.

The treads can be upgraded by adding a pair of primordial, eternal, and pegasian boots onto them. Each pair is added separately, and 4,000 demon tears are required per pair, for a total of 12,000 demon tears.

Avernic treads (max) are boots that require level 80 in Defence, Strength, Ranged, and Magic to wear. They are made by combining the base avernic treads with the primordial, eternal, and pegasian boots, as well as 12,000 demon tears.

The max version of the avernic treads offers the highest offensive bonuses of any boots for all 3 combat styles, but they lack any prayer bonus and have lower physical defence bonuses than the guardian and echo boots.

31106:
The confliction gauntlets are an upgraded variant of the tormented bracelet requiring level 90 Hitpoints to wear, providing best-in-slot magic attack and magic damage bonuses. They are made with level 83 Crafting and level 70 Smithing by attaching the Mokhaiotl cloth , a rare untradeable drop from the Doom of Mokhaiotl , to a tormented bracelet alongside 10,000 demon tears . This process must be done at a bank and is not reversible.

Compared to the tormented bracelet , the gauntlets gain +10 magic attack bonus, some defensive bonuses and a +2% magic damage bonus, alongside a passive effect with one-handed magic weapons.
31109:

31111:
Demon tears are items used to charge the Eye of Ayak as an alternative to runes, or as part of the materials required to create the avernic treads and confliction gauntlets .

They are primarily obtained as drops from the Doom of Mokhaiotl . Alternatively, they can also be obtained by chopping infected roots in the Ruins of Mokhaiotl with 80 Woodcutting , providing a non-combat method of acquisition similar to that of Zulrah's scales from sacred eels . The Eye of Ayak can also be dismantled for 10,000 demon tears.

It takes 22,000 demon tears to fully upgrade both the Avernic treads (12,000 tears), including its base components, and craft the Confliction gauntlets (10,000 tears).
31113:
The Eye of Ayak is a one-handed powered staff that requires level 83 Magic to wield. It is a drop from the Doom of Mokhaiotl upon completion of delve level 3 and higher. Like most powered staves, it is only tradeable when it is fully uncharged.

It is the second strongest powered staff, placing it between the Sanguinesti staff and Tumeken's shadow in power. The maximum damage per hit is comparatively low, but it has the fastest attack speed of all powered staves, firing at a rate of 3 ticks (1.8 seconds) compared to the other staves' 4 or 5-tick speed.

The Eye of Ayak can be dismantled for 10,000 demon tears, resulting in a loss of −38,165,578 coins.

The Eye of Ayak cannot be used in Castle Wars, Clan Wars, TzHaar Fight Pit, and Soul Wars, despite all other powered staves being usable against players in those areas.

The Eye of Ayak does not lose charges on death in the Wilderness if the item is protected, even if the death occurs past level 20 Wilderness.

The orange is a cosmetic wearable (but still edible) variant of the normal fruit . It heals 2 hitpoints when eaten, though there is a warning dialogue before the player can eat it.

The orange can be obtained by performing the sit emote on the tile west or east of a picnic that can be found in the south-western Tlati Rainforest , in between a pygmy hippo calf and a capybara , next to a lake. When the player sits next to the picnic without the orange in their inventory or bank, the message The capybara uses its nose to roll an orange towards you. appears in the chat box, and an orange is added to their inventory.

Curiously, the orange has no drop or destroy option on the item itself, presumably having the option to eat it taking the place of one of those. Attempting to eat or slice the orange will give the player a confirmation message. If consumed, the orange can be re-obtained from the friendly capybara by performing the emote in the correct location again.

This item requires 43 Agility to obtain, to climb an agility shortcut to reach the lake. It is lost on death .

This item can be stored in the magic wardrobe of a costume room .

31123:
The purple token can be obtained by completing a specific task in Varlamore centred around the capybara and pygmy hippo calf picnic located south-west of Kastori. According to Cobado, this token, alongside the seven red tokens and four nasty tokens, were hidden by the capybaras of Varlamore as a test to see how far someone would go in collecting them all.

If a player performs a Jig at the picnic, the animals will judge the player's dance moves depending on four conditions:

If all four conditions are met, the capybara will give the player the purple token. The purple token can be taken to Cobado while wearing an orange as a hat along with all 7 red tokens and all 4 nasty tokens to receive a blueberry muffin and 100,000 coins. If the player has the purple token, but not the rest of the tokens, Cobado will give the player 1 coin and tells them to find the rest if they have not yet received the blueberry muffin.

31130:
Dom is a pet dropped by the Doom of Mokhaiotl, and is a much smaller version of it. Dom can only be dropped upon completion of delve level of 6 or higher.

The first Dom players receive will cause the burrow hole to glow; subsequent Doms will not do so, even if the player loses it.

When a player receives the pet, it will automatically try to appear as their follower. At the same time, a message in the chatbox will state You have a funny feeling like you're being followed. However, if a player receives a pet while having a follower out (for example, a cat), it will be placed into their inventory. When this occurs, the message in the chatbox will instead state You feel something weird sneaking into your backpack. If the player is in a clan, the clan broadcast states [Player name] has a funny feeling like [he's/she's/they're] being followed: Dom at (number) levels. The total number of levels completed is tracked rather than kill count like most other boss pets.

If a player's inventory is full and they have a follower already, they will not receive the pet; it must instead be claimed from Probita in East Ardougne.

On death, if a player loses their pet (as a follower or in your inventory) it will wander around the area for 30 seconds before despawning. Even if the player returns in time, the pet cannot be picked up, and can be reclaimed from Probita.

A strange sound is heard when you obtain the beaver while Woodcutting. The chances of getting it are dependent on the player's Woodcutting level, and the time it takes to gather a resource.

When a player receives the pet, it will automatically try to appear as their follower. At the same time, a message in the chatbox will state You have a funny feeling like you're being followed. However, if a player receives a pet while having a follower out (for example, a cat), it will be placed into their inventory. When this occurs, the message in the chatbox will instead state You feel something weird sneaking into your backpack. This message also occurs if there is one last inventory space while the player already has a pet following them, in which case the pet will appear in the inventory instead and the resource dropped to the ground.

On death, if a player loses their pet (as a follower or in your inventory) it will wander around for 30 seconds before disappearing completely. It can then be reclaimed from Probita in East Ardougne for no cost.

A Grid Master Icon can be built in the Icon space of the Chapel in a player-owned house. It requires 45 Construction to build and gives 180 experience when built. The player must have a hammer and a saw in their inventory to build it.

Building this icon creates the Icon of the Flames of Lloigh-enn, representing Flames of Lloigh-enn which are primarily featured on the login screen of Old School RuneScape.

The spooky chair is a reward from the 2025 Halloween event . It acts as a pet when dropped and will return to the inventory after 20 ticks (12s). It can be added to the menagerie in a player-owned house . As it is considered an extra rather than a pet, it counts towards the cap of 12 extras which can be stored in the menagerie at once.

Upon returning to the inventory, a message shows: The spooky chair makes its way back to you. . If the player has no inventory space, the chair will disappear, and instead a message shows: The spooky chair doesn't feel wanted and returns to Diango in Draynor Village. . If the player enters an area where followers are not allowed, the chair will disappear and a message shows: The spooky chair doesn't like this area and returns to Diango in Draynor Village. . Attempting to drop or spin the chair before completing the event gives this message: You shouldn't play with the chair yet. Fred needs it! .

If destroyed, a replacement can be obtained from Diango in Draynor Village or from the toy box of a costume room .

Gryphon feathers are dropped by all types of gryphons . They are used to charge the horn of plenty , giving various buffs whilst training Hunter . They can be stored in a huntsman's kit .

Gryphon feathers can also be used in place of standard feathers for fletching, when making bolts, darts, and arrows, however they are not able to be used for fly fishing .
31241:
The horn of plenty is an off-hand item obtained as a drop from gryphons . Requiring level 50 Hunter to equip, the horn provides a passive invisible +2 boost to the Hunter skill. Upon equipping the horn, the player will blow the horn; this can be repeated by selecting the "Blow" option in the Worn Equipment tab.

The horn can be charged with up to 20,000 gryphon feathers , each providing one charge. The horn can be uncharged at any time, which returns any unused feathers. When charged, the invisible Hunter boost is increased from +2 to +4, consuming a charge every 25 catches. Additionally, the charged horn has a 1/10 chance to double a Hunter catch (without additional experience), consuming an additional charge whenever this occurs. This effect can be toggled on and off. This doubling effect does not work on implings , hunter meats , hunter furs (except for wyrmscraig goat fur , which works), or bones dropped by hunter creatures , nor does it work for aerial fishing or falconry as the horn needs to be equipped to receive its effects. Double hunter catches from the horn do not count towards the dry-protection on Hunters' Rumours .

As the horn provides an invisible Hunter boost, you cannot use the horn to boost for something you do not have the Hunter level for; the invisible boost only increases the player's success rates when hunting.

Charges are not lost if you die to another player in the Wilderness, assuming the item is protected on death.

Blessed strykewyrm bones are the blessed form of strykewyrm bones obtained by using them on the exposed altar on the summit of Ralos' Rise. They are broken down with a chisel to obtain 37 blessed bone shards and 5 Crafting experience, which can then be sacrificed at the libation bowl at the Teomat.

As each shard sacrificed gives 5 Prayer experience, each blessed bone gives 185 Prayer experience overall. If using a jug of blessed sunfire wine at the libation bowl instead of a regular jug of blessed wine, this is increased to 6 Prayer experience per shard, or 222 Prayer experience per bone.

Players looking to bless bones in bulk may talk to Virilis, found at the base of the exposed altar, to unnote any type of bones for a fee of 10 coins per bone.
31266:
Blessed frost dragon bones are the blessed form of frost dragon bones obtained by using them on the exposed altar on the summit of Ralos' Rise . They are broken down with a chisel to obtain 84 blessed bone shards and 5 Crafting experience, which can then be sacrificed at the libation bowl at the Teomat .

As each shard sacrificed gives 5 Prayer experience, each blessed bone gives 420 Prayer experience overall. If using a jug of blessed sunfire wine at the libation bowl instead of a regular jug of blessed wine , this is increased to 6 Prayer experience per shard, or 504 Prayer experience per bone.

Players looking to bless bones in bulk may talk to Virilis , found at the base of the exposed altar, to unnote any type of bones for a fee of 10 coins per bone.

31288:
The Sailing cape is the Cape of Accomplishment for the Sailing skill and can be purchased for 99,000 coins alongside the Sailing hood from Brass Hand Harry at the Pandemonium , by players who have achieved level 99 .

Like all skill capes , the Sailing cape gives +9 to all defensive stats , and also a +4 bonus to prayer if it is trimmed. The cape is automatically trimmed if a second skill is levelled to 99.

The Sailing cape has the perk that allows players to rename their boats without needing to visit Sleve McDichael . Unlike Sleve, the Sailing cape allows the player to choose what name they wish to give their boat, instead of being given a random name.

The cape provides unlimited teleports to the player's boats, provided a greater teleportation focus facility is installed. Furthermore, it provides unlimited teleports to the Pandemonium for both players and boats without requiring a teleportation focus, though players must disembark before teleporting their boat and any cargo in the hold will be lost in accordance with restrictions set by the Summon Boat spell.

This item can be stored in the cape rack of a costume room , as part of the Sailing cape set, along with the hood . Ultimate Ironmen will be unable to retrieve individual pieces until the full set is stored.

The Mayor of Catherby is a fish found in Catherby during and after the quest Current Affairs . The fish acts as the 26th replacement for the original fish that was voted as mayor of the town, in favour of the disliked Councillor Catherine .

Players can use the mayor's consult option at any time for advice, with the mayor indicating either agreement or disagreement on the matter at hand.

Using fish food on the mayor will consume it, resulting in the message The mayor accepts your generous donation to his campaign. Poisoned fish food has no effect.

The mayor can be stored in a menagerie of a player-owned house .

Dragon nails are an item used to make various core boat parts , facilities , and rosewood repair kits . They can also be used to construct certain types of wooden furniture (although this is not advised due to their price).

They are most commonly dropped from Frost dragons , and can also be smithed from dragon metal sheets at the Dragon forge in the Ancient Cavern with level 92 smithing. Each sheet produces 15 nails.
31408:
A giant blue krill is an abnormally coloured giant krill caught while rod fishing or trawling at a krill or shimmering shoal. Upon a successful roll for a catch, players or crewmates have a 1/2,000 chance to obtain one from a krill shoal, as well as a 1/1,000 chance to roll a rare fish from a shimmering shoal (then a 45/100 chance to roll the giant blue krill), which comes out to an effective rate of ~1/2,222.22.

Catching one results in the game message You catch a giant blue krill! instead of the usual You catch a giant krill!. If a crewmate catches it, the game message will show Jolly Jim catches a giant blue krill! for example.

It can be stuffed at the taxidermist in Canifis by using the item on her and paying 5,000 coins, returning a stuffed giant blue krill. Once stuffed, it can be mounted at a teak or mahogany display within the skill hall in a player-owned house, granting 70 Construction and 250 Fishing experience.

When obtained while trawling, the collection log entry will be completed, even if the player does not collect the krill from their trawling net.

31441:
The summon boat tablet is a magic tablet that can be broken by players to move their boat to the nearest docking point . Like the Summon Boat spell, players must be standing on a dock or mooring point that they want to summon their boat on to break this tablet, as well as having built a teleport focus or greater teleport focus on the desired boat.

Players can create this item on a mahogany eagle lectern or better with 2 law runes , 1 earth rune , 1 water rune , and 1 soft clay and at least 56 Magic .

This tablet can be made regardless of the player's current Spellbook . As with all tablets, the user does not need to have the relevant Magic level to use this tablet.
31443:
The teleport to boat tablet is a magic tablet that can be broken by players to teleport to their boat . Similar to the Teleport to Boat spell, the desired boat must have a greater teleport focus built in order to teleport to it.

Players can create this item on a mahogany eagle lectern or better with 2 law runes , 2 earth runes , 2 water runes , and 1 soft clay and at least 67 Magic .

This tablet can be made regardless of the player's current spellbook . As with all tablets, the user does not need to have the relevant Magic level to use this tablet.

A nearby gardener will watch over growing a hemp plant for 6 flax.
