Elkhorn coral can be harvested from a coral nursery after planting elkhorn frags .

Using crab paste on an elkhorn coral with 49 Herblore yields anti-odour salt , an item which is automatically consumed when setting up hunter traps to smoke them; five crab paste is required per coral, giving 15 salt.

It is also used in the first step of making haemostatic dressings by adding an elkhorn coral to a vial of water to create a elkhorn potion (unf) , then adding squid paste to create a haemostatic poultice , and finally adding cotton yarn for the dressing.

Lastly, five elkhorn coral can be used as a payment to protect pillar coral .
31484:
Pillar coral can be harvested from a coral nursery after planting pillar frags, and are primarily used in the making of super fishing potions and super hunter potions. To create a potion, players must add a pillar coral to a vial of water to create a pillar potion (unf), and then add the secondary ingredient.

Five pillar coral can be used as a payment to protect umbral coral.
31487: Umbral coral can be harvested from a coral nursery after planting umbral frags. They are used to make Armadyl brews by first adding one to a vial of water to create an umbral potion (unf), and then adding rainbow crab paste.
31490: A camphor seedling is created by sowing a camphor seed in a filled plant pot with a gardening trowel. Once watered, it will grow into a camphor sapling. A camphor sapling requires level 66 Farming to plant in a hardwood tree patch.
31492: An ironwood seedling is created by sowing an ironwood seed in a filled plant pot with a gardening trowel . Once watered, it will grow into an ironwood sapling . An ironwood sapling requires level 80 Farming to plant in a hardwood tree patch .
31494: A rosewood seedling is created by sowing a rosewood seed in a filled plant pot with a gardening trowel . Once watered, it will grow into a rosewood sapling . A rosewood sapling requires level 92 Farming to plant in a hardwood tree patch .

31502:
Camphor saplings are saplings that can be used to grow camphor trees at level 66 Farming.

They can be made by planting a camphor seed in a filled plant pot, with a gardening trowel in your inventory, and then watering the camphor seedling with a watering can. When watered, the seedling will sprout into a sapling in one crop cycle (0-5 minutes).

Planting the sapling in a hardwood tree patch, with a spade in your inventory, will give 88 Farming experience. It will grow into a camphor tree after 5,120 minutes (3 days, 13 hours, and 20 minutes).

Players can ask the gardener to protect their tree from disease whilst it grows, which requires payment of 10 white berries. This payment can be noted.
31505:
Ironwood saplings are saplings that can be used to grow ironwood trees at level 80 Farming .

They can be made by planting an ironwood seed in a filled plant pot , with a gardening trowel in your inventory, and then watering the ironwood seedling with a watering can . When watered, the seedling will sprout into a sapling in one crop cycle (0-5 minutes).

Planting the sapling in a hardwood tree patch , with a spade in your inventory, will result in it growing into a ironwood tree after 5,120 minutes (3 days, 13 hours, and 20 minutes).

Players can ask the gardener to protect their tree from disease whilst it grows, which requires payment of 10 curry leaves . This payment can be noted.
31508:
Rosewood saplings are saplings that can be used to grow rosewood trees at level 92 Farming .

They can be made by planting a rosewood seed in a filled plant pot , with a gardening trowel in your inventory, and then watering the rosewood seedling with a watering can . When watered, the seedling will sprout into a sapling in one crop cycle (0-5 minutes).

Planting the sapling in a hardwood tree patch , with a spade in your inventory, will result in it growing into a rosewood tree after 5,760 minutes (4 days).

Players can ask the gardener to protect their tree from disease whilst it grows, which requires payment of 8 dragonfruit . This payment can be noted.

31553:
Raw swordtip squid is a fish caught by lantern harpooning, requiring level 52 Fishing alongside a lantern and harpoon. With lantern fishing spots exclusive to certain islands at sea, the minimum Sailing level to catch them is 47, the level required to dock at the Onyx Crest.

Raw swordtip squid can be crushed with a pestle and mortar into squid paste, an ingredient used to make haemostatic dressings. At level 56 Cooking, it can also be cooked to make swordtip squid that heals 15 Hitpoints each.

Like most raw fish, it can also be cut with a regular knife or chum facility to create fish offcuts to use as bait for barbarian fishing and deep sea trawling. Each cutting action will also give a 1/1,024 chance of obtaining a squid beak, which is used to create wooden blowpipes. While using a chum facility, it is possible to obtain multiple beaks in one cutting action, depending on which chum facility is used, though the rate per action remains 1/1,024 regardless of how many squid are processed.
31556:
Swordtip squid is a type of fish that restores 15 Hitpoints when eaten. It can be obtained by cooking raw swordtip squid on a fire or cooking range , requiring level 56 Cooking and granting 150 experience when successful.

When cooking there is a chance to fail, resulting in burnt swordtip squid . The burn rate decreases as the player's Cooking level increases, and it will stop burning entirely at level 91, or 85 if using a cooking range.
31559:
Burnt swordtip squid is the result of accidentally burning a raw swordtip squid while attempting to cook swordtip squid . The burn rate decreases as the player's Cooking level increases, and it will stop burning entirely at level 91, or 85 if using a cooking range.

The burnt swordtip squid has no use whatsoever. Like most other burnt food, it is tradeable to other players but not on the Grand Exchange . Because of that, some players collect them or resell them to other burnt food collectors.
31561:
Raw jumbo squid is a fish caught by lantern harpooning, requiring level 69 Fishing alongside a lantern and harpoon. With lantern fishing spots exclusive to certain islands at sea, the minimum Sailing level to catch them is 47, the level required to dock at the Onyx Crest.

Raw jumbo squid can be crushed with a pestle and mortar into squid paste, an ingredient used to make haemostatic dressings. At level 71 Cooking, it can also be cooked to make jumbo squid that heals 17 Hitpoints each.

Like most raw fish, it can also be cut with a regular knife or chum facility to create fine fish offcuts to use as bait for various fishing activities. Each cutting action will also give a 1/512 chance of obtaining a squid beak, which is used to create wooden blowpipes. When cooking there is a chance to fail, resulting in burnt jumbo squid . The burn rate decreases as the player's Cooking level increases, and it will only stop burning at level 98 (96 if the elite Kourend & Kebos Diary has been completed) when cooking at the Hosidius Kitchen .
31567:

31569:

An extended stamina potion restores 40% of the player's run energy per dose, and offers a 70% reduction in run energy depletion for 4 minutes. This effect does not stack, and drinking additional doses before the timer has run out will simply reset it back to 4 minutes. When the stamina effect is active the boot in the run energy orb changes from its usual yellow to orange.

An extended stamina potion can be made at level 85 Herblore by mixing a regular stamina potion with marlin scales. Each dose grants 27.5 Herblore experience, and requires one marlin scale.

When used to charge the ring of endurance, each dose grants two charges. Drinking a dose of extended stamina potion while having a charged ring of endurance equipped will consume 2 charges to double the potion's effect, restoring 80% run energy and granting the run energy depletion buff for 8 minutes.

An Armadyl brew is a potion made by using rainbow crab paste on an unfinished umbral potion, requiring 89 Herblore and granting 205 Herblore experience.

Each dose of an Armadyl brew temporarily lowers Attack, Strength, Defence, and Magic by 10% + 2 of their current levels, and raises Hitpoints by 10% + 2 and Ranged by 10% + 4 of their base levels. This can boost the player's Hitpoints and Ranged above their base level by up to the amount restored.

One dose of super restore is enough to restore lost stats from three doses of Armadyl brew, or up to four doses of brew if the player's stats were boosted beforehand (as with a super combat potion).

Lead ore is an ore mined from lead rocks at level 25 Mining , granting 40.5 experience. Two ore can be smelted into a lead bar at level 25 Smithing , granting 15.5 experience.

Mining enhancers will work on lead rocks; wearing Varrock armour 1 and better will give a 10% chance of mining an extra lead ore, and mining gloves will prevent lead rocks from depleting after mining a certain amount of ore, depending on the type of gloves worn.

Mining lead ore is intended to provide more experience per hour than mining iron rocks outside of the Mining Guild , but less experience per hour than mining iron rocks in the Mining Guild.
31719:
Nickel ore is an ore mined from nickel rocks at level 74 Mining , granting 80.5 experience. Alongside two copper ore , it can be smelted into a cupronickel bar at level 74 Smithing , granting 42 experience.

With the exception of Varrock armour 4 (which gives a 10% chance of mining an extra nickel ore), mining enhancers do not work for nickel rocks.

At higher Mining levels, experience rates are around 25k xp/hr. At 99 Mining and with the eastern Deepfin Mine bank chest built, experience rates can be up to 28k xp/hr.

Rubium splinters are resources that are mined from rubium rocks at level 48 Mining, found in the Charred Dungeon on Charred Island. Each rock will provide a guaranteed two splinters, and may deplete randomly on each subsequent splinter mined.

At level 68, rubium deposits can also be mined for rubium geodes which can be broken down with a hammer and chisel into splinters. The amount of splinters obtained from a geode scales with Mining level.

10 splinters and 2 of any smithable cannonball can be used at an anvil to smith 2 incendiary cannonballs every 3 ticks in batches of 56 (up to 28 actions per batch). This is done by left-clicking "Smith" on the anvil; using either the splinters or the cannonball on the anvil will not work.

When fired from a ship's cannon, the incendiaries have a chance to burn their targets.
31724:
Rubium geodes are mined rubium deposits, requiring 68 Mining. Cracking open a geode with a hammer & chisel gives rubium splinters with a quantity that scales with Mining level. Each geode has to be individually cracked open as they do not process automatically, but opening geodes will start with the first geode in the inventory, meaning that you can spam click the last geode in your inventory to quickly open them all.

Rubium deposits can be found in the Charred Dungeon, which requires 60 Sailing to reach.

31803:
A spyglass is a tool used in sea charting. It is used when the player or their boat is on a glowing spot, after which a short cutscene is initiated in which the player views the nearby area through the spyglass. Note that NPCs can still attack during these cutscenes. You obtain one by talking to Chartin' Charles McAtless.

If lost, another can be obtained from the cargo hold of a boat.
31805:
The current duck is a friendly floaty duck who helps the player with charting currents at sea . The ability to chart currents is unlocked upon completion of Current Affairs , which requires a Sailing level of 22.

The current duck follows currents until reaching a predetermined end point indicated with message Your current duck comes to a stop. . It will despawn two minutes after it comes to a stop. The current duck will reappear in the tools compartment of the cargo hold on a player's boat once it is placed in the water, however it will not be retrievable from there until the current one despawns or is picked up. The current duck cannot be placed in a menagerie .

Telekinetic grab does not work on the current duck.
31807:
A crowbar is a tool used to open sealed crates as part of sea charting. The ability to open sealed crates at sea is unlocked upon completion of Prying Times, which requires a Sailing level of 12.

If lost, another can be obtained from the cargo hold of a boat, or from the crate of crowbars behind the counter of the Pandemonium pub. Thurgo can also make another crowbar by speaking with him with a hammer, steel bar, and redberry pie in the inventory.
31809:
A portable weather station is a device given by Meaty Aura Logist to measure weather patterns as part of sea charting . Charting weather requires a Sailing level of 57; boosts can be used, and must be maintained upon starting and getting readings.

Interacting with the item displays a chatbox message indicating which cardinal direction the wind is blowing toward relative to the player's current location. Following the wind readings will take the player in a circle. Taking a reading at the centre of this circle will turn it into a data filled portable weather station , at which point it is returned to Meaty Aura Logist (players must return to the original location where they received the device).

31811:
Whirlpool surprise is a type of ale that temporarily boosts Cooking by 2 and Sailing by 3, while draining Agility by 2. Drinking a whirlpool surprise results in successive game messages stating You drink the rum cocktail. It tastes great! and You feel inspired to both cook and sail!.

Two can be claimed for free from Rum-dashed Ralph upon clearing the shark rank of the Tempor Tantrum Barracuda Trial, after which it becomes available for 300 coins each at the Pandemonium pub.
31814:
Kraken ink stout is a type of ale that temporarily boosts Magic by 2 and Sailing by 1. Drinking a kraken ink stout results in successive game messages stating You drink the rich stout. It thickly coats the back of your throat. Somehow you feel more adept at magic.

The ability to purchase kraken ink stout is unlocked after completely charting 5 seas in both the Ardent Ocean and Unquiet Ocean , then showing Chartin' Charles McAtless the captain's log .

Once unlocked, players can speak to Charles again and select the chat option " What do I get from charting the sea? ", then " Can you tell me about these drinks? ". Players can buy one ale at a time for 300 coins, or 25 noted ales at once for 7,500 coins.
31817:
Perildance bitter is a type of ale that temporarily boosts Sailing by 1, Strength and Ranged by 2, while draining Magic by 2. Drinking a perildance bitter results in successive game messages stating You drink the deep red bitter. It tastes paradoxically sweet! You feel your muscles bulge and your sight become sharp!

The ability to purchase perildance bitter is unlocked after completely charting 8 seas in the Western Ocean and 5 seas in the Shrouded Ocean, then showing Chartin' Charles McAtless the captain's log.

Once unlocked, players can speak to Charles again and select the chat option "What do I get from charting the sea?", then "Can you tell me about these drinks?". Players can buy one ale at a time for 300 coins, or 25 noted ales at once for 7,500 coins.
31820:
Trawler's trust is a type of ale that temporarily boosts Sailing and Fishing by 2, while draining Attack by 2. Drinking a trawler's trust results in successive game messages stating You drink the refreshing beer. It tastes foamy and salty. You feel at one with the sea!

The ability to purchase trawler's trust is unlocked after completely charting 50 seas across all oceans, then showing Chartin' Charles McAtless the captain's log.

Once unlocked, players can speak to Charles again and select the chat option "What do I get from charting the sea?", then "Can you tell me about these drinks?". Players can buy one ale at a time for 300 coins, or 25 noted ales at once for 7,500 coins.
31823:
Horizon's lure is a type of ale that temporarily boosts Sailing by 4, while draining Thieving by 2. Drinking a horizon's lure results in successive game messages stating You drink the rich golden ale. It tastes like a fond memory. You feel optimistic about the future.

The ability to purchase horizon's lure is unlocked after completely charting 70 seas across all oceans, then showing Chartin' Charles McAtless the captain's log ; currently, this requires that players fully chart everything in the game to unlock this ale.

78 Sailing [ boostable ] is required to chart the sea, as well as a boat with an Adamant keel , Adamant helm and Eternal brazier to traverse the Crystal-flecked waters , Tangled kelp and Northern Ocean . 76 Sailing [ not boostable ] is required to obtain the brazier schematic from Buccaneers' Haven .

Once unlocked, players can speak to Chartin' Charles McAtless again and select the chat option " What do I get from charting the sea? ", then " Can you tell me about these drinks? ". Players can buy one ale at a time for 300 coins, or 25 noted ales at once for 7,500 coins.

Drinking the bottle grants 75 Sailing experience, and will deal 5 damage, as well as drain the player's Defence by 2 + 20% of their current level, and the player's Attack , Strength , Ranged , and Magic by 2 + 10% of their current level.

31834:

Drinking the bottle grants 75 Sailing experience, and will temporarily boost Farming by 5 levels, while draining Agility by ~26%. This is accompanied by a game message stating The wine makes your head spin with thoughts of fields full of giant crops.

It provides the highest consistent temporary skill boost to Farming, however it can only obtained and consumed once, and the player will have to be on a boat in order to consume it.
31835:

Drinking the bottle grants 75 Sailing experience and will cause the player to black out, capsizing their boat and leaving them on the shore near Witchaven Dungeon , as well as draining Strength and Magic levels by 20% of their current level. Players who are teleblocked will not be teleported to shore.

Players can get back on their boat with no loss of non- courier task cargo, depending on the player's Sailing level; the boat will be docked at Witchaven if the player's Sailing level is at least 34, or Port Sarim if lower.

31843:

31844:

31850:
A bottle of zogre's sloppy kisses is an alcoholic drink acquired by prying open a sealed crate in Backwater, just off the western coast of Feldip Hills. Doing so requires a crowbar in the inventory, which in turn requires completion of Prying Times to obtain.

Drinking the bottle grants 75 Sailing experience, and will inflict the player with both poison (starting at 5 damage) and disease.
31851:
A bottle of creator's cocktail is an alcoholic drink acquired by prying open a sealed crate just off the western coast of the Isle of Souls. Doing so requires a crowbar in the inventory, which in turn requires completion of Prying Times to obtain.

Drinking the bottle grants 75 Sailing experience, and will deal damage equal to one-third of the player's maximum hitpoints (rounded down); this can kill the player if their health is too low. Wearing a blue soul cape will protect the player from the drink's effects.
31852:
A bottle of soul is an alcoholic drink acquired by prying open a sealed crate just off the southern coast of the Isle of Souls . Doing so requires a crowbar in the inventory, which in turn requires completion of Prying Times to obtain.

Drinking the bottle grants 75 Sailing experience, and its effects differ depending on whether the player has drunk the bottle of soul juice . If it was not yet drunk, drinking this bottle will initiate a conversation with Death , who informs the player that they consumed a soul before extracting it, warning the player not to be so careless next time.

Otherwise, drinking this bottle will deal damage equal to 90% of the player's maximum hitpoints (rounded down); this can kill the player if their health is too low. This damage can be avoided by stepping away during the dialogue with Death .

In other words, drinking the bottle of soul will only damage you if you've drunk the bottle of soul juice before.
31853:
Bottle of zul-rye beer is an alcoholic drink acquired by prying open a sealed crate in Zul-Egil, just off the coast south-east of the Poison Waste. Doing so requires a crowbar in the inventory, which in turn requires completion of Prying Times to obtain.

Drinking the bottle grants 75 Sailing experience, and will inflict the player with venom. Any form of venom immunity (e.g. wearing a serpentine helm, drinking an antidote++) will prevent the beer from inflicting venom. Additionally, players with 66 Sailing and an adamant keel on their boat may consider obtaining the nearby bottle of crystal clear water from a sealed crate to the north-west, which will reduce venom to poison when drunk.
31854:
A bottle of Captain Clop's mango gin is an alcoholic drink acquired by prying open a sealed crate in the Western Gate , to the far east of Vatrachos Island . Doing so requires a crowbar in the inventory, which in turn requires completion of Prying Times to obtain.

Drinking the bottle grants 75 Sailing experience, and will cause the player to move in a random direction five times over the next few seconds. The player can drink the bottle and then immediately man the helm of a ship to avoid this effect entirely.
31855:
A bottle of slippery snake skins in possibly gravy is an alcoholic drink acquired by prying open a sealed crate in the Crystal Sea , to the far east of Port Roberts . Doing so requires a crowbar in the inventory, which in turn requires completion of Prying Times to obtain.

Drinking the bottle grants 75 Sailing experience, and spawns an aggressive level-90 snakeling who can inflict venom .
31856:
A bottle of crystal clear water is an alcoholic drink acquired by prying open a sealed crate in Porth Neigwl, just off the western coast of Isafdar.

Drinking the bottle grants 75 Sailing experience, and will provide six minutes of immunity to poison, which may be useful to counter the effects of the bottle of zul-rye beer that can be obtained in another sealed crate to the south-east.
31857:
A bottle of underground passteurised milk is an alcoholic drink acquired by prying open a sealed crate north-west of Ynysdail in Porth Gwenith. Doing so requires a crowbar in the inventory, which in turn requires completion of Prying Times to obtain.

Drinking the bottle grants 75 Sailing experience, and will deal damage equal to two-thirds of the player's maximum hitpoints (rounded down); this can kill the player if their health is too low.
31858:
A bottle of delicate elven wine is an alcoholic drink acquired by prying open a sealed crate in the Tirannwn Bight, just off the coast west of Mynydd. Doing so requires a crowbar in the inventory, which in turn requires completion of Prying Times to obtain.

Drinking the bottle grants 75 Sailing experience, and if the player has completed Regicide, will teleport the player to Isafdar just north-east of Tyras Camp, with their boat docking at Port Tyras (or Port Sarim if their Sailing level is below 66 or if the boat doesn't have an adamant keel built) and courier task cargo being lost. If Regicide has not been completed, then the player and their boat will remain where they were.
31859:
A bottle of sea spray is an alcoholic drink acquired by prying open a sealed crate just off the southern coast of Buccaneers' Haven . Doing so requires a crowbar in the inventory, which in turn requires completion of Prying Times to obtain.

Drinking the bottle grants 75 Sailing experience, and will cause the camera to rock back and forth vertically (like when on the Fishing Trawler ) for 20 seconds. This may be nauseating if players keep looking at the screen while the effect is ongoing, but the effect can be disabled in game settings under "Camera Effects". Alternatively, logging out after the effects have started will not cause them to resume upon logging back in.
31860:
A bottle of banker's draught is an alcoholic drink acquired by prying open a sealed crate in the Hosidian Sea, off the eastern coast of Hosidius. Doing so requires a crowbar in the inventory, which in turn requires completion of Prying Times to obtain.

Drinking the bottle grants 75 Sailing experience, and will bank all of the player's inventory items and worn equipment. If the player's bank is full, items that cannot be deposited will be dropped on the ground. Players can avoid banking their items by dropping them prior to drinking the draught and simply pick their items up after doing so.

As Ultimate Ironmen cannot use banks, drinking the bottle will instead deal damage equal to 10% of the player's Hitpoints level (rounded down).
31861:
A bottle of headless unicornman's heady beer is an alcoholic drink acquired by prying open a sealed crate in the Gulf of Kourend , to the east of Port Piscarilius . Doing so requires a crowbar in the inventory, which in turn requires completion of Prying Times to obtain.

Drinking the bottle grants 75 Sailing experience, and will fill the player's inventory with various ensouled heads . To maximise the number of heads received, the player may wish to drink this item after banking or storing any excess items in the inventory.

31863:
A bottle of crocodile tears is an alcoholic drink acquired by prying open a sealed crate in the small cove to the south of Menaphos. Doing so requires a crowbar in the inventory, which in turn requires completion of Prying Times to obtain.

Drinking the bottle grants 75 Sailing experience, and will apply desert heat damage to the player once. If the player is not carrying any full waterskins, this can deal around 5-13 damage spread across four hitsplats. Wearing the circlet of water does not prevent this damage.
31864:
A bottle of fishier bladderier stout is an alcoholic drink acquired by prying open a sealed crate in Fremensund, to the north-east of Rellekka. Doing so requires a crowbar in the inventory, which in turn requires completion of Prying Times to obtain.

Drinking the bottle grants 75 Sailing experience, and will teleport the player to an instanced version of the troll arena, where they will have to face three trolls: The rocks, Chuck up, and Daddy's special water. It is not required to kill them to complete this sea charting task, though each of them will drop an item granting a one-time 100 Sailing experience. Escaping the arena will teleport the player inside the Rellekka Longhall, after which they may drink another bottle to attempt the fight against all three trolls again, regardless of how many they defeated.

Players can get back on their boat with no loss of non-courier task cargo, depending on the player's Sailing level; the boat will be docked at Rellekka if the player's Sailing level is at least 62 and they have completed The Fremennik Trials, or Port Sarim if not.

31906:
Bronze cannonballs are ammunition used for a boat cannon during boat combat. They can be fired from bronze cannons or stronger.

Four can be made from a single bronze bar with level 5 Smithing, granting 9 experience per bar. Smithing cannonballs require the use of an ammo mould, which requires partial completion of Dwarf Cannon to obtain. Alternatively, a double ammo mould (requiring Foundry Reputation to purchase via the Giants' Foundry minigame) allows players to process two bars into eight cannonballs at the same speed as a regular ammo mould processes one bar into four.

Players with level 87 Sailing can further speed up smithing cannonballs by using the ancient furnace in the Grimstone Dungeon, which halves the time it takes to create cannonballs from 8 ticks to 4 ticks. Combining this with a double ammo mould, players can smith cannonballs at four times the normal speed.

31964:
A repair kit is an item that heals 5 health to a boat. Players can simply click the item's "Apply" option whilst on a boat to repair damage, and multiple players can do so at once to rapidly repair the boat. Additionally, crewmates can also repair the boat if instructed to, and depending on their Deckhandiness level may heal more than 5 per kit.

Players can build repair kits with 2 planks, 10 bronze nails, and 5 swamp paste, granting 43.5 Construction experience and yielding 2 kits with the completion of Pandemonium quest. Unlike other repair kits, it can be created without a shipwrights' workbench simply by using the required items on one another in the inventory.

Like food, applying a repair kit incurs the same delay as eating during boat combat.

Additionally, crewmates can also repair the boat if instructed to, and depending on their Deckhandiness level may heal more than 10 per kit.

Players can build oak repair kits at a shipwrights' workbench with 2 oak planks, 10 iron nails, and 5 swamp paste, requiring 19 Construction and granting 90 experience, yielding 2 kits per action.

Like food, applying a repair kit incurs the same delay as eating during boat combat.

31989:
Boat bottles are a single-use item obtained rarely from sorting low-tier salvage from shipwrecks . It is used to "place" a player's boat into their inventory, allowing them to transport it to another port from land. This is useful for moving boats without a teleport focus built on them.

Using the "Bottle-boat" option on an empty bottle requires an empty cargo hold, as well as being at a docking point . When using the "Unbottle-boat" option on a full bottle, players will receive a confirmation message before doing so. The bottle will be lost when the player releases the boat.

Compared with the cost of recovering a boat in order to move it to a different port, using a boat bottle on a raft will result in a profit/loss of −19,956 coins , with a skiff −16,081 coins , and with a sloop 29,794 coins .

A bottle containing a boat is always kept on death and can only be destroyed using the bank incinerator . If destroyed, the boat can be recovered at a shipwright .

Dragon metal sheets are an item used in high-level shipbuilding , with some of the best facilities on a boat requiring multiple sheets to build.

With access to the dragon forge upon completion of Dragon Slayer II , players can make dragon keel parts for dragon keels as well as dragon nails (15 per sheet). Two sheets are used to make one keel part, while two keel parts are used to make one set of large dragon keel parts (requiring 4 sheets in total). As such, a total of 20 sheets are required for a dragon keel on a skiff , and 64 sheets for a sloop .

Completion of the Pandemonium quest is also required to be able to use sheets at the forge. Attempting to make something with a dragon metal sheet without having completed the quest displays the chatbox message "You probably shouldn't just go messing around with the dragon sheets without knowing what you're doing."

The best sources for these sheets are killing lava strykewyrms or frost dragons on task, however these can be quite tedious to obtain, especially if the player does not have enough slayer points to skip for them. A slower but more consistent method is completing bounty tasks for great white sharks , orcas , and high-levelled krakens (preferably armoured krakens ), as one bounty task for each of these monsters are guaranteed at various notice boards across Gielinor.

32191:
A rune keel is a core boat part that increases the hitpoints and armour of a boat. It is built via the boat schematics board at the Shipyard, requiring level 85 Sailing and 78 Construction, granting a variable amount of Construction experience depending on the type of boat.

While sharing the same health value as the dragon keel, the rune keel has an armour rating of 800, which is 200 lower than the dragon keel's 1,000. Because every 100 points of armour provide an increase of flat armour rating of 1, any boat equipped with it has a flat armour rating of 8, subtracting 8 damage from every single incoming hit, and negating any damage hit of 8 or less.

As such, a boat with a rune keel built is fully protected from the following Sailing monsters:

All rays

All birds except for albatrosses

All mammals except for orcas

Bull sharks and hammerhead sharks

An eternal brazier is a core boat part which enables the player to safely traverse the icy seas in the Northern Ocean. It is built via the boat schematics board at the Shipyard after reading the eternal brazier schematic, requiring level 78 Sailing and 72 Construction, granting 1,373 Construction experience.

While temporary boosts can be used to build the brazier (crystal saws will work), the schematic is located within a lockbox on Buccaneers' Haven, which requires a base Sailing level of 76 in order to dock on.

Despite the required materials, completion of Making Friends with My Arm is not necessary to build the eternal brazier. However, Ironmen cannot obtain the necessary salts without completing the quest and mining them (see below).

The bronze cannon attacks every 7 ticks, and can only fire bronze cannonballs. Crewmates with at least level 1 Privateering can be assigned to operate the cannon, as long as the player has the required unboosted Sailing level.

Only one cannon can be built on a raft and skiff, while a sloop allows two.

The dragon cannon attacks every 7 ticks, and can fire up to dragon cannonballs. It can be built at specific facility hotspots on skiffs and sloops after reading the salvaging station schematic , requiring level 42 Sailing and 34 Construction , granting 372 Construction experience.
32225:
Chum stations are a boat facility used to bait shoals whilst deep sea trawling. It can be built at specific facility hotspots on the boat, requiring level 56 Sailing and 45 Construction, granting 1,522 Construction experience. It requires 64 Fishing to operate.

Operating a chum station will spread regular fish offcuts that are stored in a cargo hold into the sea, which acts as optional bait for low-tier shoals; doing so gives a 20% chance to catch an extra fish per successful catch, on top of the catch bonus provided by trawling nets. Additionally, using raw fish (except leaping fish) on the station will cut them into regular fish offcuts or fine fish offcuts at a rate of two fish per tick, though spreading fine offcuts require an advanced chum station or better.

When cutting raw fish with secondary drops at a chum station (such as haddock eyes and squid beaks), it will roll the chance of obtaining them per action rather than per fish but give double the yield if successful. For example, cutting one raw jumbo squid with a knife gives a 1/512 chance of yielding a squid beak, but cutting two at once with a chum station would give a 1/512 chance of yielding two squid beaks rather than rolling the chance for each squid.

Crewmates with at least level 1 Deckhandiness can be assigned to operate the chum station, provided that fish offcuts are stored in the cargo hold and the player has the required Sailing level. As such, players who used temporary boosts to build it must maintain the Sailing boost when a crewmate or themselves are using it.

For the upgraded chum stations, see the advanced chum station and the chum spreader.
32226:
Advanced chum station are a boat facility used to bait shoals whilst deep sea trawling. It is an upgrade to the chum station allowing spreading of all types of fish offcuts and increasing the number of raw fish cut into offcuts to three per tick. It can be built at specific facility hotspots on the boat, requiring level 68 Sailing and 61 Construction, granting 1,738 Construction experience.

Operating an advanced chum station will spread regular or fine fish offcuts that are stored in a cargo hold into the sea, which acts as optional bait for shoals; doing so gives a 20% chance to catch an extra fish per successful catch, on top of the catch bonus provided by trawling nets. Additionally, using raw fish (except leaping fish) on the station will cut them into regular fish offcuts or fine fish offcuts at a rate of three fish per tick.

When cutting raw fish with secondary drops at a chum station (such as haddock eyes and squid beaks), it will roll the chance of obtaining them per action rather than per fish but give triple the yield if successful. For example, cutting one raw jumbo squid with a knife gives a 1/512 chance of yielding a squid beak, but cutting three at once with an advanced chum station would give a 1/512 chance of yielding three squid beaks rather than rolling the chance for each squid.

Crewmates with at least level 2 Deckhandiness can be assigned to operate the advanced chum station, provided that fish offcuts are stored in the cargo hold and the player has the required Sailing level. As such, players who used temporary boosts to build it must maintain the Sailing boost when a crewmate or themselves are using it.
32227:
Chum spreaders are a boat facility used to bait shoals whilst deep sea trawling. It can be built at specific facility hotspots on the boat, requiring level 82 Sailing and 74 Construction, granting 2,028 Construction experience. Only one may be built at a time. It is the next tier station from the advanced chum station.

Operating a chum spreader will spread regular or fine fish offcuts that are stored in a cargo hold into the sea, which acts as optional bait for shoals; doing so gives a 20% chance to catch an extra fish per successful catch, on top of the catch bonus provided by trawling nets. Additionally, using raw fish (except leaping fish) on the station will cut them into regular fish offcuts or fine fish offcuts at a rate of four fish per tick; this is the only advantage over the advanced chum station, while costing an additional investment of 27,539 for a narwhal horn knife to build it.

When cutting raw fish with secondary drops at a chum station (such as haddock eyes and squid beaks), it will roll the chance of obtaining them per action rather than per fish but give quadruple the yield if successful. For example, cutting one raw jumbo squid with a knife gives a 1/512 chance of yielding a squid beak, but cutting four at once with a chum spreader would give a 1/512 chance of yielding four squid beaks rather than rolling the chance for each squid.

Crewmates with at least level 2 Deckhandiness can be assigned to operate the chum spreader, provided that fish offcuts are stored in the cargo hold and the player has the required Sailing level. As such, players who used temporary boosts to build it must maintain the Sailing boost when a crewmate or themselves are using it.
32228:
The fathom stone is a boat facility used to locate shoals whilst deep sea trawling. It can be built at specific facility hotspots on the boat, requiring level 70 Sailing and 62 Construction, granting 1,652 Construction experience.

The "Locate-shoal" option will open a menu prompting the player to choose a desired shoal to locate. Choosing a shoal will inform the player which cardinal direction the shoal is found; if a chosen shoal is not nearby, it will inform the player that there are no shoals of that type within range of the fathom stone. This option will interrupt player actions, as doing so requires them to be in front of it.

Meanwhile, the "Quick-locate" option will do the same to the last shoal chosen in the menu, or the closest shoal within range if they did not do so. This option will not interrupt player actions, nor require the player to be next to it.

While temporary boosts can be used to build the facility, players must maintain the Sailing boost whenever they wish to make use of it.
32229:
The fathom pearl is a boat facility used to locate shoals whilst deep sea trawling. It can be built at specific facility hotspots on the boat, requiring level 91 Sailing and 83 Construction, granting 2,307 Construction experience.

The "Locate-shoal" option will open a menu prompting the player to choose a desired shoal to locate. Choosing a shoal will inform the player which cardinal direction the shoal is found, as well as display an arrow marker () on the minimap; if a chosen shoal is not nearby, it will inform the player that there are no shoals of that type within range of the fathom pearl. This option will interrupt player actions, as doing so requires them to be in front of it.

Meanwhile, the "Quick-locate" option will do the same to the last shoal chosen in the menu, or the closest shoal within range if they did not do so. This option will not interrupt player actions, nor require the player to be next to it.

While temporary boosts can be used to build the facility, players must maintain the Sailing boost whenever they wish to make use of it.
32230:
A range is a facility that can be built on a boat in order to cook food at sea. It can be built at specific facility hotspots on the boat, requiring level 16 Sailing and 6 Construction , granting 90 Construction experience.

Some fish cannot be stored in the cargo hold after being cooked. Players should take care when cooking fish that can't be stored such as marlins .
32231:
A keg is a boat facility that can be filled with certain ales rewarded from sea charting . It can be built at specific facility hotspots on the boat, requiring level 33 Sailing and 25 Construction , granting 313 Construction experience. As the keg requires a barrel stand to build, players must also have cleared the Shark rank of the Tempor Tantrum Barracuda Trial .

Filling a keg requires 25 of a specific ale, which can either be noted or unnoted, but not a mixture of both. Once filled, players will receive certain benefits to activities at sea depending on the ale used. Multiple kegs can be built on a boat to fill them with different ales in order to receive multiple benefits, but filling them with the same ale will not cause their effects to stack.

Players can also freely obtain an infinite amount of the filled ale by using a beer glass on it. However, if emptied via the "Empty" option, the ales are not returned.

A keg moved with a Facility bottle will lose all of its contents and will need to be refilled with ale.
32232:
An anchor is a boat facility that can be built on a boat to keep it in place while at sea. It can be built at specific facility hotspots on the boat, requiring level 37 Sailing and 29 Construction, granting 176 Construction experience.

At sea, the anchor can be dropped and raised by clicking on it. As the player must be standing on the anchor to interact with it, the anchor cannot be dropped or raised while navigating with the helm. While the anchor is down, the boat can rotate in place but not move. Dropping the anchor stops the boat faster than lowering the sails.

Currently, the anchor has little practical use and is primarily used in situations where you may want to rotate the boat without moving it, such as switching between 2 nearby shipwrecks.

Most players forego building the anchor due to its limited functionality. It also occupies a facility hotspot for movement facilities such as the Wind catcher, and its location near the helm can easily cause misclicks.
32233:
The wind catcher is a boat facility that can store and release wind motes for a speed boost whilst at sea. It can be built at specific facility hotspots on the boat, requiring level 53 Sailing and 47 Construction, granting 741 Construction experience. As the catcher requires a captured wind mote to build, players must also have cleared the Shark rank of the Jubbly Jive Barracuda Trial, which cannot be attempted until level 55 Sailing.

Once built, the wind catcher must be activated in order to store wind motes. Whenever a player trims their sails, passes through a crystal mote, or harvests from a crystal extractor, a wind mote is stored in the catcher. The wind catcher can store two of these wind motes. Building a second wind catcher provides no additional benefit.

Trimming the sails with an activated wind catcher reduces the experience granted by 25%. Releasing a wind mote will grant the boat a burst of speed as if they had trimmed their sails, granting 40 Sailing experience, or 10 Sailing experience if the wind mote was generated by a crystal extractor. Players can do so by either selecting the "Release-mote" on the catcher, or via the Sailing Options tab.

The gale catcher is a superior version of the wind catcher that grants more experience and can store three motes instead of two.
32234:
The gale catcher is a superior variant of the wind catcher, being able to store three wind motes instead of two.

It can be built at specific facility hotspots on the boat after reading the gale catcher schematic, requiring level 79 Sailing and 70 Construction, granting 1,517 Construction experience.

While temporary boosts can be used to build the facility, players must maintain the Sailing boost whenever they wish to make use of it.

Trimming the sails with an activated gale catcher reduces the experience granted by 25%. Releasing a wind mote will grant the boat a burst of speed as if they had trimmed their sails, granting 70 Sailing experience, or 10 Sailing experience if the wind mote was generated by a crystal extractor. Players can do so by either selecting the "Release-mote" on the catcher, or via the Sailing Options tab.

For this reason, the exact placement of the facility is a low priority, so it should not be placed in the facility hotspot directly to the starboard side of the helm in a skiff, or the hotspot one tile towards the bow (front) and all the way to the port side on a sloop; these spots should be reserved for the crystal extractor instead, unless salvaging, so that it may be harvested while navigating the helm.
32235:
The crystal extractor is a boat facility that periodically generates wind motes for a wind or gale catcher. It can be built at specific facility hotspots on the boat, requiring level 73 Sailing and 67 Construction, granting 3,066 Construction experience. Though boosts can be used to build the facility, the extractor requires a Heart of Ithell to build, so players must also have 72 Sailing to clear the Shark rank of the Gwenith Glide Barracuda Trial.

Players can only build one crystal extractor on their boat.
32236:
An innoculation station is a boat facility which enables the player to safely traverse the fetid waters in the Shrouded Ocean. It is built next to the cargo hold, requiring level 40 Sailing and 37 Construction, granting 765 Construction experience.

While temporary boosts can be used to build the station, players must maintain the Sailing boost when sea charting in fetid waters.
32237:
A teleportation focus is a boat facility which enables the player to use the Summon Boat spell or magic tablet to teleport the boat to the dock or mooring point that they are currently located at. To be able to cast Teleport to Boat , players must instead build the greater teleport focus .

The teleport focus can be built at specific facility hotspots on the boat, requiring level 55 Sailing and 49 Construction , granting 2,154 Construction experience. It is recommended not to build this facility next to the helm on a skiff , as that is where the crystal extractor (unlocked at 73 Sailing) must be placed in order to be harvested from while still operating the helm of the skiff.

Much like the boat recovery service offered by shipwrights , certain items in the cargo hold (port task crates, bounty items, salvage, and fish) will be lost when summoned. Additionally, lost boats cannot be recovered with Summon Boat; the boat needs to have been docked at a mooring point to be summoned.
32238:
A greater teleportation focus is a superior variant of the teleportation focus . Having this facility on a ship enables players to use the Teleport to Boat spell, a magic tablet or the Sailing cape to teleport to a dock or mooring point where their ship is docked. The perks of the regular teleportation focus are provided by the greater teleportation focus as well, so there is no need to waste space by having both on a ship.

A regular teleportation focus does not need to be built before building a greater teleportation focus.

It can be built at specific facility hotspots on the boat, requiring level 75 Sailing and 69 Construction , granting 3,582 Construction experience.
32299:
"No trim" is the default boat trim for skiffs and sloops. It varies in colour depending what material the hull of the boat is made out of.

It can be built for free via the boat schematics board at the Shipyard.
32307:
Fine fish offcuts are created by using a knife on certain high level raw fish, which are primarily used to bait rainbow crab traps and fish shoals whilst deep sea trawling. They can also be used in place of fish offcuts or bait for barbarian fishing and aerial fishing.

For fish shoals, baiting is not mandatory (except when rod fishing shoals, where one is used per fish), but doing so via an advanced chum station or better will grant a 20% chance to catch extra fish.

Unlike regular fish offcuts, they are not prioritised over other types of bait when barbarian fishing.
32309:
Raw giant krill is a type of fish caught from giant krill shoals whilst deep sea trawling, requiring level 69 Fishing and granting 112.5 experience per successful catch with a trawling net, or 22.5 if caught with a fishing rod. They can also be caught from shimmering shoals, which can yield other deep sea fish alongside giant krill.

Cooking giant krill requires level 69 in Cooking, resulting in a giant krill and 177.5 Cooking experience. If unsuccessful, it will result in a burnt giant krill instead.
32312:
Giant krill is a type of fish that restores 17 Hitpoints when eaten. It can be obtained by cooking raw giant krill on a fire or cooking range . Cooking a giant krill requires level 69 Cooking , and grants 177.5 experience when successful.

When cooking there is a chance to fail, resulting in a burnt giant krill . The burn rate decreases as the player's Cooking level increases, and it will only stop burning entirely if the player is wearing a Cooking cape , or at level 98 (95 if the elite Kourend & Kebos Diary has been completed) when cooking at the Hosidius Kitchen .
32315:
Burnt giant krill is the result of accidentally burning a raw giant krill while attempting to cook giant krill. The burn rate decreases as the player's Cooking level increases, and it will only stop burning entirely if the player is wearing a Cooking cape, or at level 98 (95 if the elite Kourend & Kebos Diary has been completed) when cooking at the Hosidius Kitchen.

The burnt giant krill has no use whatsoever. Like most other burnt food, it is tradeable to other players but not on the Grand Exchange.
32317:
Raw haddock is a type of fish caught from haddock shoals whilst deep sea trawling, requiring level 73 Fishing and granting 128.5 experience per successful catch with a trawling net, or 25.7 if caught with a fishing rod. They can also be caught from shimmering shoals, which can yield other deep sea fish alongside haddock.

Cooking haddock requires level 73 in Cooking, resulting in a haddock and 180 Cooking experience. If unsuccessful, it will result in a burnt haddock instead.

Raw haddock can also be cut into fish offcuts by using a knife, with a chance (scaling with Cooking level) of receiving a haddock eye, a herblore secondary used to make super fishing potions.
32320:
Haddock is a type of fish that restores 18 Hitpoints when eaten. Haddock may also boost hitpoints above the base level, by 20% of the base level or by 10, whichever is lower. Similar to the anglerfish, eating a haddock will not overheal if the player is in combat in a PvP area, whether with another player or a monster.

It can be obtained by cooking raw haddock on a fire or cooking range, requiring level 73 Cooking and granting 180 experience when successful. When cooking there is a chance to fail, resulting in a burnt haddock. The burn rate decreases as the player's Cooking level increases, and it will only stop burning at level 99 (96 if the elite Kourend & Kebos Diary has been completed) when cooking at the Hosidius Kitchen.
32323:
Burnt haddock is the result of accidentally burning a raw haddock while attempting to cook haddock. The burn rate decreases as the player's Cooking level increases, and it will only stop burning at level 99 (96 if the elite Kourend & Kebos Diary has been completed) when cooking at the Hosidius Kitchen.

The burnt haddock has no use whatsoever. Like most other burnt food, it is tradeable to other players but not on the Grand Exchange.
32325:
Raw yellowfin is a type of fish caught from yellowfin shoals whilst deep sea trawling , requiring level 79 Fishing and granting 155.5 experience per successful catch with a trawling net , or 31.1 if caught with a fishing rod . They can also be caught occasionally from shimmering and glistening shoals , which require level 69 and 76 Fishing to catch from respectively.

Cooking yellowfin requires level 79 in Cooking , resulting in a yellowfin and 200 Cooking experience. If unsuccessful, it will result in a burnt yellowfin instead.

Raw yellowfin can also be cut into fine fish offcuts by using a knife , with a chance (scaling with Cooking level) of receiving three yellow fin , a herblore secondary used to make extreme energy potions .
32328:
Yellowfin is a type of fish that restores 19 Hitpoints and 20% run energy when eaten.

It can be obtained by cooking raw yellowfin on a fire or cooking range , requiring level 79 Cooking and granting 200 experience when successful. When cooking there is a chance to fail, resulting in a burnt yellowfin . The burn rate decreases as the player's Cooking level increases, and it will only stop burning at level 98 when cooking at the Hosidius Kitchen with the elite Kourend & Kebos Diary completed.

Yellowfin are useful where players lose significant hitpoints and run energy, for example during the Underground Pass quest.
32331:
Burnt yellowfin is the result of accidentally burning a raw yellowfin while attempting to cook yellowfin . The burn rate decreases as the player's Cooking level increases, and it will only stop burning at level 98 when cooking at the Hosidius Kitchen with the elite Kourend & Kebos Diary completed.

The burnt yellowfin has no use whatsoever. Like most other burnt food, it is tradeable to other players but not on the Grand Exchange .
32333:
Raw halibut is a type of fish caught from halibut shoals whilst deep sea trawling, requiring level 83 Fishing and granting 195.5 experience per successful catch with a trawling net, or 39.1 if caught with a fishing rod. They can also be caught occasionally from shimmering and glistening shoals, which require level 69 and 76 Fishing to catch from respectively.

Cooking halibut requires level 83 in Cooking, resulting in a halibut and 212.5 Cooking experience. If unsuccessful, it will result in a burnt halibut instead.
32336:
Halibut is a type of fish that restores 20 Hitpoints when eaten.

It can be obtained by cooking raw halibut on a fire or cooking range . Cooking a halibut requires level 83 Cooking , and grants 212.5 experience when successful. When cooking there is a chance to fail, resulting in a burnt halibut . The burn rate decreases as the player's Cooking level increases, and it will only stop burning at level 99 when cooking at the Hosidius Kitchen with the elite Kourend & Kebos Diary completed.

Like cooked karambwan , halibut can be used as a fast food , a subtype of food that incurs non-standard attack or eating delays when consumed. Halibut may be consumed after other foods without delay; this does not work if the halibut is eaten first, and does not work when eating two halibut in a row. This technique (commonly referred to as combo eating ) can be further enhanced by drinking a dose of Saradomin brew after your alternative food item, and before your halibut (food>brew>halibut) .
32339:
Burnt halibut is the result of accidentally burning a raw halibut while attempting to cook halibut. The burn rate decreases as the player's Cooking level increases, and it will only stop burning at level 99 when cooking at the Hosidius Kitchen with the elite Kourend & Kebos Diary completed.

The burnt halibut has no use whatsoever. Like most other burnt food, it is tradeable to other players but not on the Grand Exchange.
32341:
Raw bluefin is a type of fish caught from bluefin shoals whilst deep sea trawling , requiring level 87 Fishing and granting 220.5 experience per successful catch with a trawling net , or 44.1 if caught with a fishing rod . They can also be caught occasionally from glistening and vibrant shoals , which require level 76 and 86 Fishing to catch from respectively.

Cooking bluefin requires level 87 in Cooking , resulting in a bluefin and 215 Cooking experience. If unsuccessful, it will result in a burnt bluefin instead.
32344:
Bluefin is a type of fish that restores 22 Hitpoints and 5 prayer points when eaten.

It can be obtained by cooking raw bluefin on a fire or cooking range, requiring level 87 Cooking and granting 215 experience when successful. When cooking there is a chance to fail, resulting in a burnt bluefin. The burn rate decreases as the player's Cooking level increases, and it will only stop burning at level 99 when cooking at the Hosidius Kitchen with the elite Kourend & Kebos Diary completed, or when wearing a Cooking cape.

The bluefin is the second highest instant-health single consumption food, behind the marlin, alongside the tuna potato, anglerfish, dark crab and manta ray.
32347:
Burnt bluefin is the result of accidentally burning a raw bluefin while attempting to cook bluefin . The burn rate decreases as the player's Cooking level increases, and it will only stop burning at level 99 when cooking at the Hosidius Kitchen with the elite Kourend & Kebos Diary completed, or when wearing a Cooking cape .

The burnt bluefin has no use whatsoever. Like most other burnt food, it is tradeable to other players but not on the Grand Exchange .
32349:
Raw marlin is a type of fish caught from marlin shoals whilst deep sea trawling , requiring level 91 Fishing and granting 265.5 experience per successful catch with a trawling net , or 53.1 if caught with a fishing rod . They can also be caught occasionally from glistening and vibrant shoals , which require level 76 and 86 Fishing to catch from respectively.

Cooking marlin requires level 91 in Cooking , resulting in a marlin and 225 Cooking experience. If unsuccessful, it will result in a burnt marlin instead.

Raw marlin can also be cut into fine fish offcuts by using a knife , with a chance (scaling with Cooking level) of receiving three marlin scales , a herblore secondary used to make extended stamina potions .
32352:
Marlin is a type of fish that restores 24 Hitpoints when eaten, making it the highest immediate-healing single-bite food.

It can be obtained by cooking raw marlin on a fire or cooking range. Cooking a marlin requires level 91 Cooking, and grants 225 experience when successful. When cooking there is a chance to fail, resulting in a burnt marlin. The burn rate decreases as the player's Cooking level increases, but will never stop burning even at level 99 unless a cooking cape is equipped.
32355:
Burnt marlin is the result of accidentally burning a raw marlin while attempting to cook marlin. The burn rate while cooking these will decrease as players reach higher Cooking levels; there is no level where marlins stop being burned, although wearing a cooking cape will prevent players from burning any food.

The burnt marlin has no use whatsoever. Like most other burnt food, it is tradeable to other players but not on the Grand Exchange.
32357:
A haddock eye is a Herblore secondary used to make super fishing potions. It can be obtained by using a knife on a raw haddock from deep sea trawling, yielding one eye per haddock upon success, whose chance scales with the player's Cooking level.

If cutting on a chum facility, players will receive haddock eyes equal to the number of haddocks cut on that tick, assuming a successful cut. For example, a chum spreader can cut 4 haddocks per tick, yielding a potential 4 haddock eyes scales per tick.
32360:
A yellow fin is a Herblore secondary used to make extreme energy potions, requiring one fin per dose and granting 21 Herblore experience per fin. It can be obtained by using a knife on a raw yellowfin from deep sea trawling, yielding three yellow fins per yellowfin upon success, whose chance scales with the player's Cooking level.

If cutting on a chum facility, players will receive yellow fins equal to three times the number of yellowfin cut on that tick, assuming a successful cut. For example, a chum spreader can cut 4 yellowfin per tick, yielding a potential 12 yellow fins per tick.
32362:
Marlin scales is a Herblore secondary used to make extended stamina potions, requiring one scale per dose. It can be obtained by using a knife on a raw marlin from deep sea trawling, yielding three scales per marlin upon success, whose chance scales with the player's Cooking level.

If cutting on a chum facility, players will receive scales equal to three times the number of marlin cut on that tick, assuming a successful cut. For example, a chum spreader can cut 4 marlins per tick, yielding a potential 12 marlin scales per tick.
32364:
Camphor crates are an item made with a camphor log and four adamantite nails, by using either a hammer or chisel on the logs (both must be present in the inventory, or Imcando hammer equipped). Doing so requires level 62 Crafting, granting 50 experience.

Once made, players can use an ice cooler (purchasable from any Slayer Master) on the crate to create an empty fish crate, which are used to store deep sea fish caught via deep sea trawling,
32366:
Empty fish crates are an item made by using a camphor crate with an ice cooler, which are purchased from Slayer Masters; up to 10 can be made per action. They are used to store raw fish obtained from shoals whilst deep sea trawling; deep sea fish can only be stored within the crate in sets of 10.

Empty fish crates are stackable when empty, allowing it to only take one space in the cargo hold of a boat. When emptying a trawling net into the cargo hold with empty fish crates stored inside, the crates will automatically be filled, with any remainders stored as normal. As each crate can store 10 fish, players can effectively store up to 10 times the cargo hold's capacity in fish by storing crates filled with fish, which can drastically lengthen a trawling trip.

Filled fish crates can only be emptied while standing inside a bank, returning the crate without the ice cooler. This must be done by right-clicking the "Empty" option whilst having a banking interface open; if emptying the fish crate otherwise, the crate will be lost.
32368:
Fish crate (giant krill) is a fish crate containing 10 raw giant krill. It can be obtained by emptying a trawling net filled with at least 10 raw giant krill whilst an empty fish crate is stored in the cargo hold, which effectively allows players to store 10 deep sea fish per cargo space. It may also be made by using them on the crate.

Filled fish crates can only be emptied while standing inside a bank, returning a camphor crate without the ice cooler. This must be done by right-clicking the "Empty" option whilst having a banking interface open; if emptying the fish crate otherwise, the crate will be lost.

32380:
Fish crate (bluefin) is a fish crate containing 10 raw bluefin. It can be obtained by emptying a trawling net filled with at least 10 raw bluefin whilst an empty fish crate is stored in the cargo hold, which effectively allows players to store 10 deep sea fish per cargo space. It may also be made by using them on the crate.

Filled fish crates can only be emptied while standing inside a bank, returning a camphor crate without the ice cooler.

32386:
The Medallion of the Deep is a neck-slot item which allows the player to dive underwater without the need for a diving apparatus and fishbowl helmet . It can also be used during The Great Brain Robbery to safely explore Harmony Island. It is created by assembling eight medallion fragments found on various islands accessed via the Sailing skill, granting 750 Sailing experience along with 500 Crafting experience.

Assembling the medallion requires that the player read the waterlogged journal , which was written by the medallion's creator and contains hints on the location of the fragments. As the final fragment is found on Wintumber Island , the minimum Sailing level needed to obtain the medallion is 63.

If the medallion is lost, players can reclaim it by searching the crate where the waterlogged journal was found (near Henderson on the Pandemonium ). Upon doing so, a chatbox message will appear, stating "Against all common sense, the Medallion of the Deep has somehow found its way into this crate. You quickly grab it before you lose it again."
32388:
Medallion fragments are items found on various islands accessed via the Sailing skill through a variety of activities. There are eight of these fragments, which are assembled into the Medallion of the Deep , an item that allows the wielder to breathe underwater. The medallion is also required for a master clue .

The locations of the fragments are hinted within the waterlogged journal , which was written by the medallion's creator and must be read before the medallion can be assembled. As the final fragment is found on Wintumber Island , the minimum Sailing level needed to obtain the medallion is 63.

If the Medallion is stored in the STASH or lost, the medallion fragments do not need to be reobtained, as the complete Medallion can be retrieved from the crate on The Pandemonium , near Henderson .

32396:
The waterlogged journal is a book found in a crate near Henderson on the Pandemonium.

The journal is written by an unnamed wizard from the first Wizards' Tower (only referred to as "W.S."), who left the Order of Wizards to become a sailor. To aid their crew in finding underwater treasure, they created the Medallion of the Deep, though it was split into eight fragments after the wizard killed their crew in self-defence. The wizard was sent to Rock Island Prison, where they began having nightmares showing them the locations of each fragment. Reading the journal is a requirement for the player to assemble the Medallion of the Deep. If the Medallion of the Deep has been assembled, the journal can no longer be found in the crate.

At this time, the journal cannot be placed within a bookcase in the player-owned house.
32398:
The sailors' amulet is an item that can be obtained as loot when sorting through salvage obtained from shipwreck salvaging . The amulet allows the player to teleport to the Pandemonium , Port Roberts , Red Rock , and Deepfin Point . In order to make use of the amulet's destinations, the player must activate their corresponding Sailors' Marker there.

The amulet consumes 90% less law runes, as it uses one charge per teleport and ten charges can be added by using one law rune and 10 water runes on the amulet, up to a maximum of 10,000 charges. This makes the cost of ten charges 176 coins and the cost of fully charging it 176,000 coins . The amulet cannot be uncharged . No experience points are granted when charging the amulet, and rune-saving equipment such as a staff of water cannot be used to decrease the rune cost.

The amulet's capabilities are at its best when the player has access to Deepfin Point with level 67 Sailing , as the teleport places the player around eight tiles from the bank chest , making it incredibly useful for players who do not have a Crafting cape for a quick bank. The Deepfin Point teleport is also very close to a furnace , anvil , and charter ship .

Only one sailors' amulet can be owned at a time. If lost, players must sort through salvage for another one.

The book about lighthouses is an item obtained by bringing the captain's log to Gerardus once the Northern Ocean is fully charted, which requires a Sailing level of at least 78.

It is given to Larrissa in front of the lighthouse in order to unlock Armadylean paint for boat trims . Doing so requires completion of Horror from the Deep ; otherwise, she will be too worried about her darling to give out Armadylean paint.

As the chest is located on Charred Island, the paint requires a Sailing level of at least 60 to obtain. Players will need a rope the first time they enter the dungeon, which spawns on the southern tip of the island.

32435:
A crate of adamantite ore is an item that may be obtained from a ledger table after taking on a courier task , which must then be delivered to the corresponding destination's port by boarding their boat and sailing to said destination. Players without a crewmate to navigate their boat must store the crate in the cargo hold before they can man the helm.

Multiple of a crate may be required to be delivered for a courier task, in which case players must board their boat multiple times to store the crates (as they can only carry one at a time) or have a crewmate assist them, who will automatically take a crate when the player does so. While any crewmate can carry a crate, those with Deckhandiness levels of at least 3 can carry two at once.

Players cannot unequip the crate normally, nor can they teleport or leave the port area with the crate equipped. If the player leaves the area, a game message appears stating You're leaving port with some cargo. If you do not return it, it will be confiscated by the shipwright wizard's autonomous tracking unit. After 22 ticks (13.2s), the crate will be removed with an accompanying game message stating Your cargo has been confiscated by the S.W.A.T. team.

Multiple of a crate may be required to be delivered for a courier task, in which case players must board their boat multiple times to store the crates (as they can only carry one at a time) or have a crewmate assist them, who will automatically take a crate when the player does so. While any crewmate can carry a crate, those with Deckhandiness levels of at least 3 can carry two at once.

Players cannot unequip the crate normally, nor can they teleport or leave the port area with the crate equipped. If the player leaves the area, a game message appears stating You're leaving port with some cargo. If you do not return it, it will be confiscated by the shipwright wizard's autonomous tracking unit. After 22 ticks (13.2s), the crate will be removed with an accompanying game message stating Your cargo has been confiscated by the S.W.A.T. team.

Multiple of a crate may be required to be delivered for a courier task, in which case players must board their boat multiple times to store the crates (as they can only carry one at a time) or have a crewmate assist them, who will automatically take a crate when the player does so. While any crewmate can carry a crate, those with Deckhandiness levels of at least 3 can carry two at once.

Players cannot unequip the crate normally, nor can they teleport or leave the port area with the crate equipped. If the player leaves the area, a game message appears stating You're leaving port with some cargo. If you do not return it, it will be confiscated by the shipwright wizard's autonomous tracking unit. After 22 ticks (13.2s), the crate will be removed with an accompanying game message stating Your cargo has been confiscated by the S.W.A.T. team.

Multiple of a crate may be required to be delivered for a courier task, in which case players must board their boat multiple times to store the crates (as they can only carry one at a time) or have a crewmate assist them, who will automatically take a crate when the player does so. While any crewmate can carry a crate, those with Deckhandiness levels of at least 3 can carry two at once.

Players cannot unequip the crate normally, nor can they teleport or leave the port area with the crate equipped. If the player leaves the area, a game message appears stating You're leaving port with some cargo. If you do not return it, it will be confiscated by the shipwright wizard's autonomous tracking unit. After 22 ticks (13.2s), the crate will be removed with an accompanying game message stating Your cargo has been confiscated by the S.W.A.T. team.

Multiple of a crate may be required to be delivered for a courier task, in which case players must board their boat multiple times to store the crates (as they can only carry one at a time) or have a crewmate assist them, who will automatically take a crate when the player does so. While any crewmate can carry a crate, those with Deckhandiness levels of at least 3 can carry two at once.

Players cannot unequip the crate normally, nor can they teleport or leave the port area with the crate equipped. If the player leaves the area, a game message appears stating You're leaving port with some cargo. If you do not return it, it will be confiscated by the shipwright wizard's autonomous tracking unit. After 22 ticks (13.2s), the crate will be removed with an accompanying game message stating Your cargo has been confiscated by the S.W.A.T. team.

Small salvage is an item recovered from small shipwrecks via shipwreck salvaging . Level 15 Sailing is required to salvage these, granting 10 experience.

When sorted at a salvaging station (or the boat facility ), players will additionally receive 5.5 Sailing experience and loot.

As with all salvage, small salvage can be stored in your ship's Cargo hold .

32857:
Martial salvage is an item recovered from mercenary shipwrecks via shipwreck salvaging. Level 73 Sailing is required to salvage these, granting 138 experience.

32859:
Fremennik salvage is an item recovered from Fremennik shipwrecks via shipwreck salvaging . Level 80 Sailing is required to salvage these, granting 162 experience.

When sorted at a salvaging station (or the boat facility ), players will additionally receive 75 Sailing experience and loot.

As with all salvage, Fremennik salvage can be stored in your ship's Cargo hold .

Because of the various Fremennik helmets provided from the salvage, players may opt to bring runes or an explorer's ring to cast High Level Alchemy . It could also be beneficial to bring a soul bearer to keep the ensouled troll heads . It is not possible to reanimate ensouled troll heads while on the boat, they must be brought to the Dark Altar after sorting them. Having a seed box is beneficial for collecting the seeds. Having a plank sack is beneficial to collect the mahogany planks . Having a chum station or an advanced chum station speeds up processing the fish into fish offcuts . Alternatively, the player may build a range facility on their boat in order to gain Cooking XP from all the raw fish.
32861:
Opulent salvage is an item recovered from merchant shipwrecks via shipwreck salvaging . Level 87 Sailing is required to salvage these, granting 200 experience if a player is using the salvaging hook.

Crewmates commanded to salvage earn a reduced rate at a percentage dependent on the crew's deckhandiness .

When sorted at a salvaging station (or the boat facility ), players will additionally receive 95 Sailing experience and loot.

As with all salvage, opulent salvage can be stored in your ship's Cargo hold .

32871:
An antique lamp is rewarded from handing in a relic obtained while sorting salvage to Curator Haig Halen. A lamp is only given for the first hand-in of a specific relic, with subsequent hand-ins rewarding 5,000 coins instead.

Rubbing the lamp grants 5,000, 10,000, or 15,000 in any skill at or above level 30, 40, or 50 respectively. The amount given varies depending on the relic handed in, with relics with higher Sailing requirements offering larger lamps:

5,000 experience — rusty locket, mouldy block, dull knife

10,000 experience — broken compass, rusty coin, broken sextant

15,000 experience — smashed mirror, mouldy doll

The lamps cannot be banked, but the relics handed in to receive the lamps can be banked.
